title: M6.2: form fields in Unicode CID fonts show Japanese instead of "?"
author: chent11
body:
## What the user sees

Many Japanese forms give their fields a `/DA` font that the form's `/DR` defines as a **Type0 (CID) font with a predefined Unicode CMap**, such as a non-embedded `HeiseiMin-W3` with `/UniJIS-UCS2-H` or `/UniJIS-UTF16-H`. Choosing a Japanese value in such a combo box, or typing Japanese into such a text field, **shows `?` for every character**.

![Before and after: combo boxes and a multiline text field in a non-embedded HeiseiMin-W3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chent11/pdfcraft/pr-evidence/form-cid-fonts/before-after.png)

Synthetic test file: [cid-font-form-fields.pdf](https://github.com/chent11/pdfcraft/raw/pr-evidence/form-cid-fonts/cid-font-form-fields.pdf). It has two combo boxes (`/UniJIS-UCS2-H` and `/UniJIS-UTF16-H`) and a multiline text field, all in HeiseiMin-W3 (not embedded). Filled with `pdfcraft-cli run` (`form_fill` with 令, 昭 and a Japanese sentence, then `page_render`), built with craft-fonts.

## Cause

`appearance::dr_font` accepted only simple fonts (Type1, TrueType, MMType1). For a Type0 `/DA` font it fell back to Helvetica and encoded the text with `win_ansi`, which maps every character outside WinAnsi to `?`.

## Change

- `pdfcraft-fonts`:
  - `UnicodeCMap` recognises the predefined Unicode CMaps (`Uni*-UCS2|UTF16|UTF8|UTF32[-HW]-H|V`, ISO 32000-2 §9.7.5.2) and encodes text for them.
  - `cjk_width` measures full-width characters as 1 em and half-width forms as ½ em.
  - `wrap_with` wraps with any measure. `wrap` is unchanged.
- `pdfcraft-forms`: when the `/DR` font is such a Type0 font, field appearances use it and encode the text in its CMap. Centring, auto font size, comb cells and multiline wrapping use the CJK widths, so the sentence in the screenshot wraps inside its box.
- Type0 fonts with `Identity-H` or an embedded CMap stream still fall back to Helvetica, as before. They need the font's own glyph mapping, which is follow-up work.
- Builds without craft-fonts have no Japanese substitute font to draw with, …

title: M6.2: check boxes with non-UTF-8 state names show their mark when clicked
author: chent11
body:
## What the user sees

Japanese forms often name a check box's on state in Shift-JIS rather than `/Yes`: 「はい」 ("yes") is `/#82#CD#82#A2`. Other legacy encodings do the same, for example Latin-1 `/S#ED` ("sí"). **Ticking such a box shows no check mark.** The box disappears entirely, its frame included, and the saved file keeps a state no viewer can draw.

![Before and after: three check boxes ticked with form_fill; the two with non-UTF-8 on-state names disappear on main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chent11/pdfcraft/pr-evidence/check-box-states/before-after.png)

Synthetic test file: [non-utf8-check-box-states.pdf](https://github.com/chent11/pdfcraft/raw/pr-evidence/check-box-states/non-utf8-check-box-states.pdf). It has three check boxes, each with its own Off and on appearances: on states `/Yes` (control), `/#82#CD#82#A2` (Shift-JIS) and `/S#ED` (Latin-1). All three were ticked with `pdfcraft-cli run` (`form_fill` true, then `doc_save` and `page_render`).

What gets saved for the Shift-JIS box:

| | `/AS` and `/V` |
|---|---|
| `main` | `/#EF#BF#BD#CD#82#EF#BF#BD` (U+FFFD replacement characters) |
| this PR | `/#82#CD#82#A2`, the widget's own on-state name |

## Cause

`pdfcraft-forms` read state names (`/AP /N` keys, `/AS`, name values of `/V`) with `String::from_utf8_lossy`. A name that isn't UTF-8 became a different string. Ticking the box then wrote that string back through `Object::name`, i.e. different bytes, to `/AS` and `/V`. No `/AP /N` entry matched, so nothing was drawn.

## Change

- `forms::name_text` / `forms::name_bytes`: a lossless mapping between name bytes and text.
  - UTF-8 names read as themselves.
  - Other bytes, and `#`, are written `#XX`, as in PDF name syntax.
  - So `name_bytes(name_text(b)) == b` for every `b`.
- Used everywhere check box and radio button states and values are read or written:
  - widget `on_state` and `state`, and name values of `/V` and `/DV`
  - `/V` and `/AS` in `set_states`, and `/DV` in `set_props`
  - the sta…

title: Issue #537: pdfcraft-cli --help prints the full usage
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #537.

`pdfcraft-cli --help` exited 1 with "see source header for options", so the per-command options were only readable in `main.rs`.

**Change**
- The usage block moves from the doc header into a `USAGE` constant (one copy, so the header and the output can't drift).

- Unknown command: `unknown command 'x'; see pdfcraft-cli --help`, exit 1.

title: Redact pattern: international phone numbers match whole (refs #525)
author: echelon
body:
## What was wrong
Item 4 of #525: the **Phone Numbers** redaction pattern (`crates/redact/src/patterns.rs`, `fn phone`) accepted only 10 digits (11 with a country code), i.e. North American numbers. For `+49 2151 123456` (12 digits) the `+` candidate was rejected and the scan then matched `2151 123456`, so `+49` stayed visible after redaction.

## What changed
`phone()` now accepts, always grouped by at least one separator (space, dash, dot, parentheses), so plain unseparated numbers still never match:
- **E.164** with a leading `+`: 8–15 digits in all (`+49 2151 123456`, `+44 20 7946 0018`, `+33 1 23 45 67 89`).
- **National numbers with a trunk `0`** followed by 6–14 digits (`0211 123456`, `(0211) 123456`, `030 12345678`, `01 23 45 67 89`). To avoid false positives the first digit group must have at least two digits (no decimals like `0.1234567`), and runs that parse as a day-first date (`01.10.2026`, `09-10-2026`) are left to the date pattern.
- North American numbers as before.

`digit_run` now also lets a separator be followed by `(`, so `+49 (0) 2151 123456` is matched whole instead of the partial `(0) 2151 123456`. The parity note for `Redact patterns` lists the supported phone forms.

## Not addressed
The other items in #525 — header/footer page-number tokens, date tokens, and standard stamps following the interface language — are **not** addressed by this PR.

## Tests
- Extended `patterns::tests::phone_numbers` with the `+49 2151 123456` example (asserts a full match), more international/national positives, and negatives (day-first dates, decimals, unseparated numbers, too short / too long `+` numbers).
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` (19 passed), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

Refs #525

title: Issue #324: on Windows 11, a window dragged to another monitor takes its scale
author: cyfung1031
body:
Fixes #324

## Summary

On Windows 11, a window dragged to a monitor with a different scale factor now lands on that monitor and takes its scale, keeping its logical size. PdfCraft vendors winit 0.30.13 with the fix that winit `master` has carried since August 2025 ([rust-windowing/winit#4341](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4341), commit 488c036a). No winit 0.30 release has that fix, and eframe 0.36 depends on winit 0.30.

## Cause

The bug is in winit, not in PdfCraft. When Windows sends `WM_DPICHANGED`, winit 0.30.13 checks whether the window's new rectangle is on "the monitor with the new DPI", and asks `MonitorFromWindow` for that monitor. During a drag, `MonitorFromWindow` still returns the monitor the window is leaving. winit therefore judges the rectangle to be on the wrong monitor and nudges the window back onto the old one. That move sends another `WM_DPICHANGED`, which scales the size again. The two keep triggering each other for as long as the drag lasts. The window grows, the cursor loses its place in the title bar, and the window can stay mostly on the old monitor at the wrong scale. This matches the report in #324: 2560×1600 to 1920×1200, high scale factor to low.

Upstream reports of the same bug: [rust-windowing/winit#4041](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/4041), [rust-windowing/winit#4600](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/4600) (0.30.13 on Windows 11 24H2), [rust-windowing/winit#3040](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/3040), and [emilk/egui#7648](https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/7648) (every eframe app on Windows). The backport PRs to 0.30.x, [rust-windowing/winit#4637](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4637) (closed) and [rust-windowing/winit#4694](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4694) (open), haven't been released.

PdfCraft's own drawing already follows a scale change: the page view picks its render scale from `pixels_per_point` every frame (`canvas.rs`, `view.rend…

title: M7: Type 3 fallback glyphs get a well-formed d1, so Acrobat draws edited text instead of bullets
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## What was wrong
Edit text's Type 3 fallback (used for Japanese and other replacement text the line's own font can't show) writes every glyph procedure starting with:

```
788.9648 0 0 0 0 1000 1000 d1
```

That's seven operands, but `d1` takes six: `wx wy llx lly urx ury` (ISO 32000-2 §9.6.4). pdfium, Quartz, MuPDF and poppler ignore the extra operand and draw the glyph. **Acrobat doesn't: it draws a bullet for every character.** So edited text looked right in PdfCraft but became a row of dots in Acrobat, which is what the recipient or the print shop usually opens.

Observed with Acrobat 2020 (20.1.30002) on Windows 11, through its Explorer thumbnail renderer: edited text showed as "• • • • •". With only the `d1` line corrected and the rest of the file byte-identical, the same renderer draws the real glyphs.

## Change
`type3_path` writes `wx 0 llx lly urx ury d1` using the glyph's own bounds, rounded outward. Empty glyphs (spaces) get a zero box. Nothing else changes; the glyph outlines and widths are as before.

## Test
`type3_fallback_glyphs_declare_a_well_formed_d1` (in `pdfcraft-edit`) replaces a line with Japanese text, saves and reopens. It then checks each CharProc: exactly six operands before `d1`, `wy` = 0, and a box that encloses every `m`/`l` point of the glyph. It fails on main (seven operands) and passes here. It skips without craft-fonts, like the other fallback tests.

Gates (macOS arm64, `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` set to craft-fonts @ abb83316):
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace`: green

#528 touches the same function (proportional spacing for Cyrillic/Greek fallback glyphs). Whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase; I'll do it.

title: M1: stream data read from a file points into the file instead of being copied
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Every stream COS loads is copied out of the document's bytes (`crates/cos/src/parser.rs`, `data[start..start + len].to_vec()`). The copy then stays in the document's object cache until the document closes.

Anything that reads every object leaves a second copy of all stream data behind:

- **Full saves.** `write_full` reads every reachable object. It runs for Save As ▸ optimized and for new documents from Create, Combine, Extract and Split. It also runs on every refresh after an edit that needs a full rewrite (repaired files, security changes, redaction), because `write_incremental` falls back to it.
- **Walks over all pages.** Opening a document runs `edit::marks_present`, which loads every page's content streams just to read their `/PCMark` key.

Measured with an exact heap counter: after a full save of a 208 MB document, the document holds **208.2 MB** more than before, a second copy of every stream, until it is closed.

## Fix

**`Stream::raw` is now `pdfcraft_cos::Bytes`** instead of `Arc<Vec<u8>>`. A `Bytes` is either owned bytes or a range of a larger shared buffer. It dereferences to `[u8]` and compares by content, and its `Debug` prints the same bytes as before.

**Parsing.** A document parses its own objects with `parse_indirect_shared`, so stream data is a range of the bytes the document already holds. `parse_indirect` (public) still copies, as before.

**Unchanged:** decrypted streams and streams built in memory (`from_raw`, `flate`, encryption on save) own their bytes, as before.

**No foreign files kept alive.** `Document::set` and `Document::add` give a stream from *another* document's file its own copy of just its bytes (`adopt`). Inserting pages or combining files therefore never keeps a whole source file alive. Objects only enter a document's edits through those two methods.

`Bytes` reads with `get`, so it never panics. A stream range past the end of the file is now an error rather than an index panic.

**Other crates** needed only two…

title: A newly opened document starts at the top, not where the last session scrolled
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## What
After a restart, a PDF that had never been opened before showed up part-way down, at the page some other document was left on in the previous session. It now opens at the top of page 1.

## Why
Since #259 (#189) the page view's `ScrollArea` is salted with the document's `DocId`, so each tab keeps its own scroll offset. eframe persists egui's memory (`persist_egui_memory` defaults to `true`), scroll offsets included, to `app.ron` every 30 s and on quit, and restores it at the next launch. `DocId`s start again at 1 every launch, so the first document opened inherited the offset stored under id 1 last session, the second the one under id 2, and so on.

## How
`DocView` notes when its page view is first shown (`shown`), and on that frame the scroll offset is set to zero. Navigation queued before the first frame is applied on top, so `--page`, a PDF's open action and Reopen last session (#462, which restores pages through `goto`) still land on their page. Tabs that were already shown keep their own position, as #189 needs. egui's other persisted memory (panel sizes and the like) is untouched. Turning off `persist_egui_memory` or salting per launch was considered and rejected: the first would drop all of it, and the second would fill `app.ron` with useless entries every launch.

## Verified
- New test `crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs::a_new_document_opens_at_the_top_after_a_relaunch` scrolls a.pdf to page 4, saves egui's memory through eframe's own RON `set_value`/`get_value`, restores it in a fresh app, opens c.pdf (`DocId(1)`) and checks it starts on page 1 and then keeps its own position. It failed before the fix (c.pdf opened on page 4). `each_document_keeps_its_own_scroll_position` (#189) still passes. The new test is added as evidence on the `view.document-tabs` parity entry.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed. cargo-deny isn't installed locally, so `deny` was skipped; no dependencies changed.
- Real app on macOS through the control channel, in portable m…

title: M3: rasters reach egui without a copy on the UI thread
author: cyfung1031
body:
Follow-up to #404, which removed the renderer-side copy of each raster.

## Problem

Every page, tile and thumbnail raster was still copied once on the **UI thread** before reaching the GPU. `canvas.rs` turned `RenderedPage::rgba` (`Vec<u8>`) into an `egui::ColorImage` with `ColorImage::from_rgba_premultiplied`, which builds a new `Vec<Color32>` pixel by pixel.

The copy can't simply be skipped: `Color32` is 4-byte aligned (`#[repr(align(4))]`) and a `Vec<u8>` isn't, so the bytes can't become `Color32`s in place.

Measured on Apple M1 Pro (release), this is UI-thread time spent per result, against a 60 fps frame budget of 16.7 ms:

| Raster | UI-thread copy |
|---|---|
| 1024×1024 tile (4 MB) | 0.54 ms |
| 1275×1650 page (8 MB) | 0.76 ms |
| 2550×3300 page (33 MB) | 5.4 ms |
| 6182×8000 page (197 MB) | 36 ms |

## Fix

Render straight into memory that is already aligned to whole pixels, and let egui take it over.

**hayro, vendored patch 7:**
- `render_size(page, settings)` gives the pixel size `render` produces.
- `render_into(page, cache, settings, render_settings, buffer)` renders into a caller's buffer. vello's `render_to_pixmap` is itself `render_to_buffer` over the pixmap's bytes, so the result is the same.
- `render` is now `render_into` on a new pixmap, so its output is unchanged for every other caller.

**pdfcraft-render:**
- `RenderedPage::rgba` is now `Pixels`: the same premultiplied RGBA8 bytes, kept in a `Vec<u32>` with one word per pixel and the bytes in R, G, B, A memory order.
- It dereferences to `[u8]`, so every existing reader compiles unchanged: export, OCR, compare, the CLI, automation and tests.
- `render_page` allocates it (`render_size`) and calls `render_into`.
- #404's move-out helper is no longer needed.

**pdfcraft-ui-egui:**
- The canvas's `texture_image` reinterprets the words as `Vec<Color32>` (same size and alignment) and builds the `ColorImage` from them, without a copy.
- If the size doesn't match, it falls back to the previous copy…

title: Bookmarks and links go to their destination's position and zoom
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Bookmarks and GoTo links only went to the top of their target page. The inspector reduced every destination to a page index, so `/XYZ left top zoom`, `/FitH`, `/FitV`, `/FitR` and `/FitB*` were dropped. For example, a reportlab bookmark `[p1 /XYZ 0 420 0]` went to the top of page 1 instead of putting y = 420 at the top of the window, as Acrobat does.

Destinations now keep their view (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.2, Table 149):

- **render:**
  - `DestView` (`Top`, `Xyz`, `Fit`, `FitH`, `FitV`, `FitR`) is read from explicit arrays, `/D` dictionaries and named destinations (`/Names /Dests` and the PDF 1.1 `/Dests`).
  - `OutlineItem` gains `view`, and `LinkTarget::Page` carries it.
  - Hostile values never fail. Missing, wrong-typed or non-finite operands are null; a zoom that isn't positive keeps the zoom; an unknown type, or a `/FitR` without four numbers, falls back to the page top.
  - `PageInfo::dest_fraction` maps a user-space point to the displayed page through the crop box origin, `/Rotate` and the view rotation.
- **ui:** `DocView::go_to_dest` applies the view for bookmark and link clicks, so it also covers `ui.click` on the control channel.
  - `/XYZ` puts (left, top) at the window's top-left, beside the quick-action gutter, at its zoom. A null or 0 zoom keeps the current zoom.
  - `/Fit`, `/FitH` and `/FitV` switch to fit page, width and height, with top/left at the edge.
  - `/FitR` zooms so the rectangle fits, centred.

  The pending point is applied just before the page view's `ScrollArea` is shown, and clamped to the content.

Not covered yet: the `/FitB*` content box (it's read as the whole page), and destination positions in `doc_info` automation output.

### Verification
- **Unit tests:** operand parsing (including NaN/inf, bad types and a short `/FitR`), a fixture with every destination form, point mapping under crop offsets and rotations, and the state `go_to_dest` leaves.
- **kittest:** clicking a `/XYZ 0 420 0` bookmark on a page whose crop box is offset…

title: Linux: prefer the discrete GPU on desktops with a monitor on each GPU (fixes #445)
author: echelon
body:
**What was wrong.** On Linux, `pick_adapter` preferred the integrated GPU whenever it drove any display, so hybrid laptops (#8) stay on the low-power GPU. A desktop with one monitor on the Intel iGPU and one on an NVIDIA card looked identical, so wgpu got the Intel adapter. It passed `is_surface_supported` but then failed to configure the surface (`ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR`), and egui-wgpu panicked ("The surface isn't supported by this adapter").

**What changed** (`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs` only):
- `linux_display_gpus` now returns `DisplayGpu { pci, internal_panel }` and marks a GPU when one of its connected connectors is a built-in panel (`eDP`, `LVDS`, `DSI`).
- `pick_adapter`: a GPU driving a display still comes first. Among several, the one driving the built-in panel wins (laptops behave as before). With no built-in panel anywhere and more than one display GPU (a desktop), the discrete GPU wins. When no adapter matches a display, it still picks the most frugal one.

title: Dependencies keep only line tables in dev builds (fixes #454)

## What was wrong
On Windows each integration-test binary links the whole app and gets its own 500–600 MB PDB, so one `cargo test --workspace` needs ~38 GB of `target`. `[profile.dev.package."*"]` only set `opt-level = 2`, so every dependency (egui, wgpu, boa, hayro, …) was built with full debug info and all of it was merged into every PDB.

title: Shift+click extends the text selection (refs #527)
author: echelon
body:
## What was wrong
A plain click on a page (`canvas.rs`, the `else if resp.clicked() && !over_link` branch of the text layer) cleared the text selection whatever modifiers were held, so you couldn't extend a selection with Shift+click the way you can in Acrobat.

## What changed
- If Shift is held and there is a text selection on the clicked page, the click now moves the selection head to the nearest text position under the pointer and keeps the anchor. Clicking before the anchor selects backwards from it.
- Without Shift, or with no selection on the clicked page, a click still clears the selection, as before. Shift+click on a different page therefore clears it too.
- Parity entry `view.text-select`: added the new evidence test and updated the notes. Cross-page selection is now listed under "Missing".

## Out of scope
This covers only the first request in #527 (Shift+click). **Cross-page text selection** (dragging or Shift+clicking across a page boundary) is not implemented, because `Selection` is single-page. The issue stays open for that.

## Tests
- New kittest `crates/ui-egui/tests/text_select.rs::shift_click_extends_the_selection_from_its_anchor`: drag over "quick", then Shift+click on "brown" gives "quick brown", Shift+click before the anchor gives "The q", a plain click clears the selection, and Shift+click with nothing selected selects nothing. It fails on main (the selection is cleared) and passes with the fix.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` all pass.

title: Typed and drawn signatures stay upright on rotated pages (fixes #299)
author: echelon
body:
**What was wrong.** On pages with `/Rotate` 90/180/270 (common in scanned or landscape PDFs), Fill & Sign placed typed and drawn signatures and initials sideways/upside down. The box and the strokes/outlines were laid out along user-space axes, which the page turns, while the click point is a displayed point. Only image signatures were counter-rotated (#485).

**What changed.**
- `pdfcraft_engine::signature_image::upright_box(rotation, at, w, h)`: the displayed-axes box computation split out of `SignatureImage::rect` (which now uses it).
- `typed_signature_shape(at, text, height, rotation)`: box via `upright_box`; the normalised outlines are turned back inside it so the name reads across as displayed.
- `fill_sign::signature_at` / `typed_signature_at` take the rotation; drawn strokes map through the displayed right/up vectors from `pdfcraft_model::view_matrix_for` (the same matrix the image-signature path uses). `place()` passes `info.rotation`; `fill_sign_add` passes the page's rotation.
- The appearance is plain geometry (no form `/Matrix`), so any viewer shows it upright. On unturned pages the mapping is the identity, so nothing changes there (existing 0° tests still pass unchanged).

**Tests.**
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/fill_sign.rs::drawn_and_typed_signatures_stay_upright_on_rotated_pages`: places a drawn signature (asymmetric "L"), a typed signature and typed initials via `fill_sign::place` on 0/90/180/270 pages, renders, and checks each displayed ink box is wider than tall, anchored at the point, matches the 0° render (box ±1 px, <10% ink-pixel difference), and the L isn't mirrored. Fails on main (90°: box 30x35 instead of 150x30).
- `crates/automation/tests/automation.rs::typed_signatures_stay_upright_on_rotated_pages`: same checks via `fill_sign_add`, before and after save/reopen.
- fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and full tests of pdfcraft-engine, pdfcraft-automation, pdfcraft-ui-egui pass.

Fixes #299

title: View: the middle button pans instead of drawing with markup tools
author: codyvogt
body:
## Problem

egui's drag responses (`Response::drag_started()` and related) accept **every** pointer button. On Windows and macOS, a middle-button drag therefore went to whichever page tool was selected:

- **Draw (ink)** drew a freehand stroke with the mouse wheel button.
- Crop, text selection and annotation move/resize reacted the same way.

Linux didn't have this problem, because its middle-click auto-scroll already blocks page input while the button is in use.

## Fix

This is done in `AutoScroll` (`crates/ui-egui/src/autoscroll.rs`), so both the document view and Organize Pages get it with no tool-by-tool changes:

- **Outside Linux**, a middle-button drag that starts in the unobstructed viewport pans 1:1 while the button is held, and shows a Grabbing cursor.
- Page input is blocked from the press through the release. The press, the drag and the release never reach a tool, so a tool can't start or finish a drag with the middle button.
- A press outside the viewport, or over a dialog or popup, does nothing. Losing window focus, switching tabs or opening a dialog ends the pan (the existing `cancel()` paths).
- Non-finite pointer positions give a zero delta. No new `unwrap` or indexing.
- **Linux** is unchanged and keeps the latched auto-scroll.

## Tests

- **New unit tests** (`autoscroll.rs`):
  - 1:1 pan on both axes, including movement in the release frame

  - presses outside the viewport are ignored

  - outside Linux, the page follows the pointer
  - a primary-button drag afterwards still draws

title: M2: normalize JPEG2000 samples without overflowing
author: Streetblock
body:
A tiny JPEG2000 image with `/BitsPerComponent 32` reached `1_u32 << 32` in the vendored sample normalizer. It panicked in the public decoder and caused PageRenderer to return an error for the whole page. Wide floating-point sample scaling also wrapped the white endpoint at some supported depths.

Normalize 1–32-bit samples using the existing bit mask and exact bounded `u64` arithmetic. Refuse zero rows/components before chunking. Ordinary 1/8/16-bit values and 8-bit Gray/RGB/alpha behavior remain covered. The same code works without the std-only floating-point rounding helper.

The fixture is a contributor-written, single-pixel JPEG2000 codestream constructed in Rust. Workspace regressions exercise `Stream::decoded_image`, valid gray pixels and subsequent page content; additional vendor tests cover all supported depths and every byte value at 1/8/16 bits. No binary fixtures or assets are added.

Before the fix, the workspace cases produce two expected failures and two passing controls, including the actual shift-overflow panic. The unrelated non-8-bit alpha-mask representation remains a separate follow-up.

Validation on Debian x86_64 / Rust 1.95, rebased and checked on upstream base 0375bd1:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all eight steps passed (format, strict workspace/all-target Clippy, workspace tests, layers, Wasm, assets, cargo-deny, parity).
- `cargo check -p pdfcraft-cli --no-default-features`: passed.
- Five additional JPX normalization vendor tests passed using an identical source copy with workspace dependency pins; the images feature also checks without std on wasm32.
- CLI `doc_open`, `doc_info` and `page_render` passed on the synthetic 32-bit JPX page; the resulting 40x40 image retains the expected red rectangle pixel.

title: Fix Windows HiDPI startup crash above 8192 pixels
author: msaulc
body:
Opening a PDF attachment from classic Outlook on a mixed-DPI Windows setup can restore a 3440-point window at 250% scale, producing an 8600 × 3423 surface. The default egui-wgpu device enables only 8192 pixels, so `Surface::configure` panics before the application opens the document.

Wrap the existing device-descriptor callback and enable the selected adapter's supported 2D texture extent. Preserve its other backend-specific device requirements, GPU selection and renderer fallback. Small adapters are never asked for a larger 2D extent than they advertise. Hardware resolution limits still apply; this change does not clamp arbitrary window geometry or resolve the separate monitor-drag behavior in #324.

Closes #577.

Validation:

- The synthetic regression for the observed dimensions fails with the previous 8192-pixel behavior and passes with the fix.
- Desktop app tests: 30 passed, 1 existing ignored test.
- A real wgpu device check on WSL's llvmpipe adapter rejects an 8600 × 3423 render texture with the previous limit and accepts it with the supported 16384-pixel limit.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1392 passed, 4 existing ignored tests.

Resetting the saved window geometry allowed a launch from Outlook's temporary directory, but the crash returned after the large maximized state was restored. A per-app Windows System DPI compatibility override now lets the affected user open the attachment directly in Outlook. The source change has not been installed into that Windows release; native Windows validation of the compiled fix remains outstanding.

title: M2: bound PDF functions and reject invalid calculator operations
author: Streetblock
body:
Malformed calculator functions could panic on integer division by zero/overflow, oversized shifts and the minimum signed rotation. Stitching-function construction and nested calculator procedures also had no shared resource limits. A tiny invalid shading function could therefore turn the whole page into a renderer error.

Bound construction to 64 nested functions and 10,000 total nodes with path-based cycle detection. Shared children remain supported and count toward the work limit. Every listed stitching child must resolve; empty lists and unresolved references reject the function instead of retaining a truncated prefix. Calculator parsing and evaluation each have a shared 10,000-entry budget and a depth limit of 64. These are implementation resource limits, documented separately from PDF format requirements.

Use checked integer division and indexing, logical 32-bit shifts with zero fill, and rotation without negating `i32::MIN`. Propagate fixed-stack overflow rather than silently truncating work. Public signatures stay the same; rejection uses the existing `None`. The optional logging feature reports budget, cycle and invalid-division failures.

Workspace tests cover real public function construction/evaluation, ordinary arithmetic, exact/over boundaries, shared references, safe cycle cases and continued page rendering. Vendor unit tests cover additional internal budget paths. The original public-API regression run gives 11 expected failures and one passing control; no stack-overflow or excessive-allocation probe is used. No binary fixtures or assets are added.

author: pincetgore

### Summary
Enables dual-purpose (Single Package Authoring) installation for the Windows MSI package across all target architectures (`x64`, `x86`, `arm64`). Users can choose during setup whether to install PdfCraft only for the current user (requiring no administrator privileges or UAC elevation) or for all users (elevated into Program Files).

title: M2: bound image resampling buffers before allocation
author: Streetblock
body:
Image downsampling was selected whenever either axis shrank, even if the other axis grew enough to create a very large intermediate image. The source pixel cap did not bound destination buffers, RGBA expansion or resampling planning.

Check source/data lengths, target and crossed dimensions, RGBA/padding bytes, finite transforms and a conservative filter/scratch estimate before planning or allocating. Preserve the existing 2^28-pixel policy, allow source sides up to 2^20, and enforce u16 sides on the final backend bitmap. Valid wide sources can still shrink before that final check.

An over-budget resize or scaler failure retains the original data and dimensions when the backend can represent them, preserving image geometry. Unsupported inputs or allocation failures are logged. The handled conversion/output/scratch/padding buffers use fallible reserves; this does not claim a global process-memory budget or make opaque library allocations fallible.

Small metadata regressions use a 128-pixel budget and fail before a buffer is allocated. Real renderer controls cover valid RGB, gray and transparent wide strips, as well as a bounded source image whose unsafe anisotropic resize is refused. That last integration case is only run with the fix; the original-code regressions never request huge buffers. The original sizing run gives three expected failures and one passing control. No binary fixtures or assets are added.

Validation on Debian x86_64 / Rust 1.95, with the exact final patch rebased onto upstream 86ec142:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all eight steps passed (format, strict workspace/all-target Clippy, workspace tests, layers, Wasm, assets, cargo-deny, parity).

title: CLI: pdfcraft-cli ui refuses a control file another user could plant
author: jcl-bit
body:
The follow-up that #338 listed under "Not in this PR". #338 made the app replace the control file by rename, so a planted link can no longer redirect the write. This PR covers the other half: the client that reads the file, and what the app does when the write fails.

You didn't ask for it, so here is the risk plainly. It needs **another local user account on the same machine** (a shared workstation, a lab or terminal server, a multi-user Linux box). It can't be reached from a PDF or over the network. Four commits, so any of them can be dropped; the fourth is the change from review.

**The risk**

`pdfcraft-cli ui --control FILE` reads the port and token from FILE and sends the token, then the command, to that port. Commands include `type` (typed text) and `screenshot`. It never checked who wrote FILE. The README suggested `--control /tmp/pc.json`. In a shared `/tmp`, another user can create `/tmp/pc.json` first, naming a port they listen on. Since #338 the app's rename then fails (the sticky bit refuses it), but that failure was only logged and the app kept running. The CLI then sent every command to the other user's listener, along with the token from their own file. That gave them:
- **Everything you typed through `ui type`.** A script that fills in a password dialog this way would hand them the password.
- **Control of the replies.** The CLI prints whatever they answer as if it came from the app, and for `screenshot --out x.png` it writes their bytes to your `x.png`.

Your real token isn't exposed in that case, because the app never managed to write it.

**1. `pdfcraft-cli ui` refuses a control file it can't trust**

- A symbolic link and anything but a regular file are refused, on every platform.
- On macOS, Linux and FreeBSD, a file owned by another user is refused, and so is one with any group or other permission bits. The app always writes mode 600.
- On those systems, the owner and mode are read from the opened file, not the path, and its device and inode m…

title: Windows: Save asks where to keep an Outlook attachment instead of writing its temporary copy
author: art804
body:
## Problem

Opening a PDF attachment from Outlook opens a copy in Outlook's own cache:

- classic Outlook: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\Content.Outlook\<random>\`
- the new Outlook: a folder under the `Microsoft.OutlookForWindows` package

Save writes back to that copy, which goes wrong one of two ways:

- **The save fails,** because Outlook can still hold the file.
- **The save seems to work,** but the edits never reach the email. They're deleted the next time Outlook clears its cache.

Either way the user believes their work is saved somewhere it isn't. Other editors handle this by treating the copy like an untitled document.

## Change

`save_then` now treats a path in either cache like a document without a file. **Save** opens the Save As dialog, and the copy in Outlook's cache is left alone. After that the chosen file is the document's file, and **Save** writes it directly.

- One predicate, `is_mail_temp_copy`, matched on either path separator and in any case, so it's testable on every platform.
- **Unchanged:** Save As, autosave and crash recovery, which write elsewhere. Agent tools (`doc_save`) and `save_override` are unchanged too.
- No new strings and no new dependencies.

## Tests

`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs`:

- `outlook_attachment_copies_are_recognised_on_either_separator_and_in_any_case`
- `ordinary_paths_are_not_mail_copies`, which includes a OneDrive folder named "Content.Outlook notes" and the IE cache.
- `save_asks_where_to_keep_an_email_attachment_and_leaves_the_temporary_copy_alone`. This is end to end: it opens a file under `INetCache/Content.Outlook/…`, edits it, and Saves. The test checks three things: Save asks, the cached copy is byte-identical afterwards, and the document lands where the dialog answered (through `pick_override`). It then edits again and checks that the next Save writes without asking. The test fails with the fix reverted.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib editing::` passes (11 tests). `cargo clippy -…

title: Windows: open files in the running PdfCraft instead of a new window each time (#282, #317)
author: art804
body:
## Problem

Outlook attachments, Explorer double-clicks and Open With all start `pdfcraft.exe "<file>"`. Every file therefore gets its own process and window. After a morning of email there are a dozen PdfCraft windows open, each with one tab (#282, #317).

## Change

The first PdfCraft listens on a Unix domain socket. A later launch that **only names files** sends their absolute paths and waits for `ok`, then exits. The running app opens them as tabs through the existing `OsEvent::Open` path, the one macOS Apple events already use, and comes to the front.

- **Socket location:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PdfCraft\instance-<session>.sock`, or the data folder of a portable copy (beside `Recovery` in both cases). It's named after `SESSIONNAME` (`Console`, `RDP-Tcp#3`…), so the same user signed in twice never gets files opening on the other screen.
- **Protocol:** one line each way, `{"open":["C:\\…\\a.pdf"]}` then `ok`. Requests are capped at 1 MiB and both sides time out after 5 s. Anything that isn't a non-empty list of non-empty strings is refused.
- **What stays as it is today:**
  - `--new-window`
  - any other option (`--page`, `--control`, `--create-images`…)
  - a launch without files
  - any failure to hand over within 5 s

  All of these open a window of their own. A launch without files still starts the listener when nothing is running yet.
- **Platforms:** only Windows changes. On other platforms `claim()` returns `Alone`, so the module compiles and its tests run everywhere.

### Why a Unix socket, and why `uds_windows`

- **Isolation comes from the file system.** The socket is a file in the user's own profile, so other accounts can't create, replace or reach it. Nobody else can intercept a launch or open files in this user's window. A named pipe lives in a global namespace, and stopping squatting there needs a custom security descriptor, which in Rust means `unsafe`.
- **No `unsafe` in the workspace.** `std` has no Unix sockets on Windows, and calling Winsock direc…

A window larger than the GPU's texture limit no longer closes PdfCraft. This is the follow-up echelon suggested on #578: that PR (now on main) raised the device's limit to the adapter's, which moves the ceiling, but a window beyond the adapter's own limit still panicked in `Surface::configure`.

## The change

- `vendor/egui-wgpu`: egui-wgpu 0.36.2 as published (first commit, plus egui's `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` from the 0.36.2 tag, which the crates.io package leaves out), then one patch marked `PdfCraft patch (#577)` in `src/winit.rs`:
  - `winit::surface_fit(width, height, max_side)` shrinks both sides by one factor so neither exceeds the device's `max_texture_dimension_2d`; the longer side is set to exactly the limit. egui then draws at that factor (`pixels_per_point × render_scale`), so the whole window is drawn into the surface. On DX12, the Windows default, the swapchain uses `DXGI_SCALING_STRETCH` (wgpu-hal `dx12/mod.rs`), so the image fills the window, slightly softer, and stays lined up with the pointer. wgpu's GL backend copies the swapchain to the window unscaled (`gles/wgl.rs`), so there the fitted image sits in a corner: degraded, but no longer a crash.
  - It applies wherever a surface is sized: `install_surface`, `resize_and_generate_depth_texture_view_and_msaa_view` (start-up restore, resize, maximise, DPI change, fullscreen) and `recreate_surface`, which starts again from the window's own size. The depth and MSAA textures follow, and the screen descriptor uses the fitted size, so scissor rects stay inside the target.
  - A fitted window logs one warning when it enters that state.
- `[patch.crates-io]`: `egui-wgpu = { path = "vendor/egui-wgpu" }`, next to winit.
- `vendor/README.md`, `docs/development.md` (GPU surface limits), `ROADMAP.md` log.

## Root cause

- wgpu reports a failed `Surface::configure` as an uncaptured validation error, and its default handler panics. eframe configures the surface in `painter.set_window` before the app is…

title: F2: read glyph names by the naming algorithm, and stop reading Symbol as Latin
author: tanish2k09
body:
Phase F 4.1, task F2 (first half). **Stacked on #357** — it builds on `Std14::from_base_font` from that PR, so review #357 first; the diff here is the last commit only.

## What was wrong

I probed the current behaviour rather than reading the code, which is how both of these turned up:

```
Symbol 0x61        -> Some("a")   # should be alpha, U+03B1
ZapfDingbats 0x61  -> Some("a")   # should be a dingbat
MacExpert 0x61     -> Some("a")   # not Latin at that code
glyph_unicode("f_i")          -> None
glyph_unicode("a.sc")         -> None
glyph_unicode("uni00660069")  -> None
```

A simple font with no `/ToUnicode` fell back to StandardEncoding **whatever font it was**, so Symbol's built-in encoding was read as Latin.

**This is the map `redact` matches patterns against** (`crates/redact/src/interp.rs`), as well as what `edit` uses for text. A wrong character there is a silent redaction failure, which is why this is worth more than its size suggests: a wrong character is worse than no character.

## What changed

**Encodings.** Symbol, ZapfDingbats and MacExpert now yield *no* mapping rather than a Latin one. A named base encoding is always honoured, including on Symbol — naming one is a deliberate statement. `/Differences` still applies on top, so a font that tells us what a code means is still believed.

**One deliberate restraint, and it is the part most worth reviewing.** This keys on the base font *name*, not the `/FontDescriptor` symbolic flag. A great many ordinary Latin TrueType subsets set that flag and still rely on a Latin encoding, so suppressing the implicit table on the flag would lose real text across a large share of real documents — a much bigger regression than the bug being fixed. `the_symbolic_flag_alone_does_not_suppress_the_latin_default` pins that so it is not "fixed" into a regression later.

**Glyph names** now follow the published naming *algorithm* (not the AGL data table, which this crate does not hold): cut at the first `.`, split on `_`,…

title: Tab strip: shrink tabs before scrolling, keep Open in sight; ignore about:blank titles
author: max1e6
body:
Three commits for the document tab strip. Refs #397; builds on #416.

### M3: tabs shrink to fit before they scroll, and Open stays in sight
#416 made overflowing tabs scroll. With seven or so long file names open, the tabs still kept their full width, so they scrolled at once, and the **Open** button lived inside the scrolling area and scrolled out of sight with them.

- Tabs now **shrink first, as browsers do**: narrow tabs keep their width, wider ones share what is left equally, and their names end in "…" (measured, so they're cut where they actually stop fitting; the tooltip and accessibility name keep the whole name). Only at the narrowest (110 pt) does the strip scroll.
- **Open** sits right after the tabs, **outside** the scrolling area: right after the last tab when everything fits, and next to the controls on the right when the tabs overflow.
- `tab_cap` (the shared width) is a pure function with unit tests; `ellipsized_prefix` from the Pages panel is reused for the measured "…".
- Test: `ui.rs::tabs_shrink_to_fit_before_they_scroll_and_open_stays_in_sight` (seven long names shrink without overlapping each other, Open or Discord; with twenty, Open stays in sight left of Discord). The existing overflow, RTL and narrow-strip tab tests still pass.

### M3: arrows step through tabs that don't fit, and tabs keep most of their name
Testing with many documents open showed that tabs shrinking to 110 pt left a few characters each, with nothing to show that more tabs were hidden.

The mouse wheel still scrolls, and the active tab is still brought into view. With everything fitting, there are no arrows.

title: Decode outline titles with BOMs and raw UTF-8 consistently (refs #142)
author: echelon
body:
## What was wrong
Bookmark titles were decoded with `lopdf::decode_text_string`, which:
- keeps a PDF 2.0 UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`) as a visible U+FEFF (`trim()` doesn't strip it),
- drops the whole title when the bytes after a UTF-8 BOM are invalid UTF-8,
- decodes BOM-less raw UTF-8 (common from some producers) as PDFDocEncoding mojibake (`概述` → `æ¦‡è¿°`).

Outline editing (`pdfcraft-organize`) used a separate decoder, `pdfcraft_cos::PdfString::to_text`, so the panel and the editor could disagree.

## What changed
- `PdfString::to_text` (cos): UTF-8 after a BOM decodes lossily; a BOM-less string that is valid non-ASCII UTF-8 is read as UTF-8; Latin-1/PDFDocEncoding bytes that aren't valid UTF-8 stay PDFDocEncoding; stray leading U+FEFF (doubled BOMs) are removed.
- `crates/render/src/inspect.rs`: titles, name-tree keys and field values now decode through that same function.

The reporter's attached file decodes correctly on main, so it did not reproduce; this hardens the decoder against the encodings that produce the reported symptom (and #210).

## Tests
- `inspect::tests::outline_titles_decode_every_text_string_encoding`: synthetic outline with UTF-16BE, UTF-8+BOM, invalid UTF-8 after BOM, raw UTF-8 CJK, PDFDocEncoding Latin-1 and doubled-BOM titles. Fails on main (`["第一章", "\u{feff}目录", "", "æ¦‡è¿°", "Café", "\u{feff}A"]`), passes now.
- `object::tests::text_string_encodings` in cos, including odd-length/empty edge cases.
- `cargo test` for cos, render, organize, forms, xfdf, a11y; clippy `-D warnings` on cos and render; `cargo fmt --check`.

Refs #142

title: No form bar for push-button-only documents; Screen annotations aren't comments (refs #169)
author: echelon
body:

title: Windows: open documents in existing window via single-instance forwarding
author: mjshfrvstj-sys
body:
## Summary

On Windows, subsequent PDF launches currently create separate application windows. This change forwards ordinary document-launch paths to the existing PdfCraft instance for the same settings profile, opening them as tabs through the normal document-opening path. Multiple paths remain multiple tabs, preserving existing tabs and unsaved work.

The upstream conflicts have been resolved, retaining current upstream tests and parity definitions. Validation for the integrated commit is listed below.

## Implementation

- Owner-scoped Windows named pipe, with remote clients rejected and no new network listener or arbitrary command interface.
- An OS-held file lock elects one primary per settings profile and releases ownership on process exit or crash; stale file contents do not determine ownership.
- Strict versioned path-only requests, bounded messages, queues, concurrent clients and timeouts. The secondary exits after acknowledgement of an accepted batch.
- Forwarded paths enter the existing OS-event → `PdfCraftApp::open_path` route. No separate document loader is introduced.
- One launch-scoped owner survives wgpu initialization failure and OpenGL fallback. Both app creators borrow the same listener; discarded creators do not drain queued batches. Terminal startup failure releases resources.

Acknowledgement means **queued in memory**, not durably delivered or successfully parsed. A terminal startup failure or crash can lose pending batches. Ambiguous acknowledgement loss is reported without automatic retransmission, avoiding silent duplicate tabs.

## Compatibility

Portable profiles determine both persistence and instance identity. Independent `--create-images` launches retain their upstream image-import window and neither forward to nor own the document listener. Session restoration, initial file opening and explicit startup options retain their ordering before incoming OS-event batches are processed.

Existing tabs, unsaved changes, default-workspace sema…

title: Windows: a GPU that can't set up the window falls back to OpenGL (#519)
author: jcl-bit
body:
A GPU whose driver can't configure the window's surface no longer closes PdfCraft at launch: wgpu's error comes back as an error, and the OpenGL retry from #530 runs. This stacks on #609 (#577), which vendors egui-wgpu; its two commits come first here, and this PR adds one commit on top. Review that commit alone, or after #609 merges.

## The change

- `vendor/egui-wgpu`, a second patch marked `PdfCraft patch (#519)`:
  - `winit::catch_errors(device, f)` runs `f` inside wgpu error scopes (validation, out of memory, internal) and returns the first error instead of handing it to wgpu's uncaptured-error handler, which panics by default. Error scopes belong to the calling thread, and a lost device still goes to its own callback.
  - `Painter::add_surface`, which `set_window` uses for every new window, configures the surface inside it. On failure it removes the surface (and its depth and MSAA textures) and returns the new `WgpuError::ConfigureSurface`. eframe then returns `Error::Wgpu` from `run_native`, which `main` already retries with eframe's OpenGL renderer (glow).
  - Later reconfigures (resize, DPI change, a recreated surface) are unchanged: an error there still panics, as upstream.
  - Still a panic, because no error scope sees it: a device lost during that first configure. wgpu reports a lost device only to the device-lost callback, so the configure seems to succeed and the first frame panics on the unconfigured surface, after the app has started. A window shown at zero size is first configured on resize, outside the scopes. Both are as before.
  - eframe returns the error only for the root window at start-up. PdfCraft opens no other windows; for one, eframe 0.36.2 would log the error, or end the event loop with it.

title: M9: chain building checks CA constraints, key usage, path length and validity
author: thorstenhirsch
body:
`x509::build_chain` linked certificates by name and signature only. An ordinary subscriber certificate embedded in a PDF, or one that is itself in the trusted list, could "issue" a certificate for any identity and chain to a trusted root. An issuer now needs:
- `basicConstraints` CA:TRUE (an old v1 self-signed root without constraints still anchors),
- `keyCertSign` when it has a key usage,
- a `pathLenConstraint` that allows the CAs below it,
- validity at the signing time (or the trusted timestamp / token time) when it is known.

The signature details say why an issuer was refused.

This is the first half of the split requested on #144 ("CA checks first, then trust sets"). It is independent of #144 and #386: based on `main`, `crates/sign` only. Tests issue certificates in-process and cover each refusal, plus a signed PDF whose signer chains through an end-entity certificate (Unknown, not Valid).

Not in this PR: the signer's key usage / extended key usage, name constraints, unknown critical extensions (the trust-sets draft adds the purpose rules).

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 gates pass.

title: M9: validate a document timestamp that sits in a signature field
author: thorstenhirsch
body:
Documenso (and others) store the document timestamp as an AcroForm signature field (`Timestamp_1`) whose `/V` is a `/Type /DocTimeStamp` dictionary. Field values only went through the signature validator, which read the RFC 3161 token as a CMS signature, compared its TSTInfo with the document digest and reported "altered or corrupted since the signature was applied" for an untouched file.

- A field value with `/SubFilter /ETSI.RFC3161` is validated as a timestamp.
- Standalone timestamps are found by `/Type /DocTimeStamp` (ISO 32000-2 §12.8.5) as well as the `/Type /Sig` older writers used; `timestamp_document` writes `/DocTimeStamp`.
- The discovery cache from #419 selects its candidates with `is_document_timestamp`, which only accepted `/Type /Sig`; it accepts both now, otherwise a standalone `/DocTimeStamp` would never become a candidate.

**One existing test changed.** `field_membership_is_refreshed_even_when_discovery_is_cached` lists a signature field whose value is a timestamp dictionary and asserted `doc_timestamp == false`. That is the bug above (the timestamp checked as a signature), so it asserts `true` now; what the test is about (the field is listed once, not also as a standalone timestamp) is unchanged.

Independent of #144 and #386: based on `main`, `crates/sign` only. The two new regression tests build the same structure with the test TSA (no third-party file) and fail without the fix.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 gates pass.

title: M9: opt-in trust lists (a file of CA certificates, such as the EU Trusted Lists)
author: thorstenhirsch
body:
## What this changes

A signer can be trusted through a **list of CA certificates the user loads from a file**: `sign_trust {"eu_trusted_list": "<path>"}` (DER one after the other, or PEM), for example the EU Trusted Lists' qualified CA services. Refs #775, #87, #824: the PDF attached to #775 (a CAdES signature under Intesa SpA's qualified service, valid in Acrobat) is **Unknown** without the list and **Valid** with it.

- Off until loaded; nothing is embedded; kept apart from the user's own trusted certificates (`TrustStore::lists`). The signature details name the list that vouched.
- A list is only another set of anchors: chains through it still need CA certificates all the way (#620), and the signer is held to #749's purpose rules.
- A list vouches for signers, **never for a time-stamp authority**: trusted time still comes from the user's own certificates.
- A cut-short list is refused instead of loading as a smaller one, DER or PEM: the loader refuses a PEM block that never ends (upstream, with the `.p7b` bundles) and, added here, one that begins before the last one ended, so a bundle spliced from two cut files is not read as the second only. PEM that starts with text beginning with a `0` is read as PEM (`x509::load_certificates` too).
- A list is known by its own name (`TrustStore::add_list` / `remove_list`), so removing it takes back exactly what was loaded.
- `sign_trust` checks every argument before changing anything and revalidates the open documents once (`Session::update_trust`).

This is the EU-lists half of gap 10 (`sign.eutl`). It replaces an earlier, larger version of this PR; what was taken out is listed below.

title: Tell the user when PdfCraft draws without a GPU (#519)
author: jcl-bit
body:
## What

When wgpu's chosen adapter is a software one (`DeviceType::Cpu`: WARP on Windows, llvmpipe on Linux), PdfCraft now shows a notice in the app at launch:

> PdfCraft is drawing without a graphics processor, so it may be slow. Updating the graphics driver may help.

Until now egui-wgpu only logged "Software rasterizer detected" at warn level, so the #519 reporter only found out why PdfCraft was slow by reading pdfcraft.log. This is the second request in that issue; the launch abort itself is handled separately in #617.

## How

- `apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`: `app_creator` reads `cc.wgpu_render_state`'s adapter type and passes it to a new `notify_software_renderer`, which uses the existing toast (`notify_tr`), the same channel as the portable-mode notice. `app_creator` runs once per `run_native`, so the notice appears once per launch.
- Translations of the new string in the ten catalogs that already carry the portable-mode notice (bg, cs, de, es, fr, hu, ja, pt-br, uk, zh-hans), written clean-room from the meaning, with their `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes updated.

## Not covered

- The OpenGL fallback (glow). glow exposes the renderer string (`GDI Generic`, `llvmpipe`) only through `unsafe` calls, which the workspace forbids. When wgpu falls back to OpenGL there is no notice.
- The notice is a toast, so it disappears after 3.5 s and a later startup notice (for example, a file that fails to open) replaces it.

## Tests

- `a_software_renderer_is_shown_to_the_user`: a `Cpu` adapter sets the notice; integrated, discrete, virtual and other adapters leave it unset.
- `cargo xtask ci` green locally on Windows.

title: Edit text: lines split across content stream pieces are listed and edited (fixes #155)
author: echelon
body:
### What was wrong
A page's `/Contents` array is one content stream in pieces, split between any two tokens (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2). Edit text (`text_lines`, `text_paragraphs`, `text_edit`, the Edit text tool) parsed each piece on its own, so an operator whose operands ended one piece and whose keyword started the next (e.g. `[(After) -20 (wards)]` | `TJ`) lost its operands and the line was never listed.

### What changed
- `pdfcraft-content` (L2) gains `Pieces`: joins the pieces, parses them as one stream, maps joined positions back to pieces (`piece_of`, `pieces_of`), and `splice`s joined byte ranges back into per-piece bytes. A replacement goes into the piece its range starts in and the rest of the range is removed from later pieces, so an operator spanning pieces is replaced/removed whole.
- `pdfcraft-edit` `text_lines` interprets the joined operators; `replace_line` and `rewrite_block` splice through `Pieces` and only create new stream objects for pieces whose bytes changed. `coincident_ops` is now one set of joined op indices.
- `pdfcraft-redact`'s interpreter uses the shared helper instead of its private copy (#153), no behaviour change.
- Lines/paragraphs are still grouped only within one piece (by the piece their first operator starts in), so separate drawings in separate pieces don't merge.
- Parity note on `edit.text-edit` updated.

Not covered: `crates/edit/src/images.rs` (Edit image move/replace/delete) still parses and re-serializes one piece at a time, as the issue suspected; left for a follow-up.

### Tests
- `crates/edit/src/tests.rs::a_line_whose_operator_starts_the_next_stream_can_be_edited` (the issue's repro: lists Target + Afterwards, retypes the split line and rewrites its paragraph without stray tokens; fails on main with `["Target"]`).
- `crates/automation/tests/automation.rs::a_line_split_across_content_streams_is_listed_and_edited` (`text_lines` / `text_edit` via tools).

title: Fix #378: draw on the GPU that drives the primary display on Windows
author: rschuerer
body:
On Windows the low-power preference picked the AMD Ryzen integrated GPU on a desktop whose monitors all hang off an NVIDIA card. Presenting from the headless iGPU to a window on another GPU took the AMD display driver down, blacking out every monitor for about two minutes before PdfCraft exited.

Windows now gets the display-aware adapter choice Linux already had (#96, #445): `EnumDisplayDevices`, through the safe `winsafe` crate (MIT, `user` feature only, no `unsafe` in our code), says which adapter drives each desktop display and which is primary. `pick_adapter` matches that to the wgpu adapters by PCI vendor/device id, and the GPU driving the primary display wins, as the built-in panel does on Linux (#8). Where the system gives no display information (macOS, containers, remote sessions) the power preference alone decides, as before.

The log now names the GPU chosen ("drawing on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (DiscreteGpu, Dx12)"), the first question when a window stays black.

Tests: synthetic tests for the Windows device-id parser and the primary-display rule, plus a live test of the enumeration on the running machine. Verified on a Ryzen 7000 + RTX 3090 desktop with both monitors on the NVIDIA card: the app starts on the 3090 and the driver crash is gone. `cargo fmt`, workspace clippy with `-D warnings` and the workspace tests pass.

title: Forms: keep tiles and render unbaked field values during page re-render
author: Piohrun
body:
### Summary
In complex interactive PDF forms (such as multi-page fillable character sheets with 200+ fields), switching focus away from an edited field previously caused its text to disappear for 2–3 seconds while background page tiles re-rendered.

### Root Cause
1. When focus moves away from an edited field, the transient egui text editor is dropped.
2. Previously, `view.page_changed()` purged all GPU tiles for the page, while non-focused fields depended exclusively on the background raster tiles to show their text.
3. On dense documents, Hayro tile re-rendering takes 2–3 seconds per page, leaving the field blank until the new tile arrives.
4. Additionally, form field recalculations in `recalculate_with` and `apply_changes` performed repetitive O(N) traversals per field.

### Changes
- **Keep canvas tiles on screen (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`):** In `DocView`, mark current-tag tiles as `stale_tiles` instead of purging them immediately in `page_changed`, keeping existing sharp tiles on screen during background re-render while purging old-zoom tiles.
- **Immediate widget preview (`crates/ui-egui/src/forms_ui.rs`):** Track modified fields in `view.forms.unbaked` after successful edit application, rendering an instantaneous egui overlay (`paint_unbaked_widget`) for text, checkbox, and radio inputs until fresh raster tiles arrive. Font size scaling respects page orientation (90°/270°).
- **Scoped invalidation via form diff (`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs`):** In `apply_edit`, diff `form_before` against `doc.form` to invalidate only pages with modified fields, falling back to `document_changed` for XFA forms or page-count changes.
- **Calculation optimization (`crates/forms/src/lib.rs`, `crates/forms/src/scripting.rs`):** Hoist `fields(doc)` in `apply_changes` and `recalculate_with`, re-reading only when a calculation script returns changes.
- **Contributor attribution (`contributors/people.toml`):** Added entry for `Piohrun`.

title: Fill & Sign: remove white background from imported signature images
author: mrme2tiri-hash
body:
When a signature is imported through Fill & Sign's Image tab, a photo of a signature on paper keeps its white background. This adds `SignatureImage::remove_white_background`, which makes near-white pixels transparent and fades the transition at the edges, and applies it in `use_signature_image` so the cleaned image is what gets saved and reused.

- Pixels with every RGB channel at 245 or above become fully transparent.
- Pixels with a minimum channel at or below 210 keep their full opacity.
- Pixels in between fade.
- Existing transparency is preserved (new alpha = old alpha x keep).

Tests: adds the unit test `white_background_becomes_transparent_and_ink_is_kept`. `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine` pass, and I tried it manually by importing a photographed signature on Fedora.

Known limits: the cutoff (245) and feather (35) are fixed, so shadows and grey paper can leave a haze. There is no strength slider, checkerboard preview or auto-crop yet.

title: Forms: fields listed only as page widgets join the form
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #647.

## What
A PDF whose AcroForm `/Fields` array is empty or missing listed no fields, so nothing was fillable in PdfCraft even though every widget sat on a page with its name and value — Acrobat, the browsers and MuPDF fill those. This adopts the page widgets as fields, mirrors that in the inspector, and records the leniency in the repair log, never silently.

## How
- **forms**: `fields()` walks `/Fields` as before, then adopts widget annotations no tree entry reaches, through each widget's topmost unlisted `/Parent` (a field split across several widgets stays one field; `/Parent` loops and cycles are bounded). `adopted_page_fields()` counts them for the note. Tree-listed fields keep their order first; the rest follow in page-annotation order.
- **render**: the inspector's field list adopts them the same way (small local walker, as the file already does elsewhere), so the Fields panel, the field-count notice and menu gating follow.
- **cos/engine**: `Document::note_repair` lets the engine record the leniency when opening such a file: *"the form's /Fields list omits N fields; they were read from the page annotations"* (Document Properties ▸ Advanced, `doc_info`'s `repairs`).

Writes need no `/Fields` changes: filling writes `/V` and regenerates `/AP` on each merged widget dict, and the `/CO` calculations bind by object reference, so they run once the fields are enumerated. Saving preserves the file as-is (the empty `/Fields` list is not rewritten; the leniency re-applies on every open).

## Tests
Written first, failing before the fix:
- `crates/forms/src/tests.rs::fields_listed_only_on_the_pages_are_adopted` — adoption order, split fields, missing `/Fields`, degenerate widgets skipped, fill + appearance survive a save.

- `crates/engine/src/tests.rs::adopting_page_only_fields_is_noted_as_a_repair`.

title: macOS: add native document integration diagnostics
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Context

The macOS Finder, Quick Look, thumbnail, and Spotlight work requires observable evidence before adding platform-specific integration. PdfCraft already declares the system PDF UTI and handles open-document Apple events; this change adds a repeatable diagnostic boundary for the remaining checks.

## Problem

Bundle registration, packaging, Quick Look, Spotlight, and PDF metadata/text evidence otherwise require ad hoc commands and are easy to report inconsistently.

## Scope

- Add `cargo xtask macos-integration [--bundle APP] [--pdf FILE]`.
- Report OS/architecture, bundle identifier, minimum macOS, PDF UTI role/rank, executable architectures, nested code, and signature status.
- Probe Quick Look and Spotlight with read-only system commands.
- Inspect bounded PDF metadata and first-page text using the existing PDF parser.
- Add parser and plist-registration unit coverage.

## Non-goals

- No runtime application changes.
- No custom Quick Look or thumbnail provider.
- No custom Spotlight importer, indexing, LaunchServices registration, or database mutation.
- No XMP/OCR or PDF metadata behavior changes.
- No private or unsafe macOS API use.

## Why safe

The command is opt-in and read-only. It does not install, register, refresh, index, or mutate system state. PDF input is capped at 64 MiB, text extraction at 8 MiB and 32 pages, metadata at 1024 characters, and external-tool output at 4096 characters.

## Before

There was no repository command that gathered this cross-boundary evidence.

## After

The command produces a stable report suitable for attaching to the macOS integration investigation. It explicitly reports unavailable/no-data results instead of treating them as proof of provider selection or Spotlight metadata support.

## Proof / reproduction

```text
cargo xtask macos-integration --pdf crates/sign/tests/data/openssl-signed.pdf
```

On the validation host, this reported macOS 14.7.1 on arm64, one PDF page with the expected signed-fixture text, …

title: Print: list driverless CUPS destinations, not only permanent queues
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #652.

## Root cause

The Print dialog's printer list came from `lpstat -p -d`, which lists only **permanent CUPS queues**. A driverless IPP printer discovered on the network — the standard way printing works on modern Linux desktops — has no permanent queue: only `lpstat -e` (CUPS ≥ 1.7, 2013) names it, and CUPS builds a temporary queue on demand when `lp` sends it a job. GTK's print dialog lists these destinations via `cupsEnumDests`; PdfCraft listed none of them, so the dialog showed only *Save as PDF* even though `lp -d NAME` prints to them fine.

## What changed

- `crates/print/src/spool.rs`: `printers()` now runs `lpstat -e` alongside `lpstat -p -d` and merges the answers in the new pure `printers_parsed()` — queues first, deduplicated, default still from `-d`. A spooler that fails or doesn't know `-e` keeps today's behaviour and loses only the driverless names. Submission is unchanged: `lp -d` already makes CUPS create the temporary queue.
- `crates/print/src/tests.rs`: `driverless_printers_join_the_list_without_a_queue` covers the merge (driverless after queues, no duplicates when `-e` also lists the queue, `None` for pre-1.7 spoolers, empty `-e` output).
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`: the .deb/.rpm now **recommend** `cups-client` — without it `lpstat` is missing entirely and the list is silently empty.
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml`: `print.print-to-printer` notes and evidence updated.

### Review follow-up (b27334a)

- `lpstat_e_command` is now gated like its only caller (`printers`' unix block): off unix it was dead code, and CI's Windows clippy gate (`-D warnings`) failed to build the crate — invisible from a Linux checkout, where the function is used.
- A default destination that is itself driverless (`lpoptions -d` can name a destination no queue exists for) now keeps its default marker when appended from `-e`, instead of the dialog preselecting the first queue. The test covers this and CRLF in `-e` output.

title: M2: a ligature stays one glyph in the text layer, in every writing direction
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

When a glyph's `/ToUnicode` gives several characters (a ligature such as "ffi", the Arabic lam-alef ligature, a letter with its marks), the text layer split it into one `TextGlyph` per character and cut the glyph's box into equal parts **along view x**, whatever the writing direction. Search, copy, `text_extract` and selection then read the wrong text:

| "office" with one glyph for "ffi" | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| upright | `office` | `office` |
| turned 90° | `o ce\nf\nf\ni` (the parts land on three lines) | `office` |
| turned 180° | `oiffce` | `office` |
| turned 270° | `o ce\ni\nf\nf` | `office` |
| upright, narrow "ffi" glyph | `of ice` (the second "f" is dropped as a fake-bold copy of the first) | `office` |
| vertical CID font, one glyph for "株式" | `式\n日株語` | `日株式語` |
| Arabic "سلام" with a lam-alef glyph | `سالم` | `سلام` |
| Arabic "بَاب" with beh + fatha as one glyph | the fatha before its letter | `بَاب` |

The Arabic rows matter for PdfCraft's own output too: Add text writes shaped Arabic as one glyph per cluster with a multi-character `/ToUnicode` entry (#403).

## Cause

`TextDevice::draw_glyph` (`crates/render/src/text.rs`) pushed one `TextGlyph` per character, each a 1/n slice of the glyph box along view x. Three things went wrong:

- For turned or vertical text, x is not the writing direction, so the slices sit across the line.
- For a narrow ligature, the slices are close enough for `layout`'s fake-bold filter to drop one.
- In a right-to-left run, `layout` reverses glyphs (visual → logical). The slices had been laid out in logical order, so reversing them put the characters inside the ligature backwards.

## Change

One painted glyph is one `TextGlyph`: its `text` is the whole `/ToUnicode` string, and its `rect` is the glyph's own box (the same box a one-character glyph gets). `PageText::find`/`find_with` already map each character to the glyph that owns it, and `text_of`, `plain_text`, `word_at` and `line_rects` work on glyph…

title: M2: a character a substitute font lacks draws .notdef, not an unrelated glyph
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

A Type 0 font that isn't embedded is drawn with a substitute. For Adobe-Japan1, that is a craft-fonts Japanese face since #368. When the substitute has no glyph for a character, PdfCraft draws an **unrelated glyph** in its place:

- 𠮷 (U+20BB7, CID 13706, common in names such as 𠮷田) draws as "Ｑ" in a non-embedded Gothic font.
- ㈠㈡…, ㊀…, the squared katakana words (㌀…), fractions, superscripts and many symbols draw as random kanji.

#484 hit the same path with half-width katakana, which drew as ﬁ and ﬂ. It fixed that by switching to a face that has those characters, but every other character the faces lack still goes down this path.

## Cause

`Type0Font::map_code` (vendored hayro-interpret, `font/cid.rs`) first looks a CID up by Unicode in the substitute. When that fails, it falls through to "hope that the selected font has the right glyph order": it uses the CID (through `/CIDToGIDMap`) as a glyph index of the substitute. An Adobe collection's CIDs are not glyph indices of BIZ UDMincho, BIZ UDPGothic or the standard-14 substitutes. Glyph 13706 of BIZ UDPGothic is "Ｑ".

## Change

`PdfCraft patch:` in `map_code`. For a substitute (`fallback`) font whose CIDs come from an Adobe collection (Japan1, GB1, CNS1, Korea1, the ones with a UCS2 CMap), a CID that the Unicode lookup can't place draws `.notdef`, as a CID the font has no glyph for does. The patch doesn't touch:

- **CID-keyed CFF substitutes:** they are still looked up by CID, which is right for them.
- **Embedded fonts** (`fallback` is false): their `/CIDToGIDMap` path is unchanged.
- **Adobe-Identity and custom orderings.**
- **Successful Unicode lookups.**

The two comments in `raster.rs` that described the old behaviour are updated, and `vendor/README.md` lists the patch as (21).

## Test

`raster::tests::cids_a_substitute_lacks_are_not_drawn_as_other_glyphs` needs craft-fonts, which the Linux CI job has; without it the test skips. For HeiseiMin-W3 and HeiseiKakuGo-W5 it checks two things:

- 𠮷 (…

title: M2: kanji that Adobe-Japan1 maps to a variation sequence draw in non-embedded fonts
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

In a non-embedded Japanese font, PdfCraft draws over 200 common kanji (噂, 逢, 溢, 飴, 芦, 茨, 祇, 禰, 箸, 蔑, 詮, 謎 …) and five CJK radicals as **unrelated glyphs**, or not at all. The craft-fonts substitutes have all of these characters. A Japanese name, address or sentence using one of them shows the wrong character.

## Cause

Without `/ToUnicode`, hayro finds a CID's character through Adobe-Japan1-UCS2. That CMap maps the JIS X 0208 forms of the kanji that JIS X 0213:2004 redrew to an **ideographic variation sequence**. For example, CID 1247 is 噂 U+5642 followed by the selector U+E0100.

`Type0Font::map_via_unicode` (vendored hayro-interpret, `font/cid.rs`) only accepts a single character, so it found no glyph. `map_code` then fell through to using the CID as a glyph index of the substitute, which draws an unrelated glyph. A `/ToUnicode` entry with a variation sequence takes the same path.

## Change

`PdfCraft patch:` in `map_via_unicode`. A string made of one character and one variation selector (U+FE00–FE0F or U+E0100–E01EF) is looked up as that character in that form:

1. The substitute's own glyph for the sequence, when its `cmap` has one. BIZ UDMincho and BIZ UDPGothic carry 10,160 sequences, including the Adobe-Japan1 forms, so CID 1247 draws the JIS X 0208 form of 噂 that the CID stands for.
2. Otherwise the substitute's glyph for the character alone. The [Unicode FAQ on variation sequences](https://www.unicode.org/faq/vs.html) says the same: when a variation sequence isn't supported, the base character is displayed.

Other multi-character strings (ligatures) are still not looked up, as before. Embedded fonts don't use this path. `vendor/README.md` lists the patch as (21).

## Test

`raster::tests::variation_sequences_draw_their_kanji_in_a_substitute` needs craft-fonts, which the Linux CI job has; without it the test skips. For HeiseiMin-W3 and HeiseiKakuGo-W5 it checks four things:

- `UniJIS-UCS2-H <5642>` (CID 1247, no `/ToUnicode`) draws the same pi…
