title: Exported images keep their transparency, JPEG cut-outs included (#645)
author: DWAA1660
body:
## What was wrong
Export a PDF ▸ Image ▸ Export all images (and Edit ▸ Save image as) lost transparency, so cut-out images came out on a solid white or black background (#645):
- A JPEG with an `/SMask` (the usual cut-out photo) was written as the bare JPEG.
- Soft masks of a different size from the image, and JPEG-compressed soft masks, were dropped.
- Stencil `/Mask` images and colour-key `/Mask` arrays were ignored.

## The fix (`crates/create/src/extract.rs`)
- An image with transparency (`/SMask`, stencil `/Mask` or colour-key `/Mask`) is written as a PNG with that transparency as alpha. This includes JPEG images, which are decoded with the `image` crate's JPEG decoder (zune-jpeg, already in the tree; I enabled the `jpeg` feature in `pdfcraft-create`). JPEGs without transparency are still written byte for byte. A JPEG that fails to decode falls back to the old behaviour.
- Soft and stencil masks of a different size are scaled to the image's size. Their `/Decode` inversion is applied, and `/Matte` pre-blending is undone for grey and RGB images.
- Image sizes are checked (positive, at most 100 Mpx) before use. On main, a negative `/Width` made `image_file` (Save image as) overflow and panic.
- JPX, JBIG2 and CCITT masks are still left out (the image is exported opaque). The parity notes for `create.export-all-images` say so.

## How it was tested
- New tests in `crates/create/src/tests.rs`: `jpeg_images_with_a_soft_mask_export_as_png_with_alpha`, `soft_masks_of_another_size_and_stencil_and_colour_key_masks_become_alpha` (scaled soft mask, stencil mask, colour key, matte) and `damaged_masks_and_sizes_never_panic`. All three fail on main; the last one panics.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create` (14 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo xtask parity` all pass.

Fixes #645

title: M10.2: scan JPEG metadata beyond frame headers
author: CQMHV
body:
JPEG metadata scanning stops at SOF, so APP2 ICC profiles, JFIF density and APP14 CMYK metadata placed after the frame header are ignored. Repeated 0xFF fill bytes before a marker also cause the scanner to read the wrong segment length.

Continue scanning metadata up to the first SOS or EOI marker, skip marker fill bytes, and reject truncated segment headers or lengths smaller than two bytes with an error. The first frame still supplies the image dimensions and component count. Original JPEG bytes and the lenient ICC fallback introduced in #729 are preserved.

Added synthetic regression cases covering post-SOF metadata, fill bytes, SOS/EOI boundaries, malformed segment lengths and mismatched ICC profiles.

Validation: formatting and `git diff --check` completed. Tests were not run.

title: M3, #740: column select (Alt/Option-drag, or Edit ▸ Column select)
author: mlkonrad
body:
Fixes #740.

## Why

Dragging across text always selected everything between two points in reading order. On a table or a multi-column page that means you can't copy one column of numbers: the selection runs across every row in between. Acrobat solves this with column select: hold Alt (Option on macOS) while dragging, and only the text inside the rectangle is selected.

## What

- **Alt-drag** (Option-drag on macOS) with the Select tool selects only the text inside the rectangle drawn. The rectangle is outlined while dragging, and the cursor is a crosshair while Alt is held.
  - It also works with the text markup tools (Highlight, Underline, Strike-through…) and Redact, so a column can be highlighted or redacted. With Highlight and Redact the drag must start on text, since off text those tools draw an area box, as before.
  - A glyph counts when its centre is inside the rectangle, so a rectangle drawn a little into the next column doesn't pick up the edge of its text.
- **Edit ▸ Column select** (`edit.column_select`, quick tool `column-select` on the control channel) does the same with a plain drag. It is also the way in on desktops that keep Alt-drag for themselves (see Platforms).
- **Copy** gives one row per visual line, top to bottom. Pieces side by side (table cells, newspaper columns) are separated by a tab, so a pasted table lands in spreadsheet cells. Right-to-left rows put their cells right to left. When any selected glyph doesn't run horizontally (vertical CJK, text turned at an angle, a page shown turned by `/Rotate`), rows mean nothing, and the lines come out in reading order instead, using the per-glyph `direction` from #735.
- **render:** `PageText::glyphs_in`, `glyph_rects` (one box per run of selected glyphs, never covering unselected text) and `column_text`.
- **ui:** a selection is either a reading-order run or a column rectangle. Highlighting, Copy, markup quads and redaction marks all go through it. ⇧-click clears a column selection, since it has…

title: M7: support shaped Thai text in Add Text and UI fallback fonts
author: PuemMTH
body:

title: JavaScript: limit util.printf widths and output, and array arguments
author: haranishi
body:
Two host functions let a script make the native side allocate memory the script never holds itself, and a failed allocation aborts the process (`catch_unwind` cannot contain it). The scripting engine's own loop and recursion limits do not apply to native code. Scripts come from PDF form fields, and XFA initialisation scripts run when a document is opened.

## What changes (`crates/js/src/lib.rs`)

- **`util.printf`** (the same function is registered for XFA scripts): the width and precision of a conversion were accumulated with unchecked `usize` arithmetic and no maximum, and then reached `format!("{:.*}", …)` and `"0".repeat(pad)`. They now saturate, and a width or precision above 4096 (`MAX_PRINTF_WIDTH_PRECISION`) ends the script with a `TypeError` before anything is allocated from it. The total output is limited to 1 MiB (`MAX_PRINTF_OUTPUT_BYTES`), checked before each append (literal characters, `%%`, padding and body).
- **`strings`** (the array arguments of `resetForm` and of a field's `value`, `textColor` and `fillColor` setters): it looped over the array's `length`, which a sparse array makes free (`new Array(4294967295)`), pushing one `String` per item. An array longer than 2^20 items (`MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH`) now ends the script with a `TypeError` before the loop starts.

Everything inside the limits behaves as before.

## Tests (`crates/js/src/tests.rs`)

Small and deterministic (no timing). I ran the new tests against the code before the change: the ones that check a limit fail there, as noted; the two positive controls pass before and after. The printf tests run through both the AcroForm and the XFA runner.

- `util_printf_rejects_large_width` (before: the process aborted on the allocation), `util_printf_rejects_large_precision` (before: a panic), `util_printf_rejects_overflowing_width` and `util_printf_rejects_overflowing_precision` (before: an arithmetic overflow panic), `util_printf_rejects_limits_for_all_conversions` (`%d`, `%f`, `%s`, `%x`) and `util_p…

title: lopdf: bound compressed-object lookups and object-stream members
author: haranishi
body:
Two ways a crafted PDF took the process down while lopdf loaded it. The inspector and attachment extraction load the whole document through it, and a stack overflow or a failed allocation aborts the process (`catch_unwind` cannot contain it).

## What changes (vendored lopdf; `vendor/README.md`, items 4 and 5)

1. **Compressed-object lookup** (`reader.rs`). To read a stream's indirect `/Length` that lives in an object stream, `get_compressed_object` resolved the container with a fresh `HashSet`, so the caller's cycle history was lost, and it never checked that the container is an ordinary object. A compressed object that is its own container, two that contain each other, a container whose `/Length` is an indirect reference into itself, and a long chain of compressed objects, each stored in the next, all recursed until the stack overflowed. So did plain streams whose `/Length` names another stream, one after the other. Now the lookup passes the caller's set on (a cycle ends with the existing `ReferenceCycle` error) and requires the container's xref entry to be an ordinary in-file object (ISO 32000-1 7.5.7: a stream can't be stored in an object stream; the vendored hayro-syntax already refuses this), and `get_object` stops a chain of nested lookups at 16 with `Error::ReferenceLimit` (a valid `/Length` resolves in at most three lookups: the length, the object stream holding it, and that stream's own `/Length`). A stream whose length can't be resolved is left to the existing zero-length pass.
2. **Object-stream members** (`object_stream.rs`). Every `(object number, offset)` pair of the index was parsed from its offset to the end of the whole decoded stream into an owned `Object`, and nothing requires the pairs to point at different objects. Many pairs with the same or nested offsets (a long literal string holding balanced parentheses) kept many copies of one large object, and a member that failed to parse rescanned the rest of the stream each time. Loading decodes every…

title: hayro-syntax: cap the nesting of direct arrays and dictionaries
author: haranishi
body:
Finding the extent of a direct array or dictionary recursed once per nesting level with nothing counting the depth, and so did the lenient repair of a dictionary that has an object where a key belongs. A few hundred KB of `[` or `<<` therefore overflowed the native stack, which aborts the process (`catch_unwind` cannot contain it). It is reached just by opening a PDF: `Pdf::new` parses the trailer dictionary and skips every value in it, including entries nobody uses, and page content streams use the same functions. The other parsers here already cap nesting (`pdfcraft-cos` at 128, lopdf at 100).

## What changes (vendored `hayro-syntax`; `vendor/README.md`, item 14)

- `Reader` carries a private depth counter (cloned along with it) with `enter_container` / `leave_container`. `Array::skip`, `Dict::skip` and `parse_dict_with` enter after their opening token and leave on every way out. `parse_dict_with` is there because its repair path reads, rather than skips, an object found where a key belongs, so `<< << …` recursed through that read. Beyond 128 levels the object fails like any malformed one (`None`), so a trailer that is too deep takes the existing xref-repair path.
- 128 is where a chain of 64 direct stitching functions ends (a function and its `/Functions` array count two levels each). A chain of 65 is now refused by the parser, before the function-depth guard: the existing 65-function assertion accepts a refusal at either point, and a new test builds the chain with indirect references so that the function guard itself stays tested. The vendored hayro-interpret test of the same limit is adjusted the same way.
- Stack use, measured: one level costs about 50-80 bytes for skipping and about 650-800 bytes for the keyless-dictionary read and `{:?}`, in dev and release builds. 128 levels take at most about 100 KiB, a fifth of a 512 KiB thread stack (with hayro-syntax compiled at opt-level 0 the keyless read costs 2.7 KiB a level, 341 KiB at the cap).

title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping PDF documents from desktop file managers onto PdfCraft showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not arrive.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was added for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, updating to `winit 0.31` directly is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Adds an event loop builder hook in `native_options`: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `PDFCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `PDFCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p pdfcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

author: taylorandrew07-lab

The design is described in the note on #611.

## What this adds

With a file expanded (PR 2), single pages can be edited before combining:

- **Select pages:** click, Ctrl/⌘ and Shift, as with files.
- **Move pages:** drag them anywhere, including between another file's pages. Dragging a selected page carries all the selected pages.
- **Remove pages:** a page card's 🗑, the toolbar, or Delete.
- **Undo:** each move or remove is one undo step. The original files are never changed.
- **Combine** produces exactly the order shown.

**Model: a file can become several "parts".**
- A page moved between another file's pages splits its file into parts that share its bytes. Parts that end up side by side join again.
- In the **List view**, each part is a row with its own editable page range, so both views show the order combined.
- A split file still **counts, unlocks and combines as one file**. It doesn't trigger "Added more than once".

## Engine: a split file keeps one bookmark

Combined as separate files, a split file would get several top-level bookmarks with the same title, duplicate attachments, and lose links between its pages in different parts.

- **`pdfcraft_organize::combine_grouped`,** with `Session::combine_grouped`, copies each file once and puts its pages in the order shown. The file keeps:
  - one bookmark at its first page, plus its nested bookmarks;
  - links between its own pages;
  - its form fields;
  - one copy of its attachments.
- **A page listed twice** now gets its own copies of its annotations. A form widget on it joins the same field, so the field keeps one value.
- **The existing `combine` functions are unchanged.**

title: OCR: Recognize text in multiple files refuses paths outside the root
author: mlkonrad
body:
`ocr_recognize_files` (Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text ▸ In multiple files) turned a path outside the automation root into a per-file error and returned success. With the OCR models installed (`cargo xtask models`), `hostile_args.rs::no_tool_escapes_the_root` reports 9 leaks (`../outside.pdf`, absolute paths, a link out of the root…). Nothing was actually read from outside the root, since the per-file read was still confined, but the call should be refused like every other tool's.

It went unnoticed because without the models, loading them fails first and the call errors before the paths are looked at, and CI never installs the models.

title: Fill & Sign tools pick up placed signatures to move and resize them
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #825.

## Problem
A signature placed with Fill & Sign can only be moved with the **Select** tool. If a Fill & Sign tool is active (Sign, Initials, Add text, Check, Date):
- dragging a placed signature does nothing;
- hovering over it shows a crosshair, not the Move cursor;
- clicking it stamps another mark on top of it, or opens a text box with Add text.

Acrobat lets you pick up placed Fill & Sign items without switching tools. In PdfCraft it looks as if signatures can't be moved after they're placed.

## Cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: with `QuickTool::Fill(_)`, page input always goes to `fill_sign::page_input`, which only places marks. `comments::page_input` handles move and resize only for `QuickTool::Select`.

## Fix
- **New `comments::fill_grabs`.** With a Fill & Sign tool, a press or hover on a Fill & Sign mark (or on the selected mark's resize handles) goes to the existing Select-tool logic (`select_input`):
  - hover shows Move;
  - a click selects;
  - a drag moves (one undo step, "Move comment");
  - handles resize.

  Everywhere else the tool still places its mark, including on other comments such as rectangles. The tool stays active throughout.
- **Image signatures keep their live move/resize preview** (`signature_drag`) under Fill & Sign tools too.
- **How marks are recognised.** Comments now carry a `fill_sign` flag:
  - In the engine's list it comes from `pdfcraft_annot::is_fill_sign`.
  - In the viewer's inspector (`crates/render/src/inspect.rs`) it uses the same rules, so reopened files work too. They're duplicated there with a keep-in-step comment, because `pdfcraft-render` doesn't depend on `pdfcraft-annot`.
- **Parity:** `parity/acrobat-features.toml` (`form.fill-sign-signature`) gets the new evidence and notes.

## Testing
- [x] New test `crates/ui-egui/tests/fill_sign.rs::fill_and_sign_tools_pick_up_placed_marks_to_move_and_resize_them`. Before the fix it failed with `left: Crosshair, right: Move`. It covers:

title: Issue #390: build the DMG with hdiutil create so the app passes codesign --strict
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Fixes #390.

## Problem

`hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` writes a `com.apple.FinderInfo` (Finder location −1,−1) on every file and folder it puts in the image. `codesign --verify --deep --strict` rejects that as "resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed", on `PdfCraft.app` inside the mounted DMG and on a copy installed from it with `ditto`. Gatekeeper still accepts the app, but MDM and compliance scripts that run `--strict` report a correctly signed and notarized app as damaged. Reproduced here with the official `pdfcraft-0.5.0-macos-universal.dmg` (first rejected file: `Contents/Resources/models/ATTRIBUTION.txt`) and with an ad-hoc-signed stub app: `makehybrid` with or without `-hfs-openfolder` puts the Finder info on every file; `hdiutil create -srcfolder` with HFS+ or APFS puts it on none.

## Change

`packaging/macos/package.sh`

- Builds the image with `hdiutil create -srcfolder … -fs HFS+ -format UDZO` instead of `makehybrid` + `convert`. `create` attaches a device while it copies, which is the "Resource busy" flakiness the old comment mentions, so it gets up to five tries with growing pauses before the build fails.
- Adds a gate after signing: mounts the finished DMG read-only and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the app inside, so this can't regress quietly (option 2 from the issue). The gate fails on today's `main`.
- The volume name stays `PdfCraft`, so the `.DS_Store` layout from #272 keeps finding `.background/background.tiff` through its alias; `.DS_Store` and `.background` are copied as before.

`packaging/macos/dmg/README.md`: the sentence about `makehybrid`.

## Testing

On macOS 26 (Apple Silicon), `packaging/macos/package.sh --arch aarch64` (ad-hoc identity):

- the build passes the new gate; the mounted image has no `com.apple.FinderInfo` on any file, `.DS_Store` and `.background/background.tiff` are there, `Applications` link present, and Finder shows the #272 background with the icon layout when the image opens;
- …

title: M7: Arabic and right-to-left text with installed fonts (Add text, Edit text, rendering)
author: codestubes
body:
Arabic in PdfCraft currently needs the craft-fonts Arab face for Add text, and editing existing Arabic text breaks it (letters reversed, wrong glyphs, `?`/tofu). This PR makes Arabic work end to end with the document's own font or a font installed on the user's machine.

Refs #250, #280, #369, #766.

title: M14: start the desktop app with OpenGL unless PDFCRAFT_RENDERER asks for wgpu
author: codestubes
body:
On an Intel Iris Xe laptop (Windows 11, DirectX 12 through wgpu), the interface sometimes draws every letter from the wrong place of the font texture: broken, overlapping glyphs in menus and especially in the Edit text box. It happens after egui re-sends the font texture at run time (a font added with `ctx.add_font`, or the atlas growing), in about one launch in four, and persists until the app restarts.

## Evidence
- The CPU-side font atlas is byte-identical in good and broken runs (dumped and hashed across 8 runs), and the texture deltas egui hands to the renderer are the same; only the GPU copy is wrong.
- With wgpu's GL backend (`WGPU_BACKEND=gl`) and with `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl` (glow), 0 of 24 launches broke, against roughly 1 in 4 with DirectX 12.
- `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl` already exists "for drivers where wgpu starts but misbehaves"; this makes it the default.

## Change
- `renderer_choice`: unset or unrecognised now means OpenGL (`Gl`); `wgpu` keeps wgpu only, and the new `auto` keeps the previous default (wgpu, then OpenGL if wgpu can't start).
- The renderer test covers the new default and `auto`.

## Trade-offs for maintainers
This changes the renderer for every desktop user, including macOS and Linux and machines where wgpu works well, and it bypasses the Windows adapter selection from #378. If you'd rather keep wgpu by default, alternatives are a Windows/DirectX 12-only default, or a documented note that affected users set `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl`. I can rework it either way. I haven't found the root cause in wgpu or the driver.

## Tests
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft --all-targets -D warnings` pass; `cargo test -p pdfcraft`: 48 passed, 3 failed. The 3 are `single_instance` tests that fail identically on unmodified main on this machine.

title: fix(links): find URLs when lowercasing changes the text length (#816)
author: muraa-p
body:
## Summary

Fixes #816. `crates/annot/src/links.rs::find_urls` built a case-folded copy of the page text and then sliced the **original** characters with offsets taken from that copy. Case folding can change a string's length — U+0130 (`İ`) lowercases to `i` plus a combining dot above — so the address was found at index 41 in the folded copy while the source text was only 39 characters long, and `chars[i..j]` panicked:

```text
thread 'main' panicked at crates/annot/src/links.rs:320:34:
range start index 41 out of range for slice of length 39
```

The CLI exited 101 before `links_from_urls` could create anything; MCP reported an internal tool error but kept serving.

The fix matches the ASCII prefixes (`http://`, `https://`, `www.`) case-insensitively against the original characters, so every offset stays in the source's own index space, and uses `get()` so no lookup can index past the end. Trailing-punctuation trimming and the `www.` → `http://` rewrite are unchanged.

## Tests

- `urls_are_found_after_length_changing_lowercase` — the regression test. On the pre-fix code it panics with the exact range quoted above; with the fix it returns one match, target `http://example.com`, range `21..39` (source-character indices), and leaves the twenty `İ` characters intact.
- `url_scheme_and_www_match_case_insensitively` — locks in case-insensitive scheme and `www.` matching after multibyte text.
- The existing `urls_are_found_in_text` still passes.

Local results for `pdfcraft-annot`: `cargo test` → 33 passed; `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-annot --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean; `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-annot -- --check` → clean.

## Notes

- Crash fix, so it ships with a synthetic regression test that panicked before the change (`AGENTS.md` §4).
- Only `crates/annot/src/links.rs` changes behaviour. No tool signatures, docs, attribution or parity entries are affected.

title: fix(text): match phrases across repeated whitespace (#814)
author: muraa-p
body:
## What changed

`find()` collapsed runs of whitespace in the search query but left them in the page text. When a PDF draws two space glyphs in a row the extracted text keeps both spaces, so a phrase search for the words with a single space between them never matched. Searching each word on its own still worked, which is why it looked like only some files were affected.

The fix collapses whitespace while the page text is flattened, the same way the query already is.

## Testing

I added a regression test that draws two space glyphs between two words and checks the phrase is found. On the old code it fails with an empty range, with the fix it passes. It also checks tabs and single word searches.

The render crate suite passes (168 tests), and clippy and rustfmt are clean.

Fixes #814.

title: Security notice wraps beside its buttons instead of running under them (#785)
author: DWAA1660
body:
## What was wrong
The notice bar above the pages (security, forms, XFA, repaired file, warnings, and the signature bar) laid its message out before its buttons. In a narrow document area (a side panel such as Bookmarks open, or a longer translation like German) the message ran under **Security settings** and on into the side panel, and it wasn't centred on the buttons (even at full width the Dismiss ✕ and the pill weren't on one centre line).

## Fix
`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: a shared `notice_bar` helper, used by both the signature bar and the other notices:
- the buttons are laid out first, right to left, centred on a 28 px row;
- the message gets only the width that's left and wraps there; when less than 120 px is left it's cut short (egui shows the full text on hover) rather than stacking a few letters per line;
- the message's first line is centred on the buttons' row, and a wrapped message grows the bar downwards (never above its top edge).

## How tested
- New `editing::the_security_notice_wraps_beside_its_buttons_and_lines_up_with_them`: opens a restricted document with the Bookmarks panel open at 1700, 1250 and 900 px and checks the message ends before the buttons, the buttons share a centre line, the first line is centred on them, and that the message is one line / wrapped / cut short respectively. It fails on main.
- Checked headless renders at all three widths.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo +1.99.0 clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the ui-egui `editing` (77), `signing`, `view`, `viewer`, `xfa` and `animate` test suites pass.

title: fix(organize): reject rotation angles that are not multiples of 90 (#801)
author: muraa-p
body:
## What changed

The page rotation operation reads the degrees value and quietly divides by 90, so anything that is not a quarter turn was truncated. Asking for 45 degrees saved an unrotated page, and 91 or 135 saved a 90 degree turn, both with a successful exit. The automation page_rotate tool already refused these values, but the single edit command did not.

The check now sits in rotate_pages, before the document is touched, so any caller gets an actionable error and the pages are left as they were.

## Testing

Added a test that asks for 45 and 91 degrees and expects the error, checks the page rotation is unchanged, then confirms negative quarter turns still work. It fails on the old code because the call returned Ok.

Full organize suite passes (60 tests), and clippy and rustfmt are clean.

Fixes #801.

title: fix(edit): refuse a header start number that would wrap the next page (#804)
author: muraa-p
body:
## What changed

Page numbering adds the start number to the position of the page in the run. At the top of the u32 range that addition wrapped, so a release build saved zero for the second page and still reported success, while a debug build hit the overflow and reported it after the fact.

The whole run is now checked before anything is drawn. If the last page number would pass the u32 limit, the operation returns an actionable error and the document keeps no header, instead of a half applied run. The guard uses checked arithmetic and the loop uses a checked conversion.

## Testing

Added a test that asks for two pages starting at 4294967295 (u32::MAX). It expects the error, checks the error text mentions the missing room, and confirms no header mark was left on the document. It then shows a single page at u32::MAX still succeeds, so the limit itself is not rejected.

On the old code the test fails with an attempt to add with overflow panic. The full edit suite passes (48 tests), and clippy and rustfmt are clean.

Fixes #804.

title: fix(view): check Shift-Command-G before Command-G for find navigation (#810)
author: Hathor875
body:
Closes #810.

### Problem
In `canvas.rs::shortcuts()`, Command-G was checked before Shift-Command-G. Because `egui` modifier matching matches Command-G loosely even when Shift is pressed if Shift is not excluded, pressing `Shift-Command-G` triggered the `cmd(Key::G)` branch and navigated to the *next* search match rather than the *previous* one.

### Fix
- Check `KeyboardShortcut::new(Modifiers::COMMAND | Modifiers::SHIFT, Key::G)` before `cmd(Key::G)`.
- Add unit test in `crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs` verifying that Command-G steps forward with wrap-around, and Shift-Command-G steps backward with wrap-around.

title: Issue #774: keep the catalog out of object streams in encrypted files (Acrobat)
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Fixes #774.

## What Acrobat rejects

Reproduced on macOS with Acrobat DC: a PDF protected by PdfCraft (`doc_protect` + full `doc_save`, or Protect in the app) opens in PdfCraft, qpdf, pypdf, poppler and Apple's PDFKit, but Acrobat says "There was an error opening this document. This file is damaged and could not be repaired", before it asks for the password. It happens with every method (AES-256, AES-128, RC4-128), so it isn't the crypto.

Bisected with Acrobat:

| File | Acrobat |
|---|---|
| PdfCraft full save, unencrypted, object streams | opens |
| PdfCraft encrypted, object streams (today's output) | **damaged** |
| the same file rewritten by qpdf with PdfCraft's exact `/O /U /OE /UE /Perms`, with or without object streams | asks for the password |
| PdfCraft encrypted, `object_streams: false` | asks for the password |
| PdfCraft encrypted, object streams, xref stream uncompressed / `/W [1 2 2]` with obj 0 gen 0 / `/Encrypt` moved to the end | **damaged** |
| PdfCraft encrypted, object streams, **catalog written as a standalone object** | asks for the password |
| as above with `/Info` (incl. `/ModDate`) still inside the object stream | asks for the password |

So Acrobat needs the document catalog outside object streams in an encrypted file. qpdf's writer keeps the catalog standalone as well.

## Change

`crates/cos/src/writer.rs`: in `write_full`, when the output is encrypted, the object the trailer's `/Root` points to is written as its own (encrypted) object instead of being packed. Unencrypted output is unchanged. Everything else (Info, pages, fields, annotations) still goes into object streams.

`crates/cos/tests/writer.rs`: `the_catalog_of_an_encrypted_document_stays_outside_object_streams` — the unencrypted save still packs the catalog, the encrypted one doesn't, and the file reopens with the password with an empty repair log.

## Testing

title: M7: keep embedded CMap ranges compact instead of truncating expansion
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

A ToUnicode CMap's sequential `bfrange` is now kept as one record instead of one `HashMap` entry per code. The parser's 2^20 cap used to count expanded codes and stop parsing, so a valid CMap with more codes than that silently lost its later mappings. The cap now counts mappings (an explicit entry counts 1, a range counts 2 because it covers at least two codes), so every CMap with at most 2^20 codes is kept whole. Lookups below code 65 536 read a table; higher codes use a binary search.

## Problem and root cause

`parse_to_unicode` expanded every code of every sequential `bfrange` into a `HashMap<u32, String>` entry and stopped at `MAX_CMAP_ENTRIES` (1 << 20) expanded codes. The cap protected that expansion by discarding valid mappings: 17 ranges of 65 536 codes (about 1.1 million codes from 752 bytes of CMap) lost the last range, and the same expansion cost about 120 MiB for a 6 KB CMap. The guard was applied to the expanded representation rather than to the compact PDF one.

## Scope and non-goals

In scope:

- `crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs`: sequential ToUnicode ranges become `BfRange` records. A table gives the covering record for codes below 65 536, and a sorted cover index serves higher codes. Explicit `bfchar` and array-form entries keep their strings, and so does a one-code range. The later declaration still wins where entries overlap. `MAX_CMAP_ENTRIES` now counts mappings (explicit = 1, range = 2).
- `Metrics::text_of` returns `Option<Cow<str>>` (it returned `Option<&str>`). The one caller, in `crates/edit/src/text.rs`, changes `push_str(t)` to `push_str(&t)`.
- `encode` finds the lowest code per character from explicit entries, the encoding and each record, with no per-code expansion.

Non-goals (unchanged): codespace and CID range parsing and their `MAX_CMAP_RANGES` limit; the 65 536-code width limit per `bfrange` (wider ranges are still ignored, as before, because a lifted limit would need a bounded `encode` search); Symbol and ZapfDingbats poli…

title: fix(edit): keep a comment whose appearance is missing when flattening (#805)
author: muraa-p
body:
﻿## What changed

Flatten did not consider comments that a viewer draws from their dictionary when the file stores no appearance. It looked for `/AP /N`, drew nothing for a note that had none, and then removed the annotation anyway. A supported, visible note was silently erased and the saved page came back blank.

`flatten_which` now builds the appearance a viewer would show for every selected, visible annotation that has none, using the same builder that already draws missing appearances for display, and then draws it as usual. Widgets keep their own handling, and a subtype this build cannot render simply fails to build and is treated exactly as before.

## Testing

Added a synthetic one-page note with no `/AP` and `/Name /Comment`, flattened comments with fields off. It expects one icon drawn, no `/Annots` on the reopened page, and the flattened content stream to carry the icon's XObject. It fails on the old code with 0 drawn.

I also drove the built CLI end to end over the same fixture from the report: `doc_open`, `doc_flatten` with `comments=true` and `fields=false`, then `doc_save`. The rendered pages before and after flattening are byte-identical (469 nonwhite pixels at 267x267), and the saved PDF has no `/Annots`.

Full edit suite passes (48 tests), and clippy and rustfmt are clean.

Fixes #805.

title: fix(comments): keep a reply to a reply in the comment listing (#806)
author: muraa-p
body:
﻿## What changed

`comment_list` collected only the replies whose `/IRT` pointed at the root comment. A reply to a reply keeps its `/IRT` on the direct reply, so it was listed nowhere at all: not a root, and not in any thread. The stored comment and its parent link were always intact, only the listing missed it.

The listing now follows the `/IRT` chain to any depth, with a bound, and includes every descendant of a comment in document order. The roots and the root count are unchanged.

## Testing

Added an end-to-end test that builds a root note, a direct reply, a reply to that reply and a second root note. It asserts the listing still reports two roots and that both reply texts appear. Before the fix the thread held only the direct reply.

Full automation suite passes, and clippy and rustfmt are clean.

Fixes #806.

title: fix(comments): include replies to replies in the comment summary (#820)
author: muraa-p
body:
﻿## What changed

The comment summary gathered a comment's direct replies only, matching each reply's `/IRT` against the comment itself. A reply to a reply points at the direct reply, so its text never reached the generated summary, even though the stored discussion kept it and its parent link.

Replies are now walked to any depth, with a bound, and indented one level per reply. The output for direct replies is unchanged.

## Testing

Added a test that builds a rectangle, a reply and a reply to that reply, then checks the summary carries both texts with the nested one indented under its parent. It omitted the nested reply before the fix.

The comment tests pass, and clippy and rustfmt are clean. Two unrelated XFA timing tests in the engine suite fail on `main` as well; they do not touch this code.

Fixes #820.

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: CyberFox-81
body:
## Summary

This adds an **opt-in embedding bridge** to the web build so that a page hosting PdfCraft in an `<iframe>` can hand it a PDF and receive the bytes when the user saves, instead of the save becoming a browser download.

I built it to run PdfCraft inside **Nextcloud** as a cloud editor: a Nextcloud app adds "Edit in PdfCraft" to the Files menu, opens the PDF in PdfCraft, and writes Save back to the user's Nextcloud (as a new file version). Nothing in the bridge is Nextcloud-specific, though. Any same-origin host (Seafile, an intranet document system, a static site with its own storage) can use it the same way.

Without `?host=parent`, nothing changes: Save downloads the file exactly as it does today.

## What changes (5 files, ~210 lines added, including the test)

**`crates/ui-egui`**
- Two hook types and two fields on `PdfCraftApp`, both `None` by default, following the existing `os_events` pattern:
  - `HostSaveFn = Box<dyn Fn(&str, &[u8], bool) -> Result<(), String>>` and `host_save`: on wasm, when set, `save_then` gives the saved bytes to the host (`name`, `bytes`, `save_as`) instead of calling `download()`.
  - `HostDirtyFn = Box<dyn FnMut(bool)>` and `host_dirty`: told once per frame whether any tab has unsaved work (`first_dirty().is_some()`), so the host can warn before navigating away.
- `save_then` (wasm arm): picks host or download. On a host save it skips the "Downloaded {name}" toast because the host reports where the file went; on failure it shows the existing "Couldn't save {name}: {e}" string. No new translatable strings. `self.views[index]` became `self.views.get_mut(index)` while I was there.

**`apps/pdfcraft-web`**
- A `host` module (`Bridge`) enabled only by `?host=parent` and only when the page is framed. It registers the hooks above, listens for files from the parent, and posts `pdfcraft:ready` once listening.
- `?author=<name>` (host mode only): signs the user's comments with the host's name for them, unless the comment author is st…

title: M4: make page-label generation lazy across large documents
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

Page labels were expanded into one string per page, and the whole sequence was refused once the labels passed 4 MiB in total, so a valid document with long labels could be neither read nor edited. This PR adds a range-backed `PageLabels` view to `pdfcraft-organize`: `label(page)` builds one label and `iter()` builds the labels one at a time, so no string is kept per page. Edits now check each range from its largest number instead of building every label, so organizer edits are no longer limited by the total. Document inspection keeps its 4 MiB cap for now (see Scope).

## Problem and root cause

- `labels_from_ranges` in `crates/organize/src/labels.rs` built a `Vec<String>` for every page and failed with `custom labels exceed 4 MiB in total` once the running total passed `MAX_LABEL_TOTAL_BYTES`. Edits validated by running the same expansion (`set_page_label_ranges`, used by `number_pages`), so the cap also blocked edits.
- Root cause: an eager materialization became a correctness limit. The per-page strings were only needed to answer about one page or to stream them, and validation only needs the largest number of each range.

## Scope and non-goals

In scope: `PageLabels` (`new`, `pages`, `label`, `iter`), exported from `crates/organize/src/lib.rs`; per-range edit validation (`check_spans`) with exact Roman-numeral bounds; the organizer's regression and unit tests in `crates/organize/src/labels.rs` and `crates/organize/src/tests.rs`.

Not changed: `MAX_LABEL_BYTES`, `MAX_LABEL_TREE_WORK`, `MAX_LABEL_TREE_DEPTH`, `MAX_PREFIX_BYTES`, cycle and duplicate-start handling, numbering semantics, and the `/PageLabels` structure that edits write. `MAX_LABEL_TOTAL_BYTES` stays in `pdfcraft-cos`, because inspection still uses it.

Follow-up, not in this PR: document inspection keeps its 4 MiB aggregate cap. The inspector change (commit `a096ece`) was reverted in `95214c9`, because `Inspector::fill` keeps one label `String` per page on open. Removing the cap there n…

title: Print: Windows lists its printers and spools jobs
author: Mawfyy
body:
Fixes #756 (and the printer-not-showing duplicates #160, #244, #293, #465, #644; CIM enumeration approach community-tested in #452).

Until now `spool::printers()` returned an empty list on Windows and `submit()` errored, so the Print dialog offered only "Save as PDF". This change adds the Windows spooler path in `crates/print/src/spool.rs`, following the crate's external-command pattern (`lpstat`/`lp`/`printui`) — no Win32 API is called from Rust:

- **Printer list**: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Printer` (Name and Default only) through `powershell` (`wmic` is removed from Windows 11 24H2), one line per printer, `*` on the default, parsed by the pure `parse_windows_printers`.
- **Jobs**: the embedded `windows_print.ps1` loads the print-ready PDF with the in-box `Windows.Data.Pdf`, renders each sheet at the printer's own resolution inside `PrintPage` (one page's bitmap in memory at a time, aspect-fitted and centred), and spools it with `System.Drawing.Printing` carrying copies, collation, duplex and grayscale as the job's settings. The job reaches the script via environment variables, so printer names with spaces/quotes survive and the document's path never appears in the process list; the temp job file has a `create_new` unpredictable name and is removed however the job ends. No PDF reader is required on the machine.
- The UI, `doc_print` and the `printers` tool all go through these functions, so all three get Windows printing with no further changes. Print ▸ Properties… (printui) already worked and is unchanged.
- Printing *to* a PDF printer ("Microsoft Print to PDF") spools like any other printer and the system then asks where to save — the same as Acrobat; it is a printer choice, not a separate code path.

**Tests** (`crates/print/src/tests.rs`):
- Unit, every platform: `windows_printers_carry_one_default_and_keep_their_names`, `the_windows_job_is_the_environment_of_the_print_script`.

title: XFDF comment exchange keeps polygon and polyline vertices (#809)
author: DWAA1660
body:
## What was wrong
`export_xfdf` wrote polygon and polyline comments with only their rectangle, and `import` had no reader for their points. After an XFDF round trip the comments kept their subtype and text but had no `/Vertices`, so `pdfcraft_annot::set_appearance` couldn't draw them and the shape vanished. FDF was fine because it carries the dictionaries as they are.

## The fix (`crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs`)
- **Export:** an annotation with `/Vertices` gets an XFDF `<vertices>x,y;x,y;…</vertices>` child (ISO 19444-1, same `x,y;` form as `<gesture>`).
- **Import:** `<vertices>` is read back into `/Vertices` before the appearance is drawn. Only whole x,y pairs are kept (a trailing odd number is dropped), and an element with no numbers in it adds nothing.

## How tested
- New test `tests::xfdf_keeps_polygon_and_polyline_vertices`: a polygon (page 1) and a polyline with a closed-arrow end (page 2) are exported, the XFDF is checked for both `<vertices>` elements, and after import into a blank document the `/Vertices` arrays match the source and every imported annotation has an `/AP`. It also imports hand-written XFDF with an odd count and with junk. The test fails on main and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf` (13 tests), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo +1.99.0 clippy -p pdfcraft-xfdf --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

Fixes #809

Duplicates: none found (searched "xfdf polygon", "xfdf vertices", "polyline xfdf", "xfdf shape", "comment export polygon").

title: M11: Reduce file size shrinks office scans, and never saves a bigger copy (refs #490)
author: taylorandrew07-lab
body:
## What this fixes

#490 reports that **Reduce file size** leaves an office scan at the same size. Two problems:

1. **Scans were skipped.** Office scanners (the one in #490 is a Lexmark) write the default decode array `/Decode [0 1 0 1 0 1]` on the page image. It changes nothing, but Reduce skipped *every* image that had a decode array, so the whole page was left alone.
   - Now the default array (`[0 1]` per colour component, as integers or reals) counts as no array, and the rewritten image drops it.
   - Any other decode array (for example one that inverts the colours, or one of the wrong length) still skips the image, as before.
2. **A copy that wasn't smaller was saved anyway,** reported as "0% smaller" or "-N% smaller". On the synthetic scan below, Reduce made the file slightly *bigger*.
   - **Reduce file size** now saves nothing when the copy isn't smaller, and says: "This file is already as small as it can be made (78.9 KB). No copy was saved." (Acrobat says the file is "already minimized" in the same case.)
   - **`doc_reduce`** writes nothing in that case and returns `"written": false` (and `true` when it writes). The tool description says so.
   - **Optimize PDF** still saves, because what it discards (metadata, attachments…) may matter more than the size, but it now says "(not smaller)" instead of a negative percentage.

## Results

Synthetic A4 scan (300 ppi RGB JPEG with the default decode array, made from a demo invoice):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Reduce file size | 227.0 KB → 227.1 KB, reported as "-0% smaller" | 227.0 KB → 78.9 KB (65% smaller) |
| Reduce again on the reduced copy | (would save another copy) | "This file is already as small as it can be made (78.9 KB). No copy was saved." |

The reduced page looks the same at screen resolution (150 ppi, JPEG medium: Reduce's existing settings, unchanged).

## Tests

title: Autosave: snapshot a new unsaved document before its first edit (#815)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #815.

`Session::open_new` marked the new document dirty but left its `generation` equal to `snapshot_generation` (both 0), so `autosave_snapshots` skipped it until a later edit. Every result opened through `open_new` (Create > Blank page, combine, extract, and the automation paths) had no recovery snapshot until then.

`open_new` now bumps the generation once, the same way `mark_recovered` does, so the next autosave pass snapshots the new document exactly once. Clean documents are unchanged, and later edits are snapshotted as before.

Test: `autosave_snapshots_a_new_unsaved_document_once` (next to `autosave_snapshots_only_changed_documents`) opens a new document beside a clean one and checks that only the new one is snapshotted, only once, and again after an edit. Without the fix the first assertion fails because there are 0 snapshots.

title: organize: drop named destinations and their links when a page is deleted (#817)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #817.

`delete_pages` already removed bookmarks and links whose explicit destination went to a deleted page, but it did not look at named destinations. Names in the catalog's `/Names /Dests` tree and in the legacy `/Dests` dictionary kept their entries. When the file was saved, the page reference in those entries became `null`, and links on the surviving pages still used the names.

Now `drop_destinations_to` first prunes both named stores:

- `/Names /Dests` tree: the pairs that go to a deleted page are removed from `/Names`, in the root node and in every `/Kids` node (by reference or inline; a guard stops reference cycles).
- Legacy `/Dests` dictionary (by reference or inline): the entries that go to a deleted page are removed.
- A destination can be an array or a dictionary with `/D`, directly or by reference.

The removed names are then handled like explicit destinations to a deleted page: a link or bookmark with such a name as `/Dest`, or a GoTo `/A` whose `/D` is such a name, loses that destination. This is the same treatment that the existing code gives to explicit destinations. Names that go to surviving pages, and the links that use them, are not changed. They are not moved to a different page.

The `/OpenAction` is not part of this change (#821 handles it).

Test: `deleting_a_page_drops_the_named_destinations_to_it` uses the fixture from the issue: three pages, two tree names and two legacy names that go to the first and last pages, and four links on the middle page (one of them a GoTo action, and one legacy value a `/D` dictionary). It deletes the first page and saves. Then it checks that only `treeLast` stays in the tree and still goes to the old third page, that only `legacyLast` stays in `/Dests`, and that only the two links to the first page lost their destination. Without the fix the tree still has four entries, so the test fails.

title: Extract/Combine: a page repeated in one selection gets its own annotations (#818)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #818.

When one selection lists the same page twice (Extract Pages `pages: [1, 1]`, or a Combine Files range like `"1,1"`), `import_pages_mapped` already made a second page object, but the copier still had the first copy of each annotation in its object map. Both pages ended up pointing at the same note and link dictionaries, and `/P` named only the last page, so `comment_edit` on page 1 also changed page 2.

The fix: before copying a repeated page, the copier forgets the annotation and form-field copies it made so far (`copier.annots` / `copier.fields`). The repeated page's annotations are then copied again, together with what belongs to them (a note's `/Popup`, a widget's field), and `/P` is set to the page that holds each copy. Everything else stays shared: fonts, images, content streams and appearance streams. This matches Duplicate Pages, which already copies annotations and fields fresh (the issue's workaround).

Both Extract Pages and Combine Files go through `import_pages_mapped`, so this one change covers both paths from the issue. Link destinations work as before: a link to a page in the selection points at its copy, and a link to a page that was left out loses its destination.

Test: `repeated_page_gets_independent_annotations` extracts each page of the existing `doc_a` fixture twice: a link, a link plus a form-field widget, and a note with a popup. It checks that every copy has its own annotation objects, that each `/P` names the page holding it, and that each note's popup is separate and points back at its own note. Without the fix, the two pages share annotation objects and the test fails.

title: M12: XFA rows in areas get their instances
body:
A Designer form whose table (a top-to-bottom subform inside an area of a positioned page) asks for several rows with `<occur min="10"/>` was laid out with one row, and a FormCalc total looping over the rows stayed empty.

- layout: a repeating subform inside a top-to-bottom container in positioned content is drawn and measured once per instance (occur and data), with its own SOM index, as flowed content already was. One `instances` helper now serves flowing, table rows and this case.
- data: areas are named in SOM expressions but are not data scopes. `data_path(tpl, som)` leaves them out (unknown segments are kept), and layout, the script tree, reading and writing the datasets and the engine's value and row operations use it. Before, values Adobe's viewers saved were not read, what was filled here went under a new element named after the area (which Adobe's viewers would most likely not read), and scripts counted the rows there: one, so a loop over the table's rows failed on the missing ones.
- write_datasets_with / read_values_with take the parsed template when the caller has it (the engine's cached one); the old functions parse the document's.
- Tests: layout regression, data_path rules, and an engine round trip shaped like such a form (rows, Adobe-written values, a FormCalc total over every row, the data written back, reopening).

title: XFDF keeps a callout's leader, text-box inset, intent and arrowhead (#819)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #819.

XFDF export wrote a callout as a plain `<freetext>` with only its outer rect, and import rebuilt it without `/CL`, `/RD`, `/IT` or `/LE`. The regenerated appearance then drew a plain box over the whole annotation rectangle, with no leader or arrowhead. FDF was not affected, because it copies the dictionary as-is.

Changes, in `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs`:

- **Export:** a FreeText with a `/CL` of 2 or 3 points now writes the XFDF `<freetext>` attributes from ISO 19444-1: `callout` (`/CL`), `fringe` (`/RD`), `intent` (`/IT`) and `head` (the single-name `/LE` of a callout). The existing two-name `head`/`tail` for lines is unchanged.
- **Import:** a `callout` attribute with 4 or 6 numbers sets `/CL`, `fringe` sets `/RD`, `intent` sets `/IT` (default `FreeTextCallout`), and `head` sets `/LE` as one name, not the head/tail array used for lines. The appearance is then regenerated from these keys by the existing `pdfcraft_annot::set_appearance`, which already draws the leader, arrowhead and inset box (it also accepts 4- or 6-number `/CL`).
- Plain FreeText (no `callout`) and the FDF path behave as before.
- The crate README and module docs now list callouts among the XFDF fields that are kept.

Test: `xfdf_keeps_callout_leader_inset_and_ending` creates the callout from the issue (`rect [40,300,180,360]`, knee `[260,330]`, point `[320,200]`, `ClosedArrow`), exports XFDF, imports it into a blank document and checks that `/Rect`, `/CL`, `/RD`, `/IT` and `/LE` match the source. Without the fix it fails because the imported annotation has no `/CL`.

title: organize: deleting the opening page drops the catalog OpenAction (#821)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #821.

Deleting the page that the catalog's `/OpenAction` opens left `/OpenAction [null /Fit]` in the saved file, because `delete_pages` cleaned up bookmarks and links that pointed at deleted pages but never looked at the catalog.

`drop_destinations_to` now checks `/OpenAction` too, in both forms it can take as a destination: an explicit destination array, or a `/GoTo` action whose `/D` is one. If it opens a deleted page, `/OpenAction` is removed, the same way a bookmark or link loses its `/Dest` or GoTo `/A`. It is not moved to another page, because that would change what the instruction means (as the issue says). Other kinds of OpenAction (JavaScript, named destinations) are left alone.

Test: `deleting_the_opening_page_drops_the_open_action` covers both forms. Deleting the opening page leaves no `/OpenAction` after a full save and reopen, and deleting a different page keeps it. Without the fix, the first case reopens with `[null /Fit]` (or the GoTo action pointing at null) and the test fails.

title: Web: warn before reloading a document with unsaved changes (#812)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #812.

In the browser, eframe never raises a viewport close request on reload or tab close, so `guard_quit` never reaches the save prompt and a reload silently drops committed edits.

**Fix (web only, since native already gets a close request):**
- `PdfCraftApp` gets an `unsaved_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>`. `guard_quit`, which runs every frame on every platform, now refreshes it from `first_dirty()` first. That is the same check the quit prompt uses, so the browser warning and the native prompt agree on what counts as unsaved work.
- `apps/pdfcraft-web` registers a `beforeunload` listener on `window` that calls `preventDefault()` while the flag is set. The browser then shows its own "Leave site?" confirmation, and cancelling it keeps the page and the edits. A clean document reloads with no warning. The handler is Rust through `web-sys` (the only feature added is `Event`), so no handwritten JS is needed.

Native close and in-app tab close are unchanged.

**Test:** `unsaved_flag_follows_dirty_state` opens the form fixture, calls `guard_quit` with no close request (as on the web), and checks that the flag is clear. It then commits a field edit and checks that the next `guard_quit` sets it. Without the fix, the test does not compile because `unsaved_flag` does not exist.

title: Recovery: cancelling the password prompt no longer taints the next opened document (#813)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #813.

Recovering an encrypted snapshot sets `pending_recovered` and then raises its password prompt. `submit_password` finished the recovery after **any** successful foreground unlock. So when the snapshot's prompt went away without being answered, the next unlocked file took the snapshot's original path and recovery key. It was marked dirty, Save wrote it over the other document's original file, and the snapshot was deleted.

Two ways reach this, and both are fixed in `submit_password`:

- **Cancel** (the issue's steps): cancelling the prompt now clears `pending_recovered`, because the recovery is abandoned.
- **Another file's prompt replaces the snapshot's** (for example, a file opened from the OS while the prompt is up): recovery now finishes only when the unlocked prompt is the snapshot's own. The snapshot is opened by its name without a path, and that is the check. A wrong password re-raises the same prompt, so a retry still finishes the recovery.

The snapshot is not deleted. It is still on disk and is offered again in the next session.

Tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/recovery.rs`): both paths recover an encrypted entry, then unlock a different encrypted `b.pdf`. They check that `b.pdf` keeps its own path, stays clean and the snapshot is still in the store. Both tests fail without the fix: `b.pdf` gets `/original/a.pdf`. The existing encrypted recovery test still covers the correct-password path, and it now uses the shared `encrypted()` fixture helper.

title: Issue #813: a cancelled recovery password no longer attaches to the next unlocked document
author: ch0kemeister
body:
## Problem

Recovering an encrypted snapshot raises the password prompt and, until now, parked the snapshot's metadata in a free-standing `pending_recovered` field. Cancelling the prompt dropped the prompt but left that field set. The next encrypted document unlocked in the foreground then consumed it: `finish_recovery` gave that unrelated document the snapshot's original path and recovery key. A plain Save would write the new document over the other file and delete the other document's snapshot. Reported with a source trace in #813; reproduced here with a UI test.

## Change

The association travels with the prompt instead of the app: `PasswordPrompt` gets a `recovered: Option<RecoveryMeta>` field, set by `recover()` when the snapshot turns out to be encrypted.

- **Cancel** drops the prompt and with it the association. The entry goes back on the `recoverable` list; the snapshot stays in the store, so a later session offers it again.
- **Correct password** finishes the recovery of that document only.
- **Wrong password** re-raises the prompt for the same bytes, which keeps the snapshot.
- `finish_recovery` acts on the tab that was just opened (`views.last()`) rather than the active one, so it cannot be confused by focus.
- `pending_recovered` is gone.

## Tests

New `a_cancelled_recovery_password_does_not_attach_to_the_next_unlocked_document` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/recovery.rs`: a crashed session leaves an encrypted snapshot of A (original path `/docs/A.pdf`); Recover, Cancel in the password modal; open encrypted B with its password. B keeps `/docs/B.pdf`, is clean, A's snapshot is still in the store, and closing B leaves it there. The encryption helper is shared with the existing encrypted-recovery test.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New test on `main` without the fix | fails: B has path `/docs/A.pdf` and is dirty |
| `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test recovery` | 8 passed |
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-ta…

title: Fit to width fits the shown page in single-page view (#808)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #808.

In single-page display, View ▸ Fit to width sized every page for the widest page in the document, so a narrower page was shown too small (half width in the issue's 300 pt / 600 pt fixture).

- `fit_zoom`: `Fit::Width` now divides by the width of the page it picked for the layout, as `Fit::Page` and `Fit::Height` already do. Single-page view uses the shown page; Continuous and Two-page still use the largest page, so their zoom holds still while pages of other sizes scroll past.
- `document_area`: the scroll content width also came from the widest page in the document. With the zoom fixed, that would have centred the fitted narrow page in a strip as wide as the large page, so part of it sat off screen behind a horizontal scrollbar. The width now comes from a new `DocView::content_width`, which counts only the shown page in single-page view. Scrolling layouts compute the same width as before.

Test: `fit_width_fits_the_shown_page_in_single_page_view_only` (canvas.rs) uses the issue's 300 pt and 600 pt pages in a 1000 pt viewport. It checks that the narrow page is laid out at the side gutter and 860 pt wide, that it gets twice the zoom of the wide page, and that Continuous fit width keeps one zoom across both pages. It fails on main: the zoom is the same for both pages, and the page starts at x = 500.

title: fix(xfdf): drop the replaced note's popup when re-importing a comment (#807)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #807.

`place()` in `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs` replaced a comment with the same `/NM` but left its `Popup` in the page's `/Annots`. The XFDF import then added a new popup for the new note, so every re-import of the same note added one more popup whose `/Parent` was a note no longer on the page.

Now `place()` remembers the notes it replaces and also drops any `Popup` annotation whose `/Parent` is one of them. Other annotations on the page, notes without a popup, and comments with other names are left as they were. `place()` is shared by the XFDF and FDF import paths, so both get the fix. The crate README now says that the replaced comment's pop-up goes too.

Test: `reimporting_a_note_replaces_its_popup` imports the same XFDF note with a popup three times and checks that the page has exactly one popup and that its parent is on the page. Without the fix it finds three popups.

title: Print: a scaled annotation appearance no longer prints larger than its rectangle (#802)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #802.

When printing with comments and forms, `appearance_matrix` worked out the Algorithm 8.1 placement `A` from the appearance's BBox transformed by its `/Matrix`. It then returned `Matrix × A`. But the `Do` that draws the form applies the form's own `/Matrix` anyway, so the matrix was applied twice. In the issue's example, a scale-2 appearance printed at twice the size of its `/Rect` (outer `5 0 0 5 50 50 cm` instead of `2.5 0 0 2.5 50 50 cm`).

The function now returns only the placement `A`. This is the same matrix that flatten's `placement` (`crates/edit/src/flatten.rs`) already draws, so printing directly now gives the same geometry as printing a flattened copy. Appearances with an identity `/Matrix` print exactly as before.

Test: `a_scaled_appearance_is_not_scaled_twice` uses a 10x10 BBox with a scale-2 `/Matrix` on a 40x40 rect. It expects a placement of scale 2 at the rect origin. Without the fix, the function returns scale 4 and the test fails.

title: Measure: snap to the implicit closing edge of filled paths (#803)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #803.

`measure_snap` only added the closing edge of a subpath for `s`, `b` and `b*`. A fill closes every open subpath implicitly (ISO 32000-2 8.5.3.3), so `f`, `F`, `f*`, `B` and `B*` paint that edge too, but it was not a snap target. A triangle drawn with `... l f` therefore lost one side, while the same triangle with `h f` kept it.

Now every painting operator except a bare `S` adds the closing edge. `S` still leaves the path open, as it does when it renders.

Test: `filled_open_triangle_snaps_to_closing_edge` builds the open triangle from the issue with each operator (`f`, `F`, `f*`, `B`, `B*`, `h f`, `S`). It checks the segment count and a snap at the middle of the closing edge. Without the fix, `f`, `F`, `f*`, `B` and `B*` fail.

title: Keep every part when bookmark titles repeat in doc_split (#800)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #800.

Splitting at top-level bookmarks names each part after its bookmark. Two bookmarks with the same title (or titles that sanitize to the same name, like `Section!` and `Section?`) gave two parts the same file name, so the later part replaced the earlier one while the call still reported both.

Both split paths had the same bug, so both are fixed:

- **`doc_split` (automation / CLI / MCP):** the loop keeps a set of the names it already used and adds `-2`, `-3`, ... on a repeat (`in-Chapter.pdf`, `in-Chapter-2.pdf`). The returned `files` list now names each part's own file. The tool description mentions the suffix.
- **Split dialog, "Top-level bookmarks" (desktop and web):** `split_active` does the same, in the dialog's own naming style: `doc - Chapter.pdf`, `doc - Chapter (2).pdf`.

Names are compared case-insensitively, so `Same` and `same` also stay separate on macOS and Windows, where the file system would otherwise merge them. Bookmarks with different titles keep their names as before.

Tests:
- `bookmark_split_with_equal_titles_keeps_every_part` (automation): bookmarks `Same`, `Same`, `same` on pages 1-3 give `a-Same.pdf`, `a-Same-2.pdf`, `a-same-3.pdf`, and all three files exist.
- `split_at_bookmarks_with_equal_titles_keeps_every_part` (ui-egui, kittest): the same bookmarks through the Split dialog write `doc - Same.pdf`, `doc - Same (2).pdf`, `doc - same (3).pdf`.

title: Viewer: touchpad scrolling tracks the finger 1:1 (#759)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #759.

**Root cause.** A precision touchpad sends pixel-precise `MouseWheel` events. On Windows they arrive with no `TouchPhase::Start`, so egui never takes its no-smoothing "in touch" path and eases any delta of 8 px or more over several frames — the page lags a frame or two behind the finger. (egui's own `wheel_state.rs` documents this trade-off: it skips smoothing only while a touch is in progress.)

**Fix.** The page view now applies precise (Point-unit) wheel input itself, 1:1, through the same un-eased scroll path already used by keyboard and middle-button auto-scroll, and suppresses egui's eased copy for a short (0.25 s) window so its internal easing tail neither doubles nor trails the motion. A coarse mouse wheel (Line/Page units) keeps egui's smoothing, which is pleasant for chunky notches, and single-page paging still owns the vertical axis.

No fork of egui required — this matches the approach taken by the sibling egui apps linked in the issue.

**Test.** `precise_touchpad_wheel_scrolls_one_to_one` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/view.rs`: one 200 px precise swipe scrolls the full 200 px at once (an eased path would ramp there over ~0.1 s) and leaves no drift afterward.

Verified: all 31 `view` tests pass; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -- -D warnings` clean. Confirmed in the kittest harness; not yet exercised on physical Windows touchpad hardware.

title: fix(organize): repeated page extraction creates independent annotations (#818)
author: Hathor875
body:
## Summary
Fixes #818.

When extracting or combining pages where a source page is repeated (e.g. `pages: [1, 1]` or Combine Files with ranges like `["1, 1", "2"]`), `Copier` was caching copied indirect objects in `self.map`. As a result, subsequent copies of the same page in a single import operation reused the exact same annotation `ObjRef`s, overwrote the page ownership mapping in `annot_pages`, and pointed both copies' annotations at the last copied page via `/P`.

This change:
1. Distinguishes page-specific annotations from shared immutable resources: annotations are copied into dedicated destination objects for each page instance via a per-page `annot_map`, rather than being shared across distinct page copies via `copier.map`.
2. Preserves cross-annotation relationships on the same page instance (such as `/Popup` ↔ `/Parent` cycles and comment reply chains).
3. Keeps appearance streams (`/AP`), fonts, images, and other immutable resources deduplicated and shared through `copier.map`.
4. Associates each copied annotation's `/P` entry with its containing page instance.
5. Adds regression tests in `crates/organize/src/tests.rs` covering repeated page extraction with notes and popups, verifying independent editability, link destination rewiring / omitted destination stripping, and combine with repeated page selections.

## Test plan
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-organize`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-organize --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- `cargo xtask wasm`

title: M4: traverse large bookmark trees lazily without dropping later items
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

Bookmark listing and edits by path stopped silently at the 100,000th bookmark, so later bookmarks were missing from `organize::bookmarks`, the `bookmark_list` tool, the bookmarks panel and edits by path. The outline is now walked lazily and iteratively with no item cap. `bookmark_list` pages through every bookmark (`offset`, `limit`, `next`); the open path keeps a bounded window of the first 10,000 bookmarks (nested at most 33 levels deep) and the panel says when more exist. Pagination is not truncation: every finite, non-cyclic bookmark within the listing depth is reachable by following `next`.

## Problem and root cause

- `crates/organize/src/outline.rs`: `children_of` stopped at `MAX_ITEMS = 100_000`. The count includes the outline root, so a 100,005-item outline listed 99,999 bookmarks. Edits by path past that point failed with `there is no bookmark at [...]`.
- `crates/render/src/inspect.rs` (`outline_siblings`): every open, and every refresh after an edit, built the whole nested outline. It cut each sibling list at 100,001 items and dropped children below depth 32 without a flag. `doc_info`, `bookmark_list` and the bookmarks panel all read this copy, so the late bookmark was missing there too.
- Both walks recursed once per level. A 100,000-deep chain of bookmarks overflows the stack in `recount`.

Root cause, confirmed by the base runs below: the outline was materialised eagerly with an arbitrary cap, and two walks recursed. The change replaces that with a lazy, iterative walk, so the work for a listing is bounded by the page or window asked for. Edits keep their existing semantics, including one full `/Count` pass per edit.

## Scope and non-goals

In scope: the iterative walk, paged listing and top-level walk in `organize`; the bounded outline window in `render`; `bookmark_page` and split points in `engine`; `bookmark_list` paging and `doc_info.outline_more` in `automation`; the bookmarks-panel note in `ui-egui` (English); the bookmarks parity …

title: fix(automation): retain batch results with identical filenames
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Running an automation action on multiple PDFs with identical filenames can silently replace an earlier output.

For example, processing:

- left/report.pdf
- right/report.pdf

previously wrote both results to the same destination, results/report.pdf.

The action reported success, but only the second result survived.

## Root cause

The action_run implementation derived each output filename from the input basename.

When two inputs shared that basename, both were written to the same destination using an atomic writer that replaces existing files.

## Changes

- Detect output filename collisions before writing batch results.
- Use the existing unused-filename helper to select an available destination.
- Preserve earlier outputs instead of replacing them.
- Return an error if no available output filename can be found.
- Add a regression test covering distinct PDFs with identical basenames.

## Regression coverage

The new test checks that:

1. Both input PDFs produce separate output files.
2. Their original page counts are preserved.
3. Output filenames are distinct.
4. Running the action again does not overwrite previous results.

## Validation

- Source and committed diff reviewed.
- Regression test added but not executed.
- Rust formatting, Clippy, and unit tests remain unverified.
- Upstream CI has not run.

## Issue

Fixes #799

title: Linux: the tab strip carries the window controls, as in Acrobat
author: gyurix
body:
## What

On X11 the window manager draws its own title bar above the one the app already
has, so every window has two bars. Only the outer one carries minimize,
maximize and close, and it does not match the app it belongs to.

This turns the system frame off on Linux and FreeBSD and draws the controls in
the app's own title bar, which is where Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Acrobat put
them. The window still resizes, moves, maximizes and closes exactly as before.

## Why not leave the window manager's frame in place

It is not a matter of taste, in two places:

- **DeckCraft** draws the presentation full screen, and **PdfCraft** has a
  full-screen page view; in both, a system title bar would sit over the content.
- With client-side decorations the controls follow the app's own theme, so they
  stay legible in the dark theme instead of being a light bar on a dark window.

## How it was checked

Each app was built from this branch, installed as a `.deb` and driven with
`xdotool` on XFCE/xfwm4, 1920x1080:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| maximize / restore buttons | `_NET_WM_STATE` gains and loses `MAXIMIZED_HORZ`/`MAXIMIZED_VERT` |
| double-click on the title bar | same, in both directions |
| move by dragging the title bar | window moves |
| resize from all four edges | window resizes |
| resize from all four corners | window resizes diagonally |
| minimize, then reactivate | `_NET_WM_STATE_HIDDEN` set, then cleared |
| close | window closes, through the same unsaved-changes check |
| slideshow / full screen (DeckCraft, PdfCraft) | no controls drawn over the content |
| overlay screens (Backstage, palette) | controls stay reachable, drawn last |

## Compatibility

- macOS and Windows are untouched; both keep the system frame.
- `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_TITLEBAR=1` keeps the window manager's title bar, for anyone who
  prefers it or whose window manager needs a frame to place the window.
- The three new tooltip strings (`Minimize`, `Maximize`, `Restore Down`) are
  added to ever…

title: Linux: "Use system setting" asks the desktop, not winit
author: gyurix
body:
## What

`View ▸ Display theme ▸ Use system setting` — the default — did not follow the
system on Linux.

winit reports no system theme there: `ActiveEventLoop::system_theme()` is `None`
on every Linux desktop, in every version of winit. `ThemePreference::System`
resolved against that, and with nothing to resolve against it fell back to
whatever happened to be on screen. So:

- a fresh PdfCraft started **light on a dark desktop**;
- choosing Dark and then "Use system setting" **left it dark**, whether or not
  that matched the desktop.

macOS and Windows were unaffected: winit answers there.

## The fix

`pdfcraft-platform` gains `desktop_theme`, which asks the XDG Desktop Portal's
`Settings` interface for `org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`. That schema
name is asked first because GNOME's portal and XFCE's both answer it; the older
`org.freedesktop.interface.color-scheme` is asked second, because that is the one
KDE's portal answers.

The read happens on its own thread, so no D-Bus call is ever made from the frame
loop, and the first answer is delivered straight away rather than only on a
change. The app polls that thread once a frame, so switching the desktop theme
while PdfCraft is running is picked up within a few seconds.

A desktop that answers neither schema leaves the user's own choice alone,
exactly as before — no guessing from a theme name.

## How it was checked

Built from this branch and run on XFCE/xfwm4 with
`gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`:

| step | `theme_preference` | `theme` |
|---|---|---|
| start with the saved setting, desktop dark | `System` | **Dark** (was Light) |
| desktop set to `prefer-light` | `System` | **Light**, within 4 s |
| desktop set back to `prefer-dark` | `System` | **Dark**, within 4 s |
| explicit Light / Dark, then the desktop changes | `Light` / `Dark` | unchanged |

`crates/ui-egui/tests/theme.rs` keeps its existing coverage of the three
preferences against egui's reported system theme; `cra…

title: Issue #878: Combine stores an image once when its colour space is an indirect name
author: mlkonrad
body:
Fixes #878.

ImageMagick writes an image's colour space as its own object (`/ColorSpace 10 0 R` with `10 0 obj /DeviceRGB`). When those files are combined, each source's copy of that little object is never merged (it isn't a resource), so `dedupe` saw the image dictionaries as different and kept every copy of identical images.

`dedupe` now hashes and compares a reference to a plain value (name, number, boolean or string) as that value. The value objects themselves are still never merged, so nothing that might be edited in place ends up shared. Combine, Insert Pages and Reduce File Size all use this code.

### Results (release CLI)

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ImageMagick PDF combined 3× | 541,628 B | 181,121 B |
| 80 MB ImageMagick photo PDF combined 8× | 648 MB, 1.19 s, 1.9 GB peak | 81 MB, 0.84 s, 1.27 GB peak |

I also ran a corpus of 35 image PDFs (16-bit, alpha, palette, interlaced, CMYK and progressive JPEG, broken and hostile images, plus same-bytes-different-colour-space images that must stay separate). Every merged page renders pixel-identical to its source, before and after the change.

The merged-away image's own `/DeviceRGB` object is left in the file unreferenced: a few bytes, since `write_full` keeps every object. I left that alone rather than widen the change.

### Tests
- `dedupe::tests::references_to_plain_values_compare_as_the_values`: indirect vs. indirect vs. direct `/DeviceRGB` images merge; the same pixels under `/DeviceGray` don't; the value objects survive.
- `tests::combine_stores_an_image_once_when_its_colour_space_is_an_indirect_name`: Combine 3× and Insert Pages each end with one image.

Both fail without the fix. Gates: fmt, clippy `--all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (also with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`), `xtask layers|assets|parity|wasm`, `pdfcraft-cli --no-default-features`, `cargo-deny`.
