title: Units: read the Windows measurement system from the registry, not reg.exe
author: jcl-bit
body:
The desktop app starts reg.exe at every launch to pick the default Units: `reg.exe query "HKCU\Control Panel\International" /v iMeasure` (added in #463). This replaces it with an in-process registry read through winsafe's safe RegGetValue (the advapi feature of winsafe 0.0.29, already in the tree for apps/pdfcraft), so the app starts no child process for this.

Why: on managed PCs reg.exe is a LOLBin that EDR watches, and WDAC/AppLocker setups often restrict it. I saw it in a 4688 process-creation audit in Windows Sandbox while testing the native printing work in #1132: after printing no longer started PowerShell, reg.exe was the one child process left at startup.

Behaviour is unchanged. "1" is inches, "0" is millimetres, and a missing or unreadable value falls through to the same LC_ALL/LC_MEASUREMENT/LANG check as before. It stays Windows-only (macOS and Linux paths are untouched), and every failure path returns None rather than panicking.

Tests: the value-to-unit mapping is now a pure function (`unit_for_imeasure`) with a unit test, and a Windows test checks that the registry read returns a value the mapping understands. I have not added a test that asserts no process is started, since that needs an OS-level audit; I checked it with the Sandbox 4688 audit instead.

`cargo xtask ci` passes (all 8 steps).

title: M3: follow Windows' Animation effects setting; add an Animation effects preference
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Problem

With Windows' Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Visual effects ▸ Animation effects turned off, PdfCraft still animated wheel scrolling and Ctrl+wheel zooming. The app never read the setting, and egui spreads every coarse wheel step over about a quarter of a second with no switch to turn that off.

## What this changes

- **The Windows setting is followed.** The desktop app reads `UISettings.AnimationsEnabled` at launch and every two seconds while in use, so a change applies without a restart.
- **With animation effects off, nothing eases.** A wheel notch scrolls its whole distance, and Ctrl+wheel zooms its whole step, in the frame it arrives. egui's own animations (menu fades, opening sections, scrolling to a row) take no time, the chrome's hover and press washes are simply there, and the progress card's bar steps without its sweep. Distances are unchanged; only the easing goes.
- **New preference: Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ Animation effects**, with Use system setting (default), On and Off. On and Off decide every animation in the window, whatever the system says.

| Animation effects | System animations on | System animations off |
|---|---|---|
| Use system setting | animated | off |
| On | animated | animated |
| Off | off | off |

The choice is saved with the other preferences and can be set as `animation_effects` (`system`, `on`, `off`) on the control channel.

## How it works

- `crates/ui-egui/src/motion.rs` reads each frame's wheel input the way egui does, minus the easing, and hands the result to the scroll areas. Zoom call sites read `motion::zoom_delta` instead of egui's `zoom_delta`.
- With animation effects off, egui's style animation time is zero. The app's own fades with fixed durations (the hover and press washes, the progress bar) ask `motion::animated`.
- `apps/pdfcraft/src/motion.rs` is the Windows reader. The UI crate takes it as an injected source (`motion.source`), so tests and screenshots never depend on the machine's setting, an…

title: honour the /Lab colour space /WhitePoint (#1203)
author: Hathor875
body:
Closes #1203

## What
`/Lab` colour spaces whose `/WhitePoint` isn't D50 were rendered as if the white point were D50. Every non-D50 page (e.g. D65 `[0.9505 1 1.089]`) came out off by several levels per channel, and a D65 blue was 45 levels too red.

The old path scaled L\*a\*b\* and handed it to the bundled ICC transform, which by definition assumes a D50 connection space and dropped the `/WhitePoint`. The fix maps L\*a\*b\* to XYZ in the space's own white coordinates (ISO 32000-2 §8.6.5.4), Bradford-adapts to D65 and converts straight to sRGB, as Poppler does.

## Changes
- `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/color.rs`: `Lab` now keeps its dictionary `/WhitePoint` (and `/Range`) and converts Lab → XYZ → D65-adapted sRGB directly instead of via the LAB.icc ICC transform. Missing or degenerate white points fall back to a flat white; hostile components/ranges are clamped without panicking (`clamp_component`; no `unwrap`/`expect` in non-test code). `CalRgb::normalize_white_point_to_d65` is reused as an associated function.
- `crates/render/src/raster.rs`: regression test `lab_honours_the_space_white_point` renders the five reported D65 flat patches and checks their centre pixel against the CIE sRGB values (within ±2 levels).

## Quality gates (all in `pdfcraft-dev` container)
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — ok
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` — ok
- `cargo xtask assets` — ok (260 repository assets)
- `cargo xtask parity` — ok
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render` — 168 passed (incl. new regression test)
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine --lib` — 127 passed, 1 ignored

title: M10: print from the web build through the browser's print dialog (gap 4)
author: rp6186030
body:
The web build had no printer: `spool::submit` refuses on wasm, so Print could only download a PDF. The Print dialog in the web build now offers **Browser's print dialog** (the default there), which reaches every printer the OS knows.

- `web_print`: PdfCraft draws the print-ready sheets itself, one sheet per frame (wasm has no threads). Resolution steps down with job size: 300 dpi up to 100 sheets, 200 up to 300, 150 up to 1,000. Each sheet is capped at 64 MP and each job at 1 GiB. The sheets print from a hidden iframe with margin 0.
- Chromium ignores per-page paper sizes, so a sheet that is the paper turned sideways is rotated 90° onto it, as printer drivers do.
- Copies, two-sided and colour are greyed out because the browser's dialog sets them. If `print()` is refused, the print-ready PDF downloads instead and the notice says why.

title: M5: Insert text snaps its caret to the text (#345)
author: diegozpy
body:
Part of #345: **Insert text** placed its caret wherever the pointer was, with a fixed 8 pt box, so the proposal often pointed between two lines or inside a letter. It now snaps to the text, as a proofreader's caret does.

**Behaviour**
- On upright horizontal text, the caret's tip goes to the nearer edge of the character under (or next to) the click, on the line's baseline, and the caret is half the text's em size.
- Away from text, and on turned, sloped or vertical text, nothing changes: the caret stays at the click with its 8-unit box.
- On rotated pages (`/Rotate` 90/180/270) it doesn't snap either: the caret appearance is drawn upright in user space, so it would lie on its side next to the displayed text.
- A ligature is one glyph, so the caret goes before or after it, never inside.

**How**
- `caret_snap` (view space) reuses `PageText::nearest`, the same lookup text selection uses, and takes the baseline from the glyph's em-box quad (0.2 em above its bottom edge, as `pdfcraft_render` builds it).
- `snapped_caret` maps the tip and the caret size into user space through `PageInfo::view_to_user`, so `/UserUnit` pages get a caret of the same size relative to their text.
- `ComposerKind::Caret` carries the caret's size; `CARET_SIZE` keeps the old default.

**Tests**
- Unit: snapping to either edge and past the last character; no snap away from text, with no text, or on vertical, upside-down and sloped glyphs; user-space mapping on an unrotated page, on a `/UserUnit 2` page, and no snap on `/Rotate` 90/180/270.
- UI (`egui_kittest`): a real click in "The quick brown fox" lands between "r" and "o" on the baseline, 7 pt tall; a click away from the text keeps the default caret.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib comments::` and `--test comments`, and `cargo xtask parity` pass. I didn't run the full workspace suite locally.

title: M12: say when a form's scripts were turned off
author: arcanii
body:
The follow-up that #1081 mentioned: when a form's scripts do get turned off, the user is now told.

## What was wrong

When an XFA script runs past its time limit it is abandoned, and the form's scripts are turned off for the document. The user isn't told. `handle_js` sends script errors to the JavaScript console and nowhere else; only a script's own alerts become a notice. So the form's calculations and buttons just stop working, and the notice bar goes on reading "Dynamic XFA form laid out from its template…".

## What changed

- **The engine reports it.** `Document::xfa_scripts_off()` is set where `ran_away` is handled, on open and on an edit, so a viewer can show the state without matching error text. `doc_info` reports it to agents as `xfa_scripts_off`.
- **The app says so.** When it happens, at open or after a click, a toast says so once, and the notice bar says so from then on, ahead of its other notices, with a **JavaScript Console** button:

  > This form's scripts are turned off because one ran too long. Reopen the document to run them again.

  A notice bar the user had closed comes back for it; closed again, it stays closed. A message box of the form's own still takes the toast, as before.
- **The sentence is in 17 of the 20 catalogs,** the 15 with a coverage test among them, with their hashes in `ATTRIBUTION.toml`; Greek, Polish and Telugu show it in English. The button uses the "JavaScript Console" entry that was already there. The translations are mine and unreviewed.
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml` (`form.xfa-dynamic`) and the `ROADMAP.md` progress log are updated.

The bar itself is #832's `notice_bar`; this adds one button to it.

title: control: close the connection on malformed input before auth
author: SteamSmith
body:
## Summary

`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` documents for `serve`: *"The first request on a connection must be `{"method": "auth", …}`; anything else closes the connection."* A wrong token or a non-`auth` request does close it, but a first line that isn't valid JSON got a `-32700` parse error and the connection stayed open.

title: M14: tune Windows low-DPI JetBrains Mono hinting
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Review direction: correctness of the targeted change

**Review this PR for a low-DPI raster improvement in embedded JetBrains Mono on Windows, with logical layout and font behavior preserved.** The primary acceptance evidence is the raster comparison, the 384 matching layout signatures, unchanged glyph coverage, and the narrowly scoped Windows policy below. Timing and RSS are sanity observations only; they are not correctness evidence and do not support a performance-improvement claim. The raster probe ran on macOS with the Windows policy injected, so it does not establish native Windows output.

## Summary

This changes the embedded JetBrains Mono smooth-hinting policy on Windows by setting **symmetric_rendering** to **false**. In the fixed corpus, the low-DPI edge-contrast proxy increased at 100%, 125%, and 150% scaling; at 200% it decreased slightly. Inter raster output was pixel-identical. Logical layout signatures, glyph coverage, fallback behavior, and atlas dimensions stayed the same.

## Problem and root cause

The UI uses egui 0.36.2 smooth hinting for its embedded fonts. Symmetric rendering can soften small monospace stem edges at low pixel density. The change targets that raster tradeoff for JetBrains Mono while retaining its font data and all layout inputs. The measurement is distinct from renderer or texture-atlas corruption and from missing-glyph fallback behavior.

## Fix and invariants

The Windows font policy changes only the **symmetric_rendering** field for the embedded JetBrains Mono primary font. Other primary-font settings and all fallback font tweaks remain unchanged.

The following invariants are part of the acceptance criteria:

- The primary-font order, embedded font bytes, fallback order, glyph coverage, and logical text layout remain unchanged.
- Font sizes, fallback scaling, gamma, colors, and subpixel binning remain unchanged.

title: Reading colours: replace document colours for reading comfort (#897)
author: edurbs
body:
Closes #897 (duplicate of #488: night reading for eye comfort).

## What this adds

Acrobat-parity **Replace Document Colors** (Preferences ▸ Accessibility ▸ *Reading colours*), an app-wide preference:

- **Off** (default), four **high-contrast presets** (black on white, white on black, yellow on black, green on black), and **custom** text + page-background colours with Acrobat's two refinements — *only change the colour of black text or line art* (luminance ≤ 10%, our threshold; Acrobat's is unobserved) and *change the colour of line art as well as text*.
- Solid fill/stroke colours of text and vector line art — including stencil image masks — are remapped by luminance (`lerp(text, background, luminance)`) inside the vendored interpreter; photos, shadings and tiling patterns are never touched. The page clear colour becomes the chosen background.
- **Display only**: printing, export, print previews and view snapshots render with true colours; the document never changes.
- The preference is seeded into every document as it opens (file opens, revisions, signed versions, created documents) and applies to all open documents when changed.
- Headless: the `view_reading_colors` tool drives the same engine state, so `page_render` output matches the UI. Parity entry `a11y.replace-page-colors` is `shipped` with evidence.

## How

- `vendor/hayro`: a `ColorReplacement` setting on `RenderSettings`, applied in the solid-paint paths (`fill_path`/`stroke_path` with an `is_text` flag, plus the stencil-mask bake). Coexists with the new upstream low-detail `preview` mode.
- `pdfcraft-render`: `ReadingColors` (serde, presets, `parse`/echo helpers) flowing through `RenderConfig`.

title: M14: edits let go of the previous working file before writing the next (gap 13)
author: rp6186030
body:
## What

Every edit writes a new working file: the original plus one appended revision. The previous one

so a large file peaked at three copies after a few edits.

Each refresh path (full, comments/form, content, undo, redo, after save) now releases them first.
The working and display bytes fall back to the original (already held by the editor), and the

title: Fix viewport jitter when annotating with search active (#1254)
author: omarelders
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1254.

When an annotation was added or edited (e.g. using the Draw or Highlight tools) while a search was active:
1. `page_changed` cleared matches on the page and reset `f.current` to `None`.
2. Once the page text background reload completed, `receive_result` called `refresh_find_page`.
3. Because `f.current` was `None`, `refresh_find_page` called `flash_match()`, which set `self.goto = Some((page, frac))`.
4. As a result, the canvas viewport jumped to the match after every drawn stroke or annotation, causing jarring display jitter.

### Changes
- In `page_changed`, preserve search state rather than wiping `f.matches` and resetting `f.current = None`.
- In `refresh_find_page`, gate `flash_match` so it only fires when `current_key.is_none()` (e.g. on a freshly initiated query before any match has been chosen), preventing viewport jumps during background text reloads.
- In `receive_result`, cleanly prune matches and adjust `f.current` if a page text extraction fails.
- Added regression test `marking_while_searching_does_not_jitter_or_reset_search_state` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs`.

title: Refine search match selection and text failure jitter handling
author: omarelders
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1283 (fixing #1254).

While PR #1283 stopped `page_changed` from prematurely clearing matches and resetting `f.current` on single-page edits, two related search selection and reload edge cases remained:

1. **`DocView::rerun_find` viewport jump**: `rerun_find` iterated `self.texts.keys()` in arbitrary hashmap order calling `refresh_find_page(p)`. If the user was viewing later pages (e.g. page 3) and edited the search query or options, `f.current` was picked from page 0 first, jumping the viewport away from the user's active page.
   - **Fix**: Collect and sort all matches across known pages, select the first match at or after `self.current` (or index 0), and call `self.flash_match()` exactly once.
2. **Page text extraction failure recovery**: In `receive_result`, when page text extraction fails (`r.text == None`), if the active match was on that page, `f.current` was left as `None`. Subsequent page text reloads or search updates would see `current_key.is_none()` and call `flash_match()`, triggering display jitter.
   - **Fix**: Fall back to the next valid match on or after `self.current` without calling `flash_match()`.
3. **Tests**:
   - Added unit test `page_text_failure_preserves_valid_search_match_without_jitter` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`.
   - Expanded regression test `marking_while_searching_does_not_jitter_or_reset_search_state` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs` to verify viewed-page match selection on `rerun_find` and continuous rapid drawing across multiple pages with active search.

title: xtask: stop headless Chrome leaving macOS code-sign clones (#1196)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1196.

On macOS every Chrome/Edge launch makes a code-sign clone of the app under `/private/var/folders/...`, and a browser that is killed instead of exiting cleanly never removes it. `xtask/src/demo_pdf/chrome.rs` killed Chrome with SIGKILL as soon as the PDF was complete, so each demo PDF build left one clone behind.

**Fix** (each point of the issue)

- **Launch flags.** Chrome now starts with `--disable-features=MacAppCodeSignClone` and a throwaway `--user-data-dir` (`<temp>/pdfcraft-chrome-profile-<pid>`). The arguments are built in a new `chrome_args` helper. A `TempProfile` guard removes the profile directory when it is dropped, so it is removed on success, on timeout and on error.
- **Clean shutdown.** A new `stop` helper replaces both `child.kill()` calls (complete PDF and the 120 s timeout). On Unix it sends SIGTERM (`kill -TERM <pid>`) and waits up to 5 s for Chrome to exit. Only after that does it fall back to `Child::kill` (SIGKILL). On Windows there is no SIGTERM, so it kills the process as before.
- **Regression check.** A test that counts `code_sign_clone` directories needs macOS and a real Chrome, so it is not practical in CI. The unit tests below check the flags and the profile cleanup.

The flag and the profile are passed on every platform. `MacAppCodeSignClone` is a macOS-only feature and is ignored elsewhere. A throwaway profile also keeps the build away from the user's normal Chrome profile.

`assets/demo/README.md`, which lists the Chrome flags, now mentions the new ones.

**Tests**

- `args_disable_code_sign_clone_and_use_throwaway_profile`: the argument list has `--disable-features=MacAppCodeSignClone` and `--user-data-dir=<profile>`, and the page URL is still the last argument.
- `temp_profile_is_removed_on_drop`: a profile directory with content is removed when the guard is dropped.

title: Issue #1296: hayro-syntax applies SASLprep to AES-256 passwords (PdfCraft patch 16)
author: jay-tau
body:
Fixes #1296.

ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4.3.3 (Algorithm 2.A, step a) has an AES-256 (R5/R6) password processed with SASLprep (RFC 4013) before use. `pdfcraft-crypt` does this when it writes and when `pdfcraft-cos` opens. The vendored `hayro-syntax`, which the renderer opens files with, skipped that step (`// TODO: Do the above.`). So a password that SASLprep changes was accepted by `cos` but refused by the renderer. With such an open password, Protect was rolled back ("the password is incorrect"), and a file protected with it didn't open in a `Session` by typing it. #1296 has the table: a decomposed `café`, a no-break space, full-width `ａｂ`.

## What changes
- **`hayro-syntax`, vendored patch (16).** An R5/R6 password is tried in its SASLprep form first, then, if that differs, as given. The SASLprep form is computed as `pdfcraft-crypt`'s `sasl_password` computes it: the password as given if SASLprep refuses it, UTF-8, at most 127 bytes. The code is `aes256_passwords` in `crypto/mod.rs`, modelled on patch (14)'s `legacy_passwords` for R2–R4, and it resolves the upstream TODO. Upstream hayro 0.8.0 still has that TODO.
- **Why the as-given fallback.** Trying the password as given second keeps files written by tools that skip SASLprep opening in the renderer, as they did before.
- **Dependency.** `stringprep` is an optional dependency enabled by the crate's `std` feature, because stringprep needs `std`. Without `std`, passwords are used as given, as before. It's already in the tree through `pdfcraft-crypt`, so the root `Cargo.lock` only gains one dependency line and no new packages. As with patch (11) in `hayro-interpret`, the normalized `Cargo.toml` is edited, not `Cargo.toml.orig` or the vendored `Cargo.lock`.
- **`vendor/README.md`.** Patch (16) and its tests are added to the hayro-syntax row that holds patch (14).

## Unchanged
- Passwords that SASLprep leaves as they are, such as precomposed `café`, and everything else in the renderer.
- `pdfcraft-cos` (through `pdfcraft-c…

Case-insensitive Find lowercases capital sigma to `σ` but leaves word-final `ς` unchanged. On a page containing `κόσμος ΚΌΣΜΟΣ`, either query therefore finds only its own spelling instead of both occurrences.

title: XFA: one script thread per event, and the live form kept up to date in place
author: ysrdevs
body:
## XFA: one script thread per event, and the live form kept up to date in place

Follow-up to #230, #301 and #1175. Both reviews of the earlier XFA PRs flagged the same cost: a form with a few hundred calculate scripts hit the open-time budget and the rest were skipped with a report. Two things caused it: every script got a thread of its own, and the engine dropped its live form after every value a script settled, so the whole tree was rebuilt for the next script.

### What changes

* **`pdfcraft_js::xfa_session::XfaSession`** (new): the scripts of one event run on one thread (with the script stack), each in a fresh JavaScript context or FormCalc interpreter on a copy of the form as the engine holds it then. Scripts share nothing: not variables, not globals, not prototype changes, not objects kept from an earlier script; a script that fails halfway leaves nothing behind; what a script changed reaches the next one only through the engine, which applies the effects (with its normalisation: saved values for choice lists, template defaults, refused writes to buttons) and sends the form as it then is. A script past its time limit is abandoned on the thread and the session is dead from then on, as before; a fault in the engine (a panic) now loses only that script, and the thread is replaced for the next one. On wasm, where there are no threads, scripts run inline.
* **Engine runner**: one session per event. For a value a script settles (a calculate's result, a field it set), the one field in the live form is refreshed in place with the new `pdfcraft_xfa::refresh_value`, which computes the value exactly as the tree builder does (the data's value as saved, else the template default; radio buttons and anything the template doesn't have fall back to a rebuild). Rows added or removed, presence and access changes, resets, relayouts and data rewrites still rebuild the tree.
* **Correctness check under test**: before every script and at the end of every event, the engine's unit t…

title: M2: fix missing Chinese glyphs in non-embedded CID fonts
author: nevicia2010-hub
body:
Maintenance status (2026-10-23): this PR is retained while the shared Chinese font integration is clarified. Main now allows OFL CJK typefaces, but `crates/fonts/build.rs` excludes non-whitelisted CJK faces larger than 4 MiB. title: M1: repair exhausted xref hints without object-number overflow (#1337)

title: M3: select an image on the page and copy it
author: FrancescoClemeno
body:
Adds Copy Image. Replaces #1068, this time without the fork-specific files (update source, fork workflows, fork docs), on top of current main.

## What it does
- **Select tool:** a click on a raster image selects it (blue highlight). That includes an image drawn through Form artwork (Word, InDesign, scanners) and one with text over it (OCR layers, captions). Dragging or double-clicking still selects text, and Esc deselects. ⌘C copies the image to the clipboard as a **file in its original format**: a JPEG exactly as stored in the PDF, otherwise a lossless PNG with transparency.

title: Preferences: draw Chinese and Japanese language names in every interface language
author: aksoyutku
body:
## Problem
In Preferences → Interface language, 日本語, 简体中文 and 繁體中文 show as boxes in every non-Chinese interface (English, Turkish, …). This happens in builds without a craft-fonts Chinese face, which includes every release so far (#826). The only system font loaded in those interfaces is Segoe UI, Tahoma or Arial, and none of them have Chinese or Japanese characters. The system Chinese font was loaded only when the interface itself was Chinese.

## Fix
When the interface isn't Chinese and the build has no Chinese face, `installed_font_definitions` now also loads the Chinese font installed on the machine (the same `system_fonts::fallback(Need::Hans)` the Chinese interface uses: Microsoft YaHei, PingFang, WenQuanYi, …). It is added as a new `SYSTEM_HAN_FALLBACK` face at the very end of every font family, after the existing system fallback, so it only draws characters no other face has. This is the runtime system-font use AGENTS.md §1.4 already allows. Nothing is embedded or shipped, and `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0` still leaves it out.

## Tests
- New `cjk_language_names_draw_in_every_interface_language` in `tests/fonts.rs`. It checks the CJK language names have glyphs in every interface language and family, and that the new face sits last, appears once, and is never added in a Chinese interface. Before the fix it failed with `en interface: 日本語 lacks 日本語`. It skips when the machine has no Chinese font.
- Relaxed two existing tests that assumed `SYSTEM_FALLBACK` is always last.

- This puts a system Chinese font (about 19 MB for YaHei) in memory in non-Chinese interfaces, the same cost the Chinese interface already pays. If you'd rather load it only when the language picker opens, I can change that.

title: M7: preserve Arabic text order in copy, search and editing
author: YouseifUS

title: M14: first-page thumbnails of PDFs in Windows File Explorer
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## What

PDFs in Windows File Explorer show their **first page as a thumbnail** while PdfCraft is the default PDF app. Today they show only the document icon (see #308 for the icon itself). Windows has no PDF thumbnailer of its own, so once PdfCraft is the default, thumbnails come from nowhere. Acrobat's thumbnailer is off by default, and in our tests it didn't work for files whose type is `PdfCraft.Document`.

## How

- **New crate `pdfcraft-thumbnails` (L7)**
  - `render_thumbnail(bytes, side)` renders page 1 fitted into a `side`×`side` square, onto white, as top-down BGRA. It works on every platform and never panics: `catch_unwind`, and errors for unreadable, password-protected or empty files.
  - **On Windows** the crate also builds as `pdfcraft_thumbnails.dll`, an in-process COM server. Its class implements `IInitializeWithStream` and `IThumbnailProvider`, and it exports `DllGetClassObject` and `DllCanUnloadNow`.
  - Explorer runs it in its isolated thumbnail process (it is not registered with `DisableProcessIsolation`). Any failure returns `WTS_E_FAILEDEXTRACTION`, so Explorer keeps showing the icon. Files larger than 1 GiB are skipped.
- **`PageRenderer::page_size()`** lets the page be fitted without a full `inspect`.
- **MSI**
  - Installs the DLL and registers the CLSID (`InprocServer32`, `ThreadingModel=Apartment`).
  - Registers it as the thumbnail handler under **`PdfCraft.Document\ShellEx` only**. It never touches `.pdf` itself, so another default PDF app's thumbnails stay as they are, in line with "never forced as the default".
  - `package.ps1` builds the DLL, checks its PE machine type and signs it.
  - `test-msi.ps1` checks the registration rows and that nothing is written under `.pdf\ShellEx`.
  - The portable zip doesn't include the DLL, because nothing would register it there.
- **Parity:** the `misc.installers` note no longer says "first-page thumbnails remain unsupported".

## ⚠️ The one exception: `unsafe`

An Explorer thumbnail handler has to…

title: fix(xfdf): text data from a one-field form keeps its commas (#1321)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1321.

The tab-delimited export of a form with one field is `Name\nHello, world\n`, with no tab in it. On import, `import_table` looks for a tab in the header line, finds none and parses the file as CSV. That splits the value at the comma and keeps only `Hello`, with nothing reported as rejected.

I changed the import side, so text files people already exported read correctly. CSV always quotes a value that contains a comma, so a header with a single name followed by several unquoted cells can't be CSV: that case is now read as tab-delimited text. The existing tab branch moved into `tab_delimited()` so both places share it. Well-formed CSV (several columns, a quoted one-column value, values spanning lines) reads as before.

Tests in `crates/xfdf/src/tests.rs`:
- `one_field_text_data_keeps_its_commas` (the issue's test, plus a value with quotes) fails on main with `["Hello"]` and passes here.
- `one_column_csv_still_reads_its_quotes` guards the CSV side. It fails if the fix is instead made as "no comma in the header means text".
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

One ambiguity is left: one-column text whose whole value is wrapped in balanced quotes (`"a, b"`) still reads as CSV. Without the file extension the two can't be told apart.

title: CLI: audit rejects unknown options before reading the file (fixes #1332)
author: umesh429
body:
Fixes #1332.

## What

`pdfcraft-cli audit` never validated its options, so a misspelled long option was silently skipped (along with its value) and the command went straight to reading the file:

```
$ pdfcraft-cli audit missing.pdf --passwrod x
pdfcraft-cli: missing.pdf: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

Audit now calls `validate_options` with an `AUDIT_OPTIONS` list (`--password`), the same way `info` does:

```
$ pdfcraft-cli audit missing.pdf --passwrod x
pdfcraft-cli: audit: unknown option --passwrod
```

`--password` is still accepted, and `audit --help` / `audit -h` still print help.

## Tests

- Added two audit cases (`--passwrod x`, `--nonsense 1`) to `apps/pdfcraft-cli/tests/options.rs`. Both failed before the change and pass after.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` on macOS: 2,732 passed, 1 failed, 13 ignored. The one failure, `tab_context::ui_tests::inactive_tab_menu_closes_target_and_disables_unavailable_actions` (ui-egui), also fails on `main` without this change, so it is unrelated.

title: fix(preflight): find colour operators after any PDF whitespace (#1334)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1334.

The PDF/A device-colour scan in `uses_device_colour` split content streams only on space and LF. With CR, TAB, FF or NUL between the tokens, `0 0 0 1 k` was never seen, so `verify` missed the DeviceCMYK and `convert` gave the CMYK page an sRGB output intent.

It now splits on all six PDF whitespace characters, using the lexer's own `is_whitespace`. To do that I made it `pub` and re-exported it from `pdfcraft-cos`, rather than adding another copy of the list (there are already private ones in `content` and `optimize`). If you'd rather keep cos's API as it is, I can switch to a local copy.

Validation:
- `device_colour_is_found_after_any_whitespace` tries each separator. It also has gray and RGB controls that must still get the sRGB intent, so a fix that blocks every output intent doesn't pass. It fails on main at CR and passes here.
- `convert_does_not_give_cmyk_documents_an_srgb_output_intent` and `verify_reports_an_output_intent_that_does_not_match_device_colour` stay green.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-preflight -p pdfcraft-cos` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(sign): a signature field with a null /V can be signed by name (#1328)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1328.

The signature list counts a field as signed only when its `/V` resolves to a dictionary. Signing an existing field, though, refused any field that merely had a `/V` key. A field with `/V null`, or `/V` pointing at a null object, was listed as unsigned and then refused with "the field is already signed". Both places now use one predicate, `Field::signature`.

- A field with a signature dictionary is still refused.
- A field without `/V` signs as before (`signing_an_existing_field_and_counter_signing`).

Validation:
- `a_field_with_a_null_value_is_unsigned_and_can_be_signed` (direct and indirect null) fails on main and passes here.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

A non-null `/V` that isn't a dictionary (for example `/V ()`) is now treated as unsigned too, and is overwritten on signing. The issue allows either that or an error. Happy to switch to an error if you prefer.

title: fix(redact): removing comments keeps non-comment annotations (#1325)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1325.

`is_comment` in `redact/src/sanitize.rs` treated every annotation except Link, Widget, Popup, FileAttachment and Redact as a comment. So a Comments-only cleanup also counted and deleted Watermark, PrinterMark, TrapNet, Screen, Movie, RichMedia and 3D annotations. It now uses `pdfcraft_annot::is_comment_subtype`, which the comments list already relies on, and still leaves out file attachments (removed with Attachments) and redaction marks.

Validation:
- `removing_comments_keeps_annotations_that_are_not_comments` builds a page with a Square plus each of those types. The scan must count 1 and the removal must report `[(Comments, 1)]`, and after save and reopen the 8 non-comments must remain. On main 8 are counted and removed.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(print): refuse huge posters at the sheet limit instead of overflowing (#1335)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1335.

At a huge poster scale both tile counts saturate at `usize::MAX`, and `nx * ny` overflowed in the 1024-sheet check. With overflow checks that's a panic. Without them the product wraps to 1 and the sheet loops run. The headless `doc_print` tool accepts any finite positive scale, so a script can reach this. The check now uses `checked_mul` and treats an overflow as over the limit, so the request gets the existing "more than 1024 sheets" error.

Validation:
- `huge_posters_are_refused_at_the_sheet_limit` (scale 1e5, 1e22, `f64::MAX`) panics on main and passes here, also with overflow checks off.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-print` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: M2: snap shrunk interpolated images to whole pixels so scans stay sharp
author: philip-tam
body:
## What

A scanned page (one 300 dpi image with `/Interpolate true`) looked soft next to Acrobat at fit-to-window zooms. Related to the blurry-rendering reports (#730).

## Why

`draw_image` shrank the image to a ceil-sized raster (e.g. 794x1123 for a page that is 794x1122.5 device pixels) and then sampled that raster a second time through the bilinear image sampler at a fractional scale and offset. That second pass blended every edge.

## Fix

For an axis-aligned, interpolated, shrunk image (not a Type 3 glyph), the device rectangle is snapped to whole pixels. The image is shrunk once, to exactly that size, and drawn 1:1 at the rounded corner (`snap_minified_image` in `vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`). Rotated, skewed, flipped, Type 3 and non-interpolated images take the old path. The snapped size must stay within one pixel of the planned size, so the existing memory-budget checks still hold.

## Measured

On a synthetic single-image scan page (A4, 2480x3508 gray, `/Interpolate true`; text, rules and barcode-like bars), mean absolute error against an area-average (box) downscale:

| dpi | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 96 | 3.40 | 1.57 |
| 144 | 2.98 | 1.47 |

Edge sharpness (mean gradient) at 96 dpi: reference 17.0, before 15.3, after 16.6.

## Tests

- New `raster::tests::interpolated_minified_image_edges_snap_to_whole_pixels` (fails without the fix, passes with it).
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: everything passes except two tests that also fail on unmodified `main` on my machine (macOS, aarch64): `pdfcraft-engine` `tests::recognize_text_makes_a_scanned_page_searchable` and `pdfcraft-ui-egui` `tab_context::ui_tests::inactive_tab_menu_closes_target_and_disables_unavailable_actions`.
- Checked in the packaged macOS app only through the CLI renders above, not against Acrobat side by side with a corpus file.

title: Edit text: support per-font visual-order Indic text and nukta reordering
author: krinry
body:
This is the follow-up addressing @echelon's review on #1033 regarding Indic pre-base vowel reordering and decomposed nuktas:

### Summary of Changes
1. **Per-Font `visual_order` Flag (`Metrics.visual_order`)**:
   - `pdfcraft-fonts` now detects fonts requiring visual display order:
     - Legacy font family names (`kruti`, `devlys`, `chanakya`, etc.)
     - Embedded fonts covering Indic scripts (`0x0900..=0x0D7F`) that lack OpenType `GSUB` contextual substitution tables (`!has_gsub`).
   - Standard modern fonts with OpenType GSUB remain `visual_order = false`, ensuring logical-order text is never modified or inadvertently corrupted.

2. **Nukta-Aware Cluster Reordering (`crates/edit/src/indic.rs`)**:
   - Pre-base vowel signs (such as Devanagari short 'i' `\u{093F}`, Bengali `\u{09BF}`, etc.) are swapped across complete consonant clusters, including base consonants with decomposed nuktas (`C + NUKTA`, e.g., `\u{0921}\u{093C}\u{093F}`, `\u{0922}\u{093C}\u{093F}`) or precomposed nuktas, as well as conjuncts.
   - Implemented both `to_logical` (for reading stream text in visual order into editing logical order) and `to_visual` (for writing edits back to legacy visual-order fonts).

3. **Gated Integration in Edit Path (`crates/edit/src/text.rs`)**:
   - Pre-base vowel reordering is now gated on `line.visual_order`:
     - Text extraction (`text_lines`, `reading_lines`) applies `to_logical` only if `line.visual_order` is true.
     - Line replacement (`replace_line_with_limit`) and paragraph rewriting (`rewrite_block_with_limit`) write text in visual order only when the font has `visual_order == true`.
     - Modern logical-order fonts and documents are left completely untouched.

4. **Tests**:

title: Issue #1368: keep text a dragged paragraph passed over
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Fixes #1368 and #1316.

## Problem
In Edit text & images dragging text box A across text box B and then into empty space deleted B. The text wasn't just hidden what happens here is B's operators were removed from the page's content stream, so it was still missing after save and reopen.

## Cause
Each drag is applied as its own `EditTextBlock` edit when the mouse is released. When a paragraph is rewritten, `rewrite_block` also removes whatever `coincident_ops` returns. That function is there to clear duplicate copies of a line (fake bold, repeated layers), but it decided purely by overlap, furthermore any line covering more than half of the paragraph's box counted as a copy. After A was dropped on B the next drag found B under A, treated it as a copy of A and deleted it.

`replace_line`, `clear_block` and `rewrite_styled_block` use the same function. That is why #1316 happens where a distinct line close enough to overlap is removed when the line next to it is edited.

## Fix
A copy now also has to show the same text (`l.text.trim() == member.text.trim()`). The overlap check is unchanged. `coincident_ops` takes the paragraph's lines instead of only their boxes and the callers already had those lines.

## Tests
- New: `a_paragraph_dragged_across_another_leaves_it_alone`. It moves Alpha onto Bravo, moves it away, reopens, and checks both lines exist. It fails before the fix and passes after.
- Existing: `a_line_drawn_twice_is_replaced_everywhere` (fake bold and repeated copies) still passes.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass. With clippy 1.96, `nonminimal_bool` flags `crates/edit/src/added.rs:938`; that code is already on `main` and this PR doesn't touch it.

## A Known limit which was found
Dragging a box onto another box with exactly the same text and then away still removes the second box. From the page content alone that can't be told apart from fake bold.

title: fix(fonts): a composite /W run past the last CID stops there (#1313)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1313.

In a composite font's `/W` array, a `c [w1 w2 …]` run computed each CID as `c0 + k` without checking. With `c0 = 4294967295` the second width overflowed: a panic with overflow checks, otherwise a wrap that gave CID 0 that width. The run now stops at the last representable CID (`checked_add`), so the widths that fit are kept and the rest are dropped. `/W [0 [100 200]]` reads as before.

Validation:
- `pdf::tests::composite_width_run_past_the_last_cid_is_dropped` panics on main ("attempt to add with overflow"). With `wrapping_add` instead of the fix it fails on CID 0's width, so it catches the silent wrap too.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(ui): the Fields panel lists a field on a missing page as unplaced (#1307)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1307.

The Fields panel grouped fields by page with `info.pages[p]`. A widget whose `/P` points past the document (the issue's file has `/P 99` on a one-page PDF) panicked the UI with "index out of bounds". The panel now uses `info.pages.get(p)`, so such a field is listed under the existing "Unplaced" heading. No new strings.

Validation:
- `forms::the_fields_panel_lists_a_field_on_a_missing_page_as_unplaced` (kittest, built on the issue's fixture) panics on main at `panels.rs:1241` and passes here. It checks the "Unplaced" heading and a single "orphan" row.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(automation): content_update refuses text styling on an image (#1331)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1331.

`content_update` on an image accepted `font`, `size`, `bold`, `italic`, `color` and `align` and silently ignored them. It still reported success, marked the document dirty and pushed an undo step. The Text branch already refuses image-only arguments (`rotate`, `flip_h`, …). The Image branch now refuses text styling the same way, with `bad(...)`, before anything is edited.

Validation:
- `text_styling_on_an_image_is_refused_without_an_edit` tries each of the six keys, with and without `rect`. Each must give `InvalidArgs`, and content, `dirty`, `edit_generation`, `can_undo` and `can_redo` must stay as they were. The fixture is checked to start clean and with a redo step, so those checks mean something. Styling on text is still accepted. On main the image call succeeds.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(forms): a whole look keeps the rest of an indirect /MK (#1322)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1322.

When `set_props` applied a whole look, it read the widget's `/MK` with `as_dict()` without resolving it. For an indirect `/MK` that found nothing, so the new look started from an empty dictionary and lost the caption, rotation and any other keys. `/MK` is now resolved first, the way the `check_style` branch below already does ("Resolved first: an indirect /MK keeps its colours"). The updated `/MK` is written directly on the widget; the issue notes that keeping the indirect reference isn't required.

Validation:
- `tests::a_whole_look_keeps_the_rest_of_an_indirect_mk` checks the result after save and reopen: Cross, rotation 90, the vendor key, and the new BC/BG. The issue's test asserted the current loss; this one asserts the fix. On main it gets `(Check, 0)` instead of `(Cross, 90)`.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(forms): a literal Off value reads as Off outside buttons (#1320)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1320.

`values_of` dropped the string `Off` for every field type, because `Off` is a button's "unchecked" state. So a text, combo or list field whose value really was "Off" read as empty and exported as empty. `values_of` now takes the field kind and drops `Off` only for check boxes and radio buttons.

Validation:
- `tests::a_literal_off_value_reads_as_off_outside_buttons` checks after save and reopen that text, combo and single-choice list fields read `["Off"]` and an unchecked box still reads empty. The issue's test asserted the current behaviour; this one asserts the fix. On main it gets `[]` for the text field. Removing the filter entirely fails the check-box case, so a too-broad fix is caught.
- I also checked by hand that CSV, XML, XFDF and FDF export the value as `Off`.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-xfdf -p pdfcraft-automation` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

#1128 also touches `forms/src/lib.rs`, but not `values_of`.

title: fix(fonts): a /Differences code past 255 no longer encodes as its last byte (#1314)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1314.

A simple font's `/Differences` can name codes past 255 (e.g. `300 /Euro`). Encoding then looked the glyph up, found code 300 and wrote it as one byte, `0x2C`, a comma. The comment above the table already says out-of-range codes map nothing a simple font can show. `has_glyph` now says that for codes over `0xFF`, so `encode("€")` returns `None`, one of the outcomes the issue accepts.

I didn't drop those codes from the table as the issue suggests: `malformed_cmaps_never_panic` expects an out-of-range code to stay in the decode map (`text(u32::MAX) == Some("B")`). So decoding is unchanged.

Validation:
- `pdf::tests::differences_codes_past_one_byte_are_not_encoded` gets `Some([44])` on main and `None` here. A control checks that code 200 still encodes as `0xC8` and decodes back to "€".
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: M10: edit OCR text on scanned pages so the change shows
author: TanguAchilis
body:
Editing recognised text on a scanned page did nothing visible. After Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text, Edit text & images rewrote the word as invisible OCR text (rendering mode 3), so the page still showed the scanned word. On a form, the whole OCR layer was also grouped into one paragraph that rewrapped when a single word changed.

## What changes

- **Edits show.** Rewriting an invisible paragraph draws the new text visibly. It first covers the old words with the paper colour sampled around them, and draws the text in the scan's sampled ink colour (or the colour chosen). The paragraph's `q`/`Q` restores the invisible mode for the OCR words after it.
- **OCR words group like the page.** Words join only across a word space. A table cell, a tab stop and each scanned line stay apart, and an edited phrase grows rightwards instead of wrapping onto the line below.
- **Word widths are kept.** Styled rewrites now measure with the text matrix's horizontal scale. OCR words are stretched to fit the scan, and the vertical scale was applied twice, so rewritten words overlapped.
- **OCR text is as tall as the scanned word.** The text layer assumed every word box spans Helvetica's ascender-descender height. A capitals-only word such as "DT" spans only the cap height, so its text was about 23% too small, with the baseline too high. Size and baseline now come from the word's letters.
- **Editor.** While typing, the inline editor covers the scanned word and grows like the result.

`BlockStyle` gains `cover`, and `TextBlock` gains `invisible`. The engine fills in the cover and ink colours for an invisible paragraph unless the caller set them.

## Testing

- New engine tests on synthetic scans in `crates/engine/tests/ocr_edit.rs`: cover and ink colour, explicit colour, phrase grouping, rightward growth, word widths.
- New OCR placement test in `crates/ocr`. New kittest UI test: an OCR word opens for editing and stays open when the pointer leaves.
- `pdfcraft-edit`, `pdfcraft-ocr` and `pdfc…

title: fix(cli): edit refuses move/insert destinations past the end (#1330)
author: umesh429
body:
Fixes #1330.

`pdfcraft-cli edit --insert-blank N` and `--move PAGES:N` accepted any N and quietly appended the page when N was past the end. They now check N against the page count at the point each edit runs (1..=n+1, the same rule `page_insert_blank` / `page_move` use) and fail before writing anything:


- n+1 still appends, and a later edit can target a position that an earlier `--insert-blank` created.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass.

title: fix(sign): refuse to sign a field whose /V is not a signature (#1328)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #1374, as suggested there (issue #1328).

After #1374, a signature field whose `/V` is null (direct or indirect) is unsigned and can be signed. A `/V` that is neither null nor a signature dictionary, though (an empty string, a number, a name, an array…), was also treated as unsigned and silently overwritten on signing. Now that case is refused with "the value of the field … is not a signature", and nothing is written. Missing or null `/V` still signs, and a real signature is still "already signed".

`list_cached` still lists such fields as unsigned, since they hold no signature. So the UI still offers "Sign this field…", and the attempt now fails with a message that says why. Marking them as invalid in the list would need a new wording and its translations; happy to do that separately if you'd like it.

Validation:
- `a_field_whose_value_is_not_a_signature_is_refused_by_name` covers an empty string, a number, a name and an array, each direct and indirect. On main it signs (`Ok(…)`).
- Dropping the null exception fails `a_field_with_a_null_value_is_unsigned_and_can_be_signed`, so both sides are pinned.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(forms): keep a whitespace-only value in a text field without a format (#1323)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1323.

`keystroke` treated any whitespace-only input as "clear the field", whatever the field's format. In a plain text field (no number/date/… format) a value of a single space or tab was therefore emptied. Whitespace-only input now clears the field only when a format applies. An empty string still clears any field.

Validation:
- `tests::whitespace_only_text_is_kept_in_a_field_without_a_format` covers a space, a tab and an NBSP, with an empty-string control.
- Two new asserts in `af::tests::numbers_format_like_acrobat` check that formatted fields still clear.
- On main the first gets `[]` instead of `[" "]`.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-xfdf` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(content): skip an inline image with an unreadable key to its EI (#1318)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1318.

When an inline image's dictionary had a key or value the parser couldn't read, `inline_image` gave up and returned `data.len()`. Everything after the `BI` was dropped (the issue's `q BI … EI Q BT … Tj ET` parsed as `[q, BI]`), and none of it was counted as skipped. Now the parser looks for the matching `EI`, counts `BI`…`EI` as skipped bytes and carries on after it. The damaged image is dropped rather than kept as a half-read `BI` that would re-serialise as a different image. Without an `EI` the behaviour is unchanged. The `EI` search moved into a small `end_of_image` helper as-is.

Validation:
- `tests::an_unreadable_inline_image_is_skipped_to_its_end` gets `[q, BI]` on main and `[q, Q, BT, Tj, ET]` here.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-content -p pdfcraft-edit` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(automation): doc_save reports a required full rewrite as not incremental (#1329)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1329.

`doc_save` reported `"incremental": !full`. But `write_incremental` falls back to a full rewrite when it has to (protection, Remove Hidden Information, rebuilt files), and the flag still said `true`. It now reports `!full && bytes.starts_with(saved_bytes)`: a save is incremental only when the output really extends the bytes it was opened from. That needs a read-only `Document::saved_bytes()` accessor in the engine. The cos writer is unchanged; the cost is one prefix comparison.

Validation:
- `an_in_place_save_reports_a_required_rewrite_as_not_incremental`: a rotate stays `true`, while `doc_protect` and `doc_remove_hidden` must report `false`. On main `doc_protect` reports `true`.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation -p pdfcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: feat(preflight): verify image resolution and bleed without rewriting the file
author: Baltsar
body:
Follows the review on #1230. This is verification only. Nothing in the file is rewritten.

`print_readiness` is a read-only headless tool. It reports:

- Effective resolution where each image is drawn, from the placement matrix. A 100 px image drawn across 144 pt is 50 ppi, not "100 px on the page". Images that only appear inside a form XObject use the existing optimizer measurement (the smallest use). Below 150 ppi is a failure. Below 300 ppi is a warning.
- The page boxes that are actually in the file (media, crop, trim, bleed). Bleed is a warning when the tightest side past the trim is under 2 mm. A missing TrimBox or BleedBox is not invented.
- Output intents. A screen profile (sRGB, Adobe RGB, display) is a warning when no press profile is declared. No ICC profile is generated, and no Adobe profile name is used.
- Fonts that are not embedded. They are reported, not embedded.
- The existing PDF/A-2b structural result. This does not claim PDF/A-1b, PDF/A-4, or PDF/X.

Out of scope, on purpose: content-stream rewriting, hairline or action fixups, stripping encryption, a press-profile conversion, a dialog, and any parity row marked shipped.

Test: `ocr::printcheck::tests::a_drawn_image_is_measured_where_it_is_placed` (50 ppi fails on the drawn size, 600 ppi does not, bleed is warned only where the boxes say so).

The branch history is noisy. The diff against main is the change, so a squash merge is the right landing.

Credit as @Baltsar is enough. I have not added a `people.toml` entry.

title: fix(render): draw Turkish Ğ İ Ş ğ ş in non-embedded fonts
author: TheLastRoadRunner
body:
## Problem

Turkish letters Ğ, İ, Ş, ğ and ş render as blanks in PDFs whose fonts aren't embedded, while ı, ç, ö and ü in the same text render fine. A real case is a letter produced by iText 2.1.7: its fonts are Times New Roman (`TimesNewRomanPSMT`, `-BoldMT`, `-ItalicMT`), not embedded, and they use `/Differences` with `/Gbreve /Idotaccent /Scedilla /gbreve /scedilla /dotlessi` over the WinAnsi codes for Ð Ý Þ ð þ ý.

## Cause

Non-embedded fonts are drawn with the standard-14 stand-ins in `vendor/hayro-interpret/assets` (PDFium's Foxit fonts, CFF). Each carries about 230 glyphs, only those of the Standard, WinAnsi and Mac Roman encodings. `dotlessi` is in StandardEncoding, so ı draws. `Gbreve`, `gbreve`, `Idotaccent`, `Scedilla` and `scedilla` aren't in the stand-ins, so `StandardKind::map_code` falls back to `.notdef` and nothing is drawn. The same happens to most Latin Extended-A letters: Polish ą ę ł ń ś ź ż, Czech č ě ň ř, Romanian ă, and so on.

## Fix (vendored hayro-interpret patch 26)

When the stand-in lacks such a letter, `StandardKind` builds it from the base letter and accent the stand-in does have, the way Type 1 `seac` composites and the standard-14 AFM composites are built:

- The accent is centred on the letter. Over capitals and letters with ascenders it is raised by the difference between the letter's top and the top of `x`. In italic stand-ins it is also moved along the slant.
- Cedillas hang below the letter, and ogoneks from its right edge.
- A composite gets a glyph id above any font's glyph count, one per character code (`COMPOSITE_GLYPH_BASE + code`). `outline_glyph` builds the outline from that code. The width comes from the standard metrics of the glyph's name, as for other stand-in glyphs.
- The table, `ACCENTED_LETTERS`, holds the Latin Extended-A letters made of one plain accent. ď ľ ť and the comma-accented letters are left out.

It adds no assets and no dependencies. Text extraction is unchanged; it already mapped these names to Unic…

title: fix(ui): Current page prints the viewed page, not a page labelled with its number (#1308)
author: marcoarnulfo

Fixes #1308.

So in a document whose labels don't match positions (e.g. i, ii, 1, 2…), Current page could print a different page that happened to be labelled with that number. title: M14: Hebrew interface language and a right-to-left interface
author: 613avi
body:
Adds Hebrew (עברית, `he`) as an interface language. Arabic and Hebrew now get a real right-to-left interface: bidirectional text layout and a mirrored layout. Before this, labels were only reordered when the catalog loaded.

## Hebrew catalog
- 2,192 entries, covering every command, All tools entry and `tl!` literal. Gender-neutral modern Hebrew, translated clean-room from the meaning of the English labels.

  - Text with no right-to-left characters skips all of this.
- **`vendor/egui`: `Style::mirror_layout`.** It mirrors rows, columns, grids and text fields. In a mirrored layout, scroll areas anchor and scroll from the right.
- **PdfCraft:**
  - Catalogs stay in logical order, and file names start with an LRM so `.pdf` stays at the end.
  - The docked Tools and Inspector panels and the rail swap sides. The saved layout is unchanged.

title: Fix Lab Bradford adaptation to use LMS white-point ratios
author: FredApps
body:
Follow-up to #1237; related to #1203. The earlier merged work fixed the reported Lab conversion and Indexed scaling, but follow-up review found that non-D65 white points still acquire a tint because Bradford LMS values are scaled using XYZ white-point ratios.

For example, D50 Lab (50, 0, 0) renders as RGB (126, 117, 118) instead of neutral (119, 119, 119).

Give Lab its own Bradford adaptation using both white points transformed to LMS. Preserve CalRGB's existing flat-white/black-point pipeline and the merged Lab Indexed/Range scaling. Zero or non-finite source cone responses fall back to unadapted XYZ.

Six render regressions cover independent D50/equal-energy neutral and chromatic oracles, D65 identity, direct/Indexed consistency, an asymmetric chromatic Range, and zero/overflowing-cone fallback. The original four regressions produce three failures on base while D65 passes; all six pass with this change. A separate f64 implementation supplies frozen expectations, and external Poppler agrees with all 16 ordinary/asymmetric reference patches. Independent read-only review found no blocking issues.

Validation after a normal merge of upstream 87b448b (commit 1c8b2b0), exact tree 0375169cbc6ebd6aee36b8dc238026b8f0d2f768:
- All 262 render tests pass; workspace: 2,852 passed, 13 ignored, no failures.
- Formatting, strict workspace/all-target Clippy, layers, Wasm (31 crates), assets, and parity pass. The local cargo-deny gate skips because cargo-deny is not installed; no dependencies change.
- Workspace tests use `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=1` with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=2`, keeping parent suites serial while a CUPS child stand-in retains its normal output format. Standard runner attempts exposed an unrelated forms timing failure and that child-harness formatting issue; isolated forms and the complete final workspace run pass.
- Rebuilt CLI `doc_open`/`page_render` matches all six ordinary, asymmetric, and fallback pixel controls.

title: fix(content): count an unreadable inline image with no EI as skipped (#1318)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #1404, as suggested there (issue #1318).

When an inline image's parameters can't be read and there is no `EI` after them, `inline_image` still returned the image as a `BI` op with whatever parameters it had read and no data, running to the end of the stream, so those bytes were dropped without being counted. It now returns `Err(data.len())`, so `parse` skips the image and counts `BI` to the end of the stream in `skipped`, the same as #1404 does when an `EI` is found. A stream that ends inside the parameters (`BI /W 1`) has nothing unreadable in it and still gives a `BI` op, and a readable image whose data is cut short keeps its data, as before.

Validation:
- New test `an_unreadable_inline_image_without_ei_is_counted`: fails on main (a `BI` op, `skipped` 0), passes with the fix
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-content --lib`, plus the inline-image tests in `pdfcraft-redact` and the content tests in `pdfcraft-edit`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-content --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

title: M4: Fix Combine duplicate warnings and cache their computation
author: LabDennis
body:
Combine files used to warn that different PDFs had been added twice whenever their names and byte lengths matched. Both Grid and List now require matching bytes as well. Actual duplicate additions still warn, and split parts of a single source remain exempt.

Both views use one duplicate check, cached against the existing list revision. Candidate grouping by name and length avoids reading unrelated file contents; exact byte-slice keys distinguish candidates without relying on hash uniqueness. Adding, removing, rearranging, undoing and redoing list entries invalidate the result through the existing revision mechanism. Closing the tab clears it.

This also removes List view's all-pairs scan on every redraw. An isolated optimized microbenchmark with 1,000 differently named files measured approximately 2.27 ms per call for the previous scan, 0.17 ms to rebuild the new result, and 0.01 microseconds to reuse it on an unchanged frame. These are helper timings, not whole-application frame-time measurements; reading same-name/same-size candidates on a changed list still costs time proportional to their contents.

Two UI regressions failed before the fix and now check distinct contents, genuine duplicates, undo and redo in both views. A unit test checks cache reuse, source parts, removal, undo and closing the tab. The existing page-splitting tests remain in place. Headless screenshots were inspected with system fonts disabled.

title: M8: Bound and reuse repeated redaction overlays
author: LabDennis
body:
Applying a redaction with repeated overlay text allocated one owned string per row and then the entire drawing stream from the annotation's declared geometry. Oversized marks could therefore demand unbounded allocations, including outside the page.

Prepare appearances before changing the document, with an 8 MiB budget shared by all selected pages. Checked repeat counts and lengths bound the working row before allocation; every emitted PDF byte counts toward the output budget. Excessive or invalid appearances return an actionable `OverlayLimit` error. A small private overlay module builds, measures and encodes each repeated row once and reuses it. The budget limits generated appearance content, not input PDF size or whole-process memory.

Regression coverage checks rejection before mutation, a shared budget across pages, selected-page application, extreme geometry, escaped WinAnsi text, exact ordinary output, and engine document/undo preservation. The bounded rejection test failed before the fix; it generated about 11 MiB rather than attempting an OOM. A repeat-disabled control still applies successfully.

Performance probe (Windows, `low-disk` profile, mean of 20 helper calls): the 8000 × 800-point repeated-X case produces the same 2,841,859 bytes in 1.56 ms versus 14.39 ms before (~9.2× faster). Output lengths and hashes match across all four measured sizes. This is an appearance-generation microbenchmark; application latency and process peak memory were not measured. The ignored timing probe is included for reproduction.

title: fix(print): custom pages-per-sheet counts no longer overfill sheets (#1336)
author: MrPranklin
body:
Fixes #1336.

`Layout::multiple(n)` turns a count without a fixed grid into a near-square grid (3 → 2 × 2, 5 → 3 × 2), but `Layout::Multiple` kept only `cols` and `rows`, so `layout` filled every cell. Asking for three per sheet put four pages on a sheet, and five put six.

`Layout::Multiple` now carries `per_sheet`, set by `Layout::multiple`. `layout` places at most that many pages on each sheet; it reduces a count larger than the grid to the grid size, and it refuses 0. The spare cells stay blank, and cut-stack piles use the same count. The automation `doc_print` tool and the print dialog now pass the count through instead of dropping it. The dialog only offers 2/4/6/9/16, whose grids already matched, so in practice this changes the CLI/MCP and library results, not what the GUI does.

This adds a field to a public enum variant. Every place in the workspace that builds `Layout::Multiple` is updated. Code outside the workspace that builds it by hand would need to add the field.

Validation:
- `custom_pages_per_sheet_never_overfill_the_grid` covers 7 pages at 3, 5, 7, 4 and 2 per sheet, cut-stack order with 3 per sheet, a count larger than the grid, a count of 0, and the page count of the imposed PDF. Its first assertion fails on main (`[[0, 1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]`) and passes here.
- Manually, `pdfcraft-cli run` with `doc_print` on a synthetic 7-page PDF reports 3 sheets at 3 per sheet (groups of 3, 3 and 1) and 2 at 5 per sheet; 4 and 2 per sheet are unchanged.
- `cargo test --workspace` passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Perf: defer marker and link index scans until first use
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Review direction

Review the lazy-index lifecycle and its consumers for correctness: zero marker/link scans on ordinary open, one shared marker/added-content scan on first request, one link scan on first request, and precise invalidation after relevant edits, comments, undo and redo. These mechanism tests and unchanged ordering/index semantics are the acceptance evidence. Time and memory below are separate sanity observations on the three named PDFs; they do not establish correctness. Hosted CI is not used as evidence, and no hosted result is claimed.

## Summary

- `Session::open` initializes the marker/added-content and editable-link indexes lazily.
- Marker and added-content accessors share one `OnceLock`; repeated access reuses the scan result.
- Link edits refresh the document view while preserving marker state. Comment changes invalidate links because `LinkItem.index` is a position in `/Annots`.
- UI and automation consumers use the accessors. Canvas reads added content only in content-edit mode and links only for link tools.
- A focused counter test covers zero scans on open, cached first use, edit scopes, annotation-index shifts, and undo/redo.

## Problem and root cause

Opening a document eagerly enumerated edit markers, added content and editable links even when a caller only needed ordinary document information. Those scans scaled with annotations and marked content and repeated work for callers that never requested those indexes.

## Target and invariants

Keep `Session::open` free of marker and editable-link enumeration. Materialize each index on first use, share the marker/added-content scan, and invalidate only state whose source data changed. Preserve link ordering, annotation indices, marker semantics, and undo/redo behavior.

## Fix

The document stores lazy marker and link indexes. Content edits invalidate the marker index when their scope changes markers or added content; link edits refresh document state without discarding marker data; comme…

title: MCP: confine file access with --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root
author: isaac-levine
body:
`pdfcraft-cli mcp` gives the agent on the other end the same file access as the user running it. `--root` already confines a session to one folder for reads and writes. VectorCraft has two flags that split the two kinds of access, and its docs say the other Craft apps take the same ones so one client config works across the suite. This adds them here with the same names and behaviour:

    pdfcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

This is the same change as storytold/gridcraft#480 and storytold/wordcraft#798, so the three can be reviewed together.

Every file a tool reads has to be inside the read root and every file it writes inside the write root. A root left out grants none of its access, so the read root alone makes the server read-only. Paths are made absolute, symlinks followed (for a file that doesn't exist yet, the nearest existing folder is resolved and the rest must be plain names), then compared with the root by whole path components, so `/work2` is not inside `/work`. On Windows case is ignored and device names like `CON` and `NUL` are refused. Refusals come back as normal tool errors with VectorCraft's wording, for example `automation path rejected: outside the read root /work/project: /etc/passwd`.

**Where the checks live**

Every path a tool reads or writes already went through `Automation::resolve`, which `--root` uses. That function now also checks the path against the automation roots, so there is no new set of call sites. Two places needed more than that. `doc_save` without a `path` saves in place, to wherever the file was opened from, so it is checked against the write root too. And `text_font_files` without `directories` used to list the installed fonts, which are outside any root, so with roots it searches the read root instead (and is refused if there is no read root). The OCR pre-check of its input paths is now a read check rather than a write check.

The path logic is in `crates/automat…

title: Windows: open a path a launcher passed unquoted and split at its spaces (closes #1455)
author: magdale76
body:
Closes #1455.

Programs that build the reader's command line themselves sometimes leave the path unquoted (`pdfcraft.exe P:\Archive\00042A26 Contract.PDF`). Windows splits it at the spaces, and PdfCraft tried to open each piece ("Couldn't read 00042A26: os error 2"). Acrobat accepts this, so switching such a program's setting from Acrobat to PdfCraft broke opening.

**Change** (`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`): `rejoin_split_paths` runs on the file arguments before the single-instance hand-off. When an argument names no file but it and the following ones, joined with one space, name an existing file, they're rejoined (longest run first, at most 32 pieces). Arguments that exist on their own, or that no run turns into a file, are kept as given, so a genuinely missing file is still reported by its own name. Options (`--…`) aren't affected.

**Limit:** runs of several spaces can't be recovered, since the split has already lost them.

**Tests**
- `unquoted_paths_with_spaces_are_rejoined`: the reported case, the longest run winning, existing files left alone, nothing to join, empty input.
- By hand on Windows 11: launched the built `pdfcraft.exe` with an unquoted path containing a space, as the office program does. The file opened in a tab (checked through `--control` inspect and screenshot); before the change it showed the error. Also confirmed on the reporter's office PC with the program's "open all PDFs" button, via the batch-file workaround, which passes the same joined path.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pdfcraft --bins`.

title: Signatures: defer validation without weakening signed-file guards
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Review direction

Review the exact signed-presence and rewrite-safety behavior first. The timing and RSS figures are performance context; assess correctness from the pre-validation guard tests and the matching signature-list outputs.

## What changed

body:

## File menu in Acrobat's sections (dc4aa4d)
The File menu was one flat list in registry order. It now follows Acrobat's layout, with separators: open and create; save; reduce, optimize and export; security; revert and close; properties; print.

title: fix(text): keep doubled narrow letters in condensed text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1467.

The fake-bold dedupe in `arrange()` treated a glyph as a redraw when the same character sat less than a fifth of its height away. A narrow letter in condensed text is narrower than that (Helvetica `l` at 80 Tz is 0.18 em), so the second `l` of "Alle" was dropped and a word gap inferred in its place. A real redraw also overlaps most of its own width, so the horizontal tolerance is now capped at half the glyph's width; a neighbouring letter starts a full advance away and can't match. Zero-width glyphs (combining marks) keep the old height-based test, since half of nothing would never match an exact redraw of a mark.

title: M7: keep line breaks when editing a multi-line paragraph (#1443)
author: rp6186030
body:
Fixes [storytold/pdfcraft#1443](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1443)

Problem
Adding a word to the end of a multi-line paragraph either merged all its lines into one or reflowed lines that hadn't changed. The report has no sample file. Two independent causes produce this symptom, and both are fixed here.

1. Subset fonts that leave default-width glyphs out of /W (Chrome, Skia)
A composite subset font may omit from /W every glyph whose width equals /DW (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.3). Metrics::has_glyph treated a CID missing from /W in a subset as a missing glyph. As a result:

encode failed for any word containing such a letter (s, y, k in Liberation Sans), so source_width dropped those words when measuring;
each run's width calibration (rect width / nominal width) became inflated, up to its 2.0 clamp, so unchanged rows measured wider than the paragraph and rewrapped;
newly typed letters fell back to Helvetica.
Reproduced with a Chromium print-to-PDF page: before the fix, every row of the paragraph rewrapped on a one-word edit.

2. Text drawn rotated on the page
Line joining (text_lines, add_shown) and row/block grouping (group_layout) compared baselines and gaps in raw user space. For text drawn a quarter turn round (0 1 -1 0 … cm, common on landscape pages), every line of the paragraph has the same user-space y. So all lines joined into one TextLine, the editor opened with one row, and the rewrite drew one line. The styled region rewrite also lays rows out along the page's x axis, which is wrong for rotated text.

Fix
fonts: a composite subset font that declares an explicit /DW counts a CID absent from /W as present. This check only runs for codes the font's ToUnicode already maps, so letters the subset never kept are still rejected. Fonts without an explicit /DW behave as before.
edit, geometry: TextLine::frame_origin / frame_rect and a Pen helper express positions along and across each text's own baseline. For upright text these are exactly the old user-spa…

title: M13: Bound automation text caching and preserve partial search results
author: LabDennis
body:
Searching a large document previously retained every extracted page's glyphs and geometry for the document's lifetime. A single page extraction failure also aborted `text_find`, discarding useful matches from readable pages. This bounds retained text data and returns explicit partial search results.

Fixes #1483.

- A dedicated LRU cache shares a 64 MiB estimated text-allocation budget and a 4,096-page bookkeeping limit across all open documents. Accounting includes vector and glyph-string capacities. Oversized pages bypass retention, evicted pages remain re-extractable, revisions invalidate old entries on the next text request, and closing a document clears its entries.
- Cache entries weakly identify the PDF revision, so they cannot keep an obsolete PDF byte buffer alive. Extraction passes the renderer's `Arc<PageText>` through instead of deep-copying all glyphs. Entirely cached requests no longer construct an unnecessary extraction renderer.
- Cache population preserves a separate result for each page. `text_find` keeps readable matches, continues after failed pages and reports bounded, machine-readable warnings. Text extraction, comment placement and redaction retain strict failure semantics.
- Search order, match rectangles and `next` continuation arguments are preserved. `complete` is false for either failures or additional matches; `next` is present only for the latter. Clients should follow `next` when present and inspect warnings separately. The tool description and automation README document the additive warning fields and their limits.

Regression coverage uses generated PDFs and deterministic extraction-failure injection: a 200-page scan across two documents, LRU recency, capacity accounting, oversized/empty pages, re-extraction, revision changes, close, successful pages surrounding errors, capped continuations, missing worker results and bounded Unicode warning messages. The unchanged upstream cache was also exercised with a synthetic probe: it retained…

title: Desktop: prepare large PDFs off the UI thread
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Review direction

Review request/result ownership and race handling first: preparation must stay isolated from `Session`, and a completed document must be committed exactly once on the UI thread. Then review the responsiveness claim: a live desktop app can continue processing frames and control requests while one background worker reads and prepares a document. This PR does not claim lower total open time, CPU work, or memory use; no time or memory effectiveness measurement is offered.

## Summary

Split engine document opening into prepare and commit phases, then use a single bounded native desktop worker for live path, remote-document, dropped-file, and recovery opens. The existing synchronous engine API remains available. Password retries preserve their source metadata and are prepared off the frame thread.

The worker owns no `App` or `Session` references. It handles one active request and a FIFO queue of at most 16 waiting requests. UI state changes only when the app polls a successful result and commits it on the UI thread.
