title: M2: keep byte boundaries in packed TIFF-predictor rows
author: MMexicann
body:
Packed RGB images with TIFF horizontal differencing can lose every row after the first when a row ends partway through a byte. A valid two-row image renders red then black; Poppler renders red then green.

The shared LZW/Flate TIFF-predictor decoder calls `BitWriter::split_off` while the writer is still partway through the last byte. Align the writer at each row boundary so the next row cannot overwrite the row just returned. This applies to the shared predictor path without changing PNG predictors. Document the vendored patch and update the M2 roadmap notes without changing estimates.

Validation:

- The decoding and page-render regressions failed before the fix and pass afterward. Decoding cases cover 1/2/4-bit RGB samples with horizontal differencing and an 8-bit control; comparisons ignore unspecified padding bits.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --locked`: 258 passed. Render all-target Clippy and formatting passed.
- An independently constructed fixture passes `qpdf --check`. The real fixed CLI renders exactly the same RGB pixels as Poppler at 72 dpi; the baseline CLI renders the lower row black.

title: M4: preserve shared Type 3 glyph resources during extraction
author: MMexicann
body:
Extracting a page can delete an image used inside a Type 3 glyph when the font's resources share an XObject dictionary or resource owner with the page. The saved PDF remains syntactically valid, but a visible glyph disappears: a synthetic baseline drops from 3,562 to 961 dark pixels and Poppler reports `XObject ImB unknown`.

The XObject pruner reads page/form content, but does not interpret Type 3 glyph programs. Its existing safeguard covers only fonts that inherit the page resources. Protect the resource-owner graph reachable from explicit or inherited Type 3 resources, including nested forms, patterns and soft masks. The walk is iterative, never decodes stream data, tracks references and has a 10,000-item budget including direct children. If the budget is exhausted, leave pruning alone. Memoize explicit resources of shared indirect fonts so large repeated-font documents still prune unrelated page images. Discover glyph resources even when page/form content cannot be decoded.

Validation:

- Save/reopen regressions cover shared XObject dictionaries, shared owners with inline XObjects, nested forms, cycles, unreadable page/form streams, a 20,000-child budget fallback, and 4,000 pages sharing one font. A separate-resource control verifies ordinary unused-image pruning still works.

title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built pdfcraft and pdfcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `rustc` from nixpkgs is linked to an older LLVM than the one this Rust release targets, which breaks `rten-gemm`'s AVX512-VNNI kernels (`intrinsic signature mismatch for llvm.x86.avx512.vpdpbusd`). The flake therefore builds with the official toolchain from `oxalica/rust-overlay` (bundled LLVM, like CI).
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#pdfcraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS.

title: fix(organize): normalize rotations before adding so large quarter turns cannot overflow
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
`rotate_pages` added the page's current `/Rotate` to the requested angle before reducing it mod 360. A valid but huge multiple of 90, such as 9223372036854775800, overflows when added to a page rotated by 90: debug builds panic at `crates/organize/src/lib.rs:165` with "attempt to add with overflow", and release builds wrap and write `/Rotate 74`. A file is enough to trigger it: an out-of-range `/Rotate` in the PDF reads as `i64::MAX`, so an ordinary 90 degree rotation of that page overflows too.

The fix reduces both the current rotation and the requested angle mod 360 before adding them, so the sum stays below 720 and the result is unchanged for every rotation that did not overflow.

The first commit adds my contributor display name to `contributors/people.toml`.

## How it was tested

- New regression test `rotate_handles_large_quarter_turns` covers positive and negative angles near the i64 limits and a non-zero remainder, with both page-local and inherited `/Rotate`.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-organize rotate_handles_large_quarter_turns`: fails on unchanged main with "attempt to add with overflow"; passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-organize`: 102 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

author: FredApps
body:

title: Issue #1396: remove an imported digital ID
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Closes #1396

## In short

Once you imported a certificate (a digital ID) to sign PDFs PdfCraft kept it in the list **forever**. There was no button or menu to remove it. This PR adds a **Remove** button to the **Sign with a Digital ID** dialog.

## Why does it happens

The digital IDs you add whether you import a `.p12`/`.pfx` file or create a new self-signed one they are all kept in a list that is saved with the app settings so they come back after every restart.

The code only ever **added** to that list. Nothing removed an entry and the Sign with a Digital ID dialog. The only place the list is shown let's you pick an ID but not remove one.

## What changes for the user

- **Remove** sits next to **Configure New Digital ID** and works on the selected ID.
- It **asks first** to *Remove "Name" from this list? The file itself is not deleted.*, with **Remove** and **Cancel**.
- It only takes the ID **off the list**. The `.p12`/`.pfx` file stays where it is, because you may still need it elsewhere and deleting a key file with one click would be risky.
- The removal is saved so the ID removed forever after a restart.
- If no IDs are left the dialog goes to **Configure a Digital ID** as it does when you have never added one.
- **Keychain (macOS) and Windows certificate store IDs** can't be removed here instead the button is greyed out for them. The OS manages by itself and PdfCraft lists them again each time you sign.

## How it works

`crates/ui-egui/src/sign_ui.rs`
- New `PdfCraftApp::remove_digital_id(index)`. It refuses OS store IDs and indexes past the list, removes the entry and keeps the dialog's selection on the same ID (or the first usable one if the selected ID was removed).
- `SignDraft::confirm_remove` holds the ID waiting for confirmation. Clicking another row cancels the question.
- No change is needed in saving: `persist()` already saves whatever is in the list.

title: fix(audit): a rectangle drawn as an m/l path is a cover like re
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1510.

The cover walk in `crates/audit/src/cover.rs` only kept a pending rectangle for `re`; every `m`/`l`/`h` reset it, so the same black box drawn as a closed path was never seen as a cover. It then goes through the same opacity and colour checks as `re`. title: Open: share parse state across editing and inspection
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Review direction

Review the ownership and fallback boundary: the supplied COS source is reused only for the same `Arc<Vec<u8>>`, inspection receives fresh object/object-stream caches, and the existing 256 MiB decoded-stream limit remains in force. ## Summary

`Session::open_unguarded` already opens the editable COS document. title: M3: draw a GNOME-style title bar on Wayland (#553)
author: bmh129
body:
## Summary
Fixes #553. Part of #1001.

GNOME's Wayland compositor draws no window frames (it offers no `zxdg_decoration_manager_v1`), so winit drew its own fallback title bar. That bar ignores GNOME's theme, dark mode and button layout. PdfCraft now asks the compositor at launch (`apps/pdfcraft/src/decorations.rs`). Where the compositor draws no frames, PdfCraft turns winit's frame off and makes the tab strip the header bar, as GNOME's own apps do (`crates/ui-egui/src/window_controls.rs`):

- **Window buttons:** minimize, maximize/restore and close in Adwaita's style. They are round, with symbolic glyphs drawn in code, so no new assets. They follow the order and side given by `org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences button-layout`, read through `gsettings`; Fedora's default `appmenu:close` shows only close. They're hidden in full screen.
- **Resizing:** zones along the edges, plus L-shaped corners, sit above the rest of the UI, so a press there resizes the window instead of reaching a scrollbar. A hairline outlines the window while it isn't maximized.
- **Preferences ▸ Use system title bar:** shown only where the app draws the frame. It gives the window back winit's frame at once, without a restart. It's named as in VectorCraft and PhotoCraft, but GNOME draws no title bars for apps, so on GNOME this is winit's basic frame; the tooltip says so. Saved as `system_title_bar`, and settable on the control channel as `system-title-bar`.
- **`PDFCRAFT_TITLEBAR=app|system`** overrides the detection (documented in `docs/development.md`).

Unchanged elsewhere:
- KDE, Sway, Hyprland, COSMIC and X11 offer server-side decorations, so they keep the frame their desktop draws.
- macOS and Windows are unchanged.

### Not done
- Right-clicking the header bar doesn't open GNOME's window menu (egui has no command for it).
- The window has no shadow or rounded corners.
- The resize zones lie just inside the window rather than outside it.
- Windows still uses its system frame (the rest of #1001)…

title: fix(macos): Cmd+Q asks about unsaved changes (#1136)
author: Mahmud-Baspehlivan
body:
Fixes #1136.

## What

Two macOS quit bugs, both fixed through `craft-quit` from craft-libs (storytold/craft-libs#5 and #21, now merged; pinned to craft-libs `main` at `f58bc1a`).

**Part 2: ⌘Q quits without asking to save.** winit's default app menu sends Quit straight to `-[NSApplication terminate:]`, which skips `guard_quit`. `apps/pdfcraft` now calls `craft_quit::install_app_menu(&cc.egui_ctx, "PdfCraft")` from the app creator. The menu has the same items as winit's, but its Quit sends `ViewportCommand::Close`, which `guard_quit` handles like the close button. If muda can't build the menu, winit's menu stays and a warning is logged.

**Part 1: the close button crashes on Touch Bar Macs** (exit 133, `_NSTouchBarFinderObservation`). `crates/ui-egui` calls `craft_quit::on_close_request(ctx)` right after `guard_quit` in `logic`. When a close is allowed, it cancels it and quits through `terminate:` instead of letting eframe drop the window. A close that `guard_quit` holds for the prompt is left alone. On other platforms (including the web build) it does nothing. This change and its Touch Bar test are from @jmacek (comment below).

`craft-quit` is a workspace dependency with one pin: `ui-egui` uses the `egui` feature and the app uses `menu`. New in `Cargo.lock`: `craft-quit`, `muda`, `keyboard-types`, `crossbeam-channel`. `deny.toml` already allows craft-libs.

## Tested

Release build on an Apple M4 Pro (no Touch Bar), macOS 27, current `main` plus this PR, with an unsaved annotation:

- Close button → prompt → Cancel keeps the window and the edit.
- ⌘Q → prompt → Cancel keeps the window.
- ⌘Q → Don't Save quits. The PDF is byte-for-byte unchanged (compared with `cmp`).
- ⌘Q → Save writes the file and quits.

title: fix(xfdf): preserve quoted empty CSV values
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
A one-column CSV file whose only value is a quoted empty string, such as `Name\r\n""\r\n` (what Python's `csv.writer` writes for an empty value in a one-column row), now clears the field. Before, `import_table` dropped every record whose single cell was empty, quoted or not, so this import returned `UnknownFormat`.

The CSV parser now records whether each record contained a quote. Unquoted blank lines, including the one a trailing line break leaves, are still skipped. A line holding only `""` now counts as a record wherever it appears, as RFC 4180 reads it, so `Name\n""\nGrace\n` clears the field instead of taking `Grace`. An unquoted empty value in a one-column file (`Name\n\n`) stays ambiguous and still reports `UnknownFormat`.

Tests in `crates/xfdf/src/tests.rs`:
- `quoted_empty_csv_value_clears_a_field` covers LF, CRLF, no final newline, a blank line before the value, and a later record after it. It fails on main with `UnknownFormat` and passes here.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf` passes (30 tests), and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

title: M3: scroll the view when drawing at an edge; take back a polygon's last point
author: philip-tam
body:
## What

Two fixes for drawing comments (Polygon, Cloud, Connected lines, and the other drawing tools):

1. **Edge scrolling.** While a drawing is in progress, the pointer in a 32 px band along any edge of the document view (or just past it) scrolls the view up, down, left or right, so a point beyond what is shown can be reached without leaving the tool. The speed grows with the square of the depth into the band. It only applies within one band of the view, so the pointer over a side panel never scrolls the page. `edge_scroll` is in `crates/ui-egui/src/autoscroll.rs`; `canvas.rs` adds its result to the existing scroll delta.
2. **Take back a point.** Backspace, Delete or Undo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z) removes the last point of a polygon, cloud or run of connected lines being drawn. Removing the only point cancels the drawing. Undo only does this while such a drawing is in progress (`CommentView::undo_point`, called first from `PdfCraftApp::undo`); otherwise it behaves as before.

## Tests

- New unit tests for the edge-scroll maths: all four directions, the middle and far-away pointers, non-finite input, speed rising toward and past the edge.
- New UI test `a_wrong_polygon_point_is_taken_back_with_backspace_or_undo` (Backspace, Undo, re-clicking, finishing, and cancelling by removing the only point).
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean, and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` passes.
- No automated test scrolls the real page while drawing; I tried it by hand in a packaged macOS build (Apple Silicon) and it works there. Not tried on Windows, Linux or the web.
- I did not run the full workspace tests for this change.

title: M14: Fix(nixos): discover installed UI fallback fonts on NixOS
author: tomasmark79
body:
On NixOS, installed fonts live in `/nix/store` and are registered through Fontconfig. The UI fallback lookup only tries conventional system paths, so it misses configured fonts even when Fontconfig finds them.

title: Keep annotations readable under reading colours (#1548)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #1548.

## What

With reading colours on a dark preset, every highlight annotation rendered as a solid dark bar and the text under it was invisible (contrast ≈ 1:1). After this PR, the marked-up words render in the highlight's own colour — yellow words on black, ≈ 19:1 contrast — matching the Acrobat model where Replace Document Colors recolours *document* text and line art but never the colours a comment was given.

## Why (two causes)

1. **Annotation paints were remapped as line art.** `ColorReplacement::map` sends luminance-light paints toward the background, so the yellow fill became near-black; Multiply then darkened the remapped-white words under it into invisibility.
2. **The page background sat outside the page transparency group.** A group isolates what it wraps, so a Multiply highlight blended only with the group's transparent backdrop and never with the background — even with the annotation colour left alone, the quad would stay one flat bar with the words lost in it.

## How

- **hayro patch 26:** the `/Annots` loop in `interpret_page` is bracketed by a new `begin_annotations`/`end_annotations` `Device` signal (default no-ops), and the renderer's reading-colours mapping leaves annotation paints alone while it is set. Covers both paths: `/AP` appearance streams and the no-`/AP` `/QuadPoints` fallback; sibling cases (a black annotation underline flipping bright, light annotation colours vanishing) are fixed by the same rule.
- **hayro patch 27:** the page background is painted *inside* the page transparency group, as the initial backdrop, so Multiply blends with it. White pages are unaffected — multiplying with white is the identity (all existing light-mode render tests pass unchanged).

Display only, as the setting itself: the document is not changed, print and export are unaffected.

## Testing

author: EULArule

XFA forms: saved dynamic forms, the form's own fonts, prototypes, attachments from scripts

XFA forms opened badly or not at all:

title: M4: Mirror PDF pages horizontally and vertically (#1534)
author: LabDennis
body:
PdfCraft can rotate pages, but cannot mirror a scanned sheet, drawing or other PDF page. This adds **Flip horizontal** and **Flip vertical** to Organize Pages, the Pages menu and the command palette. They act on the selected pages (or the current page), and the corresponding CLI/MCP tools can mirror selected pages or the whole document.

Fixes #1534.

The operation reflects content about the visible CropBox in the displayed orientation, including inherited quarter-turn rotations and nonzero box origins. It adds small transform streams around the original content; it does not rasterize, decompress or rewrite the existing streams. Annotation rectangles, drawing coordinates, popup rectangles and stored appearance streams move with the content. Shared appearances are copied before changing their matrices, while field values, link actions and unknown dictionary entries remain intact.

The core separates annotation ownership checks, per-page transforms, content wrapping and annotation traversal, with a single atomic edit boundary. Duplicate page selections are handled once. Invalid geometry and annotations shared across pages fail atomically. Mirroring requires content-modification permission; assembly-only permission is insufficient. Each action is one undo step, and the mirrored result survives incremental save and reopening. Applying the same reflection twice restores the original appearance.

Automation tools: `page_flip_horizontal` and `page_flip_vertical`, with `{doc, pages?}`; omitted pages means all pages. Their command IDs are `page.flip_horizontal` and `page.flip_vertical`. The feature guide documents selection, direction and permission behavior. Existing localized labels and icons are reused.

Organize Pages after flipping the selected second page horizontally. Pages 1 and 3 remain unchanged; both flip controls are available beside the rotation controls.

title: M3: Wayland: stop retaining Ctrl zoom for pixel-only wheel input
author: tomasmark79
body:
Related to #991.

The vendored Wayland pointer handler decides whether scrolling is a finger gesture using only the presence of discrete steps. A wheel event with pixel deltas and `axis_source=wheel` therefore emits `Started`, followed by `Moved`. Wayland does not guarantee `axis_stop` for wheel, wheel-tilt or continuous sources, so egui can stay in its touch gesture indefinitely and retain Ctrl after it is released. Subsequent wheel input keeps zooming.

Use the reported axis source when choosing the phase. These sources emit `Moved`, following the same policy as discrete wheel steps, so egui uses the current modifiers. Explicit stop events, finger gestures (including their modifier retention for momentum), and unknown-source behavior retain their existing policy. Pixel deltas and scroll speed are unchanged.

The regression test compiles the production phase policy and drives a real egui context through Ctrl+wheel followed by wheel without Ctrl. It fails on the previous policy (zoom remains `1.1274968` instead of `1.0`) and passes with the fix. Additional tests cover wheel tilt, continuous sources, discrete wheels, finger momentum and unknown sources. The patch and its tests are recorded in `vendor/README.md`.

Wayland protocol reference: [wl_pointer.axis_source](https://wayland.freedesktop.org/docs/html/apa.html#protocol-spec-wl_pointer-event-axis_source).

Review follow-up:
- Merge upstream through `e88dd72` and resolve the roadmap conflicts.
- Share the Linux winit dev-dependency, pointer modules and vendor patch documentation with #1580; that branch includes this change and its combined workspace run passed (3,025 tests, 14 ignored), as did strict Clippy and the full wasm gate. Merge this PR before #1580.
- Remove the strict-Clippy exception by using an equivalent match guard in the existing forms date parser.

title: Issue #1058: an update keeps the desktop shortcut only if it is still there
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
Fixes #1058.

**Cause.** The ArtCraft Launcher installs and updates PdfCraft with `msiexec /i … /passive /norestart` and passes no properties, so `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT` always took its default of `1`. Every update put the desktop shortcut back, even for users who had deleted it, and deleting it is the only way a launcher user can say no.

**Fix** (`packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs`). `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT` no longer has a static default. Instead:
- AppSearch looks for `PdfCraft.lnk` on the all-users desktop. This runs before the old version is removed.
- A `SetProperty` after AppSearch sets the property to `1` for a first install. For an update it does so only if the shortcut is still there.
- A value given on the command line wins, as before.

The result for each case:

| Case | Desktop shortcut |
|---|---|
| First install (full UI or launcher) | Created; the checkbox starts ticked, as before |
| `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT=0` | Not created |
| Update, shortcut still on the desktop | Kept |

title: Name the failing option and page count when a chained edit page is out of range (#1550)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1550.

The wrong page number in the report wasn't caused by the chaining. `OrganizeError::NoSuchPage` holds a 0-based index, but its message printed that index as is. So `--move 5:1` on a document with 4 pages (index 4) said "page 4 does not exist". The same thing happens without chaining: `--rotate 9:90` on a 5-page file said "page 8".

**Changes**

- **The message counts from 1.** `NoSuchPage` in `pdfcraft-organize` now prints `page {index + 1} does not exist`. This fixes every caller that shows the error, including the CLI, the app and automation. `pdfcraft-edit` and `pdfcraft-annot` had the same 0-based message on their `NoSuchPage` variants, and every constructor there also passes a 0-based index, so they get the same fix.
- **`edit` names the option and the current page count**, as the issue suggests. Before each operation, `pdfcraft-cli edit` checks the `--rotate`/`--delete`/`--move` pages against the page count left by the earlier options. The error looks like `--move: page 5 does not exist; after the earlier options the document has 4 pages`. This follows the existing per-edit check for `--move` targets and `--insert-blank` positions (#1330).
- **`--help`** now says that the options run in order and that page numbers refer to the document after the earlier options.

**Tests**

- `apps/pdfcraft-cli/tests/edit.rs`: `a_page_past_the_end_after_earlier_edits_names_that_option` grows a 1-page file to 3 pages, deletes page 3, then asks for `--move 3:1`. It checks that the error names `--move`, page 3 and the 2 pages that are left, and that no output file is written.
- `organize`, `edit` and `annot` unit tests check that `NoSuchPage(i).to_string()` names page `i + 1`.

Both tests fail without the fix.

title: Print: 4 x 6 in label paper and a Label layout for shipping labels
author: Ace40063
body:
## Problem

Shipping labels (eBay, carriers) could not be printed properly on a 4 x 6 in thermal label printer (tested with a VEVOR Y486, CUPS on macOS):

- the paper list had no 4 x 6 in size;
- the paper chosen in the dialog was never sent to CUPS, so the queue's default size was used whatever the PDF was laid out on;
- labels laid out sideways on a Letter/A4 sheet came out small, rotated or cut.

## Changes

- **Paper**: `PAPERS` gains `4 x 6 in label (101.6 x 152.4 mm)` (288 x 432 pt).

  - the crop is fitted uniformly with an 8 pt margin (several 4 x 6 drivers feed 100 x 150 mm, slightly short of 288 x 432 pt);
  - content stays vector, so barcodes stay sharp and undistorted; "Turn upside down (180°)" flips it; one label per sheet.
- Choosing the label paper selects the Label layout, and the Label tab selects the label paper.
- New strings translated in every bundled catalog.

title: M2: average images shrunk more than 2:1 even without /Interpolate
author: philip-tam
body:
## What

A page that is one big image without `/Interpolate` (the usual scan of text) showed broken thin strokes at screen size: a Chinese "自" read as "白", "土" as "上", boxed characters opened up. The image was shrunk by picking single source pixels (the PDF default when `/Interpolate` is absent), which drops strokes thinner than the step between picked pixels. Acrobat, pdfium and poppler average the pixels.

## Why only beyond 2:1

#624 made non-interpolated images use nearest-neighbour so screenshots and rasterized text stay crisp, and tests such as `non_interpolated_images_are_not_smoothed_when_minified` pin that at 2:1. Nearest is fine there. Beyond 2:1 it loses information, and a scan at 300 dpi shown at screen size is usually 2.5:1 to 6:1.

## Change (`vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`, `draw_image`)

- An image shrunk by more than 2:1 (`MIN_NEAREST_SCALE = 0.5` device pixels per source pixel on either axis) is resampled by the interpolating resampler (Catmull-Rom with a kernel that grows on downscaling) and gets the whole-pixel snapping from #1377, even without `/Interpolate`.
- Up to 2:1 nothing changes.
- A source the resampler cannot take (over 2^20 pixels wide, or over its plan budget) keeps the old nearest path, so `wide_non_interpolated_sources_draw_after_shrinking` still holds.
- The image/soft-mask pairing check compares the PDF's own `/Interpolate` flags, not the new decision, so a soft-masked image does not re-enter `draw_image_with_alpha_mask` forever (a first version of this change overflowed the stack in `image_resampling_wide_transparent_sources_still_shrink`).

## Tests

- New `raster::tests::non_interpolated_images_shrunk_more_than_two_to_one_are_averaged`: 1-pixel stripes drawn 3:1 are mid-grey (they alternate black and white when picked); the same stripes at exactly 2:1 are still picked.

title: XFA: a script's time starts when its context is ready, and a value reaches every field bound to its data node
author: ysrdevs
body:
## XFA: a script's time starts when its context is ready, and a value reaches every field bound to its data node

The two follow-ups asked for in #1355.

### Script time

The session's worker now sends a `Started` reply once the engine is ready for the script it was sent (its JavaScript context built; FormCalc has nothing to build and says so at once), and the script's time limit counts from then, with the engine's start limit (10 s) covering the phase before it. This is what the one-shot path (`run_within_limits`) always did; the session had lost it, so a context's build on a busy machine was charged to the script.

### Shared data nodes

A field inside an `area` and a field of the same name outside it bind to one data node, since areas are left out of data paths. The in-place refresh of the live form (`pdfcraft_xfa::refresh_value`) now follows the data path through the tree (through areas and unnamed containers, which have no data segment, so the walk costs the depth, not the form) and gives every field bound to the node the value the tree builder would, each computed by its own template field (saved values, template default); an exclusion group bound there makes it fall back to a rebuild, as a radio button already did. The engine's value setter keeps an index of widgets by data node (built with its SOM map, dropped on relayout) and gives every widget bound to the node the value, each by its own kind (a check box by its on state, a list box by lines), including when the field the script set has no widget of its own (hidden); the data is written when the node's text differs, whether or not the first widget already held it.

The adversarial review of the first cut found the naive version of this (a scan of all widgets per value, a walk of the whole tree) quadratic: a click setting 1000 totals in a 3000-widget form took 5.4 s against 0.4 s on main. With the index and the pruned walk the same click is linear again (300 values in a 300-row form: 52 ms in a debug build)…

title: fix(sign): sign with keys in legacy CryptoAPI providers (Windows)
author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this fixes

### 1. Certificates whose key is in a legacy CryptoAPI provider can't sign (Windows)

Certificates whose private key lives in a legacy CryptoAPI provider (a CSP) are listed in
*Sign with a Digital ID* but disabled with:

> its private key's algorithm couldn't be read: Unsupported…

This hits Brazilian ICP-Brasil A3 certificates that register only a CSP. Example: Certisign's
desktopID cloud certificates, whose provider is "desktopID Cryptographic Provider"
(`PROV_RSA_AES`, `C:\Windows\System32\desktopID_Provider.DLL`), with no CNG KSP and no PKCS #11
module on Windows.

**Cause.** `windows.rs` opens every key through CNG (`CryptAcquireCertificatePrivateKey` with
`CRYPT_ACQUIRE_ONLY_NCRYPT_KEY_FLAG`, then `NCryptGetProperty`/`NCryptSignHash`). A CSP key has no
NCrypt handle, so reading its algorithm fails.

**Fix.**
- Listing reads the certificate's key provider info (`CERT_KEY_PROV_INFO_PROP_ID`). A provider type
  other than 0 means a legacy CSP. Such an RSA certificate counts as usable *without opening the key*,
  because a cloud provider would otherwise ask for approval on every listing.
- Signing a CSP key uses `CryptAcquireCertificatePrivateKey` with `CRYPT_ACQUIRE_ALLOW_NCRYPT_KEY_FLAG`
  (not silent, so the provider can show its own authorization). Then `CryptCreateHash` +
  `CryptSetHashParam(HP_HASHVAL)` + `CryptSignHashW`. The signature is byte-reversed, because CryptoAPI
  is little-endian. PKCS #1 v1.5 only: CryptoAPI has no PSS.
- If the acquired key turns out to be CNG (`CERT_NCRYPT_KEY_SPEC`), the existing CNG path signs it.
- The key is acquired and released per signature, so each signature can ask for authorization again.
- CNG certificates are unchanged.

**`unsafe`.** AGENTS.md forbids `unsafe` and asks for a maintained safe wrapper. None exists for
legacy CryptoAPI signing, as far as I could find. So the FFI is isolated in one small new crate,
`crates/wincapi` (layer 0, standalone, Windows-only). It declares the exception in it…

title: fix(edit): keep undrawn comments on page when appearance cannot be built (#1317)

title: feat(sign): sign with PKCS #11 devices (smart cards, USB tokens, cloud certificates)
author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this adds

Signing with a Digital ID on a **PKCS #11 device**: smart cards, USB tokens, and cloud
certificates whose vendor ships a PKCS #11 module. Examples: Certisign desktopID, Soluti birdID,
Serpro NeoID. The private key never leaves the device; signing goes through `C_Sign`.

This is how signing works for lawyers and companies in Brazil, where ICP-Brasil A3 certificates
(OAB, e-CPF, e-CNPJ) live on tokens or in the cloud. Until now PdfCraft could only reach them when the
OS exposed them (Keychain/CryptoTokenKit, Windows store). Most tokens and every cloud certificate on
macOS and Linux are reachable only through their vendor's PKCS #11 library.

### Finding devices

`crates/sign/src/pkcs11.rs` looks for the libraries device vendors install in their usual places on
macOS, Windows and Linux. The list follows what Brazilian court signers such as PJeOffice search,
plus desktopID for Apple Silicon, YubiKey (ykcs11) and OpenSC.
- Only existing files are loaded, each once. A library linked under two names counts once.
- A library that doesn't load (another architecture, a broken install) is skipped and logged.
- 32-bit Windows libraries are not listed.
- `PDFCRAFT_PKCS11_MODULES` (a path list) replaces the search, for testing.

### In the UI

- *Configure a Digital ID for Signing* gets a third option: **Use a Digital ID from a device
  (smart card, USB token or cloud certificate)**, as in Acrobat. The library field is optional: empty
  re-reads the devices, and a chosen library (*Browse…*) is checked, kept in the settings
  (`pkcs11_modules`) and read from then on. A library that isn't PKCS #11 is refused with the reason.
- Device certificates appear in *Sign with a Digital ID* with the device's label
  ("desktopID · Issued by …").
- A device with a PIN takes it in the password field, labelled **PIN**. A device with a protected
  authentication path (a PIN pad, or a cloud certificate approved on the phone) takes none. PdfCraft
  logs in to it in the background…

title: Detect rectangular form fields drawn with closed line paths
author: FredApps
body:
Refs #294.

A synthetic regression reproduces different detection geometry for equivalent rectangle encodings: `50 100 120 40 re S` produces a rectangle, while the same outline written with `m/l/h` produces only its top and bottom rules. Treating those edges as rules gives the default rule-field sizing instead of the printed rectangle's height. This change makes both encodings detect one 38-point field inside the 40-point outline, including through the real Detect fields command and save/reopen.

This is a partial fix. The reporter's PDF was unavailable, so the synthetic case demonstrates a cause consistent with the report, not proof of that file's exact cause. Border/default-style concerns and broader detection accuracy remain out of scope. The broader issue remains open.

The shape pass tracks straight subpaths until painting and recognizes axis-aligned four-edge rectangles with explicit closepath, close-and-stroke, repeated endpoints, or implicit fill closure. Stroke closure applies to the last subpath; fill closure applies to all. Rectangle edges do not become extra rule fields, while unrelated horizontal rules remain available. Curves, diagonals, open stroked outlines, and continued complex paths are not promoted to rectangles. The existing CTM is applied to points; controls cover scaling, restored graphics state, and 90-degree rotation. Recorded rectangle corners are bounded to four corners plus a repeated endpoint, and non-finite coordinates are rejected.

author: UmbertoCimmino
body:
## What this changes

## How you verified it

author: marcoarnulfo
body:

Fixes #1520. Also covers the text-box half of #1623 (moving an existing text box); its Arabic request is separate.

title: M13: Run conversion, OCR and optimization over folder trees
author: LabDennis
body:
The CLI could run individual tools or selected-file actions, but could not apply a conversion/OCR/compression recipe to a folder tree. This adds `pdfcraft-cli batch` and the shared `doc_batch` CLI/MCP tool.

```sh
pdfcraft-cli batch scans --root . --recursive --steps convert,ocr,optimize --out-dir processed
```

The runner discovers inputs before writing, preserves paths relative to each selected folder, deduplicates overlapping selections and processes one file at a time in an isolated engine session. It reuses the existing importers, OCR settings and optimizer. `--ppi` and `--quality` configure the Reduce File Size image settings; a larger optimization candidate retains the entering bytes.

Outputs are published through `NamedTempFile::persist_noclobber`, with numbered names on collisions, including concurrent writers. Sources and caller documents stay unchanged. Each file is published only after its complete recipe succeeds. Errors are reported per file; `--stop-on-error` is optional. The CLI prints the JSON report and exits nonzero on partial failure; MCP retains structured results and sets `isError`.

Discovery skips links/reparse points, special files and nested output folders. Root confinement is checked before discovery and before processing. Traversal is limited to 1,000 selected roots, 10,000 entries and 64 levels; individual inputs are limited to 512 MiB. The new code lives in two small modules rather than expanding the existing command dispatchers. The existing OCR argument parser is shared.

See `docs/cli-batch.md` for examples and boundaries. This is a one-shot command; it adds no watcher, service, scheduler or GUI workflow and is independent of the hot-folder work in #1063. Conversion uses the engine's supported extensions, so comic archives become available when #1587 lands without duplicating its importer here. The batch parity entry remains partial because arbitrary Action Wizard recipes, GUI folder selection and resuming are not implemented.

author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this adds

Two options in **Preferences ▸ Appearance**, both defaulting to today's look:

- **Interface font:**
  - *Standard (Inter)*: as now.
  - *System font*: read from the installed fonts, never embedded.
    - macOS: SF Pro (`SFNS.ttf`, at AppKit's 400/510/590 weights) and SF Mono.
    - Windows: Segoe UI Variable and Cascadia Mono (Consolas if missing).
  - *Font file* (.ttf, .otf, .ttc): a variable file gives its regular, medium and semibold

  - *Standard*: as now.

    - Glyph outlines grow 0.15 px, CoreText's font smoothing.
    - Glyphs sit at quarter-pixel offsets.
    - Light-theme coverage uses gamma 0.9.
    - With SF Pro, ink and covered area land within 98–101% of AppKit's.

System fonts like SF Pro need two things egui doesn't do yet:
- the optical size following the point size (variable `opsz`);
- Apple's `trak` tracking.

Without them, SF Pro reads looser and lighter than in native apps. Both are proposed upstream as
**emilk/egui#8707**. Until it lands, `vendor/epaint` (0.36.2) carries them, plus PdfCraft's own
glyph dilation for *Like macOS*. Each patch is marked `PdfCraft patch:` and listed in

In Acrobat, Edit on a scanned page first converts it ("Converting scanned page to Editable Text and Images"), so its words can be edited. title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: feat(sign): sign with ICP-Brasil cloud certificates (PSC API)
author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this adds

Signing with a **cloud certificate** through the API that Brazil's ICP-Brasil defines for its
cloud signature providers (PSC), DOC-ICP-17.01. BirdID, VIDaaS, NeoID, SafeID and the other
accredited providers implement the same endpoints, so one client reaches all of them. The key never
leaves the provider: PdfCraft sends the digest and gets back the raw signature.

### Protocol (`crates/sign/src/psc.rs`)

- OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE (S256, RFC 7636), scope `signature_session`.
- `oauth/token` for the session, `oauth/certificate-discovery` for the certificates (RSA only,
  as the CMS builder signs with RSA), `oauth/signature` with `signature_format: RAW`.
- `CloudKey` implements `ExternalKey`, so the existing CMS/PAdES path signs with it unchanged.
- HTTP goes through a small `Transport` trait. The app implements it with `ureq` and the OS roots it
  already uses for updates (`apps/pdfcraft/src/psc_http.rs`); the crate stays free of networking.

### Sign-in (`crates/ui-egui/src/cloud_sign.rs`)

- A loopback redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` or `localhost`), bound before the browser
  opens. Other redirect URIs are refused with the reason.
- The `state` is checked, the wait ends after 5 minutes, and the browser gets a plain
  "you can close this page".
- Runs on a thread; the UI polls it and repaints when it finishes.

### Providers and credentials

Each provider issues a client ID and secret to the **app**, when the app is registered with it (as
gov.br is with each of them); the holder never sees them and only signs in on the provider's page
with CPF, PIN and one-time code. So:

- `psc::KNOWN` lists the providers whose API base is known. It starts with Certisign
  (`https://remoteidcertisign.com.br/api/v0/`); others are one line each once their address is
  confirmed.
- The desktop app reads each provider's credentials at build time
  (`PDFCRAFT_PSC_<NAME>_CLIENT_ID` and `PDFCRAFT_PSC_<NAME>_CLIENT_SECRET`, e.g. from CI secret…

title: Windows: Harden single-instance IPC security
author: mjshfrvstj-sys
body:
## Summary

Strengthen the Windows AF_UNIX document handoff merged in #715 while retaining its existing socket architecture, startup election, document-opening route and separate-window fallback.

## Motivation

This follows [echelon's invitation to harden the merged socket implementation in the closing feedback on #616](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/616#issuecomment-6096621666). The changes address the requested security improvements while retaining the architecture and compatibility behavior established by #715. In particular, this contribution does not reintroduce named pipes, fatal handoff dialogs, altered secondary-launch behavior, or additional dependency packages.

Refs #616, #715, #602, #282 and #317. These references do not close the broader cross-platform or tab-management requests.

## Security improvements

- Bind each exchange to fresh primary/client nonces inside Windows `LOCAL=user` protected envelopes. Document paths remain sealed, the primary verifies its challenge before admitting a batch, and the client verifies both nonces in the acknowledgment. No reusable secret file is introduced.
- Reject malformed, truncated and oversized length-prefixed frames before unbounded allocation. Enforce versioned document-only schemas, absolute/NUL-free paths, 256 paths per batch, 32 KiB per path and a 1 MiB plaintext limit.
- Bound admission to four receivers and eight active/waiting connections, with at most 16 pending batches, 1,024 paths and 4 MiB of path data. Queue saturation rejects the entire batch before acknowledgment.
- Apply total exchange deadlines to queue wait, nonblocking IO and async crypto waits, so trickled data cannot refresh them. Shutdown signals and joins the fixed workers.
- Derive profile/session routing from Windows known-folder and token APIs instead of environment variables. Check local parents and lock files for reparse points; refuse unlocked election, preserve unrelated regular files, and remove stale sockets only after …

title: F3: one documented font-substitution chain, and report what it chose and why
author: tanish2k09
body:
Phase F 4.1, task F3.

## The problem

When a document does not embed a font program, something stands in for it — and nothing told the user what, or why. `doc_info` reported only `embedded: false`. That is the difference between **"why does my Chinese PDF show nothing?"** being a mystery and being a sentence.

The decision was also made per caller: `edit` picked a craft face by the script of the text, `Std14::from_base_font` matched Latin names, the renderer did its own thing. The order existed but was nowhere written down.

## The chain

`crates/fonts/src/fallback.rs`, tried in order, first step that yields a face wins:

| | Step | Reason reported |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the document embeds the program | nothing substituted |
| 2 | `/BaseFont` names a standard-14 face or known alias | exact published metrics |
| 3 | craft-fonts holds that exact family | never another family |
| 4 | `/CIDSystemInfo /Ordering` names a script we have a face for | Adobe-Japan1 today |
| 5 | the ordering names a script we have **no** licensed face for | **none** — draw nothing, and say so |
| 6 | otherwise, nearest of the fourteen by `/FontDescriptor /Flags` | always succeeds |

Step 5 is the point of the exercise. GB1, CNS1 and Korea1 have no openly licensed face (AGENTS.md §1.1 rules out Source Han and Noto CJK, which is Source Han rebranded), so there is no honest substitute. Reporting *none with a reason* beats quietly standing Helvetica in.

It **delegates** to the existing per-script selectors rather than restating their order, so each keeps one source of truth. And it answers the *dictionary* question only — "which face has a glyph for こ?" depends on the string being drawn and stays where the drawing happens.

## What `doc_info` now says

title: Save: fall back to a plain fsync where a volume refuses the full flush
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #981.

On macOS `File::sync_all` is `fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)`, and SMB and FUSE volumes (a mounted Cryptomator vault is one) refuse it with ENOTSUP or ENOTTY. `write_atomically_with` passed that straight up, so the staging file was removed and every save to such a volume failed. Now, on macOS only, those two errors fall back to a plain `fsync`, which is the strongest flush the volume offers; any other flush error still fails the save and keeps the original. The flush is injected into the helper so a test can make it refuse. The fallback uses `rustix::fs::fsync` (safe, already in the tree through pdfcraft-cli, no new crate in Cargo.lock). Happy to switch to just skipping the flush on those errors if you'd rather not add the dependency to ui-egui.

The crash on quit mentioned in the issue is the Touch Bar teardown one (#1136), not touched here.

title: macOS: start on wgpu on Intel Metal by skipping indirect-call validation
author: fabian-co
body:
## What this changes

On a Mac whose integrated GPU is an Intel Iris Pro (MacBookPro11,3, macOS 12.7.6), the wgpu renderer never starts: the device is lost at start-up and PdfCraft falls back to OpenGL on every launch (`the GPU renderer (wgpu) didn't start: WGPU error: Parent device is lost. Starting with OpenGL instead`). PdfCraft picks the low-power GPU by default, so this is what such a Mac gets out of the box.

The cause is wgpu's indirect-call validation: when the device is created, wgpu compiles a compute shader to validate indirect draw/dispatch arguments, and Metal's Intel compiler aborts on it. The log shows:

```
ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("new_compute_pipeline_state: NSError { code: 2, localizedDescription: \"Compiler encountered an internal error\", domain: \"CompilerError\", .. }"))
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

and each attempt leaves `MTLCompilerService` crash reports ending in `IGILErrorMessageHandlers::reportUnsupportedMaxWorkGroupSizeMetadataError` (libIGIL-Metal).

PdfCraft draws and dispatches nothing indirectly (no `draw_indirect`, `draw_indexed_indirect`, `multi_draw_*` or `dispatch_workgroups_indirect` in `apps/` or `crates/`), so this removes `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` from the window instance's flags. `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` turns it back on. This is the same fix VectorCraft already has (storytold/vectorcraft#651); PhotoCraft and LightCraft skip the check too.

Docs: a row for the variable in `docs/development.md` › Environment variables. No asset, dependency, network or `--root` change; no new `unwrap`/`unsafe`.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --locked -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: Security: fix three audit findings in redaction and signature validation
author: JeremyYao
body:
## What this changes

Three security fixes found by an audit of `main`, one commit each. In all three the operation reported success while the saved file, or the verdict shown, was wrong.

**1. M8: redaction unlinks removed images and forms from inherited and shared resources**

Apply Redactions and Remove Hidden Information give a rewritten page its own pruned `/Resources`. The dictionary the page drew through before could still name the removed image or form, and a full-rewrite save keeps whatever is still referenced. The removed image samples and form text stayed in the saved file when:

- the page inherited `/Resources` from a `/Pages` node;
- several pages shared one resource dictionary object;
- a form without `/Resources` drew the image through the page's dictionary.

Pages with their own `/Resources` (the case #1099 fixed) were not affected.

The interpreter now records the original object behind every XObject it drops or replaces. After the page loop, each page-tree resource dictionary that still names one loses that entry, unless a page drawing through that dictionary still draws the name. A dictionary that loses an entry is replaced by a private copy on its node, so a dictionary object shared with other nodes is left alone for them. If a page's use of a name cannot be told, the operation fails closed.

**2. M9: a cross-reference entry the reader sets aside is never an unchanged signed object**

`pdfcraft-cos` judges post-signing changes; the renderer draws the page. They resolve some cross-reference entries differently. A revision appended after signing could redefine a page's content stream and give the object an entry the reader sets aside while the renderer follows it (an in-use entry at offset 0, or a second entry for the same object in one section). The classifier compared the signed object with itself and reported the signature Valid while the page showed the new content.

`pdfcraft-cos` now records the entries it does not take at face value (`Docum…

title: M4: copied pages keep the resources they list only up the page tree
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Part of #1628: this is a cause that produces exactly the reported symptom, but I could not confirm it is the reporter's without their file.

The Combine list's thumbnails are drawn from each source file, where hayro looks a resource name up the page's own `/Resources` and then up the page tree. Some files rely on that: the page lists its font, and the images or forms it draws are listed only on a `/Pages` node. When pages are copied, `import_pages_mapped` keeps the page's own `/Resources` whole and only falls back to the inherited one when the page has none, so the copy loses everything listed up the tree and draws an empty page. That is the "fine in the list, blank after combining, blank when exported" in the issue. Copied pages now get their own dictionary plus the names only their ancestors list (the page's entry wins, then the nearest ancestor). Pages with complete resources are copied as before. Strictly speaking a page's `/Resources` replaces the inherited one (ISO 32000-2 §7.7.3.4), but our own reader shows these files, so the copy should keep what the user saw. Happy to switch if you'd rather follow the spec here.

I couldn't get the reporter's file, so this is the cause I could rebuild from the description: a one-page file with the form on the `/Pages` node renders in the list and comes out blank from Combine on main. - **Models on first use** (`ocr.ocr-web`): the web zip ships the text recognition models in `models/` beside `index.html` (`packaging/web/package.sh`). The first time Recognize Text needs them, the web build downloads them (about 12 MB, 64 MiB cap each). The dialog shows a spinner while it downloads, and an error with a Download retry button if it fails. `pdfcraft_ocr::Ocr::from_bytes` loads models from memory (only when their SHA-256 matches `ATTRIBUTION.toml`), and `engine::ocr::install` puts the loaded ocrs engine into the `recognizers()` cache, so every job, the engine-status checks and the Verify screen use it.
- **WebAssembly SIMD**: `.cargo/config.toml` builds `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with `+simd128`, so rten's vector kernels are used. In wasmtime, one synthetic Letter page at 150 dpi takes 8.5 s instead of 20.5 s, with the same text. Native takes 0.5 s. Relaxed SIMD is not enabled, because Firefox and Safari don't turn it on by default. The web build now needs Chrome 91, Firefox 89 or Safari 16.4 or later.
- **Web Workers**: the new `apps/pdfcraft-ocr-worker` is a module worker that holds only the OCR code. The page prepares each page and transfers its image to a worker, then places the words that come back. `OcrJob::steps()` splits #977's `run` at the engine call: `OcrSteps::next_page` renders, crops to the region and preprocesses; `OcrShot::read` / `OcrShot::place` recognise and map the words back. `lines_to_json`/`lines_from_json` carry the result, with each word's confidence and engine. With one engine (the web build has only ocrs), every merge strategy is that engine's reading, so the workers return what `run` would.

title: Export all images: CMYK JPEGs keep their colours instead of coming out as negatives
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1640.

In a PDF, a CMYK JPEG's samples are ink amounts, inverted only when the image's `/Decode` says so; that's how the page renders it. The export decoded these JPEGs with the `image` crate, which follows the convention for standalone JPEG files instead (Adobe-style CMYK, stored inverted). It also ignored `/Decode` on JPEGs. So the CMYK/YCCK images in the attached file, which have a soft mask and go through the PNG path, all came out as negatives. Now CMYK JPEGs are decoded to their raw CMYK samples with `zune-jpeg` (already in the tree through `image`; YCCK gets converted to CMYK), and `/Decode` inversion applies to JPEGs like it does to every other image. A CMYK JPEG with no mask is still written as is when its `/Decode` inverts it, since an image viewer reads that file correctly. Without the inversion the viewer would show a negative, so it's written as a PNG. Happy to switch that last part if you'd rather keep every unmasked JPEG byte for byte.

Validation:
- `cmyk_and_ycck_jpegs_export_in_the_colours_the_page_shows` (synthetic 8×8 CMYK and YCCK JPEGs, with and without a mask and an inverting `/Decode`): fails on main (cyan ink exported as black, `CMYK: [0, 0, 0, 255]`), passes here
- the attached `example_pg59.pdf`: the red banner and the other CMYK images now export in their real colours
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create --lib -- jpeg image mask cmyk`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: XFA: decode BMP and TIFF pictures
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1644.

BMP and TIFF pictures in XFA templates and data were left out with "not a JPEG, PNG or GIF". They're now recognised by their bytes (the declared type is ignored, so `image/tif` and `image/x-ms-bmp` work too), sized from their headers, and decoded the same way as GIF. That means the same `Limits`, 8-bit samples plus a soft mask when there's alpha, and only the first page of a TIFF. A TIFF is turned and flipped as its Orientation tag says, in its layout size and in its pixels, so a picture tagged as shot sideways comes out the way viewers show it. `crates/xfa` turns on the `bmp` and `tiff` features of `image`. Both were already in the workspace, so `Cargo.lock` doesn't change.

The engine had an exhaustive match on `Kind` for image fields, so it needed two new arms. A BMP or TIFF picked for an XFA image field is now kept in the data as `image/bmp` / `image/tiff`. Before this it was refused, because the layout couldn't show it.

It fails on main with `image/bmp: [..., "a image/bmp image is not a JPEG, PNG or GIF and is left out"]`.
- `a_tiff_picture_is_turned_by_its_orientation_tag` (xfa): a 2 × 1 TIFF (red, blue) tagged Orientation 6 must be 1 × 2, red above blue, both from the header and once decoded. title: control: cap line length before auth
author: SteamSmith
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1259, as @echelon suggested there: before auth, `BufReader::lines()` has no limit on line length.

`serve` in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` now reads lines with a bounded read (`take(max + 1).read_until(b'\n', …)`):

- **Before `auth` succeeds**, a line may be at most `MAX_AUTH_LINE` = 4 KiB. The auth request (`pdfcraft-cli` sends `{"token": …}` with a 32-hex token) is about 100 bytes. A longer line gets a `-32600` error and the connection is closed, after reading at most `MAX_AUTH_LINE + 1` bytes of it. No newline is needed for the limit to apply.
- **After `auth`**, lines are read whole, as before. Authenticated clients can still send large requests.
- End of stream, read errors and non-UTF-8 input end the connection exactly as they did with `BufRead::lines`; only an overlong line gets the error reply.

The reader returns `LineRead::{Line, End, TooLong}`, keeping "too long" distinct from I/O errors.

## Tests

New, in `control::transport_tests`:
- `lines_are_read_up_to_the_limit`: line at the limit accepted, CRLF stripped, final line without newline, end of stream, and an overlong line reported as `TooLong` with only limit+1 bytes consumed
- `an_overlong_line_before_auth_is_refused`: `MAX_AUTH_LINE + 1` bytes with no newline → `-32600`, then the connection closes
- `long_lines_after_auth_are_still_read`: after `auth`, a 16 KiB line is parsed (`-32700` for non-JSON) and the connection stays open

On Windows (rustc 1.99.0):
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --no-fail-fast`: all green, identical to `main` plus the 3 new tests (lib 344 vs 341).
- `tests/control.rs` passes in full (46 tests).
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo xtask wasm` (31 crates ok) are clean.

title: Render: a soft mask shrunk below its size is filtered, so thin strokes drawn through it survive
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1649.

The body text in that PDF isn't text: Word saved each line as a 2×2 black image whose `/SMask` is a 1-bit bitmap of the glyphs at about 600 dpi, so the mask alone carries the text. The mask has no `/Interpolate`, and since #624 a minified mask without it is nearest-sampled. At 100–200% that keeps one mask sample in three to six, so the thin CJK strokes fell between the samples and came out broken and aliased (the CLI render shows the same thing as the screenshot, so it's the renderer, not the UI). Now a soft mask of a different size than its image is filtered when it's shrunk, whatever its `/Interpolate`, which only asks for smoothing when the mask is enlarged. Images whose mask matches their size, and every #624 case, are unchanged.

## How you verified it

- `raster::tests::shrunk_soft_mask_larger_than_its_image_keeps_thin_strokes`: fails on main (the one-column stroke disappears, `[255, 255, 255, 255]`), passes here
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib minif` and `--lib image_resampling`: the #624 and resampling tests stay green
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render -p hayro --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- rendered the issue's PDF with `pdfcraft-cli render` at 96 and 177 dpi: the text now looks like the other viewer's
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

The change only covers masks that differ in size from their image (the Word case). A mask-sized-like-its-image or a plain 1-bit scan of text minified without `/Interpolate` still takes the #624 nearest path; I left it alone because #624 asked for exactly that, but filtering any shrunk soft mask would be a one-line widening, happy to switch. The patch is recorded as (15) in both hayro rows of `vendor/README.md` (the table has the row twice on main).

title: Embed craft-fonts by default via .cargo/config.toml [env]
author: sblount2025-design
body:
A plain `cargo build --release` from a clean clone silently produces a CJK-blind binary. build.rs warns and carries on:

```
warning: no craft-fonts embedded: Chinese and Japanese text will render as empty
boxes. Clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts next to this repo and
rebuild with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts
```

With craft-fonts already cloned beside the repo exactly as the warning asks, the build *still* needs `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` passed by hand on every invocation. A build-time requirement that lives only in a warning is one that gets forgotten, and then comes back as a bug report about missing glyphs.

This adds it to `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[env]
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR = { value = "../craft-fonts", relative = true }
```

**This is not a new convention — it mirrors `deckcraft/.cargo/config.toml`, which already ships this exact block.** The other craft apps that read `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` don't, which is the inconsistency this closes.

Properties:

- `relative = true` resolves against the repo root, so no absolute path is committed.
- No `force`, so a `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` already in the environment still wins for a one-off build against a different font set.
- If craft-fonts is **not** cloned beside the repo, behaviour is unchanged — build.rs warns exactly as it does today.
- The existing `[alias] xtask` entry is untouched.

## Verification

Built with the variable explicitly removed from the environment, so only the config could supply it:

```
env -u CRAFT_FONTS_DIR cargo build --release
```

The crate recompiled and the "no craft-fonts embedded" warning did not appear. Tested on macOS (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, against craft-fonts at its current main.

title: fix(organize): Document Properties also change the XMP title and author
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`doc_set_info` (Document Properties ▸ Description) changed `/Info` only. Files that also carry the values in their XMP packet (`/Root /Metadata`; LibreOffice exports, every PDF/A file) kept the old `dc:title` and `dc:creator`, so the file disagreed with itself after the edit:

- viewers that prefer XMP kept showing the old title (Firefox's built-in viewer does, in its tab title);
- `doc_info` reported the new `/Info` values, so an agent believed the change was done;
- on a PDF/A file, our own preflight then reports "The title in the metadata and the document information differ" (6.6.3).

The comment above `set_info` said XMP sync would come with the `model` crate. This does the small part now: when the catalog has an XMP packet, `set_info` changes the matching property as well, with the pairing PDF/A uses (ISO 19005-1 §6.7.3, the same one `pdfcraft-preflight` writes):

| Info key | XMP property |
|---|---|
| Title | `dc:title` (`rdf:Alt`, `x-default`) |
| Author | `dc:creator` (`rdf:Seq`) |
| Subject | `dc:description` (`rdf:Alt`, `x-default`) |
| Keywords | `pdf:Keywords` |
| Creator | `xmp:CreatorTool` |
| Producer | `pdf:Producer` |

The packet is edited as text (`crates/organize/src/xmp.rs`): an element is replaced where it stands (so it keeps its description's namespace declaration), a simple value written as an attribute is rewritten in place, a missing property gets an `rdf:Description` of its own (same `rdf:about`) before `</rdf:RDF>`, and an empty value removes the property, as it removes the `/Info` key. The rest of the packet (other schemas, unknown properties, padding) stays byte for byte. The stream is written unfiltered and keeps `/Type /Metadata /Subtype /XML`, so `/EncryptMetadata false` still applies to it.

Nothing changes for files without XMP (none is added), for other keys, or for packets this can't edit safely: not UTF-8, no `rdf:RDF`, or larger than 16 MiB decoded.

title: Open: opening an already-open document focuses its tab (#1620)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #1620.

Opening a document that is already open now focuses its tab instead of opening a duplicate — on every open path: File ▸ Open, drag-and-drop, double-click in the file manager (single-instance forward), the command line, Open Recent / Home, and the control channel's `ui open`.

title: M1: edit finds the pages a damaged file's readers find
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1656.

The file in the issue has two problems. The reader handled both and `edit` handled neither. Its newest xref section's `/Prev` points into a zeroed region. The reader rebuilds from object headers when that happens, but cos kept the newest section and silently dropped everything only the older section located, including two of the three pages. And the catalog's `/Pages 172 0 R` points at one of the zeroed objects, so even with every object found there is no page tree to walk. The reader finds the pages by scanning, organize found none, and `--rotate 1:90` became "page 0 does not exist".

So now:
- cos treats an unreadable older section as damaged cross-reference data and rebuilds from object headers. That's the path it already takes when the newest section is unreadable. The "older cross-reference section ... is unreadable" line stays in the repair log.
- `pdfcraft_organize::recover_page_tree` gathers the `/Type /Page` objects into a new page tree, in file order. At open the engine writes that as one more revision and reopens it, the way the XFA layout is applied, so the document opens unmodified. It keeps the result only if the reader then shows the same pages as before: same count, sizes and rotation. The scanning reader takes any dictionary with `/Contents` as a page, so it can skip a blank page or show an annotation as a page. When the two disagree, nothing is rebuilt. Page edits then fail with "the document's page tree lists no pages: the file is damaged" instead of touching a page the user doesn't see.
- On a signed document the page tree is never rebuilt. Edits to a signed file that was rebuilt from object headers are refused with the existing `SignedRewrite` error, because saving such a file is always a full rewrite and would invalidate the signatures. Before this, that save fell back to a full rewrite without saying so.

## How you verified it

- `pdfcraft-cli` `tests/edit.rs`:
  - `a_document_whose_page_tree_is_missing_edi…

title: Keep the full final spread reachable with unequal page heights
author: FredApps
body:
When the last page is shorter than its partner in the final two-page spread, using only that last page's bottom underestimates the scrollable content height. The taller left page cannot be scrolled fully into view. A synthetic four-page document at 200% zoom left 372.67 screen points below the viewport at maximum scroll.

Use the greatest bottom among the laid-out page rectangles, plus the bottom margin. The one-line correction preserves zero content height for an empty document.

Five regressions drive synthetic wheel events through the viewer and check the final spread's bottom and margin:
- taller left page;
- taller right page;
- equal-height pages;
- an unpaired final page;
- a taller left page with cover mode enabled.

Related to #187, with partial scope only: this reproduces unreachable tall-left content, not the reporter's original flash of a page from 30 pages back. That report remains open.

Validation on the approved tree based on 0a098648:

title: Text selection: dragging to the top or bottom edge of the view scrolls it
author: marcoarnulfo

Part of #1670.

A text-selection drag never scrolled the view by itself: egui's ScrollArea doesn't autoscroll a drag, so with the button held at the bottom of the window the selection stopped at whatever was on screen. title: Edit text & images: a dragged image's pixels follow its frame instead of waiting for the release
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1671. The handle half was already fixed on `main`, so this covers the preview.

The first half, where the corner handle misses even though the resize cursor is showing, is already fixed on `main` by #1116 (6d843a8e). In 0.6.0, a press between 2 and 8 px outside the corner showed the resize cursor, but the object marquee still took it and deselected the image. `image_owns_pointer` now keeps that press for the image. I checked this with a throwaway kittest that pressed and dragged from every offset within 8 px of the corner at 100%, 120% and 200% zoom. Current `main` misses none of them. What's left is the preview. While a corner (or the whole image) is dragged, only the blue frame moves, and the image pixels stay where they were until release. title: fix(sign): render Unicode characters in visible signatures using bundled Inter font
author: PINYOPATTANAWASANPORN
body:
## What this changes

Enables visible signature appearances in `pdfcraft_sign` to render Unicode characters (specifically Latin Extended-A / Central European characters such as `č`, `ć`, `ž`, `š`, `đ`) by embedding the bundled `Inter-Regular.ttf` font with `/Identity-H` encoding and a `/ToUnicode` CMap when the signer name, labels, reason, or location contain non-WinAnsi text.

When all text is within `WinAnsiEncoding`, the existing zero-byte overhead behavior (using standard `/Helv`) is preserved.

## Why

Visible digital signature appearances previously drew text exclusively using `/Helv` (standard-14 Helvetica Type 1 font with `WinAnsiEncoding`). Signer names containing valid European characters outside Windows-1252 (e.g. Slavic / Central European names like `Luka Petravić` containing `č` U+010D and `ć` U+0107) either failed during signature appearance generation with `SignError::Unsupported` or resulted in placeholder characters.

`pdfcraft_fonts` bundles `Inter-Regular.ttf`, which covers Latin Extended-A and provides full OpenType glyph mappings. By dynamically selecting between `/Helv` and embedded Inter:
1. Standard ASCII / WinAnsi signatures remain compact with zero embedded font overhead.
2. Signatures with Central European / Slavic names render accurately and cleanly.
3. Unsupported scripts (outside Inter's coverage) still return a clear `SignError::Unsupported`.

## Verification

- **Unit tests added:**
  - `pdfcraft_fonts::inter_width_measures_latin_extended_and_ascii`: verifies advance width measurement of Latin Extended characters against `skrifa`.
  - `visible_appearance_draws_central_european_characters_with_embedded_font`: signs a synthetic document with signer `"Luka Petravić"` and Slovenian metadata, validates zero `?` in appearance stream, confirms `/PCFull0` font dictionary is embedded, and validates cryptographic signature validity with `signatures(&doc, ...).status == Status::Valid`.

title: fix(ui): a tool chosen with no document runs once the picked file opens
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Since #1493, a running app opens files on the background worker. `open_then_run` (a tool chosen with no document open, e.g. Export ▸ Text) still checked for the new tab right after `open_path`. By then the file hadn't opened yet, so it opened a frame or two later and the tool never ran. `a_tool_chosen_with_no_document_asks_for_one_and_runs_on_it` has been red on `main` since then.

The fix reuses `PendingOpen.then`, which already carried the command through the password prompt. `open_path` becomes `open_path_then(path, None)`, and `open_then_run` calls `open_path_then(path, Some(command))`:

- **Inline path** (`run_inline`, or before the first frame): the behaviour is unchanged. It runs straight after the open, or hands the command to the password prompt.

I also checked the other `open_path` callers that look at `views.len()` straight afterwards. `control.rs` already handles a pending open. `reopen_last_files` runs before the first frame, so it is always inline. title: Text selection: a drag after a double- or triple-click extends by whole words or lines
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1685.

A double-click selects the word as an anchor/head run, but the drag that follows moved the head to the nearest glyph, so it extended letter by letter, and dragging left kept only the first glyph of the clicked word (the anchor). Now, while the drag belongs to a multi-click, the selection grows by the same unit the clicks chose: whole words after a double-click, whole lines after a triple-click. The clicked word or line always stays selected, and the anchor switches to its far end when the drag goes backwards, as in Acrobat and browsers. The word/line/page lookup the press and release paths already shared is now one small `click_unit` helper, reused by the drag.

Validation:
- `a_double_click_drag_extends_by_whole_words_both_ways` (tests/ui_group/text_select.rs): fails on main (`"quick bro"` dragging right, `"uick b"` dragging left), passes here

title: fix(render, ui): form-heavy documents draw and fill fast (spot-colour images, widget placement, Fields panel)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Fillable forms felt much slower than in Acrobat, both on opening and on every field filled. Profiling a real fillable character sheet (2 pages, 274 text fields, not committed) showed the fields cost almost nothing: the engine opens it in 0.04 s. The time goes into **drawing the page background**, plus two things that grow with the number of fields.

**1. Spot-colour images convert once per pixel value, not once per pixel** (vendored hayro-interpret patch 28, `f9a4b9f7`).
The sheet's background art is a 3304 × 4105 8-bit `/DeviceN [/Black] /DeviceCMYK` image whose tint transform is a PostScript calculator (Type 4) function. `decode_raster` ran that program once per pixel (13.5 million times a page) and collected four `f32`s a pixel on the way. Each page took 3.8 s and 430 MB to draw; Poppler takes 0.27 s. Because every field edit replaces the `RenderPool`, the same cost came back after each field was filled. Patching only the images' colour space to `/DeviceGray` (same fields) brought it to 0.12 s, which confirmed the cause.

An image whose pixels hold at most 16 bits of samples (8-bit Separation/DeviceN, 1/2/4-bit gray, indexed, 4-bit RGB…) now converts through a table of every possible pixel value (`rgb_via_lookup`). The table is used only when the image has more pixels than it has entries. Each sample is decoded by the same `decode_sample` the per-pixel path now shares. `fix_image_length`'s rules for short and overlong data are kept: pixels past the data are converted exactly as before.

**2. Widgets without `/P` are placed in one pass** (`f8916d37`).
`Inspector::find_widget_page` searched every page's `/Annots` for each such field (O(fields × annotations)), so a form of 8,000 such fields took 1.17 s to open instead of 0.27 s. The pages' `/Annots` are now read once, lazily, into an annotation → page map (the same pattern as `named`). A widget that two pages list is now placed on the first, as `pdfcraft-forms` places it; before, it went to whi…

title: Print: choose paper by PDF page size (#1103)
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Refs #1103 (the "Automatic (PDF page size)" option; #1212 covers the fixed default and this change is independent of it).

## What changes for users

Acrobat's **Choose paper source by PDF page size**, as a checkbox under Paper in the Print dialog, on by default and kept across restarts:

- With a **Size** layout (Fit, Actual size, Shrink, Custom), each page prints on the standard sheet it matches: A4 pages on A4, Letter on Letter, in either orientation (the same 0.5 pt match as *Match page at 100%*). Pages of a size no sheet matches print on the paper chosen in the dialog.

- **Match page at 100%** becomes a checkbox, on by default, so a page prints 1:1 on its own sheet rather than shrunk by Fit's 18 pt margin. With paper by page size it is always on offer and only sets the scale (Actual size, Auto orientation; off means Fit). Without it, it works as the button did: enabled when the viewed page matches a sheet, and it picks that sheet.
- Off: the old behaviour, except that the dialog now starts at Actual size instead of Fit.
- `doc_print` takes `paper: "auto"` for the same thing (documented in its schema; the error for an unknown paper lists it). Its default scale stays `fit`.

The print-ready PDF carries the sheet sizes; craft-print already spools it at the PDF's page sizes (CUPS with `fit-to-page=false`, Windows per page), so which tray a driver takes a sheet from stays the driver's decision.

title: Save to a mounted volume that cannot rename (#981)
author: muraa-p
body:
Fixes #981.

A Cryptomator FUSE mount, a network share or a container overlay can refuse a rename its own
filesystem could have done, answering `EXDEV` or "not supported". Every save then failed with an
error the user could only act on by saving somewhere else, and closing the app right afterwards
surfaced the same failure again.

Both the staging file and the target live in the same folder, so a rename normally succeeds and
stays atomic. Where it cannot, this copies the finished bytes across and drops the staging file:
the save lands on the volume, at the cost of the replacement no longer being atomic, which is the
most such a filesystem allows. Every other rename failure still reaches the user untouched.

The fallback is deliberately narrow — only `ErrorKind::CrossesDevices` and `ErrorKind::Unsupported`
are retried as a copy — so a genuine permission or read-only failure is not disguised as a save
that worked.

Tests cover both halves: the ordinary rename still moves the staging file rather than copying it,
and a failure the copy cannot stand in for is still reported.
