title: fix(forms): open a text field on press so dragging over it selects text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2213.

A text field's editor only opened on a completed click (`forms_ui::page_input` waited for `resp.clicked()`), so a press that turned into a drag never opened it: the gesture stayed with the page and field 1 got neither focus nor a selection. Text fields now open on the press. The editor didn't exist when the press happened, so on its first frame it puts the caret where the press landed and takes over the drag (`set_dragged_id`); from then on egui's own drag-to-select extends the selection, as in Chrome's PDF viewer and Acrobat. A side effect: a plain click now puts the caret where you clicked instead of at the end, which is also what those viewers do. Happy to switch if you'd rather keep the old caret placement for clicks.

Since the press now commits the previous field, the release of the same gesture must not commit it again, or a value its validation script refuses is validated (and alerted) twice. The click no longer commits or opens a text field when the press already did. It only keeps the new editor focused, because egui can't hit an editor until a frame has laid it out. A refused field that reopens on the press also stays open when that release lands elsewhere.

Validation:
- `forms::dragging_over_another_fields_text_focuses_it_and_selects_from_the_press` (egui_kittest: type into `name`, focus `city`, drag over `name` from inside its first word to past its end): fails on main (focus stays on `city`), passes here; without the caret placement or the drag hand-off it goes red again
- `forms::pressing_another_text_field_validates_the_refused_value_once` (a `qty` field whose script refuses values over 100, then a press and release on another field): one alert, and `qty` stays open with the typed text; committing again on the release turns it red

title: M9: cargo xtask trust-lists builds the EU Trusted Lists file
author: thorstenhirsch
body:
## What this changes

`cargo xtask trust-lists [--out FILE]` builds the file that `sign_trust {"eu_trusted_list": "<path>"}` loads (#622): the certificates of the **granted qualified CA services** (`CA/QC`) of the 30 national EU Trusted Lists, concatenated as DER and sorted, so a rerun with the same lists gives the same bytes. Today that is 875 certificates, 1.4 MB, written to `dist/trust/eutl-qualified-ca.der` (git-ignored).

Refs #775, #87, #824 (qualified signatures show Unknown): with this file loaded through #622, the PDF attached to #775 is Valid.

- CAs that issue only certificates for web site authentication (QWAC CAs, 113 of 977 granted services) are left out: they issue no signing certificates. A service that says nothing about it is kept.
- The UK's frozen list is left out by its scheme territory, not by its address.
- Deterministic, HTTPS only (a list pointed to with `http://` is fetched with `https://`; Slovakia's does), every download capped at 64 MB through a bounded read (whichever curl is installed), each of up to three tries a fresh curl with a fresh buffer, a failed list stops the run and writes nothing.
- Every certificate of an accepted service must be valid base64 and one DER SEQUENCE (what #622's loader requires of an entry), or its list fails, naming the service: the file is complete or not written, and the loader can't call it damaged.

**Order:** this is independent of #622 to build and review, but the file is only useful once #622 (trust lists in `sign_trust`) has landed. Whichever of the two lands second should update the `sign.eutl` entry and the gap-10 wording in `docs/`; I left them alone so the two PRs don't conflict.

title: fix(ui): type right-to-left text in display order, keeping typing order (#2101)
author: Mawfyy
body:
Fixes #2101

The line editor, the Add text box and the Fill and Sign type box showed right-to-left text in logical order, left to right: typing `مرحبا سلام` read backwards, and text placed where the words appeared on screen landed somewhere else once the file was saved. The saved PDF already wrote bidi correctly, so the screen and the file disagreed.

egui lays text out left to right and its caret works in the buffer's character order, so the editors now hand it the display-ordered string from a new buffer (`VisualText`) that maps every insertion, deletion, selection, copy and cut back to the paragraph's logical text; the format panel's range styles the logical span it covers. The paragraph editor keeps its per-source-line look by walking the display string with the line each character came from.

`bidi::visual_with_order` is the order map: UAX #9 display order as a strict permutation — bidi controls kept, brackets mirrored, no character gained or dropped.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`: all targets green, including new unit tests (permutation invariants, mid-sentence insert, a selection crossing a run, selection slices/spans) and two control-channel tests that type an Arabic sentence into the real Add text box and Fill & Sign, put the caret at the visual start and retype, asserting the logical text.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`: 0 warnings.
- `cargo xtask parity`: exit 0; `edit.add-text`, `edit.rtl-cjk-editing`, `misc.rtl-ui` and `misc.prefs-language` entries updated, ROADMAP progress line added.
- Live app smoke: typing `ا ببببب` draws the logical-first word at the right edge, and the committed, engine-rendered page shows the Home-caret `Z` between the two words.

## Notes
- Hebrew still has no face to draw it in a box: craft-fonts ships no "Hebr"-covering face (separate work, fonts epic).
- Comment composer and interface fields (search, dialogs) keep logical-LTR display; tracked in `misc.rtl-ui`.

title: fix(forms): Tab and Space reach check boxes and radio buttons, and a click focuses them
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2223.

Check boxes and radio buttons were click-only. The form overlay built its Tab order from text, combo and list fields alone and had nothing to show for a focused box, and a click on one (`forms_ui::page_input`) cleared the field focus, which also dropped the text still being typed in the field before it. Now every fillable field is a tab stop, in the same `/Tabs` order. A focused check box or radio button gets the blue focus ring the text fields already have, and an invisible focusable widget over it holds egui's keyboard focus, so Space toggles it and the arrows step through its radio group (selecting as they go, wrapping, and following the group to another page like Tab does) instead of turning the page. The other page keys (Page Up/Down, Home/End, and the arrows on a check box) keep working: `canvas::shortcuts` no longer stands aside for that widget, only for real text input. A box scrolled out of view lets go of the focus (there is no draft to keep), so scrolling back with the arrows doesn't change a radio choice and doesn't pull the keyboard from the find bar. A click toggles the box and focuses it, so Tab goes on from there. When the click also commits typed text, the text edit is applied first and the toggle follows on the next frame; if the field refuses the text, it reopens and the box is left alone. A focused box also draws its new state while the page re-renders (the unbaked overlay used to be skipped for the focused widget).

Two choices that are easy to change: each radio button is its own tab stop, as text fields with several widgets already are (browsers stop once per group), and Space only selects a radio button, as in browsers, while a click on the selected one still turns it off unless the group sets NoToggleToOff. Happy to switch either.

#2213 (my PR for drag-selecting in text fields) touches the same file, in the text-field press and commit code; this one stays out of those paths, so they shouldn't conflict beyond a rebase.

title: Refuse header/footer Bates numbers that would overflow u64
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/edit/src/lib.rs:445` (no existing issue): Header/footer Bates numbering panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' when the start number is near u64::MAX.

## Cause
`add_header_footer` computed each page's Bates number as `bates0 + k as u64`. `bates0` can be any u64 parsed from the template, so a start near u64::MAX with two or more pages overflowed. That panics in debug builds and wraps to 0 in release builds. Page numbers were already checked before drawing, but Bates numbers were not.

## Fix
Before any marks are removed or drawn, `add_header_footer` now checks with `checked_add` that the last selected page's Bates number fits in a u64. If it doesn't, it returns `EditError::Invalid` and leaves the document unchanged. The per-page add also uses `checked_add` instead of a plain `+`.

## Verified
- Regression test `header_bates_start_that_would_overflow_is_refused_without_drawing`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib header_bates_start_that_would_overflow_is_refused_without_drawing`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Page-number handling and the Bates token parsing in `bates_start` are unchanged.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: fix(preflight): read device colour from content operators, not whitespace-split bytes
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

`pdfa_verify` and `pdfa_convert` decide which device colour spaces a document uses by reading its content streams. Until now they found those streams by their dictionaries (no `/Type`, no `/Subtype` other than `/Form`) and split their bytes on whitespace, looking for `g`/`rg`/`k` tokens. That missed real CMYK content and made some up, so a CMYK document could be given an sRGB output intent and pass verification, and an RGB one could be refused it. Fixes #2259.

Now:

- **Content streams are found by role:** the pages' `/Contents` and Type 3 glyph procedures, which only a reference identifies; form XObjects, including the `/Type /XObject` ones that used to be skipped; and streams with a `/BBox` and no `/Subtype`, which covers appearance streams that leave out `/Subtype /Form` and tiling patterns. Mesh shadings carry a `/BBox` too, so they are excluded. Type 3 fonts are found inline in resource dictionaries too, with a depth bound.
- **Each content stream is read with `pdfcraft_content::parse`,** operator by operator: `g`/`G`, `rg`/`RG`, `k`/`K`, `cs`/`CS` with a device space name, and inline images' `/CS` or `/ColorSpace` (`/G`, `/RGB`, `/CMYK`, the full names, or `[/I <base> …]`). The abbreviations only count in inline images; anywhere else `/CMYK` is a resource name.
- **Strings, comments, inline image data, font programs, ICC profiles and shading data are never read as operators.** That also covers what #2089 fixes for font programs and ICC profiles (see below).

`pdfcraft-preflight` now depends on `pdfcraft-content` (L2 → L4, allowed; `cargo xtask layers` passes).

title: M3: screen resolution and ruler calibration for Actual size (#739)
author: aalbertiarchitecte
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #739, and adds a way to measure the right value instead of guessing it.

Actual size and every fixed zoom percentage now scale from a **screen-resolution basis** instead of a fixed 96 dpi. Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ **Screen resolution**:

- **Standard (96 ppi)**: the default and today's behaviour, so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't touch it.
- **Custom: N ppi**: Acrobat's Custom Resolution, in device pixels per inch.
- **Calibrate…**: three lines (the window's whole, half and quarter width, so a short ruler can measure one). The user measures one or more and types the length in their unit; several readings are averaged, and readings more than 2% apart are flagged.

Once calibrated, Actual size shows a page at its real size on the glass (checked on Windows 11: a 100 mm line in a PDF measures 100 mm), and percentages scale from that basis, as measured in #739 (`logical px per PDF point = ppi / 72 × zoom`). Fit modes still fit the window.

**Design.** The resolution is stored as a physical density and divided by the current pixels-per-point when drawing, so a page keeps its size when the OS display scaling or PdfCraft's interface size changes. That differs from Acrobat for a typed Custom value (Acrobat's is a logical ppi); I chose the physical one so a calibration survives a scaling change, and I'm happy to follow your call there.

`canvas::PT` stays the standard basis; `DocView` gains a `pt` field that the app sets every frame from `screen_ppi::basis`, and the eight fixed-percentage uses in `canvas.rs` read it. Setting `screen_ppi` (null = Standard), control option `screen-ppi` (`standard` or a number), dialog `calibrate-screen`.

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-ui-egui`

title: M14: the quick-action bar follows Preferences > Tools panel side
author: abszar
body:
## What this changes

Preferences ▸ Tools panel side (#1130) moves the docked Tools panel, but the floating quick-action bar (Select, Hand, the comment groups, Fill & Sign) stayed at the left edge of the document area. A user who picks Right sees almost nothing change, especially in Read mode, where the docked Tools panel isn't shown at all.

- The quick-action bar now sits at the top right of the document area when Tools is on the right, and at the top left as before otherwise.
- Its flyouts (comment groups, Fill & Sign) open towards the page, so they don't run off the window's edge.

title: Make a missing external oracle loud instead of a silent pass
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

Every test that wanted an external oracle probed for it by hand and chose for itself what to do when it was missing. The common choice — print a line and return — **reports as a pass**, so a suite with no oracles installed looked exactly like one in which every oracle agreed. 16 such probe sites across 7 files, in three different conventions.

That was not hypothetical. **No CI runner installed `qpdf`**, so `cos/tests/encryption.rs::qpdf_agrees` had never executed on a runner, while `README.md` said saved output was "independently checked with qpdf". For R2–R4 that test is the *only* check of owner-password authentication (Algorithm 7) that does not go through our own code.

This is the same failure class the repo has been bitten by twice before: the confinement test that passed with path resolution switched off, and a background monitor that ran silently for 30 minutes because `jq` was missing.

## What this does

- **`crates/oracle`** (`Class::Testkit`, dev-dependency only) holds the probes — `qpdf()`, `pdftoppm()`, `pdftotext()` — and one rule: a missing oracle is a **declared skip or a failure, never a silent pass**.
- **`PDFCRAFT_ORACLES_REQUIRED`** picks which, on the same convention as the existing `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED`. CI installs `qpdf` and sets it, so a skip notice on a runner is now a red build.
- All four live probe sites migrated: `cos/tests/encryption.rs`, `cos/tests/writer.rs` (×2), `xtask/src/gates.rs::text_oracle`, `organize/src/tests.rs`.
- `README.md`'s two verification claims made precise, and the `core.write-validity` parity note updated — it said "skipped when qpdf is absent", which is no longer how it behaves on CI.

The crate has **no panicking path of its own**; `or_skip!` expands its `assert!` into the caller, which is test code.

## Verification

**The qpdf tests were run against real qpdf (12.4.2) for the first time — they pass.** So the README claim is now both enforced and true, and this PR should not turn CI red.

title: fix(filters): preserve output-limit errors in raw Flate fallback
author: MMexicann
body:
## What this changes

Raw deflate that begins with bytes resembling a zlib header triggers the existing Flate fallback. If that retry exceeds the caller's output budget, the old code replaces its `LimitExceeded` error with the first attempt's corruption error. Strict decoding reports the wrong failure; tolerant decoding accepts an empty partial stream. For example, a one-byte raw stream decoded with a zero-byte budget currently returns `Ok([])` through `Stream::decoded_within`.

Preserve the retry's limit error. Keep the original corruption diagnostic when both attempts are corrupt, and keep successful raw fallback unchanged. The allocation cap already worked; this fixes error propagation and prevents silently accepting an over-budget stream as empty content.

Discovered while reviewing current upstream `9931329b`; no existing issue is linked. Open issues, open PRs (including contributor PRs), and recent commits were checked for overlap. No feature, dependency, asset, or contributor-name record is added.

title: One way to write a synthetic PDF fixture
author: tanish2k09
body:
**Stacked on #2266** — base is `feat/oracles-must-run`, because the layering fix in `c965a7df` is what lets `cos` dev-depend on a `Class::Testkit` crate at all. GitHub will retarget this to `main` when #2266 merges. Review the last commit only.

## What and why

55 files hand-rolled the same serialiser — number the objects, record each one's offset, emit a classic cross-reference table and a trailer — **111 times over**. The object *bodies* are properly the business of the crate under test. The envelope around them is not, and every copy is a place for a fixture to be quietly wrong in a way that makes a test prove less than it appears to.

`docs/gaps.md` gap 12 names "synthetic fixtures" as something the fidelity harness needs, and there was no shared way to make one.

## Design

`pdfcraft-testkit` has **no workspace dependencies**, on purpose: the crates at the bottom of the layering (`cos`, `geom`, `filters`, `crypt`, `arlington`) can use it in their own tests without a dependency cycle, which is also why it returns bytes rather than a parsed `Document`.

```rust
let bytes = Pdf::new()
    .version("1.4")                                        // default 1.7
    .obj("<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>")              // becomes 1 0 R
    .obj("<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>")
    .stream("", b"BT /F1 12 Tf (hi) Tj ET")                // /Length computed
    .trailer_entry("/Info 5 0 R")
    .build();
```

## Byte-identical by construction

This is the part worth reviewing. A migration that changes a fixture's bytes silently changes what the test using it proves, so `the_builder_is_byte_identical_to_the_serialiser_it_replaces` keeps a **verbatim copy of the old hand-rolled code** and asserts the builder agrees with it, across versions and trailer variations.

title: redact: clear a scanned page's JPEG image in place instead of blanking the page (#2246)
author: skylartaylor
body:
Fixes #2246.

## Root cause

A scanned page (Brother scanner, ocrmypdf/Tesseract output) is **one full-page `/DCTDecode` (JPEG) image** plus an invisible OCR text layer. `redact`'s in-place image clearing only supported Flate/LZW/ASCII85/ASCIIHex/RunLength (`crates/redact/src/image.rs` allowlist), so a partly-covered JPEG fell through to the fail-closed path in `interp.rs` that **removes the whole `Do`** — and since the one image *is* the whole page, the page comes back blank while the redaction box and (invisible) text layer remain.

## Fix

- A plain `/DCTDecode` image is decoded (via the `image` crate's jpeg feature, already in the tree), the pixels whose centres fall under a redaction region are zeroed, and the result is re-encoded as a **new JPEG** object; the `Do` is repointed at the cleared copy. Everything outside the mark survives.
- Shared pixel-hit helpers now drive both the raw and JPEG paths — `get_mut` + a `MAX_PIXELS` cap, no indexing on input-derived values.
- Fail-closed behaviour unchanged for everything else: JPX/JBIG2/CCITT, CMYK/YCCK JPEG, non-plain filter chains, non-identity `/Decode`, undecodable streams → image removed whole (no residue).
- `/SMask`/`/Mask` preserved.

## The privacy question from the issue

**The OCR text under the mark was already removed** by the text path (`show()` cuts covered glyphs out of `Tj`/`TJ` with an equivalent `TJ` displacement) — verified empirically on the reporter's file: `text_find` of the marked title → 0 matches after apply+save, `text_extract` over the marked rect → empty, raw scan of every decoded stream for the redacted glyphs' codes → no residue, while text right of the mark still matches. So there was no second defect; the new regression test pins the invariant anyway.

## Evidence

- Red/green: with `image.rs` reverted to 0.8.0 and the new test kept, the test fails with exactly the reporter's symptom (`images_removed: 1, images_cleared: 0`); with the fix it passes.
- Reporter's file: pre-fix save = …

title: Measure rendering against Poppler, and turn the pixel test on
author: tanish2k09
body:
## Why

`docs/gaps.md` gap 12: **until rendering is measured, every claim about its quality is a judgement.** Text extraction had an oracle (word-F1 vs `pdftotext`) and written output got qpdf in #2266. Rendering had nothing.

## The metric is the point

A raw pixel-for-pixel comparison is useless here. Two correct renderers disagree on every glyph edge — antialiasing coverage, hinting, subpixel stem placement — so a strict comparison reports a perfect page as badly wrong, and the number tells you nothing about whether a shading is missing.

`pixels::compare` counts a pixel as differing only when it differs from **every** pixel in the other image's 3×3 neighbourhood by more than a tolerance. A one-pixel shift finds a near match next door and is forgiven; a glyph that isn't there has no near match and is counted. It runs in **both directions** and takes the worse, because the one-directional form flatters whichever renderer is blurrier.

## First reading

`cargo xtask render-oracle`, 250 corpus files, page 1, 72 dpi, tolerance 8:

```
229 compared: median 0.89%, mean 2.16%, p90 5.35%
25 within 0.1%; 15 size mismatches, 5 we could not render, 4 Poppler could not
worst:
  84.22%  bug1552113.pdf
  20.11%  bug1743245.pdf
  13.36%  bitmap-refine-template1-tpgron.pdf
  13.01%  bitmap-refine-tpgron.pdf
  12.39%  22060_A1_01_Plans.pdf
   8.79%  ZapfDingbats.pdf
```

It **reports rather than gates** — the corpus isn't fetched on CI, and a first reading of a borrowed renderer is a baseline to improve on, not a bar to clear.

The worst results cluster on JBIG2 `bitmap-*` files (`hayro-jbig2` carries 3 local patches) and on ZapfDingbats. That aims the renderer work at something specific for the first time, which is the whole point of having the number.

## Verification

The metric's correctness lives in unit tests, and they were written to fail first:

- `a_one_pixel_shift_is_forgiven` — a shifted stem scores 0 but still reports `max_delta` 255, the honest signal
- `missing_cont…

title: redact: clear a DCT scan's pixels instead of removing the whole image
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Redacting a scanned PDF blanked the page: the page image is DCT (JPEG) coded, the pixel-clearing path only decoded lossless filters, and its fail-closed fallback removed the whole image. The fix decodes DCT images with the same `image` crate the create path already uses, clears only the pixels whose centres fall under the mark, and writes the result as a Flate image, keeping every other pixel of the scan. DeviceGray and DeviceRGB JPEGs are covered; a JPEG whose size or component count disagrees with the dictionary, or a CMYK JPEG, is still removed as before. A regression test builds a JPEG-backed page, marks the middle, and asserts the image is cleared rather than removed, the page still draws it, the marked pixels are zero, and the border survives.

Fixes #2246

title: render: average a minified 1-bit mask instead of picking strokes away
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
render: keep a minified 1-bit stroke instead of picking it away (#1700)

A 1-bit source — an `/ImageMask`, a `/BitsPerComponent 1` picture or its `/SMask` — is line art:
drawn much smaller, nearest-neighbour picking drops one-pixel strokes whenever the sample grid
misses them, so a scanned glyph's stem or a mask's bar disappears. The renderer now carries
whether an image is 1-bit through hayro's image data and area-averages a minified 1-bit source
instead of picking. Type 3 glyph images are included: main's area shrink (#3858) already covers
every other minified image, and #624 keeps nearest for Type 3 glyphs, which is where a
0.3-device-pixel bar in a glyph still vanished. Magnified images are untouched.

This supersedes the branch's earlier whole-image box average, now that #3858 performs the
row-based area shrink.

Tests:
- a minified 1-bit image-mask glyph keeps its stroke (fails without the renderer change: all
  white, the stroke is lost);
- an 8-bit colour picture with a same-size 1-bit soft mask keeps a one-pixel stroke when
  minified (CodeRabbit's request — `draw_minified_image` gained a mask bit-depth parameter).

Fixes #1700

title: organize: split a combined field/widget so every copied page owns its widget
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A widget that doubles as its own field (`/Subtype /Widget`, no `/Parent`) was copied once and shared between both copies of a repeated page, so only the last page could identify it (its `/P`) and per-page annotation edits were impossible. Page import now splits such a widget into a parent field holding the field keys (name, value, flags) and a widget child holding the annotation keys (rectangle, appearance, page), registers the parent in `/AcroForm /Fields`, and gives every later copy of the page its own widget child in the parent's `/Kids`. The repeated-page independence test no longer exempts own-field widgets, and a new test requires distinct widgets, correct `/P` per page, and one shared parent/value after save and reopen.

Fixes #1810

title: Say what the render-oracle score does and does not mean
author: tanish2k09
body:
Follow-up to #2286, from doing the first thing the new instrument asked for: looking at its most extreme reading.

## The 84% file is Poppler's bug, not ours

`bug1552113.pdf` was the worst of the first 250 at **84.22%**. The cause is Poppler. The file is a 250×50pt page with two lines of Times-Roman and a link annotation whose `/Border` width is **112**. Poppler paints that as a band across the whole page:

| ours | Poppler |
|---|---|
| both lines of text legible, no link border | a solid band over the text, only `isible.` showing |

The fixture is named **"Bug 1552113 - this text should be visible."** In our rendering it is.

So the first correction this PR makes is to the documentation of the number itself: **a high score is a disagreement, not a verdict on us.** Anything at the top of the worst list needs a person to look at both images before it is treated as our bug. That caveat is now in `docs/gaps.md` and the crate README.

## A plausible change the measurement rejected

Poppler synthesises an appearance for an annotation that has none; we draw only what the document carries. (`view.render-annotation-appearances` already records *"Link borders without /AP and printing are not covered yet"* — the oracle independently rediscovered a documented gap, which is a decent validation of it.)

That made `-hide-annotations` look like the obvious way to measure page content alone. So I measured it over the same 250 files:

| | annotations shown | hidden |
|---|---|---|
| median | 0.89% | 0.89% |
| mean | **2.16%** | 2.18% |
| p90 | **5.35%** | 5.55% |
| within 0.1% | **25** | 22 |
| new worst | — | `annotation-tx3.pdf` **45.64%**, `annotation-tx2.pdf` 18.79% |

Hiding is *worse*: it stops scoring us for appearances we don't synthesise, and starts scoring Poppler for every appearance we **do** draw. 30% of the sample has annotations and the two biases very nearly cancel.

**So the default is unchanged.** `--hide-annotations` becomes an opt-in for explaining one file at …

title: feat(plugins): sandboxed WebAssembly plug-in host (ABI v1)
author: bonjourjules
body:
## Summary

Adds a generic, sandboxed WebAssembly plug-in system to PdfCraft — the extension mechanism requested in #336 — so third-party authors can ship document tools that users install from a release build, with no repository, terminal or native binary involved.

This deliberately does **not** try to host native Acrobat plug-ins: that needs Adobe's C SDK and unsafe FFI into arbitrary machine code (as noted on #336), and cannot work in the browser build.

## The format follows PhotoCraft / VectorCraft, not a new one

PhotoCraft established a plug-in convention and VectorCraft explicitly follows it. This PR adopts the same arrangement so authors and users see one system across the Craft apps:

- **One `.wasm` file per plug-in**, manifest embedded in the module (no package format, no PdfCraft-specific file extension)
- Same manifest fields (`id`, `name`, `version`, `kind`, `author`, `description`), same `wasmi` sandbox and limits: no host imports, a fresh instance per call, 32 MiB module cap, fuel budget
- Export prefix mirrors the siblings (`pc_*`, `vc_*` → `pdf_*`): `pdf_abi_version`, `pdf_manifest`, `pdf_alloc`, `pdf_run`
- Where PhotoCraft declares a `filter` kind and VectorCraft an `effect` kind, PdfCraft declares `command` (plus its `commands` list): the plug-in receives a JSON document context and answers with a message and host-interpreted actions (`show_message`, `set_document_info`, `open_document`). The host validates everything; the guest cannot touch the document directly.

## What's in the change

- `crates/plugin` — discovery in the per-user `Plugins` folder, install (validated before anything is written, same-id installs replace), uninstall, enable/disable persisted in `disabled.json`
- `crates/plugin-sdk` + `examples/plugins/hello` — a small guest SDK and a generic example plug-in (reports document facts, stamps document info). Its `build.sh` refreshes the checked-in test fixture, the same arrangement as PhotoCraft's example.
- UI — **View ▸ Plugin…

title: Forms: Auto font size can be set on a text field again (#2250)
author: snipeTR
body:
Fixes #2250

In Prepare a Form ▸ field properties ▸ Appearance, ticking **Auto** set the font size to 0, but the disabled size box next to it was still drawn with a `DragValue` bound to that same value. egui's `DragValue` clamps the value it shows to its range (2–100 pt) by default, so on the next frame the 0 became 2.0 and Auto unticked itself.

title: Keep Auto font size in the field properties Appearance tab
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2250

## Cause
In the Appearance tab, the Auto checkbox sets the font size to 0. The font size DragValue has a 2..=100 range and clamps existing values by default. In the same frame it raised 0 to 2 and wrote it back, so Auto was lost and the size could not be set to Auto.

## Fix
The font size DragValue now uses `clamp_existing_to_range(false)`. An existing 0 (Auto) is left alone, and values dragged or typed by the user are still limited to 2–100 pt.

- Regression test `appearance_tab_keeps_auto_font_size`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test prepare appearance_tab_keeps_auto_font_size`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The forms model, which already accepts 0 as Auto, and the Bulk tab font size control, which uses a 0..=12 range and was not affected.

title: Pin that every JBIG2 conformance fixture decodes to the same picture
author: tanish2k09
body:
Acting on the render oracle's top finding — and it inverted.

## The JBIG2 cluster is Poppler's bug, not ours

Four JBIG2 fixtures sat at the top of the oracle's disagreement list (13.4%, 13.0%, and a group at exactly 6.86%). `hayro-jbig2` carries local patches, so the obvious reading was that we were wrong.

The 96 `bitmap-*.pdf` corpus files are a **conformance suite**: one small drawing encoded through every corner of JBIG2 — each generic-region template, custom AT pixels, TPGDON and TPGRON, refinement, halftone with and without skip, symbol dictionaries with Huffman tables, MMR, composition operators, random access, unknown-height segments. Those features change how the bytes are *compressed*, not what the picture *is*.

**So a correct decoder renders all 96 identically — a real test with no reference image and no oracle. The suite checks itself.**

| | distinct images across the 96 |
|---|---|
| **ours** | **1** |
| Poppler | **8** |

Poppler draws a **blank page** for the seven halftone-skip and symbol fixtures, and its output *changes when TPGRON is switched on*, which a correct decoder's cannot. Roughly a fifth of its JBIG2 output is wrong.

Confirmed visually on `bitmap-halftone-skip-grid.pdf`: we draw the picture, Poppler produces an empty page.

## What this adds

`crates/render/tests/jbig2_invariants.rs` pins the invariant. It needs no external tool, so it is immune to the oracle problem it was written to resolve. It is `#[ignore]`d and corpus-gated on the existing `pdfcraft-cos` pattern — including that an *unverified* corpus is a failure, not a skip.

On failure it names the odd files out rather than reporting a count, since that is the whole value:

```
JBIG2 coding features must not change the picture, but 1 of 97 fixtures decoded differently:
  1 file(s): ["bug1552113"]
```

That output is from **watching it fail** — I admitted one unrelated file to the set to prove the detection works. My first attempt at a failing probe (treating `-grid` as a codi…

title: edit: commit the open paragraph when a click switches text boxes
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Clicking straight into another text box while one was open for typing replaced the editor and
dropped the typed text; only a click on empty canvas (the editor losing focus) or Cmd+Enter
applied it. The click now queues the open paragraph's edit and opens the clicked box on the
following frame, once that edit has applied, so the box's block index and geometry are read from
the document as it now is. A click on the open box's own frame keeps the editor and its draft
instead of resetting it, and switching away from an unmodified editor behaves as before. A
regression test types into the top of two boxes, clicks straight into the bottom one, and
requires the first box's text applied, the edit on the undo stack, and the second box open —
before the fix it failed with the draft dropped (`["Top", "Bottom"]`).
Fixes #2022

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: The fonts README still called the standard-14 widths an estimate
author: tanish2k09
body:
Found while orienting for the font work.

F1 replaced the character-class approximation with the published standard-14 metrics, and `helvetica_width` has delegated to `Std14::Helvetica` ever since. The README kept describing it as PdfCraft's own estimate — and, more importantly, said:

> No metrics file or font program from any vendor is bundled

That stopped being true when the generated tables landed. They **are** Adobe-authored non-visual technical data: the item `AGENTS.md` §1.1 permits, carried in `std14_metrics.rs` with `adobe_data = true` in `ATTRIBUTION.toml`.

A contributor reading that README would have concluded there was no vendor data in the crate at all. That is the one kind of error that actually matters in a provenance claim, and it is mine — I left it behind in F1 when I moved the table.

Now says what *is* bundled and what still is not: widths and encodings, never a font program or a typeface.

`fonts` 65 · `fmt` clean. Documentation only.

title: Read WinAnsi 0xAD as a hyphen, so search and redaction can see it
author: tanish2k09
body:
**Needs your reading of the spec before merging — I could not settle it, and the implementations disagree.** Everything else about it is verified.

## The problem

A page that draws a discretionary hyphen through WinAnsiEncoding's `0xAD` extracts, in our map, as **U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN**. That character is invisible. So text the reader can plainly see does not match a search for it, and **`redact`'s pattern matching — which runs on exactly this map** (`crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs:1060` says so) — does not match it either.

That is the same silent-failure shape as reading Symbol as Latin in F2: the text is there, the tool cannot see it.

Found by running the text oracle, which has never been run in this repo. `XiaoBiaoSong.pdf` scored word-F1 **0.231** against `pdftotext`, and the entire gap was this one character, 104 times — our output and Poppler's were otherwise character-for-character identical.

## The change

Annex D.2 gives codes `0x2D` and `0xAD` the same glyph name, so the byte a Windows codepage calls a soft hyphen draws, and should extract as, an ordinary hyphen.

Reading table only. **Writing is unaffected**: `win_ansi_byte` maps `0xA0..=0xFF` by identity, so `'-'` still takes the canonical `0x2D` and a caller holding a literal U+00AD still writes the `0xAD` byte — which is the one that draws a hyphen anyway.

The existing round-trip test could no longer hold for that code, since two codes now mean one character. It states the aliasing explicitly rather than asserting a bijection.

## Why it needs you

The evidence is **not unanimous**:

| source | reading |
|---|---|
| a PDF library's docs, citing ISO 32000-1 Annex D.2 | glyph name at `0xAD` is `hyphen` |
| Poppler | extracts **U+002D** |
| vendored hayro | table says `173 => "sfthyphen"`, reports **U+00AD**, normalises to `hyphen` *only* for glyph lookup |

So two implementations disagree, and I cannot read the normative Annex D.2 table from here. The behavioural argument favours U+002D — a redaction tool tha…

title: M10: open Office documents as PDFs through an optional local LibreOffice
author: ArturFaleiros
body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft can now open Word (`.docx`, `.doc`), PowerPoint (`.pptx`, `.ppt`), Excel (`.xlsx`, `.xls`), OpenDocument (`.odt`, `.odp`, `.ods`) and `.rtf` files as PDFs. This is the `create.from-office` parity entry ("Create PDF from Office documents (LibreOffice sidecar)").

- **Desktop:** File ▸ Open gets a *Word / PowerPoint / Excel / LibreOffice* filter. The open worker converts in the background, and the result opens as a **new unsaved PDF tab**. The source file is never written, and Save As picks the destination.
- **Automation:** `doc_convert_office { path }` does the same headlessly and returns a new document id, like `doc_create` (CLI `run` and MCP share the table).
- **Converter:** a separately installed LibreOffice. Nothing is bundled, downloaded or started at launch. Standard Windows / macOS / Linux install paths are detected, and `PDFCRAFT_LIBREOFFICE` (an absolute path) overrides them.

How the external process is contained (`crates/platform/src/office.rs`):
- The input is checked by extension *and* magic bytes (OLE2 / ZIP / `{\rtf`), then copied into a fresh temporary directory under a fixed name (`input.<ext>`). The user's filename never reaches the command line.
- Each run gets a fresh `-env:UserInstallation` profile with macro execution off, active content off, untrusted referer links blocked, and Writer/Calc automatic link updates off. `TMP`/`TEMP`/`TMPDIR` point into the temporary directory.
- Limits: 128 MiB input (read with `take`), 256 MiB output, a 120 s deadline. On timeout or drop, the whole process tree is killed (Unix process group / `taskkill /T`). The output must start with `%PDF-`, and it then goes through the normal engine open path, which validates it.
- `--root` sessions refuse the tool **before** resolving or reading the path, because an external program can't inherit the path resolver. The web build returns "requires the desktop app".

## How you verified it

The project CI does not install LibreOffice, so the rea…

title: The text oracle scored us zero for honouring a no-copy document
author: tanish2k09
body:
## The problem

A PDF can forbid copying its text. `pdfcraft-cli text` honours that and refuses, naming the owner password as the way through. **pdftotext ignores the flag and extracts anyway.** So the oracle compared our refusal against its text and scored **0.000** — measuring obedience, not quality.

`bug1815476.pdf` is the case: a one-page Spanish form we **render perfectly** but decline to extract. It sat at the bottom of the worst list looking like a font bug, which is exactly what sent me investigating it.

## The fix

Those files are skipped and **counted**, not scored, and the count is printed rather than passed over in silence — the same rule `pdfcraft-oracle` exists for: *a comparison that did not happen must not look like one that succeeded.*

```
text oracle: 19 files with text; median F1 0.991, mean 0.854, p10 0.231
  1 skipped: the document forbids copying its text, which we honour and pdftotext does not
```

Before / after over the first 250 corpus files:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| files compared | 20 | 19 |
| median | 0.991 | 0.991 |
| **mean** | **0.811** | **0.854** |

The gain is entirely the removal of a false negative — no extraction changed.

## Design notes

Permissions come from **`Document::permissions()`**, not from matching our own error string, so the check does not break when the message is reworded. That meant a new `pdfcraft-cos` dependency for `xtask`; `xtask` is `Class::Exempt` so the layering gate is unaffected, and it passes at 37 crates.

A file that cannot be opened at all counts as *permitted*. That is a different problem, and dropping it quietly would hide it.

## Verification

Demonstrated by the before/after run above — the file that motivated the change is gone from the list and accounted for. `xtask` 48 · clippy clean · `fmt` clean · `layers` 37 crates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix(engine): give a host with no clock or time zone a real one (Session::with_wall_clock)
author: bonfim6P
body:
## What this changes

On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` the engine has neither a clock (`Session::now()` is empty) nor a time zone (`local_utc_offset()` is `0`). In a browser build that means Fill & Sign stamps **1 Jan 1970** and `/ModDate` is never written.

The only way to inject a clock today is `with_clock`, which is a test shortcut: it takes the injected instant **as local time** and zeroes the zone. A host that knows both the UTC time and its zone (a browser does: `Date.now()` and `getTimezoneOffset()`) therefore cannot use it. Inject only the clock and you get either the local dates or the UTC ones wrong by the zone's offset — 21:30 in São Paulo (UTC-3) is already the next day in UTC.

This adds `Session::with_wall_clock(clock, utc_offset)` (and `Automation::with_wall_clock` forwarding to it):

- `clock` is the **UTC** instant in seconds — what the file records (`/M`, `/ModDate`, the signing time).
- `utc_offset` is the local zone's seconds east of UTC, **asked on every use**, because the zone changes with daylight saving.
- `today()`, `signing_date()` and `stamp_by_line()` read the offset through one helper (`local_offset`) instead of three copies of `if self.clock.is_some() { 0 } else { local_utc_offset() }`. The precedence is: an injected zone, else `0` under the test clock (already local), else the system's — so **nothing changes for a native build or for `with_clock`**.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine a_wall_clock` — passes. It pins the contrast at 21:30 on 14 Oct 2026 in São Paulo: the stamped day is the 14th, `signing_date` is `D:20261014213000-03'00'`, `now_secs()` stays `00:30Z` on the 15th, a UTC zone gives the 15th, and the plain test clock still answers the 15th (which is why it can't serve a browser).

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-engine -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: feat(automation): Automation::render_pixels returns a page as RGBA, without the PNG round trip
author: bonfim6P
body:
## What this changes

`page_render` only returns PNG. A host that paints the page straight onto a canvas (a browser, a GPU texture) encodes a PNG only to decode it again, on every scroll.

`Automation::render_pixels(doc, page, scale)` returns the page as `(width, height, Pixels)` — RGBA, four bytes a pixel — using the same renderer and the same per-document cache as `page_render`. `scale` is pixels per point (1.0 = 72 dpi). `Pixels` is re-exported from the crate root so a caller can name the type. It validates exactly as the tool does: a finite scale within the tool's dpi limit, a 1-based page that exists, a document that is open.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test automation render_pixels` — passes. It checks the size agrees with `page_render` at 72 dpi, that the buffer is RGBA and not blank, that doubling the scale doubles the width, and each refusal (scale `0`, negative, `NaN`, infinite, past the dpi limit; page `0`, past the end; a document that isn't open).

title: feat(automation): an in-memory disk behind a vfs module, so the tool table runs on wasm32 (RFC)
author: bonfim6P
body:
> **This is a draft, and a request for direction before polish.** It is the most invasive of the three small changes I'd like to upstream (the others are #2317 and #2318), and I'd rather hear whether you want it, and in what shape, than have you review 600 lines you'd have asked me to redo.

## What this changes

On `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `std::fs` compiles and then fails on every call: there is no disk. `pdfcraft-automation`'s tool table reads and writes files in about 40 places (`doc_open`, `doc_save`, `page_insert_file`, the export outputs, the review sidecars…), so a browser host can't use it.

This routes those calls through a new `vfs` module that picks one of two backings:

- **the real disk** (`std::fs`, unchanged) — every native build, by default;
- **an in-memory disk** (path → bytes) — always on for `wasm32`, and, so the layer can be tested natively, behind the `memfs` feature.

A browser host puts the PDF on the in-memory disk, calls the tool, and reads back what it wrote. The whole table works without touching tool by tool. I run the engine this way in a WebAssembly build.

Every call site is a one-for-one swap of `std::fs::*` for `vfs::*`, so a native build behaves as before. Two things that need a real folder switch themselves off on the in-memory disk, with a message that says why: `doc_batch` and `Automation::with_root`. `write_atomic` is a single write there.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --features memfs --lib vfs` — 3 tests: names and bytes round-trip, `.` and `..` resolve by name and can't climb above the root, a folder isn't overwritten by a file, a file can be removed.

title: fix(optimize): reject hostile image dimensions safely
author: earlvanze
body:
## Problem and fix

Optimize could panic when a PDF image declared hostile dimensions: its pixel byte count multiplied unchecked, and conversions could truncate dimensions. Reject invalid, oversized, or unrepresentable dimensions and use checked byte counts before reading image data. The shared pixel reader also protects the image-fragment optimizer, and malformed soft masks leave their parent images unchanged.

Fixes #2178.

## Validation

- Reproduced the original hostile-dimension regression against current main: integer-overflow panic; it passes with this change.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize --profile low-disk --locked -j 2` (25 tests passed).
- Strict Clippy for all optimizer targets, workspace formatting, and the optimizer WASM check passed.
- `xtask layers`, `xtask assets`, and `xtask parity` passed.

  * Improved handling of images and soft masks with invalid, excessively large, or overflowing dimensions, preventing unsafe decoding and preserving affected content during optimization.

author: Hathor875
body:

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a right-hand panel in PDFCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the panel says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside PDFCraft and names this app's world — pages and their order, extract/split/combine/rotate, forms and their fields and tab order, redaction that removes content for good, OCR, headers/footers/watermarks, bookmarks and annotations, PDF/A, compression and export — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (organize pages plan, form field advice, redaction checklist, PDF/A and standards advice, compress and export) are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent menu or panel names — and redaction's irreversibility is said plainly. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

title: fix(oracle): take clippy's as_chunks hint in decode_pam_gray
author: Hathor875
body:
## What this changes

Unblocks CI on `main`. Clippy 1.99 adds `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, and CI runs `-D warnings`, so the ubuntu and windows test jobs have been failing at the **Clippy** step and never reaching their tests. This affects every PR into `main`, including ones that never touch `pdfcraft-oracle`. It landed with the oracle crate itself (`f988cf87` / `0754740f`).

`decode_pam_gray` is the only `chunks_exact(constant)` in the workspace. Taking the suggested `as_chunks::<4>().0` also lets the pixel be destructured as `&[r, g, b, a]` rather than indexed four times through `?`. Those four unwraps were unreachable — `chunks_exact` only yields full chunks — so the new pattern is infallible rather than merely unlikely to fail. `wanted` is `width * height * 4`, hence a multiple of four, so no remainder is dropped and the output is byte-identical.

This is a behaviour-preserving lint fix only. No test, no parity change.

## Never-crash

title: fix(print): the Print dialog waits for the printer list instead of offering Save as PDF (#160)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #160. One cause of "only Save as PDF" in the Print dialog. It doesn't explain every report there; the findings are below.

- **While the first list is read, the dialog says so and Print waits.** The desktop app reads the printer list in the background, so the dialog opens at once. title: Connect MCP tools to the running PdfCraft window
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli mcp` currently owns a separate engine session. An agent cannot fill the form a person already has open in PdfCraft. `mcp --connect FILE` uses the existing authenticated `--control FILE` channel and runs the same automation table on the window's own session. Document ids, resources, edits and Undo refer to the tabs the person sees. New documents open behind their active tab; rendering and stale selections refresh after changes.

The CLI reuses its control-file ownership/permissions checks and sends tokens only to loopback. Both control and MCP remain opt-in. A lost reply is not replayed automatically, because an edit may already have run; the next call reconnects and rereads the control file. Replies are bounded and checked for matching JSON-RPC ids.

MCP adds read-only `ui_state`, `ui_inspect` and `ui_screenshot`, including in compact mode. It does not expose UI input, which would bypass root confinement and human signing consent. The window refuses tools while a text/comment draft or edit dialog is open. MCP inspection uses protected `tool.inspect`; private signing/password views cannot be inspected or captured through the bridge; password-node values are omitted.

The agent prepares, the person signs. Connected tools refuse all `sign_*`, signature/initials placement, reusable signature-image export, redaction application and tab closure, also through command wrappers. Signing credentials are rejected before relay and again at the window dispatch boundary. Signature fields, ordinary text/dates and redaction marks may be prepared; the person signs or confirms redaction in the app. Existing headless signing remains unchanged.

The automation runner is supplied by the desktop binary, preserving crate layering: ui-egui has no dependency on automation. No provider client, model key, new listener or automatic MCP registration is added.

title: feat(automation): bookmarks and links say where on the page they go
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`bookmark_list` and `link_list` say which page a bookmark or link goes to, but not where on it. An agent checking a table of contents, or rebuilding bookmarks after an edit, can't tell "top of page 2" from "the heading halfway down page 2", and a link through a named destination only gives the name.

Each bookmark row and in-document link now carries `destination`:

| Destination | `destination` |
|---|---|
| `[page /XYZ left top zoom]` | `{"fit": "XYZ", "left", "top", "zoom"}` |
| `/Fit`, `/FitB` | `{"fit": "Fit"}` |
| `/FitH top`, `/FitBH top` | `{"fit": "FitH", "left": null, "top"}` |
| `/FitV left`, `/FitBV left` | `{"fit": "FitV", "left", "top": null}` |
| `/FitR` | `{"fit": "FitR", "rect"}` |

Plumbing: `pdfcraft_organize` reads the explicit destination array behind an explicit, `/D` or named destination (`explicit_dest`, replacing `page_of_dest`) and keeps its type and numbers in `Bookmark::view`; the engine passes it through `BookmarkRow`.

title: fix(engine): a new or recovered document stays unsaved through undo
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Narrowed after #1435.** This PR first fixed #1310, #1311 and #1312. #1435 (bartalos86) landed a fix for the same three issues today, and three of this PR's four tests pass on `main` as it is, so I've dropped that part. #1310–#1312 can be closed against #1435.

What's left is the case #1435 doesn't cover, and it can lose a whole document:

- **A new or recovered document became clean after undo.** `sync_dirty` calls a document clean when its bytes are the ones last "saved". For a new document (Combine, Extract, Create) or one restored from recovery, those are the bytes it was opened from, which were never written where the document belongs. So edit → Undo made it clean: Close didn't ask to save, and autosave stopped keeping it, so the whole combined or recovered document could be discarded without a prompt.
- **The fix.** `Editor::unsaved_file` is set by `open_new` and `mark_recovered`, and cleared by `mark_saved`. While it's set, the document stays unsaved whatever undo or Revert brings back. Revert now derives `dirty` from the same rule instead of always clearing it.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-engine -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine -j 2`
- [x] New `undo_never_makes_an_unsaved_document_clean`. A combined document stays unsaved after edit + Undo (and still gets a recovery snapshot) and after Revert. A recovered document stays unsaved after edit + Undo. Once saved, undo back to the saved state is clean.
- [x] Seen to fail: with `unsaved_file` left out of `sync_dirty`, the first assertion fails.

## Never-crash / Security

- [x] No new `unwrap`/indexing; one boolean on the editor.

title: fix(ui): on macOS, dragging a tab moves the tab, not the window
author: tisca26
body:
## What this changes

On macOS, dragging a document tab to reorder it (#1551) moved the whole window instead. The tab reordering itself worked; the drag just never reached the app. It happens with a held click and with three-finger drag on the trackpad, in v0.8.0.

**Cause.** On macOS the tab strip is the title bar: a transparent title bar over a full-size content view (`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`). For a press in that band, AppKit asks the view under the pointer whether it can move the window (`mouseDownCanMoveWindow`), and NSView answers YES for any view that isn't opaque. winit's `WinitView` doesn't override it, so AppKit started a window drag before egui saw the event. #1551 was verified on Windows, where this doesn't apply.

**Fix.** `vendor/winit` now answers `mouseDownCanMoveWindow` with the window's own `movable_by_window_background` attribute: NO unless an app asked for it (PdfCraft doesn't). PdfCraft already moves the window itself when the drag starts on the strip's empty background (`ViewportCommand::StartDrag` in `chrome.rs`), so that keeps working, and so does double-click to maximize. The value is passed to the view the same way `accepts_first_mouse` is, so it needs no `unsafe` call. Documented as winit patch (12) in `vendor/README.md`.

## How you verified it

On macOS 27.0.1 (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, on `ac89a11`:

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft -j 4 --all-targets -- -D warnings`

By hand with three PDFs open: dragging a tab (held click and three-finger drag) reorders it and the window stays put; dragging the empty part of the strip still moves the window.

author: amoisttowe1
body:

## The gap this fills

`crates/crypt/src/tests.rs` already covers this handler well: the #1185 password contract, the
owner-upgrade path (the engine half of #1762), Algorithm 7 recovery, Table 22 permission bits, and the
`/O`, `/U` and file keys that **qpdf (their published vectors, and our own from qpdf core 12.2.0) wrote for real files**. There is already one property test,
`malformed_dictionaries_never_panic`. This PR does not re-cover any of that.

Two dimensions were open:

1. **Payload length.** Upstream's encrypted round trips run three shapes — a 30-byte text and a

title: crypt: authenticate against encryption numbers qpdf wrote (plus one hand-derived vector)
author: amoisttowe1
body:
Test-only. Adds `crates/crypt/tests/qpdf_literals.rs`: three tests, seven vectors. Six quote encryption
dictionaries written by qpdf core 12.2.0 through pikepdf 9.11; the seventh is hand-derived from
ISO 32000-1 at revision 3 with `/Length` 40. Nothing else in the repository changes — this commit is
comments plus one assertion message, its parent is the reviewed head `cdbce8a`, and the push is a
fast-forward.

**Why it matters.** `create()` and `open()` share one key derivation, so a wrong-but-self-consistent
implementation round-trips cleanly. Deleting Algorithm 2 step f from `crates/crypt/src/lib.rs:393` leaves
all 17 unit tests green (`rc=0`) and fails these rows instead, with `#2358`'s property failing alongside
them. Outside numbers test conformance; round trips test only self-agreement. Every R3/R4 vector already
in the repository uses a 16-byte key, so `/Length`/n truncation is invisible in all of them; the
metadata-plain pairing shows step f's four `FF` bytes from outside, and it is the only such case here.

**Reproduction.** One blank 200×200 page, `Encryption(owner=OWNER, user=USER, allow=Permissions(extract=False), R=n)`
then `save(static_id=True)`; read `/Encrypt`. Below R=4 both `aes=False` and `metadata=False` must be
forced — pikepdf checks metadata first (`Cannot encrypt metadata when R < 4`), then AES. Revisions 2 and
3 reproduce as whole files, byte-identical across two days (`63f2d95b…`, `39afbdd5…`). Revision 4
reproduces all eight dictionary fields; its file differs by exactly one 32-byte stream, a fresh AES-CBC IV
(ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4). Revision 6 reproduces structurally, with fresh salts per run; the fixtures its two
rows were copied from were overwritten before archiving, so those rows rest on internal consistency plus
this record. A re-captured pair with retained artifacts can be added on request.

**Not verified here.** Authentication never reads `/Perms`: a corrupted one fails only this file's own
decrypt. No assertion pins crypt-filter nam…

`pdfcraft_platform::mail` from #2375. Nothing is sent by PdfCraft: the message opens in the email

  set up, it didn't open a message in time, it couldn't log on, or what it said. It offers **Open
  message and show file** (a new message with the subject, through the `mailto:` address, and the

  It never fails silently.

title: Fix util.printd panic on an escaped multi-byte character
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/lib.rs:785` (no existing issue): util.printd panics on a backslash-escaped multi-byte character in the format string.

## Cause
In `util.printd`, the `\` escape branch copied only the first byte after the backslash (`b[i + 1] as char`) and always moved forward by 2 bytes. With a multi-byte UTF-8 character such as 'é' or '€', this wrote the wrong character and left the index in the middle of the character. The next `fmt[i..]` slice then panicked, so the script stopped with an internal error.

## Fix
The escape branch now reads the whole character after the backslash, pushes it, and moves forward by `1 + ch.len_utf8()`. A regression test covers escaped 2-byte, 3-byte and ASCII characters.

## Verified
- Regression test `printd_escapes_multibyte_chars`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js --lib printd_escapes_multibyte_chars`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The other format branches of `printd` and the default branch, which already handles multi-byte characters, are unchanged.

title: Reject impossible dates such as Feb 30 in FormCalc Date2Num and Parse
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:1916` (no existing issue): FormCalc Date2Num accepts impossible dates such as Feb 30 and rolls them into the next month instead of returning 0.

## Cause
FormCalc's `parse_date` only checked that the day was between 1 and 31, without comparing it to the length of the month or allowing for leap years. `Date2Num`, `IsoDate2Num` and `Parse` therefore accepted dates like 2023-02-30, and `days_from_civil` moved the extra days into the next month (2023-02-30 became 2023-03-02) instead of returning 0 or null.

## Fix
`parse_date` now checks the day against a new `days_in(y, m)` helper, which matches the one in the AcroForm date parser and handles leap years. Impossible dates now make Date2Num return 0 and Parse return null, while real month ends like 2024-02-29 still work.

## Verified
- Regression test `date2num_rejects_days_past_the_end_of_the_month`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js --lib date2num_rejects_days_past_the_end_of_the_month`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The AcroForm date parser in crates/forms/src/af.rs already rejects these dates and was not changed. `days_from_civil` and the date formatting code were also left alone.

title: Issue #2364: an incremental save of a PDF with bytes before its header counts offsets from the header
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2364

## Root cause
A file with bytes before its `%PDF-` header counts its cross-reference offsets from the header: Acrobat, qpdf, Poppler and MuPDF all read such a file that way, and so does the file's own `/Prev`. `write_incremental` wrote the new objects, the new section and `startxref` as absolute file positions next to that header-relative `/Prev`, so qpdf reported `xref not found` and Poppler `Syntax Error: Illegal character`, and both rebuilt the table. Our own reader tries both conventions, which is why the saved file still opened here.

## Fix
`Document::offset_base` is the header offset for a file that has a cross-reference chain (0 for most files); `write_incremental` subtracts it from every offset it writes, for a classic table and for a cross-reference stream. A full save is unaffected (it writes a new file without the prefix).

## Tests
`crates/cos/tests/writer.rs::incremental_save_of_a_prefixed_file_counts_offsets_from_the_header`: a 128-byte prefix before a one-page file with a classic table, and before the same file saved in full with a cross-reference stream. After an Info edit and an incremental save, `startxref` + prefix lands on the new section, the new entry for the Info object + prefix lands on `3 0 obj`, `/Prev` is the original `startxref`, and the result reads back with two revisions and the edit. Fails on `main` at the `startxref` assertion. The saved files from both cases also open in Poppler (`pdfinfo`) with no warning; before the fix Poppler reported `Syntax Error (725): Illegal character '>'`.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos` (74 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean, on a Linux (WSL) build host.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #2365: a rebuilt file keeps the /Info and /ID of its cross-reference stream
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2365

## Root cause
The fixture is two PDFs concatenated: the second is cut off before its own cross-reference data, so no `startxref` is within reach of the tail and the file is rebuilt from object headers. The rebuild takes its trailer from the last `trailer` dictionary with a usable `/Root`, and a file written with cross-reference streams has no `trailer` keyword at all, so it fell through to "the catalog alone": `/Info` (and `/ID`, `/Encrypt`) were dropped. That is why Document Properties showed the fields empty before the save and a full save wrote only the edited `/Subject` and `/ModDate`.

## Fix
`reconstruct()` remembers the offset of every scanned object whose dictionary mentions `/XRef`, parses those, and treats each `/Type /XRef` stream dictionary with a usable `/Root` as a trailer candidate alongside the `trailer` dictionaries; the one latest in the file wins, as before. The keys a cross-reference stream's dictionary carries for itself (`/Type`, `/W`, `/Index`, `/Filter`, `/DecodeParms`, `/Length`) are dropped from the rebuilt trailer, as the chain readers drop them (a save writes its own).

## Tests
`crates/cos/src/document.rs::reconstruction_takes_the_trailer_from_a_cross_reference_stream`: a full save with object streams (its only trailer is a cross-reference stream), then a second file of 5 KB appended without cross-reference data. Opening rebuilds; `/Info` and `/ID` are in the trailer, the Info `/Title` reads, and a full save after setting `/Subject` keeps `/Title` and `/Creator`. On `main` the trailer has only `/Root`.

Verified on the issue's fixture (`openpreserve-format-corpus/jhove-errors/PDF-HUL-138/6.2017-0960.pdf`, SHA-256 `a299…22`): before, the rebuilt trailer was `<< /Root 254 0 R >>`; after, `/Info 284 0 R` resolves to Creator `Word`, Producer, CreationDate and ModDate, and a full save after a `/Subject` edit keeps them all.

title: Issue #2367: an object stream whose entry cannot place it is found by its header
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2367

## Root cause
In qpdf's `xref-compressed-in-compressed.pdf` the cross-reference stream says object stream 69 (which holds the outlines, object 70, and the page labels, 82) is itself compressed inside stream 81. The format forbids that, and 81 does not exist. `Document::objstm` loaded a container only through its cross-reference entry, so the lookup failed, every object inside read as `Null`, and a full save (which rewrites the reachable objects) wrote `/Outlines null /PageLabels null`. An incremental save copies the original bytes, which is why it kept them; MuPDF recovers them by scanning.

## Fix
When the container's entry cannot load it as a stream, `objstm` finds it by its own `N G obj` header with `scan_for`, the same last resort a plain object with a wrong offset already has (decrypted the same way). Nothing changes for files whose entries work.

## Tests
`crates/cos/src/document.rs::an_object_stream_marked_as_compressed_is_found_by_its_header`: a hand-built file with a cross-reference stream whose row for the object stream says "in stream 99" (nonexistent) and whose catalog's `/Outlines` lives in that object stream. Opening reads the chain without repair; object 4 is the Outlines dictionary, and a full save reopened still resolves `/Outlines` to it. On `main` object 4 reads as `Null`.

Verified on the issue's fixture (`qpdf/qtest/qpdf/xref-compressed-in-compressed.pdf`, SHA-256 `c990…c2`): before, objects 70 and 82 were `Null` and the full save had no outlines or page labels; after, 70 is the Outlines dictionary (Count 6), 82 the PageLabels tree (12 ranges), and a full save keeps both.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos` (75 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean, on a Linux (WSL) build host.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #2366: a trailer whose /Prev is a reference still reaches the earlier sections
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2366

## Root cause
`JA3-1998-PDF.pdf` (and `JA1-1996-PDF.pdf`; both `tiff2pdf` output, JHOVE's PDF-HUL-157 cases) ends its first trailer with `/Prev 297298 0 R`: the offset of the earlier cross-reference section written as a reference. `read_xref_chain` took `/Prev` as an integer only, so the chain ended after the first section without a note, and every object of the earlier section — pages 2–4 (objects 1, 4, 7) and their images — read as `Null`. That is the "one page where both readers find four" in the report. A full save then wrote the three missing kids as `null` (`/Kids [5 0 R null null null] /Count 4`), which is what MuPDF reports as a page-tree cycle and Poppler renders as 1×1 (Poppler: `Kid object (page 2) is not an indirect reference (null)`). The incremental control kept the original bytes, so other readers could still reconstruct them.

## Fix
`prev_offset`, used by both chain readers (`read_xref_chain` and `read_xref_chain_materialized`, since #1505): a reference-valued `/Prev` is read as the offset it names, with a repair-log note (`the trailer at 119 gives /Prev as the reference 297298 0 R; reading it as offset 297298`); the section there is still validated as before, so a wrong value just ends the chain. Any other non-offset `/Prev` is noted too instead of being dropped silently.

## Tests
`crates/cos/src/document.rs::a_prev_written_as_a_reference_still_reaches_the_earlier_sections`: a one-page file with an incremental update whose trailer says `/Prev <offset> 0 R`, against the same update with a numeric `/Prev`: both open with two revisions, the page of the first section has the same entry and reads as a Page, the update's Info reads, and the reference form leaves one repair-log line. On `main` the reference form has one revision and the page is `Null`.

Verified on the issue's fixture (`openpreserve-format-corpus/jhove-errors/PDF-HUL-157/JA3-1998-PDF.pdf`, SHA-256 `51b1…2d`): four pages read; after a `/Subject` edit and a full save, `pdfinfo…

title: Issue #2368: flattening keeps a NoRotate widget upright on a rotated page
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2368

## Root cause
An annotation with the `NoRotate` flag (`/F` bit 5) is shown upright on a page with `/Rotate`: its appearance turns with the page about the rectangle's upper-left corner (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.3), and that is how MuPDF and Poppler draw it. `flatten` placed every appearance with Algorithm 8.1 alone (bounding box → `/Rect` as it lies in user space), so on the fixture's `/Rotate 90` page the flattened `NoRotate` widget came out turned with the page and in a different place, while its two neighbours without the flag (drawn the same way before and after) looked unchanged.

## Fix
When the annotation has `NoRotate` and the page (with inherited attributes) has a `/Rotate` of 90, 180 or 270, the placement matrix is followed by that turn about `(x0, y1)` of the rectangle (`upright` in `flatten.rs`). Nothing changes for other annotations or unrotated pages.

## Tests
`crates/edit/src/tests.rs::flattening_keeps_a_no_rotate_widget_upright_on_a_rotated_page`: a plain widget and a `NoRotate` widget sharing one appearance (bbox 100×50 onto a 100×50 rect at (100, 500)) on pages rotated 0, 90, 180 and 270. The plain one is always drawn with `1 0 0 1 100 500 cm`; the `NoRotate` one with the same on 0 and with `0 1 -1 0 150 550`, `-1 0 0 -1 100 600` and `0 -1 1 0 50 550` on 90/180/270 (each keeps the appearance's upper-left corner at (100, 550) and turns it with the page). On `main` all four draw `1 0 0 1 100 500`.

Verified on the issue's fixture (`qpdf/qtest/qpdf/manual-appearances.pdf`, SHA-256 `d1da…cf`), page 2 (`/Rotate 90`, widgets 7 and 8 plain, 9 with `NoRotate`): after flattening the fields and a full save, Poppler's render at 36 dpi differs from the unflattened page by 80 pixels (anti-aliasing of the drawn appearances; the dark-pixel bounding box is identical), against 648 pixels before the fix, when widget 9's box moved.

title: Issue #2352: a CCITT image whose /Rows is 0 decodes to its height, not to nothing
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2352

## Root cause
The scanner writes each page's Group 4 image with `/DecodeParms << /K -1 /Columns 1656 /Rows 0 >>`. `/Rows 0` means "use the image height" (ISO 32000-2 Table 11: the default, 0, means the image's rows are not known in advance; viewers take the image's `/Height`). The vendored `hayro-syntax` (`src/filter/ccitt.rs`) read `/Rows` as written and only fell back to the image height when the key was absent, so it decoded zero rows: an empty image, a white page, both in the app and in `pdfcraft-cli render`, as the reporter found (and confirmed by blanking the key).

## Fix
PdfCraft patch (17) to hayro-syntax: when the image's height is known it takes precedence over `/Rows`, as other viewers do and as upstream hayro's `decode` now does (its `rows` is the image height, else `/Rows`), so the patch goes away at the next bump. `vendor/README.md` records the patch and its test, as the other patches are.

## Tests
`crates/render/tests/ccitt_rows.rs::a_ccitt_image_whose_rows_is_zero_decodes_to_its_height`: an 8 × 4 Group 4 strip made by ghostscript's `tiffg4` device (left half black), drawn as a 1-bit `DeviceGray` image over a page of its size, with `/Rows 4`, `/Rows 0` and no `/Rows`; rendered through `PageRenderer` at 1:1, pixel (1, 1) is black and (6, 1) white in all three. On `main` the `/Rows 0` case fails ("the left half is black": it renders white).

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --test ccitt_rows`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` clean, on a Linux (WSL) build host.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #2385: audit finds thick strokes, black highlights and white boxes over text
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2385

## What was missed
`pdfcraft-cli audit` took covers only from `re` rectangles and rectangular `m`/`l` paths filled with an opaque non-stroking colour, and from `/Redact` annotations. The report's three other ways of hiding text that a reader sees as redacted were reported clean (`count: 0`, exit 0) while the text stayed extractable:

| cover | now |
|---|---|
| `0 G 20 w 70 705 m 400 705 l S` (thick black stroke, "marker") | `covered-text`, rect `[70 695 400 715]` |
| `/Subtype /Highlight /C [0 0 0]` annotation over the text | `covered-text` |
| `1 g 70 695 330 20 re f` (white filled rectangle) | `hidden-under-white` (new kind) |

## Fix
- `cover.rs`: the walker also tracks the stroking colour (`G`/`RG`/`K`), the line width (`w`) and the stroking alpha (`/CA`). A single `m`/`l` segment along one axis, stroked opaquely (`S`, `s`, or `B`/`B*` with the fill), counts as the rectangle it paints: the segment widened by half the line width each side, the width taken through the CTM's scale. Slanted or bent strokes and stroked rectangles (outlines) are not covers; the module docs say so.
- `lib.rs`: the annotation pass reads `/Highlight` annotations too (colour from `/C` in gray/RGB/CMYK, `/CA` default 1, Hidden and NoView skipped); an opaque one whose contrast against the text is below the existing 3.0 threshold is a `covered-text` finding, like a filled rectangle would be. Yellow or translucent highlights are not flagged.
- A new `FindingKind::HiddenUnderWhite` (`hidden-under-white`): an opaque cover painted after the text whose relative luminance is ≥ 0.9 (white is 1.0; the `0.9 g` table shading of the existing test is 0.79 and stays unflagged) hides dark text as completely as a black one, the way forms are whited out. It is reported apart, as the report suggests, so callers can decide; a white marker stroke falls under it too.

title: fix(preflight): follow colour spaces to the device space they draw in
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

`pdfa_verify` and `pdfa_convert` now follow a colour space to the device space it actually draws in. Before, a device space that reached the page through a colour space, rather than through an operator or a bare `/ColorSpace /DeviceCMYK`, was missed. A spot colour with a DeviceCMYK alternate or an indexed image over DeviceCMYK was given an sRGB output intent and then passed verification. Fixes #2411.

This is the follow-up #2260 listed as out of scope, rebased on `main` now that #2260 has landed.

- **One function follows colour spaces** (`colour_space`): a device name is marked; an Indexed or Pattern space follows its base, and a Separation or DeviceN space its alternate. The depth is bounded (`MAX_SPACE_DEPTH`), so a cyclic or absurd chain of references stops. `[/DeviceRGB]` written as an array counts too. CIE-based and ICC-based spaces are not device colour.
- **It is applied wherever a colour space appears:**
  - an image's or a shading's own `/ColorSpace`. This replaces the bare-name check, so `[/Indexed /DeviceCMYK …]` and `[/Separation … /DeviceCMYK …]` images and shadings now count;
  - an inline image's `/CS`. This replaces the `[/I …]` special case;
  - a `/ColorSpace` resource entry, once content selects it by name with `cs`/`CS` or an inline image's `/CS /CS0`.
- **A resource entry counts only once something selects it.** Content collects the names it selects. After the content pass, those names are looked up in every resource dictionary. A space the resources merely list is not used.
- **The reading behind Separation/DeviceN alternates (ISO 19005-2 §6.2.4.3–6.2.4.4):** a device alternate needs the same output intent as the device space used directly. §6.2.4.3 limits every use of a device space and makes no exception for alternates. §6.2.4.4 requires same-named Separations to agree on their alternate, which treats the alternate as part of the colour's definition. author: wstock

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` but not `cargo xtask parity`, so a merge that leaves `parity/acrobat-features.toml` invalid passes every check — which is how `main` ended up with the duplicate keys of #2415.
