title: M11: linearized save for Fast Web View (#2645)
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2645.

PdfCraft can now save a linearized PDF, which Acrobat calls Fast Web View: a reader fetching the file over HTTP can show page 1 before the rest arrives. Parity `core.linearization` (P1) moves from planned to partial.

**cos** (`crates/cos/src/writer/linearize.rs`, new): `SaveOptions::linearize` lays a full rewrite out per ISO 32000-2 Annex F:
- linearization parameter dictionary, first-page cross-reference section and trailer
- catalog and document-level objects, then the primary hint stream (page offset, shared object and outline hint tables)
- the first page and everything it reaches, each later page with the objects only it reaches, the objects later pages share, everything else, then the main cross-reference section

Inheritable page attributes move from the page tree onto the pages. A dictionary or array several pages inherit becomes one shared object. Encryption keeps working: every object, the hint stream included, is encrypted with its new number. `is_linearized(bytes)` tells a linearized file from one an update was later appended to.

**engine / automation:**
- `Session::save_linearized_bytes`
- `doc_save` takes `linearize` (a full rewrite; refused for signed documents, like any full rewrite)
- `doc_optimize` takes `fast_web_view` (off by default, so Reduce File Size keeps writing compressed object streams)
- `doc_info` reports `linearized`

**Not in this PR:** a desktop control (Save As option, Optimizer checkbox, "Fast Web View: Yes" in Document Properties). Each new label would touch all 22 catalogs, so it is better as a small follow-up.

author: mtlcl410

title: M10: Windows without the print DLLs still starts (#2630)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2630 (and its earlier report #2360). `pdfcraft.exe` and `pdfcraft-cli.exe` import `windows.data.pdf.dll` (`PdfCreateRenderer`, through craft-print → winprint) and `prntvpt.dll` (PrintTicket) at load time. Trimmed Windows installations (NTLite) can lack them, and then the loader refuses to start the program at all — "windows.data.pdf.dll cannot be found" — even though only printing needs them.

- **Build** (`apps/pdfcraft{,-cli}/build.rs`, MSVC targets only): `/DELAYLOAD` both DLLs plus `delayimp.lib`, via `rustc-link-arg-bins`. They now load on the first print.
- **Runtime** (`crates/print/src/spool.rs`): a call into a missing delay-loaded DLL would end the process, so `printers()`, `submit` and `submit_with_progress` first check that both exist in `%SystemRoot%\System32`. Without them the printer list is empty and a job fails with "printing needs windows.data.pdf.dll, which this Windows installation lacks; use Save as PDF instead". When the system folder is unknown, nothing changes (the loader decides, as before). `printers` is now a wrapper instead of a re-export; its signature is unchanged.

The fix stays in this repo: craft-print and winprint are untouched. PhotoCraft has the same report (storytold/photocraft#6249) and could do the same.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`; clippy `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-print`, `pdfcraft`, `pdfcraft-cli` (Windows) and `pdfcraft-print` (`--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`)

title: Remove security also from files with /Encrypt inline in the trailer
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2661.

MuPDF writes the `/Encrypt` dictionary inline in the trailer. Removing it there changes no object, so `Document::is_modified()` stayed false after Remove security, and the engine took the document as unedited: the refresh after the edit, and `save_bytes`, reused the original, still-encrypted bytes, which then failed to reopen without a password. With an indirect `/Encrypt` (our files, qpdf/pikepdf) `remove_encryption` frees the object, which is why those worked. The fix counts a security change as an unsaved edit in `is_modified()`; the writer already handled the inline case correctly. Probably also what #1762 hit, though that one has no details.

Validation:
- `crates/cos/tests/encryption.rs` `removing_an_inline_encrypt_dictionary_leaves_an_unencrypted_file` (all four algorithms): fails on main (`removing security is an unsaved change`), passes here
- `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` `remove_security_from_a_file_with_its_encrypt_dictionary_in_the_trailer`: fails on main (`Reopen("the document is protected by a password")`, the error in the issue), passes here
- Both build their fixture by moving our own `/Encrypt` dictionary into the trailer, so no MuPDF output is committed; I also checked by hand that a PyMuPDF AES-256 file goes through `doc_unprotect` now.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos --test encryption`, the engine protection/security tests, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Go to page brings the page into view horizontally too
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #2665: the Go to page half. What Fit width should fit in continuous layout (the current page, as Acrobat does) is left for its own ticket, as the triage comment suggested.

When the page view consumes a `goto` it only set the vertical scroll offset, so the horizontal one stayed where it was. Next to a very wide page the normal pages sit far to one side, and going to one changed the counter while the page stayed out of sight. Now the page is brought into view horizontally too: a page that already shows whole, or that fills the window's width, keeps the scroll (so paging through a zoomed-in document stays on the same column); otherwise a page that fits is centred, and a wider one is scrolled just far enough to fill the window. Centring is a judgement call, happy to switch to the smallest scroll that reveals the page if you prefer.

This touches every `goto` (page turns, layout and fit changes), but in a document whose pages all show whole nothing moves.

Validation:

title: fix(edit): keep the right edge of a right-aligned one-row paragraph (#2582)
author: Hathor875
body:
Closes #2582

## What this changes

Part of #2582 — see the caveat at the end, which is the important part.

A one-row paragraph aligned to the right margin, or level with other text's right
edge, kept its **left** edge when words were added to it. The longer text ran past
the edge it was aligned to, and then wrapped into whatever column was left over —
the "six rows in a 126pt column" from the report.

Such a row is now recognised as right-aligned and keeps its right edge, growing
leftwards and wrapping every row to that same edge. The machinery already existed
for right-to-left text (`anchored_right`); this extends it to left-to-right rows
that carry the evidence.

- **Detection needs evidence from the page.** Either the right edge sits on the
  right margin, or it lines up with another row's right edge while the row's own
  left edge lines up with nothing.
- **A row with neither keeps growing right from its left edge, as before.** That is
  deliberate: anchoring a left-aligned row on the wrong edge would move text in
  documents that are already correct, which is a worse failure than the one being
  fixed.
- **The tolerance is a few points, not the text size.** The house precedent in
  `rewrite_styled_block` uses the text size for its centred-paragraph test, but there
  the size is compared against other rows *in the same block*. Here it is compared
  against the whole page, and the size comes from the document: a font stated at
  100pt would otherwise swallow every row on the page. `an_oversized_font_does_not_
  make_every_row_look_right_aligned` is the regression test.
- **A turned row is never treated as right-aligned.** Its edges are not horizontal.
  The angle comes out of `atan2`, so the test is an epsilon rather than an exact
  zero.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`pdfcraft-edit`, all targets)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed (`pdfcraft-edit`, 136 tests)

title: fix(comments): Add a text box takes a drag that sizes the box
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #2669 (point 3, the text box drag). The other four points are untouched; this is independent of #2704, which takes another point of the same issue.

Add a text box only reacted to `resp.clicked()` in `comments::page_input`, and the composer always sized the box with `text_box_rect` from the click point, so a drag did nothing. Now, as in Acrobat, a drag draws the box (shown while you drag) and the posted box keeps that size, measured in the page's view space so it lands where it was drawn with the view turned too (View ▸ Rotate View). The text wraps to the drawn width inside the padding and border its appearance uses. If the text needs more lines than the drawn height, the box grows down and moves up as needed to stay on the page; when even the whole page height is not enough, it keeps the drawn size and the text is clipped, as the appearance already does. A click, or a drag of a few pixels, still gives the box sized to its text as before. Growing rather than clipping is my call; happy to switch if you'd rather keep the drawn height exactly.

title: fix(forms): correct qualified-name validation and reconstruction on rename
author: Ratstack2
body:
## What this changes

Fixes two bugs in AcroForm field renaming involving fully qualified field names.

These bugs were discovered while investigating #2696, but are independent of the field-creation and UI-display problems reported there.

### 1. Incorrect duplicate-name validation

Previously, `set_props` compared a proposed partial field name against other fields' fully qualified names.

This caused two problems:

- Renaming `MASTER.first` to `last` succeeded even when `MASTER.last` already existed, producing duplicate fully qualified names.
- An unrelated top-level field named `middle` incorrectly prevented renaming `MASTER.last` to `middle`, even though `MASTER.middle` was available.

The fix validates the fully qualified name the field would have after renaming.

### 2. Incorrect full-name reconstruction

Previously, `set_props` reconstructed a field's resulting name by splitting its old full name at the last period.

This fails for malformed PDFs whose own `/T` contains a literal period, such as `ADDRESS.street`. ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.2 prohibits periods in partial field names, but such documents can still occur.

Renaming this field to `street1` could update `/T` while reporting the incorrect name `ADDRESS.street1`, causing the subsequent redraw operation to fail with `NoSuchField`.

A malformed non-text `/T`, such as `/T 5`, could trigger the same issue.

The fix derives the parent prefix from the walked field name and the field's actual `/T`, matching the existing `fields()` traversal behavior.

Renaming a field to its existing name remains a no-op.

### Relationship to #2696

**Related to #2696; this PR does not resolve it.**

Specifically, this PR does not:

- Implement creation of dotted field names such as `MASTER.account_firstname` through a proper parent/child hierarchy.
- Change how fully qualified field names are displayed in the UI.
- Change `add_field` or implement broader field hierarchy construction.

Those user-facing requests remain open.

Fixes the blank first page of #2676. It is not the Windows update: the cause is in `cos`.

The reporter's scan (`Test Print.pdf`, attached to the issue) has a classic xref table headed `1 10` whose first row is object 0's free entry (`0000000000 65535 f`), so every row is one number off: object 1 — page 1's 2544×3296 JPEG — reads as free. With the fix, the print-ready PDF and a full save of the reporter's file keep both images, and page 1 renders.

title: fix(ui): saving keeps a turned view as the pages' /Rotate (#2674)
author: cortenburg28-arch
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2674 ("pdfcraft not saving after page rotate", Windows 11).

**Reproduction.** Every *page*-rotate path already saves: `page.rotate` / `page.rotate_ccw`, the Organize buttons, Rotate Pages… and the `page_rotate` automation tool all mark the document dirty and write `/Rotate`, both for an in-place incremental save and for Save As, and the value survives a reopen. I checked this headlessly, including an inherited `/Rotate` on the page tree. What doesn't save is the **view** rotation: View ▸ Rotate View, Ctrl+Shift+Plus / Minus, and the rotate button in the page toolbar (the only rotate control on the main view). They turned the display only. The document stayed clean, Save wrote nothing new, and the file reopened upright. That matches the report.

**Fix (ui-egui only).**
- `DocView::unsaved_turn(doc)` returns the view's turn when it is non-zero and the document allows page changes.
- A turned view now counts as unsaved work: the tab's dirty dot, the close and quit prompts (`has_unsaved_work`), and the on-disk-change reload guard.
- Before the bytes are taken, Save and Save As (native and wasm) apply one undoable **Rotate Pages** edit to every page by the view's turn. They then set the view back upright, so the page looks the same and the file opens the way it was shown. If that edit fails, nothing is written and the user is told why.
- A document that refuses page changes keeps the turn display-only, as before.

This departs from Acrobat, whose turned view is never saved; whether PdfCraft should do this is an open question (see the end of this description). The `view.rotate-view` parity entry no longer claims "without changing the file", and its notes say so.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` (`-p pdfcraft-ui-egui`)
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`)

title: fix(edit): keep a one-row centred title centred when it grows (#2581)
author: Hathor875
body:
Closes #2581

## What this changes

Fixes #2581. A one-row centred title (centre 306) lost its centring when edited: it kept its left edge and grew rightwards (centre drifted to 398.025), and wrapped rows all started at that old edge. The single-style path stretches width to the page's right margin, and centring detection needed several ragged rows, so a one-row title was never recognised. A new `is_centred` helper (`text_regions.rs`) is the single source of truth for both paths; a centred block with no explicit width or alignment is centred in the box it already sits in.

title: M3: closing PdfCraft while minimized no longer saves a 0 x 0 window
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Closing PdfCraft while it is minimized (from the taskbar's "Close window", Alt+F4 on the taskbar button, or a sign-out) saved a window the next start could hardly use. eframe stores the window's settings just before `App::save`, from the window as it is then; Windows reports a minimized window as 0 × 0 at (-32000, -32000). egui-winit then opens the next start at its 64-point floor (`clamp_size_to_sane_values`) and clamps the position into the screen's corner. Found while testing on a 6K display at 225%: a 172 × 223 px window at (0, 0), and the 820 × 520 minimum size did not apply to the restored size. Reproduced on current main by minimizing and closing.

- `window_state::WindowState` (desktop only) remembers the settings eframe stored while the window was shown, starting from those it started with. In `App::save`, while the window is minimized, it puts them back; if there are none, it removes the entry so the next start opens at the default size.
- On the first frame whose size is known, a shown window at egui's floor in both directions (only reachable from such settings) gets 1440 × 920 points, at most nine tenths of the monitor, and the broken settings it started with are dropped. So people who already have such settings get a usable window once.
- `apps/pdfcraft` seeds the state from `cc.storage`. Nothing changes for a window closed while shown.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo check -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (no new warnings)

title: Layers panel: Reset to Initial Visibility
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Layers panel: Reset to Initial Visibility

The Layers panel now has a "…" Layer options menu with Reset to Initial Visibility, as in Acrobat's Layers options menu. It puts every layer back to how the file opens: the default configuration in `/OCProperties /D`, meaning BaseState, then `/ON`, then `/OFF`, which wins. This is the same rule the panel already uses when a file opens, and it covers layers that came in through Insert Pages. It brings back the file's own state, so it doesn't enforce radio-button groups, and it acts only on the active document. Layer visibility is view state here, as for the panel's toggles and set-layer-visibility actions, so a reset doesn't mark the document changed and doesn't add an Undo step. Like the opening state, the initial state doesn't read `/Usage /View` or `/AS`. Acrobat's "list layers for all pages / current page" choice in the same menu is left for another PR, so `view.layers-reset` goes to partial. No tool changes layer visibility headless, so there's no reset tool either; `doc_info` now reports each layer's `initial` state next to `visible`. The two new strings are in all 22 catalogs. Happy to switch any wording.

Validation:

title: Extract RTL lines with numbers and punctuation in logical order
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2667

## Cause
`reverse_rtl` only reversed unbroken runs of strong right-to-left glyphs, with at most one blank glyph allowed inside a run. A digit or a neutral mark such as ':' or '.' ended the run, so each Hebrew or Arabic word was reversed on its own. The words themselves stayed in the left-to-right order they were drawn in, and the punctuation stayed at the visual end of the line.

## Fix
`reverse_rtl` now runs a simplified UAX #9 pass over each line's glyphs and word gaps. The line is treated as right-to-left when it has more right-to-left glyphs than left-to-right ones. A separator between digits joins the number, and so does a %/currency sign next to it. A number that follows left-to-right text becomes left-to-right. Neutrals take the direction of the text on both sides, or the line's direction when the sides differ. Then runs are reversed by level, highest first, so numbers keep their left-to-right digit order and word gaps move with the glyphs. A regression test covers Hebrew with a number, Hebrew with punctuation, Arabic with a decimal number, and a left-to-right line with one Hebrew word.

## Verified
- Regression test `rtl_line_with_number_and_punctuation_reads_in_logical_order`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib rtl_line_with_number_and_punctuation_reads_in_logical_order`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Glyph mirroring for brackets (N0/L4), explicit embeddings, and the difference between Arabic-Indic and European digits (AN vs EN) are not modelled. Lines with no right-to-left text keep their order.

author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What does it change?

The Finder half of #2541 (#585): **"Combine files in PdfCraft" under Finder's right-click ▸ Quick Actions** on macOS. Select PDFs or pictures, choose it, and Combine files opens with them listed in order, in the running PdfCraft or a new one. Nothing is combined until Combine is pressed, as on Windows and Linux.

This branch is stacked on #2541 (`pr/combine-right-click`): the diff shows both until that one merges. Its own change is one new file, `apps/pdfcraft/src/finder_combine.rs` (409 lines, 4 tests), and three lines in `main.rs` and `apple_events.rs`.

## Why a Quick Action, and not the other ways

Finder does not start an app with the files as arguments, so the `--combine` route of Explorer and the Linux desktop action does not exist here. The ways that do:

- **A Services provider (`NSServices` in the app's Info.plist + an Objective-C method).** The proper one, but the provider is an Objective-C class with a selector that Finder calls, which means `objc2` and `unsafe`; this workspace forbids `unsafe`, and `fmv_macos_events` (what the app already uses for Apple events) delivers only Open and Quit. Ruled out by the workspace's rule, not by taste.
- **A Finder Sync extension or an app extension (Action extension).** Needs a separate signed extension target and a developer-signed bundle to be loaded; this app ships ad-hoc signed, so it would load for nobody.
- **AppleScript / `osascript` from a Services menu item.** Still needs a Services provider, or a Quick Action.
- **A Quick Action (Automator workflow in `~/Library/Services`).** What macOS offers for exactly this: Finder lists `.workflow` services from that folder, no signing, no extension, no `unsafe`. Its one "Run Shell Script" step receives the selected paths as arguments, writes them one a line to `files.pdfcraft-combine` in a fresh `pdfcraft-combine.*` folder in the user's temporary folder, and runs `open -b ai.storyteller.pdfcraft` on that file. title: M12: Cursor coordinates panel, from the top-left of the page as shown
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
View ▸ Show/Hide ▸ Cursor coordinates shows where the pointer is on the page, as Acrobat's Cursor Coordinates panel does.

Acrobat shows a small panel with the pointer's X and Y, counted from the top-left corner of the page and given in the unit set in Preferences. This PR adds the same panel at the bottom-right of the page view, opposite the page-size hint. The values are in the Preferences unit and are counted in view space, so a shifted crop box, /Rotate and /UserUnit are already taken into account: X/Y measure the page as you see it, not PDF user space. A few choices I couldn't check against Acrobat, so I'm happy to switch any of them:
- with View ▸ Rotate View the axes turn with the page, so X still grows to the right on screen;
- off every page, including the gap between pages, the panel shows dashes instead of the last value;
- whether the panel is shown is remembered across restarts.
It is also the `view.cursor_coordinates` command in the palette and over `ui.command`. There's no automation tool, since it only reads the pointer, the same as `view.page-size-hover`. Line weights, which shared its row in ui-parity.md, are still planned.

title: Keep leading spaces and tabs when wrapping plain text into a PDF
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fonts/src/lib.rs:79 (wrap_with), called from crates/create/src/lib.rs:set_text` (no existing issue): Creating a PDF from plain text drops leading spaces and tabs, so indentation is lost.

## Cause
`wrap_with` split each paragraph on ' ' and used `line.is_empty()` to mean that no word had started the line. A leading space yields an empty first word, so the next word replaced the candidate instead of being appended. Every leading space, and every tab that `set_text` had already expanded to 4 spaces, was dropped.

## Fix
`wrap_with` now tracks whether a word has started the line with a separate `fresh` flag, so leading spaces are kept. When a word is too long for the width, indentation-only text before it is dropped and no whitespace-only line is emitted. One leading space and several therefore behave the same, as they did before.

## Verified
- Regression tests `wrap_keeps_leading_spaces`, `text_keeps_leading_spaces_and_tabs`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts --lib wrap_keeps_leading_spaces && cargo test -p pdfcraft-create text_keeps_leading_spaces_and_tabs`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Wrapping of over-long words on lines without leading whitespace, the CJK measuring path, and tab expansion in `set_text` are unchanged. Over-long words on indented lines now start without the indentation that precedes them, as described above. The output for lines without leading whitespace is unchanged.

title: M4: the Bookmarks panel highlights the current page's bookmark
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The Bookmarks panel now highlights the bookmark of the page you're reading, as Acrobat does.

Acrobat's Bookmarks panel has a "Highlight Current Bookmark" option: as you scroll, the bookmark for the part of the document on screen is highlighted. Here the highlighted bookmark is the last one in document order whose destination is on the current page or an earlier one, so a page between two bookmarks belongs to the earlier one. It moves as the page changes and never expands or collapses anything. Bookmarks with no destination are skipped. When the current bookmark is inside a collapsed one, the collapsed row the reader can see gets the highlight instead. I couldn't confirm that last detail in Acrobat's public docs, so happy to switch if you know it behaves differently. The row uses the panel's existing selected wash and reports itself as selected to accessibility, as page thumbnails already do. One related fix: a bookmark whose action is not GoTo (GoToR, URI, …) no longer reads its /D as a page of this file. Before, a GoToR bookmark pointing at page 1 of another file jumped to page 1 of this one, and it would also have counted as current here; links already made this check. body:
Opening an XFA form appends PdfCraft's own revisions to the working file: the dynamic layout, the field values taken from the XFA data, and what the open scripts change. Signatures were then validated against that working file, so a certified (DocMDP P=2) form opened untouched was reported invalid, "altered since signed (pages added or removed, comments)", before the user had changed anything. This is the symptom the IRCC IMM forms show.

Keep the file as read for a signed document whose opening appended revisions, and validate the signatures against it while the working state is still just the opened one: on open, on trust changes, after undo back to it, and after Revert. Once the user edits or saves, the file Save writes is judged as before, open-time revisions included, so the verdict never hides what saving will write.

Part of storytold/pdfcraft#2759: the false "altered" on open. The trust lists and TSA trust it also asks for are separate problems.

title: M9: sign in the web build with a PKCS #12 file (sign.web-signing)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

The web build (`apps/pdfcraft-web`) can now sign. Until now its Sign dialog had no file picker and its
last step did nothing, so a .p12 could not be used in the browser at all.

- **The same Sign flow as the desktop.** Digitally sign and Certify, visible or invisible, a new or an
  existing field, PAdES B-B (`ETSI.CAdES.detached`). Configure New Digital ID ▸ Browse… opens the
  browser's file picker. The .p12/.pfx (at most 1 MiB) is held in memory for the session, listed as
  `browser:<name>`, and never written to the settings; its password is asked at each signing, as for a
  file on disk. The signed file goes where the web build's saves go: a download
  (`<name>_signed.pdf`), or the embedding page with `?host=parent`.
- **RSA through Web Crypto.** ECDSA P-256/P-384 keys sign in Rust as on the desktop (RustCrypto,
  RFC 6979). RSA keys, which most issued IDs are, sign through the browser's Web Crypto
  (`RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5`, the key imported as not extractable), because ADR-0009 keeps the `rsa` crate to
  verifying (RUSTSEC-2023-0071). Browsers offer Web Crypto only in secure contexts, so RSA signing
  needs HTTPS or localhost and says so in the dialog; ECDSA works anywhere.
- **Signing in two steps (engine).** Web Crypto answers asynchronously, so `Session::signing_request`
  runs the signer with an `ExternalKey` that only records what it is asked to sign (the CMS signed
  attributes), and `Session::complete_signing` checks the value it is handed against the certificate
  and runs the signer again with a key that answers with that value, for exactly those bytes. The
  signing time is pinned in the request, and an edit to the document in between refuses the second
  step. The result is byte for byte the file one-step `Session::sign` writes (tested for RSA and ECDSA).
  ECDSA may come back as DER or raw `r ‖ s`; the file gets DER.
- **Headless: `sign_prepare` / `sign_finish`.** The two steps as tools, for any key PdfCraft can't use
  itself (an …

author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Standards ▸ **Validate structure** checks the open document against the [Arlington PDF Model](https://github.com/pdf-association/arlington-pdf-model), the PDF Association's machine-readable form of ISO 32000-2. It checks the document as it is now, unsaved edits included. The same check is the `structure_validate` automation tool and a new `pdfcraft-cli validate <file.pdf>`, which exits non-zero when there are errors so it fits in CI. Until now `core.arlington-validation` was `planned`, with a reserved but missing `arlington` crate (gap 22).

**New standalone crate `crates/arlington` (L0, no dependencies).** The caller hands the document over through a `Source` trait, so the crate never parses a file. The engine adapts the editor's cos document to it (`crates/engine/src/structure.rs`). Starting from the trailer, the walk follows every key the model links, breadth first, and checks each object against the type its link gives it:

| What | Severity |
|---|---|

| Values have an allowed type. Rectangles have 4 numbers and matrices 6. | error |

| IndirectReference: `TRUE` / `fn:MustBeIndirect` values are references, and `fn:MustBeDirect` ones are not. | error |

| Keys the model doesn't define. A form field merged with its widget shares both key sets. | info |

title: M11: Preflight with profiles, single checks, results, reports and safe fixups (optimize.preflight)
author: guillehr2
body:
**Stacked on #2769, the PDF/X verification PR** (`feat/pdfx-validate`, "M11: verify PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3 and PDF/X-4"): the PDF/X profiles wrap that verifier, so this branch carries its commit too. Review that one first; once it merges, this PR's diff is only the Preflight commit. Both are rebased on `main` at f0c9901c.

## What this changes

PdfCraft gets Preflight: pick a profile, run it over the document, read the results by severity and check, go to each problem, fix what is safe to fix, and save a report. Seven checklist features move from planned to partial: `optimize.preflight`, `optimize.preflight-profiles`, `optimize.preflight-single-checks`, `optimize.preflight-results`, `optimize.preflight-reports`, `optimize.preflight-fix` and `optimize.preflight-single-fixups`.

- **Engine (`pdfcraft_preflight::profiles`, re-exported as `pdfcraft_engine::preflight`):**
  - A `Profile` is a named set of checks, each with a severity (error, warning, information). Profiles and every check's parameters are serde data, so a custom profile is a JSON object; `Profile::validate` refuses what a profile from outside may get wrong (no checks, more than 256, negative or non-finite thresholds, an unknown level or version).
  - `run(doc, profile, host)` returns results grouped by check: status (passed, found, skipped with a reason), and each hit's message (wording and values apart, for translation), 0-based page, object number, box in user space, the verifier's rule id or clause, details, and the fixup that addresses it. Nothing is changed.

body:
> **Stacked on #2769, the PDF/X verification PR** (`feat/pdfx-validate`, "M11: verify PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3 and PDF/X-4 (optimize.pdfx-validate)"). This branch is cut from it and checks each conversion with that verifier. Review and merge that one first; this diff then shrinks to the conversion.

Save as PDF/X ships, and Save as PDF/A learns levels u and a and CMYK output intents. Both work the same way. The conversion runs on a copy of the document, and the copy is kept only when PdfCraft's own verifier then finds nothing. Otherwise the document is left exactly as it was, and the dialog (or the tool) lists what stands in the way. **A file that claims a level and fails it is never written.** That is a behaviour change for Save as PDF/A, which until now wrote the PDF/A identification and left the problems it couldn't fix (a text document with an unembedded Helvetica came out "PDF/A-2b").

Preferences ▸ Documents and view can now show the art, trim and bleed boxes on the page, like Acrobat's "Show art, trim, & bleed boxes".

In Acrobat this is a Page Display preference, off by default. When it's on, every box a page actually defines is outlined on the page, and boxes that only fall back to the crop box are not drawn. title: XFA: explicit data bindings, keep rules, and hiding one row at a time
author: ysrdevs
body:
## Summary

The three XFA leftovers that were worth doing, closing the series on the layout side: explicit data bindings, `keep` rules, and hiding one row of a repeating subform without hiding them all.

### Explicit data bindings (`<bind match="…" ref="…">`)

Designer forms bind fields to data nodes other than their own name more often than the default-binding-only model allowed: a field bound to `$record.header.customer`, a wrapper subform marked "none" so its children bind under the parent, a repeating subform bound to `$record.order.line[*]`, a field bound "global" to the first node of its name. Until now those read nothing and wrote their values under the field's own name, which Acrobat then ignored.

* `model::Bind` (`Once`, `None`, `Global`, `DataRef(ref)`) on every object's `Common`, parsed from `<bind>`.
* `data::Binder` is the one resolver (`data_path(tpl, data, som) -> Option<DataPath>` is its one-call form; it was `data_path(tpl, som) -> DataPath`). It walks the template along the SOM path as before and applies each object's binding: `none` on a subform is transparent (its children bind under the parent's node), `none` on a field is `None` (no data node), `global` finds the first node of the name in the data (by name when there is no data), `dataRef` resolves `$record` (the data's first child; the root subform's name without data), `$data`, `$.`/relative, `[n]`, `[*]` (the instance's own index) and `a..b` (first descendant). Anything the resolver doesn't follow (`$form`, predicates, functions) binds by name with a parse warning, so a value still has somewhere to go. A `Binder` remembers the paths of one layout or live form and indexes the data by element name once, so `global` and `..` lookups don't walk the data per object.
* `Binder::instances` counts a repeating subform's instances at the node it binds to, so a table bound to `order.line[*]` gets one row per `line`; a subform bound to nothing or to one node (no `[*]`) keeps its `occur` count.
* Every …

title: M3: the Pages panel follows the current page
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The Pages panel now follows the current page, so the highlighted thumbnail never stays out of sight.

In Acrobat, when the page changes (scrolling, Page Down, Go to page, a bookmark), the page thumbnails panel scrolls to show the current page's thumbnail. This PR does the same: when the current page changes and its thumbnail is out of view, the panel scrolls just enough to show it. It doesn't recentre on every page change, so a thumbnail already in view, or one you just clicked, stays where it is. A page change while you're dragging thumbnails doesn't move the panel either. Turning the wheel or dragging the scroll bar already beats a scroll-to in egui, and the change then counts as seen, so the panel doesn't jump once you let go. I went with the minimal scroll rather than centring the thumbnail. Happy to switch if you'd rather centre it, as #2781 describes.

Closes #2781

title: M10: preserve component Decode in lossless image export
author: ahmadmuj
body:

Lossless image export and Save Image As now apply each component's Decode pair. For example, `[0, 64, 255]` with `[1 0 0 1 0 1]` exports as `[255, 64, 255]`, instead of `[255, 191, 0]`.

Indexed values map to palette indices, then round and clip. Color-key masks still compare the original samples. Malformed explicit Decode arrays return an error.

Refs #1201. This addresses only lossless image Decode. JPEG and mask Decode, ICC transforms, calibrated colors, and the existing 16-bit high-byte limit remain outside this fix.

- The CLI builds. Both export tools pass 18 exact pixel checks across RGB, gray, and Indexed images before and after save/reopen.
- Rendered page centers match the exported colors. The synthetic fixture passes `qpdf --check`.

- [x] Decode arrays have bounded lengths and finite numeric endpoints. Conversion clips values before integer casts.

## Provenance

- [x] Tests generate original synthetic inputs. No asset or font files are added, and no GPL/AGPL code is copied.

title: fix(organize): preserve page labels across extract, split, and combine (#2670)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Addresses #2670

## Problem
When extracting pages (`extract_pages` / `page_extract`), splitting a document (`split`), or combining documents (`combine`, `combine_selected`, `Combiner`, and `combine_grouped`), the source document's `/PageLabels` number tree was not carried over to the resulting document(s). Extracted, split, or combined documents lost custom page labels (such as Roman front matter `i`, `ii`, `iii` or prefixed section numbers `A-1`, `A-2`) and reverted to default `1, 2, 3...` numbering.

## Root Cause
`extract_pages`, `Combiner`, and `combine_grouped_with` in `crates/organize/src/import.rs` constructed new `Document` instances and copied pages, document info, outlines, attachments, and PDF/X output intents, but never projected or wrote `/PageLabels` ranges from the source document(s) into the output catalog.

## Solution
- Added `collect_page_labels` and `finish_page_labels` (along with shared `push_merged_range` deduplication) in `crates/organize/src/labels.rs` to project each selected run of source pages onto its destination page indices:
  - Preserves each page's resolved style, prefix, and starting number (`first_range.number(src_start)`) at the start of each contiguous source page run, plus any interior range transitions within the run.
  - Coalesces adjacent ranges that continue the previous range's numbering sequence (or share the same prefix under `LabelStyle::None`).
  - Synthesizes an explicit default decimal range (`1, 2, ...`) for unlabelled sources or leading pages prior to the first `/PageLabels` entry when combined with labelled sources so earlier labels do not bleed into unlabelled pages, while leaving outputs untouched when no source carries `/PageLabels`.
- Wired `collect_page_labels` and `finish_page_labels` into `extract_pages` (which also powers `split`), `Combiner::add` / `Combiner::finish_with_renames`, and `combine_grouped_with`.

- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-organize --all-targets …

title: M7: anchor a watermark to an edge or corner, with a distance in page units
author: Byxis
body:
> **Prerequisite:** this branch contains the commit of #1083 (repeat as a grid), which the anchor builds on. Merge #1083 first, or merge this one and #1083 is included with it. #1165 is not needed and not included.

## What this changes

A watermark could only move by an offset from the page centre, in points. A corner placement meant working out half the page minus the mark's size by hand, and it was wrong as soon as page sizes varied.

Acrobat places a mark by a vertical anchor (Top, Center, Bottom) and a horizontal one (Left, Center, Right), plus a distance. This does the same.

- **Engine (`pdfcraft-edit`).** `Watermark::anchor` (`Anchor`, `HorizontalAnchor`, `VerticalAnchor`). Centre/centre, the default, is the old placement exactly. From an edge, the distance is the gap between the page edge and the matching edge of the mark (turned by its rotation), positive inward. From the centre it keeps today's meaning (+x right, +y up). One calculation (`anchored_centre`) feeds drawing, validation and `watermark_centres`.
- **Repeat (#1083).** The anchor places one tile, the one the grid is built from, and the grid repeats outward from it, so a corner anchor puts a whole tile in that corner.
- **Page as shown.** It is measured on the page as displayed, so `/Rotate`, `CropBox` and `/UserUnit` hold: bottom-right is the bottom-right you see.
- **Tool.** `doc_watermark` takes `horizontal_from` (`left|center|right`) and `vertical_from` (`top|center|bottom`), default `center`. Any other value is an argument error. `offset_x` / `offset_y` become the distances. Existing calls keep working.
- **Dialog.** A 3×3 grid picks the anchor (Acrobat's nine combinations). The distances show in pt, in, mm, cm or picas; the engine and the tool always hold points. No new strings to translate: the labels reuse words the 11 catalogs already have, so no `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes change.

Fixes #2527.

title: fix(select): a picked picture that is edited away no longer leaves its highlight behind
author: hade0ntema
body:
## What this changes

With the Select tool, clicking a picture picks it and draws a blue highlight over it (`image_pick`). The pick was only cleared by Escape, a drag/double click, or another click. So: pick a picture, open **Edit a PDF ▸ Edit text & images**, delete the picture, and its highlight stays on the now-empty spot of the page. title: M7: fix Thai editing and offer a bundled fallback font
author: dekkeng
body:
## What this changes

Existing Thai paragraph edits can fail when the PDF embeds only a source subset. For matching Noto Sans Thai, paragraph rewriting tried to embed the approved variable face through the static-font path. For another unavailable Thai source family, the app required a full font but offered no bundled replacement in the document-font menu.

The inline editor prefers complete matching Thai layout/coverage so vowels and tones stay in one shaping run. Headless clients pass the returned `builtin:thai` choice to `text_edit`/`text_edit_layout`; its token avoids collisions with source resource names and is never saved as a PDF resource. Missing-font errors name the source family and point to this choice or loading the complete original font. Keeping source fonts never silently substitutes another family.

No new dependency, font asset, release font pin, listener, network access, or automation tool. `edit.text-edit` remains partial: preserving other source families requires their complete font; bundled Thai uses regular style; mixed contextual style runs and dictionary word segmentation remain limited.

title: Tests: make timing-dependent render and UI tests deterministic
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Seven tests failed at random on slow or busy machines, on PRs and on `main` alike (FreeBSD run 38834256439 at 5fdd820b). Each one assumed something would finish within a deadline or a fixed number of frames. They now count the work, or wait for the state they check, so they give the same answer on every machine. No assertion was removed or loosened, and none of them retries.

**pdfcraft-render**

- `raster::tests::spot_colour_images_run_their_tint_transform_once_per_sample_value` gave a 2048 × 2048 spot-colour image 10 s to draw. Patch 28 made it take about 20 ms here, but a busy CI VM still went past 10 s. The test now counts the runs: a new vendored hayro-interpret patch (34), `color::tint_transform_runs()`, counts the colours a thread has run through a Separation or DeviceN tint transform. It is a thread-local cell, bumped once per `convert_f32` batch. The test checks there are exactly 256 runs (one per possible 8-bit sample value) where there used to be 4,194,304 (one per pixel), and checks both colours as before. The render runs on the test thread, with no deadline.
- `raster::tests::shadings_with_large_sampled_functions_paint_quickly` gave 30 paints of a 2,097,152-sample ramp 10 s. Here they take 0.14 s with patch 31's flat table and 14 s with the old hash map, so the deadline barely caught the regression on this machine, and a busy FreeBSD VM went past it with the fix in place. No counter can tell the two apart, because both read every sample on every build, and the hash map only made each sample cost about a hundred times more. So the test now compares two times taken on the same thread instead of using a deadline. It builds the function, which is what every paint does, and reads its samples (decode plus `BitReader`), the part no table can skip. title: fix(edit): show backgrounds on pages that paint their own white backdrop
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

A YouTube review showed **Add Background** "not working". It works on plain pages, but on a page that first fills itself with opaque white (browsers' Save as PDF, print drivers, many generators), the background is drawn behind that fill and is completely hidden. A near-white default colour (`[1, 1, 0.85]`) made it look broken even where it did work.

- **`pdfcraft-edit`: new `backdrop` module.** Strict detection: one `re`, axis-aligned, opaque white in DeviceGray/RGB/CMYK, painted before anything else, covering the crop box (clip and ExtGState honoured). To replace it, that one fill operator becomes `n` in a **per-page copy** of its content stream, and the original stream object is left untouched for other pages that share it. The copy carries `/PCBackdrop << /Index /Op /Before /Was >>`: how many operators come before the `n`, the fill it stands in for, a SHA-256 of those operators **by value** (spacing and number formatting don't count), and the original's object number as two plain integers. **The tag holds no page content and no reference.** A page-sized picture (a scan) is reported only, never touched.
- **Remove background turns the fill back on** in the copy when the operators before it still hash the same, and a scan with the fill restored finds it painted first again, covering the page. Edits and redactions made after the fill are kept. If the original stream is still in the document with the same bytes, the page points at it again. Otherwise the fill stays off, and **Remove says which pages**: a toast in the app ("Page 1 changed after the background was added, so its own white backdrop stays off. It looks the same on white paper."), and `warnings` from `doc_remove_marks`. In the engine, `Document::edit_notices` is now a `Vec<EditNotice>`, with the existing undrawn-text notice as one variant.
- `Background` gains `replace_backdrop` (default on). The default colour is a light yellow that is visible on screen.
- **Dialog:** shows "N pages…

title: M10: running text is not a table row in Word, HTML and PowerPoint export (#2806)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2806. On the FIDE Women's Grand Prix 2024–25 regulations (the public file the report describes, `calendar.fide.com/event_files/2551/Regulations.pdf`, 14 pages, Microsoft Print to PDF), Word export lost text that `pdfcraft-cli text` extracts. The cause is table detection in `crates/export` (`tables()`), shared by Word, HTML and PowerPoint export:

- **A link inside a sentence became table columns.** The link in 6.3.2 is drawn in a second font and colour, so the page's blocks are `6.3. 2. All content shown at` · `http` · `s` · `://women` · `g` · `randprix.fide.com`, each starting where the last one ends. Two of the pieces (`s`, `g`) start within the column tolerance of the link in 6.3.3, so they formed a "column".
- **A paragraph's lines became a cell beside its first line.** In 6.3.3 the block holding the paragraph's later lines (`is managed in a professional way …`) has a box that reaches up into the first line, so it overlapped `6.3. 3. … that` and joined its row as a second column. When the table was built, the first line's cell spanned that column and the paragraph text in it was dropped.

The export put "All content shown at" and "g" in table cells, pushed the rest of 6.3.2 after the table, and lost "is managed in a professional way … capable of handling … Statistics …" entirely.

Two rules decide whether a row counts as a table row:

1. **A block that continues another adds no column.** A block that starts where another block on the same line ends (up to half its font size later, or 1 pt earlier for rounding) is the same line of text running on: a link, a change of font, a superscript. It still sits in its row, but it doesn't make the row multi-column. Found page-wide over blocks sorted by their right edge (binary search, at most 64 candidates each).
2. **The cells of a table row don't overlap.** Blocks of a row that overlap by more than the column tolerance are a paragraph's lines, not cells side by side.

title: fix(cli): info, text, render and audit take the owner password of R2–R4 files
author: enesoglu
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli info`, `text`, `render` and `audit` now accept the **owner** password of revision 2–4 files (RC4-40, RC4-128, AES-128), as `run doc_open` already did. Before, they failed with "the password is incorrect". This is item 8 of #2670 only; the other items are covered by #2799, #2789, #2744, #2687 and #2679 or remain open.

**Cause.** The renderer (vendored hayro) authenticates only the *user* password of R2–R4 files. `Session::open` works around that by handing the renderer the user password that owner authentication recovers (`pdfcraft-crypt`, Algorithm 7). The CLI subcommands passed the typed password straight to `inspect` and `PageRenderer`.

**Fix.** New `pdfcraft_engine::render_password_for(bytes, password)` returns the password the renderer takes: the recovered user password for an R2–R4 owner password, otherwise the password as given. `Session::open` and the new function share one helper (`recovered_render_password`), so there is one source of truth. The CLI uses it for `inspect`/`PageRenderer` only. The engine session and the cos document still get the typed password, so the owner password still lifts copy restrictions in `text`.

Refs #2670 (item 8 only — the issue covers several separate problems, so this PR does not close it).

title: Drop XML-illegal control characters from PDF/A XMP packet
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/preflight/src/xmp.rs:37` (no existing issue): PDF/A conversion writes XML-illegal control characters from /Info into the XMP packet.

## Cause
`xmp::esc` only replaced & < > ", so C0 control characters in /Info values (Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Producer, Creator) were copied into the XMP packet. XML 1.0 forbids those characters, so the packet was malformed and the PDF/A output invalid.

## Fix
`xmp::esc` now drops the characters XML 1.0 forbids before escaping. These are the C0 controls other than tab, LF and CR, plus U+FFFE and U+FFFF. This matches `export::esc` and `organize::pdfx::esc`. The regression test builds a document with control characters in each /Info field and checks the packet.

## Verified
- Regression test `xmp_packet_drops_xml_illegal_characters_from_info`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-preflight --lib xmp_packet_drops_xml_illegal_characters_from_info`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
DEL (U+007F) is legal in XML 1.0 and is still passed through. Reading XMP back (`unescape`) and the other XMP fields are unchanged.

title: fix(annot): drop Apple Markup's stale copy when a page's annotations change
author: Kiwi-Kwi
body:
## What this changes

A page signed with **iOS Markup** carries Apple's private copy of its markup: `/AAPL:PPK` and `/AAPL:PPKHash` on the page, and `/AAPL:AKExtras` on each Markup annotation. After PdfCraft adds a signature to such a page, iOS (seen on iOS 26.6.1) displays the Markup signature **twice**: in its own place and over the signature PdfCraft added. Every other viewer we tried, PdfCraft included, renders the file correctly. The saved PDF is valid; Apple is drawing from its now-stale private copy.

Wherever a page's annotation list really changes (add, delete, reply, mark as reviewed), the three keys are removed from the page and from the page's annotations first, so Apple falls back to drawing every annotation from its appearance stream, as other viewers do. The Markup annotation itself, its `/AP` and its flags are kept, Apple keys are only touched when present (no extra objects in an incremental save otherwise), and the drop is recorded in the document's repair log. Promoting an inline annotation dictionary to an object, which edits like `set_style` do before validating, does not count as a change and drops nothing.

## How you verified it

On a real document (signed with iOS Markup, then signed in PdfCraft 0.8.0), opened on an iPhone:

| variant | iPhone shows |
|---|---|
| as saved by 0.8.0 | Markup signature twice ❌ |
| page `/AAPL:PPK` + `/AAPL:PPKHash` removed | Markup signature twice ❌ |
| page keys **and** the annotation's `/AAPL:AKExtras` removed (what this PR does) | both signatures correct ✅ |
| PdfCraft signature flattened | both signatures correct ✅ |

So the page-level keys alone are not enough; `/AAPL:AKExtras` has to go too.

title: fix(render): clip extracted text to the page CropBox (#2670)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2670 (item 5: **Text outside the CropBox**).

When a page's `CropBox` is smaller than its `MediaBox`, `hayro::render_into` clips visual rendering to `page.intersected_crop_box()` transformed by `page.initial_transform(true)`, but `TextDevice` recorded every glyph drawn anywhere on the page without checking whether its view-space bounding box intersected the visible crop region. As a result, `pdfcraft-cli text`, `text_extract`, `text_search`, and the UI text layer extracted and matched hidden text outside the `CropBox`.

- Store the view-space visible page box (`initial.transform_rect_bbox(intersected_crop_box)`) on `TextDevice` in `extract_page_filtered`.
- In `TextDevice::draw_glyph`, skip glyphs whose view-space bounding box has no positive overlap with `self.page` (`b.x0.max(self.page.x0) >= b.x1.min(self.page.x1) || b.y0.max(self.page.y0) >= b.y1.min(self.page.y1)`), while keeping glyphs that lie inside or straddle the `CropBox` boundary.

title: M6: keep field defaults in range; disable the item without a look
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Prepare a form: Use Current Properties as New Defaults for form fields

In Acrobat's Prepare Form you can right-click a field and choose Use Current Properties as New Defaults. Fields you add afterwards with the same tool get that field's properties, and fields that already exist stay as they are. This PR adds that item to the field's context menu in Prepare a form. It saves the right-clicked widget's Appearance tab (border and fill colour or none, line width and style, text colour, font) and its font size. Each field tool keeps its own defaults, so an image field and a button stay separate even though both are push buttons, and so do a date field and a text field. The defaults are saved with the settings and survive a restart. Check boxes, radio buttons and signatures take only the border and fill properties, and their `/DA` is left alone, so the ZapfDingbats mark is unaffected. A radio button that joins a group changes only its own widget. Choosing the item doesn't change the document, and a short notice confirms it. A tool with no saved defaults behaves as before. `Edit::AddField` gets an optional `look`, so the field and its look are added in a single Undo step. `form_add_field` takes the same `appearance` and `font_size` arguments as `form_set_props`, so the same result is reachable headless. Out of scope: the General and Options properties, which Acrobat may also carry over (I couldn't confirm which ones from its docs), and a "reset to built-in" command. Detected fields and fields added by document JavaScript keep ignoring the user's defaults. Happy to switch the per-tool split, or to have Image share Button's defaults. A default read from a field is clamped to what the Appearance tab accepts, so a file with `/BS /W 15` can't leave a tool unable to make fields. title: Redaction audit: an opaque filled Square annotation over text is a cover
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A `/Square` annotation with a black interior colour is what markup tools produce when someone draws a filled rectangle over text instead of redacting — macOS Preview's rectangle shape with a fill, for example. The audit only looked at `/Redact` annotations, so the text under such a box stayed extractable and `audit` reported the document clean.

Annotation covers now come in two kinds: an unapplied `/Redact` keeps its existing `UnappliedMark` finding, and an opaque filled `/Square` (its `/IC` fill darker than the COVER_CONTRAST threshold against the line's colour) counts as a cover over any text line it hides, reported as `CoveredText` like an in-content rectangle. Translucent fills are not flagged, and the module's documented limits (unrotated user space, `/Rotate` pages) apply to these rectangles as before.

Test: the issue's shape — a line of text with a black-filled Square over one name — produces a finding; it fails on main and passes here. The audit suite passes.

Fixes #2787

title: Treat CRLF as a single line break in fonts::wrap
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/fonts/src/lib.rs:79 (wrap_with: `text.split(['\n', '\r'])`)` (no existing issue): fonts::wrap treats a CRLF line break as two breaks, so Windows-style text gets a blank line between every line.

## Cause
`wrap_with` split paragraphs on every `'\n'` and every `'\r'` separately, so a `\r\n` pair counted as two breaks and produced an empty paragraph. Callers that don't normalise line endings, such as multiline form field appearances and auto font sizing, drew Windows-style text double-spaced.

## Fix
`wrap_with` now turns `\r\n` into `\n` before splitting. A CRLF pair is one break, and a lone `\r` or lone `\n` still breaks. The regression test covers CRLF, lone CR, lone LF, two CRLF pairs in a row, and `\n\r`, which stays two breaks.

## Verified
- Regression test `crlf_is_one_line_break`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts --lib crlf_is_one_line_break`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The callers in `crates/forms/src/appearance.rs` and `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs` are unchanged, because they get the fix through `wrap_with`. The test exercises `fonts::wrap` directly, not the form-appearance path.

title: ui: fix single page scroll flashing and prefetch adjacent pages
author: anishguduru
body:
When scrolling with the wheel in non-continuous (single-page or two-page) view, turning pages caused an empty canvas flash followed by a blank "Rendering…" placeholder.

This resolves the issue by:
1. In-Frame Row Recomputation: Updating the active row bounds in-frame immediately after mouse wheel paging updates `view.current`, ensuring the target page is laid out and drawn immediately in the very same frame without an empty background flash.
2. Adjacent Page Prefetching: Prefetching adjacent pages in non-continuous layouts within the texture cache budget, ensuring rasters are already rendered before coming into view.
3. Regression Tests: Adding regression tests in `view.rs` proving immediate turn rendering without empty frames (`single_page_wheel_turn_renders_new_page_immediately_without_empty_frame`) and adjacent page prefetching (`single_page_mode_prefetches_adjacent_pages`).

Fixes #2841

title: fix(ui): turn off horizontal scroll when fitting and lock axis during vertical scroll (#2803)
author: rangoDJ
body:
Fixes #2803.

When document content fits within the window width, egui's scroll area could still allow horizontal scrolling if a vertical scrollbar was present. With non-floating scrollbars, the vertical scrollbar takes up layout width, but content width was sized against the outer window width (`avail.width()`). Because the allocated content width was wider than the inner viewport by the scrollbar's width, the scroll area allowed horizontal drift during vertical scrolling or touchpad gestures.

Changes:
- In `canvas.rs`, determine whether content fits horizontally by checking against the inner width available after subtracting vertical scrollbar allocation. If the content fits, horizontal scrolling on the `ScrollArea` is turned off and the horizontal offset is kept at zero. If the content is wider than the inner viewport (even if narrower than the window), horizontal scrolling remains enabled so content is never hidden behind the scrollbar.
- Reverted `needed_content_width` for two-page layouts back to the original simple sizing (`max_w * 2 + 2 * SIDE`), avoiding unnecessary row-chunking changes.
- In touchpad wheel handling, lock to the dominant scroll axis so unintentional horizontal jitter during vertical swipes is suppressed. Deliberate horizontal swipes and Shift-wheel scrolling continue to pan normally when zoomed in.

Validation:
- Red check on `crates/ui-egui/tests/view.rs`: with `canvas.rs` reverted to main, `horizontal_scroll_turned_off_when_content_fits` failed (`before 478, after 466` from scrollbar overflow drift) and `horizontal_scroll_turned_off_during_vertical_scroll` failed (`moved_x 15` from horizontal jitter). Both pass on this branch.
- Added `horizontal_scroll_enabled_when_scrollbar_narrows_viewport` to verify that content narrower than the window but wider than the viewport minus the scrollbar keeps horizontal scroll enabled.

title: fix(render,cos): tolerate scientific-notation numbers and huge page boxes (#2670)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Addresses #2670 (item 6: Huge MediaBox / UserUnit).

### Problem
A page with `/MediaBox [0 0 1e30 1e30]` or `/UserUnit 1e20` failed to open with `the file is not a readable PDF: the document has no pages`, whereas MuPDF and qpdf open it with 1 page:
1. `hayro-syntax` (`object::number::Number`) and `lopdf` (`parser::real`) did not accept scientific-notation exponents (`[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`). In `hayro-syntax`, `1e30` in `/MediaBox [0 0 1e30 1e30]` stopped at `1`, leaving `e30` as an invalid array element so `/MediaBox` failed to parse and the page was skipped; in `/UserUnit 1e20`, `1` was read as the value and `e20` caused the rest of the page dictionary to be discarded, losing `/Type /Page`.
2. Numbers exceeding `f32::MAX` (`~3.40e38`, such as `1e40` or 400-digit reals) or `f64::MAX` (`1e400`), or page dimensions whose width/height or `base_dimensions * user_unit` product exceeded `f32::MAX`, overflowed to `±INFINITY`, causing downstream dimension checks and area-cap calculations (`w * h` in `raster::effective_scale`) to fail or collapse.
3. Re-saving a document with `1e30` via `pdfcraft_cos::write_full` formats `1e30` as a 31-digit plain integer, which `lopdf` rejected when `i64::from_str` overflowed.

### Solution
- **`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/object/number.rs` & `src/page.rs`:**
  - Parse optional scientific-notation exponents (`[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`) in `Number::skip` and `read_inner` when preceded by at least one digit and no trailing minus, rewinding if `e`/`E` is not followed by `[+-]?[0-9]` (preserving token boundaries like `123endobj`).
  - Combine integer overflow digits, fractional shift, and scientific exponent into `net_exp: i64`, clamping overflowed magnitudes to `±f64::MAX` in `f64` and `f32::MIN..=f32::MAX` in `Number::as_f32`.
  - Clamp `Page::base_dimensions`, `Page::render_dimensions`, and scaled `base_height` in `Page::initial_transform` to `f32::MAX`.
- **`vendor/lopdf/src/parser/mod.rs`:**
  - Accept scientific-notation exponents in `real` and clamp to `…

author: FerrisEanfar
body:

Insert from File copied pages and their dependencies but left out the source catalog's `/Names /EmbeddedFiles` tree. Attachments stored only there disappeared from the result, although Combine Files already kept them.

Reuse the existing attachment collector in `insert_file_pages`, merging incoming entries with the destination's attachments. The import stays inside the existing engine edit, so undo and redo cover pages and attachments together.

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2759 (the IRCC IMM forms reported as altered). Together with #2763 it clears the false "altered" verdict. Trust (the Sectigo/USERTrust roots) and timestamp verification are separate parts of the issue and aren't touched here.

The IRCC forms are certified (DocMDP P=2) and then saved once more with Reader Extensions. title: Forms: measure a field's own simple font, not Helvetica, when laying out its text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2894.

Since #1044 a field is drawn in the `/DA` font from `/DR` when it can encode the value, but `FontText::width` still measured that font with Helvetica's table, so wrapping, quadding and `0 Tf` auto size were laid out for a different face. In Courier (0.6 em) mixed-case text overflows: the issue's field gets a 128-character first line in a box that holds 94. This measures a reused simple font with its own `Metrics`, i.e. its `/Widths`, or the standard-14 table when it has none (Courier, Times, Helvetica and their styles), which is what @MONUABST suggested in the issue, thanks for the clear write-up and the repro. For a standard-14 font without `/Widths`, `Metrics::width` (pdfcraft-fonts) now looks a code up through the font's encoding, so a `/Differences` remap is measured as the glyph it draws rather than the one WinAnsi has at that code; this also applies to the other `Metrics::width` callers (edit, redact, a11y). Helvetica fallback and the CJK path are unchanged; Symbol and ZapfDingbats never get here, since `dr_font` already sends them to Helvetica. The module comment said widths were Helvetica's, so it's updated too.

#2466 adds a `Composite` arm next to the same line with the same measurement, so whichever lands second has a one-line conflict in that `match`, happy to rebase.

Validation:
- `reused_standard_fonts_wrap_and_align_with_their_own_widths` (crates/forms): the issue's Courier field plus right-aligned Courier and Times-Roman fields. Fails on main (`every line fits the box in Courier: [128, 71]`), passes here; measuring every simple font as Courier makes it fail on the Times field (`Times: 174`)

title: fix(ui): scroll the right rail instead of overlapping its controls in short windows
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2891.

The right rail laid the navigation cluster out bottom-up in the same fixed-height panel as the panel buttons, so once the window was shorter than both groups (about 770 pt on main, which is a 1080 px screen at 150 % interface size) the cluster simply grew up over Tags and Signatures. Thanks to @musaad-sharikh for the measured thresholds, they made this quick to pin down. Now, when the heights measured on the previous frame don't fit, the rail's content goes into a vertical scroll area: the cluster sits right below the panel buttons and the rail scrolls as one column, so every control stays visible and clickable. On the frame where the rail first appears, before anything is measured, a layout that overflows is discarded and redone, so that frame never shows the overlap either. A rail that fits keeps exactly the layout it has today, so normal windows and the canvas beside the rail don't move by a pixel. Since it works from measured heights, it doesn't depend on how many buttons either group has, and also covers the extra layout and scrolling toggles in #2828.

I went with scrolling rather than folding the cluster into an overflow menu because it needs no new strings or duplicated actions and keeps the bottom-up order people know; happy to switch to an overflow ("more") button if you'd rather match Acrobat's collapsing behaviour.

title: M2: an open or diagonal five-point path is not drawn as a rectangle (#2911)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2911 (and #235, the same "M" in the ROMANS font).

`path_as_rect` in the vendored `hayro-interpret` (`src/context.rs`) took any five path elements that touch the four corners of their bounding box as a rectangle, and fill, stroke and clip all use it. The "M" of AutoCAD SHX text is an open `m l l l l` with two diagonals that happens to touch all four corners, so it was stroked as a box.

The shortcut now also requires a **closed** path (ending in `h`, or a last point back at the start) whose **every side is horizontal or vertical** (`closed_axis_aligned`). Anything else is drawn as the path it is. Recorded as PdfCraft patch (34) in `vendor/README.md`. The reporter suggested the same rule in the issue.

Two more shapes were wrong the same way and are fixed by it: the same "M" **filled** came out as a full rectangle, and an **open** path with four horizontal or vertical sides was stroked with the side it doesn't have.

## How you verified it

Each case rendered at 288 dpi and compared with MuPDF (mean absolute difference, 0–255):

| content | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| the issue's `5 35 m 35 35 l 5 20 l 35 5 l 5 5 l S` | 37.63 (a box) | 0.04 |
| the same path filled (`f`) | 71.68 (a filled rectangle) | 0.08 |
| open `5 35 m 5 5 l 35 5 l 35 35 l 20 35 l S` | 4.78 (fourth side added) | 0.00 |
| `5 5 30 30 re f` | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| closed `m l l l h S` | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| `m l l l l S` back to the start | 0.16 | 0.16 |

New test `crates/render/src/raster.rs::an_open_or_diagonal_five_point_path_is_not_drawn_as_a_rectangle` checks pixels on a 40 × 40 page:
- the M's top is stroked and its missing left side isn't;
- the filled M's notch stays empty;
- the open path's missing top part stays empty;
- a closed rectangle still strokes all four sides.

## What this changes

Fixes blank ș reported in #1666
The stand-ins for the standard fonts (PDFium's Foxit fonts) have neither the comma-below letters nor a commaaccent glyph, and the composite-letter patch from #1409 left comma accents out. A non-embedded font naming /scommaaccent therefore drew nothing, which is the blank "si" left in Romanian XFA forms, and /tcommaaccent drew a cedilla through the glyph list's alias to U+0163. title: CLI: view draws PDF pages in the terminal through the kitty graphics protocol
author: dobladez
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli view report.pdf` draws PDF pages straight into the terminal, through the [kitty graphics protocol](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/) (kitty, Ghostty, WezTerm and others): on macOS, Linux and FreeBSD, directly, over SSH and inside tmux 3.3 or later.

[!demo video](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31cf9b71-7bbb-488f-9039-7b15ee682d56)

- **A pager, like `less`.** More than one page opens a pager on the alternate screen: one page at a time, or two side by side when the window is wide enough, turning like a book. It has less-like keys and follows the window when it is resized or split.
- **Zoom.** `-` zooms out: one more page to a row each time, up to 8, so zoomed far out the screen is an overview of the document. `+` zooms back in, and from one page to a row goes to the page as wide as the window. `--zoom auto|width|N` starts at any of these.
- **Single pages print, like `cat`.** A single page (`--pages 3`), `--no-pager`, or output to a file (with `--protocol kitty`) prints at the cursor instead. Pages stay in the scrollback, like text, in rows as zoomed: `--zoom 3` prints three to a row.
- **Fast.** Two render threads work ahead, so turning to a page only places it.
  - On this machine, pages go through temporary files of raw pixels once a one-pixel probe shows the terminal takes them. kitty takes a page that way in about 10 ms, against 50–65 ms as a PNG.
  - Otherwise pages go as PNGs, compressed fast on this machine and small over SSH.
- **tmux.** Escape codes go through passthrough, and pages are Unicode placeholders that tmux keeps as text. Pages tmux threw away, or that a hidden pane or a newly attached terminal missed, are sent again.
- **`docker exec` and `kubectl exec`.** These pass rows and columns but no pixel size, so `view` asks the terminal how big its cells are (`CSI 16 t`) once at start. Pages come out as sharp as over SSH.

author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What does it change?

Rename the open document's file from its tab (#2102, #2867).

- **Rename…** on a document tab's right-click menu (beside Reveal), or a double-click on the tab, opens a small dialog with the name selected (without its extension). The file is renamed on disk in its own folder; the tab, its undo history and the view stay. Recent files, Reopen Closed Tab and the file watcher follow the new name.
- The name is checked as it is typed: the reason shows under the field, the resulting file name in grey, and Rename stays disabled until the name is usable. Enter renames.

- A document without a file shows Rename… disabled, as Reveal is.
- Automation: `doc_rename {doc, name}`, marked destructive, held to the write root for both the old and the new name.

## The rules for a name (`crates/engine/src/rename.rs`)

The same on every system, so a file renamed on one keeps working in a folder synced to another:
- no `/ \ : * ? " < > |`, no control characters, no trailing dot; surrounding spaces trimmed; at most 255 characters;
- no Windows device names (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`9`, `LPT1`–`9`), also with an extension (`aux.notes`);
- the extension is kept, and added back when left out (`notes.txt` becomes `notes.txt.pdf`); a case-only rename is allowed.

Refusals say why: name taken, read-only, in use or no permission, file gone, never saved, unsaved changes.

title: feat(annot): resize highlights, strikeouts, notes and redaction marks
author: FerrisEanfar
body:
## What this changes

Extends the existing native annotation resize path to **Highlight, StrikeOut, Text (note icon), and Redact (review mark)**. Available through `annot::set_rect`, `Edit::ResizeAnnotation`, and the existing `comment_edit` tool's `rect` field; no new tool or GUI controls.

> Edit text failed: the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+0633

Arabic draft text takes the styled-paragraph path (`rewrite_styled_block`). There, each letter the
subset couldn't encode went, one at a time, to the Type 3 fallback, which only has the Japanese
(and Hebrew) faces. Even with a glyph, each letter would have been drawn in its unjoined form.

Now a run with Arabic that its own font can't shape is drawn with the craft-fonts `Arab` face
(Noto Sans Arabic):

- **Shaping:** each row is shaped with the shaper Add text already uses (`shape_arabic`, with
  UAX #9 runs).
- **Drawing:** each distinct cluster (a letter in one of its joining forms) becomes one glyph of a
  Type 3 font, built by Add text's `type3_shaped`, inside an `/ActualText` span. So letters join,
  and copy, search and re-editing all get the typed text.
- **No font file is embedded.** The face is variable, which `embedding::validate` refuses, so the
  styled path's existing `embed_mapping` route can't take it.
- **Alignment:** right-to-left rows keep their right edge and grow toward the left margin, as the
  Hebrew path already does.
- **Clear refusals:** a build without the face refuses with a message naming the Arabic font
  rather than the Japanese one. So do the paths that don't shape: a single line (`text_edit` with
  `line`), turned text, text that also has Hebrew, and a paragraph given another font family or
  weight.

Not in this PR: how Arabic looks *inside the edit box* while typing (the other half of #2878 and
#1039). That is UI work, covered by #1572 and #2233.

All runs were scoped per crate with `-j 1`. `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` pointed at a craft-fonts checkout

title: fix(ui): keep a closed right panel closed when a PDF asks to open on its outline (#2884)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2884.

`apply_initial_view()` opened the right panel for a document's Initial View (`/PageMode /UseOutlines`, and likewise Pages, Attachments and Layers) without checking `right_panel_closed`. It now skips that step when the user has closed the panel. This is the same rule #1603 added to the automatic Comments/Bookmarks choice in `commit_open`. Layout, magnification and the initial page still apply.

Because the document no longer reopens the panel, a closed panel is no longer saved together with `docking_right: "Bookmarks"`, so it stays closed after a restart. `restore()` is unchanged. Other features (Accessibility, Signatures, comment tools) still open the panel directly without clearing the flag, so a panel they opened is still restored as it was left.

Tests:
- New `closed_right_panel_stays_closed_for_a_document_asking_for_its_outline` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/ui.rs`: close the panel, open a `/PageMode /UseOutlines` copy of the fixture, then persist, restore and open it again. Both times the panel stays closed. Without the fix it fails on the first check, because the panel opens on Bookmarks.
- `read_mode_rail_buttons_open_their_panels` closes Bookmarks with the rail button before checking that an outline document shows its outline in Read mode. It now resets `right_panel_closed` first, because closing the panel there is now (correctly) remembered.

title: Redact email addresses whose local part starts with punctuation
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs:141-146 (email)` (no existing issue): Redact email pattern misses addresses whose local part starts with '_', '-', '.', '%' or '+', so they are not redacted at all.

## Cause
`email()` only started a match at an alphanumeric character and refused to start after a local-part character (`._%+-`). An address like `_john@example.com` therefore had no valid start: `_` is not alphanumeric, and `j` follows a local character. The address was never found and stayed visible after redaction.

## Fix
A match may now start at any local-part character, as long as the previous character is not a local-part character. The local run must still contain at least one letter or digit. Addresses with a leading `_`, `-`, `.`, `%` or `+` are matched whole.

## Verified
- Regression test `emails_with_a_leading_punctuation_character`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact --lib emails_with_a_leading_punctuation_character`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The domain and TLD rules and the handling of scripts written without spaces are unchanged. A run made only of punctuation, such as `..@example.com`, still does not match.

title: M2: a post table version with swapped halves doesn't make a font unusable (#2946)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2946.

`OpenTypeFontBlob::new` in the vendored `hayro-interpret` (`src/font/blob.rs`) refuses an embedded font whose `post` table version isn't 1.0, 2.0, 2.5 or 3.0, a guard taken from pdf.js issue 9462. title: Apply JPEG EXIF orientation when creating PDFs from images
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2944

## Cause
The create path (`from_images`, used by `doc_create` from images, `doc_combine` and `doc_create_multiple`) embedded JPEGs from their stored pixels and never read the EXIF Orientation tag. Only the engine's stamp and image-placement code turned the pixels first, so portrait photos came out as sideways landscape pages.

## Fix
The EXIF-orientation helper (`upright_image`) now lives in `pdfcraft-create`, and `embed` runs every JPEG through it. Pages made from images get the turned pixel size and the swapped JFIF density, and `image_xobject` (stamps, added images) still gets the same result. The engine no longer calls the helper separately.

## Verified
- Regression test `a_jpeg_with_an_exif_orientation_becomes_an_upright_page`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-create --lib a_jpeg_with_an_exif_orientation_becomes_an_upright_page`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Orientation=1 and JPEGs without the tag are still embedded byte for byte. Other formats (PNG, TIFF, etc.) are unchanged. The helper's behaviour (re-encode at quality 92, 64 MP size cap) is unchanged.
