title: fix(forms): name detected check boxes from the nearer neighbouring label (#2943)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary
Closes #2943

When `pdfcraft_forms::detect::detect` named small square check boxes, it only inspected words to the right of each box within a 24 pt gap. On forms that place labels immediately to the left of their check boxes (such as `Monsieur [ ]   Madame [ ]` on French form 2042, where `Monsieur` ends ~5 pt before the first box and `Madame` starts 23 pt after the first box and ~4 pt before the second), the first box claimed `Madame` and left the second box as `Check Box1`.

### Root Cause & Fix
- **Consider both sides of each check box in reading order (`checkbox_label`):** Sort detected check boxes (along with any existing check-box widgets on the page) into reading order and evaluate both the unclaimed phrase immediately to the left and the unclaimed phrase immediately to the right on the same line, bounded by adjacent check boxes on that line.
- **Prevent stealing a neighbour's label:** Reject a right-hand phrase when it sits closer to the next check box on the line than to the current box (or split a multi-word span when a subsequent word sits closer to the next box than to the preceding word), and reject a left-hand phrase when it sits closer to the previous check box.
- **Choose the nearer label (preserving colon prompts):** When a box has valid unclaimed candidates on both sides, prefer the nearer one (or the left candidate when the right candidate is also immediately followed by the next box at equal distance), while treating colon-terminated row prompts (`Status: [ ] Single [ ] Married` or `Civilité : Monsieur [ ] Madame [ ]`) as headings rather than option names unless the prompt is the box's only label (`Married: [ ]`).

## Verification

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2378: the single-line path (`text_edit` with `line`, which is what the issue's `edits.json` uses).

`replace_line` decided once for the whole text: if the line's font couldn't encode every character, the whole line was set in Helvetica. title: M6: dotted field names make parent fields (#2696)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2696.

**The problem.** Prepare a form refused any field name containing a period: "field names can't be empty or contain a period". Templates for Conga and similar tools rely on names such as `MASTER.account_firstname`. It also showed an existing `MASTER.account_firstname` as `account_firstname`, both in Field Properties and on the name tags.

ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.2 does say a field's own (partial) name can't contain a period. A dotted name is therefore a *full* name: `MASTER.first` is a field `first` under a parent field `MASTER`, and that is what this PR builds.

**Changes:**
- **Adding a field** (`add_field`, `form_add_field`): a dotted name creates the parent fields it names, or reuses them if they already exist. A second `MASTER.` field joins the same `MASTER` parent.
- **Renaming** (`set_props`, `form_set_props`):
  - A dotted name is the full name. The field moves under the parents it names, and what it inherited (`FT`, `Ff`, `V`, `DV`, `DA`, `Q`, `MaxLen`) is first copied onto it, so its value and flags are kept.
  - A plain name still renames the field within its parent, as before. The existing test, where `address.city` → `town` gives `address.town`, is unchanged.
- **Clash checks:** a new full name may not equal another field's name, sit inside one, or contain one. A field with a value can't also be a parent of fields. This also closes an existing gap: renaming a field to `address` while `address.city` existed used to be accepted.
- **Reused parents:** a field joining an existing parent gets an explicit `Ff 0` / `Q 0` if it has none of its own, so it doesn't pick up the parent's flags or alignment.
- **UI:** Field Properties ▸ General and the Prepare a form name tags show the full name, as the Fields panel already did.
- **Limits:** names are capped at 32 parts, and empty parts (`a..b`, `.a`, `a.`, `a. `) are refused.
- `delete_field`'s tree removal moved into a `detach` helper, shared with rename.

title: Keep lines with footnote references in paragraph reading order (#2929)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #2929

### Problem
When a paragraph contains a line with a footnote reference (superscript) or subscript:
1. In `arrange` Step 1a, a raised superscript (or a script drawn out of content order in a separate pass) splits into its own `Seg` whenever its vertical centre is more than `0.5 * ph` from the preceding glyph's centre, and Step 1b only merges segments with matching heights (`(sa.h / sb.h - 1.0).abs() < 0.35`) and centres (`(sa.cy() - sb.cy()).abs() < h * 0.3`).
2. In Step 2 (`Blocks`), segments are sorted top-down by `bbox[1]`. Because a superscript's top edge `bbox[1]` is higher than its host line's top edge, `by_top` visits the superscript **before** its host line and appends it to the paragraph block (`members.last()`).
3. When the host line is visited next, `vgap = line.bbox[1] - sup.bbox[3]` is negative (`< -0.5 * sup.h`), so the host line is rejected from the paragraph block and pushed into a separate block emitted **after** the paragraph. Meanwhile, the next line below has a positive `vgap` from the superscript and joins the first block.
4. Drag-selecting across the paragraph selects `Block 0` (`Line 1`, the superscript, `Line 3`, ...) and completely skips the host line containing the footnote reference both visually and when copying.

### Solution
- Add `is_script_on` and `Seg::extend_box` in `crates/render/src/text.rs` so superscripts and subscripts widen their host line segment horizontally without pulling its vertical baseline band (`bbox[1]..bbox[3]`) up or down.
- In `arrange` Step 1a, keep inline superscripts/subscripts in the current segment and allow the following body text on the segment's baseline to continue the run across normal and justified word gaps.
- In `arrange` Step 1b, merge any remaining out-of-order superscript/subscript segments into the closest wider host line segment they sit on.
- In `collide`, do not treat a script overlapping an adjacent host glyph (e.g. a superscript kerned over a period or comma) as a run-level overpr…

title: M7: replacing a line keeps both of two dropped quote copies' line move and spacing (edit.text-edit)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

The behaviour this PR started with, keeping the line move and spacing of a dropped `'` or `"` (ISO 32000-2 §9.4.3, Table 107) when a line or paragraph is rewritten, landed on `main` in #2968, with the same `show_side_effects` / `dropped_side_effects` helpers and tests. This PR now adds only the case CodeRabbit asked for: a line with **two** overprinted copies, one drawn with `'` and one with `"`.

```
BT /F1 12 Tf 0 TL 72 700 Td (Target line here) Tj ET
BT 72.3 700 Td (Target line here) ' ET
BT 72.6 700 Td 3 2 (Target line here) " 0 -100 Td (Footer stays put) Tj ET
```

`replace_line` drops every copy on the target's baseline. The footer is placed from the line the second copy's `"` moved to and draws with the `3 Tw` / `2 Tc` it set, so both copies must leave their effects behind whichever of the three lines is the target, not just the first copy dropped.

The case goes into `replacing_a_line_keeps_what_a_dropped_quote_copy_did` in `crates/edit/src/tests.rs`. title: Keep seconds in FormCalc Time2Num/IsoTime2Num for ISO 8601 times
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2348-2352 ("time2num" | "isotime2num")` (no existing issue): FormCalc Time2Num / IsoTime2Num drop the seconds when they carry a 'Z' suffix or a fractional part ("12:30:45Z" gives 12:30:00).

## Cause
Time2Num/IsoTime2Num split the text on ':' and kept only the parts that parse as a plain integer. A seconds part such as "45Z" or "45.250" was dropped and read as 0. A leading "T" dropped the hour part, so the later parts shifted left. The calculation also used whole seconds only.

## Fix
The function now removes an optional leading "T" and trailing "Z", then reads hours and minutes as integers by position. It reads seconds as a decimal number, so "12:30:45Z" gives 45045000 and "12:30:45.250" gives 45045250. The existing cap on very large values is kept.

## Verified
- Regression test `built_in_functions_cover_the_common_set`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js built_in_functions_cover_the_common_set`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Time zone offsets such as "+02:00" are still not interpreted. Num2Time and the other time and date functions are unchanged.

title: M7: the docs say how to edit text inside a Form XObject (Ungroup) (#2964)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2964.

`docs/editing-existing-text.md` described what Edit text supports without saying what happens to text drawn inside a Form XObject, the way LaTeX `pdfpages`, n-up and imposition tools, HTML-to-PDF converters and stamps place content. With #3067 on `main`, that text can be edited through Ungroup, so the docs now say so:

- Text inside a form is extracted, searched and rendered; while the form is grouped it is one artwork item that moves as a whole.
- **Ungroup** (the artwork's right-click menu, or the `image_edit` action `ungroup`) draws that placement in place on the page with its resources merged. Its text then lists as paragraphs that can be retyped, and undo brings the form back.

title: M7: paragraph edits keep the advance of the text they drop (edit.text-edit)
author: mtlcl410
body:
> **Stacked on #2961.** This branch contains #2961's commit (`47184ce6`, the `'`/`"` side effects), because this fix extends the same splice. Please review only the last commit (`1bf752ea`). I'll rebase once #2961 is merged.

## What this changes

There's no existing issue: I found this by probing `text_edit` on synthetic content streams.

**The rule.** Each `Tj`/`TJ` moves the text matrix by the width of its text (ISO 32000-2 §9.4.4). A run shown later in the same text object without its own `Td` or `Tm` is placed by those advances. Examples are a raised run in another colour, or a column after a `TJ` gap.

**The bug.** The paragraph and region rewrites (`replace_block` / `rewrite_block`, `text_edit` with `paragraph`) removed the paragraph's show operators outright. A following run that isn't part of the paragraph then jumped left by the removed text's width, often onto the new text:

| Content after `BT /F1 12 Tf 72 700 Td (Target words) Tj` | main: run's x after a paragraph edit | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `1 0 0 rg 3 Ts (Red) Tj` | 72 (on top of the new text; was 142) | 142 |
| `[-20000] TJ (Far) Tj` | 312 (was 382) | 382 |

**Why only these paths.** Deleting a paragraph (`clear_block`, also used for the editing preview) already replaces each dropped operator with a numeric `TJ` of the same advance. The rewrites now do the same.

**The fix.** `dropped_advances` interprets the page and returns, for each dropped show operator, `[-1000·advance/(Tfs·Th)] TJ`, which moves the text matrix the same distance without drawing. Advances a `TJ` can't express (spacing at a zero font size) are left out, which is the previous behaviour, rather than refused. Both splices insert this after the operator's `'`/`"` side effects from #2961.

Line edits (`replace_line`) are unchanged. There, the runs after the edited text move to follow the new text (here 142 → 134), which is the line editor's existing reflow.

title: Find credit card numbers followed by an expiry, year or CVV
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs:180-190 (credit_card, via digit_run at :53)` (no existing issue): Redact credit-card pattern misses a card number when another number follows it after a space (expiry date, CVV, year).

## Cause
`credit_card` took the longest run of digits joined by single spaces or hyphens and ran the Luhn check only on that whole run. A valid card followed by a space and another number (an expiry like `12/26`, a year or a CVV) made the run too long or failed the checksum. The card was then not found and stayed visible after redaction.

## Fix
`credit_card` now tries the longest run first, then each shorter run that ends at a group boundary (before a space or hyphen), longest first. It returns the first run with 13 to 19 digits and a valid Luhn checksum. The trailing number stays outside the match.

## Verified
- Regression test `credit_card_followed_by_another_number`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact --lib credit_card_followed_by_another_number`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`digit_run` and the other patterns are unchanged. A run with no valid checksum at any group boundary, such as `4111 1111 1111 1112 12/26`, still matches nothing.

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2970.

**Cause.** Bisected between v0.8.0 (correct) and `main` (924c4da4). The first bad commit is ab45a185, #1557 "Keep annotations readable under reading colours". Its vendored hayro patch (18) moved the page background *inside* the page transparency group, as the group's initial backdrop. That way a Multiply highlight under reading colours blends with the dark background (#1548).

The commit reasoned that "white backgrounds are unaffected: multiplying with white is the identity". That holds for Multiply, but not for most other blend modes. With document colours, every object then blended with the white paper:
- A green `/BM /Screen` fill over an empty part of the page came out white.
- Difference and Exclusion came out magenta.

Only Normal, Multiply, Darken and HardLight looked right, because for them blending with white gives back the source colour.

Otherwise it paints it outside, as before #1557.

title: fix(render): knockout transparency groups knock out (#2971)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2971: knockout transparency groups (`/K true`) now knock out for every kind of element: paths, strokes, text, shadings, images and nested groups.

**Cause.** In a knockout group, each element composites with the group's initial backdrop, not with the elements drawn before it in the group, over the element's shape (ISO 32000-2, knockout groups). hayro-interpret already read `/K` (patch 28). The renderer, though, drew a knockout group like any other, so overlapping semi-transparent elements in it blended with each other.

**Fix.** There are two commits.

1. **Direct draws.** While the innermost group is a knockout group, fills, strokes, glyph outlines and shadings are drawn with `BlendMode::new(Mix::Normal, Compose::Copy)`. vello_cpu weights Copy by coverage (result = coverage · source + (1 − coverage) · destination), so an element replaces what the group drew under its shape.
   - hayro-interpret patch (35): `Device::set_knockout`, called when a `/K true` group is pushed.
   - hayro patch (19): a knockout flag per pushed group, popped with it.

2. **Images and nested groups.** These are drawn into a layer of their own. The layer covers the whole canvas and is transparent where nothing was drawn, so compositing it with Copy would erase everything else. Copy on a clipped layer doesn't work either: vello renders it into an empty clip buffer first and composites that with SrcOver. Instead, what is under the element's shape is cleared first, and then the layer composites over it as usual.
   - **Unmasked image:** its shape is its placement rectangle. The interpreter passes it to `Device::knockout_shape`, and the renderer clears it with a transparent Copy fill.
   - **Nested group:** its shape is the union of its elements' shapes. When `Device::knockout_erase_wanted` is true, the interpreter draws the group's content once between `begin_knockout_erase` and `end_knockout_erase`. In that pass every paint clears under its shape instead of painting…

title: fix(render): a stencil mask is drawn at the fill opacity once (#2975)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2975.

**Cause.** `draw_image_xobject` (hayro-interpret) draws every image XObject inside a transparency group whose opacity is the fill alpha `ca`. A stencil mask (`/ImageMask true`) is painted in the fill colour, which `get_paint` builds with that same alpha, and the renderer applies the paint's alpha again. So the opacity was applied twice:
- at `ca 0.5`, a mask came out 25 % opaque
- at `ca 0.25`, about 6 %

Rectangles and raster images, which have no paint colour, were right. This was already the case in 0.7.1.

**Fix.** Vendored hayro-interpret patch (36): once the image's group is pushed, the fill alpha is set to 1 before the stencil's paint is taken. The state saved at the start of `draw_image_xobject` is restored after the image, so nothing after it changes.

Stencils inside Type 3 glyphs and uncoloured patterns are unchanged: their wrappers ignore the group and substitute their own paint. Inline images (`BI … EI`) use the same `draw_image_xobject`, so they're fixed too.

title: Fix overflow panic for i64::MIN index in content_update/delete
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/automation/src/content.rs:141` (no existing issue): content_update / content_delete panic with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' when index is i64::MIN.

## Cause
`Automation::item` computed `(index - 1).max(0)` before checking `index >= 1`. With `index = i64::MIN` the subtraction overflows, so debug and test builds panic instead of returning the usual 'has no added item' error.

## Fix
The item lookup now computes the position with `index.saturating_sub(1)` and `usize::try_from`. Any index below 1 maps to a position that matches no item, and the existing `index >= 1` filter still rejects it. `i64::MIN` now returns the normal failed error. A regression test covers `i64::MIN`, `i64::MIN + 1`, -1, 0 and `i64::MAX` for both tools.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other tools' index handling and argument validation in `check_args`.

title: fix(render): resolve TrueType glyphs across Unicode/UCS-4 cmaps, post v2.0 aliases, and truncated FontFlags (#2159)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2159

Embedded non-symbolic TrueType font subsets (such as macOS subsets containing Slovak `č` U+010D and `ľ` U+013E in #2159) failed to render accented characters when the subset carried a `PlatformId::Unicode` `(0, 3)` or Windows UCS-4 `(3, 10)` `cmap` subtable with `post` v3.0 (no glyph names) and no `(3, 1)` Windows BMP subtable, or when `post` v2.0 used `uniXXXX` / `uXXXX` / `.suffix` names instead of the literal AGL name from `/Differences`.

### Changes

- **`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/true_type.rs`**:
  - Use `FontFlags::from_bits_truncate` when reading `/FontDescriptor /Flags` so unknown/producer-specific bits do not discard `NON_SYMBOLIC` (matching `FallbackFontQuery::new` in `font/mod.rs`).
  - Probe Windows `(3, 1)` and `(3, 10)` as well as `PlatformId::Unicode` `(0, *)` `cmap` subtables for name-derived Unicode lookups on non-symbolic TrueType fonts.
  - Resolve `post` v2.0 glyph names across exact names, AGL dot-suffix base names (`ecaron.salt` -> `ecaron`), `normalized_glyph_name`, bidirectional AGL <-> `uniXXXX` / `uXXXX` aliases, and `g<num>` names.
  - Respect explicit `/.notdef` entries in `/Differences` without falling through to raw `cmap` indices, and use `saturating_add(1)` when walking `/Differences`.
- **`crates/render/tests/truetype_cmap.rs`**:
  - Added 5 regression tests covering macOS `(0, 3)` Unicode `cmap` subsets with `post` v3.0, Windows `(3, 10)` UCS-4 `cmap` subsets, `post` v2.0 `uniXXXX` / `uXXXX` / AGL / `.suffix` resolution without a Unicode `cmap`, `/FontDescriptor /Flags` with extra bits set, and explicit `/.notdef` in `/Differences`.

title: fix(render): a visibility expression decides what an OCMD shows (#2986)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2986. This may be the cause of #2986; that depends on how cadwork marks its layers, which a sample file would show.

**The gap.** An optional content membership dictionary (OCMD) can carry a visibility expression, `/VE` (PDF 1.6): `[/And e…]`, `[/Or e…]` or `[/Not e]`. Each `e` is an optional content group or a nested expression. When `/VE` is present it takes precedence over `/OCGs` and `/P` (ISO 32000-2 §8.11.2.2). hayro-interpret evaluated only `/OCGs` and `/P`, so content under an OCMD with `/VE` stayed visible after its layers were hidden in the Layers panel.

**The fix.** Vendored hayro-interpret patch (37) evaluates the expression in `OcgState::begin_ocmd`, nested up to 32 deep. A malformed expression falls back to `/OCGs` and `/P`, as before. Malformed means:
- an unknown operator
- `/Not` without exactly one operand
- `/And` or `/Or` without any operands
- an operand that is neither a group nor an expression
- nesting deeper than 32

An operand given by reference is taken as a group, which is how producers write them.

**What I checked.** I ran 11 optional-content structures with layer A hidden through the same override the Layers panel uses:
- *Already correct:* `BDC /OC` (also nested, and inside a form), `/OC` on a Form XObject, on a form nested in a form, and on an image, OCMDs with `/P` `AnyOn`/`AllOn` and a single `/OCGs` reference, and a layer that is off in `/D /OFF`.
- *Not hidden:* the OCMD with `/VE`, fixed here.
- *Not hidden:* `/OC` on an annotation, which is covered by #2176.

title: render: average a minified 1-bit source into its snapped device rectangle (#1700, follow-up to #2288)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
<!-- Stacked on #2288 (head 1a42f48). Until #2288 is merged, only the last commit, f796686, belongs to this PR. -->

## What this changes

This follows up #2288 for #1700, as agreed in [the review thread](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2288#issuecomment-6190802399). It is stacked on #2288 (head 1a42f48); only the last commit, f796686, is new.

**The problem on #2288.** A minified 1-bit source is averaged into a raster `ceil(s × scale)` px wide, and that raster is then drawn `s × scale` px wide with `ImageQuality::Low`. So it is nearest-sampled a second time, and a whole averaged column or row (a one-pixel stroke) can fall between two pixel centres. At 9 pt and 96 dpi, for example, the 18 px Type 3 glyphs of `mask_downscale.pdf` are averaged to 9 px and drawn 8.1 px wide. An 18×1 mask inked only in column 8 or 9 then renders all white. On the fixture this shows as missing stems in several glyphs of that row; that part is a visual reading of the render, and the table below has the counts.

**What this PR does.** A shrunk 1-bit source, Type 3 glyph masks included, now takes the path that #1377 added for interpolated images:

- `snap_minified_image` gives the whole-pixel device rectangle.
- The source is averaged straight into that size and drawn 1:1 at its corner. A Type 3 glyph's raster keeps its two-pixel transparent frame, so there its corner is offset by −2 px.
- **A side shrunk by less than one pixel** gets no resize planned (`ceil` gives the source size back). On #2288, nearest sampling at the fractional scale drops a column there (18 px drawn 17.1 px wide). That side now keeps its source size and is drawn 1:1 at the snapped corner, at most one pixel wider than asked. Averaging it into one pixel fewer instead would turn crisp strokes into pairs of 50 % grey pixels wherever the two grids beat (6000 px drawn 5999.6 px wide at x = 0.6).
- If resizing fell back to the source size (allocation failure), the raster is drawn scaled as before, not placed 1:1.

title: fix(sign): explain 0x8009001D and 0xC0000225 when a store key's provider fails
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2207.

When PdfCraft lists the certificates in the Windows store for signing, a certificate whose key provider fails to load was shown only as "its private key's algorithm couldn't be read: Windows error 0x8009001D". `0x8009001D` is `NTE_PROVIDER_DLL_FAIL`: the DLL of the key storage provider holding the private key failed to load. The usual causes are smart card or token middleware that is missing or broken, or a provider that exists only as 32-bit code, which the 64-bit app can't load.

`describe` (`crates/sign/src/windows.rs`) now explains it, as it already did for a missing card, a missing provider or an unsupported operation:

> its key provider's software failed to load (a smart card or token driver that is missing or broken, or a 32-bit-only provider) (Windows error 0x8009001D)

Only the message changes. A certificate with this error is still left out of the list as before.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign -j 8 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign`, including `errors_are_explained_with_their_code`, which now covers `0x8009001D`
- [x] **Seen failing:** with the new mapping removed, the test fails

## Never-crash

- [x] One added `match` arm; no `unwrap` or `unsafe`.

## Provenance

- [x] No assets or copied code. The error code's meaning is from `winerror.h`.

## Security

- [x] No paths, channels or network touched

Also refs #1535: `0xC0000225` is the NTSTATUS `STATUS_NOT_FOUND`, which some smart card and token providers pass through when they can't find the key. It is the code an A3 certificate (key on a token) produces in that report. It is now explained as "its key provider can't find the key (the smart card or token holding it isn't connected, or its driver doesn't see the key)". The same test covers it, and fails with the new arm removed.

title: Render month and weekday names in XFA date patterns

Found while testing `crates/xfa/src/data.rs:265-281 (iso_to_pattern, with date_tokens at :242 and pattern_to_iso at :285; pattern built in crates/xfa/src/layout.rs:396 date_pattern)` (no existing issue): XFA date fields with a month-name picture (e.g. date{MMM D, YYYY}) show the literal text "mmm" instead of the month.

## Cause
`iso_to_pattern` only knew the tokens yyyy, yy, mm, m, dd and d. Tokens like `mmm`, `mmmm`, `ddd` and `dddd` were copied through as literal text, so `date{MMM D, YYYY}` showed `mmm 3, 2001`. `pattern_to_iso` could not parse them back either.

## Fix
`iso_to_pattern` now renders abbreviated and full month names and weekday names. The weekday is computed from the date. `pattern_to_iso` parses those names case-insensitively and rejects a weekday that doesn't match the date. A y/m/d run the converter doesn't know, such as `mmmmm`, now returns the ISO value unchanged from `iso_to_pattern` and `None` from `pattern_to_iso`, as the doc comment says.

## Verified
- Regression test `month_and_weekday_names_in_date_patterns`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa --lib month_and_weekday_names_in_date_patterns`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`date_pattern` in layout.rs is unchanged. It already accepts these pictures and lower-cases them. Its `E`→`d` mapping is also unchanged. I did not add a layout-level test.

title: M10: Export to Word keeps the page background colour (#2992)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2992.

**The problem.** A page coloured with Edit a PDF ▸ Background exported to Word as a white page. The text kept its colour, but the background was gone. `export::Page` carried only text blocks and images, and the Word writer had nowhere to put a page colour.

**The fix**

- **`pdfcraft_edit::page_background(doc, page)`** (new `crates/edit/src/background.rs`) reads the page's content up to the first thing it paints. That first paint is a page background when it is:
  - an opaque fill: `ca` 1, no soft mask, Normal blend
  - in a plain gray, RGB or CMYK colour (`g`/`rg`/`k`, or `cs`+`sc` in those spaces)
  - of a path with one rectangle covering the visible page (crop box, within 0.5 %), under the current `cm`
  - not clipped smaller

  Anything else painted first (text, a stroke, an image, a shading), a translucent or blended fill, a pattern, a fill with a hole, or a fill that doesn't cover the page gives `None`. This is how Edit a PDF ▸ Background draws a colour, and how many producers fill their pages.
- **`export::Page::background`** carries the colour. The engine fills it in `export_pages`.
- **The Word writer** sets it as the document's page colour: `<w:background w:color="…"/>` before `<w:body>`, plus a `word/settings.xml` with `<w:displayBackgroundShape/>`, which Word needs before it shows a background. It's added when **every page shares one non-white colour**. Word has a single background per document, so differing colours are left out rather than applying one page's colour to all.

HTML, RTF and PowerPoint exports are unchanged. They could use `Page::background` too, as per-page backgrounds, in a follow-up.

author: PerchAnton
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2592.

Adding `шалом` to a Helvetica paragraph while keeping a line break wrote five Type 3 fonts and five fallback text objects, one per distinct letter. A replacement with 300 missing glyphs was refused after 240 instead of using another font.

title: Fix cursor leaking from the PDF canvas onto the top mode bar
author: mr-mahfuj
body:
## Summary

The top mode bar (Menu / All tools / Read / Edit / Convert / E-Sign) sits above the PDF
canvas as a foreground panel, but the cursor over the bar was being driven by the
canvas's per-frame hover detection. Result: hovering the bar over a text box showed
the text I-beam, hovering over a box edge in Edit mode showed a resize cursor, and so
on. Clicks went to the bar (the bar is hit-tested correctly) — only the cursor was
wrong. This change adds a single, central guard so the canvas only writes a cursor
when the canvas actually owns the pointer.

## Root cause

`egui::Context::set_cursor_icon` (and `output_mut(|o| o.cursor_icon = ...)`) is
last-writer-wins within a frame. The PDF canvas's `page_input` family of functions
runs on every frame in every active mode and sets a cursor based on the raw pointer
position. Examples from the call sites that were setting the cursor unconditionally
when the pointer was over the bar's band:

title: Zero-pad required integer digits in FormCalc Format()
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2240-2276 ("format" builtin, number branch)` (no existing issue): FormCalc Format() ignores the integer part of a number picture: '9' does not zero-pad (Format("99999", 42) gives "42").

## Cause
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2240-2276` ("format" builtin, number branch), no existing issue. FormCalc Format() ignores the integer part of a number picture: '9' does not zero-pad, so `Format("99999", 42)` gives "42". The number branch of the `Format` builtin only counted the `9`/`z` characters after the `.` to get the decimals. It never read the integer part of the picture, so `9` behaved like `z`.

## Fix
The number branch now counts the `9` characters before the `.` as the minimum number of integer digits (capped at 20). It zero-pads the number to that width, including the decimal part, before grouping. The `$` prefix and the sign are applied afterwards. `z` stays optional, and numbers wider than the picture are not truncated.

## Verified
- Regression test `format_nine_pads_the_integer_part`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js --lib format_nine_pads_the_integer_part`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Date pictures and `Parse` are unchanged. The grouping, `$` and sign code is unchanged, but it now receives zero-padded digits for pictures with `9`.

title: fix(cos): write whole reals past the 32-bit integer range as reals
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

This came out of the review of #2877 ([comment](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2877)).

`pdfcraft_cos::writer::write_real` printed a whole-number real in one of two ways:
- below 1e15, as an integer (`r as i64`);
- above that, through `Display`, which never prints a decimal point for a whole number either.

So `Real(4e9)` was written as `4000000000` and `Real(1e30)` as `1000000000000000000000000000000`. Both are **integer** tokens:

- Our own lexer reads `4000000000` back as `Int`, so a real silently changes type across a save.
- ISO 32000-2 Annex C gives integers a range of ±2³¹−1 (reals go to about ±3.4×10³⁸). A reader with 32-bit integers may overflow on these tokens. `lopdf` rejected the 31-digit one outright, and #2877 works around that on the reading side.

Now:
- A whole-number real is written as an integer only within ±2³¹−1. Every ordinary coordinate keeps its current output (`595`, `-0` → `0`).
- Past that range it gets a trailing `.` (`4000000000.`, `1000000000000000000000000000000.`). §7.3.3 allows that form (its examples include `4.`). The digits are still `Display`'s shortest round-trip form, without an exponent.

Non-finite reals are still written as `0`. That is a separate fidelity question, raised in the #2877 review, and this PR doesn't change it.

`crates/content/src/lib.rs:401` has the same `< 1e15` integer cut-off for numbers it writes into content streams. I left it alone to keep this PR to `cos`; it can follow the same rule if wanted.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos`: all pass (56 lib tests)
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: OK

**New test.** `whole_reals_past_the_integer_limit_stay_reals` checks the exact bytes at the boundary (`2147483647`, `2147483648.`, `±4000000000.`, `1e30`, `595`, `-0`), and that values past the limit read back as `Real`. The `any_finite_real_round_trip…

title: fix(ui): the password prompt takes typing on Linux again
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Typing into the "Password required" prompt works again on Linux. Before, the cursor blinked in the field but nothing typed appeared, so encrypted files could not be opened. Fixes #2818.

**Cause.** The prompt's field called `request_focus()` on every frame. Since egui 0.36, `Memory::request_focus` also interrupts the input method (its doc comment says so). The field owns the IME output, so every frame's output set `ime.should_interrupt_composition`. egui-winit answers that with `window.set_ime_allowed(false)` and then `set_ime_allowed(true)`. In winit 0.30, that destroys and recreates the window's XIM input context on X11 and disables and re-enables text-input on Wayland. On Linux, typed keys go through the input method (on X11, winit passes every key press to `XFilterEvent` while the IME is allowed). Recreating it on every frame dropped each key while the input method still held it, so nothing reached the field. Windows delivers plain Latin keys as ordinary key input, which is why the prompt kept working there. #603, mentioned on the issue, is a different problem: a file with an empty owner password opens without asking for its password, so no prompt appears. @ch0kemeister's fix for that, on the branch [`fix/empty-owner-password`](https://github.com/ch0kemeister/pdfcraft/tree/fix/empty-owner-password), is waiting for a maintainer decision. It changes how a password is tried on open (crypt, cos, render, engine, CLI) and touches no UI code. This PR changes only the prompt's field, so the two don't overlap and either can land first.

**Fix.** Request focus only when the field doesn't have it. It still takes focus when the prompt opens and gets it back after Enter or a click elsewhere in the box. #1638 fixed the command search the same way (#1252, a Chinese IME on Windows). This prompt was the other field that asked on every frame. `password_modal` also draws the permissions-password prompt (Unlock…, and changing security), so that prompt is fixed…

title: fix(edit): a paragraph's width handle rewraps it from its whole handle, not just the inner half (#2276)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

In **Edit text & images**, hovering a paragraph draws a width handle on its left and right edges, and the pointer turns into the resize arrow a few pixels either side of the edge. Only the part of the handle inside the paragraph's box worked, though. A press on the outer half of the handle, or in the reach just outside it, started an **area selection** instead:

- its thin rectangle followed the pointer, which reads as the box being resized;
- on release it selected the paragraph at its old size, or nothing, and the text never moved.

That is what #2276 and its comment describe: the frame follows the mouse, then snaps back.

The cause is the order of the two handlers. Object selection (`object_ui`) sees the press first. It hands a press to the paragraph tool only when the press is on the paragraph's box, i.e. the text rect grown by 2 px. The paragraph tool (`edit_text_ui`) draws its 7 px handle centred on that box's edge and grabs the edge from up to 6 px outside. So in the gap between those two zones, object selection started a marquee and cleared the pending drag.

The fix: object selection now also leaves a press on a closed paragraph's edge grip to the paragraph tool.

- It uses the same edge test (`edge_at`), box (`paragraph_box`) and upright-page rule (`has_edges`) as the paragraph tool, through one new `edit_text_ui::grabs_edge`. The two can't drift apart again.
- `page_input` now uses those helpers as well, so neither the box nor the upright rule is written out twice.
- It applies only while no paragraph is open for typing on that page, which is the same condition under which the paragraph tool starts an edge drag. With a paragraph open, a press there still selects an area as before.

Nothing changes in the engine. The rewrap is the existing `EditTextBlock` with a width, so undo and redo restore the old and new widths, and the result is saved like any other text edit.

Fixes #2276

title: fix(ui): the header, footer and watermark previews show the page under the marks (#2837)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2837.

The Add/Update Header and Footer, Watermark and Background dialogs drew their preview on a blank white sheet. You could not see where the marks would land on the page's text and pictures. The preview now shows the page itself, with the marks drawn on top where the engine puts them.

- **The page's own picture.** The preview reuses the page's thumbnail from the canvas cache (`need_thumbnail` / `thumb_id`), as the Print dialog already does. It renders off the UI thread with the other thumbnails, so nothing is rendered on the UI thread. Until the thumbnail arrives the dialog shows the blank sheet it showed before. If the pages panel is open, the thumbnail is usually there already.
- **Which page.** It is the current page when the Page Range Options select it. Otherwise it is the first page the range does select, for example page 2 for "Pages from 2 to 2", or the first even page for "Even pages only". "Preview: page N of M" names that page. Before, the dialog always showed the current page, even one the range left out.
- **Size and rotation.** The page is drawn at its displayed size, after `/Rotate`, which is the frame `pdfcraft-edit` lays the marks out in. The thumbnail is rendered the same way, so a turned page shows turned, with the header along its displayed top.
- **Background colour.** It now tints the page picture (multiply) instead of being painted over it, because a background sits behind the content. White areas take the colour and the text stays on top. On a blank sheet the result is the same colour the dialog showed before.

No new strings, no engine change.

title: fix(ui): the mode tabs keep the hand over a page scrolled under them
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2755.

With the All tools panel closed, the first page sits under the mode bar's Read, Edit, Convert and E-Sign tabs, but not under All tools, which is left of the text. Once the page is scrolled up so that its text runs under the bar, those four tabs showed the page's cursor instead of the hand. With the panel open the page starts right of the tabs, so they kept the hand. That is the difference the issue describes.

**Why.** The mode bar is drawn first in a frame, and the page view runs after it, and the last cursor set in a frame wins. The page code took egui's raw hover position and tested it only against the page's whole rectangle. That rectangle goes on past the visible document area when the page is scrolled, and the top bar is on the same egui layer as the pages, so nothing else stopped it. Three things on the page did this:

- **The Select tool's text layer** (the default tool) gave the I-beam over any text under the tabs.
- **Edit text** gave the four-way arrow over a closed paragraph, or the I-beam once a paragraph was open (the issue's "click on a text").
- **The open paragraph's editor** is a foreground `egui::Area` placed on its paragraph. Scrolled up with the paragraph, it was drawn over the tabs. It showed its I-beam there and took their clicks: a click on Convert placed the caret in the paragraph instead of switching mode.

**The fix**, at each of those:

- The text layer and Edit text set their cursor only while the pages' own widget `contains_pointer()`. egui clips that widget to the visible document area, and Fill & Sign already uses the same check for its cursor. A selection being dragged keeps the I-beam past the edge, as before. Edit text's hover still returns what it did, so nothing else on the page changes.

title: M12: the page side of a measuring scale takes a unit, so 1:50 is 1 mm = 50 mm (#2752)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

A plan drawn at 1:50 now measures correctly when its scale is entered as 1 = 50 in millimetres. Before, a 10 mm line on the page read 1417 mm instead of 500 mm, and the reporter had to enter 1:17.5 to get the right lengths. Fixes #2752.

**Cause.** The page side of the Measure panel's drawing scale was always in PDF points. Its field had a fixed `pt` prefix, and Apply scale divided the real distance by that number of points. So "1 = 50 mm" was stored as 1 pt = 50 mm. One millimetre is 72 / 25.4 = 2.835 pt, so every length came out 2.835 times too big. To get the right lengths you had to enter 1 pt = 50 × 25.4 / 72 = 17.64 mm, which is the 1:17.5 the reporter found by trial and error.

**Fix.** The page side of the scale now has a unit, as a scale ratio on a plan does: "X unit on the page = Y unit in the real world".

- **Panel.** The `pt` prefix is replaced by a pt / in / mm / cm picker next to the page-side value. Until you pick one, it uses the real-world unit (in the Unit field). So 1 = 50 with Unit `mm` is 1 mm = 50 mm, which is what "1:50" means. When the real-world unit isn't one of the four (for example `m` or `ft`), it uses the display unit from Preferences (mm or in). Calibrate from two points fills in the page-side length in that unit, not in points. When you open the panel on a page, it shows the page's current scale as 1 page unit = its real length, instead of 72 pt = its real length.
- **Engine.** New `Scale::ratio(a, b, page, page_unit, real, unit, precision)` and `measure::PageUnit` in `crates/measure`. The page side is converted to points before the scale is built, so the PDF data keeps its meaning (ISO 32000-2 §12.9): the /X, /D and /A number formats convert user-space units to the real-world unit, here 50 / 2.835 = 17.64 mm per point. The /R ratio string keeps the units as entered: `1 mm = 50 mm` (it used to say `1 pt = 50 mm`).
- **Unchanged.** Scales read from files are used as stored (`Scale::read` is untouched), so existin…

title: M11: Optimize keeps a JPEG's colour transform (#1201)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Part of #1201: the "Optimization has a more serious problem" item (DCT `/ColorTransform` lost by Optimize). The `/Default*` colour spaces and the renderer's own CMYK/YCCK gap in #1201 are separate and not touched here.

Optimize read JPEG samples with the `image` crate's decoder. That decoder converts three components from YCbCr to RGB unless the JPEG itself says otherwise, and the rewritten image then lost its `/DecodeParms`. So an RGB JPEG stored untransformed (`/ColorTransform 0`, no Adobe marker) was converted anyway, and came out in other colours whenever Optimize touched it. That covers recompression, resampling, and merging page pictures printed as strips. In the test fixture the colours moved by 75 levels on average.

ISO 32000-2 §7.4.8 says an Adobe APP14 marker's transform flag decides, overriding `/ColorTransform`. Without a marker, `/ColorTransform` decides, and its default is 1 (YCbCr) for three components. `pdfcraft-optimize` (`images.rs`) now follows that:

- **Reading.** `pixels` finds the transform (`ycc_encoded`): it reads the APP14 flag from the JPEG's segments before the first scan, and `/ColorTransform` from `/DecodeParms`. It then decodes with `zune-jpeg` directly, the decoder `image` and the renderer already use (already in the lock; `pdfcraft-create` depends on it the same way). YCbCr samples are converted to RGB, and untransformed samples are taken as stored.
- **Writing.** Nothing changes. The new image is a plain YCbCr JPEG (no Adobe marker) or Flate, which is exactly what a missing `/DecodeParms` means, so dropping it stays correct.
- **Left as it is** when readers can disagree:
  - the marker and `/ColorTransform` contradict each other. The standard lets the marker win, but PdfCraft's renderer lets `/ColorTransform 0` win over a YCbCr marker;
  - either holds a value other than 0 or 1;
  - `/DecodeParms` isn't paired with the filter as §7.4 pairs them (a dictionary for a filter name, a one-element array for `[/DCTDe…

title: fix(forms): renaming a nested field checks the full name it would take
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

When you rename a field that has a parent, the new name is now checked against the other fields' names correctly, so it can't take one that's already in use. Before, `set_props` compared the new *partial* name with the other fields' *fully qualified* names. The check missed the clash it was there to catch, and it could also refuse a name that was free.

There's no issue for this; I found it reading the code. #2696 is related (periods in field names, and how dotted names are shown), but this PR doesn't resolve it.

**The defect.** A field's fully qualified name is its parents' partial names and its own `/T`, joined with periods (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.2). A rename changes only the field's own `/T`, so `MASTER.a` renamed to `b` becomes `MASTER.b`. The duplicate check in `crates/forms/src/author.rs` compared the bare `b` with every field's full name:

- **A clash got through.** With `MASTER.a` and `MASTER.b` in the form, renaming `MASTER.a` to `b` succeeded, because no field's full name is the bare `b`. The form then held two fields with the same fully qualified name. Per the spec that is one field, so their values merge: filling one fills the other.
- **A free name was refused.** With a top-level field `c`, renaming `MASTER.a` to `c` failed with `a field named "c" already exists`, although `MASTER.c` was free.

**The fix.** The new full name (the parents' part, then the new partial name) is now computed before the check, and the check compares that. The field itself is left out of the comparison, so a kid renamed to the partial name it already has still succeeds, as before. The error now gives the full name (`a field named "MASTER.b" already exists`), so it says which field is in the way. Top-level fields behave as before, because their full name is their partial name.

Nothing else about the rename changes. It still writes only the field's own `/T`: a kid stays under its parent, a field merged with its widget stays its own widget, and a field's wid…

title: fix(ui): the Read mode command leaves Edit as the Edit tab does
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Running Read mode as a command (View ▸ Read mode, Ctrl+H / ⌃⌘H, the command search) from the Edit tab now puts Edit text & images down the way choosing another tab does. A paragraph still open in the editor is applied and its editor closes.

**The defect.** #2241 made the Edit tab turn Edit text & images on, and made leaving Edit put the tool down again through `put_down_edit_text`, which also applies a paragraph still open in the editor. That code sits in `select_mode`, which only the mode bar reaches. The Read mode command goes through `switch_mode(.., false)`, whose `else` branch only set `self.mode`. Running the command from Edit therefore entered Read mode with:

- Edit text & images still the current tool, with every paragraph and image on the page boxed for editing;
- a paragraph open in the editor still open and editable over the page (`edit_text_ui::overlay` draws whenever `line_editor` is set, whatever the tool), and its edit not applied.

**The fix.** A new `enter_mode` sets the workspace together with its tool: Edit turns Edit text & images on, and leaving Edit calls `put_down_edit_text`. `select_mode` (the mode bar, and the default workspace when a document opens) and the `select_tools == false` branch of `switch_mode` (the Read mode command) both go through it, so the two routes can't drift apart again. The Read mode command still leaves the panels alone, as before. Only the tool changes.

**Relation to open PRs.**

- **#2809** (Read mode hides the quick toolbar, #2646) sets the tool to Select when entering Read mode, on both routes. That fixes the stale tool on its own, but not the paragraph: it doesn't go through `put_down_edit_text`, so an open paragraph stays open and unapplied in Read mode. This PR is the other half. The two compose: `enter_mode` applies the paragraph and puts Edit text down first, then #2809's line resets any other tool. They touch different lines of `switch_mode`, so either can land first and the other reba…

title: fix(comments): the note editor takes the keyboard once, so V and H pick tools again
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

After you add a highlight, its note editor in the Comments panel no longer holds on to the keyboard. You can still type the note straight away, as in Acrobat. Once you click the page or draw another comment, V and H pick the Select and Hand tools again instead of being typed into the note.

Part of #2669 (item 2). The other items have their own PRs: #2704 (item 1), #2706 (item 3), #2724 (item 4) and #2805 (item 5).

**Cause.** There were two causes, and each was enough to cause the bug on its own.

- The editor asked for the keyboard on every frame, whenever no other widget had it (`comments_panel.rs`, `card`). egui gives the keyboard up when you click outside a text field, so the next frame the editor took it back. Clicking the page or the toolbar never freed the keyboard.
- Adding another comment left the editor open on the earlier highlight (`editing.rs`, `apply_edit`, `Edit::AddAnnotation`). Only another highlight replaced it. Drawing a rectangle, an oval or a pen stroke is a drag, not a click, so egui never took the keyboard from the editor during it. The rectangle was added, the empty note stayed open with the keyboard, and the next V or H was typed into it.

**Fix.**

- The editor asks for the keyboard once, when it opens. `CommentView::open_editor` sets a one-off `EditorFocus::Take` and the card uses it up the first time it draws the editor. A new highlight, a double-click on a card and the card's Edit menu item all open the editor this way. After that, the keyboard goes where the user clicks, the way `search_focus` already works for the panel's search field.
- When a comment is added, `CommentView::comment_added` closes an empty editor left on another comment. An editor that already has text in it stays open with that text, so nothing typed is lost, but it gives the keyboard back (`EditorFocus::Release`, which calls `surrender_focus` the next time it draws). A new highlight then opens its own note as before, unless a note with text is …

title: M5: sticky notes stay upright where they are placed on rotated pages (NoRotate, #2583)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

On a page with `/Rotate`, a new sticky note's icon came out turned with the page (#2583: the bubble is "rotated 90 degrees"). It also did not start where it was clicked: the click was a different corner of the turned icon.

**Cause.** PdfCraft saves notes (and file attachments) with the NoRotate flag (`/F` bit 5), and draws their icon in an unturned 20 × 20 box. ISO 32000-2 §12.5.3 says what a viewer does with that flag: the appearance does not turn with the page, and the upper-left corner of `/Rect` stays where it is on the page. Neither the note's appearance nor the vendored renderer did anything with the flag. hayro-interpret fitted the appearance to `/Rect` (Algorithm 8.1) and the page turn rotated it with everything else.

**Why the renderer, not the appearance.** Rubber stamps (#1398) and typed text (#1710) are counterrotated in their appearance with a form `/Matrix`. That works for them because they do not carry NoRotate. A note does, so a counterrotated appearance would be turned twice by every viewer that honours the flag, and would still be wrong once the page is turned again later or for notes other programs wrote. Only the renderer knows both the flag and the page's current `/Rotate`. hayro-interpret is also where the other display flags are honoured: Hidden upstream, and NoView by an earlier PdfCraft patch.

**Fix.**
- **Renderer** (vendored hayro-interpret, patch 37, with a `vendor/README.md` entry). For an annotation with NoRotate, the appearance fitted to `/Rect` is then turned against the page's rotation about the rectangle's upper-left corner `(x0, y1)`. As displayed, the icon's top-left is that corner, and its width runs across and its height down, as on an unturned page. Form fields and links are left in `/Rect`, because PdfCraft takes their click targets from it (see below).
- **Where the note is drawn, for everything that points at it.** `pdfcraft_render::Annotation` (and `pdfcraft_annot::Summary`) gain `no_rotate`, and `A…

title: fix(ui): the Hand tool moves the page with the pointer
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

With the Hand tool, the page now stays under the pointer point for point, in the same frame the pointer moves. Before, it trailed behind the pointer and stuttered. Fixes #924. #1992 asks for a "mouse sensitivity" setting for the same tool. The cause there is the same lag (the reply on that issue says the hand "just needs to follow the mouse cursor"), so this should cover it too.

**Cause.** The Hand tool panned with `ui.scroll_with_delta(resp.drag_delta())` from inside the page view's `ScrollArea`. egui applies that delta in `ScrollArea::end`, after the frame's pages have been laid out and drawn. So every move showed up a frame late. Until #1986 made the page view's `ScrollArea` `animated(false)` (merged 2026-10-15, after these issues were filed), that delta was also eased in over several frames, with the target moving on every frame. That was the stutter. On top of that, the page widget senses both clicks and drags. egui only marks it dragged once the pointer has gone further than a click may wander (6 points). The points moved before that were never scrolled, so the page never caught up with where it had been grabbed.

**Fix.** The pan now runs before the `ScrollArea` lays the pages out, through `ScrollArea::scroll_offset`. When the page widget is being dragged with the Hand tool, the new offset is the last frame's offset minus this frame's pointer delta. On the frame egui recognises the drag, it subtracts everything the pointer has moved since the press instead. The offset is clamped to the content, as egui clamps it, so pulling past an end doesn't show the page there for a frame and spring it back. The page widget's id is kept from the previous frame, so the drag can be found before the widget is laid out again.

Unchanged:
- Clicks inside the click distance still don't move the page, so a right-click for the context menu doesn't nudge it.
- Letting go still stops the page where it is. The Hand tool had no fling and doesn't get one; egui's …

title: fix(web): host mode can wait for the page to confirm a save (opt-in, #1792)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

In host mode (`?host=parent`), a save counts as done as soon as `pdfcraft:save` is posted. The document is marked saved, the leave-page warning goes, and Save in the "save changes?" prompt closes the document at once. If the page has no listener, fails its upload, or navigates away, the edits are gone and nothing can bring the closed editor back. Fixes #1792.

This adds an **opt-in** acknowledgement. A page that answers saves says so once, and from then on a document counts as saved only when the page says it stored the file:

| Message | Direction | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `pdfcraft:init` (new, optional) | from the page | `acknowledgeSaves: true`, `saveTimeoutMs` (optional, default 120000, kept between 1000 and 3600000) |
| `pdfcraft:save` | to the page | `name`, `saveAs`, `bytes`, and, after `acknowledgeSaves`, `saveId` (an opaque string) |
| `pdfcraft:saved` (new) | from the page | `saveId`: the file of that save is stored |
| `pdfcraft:save-failed` (new) | from the page | `saveId`, `error` (a string the user sees) |

With the opt-in:

- The document keeps its unsaved state until `pdfcraft:saved` names the save's `saveId`, so `pdfcraft:dirty` stays `true` and the browser keeps warning before leaving.
- Save in the "save changes?" prompt (closing a tab, Close all) closes the document only then.
- `pdfcraft:save-failed`, or no answer within `saveTimeoutMs`, leaves the document open and unsaved with the notice "Couldn't save *name*: *error*" (or "...: the website did not confirm that it stored the file"). The user can save again, and a late answer for that save is ignored.
- The answer is bound to the version that was saved. If the user edits while the page stores the file, `pdfcraft:saved` leaves the newer edits unsaved and does not close the document. Typing not yet committed to a field also keeps it open.
- An answer whose `saveId` matches no waiting save (another save's, one already answered, made up) changes nothing. Ids start with a rand…

title: fix(render): draw each ICC profile through itself when two have the same stream dictionary (vendored hayro-interpret patch 40)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

No issue was filed for this. I found it while fixing #1201: its tests use several synthetic ICC profiles of the same length in one document, and some of them drew through the wrong profile.

**The defect.** The vendored hayro-interpret caches the colour space it builds from an `/ICCBased` profile stream in the interpreter's object cache. The key was `icc_stream.cache_key()`, and for a stream that is the hash of its **dictionary's bytes only**. Two different profiles whose dictionaries are byte for byte the same therefore shared one entry. That is common: `<< /N 3 /Length 3144 >>` describes any two uncompressed RGB profiles of one size. Whichever profile was read first won, and colours in the second space were converted through the first profile. The cache lives as long as the document, so this affected every page drawn after the first read, not just one page.

**The fix** (hayro-interpret patch 40, recorded in `vendor/README.md`). The space is now keyed by what its profile is read from (`IccProfileKey`), in two steps:

- **By object.** A space that names its profile stream by reference (`[/ICCBased 7 0 R]`, the normal case) is looked up by that object first. A lookup that hits does not read or hash the stream, so repeated lookups (every image drawn in an ICC space calls this) cost what they cost before.
- **By content.** On a miss, the space is looked up by the old dictionary key plus the stream's own bytes, decrypted but not decoded. Those bytes and the dictionary's filters decide the decoded profile, and the dictionary decides `/N` and `/Alternate`, so this key covers every input. A byte-for-byte copy of a profile in another object (merged documents often carry one per page) still shares one parsed profile and one transform.
- **Streams written directly in the array.** A stream written inside the colour space array has no object of its own. Its dictionary reports the object that holds the array, which every other stream written there reports …

title: fix(print): pages with Type 3 fonts go to Windows printers as pictures (#2684)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Printing to a printer on Windows no longer hands the Windows print component pages that draw with Type 3 fonts. Those pages are rendered by PdfCraft at the Print as image resolution (300 dpi unless changed in Advanced) and sent as pictures; every other page of the job stays vector, as before. Fixes #2684.

**Why.** @mtlcl410 reproduced the crash on Windows 11 with a virtual printer (FinePrint) and narrowed it to the Type 3 font Chrome wrote for the recipe's text: a glyph followed by code `0x0F` was enough. Windows.Data.Pdf renders the same page fine on its own, so the crash is in the print path (Windows.Data.Pdf drawing into Direct2D's print control, through craft-print). It is native (`0xC0000094` or `0xC0000005`), so nothing in PdfCraft can catch it and the whole app closes. Print as image (#1965) avoided it. This takes direction 2 of that comment: only the pages that need it become pictures, and only on Windows.

**How.**
- `pdfcraft_print::type3_pages(doc, pages, content)` finds the pages whose print draws with a Type 3 font. It reads resources, not content streams: the page's fonts (inherited ones too), and through form XObjects (forms in forms), tiling patterns, soft-mask groups (a shading pattern's too) and the appearances of the annotations that print under the chosen Comments & Forms. It never panics and is bounded: a seen-set per page, a depth limit (64) and a budget of 20,000 reads per page. A page whose resources go past the limit or the budget counts as using a Type 3 font, because the picture is the safe side. Broken entries (a `/Resources` that is a number, missing objects, a `/SMask` that is `/None`, cyclic forms) are not Type 3 fonts.
- `print::Settings::type3_raster: Option<Raster>` asks for this. `Session::print_pdf` renders the pages found the same way Print as image does (`print_raster::pictures`, sharing its render step with `rasterize`) and `pdfcraft_print::impose_with_pictures` draws each picture in its page's place, ove…

title: fix(ui): on-page text editors leave the mode tabs their pointer when scrolled under them
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Follows up #2755. The fix for #2755 handled the Edit text paragraph editor. Three other editors on the page had the same problem: the form text field editor, the Fill & Sign text box and the Add text box. Scroll the page up so one of them lies under the mode bar (All tools panel closed) and the Read, Edit, Convert and E-Sign tabs showed its I-beam. A click on a tab went to the editor, so the mode didn't change.

**Why.** Each editor is a foreground `egui::Area` placed at its spot on the page. egui keeps an `Area` inside the window by default, not inside the document view. So when the page scrolled under the mode bar, the editor was drawn over the tabs and hit-tested there. It sits above everything on the page's layer, so its `TextEdit` set the I-beam and took the click. Two of the tools also set their own page cursor from egui's raw hover position, tested only against the page's whole rectangle. That rectangle runs on under the chrome once the page is scrolled:

- **Form text fields** (`forms_ui::page_input`): the field's I-beam (or the hand, or the not-allowed sign) over any field under the tabs, open or not.
- **Add text** (`content_ui::page_input`): the tool's I-beam over the empty page, and the four-way arrow or a resize arrow over added text.

Fill & Sign already gates its page cursor on `resp.contains_pointer()`.

**The fix**, the same as for the Edit text paragraph editor in #2755:

- The three editors' `Area`s are `constrain_to(view.viewport_rect()).constrain(false)`. They are clipped and hit-tested only where the document shows. They stay where they belong on the page, cut off as the page is, rather than being pushed back into the window. Add text already had `.constrain(false)`.
- The form field and Add text cursors are set only while the pages' own widget `contains_pointer()`, which egui clips to the visible document area. That is the check Fill & Sign uses. What these functions return, and the clicks and drags they take, are unchang…

title: M10: exported images keep the page's CMYK and ICC colours (#2269)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2269.

The issue doesn't include the comparison image, so I built a synthetic PDF for each common kind of image. For each one I compared the centre pixel the page renderer draws with the same pixel in the exported file. Export all images, Save Image As and Word export all write images through `pdfcraft_create::image_file`, so they had the same problem.

Two things were wrong:

- **CMYK.** Export converted CMYK with its own formula, `(1 − c)(1 − k)`. The page converts it through the renderer's CMYK profile. Cyan ink came out as (0, 255, 255) where the page draws (0, 174, 239). Magenta was up to 115 levels off, and black ink came out pure black.
- **ICC profiles.** Export ignored `ICCBased` profiles: an Adobe RGB or Display P3 image came out as if it were sRGB, about 30 levels off.

Some JPEGs were also written as they are, so viewers and Word showed them in other colours: CMYK JPEGs, and JPEGs drawn through an ICC profile the file doesn't carry.

The fix reuses the renderer's own conversion rather than writing a second one:

- **Vendored hayro-interpret patch (39).** `color::device_cmyk_to_srgb` and `color::IccToSrgb` make public the conversions the renderer already uses for DeviceCMYK and `ICCBased`. Both check that input and output hold the same number of pixels.
- **`pdfcraft-render` wrapper.** `pdfcraft_render::cmyk_to_srgb` and `IccProfile` wrap them, catching panics like the rest of the crate. This keeps hayro behind `pdfcraft-render`, the bootstrap rule (ADR-0004).
- **`pdfcraft-create` (`extract.rs`).** Image export now depends on `pdfcraft-render` (L4 → L3, which `xtask layers` allows) and converts through it:
  - DeviceCMYK;
  - `ICCBased` grey, RGB and CMYK;
  - indexed palettes over those spaces, converted once;
  - 16-bit and inverted CMYK;
  - `/Matte` colours, now converted like the image, the way the renderer does.
- **JPEGs written as they are.** A JPEG is still written unchanged when the file shows the page's colours:
  …

title: fix(ui): the watermark and background previews show a file's picture (#2817)
author: guillehr2
body:
> Builds on #3009, the #2837 fix (branch `fix/2837-preview-page-content`: the marks dialogs' preview draws the page's own thumbnail). Merge that one first; this branch is one commit on top of it.

## What this changes

Item 14 of #2817, "Watermark Preview Show Image and PDF Content".

In **Add/Update Watermark** and **Add Background**, Source ▸ File (an image, or a page of a PDF) was previewed as a grey frame with the file name. You couldn't see how big the picture would come out, where an offset put it, or how its turn and opacity looked. The preview now draws the picture itself, where OK puts it.

- **Rendered the way OK brings it in.** A new engine function, `pdfcraft_engine::mark_picture`, takes the file through the same `mark_source` path OK uses: an image turned upright by its EXIF orientation (JPEG 2000, CMYK, TIFF's first page included), or a PDF page as a form, upright after `/Rotate`. It draws the picture alone on a page of its shape with `pdfcraft_edit::add_watermark` and renders it small (512 px a side for the preview). It renders twice, on white paper and over black, and takes the transparency from the difference. A PNG's alpha and whatever a PDF page leaves unpainted come through as transparent, while white the page really paints stays opaque. A file OK would refuse is refused here too.
- **Off the UI thread, cached in the draft.** The draft keeps the picture as a texture, keyed by the file and the page. One render runs at a time on a worker thread (in place where there are no threads, i.e. the web). The frame with the file name stays until the picture arrives, or when the file can't be drawn.
- **Laid out like `picture()` in `pdfcraft-edit`.** Fitted to the page at the scale relative to the page, centred plus the offset (points, right and up), turned counter-clockwise, at the opacity. A background has no turn or offset, as in the engine.

title: M2: Validate structure checks on a worker thread (core.arlington-validation)
author: guillehr2
body:
> **Stacked on #2774** (Arlington validation, branch `feat/arlington-validation`, which already carries its corpus commits). Until that merges, this PR's diff includes it; the new work is the last two commits (ff1d5ef0 and 8f84e002, a test fix for the Windows runner).

## What this changes

Standards ▸ **Validate structure** ran `pdfcraft_arlington::validate` on the UI thread. The largest file in the pinned pdf.js corpus (bug1978317.pdf, 163,867 objects) takes 1.4 s to validate in the dev profile, so the window froze for that long. title: M11: check the PDF/UA font conditions (optimize.pdfua-validate)
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

Builds on #2771 (Verify PDF/UA): **stacked on `feat/pdfua-validate`**, one commit on top. Until that merges, this PR's diff includes it; rebase once it lands.

Verify PDF/UA now checks the font conditions of ISO 14289-1 §7.21, the Matterhorn Protocol 1.1 **checkpoint 31** (all but 31-010, the licence condition, which only a person can judge), and **17-003**, that a formula's characters map to Unicode. **83 of the protocol's 87 machine conditions are checked** (54 before). The four left are 28-006, 28-014/015 (media clips) and 28-018.

- **New `pdfcraft_fonts::program`.** It reads what an embedded font program holds, using the skrifa/read-fonts already in the tree, within 16 MiB, and never draws:
  - Formats: TrueType, OpenType, CFF (CID-keyed too) and Type 1.
  - What it reads: glyph count, glyph names and CIDs, built-in encoding, cmap subtables, advance widths, and which glyphs have outlines.
  - A program that doesn't parse is `Unreadable`, not empty.
  - Small additions to `pdf.rs`, reusing the existing CMap lexer: `Metrics::cid` is now public, plus `Metrics::to_unicode_code_with`, `BaseEncoding` (the Annex D glyph names), `latin_glyph` and `cmap_program` (an embedded CMap's `WMode` and `usecmap`).
- **New `crates/a11y/src/pdfua/fonts.rs`.** Each font the content selects is held up against the codes it shows:
  - **CMap and CIDFont:** CIDSystemInfo Registry, Ordering and Supplement agree for CMaps other than Identity (31-001/002/003). The CMap is in ISO 32000-1 Table 118 or embedded (31-006). WMode matches the CMap stream (31-007). `usecmap`/`UseCMap` name only predefined CMaps (31-008). A Type 2 CIDFont names a CIDToGIDMap that is a stream or Identity (31-004/005).
  - **Against the embedded program:**

title: M11: Save as PDF/X-1a converts Lab, Cal, spot alternates, shadings and pictures of any depth (optimize.pdfx-convert)
author: guillehr2
body:
> **Stacked on Save as PDF/X** (storytold/pdfcraft#2777, branch `feat/pdfx-pdfa-convert`, itself on #2769, the PDF/X verification PR). This branch is cut from it at `bcea9dd0`. Review and merge those first; this diff then shrinks to the colour conversion.

## What this changes

Save as PDF/X-1a converts RGB and ICC-based colour to CMYK, and until now refused everything else: shadings, Lab, CalRGB and CalGray, spot colours with RGB or device-independent alternates, and pictures that weren't 8-bit or had a decode array. It now converts all of these. As before, the conversion runs on a copy and is kept only when PdfCraft's PDF/X verifier finds nothing. **What can't be converted exactly still refuses**, and the refusal names the reason.

`optimize.pdfx-convert` stays partial, with its notes rewritten.

### What converts now (`crates/preflight/src/recolour.rs`)

- **CalGray, CalRGB and Lab** (ISO 32000-2 8.6.5.2–8.6.5.4) convert through ICC profiles made from their parameters (`icc.rs`):
  - CalGray and CalRGB become matrix/TRC profiles (pure-gamma `para` curves, the matrix columns Bradford-adapted to D50);
  - Lab goes through a version 4 Lab profile that passes values straight to the connection space, after the values are adapted from the space's white to D50.

  `DefaultRGB` may be CalRGB too. A `BlackPoint` isn't compensated, as relative colorimetry doesn't.

title: fix(ocr): the text layer restores the rendering mode it sets (#3029)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3029. Thanks to @monkeyhut for the precise diagnosis.

`pdfcraft_ocr::text_layer` wrote its invisible text as

```
/OCR BMC
BT
3 Tr
/PCHelv 1 Tf
…
ET
EMC
```

The text rendering mode (`Tr`) and the font (`Tf`) are part of the graphics state, and `ET` doesn't reset them (ISO 32000-2 §9.3.1). `stamp` appends the layer as its own content stream, and a page's content streams share one graphics state, so every stream after the layer started in `3 Tr` (invisible). A header or footer added after OCR was in the file and `text` returned it, but neither PdfCraft nor MuPDF drew it.

The layer is now `/OCR BMC q BT … ET Q EMC`: the `q … Q` sits inside the marked content and restores the graphics state before anything later on the page runs.

**Not covered here.** Files already saved by 0.8.0 with an OCR layer still carry the unbalanced layer, so text added to them later would still be invisible. The issue's second suggestion is for the writers of added text (header/footer, watermark, `page_add_text`) to set `0 Tr` themselves. That would cover those files and any producer that leaves `Tr` set, but it touches several writers, so I've left it for a follow-up. Happy to send it.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-ocr -- --check`: clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ocr --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ocr --lib`: 10 passed
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine ocr`: passes
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: OK

**New test.** `the_layer_restores_the_graphics_state_it_changes` walks the layer's tokens. It checks that every `Tr`, `Tf` and `Tm` sits inside a `q … Q` and that the nesting ends balanced. With the fix reverted (the old `BT … ET` bytes), it fails with `` `Tr` outside q … Q ``.

**Render check.** A synthetic page has two content streams: the OCR layer, then `q /Artifact BMC BT /PCHelv 20 Tf 0 g 10 10 Td (Header) Tj ET EMC Q`, the shape the issue shows for the header. Dark pixels at 72 dpi:

title: fix(render): mesh triangles that share an edge leave no seam
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

No issue was filed. I found this while reviewing #3020: a synthetic Type 4 (free-form triangle mesh) shading drew a pure white line along the diagonal where its two triangles meet.

**The defect.** `TriangleSampler::sample_one` (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/encode.rs`) fills a mesh shading pixel by pixel. For each pixel it tests the pixel's corner `(x, y)` with `Triangle::contains_point`, which uses `kurbo`'s winding number and so is strict on edges. A corner that lies exactly on an edge two triangles share belongs to neither of them. That pixel gets no sample and is drawn in the shading's background (none, so white). The same happens to corners on the mesh's own sides. Shared edges that run through the sample grid are common: axis-aligned and 45° cuts of a grid, and any lattice (Type 5) or patch (Types 6/7) mesh, whose triangle grids are regular.

A red 30 × 30 square from 10 to 40 on a 50 × 50 page, cut along its diagonal, drawn with `sh` at 72 dpi:

| | MuPDF | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| two triangles, red pixels | 900 | 812 | 900 |
| the upper-left triangle alone | 465 | 406 | 465 |

**The fix** (hayro-interpret patch 41, listed in `vendor/README.md`):

- `Triangle::covers` is a barycentric point test that includes the edges, within 1e-9. A degenerate triangle covers nothing, because its zero denominator gives NaN or infinite coordinates that fail the test.
- A pixel whose corner no triangle holds strictly goes to the triangle that covers its **centre**, edges included.
- It still takes the colour **at its corner**, like every other pixel, and only if no triangle that holds the corner strictly gives it one (`entry().or_insert_with`).

So every pixel that was drawn before keeps exactly its colour. Only the pixels that were missing are filled. On the existing Coons and tensor fixtures from `patch_meshes_keep_their_corner_colours`, every pixel is unchanged from `main` (mean difference from MuPDF 0.58/255, max 2, the same as `main`).…

title: M11: Add Printer Marks (crop, bleed, registration, colour bars, page information)
author: saad-mughal435
body:
## What this changes

Print Production ▸ Add Printer Marks, the first of gap 18's print-production tools: crop and bleed marks, registration targets, a CMYK colour bar and a page-information line, placed around any page box (the trim box by default).

They are written as **printer's mark annotations**, the subtype ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.20 defines for exactly these graphics (registration targets, colour bars, cut marks), each carrying the spec's `/MN` name. Annotations rather than baked page content, so adding marks is not a destructive edit: the page's content stream and resources are untouched and the marks come off again. The rest of the codebase already handles the subtype correctly (`a11y` keeps printer marks out of the structure tree, `redact` keeps them, the renderer's inspector skips them), so this adds the producer those filters were already written for.

Details worth knowing:

- Crop, bleed and registration marks and the page information draw in a `Separation` with the colorant name `All` (§8.6.6.4), so they reach every plate. The colour bar's patches are `DeviceCMYK`.
- Boxes resolve as §14.11.2 requires: the crop box defaults to the media box and the bleed, trim and art boxes to the crop box, each clipped to the media box.
- The colour bar and page information are placed beyond whatever the corner marks and targets **actually occupy**, measured from those marks rather than re-derived from the style. Deriving it twice is how a bar ends up inside a registration target, or inside bleed marks that sit further out than the reference box does; a test over four very different styles pins this.
- Marks reach outside the box by design, so they need room on the sheet. `grow_media` enlarges the media box to fit them, writing it on the page so a shared `/Pages` node keeps the size other pages inherit; removal puts the original back, or takes the entry away again when the page had no media box of its own. Without `grow_media`, the pages whose marks fall outside are rep…

When the window height is reduced, the cluster at the bottom of the right rail (page input,

body:
## What this changes

Refs #2986 (layers hidden in the Layers panel still drawn on a cadwork export).

title: fix(reader): bound malformed-object diagnostics per load
author: PerchAnton
body:
## What this changes

Addresses **#2670, item 11 only**.

A damaged PDF could open successfully while eager compatibility loading wrote thousands of errors or warnings. The reader now shares **eight detailed records and one summary per load** across:

author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
