## What this changes

Remove Security was allowed when every `/P` permission bit was set, as if that meant "no permissions password". But a file can have a separate owner password and every bit set (pypdf and PyMuPDF do this by default) so the open password alone could strip its encryption.

title: fix(engine): printing keeps layers hidden in the Layers panel hidden (#3046)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3046.

`Session::print_pdf` handed `pdfcraft_print::impose` the document as it is. `impose` copies the catalog's `/OCProperties` into the print-ready PDF, so the sheets printed the layers in the **document's default state**. A layer hidden in the Layers panel disappeared on screen and came back on paper. *Print as image* was already right, because it renders with the document's render config, which carries the layer choices.

Now, once the layers have been changed (the panel or a set-layer action has filled `doc.config.layers`), the copy that is imposed gets its default configuration `/D` rewritten from `doc.info.layers`:
- `/BaseState /ON`, `/ON` = the visible layers, `/OFF` = the hidden ones.
- Its other entries (`/Order`, `/RBGroups`, `/AS`, …) are kept.

Only the copy changes; the document doesn't. With the layers untouched, the document's own configuration prints as before. That keeps any print-specific state the file sets up (`/AS` with `/Usage /Print`) working as the producer intended.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine`: all pass (275 lib tests, 1 ignored as before)
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: OK

**New test.** `printing_keeps_hidden_layers_hidden` uses a page with red in "Layer A" and green in "Layer B", prints it with `print_pdf`, and counts the colours on the rendered sheet:
- Untouched, both print.
- With Layer A hidden, no red pixel prints and green still does.
- Shown again, red prints again.

title: M11: PDF/X verification reads the shadings of shading patterns in /Pattern lists (optimize.pdfx-validate)
author: guillehr2
body:
> **Stacked on Verify PDF/X** (storytold/pdfcraft#2769, branch `feat/pdfx-validate`, head `4bed4382`). This branch is cut from it and adds one commit. Review and merge #2769 first; this diff then shrinks to that commit. It is **not** stacked on #2777 or #3028. It closes what #3028 lists under "Not fixed here": `pdfx::verify` didn't look inside shading patterns written into a resource `/Pattern` list.

## What this changes

`pdfx::verify` read the colour spaces of:
- shadings that are objects of their own;
- the shading written into a pattern that is an object of its own;
- the shadings in a resource dictionary's `/Shading` list.

It never opened a `/Pattern` list. So a shading pattern written into the list, with its shading written into it, was never seen. For example, this passed PDF/X-1a:

```
/Resources << /Pattern << /P0 << /PatternType 2 /Shading << /ShadingType 2 /ColorSpace /DeviceRGB … >> >> >> >>
```

RGB there also passed PDF/X-3 and PDF/X-4 under a CMYK output intent.

`defined_spaces` (`crates/preflight/src/pdfx.rs`) now walks each resource dictionary's `/Pattern` list. It covers:
- a list written into the resource dictionary or held as an object of its own;
- the page's resources, and a form's, a tiling pattern's or any other holder's inline `/Resources` (the holders the verifier already visits);
- the shadings written into the list's patterns, with the alternates and bases under their spaces.

That list is where `scn` with a pattern name looks, so content needs no new parsing. A listed space counts as used, as it already did for `/ColorSpace` and `/Shading`.

A shading or pattern that is an object of its own is still read only as itself. One shading named from several lists and patterns is therefore found once, on that object, and isn't also reported on every page that lists it. A new `written_shading()` helper does the "shading written into a pattern" test for both pattern objects and patterns in a list, so the two can't drift apart.

author: guillehr2
body:
**Stacked on #3014.** Please review and merge #3014 first. This branch is #3014's commit (437b691e) plus one commit on top, and only that last commit is new here. Until #3014 merges, the diff against `main` shows both.

## What this changes

"Back to all tools" in a tool panel and in Organize pages now leaves the workspace through `enter_mode`. The mode bar and, since #3014, the Read mode command already do. ## What this changes

Refs #2964 (text inside Form XObjects can't be edited) and #3005 (a table and signature become one box in Edit text & images).

Text drawn inside a **Form XObject** is grouped artwork in Edit text & images: it can be moved as a whole, but its text isn't offered for editing. #3005 is the common case. HTML-to-PDF converters wrap a block in a transparency group when something in it is translucent (a signature image with a transparent background), so the whole table becomes one box with no editable text. I reproduced it with a synthetic file: `object_list` shows one page-sized "image" and 0 paragraphs.

**Ungroup** draws one placement of the form in place, so its content becomes the page's own and edits like any other:

title: M7: pictures are picked where they show, not across their transparent margins (#3005)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3005 (a follow-up to #3067's known limits).

In Edit text & images, a picture is picked across its whole placement box, including its transparent parts. A PNG signature or a cut-out photo usually has transparent margins. When it overlaps a neighbouring picture, a click on the neighbour through that margin selects the transparent picture on top instead. After #3067 ungroups a #3005-style table, its three overlapping signature pictures show this directly.

Now **a picture with transparency is picked only where it shows**:
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/image_alpha.rs`): `Document::image_shows_at(image, point)`.
  - A picture with a soft mask (`/SMask`, `/SMaskInData`), a stencil or colour-key `/Mask`, or `/ImageMask true` is decoded once, through the same `pdfcraft_create::image_file` path that Export and Copy Image use.
  - Its alpha becomes an opacity grid of at most 256 × 256 cells. A cell shows if any pixel in it has alpha ≥ 16, so thin strokes and edges stay easy to pick.
  - The point goes through the inverse of the placement matrix, so flipped, rotated and skewed placements work.
  - Grids are cached per picture object for the current document generation, and every edit, undo and redo starts a new one. The cache holds at most 256 grids (64 KiB each).
- **UI:** the hover outline, click selection and drag start in `image_input` all use it.
- **Automation:** `image_hit` lists a picture only where it shows. Its tool description says so.
- **Copy Image** (`page_image_at`) picks the picture that shows under the pointer.

The whole box is still used for:
- **Form artwork.** Its transparency would need a render.
- **Pictures without transparency**, and those whose mask shows everywhere.
- **Pictures that can't be decoded:** JPEG 2000, JBIG2 and CCITT, which export can't decode either, and anything over 64 megapixels.

title: chore: cargo-deny ignores RUSTSEC-2026-0370/0371/0372 (zvariant, zbus_names, zvariant_derive; via eframe's AT-SPI)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Three advisories published on 2026-10-16 fail the **dependency licences and advisories** job on every PR, for example #3067's run [39044405250](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/39044405250/job/117430157455):

```
error[unmaintained]: `zvariant` is unmaintained          RUSTSEC-2026-0370
error[unmaintained]: `zbus_names` is unmaintained        RUSTSEC-2026-0371
error[unmaintained]: `zvariant_derive` is unmaintained   RUSTSEC-2026-0372
```

- All three are **informational (unmaintained)**: no vulnerability and no patched release. The crates were merged into `zbus` 6.
- They reach the tree only through egui's accessibility on Linux: `eframe → egui-winit → accesskit_winit → accesskit_unix → atspi / zbus 5`. PdfCraft has no direct dependency on them and can't move them until eframe does.
- No other zbus-family crate in `Cargo.lock` has an advisory (I checked `zbus`, `zbus_macros`, `zbus_xml` and `zvariant_utils` in rustsec/advisory-db).

This adds the three IDs to `[advisories].ignore` in `deny.toml`. Each gets a reason, they share one comment in the style of the existing `RUSTSEC-2024-0370` entry, and the comment says to remove them when eframe moves to zbus 6.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo deny --all-features check` (cargo-deny 0.20.2, the job's arguments): `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`.
- [x] With `main`'s `deny.toml`, the same command fails with all three IDs. The first push of this PR ignored only 0371 and failed in CI on the other two; that's fixed now.
- [x] No code change.

## Security

This is a policy change to the advisory gate, scoped to three informational advisories with the reason and removal condition recorded. Vulnerability advisories still fail the job.

title: M7: Add text writes the Central European letters of the standard fonts (#2098)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2098.

**The problem.** Edit a PDF ▸ Add text (`page_add_text`) draws with the standard 14 fonts in WinAnsiEncoding. WinAnsi has codes for š ž Š Ž, but not for **č ć đ** or the rest of Latin Extended-A (ł ő ę ď ť ă …). On current `main`:
- `page_add_text` refuses such text;
- in the desktop editor the box stays open with the text in it and it can never be committed.

So Croatian, Czech, Polish, Hungarian, Slovak, Slovenian and Turkish text can't be added.

**Why no font needs embedding.** The twelve standard text faces carry these letters (the Core14 character set: `ccaron`, `cacute`, `dcroat`, `lslash`, `ohungarumlaut`, …), and every viewer supplies those faces. A simple font can reach them through an `/Encoding` with `/Differences` (ISO 32000-2 §9.6.5.1), and viewers read them back by their standard glyph names (§9.10.2).

**What it does.**
- **`pdfcraft-fonts`**
  - `std14_metrics.rs` gets `EXTRA_LETTERS`: 66 Latin Extended-A letters with their glyph names and Core14 widths in the twelve text faces.
  - New `latin.rs` with `LatinEncoding` and `Std14::latin_text_width`.
  - `LatinEncoding` gives the extra letters a text uses codes of their own. Codes WinAnsi leaves undefined come first, then codes of WinAnsi characters the text doesn't use. The encoding is built from the text alone, so the same text always gets the same encoding.
  - `glyph_text` reads these glyph names back, so `text_lines`, find and Edit text see the letters. This also helps other producers' PDFs that name them.
- **`pdfcraft-edit` (Add text).**
  - Text with such letters gets a font entry whose `/Encoding` is `<< /BaseEncoding /WinAnsiEncoding /Differences […] >>`.
  - The entry is named `PCF<face>L<tag>`. The tag hashes the differences, so two items with different letters never share or overwrite each other's entry in the page resources.
  - Widths, wrapping, alignment and validation use the extra letters' standard widths.
  - Text that needs a shaping face (Arabic…

title: test: the image-drag pixel test waits for the page raster (flaky on windows-latest)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

`image_pixels_follow_the_frame_while_a_corner_is_dragged` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/editing.rs`, from #1677) fails intermittently on `test (windows-latest)` with:

```
the picture is drawn in the frame [[704.0 245.2] - [828.8 322.0]], not only at []
```

Two recent examples:
- #3070, [run 39047581578](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/39047581578);
- #3071, which changes only `deny.toml`.

So it isn't the PRs.

**Cause.** The drag preview draws the picture from the page raster, which arrives asynchronously. The test drags four frames after opening the document and never waits for that raster. On a slow runner it isn't there yet, so the preview draws no picture at all, hence the empty list.

**Fix (test only).** Before selecting and dragging, wait until `render_pending()` is false (up to 2 s), as other tests in this file do. Then assert that the raster arrived. No product code changes.

## How you verified it

- [x] **Reproduced the failure.** I added a 300 ms sleep to every page render (a local change, not committed) to stand in for a slow runner. `main`'s test then fails with the CI message (`not only at []`), and with this change it passes.
- [x] Without the delay, it passes as before.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --tests -- -D warnings`

# Acknowledge the new zbus unmaintained advisories

`main` went red on **dependency licences and advisories** today. Nothing in our code caused it:

title: Read stream-boundary comments as the renderer does, and isolate new marks from appended graphics state
author: skylartaylor
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3081
Fixes #3084

Two commits, in order (the second uses the comment boundaries the first records):

**1. `fix(content)`: a comment at the end of a content stream (#3081).** `Pieces::join` put a newline between a page's content streams, which ended a comment left open at the end of one stream. hayro, MuPDF and Poppler join with a space, so the comment runs on into the next stream and hides its first line. Edit text, `object_list`, the redaction audit, redaction and the Office/HTML export disagreed with the renderer, and redacting unrelated text revealed the hidden content.

- `Pieces::join` now uses a space, so every reader of the joined streams agrees with rendering.
- The parser records, per piece, whether a top-level comment runs into it and out of it. It records boundaries only, not every comment, so memory scales with the stream count. When redaction rewrites a piece, it ends an incoming comment before the first operator and leaves an outgoing one open, so hidden content stays hidden.
- `reading_blocks` (export) parses the streams joined instead of one by one. The redaction tag check uses the same joined reading.
- `Pieces::piece_of` is a binary search.

**2. `fix(edit)`: new marks inherit state from content after an earlier wrapper (#3084).** `place_tagged` wrapped the original content only if the page had no `Wrap` stream yet. Content appended after an earlier wrapper could leave a `cm`, a clip or text state set. That moved, hid or distorted every later header, Bates number, watermark, added text, flattened annotation and redaction cover.

- Placing a mark on top reads the page's operators rather than the `/PCMark` tags. When the content is well formed, the stretch from the first stream that leaves state set is wrapped once, at a stream boundary no comment runs into. Content that is already self-contained gets no new wrapper, so repeated marks don't pile up.
- Content that can't be read that precisely is wrapped whole, as before, …

title: feat: Improve automatic field detection with AI model
author: arjun-dureja
body: ## What this changes This PR adds @jbarrow's [FFDetr, used by CommonForms](https://github.com/jbarrow/commonforms), to the desktop Prepare a form tool. It detects text fields, checkboxes, and signature areas that the current detector can miss. The app asks permission for a one-time 121 MB download. Detection then runs offline in a background worker. It uses Rust and RTen, the existing OCR runtime, with at most two inference threads and a cached detector. The model stays outside the installer and Git history. The app sends no PDFs. Users can choose basic detection from the download prompt. The browser keeps its existing detector. - The dialog shows download and detection progress, with cancellation and retry. Downloads check the size and SHA-256 before atomic installation with licence notices. - Detection uses a document snapshot and rejects results if the document changes. It skips existing fields and adds transparent fields in one undoable step. - CLI and MCP tools include `form_detection_status`, `form_detection_install`, and `form_detect_fields` with `backend: "ffdetr"`. Model paths respect the configured automation roots. - English UI strings remain in code. Translations have moved to [craft-i18n PR #141](https://github.com/storytold/craft-i18n/pull/141); this PR contains no local translation catalogs. [The integration guide](https://github.com/arjun-dureja/pdfcraft/blob/feat/ffdetr-field-detection/docs/form-field-detection.md) has storage details and detection limits. In a manual check on one ten-page form, FFDetr found fields and checkboxes that basic detection missed. Radio groups, comb properties, and OCR-assisted field names on image-only pages remain unsupported. ## Before / after | Before: basic detection | After: FFDetr | | --- | --- | | |

title: Select the whole title when renaming a bookmark inline (#3099)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3099.

The inline bookmark rename field (opened by New Bookmark, Ctrl+B or renaming an existing bookmark) asked for focus but never set a selection. The caret then landed wherever egui's stored cursor for that field happened to be, so typing a new name produced things like "UntitledTable of Contents".

title: i18n: Turkish section titles and in-sentence labels keep İ and ı
author: ogzhnklvz
body:
## What this changes

Section titles are drawn upper case with `to_uppercase()`, and tool names inside sentences are lowercased with `to_lowercase()` (`in_sentence`). Rust's case mapping knows no language, and Turkish has a dotted and a dotless i (`i` ↔ `İ`, `ı` ↔ `I`), so with the Turkish catalog:

`i18n::upper_label` translates a title and upper-cases it with the Turkish rule when the label has a Turkish row. A label without one is still English and keeps the English rule, so it never reads "LİNKS". `in_sentence` lowercases with the Turkish rule in Turkish. `widgets::section_title` and the print dialog's Advanced header use `upper_label`. title: fix(render): emit clip-only text (7 Tr) to devices for text extraction (#3109)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Text drawn in clipping mode (`7 Tr`, `TextRenderingMode::Clip`) shapes the clipping path for visual rendering, but was previously omitted from device calls and thus dropped from text extraction, Search, and Redaction. This fix emits glyphs drawn under `7 Tr` to text devices with a dedicated `GlyphDrawMode::Clip` variant (distinct from `GlyphDrawMode::Invisible`), ensuring clipping-only text (such as gradient- or image-filled titles) is extracted and searchable while still allowing filtered extraction (`TextFilter { images: true }`) to preserve clipping-mode titles without retaining invisible OCR layers.

Fixes #3109

## What this changes

- Introduces `GlyphDrawMode::Clip` in `hayro-interpret::types`.
- In `hayro-interpret::interpret::text::show_glyph`, calls `device.draw_glyph(..., &GlyphDrawMode::Clip)` under `TextRenderingMode::Clip` after `clip_glyph`.
- In `hayro::renderer`, ignores `GlyphDrawMode::Clip` alongside `GlyphDrawMode::Invisible` so visual rendering does not paint clip-only text directly.
- Adds regression tests in `crates/render/src/text.rs` for `7 Tr` text extraction across search and `TextFilter` filtering, plus visual raster clipping assertions in `crates/render/src/raster.rs`.

Text typed into a comment card's note in the Comments panel reached the document only through the card's own Save button. File ▸ Save didn't write it, it wasn't counted as unsaved work, and Close or Quit could discard it without asking. Now:

- **Save writes the open note** (`commit_typing_in`, as a `SetAnnotationContents` edit), once. If the edit is refused, the note stays in the card and nothing is written.
- **A note belongs to the comment it was typed for, wherever that comment now is.** The card records a `DraftTarget`: the comment's `/NM`, or its type and exact rectangle without one. `DraftTarget::find` resolves it to that comment's **current** index, so deleting or undoing an earlier comment no longer loses the note.
  - It resolves only when **exactly one** comment on the page matches. With none or several, it never guesses and never falls back to the old index: a note with text is dropped and reported, and an empty one is cleared silently.
  - The panel shows the note only on the resolved comment's card, and that card's Save and Ctrl+Enter write to that card's own comment.
- **Close and Quit ask first** (`has_unsaved_work`), for:
  - a note that differs from its comment's text;
  - a typed note whose comment is gone. Cancel, then Redo, restores the comment and the note saves with it.

  An empty note whose comment is gone doesn't count.
- **File ▸ Revert closes an open note.**
- **Translations:** the notice "The comment being edited no longer exists, so its text was not saved." (`notify_tr`) is added to all 22 catalogs, with their `sha256` values updated in `ATTRIBUTION.toml`. The catalog coverage tests scan only `tl!("…")` literals, which is why they didn't flag it.

This follows @FredApps's review and CodeRabbit's reviews.

title: test(ui-egui): wait for the page raster before dragging an image corner
author: skylartaylor
body:
## What this changes

`image_pixels_follow_the_frame_while_a_corner_is_dragged` fails intermittently on `test (windows-latest)`, and passes on rerun:

```
the picture is drawn in the frame [[704.0 245.2] - [828.8 322.0]], not only at []
```

I found 17 failures between 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-17 on unrelated PR branches. All were Windows and all were first attempts. Linux had none. The test has been flaky since it landed in #1677.

**Cause.** The live drag preview stretches the whole-page raster (`DocView::page_raster`) into the dragged frame, and draws nothing until that texture exists. The render pool's worker threads produce that raster asynchronously. The test only ran a fixed number of frames before dragging, about 50 ms of wall time for the whole test. When a busy Windows runner hadn't parsed and rendered the page by then, no picture mesh was drawn. The frame is drawn from geometry alone, so it was still correct. That's why the message shows a right frame and an empty list.

**Fix.** This is a test-only change. It adds a bounded wait (up to 10 s, until `render_pending()` is false, then asserts) after the zoom change and after each undo, the same settle pattern `ui.rs`, `view.rs` and `comments.rs` use. The assertions are unchanged. With no raster yet, the app shows the frame without pixels. That's the intended fallback, so the product code stays as it is.

When page interpretation exhausts `MAX_NESTED_PAINTS` (50,000) or `MAX_NESTED_INTERPRETATION_DEPTH` (50) in `hayro-interpret`, nested paints and interpretations are skipped to prevent stack overflows and unbounded execution, but the interpreter did not set `CONTENT_TRUNCATED`. title: Control channel: don't lose the refusal reply to a TCP reset (fixes deadline test flake)
author: skylartaylor
body:
## What this changes

Fixes the flaky `control::transport_tests::an_unauthenticated_connection_is_closed_at_the_deadline`, which fails on ubuntu-latest at the "Dripping" half (`next_line(...).expect("the server says why before closing")`), including on `main` (run 39096170330 at d8b27058).

**Cause.** When the control channel refuses an unauthenticated connection (auth deadline passed, overlong line, bad first request), it wrote the error line and closed the socket immediately. If the client had sent bytes the server had not read yet (the dripping client always has), Linux answers `close()` with a reset instead of a FIN, and the reset discards the reply before the client reads it. macOS does not lose the data, so it only shows up on Linux. This is a real bug, not just a test problem: a client that is still sending when refused never learns why. The existing `an_overlong_line_before_auth_is_refused` test already works around it by sending exactly limit + 1 bytes "so the close below is a clean end of stream".

**Fix (first commit).** A new `close_after_reply` does `shutdown(Write)` after the reply (so a FIN follows it), then reads and discards input until the client closes its side or a linger period passes (new `Limits::linger`, 1 s), and only then closes. Every read is bounded by the time left through the existing `Reading` deadline logic; no panics, no allocations sized by input. It applies to all three refuse-and-close paths on the connection thread.

**Lingering does not cost an authentication place (second commit).** Before writing a refusal, `refuse` gives back the connection's place among `max_unauthenticated` and takes one of a separate set of lingering places (new `Limits::max_lingering`, 8). So a refused connection never keeps a real client out, and the number of lingering threads is still bounded (#1806). When all lingering places are taken, the refused connection is closed right after the FIN instead of lingering: no wait, and the small risk of a reset is…

title: Prevent oversized GPU textures after page replacement (#3149)
author: PerchAnton
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3149.

Replace Pages can commit after the canvas has collected a frame's render requests. Those requests still contain scales and page indexes for the original document. Replacing a 200×300 page with a 400×500 page at scale 4.7 can therefore ask the new renderer for a 1880×2350 image on a device whose maximum texture side is 2048.

Page-list changes now cancel that frame's demand and request another layout before submitting work to the replacement renderer. Independently, the result receiver checks actual dimensions against the current egui/GPU limit before cache eviction, pixel conversion or any page/tile/thumbnail/organize/print-preview upload. Rejected results keep the previous cached image; the next layout requests bounded backdrops and tiles.

title: fix(render): apply the JP2 palette of a JPX image with no /ColorSpace (#3179)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3179.

A `/JPXDecode` image whose dictionary has no `/ColorSpace` now takes its palette from the JP2 header. Before, every JPX image was decoded with `resolve_palette_indices: false`. When the JP2 data has a palette (`pclr`), the samples are palette indices. With no `/ColorSpace`, nothing applied the palette, so the indices were drawn as a gray image (the noise in #3179).

ISO 32000-2 §7.4.9: with no `/ColorSpace`, the colour comes from the JPEG 2000 data. With a `/ColorSpace`, that data's colour information is ignored. So the palette is resolved exactly when the dictionary has no `/ColorSpace` (`params.num_components.is_none()`). An `/Indexed` space still gets the raw indices.

The change is one line in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/filter/jpx.rs`, marked `PdfCraft patch:`. `vendor/README.md` has a separate paragraph for it. I did not edit the patch table, so this does not conflict with #2400, which adds patch 18 there.

## How you verified it

- Two unit tests in `filter::jpx::tests` decode a 257-byte, 4×2 JP2 written for the test. The JP2 has one 8-bit component that indexes a two-entry sRGB palette (red, blue), with `pclr` and `cmap` boxes.
  - `jpx_palette_is_applied_without_a_color_space`: with no colour space, the result is RGB red/blue.
  - `jpx_palette_indices_stay_raw_for_an_indexed_color_space`: with `/Indexed`, the result is the raw indices `0 1 0 1 1 0 1 0`.
- Mutation check. With the setting forced to `false` (the old behaviour), the first test fails. With it forced to `true`, the second test fails.
- Synthetic PDF with that JP2 and no `/ColorSpace`, at 72 dpi:
  - MuPDF draws red and blue;
  - `main` @ `d8b27058` draws `(0,0,0)` and `(1,1,1)`, the raw indices;
  - this branch draws `(255,0,0)` and `(0,0,255)`.

title: Prevent overflow when rotating added images through automation
author: PerchAnton
body:
## What this changes

An added image already rotated by 90° makes `content_update` panic when passed `rotate: 9223372036854775800`. This is a valid integer multiple of 360, so it should leave the orientation unchanged. Instead, the tool adds the degrees to the current rotation before reducing them: debug CLI builds exit with code 101 (`attempt to add with overflow`), and MCP returns an internal error through its panic guard.

Normalize the requested angle to quarter turns before adding it to the current orientation. The addition stays bounded, and valid large positive or negative angles retain the existing geometry, crop, flips, history and save behavior.

Found independently while testing automation integer boundaries. The separate index-overflow fix in #2979 and page-rotation fix in #1512 do not cover this added-image path.

title: Report clipping-only (7 Tr) text to the text device for extraction
author: SENESO
body:
Fixes #3109.

Text drawn with rendering mode 7 (`7 Tr`, clipping without filling or stroking) was invisible to text extraction, Find, word count, and search-redaction, even though it renders on the page. In `show_glyph`, the `Clip` arm called only `clip_glyph` and never reported the glyph to the text device.

title: fix(forms): an XFA form whose config forbids dynamic rendering is static (#3180)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3180.

An XFA form with no AcroForm fields was always classified as dynamic (`crates/render/src/inspect.rs`, the `fields.is_empty()` arm). The engine then laid out the template on open and appended the result as a revision. So for a static form without fields, the user was editing PdfCraft's layout instead of the file's own pages. Every save, even one with no change, wrote those replacement pages, and nothing said so.

As @jpeskov pointed out on the issue, the form says what it is. Adobe Designer writes `<dynamicRender>forbidden</dynamicRender>` (under `config/acrobat/acrobat7`) for a static PDF form. A form whose config says `forbidden` is now `Xfa::Static`, and its pages are kept.

- `/NeedsRendering true` still makes a form dynamic, even with `forbidden`.
- A form with no fields and nothing in the config about it stays dynamic, as before.
- Forms with fields are unchanged.

`Inspector::xfa_dynamic_render` finds the `config` packet in an `/XFA` array, or uses the whole-XDP stream. It decodes at most 16 MiB and scans for the one element with `xml_element_text`, a small byte scanner. That scanner accepts a namespace prefix and Designer's `<name\n>` tags. It returns `None` for anything malformed or cut short.

This is the `forbidden` half only. PR #1566 (EULArule, M12) reads `dynamicRender` `required` to lay out a form that already has fields. The two don't overlap: this PR only changes forms without fields.

## How you verified it

- New tests:
  - `pdfcraft-render` `inspect::tests::xml_element_text_reads_one_element_as_designer_writes_it` covers Designer's tag style, a prefix, a longer name, self-closing and empty elements, and every truncation with no panic.
  - `pdfcraft-render` `inspect::tests::an_xfa_form_without_fields_is_static_when_its_config_forbids_dynamic_rendering`: `forbidden` gives static, `required` and no config give dynamic, and `/NeedsRendering` plus `forbidden` gives dynamic.

title: Vendor and patch hayro-cmap for tolerant CMap parsing
author: charan-rathore
body:
Fixes #3177.

A `/ToUnicode` CMap with any unparsable part (a malformed `bfchar`/`bfrange` entry, a `usecmap` naming an unresolvable CMap, or a truncated stream) made the reading path discard the **whole** map and fall back to the font's encoding for every code. PdfCraft's edit layer already parses the same CMaps tolerantly, so `text_find` / search-redact missed text that edit/export could see - and MuPDF/pdftotext agree with the edit layer.

Following the vendoring pattern in `vendor/README.md` ("each patch is meant to go upstream"):

- Vendor `hayro-cmap` 0.1.0 under `vendor/hayro-cmap` with a `[patch.crates-io]` entry.
- Patch `parse.rs` (8 `PdfCraft patch:` markers) to skip malformed parts instead of discarding the map: bad `bfchar`/`bfrange` entries are skipped per-entry, an unresolvable `usecmap` drops only the base reference, and a truncated stream keeps every entry collected so far (a stream that yielded nothing still reports failure, so callers fall back exactly as before).
- `vendor/README.md` row documents the patch and its tests.

Tests (in the vendored crate, `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/hayro-cmap/Cargo.toml`):
- `bad_bfchar_entry_is_skipped`: a `<41> <ZZZZ>` entry is dropped while `<42> <0059>` still maps.
- `unresolvable_usecmap_is_skipped`: `/Bogus usecmap` is dropped while the following valid `bfchar` still maps.
- Both fail against pristine hayro-cmap 0.1.0 (RED-verified); full vendored suite: 39 passed, 0 failed. `cargo check` on the workspace passes with the patch applied.

title: fix(ui): separate print preview grayscale bitmask from PRINT_TAG (#3156)
author: Ozt-y
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3156.

In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `GRAYSCALE_TAG` was defined as `1 << 60`, which was identical to `PRINT_TAG` (`1 << 60`) from `pdfcraft-render`.

When queuing print preview rasters, requests are tagged with `PRINT_TAG` and optionally `GRAYSCALE_TAG` if `Print in grayscale` is selected:
```rust
let tag = scale_tag(scale) | PRINT_TAG | if self.grayscale { GRAYSCALE_TAG } else { 0 };
```

Because `GRAYSCALE_TAG == PRINT_TAG`, the check on incoming preview rasters (`canvas.rs:1825`):
```rust
if r.request.tag & GRAYSCALE_TAG != 0 { grayscale(img) } else { img }
```
unconditionally evaluated to `true` for every print preview raster, causing preview sheets to be converted to grayscale even when `Print in grayscale` was not selected.

### Diff sketch
```diff
crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs
- const GRAYSCALE_TAG: u64 = 1 << 60;
+ const GRAYSCALE_TAG: u64 = 1 << 59;
```

## Evidence

### Before fix (TDD RED)
Both unit tests asserting tag mask independence and color preview tagging failed:
```text
running 2 tests
test canvas::tests::print_preview_grayscale_tag_does_not_collide_with_print_tag ... FAILED
test canvas::tests::print_preview_requests_distinguish_color_and_grayscale ... FAILED

failures:
---- canvas::tests::print_preview_grayscale_tag_does_not_collide_with_print_tag stdout ----
assertion `left == right` failed: PRINT_TAG and GRAYSCALE_TAG must use distinct bit masks to prevent color previews being forced to grayscale
  left: 1152921504606846976
 right: 0

---- canvas::tests::print_preview_requests_distinguish_color_and_grayscale stdout ----
assertion `left == right` failed: color preview must not carry GRAYSCALE_TAG
  left: 1152921504606846976
 right: 0
```

### After fix (TDD GREEN)
Both unit tests pass cleanly:
```text
running 2 tests
test canvas::tests::print_preview_grayscale_tag_does_not_collide_with_print_tag ... ok
test canvas::tests::print_preview_requests_distinguish_color_and_grayscale ... ok

test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0…

title: Make app.ron readable while preserving old preferences (#2451)
author: PerchAnton
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2451. Related: #2449.

Desktop `app.ron` currently places the PdfCraft settings in one escaped JSON string. Save that block as indented JSON inside a valid RON raw string, so settings can be read and edited on separate lines. Keep the existing string-map schema, preference keys, legacy `printcraft` settings, window state, egui memory and previously stored keys.

Publish the file atomically from the native `App::save` callback. eframe uses a private temporary working copy for its compact serializer. This also handles macOS `terminate:`, which does not return through `run_native`. The wrapper delegates the existing application callbacks. Unchanged autosaves skip formatting and publication only when both the storage map and the exact contents of the validated writable target match the last successful save. Same-size/same-time external edits, deletion and read errors are cache misses. The active session remains authoritative; failed saves retain the previous cache and can retry. Cached target bytes are limited to 16 MiB; larger snapshots save without caching.

Prettification has input/output budgets. A new snapshot that exceeds them still saves in compact form; an unavailable adapter falls back to existing eframe persistence with a warning. File permissions are retained. The working directory uses tempfile's defaults (0700 on Unix); OS termination can leave it for OS temporary-file cleanup. Details are in `docs/development.md`.

title: Ungroup grouped Form artwork
author: Lcoding15
body:
<!--
Thanks for contributing to PdfCraft.

Base this on `main` — it is the only integration branch. `main` moves fast (it took
396 commits in the three days to 2026-10-12), so a PR that sits for a day usually needs
a rebase. Rebasing the same day you are asked keeps the work from dying of conflicts.
Delete any section below that does not apply.
-->

## What this changes

**Ungroup for grouped Form artwork** in Edit text & images (#2964, #3005). Some producers (WSCAD exports, for example) put a whole page's content into one Form XObject, so PdfCraft selects the entire page as one group and none of its text or pictures can be edited. Ungroup draws the form's content in place of its `Do`, wrapped as `q <Matrix> cm <BBox> re W n … Q`, with the form's resources merged into the page's under names that do not clash. The form object itself is left alone, so other pages that draw it are unchanged. Reachable from the context menu, by double-clicking the group, and headlessly through `image_edit` `ungroup`. Each Ungroup is one undo step.

Ungroup **refuses** (the artwork stays grouped, with a message) whenever painting the content directly could look different: transparency groups whose blending would change, a `Do` inside a text object, different default colour spaces, damaged or unbalanced content, and resource renames that a nested Form without its own `/Resources` would miss.

It also contains the `/ToUnicode /Identity-H` fix, which is now split out into its own PR, #3497.

**Status:** #3067 implements Ungroup too and was opened first, so I'm deferring to it (see my comment below). This PR stays open only until the maintainers confirm; the Identity-H fix should go in through #3497. If useful, the double-click to ungroup and the nested-Form rename guard can follow #3067 as a small follow-up PR.

title: M7: never encode typed text with CID 0 (#3223)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3223.

Editing a line in a PDF exported from Microsoft Word drew a box at every space once the editor closed. The reporter's file shows the cause. Its Type 0 font (`BCDEEE+TimesNewRomanPSMT`, Identity-H, `/CIDToGIDMap` stream) has a ToUnicode CMap that maps **both** CID 0 and CID 7 to U+0020: `<0000> <0002> [<0020> <004D> <00E1>]`. It also gives CID 0 a width in `/W` (`0 [778]`). CID 0 maps to GID 0, `.notdef`. The real space is CID 7, which maps to GID 3 `space`.

`Metrics::encode` keeps the lowest code that shows a character. `has_glyph` accepted CID 0 because `/W` lists it. So every typed space became `<0000>`. The reporter's Modified.pdf has 10 of those in the rewritten line and no `<0007>`. Each one draws the `.notdef` box at 778 units instead of a 250-unit space. That is also why the line got condensed (`87.08 Tz`), which looks like a different font.

CID 0 is `.notdef` in every CIDFont, and a code that a CMap leaves unmapped lands there too. So `has_glyph` now refuses CID 0 for composite fonts. Decoding is unchanged: existing text that uses CID 0 still extracts as a space.

## How you verified it

- New unit test `composite_fonts_never_encode_with_cid_0` mirrors the Word font: CID 0 and CID 7 both map to space, and CID 0 has a width. Without the fix it fails with `Some([0, 1, 0, 5, 0, 0, …])` against the expected `[… 0, 7 …]`. With the fix it passes.
- The property test `lookups_match_the_expanded_mappings` models the reverse map, so its model now leaves code 0 out too.
- End to end on the reporter's Original.pdf, replacing page 1 line 6 through `text_edit`:
  - 0.9.0 (d8b27058) writes 10 × `<0000>` and 0 × `<0007>`;
  - this branch writes 0 × `<0000>` and 10 × `<0007>`;
  - `pdftotext` reads both the same, because the ToUnicode maps both codes to a space. The difference only shows when the page is drawn.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

author: mtlcl410
body:

Fixes the first part of #3205: `pattern=phone` missed three Italian formats.

| Text | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tel. 0426/123456` (landline, slash) | missed | marked |
| `cell. 3451234567` (mobile, no separator) | missed | marked |
| `cell. +393451234567` (+39, no separator) | missed | marked |

- **Slash.** `/` now counts as a separator when it sits between two digits. It only counts in a number whose area code starts with a trunk 0 (the national rule). The second part of #3205, telling the user which numbers were not marked, is not in this PR.

title: M3: extract text from glyph names outside the Adobe Glyph List (#3169, #3170)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3169 (fixes its glyph-name case B; A is left open, see below) and #3170 (not fixed by this PR any more, see below).

A simple font without a usable `/ToUnicode` gets its text from glyph names. When a name was not in the Adobe Glyph List, the glyph was dropped from the extracted text even though the page drew it.

**Full AGL mapping** (`glyph_name_to_text` in hayro-interpret). This follows the [Adobe Glyph List Specification](https://github.com/adobe-type-tools/agl-specification): drop everything from the first `.`, split the rest on `_`, and map each part through the list or as `uniXXXX…` / `uXXXX`–`uXXXXXX` (uppercase hex only, as the specification says). `f_i`, `f_l` and `hyphen.case` now read as `fi`, `fl` and `-`. It applies to Type 1, CFF, non-embedded standard and embedded TrueType simple fonts.

**Removed after review:** an earlier version also read names that only number the glyph (`C39`, `c251`) as the code's character in StandardEncoding. @ahmadmuj showed that this invents characters: in embedded CFF and Type 1 fonts where byte 233 selects `/C1`, it extracted `Ø` for a glyph drawn exactly like `/eacute`. Such names say nothing about the character, so they read as nothing again, as on `main`.

What that costs:
- **#3170** (the 821-page book set in fonts with `C`-numbered names) gets back to extracting almost nothing. With the fallback it extracted 1,895,402 characters against 4,058 on 0.9.0; that gain came from the guess, so the issue stays open. A fix needs something that knows the glyph, such as its outline or a `/ToUnicode`, not its code.
- **#3169 case A** (`c251` small caps) likewise reads as before.

**Unit test** `text::tests::glyph_names_outside_the_glyph_list_still_read_as_text` (pdfcraft-render), one glyph per line. `/Differences` with `f_i`, `f_l`, `hyphen.case`, `C39`, `c251`, `C174`, `uni00660069`, `a12`, `foo`, `C39.sc` and `/C1` at 233 reads as `fi fl - fi`: the numbered names, `a12` and `fo…

title: Document how to write a change, with tests and a human session
author: ihsanmokhlisse
body:
## What this changes

`docs/developing.md` is the procedure for writing and fixing a change. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` point at it.

A new behaviour needs a unit test. A command or a saved file also needs a tool or crate integration test. A click, typed edit, or drag needs a session in `crates/ui-egui/tests/play/`. A bug fix is accepted only when that test was seen to fail on the code without the fix, then pass, with the older tests in the same area still green.

title: Box Type 3 glyphs by their own bounds so lines set in bitmap fonts stay apart (#3171)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3171.

## Cause

The cause is the one the issue suggests. `draw_glyph` in `crates/render/src/text.rs` gives every glyph the -200..800 em box in 1000-unit glyph space, so the box is as high as the font size. A Type 3 font's size is only nominal, though. The fixture sets its bitmap fonts at 58 pt, but the glyphs are about 5 pt high and the lines are 8.4 pt apart. Each glyph box was therefore about 58 pt high and overlapped the lines above and below. The layout then joined the six lines that start at x = 371.1 into one line and ordered their glyphs by x ("EDTwIS...").

## Fix

- `Type3::glyph_bounds` (vendor patch in `hayro-interpret/src/font/type3.rs`) reads the glyph's `d1` bounding box from its glyph procedure. If there is none (a `d0` glyph), it uses `/FontBBox` when that is non-empty. It maps the box through `/FontMatrix` into the same 1000-unit glyph space that `draw_glyph` uses. `Type3Glyph::vertical_bounds` exposes it, next to the existing `advance_width` patch.
- `draw_glyph` uses those vertical bounds for Type 3 glyphs. When they are missing or empty (for example `/FontBBox [0 0 0 0]` with no `d1`), it keeps the old em box. Outline glyphs are unchanged.

## Test

`type3_lines_are_boxed_by_their_glyphs_not_by_the_font_size`: a synthetic Type 3 font set at 58 pt with `/FontBBox [0 0 0 0]` and glyphs 100 units high (5.8 pt), and two lines 8.4 pt apart that start at the same x, like the fixture. The test expects `"ab\ncd"`. With the old em box, the two lines overlap and merge.

title: Fix blank glyphs inside overprinted numbers and word gaps next to taller glyphs in text extraction (#3172)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3172.

The issue reports two problems on the same cover headline. Both are fixed here, in `crates/render/src/text.rs`:

- **Blanks inside `1.4GB` and `1GB`.** The white sentence is a second text run drawn over the big digits, with blank glyphs where the digits sit. The runs only interleave (they do not collide by `RUN_COLLISION`), so `place_glyphs` keeps them in x order and the blanks came out between the digits. The new `drop_covered_blanks` runs after `place_glyphs` on segments with two or more text runs and removes a blank glyph when more than half of its width is covered by the ink of other glyphs on the line. A blank that stands in a gap is kept. A single-run segment is not touched, because only another run can draw over a run's blanks. Dropping a glyph from the output works the same way as the existing "fake bold" redraw filter.
- **`50FREE`.** The word-gap test used the segment height, which is the tallest glyph on the line (the 39 pt digits), so the 5.3 pt gap after `50` was under the limit. The limit for each gap now uses the smaller height of the two glyphs on either side of it. It is capped at the old line limit, so a gap that was a word break before stays one. The line's typical letter gap (tracking) is still added as before.

Test: `blanks_under_a_number_and_a_word_gap_next_to_big_digits` builds two big digit pairs and a smaller sentence drawn over them with blanks where the second pair sits. Before the fix the output keeps the blanks between `1` and `4` and joins `50` to `FR`. With the fix it is `50 FR 14 CD`.

Not in scope: the missing hyphen in `PLUG-INS` (a glyph with no Unicode, #3169) and the leader-dot word gaps in #3086.

title: Drop a glyph redrawn at the same place by a later pass, not only within 4 glyphs (#3173)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3173.

The page in the issue is drawn once per column, each pass inside its own clip. A glyph that crosses the clip edge is drawn by both passes at the same place: the R of WORLD and the s of illustrated. Text extraction kept both copies, so it gave `WOR RLD` and `illusstrated`.

**Cause**

The fake-bold filter in `arrange` (`crates/render/src/text.rs`) only compared a glyph with the 4 glyphs drawn just before it. Here the second copy comes thousands of glyphs later. The run-level redraw check does not help either, because it only looks at runs of 2 or more glyphs, and the second copy starts a different run (`RLD`, `strated`).

**Fix**

- The 4-glyph check stays as it is.
- In addition, each kept glyph is recorded in a map keyed by its text (an FNV-1a hash, new `text_hash`) and its grid cell (square cells, a fifth of the glyph height wide). A new glyph also looks up its own cell and the 8 neighbouring cells. If the latest kept glyph there has the same text and passes the same position test as before, the new glyph is dropped. This is the same grid-cell lookup that the run-level redraw check below already uses.
- The position test is the same as before, so the condensed-text rule from #1467 still applies. Only the drawing-order distance changes.

With the second R gone, `LD` starts right where the first `WOR` ends, so no word break is forced. The `RUN_OVERLAP_SPACE` code from the issue does not need a change.

**Tests**

`a_glyph_redrawn_by_the_other_column_pass_is_dropped` draws `WOR` and `illus`, then 100 other glyphs, then the second pass: `R` at the same place followed by `LD`, and `s` 0.01 pt to the left followed by `trated`. It checks that the lines read `WORLD` and `illustrated`. Without the fix both duplicates are more than 4 glyphs back, so they are kept. The existing fake-bold and condensed-text tests (`fake_bold_duplicates_are_removed`, `condensed_double_letters_are_kept`) still cover the near case.

title: Keep a subscript or superscript in its line when extracting text (#3174)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3174.

In `CO2-Emissionen` the `2` is a 4.698 pt glyph on a baseline 2.67 pt lower than the 8.1 pt `CO`. `arrange` in `crates/render/src/text.rs` starts a new segment unless the em-box centres of two neighbouring glyphs are less than half the *smaller* glyph's height apart. For `O` to `2` the centres are about 3.7 pt apart and the limit was 2.35 pt, so the `2` became its own segment. The same-baseline merge (`h * 0.3`) and the block step (size ratio) did not join it back, so the `2` came out on its own line and the sentence read `CO -Emissionen`.

**Fix**

When the next glyph starts right next to the previous one (horizontal gap smaller than the smaller glyph's height), the centre test uses half the *taller* glyph's height instead. A sub- or superscript is off the line by more than half its own height but by less than half the height of the full-size glyph beside it, so it now stays in the segment, and so does the `-` after it.

Nothing else changes: for two glyphs of the same size the limit is the same as before, and glyphs with a larger gap use the old limit. The merge, block and word-gap steps are untouched. The heuristic list in the `layout` doc comment now mentions sub- and superscripts.

**Test**

`subscript_stays_in_its_word` builds `CO2-E` with the sizes and offsets from the issue (8.1 pt `CO` and `-E`, a 4.7 pt `2` 2.7 pt lower) and checks that `plain_text()` is `CO2-E`. Without the fix the `2` is a separate segment and a separate block, so the text is not `CO2-E`.

title: Draw a note without an appearance as a fixed-size icon at the corner of its Rect (#3175)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3175.

A `/Text` or `/FileAttachment` annotation with no `/AP` gets a 20 × 20 icon appearance from PdfCraft (`NOTE_SIZE`). Both the renderer and `doc_flatten` (Algorithm 8.1, `placement`) map that box onto the whole `/Rect`. So the icon was stretched over a large `/Rect`, and in a `/Rect` with no width (LaTeX `pdfcomment`) it was scaled to nothing, while flatten still counted it as drawn and deleted the note.

**Fix:** when `apply_appearance` stores a built icon on a Text or FileAttachment note, it also sets the note's `/Rect` to a `NOTE_SIZE` box at the upper-left corner of the old `/Rect`. That is where MuPDF and Poppler draw the icon. PdfCraft's own notes already use this box (`rect_for`), so nothing changes for them.

`apply_appearance` is the one place where all these paths store the appearance, so one change covers both points of the issue:

- **Large `/Rect` (render):** the display copy from `with_missing_appearances` gets the 20 × 20 `/Rect`. The source document is not changed.
- **Large and zero-width `/Rect` (flatten):** `doc_flatten` builds the missing appearance through `set_appearance`, so the icon is baked in at its real size and position and is no longer lost.

The same applies when a foreign note is restyled or imported from XFDF and PdfCraft redraws it: the new appearance is always 20 × 20, so its `/Rect` now matches it. Notes can't be resized (`set_rect` refuses them), so no user-chosen size is lost. Notes that keep their own `/AP` are not touched.

**Tests**

- `annot`: `a_note_without_an_appearance_is_shown_at_icon_size`: the display copy gives the issue's large `/Rect`, a zero-width `/Rect` and a FileAttachment with a reversed `/Rect` a 20 × 20 box at the upper-left corner. The source document keeps its rectangles.
- `edit`: `flattening_a_note_with_a_zero_width_rect_draws_a_fixed_size_icon`: flattening a zero-width note and a large note bakes both icons in at scale 1, at the upper-left corner.

title: Shading patterns use the stroke or fill alpha current at paint time (#3176)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3176.

`Pattern::new` ran at `scn`/`SCN` and copied `graphics_state.non_stroke_alpha` into `ShadingPattern::opacity`. That caused two bugs:

- A `gs` after the pattern colour operator (`/Pat2 scn /GS2 gs ... f`) had no effect, so the fill came out opaque.
- A stroked pattern never used `/CA`, because `SCN` also read the fill alpha.

The fix:

- `Pattern::new` no longer captures alpha. `ShadingPattern::new` starts at opacity 1.0.
- `get_paint` already picks the stroke or fill paint data. It now sets the pattern's opacity from `data.alpha` at paint time, the same way solid colours use it. This covers paths, text and stencil masks, which all go through `get_paint`.
- Tiling patterns are not changed.

Test: `shading_pattern_uses_the_alpha_current_at_paint_time` in `crates/render/src/raster.rs` renders a page in the same layout as the issue's fixture: a pattern stroke with `/CA 0.25` set after `SCN`, and a pattern fill with `/ca 0.25` set after `scn`. It checks that both come out as red at 25% over white, about (255, 191, 191). Without the fix both are opaque (255, 0, 0). The test sits next to the existing render test for a soft mask on a shading pattern (#2128).

title: xtask models: PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE serves the OCR models to a build box without network
author: zberry
body:
## Why

When the Craft apps are built from source on a machine without network access, PdfCraft is the only app whose tar packaging reaches the network: `stage_models` (`packaging/env.sh`) runs `cargo xtask models DEST`, which `curl`s the two ocrs models and their licence text (#103). Pre-placing the files does not help, because `package.sh` wipes `$WORK` first and the xtask writes straight into the stage. Today we serve those downloads through a `curl` shim on `PATH`; this change makes that unnecessary without touching how releases are built.

## What

- `fetch_all` reads `PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE`. For each `[[fetched]]` file (and its `<file>.LICENCE.txt`), `fetch_verified` first looks for a file of that name in the cache directory and copies it into place; otherwise it downloads as before. Either way the bytes land in a `.part` file, are verified against the manifest's SHA-256, and are renamed only then. A cached file that fails its hash is an error, never a silent fallback to the network.
- `cargo xtask models "$PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE"` on a connected machine lays the cache out exactly as the xtask expects, so seeding it is one command. The failed-download message now says so.
- Comments in `packaging/env.sh` and the `Needs:` headers of the Linux, FreeBSD and Windows packaging scripts, plus `docs/releasing.md`, no longer say packaging needs the network unconditionally.
- Unset or empty `PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE` behaves exactly as before, so CI and releases are unaffected.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p xtask`: 52 passed (three new tests: cache hit copies without downloading, a corrupt cached file is refused, empty setting is ignored).
- `cargo fmt --check -p xtask`, `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask assets`: clean, with Rust 1.99.1.
- End to end: seeded a cache with `cargo xtask models DIR` online, then ran `xtask models` under `unshare -rn` (no network) with `PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE` set: both models, both licence texts and `ATTRIBUTION.txt` …

title: fix(content): accept inline image EI without preceding whitespace (#3108)
author: Ozt-y
body:
### Summary

Fixes #3108.

When parsing content streams in `crates/content`:
- In `unfiltered_image_end`: accept `EI` immediately at the computed sample length `end_data` (i.e. `separator == 0`), while maintaining the existing fallback heuristic when the preceding byte inside the computed span is whitespace (which signifies short/damaged payloads followed by `\s+EI`).
- In `end_of_image`: accept `>` as a valid preceding delimiter character before `EI` (`data[i - 1] == b'>'`), allowing ASCIIHex (`>EI`) and ASCII85 (`~>EI`) inline images to be delimited without intervening whitespace.

#### Diff Sketch & Call Tree
```text
Content::parse(stream)
  └── inline_image(data, pos)
        ├── unfiltered_image_end(data, begin, dict)
        │     - Computes exact end_data from W, H, CS, BPC
        │     + Accepts separator == 0 when preceding byte is non-whitespace
        └── end_of_image(data, begin)
              + Matches EI preceded by whitespace OR '>'
              + Preserves end_data = i (including '>') for ASCIIHex/ASCII85
```

Running `cargo test -p pdfcraft-content` with inline images ending directly with `EI` (`2060A0E0>EI`, `ab()EI`, `ab[]EI`):

title: fix(fonts): embedded CFF fonts declare their CMap and map glyphs through the charset
author: kouros7376
body:
## Summary

Editing text with an imported **CID-keyed OpenType (CFF) font** produced a page Acrobat refuses to parse
and, independently, the wrong glyphs for some characters. Both defects are in the CFF branch of
`crates/fonts/src/embedding.rs::embed_mapping`; the TrueType (`glyf`) branch is unaffected. One file
changed, one new test.

## Root cause

1. **Embedded CMap stream missing required entries.** For CFF fonts the Type0 `/Encoding` is an embedded
   CMap stream. It was written as a bare stream with no `/Type /CMap`, `/CMapName` or `/CIDSystemInfo`,
   all three of which ISO 32000-2 Table 118 ("Additional entries in a CMap stream dictionary") requires.
2. **CID-keyed CFF charset not applied.** A `CIDFontType0` selects glyphs by CID, and for a CID-keyed
   CFF the CID of each glyph is given by the CFF `charset` (GID → CID). The code wrote the GID as the CID
   in both the encoding CMap and `/W`. Whenever the font's charset is not the identity, the viewer drew
   a different glyph than the one measured and intended. Name-keyed CFF fonts (CID = GID,
   ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.2) were correct and stay unchanged.

## Symptoms

- Acrobat (Pro 2022) rejects the edited page: `getPageNumWords` on it fails with
  *"error parsing a form, Type 3 font or pattern"*, so its words cannot be extracted, and exporting the
  document as PNG images leaves that page out.
- Characters whose GID ≠ CID are drawn with other glyphs (in our case `(800` came out as `●00`, and `)`
  as a circled digit).

## Reproduction

1. Take any PDF with a paragraph of text.
2. `text_font_import` a CID-keyed OTF whose CFF charset is not the identity (for example Pretendard,
   OFL-1.1, `Pretendard-Regular.otf`).
3. `text_edit` the paragraph with that font, including digits and parentheses, and save.
4. Open in Acrobat: the page fails to parse (`getPageNumWords` error above) and the digits are wrong in
   other viewers. After this fix the page opens, its words are extracted, and the glyphs are right.

title: fix(edit): preserve annotation optional-content membership in marked content (#3213)
author: Ozt-y
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3213.

In `crates/edit/src/flatten.rs`, annotation flattening previously baked appearances into page streams without transferring optional-content (`/OC`) membership. This meant that annotations belonging to optional-content groups (OCGs) or membership dictionaries (OCMDs) lost their layer association once flattened, preventing viewers from toggling layer visibility dynamically.

This PR implements marked-content membership transfer and fail-closed structural validation:
- **Marked-Content Wrapping**: When an annotation has a transferable `/OC` entry, flattening registers `/PCFlOC{n}` in the page's `/Resources /Properties` dictionary (allocating collision-safe keys via `checked_add` and non-destructively cloning shared/inherited resources) and emits `/OC /PCFlOC{n} BDC ... Do ... EMC` around the appearance invocation.
- **Dynamic Layer Toggling**: Preserves layer membership (`100 / 0` and `0 / 100`) across all viewers (Acrobat, MuPDF, Poppler, PdfCraft).
- **Shared Appearance Isolation**: Annotations sharing a single Form XObject appearance stream keep separate per-call `/OC` marked-content blocks without mutating the shared appearance dictionary or stream bytes.
- **Fail-Closed Validation**: Bounded recursion (`depth <= 16`) validates ISO 32000-1 §8.11.2.2 `/VE` expressions (`/Not`, `/And`, `/Or`) and valid `/P` policies (`AllOn`, `AnyOn`, `AnyOff`, `AllOff`). Malformed expressions, cycle/depth overflows, and inline OCGs lacking catalog identity are retained intact in `/Annots`.
- **Transitive Retention Graph**: Retained annotations preserve their descendant reply chains (`/IRT`) and popups (`/Parent`) via cycle-safe graph traversal.
- **Code Quality & Upstream Cleanliness**: 100% docstring coverage across `flatten.rs` and the new regression suite; zero roadmap conflicts with `main`.

title: feat(view): invert page colours for night reading
author: pedrocaluiz
body:
## What this changes

Adds **View ▸ Invert colors** for night reading: the page is drawn in a palette of dark paper and light ink. Two modes:

- **Keep images** (the default). Text and line art take the palette through the existing reading-colours mapping; images, shadings and patterns pass through untouched.
- **Everything.** Every rendered pixel is inverted (premultiplied RGBA, alpha kept, double inversion is an exact identity), so photographs become negatives.

Palettes: soft dark gray, black and white, sepia, or a custom paper and ink pair (Preferences ▸ Reading colours).

Where it lives: `view.invert_colors` (Ctrl+I / ⌘I), a contrast button in the title bar (click toggles, right-click picks mode and palette), the View menu, `--invert-colors on|off`, Preferences, and the `view_invert_colors` tool. App-wide, saved with the preferences, display only; print previews ignore it.

## How it is built

- **Render layer** (`pdfcraft-render`): `RenderConfig` gains `invert_colors`, `invert_palette` and `invert_keep_images`. `request_reading` and `request_invert` apply the whole rule in one place, including that **the inverted view replaces the Reading colours setting and the two never stack**. The UI, the tools and `page_render` therefore agree.
- **Engine**: per-document setters and getters next to the reading-colours ones; the view is kept across `Session::reload` (a file change on disk).
- **UI**: the app holds the preference and copies it onto every document as it opens (all open paths) and whenever it changes. The reading-colours preference is never touched, so there is nothing to restore when the view is turned off.
- **Strings**: new UI strings are English in code; the translations are in craft-i18n (storytold/craft-i18n#141), so this PR no longer touches `i18n/*.tsv`.

title: Audit text drawn inside form XObjects for faux redactions
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3218

## Cause
`audit_redactions` got its text only from `pdfcraft_edit::text_lines`, which doesn't follow `Do` into form XObjects. So text drawn in a form was never checked against the covers or the `/Redact` marks, even though covers inside forms were found. Also, every rectangle inside a form was stamped with the position of the outer `Do`, so paint order inside a form couldn't be told apart.

## Fix
A new `pdfcraft_edit::form_text_lines` walks a page's form XObjects at any depth and returns their text lines in page space, each with a lexicographic paint path (page `[stream, op]` of the `Do`, then the operator index in each nested form). It fails instead of leaving text out when the depth or visit limits are reached. The audit now checks these lines next to the page's own lines, and the cover scan records the same kind of path for each rectangle, so 'painted after the text' works inside and across forms.

## Verified
- Regression tests `text_inside_form_xobjects_is_audited`, `box_before_form_text_is_not_a_cover`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-audit --lib form`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`text_lines` (Edit text) still leaves form text out (#2964), and the cover kinds the audit recognises are unchanged (#3117). Covers are now scanned before text, so the existing too-deep and cycle errors keep coming from the cover walk.

title: M10: Export ▸ Image shows the estimated size of the files (#2819, #3137)
author: SulejmaniRodrigo
body:
The Export to Image dialog now says what the files will take before exporting, in KB or MB, and the same estimate is reachable headlessly through the new read-only `doc_export_size` tool.

`Exporter::estimate` draws and encodes up to three pages — the first, the middle and the last — at the export's own resolution and format, and scales their bytes per pixel to each page's pixel count. A page whose render would exceed 16 megapixels is sampled smaller, which reads a little high because bytes per pixel fall with resolution, so the estimate errs on the large side rather than the small. On blank pages the estimate is the file's exact size; across differing pages it stays within a quarter.

The dialog measures on a worker thread with cancellation and no stale results, and only once the settings settle, so dragging the quality slider does not start a worker per frame. A cancelled estimate keeps its slot until its worker exits, so closing and reopening the dialog cannot stack renders. The new strings are English only; translations live in craft-i18n and fall back to English until they are added there.

title: Lay out vertical (Identity-V) text as columns in the edit layer
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3216

## Cause
The edit layer's `interpret` in `crates/edit/src/text.rs` never checked the font's writing mode. Every glyph moved the pen to the right, so a vertical column got a wide, short box starting at its first glyph. Neighbouring columns then overlapped and seemed to share a baseline, so `coincident_ops` took a nearby column as a copy of the edited line and deleted it.

## Fix
On each `Tf`, `interpret` now reads the writing mode through `vertical_encoding`. For `WMode 1` fonts it moves the pen down by `/DW2`'s vertical advance (default −1000), treats TJ offsets as vertical, gives each run a tall box centred on the pen, and never joins vertical runs into horizontal lines. If the writing mode can't be read (a broken, cyclic or invalid embedded CMap), the error is passed up and listing or editing that page's text is refused instead of guessing a direction.

## Verified
- Regression tests `vertical_text_lines_are_columns_and_editing_one_keeps_its_neighbour`, `text_whose_cmap_writing_mode_cannot_be_read_is_not_edited`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib -- vertical_text_lines_are_columns_and_editing_one_keeps_its_neighbour text_whose_cmap_writing_mode_cannot_be_read_is_not_edited`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Per-glyph `/W2` vertical metrics are not read: every glyph uses `/DW2`'s advance. Group moves still refuse vertical text, as before.

body:

Part of #2658 (the creation-date row). Every save goes through `pdfcraft_platform::staging::write_atomically_with`: a staging file beside the target, flushed, then renamed over it. So the file's creation date became the time of the save, on macOS (as reported) and on Windows (reproduced below).

Before the rename, the staging file now takes the replaced file's creation date. That uses `File::set_times` with `FileTimesExt::set_created` from std, on Windows and macOS, where a program can set it. title: Find and edit images whose Do or cm spans two content streams
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3113

## Cause
The image layer of Edit a PDF (`page_images`, `reading_images`, `change_image`, `translate_images`) parsed each `/Contents` piece separately. An operator whose operands end one piece and whose keyword starts the next lost its operands: a split `Do` drew an image that was never listed, and a split `cm` was dropped. The image was then reported in the wrong place, and moving it wrote a transform built from that wrong placement.

## Fix
Images are now read from the page's streams joined (`Pieces::join`), as text editing already does, and are addressed by the `Do`'s index among the joined operators. Delete, replace, transform, crop and group moves rewrite the content with `splice`/`rewritten_contents`, which rewrite every piece a split operator spans and copy every other byte unchanged.

## Verified
- Regression test `an_image_whose_operator_starts_the_next_stream_can_be_selected_moved_and_deleted`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib an_image_whose_operator_starts_the_next_stream_can_be_selected_moved_and_deleted`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Nothing outside the image layer: text editing already joins the pieces, and Form XObject contents are still parsed as their own single stream.

title: M7: work out each font's space width once per paragraph rewrite (#2616)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2616 ("every letter added or deleted freezes the program").

Each keystroke in Edit text rebuilds the paragraph's draft (`text_edit_layout` → `rewrite_styled_block`). Inside, the per-character `advance` measurement calls `source_space` for every character. When the source font can't show a space, `source_space` scans every font on the page and builds a `Metrics` for each, which includes decoding the font program. That is common: LaTeX- and Sphinx-made subsets space words with `TJ` kerning and have no space in their ToUnicode. So the draft did a page-wide font scan once per character.

The space width of each font is now worked out once per rewrite, before the per-character pass. The three call sites in `text_regions.rs` read it from that table. Results are identical; only the repeat work goes away.

## How you verified it

**Measured** with `text_edit_layout`, which is what each keystroke runs. Release CLI built with craft-fonts, 10 keystrokes appended one by one, on page 20 of NVIDIA's public *Virtual GPU Software User Guide* (Sphinx output; its body font maps no space):

| paragraph | `main` per keystroke | this PR per keystroke |
|---|---|---|
| 383 characters, with `▶` bullets | ~460 ms | ~71 ms |
| 199 characters, plain ASCII | ~255 ms | ~16 ms |
| 78 characters | ~125 ms | ~16 ms |

The JSON output of all 30 layouts is byte-identical between the two builds. Text left unchanged was already fast, ~11 ms, so the cost was in the rewrite.

**Regression test** `a_long_draft_in_a_font_without_a_space_works_out_the_space_width_once`. The page is a two-row paragraph in a Type0 subset whose ToUnicode has no space. The test lays out a 380-character draft and counts `source_space` calls through a test-only thread-local counter.
- With the fix: 1 call.
- With `text_regions.rs` put back to `main`: it fails with "worked out 1055 times for 380 characters", and takes 1.39 s instead of 0.02 s.

title: Read doubled-sign integers like --280 in the COS lexer
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3111

## Cause
`Lexer::number` tolerated a doubled sign (`--280.0`) only in its real-number branch. The integer branch passed `--280` straight to `parse::<i64>` and `parse::<f64>`, which both fail. That raised a syntax error, so a `TJ` array containing `--280` didn't parse and the whole operator was dropped by the edit layer, the export and redaction.

## Fix
The integer branch now collapses a leading doubled minus sign to a single one, as the real branch already does, before parsing. `--280` reads as `Int(-280)`, and `[(Hello) --280 (World)] TJ` parses.

## Verified
- Regression test `doubled_sign_integer_reads_like_the_real_form`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos --lib doubled_sign_integer_reads_like_the_real_form`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I didn't change the real-number branch or any other lexer behavior. I didn't change the content, edit or redaction crates, because they pick up the fix through the shared lexer. The regression test is at the lexer level and does not run the full repro PDF through Edit text, export or redaction.

title: Read /ActualText from named property lists in edit text and export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3110

## Cause
The edit layer's content interpreter (`interpret` in crates/edit/src/text.rs) read `/ActualText` only when the second `BDC` operand was an inline dictionary. When that operand was a name (`/Span /MC0 BDC`), it was never looked up in the resources' `/Properties`, because the interpreter received only the `/Font` dictionary. So Edit text and the Office export showed the glyph text instead.

## Fix
The interpreter's `logical_text: bool` flag is now `Option<&Dict>` and carries the current resources' `/Properties`: the page's in `text_lines`, and the page's or form's in `reading_lines`. A name operand is resolved there before `/ActualText` is read, with the same 4 MB size limit as before. Named lists that have no `/ActualText`, and names that are missing, still keep the glyph text.

## Verified
- Regression test `actual_text_from_named_property_list`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib actual_text_from_named_property_list`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`clear_block` and `translate_blocks` still pass `None`, so they do not read `/ActualText`, as before. The reading path (`pdfcraft-cli text`, Find) and the renderers already handle named lists and are unchanged.

title: fix(engine): undo past a security change saves in full (#3276)
author: skylartaylor
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3276. Undo past a save that changed security now appends the restored state to the newest earlier save with its security, instead of to the last saved file.

**Bug.** After undo restores a snapshot from before the last save, `Session::save_bytes` reopens the saved file and appends the snapshot as an incremental update. When the two use different encryption — undoing a saved protect, remove-protection, password change or rekey, or a compaction that renumbered `/Encrypt` — the update is read with the wrong key. Every round trip reopened with blank pages, and remove → save → undo → save left the plaintext revision inside a file that reports itself encrypted.

**Fix.**
- `Document::output_security_identity` is what a save encrypts with: the security dictionary and, below revision 5, the first `/ID`, which together determine the key. Passwords, authentication level and where `/Encrypt` lives (object number or inline) are not part of it.
- `Session::save_bytes` compares the snapshot's identity with the saved file's, recorded at `mark_saved`. When they differ, the snapshot goes onto the newest file of this session that has its security and continues its source (at worst that source), opened with the snapshot's key. Earlier saves in the same security stay in the chain; revisions in the other security, all undone, are dropped, as saving any security change already does. An unedited snapshot that is its target is saved as those bytes unchanged, so a restored signature stays valid.
- `overlay_changes_from` returns `Ok(false)`, changing nothing, when security differs or the target has a pending security change. Otherwise it takes the snapshot's `/Encrypt` place for writing only, so undo past an optimized save still appends to it, and it writes again any unchanged object packed in an object stream whose number the snapshot reuses or lacks; those read back as `null` before.

- [x] clippy with `-D warni…

title: Keep text rows in other layers, gs states or Tz out of a paragraph
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3115

## Cause
Edit text joined rows into one paragraph by position and font alone. A rewrite then wrote every row in a single row's place and state, so a row inside an `/OC` marked-content sequence, after a `gs`, or at another `Tz` lost that state, or passed it on to the edited row (for example, a visible row moved into a hidden layer).

## Fix
The text interpreter now records, for each run, the `/OC` optional content groups around it and the `gs` resources applied before it (a new `Paint` key). Runs and rows whose key differs are no longer joined into one line or paragraph, and rows with a different horizontal scale no longer join. Editing one row now leaves the others' operators and state as they were.

## Verified
- Regression test `editing_a_row_keeps_the_layer_opacity_and_scale_of_the_rows_around_it`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib editing_a_row_keeps_the_layer_opacity_and_scale_of_the_rows_around_it`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Text hidden by an OFF layer still appears in Edit text as its own paragraph. This change does not evaluate optional content visibility. A row inside a form XObject drawn within an `/OC` sequence does not inherit that layer. Two rows with different horizontal scales on the same baseline can still join.

title: fix(organize): prune named destinations without recursive calls
author: PerchAnton
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3309. Deleting a page from a deeply nested `/Names /Dests` tree could overflow the call stack. Pruning now uses an explicit stack and a seen set, visiting shared and cyclic indirect nodes once while retaining destinations for surviving pages.

Undo restores the deleted page and its names; redo removes them again and preserves surviving targets. Tests assert the actual full/incremental save modes, the incremental prefix, unsaved metadata, unchanged source bytes and rendered pixels. Shared/cyclic-node and inline-root coverage remains; the organize regressions are grouped with page-deletion tests. Roadmap/parity records describe the final behavior with unchanged estimates.

title: M2: a fax image with fewer /Rows than its /Height is decoded to its height (#3308)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #3308.

## Cause

The steel schedule table in the reporter's drawing (`pdfplot16.hdi`, AutoCAD's plotter driver) is a 2418 × 2920 Group 4 fax image in an `/Indexed` space. Its `/DecodeParms` say `/Rows 2418`, which equals `/Columns` and not the image's `/Height` of 2920. The CCITT filter decoded only `/Rows` rows, so the bottom 502 rows stayed zero, which is index 0 (black). That's the black block under the table in the screenshot. MuPDF and the reporter's other viewer draw all 2920 rows. Patching a copy of the file to `/Rows 2920` makes PdfCraft draw the whole table as well.

## Fix

Vendored hayro-syntax patch (18) in `filter/ccitt.rs`: a non-zero `/Rows` below the image's `/Height` no longer cuts the image short, and the decoder decodes to the height. When the data really ends sooner, the existing lenient path still returns the rows it decoded. `/Rows 0` keeps patch (17)'s meaning.

- `raster::tests::group4_fax_with_rows_below_its_height_decodes_to_the_image_height`: an 8 × 4 Group 4 image with `/Rows 2` and `/BlackIs1 true` (so the decoded rows are white and undecoded rows show black), through `/DeviceGray` and `/Indexed`, plus a `/Rows 4` control.
