title: The recovery folder is owner-only on Unix
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Recovery snapshots are unsaved copies of open documents. `RecoveryStore` made its folder with `create_dir_all`, so the folder got the default mode (usually `0755` with a `022` umask), and the first snapshot file got the default mode for a new file (#2544 keeps the mode only of a file that is replaced). On a shared Linux or macOS machine, other accounts could list the folder and read the snapshots of documents that are not encrypted. Encrypted documents were already safe, since they are stored encrypted.

Now `RecoveryStore::create_dir` makes the folder and, on Unix, sets it to `0700` when it is open to group or others. `claim` (when an instance starts) and `write` (each autosave) both go through it, so a folder an earlier version made is tightened at the next start. This follows `image_pick::write_clipboard_file`, which keeps its folder `0700` the same way. With the folder owner-only, the files inside are out of reach whatever their own mode, so `write_atomically` is unchanged.

Windows is unchanged: `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is already per-user.

title: Render weekday letters in FormCalc date pictures
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:1929-1957 (format_date), with DateFmt returning "EEEE, MMMM D, YYYY" at :2333` (no existing issue): FormCalc Num2Date/Format ignore the weekday letters in a date picture: DateFmt(4) gives a literal "EEEE".

## Cause
`format_date` only handled the Y, M and D letters and copied every other character into the output. `DateFmt(4)` returns "EEEE, MMMM D, YYYY", so `Num2Date` and `Format` printed the literal text "EEEE" instead of the weekday.

## Fix
`format_date` now handles runs of `E`. `EEEE` gives the full weekday name, `EEE` the three-letter name, and `E` or `EE` the weekday number (1 = Sunday). The weekday is worked out from the day serial, where 1900-01-01 was a Monday.

## Verified
- Regression test `date_pictures_render_the_weekday_letters`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js date_pictures_render_the_weekday_letters`).

title: M6: Treat AcroForm /MaxLen 0 as unlimited
author: djmushin
body:
## Summary

Fixes an AcroForm text-field compatibility issue where a field
specifying `/MaxLen 0` could incorrectly reject text input.

The fix treats an explicit `/MaxLen 0` as an unlimited character
length, including when the field inherits a positive maximum
length from a parent field.

This improves compatibility with existing PDF forms without
changing the behavior of fields that specify positive limits.

## Background — Follow-up to PR #3168

This change was originally submitted as part of #3168, which
combined AcroForm performance optimizations, text-field
compatibility improvements, and optional profiling instrumentation.

Following maintainer review, the contribution was separated into
independent pull requests to simplify review, testing, and merging.

The performance optimizations have already been submitted
separately as #3318.

This PR contains only the `/MaxLen 0` compatibility fix,
its regression tests, and supporting documentation.

Optional profiling instrumentation has been excluded.

The compatibility branch was independently rebased onto
upstream `main` at commit `932bf9c6` and validated.

This restructuring directly addresses the scope concerns
raised during the review of #3168.

## Problem

Some existing PDF forms explicitly define `/MaxLen 0` on
text fields.

Previously, PDFcraft could interpret this value as a maximum
length of zero characters, preventing users from entering text.

This could also occur when a field explicitly specified
`/MaxLen 0` while inheriting a positive limit from a parent.

In these cases, the explicit zero value should represent
an unlimited field rather than preventing input.

## Changes

- Treats explicit `/MaxLen 0` as unlimited.
- Preserves positive maximum-length restrictions.
- Ensures an explicit zero overrides an inherited positive limit.
- Adds regression coverage for the affected behavior.
- Updates the forms documentation and Acrobat feature-parity records.

author: majidninja
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3282.

The right rail puts its panel buttons (Comments, Bookmarks, … Tags) top-down and the page navigation cluster (page field, view history, prev/next, zoom, fit, rotate, page display, zoom in/out) bottom-up in the same space. Nothing stops the two from meeting, so in a window that isn't tall enough for both they get drawn on top of each other. title: Render: a five-point polyline is no longer painted as its bounding box
author: Hamza0101
body:
A PDF holding a five-point open polyline whose ends reach the corners of its own bounding box renders as a rectangle: the middle disappears and the open side comes out closed.

## Measured with `pdfcraft-cli`

Content stream, nothing else on the page:

```
0 0 0 K  2 w
80 38 m  80 21.75 l  60.571 29.875 l  40 21.75 l  40 38 l  S
```

`pdfcraft-cli render … --dpi 72`, reading the pixels back:

| | peak drawn near (60, 30) | dark pixels along the bounding box's top edge |
|---|---|---|
| **before** | **no** | **36** — a straight edge the file does not contain |
| after | yes | 0 |
| six-point zigzag (control) | yes | 0 |
| real rectangle (control) | no | 36 |

## Cause

`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/context.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) fn path_as_rect(path: &BezPath) -> Option<Rect> {
    // One MoveTo, three LineTo, one ClosePath
    if path.elements().len() != 5 {
        return None;
    }
    …
    if corners[0] && corners[1] && corners[2] && corners[3] { Some(bbox) } else { None }
}
```

The comment names the shape it means to match. `len() != 5` also admits **one `MoveTo` and four `LineTo`** — a five-point open polyline — and the corner test only asks whether all four bounding-box corners were *visited by some point*, never whether *every* point is a corner. Both call sites in `interpret/path.rs` then call `device.draw_rect(&rect, …)`.

The zigzag slips through because its ends and the points beside them land on all four corners, and (60.571, 29.875) — the peak — is simply ignored:

| point | corner |
|---|---|
| (80, 38) | max x, max y |
| (80, 21.75) | max x, min y |
| **(60.571, 29.875)** | **none — the peak** |
| (40, 21.75) | min x, min y |
| (40, 38) | min x, max y |

The condition is narrow, which is why only some art is affected: 3, 4 or 6 points are fine, and `s` (closepath + stroke) escapes it because the `ClosePath` makes six elements. So the same drawing survives if its author happened to close the path.

title: cli: info names the standard a document declares
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes the verifiable half of #3319, "PDFcraft does not recognize a PDF/A file".

## What I could check

The report has no sample file, and the bot has asked for one. But one part of it is objective, so I built a file that declares PDF/A — `pdfaid:part` 2 and `pdfaid:conformance` B in the catalog's XMP metadata stream — and inspected it:

```
$ pdfcraft-cli info declares-pdfa.pdf
{ … "encrypted": false, "tagged": false, "javascript": false, "layers": 0,
      "xfa": null, "pdf_version": "1.7", … }      # 24 fields, no mention of PDF/A
```

Detection is not the problem: `pdfcraft_preflight::declared` reads that declaration, and the app's Standards panel renders it as "PDF/A-2b". It is `info` — the documented "document summary" — that left it out, so anything driving the CLI, and anyone checking a file without opening the app, is told nothing about the standard.

## Change

`info` gains three fields, from the same `declared()` call the Standards panel makes, so the CLI and the panel agree by construction instead of parsing the metadata twice:

```
declares-pdfa.pdf    "pdfa": "2B",  "pdfua": null,  "output_intents": []
a plain PDF          "pdfa": null,  "pdfua": null,  "output_intents": []
```

`pdfa` is the part and conformance together (`"2B"`, `"3A"`), which is how the level is written and spoken; `pdfua` is the part; `output_intents` lists the condition identifiers the panel already shows. Nothing else in the summary changes.

**Where it is read.** In the CLI, not in `pdfcraft_render::Inspect`. `xtask layers` puts `render` at 3 and `preflight` at 4, so the summary struct cannot reach the declaration, while an app may depend on any layer. The document is opened once more through `pdfcraft_cos::Document::open_with_password`, with the password `info` was given, and a file that fails to parse there simply declares nothing rather than failing the command.

title: Drop U+FFFE and U+FFFF from XFDF/XML form-data export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs:192-209 (esc), used by export_xfdf (:445) and export_data XML (:594-612)` (no existing issue): XFDF/XML form-data export writes U+FFFE/U+FFFF, so the exported file is not well-formed XML.

## Cause
`esc()` in the xfdf crate escaped `& < > "` and dropped C0 control characters, but it passed the XML 1.0 noncharacters U+FFFE and U+FFFF through as raw text. A field value, comment or attribute containing one produced an export that is not well-formed XML, and roxmltree rejects it on import.

## Fix
`esc()` now leaves out U+FFFE and U+FFFF, as it does for C0 controls. This matches the XFA data writer and the Office exporter, and covers both `export_xfdf` and the XML `export_data`. The regression test exports a value with both characters, checks the XFDF and XML parse, and checks the value comes out as `abc`.

## Verified
- Regression test `xml_exports_drop_xml_noncharacters`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf --lib xml_exports_drop_xml_noncharacters`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The other `export_data` formats (FDF, CSV) and the XFA and Office writers are unchanged.

title: M10: put image pages on a chosen paper size (#3273)
author: saad-mughal435
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3273.

A photo becomes a page as large as its pixels, so a 4000 × 3000 phone picture with no stored resolution gives a 4000 × 3000 pt page (about 1.41 × 1.06 m), and a set of photos of different pixel sizes gives pages of several different sizes, none of them a paper size. The `dpi` option added for #190 changes the scale but not that.

`doc_create` (`from: "images"`) and `doc_create_multiple` (both `combine` and `separate` modes) now take:

- **`page_size`** — a paper name (`A4`, `Letter`, `Legal`, `Tabloid`, `A0`–`A6`, `ARCH A`–`E`, `ANSI C`–`E`) or `[width, height]` in points. The image is scaled to fit and centred.
- **`page_turn`** — turn the sheet to match each image's orientation, so a landscape photo gets a landscape page. Default `true`; a square image never turns the sheet.

The shape the issue asked for, as `pdfcraft-create::ImagePage`:

```rust
pub enum ImagePage {
    #[default]
    Image,                                        // today's behaviour
    Fixed { width: f64, height: f64, turn: bool },
}
```

Nothing is cropped or stretched: the scale is `min(pw/w, ph/h)`, so the aspect ratio is kept and an image smaller than the sheet is enlarged to fill it rather than left in a corner. Pixels are still never resampled.

**Two things worth noting about where the code went:**

- The paper-name match moved out of `doc_print` into `printing::paper_named`, so Create and Print answer exactly the same names instead of growing a second list. `pdfcraft-print` owns the table and is `create`'s own layer, so the name is resolved at L7 and `create` takes plain points — no new same-layer dependency.
- `ImagePage::Image` is the default and every existing entry point delegates to it, so `from_images`, `from_images_with_resolution` and `convert_to_pdf` are unchanged for their callers. A test asserts the default path writes a byte-identical file.

title: M10: exported TIFF and JPEG pages record the resolution they were drawn at
author: MortenHusted
body:
## What this changes

Pages exported as TIFF or JPEG now say the resolution they were drawn at. TIFF exports are LZW-compressed, as `encode_tiff`'s comment already said they were.

The bugs, both on `main`:
- **No resolution.** A page exported as TIFF said `1 × 1` with no unit, whatever the dpi, and a JPEG said nothing (JFIF aspect ratio 1:1). Other programs fall back to a default, usually 72 dpi, so a 300-dpi Letter page opens and prints as a 35 × 46 in poster.
- **No compression.** The TIFF was written uncompressed, although the comment says "LZW-compressed by the encoder's default". `image`'s `TiffEncoder` doesn't compress. A Letter page at 300 dpi came to 25 MB.

`pdfcraft-cli render --dpi 300` on page 1 of a 426 × 485 pt PDF, read with `tiffinfo`:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Resolution | `1, 1 (unitless)` | `300, 300 pixels/inch` |
| Compression | None | LZW |
| Size | 10.8 MB | 65 KB |

What changed:
- **Resolution.** `encode_image`, `encode_jpeg` and `encode_tiff` take the dpi to record: TIFF `XResolution`/`YResolution` in inches, the JFIF density in dots per inch.
  - `Exporter::image` records the resolution the page was actually drawn at (`dpi_used`). A page too large for the renderer at the asked resolution says the lower one, which is the one `doc_export_images` reports in `lower_dpi`.
  - `pdfcraft-cli render` records `--dpi`. It refuses oversized pages, so that is the resolution drawn.
  - This reaches File ▸ Export ▸ Image, the `doc_export_images` tool and `pdfcraft-cli render`.
- **TIFF writing.** `encode_tiff` uses the `tiff` crate directly, because `image`'s `TiffEncoder` can set neither the resolution nor the compression. `tiff` 0.11 is already in the graph through `image`, and `pdfcraft-create` depends on it the same way.
- **LZW** is a commit of its own, so it can be dropped on its own (see the last section).

title: #2922: on Windows, draw with Direct3D 12 only, not wgpu's OpenGL backend
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #2922.

## Cause
@KNUFFIXX's stacks in #2922 show the print thread hanging in `StartPage`, inside the Kyocera KX v3 driver. The driver calls `EnumWindows` and then `GetWindowTextA` on every top-level window. One of PdfCraft's windows is wgpu-hal's hidden `wgpu Device Class` window (GL backend, `gles/wgl.rs`). Its thread blocks in `drop_rx.recv()` and never pumps messages, so `WM_GETTEXT` never returns, and the job stays at Spooling with 0 bytes. With `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` that window is gone and the job prints. Upstream: gfx-rs/wgpu#10504 and #10505.

## Change
- `configure_gpu`: on Windows the instance backends go from `DX12 | GL` to `DX12`.
  - A machine where wgpu can't start still gets OpenGL through the existing glow retry in `main`. glow creates no hidden wgpu window.
  - A GPU with no D3D12 driver now draws through WARP instead of wgpu's GL backend. `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl` gives it hardware OpenGL.
- The test now asserts that GL is not among the Windows backends, and `docs/development.md` is updated.

## Testing
- On Linux: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pdfcraft gpu_backends`.
- The new assertion only runs on Windows, so CI's Windows job covers it.
- Not yet tried with a Kyocera printer. @KNUFFIXX, could you try a build of this branch?

title: Create from images: put each image on a paper size
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3273.

## The problem

A phone or camera JPEG carries 72 dpi, or no resolution at all, so a 4000 × 3000 photo becomes a 4000 × 3000 pt page — about 1.41 × 1.06 m. The `dpi` choice from #190 changes that size, but a set of photos with different pixel sizes still gives pages of different sizes, and none of them is a paper size.

## Change

`pageSize` — a paper name — or `pageWidth` and `pageHeight` in points put every image on a page of one size, scaled to fit and centred:

```
default                400×300 pt       (a page per image, unchanged)
pageSize=a4            595.28×841.89
pageSize=letter        612×792
pageWidth/pageHeight   300×300
```

Taken by `doc_create from:"images"`, `doc_create_multiple` and `doc_combine` — the three the ticket names. Omitting them leaves today's behaviour exactly as it is.

Placement is a fit, not a stretch or a crop. A 400 × 300 pt image on a 300 × 300 pt page draws as:

```
q 300.000 0 0 225.000 0.000 37.500 cm /Im0 Do Q
```

— 300 × 225, proportions kept, centred 37.5 pt up.

## Four decisions worth your eye

- **One list of paper sizes.** Names resolve through `pdfcraft_print::PAPERS`, the 20-size table Print already uses, so "a4" cannot drift from Print's A4. `create` and `print` are both layer 4 and cannot see each other, so the lookup lives in `engine` (layer 6), which already depends on both. `"letter"` and the table's own `"US Letter"` both work, case-insensitively.
- **No signature churn.** `convert_to_pdf` and `as_pdf` have twenty-one callers between them, so `convert_to_pdf_on_pages` and `as_pdf_on_pages` sit beside them and the existing calls are untouched.
- **"Scaled to fit" scales both ways.** A small image fills the page rather than sitting small in the middle of it. title: fix(windows): name the single-instance socket by the session id, so a launch without SESSIONNAME finds its session's window (#3338)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #3338.

## Cause

As @halr9000 traced it: on Windows, the single-instance socket was named after `%SESSIONNAME%` (`instance-Console.sock`, `instance-RDP-Tcp3.sock`). Task Scheduler, services and some remote shells start a process without `SESSIONNAME`. Such a launch looked for `instance.sock`, never found the window opened from Explorer, and opened a second one.

## Fix

The socket is now named by the **session id** in the process token: `instance-s<id>.sock`.
- The id is read through `winsafe`'s `HACCESSTOKEN::GetCurrentProcessToken().GetTokenInformation(SessionId)`, with the `advapi` feature added. No `unsafe` is needed.
- A scheduled launch runs in the user's session, so it gets the same id as the window opened from Explorer, and hands its files to it.
- Each session has its own id, so a launch in one session never hands files to a window in another. This answers @earlvanze's review: the first version of this PR fell back to the console's name, which could have sent a file from a Remote Desktop session to a console window.
- `SESSIONNAME` names the socket only if the id can't be read.

## Tests

title: Clamp the zoom-anchor scroll to the content so zooming out no longer jolts the page (#3266)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3266.

**Cause.** While zooming, `document_area` keeps the point under the pointer still by setting the scroll offset to `point - rel` from `view.zoom_anchor`. That offset was only kept above zero, never below the maximum scroll. Zooming out beside a page that becomes narrower (or shorter) than the window asks for an offset past the end of the content. egui clamps the offset only after the frame is drawn, so every zoom frame showed the page shifted to one side, and when the zoom stopped it snapped to where it belongs. The further the pointer is from the centre, the larger the requested offset and the bigger the jump, as the issue says.

**Fix.** A small `anchored_scroll` helper clamps the anchored offset to `0..=content - viewport` on both axes, the same bound the `goto` branch right below already applies ("egui clamps only after drawing ...") and the Hand-tool pan uses. The pointer zoom and the generic "zoom changed" fallback both set `zoom_anchor`, so this one place covers them. Inside the scrollable range the offset is unchanged, so zooming in still keeps the point under the pointer.

**Test.** `zoom_anchor_scroll_stays_within_the_content` checks an offset past the end, before the start, inside the range, and content smaller than the viewport.

title: M2: a tiling pattern drawn once shows its cell at full scale (#3349)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #3349.

## Cause

The network-switch pictures in the reporter's slides (Acrobat PDFMaker 11 for PowerPoint) are picture fills. PDFMaker writes each one as a tiling pattern meant to be drawn once: `/PaintType 1 /TilingType 3 /XStep 2147480100 /YStep 2147480100`, with a matrix that flips y, and a single image in the cell. The fill is a rectangle the size of the cell.

Vendored hayro patch (3), `tiling_cell_scale`, keeps a cell pixmap within 3000 px a side by lowering the cell's scale to `3000 / step`. With a step of about 2.1 × 10⁹, that is a scale of about 1.4 × 10⁻⁶, so the 183 × 17 picture was drawn far smaller than a pixel and disappeared. MuPDF and Acrobat draw it. Across the 19 pages, the pages with such fills (1–4, 8, 10, 17) differed from MuPDF in 10k–22k pixels at 72 dpi; with this fix they differ in about 6k–8k, which is antialiasing noise, about the same as on the untouched pages.

## Fix

Vendored hayro patch (20), in `renderer.rs` (`set_paint`, tiling branch). When the step is too large for a cell pixmap and the painted area can only meet the first cell, the cell's `/BBox` is drawn at full scale into a pixmap with a 1-pixel transparent border, and sampled with `Extend::Pad` instead of `Repeat`. So the cell shows once and nothing repeats or smears.

`shows_one_cell` decides "only the first cell". It maps the path's device bounds (grown by the stroke's width for a stroke) into pattern space, and checks that the cells one step away (k = ±1, in x and y) can't be reached. Every other path keeps today's behaviour, including the 3000 px cap.

## Tests

- `a_tiling_pattern_drawn_once_shows_its_cell`: PowerPoint's step and a flipped matrix, with the cell in the middle of the page. Filled and stroked, the cell shows, and nothing appears left, right, above or below it. An ordinary step of 20 still tiles.
- `a_large_step_still_tiles_where_the_next_cell_shows`: steps of 3100 at scale 1, just over the cap. The cell to the right, left, above and below still shows …

title: fix(a11y): join and splice page content streams with cross-stream rules (#3217)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #3217

### Problem
When a page's `/Contents` is an array of streams, ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2 specifies that they represent a single concatenated stream where tokens can be split across stream boundaries and a `%` comment at the end of one stream without a newline continues into the next stream up to its first end-of-line.

In `pdfcraft-a11y`:
1. `autotag::content_bytes`, `alt::page_content`, and `content::page_content` joined `/Contents` streams with `b'\n'` instead of `b' '`, prematurely ending any trailing `%` comment at a stream boundary so commented-out operators at the start of the next stream were parsed and emitted as live content.
2. `alt::artifact_marked_content` (`mark_decorative`) parsed and re-serialized each stream in isolation with `pdfcraft_content::parse` + `serialize_ops`, dropping operands of operators split across two content streams and stripping trailing cross-stream comments.

### Solution
- Join `/Contents` streams with `b' '` in `autotag::content_bytes`, `alt::page_content`, and `content::page_content` (matching `pdfcraft_content::Pieces::join`).
- Rewrite `alt::artifact_marked_content` to join the page's content streams with `pdfcraft_content::Pieces::join`, parse operators across the joined stream via `Pieces::parse`, and splice only matching `BDC` operator spans to `/Artifact BMC` via `Pieces::splice` so split operators and cross-stream comments stay intact.

### Testing
- Added `crates/a11y/tests/cross_stream.rs` covering:
  - `autotag_keeps_text_commented_out_across_stream_boundary_hidden`
  - `mark_decorative_preserves_shape_split_across_content_streams`
  - `mark_decorative_and_mark_artifact_keep_cross_stream_comment_hidden`

title: M2: a JP2 image in a colour space the decoder refuses is drawn by its component count (#3306)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #3306.

## Cause

As @jpeskov traced it: the veraPDF fixture's JPX image has no `/ColorSpace`, and its JP2 header's colour specification (`colr`, METH 1) names enumerated colour space 19, CIEJab. `hayro-jpeg2000` 0.3.5's `get_color_space` handles only CMYK, CIELab, sRGB, greyscale, sYCC, e-sRGB and ROMM-RGB, and returns `Unsupported` for every other enum. So `Image::new` failed, the filter returned `None`, and the image was skipped: a blank page. `hayro-jpeg2000` isn't vendored, so the fix sits in the vendored `hayro-syntax` JPX filter.

## Fix

Vendored hayro-syntax patch (20), in `filter/jpx.rs`. The normal path is unchanged. Only when `Image::new` fails, and the JP2 header has a `colr` box naming an enumerated space outside the decoded set, is the image decoded again from a copy. In that copy those `colr` enums name the space the decoder assumes when there is no `colr` box: greyscale, sRGB or CMYK for 1, 3 or 4 components (`ihdr`). Other component counts, ICC `colr` boxes and anything unreadable are left alone. The box walk is bounded and uses checked arithmetic, and handles 8-byte (`LBox` 1) and to-the-end (`LBox` 0) lengths.

Why sRGB for this file: I rendered the fixture with the enum rewritten to sRGB (16) and to sYCC (18), and compared each with MuPDF at 72 dpi.

| | mean abs diff vs MuPDF | pixels > 40 |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (blank) | 25.39 | 56,721 |
| as sYCC | 11.46 | 71,135 |
| **as sRGB (this PR)** | **0.61** | **349** |

## Tests

- `raster::tests::a_jp2_image_in_a_refused_enumerated_colour_space_is_drawn`: a 1×1 JP2 with every sample 128. It draws mid-grey with CIEJab (19) and YPbPr (22) for 3 components and bilevel (15) for 1, and with sRGB (16) as a control. On `main` the first three draw nothing.
- `filter::jpx::tests` in `hayro-syntax` (run with `--manifest-path vendor/hayro-syntax/Cargo.toml`):

title: fix(preflight): identify PDF standards by XML namespace
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

PDF/A identification currently depends on the literal `pdfaid` prefix. A valid XMP packet using another prefix, or a default namespace on its elements, is therefore not recognized in Standards and is reported as lacking identification by PDF/A verification. Resolve PDF/A and PDF/UA identification by namespace URI and local name, for attributes and elements, and reject misleading prefixes bound to another namespace. Metadata decoding is bounded to 8 MiB before allocation; the XML parser disallows DTDs and bounds metadata size (8 MiB), nesting (1,024), nodes (100,000), attributes per element (128), and total attributes (4,096). Namespace declarations count as attributes; over-limit packets are not identified.

This addresses one possible cause related to #3319; the reporter's file has not been supplied, so it does not claim to resolve that report.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-preflight --profile low-disk --locked -j 2` (16 passed); the namespace regression fails on the original implementation, and the attribute-limit and metadata-decode regressions fail when their guards are removed, and a compressed oversized fixture is rejected during decoding.

title: fix(sign): offer only certificates that may sign documents from the Windows store
author: Tomcatt
body:
## What this changes

A DoD Common Access Card (and other PIV smart cards) puts several certificates into the Windows Current User store under the same name: one for signing, one for encryption, one or more for Windows logon / card authentication. All of them have a private key, so the digital ID picker listed them as identical, selectable entries. Only the signing one produces a signature that validates. With the others, validation says "unknown" because the key usage or EKU doesn't allow document signing. In practice this means picking the right entry by trial and error.

`pdfcraft-sign` already knows whether a certificate may sign (`Certificate::signing_problem`). This PR runs that check during Windows store enumeration, *after* the private-key check. A certificate that can't sign is now greyed out in the picker and marked `unusable` in `sign_windows_ids`, with its reason (for example "it is not issued for signing documents (…)"), the same way the store already handles a key CNG can't open. Certificates without a private key are still left out entirely, as before.

`Certificate::signing_problem_clause` rewords the existing diagnostic so it follows the certificate's name in a list.

title: Clear image pixels intersected by redaction marks
author: earlvanze
body:
A redaction mark can intersect part of an image pixel without containing its center. Previously that pixel was left unchanged, and if no centers were covered the original image remained in the saved PDF. For example, a narrow mark over one edge of a 2-pixel image left both original samples recoverable after apply and save.

Clear every pixel whose transformed footprint's bounding box overlaps a redaction region. The bounding box is conservative for rotation and shear, so it can clear neighboring pixels as well. Unsupported image codecs and masks still follow the existing fail-closed removal path; this does not solve the whole-page JPEG removal tracked in #283.

Validation:
- The synthetic full-save/reopen regression failed on main (`images_cleared == 0`) and passes after the fix for unrotated and rotated images, checking that the original image resource is removed and only the intersected sample is cleared.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact --profile low-disk --locked -j 2`: 73 passed, one ignored timing probe.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets --profile low-disk --locked -j 2 -- -D warnings`; wasm32 check for pdfcraft-redact; fmt, layers, assets and parity checks passed.

title: fix(render): text extraction keeps the word gaps between Hangul words
author: kouros7376
body:
## Summary

Extracted text (`text`, `text_extract`, search, copy) ran Korean words together whenever the producer
drew the word gap by position alone, with no space glyph. Hangul was counted among the scripts written
without word spaces (Han, kana), so a gap narrower than half the line height between two Hangul words
was never a space. One function changed in `crates/render/src/text.rs`, one new test.

## Root cause

`is_cjk` (used only by the word-gap rule in `arrange`) covered the Hangul syllables (U+AC00–D7AF),
Hangul Jamo (U+1100–11FF) and compatibility Jamo (U+3130–318F) along with Han and kana. The rule
"two CJK glyphs with a gap under `0.5 × h` are one word" is right for Chinese and Japanese, which are
written without word spaces, but Korean is written with them, and a Korean word gap (about a quarter em)
is well under that limit. Producers that draw each word with its own `Td`/`Tj` (HWP exports and
scanned-and-OCR'd documents among them) therefore lost every word boundary.

## Fix

`is_cjk` now covers Han, kana, bopomofo and their compatibility and fullwidth forms, and not Hangul, so
Hangul word gaps are judged by the same position-relative threshold as Latin ones (`typical letter gap +
0.15 × h`). Han and kana keep the no-space rule.

## Before / after

A page drawn with `drawString` per word (a space-width gap, no space glyph), `pdfcraft-cli text`:

```
before: 복합문화센터건립공사설계설명서제3장
        도면번호 A-101 축척 1/200 검토자박검토
after:  복합문화센터 건립공사 설계설명서 제3장
        도면번호 A-101 축척 1/200 검토자 박검토
```

Lines drawn without a gap (`복합` `문화` `센터` butted together) still read as one word, and `建築` `設計`
with the same gap still read as `建築設計`.

## Test

`text::tests::hangul_word_gaps_are_spaces_and_han_gaps_are_not`: a quarter-em gap between two Hangul
words is a space, the same gap between two Han words is not. Fails on `main` with
`left: "복합문화센터", right: "복합문화 센터"`.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p …

title: fix(windows): present Direct3D 12 through a composition visual, so resizing doesn't stretch (#2738)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2738. On Windows, Direct3D 12 now presents through a DirectComposition visual (`wgpu::Dx12SwapchainKind::DxgiFromVisual`) instead of a swap chain made on the window itself.

With the window's own swap chain, wgpu creates it with `DXGI_SCALING_STRETCH`. While the window is being resized, Windows stretches the last frame, still at the old size, to the new window size until a new frame arrives. The text shimmered and the left panel's width bounced for as long as the drag lasted. A visual's last frame is shown at its own size instead, so the panel stays put. `WGPU_DX12_PRESENTATION_SYSTEM=hwnd` still selects the old path. It is now documented in `docs/development.md`.

A script drags the window's right edge back and forth with the real mouse, 240 frames per run. In each frame it compares the left 450 px of the window with a still reference. That region doesn't depend on the window's width, so a frame that differs there was drawn stretched.

author: pedrocaluiz

PDFs from **Microsoft Reporting Services** (bank statements, invoices, report exports) write `stream` followed by a space and then the line break: `stream \r\n`. title: Control channel: keep a covered or minimized window working on macOS
author: mateogasme
body:
## What this changes

An agent driving PdfCraft through `--control` stops working as soon as the user goes back to
another app on macOS. Once the window is covered or minimized, every `ui.click`, `ui.key` and
`ui.screenshot` times out with "the window is not being drawn". Two things cause it:

- winit reports the window `Occluded(true)` (or `is_minimized()`), so eframe's
  `ViewportInfo::visible()` is false and it runs no egui pass at all, so injected input never runs.
- Even when a pass runs, wgpu-hal's Metal surface skips acquiring a covered window's drawable on
  purpose (`CurrentSurfaceTexture::Occluded`, the workaround for gfx-rs/wgpu#8309), so
  `paint_and_update_textures` returns before the screenshot capture, and no screenshot arrives.

This keeps the control channel usable while the user works in another app, still only while
`--control` is on:

- **vendor/winit, patch (14):** `platform::macos::set_keep_drawing(on)`. While it's on, a
  covered or minimized window reports `Occluded(false)` and `is_minimized() == Some(false)`.
- **vendor/egui-wgpu, patch (3):** `winit::set_keep_drawing(on)` turns on the winit switch as
  well. While it's on, a requested screenshot whose surface texture can't be acquired
  (`Occluded`/`Timeout`) is drawn off screen into the capture texture and read back, and nothing
  is presented. `CaptureState::new_for`, `update_for` and `copy_to_buffer` make that texture from
  a size and format, since there is no surface texture to copy them from.
- **apps/pdfcraft:** `--control` calls `eframe::egui_wgpu::winit::set_keep_drawing(true)`.
  Without `--control` nothing changes.

The surface is still not presented while covered, so this adds no 1-second `nextDrawable` hang
(the reason wgpu skips it). A covered window runs egui passes only when something requests a
repaint, as a visible one does.

Measured on macOS 26.6.2 (Apple M4), v0.9.0 with and without this patch, window fully covered by
another app's maximized window, rounds of "click Nex…

title: Keep save shortcuts behind other dialogs

title: M6: a date typed without separators fills a yyyymmdd field
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A date typed without separators is now accepted by a date field whose format writes its fields side by side, such as `yyyymmdd`. On `main`, such a field refuses **every** date: typing `20261018` into a `yyyymmdd` field gives

> Invalid date/time: please ensure that the date/time exists. Field [ … ] should match format yyyymmdd

so the field cannot be filled at all, whether by typing, by `form_fill`, or from a value the calendar is asked to read.

**Why it matters.** `YYYYMMDD` is the date format of US Army forms. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, published by the Army Publishing Directorate) is a dynamic XFA form with 76 date fields, 70 of which show their date as `date{YYYYMMDD}`; its own field help asks for "today's date in Y Y Y Y M M D D format". `date_pattern` (`crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`) turns `date{YYYYMMDD}` into the `yyyymmdd` format, so on `main` each of those 70 fields refuses every date, as does any form field with `AFDate_FormatEx("yyyymmdd")`. I found this while filling that form in PdfCraft 0.9.0. There is no existing issue (searched for yyyymmdd, undelimited, AFDate and parse_date).

### Cause

`parse_date` (`crates/forms/src/af.rs`) splits the typed text into numbers at every non-digit, then gives one number to each field of the format. `20261018` is a single number: the year takes it, nothing is left for the month, and `it.next()?` returns `None`. The widths the format's letters define were never consulted.

### Fix

- `order()` now returns a `Part` per field of the format, with
  - its fixed width when typed run together: 4 for `yyyy`; 2 for `yy`, `mm`, `dd`, `HH`, `MM` and `ss`; 0 where the width varies (`m`, `d`) or the field is a name (`mmm`);
  - `joined`: the next field follows with nothing in between (`yyyymmdd`, `HHMM`).
- `parse_date` keeps runs of digits as text. A field joined to the next takes only its own width from a longer run and leaves the rest for the next field, **but only when fewer runs were t…

title: M6: the date picker follows a whole date typed while it is open
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

The date picker now moves to a date as soon as the field's text becomes one. On `main` it takes its month once, when it opens, so typing `03/14/2025` into a field whose calendar is showing October leaves it on October; the typed date only shows after leaving the field and coming back.

### Cause

`calendar()` (`crates/ui-egui/src/forms_ui.rs`) reads the field's text only while `Focus::calendar` is still `None`, on the first frame. From then on it reuses the stored month every frame, which is what keeps the ‹ › arrows working, but it also ignores everything typed afterwards.

### Fix

- `Focus` gets `calendar_text`: the text the calendar last saw.
- Each frame, if the text has changed since then **and** now parses as a whole date in the field's format, the calendar moves to that month. Otherwise it keeps the month it shows.
- So half a date (`03/1`) leaves it where it is, a whole one (`03/14/2025`) moves it, and after the arrows turn to another month it stays there until the text changes again.
- Opening the calendar and picking a day work as before. `parse_date` is unchanged; the calendar reads the text exactly as the field's format and keystroke check do.

No existing issue. This came up while filling DA Form 31 by hand.

## Screenshots

The real shell, rendered headlessly with egui_kittest: the `crates/ui-egui/tests/data/form.pdf` fixture plus a date field in its default `mm/dd/yyyy` format. I click the field and type `03/14/2025`, without leaving it.

title: M12: XFA dates are written and read in the field's data picture
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA date values are now written to, and read from, the form's data in the field's **data picture** (`<bind><picture>`). On `main`, PdfCraft always writes a date into the datasets packet as ISO (`2026-10-18`) and reads it back as ISO, whatever the field's data picture says. A form whose date fields bind as `date{YYYYMMDD}` therefore gets `2026-10-18` from PdfCraft but `20261018` from other XFA viewers. Data those viewers wrote is shown in PdfCraft exactly as stored, not in the field's own pattern.

The XFA spec separates the pictures: the `<ui>` picture is how a date is typed and shown, the `<bind>` picture is how it is kept in the data, and ISO is only the default when a field has no data picture. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*) is a real-world case: 70 of its 76 date fields bind as `date{YYYYMMDD}`. This was found while filling it.

No existing issue (searched for bind picture, data picture and XFA dates). #2993 also touches `crates/xfa/src/data.rs`, in `iso_to_pattern` and `pattern_to_iso` (month and weekday names). This PR only calls those two functions, so the two changes combine without conflict (checked by merging #2993 onto this branch).

### Cause

- `parse_field` keeps only the `<ui>` picture (`Field::picture`); `<bind><picture>` is dropped.
- `wanted` (`crates/xfa/src/data.rs`, writing the datasets) turns a typed date into ISO and writes that.
- `values_at` (reading values for a form laid out before) and the `DateTimeEdit` branch of the layout (`crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`) both take the data to hold ISO.

### Fix

title: Share compatible text field names
author: earlvanze
body:
## Problem

Preparing a form currently rejects a text field name already used by another field. This draft supports a subset of repeated-name text fields by keeping their widgets under one logical field, so they share a value and appearance.

## Changes

- Add a widget to an existing compatible, unlocked text field, or merge compatible text fields when a name-only edit matches an existing name. The existing field's value wins.
- Preserve the selected widget after merging and allow deleting individual shared text widgets, including multi-selection and undo.
- Refuse unsupported or unsafe structures; stage merges so errors do not partially modify the document.

This is partial work toward #3390, not a complete fix. Other field types, imported duplicate field dictionaries, differing properties, name changes combined with other property edits, and tagged or complex structures remain to be investigated. Acrobat behavior for these cases has not been verified. Please review the field-tree and metadata handling before removing draft status.

## Validation

- Forms unit tests and prepare-form UI integration tests; regressions cover save/reopen, shared values, selection, deletion, undo, locked and tagged fields, and malformed parents.
- Engine and UI tests, strict clippy, wasm compilation, formatting, and repository asset/layer/parity checks passed during development.
- On the host, a synthetic form renamed in the desktop properties dialog showed both widgets with the same name and retained selection of the renamed widget.

title: Add repeat placement and coloured tick stamps
author: earlvanze
body:

Placing a stamp always switches back to Select, and the stamp palette has no red, blue or green tick marks.

The palette now exposes the existing comment-tool “Keep tool selected” control for both custom and built-in stamps. Escape follows the comment-tool convention: deselect the current annotation, then put down the stamp tool. Selection now prefers a comment whose actual bounds contain the pointer before using the small hit tolerance, so a neighboring stamp no longer steals an inside click. Source-image or PDF whitespace is still included in stamp bounds, and the linked calculator remains open. The shared pin is the existing session setting and is not newly persisted across app restarts.

- Stamp UI suite: repeated placement including overlapping custom stamps, Escape, unpinning, and placement of all three ticks; existing default and rotated-page tests.

title: M12: laying out a dynamic XFA form takes off the usage rights it voids
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

When PdfCraft lays out a dynamic XFA form that carries **usage rights** (`/Perms /UR3`), it now takes them off the catalog in the layout revision and says so in the layout report (the notice bar and `doc_info`). It no longer saves a file whose usage rights are void.

Usage rights are a signature over the form as it was published (ISO 32000-1, 12.8.2.3). PdfCraft's layout revision replaces the placeholder pages and adds the fields, so the rights no longer match the form. On `main` they stay in the file anyway. Every save carries the layout revision, so every saved copy holds rights that no longer match its form. A widely used free viewer then opens the form **with every field locked**: the person PdfCraft's user sends the form to can't fill in a single box.

`strip` (taking the XFA out) already removes usage rights for the same reason, with a note. This PR moves that code into one helper, `drop_usage_rights`, and calls it from `write_form`, the one place that rewrites a laid-out form's pages and fields. Both the open-time layout (`render_into`) and a script-driven re-layout (`rerender`) go through `write_form`.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case. It is a dynamic XFA form with usage rights, and this was found while filling it. No existing issue (searched for usage rights and UR3).

### Cause

- `write_form` (`crates/xfa/src/pdf.rs`) rewrites the page tree and the AcroForm, and leaves `/Perms` alone.
- The layout is one appended revision (`prepare_open_unguarded`, `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`), and every save, incremental or full, includes it.

### Fix

- **`drop_usage_rights(doc, catalog)`**: removes `/UR3` (and the older `/UR`) from `/Perms` and keeps everything else, such as a certification's `/DocMDP`. An indirect `/Perms` is rewritten where it is rather than copied into the catalog. An emptied `/Perms` is removed. It returns whether anything was removed.
- **`write_form`** calls it and repo…

title: Persist default font size for callouts and text boxes
author: earlvanze
body:
The font size in Comment Properties changes an existing callout, but **Make Properties Default** previously left new callouts at 10 pt. This makes that choice persist for new callouts and text boxes, separately for each tool, including after restarting. New boxes are sized using the chosen font size.

Related to #3399. Long callouts placed close to the edge of a small page can extend past the page; this change does not alter placement constraints.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test comments` (51 passed), including callout save/reopen and creation after restoring defaults, plus the independent text-box default.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `git diff --check`.

title: M6: a secured form's notice bar still says it is a form
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A secured form's notice bar now still says it is a form. On `main`, the bar on any secured document (opened without the owner password, with changes or page assembly withheld) shows only *"This document is secured. Some changes are restricted by its security settings."* For a secured fillable or XFA form, that message *replaces* the form's own notice, and with it:

- the **Highlight fields** button, the only one-click way to see where the fields are;
- *"This document contains N interactive form fields."*, or for a dynamic XFA form *"Dynamic XFA form laid out from its template: …"* with **every layout note** PdfCraft recorded (pictures left out, fields drawn with `?`, and so on);
- *"This is a dynamic XFA form, which PdfCraft can't display yet…"*, the one warning that tells a user the page in front of them is a placeholder.

Secured forms are common. Government and corporate forms are routinely encrypted with filling allowed and changing withheld. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is one, and this was found while testing #3401 on it: the layout note that PR adds never appeared, because the bar showed only the security notice.

No existing issue (searched for secured, notice bar and Highlight fields).

### Fix

`notices` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) first works out what the document is as a form (XFA layout, XFA placeholder, static XFA, or interactive fields), using the same messages as before, then:

- **Secured and a form:** the bar shows the form's notice followed by the security sentence. **Highlight fields** stays, next to **Security settings** and **Unlock…**. The icon is the form's.
- **Secured and not a form:** unchanged (the lock icon and the security sentence alone).
- **Not secured:** unchanged.
- A form whose scripts were turned off still takes the bar first, as before.

Both sentences are existing translated strings, so the catalogs need no new entries.

author: earlvanze

The right rail now has dedicated single-page and two-page controls, so either layout can be selected with one click. Switching preserves the current page, zoom, and continuous-scrolling setting. The Page display menu remains available for the other display options.

title: M12: an XFA script that fails partway keeps what it changed before the error
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

An XFA script that fails partway now keeps what it changed before the error. On `main`, `Runner::run` (`crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`) returns as soon as a script reports an error, before `apply_effects`. So a script that set ten values and then threw changes nothing. JavaScript doesn't work that way: every statement before a `throw` has run, and its assignments stand. Other XFA viewers follow it, so forms are written, and tested, against that behavior.

It matters because real forms trip over their own stale references. A form is revised, a field is renamed or removed, and a script written for the old version still names it. In the viewer it was tested in, the script's earlier lines do their work and the error only shows in the console. In PdfCraft the error undoes that work, so the form stops working.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, and this was found while filling it:

1. Checking **8. CHARGEABLE** runs that box's change script. Its first part opens the leave-type boxes (`access = "open"` on *Annual (Ordinary) Leave* and eleven others) and shows the chargeable sections.
2. About 200 lines later it sets `this.resolveNode("Non_Chargeable_Section_9_and_10_Subform.Non_Chargeable_Total_Days_Requested").rawValue`. No such field exists in the template, so `resolveNode` returns `null` and the assignment throws a `TypeError` in any viewer.
3. On `main` that error discards step 1. The leave-type boxes stay protected, so nothing after them can be filled: 10a, 10b and the requestor's signature never appear.

The 10a script has the same kind of reference (`Chargeable_Total_Days_10b`, also absent from the template).

No existing issue (searched for script error, partial and effects).

### Fix

- `Runner::run` records the error as before (the JavaScript console and the error list still show it), then applies the effects the script recorded before it failed, re-laying the form out when they show or hide…

title: Honor single-page redaction selections
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

`redact_mark` silently ignores `page` for text, word, pattern and whole-page marks. For example, searching for matching text with `page: 1` marks every matching page, and applying those marks can remove content from unintended pages.

Honor `page` for each selector, reject simultaneous `page` and `pages`, and reject `pages` for rectangle marks. Document the selection rules in the tool schema.

## How you verified it

- The new two-page synthetic regression failed on main (two marks instead of one) and passes with the fix. It covers all four selectors, invalid selections without added marks, and application preserving the other page's text.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-automation`
- `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`

## Reviewer note

Calls that previously supplied both selectors, or supplied `pages` with `rect`, now fail rather than silently discarding one selector. Existing `pages` selection and the default of all pages remain supported.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Redaction marking can target a single page across text, word, pattern, and whole-page selections. Use `pages` to target multiple pages, or omit page selection to apply marks across the document.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Invalid page-selection combinations are now rejected, including specifying both `page` and `pages`, or combining `rect` with `pages`. Rectangle marking requires a single `page`.
  * Single-page redactions leave matching text on other pages unchanged.

title: Fix shaded Type 3 glyphs at translated positions
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3178. Type 3 glyphs whose painted content uses `sh` can disappear away from the page origin: the interpreter intersects transformed clip bounds with the untransformed font bounding box. Transform the font box into the same device coordinate space before initializing the glyph context.

## How you verified it

- A synthetic Type 3 glyph with a clipped axial shading is drawn at two positions. The new `shaded_type3_glyph_draws_at_multiple_positions` test failed on main (the second glyph was white) and passed with the fix.
- Rendered the issue's SHA-256-verified page 32 locally at 96 dpi: main produced scattered badge fragments; this change produces complete badges, consistent with a Poppler reference render. The external PDF is not committed.
- `cargo test --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-render --lib`: 307 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; strict clippy for `pdfcraft-render --all-targets` and `hayro-interpret --lib`; `cargo xtask layers`; `cargo xtask assets`.

`hayro-interpret --all-targets` clippy cannot compile its pre-existing `extract_images` example because the vendored package does not declare that example's `image` dependency; the changed library itself passes strict clippy. The vendored package also cannot be tested directly as a workspace package because it is not a workspace member. The regression runs through the product renderer.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed an issue where shaded glyphs could render incorrectly when the same glyph appeared at multiple positions. Shading now displays in the correct locations for translated glyphs, including when the glyph’s drawing area is clipped. This improves the consistency of documents that use shaded Type 3 glyphs.

title: Respect unspecified Type 3 glyph bounds
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

An all-zero Type 3 `/FontBBox` means the font does not specify glyph bounds. PdfCraft currently treats it as a zero-sized clip for shaded glyphs, so they disappear. Carry the enclosing page or clip bounds into the glyph context in that case; a missing box follows the same existing fallback. Nonzero font boxes still use their transformed bounds.

This is a follow-up to #3412 and is based on its head. The diff against main includes that prerequisite until it merges; rebase this draft afterward. Thanks to the reviewer of #3412 for identifying the zero-box case.

## How you verified it

- Expanded the synthetic shading regression to cover normal, all-zero and missing boxes, two glyph positions, and an enclosing page clip. The zero-box case failed before this change and the expanded test passes afterward.
- `cargo test --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-render --lib`: 307 passed before adding the enclosing-clip assertion; the expanded targeted regression passed afterward.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, strict clippy for `pdfcraft-render --all-targets` and `hayro-interpret --lib`, `cargo xtask layers`, and `cargo xtask assets` passed.
- As in #3412, the vendored interpreter's all-targets clippy includes an existing example with an undeclared `image` dependency; the changed library passes strict clippy.

title: Speed damaged xref recovery with a bounded candidate index
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

When many in-use cross-reference entries have stale offsets, recovery currently scans the whole file once per requested object. Build a shared candidate-position index on the first fallback lookup, and check candidates newest first with the existing parser. The index is capped at 500,000 candidates; if it exceeds the cap, recovery uses the existing scan. Valid offsets do not build the index, and freed xref entries remain freed.

Refs #3414. This addresses a measured recovery cost, not the whole report: a stalled open can still block the single background worker, and the reporter's original PDF and Windows handoff have not been tested.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-cos`: passed, including new tests for last-valid recovery, shared indexing, the cap and an incremental xref with a freed object.
- `cargo clippy --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Mutation: setting the index cap to zero made the index-use regression fail; restoring it passed.
- A property test compares indexed recovery against the original forward scan on generated malformed object/header, stream and comment combinations. Removing reverse candidate order makes it fail; restoring it passes.
- Synthetic two-revision COS probe, 1,498 requested objects and 92,556 bytes: one macOS low-disk-profile run took 336 ms on main with stale offsets and 2 ms on this branch; controls with correct offsets took 2 ms and 1 ms respectively. These are illustrative single runs.
- A synthetic 300-page GUI harness with stale offsets followed by a valid PDF completed in 3.09 s on main and 29 ms with an equivalent prototype before the final checked-access rewrite. Both opened; no physical Windows or reporter-file test was performed.

## Never-crash and provenance

Candidate count is capped; an oversized index falls back to the existing scan. Input-de…

title: Let a later document open while one preparation stalls
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

A stalled background PDF preparation currently holds the only open worker, so later files cannot open. Two bounded workers now share the existing 16-entry FIFO queue. One stalled preparation can coexist with a later successful open; if both workers stall, later jobs still wait.

A later successful ordinary open keeps focus if an earlier ordinary open finishes afterwards. A later failed open does not suppress the earlier successful open. A delayed document-bound tool still activates its own document before executing; converted files also respect the background focus decision. Password prompts and tool dialogs continue to hold other ready results until the interaction finishes.

Refs #3414. This does not cancel a stalled parse, establish the cause of the reporter's file, or make progress when both workers are occupied. Documents can complete and appear in a different order from the requests; that tradeoff needs review.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`: passed on macOS after merging main `43550c44` (existing ignored private-fixture tests remain ignored).
- `cargo clippy --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- A synthetic barrier test failed on the original single-worker code because the later preparation did not start. It passes here and checks that the later document opens before release and retains focus afterwards.
- Synthetic tests also cover a later failed open, an earlier converted file, and a delayed document-bound export. The open-worker suite passed ten consecutive runs on the original base; the full suite passed again after the main update.
- A delayed synthetic password-protected PDF retains the newer document’s focus through an incorrect password and successful unlock; all 21 open-worker tests passed after adding this case.

title: M10: Office export follows forms 50 deep and up to 50 000 a page and says where it stops (#3120)
author: Faabyy
body:
Export to Word, PowerPoint, HTML and RTF stopped at 12 nested forms and 4 096 forms a page and left the rest out silently, while the renderer, `text` and Find read 50 levels. A page that draws a label or table cell as a form more than 4 096 times lost the text of the later ones.

Export now follows forms 50 deep and up to 50 000 a page (the renderer's budget for nested paints). The budget also counts forms the page draws itself, so a page that draws one a million times stays bounded. `doc_export_office` returns `truncated`, `truncated_pages` and, only when something was cut, `warnings`. `reading_blocks` and `export_office` keep their signatures; the new `reading_blocks_checked` and `export_office_checked` carry the flag.

Checked against the repro in the issue: before, page 1 and 3 had no "TAIL" in the export; now all four pages do, and `nested_paints.pdf` reports pages 1 and 3 as truncated, matching `text`. New tests in `pdfcraft-edit` and the automation tests; reverting the limits or the flag makes them fail. `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, `xtask parity` and `xtask layers` pass.

Open for you: the hostile 100-way fan-out test now takes about 3.5 s (was 0.3 s) because the visit budget is ten times larger; a per-page font cache would fix that and could be a follow-up. The export dialog does not show the warning yet, that needs a UI and i18n decision. A 50-deep walk uses about 256-384 KiB of stack and is not tested on wasm.

Fixes #3120

title: M12: Fix XFA validation, form rendering and PDF417 barcodes
author: CheatCod
body:
## What this changes

Complex XFA forms previously lost their script objects and data bindings: Validate and Clear could do nothing, dependent dropdowns failed during initialize, nested validation handlers resolved the wrong scope, and PDF417 fields were absent or short and could regenerate without their answers.

Read manifest lists inside variables and their bound dataNode references, and run preSave scripts on an output copy to regenerate current payloads. Fractional unit rounding no longer splits a page-sized panel or adds a trailing empty page.
- Correct button caption typography, standard-14 measurement, letter spacing, numeric display pictures and embedded TIFF/BMP decorations.

The headless tools expose the same validation, confirmation and typing-preview behavior. No user documents, extracted scripts, screenshots, fonts or other assets are included.

title: fix(render): use unfiltered inline image byte length before EI heuristic (#3107)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Closes #3107

### Problem
When an unfiltered inline image (no `/Filter` / `/F`, or `null` / `[]`) contains the byte sequence `EI` followed by whitespace and bytes that happen to parse as a text-showing or content operator inside its sample payload, hayro-syntax's `UntypedIter::next` cut the inline image at that internal `EI` and executed the remaining image sample bytes as page content operators. As a result:
- Only the prefix of the inline image before `EI` was decoded, distorting rendered pixel values.
- Any operators embedded in the remaining image bytes (such as `BT ... (Injected) Tj ET`) were executed during rendering, text extraction (`plain_text()`), and `find()`.

Meanwhile, `pdfcraft-content` (`crates/content/src/lib.rs`) already computes the exact byte length of unfiltered inline images (including row byte padding) before falling back to heuristic `EI` scanning.

### Fix
- Teach hayro-syntax's inline image reader (`UntypedIter::next` in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/content/mod.rs`) to compute the deterministic sample byte count of unfiltered inline images (`/DeviceGray`/`/G`, `/DeviceRGB`/`/RGB`, `/DeviceCMYK`/`/CMYK`, 4-element `[/Indexed ...]`/`[/I ...]`, and `/ImageMask`/`/IM`, respecting full/abbreviated key consistency) and check for whitespace + `EI` at that exact offset before falling back to the `find_ei` heuristic.
- Align `/L` policy with `crates/content`: deterministic layout dimensions (`/W`, `/H`, `/CS`, `/BPC`, row padding) directly determine the unfiltered payload length, so a conflicting or crafted `/L` cannot force an early cut and inject operators. (Named resource color spaces like `/CS /CS0` remain a known follow-up gap as stream tokenizers do not resolve against parent resource dictionaries).
- Preserve the streaming window invariant (`complete = false`) by requesting more bytes (`NeedsMore`) whenever the current window ends before the expected sample end or before the `EI` delimiter can be confirmed.

### Verification
- Added unit tests in…

author: LetoCoder26
body:
## What this changes

This follows up #1787. That fix made a signed page's resources page content whatever keys a later revision writes. title: Edit text: refuse a rewrite of text that is a clipping path
author: Hamza0101
body:
Refs #3429 — the Edit text half, which is the part that destroys files.

Credit where it is due: @RavenCrowe666 reported it with the Photoshop source and @mtlcl410 traced it to `clear_block`'s existing guard. They converged on exactly this fix; I have implemented and measured it.

## Reproduced

A page whose only text is a `7 Tr` mask with a red rectangle painted through it, edited through `text_edit` and rendered either side:

```
before:  red pixels  1,521   (3.4% of the page — the fill shaped by the letters)
after:   red pixels 45,000   (100% of the page — a flat rectangle)
```

`doc_save` reported success with `"undo": "Edit text"`, and the file reopens without a warning. So the loss is silent.

## Change

`replace_line` and `rewrite_block` refuse render modes 4 to 7:

```
text used as a clipping path cannot be edited: its glyphs mask the artwork behind them
```

`clear_block` has refused these since before this PR — *"text used as a clipping path cannot be previewed for editing"* — so the editor already knew they were unsafe; the two rewrite paths simply did not ask. There were exactly two `render_mode` guards in `crates/edit/src/text.rs` and neither covered a rewrite.

```
clipping text   refused, no file written, document untouched
normal text     still edits → "EDITED"
```

## Tests

- `rewriting_clipping_path_text_is_refused_for_every_clipping_mode` — all four modes (4, 5, 6, 7) against both entry points, and after each refusal the page still has its one line reading `MASK`, so the assertion is that the document is *untouched* rather than merely that an error came back. Without the guard it fails.
- `painting_modes_are_still_rewritten` — modes 0, 1 and 2 still rewrite, so the guard cannot quietly widen to text that paints ink.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

title: Render: a glyph shown in a clipping mode clips even with no outline
author: Hamza0101
body:
A glyph shown in a clipping render mode (`4 Tr` to `7 Tr`) adds its outline to the clipping path, and that clip applies to everything painted after `ET` until the enclosing `Q`. When the glyphs shown have no outline — a space, say — the clip they contribute is empty, and an empty clip admits nothing.

`interpret_window` applied a clip only once a glyph had contributed an outline, so such a text object applied **no** clip and whatever followed painted unmasked:

```
q BT 7 Tr /F1 24 Tf 4 10 Td ( ) Tj ET  1 0 0 rg 0 0 40 40 re f  Q
```

filled the whole page where nothing should paint through the empty clip.

### Measured

Red pixels of a page filled red behind the text object, in this renderer and in two others:

| page | pdfcraft before | pdfcraft after | Preview (CoreGraphics) | Firefox (pdf.js) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a space shown in `7 Tr` | 100% | **0%** | 0% | 0% |
| no glyph shown in `7 Tr` | 100% | 100% | 0% | 100% |
| no text object | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| a space shown in `0 Tr` | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% |

The two independent readers agree on the first row and disagree on the second, and pdf.js's `endText` is explicit about where the line is: `pendingTextPaths` exists only once a glyph has been shown in a clipping mode, so no glyphs shown leaves the clip alone, while glyphs shown with empty outlines are clipped with an empty `Path2D`. This change draws the same line — `clip_shown` is set in `clip_glyph`, not when `Tr` selects a mode.

A glyph whose outline is unavailable (Type 3) leaves the real clip unknown, so that case stays unclipped as well.

### What this is not

An earlier version of this PR also clipped for a text object that shows no glyphs at all, and I described it as the root cause of #3123 and #3429. That was wrong, and review caught it: editing a clipping title away leaves a text object with no glyphs, which is exactly the case that must not clip, so the flood those reports describe is the edited file's own meaning. #34…

title: fix(engine): a reload keeps reading colours and hidden comments (#3443)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3443. Not `Fixes`: this closes the one path I could reproduce, and I have not confirmed it is the path the reporter hits on macOS.

`Session::reload` handles a file that changed on disk. It used to open the new bytes with a default render config, so a document shown in reading colours, or with its comments hidden, went back to the file's own look. The UI re-applies the reading-colour preference only on open (`finish_open`, `files.rs`, `create_ui.rs`), not after `reload_view`. Reload now carries both display settings over and rebuilds the renderer with them. Layer choices are not touched.

**Evidence**
- **[code]** `reload` calls `self.open(…)`, and `open` builds the config as `RenderConfig { password, ..Default::default() }` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, `build_document`). The file watcher's `reload_view` (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_watch.rs:411`) calls `session.reload` and `document_replaced`, but not `set_reading_colors`.
- **[test]** A temporary kittest probe on `main` @ `43550c44` (not committed) used `file_watch`'s own `harness` and `find_new_version`. Before the reload, the app preference and the document setting were `(true, true)`. After it they were `(true, false)`: the preference was still on, but the document's renderer was back to the file's colours. That matches the reporter's "toggling the preference off and on restores it". The same probe found that a plain in-place Save keeps `(true, true)`, so saving alone does not reset the setting.
- **[inference]** On macOS the reporter sees the revert right after saving. The watcher's Unix `Stamp` includes `ctime` (`file_watch.rs:46`). A metadata-only change made after PdfCraft's own write would make the saved file look like a new version and trigger a reload. Examples are an extended attribute written by Finder, Spotlight or a sync client. I have not verified this on macOS.

title: Tests: the parser-cancel test guards against a hang, not a 2 s limit (#1970)
author: Faabyy
body:
`waiting_worker_can_cancel_before_initializer_returns` gave its threads 2 s to start, and a busy FreeBSD VM in CI took longer. Its waits only guard against a hang: the initializer is held until the end of the test, so a waiter that can't cancel never returns, however long the guard is. They now allow 600 s, like the hang guard in `page_contents_and_nested_forms_share_one_budget` (#2812), which already covers the second test named in the issue. The test polls with a 1 ms sleep instead of `yield_now`, and the held initializer no longer panics a second time when the test fails.

title: M1: a saved file whose metadata alone changes is not a new version (#3443)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3443, fixes #3755 (the same cause, reported from macOS), together with #3452. This PR removes the trigger: the reload after every save on macOS. #3452 makes a reload keep the reading colours.

**What the reporter measured on macOS** (#3443):
- **Before and after:** `stat` right after a save in PdfCraft, then again 5 s later.
- **Result:** inode, size and `mtime` were identical, but `ctime` had moved by about 1.57 s.
- **What did it:** the system rewrites the file's extended attributes (`com.apple.macl`, `com.apple.metadata:kMDItemWhereFroms`, `com.apple.provenance`).

**[code] Why PdfCraft reacted:**
- **The Unix stamp includes `ctime`.** `Stamp` (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_watch.rs:46`) uses it to tell versions apart. So PdfCraft took its own save for another program's change.
- **Reload on:** it reloaded the document, which dropped the undo history and, without #3452, the reading colours.
- **Reload off:** every save asked "Save over the changed file?" (`disk_differs`, #2166). The reporter confirmed both behaviours.

**Now, a file that still holds the bytes the document came from is the same version.** "The bytes the document came from" is `Document::saved_bytes`, the file as last opened, reloaded or saved.
- **Watcher** (`file_changed`): it already has the file's bytes. When they equal the saved bytes, it adopts the new stamp as the document's version and doesn't reload.
- **Save** (`disk_differs`, now given the saved bytes): a stamp that differs from the basis is a change only if the length differs or the contents do. The file is read only when its length matches the saved bytes, so the read is never larger than what is already in memory.
- **A file with other bytes is a change as before,** whatever its stamp says.

An earlier draft first required "only `ctime` moved" before comparing contents. A mutation run showed that gate changed no outcome. Identical bytes need neither a reload nor a prompt, whatever moved in the metadata, so the …

## What this changes

**Measure objects: set the plan scale as an architect's ratio (1:N), applied at once.**

Fixes #2752. The reporter had to enter "1:17.5" to measure a 1:50 plan correctly. The calculation is fine. The cause is the scale fields: they read `pt [72] = [value] [unit]`, and the left field is in **PDF points** (1/72 in = 0.3528 mm), not millimetres of paper (`crates/ui-egui/src/measure_ui.rs` on `main`: the `DragValue` with prefix `"pt "` around line 356, divided out in `Scale::calibrate(…, real_distance / drawing_points, …)` around line 413).

- Entered as `1 = 50` mm, a 1:50 plan measures every length 72 / 25.4 ≈ 2.835 times too long.
- The correct value is `1 pt = 50 × 25.4 / 72 ≈ 17.64 mm`, so "17.5" looked about right.

A new unit test, `measure_ui::tests::issue_2752_a_1_50_plan_reads_true_at_1_50_not_at_1_17_5`, pins all three numbers. It uses 100 mm of paper, which is 5000 mm of building at 1:50:
- `1 = 50 mm` reads 2.835 × too long;
- `1 = 17.5 mm` reads within 1 %;
- choosing 1:50 reads exactly 5000 mm.

The PR has three commits:

1. **Plan scale as 1:N.** The panel offers the usual scales (1:1 to 1:1000) and a free `1:N` field (it also accepts `1/N`, `N` and comma decimals), with the unit (m, cm, mm) and the decimals beside it.

title: fix(edit): keep a superscript footnote marker in its paragraph's row (#3252)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3252. A footnote marker drawn with `Ts` (text rise) and a smaller `Tf` size sits on the same visual row as the body text around it, but the row-joining baseline tolerance in `group_layout` (`crates/edit/src/text_regions.rs`) was scaled by the *smaller* of the two runs' sizes (20% of it) — far tighter than a typical superscript's rise, which runs up to about half the body size. The marker split off into its own `TextLine`, and then its own `TextBlock`, fragmenting one paragraph into three separate editable zones in Edit PDF ▸ Edit text and images (and in `reading_blocks`, used by Export to Word/HTML/RTF, since both share `group_layout`).

The fix scales the tolerance by the larger of the two sizes instead. Ordinary next-line leading (about 1.2× the font size) stays well outside it, so paragraph lines that are genuinely stacked still start new rows as before — only a same-row, raised-or-lowered, smaller-or-larger run (a super/subscript) is now tolerated.

## How you verified it

```

cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit --tests -- -D warnings
cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit
cargo xtask layers
cargo xtask assets

I reverted the fix locally and confirmed it fails on `main` (3 blocks: the text before the marker, the marker alone, the text after — matching the reporter's "split into several separate text zones") before reapplying it and confirming it passes (1 block, 2 rows).

title: fix(forms): draw fields the file leaves to the viewer, for display only (#3470)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3470. A filled form whose writer left the appearances to the viewer showed its text fields empty in PdfCraft. Acrobat, Firefox and MuPDF show the values.

**[spec]** ISO 32000-2, Table 224 (printed p.529), `NeedAppearances`: "A flag specifying whether to construct appearance streams and appearance dictionaries for all widget annotations in the document … A PDF writer shall include this key, with a value of true, if it has not provided appearance streams for all visible widget annotations present in the document." It is deprecated in PDF 2.0, but files that rely on it are common.

**[code] Why the fields were empty**
- `pdfcraft_forms::need_appearances` was only used when *writing*.
- The engine's display copy draws missing appearances in memory (`display_bytes` → `pdfcraft_annot::with_missing_appearances_cached`). It skips `Widget` annotations.
- So nothing drew a text field from its `/V`. Check boxes looked right only because they use the appearance states already in the file.

**The fix**
- **New function:** `pdfcraft_forms::with_field_appearances(doc) -> Option<Document>` returns a copy in which text, combo and list widgets are drawn from their values. It uses the same generator a typed value uses (`appearance::field_appearance_drawn`, as in `redraw`).
- **Which widgets:**
  - When the form sets `/NeedAppearances true`, every such widget is redrawn, since the flag says the file's appearances aren't to be trusted.
  - Otherwise only widgets with no `/AP /N` are drawn. An appearance the file has, even an empty one, stays the file's.
  - Buttons keep their states.
- **Engine:** the display copy applies it after the comment appearances, in both `display_bytes` (page view, page images, Print as Image) and `display_bytes_for` (CLI render).
- **Saving:** the document itself is not changed, so saving writes the file as it was. Editing a field already writes a real appearance.
