title: Remove Hidden Information: clip-only text is not hidden text
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3644. **Reworked after review** — the first version kept the text, which was the wrong trade; this one removes it and fixes the flood at its cause.

Text in a clipping mode (`7 Tr`) paints nothing itself, so it is hidden from the eye while staying extractable and searchable. Remove Hidden Information takes it, as it takes `3 Tr` text, and counts it. What it must not do is leave the page flooded.

### Why it flooded

Those glyphs are the clipping path for whatever is painted until the enclosing `Q`. Taking them leaves the clip the text object set **empty** — and readers disagree about an empty text clip. From the table I measured on #3451:

| | pdfcraft | Preview (CoreGraphics) | Firefox (pdf.js) |
|---|---|---|---|
| a space shown in `7 Tr` | clips | clips | clips |
| **no glyph shown in `7 Tr`** | **paints** | clips | **paints** |

So after removal the page was reader-dependent: nothing in Preview, the fill's whole rectangle in pdfcraft and pdf.js. That is the solid box in #3644.

### What this does

A text object that loses every clipping glyph is followed by an explicit empty clip:

```
BT 7 Tr /F1 10 Tf 10 200 Td [-2000] TJ ET
0 0 0 0 re W n                               ← added
1 0 0 rg 5 195 90 20 re f                    ← the fill, now clipped away in every reader
```

Nothing is left to the ambiguity: the glyphs are gone, and the clip they set says "nothing paints through me", which is what an empty set of glyph outlines means.

### Measured

Red pixels on a four-page fixture at 72 dpi, end to end through `doc_hidden_info` → `doc_remove_hidden(["hidden-text"])` → `doc_save` → `render`:

title: fix(render): accept PDF delimiters after inline-image EI (#3578)
author: Zaxaerith
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3578.

PdfCraft's renderer could incorrectly reject the end of an inline image when the `EI` operator was immediately followed by a PDF delimiter, such as `%` (a comment) or `[` (an array).

For example, both of these are valid token boundaries:

- `EI%comment`
- `EI[] 0 d`

The editor's content parser already recognizes these boundaries, but the vendored hayro tokenizer used by rendering and text extraction did not. This disagreement could prevent the renderer from correctly processing an inline image and the subsequent page content.

This PR fixes the token-boundary check, adds regression coverage, and documents the affected behavior.

## Root cause

The issue originates in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/content/mod.rs`, inside `UntypedIter::next`.

While scanning inline-image data for a possible `EI` terminator, the tokenizer rejected any candidate whose following byte was not whitespace:

```rust
!is_white_space_character(b[2])
```

This condition incorrectly treated PDF delimiters (`%`, `[`, etc.) like regular characters.

Under PDF lexical rules, delimiters terminate the preceding token. Therefore, `EI%comment` contains a valid `EI` token followed by a comment, while `EIQ` is a single regular-character token and must not be interpreted as `EI` followed by `Q`.

The editor's parser in `crates/content/src/lib.rs` already distinguishes these cases.

## Fix

The suffix check now uses the existing `is_regular_character` function from the vendored lexer.

Consequently:

- `EI%comment` and `EI[]` are accepted as possible end-of-image boundaries and passed to the existing candidate validation.
- `EIQ` and other regular-character suffixes remain rejected.
- Normal whitespace-separated `EI` markers retain their existing behavior.
- Existing checks for false `EI` candidates inside encoded image data remain in place.

The change deliberately preserves the existing look-ahead logic, image-data slicing, cursor advancement, and bounded scanning limits …

title: Redaction: search the text on layers that are off
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3646.

The redaction search read the text the renderer extracts, and the renderer leaves out content on a layer that is off. So a word on a hidden layer was never found and never marked: the user was told every match was marked, applied them, saved — and the word was still in the file, in plain bytes, and on screen in any viewer as soon as the layer was turned on.

### Measured

The report's file: two pages with the same line, on a hidden layer on page 1 and visible on page 2.

| | `text_find` | `redact_mark` | `redact_apply` | `SECRET` in the saved bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1 | 1 | 1 | **yes** |
| after | 1 | **2** | **2** | no |

A control document with the same text and no optional content behaves exactly as before: 2 found, 2 marked, 2 applied.

### Only the search needed changing

You had already established the important half: applying a mark removes hidden content, because `Apply` walks the content stream without a visibility test. So the quads just have to be found.

The search now reads the pages with every layer forced visible, through a new `page_texts_every_layer`, and only when the document has a hidden layer — otherwise it takes the existing cached path that Find shares. `RenderConfig::layers` already existed for exactly this (per-OCG visibility overrides), so `extract_parallel` is split into a thin wrapper over `extract_with_layers` and nothing else changes.

### Two things I decided deliberately

**That extraction is not cached.** The text cache holds what Find sees, keyed per document and page; putting layer-forced text in it would hand Find the hidden content on a later call. The new method bypasses the cache, and its doc comment says why so nobody "optimises" it back in.

**Find is unchanged**, and the test asserts it. You wrote that whether Find should look at hidden layers is a product choice while redaction is the privacy promise, and I agree — so `text_find` still reports 1 on that file. If the maintainers want Find to se…

title: Accept a delimiter after EI when ending an inline image
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3578

The EI candidate check in hayro's content lexer skipped any `EI` whose next byte was not white space. An `EI` followed by a delimiter (`EI%comment`, `EI[] 0 d`) was therefore never accepted as the end of the image, and the rest of the page was lost.

The candidate check now skips an `EI` only when the next byte is a regular character, so white space and delimiters both end the token. This matches the PDF lexical rules and the edit reader. The existing look-ahead still validates each candidate.

## How you verified it

- `cd vendor/hayro-syntax && cargo test --lib inline_image`
- `content::tests::inline_image_ei_may_be_followed_by_a_delimiter` fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it.
- `content::tests::inline_image_ei_followed_by_a_regular_character_is_not_the_end` and `content::tests::ascii85_inline_image_data_may_contain_ei_before_a_delimiter` pass on `main` as well. They guard against regressions from this change.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`
- [ ] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed

**Tests.** The three new tests cover the delimiter cases, an `EIQ` negative case, and ASCII-85 data containing `EI[`, `EI/`, `EI%`, `EI(` and `EI<`. The regression test was checked to fail before the fix.

title: Select a table by rows when a drag crosses its columns
author: hectorviov
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3850.

Partly addresses #3682: drags within one column of its two-column page now select that column's text (the tester's harness measured 3/9 → 7/9 on `cols.pdf`). Drags from one column into the next still follow reading order, as on `main`; they need column-correct reading order (#3676).

Selecting text in a table selected the wrong things. A table reads column by column, so a plain drag along one row, or down and across a few rows, took the rest of the first column and the top of the next ones between its ends. On some rows the highlight jumped to the column headers and half the table. Copy gave the cells out of order. Preview selects these by rows, and this makes PdfCraft do the same.

Rebased on `main` after the module split (#4889): the row selection is in `crates/render/src/text.rs`, the padded-cell join and barcode rows in `text/order.rs` and `text/layout.rs`, the drag's pointer end in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas/selection.rs` and `canvas.rs`.

- **Visual rows** (`PageText::visual_between`, used by `Selection::rects` and `Selection::text`). The drag selects by rows when reading order between its ends would not follow them: the rest of the first row, the rows between, and the start of the last. Copy gives the cells tab-separated, as Column select does. Rows are used when either of these holds:
  - Reading order strays above or below the rows dragged over.
  - The drag ends in another column. That means across a gutter that no text of those rows crosses (checked a few lines above and below as well, so a justified line's wide word gap does not count), or with the pointer past the end of both lines.
- **Limits on the rows.** Rows never take lines left of everywhere the drag has been, and they stay in the column when the drag does. A drag in the right column of side-by-side text that ends on a hanging list marker does not pull in the left column. Running text keeps reading order whenever it covers the same glyphs, and so does a column …

title: Redaction: follow nested forms as deep as the readers do
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes the data loss in #3645. The reporting half of that issue is **not** in this change — see the end.

A form past the pass's depth limit is removed rather than walked. That is the fail-safe choice for a redaction — marked content inside a form we cannot read would otherwise survive — but it also removes whatever else that form drew, marked or not. At a limit of 12, a page with a 13-deep chain lost the text of its innermost form with nothing in it marked.

### Measured

A page drawing `HEAD` at the top, a chain of forms whose innermost draws `DEEP`, then `TAIL`. Only `HEAD` is marked. `pdfcraft-cli text` after applying and saving:

| chain | what the renderer reads | after, cap 12 | after, cap 50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `HEAD DEEP TAIL` | `DEEP TAIL` | `DEEP TAIL` |
| 12 | `HEAD DEEP TAIL` | `DEEP TAIL` | `DEEP TAIL` |
| **13** | `HEAD DEEP TAIL` | **`TAIL`** | `DEEP TAIL` |
| 14 | `HEAD DEEP TAIL` | **`TAIL`** | `DEEP TAIL` |
| 50 | `HEAD DEEP TAIL` | **`TAIL`** | `DEEP TAIL` |
| 51 | `HEAD TAIL` | `TAIL` | `TAIL` |

### Why 50

You pointed at the renderer's `MAX_NESTED_INTERPRETATION_DEPTH` and Edit text's `MAX_FORM_DEPTH`, both 50. I checked what the renderer actually *reads* rather than taking the constants on trust — the last row above is the answer. At 51 the renderer does not read `DEEP` either, so removing that form costs nothing visible and the fail-safe still holds.

So 50 is not an arbitrary bump: it is the depth at which the three readers agree, which makes the rule "anything a reader can see, this pass can walk, and anything past that is invisible and may be removed".

### Tests

`a_deeply_nested_form_keeps_the_text_nobody_marked` — chains of 1, 12, 13, 20 and 50 with only the page's own text marked: `forms_removed == 0`, `(TAIL)` still in the content, and `(DEEP)` still in the saved bytes. Then a chain of 51, which is still removed (`forms_removed == 1`), so the fail-safe is pinned as well as the fix.

Without the change it fails at the first chain…

title: M8: applying redactions drops structure-tree references to the comments and fields it removes (#2874)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2874.

When redaction removed annotations and form fields under a mark, it took them off the pages' `/Annots` but left the structure tree's object references (`/OBJR`) to them. A full rewrite of a tagged PDF then still reached the removed comment or widget through `StructTreeRoot`, and with it the redacted comment's `/Contents` and the field's `/V`.

`redact::apply` now does the following:
- It records every annotation the pages list before it runs.
- After deleting the doomed fields (step 3a), it calls `tags::drop_object_refs` with every annotation no page lists any more. That is the same helper and approach Sanitize uses since #2532. The set includes widgets of a removed field that sit on *other* pages, and the marks' pop-ups.
- Elements left with nothing to tag lose `/Alt`, `/ActualText`, `/T` and `/E`, as in Sanitize.
- Fail-closed: a structure element written in place that tags a removed annotation, or a tree too large to walk, makes `apply` return `RedactError::Tags`. The caller keeps the previous document.
- The references dropped are counted in `Report::tags`.

Sanitize's private `listed` closure is now the shared `listed_annotations` helper, so both paths use one copy.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed: `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` (82 passed, 1 ignored; the ignored one was already ignored, a manual timing probe)
- [x] `cargo xtask layers` (no violations), `cargo xtask assets` (ok), `cargo xtask parity`

**New tests** (`crates/redact/src/tests.rs`):
- `applied_redactions_drop_structure_tree_references_to_what_they_remove`: a tagged two-page PDF with a comment and a text field under a mark, both tagged with OBJRs. The field has a second widget on page 2, and a comment outside the mark acts as a control. After `apply` and a full save without object stre…

title: M2: respect column reading order in normal text selection and copying
author: lorebotta
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3682. Normal mouse selection now follows complete prose columns, including aligned paragraph breaks, while preserving justified text, hanging lists, form label/value pairs and sparse table rows.

The supplied magazine's PDF page 12 (printed page 10) has correctly positioned glyphs painted in column order. The shared `PageText` reconstructor erases narrow gutters before mouse selection runs: consecutive glyph grouping permits gaps below three glyph heights, and same-baseline merging permits gaps below 1.2 heights. Some gutters are below 11.25 pt for 9.375 pt glyphs. The UI then selects a contiguous range of that incorrect order. Lowering one merging threshold cannot fix both paths.

The renderer now partitions whitespace regions before either join, then uses the existing line reconstructor inside each leaf. Original glyph quads and direction handling remain in place. Selection, highlighting, clipboard, search and headless extraction consume the same corrected order; no special selection mode or keyboard shortcut is required.

The contributor's review correctly exposed false gutters in the earlier implementation. This revision addresses all four reported families:

- Column cuts require adjacent, substantially filled prose lines on both sides; a run of aligned whitespace alone is insufficient. Supported vertical gutters still take priority over aligned paragraph gaps. A retained subdivision tree reunites adjacent column bands under spanning headings and above footers; intervening headings and proven table rows remain barriers. Overlapping empty corridors establish continuity without a paragraph-gap threshold.
- A single local word-space advance protects larger-font headings from a body-gutter cut, even when body spaces dominate the median.
- Measured explicit-space advances include `Tw`; text-show provenance estimates implicit spaces in justified `TJ` text. Separate string boundaries prevent trailing spaces from borrowing the next column's…

title: Redaction: a pattern nothing paints with any more leaves the page
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3647.

A tiling pattern's cell is a content stream of its own and can draw anything, text included. Redacting a shape filled with such a pattern removed the fill from the page's content — the page looked right, a black box — but left the pattern in `/Resources /Pattern`, and its cell, with the text that was under the mark, went into the saved file unchanged.

### The approach

This pass does not enter pattern cells, so it cannot redact inside one. What it can do is notice that **nothing paints with the pattern any more**:

- the graphics state carries the fill and stroke pattern a `scn` / `SCN` selected, and `cs`/`CS` with another space, `g`/`rg`/`k` and `G`/`RG`/`K` clear it — so `q`/`Q` save and restore it with everything else;
- every painting operator that survives the rewrite records the pattern it drew with, in all three paths (kept whole, clipped-and-painted, or re-emitted clipped);
- a pattern the page selected but no surviving paint used leaves the page's resources.

`Report` gains `patterns_removed`.

### Measured

The report's file — one box filled from a pattern whose cell draws `SECRET`, the box marked:

```
before   applied: 1, (SECRET) in the saved bytes, /Pattern still on the page
after    applied: 1, no /Pattern on the page, (SECRET) gone
```

### The case that matters more than the fix

Two boxes filled from **one** pattern, only the first marked: `patterns_removed` is 0 and the page keeps the entry. The second box still paints the pattern, so its cell — and the word in it — must stay; it is still on the page for a reader to see. Dropping the resource there would have left a box selecting a pattern that no longer exists.

Both cases are in the test, because the second is the one a careless version of this change breaks.

A note on verifying it yourself: byte-grepping the saved file for `/Pattern` is misleading, because the *pattern object's own* `/Resources` matches too. I lost a few minutes to that before probing the prune directly — the te…

title: M2: text extraction keeps doubled letters in text condensed to 20 Tz and below (#2457)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2457 (a regression of #1467).

Text extraction drops a glyph as a "fake bold" redraw when one of the four glyphs before it has the same text and a left edge closer than `dx`. Since #1474 the threshold has been `dx = min(0.2·h, 0.5·w)`, except for glyphs narrower than 5 % of their height, which fell back to `0.2·h`. OCR text layers squeeze each word into its box down to `Tz` 20 and below, where an `l` or `i` is under that 5 %. That fallback then made `dx` a fifth of the line height, so real letters were dropped:

| Tz | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 100, 50, 30 | Hallo Mitte Wille Kommission Illustration still Brunnen Kaffee | (same) |
| 20 | Halo Mitte Wile Kommission Ilustration stil Brunnen Kaffee | Hallo Mitte Wille Kommission Illustration still Brunnen Kaffee |
| 10 | Halo Mite Wile Kommisson Ilustraion stil Brunnen Kafee | Hallo Mitte Wille Kommission Illustration still Brunnen Kaffee |
| 5 | Halo Mite Wile Komison Ilustraion stil Brune Kafe | Hallo Mitte Wille Kommission Illustration still Brunnen Kaffee |

The fix takes the direction suggested in the issue. Every glyph with a positive width is matched within half of that width. Only zero-width marks, such as combining accents, keep the height-based distance. Those marks are the case the 5 % rule existed for, and `fake_bold_duplicates_are_removed` covers them.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings`: `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] tests: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render` (313 lib tests pass, including `fake_bold_duplicates_are_removed` and `condensed_double_letters_are_kept`)
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`

**New test:** `ocr_condensed_double_letters_are_kept` lays out the issue's words with Helvetica advances at 20, 10 and 5 % horizontal scaling. It checks three things:
- each word comes out whole;

- each letter redrawn a quarter of its wid…

title: fix: draw a wide interpolated source shrunk by nearest, not skipped
author: WhatSupQuebec
body:
## What this changes

A source **wider than the 2^20-pixel resampling side cap** drawn with `/Interpolate true` was refused by the smooth sizing and then retained at its original resolution — which a `u16` pixmap side cannot hold — so the image was **dropped** and the page drew without it. A refused smooth sizing now **retries with nearest-neighbour sizing** before the original-resolution fallback, so the image is shrunk and drawn.

The nearest-sized image is not snapped and takes the nearest premultiplied path, and an interpolated Type 3 glyph image is not promoted to bicubic after the fallback.

## Scope reduction (was: smooth image minification)

This PR originally fixed scanned text made illegible by nearest-neighbour minification. The M2 series merged in `main` ([ff227b77](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/commit/ff227b77) and follow-ups) now covers that with area averaging, so the minification part of this PR was dropped. What M2 does **not** cover — verified by running this PR's regression tests against `main` — is the wide interpolated source: `wide_interpolated_sources_fall_back_to_nearest_after_shrinking` **failed on `main`** (image dropped, page white) and passes with this fix. This PR now carries only that fix: the sizing retry in `draw_image`, its regression test, and the `vendor/README.md` patch-row mention.

## How you verified it

- [x] The regression test fails on `main` (`60f60fc0`) and passes here

title: fix(a11y): resolve /MarkInfo /Marked when it is an indirect reference (#3671)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3671.

`/MarkInfo << /Marked 8 0 R >>` with `8 0 obj true` is a tagged PDF, but both readers of the flag called `as_bool` on the raw object, so an indirect reference read as "not a boolean" and fell back to `false`.

Measured on the reporter's fixture pair (`/Marked true` vs `/Marked 8 0 R`):

```
before   direct: tagged true    indirect: tagged false
after    direct: tagged true    indirect: tagged true
```

**Two independent sites had the same omission**, so fixing one would have left `doc_info` and the checker disagreeing about the same file:

- `crates/render/src/inspect.rs` — `doc_info`'s `tagged`;
- `crates/a11y/src/content.rs` — `Rule::TaggedPdf`, which also emitted "The document isn't marked as tagged (MarkInfo Marked)" for the indirect file.

Both now resolve the value before reading it. `/MarkInfo` itself was already resolved at both sites; only the flag inside it wasn't.

The test `marked_as_an_indirect_reference_still_counts_as_tagged` asserts all three cases: indirect passes, direct still passes, and **a document with no flag at all still fails** — so the fix can't quietly turn the rule into one that always passes. Negative control, with the resolve removed: `left: Failed, right: Passed`.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed (44 a11y and 62 render tests).

title: M2: text extraction and Find apply /ActualText given on structure elements (#3660)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Part of #3660: text extraction, Find and search-redaction. Word/HTML export is still to do; see below.

Replacement text (`/ActualText`) can be given on a **structure element** as well as on marked content (ISO 32000-2 §14.9.4). PdfCraft applied only the marked-content form. So an OCR layer whose misread words are corrected in its tags read as the misread words, and was found by them. With the issue's repro, before and after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `text_extract` / `pdfcraft-cli text` | Availal;!e 24/7, you c;m book an appointroP.nt online. | Available 24/7, you can book an appointment online. |
| `text_find` "appointment" | 0 | 1 |
| `text_find` "appointroP" | 1 | 0 |

**How it works:**
- **Lookup** (`crates/render/src/text/replacements.rs`): for a page with `/StructParents`, the page's entry in the structure tree's `ParentTree` gives the element owning each MCID of the page's content (§14.7.5.4). Each element is followed up `/P` to the outermost ancestor with `/ActualText`; an outer replacement covers everything inside it, as nested marked content already does. The lookup is bounded:
  - parent-tree nodes are capped, with a seen-set for `/Kids` cycles;
  - an ancestor chain longer than 256 elements gets no replacement;
  - each element's answer is memoised per page, and the number of elements resolved per page is capped;
  - replacement text is capped at 16 MiB per page.

  A cycle, a missing tree or a lookup past a bound gives no replacement, so the content keeps its own text.
- **`TextDevice`:** holds each element's sequences until the page ends (`place_held`). It then reuses the existing `/ActualText` machinery: merge and redraw dedupe.
  - The element's text replaces its sequences only when **one glyph can cover all of them and nothing else**: the same line and writing direction, adjoining (no other glyph drawn between them), and nothing a word-count filter excludes. That glyph is boxed around all of them, so a Find match, …

title: M3: let Escape close an open menu before it clears the selection (#3535)
author: hazeliscoding
body:

title: fix(a11y): read the document title from the XMP metadata, not only /Info (#3672)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3672.

PDF 2.0 deprecates the document information dictionary for everything but `CreationDate` and `ModDate` (ISO 32000-2 §14.3.3), so a PDF 2.0 file states its title in its metadata stream as `dc:title` and may carry no `/Info` at all. Every PDF/UA-2 file is of that shape. Both readers of the title looked at `/Info` alone.

Measured on the reporter's fixture pair, and on a veraPDF corpus pass file the issue names, whose `/Info` holds an `/Author` and a `/Producer` but **no `/Title`**:

```
before   title_info.pdf: "Quarterly report"   title_xmp.pdf: null
         PDF_UA-1/7.1 General/7.1-t01-pass-a.pdf: null, Title rule failed
after    title_info.pdf: "Quarterly report"   title_xmp.pdf: "Quarterly report"
         PDF_UA-1/7.1 General/7.1-t01-pass-a.pdf: "7.1-t01-pass-a", Title rule passed
```

### One reader, two call sites

The new `pdfcraft-cos::xmp` reads a simple property out of a packet, so `doc_info` and the checker cannot disagree about one file — which is exactly what happened for the tagged flag in #3671. It is text-only, like `page_labels`: no object graph, no XML library. The editing side stays in `pdfcraft-organize`, which must preserve the rest of a packet byte for byte; this only scans.

A property may be written as an element, an attribute (RDF shorthand), a language alternative or an ordered array. An alternative answers with its `x-default`, which is what a viewer shows, and falls back to the first language when the packet names none — the corpus file above says only `xml:lang="en-US"`, so without that fallback it would still read as untitled. An ordered array answers with its items joined, as Document Properties lists several authors.

### Precedence, and the other five entries

The packet wins over `/Info`. That is the order a viewer reads them in and the order Document Properties already writes them in (`crates/organize/src/xmp.rs`: "viewers that read XMP first show the packet's value"). A property stated but left **empty** is no value,…

title: Select All takes the whole document's text while scrolling continuously (fixes #2639)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #2639.

**Edit ▸ Select All (⌘A) now takes the whole document's text while scrolling continuously**, as the issue asks: copying out a multi-page document no longer needs a Select All and a Copy per page. One page at a time it still selects the page shown, as does a one-page document.

- `DocView::all_text`: set by Select All when `continuous` and the document has more than one page. Pages on screen highlight their whole text as their text layer arrives. A press anywhere on a page (any tool, text read or not), Escape, switching to one page at a time, a page selection or an edit ends it.
- **Copy** checks the document's copying permission first. Pages whose text was read for display are taken from it; the others are read on a worker thread (`DocumentCopy`, in place on the web, which has no threads), keeping only each page's text as it goes, and the clipboard gets the whole text, in page order, on a later frame. A new copy or the document closing cancels it. The text queue isn't widened to every page: far pages' text is let go to bound memory, so requesting all of them would just churn.
- `select_all()` still returns whether text is selected (callers and tests poll it until a page's text is known).

title: RTL/Arabic text: bidirectional layout (UAX #9) in vendored epaint + editing existing RTL text
author: zaidshurbaji
body:
## What this changes

Makes **right-to-left (Arabic / Hebrew) text display and editing** work. Before this, RTL text
rendered with its runs reversed, letters showed disconnected, edits were refused, and edited boxes
could not be moved.

1. **Bidirectional layout in the vendored `epaint`** (UAX #9). epaint 0.36 shapes Arabic/Hebrew
   within a run but lays runs out in logical order, and its cursor model assumes glyph index ==
   logical char index with monotonic x. This patch:
   - records each shaped glyph's logical byte (`Paragraph::glyph_bytes`);
   - fixes an RTL glyph-duplication bug (the shaper returns RTL runs in visual order, so
     `layout_shaped_run` now iterates them in reverse logical order, emitting exactly one
     continuation glyph per character);
   - adds `bidi_reorder_row` (via the `unicode-bidi` crate) to reorder each visual line for RTL and
     mixed direction, keeping glyphs in logical order with visual `pos.x`;
   - makes `Row::char_at` / `x_offset` direction-aware for caret and hit-testing.
   It engages **only on lines containing an RTL character**, so LTR/CJK layout is byte-identical to
   upstream. It is gated and self-contained, and is intended to be proposed to epaint upstream.

2. **Applying edits to existing RTL text** (`crates/edit`). When the PDF only embeds a subset that
   cannot draw a complex run, `shape_source` falls back to a bundled craft-fonts script face
   (Arabic/Hebrew/Thai); the variable fallback faces are flattened to a static instance
   (`embedding::static_instance`) so they embed; and a mixed contextual/bidi row is unified onto one
   shaping face instead of being refused.

3. **Inline editor joining** (`crates/ui-egui`): Arabic runs are displayed with the bundled shaping
   face so letters join while typing, instead of the GSUB-less subset's isolated forms.

title: Edit text: keep a line together across subsets of the same font (#3661)
author: amanmprojects
body:
## What this changes Fixes #3661. PDF writers split one font into several subsets, each a font resource of its own with its own six-letter tag. Microsoft Word draws a word through several of them: `Two-line` can be `/F1 (Two) /F2 (-l) /F1 (ine)` with both resources Helvetica-Bold. `text_lines` ended a line wherever the resource name changed, so Edit text showed three lines and Word/HTML export wrote three paragraphs (out of order when the subsets' boxes differ by a fraction of a point). With the issue's repro: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | `text_lines` page 1 | `["Two", "-l", "ine heading"]` (3 lines) | `["Two-line heading"]` (1 line) | | HTML export | three headings | one `

Two-line heading

` | The heading is still `

title: M6: calculation order: read, check, fix and set the order fields calculate in
author: Piohrun
body:
**Builds on #3550,** which is approved. Its first two commits are #3550's (renaming a field renames it in the formulas that read it); please review the last one, "calculation order: read, check, fix and set". Once #3550 merges I'll rebase this onto `main` and the diff will shrink to that commit.

This is the engine half of the calculation order, split out of the original #3708 on review: the page that shows the order in the app is #3733, stacked on this one.

## What this changes

A form's calculations run in its calculation order (`/CO`, ISO 32000-2 §12.7.3), but PdfCraft had no way to see or change that order. A field joins the end of `/CO` when it gets a calculation, so a chain defined in the wrong order (total before subtotal) shows stale numbers, and nothing said why. Acrobat has an order dialog (Prepare Form ▸ Set Field Calculation Order, with Up and Down). This adds the order, its checks and a fix, headlessly; #3733 puts them in the app.

**`form_calculation_order`** (new tool): without a change it reads the order, with each field's `reads`, `issues` (`runs_too_early`, `cycle`, `not_in_order`) and `listed`, the `extra` entries, and `fixable`. One change at a time: `order` (these first, the rest after them in their order), `field` + `move` earlier|later, or `fix: true` (only what must move moves). Every change is one undo step, labelled "Set calculation order", and the form recalculates in the new order, as after a script edit.

**Changes to existing behaviour:**
- **Editing a formula keeps its field's place in the order.** Before, every change to a calculation moved the field to the end of `/CO`, which would undo an order set by hand. A field that gets a calculation still joins the end, and one that loses it still leaves. (Field Properties sends a calculation only when it changed, so in the app this happened whenever a formula was edited.)
- A field `/CO` lists twice recalculates once, not twice.
- Recalculation runs each field by its object, not by name: of …

title: fix(sign): embed the issuers of macOS Keychain identities
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

Before: a signature made with a macOS Keychain identity embedded only the signer's certificate (`keychain.rs` returned `chain: Vec::new()`). A validator that doesn't already hold the intermediates, such as Acrobat or PdfCraft on another machine, couldn't build the path to the root.

After: `keychain::find` fills `chain` with the certificates macOS chains the identity to, the same way `windows::find` already does for the Windows certificate store, so the signature embeds them as it does for a `.p12`.

How: `SecTrust` with the basic X.509 policy and network fetch turned off is evaluated (the result is ignored, the chain is built anyway), and every certificate but the signer's is kept. It is best effort: a certificate macOS can't chain still signs. The chain is read with `certificate_count`/`certificate_at_index` because `SecTrust::chain` needs macOS 12 and the app targets macOS 11.

`crates/sign/tests/data/chain-legacy.p12` is `chain.p12` re-exported with `-legacy`, the format `security import` accepts (README updated with the command).

title: Return empty WordNum result when cents rounding carries to 1e12
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

`WordNum(…, 2)` in FormCalc printed `Ten Hundred Billion` when cents rounding carried the whole part to exactly 1e12.

**Cause:** `word_num` accepts n < 1e12, but with cents enabled it rounds n*100 and derives the whole part from that. For values like 999999999999.999, the rounding carries the whole part to 1e12. The group table stops at Billion, so 1000 goes to `words_below_1000`, and the output is `Ten Hundred Billion Dollars And 00 Cents`.

**Fix:** After computing the whole part, `word_num` returns an empty string if it is at least 1e12. This matches the existing guard at the top of the function for out-of-range input.

Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2024-2050 (word_num)`. No existing issue.

title: Keep zero annotation flags through XFDF export/import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

XFDF export then import turns an annotation with no flags into a printing one. Found while testing `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs:313-317 (xfdf_annots)` and `:~1010 (annot_from_xml, `unwrap_or("print")`)`. No existing issue.

**Cause:** XFDF export only wrote a `flags` attribute when at least one /F bit was set, so an annotation with /F = 0 got no attribute. Import treats a missing `flags` attribute as `print`, so the annotation came back with /F = 4 (Print).

**Fix:** Export now always writes the `flags` attribute, using an empty `flags=""` when /F is 0. Import already parses an empty value as 0, so the round trip keeps /F at 0.

title: fix(render): hit-test selection against the glyph quad, not its bounding box (#3693)
author: MatrixMagician
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3693.

`PageText::nearest` measured the distance from the pointer to each glyph's axis-aligned bounding box. In sheared (synthetic italic) or turned text that box is wider than the glyph and overlaps its neighbours, so a pointer on a letter was also inside the box of the letter before it, at distance 0, and the earlier glyph won. A drag ending on the last letter of a word or line then ended one or two letters short, and Copy missed it.

Now a glyph whose drawn em box (`quad`) holds the point wins, the one with the nearest centre if several do. If no quad holds the point, the bounding-box distance still decides, so pointers past a line end or between lines behave as before; a tie there goes to the nearer glyph centre rather than the first glyph. Upright and 90° text are unaffected.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

**Tests.** `nearest_finds_the_glyph_under_the_pointer_in_sheared_and_turned_text` builds the em-box quads a text matrix would produce (upright, shear 0.35, turned 45°, with narrow letters as in the issue), checks every glyph centre resolves to its own glyph, and checks pointers past either end of the line pick the end glyph. I checked that it fails without the fix (on the sheared line the "i" resolves to the glyph before it) and passes with it. `a_degenerate_or_nan_quad_holds_no_point` covers the new helper.

title: fix(text): character spacing is not a word gap in Chinese (#3713)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3713.

A label spread to the width of a longer one (分散對齊, as on Taiwanese forms and 公文) is one show with character spacing, so **every gap inside it is the same**, while the value beside it has none. The line's typical gap is therefore the value's zero, and from half a line height upwards each of the label's gaps read as a word gap.

Measured on the reporter's fixture, all nine `Tc` steps:

```
before   Tc 0.1 – 0.4 em   受文者如正本
         Tc 0.5 – 1.0 em   受 文 者 如正本        text_find 受文者: 6 of 9 lines
after    every step        受文者如正本           text_find 受文者: 9 of 9 lines
```

### Why repetition, and not width

`Tc` is added after every glyph of a string (ISO 32000-2 §9.3.2), so spread text repeats one gap. A gap that repeats between consecutive CJK characters is therefore spacing **at any width**, and a gap that stands on its own is read as spacing only below one line height (it was half of one).

Width alone cannot tell the two apart: two cells of a row two character widths apart look exactly like two characters spread by two ems. The run structure would tell them apart, but it isn't in the glyph list — `TextGlyph` carries text, box, quad and direction, and the "runs" in `arrange` are geometric groupings, not shows — so the repetition is what is left to measure.

### What this keeps, and what it gives up

Measured on a fixture of the same shape (`姓名` and `王小明` on one line):

| gap between two cells | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 20 character widths | two segments: `姓名` / `王小明` | unchanged |
| 2 character widths | `姓名 王小明` | `姓名 王小明` |

So a row's cells keep their space, and a column gap wider than about three line heights was already a separate segment.

What it gives up is a row of **evenly spaced single characters**, whose gaps repeat like a spread label's and so now join. Taking word gaps from the content's own space characters on a tagged page — the report's second direction, which §14.8.2.6.2 NOTE 1 invites — would settle that case properly, and is a …

title: Redact: count shared outline items once so the walk ends
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

Counting the bookmarks of a hostile outline no longer takes unbounded time. The count behind the bookmarks category (used by Remove Hidden Information, Sanitize and the scan report) followed `/First` and `/Next` with no record of what it had visited, so an outline whose items share children was walked along every path: 60 levels of two shared items is about 2^60 steps and the count never returned. The scan runs the count before anything is removed, so Remove Hidden Information and Sanitize hung on such a file too.

`outline_len` in `crates/redact/src/sanitize.rs` now keeps the set of items it has reached. An item that two others name is counted once, and a level stops at an item that was already counted. A total budget of 100,000 items bounds the count. The per-level cap and the depth limit of 64 are unchanged. Ordinary outlines count exactly as before. Removing the outline itself does not walk it, so the count is the only walk that needed bounding.

title: Give a redacted or sanitized copy a new file identifier
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes







A redacted or sanitized copy no longer keeps the `/ID` of the file it came from. Applying redactions and running Sanitize now make the saved copy write a fresh trailer `/ID` pair. Before, the previous revision was dropped, but the identifier still linked the copy to its original.







This is a design choice, not something the specification requires: ISO 32000-2 (section 14.4) defines `/ID[0]` as a permanent identifier that survives incremental updates of the same document. A redacted or sanitized copy is a new document derived from the original, so this PR gives it new strings in both positions. If you would rather keep `/ID[0]` and change only `/ID[1]`, that is a one-line change; tell me which you prefer.







- `pdfcraft-cos`: `Document::require_full_save_with_new_id()` and `Document::new_id_required()`. A flagged full save regenerates both `/ID` strings. An encrypted file keeps `/ID[0]`, which its file key is derived from (the empty string when the file had no usable first entry), and gets a new `/ID[1]`. `SaveOptions` gains `id_entropy: Option<[u8; 16]>`: when it is given, the new identifier depends only on that entropy and the written bytes, so tests can pin output.



- `pdfcraft-redact`: `apply` and `sanitize()` request the new identifier. `sanitize()` does so whether or not it removed anything.



- Ordinary saves are unchanged. They write the same bytes as before (checked below).







Deliberately not changed: `remove_hidden`, the per-category removal used by the remove-hidden edit and by the optimizer's discard option, still keeps the identifier. No engine, automation,…

title: M2: structure /ActualText reaches form XObjects with their own /StructParents (#3732)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
> **Stacked on #3689.** This changes the vendor patch (53) that #3689 adds, so the branch is built on top of it. Until #3689 merges, this PR also shows its nine commits. **Review only the last commit, 17a4cff3.** I'll rebase onto `main` once #3689 lands.

## What this changes

Fixes #3732 (follow-up to #3660 / #3689, from @mtlcl410's test report).

A form XObject that has its own `/StructParents` is structured content (ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.4). Its MCIDs index the structural parent tree under that key, the same way the page's MCIDs index the entry under the page's key. #3689 only applied structure-element `/ActualText` to the page's own content (nesting depth 0), so a paragraph in a tagged form still read its glyphs (`f0rm`, not `form`). Tagged generators often put whole paragraphs in forms.

- **vendor/hayro-interpret, patch (53):** the depth-0 test is replaced by a parent tree key carried in `Context`.
  - `interpret_page` enters structured content under the page's `/StructParents`.
  - `draw_form_xobject` gives a form its own `/StructParents` while it is drawn from structured content, or no key when it has none. Annotation appearances and forms inside forms are included.
  - Soft masks, patterns and Type 3 glyphs build fresh contexts that are never structured, so what they draw stays outside.
  - The hook is now `Device::structure_marked_content(key, mcid)` (was `page_marked_content(mcid)`).
- **crates/render/src/text/replacements.rs:** replacements are resolved lazily, one key at a time, as the content reaches it. Elements, texts and all budgets are shared over the page. There is a new page-wide budget for parent tree reads (nodes, `/Nums` pairs, `/Kids` and MCID items), so a page drawing many keyed forms can't make it reread a large tree once per form.
- A page whose own content has no marked content needs no `/StructParents`. The forms it draws are structured all the same.

Combine Files always added a top-level bookmark per file, with the file's own bookmarks nested under it. Users who don't want those had to remove them afterwards with Remove Hidden Information (#3679).

title: fix: terminate inline images at their known data length
author: WhatSupQuebec
body:
## What this changes

An inline image whose dictionary states its data length now ends at exactly that many bytes. A `/L` (or `/Length`, PDF 2.0 Table 91) states the encoded length outright — filtered images included; otherwise an uncompressed image's length is computed from `/W`, `/H`, `/BPC` and `/CS` (full key names included, and an image mask's optional `/BPC` defaulting to 1 per Table 87). An `EI` found strictly inside that many bytes is part of a binary scan and is skipped; the `EI` at the exact end (one whitespace byte aside) is accepted without the look-ahead heuristics, which binary content after the image can fool. Filtered images without `/L` and unknown colour spaces keep the existing heuristics, and the length arithmetic is checked.

This was split out of #3683 at review request: it changes how every content stream's inline images are parsed, so it deserves its own description and review.

Opening the Print dialog reset the printer to the system default every time (`open_print` set `printer: default, printer_picked: false`), while copies, range, paper and the rest carried over from the last print through `..keep`. So "Save as PDF" or a non-default printer had to be picked again for every print in the same session, which is what the reporter describes.

Now:
- `open_print` keeps the printer picked last time, Save as PDF included, while it is still in the list.
- `poll_print`: when the fresh printer list arrives without the picked printer (unplugged, removed), the dialog falls back to the system default rather than keeping a printer that isn't there.

This is within a session, which is what the issue asks for. Remembering the printer across restarts is part of #3434 and is not in this PR.

Fixes #3537

title: Refuse an OCR batch whose inputs would write one output file
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

Two inputs to the batch OCR tool `ocr_recognize_files` that would write the same output file no longer overwrite each other. Before, each input's searchable copy went into the output folder under its own file name, so `one/scan.pdf` and `two/scan.pdf` both wrote `out/scan.pdf`. The second copy replaced the first while both results reported success.

Now the whole batch is refused before anything happens: the output folder is not created, no input is read, and the OCR engines are not loaded. The error names the colliding file names and says what to do. A request without collisions runs exactly as before.

Names are compared the way the default filesystem compares them: without regard to case on Windows and macOS (`scan.pdf` and `Scan.PDF` are one file there), exactly elsewhere, and on Windows a trailing dot or space is not part of a name (`scan.pdf.` is `scan.pdf`). The compared name is the one the output is written under, after the separator replacement the writer already applies. The tool description says so.

Not changed here: the batch dialog in the desktop app writes its outputs the same way (`crates/ui-egui/src/ocr_ui.rs`, `ocr_files_into`). It needs its own change.

Windows x64 (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` toolchain), on the final branch:

title: M14: keep Chinese document names readable in English interfaces
author: zhanglongqi
body:
## What this changes

Chinese document names could display missing glyphs in an English or other non-Chinese desktop interface when the build has no embedded Chinese fonts. Add an installed Han fallback to the default interface font stacks while retaining the general fallback for Arabic and other scripts.

title: M9: empty signature fields show a Sign tab, sized to the field
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

Each empty signature field a click would sign now carries a small **Sign** tab in its top-left corner, so whoever has to sign can see where. On `main`, clicking an empty signature field already starts signing for it, but nothing marks the field. It looks like any other box, and a field without a drawn appearance isn't visible at all until fields are highlighted.

- **Which fields.** The fields a click would sign: an unsigned, visible field on this page, with a rectangle that passes the screen-space guard the validation badges already use. The document must allow filling (`allows_form_filling`, the check `forms_ui::page_input` makes). The form field of that name must be a signature field that isn't read-only, with a shown widget at that rectangle.
- **When.** With the Select tool, and not while preparing a form: the same condition as the field hit test, so the tab only appears where a click signs.
- **Look.** A chip in the theme's accent color with the Lucide `signature` icon and "Sign" in white, the way the app's primary buttons are drawn. The label is `tl!("Sign")`, which every catalog already translates, so no catalog changes.
- **Size.** The tab is sized to its field: 0.4 of the field's height on screen, from 10 to 18 pt. The inset, icon, padding, label and corners scale with it. It shows "Sign" from 14 pt up, when the whole tab fits in half the field's width, and the icon alone otherwise. A field too small for the 10 pt icon chip, or one whose rectangle isn't finite, gets no tab.
- **Click.** Over the tab the pointer turns into a hand, and a click opens signing for that field. The tab is drawn over every field, so a click on it goes to its own field, even where another field overlaps it and comes first in the form (which takes the click everywhere else). Where tabs overlap, the one painted last (on top) takes the click. A field that straddles the page's edge gets its tab in the part on the page, since fields take clicks on the page only, or…

title: fix(ui): a metadata-only change on disk is not a new version (#3755)
author: kekeandzeyu
body:
## What this changes

Fixes the false-positive half of #3755: on macOS, saving a document makes PdfCraft report a few moments later that the file "changed on disk". When the document had no unsaved changes, it also reloads silently, which drops the undo history.

**Cause.** Since #2218, `file_watch::Stamp` on Unix includes the change time (`ctime`/`ctime_nsec`). That is deliberate: it catches a rebuild that keeps the length and mtime. Shortly after PdfCraft writes a file, macOS adds extended attributes to it (`com.apple.macl`, `com.apple.provenance`, …). That moves the ctime and leaves the bytes alone. Both stamp comparisons then take it for a new version:
- the watcher (`file_changed`) reloads a clean document, losing undo, or shows the "changed on disk" notice on a dirty one;
- Save (`disk_differs`) shows the "file changed, overwrite?" dialog.

**Fix.** `ctime` stays in the stamp, so #2218's detection is unchanged. A changed stamp is now a hint, confirmed against the content before anything happens:
- `file_changed`: the watcher has already read the new bytes. If they equal `Document::saved_bytes()` (the file the document came from), the stamp is recorded in `known` and `basis`, and nothing else happens: no reload, no notice, and the next Save doesn't ask.
- `disk_differs`: when the stamp differs, the new `holds()` compares the file with `saved_bytes()`. A different length means a different version with no read. Same length means one read and a byte comparison. Equal bytes are not a conflict. A file that can't be read still counts as a difference, so Save still asks.

A real external rewrite still reloads or asks as before, including one that keeps the length (covered by a test).

**Not in this PR:** keeping the undo history across a *real* external change. A reload replaces the whole document, and that needs a separate design discussion (the bot suggested splitting the issue).

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-e…

title: fix(render): an isolated DeviceCMYK transparency group blends in CMYK (#3776)
author: jpeskov
body: ## What this changes Fixes #3776. Refs #2145 (Ghent PDF Output Suite 5.0, patch 16.2). The elements of an **isolated** transparency group whose colour space is `DeviceCMYK` now blend in CMYK, as ISO 32000-2 requires. Before this change, PdfCraft converted each colour to RGB and blended in RGB. Ghent patch 16.2 then showed an X in almost every cell. Now no clear X shows. Three cells keep a faint X (see "How you verified it"). *Top: `main`. Bottom: this PR. The fixture is the script from #3776.* **The rules.** Blending occurs in the group's colour space (§11.3.4). For a subtractive space, each component is complemented before the blend function and complemented again after it. For the nonseparable modes, C, M and Y blend as their complements R, G and B, and K is not blended (§11.3.5.3). K comes from the backdrop for Hue, Saturation and Color, and from the source for Luminosity. **The method.** An isolated group starts from a transparent backdrop of its own (§11.4.7). Thus the renderer can calculate its contents apart from the page. Two vendored patches do this: - **hayro-interpret patch (45)** - `CmykGroup` records the group at `Do`: the state after `/Matrix`, the root transform and the interpreter cache. It is similar to `SoftMask`. - `Device::draw_isolated_cmyk_group` is a new device hook. Its default returns `false`, so other devices do not change. - `draw_form_xobject` sends a group to the hook when the group is isolated, is not knockout, has `/CS /DeviceCMYK` and has a layer of its own. When the hook returns `false`, the contents are drawn as before, through `interpret_form_contents` (now a function of its own). - `Color::ink_tints` gives the process tints of a colour: `DeviceCMYK` as it is, and `DeviceGray` as black only (§10.4.2.2)…

title: M6: XFA calculations rerun only when what they read changed
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

After any change (a typed value, a click, a field's change script), PdfCraft reran every calculate script in an XFA form, in document order. Another viewer reruns only the calculations whose inputs changed. The difference shows on real forms: when a form carries a hidden second copy of a section whose calculation writes the visible copy's field, rerunning everything lets the hidden copy write last.

- **Reads are recorded.** Each script run reports the fields and exclusion groups whose value it read, once each, capped at 4,096 per run (`XfaOutcome::reads` and `reads_cut`). That covers `rawValue`, `value`, `formattedValue`, `isNull` and a field's text through `toString`/`valueOf`. In FormCalc it covers references, function arguments and `isNull`. Writes and other properties (presence, access) are not reads.
- **The engine keeps them per document** (`CalcDeps`): what each calculation read when it last ran, with a reverse index from fields to the calculations that read them.
- **What runs after a change:**
  - the calculations that read the changed field, or any field bound to the same data node;
  - the field's own calculation, when anything else wrote it;
  - any calculation that has never run (a new row's).

  These run round after round, in document order, until nothing is due. A user's or script's write wakes the readers even when the value is the same. A calculation's own write wakes them only when it changed the value, so calculations that agree don't keep waking each other.
- **Still every calculation:** opening, a reset, `xfa.form.recalculate()`, added or removed rows, and imported data, as on `main`.
- **Undo, redo and revert** give the document a fresh record, so the next change runs every calculation once and learns again. An edit that runs the form's scripts works on a copy of the record and keeps it only when it succeeds; an edit that runs none copies nothing. When opening can't keep what its scripts changed, it drops what they read …

title: Fill & Sign marks stay upright on rotated pages (#2392)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fill & Sign marks (check, cross, dot, line) on a page with `/Rotate` were drawn in the page's own axes. Typed text and rubber stamps already record the page rotation (`PCTextRotate`, `PCStampRotate`) and draw upright in their displayed box; marks did neither. On a page turned 180° the checkmark came out upside down (the report: scanned pages are often stored that way), and on 90°/270° it lay on its side and a line stood on end. The cross and dot only looked right because they are symmetric.

Reproduced with `pdfcraft-cli` on `main`: a checkmark and typed text on blank pages turned 0/90/180/270. The text was upright on all four; the checkmark rendered as ✓, ‹, ^, ›.

- **`annot` / `lib.rs`:** `Shape::Mark` records `PCStampRotate` on a turned page (marks are `/Stamp` annotations, like the rubber stamps that already use it).
- **`annot` / `appearance.rs`:** the turned-box and `/Matrix` code the rubber stamps had is moved ahead of the stamp `match` and shared, so marks are drawn upright in their displayed box and mapped into `/Rect` the same way. Unturned marks are drawn exactly as before.
- **`FillMark::rect_at(at, rotation)`:** the mark's box, sized in displayed axes (a line is 36 × 4 pt *as displayed*). It replaces two copies of the size arithmetic in the Fill & Sign tool (`ui-egui/src/fill_sign.rs`) and `fill_sign_add` (`automation/src/comments.rs`), which both sized the box in the page's own axes.

Marks placed before this keep their old appearance (no rotation was recorded for them).

On the comment that a **date** stamp is also upside down: dates are Fill & Sign *text*, which already carries `PCTextRotate`; in the reproduction above typed text was upright on every rotation, so this PR doesn't change it.

Fixes #2392

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-annot -p pdfcraft-engine -p pdfcraft-automation -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-annot` (45), …

title: M6: XFA formattedValue shows a date in the field's display picture
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

In XFA scripts, a date field's `formattedValue` now gives the value as the field's display picture (`<format><picture>`) shows it, as another viewer does. On `main` it gave the raw value, the ISO date, so a script doing date arithmetic on `formattedValue` read `2026-10-20` where it expected `20261020`.

- **The template keeps the display picture.** `Field::display_picture` is parsed from `<format><picture>`, apart from the edit picture (`<ui>…<picture>`).
- **`formatted_value(picture, raw)`** shows an ISO date in a `date{…}` picture, using the first of several alternatives (`date{YYYYMMDD}` turns `2026-10-20` into `20261020`). It reuses `date_pattern` and `iso_to_pattern`. It returns `None`, so the raw value stands, for:
  - other kinds of picture (`num`, `text`, `time`);
  - a clause it can't read;
  - a value that isn't an ISO date.
- **The script snapshot carries it.** The live form keeps each field's display picture, and the engine works out the formatted text when it builds the snapshot, so a value refreshed in place is never shown stale.
- **JavaScript and FormCalc** read `formattedValue` from it. A script that sets the value in the same run then reads the raw value, since the formatted text it started with is out of date.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. Its "10b TO" calculation adds the days requested to 10b FROM by reading `FROM.formattedValue` as `YYYYMMDD` (`substr(0,4)`, `substr(4,2)`, `substr(6,2)`). On `main` that read the ISO date and gave `NaNNaNNaN`. With this branch and #3397 together, FROM `20261020` with 3 days gives TO `20261022`, as in another viewer. #3397 is needed too because the same calculation also checks that `rawValue` is the 10-character ISO date, and on that branch's data pictures scripts read `20261020` until its latest commit.

No existing issue (searched for formattedValue, display picture and format picture).

title: M4: a file stamped anew with the same bytes is still the document's version
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Sync clients set a file's times again after uploading it. One of them rewrites the modification time to the whole second about ten seconds after a save (which also moves the change time); Nextcloud and Dropbox do similar things. Save's check (#2166) compares the file's stamp (length, times, inode) with the one the document was opened from or last saved as, so the next **Save asked "Save over the changed file?"** although the file on disk was exactly what PdfCraft had written.

Since #3558 the watcher compares the bytes it reads, so with Reload changed files on, a re-stamped file is recognised once the watcher has looked at it. Save still asked with the watcher off, or when it came before the watcher's next look.

Now `FileWatch::disk_differs` compares the bytes whenever the stamp moved and the length did not, as it already did when only the change time moved (Unix, #3558). It uses main's `contents_match`: block by block, no second copy of the PDF, at most the length plus one byte, the stamp checked before and after, so a write in between still counts as another version. Same bytes: Save writes at once. The comparison runs on the UI thread during Save, only when the stamp moved and the length did not, and Save then writes as many bytes on that thread; the doc comment says so. `Stamp::metadata_only_candidate` had no other caller and is gone.

Parity `core.reload-changed-files`: notes and evidence updated.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` (lib and `--test it`), `cargo xtask layers`, `assets`, `parity`, `license-check`

**Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/tests/it/reload.rs`):
- `a_file_stamped_anew_with_the_same_bytes_is_still_the_documents_version`: after a save the file's modification time is set again without changing a byte; the document is not reloaded (its undo history is still there), changes made since get no notice, Save write…

title: M5: the arrow keys move the selected comment
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

With a comment selected, the arrow keys scrolled the view (↑ ↓) or turned the page (← →), so a text box, rectangle or line could only be placed with the mouse. Now:

- an arrow key moves the selected comment **one screen pixel**, and **⌘/Ctrl or Shift and an arrow ten**, as Edit text already nudges objects (#1520);
- up is up on screen whatever the zoom, the page's `/Rotate` and the view's rotation (the step is one screen pixel mapped to user space, so it follows the zoom: fine steps when zoomed in, visible ones on a zoomed-out A0 plan);
- each press is one undo step (`Edit::MoveAnnotation`, "Move comment");
- the keys are taken before the view's navigation, which has them back as soon as nothing is selected (Escape);
- text markup stays with its text, a locked comment where it is, and nothing moves while a text field has the keyboard.

title: Alt+Left / Alt+Right go back and forward through the view history (#3632)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

- **Alt+← / Alt+→ (⌥ on macOS) go back and forward through the view history**, as in Acrobat and browsers. Following a link already records where it was followed from (`go_to_dest` → `go_to_page` pushes the history); Previous view / Next view only had ⌘[ / ⌘] (Ctrl elsewhere), and Alt+← turned the page because `canvas::shortcuts` reads ← / → whatever the modifiers. - **Nudging a selection no longer takes Alt+arrows.** In Edit text & images, `object_ui::nudge_keys` runs before `canvas::shortcuts`, and its `consume_key(Modifiers::NONE / SHIFT, arrow)` also matched a press with Alt (egui's logical matching ignores extra Alt), so with a picture or objects selected Alt+← nudged the selection and dirtied the document. title: M14: the portable copy can register as a PDF handler for the current user (#3758)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3758 (and the cause found in #625). The portable zip registers nothing with Windows, so choosing `pdfcraft.exe` under "Open with" often doesn't stick: double-clicking a PDF then never starts PdfCraft, and the log isn't touched. The MSI registers a `PdfCraft.Document` ProgID, `.pdf\OpenWithProgids`, `Applications\pdfcraft.exe` and Default Programs capabilities (`packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs`). The portable copy, by design, writes nothing outside its folder.

This is docs only:
- `packaging/windows/portable.txt`, which every portable copy ships with and which only marks portable mode by being there (`crates/ui-egui/src/portable.rs`: the contents aren't read), gets a section "Opening PDF files with this copy". It has PowerShell lines that register the copy for the current user only (`HKEY_CURRENT_USER`). They add a ProgID (`PdfCraft.Portable`, so it never collides with the MSI's `PdfCraft.Document` on a PC that has both), list it under `.pdf\OpenWithProgids`, and write Default Programs `Capabilities` (name, description, `FileAssociations\.pdf`) registered under `RegisteredApplications`, the same shape the MSI writes for all users. It then points to Settings ▸ Apps ▸ Default apps. The undo lines say to choose another `.pdf` default first, so Windows isn't left pointing at a removed ProgID.
- The README's portable paragraph says where to find it.

It doesn't add a "make default" button, the other suggestion in #3758. That would make the portable build write to the registry itself, which is a decision for the maintainers. Windows also doesn't let an app set the default; the user always picks it in Settings.

title: fix(organize): imports find the objects they added when new numbers fill gaps
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

`import_pages_with` and `insert_file_pages`, which Duplicate, Replace and Insert Pages go through, took every object numbered above the destination's highest number before the import for one the import added. That only holds while new objects get higher numbers. Once no number is left above the highest, `Document::add` fills free numbers below it (`allocate_num`). That happens when:

- the trailer's `/Size` is exhausted (4294967295 or more; cos already logs "exhausted trailer /Size"), or
- the document holds object 4294967295. An edit to an object of that number creates it: for a damaged file whose catalog is object 4294967295, Recover Page Tree writes the catalog there.

In those documents:

- the imported copies skipped resource sharing, so each import stored its fonts and images again;
- a refused import (a source too deep to follow, #1800) left the objects it had added in the destination;
- with object 4294967295, `n + 1` overflowed. Debug builds panic (`import.rs:243: attempt to add with overflow`). In release it wraps to 0, so every object in the document counts as added: a refused import frees them all, and a successful one runs resource sharing over the whole document.

Both functions now record the object numbers before the import and treat the numbers present afterwards but not before as the import's (`added_objects`). A `HashSet` keeps this independent of the order `object_numbers` returns.

`saturating_add(1)` would stop the panic but not the rest. With object 4294967295, the rollback would then free that object, which the document already had, and keep the objects the import added (see the sabotage runs below).

In the app the engine edits a working copy and discards it on error, so the refusal path never cost a user their document there. The functions still broke their own contract, and the missed resource sharing reached saved files.

Found by a local mutation fuzzer that drives the organize operations on mutated files in a debug…

title: Allow Ctrl+wheel zoom in an unfocused window (#3736)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3736.

Plain wheel scrolling already works in a visible PDFcraft window while another application has focus, but Ctrl+wheel zoom did nothing until you clicked the window first. The cause is in `document_area`: the wheel/pinch zoom branch was gated on `navigation_enabled`, and that also required `ui.input(|i| i.focused)`.

The zoom branch now uses its own `zoom_enabled` gate. It is the same check minus the focus requirement, so an open dialog, the close prompt, the command palette or disabled UI still block zoom. `navigation_enabled`, which the other page gestures use (wheel glide, the selection-drag wheel and so on), still requires focus as before, so the change covers only what the issue asks for. It is in the shared egui path, not limited to Windows, because the existing unfocused scrolling also works on every platform.

Test: `ctrl_wheel_zooms_an_unfocused_window` opens a document in an `egui_kittest` harness, marks the window unfocused, and sends a Ctrl+wheel notch over the page. It checks that the command palette still blocks the zoom, and that the zoom happens once the palette is closed. Without the fix the zoom stays unchanged and the second assertion fails.

title: fix(text): vertical CJK written without a vertical font reads down the column (#3712)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3712.

Vertical text is often written with a *horizontal* font: each character upright, placed on its own, top to bottom, columns right to left — what OCR text layers over scans of vertical books and some converters produce. Every row across the columns is one baseline, so the rows became the lines.

Measured on the reporter's fixture, through `pdfcraft-cli text`:

```
before   遊山春 / 客上天 / 慢開來 / 慢滿得 / 上櫻很 / 山花早 / 。。，
after    春天來得很早， / 山上開滿櫻花。 / 遊客慢慢上山。
```

### What the fix is

A run of upright CJK glyphs that touch down one centre is marked as what it is: text whose **writing direction is down** although each outline is upright. It then goes into the quarter turn that reads down and right to left — where a vertical font's text already goes (`to_upright(.., 1, ..)`) — so nothing new decides the reading order, and `Identity-V` pages are untouched.

Marking the direction is also what makes **Copy** keep the columns apart. `column_text` reads the direction to tell a column of text from a row of cells, so with the layout change alone it still gave

```
遊客慢慢上山。	山上開滿櫻花。	春天來得很早，
```

— the three columns joined by tabs, left to right. It now gives them as lines, right to left, which is the issue's expected text for step 4.

### Why three glyphs, and why CJK only

Two characters below each other happen in ordinary horizontal text (a one-character line above another), so two is not a column; three in a row, each touching the one above on the same centre, are. The test is also limited to CJK, which is what is written vertically — stacked Latin is more often a narrow table cell than a column of text.

### Tests

`upright_glyphs_stacked_down_a_column_read_as_vertical_text` builds the reporter's page through the real text pipeline (`extract_page`) and pins:

- the columns read right to left at **18, 24, 36 and 48 pt** apart (the issue reports all four);
- a search inside one column stays in it, with a highlight taller than it is wide — that is what a drag follows;
- Copy …

title: fix(xfdf): a field name full of periods no longer overflows the stack on export
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

The XFDF export (`export_xfdf`, which `Session::export_data` calls for XFDF) splits each field's full name on periods and nests one `<field>` element per part. That assumes the parts match the field tree's levels. A `/T` can hold periods of its own: ISO 32000-1 §12.7.3.2 says a partial name shall not contain one, but nothing stops a file from having one, and `pdfcraft_forms::fields` keeps `/T` as it is. A name can then split into far more parts than any tree has levels, and the export goes wrong at three sizes:

- From 65 parts, the export writes a file our own import refuses: `walk_xfdf` stops at `MAX_DEPTH` and the error is "XFDF fields nest more than 64 deep".
- Past about 1,020 parts, the 1,024-level XML check refuses it as well.
- By 100,000 parts (50,000 still exported), `write_node` recurses once per level until the main thread's 8 MiB stack overflows: `fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting`. That is an abort, so the engine's `guard` cannot catch it. The PDF that does this is 1.3 KB after `write_full`, because the repeated name compresses well. Dropping the nested `Node` tree recursed just as deep.

The export now nests at most `MAX_DEPTH` levels, the most the import reads back (`splitn(MAX_DEPTH, '.')`). The parts past the last level stay together in the deepest element's `name`. The import joins that onto the prefix with a period, so the same full name comes back. Names of 64 parts or fewer export exactly as before.

Found by a static read of the XFDF exporters, then reproduced in a debug build.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf -j 2`: 53 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-xfdf -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings
- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-xfdf -- --check`: clean

Two new tests:

- `field_names_with_more_parts_than_the_import_reads_still_round_trip`: names of 1 to 1,000 parts, including 63 to 66 around the limit, export and read back with the same name and value, through both `data_valu…

title: fix(annot): a comment listed many times gets one display appearance
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

`with_missing_appearances_cached` builds the copy the engine displays: on open and after every edit (`display_bytes`), and for the CLI (`display_bytes_for`). It gives every annotation without `/AP /N` an appearance. It made that check against the source document, which never gets the appearance, so an annotation that `/Annots` lists many times went through once per listing. The first listing built the stream. Every repeat took it from the cache and added another stream object to the copy, and the engine writes the copy out with `write_incremental`, so the display bytes grew with the number of listings.

A local probe used one Ink annotation with 2,000 points, listed 20,000 times in one page's `/Annots`:

- before: a 136 KB file (6.3 KB gzipped) gave a 428 MB display copy with 20,004 objects, in 2.2 s and 864 MB peak memory. The cache saves the drawing but not the copies, so every edit paid this again;
- after: 173 KB, 0.02 s, 6.4 MB.

Each annotation reference is now handled once per call, across all pages. The repeats pointed at the same dictionary, so the copy shows the same thing as before, with one stream instead of one per listing.

title: Split multi-column TJ rows into separate editable cells (#3744)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
When a PDF table row is emitted as a single `TJ` operator with large negative positioning numbers between cells (such as `[(Labor) -6713 (Remove Cabinets) -26768 (150.00) -5751 (150.00)] TJ`), `interpret` treated the entire array as one continuous `Shown` run, collapsing all columns into a single `TextLine` and `TextBlock` so editing one cell shifted or collapsed the remaining columns. Segment `TJ` arrays at intra-`BT` column jumps (`>= 3 em`, `>= 0.6 em` for invisible OCR text, or `<= -1 em` backwards) and patch only the edited cell's operand slice on replace, clear, rewrite, and group move so sibling columns keep their exact horizontal positions.

Fixes #3744

## What this changes

- **`crates/edit/src/text.rs` (`tj_segments`, `is_column_jump`, `interpret`, `TextLine`, `Shown`):** Splits `TJ` operand arrays into per-column segments whenever the horizontal gap between non-blank strings meets or exceeds the intra-`BT` line-join threshold (`3 em` of font size, `0.6 em` for rendering mode `3`, or `-1 em` backwards, accounting for horizontal scaling `Tz` and letter tracking). Each segmented `Shown` run and `TextLine` records its `TjSlice` range and equivalent thousandths-of-an-em advance adjustment.
- **`crates/edit/src/text.rs` & `crates/edit/src/text_regions.rs` (`patch_tj_slices`, `drop_and_patch`, `splice_rewrite`, `replace_line`, `clear_block`, `rewrite_block`, `rewrite_styled_block`, `move_text_blocks`, `text_edit_layout`):** Replaces or clears only the targeted `TJ` operand slice(s) with their numeric advance adjustments (and compensating delta before trailing slices in `replace_line`), keeping unselected columns in the same `TJ` operator at their original coordinates.
- **`crates/audit/src/lib.rs` (`audit_lines`):** Joins consecutive `TextLine` segments originating from the same `TJ` operator (`paint_pos()`) back into a single line box during redaction auditing so covers spanning a wide `TJ` gap and part of the following value are still measured against the who…
