title: Edit text: a table row written as one TJ array is a row of cells
author: muraa-p
body:
## What this changes

`Fixes #3744`

Edit text read a `TJ` array as one line, so a table row written as one array showed as a single line of text ("Labor Remove Cabinets 150.00 150.00"), and editing one word rewrote the whole row: the other cells were dropped from the page.

A `TJ` array now splits into runs wherever one adjustment moves the pen further than the reach that joins separate runs of one text object (3 em forward, 1 em back). That is the reach `Pen::continues` uses, so each cell is a run of its own, exactly as two separate runs of the same text object would be, and each keeps its own box, position and text matrix. A jump within that reach keeps today's single space, so kerned and justified lines stay one line.

Editing a cell rewrites the array around it: the operands before the cell, the new text, and the operands after it with the text matrix of the cell that follows. The other cells keep their places. A `Tm` sets the line matrix as well, so the rebuild puts the line matrix back and the rows after the edited one stay where they were.

The paragraph editor (`rewrite_block`) and the styled-block edit rewrites the array the same way.

**A line that continues a split array keeps the array's other cells.** A `Tj` after an array's last cell continues the line, and a run before the array joins it, so such a line carries several operators. Each line keeps the parts of the `TJ` arrays it covers (`TextLine.parts`, one entry per array: the range of the array's operands it drew, and the text matrix the following operands continue from). Every rewrite that drops a line's operators rebuilds each array the line covers around the operands the line drew, and the array's remaining operands go back with the matrix of the run that follows them. On an earlier head, a joined line dropped its `TjPart` and editing it deleted the whole array — the text loss found in review. With `parts`, both paths keep every cell, and the two new tests cover both shapes.

**Two views of the s…

title: M7: preserve Tc/Tz runs when editing earlier text (#3215 partial)
author: Linn39403
body:
## What this changes

Partially addresses #3215: preserves character spacing (`Tc`) and horizontal scaling (`Tz`) when editing earlier text, without fragmenting the public text-line selection.

The initial patch split lines at every spacing-state change. Review identified a regression on tiny Word-generated `Tc` changes: replacing a whole heading could leave its old suffix behind. The follow-up restores the original public grouping and retains private source-state spans for rewriting instead. No lossy spacing tolerance is introduced.

The latest follow-up also supports sequential kerned `TJ` arrays without falling back to lossy spacing normalization. It preserves signed source-glyph boundary adjustments consistently in measurement and output.

Line edits retain their existing non-wrapping splice behavior. Supported upright Latin paragraph edits retain the selected public rows and original duplicate/clipping selection, preserve per-span spacing, and save each output row without reintroducing fragmented line selection. Unsupported mixed-state rewrites refuse before mutation.

Includes 29 synthetic regression tests, scoped roadmap/parity updates and contributor credit. No dependency changes. This does not resolve the entire issue.

title: fix(edit): substitute a visible font when editing glyphless OCR text
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Description

Scanned PDFs produced by Tesseract / PDFium (`Glyphless` / `GlyphlessFont`) or Adobe (`HiddenHorzOCR` / `HiddenVertOCR`) place an invisible OCR text layer (`3 Tr`) over the page image using a placeholder font that carries `/ToUnicode` mappings and `/W` advances for text selection, while its embedded TrueType `FontFile2` only defines a single rectangle glyph (`.notdef` + `GID 1`) mapped across every character via `/CIDToGIDMap`.

When an OCR paragraph is edited in `pdfcraft-edit`, the replacement text is emitted visibly (`0 Tr`). Because `Metrics::encode` previously accepted `/Glyphless` (its `/ToUnicode` and `/W` tables look populated), `rewrite_block`, `rewrite_styled_block`, and `replace_line` reused the `/Glyphless` font resource for the visible replacement text, causing every character to render and print as a solid black rectangle once editing finished. In addition, `embedded_sfnt` exposed the 2-glyph rectangle `FontFile2` to the inline text editor, and `rewrite_styled_block` calibrated run horizontal scaling (`Tz`) against `source.font` even when `source.font` could not encode the run's words.

This change:
1. Detects OCR placeholder fonts in `pdfcraft-fonts::pdf` (`is_glyphless`) by checking `/BaseFont`, descendant `/BaseFont`, and `/FontDescriptor` `/FontName` (after stripping any `ABCDEF+` subset prefix) for `Glyphless*`, `HiddenHorzOCR*`, and `HiddenVertOCR*`, and gating structural detection on `CIDFontType2` fonts whose 1-outline TrueType `FontFile2` has at least 64 non-zero CIDs all mapped to that single GID in `/CIDToGIDMap` (keeping valid whitespace-only subsets and 1-glyph subsets with intentional `cmap`/`CIDToGIDMap` aliases usable).
2. Prevents glyphless fonts from encoding visible replacement text (`Metrics::has_glyph` and `Metrics::encode` return `false`/`None`, and `embedded_sfnt` returns `None`) while preserving `Metrics::decode`, `Metrics::text_of`, `Metrics::codes`, and `Metrics::width` so the original invisible OCR layer still…

title: cli: the argument bugs photocraft#7071 lists are live here too
author: Hamza0101
body:
PhotoCraft's [#7071](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/7071) lists the argument bugs a hand-written parser produces, each fixed on its own there. **Three of them are live in `pdfcraft-cli`.** Measured on `main`:

```
$ pdfcraft-cli extract f.pdf --pages 1 --out --password
$ ls
--password                 # exit 0, and the PDF is in a file called --password

$ pdfcraft-cli combine a.pdf b.pdf --out --nonsense
$ ls
--nonsense                 # --nonsense is not even an option here, and nothing said so

$ pdfcraft-cli check-one --edit f.pdf
pdfcraft-cli: check-one: missing file

$ pdfcraft-cli info /tmp/café.pdf          # that é as one Latin-1 byte
thread 'main' panicked at library/std/src/env.rs:878:51:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "/tmp/caf\xE9.pdf"
```

### The fixes

**An option whose value is a file or folder refuses a value that is another option** — `--out`, `--out-dir`, `--json`, `--root`, `--control`, `--script` — and names the way out for a file that really does start with `-`: `./--name`, which `--root` already offered and `tests/root_arguments.rs` already pins. This also closes the gap the option walk left for those: `validate_options` skips a value option's operand, so an unknown option sitting in that position was skipped too, which is why `--out --nonsense` wrote a file instead of saying what `--nonsense` was.

**Only those options.** A password or a title can be any string, `--page` included: `an_option_shaped_password_is_not_parsed_as_a_page_flag` pins `text protected.pdf --password --page`, and I would have broken it — the test caught the first version of this patch, which applied the rule to every value. For `--page`, `--dpi` and the rest, a value that is another option is already reported by the command in its own terms ("bad --page: expected a positive page number"), so nothing there changes.

**`positional` asks the option table which tokens are values**, instead of skipping the one after every option. The token after …

title: fix(render): render JBIG2 stencil masks instead of dropping them (#2134)
author: Mawfyy
body:
Two fixes for a page that renders as a solid dark layer: a JBIG2 stencil mask that cannot be decoded is dropped, and the image it masks is then painted over the whole page.

A stencil mask says *where* an image is painted, not how opaque it is. When the mask's data could not be decoded, the mask was dropped and the image was drawn over the whole page — a different picture, and a silent one. Such an image is now left out, the way an image whose own data cannot be decoded is left out, and the failure is reported: a new `RenderWarning::ImageDecodeFailure`, which the CLI prints.

The other half is the vendored decoder. `vendor/hayro-jbig2` capped a text region at 10,000 symbol instances. The index page of a 296-page book places 10,870 of them, so the region was dropped, its stencil mask with it, and the page drew the book's dark layer over its light one. The cap is replaced by PDFium's heuristic, which upstream merged as LaurenzV/hayro#1278 and which this copy predates: a region may place as many instances as its data can hold. The pixels the placements write are capped as well, since every placement copies its symbol into the region and a limit on their number does not bound that.

**Evidence.** The book is a 296-page PDF whose pages carry a light raster layer and a dark one, with a JBIG2 stencil mask cutting the text out of the dark layer. 11 of its 295 pages were affected. Page 6 against `pdftoppm`: differing pixels 63.9% → 3.8%, the rest the font antialiasing that every other page shows too; the other 284 pages match Poppler at 1–6%.

**Relation to #2309.** The first commit is a backport of the same upstream change #2309 brings with the vendored refresh, so that refresh replaces it; it is kept here so the pages render correctly before the refresh lands (#2309 currently conflicts with main). The second commit touches `hayro-interpret` and does not conflict with it.

**Tests.** The vendored crate's own test (`decode::text::tests::a_text_region_with_more_than_ten_thous…

title: M2: scans stay sharp at screen size and smooth when zoomed (area-average shrink, bilinear enlarge)
author: Kronbii
body:
Fixes #2393.

## What this changes

Scanned pages (office scanners, print-to-image drivers, conference proceedings run through Ghostscript) looked thin and broken at normal zoom, and blocky when zoomed in. Both come from how the vendored hayro renderer resamples images that don't set `/Interpolate`, which is most scans.

**At screen size, a scan is now shrunk by area averaging instead of nearest-neighbour.** Since #635 (the fix for #624), a non-interpolated image drawn below its resolution was pre-shrunk with nearest-neighbour. A 300 dpi scan shown at 100% (96 dpi) is shrunk about 3× per axis, so nearest-neighbour kept about one sample in ten and dropped most strokes of its text. The shrunk raster was then sampled again by the nearest sampler at a fractional offset, which dropped more.

![300 dpi scan at 100%: main draws letters at random weights with broken strokes; this PR keeps every stroke](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/pr-assets/compare-100.png)

**When zoomed in, a page-sized scan is now smoothed.** A non-interpolated image drawn above its resolution was sampled nearest-neighbour, so every scan sample became a block and text edges were staircases. Images of page-scan size (512 or more samples on the shorter side) are now drawn bilinearly when enlarged, the same filter already used for images that set `/Interpolate`. Icons, QR codes and pixel art keep their hard pixels.

![The same scan at 400%: staircase edges on main, smooth outlines with this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/pr-assets/compare-400.png)

The page, generator and README for these screenshots are on [`pr-assets`](https://github.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/tree/pr-assets). Everything there is synthetic: text written by PdfCraft, rendered at 300 dpi, thresholded to black and white, and placed back as image-only pages.

Both are patches to `vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`, recorded as patches (21) and (22) in `vendor/README.md`:

title: M4: delete several bookmarks at once (#3853)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3853.

The Bookmarks panel could delete one bookmark at a time. Now several can be picked and deleted in one undoable step:

- **Pick:** Ctrl/⌘-click toggles a bookmark, ⇧-click picks the rows from the last-clicked one to this one (over the rows on screen, so collapsed children and search filters are respected). A plain click still goes to the bookmark's page and becomes the pick. Picking does not move the document. Picked rows share the accent fill the Pages panel uses.
- **Delete:** Delete or Backspace with the pointer over the panel, or **Delete N bookmarks** in the right-click menu. The menu's one-bookmark commands (Rename, Move, Indent, Outdent, Set to current page) are disabled while several are picked. Escape drops the pick; an inline rename keeps Delete and Escape for itself.
- **Parents and children:** a picked parent takes its subtree with it, so picking a parent and its child is the same as picking the parent. Unpicked bookmarks and their destinations are untouched.
- **Headless:** `bookmark_delete` takes `paths` (a list of paths, at most 10,000) as well as `path`.

Engine: `delete_bookmarks` (organize) reads every path against the outline as it is before the call, so order and overlap do not matter, and a path that names no bookmark (or an empty list) fails before anything changes. `Edit::DeleteBookmarks` gives one undo step labelled "Delete bookmarks" ("Delete bookmark" for one).

### A stale pick is dropped, not applied

Picked paths mean something else after any edit, undo or redo. The pick records the document's `edit_generation()` and clears when it changes, so a reorder of look-alike bookmarks cannot make Delete act on bookmarks the user did not pick.

## How you verified it

The rebase retains all 19 code/test/parity/snapshot patch payloads unchanged. Both the new upstream Fill & Sign engine regression and this PR's bookmark regression are retained. The first parallel run exposed an unchanged upstream byte-comparison t…

title: M10: scanned pages become selectable and searchable on their own (background, view-only OCR)
author: Kronbii
body:
## What this changes

A scanned PDF has no text layer, so in PdfCraft nothing on it could be selected, found or copied. Nothing said why, either: dragging over a scan simply did nothing. Browsers recognize scans on their own, and users who switch from Chrome expect the same. PdfCraft already has Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text; this PR makes it reach the reader in two ways.

**1. Scans are recognized in the background, view-only.** When a page's text layer comes back empty, PdfCraft reads the document's pages that contain pictures, starting from the current page. Each page can be selected, found and copied as soon as it is read. Progress and **Cancel** sit at the bottom of the document area.

![Background recognition: "Recognizing text… page 1 of 3" with Cancel at the bottom of the document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/pr-assets/app-progress.png)

![Recognized text selected across lines on a scan, with the usual selection actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/pr-assets/app-selected.png)

The recognized text belongs to the view and is never written into the document. The file is not marked modified, there is nothing to undo, and nothing is asked on closing. To keep the text in the file, Recognize text still adds it as an undoable edit, unchanged. A Preferences checkbox turns background recognition off ("Recognize the text of scanned pages in the background (the file is not changed)"). It is on by default on desktop and needs the OCR models (release packages ship them; source builds use `cargo xtask models`). The web build has no worker threads and skips it.

**2. Selecting where there is no text explains why.** If background recognition is off, missing its models, or found nothing, a selection drag or double-click on a page with an empty text layer shows a bar explaining that and offering **Recognize text…**. That opens the existing dialog set to that page.

title: M7: keep a word on its line when its spacing differs by less than a thousandth of an em
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Edit text joins the runs of a line only when their text state matches (`compatible_word`, `crates/edit/src/text.rs`). Character spacing (`Tc`) and word spacing (`Tw`) were compared to 1e-6.

Word documents exported through macOS Quartz (`Producer: macOS … Quartz PDFContext`, `Creator: Word`) write each word as its own text object, and some of them get `0.0001 Tc`. On a real proposal the title line `для компании AEROSOL` is four text objects with the same font, size and baseline. Only `EROSOL` has `0.0001 Tc` (with `50 0 0 50 … Tm` inside a `0.24` `cm`, that is 0.0012 pt per glyph). The line opened as two paragraphs, `для компании A` and `EROSOL`. Clicking the word selected half of it, and an edit could only reach one part.

Now character and word spacing are compared to a thousandth of an em (`Tfs / 1000`), the unit glyph widths are given in (ISO 32000-1 §9.7.4.3). A difference below that can't be seen.
- Horizontal scale and rise still have to match exactly.
- Visible spacing still keeps runs apart: `0.5 Tc` on the same word still makes two paragraphs, which the new test checks.
- The intent of #3215 (a run with its own `Tc` mustn't be redrawn in another run's state) holds: within this tolerance, redrawing in the first run's state moves a 100-glyph line by at most 0.1 em.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

title: M7: keep an applied paragraph's look until its page is drawn again
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

When a paragraph is applied (⌘↩, clicking elsewhere, or switching to another paragraph), the edit rewrites the page in the same frame. The page raster on screen is only marked stale (`DocView::page_changed`) and stays up until the new one arrives. On the next frame `TextBackground::prepare` sees no editor and drops the textless background, and the editor itself is gone. So:
- for those frames the **old text** showed again;
- the paragraph outlines are already read from the new inventory, so the old text sat under the new outline;
- then the new raster arrived and the text jumped to its new layout (on a tiled page, tile by tile).

Edits to added items already avoid this with `MoveBackground.settling`, and pen strokes with the comment settling.

Now the paragraph editor does the same:
- **`TextBackground::remember`** records how the editor drew its text each frame: the TextEdit's galley, its position in the page's 0..1 coordinates, and the page width on screen.
- **`TextBackground::committed`** is called from `apply_edit` next to `MoveBackground::committed`. When the edit is the open paragraph's `EditTextBlock` and its textless background is ready, the background and that last look stay on screen.
- **`TextBackground::page_received`** ends this once the page is no longer drawn from before the edit. A new `DocView::page_out_of_date` tells: the whole-page raster (a tiled page's backdrop too) or any of its tiles is still stale. Both the page and the tile result paths call it, so whichever arrives last ends it.
- **Other endings.** Any other edit ends it. A zoom or a turn of the view since then stops drawing it, so the raster shows instead of rows at the wrong scale or place. Opening another editor replaces it, as before.

The look shown in between is the editor's own layout, the one the user typed into. If the saved layout differs, the text still moves once when the raster arrives. It no longer goes back to the old text first. Making the two layouts…

title: M7: keep a moved or resized page image in place until its page is drawn again
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

While a picture on the page is dragged by its frame or a corner in Edit text & images, its old place is blanked and the page raster's picture of it is stretched into the new frame (#1677). On release the edit is applied in the same frame and the drag state is cleared.

The page raster stays on screen until its replacement arrives (`page_changed` only marks it stale). So for those frames:
- the picture showed again at its **old** size and place;
- the selection frame and handles were already at the new one;
- then the picture jumped when the raster arrived (on a tiled page, tile by tile).

Resizing shows it most: the old, larger picture flashes around the new frame after every release.

Now the release keeps the move. `ImageSelection` records the old and new frames in the page's 0..1 coordinates. While the page is out of date, the selected image keeps being drawn the way the drag drew it: blanked at the old frame and stretched into the new one from the stale raster. A new `DocView::page_out_of_date` decides when to stop:
- the whole-page raster (a tiled page's backdrop too) is still `STALE_TAG`;
- or any of its tiles is still stale.

When the edit fails, the page never goes stale, so nothing is kept. A second drag before the page is drawn again takes the picture's pixels from where the raster still has it (the first edit's source frame), blanks that, and keeps it as the source on release. The drag preview's drawing moved into `stretched_picture` so both paths share it.

**Later commits on this branch:**
- **No outline where the picture was.** The dragged picture's faint inventory outline no longer trails at its old place during the drag.
- **Fresh pixels once the page raster is fresh** (from review). The old frame stays blanked while any tile is stale. Pixels come from the old frame only while the whole-page raster itself is stale (`DocView::page_raster_out_of_date`); after that they come from the destination.

title: M7: picture watermarks can have a fixed width in points (#3771)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3771 (the watermark half; see "Not in this PR").

A picture watermark was sized only as a fraction of the page, so the same watermark came out a different size on pages of different sizes. It can now be given a **fixed width in points**, the same on every page, with the height following the picture's shape.

- **Engine:** `Watermark::width` in points. `0` keeps the page-relative `scale`; otherwise it is 1 to `MAX_MARK_WIDTH` (20000, more than any page) and `scale` is ignored. Text watermarks already had an absolute size (`font_size`).
- **Tool:** `doc_watermark` takes `width`. A value outside 1 to 20000, or not a number, is an error rather than being clamped, because a size the caller asked for should not quietly change.
- **Dialog:** a **Width** checkbox with a points field in Add Watermark ▸ Source ▸ File (starts at 144 pt). The Scale slider is off while it is ticked. The value is remembered while the box is off and left out of the edit. It reuses the existing "Width" string, so there are no catalog changes.

### Hardening that came with it

The picture's size comes from the file the user picks, so it can be anything a file says. With a fixed width the height follows from the shape and could overflow, so `placement()` now works out where a picture lands and **refuses before anything is changed** (including before `replace` removes an existing mark) when:

- the picture's size is not finite (`NaN`, `±inf`), or
- at a fixed width, the picture would be taller than the limit (an overflow would otherwise write `inf` into the content stream).

The same up-front check now runs for **backgrounds**, which share `picture()`. Scale factors are written with `matrix_number` instead of 3 decimals: with 3 decimals a 612 pt source at "1 pt wide" drew 1.2 pt wide, and a 10 000 pt one rounded to `0` and drew nothing. At a fixed width the picture’s real proportions are used, including source sides below 0.01 pt; zero or negative source dimensions are ref…

title: Print: Japanese paper sizes (はがき・封筒・JIS B4/B5)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

PdfCraft's Print dialog and the `doc_print` tool listed the US, ISO A, ARCH and ANSI sheets only, so a Japanese sheet had to be entered as a custom size — and there were no JIS B sheets at all. Japanese printing uses **JIS P 0138** B4 257 × 364 mm, B5 182 × 257 mm and B6 128 × 182 mm, which are not the ISO 216 sheets (250 × 353 mm and 176 × 250 mm), and its office and book papers are not in the list either. Reference: #3811 (a print paper size was requested).

- **Papers added** (`crates/print/src/lib.rs`, `PAPERS`; points at 72/25.4 from millimetres):
  - **JIS B4/B5/B6**: `B4 (JIS)` 728.50 × 1031.81 pt, `B5 (JIS)` 515.91 × 728.50 pt, `B6 (JIS)` 362.83 × 515.91 pt
  - **ISO B4/B5**: `B4` 250 × 353 mm and `B5` 176 × 250 mm. These were absent; they are added so a plain `B4`/`B5` means the ISO sheet, as PDFs use it, and the JIS sheets are clearly labelled.
  - **はがき** `Japanese Postcard` 100 × 148 mm, **往復はがき** `Japanese Double Postcard` 148 × 200 mm
  - **封筒 長形3号/長形4号** `Japanese Envelope #3` 120 × 235 mm, `Japanese Envelope #4` 90 × 205 mm (長形4号)
  - **角形2号/角形3号** `Kaku #2` 240 × 332 mm, `Kaku #3` 216 × 277 mm
  - **四六判** `Yonroku-ban` 127 × 188 mm
- **Name resolution** (`find_paper`, used by `doc_print`): a paper is named by its label, the name before its notes (`ARCH D` for `ARCH D (24 x 36 in)`, `4 x 6 in label`, `Letter` for `US Letter`), ignoring case, spaces and punctuation — `B5 (JIS)`, `b5 (jis)` and `b5jis` are the same sheet. An unknown name is still refused with the list of names.
- **Print spooler** (`cups_media`) — **this changes the `media` option for the new sheets; please read this part.**
  - JIS B4/B5/B6 keep their PPD names (`B4`, `B5`, `B6` — on a PPD those *are* the JIS sheets), and A6 gets `A6`.
  - ISO B4/B5 and the Japanese sheets are now asked for as **`Custom.<width>x<height>mm`** (e.g. `Custom.100x148mm`, `Custom.90x205mm`), the form the CUPS options documentation specifies and the one the system media lookup recognises.…

title: M4: a new bookmark goes to where the reader is (#3865)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3865.

A bookmark made in the app always went to the top of the page, so two sections on one page could not be bookmarked apart. A new bookmark now records where the reader is:

- **Text selected:** the top-left of the selection, on the selection's page.
- **Nothing selected:** the top of the window, on the page showing there.

It is written as `/XYZ left top null`: the reader's zoom is kept, and when only the top is pinned the horizontal position is too (so a bookmark made while scrolled sideways does not snap the view back). Clicking it goes there, through the existing destination handling. With no layout yet (before the first frame) it goes to the page top, as before.

- **render:** `PageInfo::xyz_for_view`, the inverse of `dest_fraction`. It pins only the coordinates it is given. On a page turned a quarter, the displayed y decides the user `left` and the displayed x the user `top`.
- **organize:** `add_bookmark_at` (`add_bookmark` calls it with no position). A coordinate that is not finite is refused with `OutlineError::BadPosition` before anything changes.
- **engine:** `Edit::AddBookmark` takes `left` and `top` (both `None` is the page top, as before). Existing constructors are updated.
- **automation:** `bookmark_add` takes `top` and `left` in points from the top-left of the displayed page, the convention `bookmark_list` already reports, so a position round-trips. Out-of-range or non-numeric values are errors rather than being dropped.
- **ui:** `DocView::bookmark_position`, used by ⌘B and the New bookmark button.

### Cases that needed care

- **A turned page** (`/Rotate`): the window's vertical is a user x, so that is what is pinned.
- **A turned view** (View ▸ Rotate View): the screen's vertical is the view's x at 90° and 270°, and the selection's top-left corner is a different corner of its bounds at each quarter turn.
- **A spread of pages of different heights** (two-up, cover): the shorter page can start below the window's t…

title: M7: an added picture resized by a corner shows only at its new size
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

When an item added in this session is moved, `MoveBackground` (`content_ui.rs`, #1488) renders the page without it once per gesture. The item's own pixels then follow the pointer over that background, and stay in their new place after the release until the page is rendered again (`settling`).

A corner resize got none of this. `MoveBackground::prepare` keyed it on `Grab::Move` only:
- while the corner was dragged, only the outline and handles followed it (`paint_page`), and the picture stayed at its old size under them;
- after the release, the page raster still had the old size until the new one arrived.

So resizing an added picture always showed two sizes at once.

Now a picture's corner resize uses the same background:
- **During the drag,** its pixels are stretched from the box it had into the dragged box (`dragged`, which already keeps the aspect ratio for pictures).
- **After the release,** they are drawn into the applied box until the page is rendered again.
- **A move** is the same stretch with an unchanged size, so it is drawn as before.
- **Text resized by a corner** rewraps rather than stretches. It keeps the outline only, as before.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

2. While dragging, it reads the pixels back. The kept quarter must be red, and the part that goes must have no red.

title: M5: Wayland tablet pens and pressure-sensitive ink
author: mgaux-dev
body:
## What this changes

On Wayland, winit 0.30 binds no tablet protocol, so compositors turn a graphics-tablet pen into a plain pointer and its pressure is lost. This PR makes the pressure reach the app, then uses it for ink.

### 1. Wayland tablet pens in the vendored winit (patch 14)

`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/seat/tablet/` binds `zwp_tablet_v2` and reports a pen the way winit 0.30 already does on Windows (`WM_POINTER` / `PT_PEN`):

- **Tip down:** `WindowEvent::Touch` whose `force` is the pen pressure (0–1). egui-winit turns it into the primary pointer, so every tool behaves as before.
- **Hovering:** `CursorEntered` / `CursorMoved` / `CursorLeft`.
- **Barrel buttons:** middle (`BTN_STYLUS`) and right (`BTN_STYLUS2`) clicks, as libinput desktops map them.
- **Cursor:** the pen's cursor is set through `wp_cursor_shape_v1`, follows the window's cursor and is hidden with it.
- **Opt-out:** `WINIT_WAYLAND_TABLET=0` leaves tablets to the compositor's pointer emulation.

### 2. Ink width follows pen pressure

A pen that reports pressure now draws thinner where it presses lightly, scaling linearly from 10% of the chosen width at no pressure to 100% at full pressure (`pdfcraft_annot::pressure_width`).

- **While drawing:** the Draw tool records a pressure for each point and paints the stroke at those widths. The stroke shown between release and the page re-render keeps them too. The pressure comes only from the touch that drives egui's pointer, claimed by egui-winit's rule: the first touch to start while none is down, until it lifts. A second contact, such as a hand on a screen that reports force or another pen, can't change a stroke's pressure or lend it to the next stroke.
- **Saved PDF:** `Shape::Ink` gains `pressure`, shaped like `strokes`, or empty for a mouse. The annotation stores it in a PdfCraft-only key, `/PCPressure`, parallel to `/InkList` (one number per point, 0–1, rounded to thousandths). The appearance stream strokes each curve segment a…

title: check: judge a file by a page budget and render every page when asked
author: Axiomatic47
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli check` judges each file by one wall-clock budget (`--timeout`, 20 s by default), so a long volume that renders steadily is reported as a timeout beside a page that truly stalls. In a rendering census of a 12,000-file law library at 36 dpi with a 30 s budget, 35 United States Reports volumes (vols. 158–224, 450–950 pages each) read as timeouts in one shelf, while every one of them renders whole: a 784-page volume takes 93 s. The child, `check-one`, also stops after 500 pages without saying so, so the rest of such a volume is never rendered.

After this change:

- `--page-timeout S` judges the file by its pages: it is killed only when no page completes within S seconds. Given alone it lifts the file bound; given with `--timeout`, both apply. The parent asks the child for one progress line per page (`check-one --progress` prints `{"page":n}` before its result) and reads the child's stdout on a thread while it polls, so the page clock resets as pages complete.
- `--max-pages N` sets how many pages `check-one` renders (500 as before; `0` means every page) and is passed through from `check`.
- Every report row carries `checked`, the number of pages that ran; a timeout row says how many pages completed before it.

Nothing changes without the new flags: no flags still means 20 s per file and the first 500 pages, and the existing JSON keys are unchanged. Two small things to know: the parent always asks the child for its page lines, so a timeout row's `checked` is right whichever budget ended it; and `--timeout` now accepts fractional seconds (`--timeout 2.5`) where it took whole seconds before.

Two things noticed in the same census, left for their own PRs: `check` reports a dangling file symlink as `crash` (the child's read fails and exits 1; 262 such rows in one folder of removed links), and a progress line could carry the page's render time for a per-page census.

- `cargo clippy -p…

title: M3: Find ignores accents by default, with an Accent-sensitive option (#3460)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3460. Carries the accent setting through the Replace feature now on main (#3841).

Find now **ignores accents by default**: `cafe` finds `café` and `CAFÉ`, `resume` finds `résumé`, and `s` finds `š`, `ș` and `ş`. The find bar has an **Accent-sensitive** checkbox in Find options (off by default) for when the exact spelling matters. It is independent of Case-sensitive and Whole words only. The options button lights up when any option is on.

`text_find` and `text_replace` both take `accent_sensitive` (default `false`), so headless finding and replacement agree. The Find bar passes its Accent-sensitive setting to Replace and Replace all. A `text_find` continuation with `start_page` and `skip` keeps whatever the caller passes again.

### What counts as an accent

Only **Latin letters** fold. A precomposed letter whose canonical decomposition is an ASCII letter plus combining diacritical marks (U+0300–036F) matches its base letter, and so does such a mark drawn as a separate glyph after a Latin letter (decomposed text). Everything else stays distinct:

- letters with no decomposition (`ł`, `ø`, `đ`, `ß`), which are letters of their own;
- the kana (`が` is not `か`), whose voicing mark is outside that block;
- Cyrillic (`й` is not `и`) and Greek.

### Changes

- **render:** `fold_accents`, `FindOptions { case_sensitive, whole_words, accent_sensitive }` (derives `Default`: all off) and `PageText::find_options`. **The older `find`, `find_opts` and `find_opts_limited` still match accents as written**, so Search & Redact stays unchanged. Replace uses the new options-aware `find_in_text_options` path; existing direct engine Replace callers retain their literal default.
- **render, new dependency edge:** `unicode-normalization` is now a direct dependency of `pdfcraft-render`. It was already in the build (through the text shaping stack), so `Cargo.lock` changes by one dependency line and no new crate or version.
- **ui:** `Find.accent_sensitive` and t…

title: Selection: vertical CJK placed one glyph per baseline copies in column order (#3712)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this fixes

**#3712:** vertical Chinese (and Japanese) written *without a vertical font* — one upright glyph placed on its own, top to bottom, columns right to left, the way OCR text layers and some converters write vertical text — is selected and copied **row by row across the columns** instead of column by column.

The issue's synthetic `stacked.pdf` has three 12 pt columns 18 pt apart reading 「春天來得很早，」「山上開滿櫻花。」「遊客慢慢上山。」. A drag down the right column copies `春 / 客上天 / 慢開來 / 慢滿得 / 上櫻很 / 山花早 / 。。，` instead of `春天來得很早，`.

**Cause.** Reading-order layout (`crates/render/src/text.rs::arrange`) groups glyphs by baseline: glyphs on one baseline form a segment, and segments on the same baseline that nearly touch are merged. The columns' rows are exactly such baselines, so the rows became lines. Nothing read a stack of single upright glyphs as a vertical line.

## The heuristic

- In reading-order layout, before horizontal segmentation, **consecutive upright CJK glyphs that stack** are grouped into a vertical column. A pair continues a stack when: both glyphs are kana/kanji or their punctuation (`is_cjk`), their boxes overlap horizontally by ≥ 60 % of the narrower box, their heights differ by < 35 %, and the lower box touches or nearly touches the upper one from below (`-0.5 h ≤ drop ≤ 0.6 h`). Two consecutive glyphs are enough, so short vertical labels work.
- A column is **one segment and one line**: it is excluded from the same-baseline merge (so the rows across columns cannot form), and its glyphs stay in content order, top to bottom (the existing x sort ties on x and falls back to content order).
- Block order takes a group of vertical columns **right to left**: the rightmost column of the group first (even if the content stream drew the columns left to right), then its nearest column on the left that shares vertical space. Horizontal text keeps the existing left-then-right column rule.
- Untouched: Identity-V vertical fonts and turned baselines go through the…

title: Deps: update rustls-webpki and webpki-root-certs (RUSTSEC-2026-0382/-0383)
author: midasdf
body:
## Background

`cargo-deny`'s **advisories** check has failed on main since **2026-10-21**, when two RustSec advisories were published for the emSign/emudhra certificate incident (private keys for several intermediates are now well known):

- **RUSTSEC-2026-0382** — *Certificate verification may accept distrusted intermediates* — `rustls-webpki 0.103.15` affected, fixed in **≥ 0.103.16**.
- **RUSTSEC-2026-0383** — *Bundled root certificates allow trust in distrusted emSign intermediates* — `webpki-root-certs 1.0.9` affected, fixed in **≥ 1.0.10**.

main's `Cargo.lock` pins exactly those two versions, so **every branch's `dependency licences and advisories` job fails**, including unrelated PRs: runs [39624013324](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/39624013324) (`fix/image-holds-until-redraw`), 39623789598 (`fix/editor-holds-until-redraw`), 39623757124 (`fix/editor-opens-without-fade`), 39623744308 (`fix/join-near-equal-spacing`) and 39623255159 (`fix/field-tooltip-3854`) all fail the same job with the same two advisories, and PRs #3869, #3886 and #3892 show green wasm32/ubuntu/windows jobs with only this deny job red. This PR fixes it once for main.

## Change

`Cargo.lock` only, two entries:

```
rustls-webpki    0.103.15 -> 0.103.16
webpki-root-certs 1.0.9   -> 1.0.10
```

No manifest change, no other package, version or dependency edge moves (`git diff --stat Cargo.lock` → 4 insertions, 4 deletions: the two `version` and two `checksum` lines). A plain `cargo update -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-root-certs` also repointed `windows-sys 0.52` edges on several unrelated crates while re-resolving, so the two entries were changed directly and the resulting lock was validated by the resolver.

author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3557.

The Preferences settings scroll when the window is short, but the **OK button was the last thing inside the scrolled content**. In a short window it was off screen until you scrolled to it, and the dialog was cut off partway through the Light/Dark theme cards, which is the layout the report describes ("the confirmation button needs to scroll to the bottom to display", "the height is not right, there is too little displayed content"). I reproduced it headlessly with the `shot` example in a 1000×560 window: the dialog ended mid theme cards with a fade and no OK.

### A regression this nearly introduced, and the fix

A scroll area starts from the room its modal offers it, and a modal offers more each frame for the first few. With OK inside the scroll that never showed, because the settings demanded far more than the offer. With OK outside, the dialog **opened small and stretched by about 45 pt a frame for ten frames**, and clicks in its first frames landed on controls that were still moving. title: fix(platform): a save on a Mac SMB share no longer hides the file
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## What this changes

On macOS, saving a PDF that lives on an SMB share (for example a Windows file server) could make the saved file **hidden**: invisible in Finder and in Windows Explorer, so it looked as if the save had deleted the document.

Cause: `write_atomically` (used by the desktop save and the automation tools) writes a dot-named staging file (`.{name}.pdfcraft-{suffix}.tmp` / `.{name}.{suffix}.pdfcraft-tmp`) and renames it over the target. macOS smbfs gives every new file whose name starts with a dot the server's "hidden" attribute, which shows up as `UF_HIDDEN` on the Mac, and the rename carries that flag over to the target.

Repro on a Mac with an SMB share mounted: create `.x.pdf.pdfcraft-0.tmp` (`ls -lO` shows `hidden`), write it, fsync, `rename()` it over an existing `x.pdf`; `ls -lO x.pdf` now shows `hidden`. We hit it with real 20–30 MB PDFs on a shared office folder.

Fix: before the rename, `staging::write_atomically_with` clears `UF_HIDDEN` on the staging file if it is set (macOS only, best effort: a failure is ignored and the save goes ahead as before). rustix has no `chflags` and the workspace forbids `unsafe`, so this adds `nix` (0.30, `fs` feature only, macOS-only target dependency) for its safe `chflags` wrapper; its dependencies (`libc`, `bitflags`, `cfg-if`, `cfg_aliases`) are already in the lock file.

Windows is unchanged: a leading dot does not set `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN` there.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked -p pdfcraft-platform -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --locked -p pdfcraft-platform -j 2`: 17 passed

title: M9: closing a half of a side-by-side comparison keeps the app running (#3915)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3915.

In a side-by-side comparison, drawing a half can close that half's own tab: a snapshot tab's notice bar **Close** sets `close_requested`, and `document_area` then calls `close_tab`. `compare_area` kept using the view indexes it was given, so:
- closing the **right** (new) half panicked at the scroll sync, `app.views[new]` (`compare_ui.rs:354`, as the issue describes);
- closing the **left** (old) half shifted the indexes, and the right half was then drawn with a stale index, which panicked inside `document_area` (`canvas.rs:2371`).

The frame isn't guarded (#3914), so either case closed the app and lost every unsaved tab.

Now `compare_area` takes the two halves' document ids on entry, and finds each half again by id before drawing it and before the scroll sync. When one is gone, the frame ends there. On the next frame `side_by_side` no longer finds the pair, and the remaining tab draws normally.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test compare`: 6 passed
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: passes; no assets were touched

**Test.** `compare.rs::closing_either_half_of_a_side_by_side_comparison_keeps_the_app_running` compares two versions side by side, sets `close_requested` on one half's view (what the snapshot bar's Close does), and runs three frames. It checks that the tab closed and the app is still running, for each half in turn.
- Without the fix it fails at `compare_ui.rs:354`, the issue's line.
- Mutation check: going back to the stale index inside the loop alone fails the left-half case (`canvas.rs:2371`), and removing the lookup after the loop alone fails the right-half case. So each of the two lookups is pinned.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

title: M12: support zero-instance XFA subforms
author: nnamdiarimah
body:
## What this changes

Optional XFA subforms can start with zero instances, add their first instance, remove their last, and retain their values and structure through edits, undo/redo and save/reopen.

- Apply blank-merge initial counts and data-merge minimum/maximum limits, including zero and optional singletons. Preserve initial data groups through unrelated edits and imports (#4744).
- Retain dormant definitions for JavaScript and FormCalc instance managers without creating phantom fields or running absent instances' scripts.

- Measure and draw each instance in its own data scope across vertical/horizontal flow, positioned containers, areas, tables, cells and page masters. Positioned copies retain their template offsets and may overlap. Repeated cells consume separate column spans; inferred columns account for each row's live cells.
- Omit absent content and overflow leaders from geometry. Growable horizontal groups split at leaf boundaries even with keep hints; fixed-height blocks retain their move-whole behavior. Preserve content-area origins and enclosing borders/fills/margins across supported breaks.

title: M7: a text editing session for one paragraph
author: komo1iddin
body:
First step of #2512.

## What this changes

Editing a paragraph calls into `pdfcraft-edit` once per keystroke (`text_edit_layout`) and once more to apply (`rewrite_block`). Each call reads the page again from whatever document it is given. Nothing ties the draft to the document state it was made against, so an edit queued from an older state can rewrite another paragraph (#2022, #2516).

This adds `pdfcraft_edit::TextSession`, a plain value with no threads:
- **`TextSession::open(doc, page, block)`** reads the page's lines once. It keeps them with the paragraph as it was, a clone of the document, and its `ReadState` (#2504).
- **`layout(text, style)`** lays a draft out with the same rewrite Apply runs, on a copy of the opened document. Every draft starts from the same page, so no draft sees another's output. It returns today's `TextEditLayout`.
- **`commit(doc, text, style)`** writes the draft into `doc`, but only if `doc` still reads as the opened state. Otherwise it returns `the paragraph changed while it was being edited` and leaves `doc` untouched.
- **`is_current(doc)`** lets a caller check that state first.

`text_edit_layout` and `rewrite_block` now open a session and lay out or commit once. That leaves one code path, and their output is unchanged. There are no caches yet; the next step adds them, each under the test below.

title: M6: values typed into Password fields are written to no file (#3926)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3926.

A value typed into a text field with the **Password** flag was kept in the field's `/V` like any other value. Every file PdfCraft writes therefore held it in plain text: Save, a full rewrite (Save As ▸ optimized), Reduce File Size / Optimize PDF, and the recovery snapshots written by autosave.

**What the specification says** [spec]. ISO 32000-2:2020 §12.7.5.3, Table 231 "Field flags specific to text fields", bit 14 Password (p. 540):
- Normative: "Characters typed from the keyboard shall instead be echoed in some unreadable form, such as asterisks or bullet characters." PdfCraft already does this (`appearance.rs:447`).
- In a **note** to the same row: "To protect password confidentiality, it is imperative that PDF processors never store the value of the text field in the PDF file if this flag is set."

The second sentence is a note, so it's informative rather than a `shall`. But it is explicit and strongly worded, and this PR follows it.

**How.**
- `pdfcraft-forms` gains `has_password_values` and `clear_password_values`. The latter removes `/V` from every text field with the Password flag.
- `pdfcraft-engine` writes each file from `writable(&editor.cos)`: a copy without those values when there are any, otherwise the document itself, so there's no extra cost.
  - `save_bytes`, in both the appending and the rebased-on-last-save branches;
  - `save_full_bytes`;
  - `OptimizeJob::run`, which covers Reduce File Size and Optimize PDF;
  - `autosave_snapshots`. If the copy can't be made, no snapshot is written for that document, rather than writing the plain value.
- The open document keeps the value in memory, so scripts and the session still see it. The masked appearance (`*******`) is written as before.

title: M14: JPEG and TIFF export refuse a raster of the wrong length instead of panicking
author: Piohrun
body:
The follow-up promised on #2425, where FredApps found that a raster of the wrong length slipped through PNG export. JPEG and TIFF export had the same gap, and it turned out to be a panic as well.

## What this changes

`encode_jpeg` and `encode_tiff` composite the raster over white with `as_chunks::<4>()`, which drops a partial trailing pixel, and pass the result to encoders that trust its length. Running each case before this change:

| Raster for its size | JPEG | TIFF |
|---|---|---|
| a partial pixel at the end (1–3 bytes) | written as a valid image | written as a valid image |
| a pixel too many | **panic** | written as a valid image |
| a pixel short | **panic** | **panic** |
| empty | **panic** | error |
| a size whose byte count overflows | **panic** | error |

The JPEG panics come from `image`'s `JpegEncoder::encode`, which checks the buffer length with `assert_eq!`. The TIFF one comes from `tiff`'s `write_data`, which compares the buffer with the pixel count rather than the sample count, then slices it per strip.

The check `encode_png` gained in #2425 is now `check_raster`, and all three encoders call it first: a raster that is not exactly `width × height × 4` bytes (checked arithmetic), or has no pixels, is an error, in every format. Rendered pages are always the right size, so what Export ▸ Image, `pdfcraft-cli render` and `doc_export_images` write is unchanged; `encode_jpeg` and `encode_tiff` are public, so a caller passing a wrong buffer now gets an error instead of a crash.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-engine` (all targets)

**Tests (unit, `engine::export::raster_tests`).**

title: Reject rounded page rasters beyond the pixel budget
author: narain1
body:
## What this changes
`render_page` sizes the raster with `render_size`, which rounds each side up, but the pixel cap (`MAX_PIXELS`) was only applied to the unrounded scale. A page such as 8000.5 x 7999.5 pt rounded to 8001 x 8000 (64.008M pixels) and went on to `Pixels::zeroed`, allocating about 256 MB past the documented budget, in both normal and `reject_oversize` modes.

The final integer product is now checked against `MAX_PIXELS` before the allocation, using the existing error channel (`page N raster size WxH exceeds renderer pixel limit`). Exactly 8000 x 8000 is still allowed. Tiled requests for large pages are unaffected.

## How you verified it
- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-render`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib` (318 passed)

**Tests.** To avoid allocating hundreds of MB in a test, `Pixels::zeroed` has a `#[cfg(test)]` allocation probe that refuses and records the request. It is test-only, with no hook or counter in release code. The new tests cover: the rounded over-cap page never reaching the allocator in both modes; the exact cap still reaching it; small pages rendering with exact pixels and large pages still tiling; and invalid page or scale requests never reaching it.

I reverted the guard and confirmed `rounded_pixel_budget_rejects_before_actual_allocation` fails (`Attempts { calls: 1, first: Some((8001, 8000)) }`, expected no calls), then restored it.

title: M7: opening a paragraph leaves the page as it is until it changes
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Clicking a paragraph in Edit text & images used to change how it looked at once:
- **Until the textless background was rendered,** the editor covered the paragraph with an opaque box, white or dark for pale text (#913). On a coloured banner or a shaded table row, the background flashed to the cover's colour and back.
- **The editor then drew the text again** in its own fonts and layout, over a textless page. So even an unchanged paragraph shifted or changed face the moment it was opened.

A screen recording on a real proposal (a table and banners) shows both, and a third case:
- **A quick click** (press and release in one frame) straight from one open paragraph into another switches editors inside `page_input`. In that frame:
  - the first paragraph's textless page had already been painted, so its text disappeared;
  - the new editor's frame took the first paragraph's measured draft extent (`draft_rect`) and spanned both paragraphs.

Now an unchanged paragraph is the page's own text:
- **Textless page deferred.** `TextBackground::paint` reserves a place under the page's later shapes for the textless page, instead of painting it. The editor fills that place (`TextBackground::reveal`) only once the paragraph has changed, after this frame's typing. Until then the page raster, with its own text, shows.
- **Text invisible while unchanged.** The editor lays the text out as before for the caret and the selection, but draws it in no colour while it equals what was opened (`unseen`).
- **Cover only when needed.** The opaque cover is drawn only for a changed paragraph whose background isn't ready yet, also in a place decided after the frame's typing.
- **Frame from its own paragraph.** The editor's frame uses `draft_rect` only when it was measured for the open paragraph (`TextBackground::draft_rect_for`).

Opening a paragraph therefore draws only its frame and caret. The first keystroke switches to the textless page and the editor's text, as before.

title: perf(render): read PDFCRAFT_TEXT_DEBUG once instead of per glyph
author: narain1
body:
## What this changes
`TextDevice::draw_glyph` calls `std::env::var_os("PDFCRAFT_TEXT_DEBUG")` twice for every glyph it draws. `getenv` scans the whole process environment under a lock, so text extraction pays that cost on each glyph. The variable is now read once into a `OnceLock`. Behaviour is unchanged when the variable is unset, and when it is set the same debug lines are printed.

One caveat: the value is now fixed at the first glyph of the process, so setting the variable later in the same process has no effect. It is a debug switch read from the shell, so I think that is fine, but say if you would rather keep it dynamic.

## How you verified it
- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-render`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib` (313 passed)

**Measurement.** I found this by sampling all-page text extraction on a 391-page PDF (macOS arm64, release build): `getenv` was the single hottest leaf frame. With only this change, median all-page text extraction (15 runs, same machine, built against the revision I pin, `516caea`) went from 623 ms to 551 ms on that file (-12%), 24.0 to 20.2 ms on a 14-page file and 87.4 to 83.1 ms on a 65-page file. The extracted text and structured output were byte-identical (hashed) before and after on all three files.

**Tests.** There is no new test: this removes repeated work and does not change what is produced, and the flag is read once per process so a unit test cannot toggle it. The existing render tests cover the glyph path.

title: M14: the --control file is owner-only on Windows too, and the CLI checks it (#3922)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3922.

`pdfcraft --control FILE` writes the loopback port and a random token to `FILE`. `pdfcraft-cli ui` then reads it to drive the app: opening paths, saving, exporting, typing, taking screenshots. The doc comment, the README and AGENTS.md §3 promise an "owner-only file". On Unix that holds. On Windows it didn't:
- **App:** the staged file inherited its folder's access list. A new folder at a drive root, `C:\Users\Public` and `C:\ProgramData` let *Authenticated Users* or *Users* read what is created in them, so another signed-in user could read the token and drive the app.
- **CLI:** the owner and mode check was `#[cfg(unix)]`, so on Windows a file planted in a shared folder by another user was trusted. The CLI would then send commands, typed text included, to that user's listener.
- The README's `~/.pdfcraft-control.json` example doesn't work in cmd.exe, which doesn't expand `~`.

### How PdfCraft handles this on each system

| | macOS, Linux, FreeBSD (unchanged) | Windows (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Creating the file | Fresh staged file with a random name, `create_new`, **mode 0600**, renamed over `FILE` | Same staging. Before the token is written, the file gets an **access list of its own with only the current user and SYSTEM** (inheritance removed), and its **owner is set to that user**. If either step fails, nothing is written. |
| CLI before reading | Refuses a symlink or non-regular file. On the opened file, checks the **owner uid** and that the group/other mode bits are clear | Same symlink and regular-file checks. Then, **through the one handle the contents are read from**, reads the **owner and access list** (SDDL) and compares accounts **by SID**. Refuses a file owned by another account, or one that any account other than the user or SYSTEM may use. |
| Time of check vs. time of use | The check is on the opened file (`fstat`), and dev/inode must match the path | The handle is opened shared for reading only, so the file can't…

title: perf(render): look CFF glyph names up in a map (vendored hayro-interpret patch 44)
author: narain1
body:

`CffFontBlob::glyph_index_by_name` (vendored `hayro-interpret`) searched the whole CFF charset, with a string lookup per glyph, every time it was called. It is called for each character code of a font that maps by glyph name (`StandardKind::map_code`), and it already carried a `TODO: This is probably slow to do repeatedly?`. It now builds a name to glyph map the first time it is needed and shares it between clones of the blob.

The first glyph with a given name still wins, as it did when the charset was searched in order, so results are unchanged. This is vendored patch (44) for `hayro-interpret`, registered in `vendor/README.md` with its test.

title: fix(render): refuse Identity codes with no route to a glyph (#3529)
author: amoisttowe1
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3529.

A Type 0 font that loads, `/Encoding /Identity-H`, whose descendant CIDFont names no Adobe
character collection (`/Ordering (Identity)`, or `CIDSystemInfo` absent), and for which the file
carries no readable program: its two-byte codes number glyphs of the font named by `/BaseFont`,
and that font is not in the file. Substitution can give us a face to draw with — measured here,
the Helvetica-shaped standard stand-in — but not that font's glyph *numbering*, so such a code has
no route to any glyph. `map_code` previously fell through and used the number as a glyph index of
the stand-in, which is the mechanism behind the strings the report quotes (`AX:adeW`, `;HžMarkings`). Those
codes now draw `.notdef`, exactly as an unmapped CID in a font that is present.

The rule, not the appearance: whether anything is visible depends on what the stand-in's `.notdef`
looks like. All fourteen standard faces this build can substitute (`Helvetica` through `ZapfDingbats`,
measured) have an empty `.notdef` — a page of `<0000>` inks 0 pixels for every one of them — so the
runs come out blank, which is the "render nothing" outcome #3529 asks for. A substitute with a visible
`.notdef` would show boxes instead and still be correct by the rule.

Measured at base `606c560d` on macOS 26.6 (Apple silicon), built without craft-fonts,
every row in both states — guard present and guard removed; dark = an RGBA pixel with R, G
and B all below 128 on a 400×120 page at scale 1 (wide enough that nothing clips):

| fixture (`/Identity-H`, no program, no `/ToUnicode`)                          | before | after |

| blank page (baseline)                                                          |      0 |     0 |
| `<0030 0047 0050 0053>`, `/BaseFont /MinionPro-Regular`                       |    720 |     0 |

title: fix(engine): guard undo and redo refresh and roll back on failure (#3925)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
`Session::undo` and `Session::redo` swapped `editor.cos`, `editor.keys`, and the `undo`/`redo` stacks and then ran `Self::refresh_scoped(doc, scope)` outside `guard(...)`, without rolling back the swapped state on a panic or error. Wrap `Self::refresh_scoped` in `guard(...)` inside both `undo` and `redo`, and on any failure or panic swap `editor.cos`, `editor.keys`, and the `undo`/`redo` stacks back and re-run `Self::refresh(doc)` (falling back to `Self::show_released(doc)`) before returning the error.

### Problem
In `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, `Session::apply` wraps its refresh in `guard(...)` and rolls back `editor.cos`, `editor.keys`, and `editor.undo` if the refresh returns `Err` or panics. By contrast, `Session::undo` and `Session::redo` cleared `doc.edit_notices`, swapped `editor.cos` and `editor.keys`, pushed the previous entry onto `editor.redo` / `editor.undo`, and called `Self::refresh_scoped(doc, scope)` directly without `guard(...)`. If `refresh_scoped` panicked (for example after `release_working` replaced `doc.renderer` with an empty inline buffer) or returned `Err`, the editor state stayed swapped while `doc.info` and the renderer remained on the previous state or empty.

### Solution
- Wrap `Self::refresh_scoped(doc, scope)` in `guard(...)` in both `Session::undo` and `Session::redo`, converting any caught panic into `Err(EditError::Reopen(m))`.
- When `refreshed` is `Err(e)`, pop the pushed entry back from `ed.redo` (in `undo`) or `ed.undo` (in `redo`), restore `ed.cos` and `ed.keys`, push the entry back onto its original stack, call `Self::adopt_keys(doc)`, and run `guard(|| Self::refresh(doc))` with fallback to `Self::show_released(doc)` so `doc.info`, `doc.bytes`, `doc.display`, and `doc.renderer` stay consistent with `editor.cos`.
- Clear `doc.edit_notices`, update `doc.dirty`, and increment `doc.generation` only after the refresh succeeds.
- Add `tests::undo_and_redo_roll_back_on_a_refresh_panic_or_error` covering single-panic rollback, double…

title: M10: a symbolic TrueType font without an encoding reads its glyph names (#3962)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3962.

**The cause.** The file's body text is set in a symbolic TrueType subset with no `/Encoding` and no `/ToUnicode`. The codes are glyph positions in the Macintosh order, 29 below ASCII (`S` is 0x36), and the font's own `cmap` maps each code to the right glyph. So the page draws correctly, but both of our readers took the code itself as a character:
- **Extraction and Word export** (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/true_type.rs`, `EmbeddedKind::code_to_unicode_name`) read a code with no encoding as WinAnsi, so 0x36 became `6`.
- **The editor** (`crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs`, `unicode_map`) read it as StandardEncoding, the same `6`. Typing encoded back through that map, so it would have set the wrong glyphs too.

**What the specification says.** ISO 32000-2 §9.10.2 gives two ways to map a simple font's codes to Unicode: a ToUnicode CMap, or the glyph name the encoding selects, looked up in the Adobe Glyph List. When neither applies, "there is no way to determine what the character code represents", and the processor may choose. That is the case here.

**What this does.** Both readers now take the `post` table name of the glyph the code actually selects, through the same `cmap` lookup the renderer uses (the code, then 0xF000/0xF100/0xF200), when that name has a Unicode value. MuPDF reads this file's text the same way: on a synthetic copy of the structure below, it extracts `Solid state equipment has operational characteristics.` while pdftotext gives the shifted text.

The new reading applies only when all of these hold:
- the font is not flagged Nonsymbolic;
- it names no base encoding (a `/Differences` entry still wins for its code);
- its program is an embedded TrueType (`FontFile2`);
- the glyph's name stands for some text. Both readers apply the same Adobe Glyph List rules: drop any suffix from the first `.` (`a.ss01` reads `a`), read `_` components (a ligature gives several characters), and accept `uni` with groups of four hex digits…

title: M3: resize and move the window again right after a resize or move (Wayland)
author: bmh129
body:
## What this changes

With PdfCraft's own title bar on GNOME/Wayland (#1530), a second resize by a window edge, or a second move by the empty tab strip, now works straight after the first. Before, nothing happened until you clicked inside the window.

**Cause.** `ViewportCommand::BeginResize` and `StartDrag` hand the pointer to the compositor. On Wayland the compositor keeps the button's release, and winit reports only that the pointer left (`Event::PointerGone`), which egui deliberately doesn't count as a release. egui therefore still thought the primary button was held, and the next press on an edge or the tab strip didn't start a drag (`drag_started()` never fired). A click inside the window delivered a real press and release and reset it.

**Fix.**
- `window_controls::desktop_grab` sends the command and notes the hand-over. Edge resizing (`resize_edges`) and moving by the tab strip (`chrome.rs`) now go through it.
- `window_controls::release_after_desktop_grab`, called first in `raw_input_hook`, adds the primary button's release to the next input: once, and only if that input doesn't already bring one.
- It doesn't check the backend. Where the real release does arrive (X11, macOS), egui sees a second "released" for a button that is already up, which does nothing.

Ported from the same fix in WordCraft (`1581c288`, `window_controls.rs` is shared code between the two apps). None of the vendored winit patches is involved; the change is on the egui side.

title: M3: hand the launcher's activation token back from the first window (Linux)
author: bmh129
body:
## What this changes

Opened from the menu or dock on Linux, PdfCraft now hands the launcher's activation token back from its first window. GNOME's busy cursor clears as soon as the window appears, instead of staying for about 15 seconds, and on Wayland the window opens with keyboard focus.

**Cause.** A launcher with `StartupNotify=true` (the packaged `ai.storyteller.pdfcraft.desktop`, the RPM's and the Flatpak's) puts an activation token in the environment: `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` on Wayland, `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID` on X11. It shows a busy cursor until a window hands the token back. winit only hands a token back if the window was created with one (`WindowAttributesExtStartupNotify::with_activation_token`), and eframe 0.36.2 never gives it one and offers no way to pass it in. So the token was never used: Mutter kept the busy cursor until its timeout, and the window didn't get focus.

**Fix.** This is vendored winit patch 14, in the new `vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/startup_token.rs`, called from `Window::new` in `platform_impl/linux/mod.rs`:
- The first window the process creates without a token takes the one in the environment. The variable it reads depends on the backend.
- Later windows never take it, since the token is spent once handed back. A token given explicitly still wins, and also counts as the first window.
- An empty token, or one over 1,024 bytes, is ignored. On X11 the token is written to a window property and sent to the window manager. A huge `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID` could fail that request, and with it window creation, so PdfCraft wouldn't start.
- The variable is **left in the environment**, unlike winit's `reset_activation_token_env`. Changing the environment while other threads may read it is unsound on Linux, and PdfCraft starts threads before its first window. The cost is that processes PdfCraft starts inherit a spent token. That should be harmless: a compositor rejects a spent token, and a second X11 "remove" for the same ID does nothing.

title: M6: a document script that throws no longer stops the form's other scripts (#3940)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #3940 (item 2, custom `/C` calculations left blank; items 1 and 3 are separate, see below).

`pdfcraft_js::run` evaluated the document-level scripts in one `?` chain before the field script (`crates/js/src/lib.rs`, `run_here`). If any document-level script threw at top level, the `?` returned before the field script ran, so **every** Calculate, Format, Validate and Keystroke script in the form failed, and `js_run` failed before reaching the user's script. The form in #3940 does exactly that: its document script defines the helpers the `/C` actions call, then copies a button icon with `buttonSetIcon(buttonGetIcon())`, which PdfCraft doesn't have, so all 132 calculated fields stayed blank.

Each document-level script is now evaluated on its own. One that throws stops where it failed (what it defined before the error stays defined), the others and the field script still run, and the error is collected in a new `Outcome::doc_errors` (`document script N: <error>`) instead of failing the field script:

- the engine reports those errors with the other script errors, **once** per run rather than once per field script (the document scripts run again before every field script, so a form with 132 calculations would otherwise repeat the same line 132 times);
- `js_run` returns them as `document_errors`, so an MCP client sees which document script failed and why, as the reporter asked.

Reproduced first with a synthetic form (text field `a`, calculated `c` whose `/C` calls a document-level helper, a document script that defines the helper and then calls `buttonSetIcon`): on `main` 88dad98d, `form_fill a=21` leaves `c` empty and `js_run` fails with `TypeError: not a callable function`; the same form without the `buttonSetIcon` line gives `c = 42`.

Not in this PR:
- `app.popUpMenuEx` (item 3): #2081 implements it.
- `Field.buttonGetIcon` / `buttonSetIcon` (item 1): still missing; with this PR their absence costs only the icon copy, not the whole form…

title: M6: calculations read their notation only from a comment, and a regex after a condition as a regex
author: Piohrun
body:
The follow-up promised on #3550, for the two findings CodeRabbit raised outside its diff there, plus a third from its review here. Each was reproduced before fixing.

## What this changes

`af.rs` reads Calculate scripts for two things: what the Calculate tab shows and the form calculates (`parse_calculate`), and where a script names fields, which a rename rewrites and the calculation order reads (`calculation_sites`, `calculation_reads`). Both readers took the wrong text in three cases.

1. **Notation markers outside a comment.** Both found `BVCALC` and `EVCALC` anywhere in the script. In `var s = "BVCALC a EVCALC"; event.value = …;`, the string read as the notation `a`: a rename of `a` rewrote the string, and the field calculated as `a` instead of running the script, which never ran. The lexer now keeps the text of each comment, and the notation is read only from the first comment that holds `BVCALC` and an `EVCALC` after it, as Acrobat writes it (`/** BVCALC a + b EVCALC **/`). A line comment counts, and a block comment that never ends still runs to the end of the script. Both readers use the same `notation_range`, so the Calculate tab and a rename still agree on what a script reads.
2. **A regular expression after a condition.** A `/` after any `)` was read as division. After the condition of `if`, `while`, `for` or `with`, it starts a regular expression. So in `if (flag) /getField("a")/.test(x)`, a rename of `a` rewrote the regex. Worse, in `if (flag) /"/.test(x)` the quote started a string that hid the script's real `getField` calls, and a rename left them stale. The lexer now notes which `(` opened such a condition, and a `/` after its `)` starts a regular expression. That includes the `while` that ends a `do` loop: the loop ends at its `)`, so a `/` after it starts the next statement. A method with one of those names (`o.if(x)`) doesn't count. After any other `)`, a `/` still divides.

title: fix(automation): guard MCP dispatch and bound line and file reads (#3924)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3924.

- **Guard all MCP methods in `McpServer::handle`:** `guarded_dispatch` now wraps `self.dispatch(method, &params)` for every JSON-RPC request method rather than only `tools/call`. Tool calls continue to report caught panics in the tool result (`isError: true`) via `guarded_tool`, while resource and protocol methods (`resources/read`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `initialize`, `tools/list`, `ping`, etc.) report a JSON-RPC internal error (`-32603`) so an unexpected panic in `doc_info` or `doc_inspect` cannot terminate the server or discard unsaved session edits.
- **Bound MCP request line reads and survive non-UTF-8 lines in `McpServer::serve`:** Replaces uncapped `BufRead::lines()` with `read_line_limited` capped at `MAX_LINE_BYTES` (16 MiB) and `drain_line` (which discards the remainder of an overlong line via `fill_buf`/`consume` without buffering it in memory). Overlong lines receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` (`-32600`) reply, undecodable non-UTF-8 lines receive a `PARSE_ERROR` (`-32700`) reply, oversized line buffers are shrunk back to 64 KiB, and the server continues serving subsequent requests.

title: Clippy keeps rsa verification-only (RUSTSEC-2023-0071)
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

`deny.toml` ignores RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin: a timing side channel in RSA private-key operations, with no fixed `rsa` release). The ignore is safe only because `pdfcraft-sign` uses `rsa` to verify signatures and nothing else; private-key operations use aws-lc-rs (ADR-0009). Nothing checked that.

`clippy.toml` now disallows:

- the `rsa` types that hold a private key: `RsaPrivateKey`, the PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS signing keys, and the two decrypting keys. The wrapper types are listed because their `random()` constructors make a private key without naming `RsaPrivateKey`.
- the ways to make or use a private key without naming those types, for a key returned by another crate or used through a generic: the `RsaPrivateKey` constructors and its `decrypt`, `decrypt_blinded`, `sign` and `sign_with_rng`, the private-key methods of `rsa`'s own traits (`Decryptor::decrypt`, `RandomizedDecryptor::decrypt_with_rng`, `PaddingScheme::decrypt`, `SignatureScheme::sign`), and `rsa::hazmat::rsa_decrypt` and `rsa_decrypt_and_check`. The generic `signature` and `pkcs8` traits stay allowed, because the ECDSA keys use them too.

No code uses any of them today, and only `pdfcraft-sign` depends on `rsa`. #2772 signs RSA in the web build through Web Crypto for the same reason. If #629 ever moves signing to RustCrypto `rsa`, the ignore in `deny.toml` would have to go too, and this rule with it.

Split out of #2268, so each PR does one thing.

## How you verified it

- `cargo clippy --locked -p pdfcraft-sign --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `main` (9a0ec645): clean. `pdfcraft-annot`, which has no `rsa` dependency, is also clean, so the paths don't warn in crates that can't resolve them.

title: fix: Issue #4017. Flattening removes empty fields it cannot draw
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Fixes #4017
 
**Bug.** `doc_flatten` with `fields: true` left text fields that had no value and no appearance stream in `/AcroForm /Fields` and on the page. The flattened file could therefore still be filled in.
 
**Why.** Flatten keeps every widget without an appearance so its value is not lost with nothing drawn in its place (#1794). A field with no value has nothing to lose but it was kept too.
 
**Fix.** A widget without an appearance now stays only when its field has a value. That is its `/V` or the nearest one inherited through `/Parent` (bounded walk with a seen-set). A missing value or an empty string or an empty array counts as no value. Comments and valued widgets behave as before.

title: M10: odd and even pages are page numbers, as Acrobat counts them (#3984)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3984: with the range `4–11` and **Even pages only**, printing started at page 5.

`print::range::narrow` kept the odd or even *places* in the chosen pages (the first one chosen counted as "odd"), and its doc comment said Acrobat does the same. Acrobat counts **page numbers**. Odd and even now keep the pages whose number is odd or even, for a typed range, picked thumbnails and the current page alike, in the order given; Reverse turns that round.

| Range, Even pages only | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `4–11` | 5, 7, 9, 11 | 4, 6, 8, 10 |
| `3–11` | 4, 6, 8, 10 | 4, 6, 8, 10 |
| `2, 7–10` (Acrobat's example) | 7, 9 | 2, 8, 10 |

### Basis

Adobe's published manuals, by title, the "Last updated" date printed on their pages, and printed page:

- *Adobe Acrobat DC Help* (last updated 11/28/2019), Printing ▸ Options in the Print dialog box ▸ Pages to Print, p. 515: "Odd Or Even Pages Choose which pages to print: All Pages In Range, Odd Pages Only, or Even Pages Only. For example, if you set the range to 2, 7–10 and choose Even Pages Only, only pages 2, 8, and 10 print."
- *Using Adobe Acrobat 9 Pro* (last updated 9/30/2011), Options in the Print dialog box, p. 413: "Selecting Odd Pages Only or Even Pages Only affects which pages in a range print. For example, in a range that includes 2, 7–10 with Even Pages Only selected, only pages 2, 8, and 10 will print."

The header/footer/watermark page ranges (`marks_ui`) and Extract's odd/even filter in #3729 already count page numbers, so this also makes the three agree.
