title: M7: letters a TrueType subset dropped take another font, whatever its /Widths says
author: komo1iddin
body:
Fixes #4038.

## What this changes

For a simple font, `Metrics::has_glyph` took a nonzero `/Widths` entry as the glyph being there. Some producers write a subset TrueType font with a width for every code from 32 to 126, the dropped glyphs' too. An edit that added such a letter then encoded it in the subset (`Metrics::encode` succeeded, so `source_encodes` reused the font), and the letter drew as a `.notdef` box.

Composite subsets already ask their program (`cids_with_outlines`, #2153). Now simple subsets do too:
- **`codes_with_glyphs`** reads a subset simple font's embedded sfnt program (`FontFile2`, or an OpenType `FontFile3`) once. It marks each code (0–255) whose glyph the program has. The glyph is looked up the way the renderer does, and in a TrueType program it must have an outline, unless the code shows white space. A subsetter either drops a glyph or leaves it empty.
- **`simple_glyph`** is that lookup: the encoding's character in the Unicode cmap, else the code in a symbolic cmap. It is moved out of `embedded_widths`, which now shares it.
- **`has_glyph`** also needs the code's bit when the font has that set. A space (code 32) is kept as before.

Without a readable sfnt program (bare CFF, Type 1, none) nothing changes.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

title: M9: remote (server-side) signing with an OTP — CSC API and Aruba ARSS
author: Emerald313
body:
## What this changes

Adds remote signing: the key stays at a signing service (a QTSP's "firma remota" / cloud
signature), authorised per signature with a one-time password. This is how most Italian and
many EU qualified signatures are used today, and it is what #2596 asks for. Proposed there
first: https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/2596#issuecomment-6314557696

- **Only a digest leaves the machine.** PdfCraft writes the PDF, the ByteRange and the CMS
  locally, as for every other digital ID. The service receives only the SHA-256/384 of the
  CMS signed attributes, through the existing `ExternalKey` trait (`crates/sign/src/remote/`).
  Every signature the service returns is checked against the certificate's key before it is
  embedded, so a wrong or foreign signature is never written.
- **Two protocols:**
  - the **Cloud Signature Consortium API**, v2 (2.0–2.2) with the v1 dialect tolerated:
    `info`, `auth/login` (HTTP Basic), `credentials/list|info`, `getChallenge`/`sendOTP`,
    `credentials/authorize` (with `authorizeCheck` polling), `signatures/signHash`,
    `auth/revoke`. Auth objects and `auth/expression` (AND/OR/XOR) are honoured;
  - **Aruba's ARSS** `signhash` (SOAP, public WSDL), which Aruba's remote signatures use
    instead of CSC.
- **Network stays opt-in and outside the libraries.** `sign`, `engine`, `automation` and
  `ui-egui` contain no network code. The transport is a trait the caller injects, like
  `TimestampAuthority`. The HTTPS implementation lives in `pdfcraft-platform` behind a new
  `https` feature, on the `ureq` + rustls + `rustls-native-certs` stack that Help ▸ Check
  for updates already uses (no new crates in `Cargo.lock`). Only the desktop app and
  `pdfcraft-cli run` wire it; `pdfcraft-cli mcp` only with `--remote-signing`; `batch` never.
  A connection is made only when the user adds a remote account or signs with one. HTTPS
  only (plain HTTP only to loopback), the OS's trusted roots, no redirects, responses
  capped …

author: Ridzzz0Alam

Refs #3929 (three of its eight items. The UI items stay open)

title: fix: Issue #4018, form_fill warns when a value does not fit its field (#4018)
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Fixes #4018
 
**Bug.** With a fixed font size in a text field's `/DA` the `form_fill` tool saved the whole value but the appearance cut it at the edge of the box. The result only said `"filled": n`. A person sees the cut but an agent filling forms through the CLI or MCP did not.
 
**Why.** The appearance builder laid the text out and clipped it but nothing reported it. `form_fill` already warns about characters the font cannot draw and a cut-off value is the same kind of silent loss.
 
**Fix.**
- The text appearance builder (`forms::appearance`) notes when the text it lays out does not fit. That means one line wider than the box or wrapped lines whose descent falls below it. It uses the same layout it draws with so nothing is measured twice. `field_appearance_drawn` keeps its signature and output.
- `forms::appearance::value_overflow` asks that for one widget and `engine::Document::field_overflow` asks it for a field by name.
- `form_fill` adds a `warnings` entry for each filled field that is cut off. For example `form field "single_12pt" (page 1): the value does not fit: 200.76 pt wide at 12 pt, room for 136 pt, so the box shows only part of it (the whole value is saved)`.
- Auto-sized fields (`0 Tf`) shrink to fit and are not reported unless they hit the 4 pt minimum and still do not fit.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-forms`, `-engine` and `-automation`
- [x] tests pass: `pdfcraft-forms` (140) plus the form/field tests in `pdfcraft-engine` and `pdfcraft-automation`

title: M10.5: print through the macOS system print dialog
author: fitb-greg
body:
## What this changes

On macOS, the Print dialog offers **System print dialog…** in the printer list, between the printers and Save as PDF. Print composes the print-ready PDF exactly as for a printer: pages, sizing, Multiple/Booklet/Poster/Label, comments and forms. It then hands that PDF to macOS's own print panel. From there the person reaches what PdfCraft's dialog does not offer: the PDF menu (PDF services such as fax workflows, Open in Preview, Save to iCloud; see #2157), presets, and the driver's own panes.

- **Dialog:** with the choice selected, Copies, Two-sided and Properties… are disabled, as for the browser's print dialog, and a hint says the system dialog chooses them. PdfCraft's dialog closes at once. The progress card shows "Waiting for the system print dialog…" until the panel closes, then a notice says *Printed through the system print dialog*, *Cancelled*, or the error.
- **How it opens the panel:** `crates/print/src/system_dialog.rs` writes the PDF to an owner-only (`0600`, `create_new`) temporary file. It runs `/usr/bin/osascript -` with a short AppleScriptObjC script on stdin, which uses PDFKit's `printOperationForPrintInfo:scalingMode:autoRotate:` with `kPDFPrintPageScaleNone` and `showsPrintPanel`. The temporary file is removed whatever happens. The answer (`printed` / `cancelled` / `error: …`) is read defensively: a non-zero exit is never success, and stderr is capped.
- **Automation:** `printers` now reports `system_dialog` (true on macOS), and `doc_print` accepts `printer: "system-dialog"`, returning `system_dialog: printed|cancelled`. The names match the Flatpak portal PR #3066 so the two compose.
- **Other platforms:** nothing changes; the choice is not offered.

Helps with #2157 (macOS PDF Services) without closing it: PDF services are reachable through the system dialog, not listed in PdfCraft's own printer list.

title: fix(comments): thread replies by their /IRT reference, count comments like Acrobat
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

Comment replies were filed under their parent by the parent's `/NM`, matched across the whole document. `/NM` need not be unique, and PyMuPDF names the first comment on every page `fitz-A0`. On a 48-page review written that way by PyMuPDF (28 comments, 16 replies), every reply landed under page 1's comment, and the other pages showed none.

The Comments header comment count also disagreed with Acrobat. It counted comments and replies together, 28 + 16 = 44, where Acrobat counts only the comments and says 28.

The attached PDF is the file that was used for the manual user testing. 
[EU_AI_Education_Guidelines_2026_annotated.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33819539/EU_AI_Education_Guidelines_2026_annotated.pdf)

**Comment Threading**
- A reply now finds its parent through `/IRT`, the reference that points at the parent object, instead of through the parent's name. The parent is stored as its page and its position in `/Annots`.
- Both places that read comments do this: `inspect`, when a file opens, and `pdfcraft_annot::summaries`, after each edit.
- Everything that shows threads uses the result: the Comments panel, comment properties, the canvas context menu, the engine's comment summary and `comment_list`.
- Replies to replies now show in the panel, under the comment the thread starts from. Before, the panel didn't show them at all (#806/#839 fixed this only for `comment_list`).
- Some `/IRT`s point at nothing usable: the annotation itself, a loop, a pop-up, or an object no page lists. Such an annotation now shows as a normal comment. Before, it was hidden everywhere but still counted.

**Header**

title: ui: preview Times in Tinos so the editor, font picker and Header & Footer show the real face
author: homeass
body:
Picked during Korean font testing: the in-place paragraph editor, the Add-content font picker and the Header & Footer preview draw Times and Helvetica **identically** — the UI ships only proportional (Inter) + monospace faces, so the family a user chooses never appears until the text is committed.

This adds **Tinos** (Steve Matteson, metric-compatible with Times New Roman) as the serif UI face and routes `Times` to it in all three places, including its bold and italic variants. Because Tinos is metric-compatible, the editor's wrap preview now matches the committed Standard-14 Times output.

- Assets (§1.5): four static TTFs from `google/fonts`' `ofl/tinos` + the canonical OFL text from the author repo (google/fonts **relicensed Tinos from Apache-2.0 to OFL-1.1** and moved it `apache/→ofl/`; METADATA.pb confirms `license: "OFL"`; not Adobe-derived, so §1.1/§1.2 hold). One ATTRIBUTION.toml entry per font; `cargo xtask assets` green; ATTRIBUTION.md regenerated, not hand-edited.
- `theme.rs`: `serif` / `serif-bold` / `serif-italic` / `serif-bold-italic` registered exactly like `semibold` (Tinos first, then the same fallback stack).
- `edit_text_ui.rs`: shared `preview_family(family, bold, italic)`; `editor_font` calls it. Helvetica italic still previews upright (Inter has no oblique) — unchanged behavior, now named in the code.
- `marks_ui.rs` + `format_text_ui.rs`: the header/footer preview and the picker's own labels use the same mapping, so the picker shows serif/sans/mono at a glance.

Tests: `the_serif_families_are_registered_and_resolve`, `the_editor_font_follows_family_weight_and_slant`. Gates: fmt · clippy `-D warnings` · `pdfcraft-ui-egui` 542 lib + 92 integration all pass · `xtask assets` / `layers` · `cargo check --locked -p pdfcraft`.

title: M12: --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root may be repeated (#4022)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4022.

`pdfcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root` and `--automation-write-root` can now each be given more than once (`--flag DIR` or `--flag=DIR`, mixed freely), so one session can read from a project folder and a shared assets folder without widening the root to their common parent. - **A bad folder anywhere in the list stops the server** (missing, not a folder, empty), never a root silently left out.

- **`text_font_files` without `directories`** searches every read root instead of the first.
- **Font discovery accepts up to 4096 roots**, with a separate allowance for 4096 descendant entries, instead of an independent 16-root cut. Explicit roots are resolved; descendant symlinks are skipped. Main’s deterministic ordering, face/content deduplication, accepted-font byte budget and separate read-byte allowance are preserved.
- API: `AutomationRoots::with_folders(&[PathBuf], &[PathBuf])`, `read_roots()` / `write_roots()`; `new(Option, Option)` still works and delegates.

title: M9: visible signatures read upright on rotated pages
author: vjeko2404
body:
## What this changes

A visible digital signature (Digitally sign / Certify, the `sign_document` tool) placed on a page with `/Rotate` was drawn in user space, so its graphic and details turned with the page. Scanners often store pages landscape with `/Rotate 270` so they display portrait. On those, the signature (stamp image plus "Digitally signed by …") came out sideways, while the page itself looked correct. Stamps (#1398) and Fill & Sign marks (#2392) were already fixed for this. Digital signatures were not, and I found no existing issue or PR for it.

Now, in `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs`:

- **New signature field on a turned page:** the widget gets `/MK /R` equal to the page rotation (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.19). The rotation is read through `pdfcraft_model::pages`, so an inherited `/Rotate` counts too.
- **Appearance:** laid out in the box as displayed (sides swapped for a quarter turn), with a `/Matrix` from `pdfcraft_model::view_matrix_for`. That maps the box exactly onto `/Rect` (§12.5.5), the same convention `pdfcraft-forms` uses for `/MK /R`.
- **Existing field:** signing it follows that field's own `/MK /R`. A field without one is drawn exactly as before.
- **Pages that aren't turned:** the same appearance as before, with no `/MK` and no `/Matrix`.

One new dependency: `pdfcraft-sign` → `pdfcraft-model` (L4 → L2; `cargo xtask layers` passes).

title: fix(js): bound sandbox memory growth and check runtime-compiled source (#4001)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary

Hardens the JavaScript sandbox in `crates/js` (`lib.rs` and `xfa.rs`) against unbounded memory growth and unchecked runtime-compiled scripts:

- **Runtime-compiled source checks (`eval` / `Function`):** Installs `SandboxHooks` (`boa_engine::context::HostHooks`) on both AcroForm and XFA JavaScript contexts. `ensure_can_compile_strings` checks parameter and body lengths against `MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES` before converting to host strings and applies `refuse()` to each parameter, the function body, and the combined function signature + body.
- **Buffer and intrinsic string/array bounds:** Caps `HostHooks::max_buffer_size` to `16 MiB` (`MAX_BUFFER_BYTES`) and bounds `String.prototype.repeat`, `String.prototype.padStart`, `String.prototype.padEnd`, `Array.prototype.join`, and `Array.prototype.toLocaleString` to `MAX_STRING_UNITS` (`4 MiB` UTF-16 code units) and `MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH` (`1 << 20` elements) so oversized allocations throw `RangeError` before allocating.
- **Host-side copy bounds:** Bounds `text()` conversions to `MAX_STRING_UNITS` before allocating a Rust `String`, caps cumulative UTF-8 bytes in `strings()` to `MAX_HOST_BYTES` (`1 MiB`), and caps AcroForm `Host` (`alerts`, `console`, `requests`) and XFA `XHost` (`console`, `LaunchUrl`, `ResetData`) by item count, line length (`xfa::clip`), and total retained bytes (`MAX_HOST_BYTES`).

Closes #4001

## Verification

- Added unit and child-process regression tests (`runtime_compiled_source_and_host_copies_are_bounded` and `sandbox_memory_and_eval_limits_hold_in_child_process`) in `crates/js/src/tests.rs`.
- Verified `cargo test -p pdfcraft-js` (55 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-js --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.

title: Stamps follow the interface language, in every script
author: StephanePERREUX
body:
## Summary
- The stamp palette (Add a stamp) shows the stamps in the interface language, e.g. `CONFIDENTIEL` instead of `CONFIDENTIAL` when the UI is French, and stamps are placed in it.
- Labels and dynamic "By … at …" lines in 36 languages: every interface language, plus European Portuguese (`pt-pt`, automation only).
  - Latin script (French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Catalan, Norwegian Bokmål, Finnish, Indonesian, Czech, Polish, Slovenian, Turkish, Lithuanian, Albanian, Romanian, Hungarian): Helvetica text; letters WinAnsi lacks (č ř ł ő ş ț …) use Helvetica's own glyphs through a per-stamp `/Differences` encoding.
  - Other scripts (Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian, Kazakh, Greek, Vietnamese, Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Korean, Arabic, Central Kurdish, Persian, Thai, Hindi, Telugu, Lao): glyph outlines, filled, marked with `/ActualText`. New `pdfcraft_fonts::line_outline` splits a line into bidi runs (UAX #9) and face pieces and shapes each with harfrust (already a dependency): conjuncts, joining forms, marks, right to left.
- Faces: the bundled Inter draws Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese in every build. The other scripts use craft-fonts faces when the build has them (`CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`).
- Without the faces: the UI places the stamp in English (`StampLang::for_interface`), the automation `comment_add` refuses the `lang` with a message naming craft-fonts, and a stamp drawn by a build that had them keeps its artwork (it can't be restyled there rather than be redrawn in another language).

title: A number set across a vertical column belongs to it (#3711)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Split out of #3812 at review request, and **stacked on it** — this needs that PR's column detection.

縱中橫 (tate-chu-yoko): a number in vertical CJK is usually set *across* the column — 「2026年10月21日」 — so its digits are horizontal glyphs among vertical ones. Split by writing direction, they became a flow of their own, written out before or after all the vertical text: a drag down the column missed them, and a drag that began on them selected another part of the page.

```
before   第12 頁        the number is a flow of its own, with a gap read as a space
after    第12頁
```

`across_in_columns` finds the horizontal runs that sit inside a column and gives each glyph a box in the column's own frame, so the run joins the column at its own height instead of becoming a flow. A run belongs to a column when it is centred on it, no wider than 2.5 of its width, no taller than 1.4, beside one of the column's own characters, and at most `MAX_ACROSS` (4) glyphs — two to four digits is what 縱中橫 is for, and a longer run beside a column is text of its own.

The slot the run is laid out in is the hole between the characters above and below it, so no gap is left at either end for the layout to read as a word space.

### Tests

`a_number_set_across_a_vertical_column_stays_in_it` builds the fixture through the real pipeline (`extract_page`) and pins:

- `2026年10月21日出版` and `第12頁共有三段` as the two columns, with a heading above them unaffected;
- a search across the join (`年10月`) matching once, with one highlight down the column;
- a drag over the page copying the columns right to left;
- and the negative case: `年\n月\n12` — a number centred in a *large* gap, which is not part of the column — stays three lines.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

### From the #3812 review

`placed` is a `HashMap` from glyph index to box, not a list scanned per glyph (`placed.iter().find`, `joined.contains`): a page can hold as many of these runs as it has columns.

title: Build each crate's integration tests as one binary
author: aiongg
body:
Every `tests/*.rs` file builds into its own executable that links the whole crate graph, so a debug test build writes tens of GB. This moves each crate's integration tests into `tests/it/` as modules of one `tests/it/main.rs`.

- Nine crates get one `it` binary: pdfcraft, pdfcraft-cli, automation, cos, crypt, engine, render, sign, ui-egui. Crates with a single test file keep it as it is.
- Test executables: 150 → 52 (37 unit, 15 integration), 2.17 GB in total.
- ui-egui `perf.rs` keeps its own process: its frame-time budgets would be measured beside other tests.
- The GPU tests share one lock now that they run in one process. Five files had their own `static GPU` mutex. `the_drop_line_shows_in_front_of_the_first_tab` rendered without one.
- Path fixes the move needs: `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`/`#[path]` gain one `../`, `mod support` becomes `use crate::support`, and the Linux-only `winit_wayland_scroll` module that compiles vendored winit source lives in `main.rs`. Docs, READMEs and ATTRIBUTION name the new paths (`--test it <filter>`).

Testing: `cargo test --workspace` passes 4,445 tests with 16 ignored, the same per crate as CI on 80b7d2152. clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, `xtask parity` and `xtask assets` pass.

title: fix: Part of #3504, not "Fixes", Text extraction says when the content budget cut a page.
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Part of #3504 and not a full Fix.
 
**Bug.** When a page's content inflates past the renderer's budget (256 MiB or 64× the compressed size) the renderer stops reading it and reports `ContentTruncated`. `pdfcraft-cli render` prints that warning but text extraction threw it away. `pdfcraft-cli text` printed the text before the cut with no warning. The tools `text_extract` and `text_find` and the search-based `redact_mark` treated the partial text as the whole page. A search redaction could report success while the text past the cut was never marked. The editor and the redaction apply step still read that text.
 
**Fix.**
- `PageText` gets `truncated`. The renderer sets it (in `finish`) when the cut happened so the flag survives the automation page-text cache.
- `pdfcraft-cli text` prints the same warning as `render`.
- `text_extract` and `redact_mark` (find and words and pattern) add a warning naming the page. `text_find` counts the page in `warning_count` and is no longer `complete`.
- A page within budget is unchanged.
**Not covered.** This does not make the readers use one cap. The renderer stops at 256 MiB per page while the `cos` readers allow 1 GiB per stream and that is a design call. The app's Find and export and word count (`filtered_text`) and the engine's other text readers do not show the cut yet. The `parity/` note says so.
 
## How you verified it
 
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-render`, `-automation`, `-cli` and `-ui-egui`
- [x] tests pass on `pdfcraft-render`, `pdfcraft-automation` and `pdfcraft-cli`

title: Attachments: a saved attachment keeps the PDF's Mark-of-the-Web on Windows (#3990)
author: mmmaarian03-crypto
body:
Fixes #3990.

## The problem

Save in the attachments panel wrote the file with no `Zone.Identifier` stream. An embedded file from a PDF that arrived by email or from a browser became a trusted local file to SmartScreen, Office's Protected View and the internet-macro block.

## The change

- New `pdfcraft_platform::zone::mark_from(target, source)`: gives `target` the source PDF's own `Zone.Identifier` (copied as it is, up to 64 KiB, when it reads as a zone), or the Internet zone (`ZoneId=3`) when the PDF has none or isn't a file. It is a plain alternate-data-stream write with no `unsafe`, and a no-op off Windows.
- `attachment_action` calls it after the atomic write. Best effort: on a volume without alternate data streams (FAT32, exFAT, some network shares) the save still succeeds, unmarked, as before.
- Parity: `view.attachments-panel` cites the new test.

Not in this PR: macOS `com.apple.quarantine`, and Open on a PDF attachment, which opens it in a tab without writing a file.

## Checked (Windows 11 x64)

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-platform zone`: no zone, a copied zone, and a stream that isn't a zone or is too large.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test pickers attachment`: the new `a_saved_attachment_carries_the_documents_zone` (a PDF opened from a file with a zone, from a local file, and from bytes) fails without the change; the existing attachment tests still pass.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-platform -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask parity`.

Fixes #4076.
 
**Bug.** The desktop app's argument loop took `--help` as a view setting called `help` (and swallowed the next argument as its value) and took `-h` as a file to open. Both started the window so a scripted `pdfcraft --help` never returned.

title: M5: a callout's arrow point, knee and text box change on their own (#1152)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1152. A selected callout now has handles on its three parts, as the issue asks. The behaviour follows what Acrobat does, observed in Acrobat Pro DC (a 2021 Continuous release) with synthetic files (numbers below), and Acrobat DC Help (PDF edition, "Last updated 11/28/2019"), p. 357: "Callout text boxes have three parts: a text box, a knee line, and an end-point line. You can resize each part by dragging a handle. The knee line can be resized in one direction only".

- **Arrow point and knee handles.** Dragging the arrow point moves it alone. Dragging the knee moves it along its knee line only (level knee lines sideways, upright ones up and down). It can be lengthened, and it stops 12 pt from the box.
- **Text box resize handles.** The eight handles sit on the text box (`/Rect` inset by `/RD`), not on `/Rect`, which also holds the leader line. While the side the line meets stays where it is, the line doesn't change.
- **Moving.** Dragged from inside, the box moves alone: the arrow point stays and the knee comes along. Dragged by its leader line, the whole callout moves.
- **Laying the line out again.** When the side the line meets is moved, or the knee is dragged into the box, the line meets the middle of the side facing the arrow point, with a 12 pt knee line.
- **New callouts** get Acrobat's knee line: 12 pt, level, out from the middle of the side facing the arrow point. This applies to the Callout tool and to `comment_add` without `knee`.
- **Preview.** While a part is dragged, the line is drawn to where it will meet the box.
- **Engine and automation.** `set_points` (`Edit::ReshapeAnnotation`, `comment_edit` `points`) takes a callout's arrow point and optional knee. `comment_list` gives a callout's `points` and `text_box`. `comment_edit` `rect` resizes its text box. Each change is one undo step.

title: fix(print): M10 — Windows ya no cambia las letras de las fuentes TrueType incrustadas (#3132)
author: j7121994
body:
## Qué cambia

Al imprimir desde PdfCraft en Windows, el texto de las fuentes TrueType incrustadas como subconjunto salía con las letras cambiadas, aunque en pantalla y en el PDF de impresión todo estaba bien. Este PR lo corrige: antes de entregar el trabajo a la cola de Windows, cada programa TrueType u OpenType incrustado recibe un nombre que ninguna fuente instalada tiene. Fixes #3132.

### El error

Un subconjunto incrustado vuelve a numerar sus glifos. ReportLab, por ejemplo, numera los de Arial por orden de código: en el subconjunto normal el espacio es el glifo 11 y en el negrita el 8, mientras que en la Arial instalada es el 3. El camino de impresión de Windows (Windows.Data.Pdf dibujando en el print control de Direct2D, a través de craft-print) conserva los números de glifo del subconjunto, pero los dibuja con **la fuente instalada que se llama igual**. Cada letra sale entonces como el glifo de la Arial del sistema que tiene ese número:

| Texto (fuente) | Impreso |
|---|---|
| `Revisión de clientes,` (Arial Bold) | `Wj{nxn s%ij%hqnjsyjx1` |
| `insolvencias y fianzas` (Arial Bold) | `nsxtq{jshnfx%~%knfsÄfx` |

title: fix(edit): setting a paragraph's width no longer panics on text larger than a page
author: Matoo125
body:
## What this changes

`rewrite_block` clamps a requested paragraph width between the text's size in user space (`size * k`) and the largest page PDF allows (14 400 pt), in `crates/edit/src/text.rs`. `f64::clamp` panics when its minimum is the larger, so text set above 14 400 pt crashed the app as soon as its paragraph was given a width. The size can come from the file (`/F 20000 Tf`, or `1 Tf` scaled up by `Tm`) or from the request (the automation tools pass `size` through).

The lower bound is now capped at 14 400 pt too: `w.clamp((size * k).min(14_400.0), 14_400.0)`. Such a paragraph gets the widest width allowed, and `f64::min` also turns a NaN size into the cap. Nothing else changes for text below 14 400 pt.

title: fix(cos): one decode budget per page walk, so repeated stream references cannot multiply decoding
author: aiongg
body:
## What this changes

`MAX_DECODED` bounds one decode, but most page walks gave every `/Contents` entry and every form XObject occurrence a fresh allowance. A small file whose `/Contents` names one compressed stream thousands of times, or whose forms draw one form thousands of times, made these walks decode and keep gigabytes. Eleven findings across nine crates share this root cause, so this PR adds one shared bound and uses it everywhere.

**The shared bound.** `pdfcraft_cos::DecodeBudget` holds what one operation may still decode: a cumulative decoded-byte allowance, a form-entry counter and a seen-set of stream refs. Every decode in the operation is charged to it (`decode`, `decode_strict`, `decode_within(max)`, `decode_contents`). A decode that runs past the remaining allowance spends all of it, so a bomb referenced many times is inflated once. `DecodeBudget::page()` is 256 MiB decoded (`MAX_PAGE_DECODED`) and 50,000 form entries (`MAX_PAGE_FORMS`). Unit test: `budget::tests::repeated_references_share_one_allowance`.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| 733e38bfa | `DecodeBudget` |
| 92ab0e932 | A spent budget reports its whole allowance in the error |
| ea4939cd0 | `decode_strict`, charged to the budget |
| 735c80c6c | `decode_within(max)`: a per-stream bound inside the shared one |

**The callers.** Each regression test is a unit test in the crate's `src/tests.rs` (or the named module) and was seen failing with its fix reverted. The optimize, print direction and edit image-record tests were first run against the old signatures and then adapted to the new ones.

Thirteen places in nine crates let a small file make PdfCraft decode, parse or keep far more than the file holds. They fall into three groups:

title: test(sign): serialize the Keychain search-list tests
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

Before: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign --test it keychain -- --ignored` ran the two Keychain tests in parallel. Each saves the user's keychain search list, changes it and restores what it saved, so one could undo the other's temporary keychain, or put back a keychain the other had already deleted (CodeRabbit's comment on #3716).

After: a shared lock runs them one at a time. With the lock alone, `keychain_identities_carry_their_issuers` still failed about one run in ten when it ran second. The Security framework caches the search list in the process and picks up `security list-keychains` asynchronously, so `keychain::find` did not see the new keychain yet. The test now waits up to five seconds for the identity to appear.

The issuer test also failed on every run after the first for a while: trustd remembers which keychain file it found an issuer in, and each run used a new path (with the process id) and deleted it, so the next run's evaluation looked in the deleted file and got an empty chain. The test keychain now lives at one fixed path, and a copy left by a killed run is deleted first.

The review fixes restore the search list before deleting the keychain and fail the test when restoring it doesn't succeed.

Only test code changes.

title: Fix: a pen on Wayland opens the window through Xwayland (#3650)
author: mgaux-dev
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3650.

winit 0.30 doesn't support the Wayland tablet protocol (`zwp_tablet_v2`), so the compositor decides what a pen does in the window. On KDE Plasma a hovering pen moves the cursor but its tip never clicks; on Hyprland (#3650) it does nothing at all. Xwayland supports the protocol itself and hands X clients the pen as a pointer, so through Xwayland the pen hovers, clicks and draws. PhotoCraft makes the same choice.

At startup (`apps/pdfcraft/src/pen_display.rs`), the event loop is built with winit's X11 backend (`EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11` through eframe's `event_loop_builder`) only when all of these hold:

- winit would use Wayland (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` or `WAYLAND_SOCKET` set);
- `PDFCRAFT_NATIVE_WAYLAND` is unset, empty or `0`;
- a pen is attached: `/proc/bus/input/devices` lists a device with `BTN_TOOL_PEN` **and** absolute X/Y axes (the key alone isn't enough, since a uinput virtual keyboard can claim every key code);
- `DISPLAY` is a local display (`:N` or `:N.S`) whose socket `/tmp/.X11-unix/XN` exists;
- the libraries winit loads for X11 are installed (looked for in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and the usual library directories, then in `ldconfig -p`).

The last two are checked because winit allows one event loop per process: an X11 start that failed couldn't fall back to Wayland, and the app wouldn't open at all. If they can't be confirmed, the window stays on Wayland, as before, and a warning is logged. The choice is made once, so the OpenGL retry opens on the same display server. Other platforms are unchanged.

Still missing: pen pressure (winit's X11 backend doesn't read it, so ink is a fixed width), and a pen plugged in after launch only takes effect at the next launch.

title: M5: review statuses are hidden, chain and show per reviewer, as in Acrobat (#4122)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4122.

Review statuses now follow ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.3: a state belongs to one user, a user's next change replies to their previous state reply, and PdfCraft shows one status per reviewer.

**Writing** (`crates/annot`):
- Status replies (`/StateModel /Review`) are written with the **Hidden** flag (`/F 30`, Table 167 bit 2). A state reply records a state, not a note (§12.5.6.3: "The state is not specified in the annotation itself but in a separate text annotation"), so it is not drawn as a note icon or listed as an ordinary reply.
- A reviewer's next change replies to **their previous state reply**, not to the comment. §12.5.6.3 requires this: "Additional state changes shall be made by adding text annotations in reply to the previous reply for a given user." Checkmarks (`/StateModel /Marked`) chain the same way. Another reviewer, or the other state model, starts its own chain on the comment.

**Reading** (`ReviewStates` in `crates/render`, used everywhere states are shown):
- A state reply belongs to the comment its `/IRT` chain reaches past earlier state replies. Loops and chains longer than 64 belong to nothing.
- `statuses(c)` gives each reviewer's latest status, in the order they first set one. A status set back to None stays listed: None is a state of its own (Table 174).
- `marked_by(c, author)` is that reviewer's own checkmark. `marked(c)` lists who has one on.

**Where it shows**:
- **Comments panel**: one badge per reviewer with their name, for example "Bob: Rejected", and a None badge for a status set back to None.
  - The status filter hides a comment only when every reviewer's status is hidden. A comment with no status counts as None.
  - The checkmark button, the "…" menu and the checkmark filter use the current author's checkmark (Preferences ▸ Commenting author), since Marked is a state of the user who set it (Table 174).
  - Status text stays searchable.
- **The comment's right-click menu** on the page uses the current au…

title: Accessibility: set a table's Summary and a header cell's Scope (#4103, #4104)
author: pat26-dotcom
body:
## What this changes

`accessibility_set_tag_property` takes two more properties:

- `summary` on Table tags: the table's `Summary` attribute (Fixes #4103).
- `scope` on TH tags: `Row`, `Column` or `Both` (Fixes #4104).

Both are Table attributes, so they are written into the tag's attribute object with `/O /Table`
in `/A`, not into the tag dictionary:

- An existing Table attribute object is edited in place in `/A`; other attribute objects (e.g.
  `/O /Layout`) and the revision numbers that follow them in an `/A` array stay as they are.
- Without one, a new `<< /O /Table … >>` is added (as `/A` itself, or appended to the array).
- An attribute object reached by reference is copied into the tag's own `/A` before it is edited,
  so other tags sharing that object keep their value.
- Clearing removes the key; an attribute object left with only `/O` goes, and so does an `/A`
  left empty.
- The tag's type is checked after the role map (a `/MyTable` mapped to `/Table` takes a summary).
  Wrong tag types and other scope values are rejected with an error.

`accessibility_tags` (and `pdfcraft_engine::a11y::tags`) now also lists `summary` and `scope`.
Undo works as for the other properties ("Change tag properties").

A correction to #4104 as I filed it: `table-headers` reports tables *without* header cells, which
is fixed by changing a cell's type to TH (already possible). `Scope` doesn't change that rule;
it tells assistive technology which cells a header applies to, which PDF/UA-1 expects of a TH
in a table that doesn't use `Headers`/`ID` (Matterhorn checkpoint 15-003).

title: fix(sign): judge a page's indirect /Annots array by the annotations it gains
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

When a page's `/Annots` is an object of its own (`/Annots 12 0 R`), adding a signature widget or a comment in a later revision updates that array in place and leaves the page dictionary unchanged. The validator classified the changed array as "other changes", so **countersigning such a document made every earlier signature show as invalid**.

This is common in real files: a multi-signer contract from a Brazilian signing service had 4 of its 9 signatures reported invalid, although each one's digest verifies and every later revision only adds a signature field. PdfCraft hits it on its own output too: sign a PDF whose page has an indirect `/Annots` twice, and the first signature turns invalid.

A changed array that was a signed page's `/Annots` is now judged like an inline `/Annots`, by the annotations it gained (signature, form fill or comments, via the existing `added_annots`), under the same DocMDP rules. It still has to have been that page's array in the signed revision, so a later revision cannot name some other object as `/Annots` to slip a change through.

I searched open and closed issues and PRs and found nothing on this. #3440 reworks the same function; I built its branch and it does not cover this case (the repro still reports the first signature invalid there). The change is small, so whichever lands first, the other rebases easily.

title: fix(sign): let an LTV update declare the ESIC extension in the catalog
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

PAdES LTV writers add the `/DSS` and, in the same revision, declare the ESIC developer extension in the catalog: `/Extensions << /ESIC << /BaseVersion /1.7 /ExtensionLevel 2 >> >>` (ISO 32000-2 §7.12). The validator only allowed a short list of catalog keys to change after signing, so this update counted as "document structure" and **the signature the LTV data protects showed as invalid**. I hit it on a notarial deed from a Brazilian e-notary service; poppler verifies its digest, and the only post-signing revision adds the DSS, XMP and `/Extensions`.

`/Extensions` may now gain declarations after signing. A declaration that was in the signed catalog may not change or disappear (that is still "document structure"). Developer extensions only declare what a file uses and do not change what a page shows.

I searched issues and PRs (DSS, LTV, Extensions, ESIC) and found nothing on this, and #3440 keeps the same catalog key list.

title: Search: keep the match in the middle while a zoom is still on (#3530, builds on #3547)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Depends on #3547, which should be merged first. This PR builds on its centring of the active match.

Fixes #3530. **Builds on #3547** by @MarekSpodBiedry: its commit is included unchanged (cherry-picked, authorship kept). Once #3547 is merged, this PR is the single commit on top of it.


#3547 centres the match on a find step. Even with it, the match could still end up out of view after zooming, but only now and then. I reproduced two causes:

1. **A zoom pending in the same frame.** If a zoom anchor was pending (Ctrl+wheel, pinch, a zoom button or key), the layout took the anchor branch and put the step's `goto` off to the next frame. There, its page-top offset (60 pt below the window top, scaled by the zoom) undid the centring. At 600 % that puts the match below the window.
2. **The eased Ctrl+wheel zoom.** egui spreads a wheel notch over about a quarter of a second (`motion.rs` explains this). Every frame of that set a new zoom anchor at the pointer, so the rest of the zoom moved the match you had just stepped to away from the middle again. A step taken shortly after a Ctrl+wheel zoom often ended up off screen.

What happens now:

- A step whose match centre is known scrolls to that point alone (both axes in one frame) and drops any pending zoom anchor (`flash_match`).
- A zoom that happens before the step is laid out, or while a wheel zoom is still easing, anchors on the match at the window's centre instead of the pointer. This covers Ctrl+wheel, pinch, buttons and keys through `zoom_at`, and a fit zoom that changes. The view keeps anchoring on the match until the first frame with no zoom gesture after the step, or until any other jump (`go_to_page`).
- If a match centre is not finite (a hostile page's glyphs spanning −∞…∞; NaN survives `clamp`), the step falls back to the page jump instead of using a NaN scroll target or zoom anchor.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --al…

title: M6: scripts see xfa_version, and xfa_installed in XFA forms
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

Form scripts now see two globals that XFA forms check before anything else:

- `xfa_version` (3.5) in every document;
- `xfa_installed` (`true`) only in documents with an XFA form.

On `main` neither exists, so an XFA form's version check decides the viewer is too old.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. One of its document-level scripts begins:

```js
if (typeof(xfa_installed) == "undefined" || typeof(xfa_version) == "undefined" || xfa_version < 2.8)
```

When that test is true, the script alerts that the form "requires a newer version" and then calls `app.findComponent`, which PdfCraft doesn't define. PdfCraft runs document-level scripts before every script. So on `main`, every script in this form, down to `1 + 1` in the `js_run` console, raises that alert and then fails with `TypeError: not a callable function`.

No existing issue or PR (searched for xfa_installed and xfa_version).

### Where the values come from

The values come from black-box measurement in another viewer, with two synthetic files: a plain AcroForm and a one-field XFA form. Each prints `typeof` and the value of both globals.

| | plain form | XFA form |
|---|---|---|
| `xfa_version` | number, 3.5 | number, 3.5 |
| `xfa_installed` | undefined | boolean, `true` |

This branch gives the same four answers. A document counts as an XFA form when its AcroForm has an `/XFA` entry (`pdfcraft_xfa::xfa_shape`), so a form whose XFA was stripped reads as a plain form again.

title: Reject non-hex characters in XFDF colour parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Found while testing `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs:236-243 (parse_hex)`. There is no existing issue.

title: Comments: turn by a rotate handle (Tab: quarter turns)
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Comments can be turned. A selected rectangle, oval, text box, typewriter text, line, arrow, connected lines, polygon, cloud or drawing gets a rotate handle above its frame: a round button with a turning arrow on a stem, which lights up under the pointer, says how it works in its tooltip and is named *Rotate* for screen readers.

- **Drag** turns the comment about its middle, showing its turned outline and the angle; **Shift** holds it to 15° steps.
- **Tab while dragging** sets quarter turns (Shift+Tab back), and the pointer stops turning it. Taken in `raw_input_hook` before egui moves the keyboard focus with it.
- The page's **right-click menu** turns the selected comment a quarter either way (*Rotate counterclockwise* / *Rotate clockwise*, existing labels).
- One undo step: `Edit::RotateAnnotation { page, index, degrees }` ("Rotate comment").

**How it is stored.** Lines, connected lines, polygons, clouds and drawings turn their points: plain PDF, the same in every viewer. PDF has no angle for rectangles, ovals and FreeText, so those keep their own box in `/PCBox` and the angle in `/PCAngle`; the appearance is drawn upright in that box and turned about its centre by the form's `/Matrix`, and `/Rect` is the turned box's upright hull. Viewers map the turned `/BBox` onto `/Rect` (§12.5.5), which is exactly that hull, so every viewer shows the comment turned and unscaled. A program that redraws the appearance from `/Rect` shows it upright again; I'd rather keep the comment's type than turn a rectangle into a polygon (and ovals have no such way out).

- Moving takes `/PCBox` along. A turned text box fits its own box and grows from its top edge as it reads (that edge stays put on the page); it is typed into through the comment card.
- A turned box is hit inside its turned outline (not in the corners of the hull) and shows that outline when selected. It has no resize handles yet.

title: M12: dynamic XFA forms tab in their template's traversal order
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A dynamic XFA form that PdfCraft lays out now tabs the way its template's `<traversal>` says. On `main` the traversal is ignored, so Tab follows the order the layout happened to write the widgets in, which is document order.

The template's `<traverse>` links are parsed: `next`, plus `first` on a container. The arrow-key operations are ignored. After layout, a new `traverse` module works out the order and writes each page's widgets in it. The laid-out pages have no `/Tabs`, so the forms crate (and other viewers) tab in annotation order, and nothing else needs to change.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. Its template has 947 `next` links and 22 `first` links, many of them through draws (`#draw[3]`). On `main`, Tab jumps around the page: Name → Rank → Date → DoD ID, then Organization before Leave Address, then the approval blocks out of order. With this branch it goes down the page block by block: Control Number, Name, DoD ID, Rank, Date, Leave Address, Organization, the type-of-absence boxes, blocks 9–10 (supervisor, then approver), then departure, extension and return, remarks, and the leave dates. Each row goes left to right.

No existing issue or PR (searched for xfa traversal, xfa tab order and tab order dynamic form; #3527 is AcroForm `setPageTabOrder`).

### How Tab follows the traversal

I measured this black-box in another viewer, with two synthetic forms. Each field's enter script appends its name to a protected log field, so the log records the order after a run of Tab presses. Both forms are now fixtures (`fixtures::traversal_template` and `fixtures::traversal_targets_template`), and this branch gives the same order for both:

title: M6: read-only form fields are Tab stops; protected XFA fields stay out of the order
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

Tab now stops on read-only form fields. A read-only field takes the focus and shows the focus frame, but nothing changes it: no editor opens, typing does nothing, Space doesn't tick a check box or pick a radio button, the arrows don't move a list box's selection, and a combo box opens no list. Shift+Tab goes back through the same stops. On `main`, Tab passes over every read-only field.

A laid-out XFA form's protected fields are still passed over. PdfCraft lays out both `access="readOnly"` and `access="protected"` fields as read-only AcroForm fields, so they now need telling apart. The layout marks a protected field's widget with a private `/PCXfaNoTab true`, next to the existing `PCSom`, `PCXfaClick` and `PCXfaImage` keys. The forms crate gives a marked widget no place in the tab order (`tab = usize::MAX`), and the widgets after it close up. The mark is on the widget, so a protected button in an exclusion group is passed over on its own. Stripping the XFA takes the mark out with the other private keys.

This follows storytold/pdfcraft#4149, which makes laid-out XFA forms tab in their template's `<traversal>` order. That order was measured black-box in another viewer, on a synthetic probe form (now `fixtures::traversal_template` in #4149). In that viewer, Tab stops on the read-only field D4 but not on the protected field D5, and Shift+Tab is the exact reverse. The public documentation of XFA's `access` attribute says the same: a read-only field stays in the tab order and a protected one leaves it, though the user can change neither. This was the one measured difference left after #4149. It matters on real forms such as DA Form 31 (a public Army leave form), whose leave-type check boxes are read-only.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched issues and PRs for read-only tab, readonly tab, tab skips read-only and protected field tab). #4149 touches the same `form.tab-order` parity entry (see below).

title: M4: a save prompt that opens in the background asks for the user's attention
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

When "Save changes?" opens while PdfCraft is in the background, PdfCraft now asks for the user's attention: on macOS the Dock icon bounces until PdfCraft is active again, on Windows the taskbar button flashes until the window comes to the front, and on X11 the window gets the urgency hint. When the user comes back, or the prompt is answered, the request is withdrawn.

This happens when the user quits from the Dock menu while another app is in front, or logs out (macOS sends the same quit event), or when an agent calls `ui.quit`. On `main`, PdfCraft correctly keeps the window open to ask about the unsaved work, but nothing tells the user. It looks as if PdfCraft simply didn't quit. I ran into this on macOS 27: PdfCraft had unsaved changes when I quit it, another app was in front, and I couldn't tell why PdfCraft hadn't quit.

How it works: `attend_save_prompt` runs last in `logic`. It sends `ViewportCommand::RequestUserAttention(Critical)` on the frame the prompt opens while the window isn't focused. It sends `Reset` once the window has focus again or the prompt has closed. It uses egui's own viewport command, so there is no `unsafe`, no new dependency, and nothing outside `ui-egui`.

**Why a critical request.** Apple's documentation for `NSApplication.requestUserAttention(_:)` says that when an inactive app presents a modal panel, AppKit makes this request itself, with `NSCriticalRequest`. A native app's "save changes?" alert therefore bounces until the user comes back. PdfCraft's prompt is drawn by egui, so AppKit never sees it, and PdfCraft has to ask itself. An informational request bounces the icon once, for one second. That is easy to miss, and the prompt is holding up the quit the user asked for. winit 0.30 maps `Critical` to `NSCriticalRequest` on macOS, `FLASHW_ALL | FLASHW_TIMERNOFG` on Windows, and the urgency hint on X11.

**When it doesn't ask.** A prompt that opens while PdfCraft is in front asks for nothing. Leaving with the promp…

title: M2: a symbolic TrueType font reads its (3, 0) cmap before its (1, 0) one (#4156)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4156.

A symbolic TrueType font now draws through its Windows (3, 0) `cmap` subtable before its Macintosh (1, 0) one, as ISO 32000-2 §9.6.5.4 prescribes:

> When the font has no Encoding entry, or the font descriptor's Symbolic flag is set … If the font contains a (3, 0) subtable, … [the codes] shall be used to select the associated glyph description from the subtable. Otherwise, if the font contains a (1, 0) subtable, single bytes from the string shall be used to look up the associated glyph descriptions from the subtable.

**Cause.** `EmbeddedKind::map_code` in the vendored `hayro-interpret` (the branch taken when the Nonsymbolic flag is not set) tried the cmap records in the order the font lists them, and kept the first match. Records are sorted by platform ID, so (1, 0) came before (3, 0). The #4156 sample was written by SAS 9.4. Its embedded `AlbanyAMT` subsets are symbolic (`/Flags 4`) with no `/Encoding`, and their (1, 0) table is wrong: code 43 maps to `V`, 49 to `glyph17408` and 56 to `p`. The (3, 0) table maps them to plus, one and eight, which agrees with the fonts' `/ToUnicode`. So "8" drew as "p", "+" as "V", and "1" and "%" not at all.

**Fix.** The Windows (3, 0)/(3, 1) records are tried first. The Macintosh and Unicode records still serve codes the (3, x) ones leave out, so a font whose (3, 0) table is incomplete loses nothing it drew before. The patch is marked `PdfCraft patch (#4156)` and listed in `vendor/README.md`.

With this branch, `pdfcraft-cli render` draws the #4156 sample the same as MuPDF, with every "1", "8", "+" and "%" in place.

No other open PR changes this branch of `map_code`. #2980 and #3969 touch TrueType cmaps, but only in the non-symbolic path and in text extraction.

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed

ARCH E1 is 5101.1's `na_wide-format_30x42in` (also in the IANA registry). title: fix(linux): say why no file dialog opened, and keep the work that asked (#3988)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3988 (the first of the two parts the triage comment split out: tell the user when no file dialog can open, instead of dropping the work).

On Linux, when the desktop portal runs but the backend that draws its file chooser doesn't (#3988: `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` started without `DISPLAY` and died), every Open, Save and Reduce File Size dialog did nothing, said nothing, and threw away the work that asked for it.

**Why the app couldn't tell.** I reproduced it with the real `xdg-desktop-portal` 1.22 on a private bus whose GTK backend can't start. The portal still lists `org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser` (version 4) and accepts `OpenFile`, then answers the request with `Response` code 2. rfd 0.17 maps any non-zero code to an empty answer (`portal/mod.rs`, `parse_response`) and only falls back to zenity when the portal can't be reached at all, so a dead backend looks exactly like Cancel. A check of the portal alone (like PhotoCraft's `file_dialog_probe`) also says "fine" in this state.

**The fix.**
- `pdfcraft_platform::file_dialog_probe::why_empty()` runs on the picker's worker thread, only after an empty answer. It reads the `.portal` files the portal reads (`XDG_DESKTOP_PORTAL_DIR`, else `portals` under the user and system data folders), takes the backends that implement `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser`, and asks the bus (`NameHasOwner`) whether any of them is running. A backend that just handled a request is still running, so "none is running" means the panel never showed. It only reads bus state: it never activates a backend, which would start every installed backend after every Cancel. With no portal it falls back to zenity's presence, as rfd does.
- Anything it can't tell counts as working, so a Cancel on a working desktop stays silent. Inside Flatpak and Snap it says nothing: the bus proxy and AppArmor hide or refuse the backend names, so a running backend would look missing. (That leaves the reporter's Snap case open. It …

title: chore(sonar): exclude vendored crates and the spec-mandated MD5/RIPEMD-160 (SonarCloud rust:S4790)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

Scopes SonarCloud's analysis in `sonar-project.properties`. No code changes.

**193 findings addressed:**

- **186 findings in `vendor/`** (every rule there: rust:S3776 52, rust:S2208 49, rust:S8863 30, rust:S1612 17, rust:S107 10, rust:S4790 9, rust:S8862 7, rust:S3329 4, rust:S4325 2, rust:S9045, rust:S7425, rust:S9168, rust:S7424, python:S3457, python:S1172 1 each). `vendor/` holds third-party crates (hayro*, lopdf, winit, vello_common, egui-wgpu) that we carry with small patches marked `PdfCraft patch:` and intend to drop once upstream releases the fix (`vendor/README.md`). - **7 rust:S4790 (weak hash) findings**, scoped by file to the rule:
  - `crates/crypt/src/lib.rs` (6): MD5 is the hash that ISO 32000 §7.6.4 mandates for the RC4 / AES-128 standard security handler (Algorithms 1–5). We cannot open or write those files without it.
  - `crates/sign/src/keys.rs` (1): RIPEMD-160 is one of the digests an existing CMS signature may name. We compute it to verify such signatures, not to choose it for new ones.

  S4790 stays on for every other file.

## How you verified it

Config only; the SonarCloud check on this PR shows the scoped result.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

Whether you would rather keep `vendor/` in the analysis. If so, drop the `sonar.exclusions` line and those findings come back as upstream's to fix.

title: M4: bookmarks show and set their title colour and style (ISO 32000-2 Tables 151, 152)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3193 (point 2: "a button for setting the background color … so as to mark certain rarely-used chapters").

**The need.** Readers of long documents mark bookmarks to tell them apart, for example rarely used chapters or sections still to review. PDF already has a place for this:

- ISO 32000-2 §12.3.3 gives every outline item a title colour, `/C`. Table 151 defines it as "An array of three numbers in the range 0.0 to 1.0, representing the components in the DeviceRGB colour space", with black as the default.
- It also gives style flags, `/F`. Table 152 defines bit 1 as italic and bit 2 as bold, and the default is 0.

PdfCraft ignored both, so a file whose author coloured or emboldened its bookmarks showed every title alike, and nobody could set them.

**1. The panel shows them** (6dec7b34)
- The inspector (`OutlineItem`) and the bookmark list (`organize::Bookmark`, which is used once a document is edited) now read `/C` and `/F`.
  - Each colour component is kept within 0–1.
  - Black (the default), and a `/C` that isn't three numbers, read as no colour.
- The Bookmarks panel draws bold titles in the semibold face, italic ones slanted, and each colour as given.
  - A colour is lightened towards the text colour only as far as it needs to reach 3:1 contrast on the panel (`theme::readable`). Dark blue stays readable in the dark theme, and red on white is unchanged.
- `bookmark_list` reports `color`, `bold` and `italic` where they differ from the defaults.

**2. Users can change them** (967a20db)
- Each bookmark's menu gains:

- Writes follow the tables:

title: fix(ui): Ctrl+Z in an open paragraph undoes the document, not stale text
author: RiceDee
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4176.

`edit.undo` leaves Ctrl+Z to a focused text field, so with a paragraph open in Edit text it went to the paragraph editor's own `TextEdit` undo history. After a formatting change (which applies at once and refreshes the editor's text), that history still held the text from before it, so Ctrl+Z put it back into a box laid out for the page after the change, and the document kept the change. The box shares its id across paragraphs, so it could also put back another paragraph's text.

- **The box's history starts at what the page has** (`forget_typing_before`): on opening, and whenever formatting applies. Undo in the box takes back only typing done since. The same goes for the Add text box, which now has its own fixed id (`content_ui::input_id`).
- **Undo and Redo reach the document** from a focused page box once it holds no typing the page doesn't have (`commands::registry_shortcuts`); while it does, they stay the box's, as before.
- **An open box is applied and closed before an Undo or Redo step** (`close_text_editors`), as clicking away applies it, so it never shows a state the document has left. If its text can't be applied (text the standard fonts can't draw, a refused rewrite), the box stays open and the step doesn't run: nothing typed is lost.

Related to #2512, whose session design makes this one undo step per session; this keeps today's one-step-per-format-change behaviour and only stops Undo going to stale text.

## How it was verified

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-ui-egui`, all targets

title: M11: PDF Optimizer ▸ Clean Up stores LZW streams with Flate (optimize.flate-unencoded)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The PDF Optimizer's Clean Up panel in Acrobat has two Flate options under "Object compression options": "Use Flate to encode streams that are not encoded" and "In streams that use LZW Encoding, use Flate instead", described as "Applies Flate compression to all content streams and images that use LZW encoding" ([Optimizing PDFs](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/optimizing-pdfs-acrobat-pro.html)). `optimize.flate-unencoded` had the first one; its note said "LZW not yet re-encoded". This adds the second as its own checkbox in Clean Up and as `lzw_to_flate` on `doc_optimize` (which now reports `lzw_streams`). It is on by default like the neighbouring Flate option: I couldn't find Adobe stating this checkbox's default, only that in Clean Up "By default, only elements that don't affect functionality are selected", which this one doesn't; happy to switch it off by default if you know otherwise.

For each stream with an LZW filter, the filters up to the last LZW one are decoded strictly, with its `EarlyChange` and predictor, and the result is Flate-encoded under the same predictor, so a predicted image stays predicted. `EarlyChange` goes away (it is LZW's alone), filters applied before the LZW one (an ASCII85 layer, say) go with it, and the ones after it keep their bytes: `[/LZWDecode /DCTDecode]` becomes `[/FlateDecode /DCTDecode]` with the same JPEG. The re-encoded stage is decoded once more and compared, so a predictor the encoder can't reproduce leaves the stream alone. Streams whose LZW data doesn't decode cleanly are left as they are, as are streams with `/Crypt`, an external `/F`, `/DecodeParms` that can't be read for certain (an indirect reference, an array of the wrong length), cross-reference and object streams (rewritten on save), and streams that decode past 256 MiB (`MAX_PAGE_DECODED`), since the data and its check are held together. The stream is converted whether or not it gets smaller, since the option is also how LZW is removed for PDF/A and PDF/X; hap…

title: M5: sticky notes draw the icon they name (ISO 32000-2 Table 175)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**The need.** A sticky note's icon is how readers tell notes apart on a page at a glance: a question, a key point, an insertion. PdfCraft broke this in two ways.

- **Its own icon choice did nothing.** The Properties dialog offers seven icons, but it drew only two shapes: Comment, and a page for everything else. Choosing Key, Help, Insert, New paragraph or Paragraph left the note looking the same.
- **Notes in received files lost their icons.** Notes that name other icons drew as the same page. That covers the standard names and further common ones such as Check or Star. Changing such a note's colour also redrew it as a page, so its icon was lost.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.4, Table 175 (`Name`) lists Comment, Key, Note, Help, NewParagraph, Paragraph and Insert, and says the viewer "shall provide predefined icon appearances for at least the following standard names", adding "Additional names may be supported as well".

**The change**
- `annot::appearance::note_icon` draws a shape of its own for each of the seven standard names. It also draws seven further names in common use: Check, Circle, Cross, CrossHairs, Star, RightArrow and UpArrow.
- The new icons are drawn the same way as the existing Comment and Note icons: simple geometric drawings in the appearance stream, filled in the note's colour with a dark outline. No image or icon files are involved.
- `NoteIcon` gains the further names, with `NoteIcon::ALL`. The Properties chooser and `comment_add` offer all fourteen; the chooser shows the PDF names, as before, so no new UI strings.
- A note keeps its icon when its colour changes.
- Any other name still draws as Note, the table's default.

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed: `pdfcraft-annot`, `-automation`, `-ui-egui`, 9 suites, 1,892 passed. The one failure, `control_open_replies_pending_while_the_worker_opens_and_focuses_…

title: M3: a Launch link that names a PDF opens it in PdfCraft (ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.6)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4168.

**The need.** Document sets often link their parts with Launch actions. The file in #4168 has 268 links such as `..\se\se_ST.pdf`, each meant to open a sibling PDF. PdfCraft follows no Launch action, so these links did nothing. Written as GoToR, the same link opens.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.6: a Launch action "launches an application or opens or prints a document". A document must not be able to start programs. Opening a PDF, though, is exactly what a remote Go-To already does, with its own checks.

**The change** (`render::inspect`, `launch_pdf`)
- **What counts.** A Launch action whose `/F` names a `.pdf` file, and that has no `/Win` launch parameters, is read as the remote Go-To to that file's first page. `/Win` (Table 208) names an application, an operation and arguments.
- **How it opens.** The link becomes `LinkTarget::RemoteGoTo { launch: true, … }` and goes through the same path as a GoToR link:
  - PDF files only;
  - `--root` confinement;
  - confirmation for absolute paths;
  - opened as a document in PdfCraft, never handed to the operating system.
- **Path separators.** Windows writers separate such paths with `\`, while §7.11.2.1 separates components with `/`. A Launch path that contains no `/` has its `\` read as `/`.
- **Everything else stays unfollowed:** any other Launch action, one with `/Win`, a URL file system, or a name that isn't `*.pdf`.

title: M7: preserve paragraph frames when resizing upright and rotated text
author: enriquemelzer-bit
body:
## What this changes

Resizing an existing paragraph preserves its chosen width and height independently of glyph bounds, including text at arbitrary angles. Words wrap along the baseline and remain visible outside the chosen height. Frame dimensions persist through typing, movement, undo/redo and save/reopen. Refs #3474.

title: M9: sign with PKCS #11 smart cards and tokens; opt-in timestamps and LTV
author: MarAvFe
body:
Smart cards and USB tokens sign through the vendor's PKCS #11 module (cryptoki, Apache-2.0; native only). Certificates are listed without a PIN; signing logs in with a zeroized PIN (none on PIN-pad readers) and signs on the token (RSA PKCS #1 v1.5, ECDSA P-256/P-384). When a card holds an authentication and a signing certificate, only the nonRepudiation one is offered.

- Sign dialog: Configure New Digital ID > Use a smart card or token, module prefilled from known middleware locations; card PIN in Sign as. Card IDs list on every desktop platform. Named IDs sort before IDs named by a bare GUID.
- CLI and agent tools: sign_card_ids; sign_document takes a pkcs11: id. The module comes only from --card-module, the PIN only from a terminal prompt in pdfcraft-cli run; network only with --network.
- Long-term validation, opt-in (Preferences > Signatures): a timestamp server URL and an LTV switch. Signing then runs on a thread behind a cancellable modal: RFC 3161 signature timestamp, missing issuers from AIA, OCSP or CRL that verify and cover the signing time, /DSS, and a document timestamp (PAdES B-LTA). pdfcraft-sign stays transport-free (ltv::Fetch); HTTP lives in pdfcraft-platform::http.
- pkcs11_probe example: a stand-alone card check.
- docs/smart-card-signing.md.

title: M5: cloudy squares, circles and text boxes are drawn (comment.cloud)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**The need.** Reviewers mark areas of drawings and documents with cloudy rectangles, ellipses and text boxes. When a PDF carries such a comment without a stored appearance, PdfCraft drew none of them, so the marked area was simply invisible. A polygon whose cloudy border has intensity 0 (or no intensity) drew a cloud anyway.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.5.4:
- Squares, circles and polygons (PDF 1.5), and text boxes (PDF 1.6), may have a border effect.
- Table 169 says `/BE /S /C` draws the border "as a series of convex curved line segments in a manner that simulates the appearance of a cloud", and that "the width and dash array specified by BS shall be honoured".
- Its intensity `/I` is "in the range 0 to 2. Default value: 0".
- Table 180's `/RD` gives the differences between "the left, top, right, and bottom coordinates of Rect and those of the square or circle".

**Commit 1: cloudy squares, circles and text boxes are drawn**
- `cloud_intensity` reads `/BE`. A border is cloudy only for `/S /C` with `/I` above 0; intensity 0, the default, draws a plain border.
- A cloudy square or circle draws its bumps around `/Rect` less `/RD`, in the order left, top, right, bottom. Without `/RD`, the bumps are inset by their own height so they stay inside `/Rect`. A circle's outline gets one point per bump.
- A cloudy text box draws its background and border as the cloud, with the text inside. A cloudy callout keeps its own appearance, as before.

**Bump size.** The standard leaves the bump size open. Squares, circles and text boxes use the radius PdfCraft's polygon clouds already had: 6 + 1.5 × the line width at intensity 1, doubled at intensity 2. An earlier commit halved it; at review (2026-11-02, bec647cbd) the size went back to what it was, so this PR doesn't change how existing clouds look.

**Plain squares and circles honour `/RD` too.** Table 180's `/RD` describes the square or circle itself, cloudy or not. So a plain square or circle without an a…

title: fix(audit): covered_text reports the words under the cover, not the whole line
author: mercuryVM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4164.

**Problem.** A text line joins the runs painted on one baseline, and when a cover hid part of a line the audit reported the line's whole text in `covered_text`, including words painted beside the cover that stay visible. The issue's repro (a cover over `SECRET`, then `tail` at x 200, outside it) reported `["SECRETtail"]`.

**Fix.** As the issue suggests, the text now comes from `pdfcraft-edit`:

- `TextLine` keeps each joined run's text together with the end of its word boxes in `ink` (private field `runs`), exposed read-only as `TextLine::runs()` → `(&str, &[[f64; 4]], bool)` per run, in content order: its text, its word boxes, and whether joining put a space before it. No new public type.
- When the line's text is reordered for reading (right-to-left via `bidi::to_logical`, or visual-order Indic via `indic::to_logical`), the runs no longer read like the line, so they are cleared and `runs()` yields nothing. This covers both reorder sites (`text_lines_in` and the form-aware walker).
- `pdfcraft-audit`: `Budget::hidden_text` takes the cover's rectangle, and a new `covered_words` reports the runs whose word boxes the cover overlaps (positive-area intersection), joined as the line joins them (a word shown in two adjacent runs stays one word; a space where the line has one, or where uncovered runs were left out between them). It falls back to the whole line when the runs can't say: a line of one run, a reordered line, or a cover that matched on the line's box but overlaps none of its words. Same for filled-rectangle covers and annotation covers (`/Redact`, opaque `/Square`).

Which lines count as covered is unchanged (`is_cover` / `covers` are untouched); only the reported text gets narrower. The copy-permission and output bounds work as before: withheld text is still never assembled. The comparison bound now also counts runs (see Review).

Editing existing text in a Simplified Chinese PDF fails today with `the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+8054` (联): the only CJK faces in the fallback chain are Japanese ones, and none of them has the Simplified-only characters. Towards #2095.

title: M11: Convert to PDF/A needs the owner's permission on an encrypted document (#3921)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3921.

`check_permission` gated `Edit::ConvertPdfA` by `p.modify()` alone. But `pdfcraft_preflight::convert` starts by removing the encryption, since PDF/A forbids it. So a document opened with the user password, whose owner allowed changes but withheld printing and copying, could be converted and saved as an unencrypted copy with every restriction gone. That is a change of security, which the engine otherwise reserves for the owner.

`ConvertPdfA` now needs `unrestricted(p)`, the same rights as Protect and Remove security. Otherwise it is refused with `NotPermitted("removing the encryption, which PDF/A forbids")`, so the user sees why Save as PDF/A was refused.

- An unencrypted document has no permissions, so it converts as before.
- A batch containing the conversion is refused by the existing `Edit::Batch` recursion.
- The comment on #3921 said a fix already existed elsewhere. I checked: on `main` (`0dc77fe4`) the new test fails (output below).

**Every route goes through this check.** `Session::apply` is the only caller of `check_permission` and the only way into `run_edit`. The UI (`standards_ui.rs`), the `pdfa_convert` automation tool (`a11y.rs`) and actions (`actions.rs`) all call it. Undo and redo only swap snapshots that an earlier `apply` already allowed.

author: qwe3084614
body:
## Problem

PDFs generated by Chinese government systems (customs declarations, invoices, tax forms) almost always set their Chinese text in a **composite (CID) font that is not embedded** — typically `STSong-Light` with `/Encoding /UniGB-UCS2-H` and `/CIDSystemInfo << /Registry (Adobe) /Ordering (GB1) /Supplement 2 >>`, exactly the shape of the fixture in `crates/render/src/inspect.rs`.

In current PdfCraft **all of that text draws nothing**: company names, field values, whole columns. Every other viewer the user is likely to have (Edge, Chrome, WPS, Adobe) renders the page, so this reads as a defect, and it makes an entire class of documents unusable for reading.

## Why it happens

- `crates/fonts/src/fallback.rs`, step 5 of the substitution chain: for the `GB1` / `CNS1` / `Korea1` orderings there is no licensed face, so the chain reports none and the caller draws nothing. That is the *right* answer for the bundling policy — but the user-visible result is missing text.

For `UniGB-UCS2-H` documents this is easy to fix at runtime, though: the encoding *is* Unicode, so `Type0Font`'s existing `map_via_unicode` path ("Yay, Unicode worked!") accepts **any** Unicode font as the substitute — no CID-keyed CFF needed. author: Matoo125

## What this changes

Reduce File Size (Clean Up) removes named destinations that nothing refers to. `referenced_names` in `crates/optimize/src/links.rs` collected the used names by reading `/Dest` and a GoTo's `/D` **directly** with `dest_name`, which only recognises a string or name. title: M2: text extraction finishes a column before the next one across a paragraph gap (#3658)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3658.

On a two-column page, text extraction and Find read the top of the left column, then the whole right column, and only then the rest of the left column. This happened whenever an ordinary paragraph gap separated the left column's blocks.

The cause is step 3 of `arrange` (`crates/render/src/text.rs`). It took the top-most unread block next. It preferred a block to its left only when the two overlapped vertically, which a block below a paragraph gap never does.

**The new rule.** The next block is the nearest unread block below the one just read that:
- overlaps it horizontally (by more than 30% of the narrower width), and
- starts at most 2.5 times the height of its last line below it.

That block is skipped when another unread block:
- **sits above it in its own span.** This is the rest of a column above a full-width heading or footnote.
- **is beside it on its left,** as before.
- **shares its first line.** The two first lines overlap by at least 30% of the taller one. That is a table or form row, which still reads across, including labels and values in different sizes or on shifted baselines. A line that only touches it, or a small footnote marker, is not a row.

When the rule declines, the old top-most rule applies unchanged, so the result is never worse than `main`'s. Footers, footnotes and captions further down keep their old place. Extraction, Find and copy share this order.

| `pdfcraft-cli text` on the issue's `columns.pdf` | |
|---|---|
| before | Two columns · A1 A2 A3 · B3 B4 · C1 C2 · B1 B2 |
| after | Two columns · A1 A2 A3 · B1 B2 · B3 B4 · C1 C2 |

`text_find` for "B2 second paragraph B3 second paragraph" now finds 1 match (was 0). The wrong join "C2 third paragraph B1 second paragraph" finds 0 (was 1).

**Known limit.** When a paragraph in the next column starts on the same line as the continuation (text on a baseline grid), it counts as a row. The top-most rule then applies, so the order of #3658 comes back. Telli…

title: M7: edited text keeps the spaces typed, except at the edges of a stretched justified row (#4199, #3797)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4199. Fixes #3797.

Editing a paragraph and saving collapsed every run of typed spaces to one, and dropped an indent or trailing spaces. "Hello     world   end" was saved as `(Hello world end) Tj`. Adding a space to a paragraph therefore did nothing after Apply, which is #3797.

**Cause.** `rewrite_block_from` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs`) is the single-style paragraph rewrite behind `replace_block` and `Edit::EditTextBlock`. It split the typed text at any white space and joined the words with one space, and `wrap()` did the same. The single-line path (`replace_line`) and the styled region path (`rewrite_styled_block`) already kept spaces. Text extraction was not at fault: the saved content stream itself had lost them.

**Fix:**
- **The text is kept as typed.** CR and CRLF become line breaks, and any other white-space character becomes one space each.
- **`wrap()` keeps each run of spaces,** including an indent and trailing spaces. It drops only the spaces where a row soft-wraps.
- **Centred and right-aligned rows** are measured to their last word, so spaces typed after a title don't shift it. The editor's draft box is measured the same way, so the preview box equals what Apply draws.
- **A justified row that isn't the last one** still drops its indent and trailing spaces, exactly as on `main`, so word spacing reaches only the spaces between its words. Its output is byte-identical to `main`. Keeping an indent on a justified row is a possible follow-up; see below.
- **A paragraph at `0 Tz`** is not justified, which avoids an infinite `Tw`.
