title: M6: check boxes, radio buttons and push buttons without an appearance are drawn, and comb fields show their cells (ISO 32000-2 Table 192, 12.7.5)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4367.

**The need.** A form can leave its appearances to the viewer, with `/NeedAppearances` or with widgets that have no `/AP`. #3475 draws text and choice fields in that case, for display only. Buttons were left out:
- a check box or radio button that is on but has no appearance showed nothing, not even its border;
- a push button with none showed nothing;
- a comb field showed its characters but not its cells.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- Table 192: `BC` and `BG` are the widget's border and background colours. `CA` is "the widget annotation's normal caption", and it "may be used with any type of button field, including check boxes … and radio buttons".
- §12.7.5.2.3: a check box shows the appearance of its `/AS` state, and the example's on state draws `(4) Tj` in `/ZaDb`, the ZapfDingbats check mark (Annex D.6).
- Table 168: `/S /B` is a beveled border, "a simulated embossed rectangle".
- Table 228, Comb: "the field shall be automatically divided into as many equally spaced positions, or combs, as the value of MaxLen".

**The change** (`pdfcraft_forms::with_field_appearances`, `appearance.rs`)
- **Check boxes and radio buttons** with no normal appearance for their state (`/AS`; else a check box's `/V`; else Off), or none at all, are drawn into the display copy (`button_state_shown`):
  - the `/MK /BG` background and the `/MK /BC` border, through the existing `frame` (`/BS` width and style);
  - when the state isn't Off, the first character of `/MK /CA` in the standard-14 ZapfDingbats font, so no font program is needed and it renders on wasm;
  - without a usable caption, `4` (check mark) for a check box and `l` (dot) for a radio button;
  - in the `/DA` colour, at the `/DA` size, or at 80% of the room inside the border for `0 Tf`.
  - When the widget has a state dictionary, an Off state without its own appearance stays blank: the spec allows Off to be missing.

title: M12: XFA check boxes and radio buttons run their click scripts when a click changes them
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A dynamic XFA form's check boxes and radio buttons now run their own `click` scripts each time a click changes them. On `main`, only push buttons run click scripts; a check box or radio button runs its change and exit scripts, and its click scripts never run. Forms use them for approval boxes: show a message when the box is ticked, move the focus on, or unlock the fields that follow. A click script reads the new value (`this.rawValue` is already the value the click set).

- **Engine** (`engine/src/xfa.rs`): `on_changes` already runs a field's change, exit and validate scripts after its value changes. For a check box or radio group, it now also runs the click scripts of what was clicked: the check box itself, or the radio button now on. Each radio button is a field of its own in XFA, with scripts of its own, and its widget carries its own SOM path; `FieldInfo` now keeps each button's on state and SOM path, and `Runner::clicked` picks the button whose on state is the group's new value.
- **Order:** one constant, `TOGGLE_ORDER`, says what runs once the click has set the value: the field's change scripts (a radio group's, as for any value change), then the click scripts. Exit scripts follow, as after any change (unchanged from `main`).
- **What a click script may do:** it runs as a click, so it may move the focus, print or open links like a push button's. `setFocus` comes back as a focus request; the app doesn't act on focus requests yet (unchanged).
- **Where it runs:** clicking the box or button in the app, and `form_fill` on a check box or radio group, which already ran the field's change scripts, as a click does. `js_run` with `field` still runs a field's click script on its own, without changing it.
- **Not changed:** a text field's click script doesn't run when its value changes; it would run when the field is clicked into, which is a focus event and not part of this PR.

No issue or other PR covers this. I searched for checkbox click script,…

title: M2: Invisible annotations of unknown types and popups don't paint their appearance on the page (ISO 32000-2 Table 167)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4370.

**The need.** PdfCraft painted two kinds of annotation appearance that belong nowhere on the page:
- An annotation whose `/Subtype` is not a standard type, with the Invisible flag set, was drawn from its `/AP` as if the flag were clear.
- A `/Popup` annotation that carries an `/AP` had it painted as page content.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 decides both.
- Table 167, bit 1 Invisible: for an annotation that is not one of the standard types, "If set, do not render the unknown annotation and do not print it even if the Print flag is set." The standard types are the 28 of Table 171.
- §12.5.6.14: a popup "shall not appear alone but is associated with a markup annotation" and "shall have no appearance stream or associated actions of its own". The viewer shows it as a window for its parent.

**The change**
- **Renderer** (`vendor/hayro-interpret`, `interpret_page`, patch 56). The annotation loop skips:
  - an annotation with `/F` bit 1 whose `/Subtype` is none of the Table 171 types (`is_standard_annotation_type`); a missing `/Subtype` is not a standard type;
  - every `/Popup` annotation.
  - This covers the page view, `page_render`, the CLI `render` command and printing as pictures, which all draw through it.
- **Printing** (`crates/print`, `prints`). The Invisible rule is applied there too, so vector printing agrees with the screen. Popups were already left out of printing.
- **Unchanged.** Invisible means nothing for a standard type. Links, `/AS` state selection, zero-size `/BBox` and `/CA` with an appearance already followed the spec and are untouched.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: M2: a stand-in for a non-embedded font keeps its glyph shapes at wider /Widths advances (Arial,Bold no longer draws i and l as blocks)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4373.

**The need.** A simple font that a document names but doesn't embed is drawn with a standard-font stand-in. `Arial,Bold` is drawn with Helvetica-Bold, for example. Each stand-in glyph was then scaled horizontally to its `/Widths` advance, both narrower and wider. With 600-unit widths, `i` and `l` (278 units in the stand-in) were widened 2.16 times into solid blocks, and the line read as a heavy fixed-pitch face.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §9.2.4: "the Tj operator shall position the consecutive glyphs of a string according to their widths". The widths (§9.6.2.1, Table 109, `Widths`) place the glyphs. Nothing asks for a glyph's outline to be reshaped to fill its advance. How a substitute is drawn is left to the processor (§9.5, NOTE 5; §9.8.1).

**The change** (vendored `hayro-interpret`, `StandardKind::outline_glyph`, patch 57)
- **Substituted fonts** (`fallback`: the name isn't one of the standard 14, as with `Arial,Bold`, `ArialMT` and `TimesNewRomanPSMT`): a glyph is still narrowed to a narrower `/Widths` advance, so neighbours don't overlap. It is no longer widened to a wider one, since the advance already moves the next glyph on.
- **Exact standard-14 fonts** are unchanged. They still match their standard metrics in both directions.
- Text extraction, advances and `/Widths` handling are unchanged. Only the outline's horizontal scale is affected.

title: M3: a document opens at its /OpenAction destination, position and named destinations included (ISO 32000-2 Table 149, 12.3.2.4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4375.

**The need.** A PDF can say where it opens (`/OpenAction`). PdfCraft opened the right page, but always at the page's top. `[p3 /XYZ 100 500 2]` showed page 3 at 200% with the top of the page at the top of the window, not the point (100, 500). `[p2 /FitH 400]` fitted the width but also showed the top. A go-to action to a named destination opened page 1. `/NonFullScreenPageMode` was never read.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- §7.7.2, Table 29, `OpenAction`: "A value specifying a destination that shall be displayed or an action that shall be performed when the document is opened."
- §12.3.2.2, Table 149: `/XYZ` displays the page "with the coordinates (left, top) positioned at the upper-left corner of the window", and a null or 0 operand keeps the current value. `/FitH` puts "the vertical coordinate top positioned at the top edge of the window", and `/FitV` puts `left` at the left edge.
- §12.3.2.4: "a destination may be referred to indirectly by means of a name object (PDF 1.1) or a byte string (PDF 1.2)", through the catalog's `/Dests` or the `/Names /Dests` name tree.
- §12.2, Table 147, `NonFullScreenPageMode`: how to display the document "on exiting full-screen mode": UseNone (neither outline nor thumbnails visible), UseOutlines, UseThumbs or UseOC. It is "meaningful only if the value of the PageMode entry … is FullScreen".

**The change**
- **Resolving** (`render::inspect`). `DocInfo::open_dest` holds the opening destination as (page, `DestView`). It comes from the existing `dest()` resolver that bookmarks and links use:
  - an explicit array;
  - a `/GoTo` action's `/D`;
  - a name or string, looked up in the `/Names /Dests` tree and then in the catalog `/Dests`. A bare name or string as `/OpenAction` is accepted too: Table 29 asks for an array or an action, and reading leniently costs nothing.

  Any other action (a script, a remote go-to), an unknown name, or a page outside the document gives `None`.

title: M3: documents that hide the toolbar, menu bar or window controls open that way, with a key to bring them back (organize.initial-view)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4377.

**The need.** PdfCraft reads a document's viewer preferences and lets Document Properties ▸ Initial View edit them. When the document opens, though, only `DisplayDocTitle` and the layout, zoom, page and panel parts take effect. A document that asks to hide the toolbars, the menu bar or the window's controls (a kiosk-style form, a presentation handout) opened with all of them shown, and `FitWindow` and `CenterWindow` did nothing. A `/PageLayout /SinglePage` document opened at fit width, so the "one page at a time" it asks for was taller than the window.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.2, Table 147:
- HideToolbar: "hide the interactive PDF processor's tool bars when the document is active"; HideMenubar: the same for the "menu bar".
- HideWindowUI: "hide user interface elements in the document's window (such as scroll bars and navigation controls), leaving only the document's contents displayed".
- FitWindow: "resize the document's window to fit the size of the first displayed page"; CenterWindow: "position the document's window in the centre of the screen".
- §7.7.2 Table 29 defines SinglePage as "Display one page at a time" and says nothing about the zoom.

**The change** (new `crates/ui-egui/src/viewer_prefs.rs`, called once from `open_prepared` after `apply_initial_view`)
- **Hidden per tab.** The tab's `DocView` stores what its document asked to hide and what is hidden now. The flags apply only "when the document is active": another tab shows the usual interface.

title: M2: a non-embedded CIDFont's fallback request carries its descendant's font descriptor (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4, §9.8)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4379.

Part of #234.

**The need.** When a CIDFont isn't embedded, the resolver gets a `FallbackFontQuery` so that it can pick a substitute of the right style. For CID fonts that query was built from the Type 0 font dictionary. It looked there for `/FontDescriptor` and never found one, so every request said "not serif, not italic, weight 400". A resolver couldn't tell Song or Mincho from Hei or Gothic, or see `/FontWeight 700`.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- §9.7.6.1, Table 119: a Type 0 font dictionary has no `FontDescriptor` entry.
- §9.7.4.1, Table 115: the CIDFont's `FontDescriptor` is required.
- §9.8.1, Table 120 (`FontWeight`, `FontFamily`, `FontStretch`, `Flags`) and §9.8.2, Table 121 (Serif is bit 2, Italic bit 7).

**The change** (vendored `hayro-interpret`, patch 58)
- `FallbackFontQuery::with_descriptor(dict, descriptor)`: the name from `dict`, the style from `descriptor`. `FallbackFontQuery::new(dict)` now calls it with `dict`'s own descriptor, so simple fonts are unchanged.
- `Type0Font::new` builds its request with the descendant's descriptor, the one it already reads for `FontType::new` and `select_standard_font`. The name still comes from the Type 0 font, and the character collection is set as before.
- `vendor/README.md` lists patch (58) and its tests.
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml`: the CID-fonts note now says that the Japanese face also follows the descriptor's Serif flag and `/FontWeight`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`pdfcraft-render`)

title: M7: paste image files copied in Explorer or Finder onto the page (#1289)
author: Daktyl198
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Daktyl198"} -->
_Requested by **Daktyl**_
 
## What this changes
 
Part of #1289. ⌘V / Ctrl+V with a document showing already places a screenshot or a picture copied in a browser on the current page (#2494). Image files copied in Explorer, Finder or a file manager did nothing until now, because the clipboard then holds a file list, not pixels. Now each one is placed on the current page in its own format, the same way Add Image places a file.
 
- **File list first.** The clipboard's file list is read before its picture. Finder puts a copied file's icon on the pasteboard next to the file, and that icon is what `get_image()` used to return. `clipboard_picture` makes this choice and only reads the picture when there are no files.
- **Copied files that aren't pictures** (PDFs, documents, folders) are left alone. When nothing could be placed, a notice says so ("None of the copied files is a picture to place …"), unless a file has already said why: one that has since gone missing says "Couldn't read …", and that notice isn't replaced.
- **Only regular files are read.** A named pipe or a device called like a picture is refused before it is opened, because opening a FIFO waits for a writer on the UI thread. The opened handle is checked again before anything is read.
- **Limits.** A paste takes at most 50 files, of up to 256 MB each, read with a cap (`read_capped`) so an oversized file is never read whole. A notice says when either limit applies.
- **Restricted documents.** A document that refuses the edit says so once, not once per file. `add_image` now returns whether it placed the image.
- **Existing users will notice** that Copy Image in its original format, which puts a file on the clipboard, can now be pasted back onto a page. Before, that paste did nothing on Windows and Linux.

title: M3: a closed top-level bookmark opens closed (ISO 32000-2 Table 151 /Count)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4388.

**The need.** A document can keep a bookmark closed, so its children stay hidden until the reader opens it. The Bookmarks panel honoured that below the top level, but opened every top-level bookmark regardless. A document with closed chapters opened with all of their contents spread out.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.3.3, Table 151, `Count`: "If the outline item is closed, Count is negative". When an item is closed, "all of its descendants in the hierarchy shall be hidden". Nothing exempts the top level. `Count` is "Required if the item has any descendants". A bookmark with children but no `/Count` stays closed, as it already did at deeper levels: only a positive `/Count` says open.

**The change**
- **Panel** (`ui-egui`, `panels.rs`, `outline_item`). The `|| depth == 0` that forced top-level items open is gone, so every level starts as its `/Count` says. The reader's own toggles and a search still override it, as before. Expand all, expand top-level and collapse all are untouched.
- **Moving a bookmark** (`organize`, `outline.rs`, `move_bookmark`). Indenting a bookmark under one that had no children gave that parent a negative `/Count`, so it stayed closed. The forced top-level open used to hide this. Now a bookmark moved into a different parent opens that parent, as adding a bookmark already did. The two share one helper, `show_children`. Reordering inside a parent leaves its open state alone.
- **Docs.** `OutlineItem::open` now says which `/Count` values mean open.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed: `pdfcraft-organize` 156, `pdfcraft-render` 402, `pdfcraft-ui-egui` 1483 passed, 0 failed; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean

title: M2: an Indexed image with a short lookup table or an out-of-range hival is drawn as most readers draw it, and one with no table is skipped with a warning (view.render-pages)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4392.

**The need.** An image in `[/Indexed /DeviceRGB 7 <FF0000 00FF00>]` (hival 7, but only 2 of its 8 entries) was drawn entirely black, including indices 0 and 1, whose entries are red and green. The vendored interpreter rejected the whole colour space when the table ran out. The image then fell back to DeviceGray, and its index values 0 to 7 were painted as grey levels 0/255 to 7/255. Nothing reported it.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §8.6.6.3:
- "The hival parameter shall be an integer", and "hival shall be no greater than 255".
- "The colour table data shall be m × (hival + 1) bytes long", where m is the number of components in the base space.

ISO doesn't say how a reader should recover from a table that breaks this. Some samples of such an image have no colour at all, so it can't be drawn as written.

**The change** (vendored `hayro-interpret`, patch (80); `pdfcraft-render`)
- **The check.** `color::is_malformed_indexed` flags an Indexed space when:
  - `hival` is not an integer in 0..=255 (negative, over 255, a real with a fraction, or not a number);
  - the lookup table is missing or shorter than m × (hival + 1) bytes. A stream is measured after decoding.
  A table longer than needed is fine and its first bytes are used, as before. The lookup can be a string or a stream, given directly or by reference. An Indexed space whose base can't be read is judged only by its `hival`, because the table size depends on the base; with a usable `hival` it keeps today's handling.
- **The size check.** `hival` is range-checked to 0..=255 as an `f64` before it becomes an integer. The required size (hival + 1) × m is computed with `checked_add` and `checked_mul`, so a size that doesn't fit counts as malformed and never wraps. In practice the range check already keeps it within 256 × the base's component count.
- **A lookup string given by reference.** In the upstream code, `Indexed::new` (and the first version of the check) tried the lookup as a …

title: M2: layers open in the state the view auto state sets, and the Layers panel follows /Order (view.layers-panel)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4395.

**The need.** Two parts of the default optional content configuration were not read.
- A layer whose usage says it is off when viewed (`/Usage /View /ViewState /OFF`), and which the configuration's auto state (`/AS`) manages for the View event, drew on screen anyway. In the 16-case fixture in the issue, case N differs from ISO 32000-2 and the other 15 follow it.
- The Layers panel listed every group in `/OCGs`, flat, including groups the document doesn't present.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- §8.11.4.3, Table 99, `AS`: usage application dictionaries that "specify how interactive PDF processors shall … automatically set the state of optional content groups".
- §8.11.4.4, Table 101: the categories named by `Category` are examined for each group in `OCGs`. "If all the entries yield a recommended state of ON, the group's state shall be set to ON; otherwise, its state shall be set to OFF." For View, "The state shall be the value of the ViewState entry." A group in several `OCGs` arrays is ON "only if all categories in all the usage application dictionaries it appears in have a state of ON".
- Table 99, `Order`: nested arrays may be shown "in a tree or outline structure", and a leading text string is "a non-selectable label". "Any groups not listed in this array shall not be presented in any user interface that uses the configuration." In the default configuration the default is an empty array.

**The change**
- **View auto state** (vendored hayro-interpret patch (103), `OcgState::from_catalog`). The renderer applies it after `/BaseState`, `/ON` and `/OFF`, and before the Layers panel's toggles (`ocg_overrides`), which still win.
  - It applies every `/AS` entry whose `/Event` is `/View` and whose `/Category` includes `/View`.
  - Each listed group with a `/ViewState` of ON or OFF gets that recommendation. A group is ON only if all of its recommendations are ON.
  - A group with no recommendation keeps its configured state. That covers…

title: M6: a turned field keeps its place and its text runs along the turn (#4296)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4296.

**The need.** In Prepare a form, a tall text field placed along a page edge was given Rotation 90° or 270° in Properties ▸ Position. Its width and height swapped around its centre, so the field jumped out of place. When text was typed into it in Preview, the text was still shown upright. The expected result: the field stays where it was placed, and its text runs along the turned direction.

**The basis.**
- ISO 32000-2 Table 192 (`/MK /R`): "the number of degrees by which the widget annotation shall be rotated counterclockwise relative to the page", a multiple of 90.
- §12.5.5, Algorithm: appearance streams. The appearance's `/BBox` is "transformed, using Matrix", and then mapped "to align with the edges of the annotation's rectangle (specified by the Rect entry)".
- So `/Rect` stays the area the widget takes up on the page, whatever `/R` is. The rotation belongs in the appearance, through its `/Matrix`. Nothing in the spec asks for `/Rect` to change.

**The change**
- **Engine** (`forms::author::set_props`, used by Properties and by `form_set_props`): a rotation now changes only `/MK /R`, and the rectangle swap is gone. The appearance is redrawn the way #516 already lays it out: in in an upright box as wide as the field is tall, with a `/Matrix` that turns that box onto `/Rect`. A tall field turned 90° therefore holds a run of text going up its long side. Because nothing is resized any more, the "field is too small" refusal (which could only come from the swap) is gone too.
- **Properties ▸ Position** (`ui-egui::prepare`): picking a rotation no longer rewrites Left/Bottom/Width/Height.
- **Typing in a turned field** (`ui-egui::forms_ui`). The text is turned by `/MK /R` less the page's `/Rotate` and the view's rotation (both clockwise), which is how the page shows it. On screen:
  - The in-place editor stays over the field and keeps the keyboard and the pointer. It draws nothing itself; its text, selection and caret are painted tu…

title: M11: the optimizer stores Group 3 fax as Group 4, and packs black-and-white RGB and two-entry indexed images to one bit
author: Piohrun
body:
**Builds on #4384**, which builds on #4335 and #4304. Their commits come first. Please review the last nine: the two you saw ("the optimizer stores Group 3 fax images as Group 4 when smaller" and "the optimizer packs black-and-white RGB and indexed images to one bit", its subject reworded from "two-entry indexed", as an indexed image of any palette size packs when its samples are 0 and 1) and six from pre-push reviews (black-and-white RGB stays RGB where grey would be drawn otherwise; tests the mutation runs asked for; damaged Group 3; decode arrays read as numbers; the docs; Group 3 on bytes through the Group 4 step), and black-and-white RGB used beyond the page content read stays RGB. Once the PRs below merge I'll rebase, and the diff will shrink to them.

Monochrome Images left three common kinds of black-and-white image as they were:

- **Group 3 fax images.** A CCITT image that wasn't resampled was never decoded, so Group 3 (what fax software writes) stayed Group 3, though Group 4 codes each row against the one above and is usually much smaller. `optimize.mono-compression` listed "Group 3 to Group 4 without resampling" as missing.
- **Black-and-white RGB.** Some phone and scanner apps write a black-and-white page as eight-bit RGB. It went to the colour settings, so Reduce File Size made it a 150 ppi JPEG.
- **Indexed images of two colours.** Indexed images that use only palette entries 0 and 1 (as PDF printers write them) weren't touched at all.

## What this changes

1. **Group 3 becomes Group 4 when smaller.** Only Group 4 alone skips decoding now; Group 3 (one- or two-dimensional) is decoded and stored again as Group 4 when that is smaller as stored. Retain keeps it. It reads the image's CCITT parameters through `pdfcraft_cos::Document::fax_params` (its `/DecodeParms` entry with Table 11's defaults), which moved down to #4384, where redaction uses it too.

Hebrew (`he`, **עברית**) is an interface and date language, the third right-to-left one after Arabic and Central Kurdish.

- **Catalog** `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/he.tsv`: 2,762 entries, every `(context, English)` key of the current union of the bundled catalogs (commands, All tools, dialogs, tooltips, the engine's sentences, `@id` and `@plural` rows, the `calendar`, `certificate` and `key` contexts), written in logical order with the usual verbal-noun UI style (`שמירה`, `פתיחה…`). title: fix(render): degenerate subpaths, all-zero dash arrays and negative line widths stroke as the spec says (hayro-interpret patch 61)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4409.

**The need.** Three strokes came out wrong:
- `20 w 1 J 90 60 m h S`, a single-point closed subpath with round caps, drew nothing.
- `20 w 2 J 30 60 m 30 60 l S`, a zero-length subpath with projecting square caps, drew a 20 pt square.
- `4 w [0 0] 0 d … S` drew a faint line, every pixel along it half covered.

A negative width (`-6 w`) already drew a one-pixel line in the stroke colour, but devices were handed a width of −6.

**The basis.**
- ISO 32000-2 §8.5.3.2: "If a subpath is degenerate (consists of a single-point closed path or of two or more points at the same coordinates), the S operator shall paint it only if round line caps have been specified, producing a filled circle centred at the single point. If butt or projecting square line caps have been specified, S shall produce no output". The rule applies "only to zero-length subpaths of the path being stroked, and not to zero-length dashes in a dash pattern of a non-degenerate subpath", and "A single-point open subpath (specified by a trailing m operator) shall produce no output."
- §8.4.3.6: the dash array's numbers "shall be nonnegative and not all zero".
- §8.4.3.2: "A line width of 0 shall denote the thinnest line that can be rendered at device resolution".

ISO doesn't say how to recover from an all-zero dash array or a negative width; this follows the solid/thinnest-line reading used by other readers.

**The change** (vendored `hayro-interpret`, patch 61)
- **Degenerate subpaths** (`interpret/path.rs`, `resolve_degenerate_subpaths`). Where the interpreter strokes a path, each subpath is checked: does it have a segment or a `ClosePath`, with every point, control points included, at its start? With round caps such a subpath becomes a segment a thousandth of the line width long, centred on the point, which kurbo caps as a dot of the line width. With butt or square caps it is left out. Other subpaths, and zero-length dashes in them, are not touched, and the path is borrow…

title: M10: Word export keeps an italic run inside its sentence's paragraph (#4158)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4158. This is the smaller step from the analysis on the issue. A style change inside one line no longer splits the paragraph. A style change that wraps onto the next line still does, because the reading blocks keep their style boundaries (see the last section).

**The need.** In #4158, Export ▸ Word wrote 6,057 paragraphs for a court opinion, and most of them were fragments such as `v.`, `Id.` and `Chevron`. `group_reading_blocks` keeps style boundaries, so "Before *Chevron* after." reaches the exporter as three blocks. Every Office writer then emitted one paragraph per block.

**The basis.** This is the exporter's own design. No ISO 32000 clause governs Word output.
- The crate already defines a block that "continues another on the same line": it starts where that block ends (up to half an em later) and overlaps it vertically. It uses this test (`continuations`) to keep links and superscripts out of table cells (#2806).
- A WordprocessingML paragraph can hold several runs, each with its own run properties. HTML, RTF and DrawingML work the same way.

**The change** (`crates/export`, plus one field filled in by `crates/engine`)
- **Which block continues which.** `continued_from` names the block each block continues: of the candidates, the one that ends nearest to where it starts. `continuations` is now its `is_some`, so table detection behaves exactly as before.
- **Grouping.** `paragraphs` walks the blocks left to right. A block joins the paragraph of the block it continues only when:
  - that block starts strictly further left (so the links cannot form a cycle, and each paragraph is known before anything joins it);
  - both have the same rotation;
  - neither is a table cell or the slide title.
  
  Runs stay in order along the line, whatever order the blocks arrive in. The paragraph sits where its first run is.
- **Writers.** Every writer now emits one paragraph with one run per block, and each run keeps its size, bold, italic and co…

title: Redaction keeps images still drawn through a form without /Resources
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

`content_draws` in `crates/redact/src/interp.rs` tells whether some content draws an XObject, directly or through a form that has no `/Resources` of its own (such a form draws through its caller's). #4356 changed its recursion to pass the caller's `content` again instead of the nested form's decoded data. A name drawn only inside such a form is never found. The #4356 description lists only the `prune_doomed_xobjects` extraction for this file, so I take the change as unintended.

Both callers treat "not drawn" as "drop the entry": `unlink_doomed` for page-tree resource dictionaries (Apply Redactions, and the content pass of Remove Hidden Information) and `prune_doomed_xobjects` for surviving forms. So an image removed under a mark, but still shown elsewhere through such a form, disappears from there too. That can be the same page or another page that shares the resource dictionary. Nothing leaks. Too much goes.

The recursion reads the nested form's data again, as before #4356. The depth limit, the `seen` set and the fail-closed `None` are unchanged.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact`: 137 passed, 1 ignored (already ignored on main)
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`: not run, no crate boundary or asset touched

**Tests.** Two in `tests/surviving_references.rs`, next to the surviving-form tests:

- `an_image_a_surviving_forms_nested_form_draws_is_kept`: a surviving form that shares the page's resources draws the image through a nested form without `/Resources`.
- `an_image_another_page_draws_through_a_form_without_resources_is_kept`: two pages share one resource dictionary, and the second shows the image only through a form without `/Resources`.

With the #4356 recursion put back, both fail on the `full_save_holds` assertion: the image is gone from the saved file.

title: M11: PDF Optimizer can discard form submission, import and reset actions (optimize.discard-form-actions)
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

PDF Optimizer ▸ Discard Objects had no option for form actions (`optimize.discard-form-actions` was planned). The reference app's help page describes it: "Discard All Form Submission, Import And Reset Actions: Disables all actions related to submitting or importing form data, and resets form fields. This option retains form objects to which actions are linked." ("Discard Objects panel", https://web.archive.org/web/20221217175446/https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/optimizing-pdfs-acrobat-pro.html).

- Discard Objects has a new checkbox, "Discard all form submission, import and reset actions", off by default (`Settings::discard_form_actions`).
- It removes `/SubmitForm`, `/ImportData` and `/ResetForm` actions from `/A` entries (links, widgets, bookmarks), the catalog's `/OpenAction`, every `/AA` trigger and `/Next` chains. The fields, buttons and links stay, and an emptied `/AA` is removed.
- When a removed action has `/Next` actions, they take its place in the same order. When an indirect action, `/Next` array or `/AA` dictionary that holds a form action is shared, the cleaned value replaces that object once and every entry that uses it keeps its reference.
- An object that holds a form action more than 64 direct objects deep, chains form actions more than 64 deep, or makes the walk look at more than 100,000 action values stops the optimization with the new `OptimizeError::ActionLimit`, and so does a document that makes it look at more than 1,000,000 in all. Deep nesting with no form action in it is left as it is, and so is an indirect `/Next` array that lists itself.
- `doc_optimize` takes `discard_form_actions` and returns `form_actions` (each action counted once). It now also returns `print_settings`, which `Report` already counted.
- JavaScript that calls `submitForm` or `resetForm` is not changed; "Discard all links, actions and JavaScript" removes the JavaScript in links, widgets, `/AA` triggers, `/OpenAction` and the document's scripts…

title: M2: tiling pattern cells sit at their XStep/YStep multiples at every scale (ISO 32000-2 8.7.3.1)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4420.

**The need.** At screen resolutions a tiling pattern's cells drift from where they belong, and the drift grows with every step from the pattern's origin. In the fixture (a 10-point stroke painted with a 20-point-step pattern, about 400 points from the page origin) the cells are about 4 px right and 10 px up at 110 dpi: the bottom edge of the stroke shows slivers instead of whole cells. At 400 dpi it looks right, which hid it.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §8.7.3.1, Table 74: `/XStep` and `/YStep` are "the desired horizontal [vertical] spacing between pattern cells, measured in the pattern coordinate system", and "the key pattern cell … is then displaced by multiples of XStep and YStep to replicate the pattern". The `/TilingType` values let a reader distort a cell or vary the spacing by at most 1 device pixel; none allows an error that accumulates.

**The change** (vendored hayro patch (25), `vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`, `set_paint` tiling branch)
- **Cause.** The cell pixmap is `round(scale × step)` pixels a side and repeated with `Extend::Repeat`, but the cell was drawn, and the paint transform mapped the pixmap back to pattern space, at the unrounded `scale`. So the pixmap repeated every 31 px while a step is 30.56 px at 110 dpi: 0.44 px further per step.
- **Fix.** New `tiling_cell_pixels(scale, step, max)` returns the side and the scale to draw at, `side / step`, so one step is exactly the pixmap's side. The cell and the paint transform both use that scale. The cell is distorted by at most half a pixel inside the pixmap, and the paint transform maps it back, so in device space the period is the true step, under any pattern matrix.
- **Bounds.** The side stays within 1 and the existing 3000 px cap (`tiling_cell_scale`, unchanged), and the cap itself is at most `u16::MAX`. A step under half a pixel gets one pixel instead of a 0-wide pixmap. When `scale × step` isn't finite and positive, the scale is kept and the side is bounded:…

title: M2: a luminosity soft mask in a DeviceCMYK group converts as ISO 32000-2 10.4.2 says, so 100% K masks fully
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4422.

**The need.** A luminosity soft mask whose group is composited in `/DeviceCMYK` did not mask fully where the group paints 100% K. About an eighth of the masked paint came through (a mask value of 0.125 instead of 0), so red filled under such a mask showed as light pink over the backdrop. Gray and RGB groups were not affected.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §11.5.3: for a device colour space, the group's colour is converted "to DeviceGray by implementation-defined means and use the resulting gray value as the luminosity, with no compensation for gamma or other colour calibration". Its Example 2 gives `Y = 1 − min(1, 0.3 × C + 0.59 × M + 0.11 × Y + K)` for DeviceCMYK, and §10.4.2.3 gives the same DeviceCMYK to DeviceGray conversion. Table 142: `/BC` is a colour in the group's colour space.

**The cause.** The mask group is drawn into an RGB buffer and its luminance is read from that buffer. A `/DeviceCMYK` colour reached the buffer through the CMYK display profile, where 100% K is a dark grey rather than black. That is exactly the colour calibration §11.5.3 leaves out.

**The change** (vendored `hayro-interpret`, patch 63)
- **When it applies.** `SoftMask::new` notes when a luminosity mask's group `/CS` is `/DeviceCMYK` itself, by name. An ICC-based or calibrated group space keeps its own conversion and is not touched.
- **Content.** `SoftMask::interpret` sets `Context::luminosity_in_device_cmyk`. While it is set, `get_paint` gives a `/DeviceCMYK` fill or stroke colour as the DeviceGray colour `color::device_cmyk_to_gray` computes. This covers paths and text, in nested forms too. A gray triple reads back as itself through the mask's luminance weights (they sum to one), so the mask value is the ISO gray.
- **Backdrop.** A four-component `/BC` in such a group becomes the same gray.
- **Conversion.** `device_cmyk_to_gray` clamps each component to [0, 1] (NaN and infinities read as 0) and counts a missing component as 0.
- **Unchanged.** C…

title: Zeroize key material, KDF buffers, and UI password drafts (#3928)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:

title: M2: Type 3 text in rendering mode 7 is not rendered and adds no clip (ISO 32000-2 9.3.6)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4429.

**The need.** Text in a Type 3 font shown with `7 Tr` was painted, filled in the current fill colour (black by default). Clip-mode text is normally followed by a fill, so the glyphs showed wherever that fill didn't reach. In the issue's fixture that is a black bar beside a red box.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §9.3.6, after Table 104:
> Where text is drawn using a Type 3 font:
> • if text rendering mode is set to a value of 3 or 7, the text shall not be rendered.
> • if text rendering mode is set to a value other than 3 or 7, the text shall be rendered using the glyph descriptions in the Type 3 font.
> • If text rendering mode is set to a value of 4, 5, 6 or 7, nothing shall be added to the clipping path.

The same clause says that when "the only glyphs shown have no outlines … no clipping shall occur".

**The change** (vendored hayro-interpret patch 64, `interpret/text.rs`)
- **Mode 7.** `show_glyph` keeps mode 7 for a Type 3 glyph instead of turning it into a fill (patch 42 did that for every mode but 3). The glyph goes to the device as `GlyphDrawMode::Clip`: nothing is painted, and text extraction keeps it as clipping text, not as an invisible OCR layer.
- **The clip.** `clip_glyph`'s Type 3 arm is now a deliberate no-op citing §9.3.6. It used to log "not implemented". Text shown only in a Type 3 font leaves no clip at `ET`, and outline glyphs in the same text object still shape theirs.
- **Unchanged.** 0, 1, 2 and 4 to 6 render the glyph descriptions filled (patch 42), and 3 renders nothing.
- **Records.** Patch 64 is recorded in `vendor/README.md`, with patch 42's note and its renamed test. The `view.render-type3` notes in `parity/` now say how the modes apply.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed: `pdfcraft-render` (`--all-targets`) and `hayro-interpret` (`--lib --tests`)

title: M2: zero-area fills and clips mark the pixels they touch (view.render-pages)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4432.

**The need.** A rectangle with no height or no width encloses no area, and the rasteriser marked no pixels for it.
- **As a clip.** `10 10 100 0 re W n` hid everything painted after it. A fill of the whole box through that clip left the page blank.
- **As a fill.** `10 10 100 0 re f` fell back to a thinnest-line stroke. On a pixel boundary that stroke half-covered two rows, a faint line where one solid row belongs. So the fill and the clip of the same rectangle marked different pixels.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §10.7.4, "Scan conversion rules":
- A shape paints "any pixel whose half-open square region intersects the shape, no matter how small the intersection is".
- Its example: "A zero-width or zero-height rectangle paints a line 1 pixel wide."
- And: "For clipping, the clipping region consists of the set of pixels that would be included by a fill operation."

**The change.** hayro-interpret patch (65), `degenerate_fill_area` in `interpret/path.rs`.
- **What counts.** A fill or clip path whose bounding box has exactly no width or exactly no height, but not both. A box with area, however thin, is filled as the shape it is (scaled up, a "nearly zero" side can cover many device pixels).
- **One area per subpath.** Each subpath gets its own area, so a gap between two subpaths on the same line stays unpainted. The areas wind the same way, so the non-zero rule paints their union.
- **Along a device axis.** When the line stays within one device row or column, it gets the run of whole device pixels it touches, by the half-open rule: floor of the low end to ceiling of the high end, at least one pixel. A span under 1/256 of a pixel across is taken at its middle, so a CTM whose rounding tilts the line slightly still marks one row or column.
- **Rotated or skewed CTM.** Otherwise (the line crosses rows and columns) it gets a band one device pixel wide centred on the line, like the thinnest line of §8.4.3.2.
- **Fill rule.** The area is fil…

The reference app's help page lists it in the Discard User Data panel: "Discard External Cross References: Removes links to other documents. Links that jump to other locations within the PDF are not removed." (https://web.archive.org/web/20221217175446/https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/optimizing-pdfs-acrobat-pro.html).

- Discard User Data has a new checkbox, "Discard external cross-references", off by default (`Settings::discard_external_refs`).
- It takes `GoToR`, `GoToE`, `Launch` and `ImportData` actions, and `Thread` actions with an `/F`, out of the `/A` entries of link annotations and bookmarks. The actions chained after a removed one through `/Next` take its place in the same order; entries there that are not actions (a null, or a reference to one) do not.
- The page names links, so only link annotations (`/Subtype /Link`, also when the name is stored as an indirect object) and bookmarks are changed. Other annotations, such as form fields, keep their actions.
- A link left with no action and no `/Dest` is removed from its page, and from every other page or place in `/Annots` that lists the same link; a shared link counts once in `external_links`. When the link is an indirect object, that object is also rewritten without the action, so anything else that refers to it (the structure tree, for example) holds no action to another document. A bookmark keeps its title, its place and its children; bookmarks stored directly inside another bookmark are changed where they are.
- Links within the document (`/Dest`, `GoTo`) and web links (`URI`) stay. An indirect action that changes is written as a new indirect object, except the first action left at the head of an `/A`, which is copied into the `/A` directly when other actions follow it. Objects that use the old action keep it.

title: M9: a document timestamp lands in a signature field, where validators look
author: amoisttowe1
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4301.

`timestamp_document` appended its `/DocTimeStamp` dictionary with nothing pointing at it.
#4301 (from @alehel's review note on #4226): validators that discover signatures through
the AcroForm field tree may therefore miss a document timestamp. PdfCraft's timestamps
were such dictionaries. This makes us write the layout our validator has read since #621:

- The dictionary is stored as `/V` of a Sig field, reachable catalog → AcroForm `/Fields`
  → widget — the layout `sign()` writes for new fields. The field is its own widget:
  zero-area `/Rect`, `F 132` (Print|Locked), no `/AP` — a timestamp stamps the file, not a
  place on the page; page 1's `/Annots` gains it (redirected to a fresh array whenever
  the entry references one, rewritten inline otherwise) and AcroForm gains `/SigFlags 3`
  (SignaturesExist | AppendOnly), as `sign()` does. The name is `Timestamp_n`, counted
  past the names of existing named signature fields — `sign()`'s policy for `Signature{i}`.
  Basis: ISO 32000-2 §12.8.5, the document timestamp dictionary.
- A new Sig field is a form change: like `sign()`, linking requires permission bits 6 and

title: M2: a Separation /All colour paints every colourant, gray 1 − tint on screen (ISO 32000-2 8.6.6.4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4438.

**The need.** A Separation colour space whose colourant is the special name `/All` was drawn through its alternate space and tint transform, as if `All` were an ordinary spot ink. With `[/Separation /All /DeviceCMYK <</FunctionType 2 /Domain [0 1] /C0 [0 0 0 0] /C1 [1 0 0 0] /N 1>>]`, `0.5 scn` filled a box light cyan. `All` is the space registration targets and crop marks are drawn in, so they took whatever colour the writer's tint transform gave instead of the neutral "every ink" colour they stand for.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §8.6.6.4: the name All "shall refer collectively to all colourants available on an output device"; painting operators "shall apply tint values to all available colourants at once", and on an additive device such as a monitor the tint values "shall be complemented by subtracting from 1". So on screen a tint t is the gray 1 − t on R, G and B, whatever the alternate space and tint transform say. The same clause has `None` paint nothing.

**The change** (vendored `hayro-interpret` patch 66, `src/color.rs`)
- **Reading the space.** `Separation::new` notes when the colourant name is `All`. The vendored comment saying `All` was ignored is gone.
- **Converting.** `Separation::convert_f32` writes the gray 1 − t for each tint of an `All` space and never evaluates the tint transform. The tint is clamped to [0, 1] first, and a NaN tint becomes black through the existing saturating cast.
- **Reach.** Fills, strokes, images in the space and shadings in the space all convert through this function. The print path (`engine::print_raster`) renders an RGB raster through the same `PageRenderer`, so it follows too. There is no CMYK or separations output path on `main` to change.
- **Unchanged.**
  - `/None` still paints nothing.
  - Any other colourant name still goes through its alternate.
  - A DeviceN space that names `All` keeps its alternate: §8.6.6.4 gives the name this meaning for Separation spaces, and DeviceN's own…

title: Reject non-finite numbers in XFDF coordinate lists on import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

XFDF import no longer accepts non-finite coordinates. `csv()` in `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs` (lines 274-276, used by `annot_from_xml` at 924-928) parses coordinate lists with `str::parse::<f64>()`, which accepts `nan`, `inf` and `infinity`. `annot_from_xml` only checked the list length, so these values reached `/Rect`, `/L`, `/CL`, `/Vertices`, `/QuadPoints` and `/InkList`. The writer prints a non-finite real as `0`, so a saved file held an invented 0 coordinate.

Fix: `csv()` now returns an empty list when any entry is non-finite, so the list is treated like any other unusable one. An annotation with a bad `rect` is skipped, as already happens for a malformed rect. A line, callout or vertex list with a bad value is left out. The annotation is still imported if its `rect` is valid. Import still succeeds, and other annotations in the file are imported normally.

No existing issue is linked for this change.

- Regression tests `tests::import_skips_annotations_with_non_finite_coordinates` and `tests::import_drops_non_finite_numbers_from_every_coordinate_list` fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf non_finite`).

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4450.

**The need.** A combo box with the Edit flag (`/FT /Ch /Ff 393216`: Combo plus Edit) opened only its drop-down list on the page. There was no text box, so a value that isn't one of the options could not be typed, and keystrokes went nowhere. `form_fill` already took such a value headlessly, so only the page editor was missing.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:2020 §12.7.5.4: a combo box "may be accompanied by an editable text box in which the user can type a value other than the predefined choices, as directed by the value of the Edit bit in the Ff entry". Table 233, bit 19 Edit: "If set, the combo box shall include an editable text box as well as a drop-down list; if clear, it shall include only a drop-down list."

**The change** (`ui-egui::forms_ui`)
- **The text box.** An editable combo box opens a single-line text box over the field, styled like a text field's editor, as well as its list. The list works as before.
- **Committing.** Enter, Tab or a click away commits the typed text as `Edit::SetFieldValue` with `FieldValue::Choice`, which is the path `form_fill` and the list already use. Undo, field scripts and appearance regeneration therefore work as they do for any fill. A pick from the list still sets an option and discards the typing.
- **Shown text.** The text box starts on the shown text of the picked option, not its export value. Typing an option's shown text picks that option, because the engine maps it to the export value.
- **Without Edit,** a combo box is unchanged: a drop-down list only, and typing does nothing.
- `draft_text` (the editor's starting text) is also used where a re-opened draft is refreshed after an accepted edit (`editing.rs`), so the same field shows the same text either way.
- DoNotSpellCheck (bit 23) needs nothing, since the text box does no spell checking. CommitOnSelChange (bit 27) is already met, because a pick commits at once. MaxLen doesn't apply to choice fields.

title: M6: with NeedAppearances, check boxes and radio buttons draw their /MK caption (ISO 32000-2 Table 224)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4453.

**The need.** A form that sets `/NeedAppearances true` leaves its widgets' appearances to the viewer. PdfCraft already redraws text and choice fields for such forms (#3470), but check boxes and radio buttons kept the appearance streams the file carries. In the reported form, a check box whose `/MK /CA` is ZapfDingbats `4` (a check mark) has a filled square as its `/AP /N /Yes`. Checked, it showed the filled square, while most other readers show the check mark. A copy saved by PdfCraft looked the same.

**The basis.**
- ISO 32000-2 §12.7.3, Table 224, `NeedAppearances`: "A flag specifying whether to construct appearance streams and appearance dictionaries for all widget annotations in the document". It is deprecated in PDF 2.0, where appearance streams are required, but PDF 1.x forms still set it.
- Table 192, `/MK /CA`: "The widget annotation's normal caption, which shall be displayed when it is not interacting with the user". Unlike the other push-button entries, `CA` may be used with any type of button field, check boxes included.
- §12.7.5.2.3: the state is selected by `/AS` (or `/V`), and the standard example draws the on state as ZapfDingbats `(4) Tj`.

**The change** (`pdfcraft_forms::with_field_appearances_cached`, display copy only)
- **When.** When the form sets `/NeedAppearances`, every check box and radio button widget that has an `/MK` dictionary is drawn in its current state, whatever appearance the file gives it. This uses the `button_state_shown` path merged in #4368:

title: M7: opt-in grant for installed fonts that permit editable embedding
author: Hagma2023
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2077 (the engine and automation half of it).

A font the user selects only enters a PDF if its name table declares an open licence. That rules out the faces most office documents are set in (Arial, Calibri, Verdana…), even though their vendors declare editable embedding in OS/2 `fsType`, which `validate()` already enforces for every font. So a paragraph set in a subset of Calibri can't get a new character in Calibri, and bold/italic can't switch to the installed Calibri Bold.

This adds an explicit, opt-in grant instead of changing the default:

- `pdfcraft_fonts::embedding::FontGrant { OpenLicence (default), InstalledEmbeddable }`, re-exported from the engine.
- `validate_document_input(bytes, grant)`: under `InstalledEmbeddable` the open-licence declaration is not required. Everything else stays: the `fsType` gate in `validate()` (restricted 0x0002, preview & print 0x0004 and bitmap-only 0x0200 are refused), the excluded families and the Adobe-authored check apply under either grant.
- `Edit::RegisterTextFont { page, bytes, grant }`, `text::register_text_font(…, grant)` and `text_fonts::discover(roots, grant)` carry it through.
- Automation: `text_font_files` and `text_font_import` take `installed: true` (default false).
- The desktop app passes the default, so its behaviour is unchanged. The setting the issue proposes ("Allow installed fonts that permit embedding", off by default, with a one-time licence notice) and `.ttc` collections are left for a follow-up, so this PR stays reviewable and doesn't touch the i18n catalogues.

Nothing is bundled, shipped or committed: the font is read from the user's machine at the user's request, and the user answers for its licence when sharing the PDF (AGENTS.md §1.4).

- `cargo fmt --check`

title: M2: the standard 14 fonts fit the Euro to its standard width (view.render-pages)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4458.

**Scope: one change, two subjects it is tested on.** The code change is one patch (77): the renderer reads a bundled stand-in glyph's own advance, so it can fit the glyph to the standard width. The subjects are separate. The Euro in WinAnsiEncoding (code 128, Annex D Table D.2) was drawn too wide, and this is the bug the patch fixes. The check mark in ZapfDingbats (a20, the `/MK /CA` caption `4` of a check box) is tested because the same patch now applies to it. It already fitted its advance, so its tests guard against a regression and change nothing that is drawn. The two can be reviewed separately: `vendor/hayro-interpret` and `crates/render/tests/it/euro_width.rs` for the Euro, and `crates/render/tests/it/symbol_dingbats_width.rs` and `crates/engine/tests/it/dingbat_check_box.rs` for Symbol and ZapfDingbats.

**The need.** A standard 14 font named without embedding and without `/Widths` drew the € so wide that the next glyph ran into it. "€5", "€€" and "a€b" collided in Helvetica, and more in Times-Roman and Times-Bold. The advances were right. The € itself was drawn up to 722 units wide in a 500-unit advance.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §9.6.2.2: for the standard 14 fonts, `Widths` and `FontDescriptor` were optional in PDF 1.0 to 1.7, and a PDF processor "shall have these fonts, or their font metrics and suitable substitution fonts, available". So the substitute has to fit the standard metrics. Annex D, Table D.2: the Euro is WinAnsiEncoding code 200 (octal), that is 128. §9.2.4: the advance places the next glyph, so a glyph wider than its advance overlaps it.

**The change** (`vendor/hayro-interpret`, patch (77))
- **Root cause.** The metrics were never the problem: the renderer's standard metrics and the writer's `Std14` table both already give the Euro 556 (Helvetica family), 500 (Times) and 600 (Courier), and every other WinAnsi name has a width in both. The renderer fits a substitute glyph to the standard width only when …

author: tzhazuma
body:
This adds `apps/printcraft-android`: a Gradle project that hosts the existing egui UI inside an `android-activity` window, plus one small seam in the shared UI crate — PrintCraft is the one Craft app whose file dialogs live *inside* `crates/ui-egui` instead of a host hook.

PrintCraft is pure Rust (the parser, interpreter, rasteriser and text extractor are its own crates), so the only platform code here is the Java picker bridge.

## What the shell does

- **Entry point** — builds as `libmain.so`, loaded with `System.loadLibrary`; `android_main` is the usual `android-activity` entry.
- **The shared-crate seam** — `rfd` 0.17 does not compile for Android at all (its platform traits go unimplemented there) and `arboard` has no Android backend. `crates/ui-egui/src/fd.rs` is a drop-in: on every platform `rfd` supports it re-exports `rfd`'s types unchanged, and on Android it is a lookalike with the same builder API that asks a `Host` the app shell installs. The call sites become `crate::fd::{FileDialog, AsyncFileDialog}` — mechanical and platform-neutral; `rfd` and `arboard` move behind `not(target_os = "android")`, and the two `arboard` calls get an Android twin that returns `None` (the app's own snapshot still pastes).
- **Pickers** — the Storage Access Framework answer: an open copies the picked document into `<filesDir>/import/`; a save reserves a path in `<filesDir>/export/` and a worker publishes the finished file to the `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` destination once it stops growing. File ▸ Open uses the *asynchronous* dialog the UI already polls, so the answer arrives on a later frame and the app's own `process_picked → open_path` opens it — no dialog code was rewritten.
- **Phone start-up state** — Read mode with the left tool panel closed, 40 pt hit targets, no zoom, plus a command-palette long-press (top 9%, 500 ms) that runs the app's own commands.
- **Fonts and self-test** — the system CJK face is appended to egui's live definitions after the theme install; a back…

title: M12: reject impossible dates in XFA picture conversions
author: wireless89
body:
## What this changes

XFA date-picture conversions accepted impossible dates such as `1900-02-29` and `2026-04-31`, and could display an invented weekday. Validate calendar dates and weekdays with the existing workspace `chrono` dependency. Invalid or out-of-range stored dates retain their raw value; valid leap dates still convert.

The review follow-up also caps date-pattern tokenization at **4096 UTF-8 bytes**, checked before allocating character/token lists. An oversized pattern is refused explicitly and callers retain raw values. This is an application resource budget, not an XFA specification limit or a bound on total form memory. XML/picture extraction retains its existing input-sized costs.

## How you verified it

Current head: `124aa828e8043142ed032a5def0fef3703cae9c4`, integrated with main `b36bdaeac6f53f26ce03187e91e6230c71eaece2` (2026-11-01). On macOS arm64, Rust 1.99.1:

- `cargo test --locked --offline -p pdfcraft-xfa -j 2`: **150 passed**, 0 failed.
- Format, strict scoped Clippy/all-targets, scoped wasm32, layers, assets, parity and diff checks passed.
- Calendar regressions cover invalid dates, valid leap dates, weekday consistency, layout/live-script values, unchanged datasets synchronization, unrelated edits, unbound data and incremental save/reopen.
- Three new budget regressions cover the exact boundary, over-budget refusal, multibyte byte counting, and unchanged stored data through an unrelated edit and save/reopen. All three were observed failing without the tokenizer guard on the previous base; they pass with the guard.
- A synthetic 1 MiB separator pattern on the previous head created 1,048,576 tokens with 25 MiB of retained vector/string capacities, excluding the temporary character vector and allocator overhead. This measures allocation amplification, not RSS or a demonstrated crash.

Rebase conflicts were in progress/parity records and the shared test-file append point. Upstream entries/tests were retained; the source, test and crate-REA…

title: M12: honor named-month XFA data pictures on read and write
author: wireless89
body:
## What this changes

An XFA field bound with `date{DD MMM YYYY}` currently leaves `18 Oct 2026` as the script's raw value and as the widget text, even when its edit picture is `MM/DD/YYYY`. Filling a new date then writes ISO text such as `2026-10-19` into the datasets instead of the declared `19 Oct 2026`.

`data_date_letters` recognizes only numeric month tokens when checking that a data picture contains a whole date. Accept the existing `MMM` and `MMMM` tokens too. The shared converter already reads and writes English month names; this connects those existing capabilities to data binding. A year and an original `D` or `DD` day-of-month token remain required. Check the original picture before normalization maps weekday `E`/`EE` to `d`/`dd`. Weekday-only and unsupported month runs do not qualify.

## How you verified it

Validated on macOS arm64, Rust 1.99.1, rebased onto main `fa5f9f8c3b3add965f7ec82c743cf02207c55c93` (2026-10-30). Conflicts were limited to progress documentation; all upstream progress text was retained and the feature's source/test additions and removals match the previous revision.

- `cargo test --locked --offline -p pdfcraft-xfa -j 2`: **134 passed**.
- Format, scoped strict Clippy (`--all-targets -- -D warnings`), scoped wasm32 check, layers, assets, parity and diff checks passed.
- All original named-month data-picture regressions were observed failing before the fix. They exercise actual XFA/COS reads and writes, layout and live-script values, edits, incremental save/reopen, dataset spelling and unrelated-data preservation, including a field with initially empty data.
- Additional regressions reject weekday-only data pictures and numeric `E`/`EE` anywhere in the picture, including beside an original `D`/`DD`. They were observed failing before the corresponding corrections; incomplete pictures preserve stored text and new dates use ISO. Named `EEE`/`EEEE` weekdays beside a day-of-month remain supported.

title: M3: copied text keeps one line per baseline, reading order for turned lines, letters for ligatures (#4467)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4467.

**The need.** Copy and `text_extract` broke text into more lines than the page shows.
- **One baseline, several lines.** Runs drawn too far apart to merge, or in different sizes, or out of order each got a line of their own: `08` / `first` / `second` for a row that reads `08 first second`.
- **A turned line at the end.** A word set upwards in a row came out after the whole page.
- **The ligature character.** A glyph named `/fi` in the font's encoding came out as U+FB01, so a pasted `office` was not the word, and Find missed it.

**The basis.**
- **Ligatures.** ISO 32000-2 §9.10.3: its ToUnicode example maps the ff, fi and ffl ligature glyphs to "a Unicode scalar value for each character in the ligature: LATIN SMALL LETTER F (U+0066) LATIN SMALL LETTER I (U+0069) for f i". 4 of 5 other readers copy the letters.
- **Lines and turned text.** ISO 32000-2 does not say how untagged text forms lines (§14.8.2.6.2 leaves word and line finding to the processor), so this follows most other readers:
  - a baseline reads as one line, left to right (4 of 5);
  - columns stay apart (5 of 5);
  - a turned line reads in its place (4 of 5).

**The change** (`crates/render/src/text.rs`)
- **Ligature letters** (`draw_glyph`, `ligature_letters`). U+FB00–U+FB06 become their compatibility decomposition: ff, fi, fl, ffi, ffl, st, st. Nothing else is normalised, and the glyph keeps its one box.
- **One line per baseline** (`arrange`, step 4; `same_line`). The next block joins the line just read, with a space at the gap (more than `WORD_GAP` heights), when:
  - its first line's baseline is within a fifth of a height of that line's;
  - it starts to that line's right;
  - it is less than `SAME_LINE_GAP` = 8 heights of the taller run away.

  Baselines are compared as the em box bottom less a fifth of its height, so a 9 pt label and a 14 pt word on one baseline match.
- **What stays apart.**
  - Two columns: a column of several lines is read only after the c…

title: M3: Find matches ligatures and words split by a line-end hyphen (#4469)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4469.

**The need.** Find and `text_find` missed two kinds of words people search for:
- **Ligatures.** `office` was not found where the page draws `of` + an fi ligature glyph whose text is U+FB01. Fonts that name the glyph `/fi`, and ToUnicode maps or `/ActualText` that give U+FB00–U+FB06, all produce this.
- **Divided words.** `example` was not found where the line ends in `exam-` and the next starts with `ple`, and neither was `exam-ple`.

**The basis.**
- **Ligatures.** ISO 32000-2 §9.10.3 maps ligature glyphs to the letters they stand for ("a Unicode scalar value for each character in the ligature: LATIN SMALL LETTER F (U+0066) LATIN SMALL LETTER I (U+0069) for f i"). Every other reader I compared (5 of 5) finds `office`.
- **Divided words.** §14.8.2.3 has writers mark a hyphen that only divides a word as U+00AD, but untagged PDFs rarely do. ISO is silent on how search treats a U+002D at a line end, so this follows most other readers: 4 of 5 find `example`.

**The change** (`crates/render/src/text/search.rs`, used by Find, `text_find` and Search & Redact's word list)
- **Ligatures.** U+FB00–U+FB06 read as their letters (ff, fi, fl, ffi, ffl, st, st) in both the page and the query, before case folding and whether or not the search is case-sensitive.
  - Each letter stays owned by its glyph, so the highlight covers the ligature.
  - Nothing else is normalised (U+FB13, full-width letters and circled digits stay distinct).
- **What counts as a divided word.** A glyph divides a word when:
  - it ends its line with a visible hyphen (U+002D or U+2010), past any invisible characters find skips (a line that ends in a soft hyphen, U+00AD, already runs on to the next on `main`);
  - a letter comes before the hyphen, in the same glyph or in the glyph before it on the line with no word gap;
  - the next line starts with a letter.
- **How it is searched.** When a page has such a glyph, it is searched in three readings:
  - as written, where the b…

title: M7: synthetic bold and italic per range in the text's own face
author: Hagma2023
body:
## What this changes

Bold and italic in a face that has no bold or italic variant. Today, a paragraph set in an embedded face can only become bold by switching to a standard family (`BlockStyle.bold` swaps the face to Helvetica/Times/Courier-Bold), and a range can't become bold or italic at all unless it is already in a standard family. Word processors solve this by drawing the variant synthetically; this does the same, per range or for the whole paragraph:

- `RangeStyle::synthetic_bold` / `synthetic_italic` and the same on `BlockStyle` (`Option<bool>`).
  - **Bold:** the run is filled, then stroked in its own fill colour, `SYNTHETIC_BOLD` = 1/30 em wide (`2 Tr`, round joins, no dash). Every fill colour space carries over (`g/rg/k/cs/sc/scn` → `G/RG/K/CS/SC/SCN`).
  - **Italic:** the text matrix's vertical axis is sheared along the baseline by `SYNTHETIC_SLANT` = tan 12° (`slanted()`).
  - The face, advances and wrapping stay as they were. `Some(false)` takes either away again, also where a word processor drew it (a stroke in the fill colour; an outline in another colour stays).
- Automation: `text_edit` takes `synthetic_bold` / `synthetic_italic` for the paragraph and in each `ranges` item.

Three reading fixes were needed so a slanted run survives the next edit. Each one also applies to word-processor PDFs that use sheared italic today:

1. **`same_plane` compares the vertical axis upright.** A sheared word was another "plane", so `Plain *words* here` fell apart into three paragraphs after one italic word.
2. **`upright_height`: a line's size and `k` come from the height square to its baseline**, not from the length of the slanted axis. A 12 pt slanted word read as 12.27 pt.
3. **A run's box (`rect`/`frame`) is its cell standing upright on the pen's path**, as an italic face's box is its advance. The rise still moves along the real axis (group moves use `Ts`).
   - The parallelogram's bounding box was wider by the slant. That made the next rewrite stretch the ru…

title: M3: web and email addresses written as page text open like links (#4207)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4207.

**The need.** Many PDFs, among them office exports and scans run through OCR, show web and email addresses as plain page text with no link annotation over them. In PdfCraft such an address did nothing: no link cursor on hover, nothing on a click (#4207). The reader expects it to open the way a link does.

**The basis.** No clause of ISO 32000-2 covers this. The standard defines link annotations (§12.5.6.5) and URI actions (§12.6.4.8), not reading addresses out of page text. The basis is the issue, and this follows the rules PdfCraft already applies to addresses that come from documents.

**The change**
- **Detection** (`engine::text_links`, new).
  - `find_text_links` runs the detector Create links from URLs already uses (`pdfcraft_annot::links::find_urls`) over a page's extracted text, through `PageText::find_with`. It returns each address with one view-space rectangle per line.
  - It finds `http://` and `https://` addresses, `www.` addresses (opened as `https://`; `find_urls` itself keeps `http://` for the links it writes into documents) and email addresses (`mailto:`).
  - Sentence punctuation (`.` `,` `;` `:` `!` `?`) and brackets around an address are left out. Text that only looks like an address (`example.com`, `https://x`, `user@localhost`, `a@b.c`) is not found.
  - Work is capped: at most 512 addresses per page, and nothing is searched on a page of more than 200,000 glyphs.
  - `TextLink::covered_by` tells when a link annotation lies over the address. The annotation is what the document asks for there, so it wins.
- **Desktop** (`canvas`).
  - With the Select tool, an address in the page text shows the link cursor and its address on hover.
  - A click goes through `request_document_url` with `LinkOrigin::Link`. That is the same `links::document_url` check (http, https and mailto only, hidden characters, mail parameters, length) and the same confirmation as a link annotation.
  - The addresses are found once per page tex…

title: M3: relative links resolve against the document's base URI, and a link is active only in its QuadPoints (view.follow-links)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4473.

**The need.** Two kinds of link didn't work the way the document describes them:
- A URI action written as a relative address (`page.html`) in a document whose catalog gives `/URI << /Base (https://example.com/base/) >>` was refused as "the address isn't a complete web or email address".
- A link whose `/QuadPoints` cover only the first word of a line opened from anywhere in its `/Rect`.

**The basis.**
- ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.8, Table 211. `Base` is "the base URI that shall be used in resolving relative URI references. URI actions within the document may specify URIs in partial form, to be interpreted relative to this base address."
- ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.5, Table 176. `QuadPoints` are "n quadrilaterals in default user space that comprise the region in which the link should be activated". The region is `Rect` when the entry "is not present, or the PDF processor does not recognise it, or if any coordinates in the QuadPoints array lie outside the region specified by Rect".

**The change**
- **Base URI** (`render::link_area::resolve_uri`, used by `inspect`).
  - Inspection reads the catalog's `/URI /Base` (a string of at most 8 KiB) into `DocInfo::uri_base`.
  - A URI action without an RFC 3986 scheme is resolved against the base by RFC 3986 §5, through the `url` crate. It is already in the tree, and `engine::links` checks addresses with it. `LinkTarget::Uri` then carries the resolved address.
  - The base is used only when it is an `http`/`https` address that names its host as written (`https://host/…`). The result must keep the base's scheme.
  - An address that already has a scheme is never touched.
  - An address or base with control characters, or whitespace other than a space, is left as written. The URL rules would drop those characters and read `java\nscript:` as a scheme.
  - The resolved address then goes through the same `links::document_url` check and confirmation as before.
- **QuadPoints** (`render::link_area::link_quads`…

title: M7: a moved text box's drag preview shows the box alone (#4464)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4464.

**The need.** Add a text box over something on the page (a filled shape, a picture, other text), finish it, then drag it. The preview that follows the pointer carries a copy of whatever the box covered at its first place. It looks as if the page content is being moved, though on release only the text moves.

**The basis.** A pure display fix; no PDF semantics change. The cause: during a move (#1488), the moving pixels were cut from the page's own raster inside the item's box. That raster has the item *and* everything under it.

**The change**
- **`pdfcraft_edit::isolate_content`** (new). On a copy of the document, leaves item `index` alone on its page: `/Contents` becomes the item's own stream, `/Annots` goes. The item's stream already starts from the page's initial graphics state (`place_tagged` closes everything drawn before it), so it draws the same on its own.
- **`Document::added_content_alone`** (new). Renders that copy with `RenderConfig { transparent: true, .. }`. Read-only, like `added_content_preview`: working bytes, dirty state and undo history are untouched.
- **`MoveBackground`** (`ui-egui`). Renders both rasters per gesture: the page without the item (as before) and the item alone. The moving pixels now come from the item-alone raster, mapped from its first box onto the dragged one, so what it covered stays where it is. The preview shows once both rasters are in; until then, or if either render fails, the item stays put while dragged, as before. The same holds for a picture resized by a corner and for the frames after release while the page re-renders.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

title: M12: embed a Unicode fallback for fixed XFA page text
author: wireless89
body:
## What this changes

Fixed XFA page text outside WinAnsi currently paints `?` and reports that standard fonts cannot draw it. Use the already bundled Inter Regular when it covers the entire affected span, with embedded Unicode mappings for copying/text extraction. This includes Latin Extended, Greek, Cyrillic and symbols such as `►` (U+25BA). Ordinary spans retain their standard face.

Reject spans with an unusable advance before allocating any persistent font objects, preventing repeated relayouts of a standalone combining mark from accumulating unreachable fonts. Fit the replacement to the advance already measured by layout, preserving existing wrapping, alignment and link bounds. Embed the complete font lazily and reuse its validated resource across pages and relayouts, including save/reopen. No new font asset or dependency is introduced.

This complements #2761 (field appearances) and #1566 (fonts embedded in the source document): this change addresses fixed page text when the source has no embedded font. The U+25BA warning was also reported separately in #1637; this does not address that issue's other layout concerns.

This addresses the fixed-page-text part of #4938. Unicode values in editable fields remain a separate forms-layer issue, so #4938 must stay open. CJK, Arabic and Hebrew spans require other fonts and, where applicable, shaping. An affected span containing an uncovered character retains the existing fallback and warning.

## How you verified it

Validated on macOS arm64, Rust 1.99.1, rebased onto main `fa5f9f8c3b3add965f7ec82c743cf02207c55c93` (2026-10-30). Conflicts were limited to progress documentation; all upstream progress text was retained and the feature's source/test additions and removals match the previous revision.

title: fix(sign): let a writer raise the catalog /Version after signing
author: akbartriasno
body:
## What this changes

A later revision that raises the catalog's `/Version` no longer makes an earlier signature show as invalid with "document structure". `/Version` may now be added or raised after signing. A signed version may not go back or be dropped, and one that does not read as a version may not change at all.

PAdES LTV writers add the `/DSS` and lift `/Version` in the same revision. ISO 32000-2 §7.7.2 provides the entry so a version can be raised by an incremental update. `/Version` was not in the catalog keys that may change after signing (`change_kind` in `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs`), so the signature the DSS protects was judged altered.

Follow-up to #4133, which let `/Extensions` gain declarations. That file shape still failed on `main` after #4133, and the only remaining cause was `/Version`.

I hit it on an invoice signed with VIDA (PAdES, ECDSA P-256) and then stamped with an Indonesian e-Meterai (second signature, `ETSI.CAdES.detached`). Its revisions are: the first signature; a DSS revision that adds `/DSS`, `/Extensions /ADBE` and `/Version /1.7`; the e-Meterai signature, whose revision also adds `/Extensions /ESIC`; and a last DSS update. poppler's `pdfsig` reports both signatures valid, and the PdfCraft 0.13.0 release flagged the first one. With this change the same file validates in a local build. I searched issues and PRs (DSS, LTV, Extensions, ESIC, signature, document structure) and found only #4133 and #3440; #3440 keeps the same catalog key list, so it does not cover this.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign`: 119 pass)
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`: not applicable, no crate boundary or asset touched

**Tests** (`crates/sign/tests/it/pdf.rs`):
