title: feat(ui): Ctrl+Shift+→ / ← open the next / previous PDF in the document's folder (#4267)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Ctrl+Shift+→ / ← (⇧⌘→ / ⇧⌘← on macOS) now open the next / previous PDF in the same folder as the open document, also under File ▸ Open next / previous PDF in folder.

Acrobat has no command like this, so it follows the request in #4267: only files ending in `.pdf` (any case) in the document's own folder, no subfolders, folders or files whose name starts with a dot (macOS `._name.pdf` resource files would otherwise show up on some drives). The order is natural rather than plain alphabetical, so `scan2.pdf` comes before `scan10.pdf`, which is what a folder of numbered invoices needs; happy to switch to plain alphabetical if you prefer. The file opens through the normal open path, in its own tab, so the document you came from keeps its tab and any unsaved changes, and a file that is already open just comes to the front. At the first or last PDF, or for a document that was never saved to a folder, nothing opens and a notice says why. Text fields keep the shortcut for extending the selection, and the web build has no folder, so the command is disabled there. The folder is read once per keypress. Before this, Ctrl+Shift+→ also turned the page (the canvas ignores the modifiers on the arrows); plain → and Ctrl+→ still do. Same with Ctrl+Shift+→ nudging a selected comment, which Ctrl+→ still does. If you'd rather keep these keys free, happy to switch the shortcut.

Left out: following the file manager's own sort order (each one keeps it differently) and toolbar buttons. Also open: whether stepping should replace the current tab instead of adding one; I kept the tab so nothing unsaved is ever at risk, but that piles up tabs on a long folder. A password-protected or unreadable PDF stops the stepping there, since stepping starts from the active tab; remembering the last file tried would get past it, if you want that.

Validation:
- `commands::ctrl_shift_arrows_open_the_next_and_previous_pdf_in_the_folder`: fails on main (Ctrl+Shift+→ leaves `scan1.pdf` shown instead of opening …

title: feat(view): add cursor coordinates floating window and tool (view.cursor-coordinates)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Implements Acrobat parity feature `view.cursor-coordinates` (milestone M12 / P2):
- **Engine Command (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`)**:
  - Registers `view.cursor_coordinates` ("Cursor coordinates") with shortcut `Ctrl+Y` (`Cmd+Y` on macOS) and icon `mouse-pointer-2`.
  - Document-scoped command (`Needs::Document`).
- **Headless Automation Tool (`crates/automation/src/cursor_coords.rs`, `crates/automation/src/tools.rs`, `crates/automation/src/lib.rs`)**:
  - Implements `view_cursor_coordinates` tool supporting coordinate evaluation across user and view spaces, configurable bottom-left and top-left origins, and unit formatting in `pt`, `in`, `mm`, and `cm`.
  - Returns page dimensions and evaluated point coordinates formatted per unit precision.
  - Registered in the automation tool catalog and dispatched via `Automation::call`.
  - Added end-to-end integration test in `crates/automation/tests/it/automation.rs::cursor_coordinates_tool_evaluates_points_and_dimensions`.
- **UI Floating Window & Controls (`crates/ui-egui/src/cursor_coordinates_ui.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/chrome.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/commands.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs`)**:
  - Non-modal, movable floating window (`egui::Window`) tracking mouse pointer over document pages in real time.
  - Displays `X`, `Y` coordinates and current page `Width` and `Height`.

title: fix(xfdf): a multi-select choice holding ", " survives Export/Import Data as XML, CSV or text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4484.

XML, CSV and text keep a multi-select list's choices in one cell joined by ", ", and the import split that cell at every ", ", so an option with a comma in it ("Smith, John") came back as pieces that match nothing and the field was refused. The cell is still split at every ", " first, and if every piece is one of the field's options (export value or display text, as `set_value` accepts) that is the result, so every cell that was accepted before gives the same result as before. Only when some piece isn't an option is the cell read as a run of the field's own options separated by ", " (a small left-to-right pass over the cell, trying each option at each reachable position, comparing both the export value and the display text), which needs no change to the export format. If the cell isn't made of the field's options either, it is split as before, so what used to be refused is still refused.

title: M6: radio buttons sharing an on state are exclusive unless RadiosInUnison (form.fill-checkbox-radio)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4488.

**The need.** A radio group can give several buttons the same on state, for example `Yes`, `Yes`, `No`. When its RadiosInUnison flag was clear, clicking one `Yes` turned on every `Yes`. Clicking the other `Yes` then changed nothing, so it could never be chosen on its own. The value model named only the on state, so `set_states` turned on every widget that had it, and the click decided "already selected" from `/V`, which is the same for both buttons.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- Table 229, RadiosInUnison: "If clear, the buttons are mutually exclusive (the same behaviour as HTML radio buttons)".
- §12.7.5.2.3, after EXAMPLE 2: "If it is not set, at most one radio button in a field shall be set at a time."
- §12.7.5.2.4: `/V` holds the on state of "whichever child field is currently in the on state", and where `/V` and `/AS` differ "the value of the AS key shall be used". With two `Yes` buttons, `/V` is `/Yes` whichever is on, and only the widgets' `/AS` tells them apart.
- Table 229, NoToggleToOff: if clear, "clicking the selected button deselects it".
- Table 230: with `/Opt`, on states may be positions (`/0`, `/1`, …) to tell buttons with the same export value apart. Those buttons already have distinct on states, so they are unaffected. The `/Opt` handling from #532 (`state_for`, `export_of`) is unchanged.

**The change** (`forms`, `ui-egui::forms_ui`, `automation`)
- **One button, not one state.** A new `FieldValue::Widget(i)` turns on widget `i` of a check box or radio group, as a click on it does. A click, Space and the arrow keys now send it.
- **Exclusive unless in unison.** In a radio group without RadiosInUnison, `set_states` turns on only that widget, and every other widget gets `/AS /Off`. A check box, or a radio group with RadiosInUnison, still turns on every widget that shares the state (§12.7.5.2.3 EXAMPLE 2).

body:
## What this changes

Part of #4340 (the headless half).

The renderer reports when a page's picture is incomplete or approximate (`RenderWarning::ContentTruncated`: content past the page's safety budget was skipped; `RenderWarning::ColourFallback`: a colour that could not be computed was painted in a fallback colour). body:
## Real forms

Two public forms have check box fields whose kids have different on states. Each fill below was made with `form_fill`, saved, reopened, and read back with PDFium and MuPDF, which agree on which kid's `/AS` is on in every row. `main` is f42fda734.

- `issue12716.pdf` (https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/12716), the CMS-1500 health insurance claim form. 11 of its 12 check box fields are like this: `sex` (M/F), `insurance_type` (7 kinds), `rel_to_ins` (S/M/C/O), `ssn` (SSN/EIN), `ins_sex` (MALE/FEMALE) and six YES/NO pairs.

| Form | Filled | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issue12716.pdf` | `sex = "F"` | M on, F off | F on, M off |
| `issue12716.pdf` | `insurance_type = "Group"` (opens with Other on) | Medicare on, the rest off | Group on, the rest off |

## What this changes

Fixes #4495.

**The need.** A check box field can have several widget kids with different on states, for example `A` and `B`. PdfCraft could only ever tick the first one. With `A` ticked, clicking `B` cleared the field, so `B`'s tick flashed and vanished. With nothing ticked, clicking `B` ticked `A`. There were two causes:
- The click sent `Check(f.value.is_empty())`, a field-wide toggle. Whichever kid was clicked, a field that was on turned off.

title: M8: after Apply redactions, Save asks where and proposes the name with _Redacted (protect.redact-filename-suffix)
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

After Apply redactions, Save wrote the redacted document over the file it was opened from. The reference app's help page "Removing sensitive content from PDFs" (section "Redact sensitive content") says that after Apply: "The Save As dialog is displayed. Specify a filename and location. The suffix “_Redacted” is appended to the filename." (https://web.archive.org/web/20221231010434/https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/removing-sensitive-content-pdfs.html).

- The view counts the Apply redactions steps in effect (`DocView::redactions_applied`). While the count is above 0, Save on the desktop works as Save As: it asks where, and the dialog proposes `<stem>_Redacted.pdf` (for example `contract_Redacted.pdf`) in the document's folder. The `.pdf` extension is matched in any letter case. The web build downloads under that name, and a host page (`?host=parent`) receives the first save after Apply redactions as a Save As.
- Undo of an Apply redactions step takes one off the count and Redo adds it back. Revert, Reload and a successful desktop save set it to 0, so the next Save writes in place. The web build keeps the count after a download, so later downloads also carry the `_Redacted` name. A name that already ends in `_Redacted` keeps one suffix.
- Save after Apply redactions no longer writes over the opened file without asking. Sign's save proposes `{stem}_signed.pdf` the same way (`crates/ui-egui/src/sign_ui.rs`).
- The naming helper, `redacted_file_name`, is in `pdfcraft-redact` (re-exported by the engine). The `redact_apply` tool's result now carries the same name in `save_as`, for `doc_save`'s `path`. `doc_save` without `path` still writes in place.

title: M6: a value the validate action rejects is dropped and the field keeps its value (#4498)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4498.

**The need.** A text field whose validate action rejects the typed value (a range it is outside, or a script that sets `event.rc = false`) showed the message but kept the rejected text in its editor and pulled focus back to it on Tab or a click. The user could not move on to the next field without first fixing the text by hand. Every other reader tested (5 of 5) shows the message, puts the field back to its previous value and lets focus move on.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 Table 199: the `/V` action "shall be performed when the field's value is changed. This action may check the new value for validity." It doesn't say what a reader does with a rejected value, so this follows the behaviour all five other readers share. The engine already treated a rejection as no change: the edit runs on a copy, so the document and undo history were untouched. Only the interface held on to the text.

**The change**
- **`forms`:** a new `FormError::Rejected` tells a validate refusal apart from the others. It covers the range check and a custom validate script returning `event.rc` false; its message is the range's text or the script's alert. A keystroke (format) refusal stays `Invalid`/`Format`, since it is about the typing.
- **`engine`:** `EditError::is_rejected_value()`.
- **`ui-egui` (`editing.rs`):** `apply_edit` now wraps `try_apply_edit`, which returns the error. When typed text is rejected by the validate action, the draft is dropped instead of reopened. The field shows its kept value, and the editor that Tab or a click opened on the next field stays open. A format refusal still reopens the editor with the text (#166).

title: M7: dotted day-first dates in header and footer
author: Hagma2023
body:
## What this changes

Header and footer dates come from a fixed token list (like Acrobat's dialog): US (`m/d/yyyy` …), ISO (`yyyy-mm-dd`) and day-first with slashes (`d/m/yyyy`, `dd/mm/yyyy`). The dotted day-first forms used in German-speaking countries and much of Central and Eastern Europe were missing, so a footer there couldn't show `24.10.2026`.

- `edit::expand`: `<<dd.mm.yyyy>>`, `<<d.m.yyyy>>`, `<<dd.mm.yy>>`, `<<d.m.yy>>`.

title: forms: clear typed XFA password field values from datasets on save (#3944)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3944

Although #3943 cleared the AcroForm `/V` (and masked `/AP /N`) of Password-flagged text fields when writing a document to disk, editing an XFA `<passwordEdit/>` field also mirrors the typed value into the XFA `datasets` stream (`xfa_sync_datasets`), and incremental updates could retain earlier edits' datasets or masked appearance streams in the document overlay. title: Fix FormCalc Round overflowing to infinity for large values
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

FormCalc `Round()` no longer returns infinity for large values with decimal places.

Cause: `Round` computes `(a * k).round() / k` with `k = 10^places`. When `a * k` exceeds f64::MAX, the product becomes infinity, so `Round(1e300, 12)` returned infinity instead of 1e300.

Fix: `Round` checks whether the scaled product is finite. If it is not, it returns `a` unchanged, since a value that large has no fractional digits to round. Ordinary rounding is unchanged.

title: Match email addresses followed directly by a hyphen
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

The email redaction pattern in `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs` (lines 216-221, `email`) missed an address followed directly by a hyphen.

**Cause:** The domain scan in `email` accepts `-` anywhere, including after the TLD. For `bob@example.com-`, the TLD check saw `com-`, which is not all alphabetic, so it rejected the address. In `bob@example.com-bob2@example.org`, the match started at `example.com-bob2@example.org` and left `bob@` unredacted.

**Fix:** After the domain scan, `email` ends the domain at a hyphen that directly follows the TLD letters of the last label. This happens in two cases: only hyphens follow (the domain ends there), or the scanned run is followed by `@` (the hyphen starts another address's local part). The tests cover the trailing-hyphen cases and `bob@example.co-uk`.

This PR has no linked issue (found while testing `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs:216-221`).

title: M12: an XFA date field keeps what its patterns don't read as typed, and reads its own patterns first
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

An XFA date field refused much of what another viewer accepts. Typing `10/18/2016` into a field with only a display picture got "Invalid date/time ... should match format yyyy-mm-dd". So did `xyz`, and ISO dates typed into a field with a different edit picture. It also stored some dates wrongly: `18OCT16` in a `date{YYYYMMDD}|date{DDMMMYY}` field was taken by the generic lenient parse and kept as typed, where the field's own DDMMMYY pattern gives 2016-10-18.

On a synthetic form in another viewer, a typed value is:
- stored as an ISO date when one of the edit picture's patterns reads it;
- otherwise kept exactly as typed, with no error.

This is also XFA 3.3's rule: text that can't be canonicalized through the edit picture is taken as canonical and stored as entered (chapter 4, "Rule 2, Input Parsing a Data Value Using a Picture Clause", p. 163).

ISO text (`2016-10-18`, `20161018`) is kept as typed and shown through the display picture.

**The change:**
- The XFA layout marks generated date fields `/PCXfaDate true`.
- The forms layer (`af::Actions::keystroke` and `format_value`) never refuses text for such a field. It shows a date only for a value that already is one: in the field's pattern, or ISO. Anything else is shown as typed rather than read loosely into a date the data doesn't hold.
- The engine tries the edit picture's alternatives (#3552's `typed_date`) *before* the field's own format, not only after a refusal. A date one of its own patterns reads is therefore never mistaken for another.
- `strip` removes the key with the other private keys. Ordinary AcroForm date fields are unchanged.

title: M3: an attachment's row opens on a double-click and has a right-click menu (#3466)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3466 (both parts the issue was split into: the right-click menu, and a double-click that opens).

In Acrobat, a right-click on an attachment in the Attachments panel offers Open and Save, and a double-click opens it. PdfCraft's panel had only the buttons at the end of each row.

- **Double-click** a row: a PDF opens in a new tab, as the row's Open button does. Any other file is saved, through the same Save dialog as the Save button, because PdfCraft opens only PDFs and doesn't hand attachments to other programs.
- **Right-click** a row: a menu with that row's own actions, using the buttons' existing labels, so there are no new strings to translate:
  - *Open in a new tab*, for PDFs;
  - *Save attachment…*;
  - *Delete attachment*, for the document's own attachments when it may be modified, the same condition as the button.
- **The buttons keep their clicks.** The row senses clicks through `egui::UiBuilder::sense`. egui registers that sense *below* the row's children, so a click on Save, Open or Delete still goes to the button.
- **The name and details labels are no longer selectable.** A selectable label takes the click itself, so a double-click on the name never reached the row. The labels still truncate and show their full text on hover.

All three actions call the same code paths as the buttons (`attachment_action`, `Edit::DeleteAttachment`), so Save keeps its behaviour, Mark-of-the-Web work included (#4091), and Delete stays one undo step.

title: edit: preserve gap-drawn spaces and indents in subset fonts via /ActualText (#4229)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #4229

## Summary
When editing text in a subset font that has no `' '` glyph (`metrics.encode(text)` returns `None` for strings containing `' '`), `source_show` emits each `' '` as a numeric `TJ` positioning adjustment (e.g. `[-330] TJ`) while painting non-space words with `(word) Tj`. Previously, reading the rewritten line back via `text_lines`, `text_blocks`, or `PageText` relied solely on inter-word horizontal gap inference, which collapsed multi-space runs (`"  "`) into a single `' '` and dropped leading/trailing space indents (`"  ab"`) because no glyph preceded or followed the `TJ` displacement.

## Changes
- **`crates/edit/src/text.rs`**:
  - `source_show`: When `metrics.encode(text)` is `None` and the emitted operators paint at least one glyph (`out.iter().any(|op| op.is("Tj"))`), wrap the emitted operators in `/Span << /ActualText (...) >> BDC ... EMC` carrying the logical text (`bidi::to_logical` after `indic::to_logical` when `metrics.visual_order`).
  - `interpret`: Retain numeric-only `TJ` operators inside an open `/ActualText` replacement (`actual.iter().any(Option::is_some)`) so leading/interior/trailing space adjustments inside the span are included in the merged `Shown`'s origin `tm`, `rect`, `frame`, and `extra_ops` (while `ink` remains restricted to the non-space words' glyph ink boxes), and filter out any zero-glyph non-`actual_text` entries before `positioned_tracking` in case an `/ActualText` `BDC` is unclosed.
  - `rewrite_block_from`: When `reuse && m.encode(" ").is_none()`, pass `tw + stretch` directly to a single `source_show` call per line rather than splitting the line at spaces into separate per-word calls.
- **`crates/edit/src/text_regions.rs`**:
  - `assign_subset_space_fonts` / `rewrite_styled_block`: Assign any space on a wrapped row whose font resource cannot encode `' '` to the nearest preceding or following glyph-bearing character on that row (copying both style index and font resource in two linear passes), so spaces betwee…

author: dotCooCoo

Page properties in the Organize pages panel was listed as planned. title: M12: run an XFA signature field's preSign scripts before it is signed and postSign after
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA signature fields' `preSign` and `postSign` scripts never ran. DA 31, for one, has a pair on each of its 35 signature boxes:
- **preSign** shows an "Electronic Signature Notice", sets the box's date field to today and makes it read-only.
- **postSign** clears and unlocks that date again if the box turns out unsigned.

Signed in PdfCraft, those boxes got no date and the date field stayed editable.

**The change:**
- `Session::run_sign_event(doc, field, SignEvent::Before | SignEvent::After)` runs a signature field's `preSign` or `postSign` scripts as one undoable step, through the existing `Edit::XfaEvent`. It returns `Ok(false)`, changing nothing, when there are none: not a laid-out XFA form, JavaScript off, no such field, or no such script. `clickable_som` becomes `scripted_som(…, activity)`, so both share the lookup.
- **What gets signed is what the signer saw.** A `preSign` script changes the form right before it's signed, so the signer has to see those changes first.
  - **In the app,** `preSign` runs as signing begins (`start_signing`): its message and what it changes show under the Sign dialog before the signer confirms. The step stays pending (`presign`). If signing ends without a signature (the dialog cancelled, the save picker cancelled, or signing failed and the dialog closed), it is taken back by `settle_presign`, checked every frame, provided it is still the last edit (`Document::undo_depth`). `postSign` runs once signed; its change comes after the signature, so it is left to save.
  - **Through `sign_document`,** the scripts run only when the caller asks (`run_form_scripts: true`): an agent hasn't seen the page. The result's `form_scripts` lists every field `preSign` changed (`changed`: field, value and read-only before and after), with `before_signing`, `after_signing`, the scripts' `alerts` and `errors`, and `unsaved_changes`. Not asked, the scripts don't run and `form_scripts.skipped` says the box has them.

title: M7.5: crop an added image by more than half from one side
author: Hagma2023
body:
## What this changes

An added image's crop was capped at 45 % **per side**, in three places:
- the Edit panel's 0–45 % drag values;
- `content_update` (`< 0.5`);
- the drawing matrix, which silently cut any larger value down to 0.45.

So keeping only the right third of a picture (70 % off the left) wasn't possible. `added_images_rotate_flip_and_crop_as_drawn` even set 0.5 and passed only because of that silent clamp.

The limit is now **per axis**: a side may trim up to 95 %, as long as left + right, and bottom + top, keep at least 5 % (`AddedImage::MIN_CROP_KEEP`).

- `AddedImage::crop_valid` is the rule for input. `content_update` refuses anything else, saying what is allowed, and its schema says so too.
- `AddedImage::clamp_crop` brings a crop read from a file (untrusted) into range. Non-finite or negative sides trim nothing. An axis that trims too much keeps its two sides' proportion. The matrix uses it, so it no longer needs its own `max(0.05)`.
- Edit panel: each side's drag value goes up to 95 % minus its opposite side. A new crop is still applied once, when the drag ends.

title: fix(forms): enforce mutual exclusion when RadiosInUnison is clear (#4488)
author: YusufMntm
body:
Fixes #4488

## What this changes

Resolves high-priority bug #4488 where clicking one of two radio buttons that share an on state turned both buttons on when `RadiosInUnison` was clear.

Per ISO 32000-2:
- **Table 229 (RadiosInUnison)**: "If clear, the buttons are mutually exclusive (the same behaviour as HTML radio buttons)."
- **§12.7.5.2.3**: "For radio buttons, the same behaviour shall occur only if the RadiosInUnison flag is set. If it is not set, at most one radio button in a field shall be set at a time."
- **§12.7.5.2.4**: Where `/V` and `/AS` differ, "the value of the AS key shall be used. The two `Yes` buttons share `/V /Yes`, and only their `/AS` tells them apart."

### Changes:
1. **`crates/forms/src/lib.rs`**:
   - Extended `FieldValue` with `RadioWidget(ObjRef, Option<String>)` so that button clicks and targeted fills can specify the target widget.
   - In `set_states`, when `RadiosInUnison` is clear on a radio group (`!f.has(flags::RADIOS_IN_UNISON)`), ensure at most one widget receives the on-state in `/AS`. title: M3: links run Named, Hide and ResetForm actions and their /Next chains (view.follow-links)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4524.

**The need.** A link annotation with a named action, a hide action or a reset-form action only showed "This PDF uses the unsupported {s} action." and did nothing. A link whose `/Next` chained more actions ran none of them. Push buttons already run all three, so a page-turn, show/hide or clear-form link did nothing while the same action on a button worked.

**The basis.**
- **Named actions:** ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.12, Tables 215–216. NextPage, PrevPage, FirstPage and LastPage are actions processors "shall support". For any other name, "if the viewer does not recognise the name, it shall take no action". The Table 215 NOTE also allows nonstandard named actions. GoBack and Print are supported because documents use them widely.
- **Hide:** §12.6.4.11, Table 214. `/T` is an annotation reference, a fully qualified field name, or an array of them. `/H` defaults to true.
- **ResetForm:** §12.7.6.3, Tables 241–242. It resets the listed `/Fields`, or all fields except them when bit 1 of `/Flags` (Include/Exclude) is set.
- **`/Next`:** §12.6.2, Table 196 and its Note 1. Chained actions run in order, "each followed in turn by any actions specified in its Next entry, and so on recursively".

**The change**
- **Reading** (`render::inspect`). `LinkTarget` gains `Named(name)`, `Hide { fields, hide }` and `ResetForm { fields, exclude }`. `Link` gains `next`, the chained actions in the order they run. The action parser was split out of `link()` so the head and each chained action are read the same way.
  - **Hide.** A widget or field reference names its field by the fully qualified name, built from `/T` up the `/Parent` chain (bounded, with a seen-set). A reference to an annotation that belongs to no field is skipped. If nothing is left, the action stays unsupported and the existing notice shows.
  - **ResetForm.** A field reference is read by its `/T`, exactly as push buttons read it today (`pdfcraft_forms::button_action`). An entry that names no f…

title: XFA: ready events run in the other viewer's order, and layout:ready again after a new layout
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #3589:** its commits (and a merge of `main`) are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

An XFA form's ready events now run when and in the order another viewer runs them. On a synthetic form, that viewer logged this on opening: the field's `initialize`, then the root subform's; the root's `form:ready`, then the field's; the root's `layout:ready`, then the field's; then `docReady`. When a click showed a hidden section that took the form to a second page, it ran `layout:ready` again for both objects, and the root's script read the new page count.

A second synthetic form, with a calculated field and two more fields, placed the calculations: they run once `initialize` has run, before `form:ready`, as XFA 3.3 orders them (the form ready event fires after the calculations and validations; p. 213, p. 388, pointed out by @mtlcl410). It also showed the siblings' order: `form:ready` runs in the exact reverse of `initialize`'s order (the root, then its fields last to first), while `layout:ready` runs the root and then its fields in document order.

Before this change, PdfCraft:
- ran `initialize` parents first, and `docReady` interleaved with `initialize`, before the form was laid out;
- never ran `form:ready` (`<event activity="ready" ref="$form">`);
- ran `layout:ready` once, on opening, so a form that reacts to its own layout (page numbers, sections that appear) saw only the first one;
- kept the open-time page count for a whole event, so `xfa.layout.pageCount()` read the old count after a re-layout.

Changes, all in `crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`:
- `on_open` runs `initialize` children first (`children_first`, siblings and an object's own events keeping their order), then the calculations, then `form:ready` in the reverse of that order (`objects_reversed`, an object's own events keeping theirs), then `layout:ready` and `docReady` parents first. When a ready script wrote a value, the calculations run once more…

title: M3: a GoToE link opens the PDF embedded in the document at its destination (view.follow-links)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4529.

**The need.** A link with an embedded go-to action (`/S /GoToE`) only showed "This PDF uses the unsupported GoToE action." The PDF it pointed to was attached to the same document, and the Attachments panel could already open it in a tab. The link that goes to it did nothing.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.4, Tables 204–205:
- **The action.** A GoToE action is "similar to a remote go-to action but allows jumping to or from a PDF file that is embedded in another PDF file". `/T` is a target dictionary that locates the target relative to the source. `/D` is the destination in the target.
- **The target dictionary.** `/R /C` means the target is a child of the current document. It is named by `/N`, "the name of the file in the EmbeddedFiles name tree". For a file attachment annotation, `/P` gives the page (an integer, or a named destination) and `/A` the annotation (its index in `/Annots`, or its `/NM`).
- **PDF only.** "Embedded go-to actions work only for files of Type PDF."

**The change**
- **Reading** (`render::inspect`). A new `LinkTarget::EmbeddedGoTo { source, destination, new_window }`. `source` is the existing `AttachmentSource`: `Document { key }` for `/N`, or `Annotation { page, index }` for `/P` and `/A`.
  - **Keys.** `/N` is converted and spent from the text budget the same way the EmbeddedFiles keys in `DocInfo::attachments` are, so the two match exactly.
  - **Annotations.** `/P` can be a page number or a named destination of this document. `/A` can be an index or an `/NM`, which is looked up in that page's `/Annots`.
  - **Destination.** `/D` is read by the GoToR reader's destination code, now split out as `remote_destination`. A target document's explicit destination names its page by number.
  - **Not followed.** The parent (`/R /P`), a nested target path (`/T` inside `/T`), a target under another root document (`/F`) and any malformed target stay `Other("GoToE")`, so the existing notice shows.

title: M6: list boxes show and pick the option /I names, and a single-select list shows one value (#4531)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4531.

**The need.** Some list boxes highlight the wrong rows, and some picks don't survive a save:
- A list box with `/Opt [[(1) (One-A)] [(1) (One-B)] [(2) (Two)]]`, `/V (1)` and `/I [1]` highlighted both One-A and One-B. 5 of 5 other readers tested highlight One-B alone.
- Picking One-B wrote `/I [0]`, so the file reopened as One-A.
- A list box without MultiSelect but with `/V [(TW) (JP)]` highlighted two rows.

**The basis.**
- ISO 32000-2 Table 234, `/I`: it "shall be used when two or more elements in the Opt array have different names but the same export value", and "if the items identified by this entry differ from those in the V entry …, the V entry shall be used".
- Table 233, MultiSelect: "if clear, at most one item shall be selected". An array `/V` on a single-select list is therefore malformed. The other readers split on how to show it, with no majority, so the tie-break is the first value only.

**The change**
- **Two commits, one per fix.**
- **Which rows are selected** (`forms`): a new `Field::selected` holds the selected option positions.
  - `/I` is used when it is an array of integers, strictly ascending, in range, and names exactly `/V`'s export values.
  - Otherwise `/V` decides, and each value selects the **first** option with that export value. This is what the writer records when it is given only an export value, so a pick still shows the same row if another tool drops `/I`. A test pins it.
  - List appearances highlight by position, not by export value.
- **Picking** (`forms`, `ui-egui`):
  - `FieldValue::ChoiceIndices` picks options by position.
  - A value given as display text (`"One-B"`) now records that option's position in `/I` as well.
  - List-box clicks, Ctrl/Shift-clicks, the arrow keys and the unbaked overlay all work by position. A pick writes `/V (1)` with `/I [0]` or `/I [1]`, and it survives a save and reopen.

title: Tests: XFA calculation tests no longer fail when the machine is busy
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

`hundreds_of_xfa_calculations_run_in_one_engine_within_the_open_budget` (engine) and `hundreds_of_xfa_calculations_open_and_recalculate_within_their_budgets` (automation) fail at random under load. The scripts of an opening or a change share a 3 s wall-clock budget (`OPEN_BUDGET_MS` in `crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`), and a click's scripts share 5 s (`EVENT_BUDGET_MS`). Each script has 1 s or 3 s (`timeout_for`), and the engine has 10 s to start (`ENGINE_START_LIMIT`). On a busy machine the tests go past one of these limits, and the calculations they check are skipped: "The form's scripts were stopped: the scripts took more than 3 seconds; 73 more were skipped". The tests now run with the time limits raised 100-fold, and the engine test also counts the script engines started (a per-thread counter, as `tint_transform_runs` in #2812). A new test checks that the limits stop the scripts. The shipped limits are unchanged.

- `Session::with_xfa_time_scale(factor)` and `Automation::with_xfa_time_scale` multiply each of these limits for a test. The default is 1.
- `pdfcraft_js::xfa_session::engines_started()` counts the script engine threads started on the calling thread.
- Three more tests that failed the same way under load run with the limits raised: `repeated_xfa_print_buttons_work_through_tools_and_after_reopen` ("the script engine took longer than 10 s to start"), `xfa_scripts_run_for_buttons_and_field_changes_through_tools` and `xfa_data_import_adds_and_removes_rows_of_a_dynamic_form`.

title: XFA: a form saved with its pages is laid out when it requires dynamic rendering, unless signed
author: EricKaden
body:
Split out of #1566 by @EULArule, who asked for it to be taken over in two PRs. The other part, required fields, is #4537.

## What this changes

Some viewers save a dynamic XFA form with its pages drawn. They leave no `/NeedsRendering` and keep only the signature boxes as AcroForm fields. PdfCraft took such a file for a static form, because it has fields, and showed its pages as they were saved: nothing on them could be filled in, because the other fields live in the template.

Such a form is now laid out from its template when its configuration says `<dynamicRender>required</dynamicRender>`, as #1566 did. Designer writes that value for a dynamic form, as it writes `forbidden` for a static one (#3180).

**Signed forms are left as saved.** If one of the signature boxes is signed, the form opens exactly as before. Laying it out would replace the pages the signature covers. PdfCraft would then report that signature as broken, since the open-time layout is an appended revision. Another viewer would see changed pages after the signature too. #1566 noted this ("a signature made before the layout is reported as invalid because the pages changed"). Making a signed form fillable needs a save that keeps the signed revision's pages, the design question in #4309, so it is not attempted here.

The same rule is in both places that decide:
- `pdfcraft_render::inspect`, which sets `DocInfo::xfa`;
- `pdfcraft_xfa::is_dynamic`, which `render_into` checks.

The xfa crate reads only the configuration packet (`config/acrobat/acrobat7/dynamicRender`), never the same element in the template or data. It finds signed boxes by walking the AcroForm's fields, at most 32 levels deep and 10 000 fields.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and tests on `pdfcraft-xfa`, `pdfcraft-render` and `pdfcraft-engine`.

title: M5: a comment's text, border or line, and fill each at an opacity of its own
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Comment Properties had one opacity for a whole comment: a text box's see-through background took its text and border with it, and a rectangle marking an area on a plan couldn't have an opaque line over a faint fill (a tester's request).

- **Comment Properties** shows an opacity per part where a comment has parts: a text box, typewriter text or callout its **Text**, **Border** and **Fill opacity**, a rectangle, oval, polygon or cloud its **Line** and **Fill opacity**. The rows stay put for the kind of comment; a part that isn't drawn (no fill, no border) is greyed. Lines, drawings and the rest keep one **Opacity**.
- **Make Properties Default** carries the parts into the tool (saved with the settings), so the next rectangle is drawn with the same faint fill.
- The quick bar's Opacity and `StyleAnnotation`'s set the whole comment's, as before: its parts drop opacities of their own.

**In the file:** the line's stays `/CA`; the fill's is `/ca` (PDF 2.0: the opacity of what is filled; Table 172); the text's is `/PCTextOpacity` (PdfCraft's own), each written only where it differs from the one it would follow (fill → line, text → fill), so a comment at one opacity keeps just `/CA`. The appearance draws `/GS0` (strokes at the line's, fills at the fill's, one `B` for a filled shape) and `/GS1` for the text, so every viewer shows it; an app that redraws the comment from its keys (Acrobat after editing it) uses one opacity again. Older comments with `/CA` alone are drawn as before.

Engine: `Style::{fill_opacity, text_opacity}`, `Edit::PartOpacity { page, index, fill, text }`, `annot::{set_part_opacity, appearance::{PartOpacity, part_opacity}}`, `Props::{fill_opacity, text_opacity}`. Headless: `comment_add` / `comment_edit` take `fill_opacity`, `text_opacity` (refused for comments without that part); `comment_list` reports `opacity`, `fill_opacity`, `text_opacity`. title: M5: a double-click on a comment card's text edits it
author: ohagmann
body:

title: XFA: a field's change scripts run for every keystroke and may rewrite what it enters
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4359:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

Another viewer runs an XFA field's `change` scripts for every keystroke, before the value is committed. The script sees the keystroke and may rewrite what it enters. PdfCraft ran them only once, when the value was committed, so a field couldn't refuse a typed character. Forms rely on this: a day count that keeps only digits, or a date field that refuses typing and points to its picker.

Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form:
- Typing `a` then `b`: `change=[a] new=[a] prev=[] sel=0-0`, then `change=[b] new=[ab] prev=[a] sel=1-1`.
- A backspace: `change=[] new=[a] prev=[ab] sel=1-2`.
- Select-all and `q`: `change=[q] new=[q] prev=[a] sel=0-1`.
- A script that rewrites `xfa.event.change` changes what is entered: `toUpperCase` gives `ABC`, and stripping non-digits from `a1b2` gives `12`.

The change spans four crates:
- **js:** `XfaEvent` carries a keystroke's `change`, `selStart` and `selEnd` (`newText` and `prevText` as before). `XfaOutcome::change` is the `xfa.event.change` a change script ends with. FormCalc reads `$event.change`, `selStart` and `selEnd`, and may assign `$event.change`.
- **engine:**
  - `Session::field_keystroke(id, name, widget, &Keystroke)` runs the field's change scripts for one keystroke, through `xfa::keystroke`. Each script sees what the one before it entered. The call returns what the keystroke enters, or `None` when the field has no change scripts.
  - The scripts run on a copy of the document. Only what they enter, and what they show or ask for, is kept: message boxes and beeps go out as usual. Their other changes come when the value is committed, which runs the change scripts again as before. Nothing in the document changes per keystroke, so typing leaves no undo steps.
- **ui-egui:** the field editor reads each keystroke off its text before and after (`keystroke_between`: the shortest repl…

title: XFA scripts: the bare event is named as the field event, of type Field, and its target has numPages
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #3575:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

XFA scripts can use two event objects: `xfa.event` and the bare `event`. Until now PdfCraft named the bare `event` by the XFA activity (`click`, `change`, …), gave it no `type`, and its target (the document, from #3575) had only `exportDataObject`. Scripts that branch on `event.name` or `event.type`, or read `event.target.numPages`, took the wrong path.

After this PR the bare `event` in an XFA script has:

- **`event.name`**: the matching field event's name.
  - Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form: a click script sees `Mouse Up`, a change script `Keystroke`, an exit script `Blur`.
  - Taken from the event table in the public JavaScript API reference for PDF forms, not measured: enter → `Focus`, mouseDown → `Mouse Down`, mouseUp → `Mouse Up`, mouseEnter → `Mouse Enter`, mouseExit → `Mouse Exit`, calculate → `Calculate`, validate → `Validate`.
  - Activities with no field event in that table (initialize, ready, layoutReady, docReady, preSign, postSign, and the rest) keep their XFA name, as before.
- **`event.type`**: `Field` (measured) for the field events above. Activities that keep their XFA name have no `type`, as before.
- **`event.target.numPages`** (measured): the document's page count. It is a read-only getter that calls the same function as `xfa.layout.pageCount()`, so the two always agree. `exportDataObject` is unchanged.

`xfa.event` is unchanged. Its `name` is still the activity and its `target` is still the form node.

The code is `field_event` and `install` in `crates/js/src/xfa.rs`. FormCalc's `$event` has no bare `event`, so it is unaffected.

## How you verified it

`check_local.sh … pdfcraft-js pdfcraft-engine` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests in the worktree's own target dir) printed `[fix/xfa-acrobat-event-fields] ok: clippy clean, tests passed=466 (not pushed)`.

title: Forms: a script that fails says so in one notice per action, with a button to the JavaScript console
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4306:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

A form script that fails no longer fails silently. Before this, the error from a failing AcroForm JavaScript or XFA JavaScript/FormCalc script (a button whose click script throws, say) went only to the JavaScript console log. Nothing in the app said so, and the button just looked broken.

Now, when scripts run for something the user did (a button's click and the calculations it sets off, a field change, an XFA form's opening) and one or more of them failed, the toast shows one notice for that action: "A script in this form failed: <first error>". The error is clipped to its first line, at most 120 characters. Under it is a **JavaScript Console** button, which runs the existing `tools.js_console` command.

- **One notice per action.** Every script output the app is handed for one action goes through `handle_js` once, and the notice quotes the first error. A button's own outcome and what its changes then set off (calculations, validations) used to reach the app in two batches, one of them a frame later. They now arrive as one batch, so a click whose button and calculation both fail gives one notice. Failing again while the notice shows (clicking a broken button twice) restarts that notice; it doesn't queue a second one.
- **It waits its turn.** The notice joins #4306's queue after the action's own messages, since the error is what ended the script. At most one failure notice waits, and it is the latest action's. If another notice replaces it before its time, it is shown again once the toast is free, like #4306's left-out count.
- **It doesn't get in the way.** It is the existing non-modal toast. Its button takes focus only when clicked, so typing into a field goes on while the notice shows. It stays 6 seconds, longer than the toast's usual 3.5, because it has a button to reach, and it stays up while the pointer is over it. Clicking the bu…

title: fix(forms): respect /I when options share export values and single value on single-select (#4531)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4531

- **Respect /I when options share export values:** According to ISO 32000-2 Table 234 (/I Entry), when multiple options in Opt have the same export value or when choice field values are represented as an array, /I specifies the zero-based indices of the selected options. When /I is present and its export values match /V, /I determines the exact selected rows rather than highlighting every row sharing the export value. If /I is absent or differs from /V, /V takes precedence.
- **Lenient single-select list box array /V handling:** In single-select list boxes (without MultiSelect flag), if a malformed PDF specifies an array /V, lenient viewers highlight and keep only the first item (row) and on save write a single string /V.
- **Field indices & automation/UI parity:** Added indices: Vec<usize> to Field and FieldValue::ChoiceIndices(Vec<usize>). Both UI selection (click/drag, combo box dropdown, arrow key navigation) and headless automation ( orm_fields and  orm_fill) track and set exact option indices so duplicate export value options can be unambiguously inspected and manipulated headlessly and interactively.
- **Appearance generation:** Appearance stream generation for list boxes now highlights only the exact selected rows via resolved choice indices.

author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

The errors of a form's scripts went to the document's script output, which automation reads only in `form_set_script` and in an XFA button click. `doc_open` returned only the document summary, and the `warnings` of `form_fill` and the other edit tools did not include them. title: M14: a drag across checkboxes checks or unchecks them all (#1662)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1662.

Press on a checkbox and drag over the ones next to it: each checkbox the pointer goes over takes the first one's new state, until the button is released. This is the behaviour VectorCraft (storytold/vectorcraft#1600) and PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#3521) use, and it follows their design: the first box toggles when the drag starts, its new state is kept in the egui context, and every box the drag crosses takes it.

- **One place.** The change is in `widgets::checkbox`, which every labelled checkbox goes through (clippy.toml disallows the others). Preferences, dialogs and panels all get it at once.
- **A click is unchanged.** It still toggles one box, through egui's own click.
- **The drag belongs to the checkbox.** The checkbox now senses drags as well as clicks (`Response::interact`). Without that, a drag in a scroll area (Preferences, most dialogs) would scroll the panel. A press that moves and comes back before the release toggles the box once, not also as a click.
- **`changed()` still works.** `interact` returns a new response, so the change a click made is carried over to it. Every box the drag sets is marked changed too, so callers that act on `changed()` (comment filters, field properties, the optimizer) see drag changes as they see clicks.
- **Left alone:** a disabled box, a box clipped out of view (rows scrolled under the OK row), and a box under another layer (a menu open over a dialog).
- **The drag ends with its own release.** The state counts only while the box the drag started on is still being dragged, so a release on a frame that draws no checkbox (a dialog closing) leaves nothing behind.
- **Not changed: the page checkbox on Organize Pages thumbnails** (`checkbox_without_text`). It keeps taking clicks only, because a drag that starts on it moves the page, as a drag on the rest of the thumbnail does. The issue also limits this feature to the interface's own checkboxes, not PDF form fields, which this doesn't t…

title: M14: Ctrl+Tab can go through the tabs most recently used first (#2063)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2063.

Next tab and Previous tab (Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab; ⌃Tab on macOS) can now follow the order the tabs were last shown in, as Windows' Alt+Tab does, instead of their order on screen. It is a choice in **Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ Next tab and Previous tab**: *In tab order* (the default, unchanged from #1551) or *Most recently used first*.

As the issue asks:
- **One press goes back to the tab shown before.** Switching between two of five open files is a single Ctrl+Tab each way.
- **While Ctrl is held, the order of the first press holds.** Tab again goes on to the tab shown before that one, and Shift+Tab steps back in the same order. Letting go of Ctrl makes the tab you landed on the most recent one.
- **Without Ctrl** (the command palette, `command_run`), each step is a cycle of its own, so Next tab goes back and forth between the two most recent tabs.

How it works:
- **The history is in a module of its own, `tab_cycle.rs`.** It is pure logic with unit tests, so the UI files only get small hooks.
  - `RecentTabs` keeps the open tabs most recently shown first, keyed by document id rather than position, so moving and closing tabs keep it right.
  - A tab closed during a cycle drops out of it, and one opened during it comes last.
  - A tab opened in the background, never shown, comes after every tab that was.
  - Home takes no part, as in tab order. From Home, Next tab goes to the most recent tab.
  - Combine files takes part like a document.
- **Every frame records the tab showing** (`note_shown_tab`, at the start of `shortcuts`, before the modal early returns), so a tab shown by a click or by opening a file counts. Ctrl held keeps the cycle going.
- **The choice is saved** as `tab_cycle` (`"tabs"` / `"recent"`) and can be set with `set tab_cycle recent` over the control channel.

title: refactor(ui): panel docking uses craft-ui's shared Workspace and DockCommand
author: aiongg
body:
## What this changes

Panel docking uses craft-ui's shared docking (`craft_ui::docking::Workspace`, `DockCommand`) instead of pdfcraft's own copy of the workspace model, its validation, its actions and the `ui.dock` parameter parser. craft-ui, craft-quit and craft-docpath are pinned to craft-libs 6e7f285, which includes the docking follow-ups. craft-print stays at 666c358.

- pdfcraft has no panel lock, so `restore` clears a settings file's `locked` flag and saved arrangement before validating.

title: fix(links): support Named, Hide, ResetForm actions and /Next chaining (#4524)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4524

- **Named actions:** Links with `/S /Named` now support standard page navigation actions (`NextPage`, `PrevPage`, `FirstPage`, `LastPage`, matching push button support in `canvas.rs`). Unrecognized or non-navigation named actions (such as `Save`, `Print`) take no automated action without confirmation.
- **Hide actions:** Links with `/S /Hide` now show or hide the target fields (`/T`) and their children according to `/H` (default `true` hides, `false` shows). Targets can be field names, arrays of names/references, or indirect references (resolved by qualified name).
- **ResetForm actions:** Links with `/S /ResetForm` now reset the specified fields (`/Fields`) or all fields except the specified fields (`/Flags` bit 1 exclude flag). When `/Fields` is omitted or empty, all fields in the document are reset to their default values (`/DV`). When `/Fields` is present in include-mode but none of the targets resolve, no fields are reset.
- **`/Next` action chaining:** An action dictionary can chain subsequent actions through `/Next` (either a single action dictionary or an array of actions, per ISO 32000-2 §12.6.2 Table 196). Inspector parses and collects chains into `LinkTarget::Sequence(...)` up to `MAX_ACTION_CHAIN = 64` actions with cycle detection via `HashSet<ObjectId>`. Visited nodes are globally bounded by `MAX_ACTION_VISITS = 1024` to prevent exponential DAG fanout.
- **Headless automation and UI tooltips:** `doc_info` serialization exposes `Named`, `Hide`, `ResetForm`, and `Sequence` link targets. In the UI, hover labels display user-friendly translated tooltips for named, hide, and reset-form actions.

title: M4: Duplicate pages can give the copies' form fields names of their own (#2228)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2228.

When a page with form fields is duplicated, the copies keep the fields' names. Fields of one name are one field, so filling in a copy fills in the original too. The issue asks for an option that gives the copies names of their own, so a form can be extended page by page.

- **New command: *Duplicate pages with new field names*** (`page.duplicate_renaming_fields`), in the Pages menu, the command palette, and Organize pages ▸ Insert next to *Duplicate pages*. title: fix(automation): XFA clicks and form edits return only the script output they produced
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

An XFA button click through `run_javascript` (`js_run` with `field`) and the `form_set_script` tool returned `take_js_output`, the document's whole waiting script output, as their own. In automation nothing else takes that output, so the next click or script change returned the alerts, console lines and errors of opening and of earlier edits as its own: after `form_fill` set a value that fails validation, a click on a button that shows "Hello 500" returned `["Quantity must be 100 or less", "Hello 500"]`. Several tools that apply an edit, `js_run` among them when its script changes fields, also left their edit's output, such as the warnings for XFA data they could not write, in that output for the next click or `form_set_script` to report.

This pull request makes these changes:

- `Session::with_own_js_output` runs an operation with the waiting output set aside and returns only what the operation added. The output limits count that output alone. What was waiting stays for `take_js_output`, and the output of an operation that fails joins it.
- The XFA click path and `form_set_script` return only the output of their own edit.
- The accessibility edits, `js_set_document_script`, `form_set_actions`, `pdfa_convert`, `ocr_recognize`, `doc_compare_mark` and `form_detect_fields` add the errors their edit produced, such as XFA values that could not be written to the form's data, to the result's `warnings`.
- `js_run` without an XFA click adds the errors of applying its script's field changes to `warnings`, and returns the alerts, console lines and requests of the field scripts that those changes ran with the script's own. Its tool description says so.

This branch and #4551 change different lines and merge without conflicts. #4551's `take_js_errors` in `doc_open` and `apply` takes the errors that were waiting, and the tools here no longer leave their own behind for it. title: M4: New bookmarks from text styles, for headings that aren't tagged (#1693)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1693.

Bookmarks can now be made from **how the headings look**. The issue's example: every chapter title is set in one font, at one size, in italic. *New bookmarks from structure* finds nothing in such documents, because their headings aren't tagged, and most PDFs from word processors and typesetting are like that.

**Bookmark options ▸ New bookmarks from text styles…** (also in Pages and the command palette, `bookmark.from_text_styles`) opens a dialog:
- **The document's text styles** are listed, the largest first. Each shows its font (without the subset tag, so `ABCDEF+Garamond` and `GHIJKL+Garamond` are one font), the size the text is shown at, bold and italic, how many lines use it, and a sample: *Helvetica-Bold, 18 pt, bold · "Introduction" (2 lines)*.
- **One style per bookmark level**, up to four. The largest style is offered for level 1, and a level opens once the one above it has a style. Each list is named after its level for screen readers.
- **Create**:
  - every line in a level's style becomes a bookmark of that level, nested under the bookmark of the level above it before it, all under a new first "Untitled" bookmark, as New bookmarks from structure does;
  - a heading set on several rows is one bookmark;
  - each bookmark goes to the top of its heading (`/XYZ null top null`), not just its page;

title: M2: an image whose data stops short keeps its height and lines up with its soft mask (#2780)
author: hazeliscoding
body:
## What this changes

An image or soft mask whose data stops short of its `/Height` now keeps that height. The rows present are drawn where they belong. The missing samples are raw zeros, decoded like the rest, the way 1-, 2- and 4-bit samples already were and the way Chrome draws them.

8-bit data was cut to the rows present (`fix_image_length` in vendored hayro-interpret, and a copy of the rule in `rgb_via_lookup`):

- A short image was drawn short. Its missing rows were left unpainted, and its `/SMask` was squeezed into the rows it had. On the scanned pages in #2780, the colour layer's data ended early, so the full-height text mask was squeezed with it and the text came out as a faint ghost.
- A short soft mask was stretched over the whole image.

Every path now pads the raw samples before `/Decode` and before any inversion: the 8-bit fast path, the per-pixel and colour-table paths, both mask paths, and the colour-key `/Mask`. `rgb_via_lookup` no longer keeps its own copy of the length rule.

**A sample cap, because padding expands data.** Every sample an image says it has is now padded and then expanded (to `u16`, then `f32`). `image_size_ok` caps only pixels, so a few bytes of a many-ink image could ask for a huge allocation: a 32-ink image of one byte took 4.2 GB and 11 seconds at 2^25 pixels, and would ask for 32 GiB at 2^28.

Images and masks are now also capped at 2^30 samples (`image_samples_ok`, four a pixel at the pixel limit). The cap is checked in `decode_context` before anything is expanded. An image over it is left out with `ImageDecodeFailure`. No gray, RGB or CMYK image within the pixel limit is affected.

Fixes #2780. The cause is the one @imamehoiho-oss found in the issue. Their file wasn't attached, so this is fixed and tested on synthetic images. `vendor/README.md` records this as hayro-interpret patch 67.

**What other viewers do.** I checked Chrome's PDF viewer (pdfium) as a black box, with synthetic 1 × 4 DeviceGray images whose data stops a…

title: XFA: a radio group's own enter and exit scripts run when the focus enters or leaves the group
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4359:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the commit "M12: a radio group's own enter and exit scripts run when the focus enters or leaves the group".

## What this changes

An XFA exclusion group, a set of radio buttons, can have enter and exit scripts of its own, as each of its buttons can. #4359 runs a button's enter and exit whenever it gains or loses focus, but PdfCraft never ran the group's. A form that reacts to the focus entering or leaving the group as a whole, for example to show a hint or check a choice when leaving, did nothing.

Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form (exclusion group `grp`, buttons `r1` and `r2`, all logging their events):
- **Clicking into the group:** `grp enter` → `r1 enter`.
- **Moving to the other button:** `r1 exit` → `r2 enter`. The group's scripts don't run.
- **Leaving the group:** `r2 exit` → `grp exit`.

PdfCraft now does the same:
- **engine:** `Session::field_focus_crossing(id, name, widget, focus, crossing)`.
  - When `crossing`, a radio button's focus change also enters or leaves its group. Enter runs the group's enter before the button's; exit runs the group's exit after the button's.
  - A move between two buttons of one group passes `crossing = false`, so only the buttons' scripts run.
  - `Session::field_focus` keeps its meaning (the focus crosses the field) and now includes the group.
  - Each object's scripts are an edit of their own, so one that changes nothing still leaves no undo step. Which of them run is decided before any does, so an exit the value's change already ran is still skipped.
- **xfa:** `has_focus_scripts` counts a group's own enter and exit scripts, so a form whose only focus scripts are a group's still runs them.
- **ui-egui:** the app's focus tracking passes `crossing = false` when the focus moves between two widgets of the same radio field.
- **automation:** `form_focus` takes `within_group` (default false) for a move between two…

title: fix(automation): page_enhance_camera reports the XFA data it could not write
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

`page_enhance_camera` applies its page replacement through `Session::enhance_camera_page_at`, and `page_enhance_scan` applies its edit through `Session::enhance_scanned_pages`. Neither goes through the tool's edit helper. On a dynamic XFA form each of these edits writes the form's data, and the warnings for values it could not write ("XFA data not written for fields whose data node holds structured content: ...") went to the document's script output. The tools returned no warnings, so the next XFA click or `form_set_script` returned those warnings as its own.

This pull request makes these changes:

- `page_enhance_camera` and `page_enhance_scan` run their edits inside `Session::with_own_js_output` and add the errors each edit produced to the result's `warnings` with `with_warnings`.
- `command_run` returns them the same way, because it calls the tool.

`command_batch` runs each step through `command_run`, so it reports what each step's tool reports. The engine's actions run in a session of their own (`actions::run_on`), so their output does not stay in the automation session.

title: M2: a 16-bit image with an odd byte count is drawn instead of crashing the page
author: hazeliscoding
body:
> **Stacked on #4561.** Both PRs add a numbered patch to the same line of `vendor/README.md`, so this one is based on #4561's branch to avoid a conflict there. Only the last two commits are new here. I'll rebase onto `main` once #4561 merges.

## What this changes

A 16-bit image whose data has an odd byte count crashed the page render. `get_components` (vendored hayro-interpret) paired the bytes with `chunks(2)` and read `v[1]`, which panics when the last chunk has a single byte:

```
panicked at vendor\hayro-interpret\src\x_object.rs:1171:48:
index out of bounds: the len is 1 but the index is 1
pdfcraft-cli: renderer crashed on page 1
```

That's from the released 0.13.0 CLI. It happens in two cases:

- **Data cut short mid-sample:** 5 bytes for a 1 × 4 image.
- **A complete image followed by one stray byte:** for example a line end counted in `/Length`. A 1 × 1 image with 3 bytes is enough.

The samples are now read in whole pairs of bytes (`as_chunks::<2>()`, which needs no indexing). A last byte without its pair reads as a 0 sample, as an incomplete 1-, 2- or 4-bit sample already does (`BitReader::read` returns `None`, and `get_components` reads that as 0). So a half sample means the same thing at every bit depth:

- A stray byte after a complete image becomes one extra sample, which is dropped with the rest of the excess.
- An image whose only data is that one byte is still drawn, as a 1-bit image with any data is.

`vendor/README.md` records this as hayro-interpret patch 68. I found it while reading `get_components` for #4561, and no issue or PR mentions it.

title: M2: a colour-key mask keys the raw samples of an image with an inverted Decode
author: hazeliscoding
body:
> **Stacked on #4565, which is stacked on #4561.** All three add a numbered patch to the same line of `vendor/README.md` (67, 68, 69), so they form one chain to avoid conflicts there. Only the last commit is new here. I'll rebase onto `main` as the others merge.

## What this changes

A colour-key `/Mask` is now tested against an image's raw samples, as ISO 32000-2 §8.9.6.4 specifies, also when the image's `/Decode` is inverted.

The 8-bit fast path in vendored hayro-interpret inverts an image with an inverted default `/Decode` in place. `resolve_alpha` then tested the key against the inverted bytes, so it masked the wrong samples. This affects complete images, not only short ones.

I checked a 1 × 4 DeviceGray image with `/Decode [1 0]`, `/Mask [0 0]` and data `00 FF 00 FF` on a blue page:

| | rows |
|---|---|
| Chrome's PDF viewer (black box) | masked, black, masked, black |
| released 0.13.0 | white, masked, white, masked |
| this PR | masked, black, masked, black |

`decode_raster` now records whether the fast path inverted the data in place, and the colour key turns the data back into raw samples (255 − c) before comparing. There's no copy of the image. `vendor/README.md` records this as hayro-interpret patch 69.

CodeRabbit raised this on #4561. That PR is about short data, and this bug was already there for complete images, so it gets its own PR.

title: automation: compare canonical root components exactly and test roots-only escape confinement (#4003)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What & Why

Closes #4003 (completing the remaining two hardening items after `be0ec707` / #4289):

1. **Exact canonical component comparison in `file_access::same_component` (`crates/automation/src/file_access.rs`):**
   - Previously, `same_component` compared all path components on Windows with `a.to_lowercase() == b.to_lowercase()`. Because `Root::open` and `file_access::resolve` already canonicalize existing directories on disk via `std::fs::canonicalize`, normal path components inside an existing Windows directory already carry their exact on-disk casing, while `str::to_lowercase()` applies Unicode case-folding that NTFS does not (for example folding U+212A KELVIN SIGN `'K'` to `'k'`, allowing a sibling folder `inK` outside read root `ink` to pass the containment check on Windows) and ignores per-directory case sensitivity (`FILE_CS_FLAG_CASE_SENSITIVE_DIR`).

2. **Escape confinement loop under both `--root` and `AutomationRoots` (`crates/automation/tests/it/hostile_args.rs`):**
   - `no_tool_escapes_the_root` now runs its full tool/property/escape-vector sweep under both `--root` (`Automation::with_root`) and roots-only (`Automation::with_automation_roots`) confinement modes, including `..` and symlink traversal anchored at `root` as well as Windows device pipe paths.

title: XFA: check box and radio exit scripts wait for the focus to leave
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4563 (and so #4359) and #4369:** their commits are included here until they merge. This PR's own change is the commit "M12: check box and radio exit scripts wait for the focus to leave". The merge commit before it resolves #4359 against #4369 in `on_changes` (#4369's change and click order, with #4359's record of the exits that ran, per object), which whichever of the two merges second needs anyway.

## What this changes

A check box or radio button keeps the focus while it is clicked. Measured black-box in another viewer on synthetic forms, it runs its exit scripts once, when the focus leaves:
- **Check box (Q48):** `cb enter` → `cb change 1` → `cb click 1` → (second click) `cb change 0` → `cb click 0` → (focus to the next field) `cb exit 0`.
- **Radio group (Q49):** `grp enter` → `r1 enter` → `grp change 1` → `r1 change` → `grp click 1` → `r1 click` → (click r2) `r1 exit` → `r2 enter` → `grp change 2` → `r2 change` → `grp click 2` → `r2 click` → (focus out) `r2 exit` → `grp exit`.

PdfCraft ran the exit scripts with every click: the button's and then the group's, before the focus had gone anywhere. A form that checks a choice or moves on when the field is left did so after each click. In the app, a click on a check box also applied its value before the focus scripts, so its enter ran after its change and click.

- **engine:**
  - The session records which XFA object has the focus, as `field_focus` hears it: a field's widget, or a radio button.
  - A check box or radio group set while it has the focus (its widget, or any button of the group) runs no exit scripts with the change. `field_focus` runs them as the focus leaves, once.
  - Text fields commit as they lose the focus, and a value set without the focus on the field (`form_fill` on its own, a script) has no focus to lose. Both keep running exit with the change, as before.

title: M4: Document Properties reads a named opening destination's page, so choosing page 1 replaces it (ISO 32000-2 12.3.2.4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4572.

**The need.** When a document opened at a named destination, Document Properties ▸ Initial View showed page 1 at the default magnification, wherever the name actually went. Choosing page 1 then changed nothing: the dialog counted it as "unchanged" and kept the named action, so the document still opened on, say, page 3. `doc_initial_view { "page": 1 }` did the same.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- §7.7.2, Table 29, `OpenAction`: "A value specifying a destination that shall be displayed or an action that shall be performed when the document is opened." With the entry absent, "the document shall be opened to the top of the first page at the default magnification factor."
- §12.3.2.4: "a destination may be referred to indirectly by means of a name object (PDF 1.1) or a byte string (PDF 1.2)". A named destination stands for the explicit destination it names.

**The change** (`organize::view`, plus a small helper in `organize::outline`)
- **Reading.** `initial_view` now resolves a named opening destination: a bare name or string as `/OpenAction`, or a GoTo action whose `/D` is a name or string. It is looked up in the `/Names /Dests` tree, then the catalog `/Dests`, with the resolver bookmarks already use (`explicit_dest`: destination depth 8, name tree depth 32 with a seen-set). The page and magnification shown are where the document really opens. A name that names nothing still reads as page 1.
- **Writing.** `set_initial_view` is unchanged in shape. It keeps the opening action when the page and magnification equal what `initial_view` reads, and otherwise writes an explicit destination (or, for page 1 at the default magnification, removes `/OpenAction`). Because the read is now right, choosing page 1 on a name that goes to page 3 is a change, and an explicit `[page1 /XYZ null null 2]` replaces it. The magnification the name had is kept unless the user changes it.

title: M14: pinned tabs open at every start (#2926)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2926.

**Pinned tabs**, as the issue asks: a pinned file is open every time PdfCraft starts.

- **A document tab's right-click menu** gets *Pin Tab*, or *Unpin Tab* on a pinned one. It's only offered for documents that have a file, since an unsaved new document has nothing to open again.
- **A pinned tab shows a pin** where the others show a page, and it moves to the end of the pinned tabs at the start of the strip.
- **At every start the pinned files open first**, in the order they were pinned. This happens whatever *Reopen the files that were open when PdfCraft last closed* says; with that preference on, the session's files follow and none opens twice. A file given on the command line isn't opened twice either. A pinned file that is missing at a start, such as one on a drive that isn't connected, is skipped but stays pinned.
- **Only *Unpin Tab* unpins.** Closing a pinned tab closes it for this session. That is deliberate: quitting with unsaved changes closes the tabs one by one as each is answered (`close_and_continue`), so unpinning on close would lose pins on every such quit.
- **The pins are saved** with the other settings as `pinned_tabs`, as absolute paths, so a file opened by a relative path matches. They are read back leniently: text entries only, each once, at most 64.

The changes are in `tab_context.rs` (the actions and the reading), `last_session.rs` (opening at start), `chrome.rs` (the menu item and the icon) and `lib.rs` (the field and its persistence). The `pin` icon is the bundled Lucide one, so there are no new assets. New strings: *Pin Tab*, *Unpin Tab*, and the notice when 64 are pinned.

title: proposal(redact): prevent retention of confidential vector paths behind clipping (F-008)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Fixes security finding **F-008** (CWE-200 / Sensitive Data Exposure): Partial vector redaction hides the covered area with clipping (`clip_out`, `W/W*`) but retains the complete original drawing instructions (`body`, painting operator).

### Root Cause
When a vector path intersected a redaction region but was not completely covered (`!scope.covered(b)`), `crates/redact/src/interp.rs` used `clip_out` to add an inverse clipping path around the redaction rectangle. However, it still emitted the full original drawing path (`body`) and painting operator. For paths with clipping flags, it additionally retained the path geometry via `ops.extend(body); ops.push(Op::new("n", vec![]));`. An adversary or recipient could extract confidential outlined text, signatures, or geometry from the PDF content stream despite the visual redaction overlay.

### Proposed Fix
- Remove vector paths that intersect redaction marks completely, whether fully or partially covered.
- Refuse partial clip retention so that no drawing geometry is retained in the content stream.
- Increment `scope.report.paths_removed` for partially covered paths that are removed.
- Add an integration test (`partially_covered_vector_paths_do_not_leak_drawing_commands`) verifying that vector drawing commands are stripped and do not leak into the content stream.
- Update `parity/acrobat-features.toml` notes accordingly.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` passes (143 unit and integration tests).
- `cargo fmt --check` passes cleanly.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact -- -D warnings` passes with zero warnings.
- `cargo xtask parity` passes.

title: proposal(redact): unlink unused Type 3 glyph programs and fonts on redaction (F-011)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

This proposal addresses finding **F-011** (CWE-212 / Sensitive Data Exposure) in `pdfcraft-redact`.

### Problem
Previously, when displayed Type 3 characters were removed during redaction or sanitization, their font dictionary in `/Resources` preserved the original glyph programs and graphical resources in `CharProcs` and `Resources`. When saved with a full save, those references kept confidential glyph geometry, embedded images, or vector payloads recoverable in the saved document even after all displayed uses were redacted.

### Changes
1. **Type 3 Font Analysis and Encoding Mapping**: Added `type3.rs` and `type3_tables.rs` to map character codes to glyph names across standard base encodings (`StandardEncoding`, `WinAnsiEncoding`, `MacRomanEncoding`, `MacExpertEncoding`) and `/Differences`.
2. **Surviving Glyph Tracking**: Implemented content stream inspection across all pages, page-tree resource holders, and reachable form XObjects to track active Type 3 font glyph usage in post-redaction content.
3. **Glyph Unlinking & Exclusive Resource Pruning**:
   - Unlinked unused glyph programs from `CharProcs`.
   - Pruned exclusive resources (`/XObject`, `/ColorSpace`, `/Pattern`, `/Shading`, `/ExtGState`, `/Font`, `/Properties`) from the Type 3 font's `/Resources` that were only used by removed glyphs.
   - Removed completely unused Type 3 fonts from resource dictionaries (`/Font`).
4. **Fail-Closed Safety**: If Type 3 font cleanup cannot be safely established (e.g. unreadable stream, unsupported/corrupted encoding, or malformed CharProcs), redaction fails closed rather than returning a file containing residual sensitive data.
5. **Tests**: Added regression tests in `crates/redact/src/tests/surviving_references.rs` verifying that:
   - Unreferenced Type 3 glyph programs and exclusive image resources do not survive a full save.
   - Surviving glyphs and their resources remain intact and functional.
