title: M12: document rulers
author: chrisamidon
body:
# M12: Document Rulers

This pull request adds optional, read-only document rulers to the PdfCraft native viewer.

The ruler implementation is built into the existing egui document canvas and uses the same final page geometry, viewport, scrolling, layout, rotation, and zoom transformations used to paint document pages. This keeps ruler ticks, labels, and pointer indicators aligned with the displayed document without changing page layout or scroll extents.

## User-visible behavior

When a document is open, rulers can be toggled through:

- **View → Rulers**
- The command palette
- **Ctrl+R** on Windows and Linux
- **Command+R** on macOS

Ruler visibility is persisted as a viewer preference and is disabled by default.

When enabled, PdfCraft displays:

- A horizontal ruler above the document viewport
- A vertical ruler beside the document viewport
- Adaptive major, medium, and minor tick marks
- Labels using the configured display unit
- Pointer indicators on both ruler axes
- Coordinates aligned with the active visible page
- Facing-page coordinates that exclude the screen-only gutter between pages

Supported display units include:

- Inches
- Millimetres
- Centimetres
- Points

Tick intervals adapt to the current zoom so the rulers remain readable from the minimum supported zoom through high-magnification document inspection.

## Layout and geometry

The ruler overlay consumes the final snapped page transforms produced by the canvas. It does not perform an independent page-layout calculation.

This provides several important guarantees:

- Showing rulers does not change page size or document geometry.
- Showing rulers does not change scroll extents.
- Tick positions remain aligned with rendered page edges.
- Horizontal and vertical axes use the same active-page geometry.
- Facing-page layouts do not treat the visual gutter as PDF distance.
- Rotated pages retain the correct document coordinate scale.
- Navigation destinations account for the horizontal ruler inset.…

title: Forms: a field's Mouse Down, Mouse Enter, Mouse Exit, On Focus and On Blur actions run
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4359:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR adds the AcroForm side to #4359's focus tracking (`run_focus_scripts`), so it builds on that rather than adding a second tracker. Its own change is the commit "M6: a field's mouse and focus actions run as the pointer and the focus move".

## What this changes

ISO 32000-2 §12.6.3, Table 197 gives a widget an action for each of six triggers: Mouse Up (`/A`, or `/AA /U`), and `/AA` D (Mouse Down), E (Mouse Enter), X (Mouse Exit), Fo (On Focus) and Bl (On Blur). PdfCraft lets you set all six in Field Properties ▸ Actions, but only a push button's Mouse Up ever ran. Forms use the others to show help text on hover, highlight the field being filled in, or check an entry when it is left. In PdfCraft those did nothing.

Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form (every trigger of two text fields, a push button and a check box logs `event.name` into a log field):
- **Hovering:** `a Mouse Enter`, then `a Mouse Exit`.
- **Clicking from a, after typing in it, into b:**
  - moving there: `a Mouse Exit`, `b Mouse Enter`;
  - the press: `b Mouse Down`, then `a Keystroke commit`, `a Validate`, `a Blur`, then `b Focus`;
  - the release: `b Mouse Up`.
- **Tab:** `b Blur`, then the next field's `Focus`. An unchanged field doesn't commit.
- **Clicking the field that has the focus:** `Mouse Down`, `Mouse Up`.
- **Push buttons and check boxes** take the focus on a click like a text field.

PdfCraft now does the same:
- **forms:**
  - `widget_action(doc, field, widget, trigger)` reads a widget's action for any trigger: the widget's own first, then the field's, since a field with one widget is often one dictionary.
  - Its action parser is the one a push button's Mouse Up already used, split out (`parse_action`).
  - `Trigger::event_name` gives `event.name`: Mouse Up, Mouse Down, Mouse Enter, Mouse Exit, Focus, Blur.

title: Reject '+' as a hex digit in FormCalc url Decode escapes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

FormCalc `Decode(..., "url")` no longer accepts a `+` sign as a hex digit in `%XX` escapes. Previously a malformed escape such as `%+f` was decoded as byte 0x0F. Now it is left as literal text, the same as `%zz`. Valid escapes such as `%2F` decode as before.

Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2280-2284`. There is no existing issue, so there is no `Fixes #` line.

**Cause:** the url branch of Decode passed the two characters after `%` to `u8::from_str_radix(h, 16)`, which accepts a leading `+`.

**Fix:** before parsing, the decoder checks that both characters after `%` are ASCII hex digits. Anything else stays unchanged.

title: fix(xfa): render lines without width as vertical and without height as horizontal
author: manurosado
body:
## What this changes

In dynamic and static XFA forms, vertical dividing lines frequently omit the `w` attribute and horizontal lines omit the `h` attribute, while template declarations may set `slope="/"`.

Previously, `Layouter::measure()` defaulted missing line widths to the full available container width (`avail_w`), and `Layouter::draw_draw()` drew diagonal strokes connecting opposite corners whenever `slope_up` was true. As a result, standard vertical table column separators and horizontal field boundaries were rendered as full-width diagonal slashes across table cells and forms.

This PR fixes line orientation by:
1. In `Layouter::measure()`: when `d.value` is a `Value::Line`, bounding its natural width to the edge thickness plus horizontal margin (`(edge.thickness.clamp(0.1, 20.0) + c.margin.horizontal()).min(avail_w)`) instead of expanding across `avail_w`.
2. In `Layouter::draw_draw()`:
   - If width `w` is omitted or `(d.common.h.is_some() && inner.w <= edge.thickness * 2.0)`, drawing a strict vertical segment from `(inner.x + inner.w/2, inner.y)` to `(inner.x + inner.w/2, inner.bottom())`.
   - If height `h` is omitted or `(d.common.w.is_some() && inner.h <= edge.thickness * 2.0)`, drawing a strict horizontal segment from `(inner.x, inner.y + inner.h/2)` to `(inner.right(), inner.y + inner.h/2)`.
   - Only drawing diagonal strokes when both width and height are explicitly positive and distinct from the edge stroke thickness.
3. Added docstring to `draw_draw` in `crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`.
4. Added unit test `xfa_line_without_width_is_vertical_and_without_height_is_horizontal` in `crates/xfa/src/tests.rs` covering lines without width (vertical), lines without height (horizontal), and narrow lines.

## How you verified it

Ran `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa` against `main`:
- 124 passed; 0 failed.
- Verified that axis-aligned lines in multi-page XFA forms render strictly horizontally or vertically without diagonal slashes.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] cli…

title: Forms: a push button takes the focus on a click and as a Tab stop
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4585 (and so #4359):** their commits are included here until they merge. This PR's own change is the commit "M6: a push button takes the focus on a click and as a Tab stop".

## What this changes

A push button took no focus in PdfCraft. Clicking one ran its action, but the focus didn't move to it, and Tab went past it. So a push button's On Focus and On Blur actions (#4585) never ran, and a keyboard user couldn't reach a button at all.

Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form (every trigger logs `event.name`):
- **Tab from text field b reaches the button:** `b Blur`, then `btn Focus`.
- **A click on the button from text field a:** `btn Mouse Down`, then `a Blur`, then `btn Focus`, then `btn Mouse Up`.
- **A click on the button that has the focus:** `btn Mouse Down`, then `btn Mouse Up`.
- **From the button to a check box:** `cb Mouse Down`, then `btn Blur`, then `cb Focus`, then `cb Mouse Up`.

PdfCraft now does the same (ui-egui):
- **A click on a push button focuses it**, as a click on a check box does. The field it leaves commits and blurs first, then the button's Focus runs, then its action (Mouse Up), in #4585's order.
- **Tab and Shift+Tab stop at push buttons** (`takes_focus`: the fields that can be filled in, plus push buttons that aren't read-only), in the document's tab order.
- **On a focused push button:**
  - Space or Enter presses it (its action, as a click's release runs it);
  - Tab moves on;
  - Escape or a click elsewhere leaves it.
- **The keyboard holder is shared.** The invisible widget that keeps Space, Tab and the arrows from scrolling the page under a focused check box now serves push buttons too (`hold_keys`).
- **Laid-out XFA buttons** are push buttons as well, so they now run their XFA enter and exit scripts (#4359) when they gain and lose the focus.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and tests on `pdfcraft-ui-egui`. The existing button, check box and XFA button tests pass un…

title: M4: bind property drafts with edit-session and replay UI scenarios
author: PerchAnton
body:
## What this changes

Document Properties can currently overwrite newer metadata with an old draft. An intervening edit followed by Undo can also let the stale draft create a new history entry and discard Redo. Two real UI regressions failed on main `418ac6a2` before the production change and pass with this patch.

Bind Description, Initial View and accepted Custom properties to the original document identity, edit generation and modification permission with `edit-session`. OK rechecks and consumes the draft, then dispatches one existing engine batch. Cancel/Escape and no-ops issue no edit; an engine refusal retains the draft for correction. Clean inspection tabs retain same-document live refresh, while pending edits and unaccepted Custom input cannot be rebased.

Add a PdfCraft-owned JSONL example adapter using real egui widgets and the engine, ten scenarios, and optional local replay through `interaction-check`. Includes save/reopen, one-step Undo/Redo, invalid Custom input, stale edits, edit-Undo ABA, reload, tab switch, target close and live inspection. Python is development tooling only.

Related #3917 (Document Properties scope only). This does not replace the OS-open queueing work in #4042 or claim to fix other dialogs.

## Dependency review

The Rust runtime in this proposal is a [reviewable vendor snapshot](https://github.com/PerchAnton/pdfcraft/blob/da0114a2fa59d89b2928c509a0904254680366e1/vendor/README.md#edit-session) of edit-session 0.1.0-alpha.2. I maintain the library. Its manifest, Rust source, lifecycle tests and both licenses match upstream commit `033f7c3a`. Maintainers can review exactly what would ship.

The ten [interaction-check scenarios](https://github.com/PerchAnton/pdfcraft/blob/da0114a2fa59d89b2928c509a0904254680366e1/docs/document-properties-sessions.md#replaying-the-real-dialog) run locally when a developer explicitly invokes the pinned Python tool. author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

Import comments read XFDF, FDF, XML, XDP, CSV and text data files only, and `comment.import-from-pdf` was planned. The reference app's help page says "Comments can be imported from a PDF document", that "the comment positioning matches that of the file from which they were imported", and that importing from a ten-page document into a two-page one brings only the comments of the first two pages (Import and export comments, https://web.archive.org/web/20251226015046/https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/importing-exporting-comments.html).

- Comments ▸ Import comments now lists `.pdf` files. Each comment of the chosen PDF is copied onto the page with the same number, at the same place, with its appearance stream, its pop-up, its replies and its layer. Comments on pages past the document's last page are left out, and so are replies to them. Links, form fields and redaction marks are not copied.
- A comment named (`/NM`) like one already on its page replaces it, as an XFDF or FDF import does. Names are compared as text, whatever their encoding. A locked comment, or an annotation of that name that is not a comment (a link, a screen or 3D annotation, a redaction mark, a widget), stays, and the copy is added beside it without the name.
- The import is one undo step. A PDF without comments is refused with "nothing in the file matches this document", and a PDF that needs a password is refused.
- `pdfcraft_organize::import_comments` does the copying with the page copier that Insert Pages uses. `Edit::ImportData` reads a file that starts with `%PDF-` as a PDF. Any other file goes to the data importer first, and is read as a PDF when that fails, `%PDF-` occurs in its first 1,024 bytes and the PDF reader opens it. `doc_import_data` takes a PDF the same way.
- `form.import_data` (Import form data…) lists the same files as before.

title: M5: review statuses are hidden, chain per reviewer and show per reviewer, by /IRT reference (#4122)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4122.

Supersedes #4126 (reworked on main's /IRT threading).

Review statuses now follow ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.3: a state belongs to one user, a user's next change replies to their previous state reply, and PdfCraft shows one status per reviewer.

**Writing** (`crates/annot`):
- Status replies (`/StateModel /Review`) are written with the **Hidden** flag (`/F 30`, Table 167 bit 2). A state reply records a state, not a note (§12.5.6.3: "The state is not specified in the annotation itself but in a separate text annotation"), so it is not drawn as a note icon or listed as an ordinary reply.
- A reviewer's next change replies to **their previous state reply**, not to the annotation. §12.5.6.3 requires this: "Additional state changes shall be made by adding text annotations in reply to the previous reply for a given user." Checkmarks (`/StateModel /Marked`) chain the same way. Another reviewer, or the other state model, starts its own chain on the annotation.
- A reply with a `/StateModel` but no `/State` has the model's default state (Table 175).

**Reading** (`ReviewStates` in `crates/render`, used everywhere states are shown):
- States are found by **object reference**, on main's settled `parent` links (#4061), not by `/NM`. A state reply sets the state of the first annotation up its `/IRT` chain that is not itself a state reply: §12.5.6.3 says its `/IRT` "shall refer to the original annotation", and later changes reply to the previous state reply. So a status set on a reply is that reply's, at any depth of the thread, and is never folded into the thread's comment; `comment_list` reports it on the reply, as main already does.
- A loop, or a chain to nothing listed, belongs to nothing.
- `link_replies` and `thread_tops` now settle a chain of any length (a seen-set against loops, each annotation walked once) instead of stopping at 64 steps, since a reviewer's long status history is a long `/IRT` chain.
- `statuses(c)` gives each reviewer's late…

title: M12: an XFA form laid out again by its scripts rebuilds its pages in the view (#4603)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4603.

**The need.** On a dynamic XFA form, a field change whose scripts lay the form out again (a check box's change script that shows a hidden section) writes new pages into the document, but the session kept the old page list. The new section's fields had no page rectangle, the field list kept its old length, and saving failed with "the edit changed the page count from 1 to 2", so the form could not be saved once the section was shown. A picture chosen for an XFA image field, and a reset whose calculations show or hide a section, took the same path.

**The basis.** XFA 3.3, chapter 30, config `dynamicRender` (p. 1300): the form may "re-render itself during the session to show or hide objects, instantiate pages, and so on". Chapter 7, "Basic Layout in Dynamic Forms" (pp. 269-270): content that no longer fits "moves on to the next available page within the page set". The page tree written must keep `/Count` equal to its page objects (ISO 32000-2, Table 30, p. 103), and the session's page list must match the file it saves, which the save check of #1698 enforces.

**The change** (`pdfcraft-engine` only, plus one test fixture in `pdfcraft-xfa`)
- `XfaRun` gains `relaid`. `Runner::relayout` sets it just before it calls `pdfcraft_xfa::rerender`, so a layout that fails part way, after it may have replaced fields, still counts.
- `EditCtx` gathers it from every script run inside an edit: `on_changes` (field changes and resets), `on_data_replaced` (pictures) and `on_event`.
- After the scripts, `apply` raises the edit's scope to `Scope::Full` when the form was laid out again, as the text-growth path of #2624 already does. The decision is "laid out again", not "the page count changed": the page objects, widgets and sizes are all replaced even when the count stays the same.

title: M12: XFA repeating rows lay out past 50, and tables in positioned containers repeat their rows (#4607, #4615)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4607. Fixes #4615.

**The need.** On a dynamic XFA form, repeating rows were lost in two ways:
- **Past 50 (#4607).** A repeating subform laid out at most 50 instances, so rows 51 and on of a long list or table never appeared. That held whether the rows came from the data or from a button's `addInstance`. Calculations over the rows saw only those 50.
- **A table in positioned content (#4615).** A table (`layout="table"`, rows `layout="row"`) placed at its own position in a positioned subform laid out each row subform **once**, whatever the data or `occur` asked for: 5 data rows gave 1, `max="3"` gave 1, and no warning was recorded. The same table in a flowed subform repeated its rows. The table was also measured with one instance of each row, so what followed it in a top-to-bottom container sat right after that row.

**The basis.**
- XFA 3.3, chapter 17, "The occur element" (p. 786): `max` is "the maximum number of occurrences for the enclosing container, or -1 to set no upper boundary for occurrences". Chapter 9 (p. 336) says the same: -1 "means that the number of occurrences is unlimited", and pagination "is performed downstream by the layout process". A form's own `max` still stops the rows: "it can be copied at most twenty times into the Form DOM", and a row past it "would simply be ignored".
- Chapter 8, "Tables" (p. 327): "A table subform represents an entire table and contains everything in the table. A row subform represents one row of a table and contains everything in the row." Chapter 7, "Layout Strategies" (p. 265): "Dynamic forms may contain a mixture of objects laid out using different layout strategies"; "Repeating Elements using Occurrence Limits" (p. 263): `max` "Regardless of the data no more than this number of instances may be included". The count belongs to the row and its `occur`, not to the layout of the table's parent.

**The change** (`crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`)

title: feat(edit): Esc in an open paragraph selects its box, so Delete removes it
author: meethere
body:
## What this changes

In **Edit text & images**, a click inside a paragraph opens it for typing. Selecting the whole box (to delete or move it) meant aiming for its thin frame; a press a few pixels inside put the caret in the text instead, which users found hard (#2203: "it many times selects individual character inside the box").

Now **Esc** in the inline editor leaves the text and selects the paragraph's box, as Acrobat does when Esc leaves a text box. **Esc then Delete** removes the paragraph (with #4111's object-selection delete), the arrow keys nudge it and its frame drags it. Esc still discards an unapplied draft, as before.

- `ObjectSelection::select_paragraph_next(page, block)`: the editor overlay has no document inventory, so it records the request.
- `ObjectSelection::prepare`, which has the document, selects that paragraph **after** its own Escape check. `prepare` runs before the overlay in the frame, so the Esc that closed the editor cannot clear what it selected.
- `clear()` drops a pending request, so a disabled tool or a cleared selection never selects later.

title: fix(edit): catch paragraph edges and frames without aiming for the hairline
author: meethere
body:
## What this changes

In **Edit text & images**, a paragraph's rewrap handle and an open paragraph's frame were hard to catch (#2203: handles "not precise", "sometimes I can't get them to appear"). Measured on `main` (see the table in #4190's thread): the edge grip reached ±6 px around the outline, and further inside a press moved the box instead.

- **`EDGE_REACH` 6 → 8 px.** A narrow box still keeps its middle for moving (`inside` stays capped at a quarter of its width).
- **One `FRAME_REACH`, 8 px.** An open paragraph's frame had two reaches: 4 px for the move cursor drawn in `edit_text_ui` and 6 px for the press `object_ui::on_frame` takes. Between 4 and 6 px a press selected the box with no cursor saying so. `object_ui` now uses `edit_text_ui::FRAME_REACH`, so the move arrow shows exactly where a press takes hold.

Refs #2203.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2`: 506 lib + 1150 integration passed, 0 failed

title: fix(ui): keep added image corner resize responsive and clip out-of-bounds drag preview (#4477, #3938)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4477
Fixes #3938

In **Edit a PDF** (`QuickTool::EditText`), resizing or moving an added image had four interacting issues:

1. **Corner handle presses hijacked by object marquee (`object_ui.rs`, `content_ui.rs`):** `paint_page` draws the four circular resize handles centered on `r.expand(1.0)` with radius `3.5` (reaching `4.5` px outside `r`), while `object_ui::page_input` ran before `content_ui::page_input` and only checked `r.expand(2.0).contains(p)` without checking `content_ui::select_grabs`. Pressing on the outer portion of a corner handle where the resize cursor is shown missed `hit`, called `leave_single(view)` (clearing `view.content.selected`), and started an object marquee that placed the image into `view.objects.selected` on release, preventing `content_ui::page_input` from responding again.
2. **Handles and items extending past the page edge (`content_ui.rs`):** `content_ui::page_input` and `select_grabs` filtered the pointer to `xf.rect` before checking `corner` and `hit`, so corner handles at or beyond the page boundary (or an image dragged partially out of bounds) stopped responding once the drag was released.
3. **Inward corner resize along one axis (`content_ui.rs`):** `dragged` computed the proportional scale factor with `.max(...)` across the two axes (`((w + dx) / w).max((h + dy) / h)`), which froze shrinking whenever the other axis did not also move inward. It now uses the axis with the larger relative pointer change, matching `edit_text_ui`.
4. **Out-of-bounds drag preview distortion (`content_ui.rs`):** `MoveBackground::paint` sampled `page_tex` across the full unclipped `r.expand(1.0)` quad and started a second drag during `settling` from `from` instead of the settled box. When an added image extended outside `xf.rect`, `xf.screen_to_norm` produced UV coordinates outside `0.0..=1.0`, clamping and smearing page-border texels across the out-of-bounds portion of the dragged image. `MoveBackground::paint` now clips t…

title: fix(comments): count comment drafts as unsaved work and post them on save (#3918)
author: adiraj66132
body:
## What this changes

A comment being typed lived in the app, not the file, and nothing counted it as work. Close, quit and
the auto-reload on an external change all went through `has_unsaved_work`, which listed form drafts,
the open text box and the paragraph editor but not the three places a comment is typed:

- the floating composer card (`comments.composer`) — a new note, text box, callout, caret or replacement;
- the reply box under the selected card (`comments.reply`);
- the "Add a comment" box at the top of the Comments panel (`comments.add_box`).

All three are now counted, so closing, quitting or reloading asks first; and **Save posts them as
annotations before writing**, the same way `save_then` already commits form typing and the open text
box. Nothing typed is ever dropped behind a save that the user chose.

What counts as unsaved and what gets posted now share one rule:

- `comments::can_post` — what the card's Post button allows (text, or an edit being cleared).
- `comments::composer_changed` — whether the card holds anything Post would post. An *edit* card is
  only work when its text differs from the comment's own, so opening Edit and closing the document
  no longer prompts or rewrites the comment.

`comments::submit_composer`, `submit_reply` and `submit_add_box` are the single place each edit is
built: the panel and the card call them, and so does Save. `new_comment` lost its `PageCx`
parameter (it only ever read `page` and `prefs`), which is what lets Save build a comment without a
live page transform.

`comments.editing` (the inline edit of a card's text) is deliberately **not** touched here: PR #3125
already counts it and commits it, and both changes edit the same expression. Whichever lands second
reconciles one adjacent line.

Fixes #3918

title: fix(forms): allow deleting individual radio buttons from a group (#4609)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4609.

In Prepare Form mode, deleting a single radio button previously deleted the entire radio group and all its buttons because `prepare::delete_selected` ignored widget indices and issued `Edit::DeleteField { name }`.

This change:
1. Adds `delete_widget` (and `delete_widget_object`) to `pdfcraft_forms::author`:
   - If the field has only one widget remaining, delegates to `delete_field`.
   - If the field has multiple widgets:
     - Removes the widget object from page `/Annots` arrays.
     - Removes the widget object from the field's `/Kids` array.
     - Removes the corresponding entry from `/Opt` if `/Opt` is present and matches the widget count.
     - Resets `/V` and `/DV` to `/Off` if the deleted widget was the actively selected choice.
     - Cleans up calculation order `/CO`.
     - Regenerates appearances for the remaining widgets via `redraw_field`.
2. Adds `Edit::DeleteWidget { name: String, widget: usize }` to `pdfcraft_engine` with full atomic undo/redo support.
3. Updates `prepare::delete_selected` in `ui-egui`:
   - Inspects the field's widget count using `form: &[FormField]`.
   - Emits `Edit::DeleteWidget` when a single widget from a multi-widget field is selected.
   - When all widgets of a field are selected (or for single-widget fields), emits `Edit::DeleteField`.
   - When multiple individual widgets or fields are selected, batches them atomically and deletes widgets in descending index order to avoid index shifting.
4. Adds support for an optional `widget` index parameter in the headless `form_delete_field` automation tool.
5. Adds comprehensive unit tests in `forms` and `engine`, a headless automation test in `automation`, and UI integration tests in `ui-egui`.

title: Reject non-hex characters in XFA image hash parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

XFA image hash parsing no longer accepts `+` as a hex digit. Before this change, `parse_hex32` (`crates/xfa/src/pdf.rs`) only checked the length and then called `u8::from_str_radix` on each byte pair. That function accepts a leading `+`, so a string like `+f000...` decoded as a valid hash with a first byte of 0x0F.

`parse_hex32` now returns `None` unless every byte is an ASCII hex digit, before it parses any pair. A regression test covers the `+`, `-` and space prefixes, and checks that mixed-case hex still parses.

No existing issue. Found while testing `crates/xfa/src/pdf.rs:50-52`.

## How you verified it

- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Never-crash

- [ ] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests, unless it is provably infallible with a comment saying why
- [ ] No indexing or slicing with input-derived positions (`get`, and strings only at char boundaries); checked or saturating arithmetic; allocations sized by input are capped; recursion is bounded
- [ ] No `unsafe`

Fixes #4616.

Add Watermark (and Update Watermark) now has a **Saved Settings** row, like Acrobat's. Type a name and press **Save Settings** to keep the watermark as it stands. title: M6: a static XFA form whose data fills thousands of fields opens in seconds (#4637)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4637.

**The need.** Opening a static XFA form gives its fields the values held in its XFA datasets. Each value went through `forms::set_value`, which reads the whole field tree to find the field and reads it again to recalculate. n values cost about 2n readings of n fields, so the open time grew with the square of the fields. A public 136-page form with about 6,000 fields took 261 s to open, and a 95-page one with about 4,000 took 112 s.

**The change**
- **`forms::set_values`** fills a batch as `set_value` fills each value in turn, but:
  - it reads the form once;
  - it recalculates once, after the last value. The calculation order (ISO 32000-2, Table 224, `/CO`) runs once over the final values.
- **Same results as one by one:**
  - Fields with the same fully qualified name (§12.7.4.2) still share the value.
  - A name the batch already wrote, or a twin of one, makes the form be read again first. That write then starts from what the earlier one left. For example, clearing a no-toggle-to-off radio group the batch just selected is still refused.
  - Each value reports its own result.
  - A failed recalculation fails the batch, as it fails `set_value`.
  - A batch where nothing is filled recalculates nothing.
- **`set_value_with`** now uses the same write path (`fill`), so the two cannot drift apart.
- **The engine** (`xfa_values_from_datasets`, on open and on an XFA data import) collects the changed values and fills them with `set_values`. It finds fields by name through a map, not a scan per value.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-forms`, `pdfcraft-xfa` and `pdfcraft-engine` (`--all-targets`)

title: fix(edit): resizing an image under a shared clip scales its own clip too
author: meethere
body:
## What this changes

Resizing an existing image in **Edit text & images** grew the picture but left it showing only through its old box, with the rest cut off. Seen on a real lab-report PDF (not attached: it holds personal data). Its generator draws every picture as

```
q  x y w h re W n   (the picture's own clip, its size or a little wider)
   w 0 0 h x y cm  /Im Do
Q
```

inside an outer `q … re W n … Q` that the section's text shares. An invoice whose pictures have no clip resized fine.

`image_transform_scope` (#1049, #1269) only accepted a scope containing **every** active clip. Under the section's clip none does, so it fell back to transforming the `Do` alone: the picture's own clip stayed at the old size.

Now, when no scope contains every clip, the **outermost scope holding only the image** is used. It holds all of the image's private clips, which move with it; anything outside it is shared with other content and stays. The existing case of a clip shared with a caption inside the same scope (`cropped_image_resizing_moves_private_clips_and_keeps_shared_ones`) keeps its fixed clip. `crop_image` uses the same scope, so cropping such a picture replaces its own clip.

Related: #1022 / #1049 (the same bug without an outer clip).

body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4614.

The window's AccessKit root node (role Window) had no name, so AT-SPI clients on Linux saw a top-level frame with an empty accessible name. The same was true of UIA on Windows. The root node now takes the window title, "b.pdf — PdfCraft", and follows it whenever the title changes (another tab, a document that asks to show its title, Combine files).

title: M14: keyboard shortcuts can be changed, removed and reset (#4635)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4635.

Help ▸ Keyboard shortcuts was read-only. Now every registered command's key can be changed there:

- **Change** waits for the next key press, which becomes the command's shortcut. Escape on its own stops waiting without closing the dialog.
- **Remove** leaves the command without a key, and **Reset** gives it its default back.
- **Reset all shortcuts** puts every command back to its default.
- **Find a command** searches all registered commands, so a command without a key can get one. Without a search, the list shows the commands that have a key, as before.

What the dialog refuses, and what it does about conflicts:
- **One key runs one command.** Taking a key another command had takes it from that command, and a notice says so: "Ctrl+S was taken from “Save”, which now has no shortcut." Reset does the same if the default was given away meanwhile.
- **Refused with a reason:** Alt combinations (the `Shortcut` model has no Alt), Escape/Tab/Enter/Space/Backspace without Ctrl, and the keys the document view reads itself (Copy, the zoom and page keys, Find next/previous, Select all, Rotate view). The view reads those after the registered commands, so binding one would silently break it.
- **No typing hijack.** A key of the user's own without Ctrl (a letter, F5) doesn't fire while a text field has the keyboard, whatever the command normally allows, so it never takes over typing.

How the binding is shared:
- The changes are published to the egui context each frame (`custom_shortcuts::publish` / `effective`).
- The key handling (`registry_shortcuts`), the menus, the palette, the tooltips (Next/Previous view), the search field's key hint and the control channel's `commands` list all read the same binding.

Persistence follows the never-crash rules:
- Changes are kept in the settings under `shortcuts`, as `{ "command id": "cmd+shift+J" | null }`.
- Reading them back is lenient: unknown commands, unreadable keys and anything a press would be …

title: fix(platform): a saved file keeps its hidden and system attributes on Windows
author: FriedCerebrum
body:
## What this changes

Every save writes a staging file beside the target and renames it over the target. On Windows the renamed file keeps the *staging file's* attributes, not the replaced file's, so a hidden or system PDF came out of a save visible.

The staging file is now created with the replaced file's `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN` and `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM`, through std's `OpenOptionsExt::attributes` (no `unsafe`, no new dependency). A hidden target's staging file is hidden from its first moment, and a plain target's staging file is created explicitly plain. A new file gets neither attribute. Read-only targets are still refused before staging, as before. The archive bit is left to the system, as on any changed file.

The writer is shared, so the desktop save and the automation tools/CLI both get this.

Refs #4593. On local NTFS a plain file does **not** become hidden. I checked that with plain renames on Windows 11 26200, and the new test pins it. So I couldn't reproduce the report itself. My guess is that the reporter's file sits on an SMB/NAS share that hides dot-prefixed names (Samba's `hide dot files`). Staging names start with a dot. Asking the reporter where the file lives would settle it. If it is a share, this change at least asks for plain attributes on the staging file explicitly, but I haven't verified it against a share.

## How you verified it

On Windows 11 (26200), Rust 1.99.1:

title: M8: Sanitize can remove or flatten a signed document's signatures (#4622)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4622: all three modes the issue proposes (`abort`, `remove`, `flatten`).

Sanitize Document on a signed file used to be refused, with no way forward. Refusing is still the default, but the signatures can now be given up explicitly. A sanitized rewrite invalidates them anyway, and their certificates, names and timestamps are hidden information too.

- **redact:** `sanitize::Signatures { Remove, Flatten }` and `sanitize::sanitize_signed(doc, how)`.
  - **Remove** (`sanitize_removing_signatures`): every signature field goes, signed or empty, document timestamps included. Its widgets, and with them how it looks on the page, are removed through `forms::delete_field_object`.
  - **Flatten** (`sanitize_flattening_signatures`): the signature fields stay through to Sanitize's form flattening, so each one's look becomes page content like any other field's. The signature dictionary with the certificates, the signer's name and the timestamp goes with the form: once `/Perms` is gone too, nothing reaches it. Whatever the appearance itself shows, such as "Digitally signed by …" and a date, stays visible, as the issue says.
  - **Both modes also remove** any signature widget a page lists that the form adopts no field for, found by walking `/FT` up the `/Parent` chain (bounded, cycle-safe), plus the catalog's `/Perms` (DocMDP, UR3) and `/DSS` and the form's `/SigFlags`.
  - Then the usual Sanitize runs, and the save is a full rewrite, so no earlier revision is left.
  - No signature validation is involved: valid, expired, untrusted or malformed signatures are all handled the same way.
- **engine:** `Edit::SanitizeSigned(SanitizeSignatures)`, labelled "Sanitize document and remove signatures" or "… and flatten signatures", and undoable until saved. It is the one full rewrite the signed-document guard lets through. `Edit::Sanitize` still returns `SignedRewrite`.

title: Keep the part of an email address before an apostrophe when redacting
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Email redaction no longer drops the part of an address before an apostrophe. The email scanner's `local` closure in `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs` did not accept an apostrophe in the local part. It treated `'` as a boundary and started the match after it, so for `o'brien@example.com` only `brien@example.com` matched. Search and Redact share that span, so the leading `o'` stayed visible.

The local part may now contain an apostrophe, but a match cannot start on one. `o'brien@example.com` and `'john'@example.com` are now matched as `o'brien@example.com` and `john'@example.com`. A quote around an address (`'john@example.com'`) stays outside the match.

No linked issue. Found while testing `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs:216` (email, `local` closure).

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: fix(redact): preserve empty clips when redacting clipping titles
author: robertobulltech
body:
## What this changes

Redacting every glyph of a clipping-mode title used to remove its mask, allowing following artwork to cover the page. The redaction interpreter tracks removed and surviving clipping glyphs across text shows and content-stream pieces, then writes an explicit empty clip after `ET` when none survives. Partial removal retains surviving clipping glyphs. Hidden-text cleanup shares this protection.

Fixes #3123. The editor-side refusal was handled separately in #3447; this PR addresses redaction.

## CI failure and review fixes

- **Failing automation regression:** current main removes intersecting vector paths whole. The old page-sized vector fill therefore disappeared in the non-clipping mode-0 control. The fixture now uses a constant blue shading, which remains outside the redaction. The pixel comparison still covers the entire page outside the mark, after save/close/reopen.
- **CodeRabbit: inner `q ... Q`:** the reported symptom was real, but the cause was in the renderer. Pending glyph outlines accumulate until `ET`; restoring the redaction flags would make the saved result expose artwork in Poppler. The renderer now preserves pending outlines across explicit `Q`, without resurrecting outlines already consumed at `ET`. Outlines are recorded in device space so changes to the CTM cannot move them. Applied graphics-state clips still restore normally. The text-object accumulation in redaction is retained. This follows the accumulation rule in [the PDF reference, §5.2.5](https://opensource.adobe.com/dc-acrobat-sdk-docs/pdfstandards/pdfreference1.7old.pdf); [erratum 368](https://pdf-issues.pdfa.org/32000-2-2020/clause09.html) additionally saves/restores the text matrices.
- **CodeRabbit: stray pixel:** use an open move-only path (`0 0 m W n`) instead of a closed zero-area rectangle. A translated rectangle was observed retaining one pixel in external Poppler at 72, 144 and 300 dpi; the move-only path retained none.

title: feat(automation): doc_info reports every page's media, crop, bleed, trim and art boxes
author: acosimati
body:
## What this changes

`doc_info` listed only each page's displayed width and height, although the engine already
computes the five page boxes (`Document::page_boxes`, ISO 32000-2 §14.11.2) and `page_set_box`
can write them. A print workflow needs to read the trim and bleed boxes back, and an agent that
sets a box had no way to confirm what it set. Every entry of `pages` now carries
`boxes: { media, crop, bleed, trim, art }`, effective values (a missing box is its parent's),
in the tools' convention: points from the top-left of the displayed page, the same rect
`page_set_box` takes, so a rect written with `page_set_box` reads back unchanged. The crop box
is therefore `[0, 0, width, height]` and the media box may have negative coordinates when it
extends past the crop. `boxes_user` is the same five boxes in PDF user space (`[x0, y0, x1, y1]`,
y up, unrotated), as the file stores them, for prepress checks that want absolute values. Both
are `null` when the document can't be read for editing. The tool description names the two
fields and their conventions.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`

title: fix(annot,ui-egui): guard comment edits against non-comments and stale state (#3916)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Closes #3916

## Root Cause
1. In `crates/annot/src/lib.rs`, `annot_ref`, `delete_annotation`, and `props` indexed directly into a page's `/Annots` array without verifying `is_comment_subtype`. As a result, passing a `/Annots` slot occupied by a non-comment annotation (`/Widget`, `/Link`, `/Popup`, `/Watermark`, etc.) allowed comment operations (`delete_annotation`, `set_contents`, `move_annotation`, `set_color`, `props`, etc.) to mutate or remove form widgets and links.
2. In `crates/ui-egui/src/comments.rs`, `CommentView` retained `selected`, `editing`, `composer` (`ComposerKind::Edit`), and `gesture` across document and page updates (`DocView::document_changed`, `apply_edit`) without checking whether the referenced `(page, index)` comment slot still existed in `DocumentInfo::annotations`, allowing stale selections or open edit composers to target a shifted or non-comment `/Annots` slot.

title: M12: an XFA corner is a right angle unless its join is round, and is drawn with its own line
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

This corrects #4319, which rounded every XFA corner that has a `radius`. It never read the corner's `join`. In the XFA specification that defaults to `square`, a right angle; a radius rounds a corner only when `join="round"`. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) draws its page frame as a `<rectangle>` with `<corner radius="5.08mm" thickness="0.441mm"/>` and no `join`. Since 0.14.0 PdfCraft drew that frame with round corners, and the curve ran across the fields at the frame's corners (block 1, Control Number, and the Personnel/Finance "to date" field). Another viewer draws the frame square.

How another viewer draws `<corner>`, measured on two synthetic forms (each case on a `<rectangle>` value and on a subform `<border>`):

- **The radius always trims the edges.** Each edge stops the radius short of each of its corners, whatever the corner's shape or presence, and the corner fills the gap.
- **Shape.** The default `square` is a right angle, `join="round"` a quarter circle. `inverted="1"` turns a square corner into a notch the radius deep, and a round one into a quarter circle centred on the box's corner.
- **Each corner has its own line.** It is drawn with the corner's `thickness`, `color` and `stroke` (0.5pt solid black by default), not the edge's. A hidden corner leaves a gap between the trimmed edges.
- **The fill follows the corners' shapes**, hidden corners included.
- **Plain rectangles.** A box whose corners are all right angles lined like its edges (thickness, colour and stroke, not presence) is drawn as a plain rectangle. Its edges meet whole at the corners, and when they are hidden the corners are too. DA Form 31's frame is one; so are its grey boxes, whose edges and corners are hidden.

Changes, all in `crates/xfa`:

- **`model.rs`, `parse.rs`.**
  - `Corner` gains `round` (from `join`) and `line`, its own presence, thickness, colour and stroke, read as an edge's.
  - `Border::radii` gives each corner's…

title: M10: preserve TIFF associated-alpha colors on import
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

Translucent TIFF images with associated alpha no longer have their transparency applied twice when imported into a PDF.
For example, a premultiplied 8-bit pixel `[32, 64, 96, 128]` now becomes straight RGB `[64, 128, 191]` with alpha `128`, instead of keeping the dark premultiplied colors behind the same soft mask.
RGBA and explicitly tagged BlackIsZero grayscale-alpha work at 8 and 16 bits through Create PDF and Add Image, including files whose alpha metadata changes between TIFF directories.
Unassociation happens at source precision before the existing 16-bit high-byte reduction.
Zero alpha clears associated colors, and malformed associated colors greater than alpha are clamped.

The importer also refuses unsupported planar alpha and multiple-extra RGB layouts before reading pixels.
The pinned decoder's legacy `read_image` reads only the first plane of planar TIFFs and can compact multiple extra samples away, so treating those buffers as complete interleaved alpha data produced incorrect output.
Existing straight-alpha, unlabelled RGB and explicitly unspecified/unknown extra-sample compatibility behavior is retained.
Related to the TIFF/image semantics discussed in #1201; this does not resolve that broader audit.

## How you verified it

- Reproduced through a freshly built upstream `20eebc1c` CLI before production changes: associated RGBA colors are embedded premultiplied behind an additional alpha mask, while equivalent straight-alpha controls render correctly.
- Observed the original associated-color and GrayA regressions fail, then the planar-RGBA refusal regression fail at its intended runtime assertion.
- Independently byte-validated corrected five-sample TIFF controls, reproduced their lost extra/alpha meaning through 30 pure-main CLI calls, and observed the new native refusal regression fail before adding the layout guard.

`native_options` in `apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs` sets the window icon with `ViewportBuilder::with_icon`, which `eframe` passes to `winit`'s `set_window_icon`. On Windows, `set_window_icon` only sets the small icon (`ICON_SMALL`, used by the title bar), leaving the big icon (`ICON_BIG`, used by the taskbar and Alt+Tab) unset so Windows displays a generic application icon.

## Changes
- **`apps/pdfcraft/Cargo.toml`**: Added `winit = { version = 0.30, default-features = false }` under `[target.'cfg(target_os = windows)'.dependencies]` (already in the lockfile via `eframe` and patched to `vendor/winit`).
- **`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`**:
  - Added `taskbar_icon` and `set_taskbar_icon` on Windows to decode `APP_ICON_PNG` and set `ICON_BIG` via `winit::platform::windows::WindowExtWindows::set_taskbar_icon` on `cc.winit_window()` in `app_creator`.
  - Added unit test `the_window_and_windows_taskbar_icons_load_from_the_bundled_png` verifying `APP_ICON_PNG` decodes cleanly for both the viewport icon and the Windows `ICON_BIG` taskbar icon.

title: perf(ui): reloading waits for the system's change notifications instead of looking every 250 ms
author: ZJHeepfixer
body:
## What this changes

The worker that reloads a document when its file changes on disk (#431) looked at every open file's metadata every 250 ms for as long as a document with a file was open. That is four wakeups a second for the whole session, focused or not, whether anything changed or not, and it was most of PdfCraft's idle cost: on an M2 Max with a PDF open, the process woke 4.2 times a second, and `sample` showed only `pdfcraft-watch` in a timed wait. The parity entry already listed "OS change notifications (polling adds up to 250 ms)" as missing.

The worker now follows the folders of the open files through the system's change notifications (FSEvents on macOS, inotify on Linux, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows), through the `notify` crate, and looks only when one of them says something changed there:

- **What a notification means.** Any notification, or an error saying some were lost, is a reason to look. The stamps still decide what changed, exactly as before, so a path spelled differently in a notification (`/var` against `/private/var`, a case difference, a link) can't hide a change.
- **Bursts and busy folders.** A burst of notifications is one look. A folder that never stops changing (a build directory, Downloads) costs at most one look per `SETTLE` (40 ms), not one per change.
- **Unchanged.** Reading a changed file once it has settled and ends in `%%EOF`, epochs (#1802), PdfCraft's own saves, and the notice for unsaved changes all work as before.
- **Where it still looks every 250 ms.** In these cases a notification can't be trusted, so the worker keeps looking every 250 ms, as before:
  - files on a network or FUSE volume, which another computer (or the FUSE server) can rewrite without this one being told. `statfs` says which: `MNT_LOCAL` on macOS, the `f_type` magic numbers on Linux. ReadDirectoryChangesW does report changes on SMB shares, so Windows has no exception;
  - files whose folder is missing or couldn't be watched. The folder is followed ag…

title: Draw callouts upright on pages with /Rotate
author: Silvertree2010
body:

Fixes #4686

**Cause.** Callouts skipped the page-rotation handling that text boxes use. The UI laid the box out with rotation 0, and the appearance builder exempted callouts from the `/PCTextRotate` turn. author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4527:** its commits (and #3589's, which #4527 builds on) are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

An XFA form now runs its fields' validate scripts on opening. Before, PdfCraft ran them only after a value changed. #4527's description lists this as a gap.

Measured in another viewer on a synthetic form, with:
- a field that passes;
- a field with a value that fails, with its own message;
- an empty field that fails;
- a calculated field.

On opening, every field with a validate script ran it, in document order, after the calculations. An earlier probe on #4527 puts that before `form:ready`. - `Runner::validates` runs every validate script of the form in document order, each on its field's value.

title: M12: XFA fields validate before they exit, and a list box validates and exits as the focus leaves it
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4573:** its commits (and those of #4359, #4563 and #4369, which it builds on) are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

XFA fields now run their validate scripts before their exit scripts, each kind of field at the moment another viewer runs them. A list box now keeps the focus as items are picked in it, as a check box does. #4573 listed list and combo boxes as not covered.

Measured in another viewer on two synthetic forms, each field logging its enter, change, validate, exit and click scripts:
- **Text field:** typing runs change; leaving runs validate, then exit.
- **Check box:** a click runs validate, then change and click; exit waits for the focus to leave.
- **Drop-down:** picking an item runs change, validate and exit at once. The drop-down gives up the focus as the item is picked, so clicking away afterwards runs nothing more for it.
- **List box:** picking an item runs change and click. The list keeps the focus; validate and exit run as the focus leaves it.

Before this change, PdfCraft ran exit before validate for every field. A check box validated after its change scripts, and a list box validated and exited with every pick.

Changes:
- `crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`, `on_changes`:
  - A check box or radio button runs its validate scripts first, before `TOGGLE_ORDER`.
  - Any other field runs them after its change scripts and before its exit scripts.
  - A list box with the focus keeps it, like a check box: its exit waits, and its SOM path goes into `FocusLeft::unvalidated`.
  - `FocusLeft` holds what is left for the focus to finish (the exits that ran, the list boxes still to validate), so `on_changes` keeps seven arguments.
- `Runner::validate`: one validate script, with the existing alert rule (a failing value shows its message, an empty one doesn't). It is shared by `on_changes` and `on_focus`.

title: M6: a click in the field being edited runs its Mouse Down and Mouse Up
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4589:** its commits (and #4585's, which it builds on) are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

A click in the text field being edited now runs that field's Mouse Down and Mouse Up actions. Before, the open editor took the press, and the page never saw it, so neither ran.

The order comes from the synthetic form measured for #4585 in another viewer. A click on the field that has the focus runs only Mouse Down and Mouse Up: no Blur, no Focus. A press that drags to select text runs them too, the Mouse Up as the button comes up over the field.

Changes, in `crates/ui-egui/src/forms_ui.rs` (`overlay`, the field editor, which the page-input rule exempts):
- A press in the open editor queues the field's Mouse Down (`pressed_on`), as a press on the page does, and records that the press began there (`FormView::editor_press`).

title: perf(forms): an XFA redraw reads the form once, not once per field
author: MoriartyPuth
body:
## What this changes

Regenerating the widget appearances of **every** field of a form used to cost one
whole-form reading per field. A dynamic XFA form is laid out at open and its field
appearances are regenerated then (and again after every script event that lays it out
again), and such forms have thousands of fields — so opening one was **quadratic in the
field count**: this branch brings `pdfcraft-cli info` from 2.36 s at 1,000 field rows to
0.13 s, and 23.73 s at 4,000 to 0.63 s (8,000 fields went from about 12 minutes to
1.69 s, measured on an older build). After this PR, laying out a 4,000-field form reads
the form 2 times, not 4,001 times.

Concretely, on current `main` `engine::xfa_redraw` loops over the form's fields and calls
`pdfcraft_forms::redraw_field(name)` per field — and `redraw_field` starts by reading the
whole form to find its field by name (`author/look.rs`: `fields(doc).into_iter().find(…)`).
One full-form enumeration (page `/Annots` maps, inheritance, HashMaps) per field. The
widget-redraw loop body now lives in `redraw_widgets_at`, which takes a field that is
already resolved; `redraw_field` keeps the by-name lookup for its own callers (unchanged
behaviour), and the new `redraw_all_fields` reads the form once
(`fields_with_adopted`) and redraws every field from what it already knows. The engine's
`xfa_redraw` is now one call to it. A signed signature field still keeps the picture its
signer's application drew (the skip moves with the loop), and a field whose appearance
cannot be drawn still produces an error naming the field.

## How you verified it

Measured with a synthetic ladder (a one-page dynamic XFA form with K subform/field rows;
`pdfcraft-cli info`, release build, sums of three runs agreeing):

| K fields | `main` (measured on `d764a8eb`) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 2.36 s | 0.13 s |
| 2,000 | 5.47 s | 0.26 s |
| 4,000 | 23.73 s | 0.63 s |
| 8,000 | 715 s (measured on `0b670caf`) | 1.69 s |

title: input: macOS nine-grid IMEs commit unmarked text, and their code keys no longer type digits (#4687)
author: andyau98
body:
## Summary

Nine-grid input methods such as 九方 (Q9 M9) never call `setMarkedText`: they swallow their code keys silently (no IME callback at all) and commit the chosen character from inside `keyDown:` with `insertText:replacementRange:` and `replacementRange = NSNotFound`. winit dropped that commit (no `pending_commit`), and it also sent the swallowed code key to the app as `KeyboardInput` text, so typing a character inserted its digits and the character never arrived — #4687.

- Track whether an IME callback ran for the key being handled by `keyDown:` (`ime_callback_fired`, set in `insertText:`, `setMarkedText:` and `doCommandBySelector:`).
- In `insertText:`, treat a commit inside `keyDown:` with no marked text, no pending commit and a string different from the event's characters as an unmarked commit: announce `Ime::Enabled` if the state is still `Disabled`, then emit `Ime::Commit`, mirroring the existing mouse-commit branch.
- In `keyDown:`, call `NSTextInputContext.handleEvent(&event)` (which reports whether the input context consumed the event) instead of `interpretKeyEvents`, and skip the `KeyboardInput` entirely for a key consumed with no callback and nothing forwarded by `doCommandBySelector:`. Clearing only `KeyEvent::text` was not enough: egui-winit falls back to `logical_key.to_text()`, which still types the digit.

The patch is confined to the vendored winit (`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/macos/view.rs`, winit 0.30.13). If you would rather carry this as a winit upstream change first, the same logic can be proposed there (rust-windowing/winit#3617, rust-windowing/winit#4650).

## Testing

macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6, aarch64), Q9 M9, in PdfCraft 0.14.0 built from this branch:

- Keyboard: the nine-grid digit codes no longer appear, and the chosen character commits cleanly (keyboard and mouse candidate selection).
- Backspace, Enter and the arrow keys still reach the app; no Windows or Linux paths are touched.

title: fix(check): check dynamic XFA forms after they are laid out
author: MoriartyPuth
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli check` never checked a dynamic XFA form's real pages. It took the page count
from the file's page tree and rendered those pages from the raw bytes — for a dynamic XFA
form, that is the one placeholder page the file still holds (the template is what layout
turns into pages at open). So `check` reported

```
{"file": … , "status": "ok", "pages": 1, "warnings": 0, "ms": 1, …}
```

for a synthetic 7 KB dynamic form the app lays out into two pages, and `ok / pages=1 /
0 warnings` for every larger dynamic form too (a 400-page laid-out form: `ms: 10`). This
contradicts the other file-reading verbs on the same file — `info` says `pages: 400`,
`pdf_pages: 1`; `text` reads a page 3 the placeholder tree does not have; `render --page 3`
draws a laid-out page. `tests/it/xfa.rs` states the rule those commands already follow
(#1645): **page commands must use the same dynamic XFA layout as the app and tools** —
`check` is the one command outside it.

Two consequences beyond the numbers:

- The ok verdict was about pages the app never shows. When the layout itself misbehaves,
  `check` cannot see it: any crash/hang/error that lives in opening a dynamic form
  (`Session::open` — template parse, script events, appearance generation for the laid-out
  pages) passes the sweep as long as the placeholder page renders.
- `cargo xtask fuzz` drives `check-one` on mutated seeds, which inherits the same blind
  spot: a mutation that only breaks the template still passes, because the layout pipeline
  never runs.

`check` now opens a dynamic XFA form the way `info`/`text`/`render` do, through
`Session::open`, and checks the laid-out copy: `pages` counts the laid-out pages (what
`info`'s `pages` reports), the pixels+text loop runs per laid-out page, and a failed open
is reported as the `open-error` a user would get opening it in the app. A form that cannot finish the layout
inside `--timeout` reports as `{"timeout": 1}` in the parent's summary, so large dynami…

title: fix(print): fall back to the lpoptions listing when the PPD is unreadable (#4699)
author: lordwotton29
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4699.

`cupsd` keeps `/etc/cups/ppd/<queue>.ppd` at `0640 root:cups` on Arch and similar setups, so an ordinary desktop user cannot open it. `printer_options_via_within` turned that permission error into `None`, and `Print ▸ Properties…` showed *"This printer offers no settings of its own."* — although `lpoptions -p <queue> -l` was returning every option, with its choices and default, to that same user.

When the PPD is missing, unreadable, or parses to no options, the list is now built from that `lpoptions -l` listing. Options Craft handles itself (`PageSize`, `PageRegion`, `Duplex`, `Collate`, `ImageableArea`, `PaperDimension`) are skipped to match `parse_ppd`; the starred choice becomes the default; keys and choice names pass the same conservative checks the PPD path uses; and the option list, the choices per option and the labels are capped at the same numbers `parse_ppd` uses (400, 400, 256).

Where an option's value has to be typed, CUPS prints `Custom`, `Custom.<TYPE>` (`Custom.PASSCODE`, `Custom.STRING`) or `Custom.WIDTHxHEIGHT` in place of the choices. The dialog collects no such value, so those templates are dropped instead of offered as selectable text; an option whose choices are *all* templates disappears with them, and a starred template never becomes the default.


A line is split at its **last** colon, not its first. `list_group()` prints the option as `"%s/%s:"` from the PPD's keyword and translated text, and every choice as a bare `" %s"`, so the text can carry a colon (`Supporto: Tipo`) while a choice keyword cannot. Splitting at the first colon turned the rest of the text into invented choices.

When the choice CUPS marks is a custom-value template, the template is dropped and **no default is stood in its place**. The parser used to promote the first retained choice, and the dialog showed it as the printer's default; but only options changed away from the default are submitted, so CUPS kept the template and the value …

title: fix(ui): the page sets its cursor once, from the top claim the tool reaches
author: alehel
body:
## In short

The cursor's shape is a promise about what a click will do: a hand follows a link, an I-beam selects text, a four-way arrow moves something. Until now about twenty parts of the page view each set the cursor, and whichever ran last in a frame won, whatever a click would actually do. So with the stamp tool over a link you saw the link's hand but a click placed a stamp, and with the Select tool over a comment lying on text you saw the I-beam but a drag moved the comment.

With this PR each part instead asks for a cursor, with a rank (an open editor outranks a resize handle, which outranks a comment, which outranks a link, and so on), and the page picks the highest-ranked request the current tool cares about, once per frame. A link counts only for the tools that follow or edit links, so the stamp keeps its crosshair. A link's tooltip shows only with its hand, because it says where a click goes; a comment's tooltip shows with any tool beside that tool's cursor, because it is only information, as in Acrobat.

The cursor now tells the truth, a new tool declares what it wants instead of patching one pair of tools at a time, and a test fails if any page code sets the cursor directly again. PR 3 makes the click use the same answer, so the cursor and the click can't disagree at all.

## Why

This is PR 2 of three for the page pointer router, after #2685 (merged).

Bugs about "what the cursor registered" kept coming back in the page view, and each fix only covered one pair of tools. A review on 15 October found the cause: the page view had no single place that decided what was under the pointer. All pages are one egui widget, and about twenty tool modules each tested the pointer themselves and **set the cursor themselves**. egui keeps the last cursor set in a frame, so the order of the per-page chain decided the cursor, while a separate set of booleans decided who acts on a press. Nothing made the two agree, and the cursor promised one thing while a press did anoth…

author: alehel
body:

**Update Background**, **Update Watermark** and **Update Header and Footer** previewed the new marks on the page's thumbnail. That thumbnail still has the marks Update is about to replace:

- A background colour is previewed as a tint multiplied onto the page. Update the default pale yellow to light blue and the preview shows a muddy teal, which is the blue multiplied onto the yellow.

A blank sheet shows until the render arrives. If the page can't be prepared or rendered, the preview falls back to the thumbnail, as before. Add, and pages without marks of that kind, still use the thumbnail. The render is released when the dialog closes.

Other kinds of mark stay in the preview: Update Watermark still shows the background, and Update Background still shows the watermark.

title: fix(comments): delete or edit one reply from its own menu, keeping the thread
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

In the Comments panel a reply had no menu. The only **Delete** was on the comment card's **…**, and it deletes the whole thread (`DeleteAnnotation` on the comment, which takes every reply with it). A reviewer couldn't remove one wrong reply without losing the comment and everyone else's replies. Headlessly, `comment_delete` with a reply's id or page and index already deleted just that reply, so the app and the tools disagreed.

Now, on the selected card, **each reply has its own "…"** ("Options for this reply"), with:

- **Edit**: opens the panel's inline editor on that reply, in place of its text. Save changes the reply's `/Contents`, not the comment's.
- **Copy text**: copies the reply's text.
- **Delete**: deletes that reply alone. The comment, its other replies and its status stay, as one undo step ("Delete comment").

This follows Adobe's public help, which says to delete a reply from that reply's own options menu, and to edit a comment from its options menu ([Reply to comments](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/share-and-review-documents/manage-reviews/reply-comments.html), [Delete comments](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/share-and-review-documents/review-documents/delete-comments.html), [Edit comments](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/share-and-review-documents/review-documents/edit-comments.html)). I read no Acrobat files.

Decisions:

- **A reply with replies of its own takes them along**, with its pop-up and any status or checkmark set on it. That is what `pdfcraft_annot::delete_annotation` already does for a comment and what `comment_delete` already did for a reply. Keeping them would leave `/IRT`s pointing at nothing. One undo brings them all back.
- **A locked reply's Delete is greyed out** (the engine refuses it anyway). Edit stays available, because the Locked flag doesn't restrict the contents (ISO 32000-2 Table 167), as on the card.
- **Status and checkmark replies stay badges**, with no menu. A Replace Te…

title: audit: detect image covers over extractable text (#3117)
author: robertobulltech
body:
## What this changes

Pasting a black image over extractable text currently passes the faux-redaction audit. Image XObjects, stencil image masks and inline images now produce `covered-text` findings through the engine, `doc_audit_redactions` and `pdfcraft-cli audit`.

Refs #3117 **(image cases only)**. This leaves Type 3 covers and path-fill colour/clipping changes separate from #3155; the original issue has not been edited.

- Decode lossless DeviceGray/RGB/CMYK samples, Decode arrays and stencil polarity. Measure the union of painted sample regions, excluding unpainted stencil bits and nonopaque soft-mask samples.

- Retain each text run's showing operator to distinguish text painted before and after an image, even when those runs join one line. Preserve the existing contrast and translucent-cover policy.
- Return an incomplete-audit error for unreadable/ambiguous content, unsupported image analysis, unaudited form text combined with images, or exhausted image/decode/comparison bounds. A partial walk cannot become a clean result.

The issue's exact synthetic generator was run on unmodified main `86a4120a`: only page 6 was reported. After the fix, **pages 1, 2, 3 and 6** are reported by both CLI and automation. author: KyleKassen

title: M8: retain safe clipping when redacting painted vector paths
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

Applying a redaction to a partly covered vector clip-and-paint path removes its clip, making later artwork visible outside the original clipping region.
A fully covered path retains its original clipping geometry, and construction in earlier content streams can survive removal of its later painting operator.
This follows up the vector-path removal policy in #4577.

Removed clip-and-paint paths now leave an explicit empty clip, and construction tails in earlier streams are retired together while preserving preceding text and completed paths.
The empty clip conservatively hides subsequent drawing, including outside the marked area, until the previous graphics state is restored.

## How you verified it

Added meaningful docstrings to the touched helpers/regressions in response to CodeRabbit's documentation-coverage warning.

The real CLI reproduced the regression on main `833cd63c`: previously hidden green artwork becomes visible after mark/apply/save/reopen.

title: feat(web): page host mode, so a page can host PdfCraft in its own document (#4731)
author: helenkwok
body:
Closes #4731.

A page that loads the PdfCraft module into its own document can now opt into the host bridge with `data-host="page"` on `<canvas id="pdfcraft">`. The messages are the `?host=parent` ones, carried as non-bubbling DOM `CustomEvent`s on the canvas: PdfCraft dispatches `pdfcraft:ready`, `pdfcraft:save` (`name`, `saveAs`, `bytes`), `pdfcraft:dirty` and `pdfcraft:failed` with the message fields as `detail`, and the page dispatches `pdfcraft:open`.

**Design.** `host::Bridge` now holds a `Transport` (`Parent` or `Page`) with one `send`, and the two differ only in how an event goes out and how `open` comes in; save, dirty, ready and failure reporting are shared. `?host=parent` is checked first and behaves as before, including no bridge for an unframed page or a cross-origin parent (#2167). Only the exact attribute value `page` opts in (`page_host_enabled`, unit-tested). `packaging/web/README.md` documents it with a host-page example that adds its listeners before `init`. No `parity/` entry or automation tool: this is a second transport for the existing embedding surface, which has neither.

**Checks.** On Linux: fmt and clippy (`-D warnings`) pass; the workspace tests (no fail-fast) 5057 passed, 2 failed (`links::about_dialog_has_contributors_and_models_tabs` and `control::simplified_chinese_about_tabs_and_credit_controls`, which fail the same way on unchanged `main` in my container and pass on this branch when run alone). In a browser, with a release build of this branch: a page with `data-host="page"` received `pdfcraft:ready`, opened a six-page PDF it dispatched, and on Ctrl+S received `pdfcraft:save` (`saveAs: false`) with the document instead of a download.

title: perf(render): cache bounded derived image pixels
author: ishveet
body:
# perf(render): cache bounded derived image pixels

## What this changes

Repeated draws of the same large PDF image currently repeat decoding and resampling when the decoded source exceeds the existing 64 MiB source-cache limit. This adds a bounded cache of eligible final-size pixels in the Hayro renderer, using the existing decode, filtering and image-sampling behavior. It avoids retaining the large decoded source solely for reuse.

The cache is limited to ordinary device Gray/RGB raster XObjects with complete resource/settings identity. Masks, soft masks, stencils, inline images, JPX, transfer functions, Type3 rendering, patterns and knockout groups remain on the existing path. FIFO eviction is deterministic; retained pixel payload is capped at 16 MiB and bookkeeping at 512 entries per `RenderCache`.

This is a follow-up to [#2436](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2436), whose discussion left scaled-image caching for follow-up. Coordinate with [#2068](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2068), which is still migrating rendering to shared `craft-pdf`; if that migration lands first, port the backend change there rather than duplicating it in the app adapter.

## Measurements

Three fresh processes per binary/workload, three renders per process. Cold is the first render with an empty renderer cache; warm is the median of the six subsequent renders. Peak is median Windows process peak working set, sampled every 10 ms.

Reproduction argument sets (run each executable in three fresh processes; the example writes its fixture and first RGBA output under the process working directory):

title: M14: cargo xtask perf, performance budgets for large documents (gap 13)
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What

`cargo xtask perf` adds performance budgets for large documents (gap 13, `misc.performance-budgets`).

- It generates deterministic synthetic PDFs in a temporary directory (never committed): 10 pages, 1,000 pages, and 10,000 pages plus 64 MiB of filler (about 97 MiB).
- For each size it runs the release `pdfcraft-cli` once per phase, in its own process: open, scroll (render the first 10 pages at 72 dpi), edit (set a title, rotate a page), incremental save, full save.
- It records wall time and, on Linux, peak resident memory (`VmHWM`), keeps the fastest time and highest peak of `--runs` (default 3), writes JSON to `target/perf/results.json`, and compares against the committed `xtask/perf-budgets.json`. It exits non-zero when a budget is exceeded or a phase has no budget.
- `.github/workflows/perf.yml` runs it nightly, on demand, and on changes to the benchmark. It is **not** a required check.
- Updates `docs/gaps.md` gap 13, `docs/roadmap.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, the README command list and the `misc.performance-budgets` parity entry (now `partial`).

## Why

Gap 13 lists budgets as missing; memory and timing so far were one-off manual measurements. This makes them repeatable and checkable.

## How the numbers were chosen

Measured on a GitHub `ubuntu-latest` runner: the slowest `large` phase took 1.3 s and peaked at 347 MiB; open was 0.4 s at 145 MiB. Budgets are at least eight times the measured time and 2.5 to 4 times the measured peak (for example `large` saves: 20 s, 1000 MiB). They catch an order-of-magnitude regression such as an extra copy of the file, not a few percent. Times for a phase include the open, since each phase is its own process.

## Verification

- Unit tests: budget comparison (within, over time, over memory, unreadable peak, missing budget, unknown fields), the committed budgets covering every size and phase, generator determinism, page count (parsed with `lopdf`), filler size, and phase scripts.
- The Performance workflow passed and produ…

title: M7: an added text box or picture dragged onto another page moves there (#4655)
author: x-labb
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4655. Dragging an added text box (or an added picture) from one page and releasing it over another used to make it vanish: the release was read in the page the drag began on, so the item was saved far outside its own page (text dragged up from page 2 of a 400-pt page was saved at y=610).

Now, released over another page:

- the item is pasted onto that page, with its box where the pointer left it, kept whole inside the page's edges, and deleted from its own page, as **one undo step** ("Edit content"). Same-page moves, resizes and releases over the gap between pages behave as before.

One thing worth a look: a page below the item's own is not yet in `screen_xforms` when the item's page reads the pointer (pages are registered as they are painted), so while an item is moved `document_area` builds every visible page's frame first (`page_frames`) and passes it to `content_ui::page_input`.

title: M2: a non-symbolic TrueType font finds its glyphs by standard post names
author: exploded
body:
## What this changes

A non-symbolic TrueType font now finds its glyphs by name when its version 2.0 `post` table uses only standard Macintosh glyph names.

**Symptom.** PDFs printed from Chrome (`/Producer (PDFium)`) render every character as a box, while text extraction and search work. In the file that prompted this, the embedded `Helvetica` and `Helvetica-Bold` subsets are TrueType, `/Flags 32` (Nonsymbolic), `/Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding`.

**Cause.** Those subsets have:

- a single `cmap` subtable, platform 0 encoding 3 (Unicode BMP), and no (3, 1) or (1, 0) subtable, and
- a version 2.0 `post` table in which every glyph takes a standard Macintosh name (all indices < 258), so the table ends after the index array and has no string data.

`EmbeddedKind::map_code` looks codes up through (3, 1) and (1, 0), then falls back to the font's glyph names. read-fonts gives the empty string data as `None`, and `OpenTypeFontBlob::glyph_names` returned early on `None`, dropping all names, including standard ones that need no string data. With no route left, every code mapped to `.notdef`.

**Fix.** In `OpenTypeFontBlob::glyph_names`, missing string data reads as an empty list of custom names, so standard names still resolve. This is vendored `hayro-interpret` patch (67), marked `PdfCraft patch:` and listed in `vendor/README.md`.

**Relation to #2980.** #2980 also probes (0, x) Unicode `cmap` subtables on the non-symbolic path, which would fix these Chrome files by a different route. It doesn't touch `glyph_names`, so the two are independent. This PR covers fonts whose only route is the `post` names, for example a (0, 3) table that misses a code. The test is built so #2980's change doesn't make it pass on its own: its one `cmap` subtable maps nothing.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` (`pdfcraft-render`. The `blob.rs` hunk matches default rustfmt style, like the rest of the vendored file.)
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`cargo clippy -…
