title: M7: Remove watermark also removes watermarks other editors marked as artifacts (#4957)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4957 for removal: **Remove watermark** now also removes watermarks that other editors (Acrobat and the rest) wrote as artifacts, not only the ones PdfCraft added. Updating such a watermark and reading its settings back into the dialog are not part of this PR (see the limits).

A watermark written by another editor is page content marked `/Artifact <</Subtype /Watermark /Type /Pagination>> BDC … EMC` (ISO 32000-2 §14.8.2.2), with the properties inline or a name in the page's `/Properties` (the dictionary and its `/Subtype` may be indirect objects; names may use `#` escapes). Removing one cuts exactly those bytes out of the page content; everything else is copied as it was.

- **Edit ▸ Remove watermark** is offered for a document whose only watermark was made by another editor, and it stops being offered once it is removed (undo brings both back). The detection is cached per document revision and reset when content changes; a document over 5,000 pages, or with a page that can't be read, is offered the command without being checked.
- **Headless:** `doc_remove_marks` with `kind: "watermark"` goes through the same edit; its description says so.
- **Engine:** `pdfcraft_edit::remove_foreign_watermarks`, called by `Edit::RemoveMarks { kind: Watermark }` after PdfCraft's own marks, and `foreign_watermarks_present`.

### When a watermark is *not* cut out

Marked content does not save and restore the graphics state, so cutting one out can change how everything after it is drawn. A watermark is cut only when nothing it does can reach what follows:

- every state change inside it (`cm w J j M d ri i gs`, colour operators, `W W*`, `Tc Tw Tz TL Tf Tr Ts TD "`) sits inside its own `q … Q`;
- it does not sit inside, open or close a text object or a path that the content around it owns (cutting a `Tj` can move the text after it; `q … Q` restores the text matrices inside a text object, but not the current path, and this conservative scan does not rely on …

title: fix(forms): editing or sorting a list's items keeps its selected indices on the same items
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

A list box or combo box stores its selection twice: as values in `/V` and as positions in
`/Opt` in `/I` (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.4). `set_value` keeps both in step. But `set_props`,
which rewrites `/Opt` when the items are edited (Properties → Options, or `form_set_props
options`) or sorted ("Sort items"), left `/I` as it was. So `/I` pointed at whatever now
sits at the old positions.

Example: `/Opt [A B C]`, `/V [B C]`, `/I [1 2]`, then remove A. `/I` stays `[1 2]`, which now
means C and the new item D. A reader that uses `/I` to tell which items are selected then shows
the wrong ones.

After `/Opt` is rewritten, `set_props` now re-points the field's selection at the new list:

- `/I` lists the new positions of the selected values still offered, sorted and deduplicated.
  It is removed when none of them is offered any more. This is the same rule `set_value` uses.
- For a list box, `/TI` (the first visible row) follows the same `ListRows::top_showing` rule
  `set_value` uses: it stays put while the selected rows are still visible, otherwise it
  scrolls to them, clamped to the last full page. The field's `/TI` is updated, and every
  widget that carries its own scrolls by its own row and size (a widget's `/TI` is read first,
  and one past the end draws no options). `set_value` now scrolls such widgets the same way.

`/V` itself is not touched. A selected value that is no longer an item stays in `/V`, as it
does today.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: fix(forms): clearing a field's default leaves it with none, not its parent field's
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

`/DV`, a field's default value, is inheritable (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.1). A field under a parent
field takes the parent's `/DV` when it has none of its own.

Clearing a field's default in Properties, or through `form_set_props` with `"default": ""`,
removed the field's own `/DV`. For a field with a parent that has a `/DV`, that brought the
parent's back. Example: `address` has default `Main St` and its kid `address.city` has
default `Elm`. Clearing the city's default left `Main St` as the city's default, so Reset
Form filled the city with `Main St`.

`set_props` now checks whether an ancestor sets `/DV` (new `tree::ancestor_sets`, cycle-safe
and capped like `inherited`). If one does, clearing writes an empty default of the field's own
instead of removing the key: `/Off` for a check box or radio button, and `()` otherwise.
Without such an ancestor the key is removed, as before.

`/V` is inheritable too, and clearing a value had the same shape: a kid field cleared by
`set_value` or Reset Form lost its own `/V` and showed its parent's. When an ancestor sets `/V`,
clearing a text or choice field now writes an empty value of its own (`()`, which reads as no
value). Check boxes and radio buttons already write `/Off`.

author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

JPEG dimensions are checked before allocating a decoded raster.

title: M9: import certificates to trust from the Signatures panel
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

Before: a certificate could only be trusted from the app by pressing "Add to trusted certificates" on a signer the open document already showed. Importing a CA certificate or a `.p7b` bundle was possible only through the `sign_trust` automation tool. So a signature whose PDF embeds only the signer's certificate stayed *Unknown*. Many Brazilian (ICP-Brasil) signatures are like this.

After: the Signatures panel has **Import certificates…** next to Validate all.
- It reads `.cer`/`.crt`/`.pem`/`.der` files and `.p7b`/`.p7c` bundles, with the same parser `sign_trust` uses (#3561).
- Several files can be picked at once, because ITI publishes the ICP-Brasil CAs as a ZIP with one `.crt` per authority.
- A dialog lists each certificate once, with its issuer, validity, CA or end entity and full SHA-256 fingerprint, and a note to compare the fingerprint with the one the authority publishes.
- The files are read on a worker thread, and the dialog opens when the result arrives, so a large pick doesn't hold up the frame.
- Nothing is trusted until the user confirms. Certificate authorities start ticked and end-entity certificates don't, so confirming a whole bundle never trusts an individual signer by accident. Only the ticked certificates that aren't trusted yet are added, in one revalidation (none when nothing new is added), and certificates already trusted are shown disabled.
- Before anything is read: a path that isn't a regular file (folder, pipe, device), a file over 8 MiB, more than 2000 files, or more than 32 MiB in all is refused. Each read also stops at the per-file limit. One unreadable file refuses the whole import and names that file. Fingerprints are computed once when the list is read.

How: `CertImport` in `tools/sign_ui/panel.rs` holds what was read and what is ticked. `import_dialog` draws the dialog. `PdfCraftApp::trust_certificates` adds a batc…

title: M10: preserve unitless image pixel aspect ratios
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5008.

Create PDF and Add image previously treated unitless PNG pHYs and JPEG JFIF densities as square pixels.

For unitless density pairs, imports now preserve the declared pixel aspect by normalizing the denser axis to 72 dpi and expanding the other axis without resampling.

Proportional density pairs produce the same natural dimensions, and explicit DPI continues to override both axes.

JPEG EXIF correction retains unitless JFIF density and swaps its axes for quarter turns.

The JFIF scanner handles marker-fill bytes, validates segment boundaries, and stops at image data.

Page placement uses canonical PDF real serialization so a small positive dimension is not rounded to zero by fixed three-decimal formatting.
Natural Add image placement also accepts positive finite sub-point boxes and retains precise clipping and image transforms.
Image bounds returned by listing and copying retain their numeric precision for reuse as input.
Zero or non-finite sizes and non-finite composed transforms are refused before writing page content.

For TIFF, ResolutionUnit=1 uses paired positive X/Y rational densities as aspect-only metadata under the same normalization policy.

TIFF ratios below one are preserved; missing, malformed, zero, or zero-denominator pairs fall back to the existing square-pixel behavior.

TIFF inch and centimeter resolutions retain their absolute-size behavior, and explicit DPI remains the override.

Ordinary PNG and JPEG samples remain unchanged; ordinary JPEG bytes remain unchanged.

This policy interprets aspect-only metadata for natural placement and does not claim that it establishes physical size.

PNG viewers may ignore optional pHYs metadata, so this is an import-fidelity improvement rather than a mandatory conformance claim.

The existing JPEG orientation decode limit and separate ICC-profile limitation (#4669) remain.

- Reproduced the PNG/JPEG issue through a freshly built CLI before the fix: un…

title: M3: select text across pages (view.text-select)
author: TheSuperStew
body:
## What this changes

Text selection can now run across pages. Until now a selection could only belong to the page it started on: the drag extended it only while the pointer was over that page, and `Selection` held a single page (the #721 test even pinned "the selection stays on its own page (a selection can't span pages yet)").

A reading-order selection now goes from its anchor glyph to a head glyph on any page (`Span::Run` gains `head_page`). It covers the rest of the first page, the pages in between whole, and the last page up to the pointer.

- **Drag** onto another page extends the selection, including with the edge and wheel scrolling of #721/#1670. A quick drag that is already off its page (in the gap or on the next page) when egui reports the drag start now still starts the selection at the press. Before, it started nothing.
- **⇧-click** on another page extends the selection there, keeping its anchor.
- **Copy** puts each page's part on a line of its own, as Select All of the document does. It waits until every page the selection covers has its text read, so it never copies short. Those pages' text layers are queued and kept while the selection lasts.
- **Highlight, underline, strikethrough and Redact** (from the floating bar, from dragging with the tool, or from picking the tool after selecting) put one mark on each page, as a single `Edit::Batch` undo step named like one mark ("Add highlight"). That wording is already in `EDIT_LABELS`, so the catalogues translate it. A batch made only of added annotations refreshes just its pages, as a single added annotation does.
- **Add comment** and **Replace text** each sit on one page, so they are greyed out for a selection across pages.
- **Related fix:** the Redact and area-highlight box now starts only on the page the button went down on. A quick drag from one page's text that was already over the next page used to start a stray box there.

No new UI strings, no engine changes.
Fixes #5305

title: M10: Windows prints each page at the driver's resolution, not ~96 dpi
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

On Windows, PdfCraft hands the print-ready PDF to craft-print, which draws it with `Windows.Data.Pdf` into the XPS print API. At the pinned winprint revision (`5f80b9b`) each page was rendered at its size in DIPs, so pictures reached the paper at about **96 dpi**, whatever the source resolution or the driver's quality setting. A large scan fitted to small paper suffers most: an A0 drawing on A3 is about 35 % of its size, and every pixel the renderer drew is visible. That is why:

- "Microsoft Print to PDF" output is as jagged as the paper, so the loss happens before the driver,
- "Print as image" does not help: the sheet it builds goes through the same renderer.

This bumps `craft-print` to storytold/craft-libs#396, which pins winprint to storytold/winprint.rs#7 (upstream ArcticLampyrid/winprint.rs `a4da89b`, `5d49639`). Pages are now rendered at the resolution in the ticket's DEVMODE, and negative `DMRES_*` values are no longer passed as a raster DPI. No pdfcraft code changes. `Cargo.lock` loses winprint's pdfium build dependencies (reqwest, sigstore …), which #7 makes on-demand. It gains `roxmltree 0.21`, which craft-print moved to on its `main`.

Improves #4941 (96 → ~154 ppi for an A0 scan on A3). Full resolution is blocked by a per-image cap in `Windows.Data.Pdf`, tracked in #5131.
Also addresses #4446 and #4769, and the cause reported in #3514. Unrelated to #4800, where 1-bit stencils are nearest-sampled in PdfCraft's own renderer.

**Draft until the chain is merged:** winprint.rs#7, then craft-libs#396. After that, re-pin `craft-print` to the merge commit of #396.

title: perf(engine): export page images on worker threads (about 80% less wall time)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## Summary

Export ▸ Image (PNG, JPEG, TIFF) was spent almost entirely in the image encoders, one page after another on one thread. On the benchmark document, drawing all 55 pages at 150 dpi took about 0.34 s, while encoding them took 1.1 s (PNG), 2.0 s (JPEG) and 1.8 s (TIFF). The encoders belong to the `png`, `image` and `tiff` crates and were already tuned (#2425). This PR draws and encodes several pages at once instead, so the same files are written in about a fifth of the time. Every file is byte-identical to before.

## What changed

- `pdfcraft_engine::export::Exporter::images(pages, dpi, format, sink)` exports a list of pages and hands each file to `sink` in page order. Worker threads each get their own `PageRenderer` (the same pattern as `automation::pages::extract_parallel`), using one worker per core minus one, up to 8.
  - Memory stays bounded. A worker draws at most one page ahead of `sink`, and fewer workers run when 1 GiB can't hold that many of the largest page (raster, RGB copy and encoded file).
  - The first page error, or the first error `sink` returns, stops the export and is returned. Every page before it has been handed to `sink` and none after it, as before.
  - A panic while drawing a page becomes that page's error. A panicking `sink` stops the workers instead of leaving them waiting.
  - With one page, one core, or on wasm, it runs the existing per-page loop on the calling thread.
- `Exporter::image` and the workers share one `draw_image` helper, so both paths draw and encode a page the same way.
- Export ▸ Image (`export_ui.rs`) and the `doc_export_images` automation tool now call `images`. Progress still shows "Exporting… n of m", where n is now the number of pages written. In the tool, a write error is still returned as it was, not as a page error.
- `crates/engine/examples/export_bench.rs` is the benchmark.

## Benchmark

```
cargo run --release -p pdfcraft-engine --example export_bench -- FILE [DPI] [png|jpeg|tiff] [RUNS]
```

title: M10: Word, HTML and RTF export mark right-to-left text (#4653, direction half)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Addresses the **direction half** of #4653 (Arabic in PDF conversion). The other half, getting the characters out of the PDF in logical rather than visual order, is the text extraction's and is not changed here (see the limits).

The Word, HTML and RTF exporters had no right-to-left handling at all: an Arabic or Hebrew paragraph came out as left to right, so it was aligned and ordered as if it were English. Now a paragraph, heading, table cell or text box that reads right to left is marked so:

- **Which text:** its first strong character, by its **Unicode bidi class** (R and AL are right to left, L is left to right; digits, punctuation and spaces decide nothing), the same rule as HTML `dir="auto"`. So an LRM mark before Arabic makes it left to right, and the Hebrew maqaf, though it is punctuation, starts a right-to-left text. Across a paragraph's runs, the first strong character of the paragraph decides.
- **Word:** `<w:bidi/>` on the paragraph (after `w:pStyle`, before `w:spacing`, the order the schema requires), including table cells and positioned text boxes; on the runs `<w:rtl/>`, and the complex-script bold, italic and size (`bCs`, `iCs`, `szCs`) on every run.
- **HTML:** `dir="rtl"` on `p`, `h1`–`h6` and `td`. **RTF:** `\rtlpar` on paragraphs and cells.
- **Mixed text in one run** (the common single-run case) is cut into runs so that only text that is right to left for certain is marked `w:rtl`: the strong Arabic or Hebrew characters, the combining marks and joiners attached to them, and the spaces and punctuation strictly between two of them. Latin letters, digits and weak characters, and the punctuation and brackets at the edges, are left in runs **without** `w:rtl`: Word treats every neutral and weak character in a `w:rtl` run as right to left, which would reverse numbers and misplace paired brackets. A mark after skipped neutrals stays pending with them until a real strong character commits it.

New dependency edge: `pdfcraft-export`…

title: fix(platform): preserve visibility when saving files to network paths (#5001)
author: YusufMntm
body:
Closes #4593. Refs #5001, #6119, #6029

## What this changes

Preserves file visibility when overwriting files on Windows network shares (Samba/NAS) without disturbing archive bits or other attributes on local saves:
- **Server dot-file unhiding**: Samba and NAS shares automatically mark dot-prefixed staging files as hidden and persist that attribute through atomic renames (`std::fs::rename`), causing overwritten visible files to unexpectedly disappear (#4593, refs #5001, #6119, #6029).
- **Targeted attribute restoration**: On Windows, after the rename completes, we compare the saved file's `KEPT_ATTRIBUTES` (`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN | FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM`) against the replaced file's baseline. We restore attributes via `std::fs::set_permissions(path, keep.permissions())` *only* if the saved file's hidden or system bits differ from the original file's. Failed attribute restoration is logged at `warn` level.
- **Archive bit preservation on local files**: On local NTFS/FAT filesystems where attributes already match, `set_permissions` is skipped entirely. This guarantees the newly written file retains the system-assigned Archive bit (`0x20`), ensuring incremental backup utilities (`robocopy /M`, `xcopy /M`) detect the modification, while avoiding leaking stale offline or index flags.
- **New file semantics**: When saving a new file (`keep` is `None`), no prior baseline attributes exist and server defaults apply.

## How you verified it

- [x] cargo fmt --check
- [x] clippy with -D warnings on the crates changed (`cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-platform -- -D warnings` clean)
- [x] Unit & integration tests pass on `pdfcraft-platform`: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-platform --lib staging::` passes (all 11 tests pass, including `a_replaced_file_restores_attributes_if_server_hides_staging_file` and `a_replaced_local_file_keeps_archive_bit_intact`)

title: M3: a file named with open parameters opens at their destination (#3425)
author: hazeliscoding
body:
## What this changes

Help systems start a PDF reader with open parameters after the file name, such as `manual.pdf#nameddest=Intro` or `manual.pdf#page=12`. PdfCraft read the whole string as the file name and failed with "os error 2" (#3425). A path that names no file, but whose part before a `#` does, now opens that file at the named destination or page:

- at launch,
- when another launch hands the file to the running app, at the place asked for last if it's asked twice before it has opened,
- and in its tab when the file is already open.

`page` (1-based) and `nameddest` are read, plus a bare `#Intro` as a destination name, as browsers' PDF viewers do. Other parameters (`zoom`, `view`, `pagemode`, `search`…) are ignored, and the file still opens. A path that names a file is never split, so a `#` in a real file or folder name still works.

The named destination is looked up in the target's `/Names /Dests` tree or catalog `/Dests` (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.4). In the running app the lookup runs off the UI thread, because a large manual's name tree takes a noticeable moment to read. The same lookup now applies a GoToR link's named destination, in the app and in `link_open`, instead of opening the file at its default view with a warning.

Headlessly, `doc_open` reads the same open parameters, through the parser in `pdfcraft_engine::open_parameters` that the app uses. It reports the destination the way `link_open` does.

Fixes #3425

title: fix(ui): prevent mouse wheel scrolling from triggering kinetic fling jumps (#4917)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Closes #4917.

Prevents discrete mouse wheel scrolling from triggering unexpected kinetic fling momentum and animation jumping:
- In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas/fling.rs`, restricts fling momentum calculation exclusively to genuine touchpad gestures that began with `TouchPhase::Start` and continuous `MouseWheelUnit::Point` input. Movement without a preceding `TouchPhase::Start` is ignored, and any discrete wheel step (`MouseWheelUnit::Line` / `MouseWheelUnit::Page`) immediately stops and resets gesture tracking.
- In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, whenever discrete wheel steps occur in a frame (`line_base`, `boost_extra`, `input.line`, or `has_page`), any in-progress fling is halted and its gesture state reset, preventing kinetic drift from compounding with mouse wheel notches. Also resets fling state when resetting coarse viewport state.
- Added headless integration tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/canvas.rs` simulating rapid discrete wheel scrolling and active glide interruption.
- Added unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas/fling.rs` ensuring discrete wheel notches and unstarted gestures never glide.

title: M10: Recognize text no longer clips the first and last letters of a line
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

Recognize text dropped the first and last letters of many lines on 300 dpi scans: "The" came out as "he", "and" as "an", and closing full stops went missing. On clean synthetic pages that was about 4 % of the words, while Tesseract and PaddleOCR read the same pages without errors.

**Cause.** ocrs grows each detected word box by a fixed 3 pixels before it cuts the line image out for recognition. At 300 dpi that is less than one pixel of its 800 x 600 detection input, so the line images clip the edge letters. Because the margin is fixed in pixels, it gets worse as the resolution rises:

| synthetic pages | 150 dpi | 200 dpi | 300 dpi | 400 dpi |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| word errors before (text A / B) | 0.7 / 1.9 % | 0.8 / 3.1 % | 4.3 / 4.0 % | 8.4 / 6.9 % |
| word errors after | 0.1 / 0.4 % | 0.1 / 0.2 % | 0.05 / 0.2 % | 0.3 / 1.2 % |

**Fix (`pdfcraft-ocr`).**
- After `find_text_lines`, each line is widened by fractions of its median word height: 0.12 above and below every word, and 0.1 before the first and after the last word (0.15 at first; that cost a noisy form label at 150 dpi, see the comments). Line finding itself is unchanged; widening before line finding merged lines.
- The recognised word boxes are clipped back to the line's original box, so `text_layer` sizes the invisible text exactly as before.
- Boxes lying on their side (up axis horizontal) are handled.

The factors come from a sweep over two texts at 150, 200, 300 and 400 dpi. The neighbouring values (0.12–0.18 across, 0.05–0.15 along) all land at 0.30–0.41 % word errors, so this is a plateau and not a lucky point. Mean over the 8 sets: character errors 0.59 % → 0.06 %, word errors 3.78 % → 0.30 %.

title: fix(redact): an image too large to count its pixels is removed, not a panic
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

Redaction clears the covered pixels of an image in place when it can decode it (`image::decode_and_clear`). Before decoding, it refuses images over `MAX_PIXELS` with `(w as u64) * (h as u64) > MAX_PIXELS`. `/Width` and `/Height` come straight from the file as `i64`, so two dimensions of 2^32 or more make that product overflow `u64`. In a debug or test build that panics with `attempt to multiply with overflow` at `crates/redact/src/image.rs:64`, reached from `apply` through the content interpreter's `Do` for any image a redaction mark overlaps. Release builds wrap instead, and the `checked_mul` chain further down then refuses the image, so this is a debug-only panic, not a release crash.

The size check now uses `checked_mul`, and an overflowing product counts as too large. The image is then removed whole, which is what release already did. Images within `MAX_PIXELS` are cleared exactly as before.

title: fix(create): a mask wide where its image is tall is scaled without a huge buffer
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

When an image is exported (Export Images, Save Image As, Copy Image, and the automation `extract_images` tool), a soft mask or stencil `/Mask` of a different size is scaled to the image with `image::imageops::resize` in `gray_plane` (`crates/create/src/extract.rs`). `resize` scales the height first, into an `Rgba32F` buffer of the mask's width × the image's height, at 16 bytes a pixel. `size` caps the mask and the image at `MAX_PIXELS` each, but not that product. A mask that is wide where its image is tall makes the product huge: a 1 × 1,000,000 image with a 1,000,000 × 1 mask asks for 16 TB, the allocation fails, and the process aborts (`memory allocation of 16000000000000 bytes failed`, SIGABRT). That happens in release builds too, and `catch_unwind` cannot catch it. The PDF needs about 2 MB of samples, less once compressed.

When the mask's width × the image's height is over `MAX_PIXELS`, the mask is now scaled to the image's width first and then to its height. The two buffers are then the mask's own size and the image's own size, both at most `MAX_PIXELS`. Every mask under that bound is scaled exactly as before.

Found by a static read of the create crate, then reproduced in a debug build.

title: fix(render): read a precomposed Latin ligature as its own letters in Find
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4469 (the ligature-matching half of it; the hyphen-at-line-end
half is a separate, independent problem in the same file).

A font's ToUnicode CMap, or the Adobe Glyph List fallback for a glyph
literally named `fi`, can give one glyph the precomposed ligature
scalar (`U+FB00`–`U+FB06`) instead of decomposing it into separate
letters itself — the Adobe Glyph List maps the glyph name `fi` to
`U+FB01` (`crates/fonts/src/encodings.rs:163`), which is correct per
spec for that one glyph. `Find` compared characters one for one, so a
query like `office` never matched a page whose `fi` glyph carries
`U+FB01`, even though the page visibly draws "office".

`crates/render/src/text/search.rs` expands the eight Latin ligature
scalars into their own letters, on both the page's characters and the
query, before the literal match runs. This is the one place `Find`,
the `text_find` automation tool and Search & Redact's word search
(`redact_mark` with `find`/`words`) all go through, so all three are
fixed together.

Out of scope: the hyphen-divided-word half of #4469 (`exam-` / `ple`
across a line break), which the issue's own first comment asks to be
tracked separately from this one.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render` — 313 unit tests + 4 search
  integration tests, including the existing 2000-case differential
  fuzz test (`search_matches_reference_for_unicode_gaps_limits_and_word_boundaries`)
  that compares `find` against an independent reference implementation
  — unaffected, since its alphabet uses the already-decomposed `"ffi"`
  string, not the precomposed scalar.
- Proved the regression first: reverted the `search.rs` change,
  confirmed the new test (`a_precomposed_ligature_matches_its_separate_letters`)
  fails with `left: [] right: [0..5]`, then restored the fix and

title: M10, #2285: opt-in GPU text recognition (crates/ml)
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

This adds opt-in GPU text recognition for #2285. Nothing changes unless `PDFCRAFT_OCR_GPU=1` is set.

**This branch builds on #5058** (line padding). Its first commit is that PR; please merge #5058 first. Only the second commit is new here.

- **New `pdfcraft-ml` (L3, the slot `xtask/src/layers.rs` already reserves).** With feature `gpu` (native only) it runs both ocrs models in wgpu compute shaders, read from the same `.onnx` files rten loads:
  - a convolutional graph executor (implicit-GEMM, depthwise and single-channel convolutions, ConvTranspose, pooling, Slice, Concat),
  - the bidirectional GRU in one dispatch per layer for all lines, each line at its own length,
  - the detector's grey/resize/threshold steps on the GPU.

  Without the feature the crate is empty.
- **`pdfcraft-ocr` gets a `gpu` feature**, inside the ocrs engine (`Ocr` in `ocrs.rs`, behind `OcrsRecognizer`, since #977), so merging with other engines and preprocessing work as they do on the CPU. The desktop app and CLI enable it through `pdfcraft-engine/ocr-gpu`. The GPU is used only if all of these hold:
  - `PDFCRAFT_OCR_GPU=1` is set,
  - the models are ONNX,
  - a **self-check against rten** at load passes: a synthetic page and line, mask and best classes compared.

  Any GPU error sends that call, and every later one, to the CPU. `Ocr::backend()` says where recognition runs and why the GPU is not used.
- **The GPU path keeps the CPU pipeline's steps.** ocrs prepares the image and finds the lines, the lines are padded as in #5058, and ocrs cuts the line images. Only the two model runs move to the GPU, and characters get their boxes from their CTC steps as ocrs places them.

## Layering — please decide

`xtask layers` lists `wgpu*` as a UI crate (L7+). This PR adds a narrow exemption, `GPU_COMPUTE = ["ml"]`: only `ml`, only `wgpu`, compute only (no window or surface). A test pins that `ml` still may not use egui/winit/eframe and that no other crate below L7 may use wgpu…

title: M12: XFA date pictures read a two-digit year with the century split of 30
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA picture clauses read a two-digit year (`YY`) with a century split of 30 by default. The XFA 3.3 specification, chapter 26 (Picture Clause Reference), p. 1171, gives a "century split option ... set by default to 30". PdfCraft split at 50, so `30` to `49` came out 100 years late (`450101` read as 2045-01-01, not 1945-01-01). This came up in review of #4511 and #4522, but the window predates both, so it gets its own PR.

Both XFA picture readers now use the spec's default (`CENTURY_SPLIT = 30`): `00` to `29` are 2000 to 2029, and `30` to `99` are 1930 to 1999.
- `crates/xfa/src/data/dates.rs` `pattern_to_iso`: the datasets reader and writer, scripts' `rawValue` and typed edit-picture alternatives. Because `iso_to_data` only writes a date in a two-digit data picture when it reads back unchanged, that picture now holds 1930 to 2029. 2030 and 1929 stay ISO, where 2050 and 1949 did before.
- `crates/js/src/formcalc/dates.rs` `parse_date`: FormCalc's `Date2Num` and `Parse` with a `YY` picture.

The other two-digit-year readers keep 1950 to 2049, because they follow other specifications:
- `crates/forms/src/af/format.rs` and `crates/js/src/format.rs` (`AFDate_*`, `util.scand`/`printd`) follow the AcroForm JavaScript API, not XFA picture clauses.
- `crates/sign/src/der.rs` reads UTCTime, where RFC 5280 §4.1.2.5.1 fixes 1950 to 2049.

## How you verified it

The local gate (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, `cargo xtask parity`) passes on `pdfcraft-xfa` and `pdfcraft-js`.

New and updated tests, at the boundaries `29`, `30`, `49` and `50`:
- `xfa::tests::a_two_digit_year_splits_its_century_at_30` covers `pattern_to_iso` and `data_to_iso` with `yymmdd`.
- `xfa::tests::a_date_its_data_picture_cant_hold_is_written_as_iso` now pins 1930 to 2029 as written in `yymmdd` and 2030, 1929 and 2050 as kept in ISO. Before, it pinned 2050 and 1949.

title: fix(edit): Office export respects a form's /BBox and a page's re/W/n clip
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What this changes

Addresses the Office-export part of #3503, left open by #3628.

A form XObject's `/BBox` clips its content (ISO 32000-2, the form
dictionary's `BBox` entry: "these boundaries shall be used to clip the
form XObject"), and the renderer already honours it. Export to
Word/HTML/PowerPoint/RTF reads a page's text through
`reading_lines`/`reading_blocks` (`crates/edit/src/text/lines.rs`),
which walks form XObjects with no notion of a clip at all, so text a
form's `/BBox` clips away -- never drawn -- was still read and
exported.

Text drawn outside the clips in force is now left out of reading, as the renderer leaves it out of the picture. Four commits:

1. A form's own `/BBox`: `form_call` resolves it (exactly four finite numbers, or no bound), in page space under the form's matrix.
2. A page's own `re ... W`/`W* ... n` clip, tracked in the text interpreter's graphics state (`Ts`), so `q`/`Q` save and restore it.
3. From review: the clip in force is a convex **region**, not a bounding box. It is made of a rectangle's corners under its matrix, so a turned clip keeps its shape. Clips in force **intersect** (Sutherland-Hodgman): a form's `/BBox` is intersected into the clip it inherits at its `Do`. Its content starts with a stack of its own, so a `Q` inside cannot lift that clip. This replaces the earlier per-form stack. A run is read when the separating-axis test finds no gap between its box and the region. A region past 32 corners becomes its bounding box, which holds all it held, so a stream that sets clip after clip stays bounded.
4. From the second review: a clip is the **union** of its parts, one region per `re` of its path, and clips intersect part by part. A path of more than 16 rectangles keeps the box around them. Whether a region has area is judged against the square of its perimeter, so the test is the same at any scale, and it is measured from its first corner, so it keeps its precision far from the origin. A finite clip of no area, or an in…

title: sign: refuse to sign a document certified with no changes allowed

title: fix(render): cap a JPEG 2000 codestream's SIZ size at 2^28 pixels (#5078)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

A JPEG 2000 image is now refused when its codestream's SIZ marker declares more than 2^28 pixels, the same cap `image_size_ok` applies to `/Width` x `/Height`. The check runs in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/filter/jpx.rs` on the header read at full resolution, before `Image::decode` (which makes the infallible allocation), and fails the same way as other undecodable images. It uses the full-resolution size because a `target_resolution` shrinks the reported `width()`/`height()` but each tile's coefficient buffers are still allocated at full size (review on this PR); the header is then re-read at the target resolution only when one is set. Logged as hayro-syntax patch (36) in `vendor/README.md` (main has since taken 29-35).

Fixes #5078

## How you verified it

`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean on `pdfcraft-render` (which compiles the vendored hayro-syntax). Regression tests in `jpx.rs`'s `tests` module, adopted from the reviewers' patches:

- `a_codestream_over_the_pixel_cap_is_refused` (croquete1): a `/Width 1 /Height 1` image whose single-tile codestream declares 65536 x 65536 (2^32 pixels) returns `None` from `jpx::decode`, with and without a 1x1 target resolution (the target case has four decomposition levels, so the target really shrinks the reported size to 4096 x 4096, under the cap); the same builder at 1x1 decodes, so the `None` is the cap, not a parse error.

title: fix(js): follow every reading of a script in the nesting guard, so a regex can't put it out of phase (#5079)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

The nesting guard that keeps hostile scripts from overflowing the stack in boa's parser could be put out of phase, and this replaces it with one that can't be. boa parses by recursive descent with no depth limit of its own (boa_parser 0.22 has none to turn on), and a stack overflow aborts the process, since `catch_unwind` can't catch it.

**The problem.** `refuse()` scanned bytes and guessed where strings begin. A quote inside a regular expression put it out of phase with the real strings. The first version of this PR counted opening brackets inside skipped text, which closed the reported `/'/` reproduction. It still let closing brackets inside *real* strings count as code. `x=` followed by 5,000 lines of `(/"/,"))))",` nests 5,000 deep in 65 KB (under the 256 KiB limit), while that scan never went past depth 1. The same works with `'`, and with template literals, which the scan didn't read at all.

**The fix.** The guard now lives in `crates/js/src/nesting.rs`.
- **It doesn't guess.** Whether a `/` is a division or starts a regular expression depends on where the parser is: boa's parser, not its lexer, sets that. So the scan follows every reading at once. At each `/` that isn't a comment, it splits into a division reading and a regular-expression reading, and counts nesting on each. boa's reading is always one of them, so the deepest count is at least boa's real depth. That makes it a sound bound, not a mitigation for one reproduction.
- **It drops readings boa rejects,** at the byte where boa stops with a syntax error: a string or regular expression running into a line break, or a regular expression whose groups don't match. boa runs `regress::try_parse` on each literal as it lexes it. This keeps ordinary divisions such as `Math.round(a / b * 100) / 100` from leaving stray readings that add up to false depth.
- **It reads the rest of the lexical grammar that changes what's code:** strings with escapes and line continuations, comments, templat…

title: fix(crypt, engine): refuse page extraction when Protect allows any change except extracting pages (#5081)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Adds `Permissions::extract_pages()`: `assemble()` **and** copying (bit 5), as #5081 asks, since extracted pages carry their text and graphics into a file without the source's protection. It is used for Extract, Split, Split by size and every Combine/Insert/Replace/paste source check (`sources::source_document`). Changes within the document (rotate, delete, move, insert) keep `assemble()`.

Since this PR was opened, #6309 made `assemble()` revision-aware on `main`: bit 11 alone at revision 3 and later, bit 4 at revision 2. That already refuses "Any except extracting pages" at revision 3+. This PR builds on it:

- At revision 2, `assemble()` reads bit 4, which "Any except extracting pages" sets, so such a file could still be extracted and split into unprotected copies. Requiring copying closes that.
- New `Needs::PageExtraction` greys out Extract and Split up front. It reuses the existing security-refusal string, so no catalogue changes.
- `Document::allows_page_extraction()`, and an `extract_pages` key in the automation security JSON.
- `page_extract` with `separate: true` extracts and writes one page at a time (`extract_separate`), so it no longer buffers every page. The first page is extracted before `out_dir` is created, so a refused extraction leaves no empty directory. If a later page fails, the files this call wrote are removed, and `out_dir` too if this call created it (review on this PR).
- Insert Pages checks a PDF through the same path as the insert itself: new `Session::insert_source(dest, name, bytes)`, which the UI's insert now calls (review on this PR).

title: fix(cos): cap the total entries a materialized xref-stream chain merges (#5082)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

`read_xref_chain_materialized` in `crates/cos/src/document/reader.rs` keeps a running total of the rows it merges across the cross-reference chain. Past `MAX_XREF_OBJECTS` (8,388,607) it returns `CosError::Syntax` ("cross-reference chain lists more than 8388607 entries"). The open path then rebuilds the index from object headers and logs the repair, as it already does when a single section decodes past that cap. Before this, the per-section cap and the 10,000-section chain limit multiplied, so the merged map had no overall bound.

Each section adds `sect.len() + odd.len()`: its entries plus the rows it set aside, including those from a hybrid `/XRefStm`. Set-aside rows are kept for the whole chain, and a section can set aside nearly everything it lists. The count is of rows merged, not the map's size, because a chain that relists the same objects costs as much to merge. A section's rows never outnumber what the compact reader counts for it, and that reader stops at 2,000,000 rows. So no chain the compact reader accepts is refused here.

The limit itself lives in `read_xref_chain_materialized_with_limit` (`pub(super)`). The existing entry point, `read_xref_chain_materialized`, calls it with `MAX_XREF_OBJECTS`, so tests can reach the limit in a few rows. Both functions have doc comments.

Fixes #5082

## How you verified it

Three regression tests in `crates/cos/src/document/tests.rs`. The two small-limit tests were suggested by @Harrison-Booth in review.

1. `a_cross_reference_chain_past_the_total_cap_is_refused_and_the_file_reconstructed` runs end to end at the production cap. It builds a synthetic file:
   - a catalog, a page tree with one page, and a chain of three cross-reference streams;
   - the newest stream locates objects 0 to 6;
   - two older Flate-compressed streams each list 4,200,000 rows (`/W [1 0 0]`, disjoint `/Index` ranges). Each is half the per-section cap and too large for the compact reader. Their rows are in use at offset …

title: fix(render): bound the objects lopdf's fallback parses from object streams and arrays (#5083)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

lopdf's fallback loader (used by `inspect` when the lazy reader fails, and always by `attachment_data`) parsed every object stream eagerly, capping only decoded bytes. A stream of `0 0 0 …` inside the 256 MiB limit built ~120M `Object`s (10+ GB) and aborted. This bounds what it builds:

- **Per top-level object:** at most 4,194,304 objects (`parser::MAX_OBJECT_NODES`, the same as cos's `MAX_NODES`), counting every array element and dictionary value at any depth. One budget is threaded through `array` / `_dictionary` / `_direct_object`. An object is charged once it is built, so failed `alt` branches cost nothing, and an exhausted budget is a nom `Failure`.
- **Per object stream:** at most 1,000,000 index entries (cos's `/N` clamp), and the index list is no longer allocated from the whole block.
- **Per load:** at most 8,388,608 objects across all object streams, in an atomic `NodeBudget` shared by rayon workers. A member reserves up to its own byte length (every object takes at least one byte) and refunds what it doesn't use, so parallel members can't hold the budget between them. Once the budget is spent, the remaining members are skipped with a warning.
- **`convert` in `crates/render/src/structure.rs`:** the depth limit is now 128, one level per array or dictionary, matching cos's parser. Before, it was 100 with two levels per dictionary, so ~51 nested dictionaries alone forced the lopdf fallback.

Logged as lopdf patch (7) in `vendor/README.md`.

Fixes #5083

## How you verified it

`cargo fmt --check` on `pdfcraft-render` and `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings` (which compiles the vendored lopdf). Regression tests in `crates/render/src/inspect/tests.rs`, where lopdf patches are tested in-tree (the vendored lopdf's own tests need its missing `assets/example.pdf`):

title: M3: text selected on a page becomes the primary selection on Linux (#4821)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4821.

On Linux and the BSDs, text selected on a page now becomes the **primary selection**, so a middle click in another application pastes it. This is the X11 convention, and Wayland's `primary-selection` protocol carries the same behaviour.

- The text is written once the page selection has held still for a frame, so a drag doesn't write it on every frame. If the frame after a change isn't otherwise drawn, the app asks for a repaint so the selection still settles.
- egui only writes the regular clipboard, so this goes through `arboard` (`LinuxClipboardKind::Primary`). arboard uses the compositor's data-control protocol where it is offered (niri, sway, KDE…) and X11 otherwise, Xwayland included. `wayland-data-control` was already enabled through egui-winit; `crates/ui-egui/Cargo.toml` now declares it explicitly for these targets. `Cargo.lock` is unchanged.
- A `primary-selection` worker thread owns the clipboard. Connecting and setting both make round trips to the compositor or X server, so they never run on a frame. The thread takes the newest pending text from a single replaceable slot, so a stalled display holds at most one string. Owning the clipboard also keeps the selection served on X11.
- The regular clipboard is untouched; Ctrl+C works as before.
- Whole-document Select All (continuous scrolling, #2639) is not read just for this: its pages are read only when copied.
- A document whose security refuses copying (Table 22, bit 5) gives no primary selection, and says nothing about it, because the user only selected text.
- When the selection clears, the last text stays in the primary selection, as on X11. Selecting the same text again takes the primary selection back from whichever application took it in the meantime, even after a one-frame clear.
- On macOS, Windows, Android and the web build, nothing changes.

Not part of this: middle-click paste *into* PdfCraft's own text fields, and selections inside Edit text.

On the supported single-style justification path, spaces typed at the start of a stretched row (any row but the last) are kept as an indent. Before, they were dropped on save. The row still ends at the margin, reads back with its indent, and survives a second edit.

Upstream restrictions remain in place: selected-row alignment of existing paragraphs and explicit justification of mixed-style existing paragraphs are refused before mutation. This PR does not add persistence of whole-paragraph justification intent across reopening; a later text-only edit preserves the source spacing rather than justifying again.

**Writing a stretched row** (`crates/edit/src/text/rewrite.rs`)
- The leading spaces are drawn at their own width, in the row's text object and under the row's `Tw`. A `TJ` adjustment then takes back the word spacing `Tw` added to them.
- The indent and the words go out as one `TJ` (`one_show`), for example `18.32 Tw [(    ) 6106.67 (Pack my box…)] TJ`. Two things depend on this:
  - The reader only keeps the spaces when they share one text-showing operator with the words. A spaces-only `Tj` before the words is dropped.
  - The row's line keeps the one word spacing it is stretched with. Drawing the indent at `0 Tw` first would make the reopened row read as `0 Tw`. That is approach 2 in the issue, and it ended with `200 Tz` on the next edit.
- The words are stretched over the width less the indent. The row starts at the paragraph's left edge, its first word starts after the indent, and its last word ends at the margin.
- Spaces after a stretched row's last word are still left out, as before.

**Editing it again through the styled path** (`crates/edit/src/text_regions/styled.rs`)
- Spaces drawn as a natural-width indent are measured and drawn without word spacing (`indent_len`, `same_run`, `row_widths`). An indent originally drawn with its words’ spacing keeps that spacing instead. Before, each one took the source row's stretch…

title: fix(forms): name tree nodes sharing one long /Kids array no longer exhaust memory
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

`document_scripts_named` (`crates/forms/src/scripting.rs`) walks the document's JavaScript name tree with a stack. It visits each node object once and stops after 10,000 visits, but it queues every node's whole `/Kids` array, and the seen check only skips repeated entries once they are popped. Nodes that share one long `/Kids` array, which a well-formed tree never does, each queue all of it again. 10,000 nodes sharing an array of 210,000 entries ask for about two billion queued `Object`s. The process runs out of memory and is killed, or aborts when the allocation fails, so the engine's `guard` cannot catch it.

The walk runs whenever a `JsRunner` is built (a form edit that runs scripts, or a script action), for the Document JavaScripts list in the UI, and for the `js_document_scripts` automation tool.

The walk now queues only kid references (`/Kids` holds indirect references, ISO 32000-2 §7.9.6), each the first time it is listed, so the stack never holds a copy of a direct object or a repeat. Nodes are told apart by object number, the way `Document::get` finds them, so a node listed as `4 0 R`, `4 1 R` and so on is still read once. It counts every `/Kids` entry it reads; past `MAX_QUEUED_KIDS` (2^20) it reads no more kids, but still reads the nodes already queued. Kids are read in the order listed.

Nodes can share a `/Names` array the same way. 9,999 nodes sharing one that names 1,000 scripts returned ten million scripts and used 1.3 GB; naming 10,000, the process was killed at a 1.5 GB memory limit. Each indirect `/Names` array is now read once (10,000 scripts in 9 ms for the second case). `/Kids` and `/Names` arrays are read in place, so a direct one is not copied. Well-formed trees under the bound give the same scripts as before.

Found by a static read of the forms crate, then reproduced in a debug build.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms -j 2`: 190 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms -j 2 --all-targe…

title: fix(xfa): AcroForm field walks read each field once and bound what they queue
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

Two walks over the AcroForm field tree in the XFA crate trust `/Kids` to form a tree. A malformed file can list a field more than once, or list a field among its own kids, and each walk then does far more work than the file's size.

`fields_by_som` (`script.rs`), called from `strip.rs` and from the engine whenever it maps XFA fields to SOM paths, recurses into every `/Kids` entry up to `MAX_DEPTH` (64) with no seen set. A field whose `/Kids` lists itself twice is walked once per path to it, 2^64 times at the depth limit, so the call never returns. The `out.len()` cap never stops it, because the repeated field adds no new entry. The walk now reads each field once, telling fields apart by object number as `Document::get` does (`5 0 R` and `5 1 R` are one field). It counts every `/Fields` and `/Kids` entry it looks at, references or not, against `MAX_FIELD_STEPS` (2^20), so fields sharing one long `/Kids` array also stay bounded: counting only references, 5,000 fields sharing an array of a million `null`s took 20 s, and the walk now stops after 2^20 entries (5 ms). Once the budget is spent, every loop stops, and each `/Kids` array is read in place instead of copied at every level.

`existing_fields` (`pdf.rs`), run by `write_form` when laying out an XFA form, counts fields as it pops them but queues each field's whole `/Kids` array first. The fields down one branch each queue the whole array again, at up to `MAX_FIELD_DEPTH` (32) levels, so a shared array of a million entries puts about 32 million entries (each with a copy of its parent's full name) on the stack. Fields are now queued as references, each the first time its object number is listed, so a repeat takes no room; at most `MAX_FIELDS_SEARCHED` (20,000) are ever queued, and at most `MAX_KIDS_READ` (2^20) `/Fields` and `/Kids` entries are read in all while queuing. The search of a signed field's kids for its appearance has its own `MAX_KIDS_READ` budget, so it can never leave a field's kid…

author: mtlcl410

## What this changes

Empty table rows are now as tall as the form designs them, not almost twice as tall, so tables no longer spill onto extra pages.

title: M10: Enhance scanned file cleans scanned pages in place
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

Scan & OCR ▸ **Enhance scanned file** (Acrobat's Enhance ▸ Scanned document) now works. Until now the clean-up filters only existed for camera photos. It has three filters, each its own switch:

- **Background removal**, level 0–100. This is the camera clean-up's level: the paper's illumination is evened out per channel, so a grey, yellowed or unevenly lit background turns white. Then the contrast is raised. Colour ink stays colour.
- **Edge shadow removal**, new. Inside the outer fifth of each side, every column and row is lightened to the brightest paper of that band. That removes book gutters and copier borders, which the camera's coarse block grid misses. A black scanner border (more than 3× darker than the paper) is left alone.
- **Despeckle**: dark pixels with at most one dark neighbour turn white. It works on grey, RGB and 1-bit scans.

**In place, not re-rendered.** The camera tool replaces the page with a picture. That would lose a scan's invisible OCR text, comments and links, so this tool doesn't do it. Instead:

- **Which images get cleaned.** A page counts as a scan when its pictures cover at least half of it. This is the same rule as `scan_fields::is_scan`, which is now shared through `scan_images`. The pictures that each cover at least a tenth of the page get cleaned.
- **How they are rewritten.** Each one is decoded, cleaned and written back into **its own image object**, at the same size and in the same colour space:
  - a JPEG stays a JPEG (quality 90)
  - other grey/RGB images are stored losslessly (Flate)
  - a 1-bit image stays 1-bit, with its decode array
  - every other dictionary entry is kept (`/SMask`, `/Interpolate`, `/Intent`, …)
- **Shared images** are cleaned once, and their pages are reported.
- **Everything else on the page is untouched**: content streams, text layer, annotations and fonts. The tests compare these objects before and after.
- **Images that are not cleaned are reported, never skipped silently**, ea…

title: M10: Recognize text can downsample the scan under the text (Searchable Image)
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

Recognize Text gets Acrobat's second searchable-image output, **Searchable Image** (downsampled), next to **Searchable Image (Exact)** (parity `ocr.ocr-downsample`, planned → shipped; `ocr.searchable-image` notes updated).

After recognition, in the **same undo step** as the text layer ("Recognize text"), the image XObjects drawn on the pages that were read are resampled down to the *Downsample to* resolution when their effective resolution is more than 5% above it:

- The resolution is the **smallest over every use in the document** (through forms), so an image also drawn larger on another page is measured there and never made too coarse.
- **In place**: same object number, same placement matrix, so the invisible OCR text (in page space) lines up exactly as over the exact image (the test compares glyph boxes of both).
- **Kind kept**: colour space, `/Decode`, `/SMask`/`/Mask` streams (both map onto the unit square whatever their size, ISO 32000-2 §8.9.6.3, §11.6.5.3), `/Interpolate` etc. 8-bit grey/RGB JPEG stays JPEG (q 85), other 8-bit becomes Flate; **1-bit images and image masks stay 1-bit and lossless** (area-averaged, thresholded at half, Flate).

title: M11: Recognize text can save the result as PDF/A
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

Recognize Text can save its result as PDF/A (Acrobat's "Make scans PDF/A compliant"; parity `ocr.scan-pdfa`, planned → shipped), for single documents and for Recognize text in multiple files.

- **Dialog:** a "Save as PDF/A-2b" check box. After recognition the document is converted exactly as *Apply PDF standards ▸ Save as PDF/A* does (`Edit::ConvertPdfA`), **in the same undo step** as the words, then checked; the toast says "saved as PDF/A-2b", or what still keeps it from complying, or why it couldn't be converted. Edit's automatic OCR of a scanned page never converts. The multiple-files command uses the dialog's last choices (as it already does for resolution and language) and its summary counts the files saved as PDF/A and names the ones that aren't yet.
- **Refusals don't lose the words:** when the conversion can't be applied (security that doesn't allow removing the encryption, which PDF/A forbids — #3921; a signed file that would need a rewrite) the words are added on their own and the reason is reported.
- **The text layer font.** The OCR layer is non-embedded Helvetica in text rendering mode 3. PDF/A-2/3 only require programs for fonts *used for rendering* (ISO 19005-2 §6.2.11.4.1), and mode 3 renders nothing, so that's compliant — veraPDF 1.30.3 agrees (see below). PdfCraft's own check, however, could not tell: it checked every indirect font object regardless of use, and **never saw fonts written directly into a resource dictionary at all** — which is how PdfCraft's own *Add text* writes `/PCHelv`. So `pdfa_verify`/Save as PDF/A said "compliant" for a page with visible, unembedded Helvetica that veraPDF fails on 6.2.11.4.1. New `crates/preflight/src/fonts.rs` walks what pages draw (content, nested forms, annotation appearances), following `Tr`/`Tf` through `q`/`Q` and into forms (which inherit the caller's state), and:
  - excuses a font only drawn in mode 3, but only on complete evidence (all content read, no depth/form limit hit, not…

title: Dialogs: a dialog no longer keeps a taller one's height (#5118)
author: mmmaarian03-crypto
body:
Fixes #5118.

## Problem
Every dialog is shown in one shared modal, and egui keeps a modal's size from the frame before. A dialog whose button row is a bare right-to-left layout centres that row in all the height it is offered, so after Preferences, Print opened as tall as Preferences, with blank space above Cancel / Print, until restart. title: feat(optimize): add presentation preset, tiled slide flattening, dimension capping, and target-size budgeting
author: Qurayshe
body:
Many like #2820 already mention this, but some compression features are still missing in this version, so this is an attempt to implement a few simple ones. When working with files where images were split and tiled (e.g. InDesign), the compression tool can now properly recognize this, which helps with compression efforts. The end result is mostly designed for non-print exports (e.g. portfolios, presentations), but some of the parts may be useful for print media too.
Also adds JPEG 2000 / palette decoding for recompression, longest-side pixel dimension limits, and target file size budgeting.

## What this changes

Adds presentation slide optimization, longest-side pixel dimension capping, JPEG 2000 & palette image recompression, and target file size budget optimization to `pdfcraft-optimize`:

1. **Slide Background Flattening (`flatten.rs`):** Detects presentation slides containing many split image tiles (commonly generated by InDesign/Keynote transparency flatteners), composites the background into a single JPEG via `PageRenderer`, and preserves the original selectable vector text layer on top. Retains any page `/XObject` resources referenced by Type 3 font glyph procedures while detaching unused background tile streams.
2. **Dimension Capping & Extended Formats (`images.rs`):** Adds `max_image_dimension` to cap oversized 4K/8K images that escape standard physical-inch PPI thresholds due to large canvas point dimensions. title: M10: Recognize text reads multi-column pages column by column and keeps its line breaks
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

ocrs's line finder joins words that sit at one height into one line, **also across the gutter between two columns**, and returns the lines top to bottom. On a two-column page every recognised line therefore runs from the left column into the right one, and the text comes out interleaved. That is what `ocr_recognize` returns and what goes into the text layer in content order.

`Ocr::recognize` now puts its lines in reading order (new `crates/ocr/src/layout.rs`):

1. **Split at gutters.** A line is split wherever two neighbouring words are more than 0.8 line heights apart. A word space is about a third of a line height.
2. **Order by recursive XY cuts.** The page is cut at its widest empty band, down or across, and each part is cut again the same way. Band widths are compared in line heights, so a narrow gutter that runs the full height wins over the space between two paragraphs. The result: a heading over both columns comes first, then each column from top to bottom.
3. **Rows when no band is left.** When there is nowhere left to cut, lines are read in rows, top to bottom and each row left to right.

Single-column pages keep their order.

**Line breaks.** The text also kept no line breaks at all. `OcrPage::text()` (what `ocr_recognize` returns as `text`) joined every word of a page with spaces, so a page came back as one long line. `OcrPage` now records how many words each recognised line holds (`line_lengths`), and `text()` puts a newline between lines. If the lengths do not add up, no word is lost and no empty line is written. Tests: `ocr::tests::page_text_breaks_between_lines` (unit) and `tests::recognised_text_keeps_its_lines` (end-to-end with the models). Both fail with the old `text()`.

**Measured** on the MDPBench public split, DE/ES/FR, 480 pages. It used the official evaluation (`pdf_validation.py` + `calculate_scores.py` from Yuliang-Liu/MultimodalOCR) with the same metric as the paper; formulas are not scored. The OCR was `en` on a b…

title: Add text: Korean with an embedder-supplied face
author: taxjung85
body:
## Korean in Add text, drawn with an embedder-supplied face

We embed PdfCraft's PDF window in a Korean web app (the wasm build). Add text currently refuses Hangul ("The PDF text fonts can't draw “ㅇ” (U+3147)"), so Korean users can't add a single word to a PDF.

This draft adds a Korean face slot that follows the Thai / Arabic / Hebrew path exactly:

- `pdfcraft_fonts::set_document_korean_font(&'static [u8])` lets the embedding app supply a face once (first one wins; unreadable bytes are refused). Nothing is built in and **no font file is committed**, so AGENTS.md section 1.4 stays intact. We pass an OFL-1.1 face (Pretendard) from our own app.
- `ShapedScript::Korean`, `korean_has`, `shape_korean` (harfrust, `script::HANGUL`, grapheme clusters).
- In Add text, a character the standard fonts can't draw and the supplied face can (`korean_drawn`) is shaped with that face and drawn as Type 3 outlines with a ToUnicode map, like the other shaped scripts. The face file is never embedded; only the glyphs used are drawn. Line wrapping, `first_undrawable` and the apply-time check use the same rule.
- Without a supplied face nothing changes: such text is refused as before.

### Test

`crates/edit/tests/korean_face.rs` runs in its own binary because the face is process-wide. Inter stands in for a Korean face (U+0150 takes the same path as Hangul): refused before, drawable after, written as Type 3, and read back by `list_added` with the same text. `cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit -p pdfcraft-fonts` passes locally.

We have shipped the same change on the 64e0868 base in our app, and checked a saved PDF: the text renders, and copying it returns the original Korean.

### Questions for you

- Would you rather have a craft-fonts face (e.g. a `Kore` script face) as the built-in source, with this setter only as an embedder override? We're happy to rework it that way.
- If you want this reachable headlessly (automation tool, parity entry), tell us where you'd like it and we'll add it.

title: M3: select several document tabs and drag them together (#4590)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4590.

Several document tabs can now be selected and moved together:

- **Ctrl-click (⌘-click on macOS)** adds a tab to the selection or takes it out. A tab added becomes the document shown. Taking out the shown one hands over to its neighbour in the selection. The last selected tab can't be taken out.
- **Shift-click** selects the run from the last tab clicked without Shift (even one just taken out with Ctrl/⌘), in the strip's order. Ctrl+Shift-click adds the run to what was already selected.
- **A plain click** selects that tab alone. A click on a selected tab without dragging returns to one tab.
- **Dragging a selected tab** moves the whole selection as one run, in strip order (not click order), to the drop line. Other tabs keep their relative order, and the same document stays shown and the same tabs selected, so the group can be moved again. A drop that would leave the order unchanged draws no line and moves nothing.
- **Dragging a tab that isn't selected** moves it alone, as before, and leaves the selection as it is.
- **Selected tabs** are drawn raised, halfway between the active tab and the strip, so the shown document still stands out.
- **The selection is forgotten** once another document is shown by any other route: Ctrl+Tab, opening or closing a file, or Home. Coming back later selects that tab alone.

Context-menu actions (Close Tab, Reveal) still act on the one tab clicked, as the issue asks for this first step.

Implementation:
- `app/tabs.rs` (new) holds the selection (`TabSelection`, by `DocId`, with the active document it was made with), `click_tab`, `dragged_tabs` and `move_tabs`. `move_tab` now delegates to `move_tabs`.
- In `chrome.rs`, `drop_index` and `drop_marker` take the set of moving tabs instead of one.

title: Preserve macOS ACLs during atomic document saves
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

Atomic macOS Save currently replaces the destination's ACL with the staging file's ACL.
An explicit deny can disappear, and a private file can gain permissions inherited from its folder.
This preserves the destination's native extended ACL before writing PDF data, using the same held descriptor for its ACL, mode, group, xattrs and creation date.

Staging remains owner-only until its ACL is installed.
Replacement refuses any inherited staging ACL and any captured source deny-delete entry before applying that ACL or writing PDF data.
The latter prevents a failed replacement from leaving undeletable staged PDF data.
The deny-delete check deliberately applies regardless of principal or effective group membership.
Errors retain the original file and unsaved edits, with a Save As suggestion.
Save As preserves an existing destination's policy; a fresh name follows the chosen folder's normal inheritance.

Refs #2658 (partial).
Windows DACLs and hard-link identity remain outside this change.
Observed destination changes refuse publication, without promising atomic locking against hostile concurrent filesystem changes.
Cleanup is attempted; an inherited delete denial or directory permissions can prevent removal of an empty staging file, which receives no PDF payload.

## How you verified it

The ACL-loss, inherited-access and deny-delete cleanup regressions were each observed fail before their corresponding fixes.
Actual rebuilt CLI/MCP workflows verify incremental and full Save, refusal with retained dirty edits, successful new-path Save As, ACL/mode preservation and saved bytes reopened with the intended page rotation.

title: M10: Recognize text reads a page region by region and breaks it into paragraphs (PP-DocLayoutV3)
author: huppiflupp
body:
**Stacked on #5157** (`feat/ocr-reading-order`): the first four commits are that PR's; review the last two here. Once #5157 merges this rebases onto `main`.

## What this changes

Recognize text now uses a layout model, PP-DocLayoutV3, to read a page region by region and to break the recognised text into paragraphs.

- **Model as an optional asset.** `doclayout.onnx` is `inference.onnx` from HF `PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_onnx` at revision `46bbdf188bb0a772c08aed74882ce7e51a8f1ea6`: 130 502 049 bytes, SHA-256 `45bf7175…cf28ba`, Apache-2.0. It has an `ATTRIBUTION.toml` entry (`kind = "model"`), so `cargo xtask models` fetches and verifies it and the desktop packages stage it with the others (`stage_models`). Discovery looks for it on its own in the usual model directories (`Models::find_layout`). Without it, `recognize` behaves exactly as in #5157.
- **`crates/ocr/src/regions.rs`: region detection.** It loads the model once, next to the recogniser (`Ocr::find`). The page picture is stretched to 800 × 800 (area-averaged when shrinking), channels first, scaled to 0–1. The model gets `im_shape` and `scale_factor`, and returns its boxes in page pixels. Rows go through `regions_from_rows`:
  - score ≥ 0.5;
  - a known label;
  - a finite, non-empty box, clipped to the picture;
  - a finite rank, or last;
  - at most 1 000 regions.
- **`crates/ocr/src/layout.rs`: `paragraphs`.**
  - Each line (the union of its words' boxes) goes to the region covering at least 50 % of it; the best overlap wins, and the first in rank order on a tie.
  - Regions are read in the model's rank order. Within a region, lines keep their #5157 order, and each region is one paragraph.
  - A line in no region becomes a paragraph of its own, right after the paragraph of the line before it (see "Loose lines" below).

title: fix(sign): a later approval signature or a /Perms change breaks a P=1 certification, a document timestamp does not
author: LetoCoder26
body:
## What this changes

DocMDP P=1 ("no changes allowed", ISO 32000-2 §12.8.2.2) didn't stop later signatures. `classify_changes` permitted `kind::SIGNATURE` at every level, so a P=1 certification stayed **Valid** after a second approval signature, whether in a new field or in an empty one. A change to the catalog's `/Perms` (which names the certification signature) was also judged as signing.

Under P=1 now:
- **A later approval signature breaks the certification.** That is, a signature field holds a value the signed revision didn't give it, other than a document timestamp (`later_approval_signature`).
- **A `/Perms` difference** between the signed and the current catalog is a disallowed `STRUCTURE` change.

**Document timestamps keep a P=1 certification valid**, standalone or held by a field, because PAdES long-term archiving adds them to certified documents. This is where it differs from #4576, which marks them `Disallowed(["signature"])` (see the comparison in #3440). Approval signatures, P=2 and P=3 are unchanged.

This is one of several small PRs split out of #3440, rebuilt on current `main`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-sign` (`--all-targets`)
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign`: 146 passed, 3 ignored
- [x] `cargo xtask parity`

**Tests.** Both tests fail with the change reverted and pass with it:
- `a_later_signature_breaks_a_no_changes_certification_but_a_timestamp_does_not` covers the following:
  - under P=1, a second signature in a new field and in the empty field breaks the certification;
  - a standalone document timestamp and a field-held one don't;
  - under approval, P=2 and P=3, counter-signing stays valid with `Allowed(["signature"])`.
- `the_catalogs_perms_do_not_change_under_no_changes` checks that `/Perms`, dropped or pointed elsewhere under P=1, gives `Disallowed(["document structure"])`.

title: fix(sign): a signature validates only from its own signed field and dictionary
author: LetoCoder26
body:
## What this changes

A signature was reported **Valid** once its bytes checked out, without checking that the field and dictionary it was read from are the signed ones. A later revision could add a second signature field whose `/V` either:
- **copies** the signer's dictionary (the same `/ByteRange` and `/Contents`) with a `/Reason` of the forger's choosing, such as "I agree to pay 1,000,000"; or
- **names** the signer's own, unchanged dictionary.

Either one showed as a second valid signature by the same signer, with a field name, page and text the signer never signed.

`classify_changes` now receives the signature's own field and indirect `/V` (`Own`). If either is absent from the signed revision or changed since, that is a disallowed change. The signer's real signature stays **Valid**, because adding a signature field is still a permitted change.

This is one of several small PRs split out of #3440, rebuilt on current `main`. It's independent of #5173.

title: fix(sign): an unsigned signature field changes as a signature only when it is signed in place
author: LetoCoder26
body:
## What this changes

`change_kind` froze a signed signature widget only when the widget itself set `/FT /Sig` and held `/V`. Any change to an *unsigned* signature widget counted as a signature change, which every DocMDP level permits. On current `main`:
- moving an unsigned signature widget over the page and redrawing it validates under P=1 ("no changes");
- writing a value while moving the widget validates at every level;
- a signed kid whose parent sets `/FT` can be moved and redrawn, and a later signature doesn't notice;
- legitimately signing an inherited-`/FT` field later is reported as `["form fill", "signature"]` instead of `["signature"]`.

`field_info` now reads `/FT` and `/V`, each from the nearest field that has it, since both are inheritable (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.1). `signature_field_change` then judges a signature field by its signed role:
- **signed:** any change is page content, as before;
- **unsigned:** a change is a signature change only when it signs the field and leaves it in place, meaning the same `/Rect` (compared as numbers) and the same `/Parent`, `/Kids`, `/P`, `/Subtype` and `/FT`. Strings may be rewritten, since a writer that re-encrypts the file writes them anew.

Any other edit is an ordinary form-field edit, and moving the widget while signing it is "other changes".

This is one of several small PRs split out of #3440, rebuilt on current `main`. It's independent of #5173 and #5175.

## How you verified it

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-sign` (`--all-targets`)

title: perf(cos): a resource dictionary repeated in every page is parsed once (a 3,753-page plot opened in 143 s, now 3.5 s)
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

A CAD plot of 3,753 A2 pages (801 MB) took **143 s and 12 GB** to open, and the window showed no page for over three minutes. Its pages are ordinary; what is unusual is that a header-and-footer tool had copied the plot's one shared resource dictionary into every page: each page object lists the same 10,816 shadings directly in its `/Resources`, 195 kB per page and 730 MB in all, although only 110 pages draw a shading.

Every walk over the pages parsed all of those dictionaries again. Opening walks the pages about eight times (form fields and adopted widgets, field appearances, signatures, missing annotation appearances, the page count, inspection), and the editor cache, capped at 1,024 objects, never held the pages between walks. Inspection then converted each page's resources into lopdf objects as well: 40 million entries kept while the panels are filled.

- **`pdfcraft-cos`: `Dict` shares its entries between clones** (an `Arc`, copied on the first change: `set`, `get_mut`, `remove`). Equality, iteration order, the key index and `Debug` are unchanged. `Dict::shares` tells whether two clones still share.
- **`pdfcraft-cos`: the lexer reads a recurring large dictionary once** (`parser::SharedDicts`, one per document, shared by its clones and scan readers). A nested dictionary of 8 kB or more that parses cleanly is kept, at most 16 of them and 16 MB of their bytes; when full, one that no copy has reused yet makes room. A dictionary that starts with exactly those bytes at the same depth is the earlier parse: the bytes are compared, not just hashed, and the end is checked first (copies that differ usually differ in their last entries). The node budget counts its nodes as a fresh parse would, so `object too large` still fires at the same point. Only the innermost large dictionary is kept: the copies of one that encloses it tend to differ elsewhere (here each page's `/Resources` names its own footer XObject). Decryption happens after the parse, per o…

title: perf(edit): headers, watermarks and backgrounds read the page list once and share extended resources (a 3,753-page footer took 248 s, now 10 s)
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Adding a footer ("Seite <<1>> von <<n>>" and the drawing number) to a 3,753-page CAD plot hung the app in 0.14.0. With the open-time fix of the companion PR it finished, but took **248 s** and grew the file from **56 MB to 267 MB**.

- **The page list was read again for every page.** `add_header_footer`, `add_watermark` and `add_background` called `page_list` two or three times per marked page, each a walk over the whole page tree, so marking all pages was quadratic. The steps after a page's first change (`place`, `place_inside_wrapper`, `add_picture_resource`) read the page's resources and contents from the page object itself and use the listed page only for its object number, so the list is now read once, before the loop.
- **Every page got its own copy of the resources it inherits.** The plot's pages inherit one resource dictionary from the page tree (`/Resources 3755 0 R`, 10,816 shadings). To add the footer font, each page received a direct copy of it. Pages that share one indirect resource dictionary now share one extended copy per addition (`DerivedResources`, keyed by the dictionary and what is added): a new indirect object with the font, the opacity state or the picture added, which each marked page points to. The original stays untouched for the pages that keep it. A page with direct resources still gets its own copy, as before, and so does a single stamp (`stamp` passes no `DerivedResources`).

The plot, `doc_header_footer` with left and right footer text through `pdfcraft-cli run`, saved as a new file (release):

title: Roll human_size over to MB when KB rounds to 1024.0
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Found while testing `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs:39-45` (no existing issue): `human_size` shows sizes just under 1 MiB as "1024.0 KB".

**Cause:** `human_size` chose the unit from the raw byte count, so sizes from 1,048,525 to 1,048,575 bytes stayed in KB. Dividing by 1024 and rounding to one decimal then gave "1024.0 KB".
