title: Redaction keeps Type 3 glyphs that annotations, patterns and soft masks show
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up to #4579 (F-011). `unlink_type3` unlinks the Type 3 glyph programs that nothing shows any more. To find what is still shown, it scans page content and the forms reached through `/XObject`. Three other things draw content and were not scanned:

- annotation appearance streams (`/AP` `/N`, `/R` and `/D`, including per-state dictionaries),
- the cell of a tiling pattern selected with `scn` or `SCN`,
- the group of a soft mask set with `gs`.

When one of them shows a glyph of a Type 3 font that a page or form also lists, the glyph counted as unused. Its program left `/CharProcs`. When nothing on the pages showed the font at all, it lost `/CharProcs` and left the page's `/Font`. The stamp, comment, field, pattern or mask then drew nothing for that glyph. `unlink_type3` runs on every Apply Redactions, so this happened even when the mark covered only text in another font. Nothing leaks. Too much goes.

The scan now also walks those three. Each is scanned once per stream, font and drawing holder (the same `seen_forms` key as forms), through its own `/Resources` or its caller's when it has none, and with no current font. Forms take the same path through a shared `scan_stream_object`, with the same behaviour as before.

**Rebased on `main` after #3680 (2026-11-07).** #3680's pattern guard refuses Apply Redactions on a page whose tiling pattern shows text or has no `/Resources`. So `prune_type3_from_resources` no longer reads tiling patterns, only soft mask groups (f0e400c1). `unlink_type3` still follows a pattern's cell, which matters for patterns on pages the mark is not on, so the pattern test now puts the pattern on a second page. The test for a pattern without `/Resources` is gone: Apply Redactions refuses that file now. Remove Hidden Information runs no pattern guard; there, a page font that only such a malformed pattern uses goes, as on `main`.

title: fix(render): a gray drawn with the Color blend mode is no longer drawn black
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Some grays painted with `/BM /Color` into an empty isolated group come out solid black. On
`main` today, nine of the 256 gray levels do, `0.96 g` among them: filled under `/BM /Color` in a
`/Group << /S /Transparency /I true >>` form it renders (0, 0, 0) where it should render about 245,
since with nothing beneath it the blend result is the source colour (ISO 32000-2 §11.3.5.3,
§11.4.7).

The cause is in vello_cpu 0.0.8's `clip_color` (`fine/highp/blend.rs`), shared by the
nonseparable modes. After `set_lum`, a gray has three equal components. When rounding leaves
them just below 0 or above 1, `l - n` (or `x - l`) is 0, the clip divides 0 by 0, and the NaN
survives into the pixel even where the backdrop's alpha is 0. Hue and Saturation are not
affected, because `set_sat` zeroes the channels first.

linebender/vello fixed this in vello#2000 (by zlstringham, merged 2026-10-16; issue
vello#1999), but no vello_cpu release carries it yet. This PR vendors vello_cpu 0.0.8 under
`vendor/`, following the existing vendor convention (a `PdfCraft patch:` marker, a README row
and a `[patch.crates-io]` entry), with that one function backported. Drop the copy once
pdfcraft moves to a vello_cpu release that has the fix.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render`: 400 + 45 pass (1 existing ignore)

title: Honor CARGO_BUILD_TARGET in FreeBSD packaging for aarch64 release builds
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Root cause

`packaging/freebsd/package.sh` already validated `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` and named the archive after the arch, but:

- `cargo build` never received `--target`, so a cross build compiled for the host triple and the `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/<triple>/release` BIN path pointed at nothing.
- `host-tuple` was not resolved to the build host's triple, so it was rejected as unsupported.
- The `--version` smoke run was skipped only when the target arch differed from the host, so a `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` build for the native arch still ran its binary.

## Change

- `host-tuple` resolves to `rustc -vV`'s host triple before validation.
- `cargo build` gets `--target "$CARGO_BUILD_TARGET"` when set (unset path unchanged).
- The `--version` smoke run is skipped whenever `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` is set; the ELF/FreeBSD executable check still runs on the staged binaries.
- Matches the deckcraft #1507, gridcraft #2847, filmcraft #3534, lightcraft #3275 and photocraft #9989 PRs. `release.yml` is not changed and aarch64 is not opted in anywhere.

## Dry-run (Linux x86_64 host, stubbed `cargo` and `file`, real `bash`)

| Case | Exit | Archive | cargo build args | Smoke run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unset | 0 | `pdfcraft-0.15.0-freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | no `--target` | ran |
| `x86_64-unknown-freebsd` | 0 | `pdfcraft-0.15.0-freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | `--target x86_64-unknown-freebsd` | skipped |
| `aarch64-unknown-freebsd` | 0 | `pdfcraft-0.15.0-freebsd-aarch64.tar.gz` | `--target aarch64-unknown-freebsd` | skipped |
| `i686-unknown-freebsd` | 2 | none | cargo not invoked | n/a |
| `host-tuple` (this Linux host) | 2 | none | rejected as `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | n/a |

`bash -n` and `shellcheck -x` pass. The stubs mean the real FreeBSD binaries and the cargo build were not exercised; `host-tuple` on a real FreeBSD host is untested.

title: feat(print): Pages to Print > Area... prints a dragged area of the page
author: Janiz-zzz
body:
**Pages to Print ▸ Area…** prints just a dragged area of a page, which Acrobat users do with the Snapshot tool and Print's *Selected graphic*.

**How it works**
- The Print dialog's *Pages to Print* row gets an **Area…** choice. Choosing it steps the dialog aside and says "Drag a rectangle around the area to print".
- The rectangle is dragged on the page as with *Take a snapshot*. The dialog then comes back with a **Selected area** tab under *Page Sizing & Handling*, the preview showing only that area, and the earlier choices (printer, copies, paper…) kept.

- Choosing All, Current page or Pages again goes back to whole pages, and the next Print starts without the area. The page goes back to Select once the rectangle is drawn.

**Headless** (AGENTS.md §3): `doc_print` takes `layout: "area"` with `area: [x0, y0, x1, y1]` (points on the displayed page, origin bottom left) and `flip`; a missing, flat or malformed area is an `InvalidArgs` error.

- `ui-egui`: `Handling::Area`, `PrintDraft::pick_area`, `QuickTool::PrintArea` (the marquee of Snapshot), `open_print_area`; `finish_sign_requests` now goes on with the tool `finish_marquee` leaves, so Print area hands the page back to Select.

title: Honor LockedContents annotation flag against content edits (#5216)
author: kk376
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5216

According to ISO 32000-2 Table 167 (Annotation flags):
* Bit 8 (Locked, 128) forbids deleting or modifying position/size/properties, but explicitly allows editing annotation contents.
* Bit 10 (LockedContents, 512) forbids modifying the contents and appearance of the annotation, but permits deleting or moving it.

Previously, the LockedContents flag was unparsed and unchecked, allowing text edits to proceed on annotations with flag bit 10 set.

This change:
1. Defines `FLAG_LOCKED_CONTENTS = 512` in `pdfcraft-annot` and adds `unlocked_contents` validation in `set_contents`, returning `AnnotError::Invalid` when the comment's contents are locked.
2. Exposes `locked_contents: bool` in `Summary`, `Props`, `pdfcraft_render::Annotation`, and the headless automation comment listing.
3. Gates editing triggers in `ui-egui`:
   * Disables double-click inline editor on canvas and in the comments panel when `locked_contents` is true.
   * Disables the "Edit" / "Edit text..." action in the comment card popup menu and canvas context menu.
   * Displays the lock icon when either `locked` or `locked_contents` is true.
4. Adds unit and engine regression tests.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`pdfcraft-annot`, `pdfcraft-render`, `pdfcraft-engine`, `pdfcraft-automation`, `pdfcraft-ui-egui`)

title: fix(ui): preserve rendered page tiles after partial render failures (#623 item 4)
author: ishveet
body:
## What this changes

Refs #623, item 4 (viewer behavior only). This partial fix leaves the issue's other items open.

A failed pixel request currently replaces a whole page with an error even if another tile or backdrop rendered successfully. This change preserves useful visible pixels and shows an error notice beside them. When no cached pixels intersect the visible page region, the existing full-page error remains.

- Suppress identical failed requests while allowing other tiles, thumbnails, organize-grid images and print previews to finish.
- Keep main-canvas diagnostics separate from aggregate `page_errors()`, so a failed preview cannot put a false warning on a successfully rendered main page.
- Hide obsolete zoom/pan diagnostics after current rendering succeeds, while retaining recent failure history to suppress repeated failures.
- Bound failure retention per page/consumer by `max(64, current pixel demand)`, then trim it as demand changes or ends. An untried healthy tile can progress even after 64 other visible requests fail.
- Preserve page/document invalidation, stale-result rejection, recovery and existing texture/cache admission checks.

No watchdog budgets, PDF interpretation, raster-cache architecture, GPU rendering or localization changes. No speedup is claimed.

## How you verified it

Windows 11 x86-64, Rust/Cargo 1.98.1. Cargo checks used the low-disk profile, locked/offline dependencies and two jobs. Visual tests used Vulkan and `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0`.

The build used the project's existing CI font input: [craft-fonts at b076417](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/tree/b076417b5880bd4154bd22f00695b1d28c6bea83), with `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1`. title: M12: XFA field names made up for repeated fields never take a name the template uses (#5224)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A field that repeats gets a PDF field name with a suffix (`numP_Subvention` → `numP_Subvention_2`). That suffixed name is no longer allowed to be one the template already gives another field. The layout collects the template's own field, exclusion-group and group-member names first, and skips them when it makes up a name. A template's own name is never renamed.

The same holds for the name an unnamed field or group gets (`field`, `group`): it no longer takes a name the template gives another field, so a field the template names `field` keeps it.

Fixes #5224

## How common

**About the numbers:** we test against 500 XFA forms that governments, universities and public bodies in more than 50 countries publish online. 245 of them are dynamic (PdfCraft lays out their pages itself), and the counts here are out of those 245.

All 245 open, on main and on this branch (rebuilt on current main, 2026-11-01):
- On main, **3 (1.2%)** have two different fields sharing one PDF name, **7 names** in all.
- On this branch: **0**.

| Form | Shared names on main | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Cerfa 12156, *Demande de subvention* (France) | 1 (`numP_Subvention_2`) | 0 |
| Ministry of Justice (Israel), income form | 3 (`Cell1_2`, `Cell2_2`, `Cell4_2`) | 0 |
| EMA eAF human marketing authorisation application | 3 (`btnSection1_2`, `btnSection2_2`, `btnSection4_2`) | 0 |

(The first version of this description named the EMA *variation* form for the third row; it is the marketing authorisation application form, as the counts above show.)

On Cerfa 12156, filling `numP_Subvention_2` with `1234` (the page-4 budget line) sets two fields on main, the page-7 budget total among them; on this branch it sets one, and the total is named `numP_Subvention_5`.

## Why this is right

ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.2 (Field names): field dictionaries with the same fully qualified field name are one field, and "shall have the same field type (FT), value (V), and default value (DV)". Two templ…

title: fix(render): an isolated DeviceCMYK transparency group blends in CMYK (#3776)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Supersedes #3777, at @jpeskov's request. Fixes #3776. Refs #2145.

**Merge after #5199.** This branch merges #5199's branch (its vello_cpu fix for gray under the Color blend mode), which the K ink pass relies on; once #5199 lands, that part of the diff disappears.

This is jpeskov's work, rebased onto current `main`. His three commits are unchanged in substance and keep him as their author. Our commits on top:
- renumber the patches;
- move one doc comment back onto its function;
- fix one interaction with the knockout-group support that landed on `main` after #3777 was opened (below).
- from review: reset the paint transform a preceding pattern leaves before drawing the group, and pin both review cases with tests (a pattern before the group; Color over an empty group at every K level).

The elements of an **isolated** transparency group whose colour space is `DeviceCMYK` now blend in CMYK, as ISO 32000-2 §11.3.4 requires. Before this change, PdfCraft converted each colour to RGB and blended it in RGB. A print test file's blend-mode patch then showed an X in almost every cell: magenta under black with Difference stayed magenta instead of turning green.

**The rules.**
- Blending happens in the group's colour space (§11.3.4). A subtractive space's components are complemented before the blend function and complemented again after it.
- For the nonseparable modes, C, M and Y blend as complemented R, G and B (§11.3.5.3).
- K is not blended. It comes from the backdrop for Hue, Saturation and Color, and from the source for Luminosity.

**The method.** An isolated group starts from a transparent backdrop of its own (§11.4.7), so its contents can be computed apart from the page.

  - `CmykGroup` captures the group at `Do`.
  - `Device::draw_isolated_cmyk_group` is a new hook. Its default returns `false`, so other devices are unchanged.

title: perf(ui): index Compare shading marks by page (refs #3920)
author: ishveet
body:
Part of #3920. This addresses the Compare shading overlap-scanning slice only.

Previously each visual region scanned every text rectangle and, on the old side, every previously accepted visual region, including marks from unrelated pages. The shading routine now groups text rectangles and accepted old-side visual rectangles by page, then checks candidates only within that page.

The original vectors still determine output order. The inclusive rectangle comparisons, f64-to-f32 conversions, insertion/deletion/replacement colors, visual-only/text-only filters and old-side deduplication are preserved. The indexes live only for one shading call and use sparse page keys. Regression tests compare ordered output bits against an independent copy of the prior algorithm across both panes, all filter combinations, edge contacts, sparse pages, non-finite/degenerate rectangles, 500 pages and dense single-page inputs.

This is one bounded part of #3920; Compare text extraction and visual rasterization still run synchronously on the UI thread.

title: Reject malformed UTF-8 before importing or merging form data
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5242.

Reject malformed UTF-8 before parsing generic XFDF, XML, CSV or tab-delimited form data.
Previously, the CLI accepted `caf\xff` in UTF-8 XML and saved/reopened `caf�`, reporting a glyph warning rather than an encoding error.

For spreadsheet extraction, an identifiable XFDF root keeps `%PDF-` in XML comments or values on the strict text path.
A small allocation-free lexical check skips an optional BOM and terminated comments/processing instructions before that root; strict UTF-8 and the full XML parser still validate the file.
Unrecognized prefixes retain the existing PDF-header heuristic; unsupported declarations such as DOCTYPE are outside this identification rule.

title: fix(forms): clearing a field's length limit leaves it with none, not its parent field's
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up to #4991, as offered there. `/MaxLen`, a text field's character limit, is inheritable (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.3). A field under a parent field takes the parent's limit when it has none of its own.

Clearing a field's limit in Properties, or through `form_set_props` with `"max_length": 0`, removed the field's own `/MaxLen`. For a field under a parent with a `/MaxLen`, that brought the parent's limit back. Example: `address` has `/MaxLen 3` and its kid `address.city` has `/MaxLen 8`. Clearing the city's limit left it limited to 3 characters, so `form_fill` with `Absalom` failed with "takes at most 3 characters".

`set_props` now checks whether an ancestor sets `/MaxLen` (`tree::ancestor_sets`, from #4991). If one does, clearing writes `/MaxLen 0` on the field instead of removing the key. `read.rs` already reads 0 as "no limit" and lets it override an inherited limit (#3323). Without such an ancestor the key is removed, as before.

## How you verified it

On `main` @ `3109bb23`:

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-automation`
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask parity`

New tests:

- `forms`: `clearing_a_kids_length_limit_does_not_bring_back_its_parents`. A text kid with its own limit under a parent with `/MaxLen 3` has its limit cleared. After save and reopen it has no limit, holds `/MaxLen 0` of its own, and takes a 7-character value. A field with no parent limit still loses the key.
- `automation`: `clearing_a_kids_length_limit_through_tools_does_not_bring_back_its_parents`, end to end through `form_set_props`, `form_fill` and `form_fields`.

Revert proof: with the new `MaxLen 0` arm removed, both tests fail. The unit test reads the parent's `Some(3)`. The end-to-end test fails at `form_fill`: `"address.city" takes at most 3 characters`.

title: M3.9: the control screenshot test makes its renderer before the 5 s deadline
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

`control::screenshots_of_window_and_region` (in `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/control.rs`) failed in my first `cargo xtask ci` run on a clean `main` on Windows:

```
ui.screenshot: the screenshot did not happen within 5 s: the window is not being drawn (it may be hidden, minimized or covered); bring it to the front and retry
```

It passes when run on its own, so it depends on how busy the machine is.

**Cause.** The kittest harness makes its wgpu renderer lazily, on the first render (`LazyRenderer` in egui_kittest). The test's first `ui.screenshot` request is that first render. So the request's 5 s deadline (`NOT_DRAWN_TIMEOUT` in `control.rs`) also has to cover creating the GPU device and pipelines. When nextest runs many test processes at once, that alone can take longer than 5 s. The real app never pays this inside a request, because its renderer exists before the window is first drawn.

**Fix.** The test calls `h.render()` once before its first request, so the renderer exists before any deadline starts. Only this test changes; no product code changes.

## How you verified it

Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (x64, 12 cores), Rust 1.99.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.150.

I ran 16 copies of the test binary at once (`it-*.exe --exact control::screenshots_of_window_and_region`), on the same build with and without the fix:

| | 8 at once | 16 at once |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (no fix) | 1 passed, 7 failed | 0 passed, 16 failed |
| with the fix | 8 passed | 16 passed |

With timing added temporarily under 16-way load, the first render took 1.4–6.2 s. The screenshot request after it took 0.3–1.0 s. One copy alone passes either way.

- [x] the test fails without the fix: I reverted it on the same build and reran 16 at once (0 passed)

## Never-crash

Test-only change. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, no `unsafe`.

title: M12: a PDF portfolio opens on its initial document and shows its files (#1652)
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A PDF portfolio (a catalog with a `/Collection`, ISO 32000-2 §7.11.6) keeps its documents as embedded files. Its own pages are only a cover sheet, written for viewers without portfolio support. PdfCraft showed that cover sheet and nothing else. The Attachments panel lists the files, but a reader who keeps the right panel closed never sees it, so the portfolio looked like a one-page document asking for another viewer.

Now:

- **Engine:** `DocInfo::portfolio` reads the collection dictionary (Table 153):
  - `initial` is the attachment whose `/EmbeddedFiles` key `/D` names, decoded as the keys are. It is `None` without `/D`, when the portfolio's own pages are the initial document.
  - `view` is `/View`: details, tile, hidden or custom.
- **Opening:** a portfolio that opens as the active tab presents the PDF its `/D` names in a tab of its own (a PDF by its bytes, whatever its name). That tab opens on the next frame, never from inside the open, and only while the portfolio is still the active tab and nothing else is under way (a prompt, a file picker, or a file still opening in the background that will come to the front: in the open worker on desktop, or a browser read of a dropped or picked file on the web). The document is kept by its name-tree key, so an attachment deleted meanwhile can't change which one opens. So a file opened together with it keeps the front, its password prompt included, and a portfolio inside the portfolio waits until the reader opens it: a nested file can't open tab after tab.
- **The portfolio's tab** shows its files in the Attachments panel even with the right panel closed, without changing that preference. Leaving the tab gives back the panel the list replaced, unless the reader changed panels meanwhile (in Read mode, that panel is the one Read mode gives back when it ends, and a panel picked in Read mode stays). The panel goes back before the initial document opens, so that document gets the panels any other would, not…

title: M3: allow narrower side panels and hide thumbnail controls when narrow
author: hajdukste
body:
## What this changes

The side panel (Pages, Bookmarks, Comments and the rest) can now be resized down to **240 points** (previously 260), matching Acrobat's narrowest panel. In Pages, the thumbnail-size label, slider and buttons hide below 280 points of content width, which is any panel narrower than 309 points. They return when the panel is widened, keeping the selected thumbnail size.

This follows Acrobat, observed black-box: its Pages panel stops at about 240 px, measured with an on-screen ruler, and shows no thumbnail-size slider at that width. A wider panel shows the slider. Per `AGENTS.md` §1.1, no Acrobat screenshots are included here.

Two narrow-panel issues from review are fixed too:

- **Resizing keeps the current thumbnail in sight.** A resize reflows every thumbnail under the same scroll offset, which could carry the current page's thumbnail out of view. If it was in sight, the panel now follows it back, the same way a page change does. If the reader had scrolled away from it, the panel stays where they left it.
- **The selection count no longer runs under the buttons.** "N pages selected" moved from beside the title, where at 240 points it ran under Page tools, to the line under the title. It is truncated short of the buttons, and hovering shows it in full. While two or more pages are selected, the header is about 8 points taller.

Apart from those, the runtime change is one width-limit adjustment and an early return in the existing controls. Default widths, thumbnail zoom bounds and the Tools pane are unchanged. `ui.panel` and saved settings use the same limit.

PdfCraft only. Before is current `main` (15c505d1) and after is this PR, both with the same contributor-original synthetic PDF.

title: M3: Reveal in File Explorer doesn't report failure after it worked (Windows)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

On Windows, Reveal in File Explorer (tab menu) opens Explorer at the file's folder with the file selected. A moment later PdfCraft shows "Could not reveal the file in the system file manager" anyway, for about 3.5 seconds.

**Cause.** `reveal` runs `explorer.exe /select,"<path>"` and treats a non-zero exit status as failure. But Explorer exits with 1 even when it has opened the folder and selected the file. On Windows 10 22H2 I checked a path with spaces and the `\\?\C:\…` form: each time it showed the right folder with the file selected, and exited with 1.

**Fix.** In `reveal_via`, on Windows only Explorer not starting counts as a failure; a non-zero exit is still a reveal. macOS, Linux and FreeBSD are unchanged: their exit status still counts, and Linux and FreeBSD still fall back to `xdg-open`.

I found this while checking #2700 and #2654 on Windows. The Documents-folder problem in those is already fixed by #2625; this is a separate, smaller bug.

## How you verified it

Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (x64), Rust 1.99.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.150.

- New unit test `explorer_exiting_with_1_has_still_revealed_the_file`. It fails on `main` (`left: Err("Could not reveal the file in the system file manager")`, `right: Ok(())`) and passes with the fix. It uses a stand-in runner, so it runs on every platform and starts no Explorer.
- In the real app, with a portable copy driven through the control channel: I opened `…\reveal test\folder with spaces\a b.pdf` and chose the tab's Reveal in File Explorer. Then I polled `ui.state` every 200 ms and read the new Explorer window through `Shell.Application`.
  - `main`: Explorer shows that folder with `a b.pdf` selected, and the notice "Could not reveal the file in the system file manager" is up for about 3.5 s.
  - this branch: the same Explorer window and selection, and no notice.

title: fix(geom): normalize quad ordering for perspective foreshortening and scale
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Problem
- `order_quad` selected the top-left corner by minimising `x + y`, which misordered foreshortened perspective quads (e.g. a landscape page photographed from below where `bl[0] + bl[1] < tl[0] + tl[1]`) and tilted narrow quads.
- `order_quad` multiplied `size * size` directly when checking convexity and area thresholds, which overflowed `f64` on large finite coordinates (e.g. `1e160`).

### Root Cause
- `order_quad` evaluated raw `x + y` sums and unnormalised cross products rather than normalising coordinates by the bounding box.

### Fix
- Add a private `bounds` helper in `crates/geom/src/perspective.rs` and normalise `order_quad` coordinates by the bounding box before sorting, scoring candidate rotations by normalised left-edge `x` and top-edge `y`, and evaluating convexity/area.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-geom`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-geom --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: M7: links that go to a page open at a chosen zoom (edit.action-goto)
author: Ethunxxx
body:
## What this changes

A go-to-page link can now open its page at a chosen zoom, as Acrobat's Go to a page view does. Before, it always opened at Fit Page (`edit.action-goto`: *"go to a page (Fit view); named destinations and zoom pending"*).

The zooms and what each writes (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.2, Table 149):

| Zoom | Destination |
|---|---|
| Fit Page | `[page /Fit]` |
| Fit Width | `[page /FitH null]` |
| Fit Height | `[page /FitV null]` |
| Fit Visible | `[page /FitB]` |
| Actual Size / a percentage | `[page /XYZ null null z]` |
| Inherit Zoom | `[page /XYZ null null null]` |

Positions are written `null`, as `add_bookmark` writes a new bookmark.

- **Engine** (`crates/annot/src/links.rs`):
  - `LinkAction::Page(usize)` becomes `Page { page, zoom: LinkZoom }`.
  - Links other tools wrote read back as the nearest zoom: `/FitBH` as Fit Width, `/FitR` as Fit Page, an `/XYZ` zoom of 0 or `null` as Inherit, and a `GoTo` action like a `/Dest`.
  - A zoom outside 1–6400% reads as the destination has it, so `link_list`'s `zoom` agrees with its `destination`. It is brought within 1–6400% only when the user changes the destination.
  - A zoom that isn't a positive percentage is refused before anything is written.
- **Automation:**
  - `link_add` and `link_edit` take `zoom`: `fit_page` (the default, as before), `fit_width`, `fit_height`, `fit_visible`, `actual`, `inherit`, or a percentage (1–6400). The names match `doc_initial_view`'s `magnification`.
  - On `link_edit`, a new `to_page` keeps the link's zoom, and a `zoom` alone keeps its page.
  - `link_list` reports each page link's `zoom`.
- **UI:** a Zoom dropdown under Page in Link Properties ▸ Go to a page view. Every label but "Inherit Zoom" was already in the catalogues.
  - From a million percent up, the label uses exponent form (`1.8e308%`), so another writer's absurd factor can't make a 309-digit label.

title: Reload: a file changed under an open dialog waits for it to close (#3917)
author: mmmaarian03-crypto
body:
Refs #3917 (the file-watcher half). The OS Open half is in #4042, so this leaves it alone.

**Problem.** The file watcher reloaded a clean document in place even while a dialog was open over it. Most dialogs act on the active document when OK is pressed, so Rotate, Protect, Comment Properties and the rest could apply to a version the user never saw (a LaTeX/Typst build or a sync client rewriting the file).

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/platform/file_watch.rs`). While a modal is open, the newest version found for the active document is held instead of applied. When the modal closes it goes through the usual checks (stale epoch, own save, unchanged bytes, unsaved work → notice bar) and loads. Only the newest version is kept, so a build loop under a dialog doesn't pile up file contents. Other tabs reload as before.

**Verified**
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test it reload::`: 12 passed, including the new `a_file_rebuilt_under_an_open_dialog_reloads_when_the_dialog_closes` (rebuilds the file twice under Rotate pages, checks it isn't replaced, then that the newest version loads after the dialog closes). It fails without the change (4 pages instead of 2).
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib file_watch`: 2 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`: clean (Windows 11).

**Not covered.** Giving every dialog draft a `(DocId, generation)` check, the issue's third suggestion. The OS Open / drag-and-drop path (#4042).

title: feat(annot,ui): support one-click bulk deletion of comments (#5119)
author: marcwgls
body:
## What this changes

Part of #5119

Adds one-click deletion of unlocked comments on the current page (`comment.delete_page`) or in the whole document (`comment.delete_all`), so a heavily annotated document no longer has to be cleaned up one comment at a time. Both are a single undo step.

### Scope compared with the issue

#5119 asks to delete "all annotations". This PR deletes all unlocked *comments*, the ones the Comments panel lists, and deliberately leaves the following in place:

- links, form fields (`/Widget`) and the other non-markup annotations (`/Screen`, `/Movie`, `/RichMedia`, `/3D`, `/PrinterMark`, `/TrapNet`, `/Watermark`): deleting them would break the document's navigation and forms, which is not what clearing review comments is for;
- redaction marks and Fill & Sign items: they belong to the Redact and Fill & Sign tools, which apply, clear and sign them;
- locked comments, with their whole thread (replies, statuses, checkmarks).

### Details

- `pdfcraft_annot`: `delete_all_annotations(doc, pages)` reads every page's `/Annots` once and tells comments, replies and threads apart exactly as the comment list does (`pdfcraft_render::link_replies`), so the number it returns matches what the Comments panel shows. A deleted comment's replies and pop-ups go from every page, also when only one page is cleared (the same as deleting a single comment). A reply whose thread starts at a locked comment or on a page not being cleared stays. Only pages whose `/Annots` change are written.
- `pdfcraft_engine`: `Edit::DeleteAnnotations { pages }`, labelled "Delete page comments" / "Delete all comments". An edit that would delete nothing is refused, so it never pushes an empty undo step. `comment.delete_all` and `comment.delete_page` are registered under `Needs::Annotate`, and "Delete all comments" is in the Comment tools catalog.

title: fix(redact): measure glyphs against marks with at most one em of height
author: helenkwok
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5255.

Redacting text on one line could delete glyphs on the next line, outside the filled box, when the lines are set solid (line spacing = font size). `SECRET word here` under a marked `Account: 12345678` became `SECRET`.

A mark made from a text selection covers the selected line's em box: text selection measures each glyph from descent −0.2 to ascent 0.8 em (`crates/render/src/text/device.rs`). The redactor measured the same glyphs from the font's own descent to ascent, which is taller than one em for many fonts (Monaco 1000 / −250, and the 0.9 / −0.25 fallback): up to 1.5 + 0.6 em after the clamp in `crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs`. With 12 pt lines, the line below's glyph box then reached about 2 pt into the mark, past `glyph_hit`'s 1 pt threshold, and those glyphs were removed while the fill only covered the mark.

`show` now measures a glyph against marks with its descent-to-ascent box scaled to at most one em (`em_box`). Fonts whose box is one em or less (the redact tests' font, 800 / −200) are unchanged, and the overlap rule itself (a fifth of the glyph or a point, both ways) is unchanged. The hidden-text rule (`Remove Hidden Information`) still uses the full box. The crate README says how the glyph height is taken.

title: M9 #3442: a form fill may rewrite existing field appearances and /DR in place
author: charlieruk
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3442.

A writer that fills a certified form by redrawing a field in its **existing** appearance stream, or by adding a font to the **existing** indirect `/AcroForm /DR`, had those objects classified as `kind::OTHER`. DocMDP P=2 refuses that, so legitimate form filling made the certification invalid.

`classify_changes` now gives objects of the signed revision a form role, used only when a change would otherwise be `OTHER`:

- **Appearance**: the `/AP` dictionary, the `/N` `/R` `/D` dictionaries of states, and the appearance streams of an *ordinary* widget (text, button or choice field, with `/FT` its own or inherited). Any rewrite is a form fill.
- **Resources**: the AcroForm's `/DR` and its category dictionaries. These count as form fill only when they gain entries; changing or dropping an entry, or pointing it at another object, is not.

The policy, documented on `form_fill_roles`:

- A role comes from the **signed revision** only, never from what a later revision says an object is.
- An object qualifies only when that role is **all** it held. The signed file is walked from the trailer, skipping only the ordinary widgets' `/AP` edges and the AcroForm's `/DR` edge. Anything that walk still reaches keeps its strict judgement:
  - page content or resources
  - a signature field's appearance, or another annotation's appearance
  - an action or script
  - catalog entries
- Each object must have the shape of its role. An appearance dictionary has only `/N` `/R` `/D`. A states dictionary holds only references to streams. An appearance is an untyped or `/Type /XObject` stream. `/DR` has only resource categories.
- Signature widgets, comments and widgets without a field type get no role.
- The walk runs lazily, only when a change would otherwise be refused. Past 500,000 objects it gives up and nothing qualifies, so changes are judged as before.

Rewriting an ordinary field's appearance in place grants nothing a form fill can't already do, becau…

title: fix(redact): measure glyphs by their outline ink when the font program is readable
author: helenkwok
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5298. Stacked on #5281: until that merges, this PR's diff includes it; the change here is the last commit.

Since #5281, redaction measures a glyph against marks with its descent-to-ascent box scaled to at most one em. Ink outside that box (a tall accent, a swash) could sit under a mark and be kept, and the verification pass, which tests the same box, did not flag it; #5281 only counted such glyphs in `Report::glyphs_beside_marks`.

Now, when the font's program is embedded and readable, each glyph is measured by its ink:

- `pdfcraft-fonts` gains `GlyphInk` and `Ink` (`crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs`). `GlyphInk::from_dict` reads a `FontFile2` or OpenType `FontFile3` program with `skrifa` (already a dependency). Simple fonts map codes to glyphs the way `embedded_widths` already does (encoding glyph names through the `cmap`, then the symbolic `cmap` ranges); Type 0 fonts over TrueType go through `/CIDToGIDMap` (identity when absent or a name). `GlyphInk::ink` returns `Ink::Box` (the box the outline's points span, control points included, so it holds every curve), `Ink::Blank` (the glyph draws nothing) or `Ink::Unknown`.
- `show` in `pdfcraft-redact` tests `Ink::Box` against marks with the existing rule (a fifth of the glyph or a point, both ways). `Blank` and `Unknown` keep the one-em box; only `Unknown` glyphs are still counted in `glyphs_beside_marks`, since a blank glyph has no ink to leave behind.
- Bare CFF, Type 1 and Type 3 programs and non-embedded fonts are not read: their glyphs stay `Unknown`, exactly as before this PR.
- The reader is built per font only when the page has marks, and cached per font name for the page.

The crate README says how the glyph box is taken.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-fonts -p pdfcraft-redact --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-fonts -p pdfcraft-redact --no-deps --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`

title: Reject out-of-range fields in Time::from_pdf
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

`Time::from_pdf` in `crates/sign/src/der.rs` accepted impossible dates. It parsed each date field as a `u32` and only checked that the year was non-zero, so month 13, day 99 or hour 25 returned `Some`. With a time zone suffix, `unix()` mapped the invalid date to the epoch day, so the result was a bogus 1969/1970 time. That value is the /M fallback signing time used at `crates/sign/src/pdf/validate.rs:222`.

After parsing, `from_pdf` now validates the date with `chrono::NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt` and the time of day with `chrono::NaiveTime::from_hms_opt`. It returns `None` for an impossible month, day, hour, minute or second, so a malformed /M date is shown as unknown.

No existing issue.

## How you verified it

- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `editing::a_custom_property_whose_name_the_tools_refuse_is_listed_and_left_alone`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Never-crash

- [ ] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests, unless it is provably infallible with a comment saying why
- [ ] No indexing or slicing with input-derived positions (`get`, and strings only at char boundaries); checked or saturating arithmetic; allocations sized by input are capped; recursion is bounded

title: M3: full screen plays page transitions and display times, and its keys and clicks go the right way (#379, #5315)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #379. Fixes #5315.

Full Screen Mode (Ctrl+L / ⌘L) now plays a PDF's own presentation settings, and keys and clicks that went the wrong way or did nothing now work.

**Transitions and display times** (ISO 32000-2 §12.4.4):
- A page's transition (`/Trans`, Table 164) plays when the page comes into view. It runs from the outgoing page's raster to the incoming one's, using the geometry `render::transition` already computes for each style (#2084).
- A page's display time (`/Dur`) advances to the next page once the page is up, counted from the end of its transition. It stops at the last page, and the reader can turn the page sooner (NOTE 1). A page without `/Dur` does not advance by itself, as the spec says.
- A slide deck exported with timings and transitions, the case #379 describes, now plays as a presentation.

**When a transition doesn't play:** two-page spreads, a rotated view, and the Animation effects preference set to off change pages at once. A transition waits until the incoming page has rendered, so it never runs into a blank page.

**Pointer:** a still pointer hides after three seconds and shows again when it moves, so it doesn't sit on a slide.

**Going back a page** (#5315):
- **Right-click** goes back a page, as a left click goes forward. Full screen shows no context menu, as it shows no tools. *Adobe Acrobat Help* (2019), "Full Screen preferences", p. 69: "Left Click To Go Forward One Page; Right Click To Go Back One Page".
- **Shift+Enter** goes back a page; it went forward like Enter. *Adobe Acrobat Help* (2019), "Read a document in Full Screen mode", p. 66: "To go to the previous page, press Shift+Enter".

**First and last page** (#5315): Shift+Ctrl+Page Up or Up Arrow goes to the first page, and Shift+Ctrl+Page Down or Down Arrow to the last, as Home and End do. Before, Shift+Ctrl+Page Down went forward one page and Shift+Ctrl+Down Arrow did nothing. This works outside full screen too. *Adobe Acrobat Help* (2019), "Keys fo…

title: M2: a tiling pattern paints at the fill or stroke opacity in effect (ISO 32000-2 11.6.4.4)
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

A tiling pattern now paints at the fill or stroke opacity (`ca` / `CA`) in effect when it paints, as ISO 32000-2 §11.6.4.4 asks for every painting operation. Before this:

- a **coloured** tiling pattern (`/PaintType 1`) drew fully opaque whatever `ca` said;
- an **uncoloured** one (`/PaintType 2`) took the fill opacity current at `scn`, so a `gs` after it had no effect, and a stroke took the fill opacity too.

This is the tiling half of #3176 / #3246, which fixed the same thing for shading patterns and deliberately left tiling patterns alone.

Found by black-box testing against Poppler, MuPDF and PDFium with synthetic files: on a page mixing several paint types, about 3.5 % of the pixels differed from the majority of the other engines, from a pattern fill under `/ca`; the file below reduces it to that.

**Minimal file** (801 bytes, uncompressed). Python 3, standard library only, writes `tiling-pattern-ca.pdf`: a tiling pattern of two blue squares fills two bands, with `/ca 0.5` set before `scn` in the top band and after it in the bottom one.

```python
def pdf(path, objs):
    out, offs = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.7\n"), []
    for i, o in enumerate(objs, 1):
        offs.append(len(out))
        out += b"%d 0 obj\n" % i + o + b"\nendobj\n"
    x = len(out)
    out += b"xref\n0 %d\n0000000000 65535 f \n" % (len(objs) + 1) + b"".join(b"%010d 00000 n \n" % o for o in offs)
    out += b"trailer\n<< /Size %d /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % (len(objs) + 1, x)
    open(path, "wb").write(bytes(out))

def stream(extra, data):
    return b"<< /Length %d %s>>\nstream\n" % (len(data), extra) + data + b"\nendstream"

content = b"/GS gs /Pattern cs /P scn 20 110 160 70 re f\n/Pattern cs /P scn /GS gs 20 20 160 70 re f"

title: Tests: a test process still running after 10 minutes fails as TIMEOUT (#5261)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Part of #5261. This is a mitigation; it doesn't fix the hang itself.

On Windows a test process can spin at exit, while `d3d11.dll` unloads, after its test has passed (#5261 has the stack). nextest had no time limit, so `cargo xtask ci` waited for that process forever, until someone found and killed it by hand.

`.config/nextest.toml` now sets `slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 10 }` for the default profile. A test process still running after 10 minutes is killed and reported as `TIMEOUT` with its name, and the run fails instead of hanging. A test is still marked `SLOW` after 60 s, as nextest already does.

The limit is generous. In four full Windows gate runs today the slowest test took 25 s (`fill_sign::lines_grow_and_shrink_with_their_handles_before_release`), on a 12-core machine running the whole suite at once. So 10 minutes leaves about 24 times that for slower CI runners and coverage builds. `cargo test` (no nextest) is unaffected.

`docs/architecture.md` (gates section and revision history) and the ROADMAP progress log say so.

## How you verified it

Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (19045), Rust 1.99.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.150.

- [x] **The mechanism, on this nextest:** with the period set to 1 s and `terminate-after = 1`, `cargo nextest run -p pdfcraft-print a_process_left_holding_the_output` reported `TIMEOUT [1.028s] … a_process_left_holding_the_output_does_not_extend_the_wait` and `error: test run failed`. That test takes about 3 s. I then set the real values.

title: M3: text_find can stop at its limit without reading on to the end (#5328)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5328.

`text_find` looks one match past `limit` so that `next` proves another match exists. When a document has exactly `limit` matches, that lookahead reads every later page to learn there is no further one. A search for the first occurrence on page 1 of a 3,000-page manual therefore extracts the whole document, and it reports a warning when a distant page fails.

This adds an opt-in `stop_at_limit: true` (option A in the issue):
- The search ends at the `limit`th match. Later pages are neither extracted nor cached, and they cannot add warnings.
- The answer carries `stopped_at_limit`.
  - When it is `true`, `complete` is `false` and `next` is the position just past the last match (`skip` counts within the page). That is where to resume, not a promise of another match: following it may return no matches and `complete: true`.
  - When it is `false`, the search ran out of pages before reaching the limit, and `complete` keeps its usual meaning.
- Without the flag, nothing changes: same lookahead, same `next`, and no new field. Existing callers see identical answers.

The tool schema and the automation README document the two modes.

title: M2: smooth small enlarged images that have many colours (#5338)
author: iAmRarted
body:
> **Depends on #3858.** This branch is built on its head (842928f1), so until #3858 merges the diff here includes its commit too. The two commits to review are 5d23c405 and b5f620c6 (+137 / −15 over #3858). Once #3858 lands I'll rebase onto `main`.

## What this changes

Fixes #5338.

Small screenshots embedded in a PDF (a terminal, a slide, a dialog) are now smoothed when zoomed in, as Chrome and Firefox draw them. They used to be drawn nearest-neighbour, so their text had staircase edges.

#3858 smooths enlarged images without `/Interpolate` only when their shorter side is at least 512 samples. Screenshots in course notes and slide decks are far smaller: on the page that prompted this, the terminal capture is 305 × 230 samples (~100 dpi on the page), and #3858's render of it is byte-identical to `main`'s.

**Rule.** An enlarged image under 512 samples is also drawn bilinearly (`ImageQuality::Medium`, as #3858 does) when it has more than 16 distinct colours (`HARD_PIXEL_COLOURS`). Size can't tell a screenshot from pixel art, but colours can: QR codes, bilevel images, few-colour icons and pixel art use a handful, while antialiased text or a photo has hundreds of shades. The rest of #3858's rule is unchanged.

**Cost.** `has_many_colours` stops at the 17th colour, so a screenshot or photo is decided within its first rows. It reads at most `COLOUR_SCAN_SAMPLES` (2^20) samples. An image is drawn once per tile, and a few-colour strip under 512 samples across can still hold up to `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` samples, so without the cap a single strip would be read in full on every tile. It only runs for enlarged, non-interpolated images under 512 samples outside Type 3 glyphs.

## What this changes

#5171 labels `table` regions but reads them as plain paragraphs, so MDPBench scores every table at 0. With the optional table structure model, Recognize text now reads a table region as a table: rows, cells, column and row spans, and the recognised words placed in their cells.

  - `TableModel::read` crops the region from the page picture and scales it so its longer side is 488 px (area-averaged when shrinking, the same weights as `regions.rs`). It normalises with the ImageNet mean and deviation, as BGR planes, and pads the picture to 488 × 488 with zeros.

title: fix(render): draw non-embedded CJK CID fonts of every Adobe collection, with per-character fallback faces
author: cyfung1031
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5329.

Text in a CID font that the PDF doesn't embed and that belongs to the Adobe-GB1, CNS1 or Korea1 collection drew nothing. Examples: `STSong-Light` with `GBK-EUC-H`, as CNKI/CAJ2PDF papers use; `MSung-Light`; `HYSMyeongJo-Medium`. The renderer's only CJK stand-in was a Japanese face for Adobe-Japan1, and hayro's own substitute is Times. `doc_info` reported such fonts as having "no licensed face". More generally, any character a Type 0 substitute had no glyph for drew `.notdef` (Adobe collections) or the substitute's glyph at the CID's index, an unrelated glyph (any other collection).

Four commits:

1. **Vendored hayro-interpret patch (71): further faces.** `InterpreterSettings::further_faces` gives a substituted Type 0 font the faces to try, in order, for characters its substitute lacks. Characters are looked up by Unicode (`/ToUnicode` or the collection's UCS2 CMap), never by CID.
   - Faces are parsed lazily, only when a character needs one.
   - A face that is the substitute itself is skipped.
   - A further face's glyph id carries the face's position above its 16-bit id, so glyph caches keep the faces apart.
   - Outlines are fitted to the PDF's `/W` advance.
   - `OutlineGlyph::font_data` is `None` for such glyphs.
   - The default is no further faces, and embedded fonts are unchanged.
2. **`pdfcraft_fonts::fallback` ranks faces for every CJK collection.** The substitution chain `doc_info` reports is now also what the renderer uses, so the face a report names is the face drawn. author: Saifallah-star
body:
Fixes #5348.

Allows dragging an open PDF tab out of the tab bar into open space to tear it off into its own independent window viewport. Users can also right-click any tab and choose **"Move to New Window"**.

- Detached tabs run in secondary native OS viewports via `egui::Context::show_viewport_immediate`.

- Closing a detached window via OS close button intercepts premature closure, prompting for unsaved modifications directly within the child viewport before tearing down.

---

1. **Active Tab Isolation & Desynchronization Prevention**:

   - `commit_typing_in` preserves active tab invariants for detached documents with in-flight form typing.

## What this changes

Redacting a paragraph could remove an image that sits elsewhere on the page. Office suites crop an image by placing it larger than its crop and clipping it: LibreOffice exported a workbook's logo as a 1920×1080 JPEG placed at 1637 × 791 pt from (−272, −142), larger than the A4 landscape page, clipped by `64.36 389.834 168.63 136.746 re W* n` to the logo. Redaction tested the image's whole placed area against marks, so any mark on the page reached it. Its pixels can't be cleared (DCT, and the same for an image with an `/SMask`), so the logo was removed whole.

The graphics state now carries the box of the clipping paths in force that the output keeps (saved and restored with `q`/`Q`). A clipping path the redaction removes clips nothing any more, so it doesn't narrow the box. Image XObjects and inline images are measured by the part of their placed area inside the box: an image whose hidden part alone reaches a mark is left as it is, and one whose visible part is under a mark is cleared or removed as before. Text and paths are measured as before. The crate README says how images are measured.

title: fix(model): reject degenerate and overflowing page boxes in rect
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Problem
- `rect` in `crates/model/src/lib.rs` returned `Some([x0, y0, x1, y1])` for zero-width or zero-height `/MediaBox` arrays (e.g. `[0 0 0 792]`), where `Page::crop`'s `r[2] > r[0] && r[3] > r[1]` check only applied when `/CropBox` was also present.
- `rect` accepted extreme finite coordinates (such as `[-1e308, 0, 1e308, 792]`) where `r[2] - r[0]` or multiplying by `user_unit` overflowed to `f64::INFINITY` in `Page::display_size`.

### Root Cause
- `rect` used `filter_map` over array entries and did not verify `w > 0.0 && h > 0.0` or that `(w * MAX_USER_UNIT)` and `(h * MAX_USER_UNIT)` remain finite.

### Fix
- Read the first four entries of a page box by position (`[a, b, c, d, ..]`), matching `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/object/rect.rs`, and require finite coordinates with `w > 0.0 && h > 0.0` and finite `(w * MAX_USER_UNIT)` / `(h * MAX_USER_UNIT)` in `rect`.
- **Behaviour note:** Callers that computed a scale from a zero-width `/MediaBox` now receive the `612 x 792` fallback box (`612` wide) instead of `0`.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-model`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-model --all-targets -- -D warnings`


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Rectangle inputs now accept arrays with four or more entries and use the first four coordinates. Reversed coordinates are normalized, while non-finite values, zero-size or negative-size rectangles, and dimensions that become non-finite when scaled are rejected. This also covers malformed inputs and extreme numeric values.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: M12: XFA master-page fields keep their own value on each page (#5365)
author: mtlcl410
body:
### What this changes

Content on a master page that the layout repeats on several pages now has a SOM path for each page (`Area[0]`, `Area[1]`, …), not one shared `Area[0]`.

- **Layout:** each page's copy is named by its own page.
- **Data:** each copy binds apart, so a value typed on page 3 stays on page 3. A field bound with `match="global"` or an explicit `bind ref` still binds as instance 0 on every page, so it shows one shared value (XFA 3.3 p. 271).
- **Scripts:** the live form has one page-area node per page made from it. A button repeated on every page runs its click script as the copy that was clicked.
- **Stale events:** a script can lay the form out again during opening, after the events to run were listed. An event whose object is gone (for example, a page the form no longer fills) is now skipped. Before, it ran with `this` at the form's root. Two questionnaires from the Canton of Aargau (*Anhörung Geldspielgesetz* and *Anhörung Teilrevision Landwirtschaftsgesetz*) have a master-page button whose initialize script sets `this.presence = "hidden"`. With per-page nodes, that script hid the whole form, so 3 pages became 1. Skipping the gone event keeps them at 3 pages.

Fixes #5365

### How common

Fixes the 52 forms (21.2%) in the issue: the copies on later pages keep their own values. On DD 214, the four "Page" boxes read `1`, `2`, `3`, `4` after save and reopen (main: `1`, `1`, `1`, `1`).

### Tests

- `page_master_content_repeated_on_each_page_has_its_own_som_index` (`crates/xfa/src/tests.rs`): a master page used on three pages gives its field three SOM paths and three data nodes, and a `match="global"` field stays shared. It fails with either the layout half or the data half reverted.

title: M12: a flowed XFA subform in a table cell is as tall as its content (#5367)
author: mtlcl410
body:
### What this changes

A cell of a table row that is a flowed subform (`tb`, `lr-tb`, `rl-tb` or `table` layout) is now as tall as its content, even when it gives a height. Before, it was as tall as that height. `maxH` still caps it.

Unchanged:
- a positioned cell keeps its height;
- a flowed subform outside a table keeps its height.

This departs from the text of XFA 3.3. A height "fixes the height … of a container" (p. 275), and a row's cells take "their natural sizes" (p. 329). Adobe Acrobat and PDF-XChange Editor both lay such a cell out as tall as its content, and this follows them. On the Dutch *teruggeleiding* form, both end the child's row right after its last question.

`measure`'s content-height calculation (its `None` arm, about 30 lines) moves unchanged into a new `content_height` function, which `measure` calls, so the table code can use it too.

Fixes #5367

### How common

12 of the 245 dynamic forms (4.9%) change; see the issue for the list.
- *Aanvraagformulier omgang*: section 2 starts under its heading on page 2, and the form drops from 11 pages to 10.
- EMA veterinary eAF: 72 → 73 pages. Some of its cells have more content than their height, so they grow.

### Tests

All in `crates/xfa/src/tests.rs`. "Fails" means the test fails with the code fix reverted (`measure.rs` at the merge base, tests kept).

- `a_flowed_subform_in_a_table_cell_is_as_tall_as_its_content` (fails) checks four cases:
  - a flowed cell with `h` is as tall as its content;
  - a positioned cell keeps its `h`;
  - a flowed subform outside a table keeps its `h`;
  - the cell is measured at its column's width, not its own (in a 1in column, a 5in-wide `lr-tb` cell wraps).
- `a_flowed_cell_grows_past_a_small_height_and_keeps_margins_and_max_height` (fails): a flowed cell grows past a 0.2in or zero `h`; its margins count; `maxH` still caps it; a `table`-layout cell is included; a cell spanning two columns is measured at both columns' width.

title: fix(text): a narrow move between two runs is a word gap in text set close
author: nct88
body:
## What this changes

Text extraction, search and copy now break words at a narrow gap that a producer left as a move between two runs, with no space character, in text set close.

SlideOcean's free-font PDFs draw the logo "slide ocean" as two runs with a `Td` move between them. The gap is 5.5 pt (0.12 em at 45 pt), and the line's letters are 1.5 pt apart. A word gap had to be wider than the typical letter gap plus 0.15 em (8.3 pt here), so PdfCraft read "slideocean". pdftotext 4.00, run as an external process, reads "slide ocean".

A gap now also breaks words when it is wider than three times the line's typical letter gap and than 0.1 em of the line height. This only matters for lines set close. Tracked text still goes by the old threshold, because its typical gap is wide.

title: CI: workflows only call craft-common-actions at @main (AGENTS.md; windows-arm64 unpinned)

**Also in this PR:** `windows-arm64.yml` moves from its SHA pin to `@main`. title: M12: a edição de um campo XFA sobrescreve o stream datasets no lugar, sem o deixar órfão (#5155)
author: croquete1
body:
## O que muda

Resolve #5155. A edição de um campo de um formulário XFA estático deixava um stream `xfa:datasets` órfão a cada gravação.

`put_stream` (crates/xfa/src/data/write.rs) só sobrescrevia o stream datasets no lugar quando este era o ObjRef `reuse` ou já se encontrava no overlay. A primeira edição de um stream herdado de uma revisão anterior (reuse `None`, ainda não editado) caía em `doc.add`, que criava um objeto novo, reapontava a entrada `/XFA` e deixava o stream anterior sem referência. Ao longo do ciclo interativo escrever/gravar/escrever/gravar, o ficheiro crescia um pacote `xfa:datasets` morto por cada edição.

O stream datasets é propriedade exclusiva do array `/XFA` (ou é o único stream `/XFA`), pelo que o objeto referenciado passa a ser sempre sobrescrito no lugar quando é indireto, incluindo um proveniente de uma revisão anterior. `reuse` fica subsumido e deixa de ser consultado.

## Como foi verificado

- Teste de regressão `xfa_field_edits_across_saves_do_not_orphan_datasets_streams`: abrir um formulário XFA estático, editar um campo, registar a gravação (que faz rebase e limpa o overlay), editar outro campo e gravar de novo — o ficheiro guardado contém exatamente um stream datasets. Comprovado a falhar antes da correção: reporta 2 streams.
- Correção de `data_ops_of_one_event_are_one_datasets_rewrite`, que afirmava `before + 1` e fixava o comportamento de orfanização em vez do reaproveitamento no lugar; passa a afirmar `before`.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` (pdfcraft-xfa, pdfcraft-engine)
- [x] clippy com `-D warnings` nos crates alterados
- [x] testes nos crates alterados (129 xfa, 50 engine xfa, incluindo o novo teste e o teste de password/datasets)
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` / `assets` — sem alteração de fronteiras de crate nem de assets

## Never-crash

Sem novos `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unsafe`; a alteração é uma simplificação de ramo em `put_stream`, sem nova indexação nem aritmética derivadas de input.

title: M12: uma linha de texto editada alarga o recorte que a delimita, para mostrar uma substituição mais longa (#5207)
author: croquete1
body:
## O que muda

Resolve #5207. Editar uma linha de texto num PDF cujos runs estão delimitados por um retângulo de recorte apertado fazia o texto desaparecer quando a substituição era mais longa do que o original.

Os geradores que compõem a partir de HTML envolvem cada caixa de texto em `q x y w h re W n … BT … Tj ET Q`. `replace_line` reescrevia os operadores de texto mas mantinha o recorte, pelo que a substituição era cortada no limite da caixa.

- **Alargamento do recorte**: quando o recorte em vigor delimita a linha, `replace_line` alarga-o até onde o texto novo termina. Só se aplica a recortes retangulares, na vertical e não invertidos.
- **Verificação de vizinhos**: o recorte não é alargado se outra linha da página, na mesma faixa de altura, começar dentro do espaço que o alargamento ocuparia. Nesse caso o texto novo continua a ser cortado, como antes, em vez de ficar sobreposto ao texto vizinho.
- **Correções de Tz e de fontes Type3** (commits anteriores deste branch): o sentido do avanço com `Tz` negativo e a largura das fontes de substituição passam a ser medidos corretamente.

title: feat(edit): draw non-WinAnsi text in headers, footers and watermarks as Type 3 Inter glyphs
author: so-sai
body:
### What this changes
Currently, Header, Footer, and Watermark tools only support standard WinAnsi fonts. Text with non-Western characters (e.g., Vietnamese, Cyrillic, Greek) is refused. 

This PR implements a generalized Unicode fallback for these tools without relying on pending PRs or embedding full font files:
1. It detects non-WinAnsi text.
2. It normalizes the text from NFD to NFC. (Note: While many IMEs output NFC directly, decomposed NFD text is common when copy-pasting from macOS, web sources, or specific IME settings. Normalizing ensures diacritics render attached).
3. It routes the rendering through the existing Type 3 vector glyph mechanism (`fallback.rs`) using the bundled Inter font.
4. If Inter cannot draw the character (e.g., Han, Emoji), it still refuses with a clear error message naming the specific character.

### Key Architectural Highlights
- **Zero PDF Bloat:** Extracts only the used glyph outlines into a shared Type 3 font object (`Object::Ref`), avoiding the ~412 KB overhead of embedding full TrueType binaries. Our regression test `long_vietnamese_watermark_keeps_file_size_bounded` verifies a <2 KB delta across multiple pages while maintaining full text extraction via `/ToUnicode`.
- **Single Source of Truth for UI & Engine:** Shares `sanitize_mark_text` across `ui-egui` and the engine to handle NFC, CRLF, tabs, and NBSP consistently, preventing preview/apply sizing mismatches.
- **AEC & Engineering Symbols:** Includes verified regression tests for standard technical symbols (`±`, `≤`, `≥`, `Ø`).
- **Upstream-aligned:** Reuses the existing `draw_shaped` / Type 3 infrastructure in `crates/edit/src/text/fallback.rs` with zero new crate dependencies (the locked `unicode-normalization` is already in the workspace).
- **Atomic Replacement:** By rebasing onto the latest `main`, this PR now automatically benefits from the transactional mark replacement recently added in #5704. If an error occurs mid-replacement, the document is safely rolled back.

title: fix(ui): selecting in an unchanged paragraph lands on the words the page shows (refs #5185)
author: TiagoCK
body:
## What this changes

Refs #5185 (its symptom: highlighting text in Edit mode shows it in a different font). Found on an
OCR'd problem set: a LaTeX PDF that iOS flattened to images, which Edit text OCRs on entry.

While a paragraph is unchanged, the page shows its own text and the editor's galley is drawn
unseen; it only places the caret and the selection (#3952). When the editor can't load the PDF's
font (an OCR layer, or a Type 1 program such as LaTeX embeds), that galley is laid out in a
stand-in face, and `editor_job` stretches each run to its width by spreading the difference
between its letters as extra letter spacing. Two things went wrong:

- **The selection drifted.** The spacing also fell on the space after each run, and a one-letter
  run ("a") took its whole difference there. Every word boundary drifted a little, and the error
  accumulated along the row. On the OCR'd sentence (23 runs, one per word, at OCR-estimated sizes
  from 9.0 to 15.6 pt), a drag over "kind" selected "of a".
- **Selecting showed the stand-in text.** egui recolours selected glyphs with
  `selection.stroke.color`, so the unseen stand-in glyphs were painted over the page in the
  selection colour, on an opaque fill: a serif paragraph turned sans when highlighted.

Now:

- **`place_on_source_words`** (`edit_text_ui/layout.rs`) puts each word's unseen glyphs across that word's box on the page. The box is the run's `ink` box when the run's words and ink boxes pair up, and otherwise the run's `rect` spanning all its words. Within a word the stand-in's
  proportions are kept, and the spaces fill the gaps between words. It runs only when the paragraph is unchanged and upright (`rotation` under 0.5°). A row with a character it can't place, or with boxes out of reading order, keeps its layout as before.
- **While the paragraph is unchanged** (`overlay`), the selection paints no glyphs (a transparent
  `selection.stroke.color`) and its fill is a tint (`gamma_multiply(0.45)`), so the page's ow…

title: M12: a picture an XFA form links is drawn from the PDF's XFAImages name tree (#5392)
author: mtlcl410
body: ### What this changes A template's `` with no picture written into it is now looked up in the PDF's `/Names /XFAImages` name tree, by the URI the template writes (XFA 3.3 pp. 257–258), and drawn. Before, it was left out. - **Where it's looked up:** only in that name tree. A link is never followed outside the file. The spec warns: "XFA processors using untrusted forms should only resolve URIs within the package." - **When it's looked up:** after the template is read and before it is laid out. This happens both when the form opens (`render_into`) and when the template is read again (`template_of`), so a picture keeps its size in the layout. - **What's covered:** draws, field values and captions, on the body pages and on the master pages. - **What isn't:** a link the file holds nothing for stays out, with the same warning as before. The new code is `crates/xfa/src/linked_images.rs`. `Value::Image` now keeps the `href` it was linked by. Fixes #5392 ### How common - 12 of the 245 dynamic forms (4.9%) now show the pictures they link; see the issue for the list. - UNLV's *Administrative Faculty Annual Evaluation Form*: the UNLV logo is back in the heading of page 1. ### Tests - `a_linked_picture_is_drawn_from_the_pdfs_xfa_images` (`crates/xfa/src/tests.rs`): - a form with two linked pictures, one held in a split name tree (under `Kids`) and one not held; - the held one gets its bytes and is written as an image (with its soft mask); - the other stays out, with one warning. - With the lookup switched off, the test fails. - `a_hostile_xfa_images_tree_is_walked_once_and_gives_nothing`: - three hostile trees: `Kids` that lead back to themselves, a name that isn't a string, and a name for something that isn't a stream; - none hangs or panics, and no picture is drawn.…

title: M3: the GPU device starts with far less memory: 65,536 bindings and small memory blocks (#5355, #5400)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Two settings for the GPU device PdfCraft creates. Each sizes memory that is reserved when the device is created, before anything uses it. Both are in `configure_gpu` in `apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`, in the descriptor closure it installs.

1. **Part of #5355: the descriptor heap.** On Direct3D 12, wgpu allocates a descriptor heap for every binding the device may hold. wgpu's default limit is 1,000,000 and PdfCraft kept it, because `surface_texture_limits` clamps to the adapter's limits, which are also a million. wgpu's own documentation of `max_non_sampler_bindings` warns about this on integrated GPUs. The device now asks for at most `MAX_NON_SAMPLER_BINDINGS` = 65,536 (`binding_limits`, applied after `surface_texture_limits`).
2. **Part of #5400: the memory hint.** wgpu's default `MemoryHints::Performance` starts the device's suballocation pools at 128 MiB of GPU memory and 64 MiB of upload memory, nearly empty at startup. The device now uses `MemoryHints::MemoryUsage` (`MEMORY_HINTS`). Its pools start at 8 and 4 MiB and double as they fill, up to 64 and 32 MiB (wgpu-hal's `AllocationSizes::from_memory_hints`). Only Direct3D 12 and Vulkan read this hint.

Not covered: #5355's duplicate system-font buffers (`system_fonts.rs`, also being changed by #5132 and #4832), #5400's allocator telemetry, and #5417 (unselected adapters kept alive).

## How you verified it

Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (19045), Rust 1.99.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.150. This PC has an AMD RX 7900 XT and an AMD integrated GPU; `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low` makes the app use the integrated one. All runs used portable debug builds on a one-page PDF, with private bytes read from Windows 10 s after launch, two runs each:

title: fix(edit): an edited OCR phrase under its scan image is drawn on top (#3973)
author: KenM76
body:
fix(edit): an edited OCR phrase under its scan image is drawn on top (#3973)

## What this changes

Fixes #3973. Fixes #5387.

Some OCR tools write the invisible text layer (`3 Tr`) first and draw the opaque page image after it. The sample in #5387 is one: the OCR text, then a form XObject that paints the full-page scan. Edit text rewrote the phrase where its text was, so the paper-coloured cover and the new visible text were painted under the scan. The edit was saved (text extraction and search find it), but nothing showed on the page. Typing a line break (the multi-line case in the report) goes through the styled path, which had the same problem.

Now, when the rewritten paragraph was invisible and something painted after it covers it (an image or form XObject whose visible box overlaps the paragraph's, or any inline image or shading):

- the cover and the new text go on top of the page, in their own `q`/`Q` (`place_tagged`, tagged `Edited`);
- they are drawn from the initial graphics state with the paragraph's CTM;
- only the state that the following text expects stays where the paragraph was.

Both rewrite paths do this (single style in `rewrite_block_from`, styled rows in `rewrite_styled_block`). An OCR layer drawn over its scan, the usual case, is rewritten in place as before, so the reading order of the page's text does not change.

Not addressed here: #2413 and #3836 (glyphless OCR fonts) are about which font the edit is drawn in, not about paint order.

title: M10: Recognize text finds small print on large pages (tiled detection)
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

Recognize text now finds small print on large, dense pages (newspapers, small print, blurred photos).

The ocrs detection model reads a fixed 600 × 800 pixel input, so ocrs shrinks every page to that size before detecting words. A full page at 300 dpi (2480 × 3508) is shrunk about four times, and small letters disappear. With this change:

- **When (size):** an axis is cut in two when the page is at least twice the detector's input along it (width ≥ 1200 px, height ≥ 1600 px for the ocrs models). Any full page at 300 dpi becomes 2 × 2 tiles; a landscape page may become 2 × 1. The input size is read from the detection model when it loads. Pages below that size (72 to 150 dpi renders, screenshots) are read exactly as before and cost nothing extra.
- **When (text size):** a page that passes the size rule is tiled only if its text is small once the page is shrunk to the detector's input, decided by a cheap pixel signal, the **line pitch** (`crates/ocr/src/pitch.rs`). The page is box-averaged to a grey copy of at most 1600 px a side and cut into a 6 × 6 grid of blocks. In each block, the ink is summed per pixel row, the slow trend (shading, pictures) is removed with a moving average, and the autocorrelation is taken. The block autocorrelations are averaged, and the first strong peak is the pitch. Lines in columns that don't line up still agree on the period, and blank blocks are skipped. The same runs on pixel columns for sideways pages, and the axis with the stronger peak wins. The pitch is converted to detector pixels (pitch × 800 / page height). The rule:
  - pitch **under 9 detector pixels**: tile;
  - ink but **no clear line spacing** (no autocorrelation peak above 0.05): tile, because the measurement showed these pages (blurred, creased, oblique or moiré photos) gain on average;
  - large print, and blank pages: detect whole, as before.
  It costs 6.6 ms per page on average (median 5.1 ms, max 45 ms) and reads every pixel once.
- **How:** tile…

title: Headers, footers and text watermarks draw Cyrillic and Greek instead of refusing them
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Add header and footer and Add watermark refused any line with a character outside WinAnsiEncoding. So a footer like `Страница <<1>> из <<n>> / Page <<1>> of <<n>>` could not be added at all, though the dialog previewed it. #2107 made the dialog refuse it before OK. This makes it work.

A line the chosen standard face can't draw is now drawn in the bundled Inter face (`pdfcraft_fonts::document_latin_fonts`), when Inter has every character of it. Upstream already documents Inter as "the face for Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text written into PDFs", so I take Greek too, not only Cyrillic. The same rule also takes the Latin letters WinAnsi lacks, such as Polish U+0141 or Czech U+0159. Every build has Inter, so this needs no craft-fonts.

- Lines the standard face can draw are drawn exactly as before: same face, same operators, nothing embedded. A run with only such lines writes the same content as today.
- Inter is embedded once per run as a full face (`embedding::embed`), and every marked page names that one Type0 font, as `PCFull<n>` (the name `embed` gives a full face, so later embeddings on the page recognise it). Update reuses the copy the first page already has. Header, footer and watermark runs on the same pages share it too.
- Centred and right-aligned lines, underlines and the fitted watermark size use Inter's widths for an Inter line.
- A tab is drawn as a space and a soft hyphen as a hyphen, as the standard faces draw them. Inter has no glyph for either.
- A line with Thai is left to the Thai face #6632 added: its Thai from that face, the rest in the standard face, as on `main`. A Thai line and a Cyrillic line can share one mark. Cyrillic or Greek on the same line as Thai is refused, as the Thai path draws the rest of its line in WinAnsi.
- Text Inter can't draw either (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew) is still refused, before anything changes. The refusal now names the character neither face draws (the first Chinese character in `Бележка:` followed by…

title: Create PDF from text takes Cyrillic and Greek, and reports no longer escape them
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Create PDF from text sets the text in Helvetica with WinAnsiEncoding. A text file with any character outside it was refused, so a Russian or Greek `.txt` file could not be converted at all. That covers Create > PDF from file, Create from clipboard text, Create multiple files, a `.txt` added to Combine or Insert pages, and the `doc_create` and `doc_create_multiple` tools. A comment summary or compare report that quoted such text wrote each of its letters as `[U+XXXX]`.

Now, text Helvetica can't draw is set, whole, in the bundled Inter face (`pdfcraft_fonts::document_latin_fonts`) when Inter has every character of it. Upstream documents Inter as the face for Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text written into PDFs, and every build has it.

- Text Helvetica can draw is set exactly as before: same font object, same operators, same bytes.
- Text set in Inter keeps the page size, margins, line height, tab width and form feeds. Lines wrap by Inter's widths, with the same `wrap_with` and the same pagination code. Inter is embedded once as a full face (`embedding::embed`) and every page names it as `/F1`.
- A soft hyphen is drawn as a hyphen, as Helvetica draws it. Inter has no glyph for it.
- Text Inter can't draw either (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai) is still refused by `from_text`. The refusal now names the first character neither face draws, with its line, and not the first one Helvetica can't draw. `from_text_escaped` escapes such text exactly as before, Cyrillic included, with the same `ESCAPED_NOTE`.

The changes are in `crates/create`: a small `text_font` module and hooks in `from_text`, `from_text_escaped` and `set_text`. The doc comments of `Session::create_from_text` and `create_report`, the `crates/create` README, the `doc_create` tool description and a comment in `assemble.rs` said Western European only; they now say what is taken.

I found no upstream issue for this.
