title: M12: um campo XFA liga-se ao seu nó de dados dentro de um contentor que o template não tem (#5337)
author: croquete1
body:
## O que muda

Resolve #5337. Um formulário preenchido contra um esquema XML normalizado (UBL, por exemplo) tem um Data DOM com mais estrutura do que o template: os campos ficam dentro de um contentor (um `RootSub`) que o template não tem. A independência de dados do XFA (XFA 3.3, "Principles of Data Binding") exige que o campo se ligue a esse nó de dados existente, mantendo a estrutura própria dos dados e os valores que nenhum campo liga.

Ao escrever o valor de um campo, `merge_values` comparava cada segmento do caminho de dados apenas com os filhos diretos, pelo que um caminho como `form1/TextField1` cujo nó de dados é `form1/RootSub/TextField1` não era encontrado; era acrescentado um `form1/TextField1` plano ao lado do contentor, duplicando os dados e deixando o nó real desatualizado.

`merge_values` passa a ligar-se, quando o segmento-folha não tem irmão direto com o seu nome, ao único nó de valor inequívoco abaixo do elemento correspondido mais profundo. O recurso é deliberadamente estreito: apenas um único descendente de valor correspondente e apenas para a folha, de modo que um formulário cujos dados correspondem ao template (todos os casos atuais) fica inalterado.

## Como foi verificado

- Teste de regressão `a_field_binds_to_its_data_node_inside_a_container_the_template_lacks`: um valor escrito para `form1/TextField1` atualiza o `form1/RootSub/TextField1` existente no lugar, não acrescenta nó plano e mantém o `TextField3` não ligado. Comprovado a falhar antes da correção (o nó plano é acrescentado).
- Ponta a ponta no ficheiro do relatório, via `pdfcraft-cli`: preencher um campo e gravar produz `form1/RootSub/TextField1 = XX` no lugar, sem nó duplicado e com o `TextField3` preservado.

title: M4: bookmarks run their actions as links do (organize.bookmark-actions)
author: Ethunxxx
body:
## What this changes

A bookmark's action (`/A`, ISO 32000-2 §12.3.3 Table 151) was read only for a `/D` key, whatever its type. Two things went wrong:

- **A bookmark into another PDF went to a page of this one.** A remote go-to's `/D` names a page or destination of the *other* file (§12.6.4.3, page numbers rather than page references), but the outline reader took it as this document's. `page_of` accepts bare integers for lenient local destinations, so `/A << /S /GoToR /F (other.pdf) /D [4 /Fit] >>` jumped to page 5 here. `bookmark_list` and Split ▸ by top-level bookmarks (`pdfcraft_organize::outline::item_dest`) read it the same way. A string destination was looked up among *this* file's named destinations.
- **Every other action did nothing.** A bookmark that opens a web address, launches a PDF or changes layers had no page, so clicking it did nothing and showed no message. Links handle all of these.

Now bookmarks run their actions the way links do:

- **`pdfcraft-render`**: `link()`'s action parsing moved into `Inspector::action_target`, which links and bookmarks share. `OutlineItem` gains `action: Option<LinkTarget>` for a bookmark whose action goes nowhere in this document. Only a go-to's `/D` gives `page`/`view`. An action with no `/S` at all is still read as the go-to its `/D` suggests, as before. Bookmark web addresses are spent from the same text budget as links' (`MAX_LINK_ATTACHMENT_TEXT_BYTES`).
- **`pdfcraft-organize`**: `item_dest` takes an action's `/D` only for `/S /GoTo`, or an untyped action; an indirect `/S` is resolved.
- **`pdfcraft-ui-egui`**: clicking such a bookmark sends `Nav::Action` through the canvas's existing `follow_link`. A web address asks first (the same "A link wants to open…" prompt), a remote go-to or Launch-PDF opens that file at its page (absolute paths still ask), a layer change applies, and other actions get the usual "unsupported action" notice. No new strings.

title: M8: secure redacted copy: every page flattened to pixels, optionally required by a host's policy.json
author: henrikkvamme
body:
## What this changes

Applying redactions in place removes what the content interpreter finds under each mark, and then cleans a list of other places where a copy of the text can be: metadata, tags, `/ActualText`, patterns, layers and more. A place that is not on the list stays in the file, and the check after the apply runs the same interpreter, so it has the same blind spots. Many of the open redaction issues are of this type, for example #3646 (hidden layers), #3647 (tiling patterns), #3122 (`/ActualText`), #2448 (Info and XMP) and #3999 (references to removed objects).

This PR adds a second way to apply redactions. It does not depend on finding every hiding place: a **secure redacted copy**.

1. The renderer draws every page of the source with its form fields and links, without comments, with reading colours off. From the same reading of the file it also reads each drawn page's Redact annotations (`PageRenderer::page_redactions`).
2. Each mark's rectangles are painted straight into the pixels of its page, through the transform the renderer drew that page with (`PageRenderer::page_geometry`: crop box, `/Rotate` and `/UserUnit` as the renderer resolved them), grown by 2 device pixels. The colour is the mark's `/IC`, or white for a mark without one.
3. A new document is built from those pictures only: one RGB image per page, at the page's displayed size, with an invisible OCR text layer when OCR is installed.
4. The document is read back and refused unless it holds only what step 3 writes: no `/Info`, metadata, outline, annotations, form fields, structure tree, layers, other objects or other revisions.

One reader decides both what is drawn and where the boxes go. Nothing in the source is interpreted a second time to place a box, and no page is matched between two readers. So inherited resources, colour spaces, fonts, page-tree shapes, page order and object resolution cannot move a box away from what was drawn.

The source document and its marks do not change. The…

Dragging a paragraph (Edit text & images) or a selected object past the edge of its page moved the content outside its crop box. The page clipped it, so it disappeared, while the blue box was still drawn over the next page. Dragging it back brought it back.

title: perf(render): undo PNG predictors a byte row at a time (#5430)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5430.

The renderer decodes images through the vendored hayro-syntax. Its `apply_predictor` undid PNG predictors (10–15) through the bit-level `BitChunks`/`BitWriter` readers that TIFF predictor 2 needs, one sample at a time, although PNG filters are defined on bytes (ISO 32000-2 §7.4.4.4; PNG specification §9). Each image paid that cost on every byte, whatever its row filters.

Now PNG predictors are undone by `unfilter_png`: a row at a time on byte slices, with the filter type read per row and the left, up and up-left bytes carried as slices. TIFF predictor 2 keeps the old path. The PNG branch of the old loop and the `Up`, `Avg` and `Paeth` predictor types it alone used are removed. This is vendored hayro-syntax patch 35 in `vendor/README.md`; like the others, it is meant for hayro upstream.

Unfiltering one 993 × 936 RGB image (the issue's image size), release build, mean of 20 runs on random bytes:

| Row filter | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Up | 62 ms | 3 ms |
| Sub | 64 ms | 5–6 ms |
| Average | 71 ms | 6.5 ms |
| Paeth | 63 ms | 16 ms |

These are the predictor step alone; I have not timed whole pages against MuPDF or PDFium. The timing was a throwaway `#[ignore]` test calling `apply_predictor` on that image (`cargo test --release --manifest-path vendor/hayro-syntax/Cargo.toml --lib <name> -- --ignored --nocapture`); it is not part of this PR.

**It also changes what some images look like.** When a pixel is not a whole number of bytes and is more than one byte (three 4-bit samples, five 2-bit ones), a row of odd width ends part-way through a pixel. The bit-level path dropped the last byte of each such filtered row, so every later row started a byte early and the picture came out sheared, with zeros at the end. That byte is now kept.

title: M2: a JPX image on a rotated page draws instead of crashing (#3884)
author: jweaver3
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3884.

`Renderer::image_draw_size` (vendored `hayro`) produced the size hint passed to `hayro-jpeg2000` by mapping the image corners `(w, 0)` and `(0, h)` as *points*, so the translation was included. On a `/Rotate 90` page (common in Acrobat Paper Capture scans) one corner falls on the device origin, which makes one side of the hint 0. `hayro-jpeg2000` 0.3.5 then computes `image_width / target_width` (`codestream.rs:150`), and the page fails with "renderer crashed on page N: attempt to divide by zero".

The hint is now taken from the transform's linear part: the device length of each image axis, the same lengths the preview tiny-image check already used, now computed once. Each side is at least 1. The patch is recorded in `vendor/README.md`.

This supersedes the guard in #1883 and does not depend on the `hayro-jpeg2000` 0.4.1 bump in #2309. Both of those PRs are open and conflict with `main`. If #2309 lands, this fix still corrects the hint itself, not just the division.

title: Reject 9-byte DER INTEGER with non-zero leading byte in Tlv::u64
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

`Tlv::u64` in `crates/sign/src/der.rs` (lines 214-219) silently truncated a DER INTEGER of 9 bytes with a non-zero leading byte. It accepted up to 9 content bytes, because a leading 0x00 may precede 8 value bytes, but it never checked that a 9-byte value starts with 0x00. For example, 2^64+5 passed the check, and the fold shifted the high byte out of the u64, so the call returned `Ok(5)`.

`Tlv::u64` now returns an error when the content is 9 bytes long and the first byte is not 0. A valid 9-byte encoding of 2^63 still parses.

No existing issue is linked.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `editing::a_custom_property_whose_name_the_tools_refuse_is_listed_and_left_alone`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Never-crash

Every PDF, script, MCP call, settings file and keystroke is untrusted input (`AGENTS.md` §4).

- [ ] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests, unless it is provably infallible with a comment saying why

title: M3: Copy Image and Cut Image put the picture on the clipboard in the web build (view.copy-image)
author: BrockDawg
body:
## What this changes

In the web build, right-click ▸ **Copy Image** and **Cut Image** on a picture refused with "the web version can't put images on the clipboard yet; use Save Image As".
They now put the picture's own pixels, at full resolution, on the browser clipboard as a PNG, as the desktop build already does through `arboard`.

eframe's web runner already writes egui's `OutputCommand::CopyImage` to the clipboard (`navigator.clipboard.write` with an `image/png` item), so the wasm branch of `copy_page_image` now queues the picture with `Context::copy_image` on the app's stored frame context (`self.ctx`) instead of refusing.
No new crate, no new `web-sys` feature, no JS.

- On a page that is not a secure context, browsers forbid clipboard writes and eframe would only log the failure, so the user would see "copied" with nothing copied. That case is refused up front: "the browser only allows copying on a secure (https) page; use Save Image As". A refused copy makes Cut remove nothing (`cut_page_image` already returns early when the copy fails).
- The pixels go in through `ColorImage::from_rgba_premultiplied`, which keeps the engine's straight RGBA byte for byte, because eframe encodes the image's bytes into the PNG as they are. `from_rgba_unmultiplied` would premultiply them and darken every translucent pixel (CodeRabbit caught this; third commit).
- The pixel buffer is checked against `w × h × 4` (checked arithmetic) before that constructor, which asserts it; a mismatch is an error, not a panic.
- The native branch, `copy_page_image`'s signature and `canvas.rs` are untouched; desktop behaviour is unchanged.

## How you verified it

All in a Linux codespace, rustc/cargo 1.99.1, scoped to `pdfcraft-ui-egui`, first on `67d4f181` (with `main` at that commit as the baseline) and again after rebasing onto `fa5f9f8c`; the tested files' git hashes equal the committed ones.

title: fix(edit): an edited OCR phrase is drawn at one size (refs #3313)
author: TiagoCK
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3313 (its size half: "each word comes out at a different size and width"). Found on the
same OCR'd problem set as #5390: a LaTeX PDF that iOS flattened to images, which Edit text OCRs on
entry.

Recognize text sizes each word on its own: the word box's height divided by a guess at how much
of the em its letters fill, cap height, x-height or a descender (`ink_extent`,
`crates/ocr/src/lib.rs`). When the scan isn't set in Helvetica, one phrase's words come out several
points apart; one line of the problem set ran from 9 to 15.6 pt. Nobody sees this while the layer
is invisible, but once the phrase is edited, both the editor and the saved text drew every word at
its own size.

Now an OCR phrase is set in one size, the median of its words' sizes, as the outline in #3313
suggests:

- **`TextBlock::size`** of an invisible block with several runs is that median, not the first
  word's. `TextBlock::phrase_size()` returns it for invisible blocks and `None` for visible ones.
  The Format panel shows it too.
- **Styled rewrite** (`rewrite_styled_block`): every run defaults to the phrase size, and each
  run's width calibration is scaled by its own size over the phrase's, so every word still spans
  the box the scan shows it in (`a_rewritten_ocr_phrase_keeps_its_word_widths` still passes).
- **Single-style rewrite** (a new family or bold): the phrase size replaces the first word's.
- **Inline editor** (`editor_job`): while typing, every word is laid out at the phrase size, so
  the draft matches what Apply writes.

Visible text is unchanged: `phrase_size()` is `None` for it.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit -p pdfcraft-engine -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0

Everything after it is unchanged: the same gates (dialogs, palette, a text field with the keyboard, Organize Pages, Prepare Form), the same clipboard read and the same Add Image path.

title: fix(compare): visual compare no longer overflows on declared sizes its buffers cannot hold
author: jayzed80
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft_compare::visual_regions` computed pixel offsets with unchecked `u32` multiplication. A damaged or hostile render that declares huge dimensions (for example `u32::MAX` x `u32::MAX`) with a short buffer panicked with "attempt to multiply with overflow" (debug) or wrapped and looped (release). It now returns no regions when either buffer is smaller than its declared `width * height * 4`.

author: charlieruk
body:
## What this changes

This is the UI follow-up to #5208 (Markdown export for #1595), as agreed with @AdrianTM on that PR.

#5208 added the Markdown export to `doc_export_office`, but the only way to reach it was headlessly, with a `.md` path. This PR adds:

It goes through the existing `export_office_dialog` with `OfficeFormat::Markdown`, so it saves the same way Word, HTML and RTF export do: a save panel named `{document}.md`, and a download on the web. It needs the copy permission, like the other exports.
- **Menu entries.** It is listed in **File ▸ Export** after HTML, and in **All tools ▸ Export a PDF** as "Markdown (.md)".
- **Translations.** The "Export to Markdown…" label is translated in all 34 catalogues, following each catalogue's "Export to RTF…" row. "Markdown" is kept as a name. Turkish, Hungarian, Kazakh, Korean and Polish needed a different case ending or "format" wording.
- **Parity.** In `create.export-markdown`, the command and the new UI test are added, and "a menu item" is removed from the missing list. Its status stays `partial`, because images, lists, links and text colour are still missing.

title: M10: read text set in a negative font size as lines and paragraphs
author: charlieruk
body:
## What this changes

Some producers draw text with a negative font size. A TI application note does this, for example. The page's CTM is flipped (`1 0 0 -1 0 0 cm`), the font size is negative (`/F6 -10 Tf`, `-100 Tz`), so the glyphs read upright again, and every word is placed with its own `Tm` + `Tj`. This is valid PDF, and it renders correctly.

PdfCraft read such a line's size with its sign (`-10`). Every grouping threshold multiplied by the size then failed, for example `gap < size * 1.5` in `text_regions/grouping.rs`:
- **Each word became its own block.** `text_paragraphs` listed one paragraph per word.
- **Word, HTML, RTF and Markdown export were unreadable.** They put one word per paragraph, and `level()` (`size >= body * 1.6`, with negatives) made most longer words `#` headings. Word also got negative font sizes.

Markdown export of that note, before and after:

```markdown

The                                |
# assembler                        |  The assembler and link step create object files in common object
and                                |  file format (COFF). COFF is an implementation of an object file
# link                             |  format of the same name that was developed by AT\&T for use on …
```

**Fixes:**
- `text/interp.rs`: a line's size is the magnitude (`ts.size.abs()`), in user space as before.
- With paragraphs now joined, rewriting one exposed a second bug. Converting a size in points back to text space dropped the source's sign, so the rewrite wrote a positive `Tf` under the flipped CTM. The text was then drawn **mirrored**, running left from where it started. This affected:
  - every mixed-style rewrite (`text_regions/styled.rs`, `size_of`). On `main` the same code turned `-10` into `max(0.1)`, so it drew 0.1 pt text there instead;

author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2563 (and its duplicates #3829 and #5447).

PdfCraft now takes every craft-libs crate at `04aa1703`, the revision `craft-update` already uses, instead of `e11f9d9a`. Among the crates that moved, only craft-print's code differs between the two:

title: sign: the GOST R 34.11-2012 digest (Streebog, RFC 6986)
author: Bra1nZ
body:
Preparation for GOST signing support (PKCS#11 layer is in #4968; the overall design is summarized in #5468).

**What this adds** — `sign::gost_digest`, a self-contained module computing the GOST R 34.11-2012 digest ("Streebog") in both widths:

- `digest_256(&[u8]) -> [u8; 32]` and `digest_512(&[u8]) -> [u8; 64]`;
- the 8×256 multiplication tables of the linear transform are derived at compile time (`const fn`) from the standard's substitution π, permutation τ and matrix A, so the source carries the RFC's numbers instead of 16 KiB of precomputed tables;
- iteration constants are written exactly as RFC 6986 §6.5 prints them and converted to the little-endian block order at compile time.

**Why include the digest at all** — the certified signing operation stays in the token (we do not implement СКЗИ); but the digest is a byte-level format the token's GOST mechanisms take as input to `C_Sign`, and the name CMS `digestAlgorithm` refers to. The module is unused for now; the following PRs wire it into `DigestAlg` and the PKCS#11 GOST detection.

**Tests** — the official RFC 6986 vectors (M1 and M2, both 256 and 512 bits), plus the empty-message digests and an ASCII message, all cross-checked against an independent pure-Python reference implementation (pygost) that passes the same RFC suite.

title: M11: Monochrome Images averages indexed black-and-white images, the palette saying which sample is dark (optimize.downsample-images)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Builds on #5461, which it merges rather than rebases onto, so review it against that branch. PDF Optimizer ▸ Monochrome Images ▸ Downsample now averages indexed black-and-white images too, with the palette deciding which sample is dark.

#5426 (d7f3e671) left indexed images at their resolution rather than guess which sample is dark, and pinned that with "Unknown palette polarity is never guessed". Reading the palette makes it known rather than guessed:
- `dark_is_one` maps samples 0 and 1 through the decode array to palette entries, rounded and clipped to `hival` (ISO 32000-2 §8.9.5.2).
- It compares how light those two entries are (`lightness`): the grey value, or Rec. 601 luma over `DeviceRGB`.
- Only `DeviceGray` and `DeviceRGB` bases count, since there the palette's values are the colour. Under `/DefaultGray` or `/DefaultRGB`, no polarity is asked for, as before.
- The table may be a string or a stream, given directly or by reference, of at most 4 KiB as read and 16 KiB of raw data. It is read only for an image about to be resampled. Images share a table, so without this 1,000 images sharing 16 MiB of table took 16 to 60 s with none of them resampled.
- `/Indexed` may be given by reference, and the base as `[/DeviceRGB]`.
- An indexed image used beyond the page and form resources the optimizer reads (an annotation's appearance, a pattern, another image's `/Alternates`) keeps its resolution, since default colour spaces in force there could change which entry is darker. Grey stays out of that check: its sample 0 stays dark, and #5426's rule is unchanged.
- An image with a colour key keeps its resolution, grey included. The key can hide the dark sample a tie goes to, which lost a thin visible rule: a white rule on a hidden black went from 255 to the backdrop's 128.
- These still say nothing, so the image keeps its resolution:

title: M11: Monochrome Images reads JBIG2 scans: averaged like any, and stored again as JBIG2 (optimize.mono-compression)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Builds on #5471 (which builds on #5461), which it merges rather than rebases onto, so review it against that branch. **#5491 has to land before this one:** this PR makes the optimizer decode JBIG2, and #5491 is what bounds the memory and the time that takes. PDF Optimizer ▸ Monochrome Images now handles JBIG2 scans.

#5461 made `Document::decoded_image` read JBIG2, with the page exactly the image's size. It kept the optimizer's monochrome step away from JBIG2 until that step could store JBIG2 again. This commit lets it, treating JBIG2 the way it treats Group 4:

- **Above the threshold:** a JBIG2 image is averaged like any black-and-white image. It is stored as the smallest of what the chosen compression may store. Under Retain it is stored as JBIG2 again, keeping its kind of compression.
- **Not resampled:** it is stored again as the compression asks, but only when that is smaller.
  - A generic region becomes symbols when JBIG2 is asked for.
  - JBIG2 behind ASCIIHex is stored again alone, as Group 4 where that is smaller.
- **Symbol-coded scans:** a symbol-coded scan (as jbig2enc usually writes) that is averaged loses its exact repeats. It often comes out larger, and then stays as it is. The README and parity note say so.
- **Globals and page size:**
  - A JBIG2 image stored again refers to no `/JBIG2Globals`.
  - One whose JBIG2 page isn't the image's size isn't read, and stays as it is.

Also updated:
- the `doc_optimize` description: under Retain a JBIG2 image stays JBIG2, and JBIG2 images are among those stored again;
- `docs/architecture.md` and the `core.image-filters` note: the optimizer is now among JBIG2's readers;
- the `optimize.downsample-images` evidence.

title: M11: the monochrome test's scan is smaller as Group 4 with either Flate backend (xtask ci on Windows)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

`cargo xtask ci` fails on Windows at current `main` (`fa5f9f8c`), in one test:

```
FAIL pdfcraft-optimize::optimize monochrome_images_keep_what_they_should
assertion `left == right` failed: the scan: Group 4 is smaller
  left: Some("FlateDecode")
 right: Some("CCITTFaxDecode")
```

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize` passes, so the failure only shows when the whole workspace is built, as in `xtask ci`.

**Cause.** On Windows, craft-update depends on `zip` with its `deflate` feature, which turns on flate2's `zlib-rs` backend (`cargo tree --workspace -e features -i flate2`). Features are unified across the workspace, so `pdfcraft-filters`' Flate is then zlib-rs rather than miniz_oxide. The test's synthetic scan sat between the two backends:

| The scan's edges | Flate, miniz_oxide | Flate, zlib-rs | Group 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ragged by five samples (`main`) | 8,300 bytes | 7,345 bytes | 7,557 bytes |
| ragged by four samples (this PR) | 7,187 bytes | 6,238 bytes | **5,468 bytes** |

With zlib-rs, Flate was smaller, and the optimizer rightly kept it. Only Windows is affected: `zlib-rs` is on for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`, and off for Linux, macOS and FreeBSD.

**Fix.** The scan's band edges are ragged by up to four samples instead of five. Group 4 then codes every edge relative to the row above (a move of at most three), and it is smaller than Flate from either backend. The scan stays ambiguous: the optimizer still declines to downsample it, so the Retain half of the test, which expects its 1,200 columns and Flate kept, is unchanged. The test came in with #5426.

As a side effect of the same unification, the Windows app compresses Flate streams with zlib-rs while the other platforms use miniz_oxide. That is harmless, but it is why a size comparison in a test can differ by platform.

## How you verified it

Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (19045), Rust 1.99.1. `cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize -p pdfcraft --test optimize` builds t…

title: M8: a redacted black-and-white scan is stored as Group 4, or JBIG2 again, when smaller (protect.redact-image-pixels)
author: Piohrun
body:

Builds on #5461, which it merges rather than rebases onto, so review it against that branch. Redaction wrote every cleared image as Flate, so a redacted Group 4 or JBIG2 scan page grew several times over until Optimize ran again.

A cleared one-bit image of one component (a scan, as a rule) is now stored as the smallest of the following, counted as stored with its dictionary, since a tiny image can lose by Group 4's parameters:
- Flate;
- CCITT Group 4;
- JBIG2, but only when the image was JBIG2. JBIG2Decode is PDF 1.4, which such a file already is.

How it's stored:
- Both codes are made from the cleared samples, so nothing of the original's code is carried over.
- Rows that Group 4 or JBIG2 can't code (too wide) fall back to Flate.

title: M12: an XFA check box without a width is as wide as its box and caption
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Fixes the radio-button half of #5442: each Yes/No group showed one circle where there should be two.

In that form each choice in a positioned `exclGroup` sets only `minW="20.32mm"`, with no `w`. A field without `w` is growable in width (XFA 3.3, Ch.8 growable objects; Ch.2 field auto-size): it should take its content's width, clamped by minW/maxW. The layouter gave every non-button field without a width all the room left in its container instead. So the first choice stretched to the group's right edge, its box (drawn at the field's right end) landed on the last choice's box, and one hid the other.

A check button without a width is now as wide as its box and widget margins plus its caption: beside the box, the caption's reserve or else its text; above or below, the wider of the two. That width is capped by what is available and clamped by minW/maxW. Other fields still take the available width; this PR doesn't touch them.

The data half of #5442 is separate, and other PRs work on it (#5475, and #2783 for explicit binds). This PR touches only the check-box width, so it doesn't overlap them.

title: M7: a paragraph on a turned page is edited at its own size (#2522)
author: DerKarussellbremser
body:
## What this changes

Addresses #2522. On a page turned a quarter, the inline editor of Edit text & images drew the paragraph several times too large, with its letters on top of each other and a frame far too tall. It happens with every text on such a page, and scans are often stored that way.

The editor took its scale from the box's width on screen over its width in user space. On a page turned a quarter those are different sides of the box, so a word 80 pt long and 17 pt high came out at 4.6 times its size (scale 6.15 instead of 1.33 at 100%), and more on a longer line. The width it spread the letters over came from the same short side, which is why they overlapped.

The editor now reads the source box, rows and baselines in the frame the page is read in, from the page's `/Rotate` and the view's rotation (`PageXform::turn`, `reading_rect`). The letters are spread over the line's length along its own baseline (`TextLine::frame_rect`, now public).

Only the editor changes. The applied edit was already right: after the fix a word edited at each turn kept its place, size and direction when read back.

title: fix(ui): list X.PDF in file pickers on Linux and the BSDs (#5481)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

On Linux and the BSDs, a PDF named `Report.PDF` (or `scan.Pdf`) is now listed in the Open dialog. So are images, fonts, form data and every other picker filter, whatever the letter case of the extension.

rfd 0.17 sends each filter extension to the XDG portal, GTK and Zenity as the glob `*.<ext>`, and those backends match it case-sensitively. So the filter `pdf` hid `Report.PDF`. The new `platform/file_filter.rs` adds `AddFilterAnyCase::add_filter_any_case`. On those platforms it passes each letter as a bracket class (`pdf` → `[pP][dD][fF]`, `jp2` → `[jJ][pP]2`, `*` unchanged). On Windows, macOS and the web, which already ignore case and would read brackets literally, it passes the extension unchanged. Every `add_filter` call in `ui-egui` now goes through it, so a new picker can't miss it by accident.

Fixes #5481

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: 37 crates, no violations (no asset touched)

**Tests.** `platform::file_filter::tests` pins the transform for the case-sensitive platforms (`pdf`, `PDF`, `jp2`, `*`) and the pass-through for the others. **Revert proof:** with `any_case` returning the extension unchanged, `a_case_sensitive_picker_gets_a_glob_matching_every_case` fails (`left: "pdf"`, `right: "[pP][dD][fF]"`). title: fix(render): a JBIG2 page's segments are bounded in what they hold and refer to (hayro-jbig2 patches 5 to 9, hayro-syntax 29)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A few kilobytes of JBIG2 in a PDF could exhaust memory in the viewer, in Export ▸ Images, and in anything else that decodes it. This bounds the memory a JBIG2 decode can take, and the decoding work it can ask for.

Each JBIG2 bitmap was already bounded on its own, by the earlier local patches to the vendored `hayro-jbig2`. Nothing bounded what a page's segments hold for later ones, how far one segment could multiply what they held, or what the parser builds before decoding starts.

The patches in `vendor/hayro-jbig2`:
- **Everything held is counted.** `PageState` now counts the regions, pattern and symbol dictionaries and Huffman tables it stores, with bitmap headers, retained coding contexts and a charge per stored item, and refuses past 64 MiB, two square bitmaps of 16,384 a side, with `OverflowError::RetainedBitmaps`.
- **A dictionary's symbols are counted as they are made.** New and exported symbols count against what the page has left, before each is copied. Counted only once stored, one symbol exported again and again had already taken the memory.
- **A segment may refer to at most 2^20 symbols.** References may repeat, so one segment could name one dictionary 65,535 times. The count is checked before anything is collected.
- **A halftone grid has at most 2^25 cells,** since each cell takes a 4-byte value while it decodes.
- **A pattern dictionary keeps at most 16 MiB of shifted copies, and none that wouldn't fit what the page has left.** They only speed up drawing, so otherwise the patterns are combined the slow way.
- **A custom Huffman table has at most 2^16 lines, and a stream with its globals at most 2^20 segments and 2^22 references.** These are checked as they are read, because both grew before anything counted them.
- **A page past the bounds is refused when the stream is opened.** Callers size their output from the page header before the page bitmap is made.

- **A stream may ask for at most 2^30 units of decoding work,** four of…

title: feat: add Linux smartcard PDF signing and certificate encryption
author: joshuashaffer
body:
## What this changes

Adds Linux PKCS #11 smartcard support alongside existing certificate-file signing. RSA and ECDSA signatures are created on the token; private keys stay on the device. Signing and discovery run in cancellable background jobs, with explicit PIN retry and protection against late results overwriting changed documents or destination files.

Adds certificate-based PDF encryption and token-based opening. PDF data uses AES-128 or AES-256; the card unwraps the recipient content key. Authenticated documents retain their encryption and recipient permissions through rendering, editing, undo/redo, recovery, and saving without retaining a token PIN or writing a decrypted temporary PDF.

Includes engine APIs and CLI/MCP tools: `sign_token_ids`, existing signing tools accepting `pkcs11:` identities, `encryption_token_ids`, `doc_open_token`, and `doc_protect_certificates`. Native PKCS #11 providers run in bounded, disposable worker processes so a provider crash, hang, cancellation, or application exit is recoverable.

Addresses #318 and the direct PKCS #11 option in #238; NSS database integration is not included. Related: #2677 also proposes Linux token signing, together with signature styling. This PR includes certificate encryption/opening, provider process isolation, and background cancellation; signature styling is outside its scope.

title: Text from a justified line keeps one space between words
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

LibreOffice stretches a justified line on both sides of each space glyph: a TJ gap before the space, then the space glyph, then a gap after it. The text reader turns a large TJ gap into a space, and the space glyph added a second one. So every space of a justified LibreOffice line read as two: "Word  next  last". That showed in Edit text and in every export that reads the page's text.

Now a space glyph right after a gap that already read as a space is that space. A gap after the space glyph, and a space glyph with no gap before it, read as before. The same holds down a vertical column.

Where the code is: `show_text` in `crates/edit/src/text/interp.rs` remembers whether the text ends in a space that came from a gap, and drops the leading space of the next glyph's text once.

title: Exports keep italic that a word processor draws by leaning the letters
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

LibreOffice and Word draw italic in a font that has no italic face by leaning the regular letters through the text matrix (LibreOffice writes `1 0 0.2679 1 x y Tm`, 15 degrees). The font's name and flags say nothing about it, so Export to Word, HTML and RTF set those words upright.

- `reading_blocks_checked`, the reading export uses, now marks a line italic when its text matrix and CTM lean its letters right by 5 to 45 degrees. The angle is measured between text space's y axis and the upright of the baseline, so it holds for turned text too. Text leaning left, mirrored text and a degenerate matrix stay upright.
- `export_pages` takes `italic` from that reading as well as from the font's name.
- Copy with formatting (`rich_copy`) already takes `italic` from the same reading, so it keeps such italic too, with no change of its own.
- Editing (`text_blocks`) reads such text as before, as the upright face it is drawn in, so retyping a leaning line doesn't put an italic face on top of the lean.

Related: #4471 draws synthetic italic in the editor by the same kind of lean; this is the reading side, for export.

## How you verified it

**Rebased onto `main` d749fd80 on 2026-11-12.** `main` now reads bold and italic from the font name in `weight_and_slant`, so `compare.rs` reads `italic: b.italic || italic`, as `rich_copy.rs` already does. Re-run on Linux (Rust 1.99.1): fmt and clippy `-D warnings` on pdfcraft-edit and pdfcraft-engine clean; `pdfcraft-edit` lib 600 passed, `pdfcraft-engine` lib 764 passed; both new tests fail again with the change taken out (engine: `left: (Some(false), Some(false))`, `right: (Some(false), Some(true))`). title: Word and HTML exports name the document's language
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Export to Word names no language, so Word checks the spelling of every export as English. A document in any other language comes back with every word underlined, and Word's hyphenation and proofing work against the wrong dictionary.

The PDF already says its language: the catalog's `/Lang` (ISO 32000-2 14.9.2), which Acrobat, LibreOffice and Word itself write, and which the accessibility check's language fix sets. Export now takes it:

- **Word:** when `/Lang` is a well formed language tag, it is the default language of the text (`w:docDefaults/w:rPrDefault`), in the attribute Word keeps for its script: `w:eastAsia` for Chinese, Japanese and Korean, `w:bidi` for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu, `w:val` for everything else. A script subtag decides over the language (`pa-Arab-PK` is right-to-left, `sr-Latn` and `zh-Latn` are not); one inside an extension or private use names no script.
- **HTML:** both HTML exports, with CSS and without (#5938), get `<html lang="...">`, which browsers use for spell checking, speech and hyphenation.
- **No `/Lang`, or a malformed one:** both files are byte for byte what they were. The tag is checked strictly (a primary language of two or three letters, then subtags of one to eight letters or digits; a singleton needs a subtag after it, except inside private use; 255 characters at most, only so a `/Lang` can't write an unbounded string) and escaped anyway.

`docx_with_language`, `html_with_language` and `html_simple_with_language` take the language. `docx`, `html` and `html_simple` keep their signatures and call them with none, so no caller has to change. The engine reads `/Lang` through the existing `initial_view` (organize's catalog reader) in `export_office_checked`, so the `doc_export_office` tool gets it too.

PowerPoint, RTF and Markdown are left as they are: RTF wants a Windows language number (LCID), which would need a table, and PowerPoint sets the language per run.

I found no upstream issue or PR for th…

title: XFA: fields in a match="none" subform read their data from the parent (#5483)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

A subform bound with `<bind match="none"/>` no longer counts as a data scope. The fields it holds now find their values under the parent's data node, which is where Designer writes them (XFA 3.3, "Data Binding", match none). Until now, a form whose sections were all `match="none"` opened blank even though every value was in `xfa:datasets`.

- `Subform` gets an `unbound` flag. The parser sets it from `<bind match="none">`.
- `data_path` skips an unbound subform the same way it already skips an area. The subform's name stays in the SOM path; only the data path leaves it out.
- Reading values, writing them back on save, and layout all go through `data_path`, so all three agree. A fill-and-save puts the value back at the same flat path.
- `split_instance` (engine) returns `None` for an instance of a repeating unbound subform. Such an instance has no data node, and its data path ends at an ancestor; without the guard, `addInstance`/`removeInstance` would copy or remove that ancestor's data group.

Fixes #5483.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-xfa -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa -p pdfcraft-engine`: 130 and 389 + 16 passed

title: fix(cos): read FF FE-BOM text strings as UTF-16LE
author: arielsrossi
body:
## What this changes

GeoPDF layer (OCG) names written by some GIS software carry an `FF FE` BOM over UTF-16LE. `PdfString::to_text` only knew the spec's `FE FF` (UTF-16BE) BOM, so the names fell through to PDFDocEncoding and showed as `ÿþO t h e r 3` in the Layers panel. Fixes #5503

- [x] Slicing uses `as_chunks::<2>()`, so an odd trailing byte is dropped and the decode is lossy, never panics

title: M11: JBIG2 encodes only what its decoder takes: Optimize no longer stores large images PdfCraft can't draw
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Optimize could make a large black-and-white image vanish in PdfCraft, without any warning.

`encode_jbig2` took rows of up to 2^20 samples and any number of them, while `hayro-jbig2`, which draws and reads these streams, takes 65,535 on a side and 2^28 samples. The optimizer doesn't read back what it stores. So with Monochrome Images set to JBIG2, a black-and-white image (1-bit, or packed to 1 bit) with a side of 65,536 or more, and under the optimizer's 80 million pixels, was replaced, whenever JBIG2 came out smaller, by a JBIG2 stream PdfCraft's decoder refuses, and was reported as recompressed. PdfCraft then drew nothing there; Poppler and Ghostscript draw it bit for bit.

| Size | Dark pixels PdfCraft draws, before Optimize | After Optimize, on `main` |
|---|---|---|
| 65,535 × 16 | 37,650 | 37,650 |
| 65,536 × 16 | 37,875 | 0 |
| 16 × 65,536 | 37,875 | 0 |
| 100,000 × 8 | 48,000 | 0 |

The encoder now refuses what the decoder can't read, so such an image isn't stored as JBIG2: the image step leaves a 1-bit one as it is unless it is averaged (Clean Up may still Flate an unfiltered or LZW one), and one packed from more bits may become 1-bit Flate. `MAX_JBIG2_COLUMNS` goes from 2^20 to 65,535, and rows and total samples are checked too, the total against `MAX_JBIG2_PIXELS`, the decoder's own bound. Symbol coding's limit of 2^24 rows can't be reached any more, so it goes. Redaction's use of this encoder, from #5474, is safe either way: it only encodes what the decoder read, and keeps the smaller of Flate and Group 4 if refused.

## How you verified it

- `pdfcraft-filters` and `pdfcraft-optimize`: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and tests (206 passed in 8 suites, 0 failed)
- `cargo xtask layers`, `assets` and `parity`: pass

New tests:
- `it_encodes_only_what_the_decoder_takes` (filters): each side and the total, at their exact bounds, with what the generic coding writes at each decoded by `hayro-jbig2`. With the read-back below, of …

title: CLI: parse pdfcraft-cli arguments with clap and thiserror (RFC-0012)
author: marshiyar
body:
The hand-written parser kept an option table per command, accepted a flag's value whatever it was, kept the first of a repeated flag, reported every mistake as exit 1 and printed a hand-kept usage text. Following RFC-0012 (storytold/craft-contrib#18), as PhotoCraft did (photocraft#7071, #9167):

- **clap derive** (`cli.rs`): subcommands, `PathBuf` paths, ranged numbers (`--dpi`, `--timeout`, `--quality`, `--ppi`), page lists, `--rotate PAGES:DEGREES` / `--move PAGES:TO`, `key=value` JSON arguments, `ArgGroup`s (`split --every | --before`, `run <tool> | --script`). Unknown or repeated flags, bad values and conflicting flags are usage errors (exit 2) before any file is opened. `edit` still runs its options in the order given. Help comes from the doc comments; `-V`/`--version` work everywhere.
- **thiserror** (`error.rs`) replaces `Result<_, String>`: `CliError` for a command that ran and failed, `ValueError` for a rejected value, `UsageError` for flag combinations clap cannot express. Failures print as `error: <message>`; exit codes are 0 / 1 / 2.
- The crate is a library with `run(args, out, err)`; `main` only passes `args_os` and the real streams. Results go to `out`, diagnostics to `err`.
- `examples/man-and-completions.rs` writes shell completions and one man page per command (clap_complete and clap_mangen are dev-dependencies only).

Unchanged: the subcommands and their flags, the JSON results, exit 1 for a failed command (`audit` finding faux redactions included), the closed-stdout behaviour, `--root` and the automation roots, and the MCP server (still opt-in, still on stdio).

Different (RFC-0012 and the photocraft#7071 decisions):

title: M5: restyling a group member restyles the whole group; moving or deleting one acts on it alone (#5516)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5516.

**Depends on #4358.** This branch is built on #4358's branch, so until #4358 merges, this PR's diff also shows #4358's commits. This PR's own change is the last commit.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.2: "Operations that manipulate any annotation in a group, such as movement, cut, and copy, shall be treated by interactive PDF processors as acting on the entire group." The group's attributes, `C` among them, come from the primary. We compared readers on synthetic files and follow Acrobat desktop, where the readers disagree; see "How other readers handle a group" below.

**Engine (`crates/annot`)**

`group_members(doc, page, index)` is new. It returns every member of the group the annotation belongs to, as `(page, index)`:
- The primary comes first, then its subordinates and theirs, all on the annotation's page.
- The primary is found up the `/IRT` chain. A loop, or an `/IRT` that points to another page or to nothing listed, ends the chain there.
- A chain longer than the 64-step depth limit is refused, so a restyle never acts on part of a group.
- An annotation in no group is a group of one.

`set_style` and `set_fill` apply to the whole group, as Acrobat does. The member you act on behaves as before, errors included. The others take what applies to them:
- colour and opacity go to every member;
- a width goes only to members drawn with a border;
- line endings go only to a member with as many (a callout has one; a line or polyline has two);
- a fill goes only to members that can be filled.

A member that can't be redrawn keeps its look. One locked member refuses a restyle or fill of the whole group, with "a comment in its group is locked"; the locked member itself says "the comment is locked", as any comment does.

`move_annotation` moves only the member asked for, as Acrobat moves the member dragged. Deleting is #4358's: only the member clicked.

title: M12: a page break splits an empty XFA text field that grows with its text (form.xfa-dynamic)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5521.

An empty multi-line XFA text field that grows with its text (it has `minH` and no fixed `h`) no longer moves whole to the next page when it doesn't fit. It starts where it is and its widget runs to the bottom of the content area. The rest of its box goes on at the top of the next one, closed on every side.

**What still moves whole, as before:**
- a field that is kept intact, holds a value, is on one line, or has a fixed height;
- a field with no room above the break for one line of its text, together with its caption and border.

When the field is inside a bordered section, the section breaks with it: its border closes on the first page, under its bottom margin (which the field leaves free), and opens again on the next page.

**The basis**
- XFA 3.3 pp. 291–292 (content splitting): text may split between its lines, and an object is kept intact only when it asks for that (`keep intact="contentArea"` or `"pageArea"`). A field's default is `none`.
- XFA 3.3 pp. 629–630: a border's `break` defaults to `close`, so each piece of a split field, and of a split section, is drawn with its own closed border.

**How it works (`crates/xfa/src/layout`)**
- `flow.rs`: `place_block` lets `split_block` split a field that `splittable_widget_since` accepts. When a piece crosses a content area, the enclosing flowed subforms break with it through `break_frames`, so their borders close and reopen as they do when a field moves on whole. Before this, `next_area` marked those frames lost, and the section borders went missing.
- `pages.rs`: `frames_bottom()` adds up the bottom margins of the open frames. A field being split stops above them.
- A field that turns out to have no room for a line is laid out again and moves whole. Its frame margins and names are kept, exactly as for a field that can't split.

## Effect

About the numbers: we test against 500 XFA forms that governments, universities and public bodies in more than 50 countries publish online. 2…

## What this changes

`Scale::new` derives the area unit as `"{unit}^2"`, which is two characters longer than the unit. `Scale::validate` applied the same 24-character limit to both strings, so units of 23 or 24 characters failed because of the derived area unit. The error message blamed a unit that was within the limit.

`Scale::validate` (`crates/measure/src/lib.rs`, `:136-141`) now checks the unit against 24 characters and the area unit against 26, which leaves room for the `^2` suffix. Units longer than 24 characters are still rejected.

Found while testing `crates/measure/src/lib.rs:88-101` (`Scale::new`, `area_unit` built at `:95`) with `Scale::validate` at `:136-141`. No existing issue.

title: M2: a reference in a colour space or array isn't lost: Indexed tables, Pattern spaces, /Decode, /W and functions
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Three ways a reference in a colour space or an array was lost in `hayro-interpret` and `hayro-syntax`. ISO 32000-2 §7.3.10 lets any object be indirect, and the renderer read each of these wrongly.

| Input | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `[/Indexed /DeviceRGB 1 5 0 R]`, the table a string in object 5 | the space can't be read, and draws in grey from the index | the palette's colours |
| `[/Pattern /DeviceCMYK]`, a cyan through an uncoloured pattern | red: the components are taken as RGB | cyan |
| `[/Pattern 7 0 R]`, and `[/Pattern /DeviceGray]` at 0.5 | the same: dark red for the grey | the underlying space |
| `/Decode [7 0 R 0]` on an image | the image isn't drawn | decoded |
| `/W [20 0 R [500 600]]`, `/W2` the same way | that entry and all after it fall back to `/DW` | read |
| A function's `/Encode [7 0 R 0]`, and its `/Domain`, `/Range` and `/Decode` | the array is lost | read |

**Indexed (`hayro-interpret` patch 71).** The table was tried as a stream first, then as a string. A failed read leaves a direct object in place, but it uses up a reference, so nothing was left to read as a string. It is now read once, as whichever it is.

**Pattern (`hayro-interpret` patch 72).** The family name was read twice, and the second read took the underlying space when that was a name or a reference. A direct array survived because a failed read leaves it in place. `[/Pattern /DeviceCMYK]` is ordinary PDF, so this affects real files, not only unusual spellings.

**Nesting (`hayro-interpret` patch 74).** Following a Pattern's underlying space added a way into a recursion Indexed, Separation and DeviceN already had. Reading an object already being read is refused, which ends a cycle but not a chain: 5,000 spaces each naming the next, 180 KB of file, overflowed a 2 MiB stack and aborted the process. Colour spaces now nest at most 32 levels, through all five ways one names another, an ICC profile's `/Alternate` included. A legal file goes five. Past the l…

title: Reject non-digit characters in DER UTCTime/GeneralizedTime fields

body:

title: M1: encryption reads every legal form: crypt filters by reference, a stream's own filter on screen, and full saves that keep /Encrypt
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A stream can name its own crypt filter (`/Crypt` in `/Filter`, its name in `/DecodeParms`), and any part of that can be indirect (ISO 32000-2 §7.4.10, §7.3.10). Neither reader handled that, and full saves lost data for some spellings of the `/Encrypt` dictionary itself.

**`pdfcraft-cos` read only the direct forms**, and took anything else for no name, which means `/Identity`. So:

- A stream selecting a filter by reference was **saved in the clear** in a file meant to be encrypted.
- In a file from elsewhere, its ciphertext was read as data.
- `/StmF` by reference left every stream undecrypted. `/StrF`, `/EFF`, `/CFM`, `/Filter`, `/EncryptMetadata` and a filter's `/Length` are fixed too.
- A stream's `/Type` is read through references now, and so are `/Type` and `/ByteRange` on a signature dictionary that is an object of its own, so metadata left readable, embedded files under `/EFF`, and signature `/Contents` behave the same in either form. A null or dangling entry reads as absent.

**The renderer never used a stream's own filter**, in any spelling. It decrypted every stream with the document's filter, then failed on `/Crypt` as a filter it couldn't decode, so a page whose content had `/Crypt` in its chain stayed white. It now uses the filter the stream names, `/Identity` without one (`hayro-syntax` patch 30). In the same patch:

- `/DecodeParms` is read in either form, whichever form `/Filter` has. `[/Crypt]` with a lone dictionary, an everyday spelling, read as `/Identity`, and `[/FlateDecode]` with a lone predictor dictionary lost its predictor.
- A V4 or V5 file without `/StmF` or `/StrF`, which are optional and default to `/Identity`, couldn't be rendered at all.
- A `/CF` entry named `/Identity` isn't used: that name always means no encryption.

**A full save could lose a whole document.**

| Input | Before |
|---|---|
| A direct `/Encrypt` with `/CF` or `/StmF` by reference | what it refers to was dropped, and its references kept the o…

title: UPD.1: a failed update says why at the next start (#5546)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Part of #5546 (the update to 0.16.1 doesn't go through: PdfCraft restarts on the same version and offers the update again).

On Windows, **Update and restart** downloads the new version and closes PdfCraft, and a helper copy of the old program installs it. When that install step fails, the helper starts the old copy again and writes the reason to `self-update-error.txt` in the logs folder, for `craft_update::self_update::take_failure` to read at the next start. Nothing in PdfCraft reads it, so the user only sees the same update offered again, with no reason, which is what #5546 describes. The ArtCraft Launcher already reads it, in its `main.rs`.

With this change, the start after a failed update:

- shows **"The last update didn't install: {reason}"** in the notice bar, as PdfCraft already does for a portable folder it can't write and for a software renderer, and
- logs it to `pdfcraft.log` as a warning, so a report can include it.

`take_failure` removes the file, so the reason is shown once. The update is still offered again, as before.

The file is in the user's folder, so its length isn't PdfCraft's to trust. A reason longer than 600 characters is cut to its first and last 300, joined by " … ", in the notice and the log alike. The end is kept because a failed put-back ends by saying where the previous files are.

**Windows only.** The app crate takes `craft-update` only on Windows, and only the Windows update helper records a failure. So the call, `notify_failed_update` and its test are `#[cfg(windows)]`, like the `self_update::finish` call at the top of `main`. Other platforms are unchanged.

This doesn't fix the update itself. #5546 has a triage note on what fails, including why a 0.15.0 copy can't update itself in some cases. Those causes are in craft-update and the 0.15.0 release, not in this repository.

title: engine: doc_audit_visibility — audit text a reader does not see
author: Bra1nZ
body:
## What it does

A new read-only `doc_audit_visibility` tool lists what a text extractor would read that a human reader does not see, per page — the raw material of prompt-injection checks on documents an agent (or the file-sharing layer around one) is about to trust:

- text painted by **no render mode** (ISO 32000-2 §9.3.3 render modes 3/7, and clip-shaping glyphs);
- glyphs **wholly off the displayed page**;
- **transparent** fill (alpha < 13/255) or **near-white** fill (Rec. 709 luminance ≥ 0.95);
- **tiny** text (em-box height < 1.5 pt);
- **concealed Unicode characters** an extractor passes through: zero-width (U+200B–200D, U+2060–2064, U+FEFF), bidi controls (U+202A–202E, U+2066–2069) and tags (U+E0000–E007F). Emoji ZWJ sequences (U+200D) are flagged too — for review, not conviction.

Each finding reports the kind, an exact count, at most 8 per-glyph samples (escaped) and rectangles in page points, like `comment_list`/`doc_info`; the report carries per-kind totals. Pages can be selected; duplicates collapse.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

- The **classification thresholds**: Rec. 709 luminance ≥ 0.95 (near-white), alpha < 13/255 (transparent), em-box height < 1.5 pt (tiny). They decide what the audit flags; they are our classification, not the format's.
- **U+200D emoji ZWJ sequences are flagged** — they extract but hide their glyphs; a review signal, not a conviction.
- The `/ActualText` handling: the second commit (`c129f525`) added replacement-record capture, made the configuration view-independent and streams the classifier; the third (`b4e59c19`) bounds the aggregation of a replacement record and flushes an unclosed span at the page end, so a report can neither grow without bound nor miss a still-open `/ActualText`.

## Structure

- `crates/render/src/text/audit.rs` — `AuditDevice`: records every glyph an extractor reads (unlike text extraction, nothing is dropped), with paint colour, render mode and em-box geometry; `audit_page` + `PageRe…

title: redact: independent redaction proof machinery (snapshot, sweep, budget)
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

An independent proof that a redaction removed what it claimed to remove, as a new module of
`pdfcraft-redact`, on top of current `main`:

- **Snapshot** — before applying, record per region what the interpreter is about to remove
  (the glyph runs and their character codes), a digest of each page's content, and the text of
  the whole document as a separate extractor reads it.
- **Sweep** — after applying, serialize the document the way a save would and sweep the output
  for those strings on every surface a reader could recover them from: the raw file, string
  objects, decoded streams (orphans included), the text of every page (read by a minimal
  extractor of its own, not the interpreter's metrics or hit test), the Info dictionary, the
  XMP packet, embedded files (PDF attachments swept recursively) and the revision structure.
  Each string is looked for in every encoding a PDF can hold it in.
- **Paint and placement** — place every glyph still shown on the redacted pages with its own
  text-state tracking and width model, and re-check the images, paths and shadings under each
  region, on the page and in the appearance streams of the annotations left on it.
- **Budget** — every stream is decoded under a per-stream cap and a cumulative cap, and all
  searching runs under a work budget: a document that needs more is reported as unswept, not
  skipped.

The proof fails closed: a survivor, or anything it could not sweep, fails it. It holds counts
and digests, never the redacted text, unless the caller asks for plaintext. It is not wired
into `apply` yet: the engine integration (`verify_save`, `redaction_snapshot`,
`RedactOutcome`) follows in a stacked PR.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-redact`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` (212 tests) and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine`
- [x] `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p pdfcraft-redact`

title: tests(ui): the Search panel snapshot no longer depends on which page's text arrives first
author: guillehr2
body:
The Search panel snapshot in `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/panel_snapshots.rs` fails now and then on PRs that don't touch search. Seen on CI on FreeBSD 15 x86_64 (on storytold/pdfcraft#2412), and locally under load.

## Cause

Each page is searched as its text arrives on a worker, and the match made current is the first one found. When page 2's text arrives first, page 2's match stays current, and the snapshot shows `[on]` on page 2 instead of page 1.

## Fix

The test already waits until both pages are searched. It now calls `rerun_find()` then, so the current match is the first from the page in view, as it is for a new query. The production code is unchanged.

The other two timing-dependent UI tests I had seen (the shared forms scratch folder and the 30-frame pending-open wait) are already fixed on main.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `panel_snapshots::every_panel_matches_its_snapshot`: five runs, all pass.

title: Select the bookmark title when creating or renaming a bookmark (#5529)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #5529.

The inline rename field in the Bookmarks panel asked for focus without setting a selection, so the caret landed wherever the stored cursor was, usually at the end of the default text "Untitled". Typing then appended to the old title instead of replacing it.

The field is now a small function, `rename_field` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/bookmarks.rs`. On the frame it takes focus it stores a selection of the whole title, then asks for focus, so typing replaces the old text right away — for a new bookmark (⌘B/Ctrl+B, the panel's add button) and for rename (context menu, double-click). It is a one-shot: after the user moves the caret, later frames leave the caret and selection alone, exactly as the toolbar zoom box in `chrome.rs` does.

Tests:
- Three unit tests on `rename_field`: the first focus selects the whole title; a multibyte title is counted in characters, not bytes; a caret the user collapses to is kept by the next frame.
- Two kittest tests driving the panel like a user: typing a new name straight after ⌘B replaces "Untitled", and rename from the context menu replaces the old title with no Ctrl+A.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` passes. The one failure in `tests/it`, `editing::a_custom_property_whose_name_the_tools_refuse_is_listed_and_left_alone`, is pre-existing on `upstream/main` f137a289 in this environment: a missing U+FFFD glyph in the font fallback, unrelated to this change.

title: M3: a fast wheel spin scrolls smoothly, its boost eased like each notch (#5371)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5371 (mouse-wheel scrolling has been choppy since 0.10.1, especially when the wheel turns quickly). Likely the stutter in #4173 too, where a commenter found that reverting #1094 fixed it on Linux.

0.10.1 added wheel acceleration (#1094, for #1072). When notches arrive within 80 ms of each other, each notch gets up to five more notches' worth of distance, the "surplus". egui still eases each notch's own distance over the following frames (90% within 0.1 s). The surplus, however, was scrolled all at once in the frame the notch arrived. On Windows and Linux a notch is 100 points, so at full speed every notch jumped the page about 500 points in one frame and then crawled for the next two.

Measured headlessly at 60 frames a second, with a notch every 50 ms once the multiplier has peaked, in points per frame:

| | each notch's three frames |
|---|---|
| `main` | 546, 32, 22 |
| this PR | 279, 191, 130 |

The surplus now goes into a small accumulator (`wheel_boost::Surplus`) and is released on egui's own curve, so a fast spin moves as smoothly as single notches. What stays the same:

- **Acceleration and total distance.** All of the surplus still arrives, up to a backlog of one frame's cap of wheel input (`MAX_FRAME_POINTS`, 8,192 points). In a full-speed spin of 100-point notches the backlog stays around 230 points; only a free-spinning wheel gets near the cap, and the cap keeps the page from scrolling on long after it stops.

title: Fix XFA forms dropdown menu and info display issues
author: am2222
body:
## What this changes

An XFA drop-down or list box whose options come from the data (`<bindItems>`, XFA 3.3 "Dynamic Properties") now lists those options. On `main` such a field showed the template's own `<items>`. Those are often empty, or a single placeholder, so the field offered the wrong choices or none (#3072).

Fixes #3072

Each data node the `ref` names becomes one item:

- **Saved value:** what `valueRef` names under that node. This can be the node's own value (`$`), an attribute (`lic`, `@lic`) or a child.
- **Label:** what `labelRef` names. With no `labelRef`, or an empty one, the saved value is also the label, as the spec says ("If there is no labelRef attribute then the value strings are also used as labels").
- Saved values are kept only when some differ from the labels, as for `<items>`.
- The value bound to the field stays selected.

The `ref`s it follows:

- `xfa.datasets.…`, `$datasets.…` and `!…`: lists kept in the datasets packet beside `xfa:data`, where Designer's forms keep them.
- `$data.…` and `$record.…`.
- Path steps by name, with `[n]` or `[*]`.

A `ref` it can't follow keeps the template's own items and adds a layout warning that names the field. That covers a `ref` relative to the field's bound data, which is the spec's default context, as well as SOM predicates, class names (`#dataGroup`) and `connection` (web-service data).

Lists are capped at 1,000 items, with a warning.

title: Ignore a negative trailer /Size in incremental saves
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Found while testing `crates/cos/src/writer.rs:248` (no existing issue). Incremental save wrote `/Size 4294967295` when the source trailer `/Size` was negative.

**Cause:** `write_incremental` cast the source trailer's `/Size` with `as u32`. A negative value (from a damaged or hostile file) wrapped to 4294967295, which was written as the new `/Size`, in the classic trailer or the xref stream.

**Fix:** The trailer `/Size` is clamped to `0..=u32::MAX` before the cast, so a negative value counts as 0 and the written `/Size` is `next_num()`. The save sanitizes the value and does not fail.

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `editing::a_custom_property_whose_name_the_tools_refuse_is_listed_and_left_alone`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

title: M2.6: the images of a run, and a page's JBIG2 images, share one allowance of decoding
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

#5491 limits how long one JBIG2 image can take, to about 6 s to 17 s. Nothing limited a file of many images made to reach that, so a small file could still hold an operation for hours: images × seconds each. An image sharing `/JBIG2Globals` also decodes them again, so the cost adds up on honest files too.

Now the images of one run share one allowance, counted in the JBIG2 decoder's steps, where a step is about a pixel. That means every image in a run, not only JBIG2: a few KB of Flate inside Flate can ask for a gigabyte, so charging JBIG2 alone would leave the same file one `/Filter` entry away from it.

| Run | Allowance | Past it |
|---|---|---|
| Image export, Office export, Optimize, redaction | 2^34 steps, plus 2^13 for each byte of the file | see below |
| Rendering a page, JBIG2 images only | 2^30 steps, what one image may take | the image isn't drawn, like one that can't be decoded |

An image is charged what it costs, not only what it decodes:

- **Its filters, whatever the image:** a step for each byte read and each byte a stage decodes, as it happens. A chain that fails or goes past its image's limit has still paid, and no stage runs past what is left. `/JBIG2Globals` pay the same when they have to be read, and kept ones don't.
- **Its pixels, whatever the image:** a step each, before it is read, as what reads it goes through them one by one however few bytes hold them. A blank page of 100 million pixels can be 19 bytes of fax.
- **A fax image:** 4 steps a byte of code and a step a byte of the rows it asks for, before it is decoded, since a blank row takes one bit.
- **A JPEG, when it is decoded:** 4 steps a byte and 2 a sample before anything reads it, in Optimize, and in an export that reads it as a mask or to apply one, its header having to agree with its dictionary. A lone JPEG is exported as it is, at no cost, unless it is a CMYK file whose inversion has to be undone.
- **A JBIG2 image, reading it:** 4 steps a byte of the strea…

title: M6: copied pages paste whatever the system clipboard holds (#5406)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Part of #5406 ("it shows a copied notification, but nothing is copied"). On Windows, Ctrl+V and Edit ▸ Paste in Organize Pages paste the copied pages only when the system clipboard happens to hold text.

Copying pages keeps them on PdfCraft's own page clipboard (`page_clipboard`) and leaves the system clipboard as it was. Organize Pages, though, pasted them only on egui's `Paste(text)` event. The storytold egui-winit swallows the Ctrl+V key press and release, then reads the **system** clipboard:

- text → `Paste(text)`
- a picture alone → `PasteImage`
- neither → no event at all

Edit ▸ Paste sent `ViewportCommand::RequestPaste`, which comes back the same way. So right after a screenshot, or with nothing on the system clipboard, both did nothing, even though Edit ▸ Paste was enabled.

With this change:

- **Ctrl+V in Organize** also takes `PasteImage` as the paste. The pages come from PdfCraft's own clipboard either way. In other views `paste_image_key` already returns early for Organize, so nothing is pasted twice once #5457 lands.
- **Edit ▸ Paste in Organize** pastes the copied pages directly (`paste_pages`), as the right-click **Paste after** does. With a text field focused, it still sends `RequestPaste`, so text fields paste as before.

**Ctrl+V when the system clipboard holds neither text nor a picture** (an empty clipboard, or files copied in Explorer) isn't fixed here: egui-winit swallows the keys and sends nothing. #6426 fixes that case by putting a line naming the copied pages on the system clipboard. This PR is still needed with it:
- A picture copied in another app after the pages arrives as `PasteImage`, which the page grid ignores on `main`.
- Edit ▸ Paste pastes the pages directly instead of going round through the system clipboard.

The two touch different files and merge cleanly.

author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5488.

`panels_with_hundreds_of_items_stay_within_the_frame_budget` failed on about a fifth of CI runs because the comments panel overran the 40 ms budget. The panel laid out **every** card and "Page N" header on every frame, 500 of each in the fixture, whether they were in view or not. Now, in `panels/comments_panel.rs`:

title: Repair scan: an object whose header names another generation is still found (#5580)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #5580.

`poppler-85140-0.pdf` is 340 bytes with no cross-reference table, so hayro rebuilds one by scanning for `N G obj` headers. Its one page's header reads

```
3 18446744073709551616 obj
```

while the page tree points at `3 0 R`. Before 1399d38e the digits wrapped and 2^64 wrapped to exactly 0, so the header read as `3 0 obj` and the file opened by accident; since then an overflowing integer becomes a real, `ObjectIdentifier::read` refuses it, and the object vanishes from the rebuilt table:

```
$ pdfcraft-cli info poppler-85140-0.pdf
pdfcraft-cli: the file is not a readable PDF: the document has no pages
```

### The generation number is not really the point

The issue describes this as an overflow, and I started there, but it is a **mismatched generation in a rebuilt table** — the overflow is just the instance that used to work by accident. The same file with `3 99999 obj`, a perfectly readable `i32`, is refused identically on `main`. That row is in the new test, and it is the one the control fails on first:

```
generation 99999: the page is found: Some("page 1 does not exist")
```

So option 1 from the issue (record the file as a known `open-error`) would have papered over a general defect rather than accepted one malformed file. I took **option 2**, confined to the reconstruction path.

### What changed, all in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/xref.rs`

A table rebuilt by scanning the file has no revision history to tell two generations of an object apart, and a file that needs rebuilding references everything as `N 0 R` whatever its headers say. Three parts, each needed — I found the second and third only after instrumenting the scan, because fixing either alone changes nothing:

1. **`read_object_header`** — the scan takes a generation number it cannot read as 0. A generation is at most 65,535 (ISO 32000-2 §7.5.4), so a value outside that is not a generation at all.
2. **A generation-0 alias** — every scanned object is also filed under generation 0, so `3 …

author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Part of #517: split **one page into several pages**, for scanned book spreads, 2-up handouts or A3 sheets that hold two A4 pages. This PR is the engine and the headless tool. The Organize dialog is a follow-up.

title: M3: on Windows, a GPU wgpu can only reach through OpenGL draws with eframe's OpenGL renderer (#4134)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4134 and #5553: on Windows, PdfCraft opens a white window and closes about two seconds later on GPUs with no Direct3D 12 driver. Intel HD Graphics 2500 and 4000 (Ivy Bridge) are the reported ones, and #519 was the same class of GPU.

Three reporters' logs show the same sequence. With no Direct3D 12 adapter, wgpu picks its **OpenGL backend** (`drawing on Intel(R) HD Graphics 4000 (IntegratedGpu, Gl)`). That backend then fails in `Surface::configure` (`Failed to wait for GPU to come idle before reconfiguring the Surface`), which wgpu treats as fatal, so the process exits with code 101. By then the app has started, so the start-up retry with OpenGL (`retry_with_gl`) can't take over. All three found that `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl`, eframe's own OpenGL renderer (glow), works on the same GPU.

This takes the narrow fix suggested in #4134. On Windows, the adapter selector declines an adapter that wgpu would use through its OpenGL backend. wgpu then fails to start, and the existing retry starts the app with glow, as `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl` does. The log says why:

```
WARN  pdfcraft: wgpu found no Direct3D 12 adapter for <GPU>, only its OpenGL backend: drawing with eframe's OpenGL renderer instead
ERROR pdfcraft: the GPU renderer (wgpu) didn't start: … Starting with OpenGL instead; set PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl to skip wgpu.
INFO  pdfcraft: renderer: OpenGL (glow)
```

The selector now also runs on Windows when no display names its GPU by PCI ids, as over Remote Desktop (one #4134 reporter used it); before, wgpu's own choice took over there. With no display known, `pick_adapter` ranks adapters by kind, most frugal first (CodeRabbit's review).

**What doesn't change:**

- A GPU with a Direct3D 12 adapter: the selector already preferred it over the same GPU's OpenGL adapter. This PC logs `drawing on AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT (DiscreteGpu, Dx12)` as before.
- Other platforms.

body:
## Summary

Adds a native GNOME frontend, `apps/pdfcraft-gtk`, built on `pdfcraft-engine` (GTK4 + libadwaita via gtk4-rs 0.11 / libadwaita 0.9). The existing egui app and the CLI are untouched.

- Tabbed shell (AdwTabBar) with menubar generated from the command registry (209 commands), command palette, open/save/save-as/revert/close-all, closed-tab history with reopen and reveal in file manager.
- Multi-page viewer: zoom, fit page/width, single/two-up, continuous, reading mode, page navigation history.
- Side panels: pages with live thumbnails, bookmarks (add/rename/delete/move/indent/set page), comments (delete), fields (value, checkbox toggle, properties: tooltip/read-only/required), layers (visibility + reset), attachments (delete), signatures.
- Interactive tools: annotations (note, text, markup, shapes, ink, callout, eraser), redaction (mark + apply), Fill&Sign (text, marks, date, saved signature/initials), digital signatures (p12 dialog, visible/invisible, certify).
- Commands not implemented natively dispatch through `pdfcraft-automation` (`command_run` + JSON Schema forms), so all 209 registry commands have a destination (96 native handlers + 113 automation routes).
- Color-coded tools rail generated from `engine::catalog` (`TOOL_CATEGORIES`/`TOOL_GROUPS`), with lucide icons tinted per group hue.

## Engine/automation changes

Additive only: public re-exports in `pdfcraft-engine` (render types, `FieldProps`, `AttachmentSource`, `OutlineItem`, etc.) so the frontend respects the layer rules, and a `session_mut()` helper in `pdfcraft-automation`.

## Testing

- `scripts/gtk-qa.sh` runs headless Xvfb QA modes (smoke, viewer, document ops, editing, annotations, redact, fill-sign, digital sign, page ops, exports, panels, parity...); the aggregate `captures` mode currently runs 23 gates green.

## What this changes

Fixes #5588.

title: fix(xfa): handle XML declarations at packet boundaries
author: ishveet
body:
## What this changes

Fix dynamic XFA forms that fail to lay out when multiple named XFA packets contain their own XML declarations.

Previously, PdfCraft concatenated the packets into a single XDP document. XML declarations at later packet boundaries then caused `UnexpectedDeclaration`, preventing dynamic XFA layout.

The fix:

- Preserves the initial XML declaration and handles subsequent legal packet-leading declarations.
- Tracks XML lexical context across packet boundaries, preserving comments, CDATA, processing instructions and quoted attributes.
- Preserves packet ordering, original PDF streams and existing encoding behavior.
- Rejects malformed declarations while preserving meaningful error reporting.
- Retains existing dynamic-XFA classification for successfully decoded packets.
- Adds synthetic XFA and headless automation regressions.

title: M10: ClearScan as an editable-text OCR output (#4733)
author: Megatherium
body:
Fixes #4733

## What this changes

Recognize Text can replace the lettering on a scanned page with resolution-independent Type 3 outlines, in the spirit of Acrobat's ClearScan.

Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text ▸ In this file ▸ Output ▸ Editable text and images runs it. Sensitivity (0–100) and downsample (1–8) appear only for that output. The run is a worker with stage progress and Cancel. Pages already built are kept, as one undo step named ClearScan. Multiple files stays Searchable Image (Exact).

Headless, the same step is `ocr_clearscan` (`pdfcraft-cli run` and MCP). The scan is deskewed and binarized (Sauvola), glyphs are clustered and traced (Suzuki–Abe contours, Schneider cubics via `kurbo`), and written as an uncolored Type 3 font with `/ToUnicode`. The lettering, plus a one-pixel halo, is painted out with the local paper colour. Photographs and rules stay. Grey and a flat tint are Flate; a photograph is JPEG. There is no JBIG2 encoder in this tree (the usual one is AGPL), so a monochrome scan stays Flate. Comments, links and bookmarks stay.

English Latin only. Still missing, and said so in `parity/acrobat-features.toml` and `docs/clearscan.md`: opening those Type 3 glyphs in Edit text, and a textured background (the paint is one flat paper colour). Searchable Image does not deskew. Deskew is marked partial for the ClearScan path only.
