title: M1: a file of 1 GiB or more opens from disk, with only its structure in memory
author: VoiceLessQ
body:
## What this changes

A clean, unencrypted PDF of 1 GiB or more now opens from disk. Its structure stays in memory and its large stream bodies are read when something wants them. Until now the whole file was read at open, so a 5 GB scan needed 5 GB free before the first page showed. Refs #3976.

Gap 13 said this had to wait for the renderer decision, because hayro parses one contiguous buffer. That is true of a file's structure, not of its stream bodies. A file of gigabytes is that size because of those bodies, and in 5 local PDFs of 4-7.5 MB, streams of 4 KiB or more held 89-99% of the bytes.

- `OnDiskFile` (`crates/cos/src/on_disk.rs`) walks the file object by object and holds everything except proven stream bodies of 4 KiB or more, in order, as one buffer.
- `cos` and hayro-syntax (patch 34) take file offsets through a small table and read a body when asked. Any future renderer needs the same one callback, so this does not get in the way of gap 2.
- `PdfSource` is what a renderer reads: a file in memory or a file on disk. Everything that took bytes takes either, and call sites that pass bytes did not change.

What a user sees: a large file opens, with a notice saying it is being read from disk. Pages, text, search, bookmarks, comments and attachments read as usual, and Save As copies the file a piece at a time. **Load to edit** reads the whole file on the worker and puts it in the same tab at the same page, after which everything behaves as it does today.

`doc_open` takes `on_disk: true`, and a file over the tools' 512 MiB limit now opens this way instead of being refused.

Measured on a synthetic 2.16 GB file (60 pages of 6000x6000 images, bookmarks, one incremental update), release build, Linux, file in the OS cache:

| | Peak memory | Time |
|---|---:|---:|
| App, file open from disk | 388 MiB | |
| App, after 12 pages, 400% zoom and a search of all pages | 768 MiB | |
| App, after Load to edit (the cost of holding it whole, as before) | 2,776 MiB | 2.5 s to…

title: M3: the wheel scrolls right after Alt+Tab back, before the mouse moves (#1518)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1518: after **Alt+Tab back** to PdfCraft, the mouse wheel scrolled nothing until the mouse was moved.

**Cause.** When another window covers the pointer, the windowing layer reports the pointer gone. Switching back sends no pointer move until the mouse actually moves, so egui knows no pointer position. `ScrollArea` only takes wheel input while it contains the pointer, so the wheel was dropped.

**Fix.** `raw_input_hook` gets a new step, `drag_pointer::locate_wheel`. When a frame
- turns the wheel,
- has no pointer move (or `PointerGone`) of its own, and
- egui knows no pointer position,

the hook asks the system where the pointer is and puts that `PointerMoved` first, if it is inside the window. The system query is `drag_pointer::in_window`, the existing one used for file drags: `winsafe::GetPhysicalCursorPos` on Windows, `NSEvent::mouseLocation` on macOS. So there's no new dependency and no `unsafe`. On other platforms `in_window` returns `None`, and nothing changes there.

It's the real pointer position, not a guess from before the switch. If the mouse moved while another app had focus, the wheel goes to whatever is under it now.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --lib`: 606 passed. `--test it`: 1265 passed, 4 ignored

**New test:** `platform::drag_pointer::tests::a_wheel_with_no_known_pointer_asks_the_system_where_it_is`. A wheel frame with no known pointer gets the system's position first. Nothing is added when egui knows the pointer, when the frame moves or loses the pointer itself, when there is no wheel, when the system can't tell, or when the pointer is outside the window or not a number.

**Fails without the fix:** with the insertion removed, the test fails on its first assertion.

**Real input, Windows 11** (portable copy, 13-page PDF; `user32` `keybd_event` Alt+Tab with a maximised windo…

title: fix(a11y): resolve indirect structure kids, parent tree keys, and table attributes
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary

- **`crates/a11y/src/autotag_fields.rs` (`tag_form_fields`)**:
  - Accept 1-element `/StructTreeRoot /K [document_ref]` arrays (direct or indirect) in addition to direct dictionary references per ISO 32000-2 Table 354.
  - Resolve `/Document /K` before appending new `/Form` elements so an indirect `/K` array is expanded flat rather than wrapped as a nested child array.

title: Duplicar separador de documento (#5604)
author: croquete1
body:
## O que muda

Passa a existir **Duplicar separador** no menu do separador. Abre um segundo separador do mesmo documento, ao lado do primeiro, na mesma página, zoom e disposição. Uma edição feita num separador aparece nos dois. O documento só fecha quando fecha o último separador.

- Guardar, recarregar e o aviso de alteração em disco chegam a todos os separadores do documento. Mover separador mantém o separador ativo pelo índice.

Relacionado com #5604 e com #2518 (vista dividida). **Não fecha #5604**: a vista em mosaico ou grelha do mesmo issue fica para um PR próprio.

  - Preserve each multi-widget field's relative widget tab order (`w.tab`) when converting a page from `/R` or `/C` tab order to manual annotation order, instead of reverting its widgets to `/Kids` order.
  - Track fields by index rather than name so duplicate field names or duplicate widget references in `/Annots` do not drop or shift widgets.
- **`crates/forms/src/af/calc.rs` (`js_tokens`, `eval_notation`)**:
  - Stop regular expression literal scanning when a backslash is followed by a line terminator (`\n`, `\r`, `U+2028`, `U+2029`) or EOF, and advance by full UTF-8 character width after `\` in regex and template literals.
  - Support unary `+` alongside unary `-` in simplified field notation (`eval_notation`).
- **`crates/forms/src/af/script.rs` (`Parser::string`, `Parser::arg`, `Arg::num`, `call`)**:
  - Avoid aborting `Parser::string` when an unpaired UTF-16 high surrogate (`\uD800`..`\uDBFF`) appears near the end of a string or before a non-surrogate escape.
  - Reject non-finite parsed numbers (`Infinity`/`NaN`) in `Parser::arg` and `Arg::num`.
  - Match calls via `js_tokens` in `call` so occurrences inside comments/strings or prefixed identifiers (`my_AF...`, `$AF...`, `.AF...`) are skipped while still supporting dotted call targets (`this.resetForm`).
- **`crates/forms/src/author/tree.rs` & `crates/forms/src/author/join.rs`**:
  - Treat `null` dictionary entries (direct or indirect `Object::Null`) as absent per ISO 32000-2 ?7.3.9 in `holds_value`, `check_place`, `attach`, `inherited`, `ancestor_sets`, and `has_opt`.
  - Check inherited `/Opt` on ancestor fields in `has_opt` per ISO 32000-2 ?12.7.5.2.

title: M12: XFA edges keep their own dash patterns (#5561)
author: hsmith-dev
body:
## What this changes

Fixes the dash-pattern part of #5561. Three things were wrong in `crates/xfa`:

- `parse.rs` folded `dashDot` and `dashDotDot` into `Stroke::Dashed`.
- `pdf.rs` and `pdf/common.rs` wrote one `[2 2] 0 d` for every stroke that isn't solid.
- `layout/draw.rs` dashed a `<line>` only for `Stroke::Dashed`, so a dotted line drew solid.

What changes:

- `Stroke` gains `DashDot` and `DashDotDot`.
- `Item::Line` and `Rounded::edge` carry the edge's `Stroke` in place of a `dashed: bool`.
- A single `pdf::common::dash` writes each stroke's pattern, in multiples of the edge width, with projecting caps (`2 J`). Square edges, rounded edges and lines all use it.
- A new `pdf::common::line` writes a line item. It takes over from the inline `format!`, so the output can be tested.

At 3pt the patterns are exactly what Acrobat flattens the issue's `line.pdf` to, per KenM76's triage on the issue: `[12 6]`, `[3 6]`, `[9 6 3 6]` and `[9 6 3 6 3 6]`. Solid and 3-D (relief) strokes stay solid.

This PR leaves out `rotate` (also in #5561), zero-size lines (#4588) and corners (#4675).

title: fix(create,optimize): a mask of other proportions doesn't take the process down
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A file of about a kilobyte could abort PdfCraft. A soft mask of other proportions than its image is scaled to the image, and scaling goes down first, through a buffer of the source's width by the target's height at 16 bytes a pixel. Each image's own size limit says nothing about that product.

| Mask → image | File | Before |
|---|---|---|
| 20,000 × 1 → 1 × 20,000 | 1,034 bytes | peak 6.1 GB, 2.35 s |
| 60,000 × 1 → 1 × 60,000 | about 1 KB | `memory allocation of 57600000000 bytes failed`, exit 134 |
| 100,000 × 1 → 1 × 100,000 | about 1 KB | asks for 160 GB and aborts |

With this change the 100,000 × 1 and 100,000 × 64 shapes export, which the test holds to.

It reaches image export, Office export, Copy Image and signature images through `gray_plane`, and Optimize at its default settings through `resample`.

Such a picture is now scaled across first, which holds no more pixels than one of the two has, so the existing size limits bound it. It takes this route only when the product is more than a quarter over the larger of the two sizes, so a mask of its image's shape scales exactly as it did, to the byte. A mask further from that than a quarter comes out within a level or so of what it did, as a resize of two steps rounds twice; noise can differ more with Optimize's sharper filter.

### Limits

- The buffer is still 16 bytes a pixel, so an image at the 100-megapixel limit can hold up to about 2 GB while it is scaled.
- There is no total across a document: every image can point at one mask, and each rescales it. In image export that costs seconds an image at about 265 bytes each. #5569 charges a mask's pixels to the run, which bounds that once it lands.
- The two functions are one idea written twice, in `pdfcraft-create` and `pdfcraft-optimize`, with their own filters: neither crate depends on the other.

## How you verified it

- Gate on `pdfcraft-create` and `pdfcraft-optimize`: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, 140 tests. Mutation …

title: M2: a DeviceCMYK page group blends its page and inherited groups in CMYK (#4887)
author: hsmith-dev
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4887. This covers what the issue asks for, but not the ICC-based CMYK and RGB follow-ups it lists under "Still to cover".

On a page whose `/Group /CS` is `DeviceCMYK`, blending now happens in CMYK (ISO 32000-2 §11.3.4, §11.4.7). That applies on the page itself and in the non-isolated and knockout groups that inherit the page's space (Table 145). It also applies in isolated `DeviceCMYK` groups, as it already did since #5228. Before, everything outside an isolated group blended in RGB, so magenta under black in `/BM /Difference` stayed magenta instead of going green.

The fix reuses #5228's two ink passes rather than adding new machinery. All of it is in vendored code, as hayro-interpret patch (71) with hayro patch (27):

- **`interpret_page`:** offers the page's contents, not its annotations, to `Device::draw_isolated_cmyk_group` as a new `CmykGroup::for_page`. hayro draws them in the cyan-magenta-yellow and black passes and converts the result once, the way it already handles an isolated group. Patch (18) already draws the page group from a transparent backdrop of its own, so its contents can go through the same path. Annotations are drawn afterwards as before.
- **Nested groups inside a page pass need no new code.** Inside a pass:
  - a plain non-isolated group is drawn straight into the pass;
  - an isolated `DeviceCMYK` group is declined and drawn inline;
  - a knockout group uses its existing passes;
  - an isolated group naming another space makes the whole page fall back, as #5228 does for nested groups.
- **Only pages that can blend are offered.** That is the `cmyk_group::page_blends_in_device_cmyk` check. Every press-ready PDF has a CMYK page group, so a page reaching no blend mode other than `Normal` never takes the passes. The check reads the graphics states of the page's resources, and of the forms, tiling and shading patterns and Type 3 fonts inside them. title: Keep overlapping text runs of different sizes from interleaving
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

The pass added in #2929 attaches smaller runs to a larger host segment as sub- or superscripts. It accepts any negative horizontal gap, so a smaller run drawn across the host's glyphs (e.g. 'Fuel' under 'COPY ME') passes the script geometry check. It is then merged into the host segment, and sorting by x interleaves the glyphs of the two runs.

The fix: the attach filter now also rejects a candidate when the summed x-overlap of the host's glyphs with the candidate's extent exceeds half of the candidate's width. A real sub- or superscript sits beside its host's glyphs, not across them. The new `Seg::covered` helper runs last, so only pairs that already pass the cheaper geometry checks pay for the glyph scan.

Fixes #5616

title: M7: preserve Arabic source-font edits, Unicode and positions
author: eliassader
body:
Submitted head: `268bc0c2` (review update; no Rust production changes).

## What this changes

Arabic paragraphs whose PDFs embed a complete editable static source font now retain that font, logical Unicode, mark positions and spacing through repeated replacement, undo/redo and incremental save/reopen. Previously a partial PDF encoding could split a contextual span between resources, a leading zero-advance mark could shift the baseline, and missing spaces or tracking could introduce placement drift.

This is a bounded correction to the existing source-font editing path. It uses existing `harfrust` OpenType shaping (Arabic programs without GSUB are refused) and `unicode-bidi` visual runs. Logical ToUnicode ownership remains separate from positioned glyph emission. It does not introduce a code-point joining table or a new bidi engine.

title: M12: an XFA draw placed by position turns about its anchor
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Part of #5561, for dynamic forms. Nothing under `crates/xfa/src` read `rotate`, so a turned line, picture or label was drawn as if it stood upright.

The form attached to #5561 doesn't reach this code as it stands: its config says `dynamicRender` is forbidden, so PdfCraft shows the page Acrobat flattened, which is right already. Its template, forced through layout, gives the same anchors and offsets as that page, which is what the test holds to.

A draw placed by position now turns about its anchor, counter-clockwise, by a multiple of 90 degrees.

- **The direction comes from Acrobat itself.** The form in #5561 carries the page Acrobat flattened, and that puts the three turned lines exactly where this does: from the anchor by (+28.8, +50.4), (-50.4, +28.8) and (-28.8, -50.4) at 90, 180 and 270 degrees. The test holds to those figures. Adobe's Designer scripting reference says the same.
- **A turned draw is one item.** A page break moves it whole, and what it holds is written unturned under one matrix, so text, pictures and borders need nothing of their own.
- **Its container grows to the box it stands in**, in height and in width, through one `Node::standing_box` that drawing and both measurements share. Without that, the next block runs through a turned label or stands off from it. This goes by what is drawn: how Acrobat sizes a growing container around a turned draw wasn't observed.
- **Two things read inside it.** The page count is filled in, and a link annotation turns with its text. Pieces of one link in turned text stay separate annotations, as joining them goes by the line they stand on unturned.
- **`rotate` reads as** a whole number of quarter turns: `90`, `90deg`, `450` and `-90` all work. Anything else, such as `45`, leaves the draw as it stands. Adobe's reference asks for a non-negative multiple of 90; how Acrobat treats a negative one wasn't observed.

title: M5: a reply is not drawn on the page or flattened into it (comment.reply)
author: mtlcl410
body: ## What this changes Fixes #5631. Replies go with their comment at any depth of the thread and in any order of `/Annots`: what points at each annotation (a pop-up by `/Parent`, a reply by `/IRT`) is gathered once and followed from what went, instead of one pass that missed a reply listed before the reply it answers. - `vendor/README.md` lists patch (81) and its test; `parity/`: `comment.reply` and `comment.flatten` notes and evidence. title: M2: a shrunk image on a turned or mirrored page snaps to whole pixels (#5530)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What this changes

Refs #5530 (see the caveat at the end: not "Fixes" until the reporter's file confirms it).

hayro patch 14 (`snap_minified_image`, `vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`) shrinks an interpolated image **once** to its whole-pixel device rectangle and draws it 1:1, instead of shrinking it to a rounded-up size and resampling that a second time at a fractional scale and offset (the path its own comment says "blurs scans and photos"). It only accepted an upright transform (`a > 0, d > 0, b = c = 0`). So every image on a page under `/Rotate 90`, `180` or `270` — and any image placed turned or mirrored by its own matrix — still took the double resample. That matches #5530: the same scanned page matches PDFium upright and drifts and softens when rotated.

The snap now accepts every transform whose axes lie along the device's: the eight quarter-turns and mirrors. It returns the 1:1 transform that draws the shrunk raster from the snapped corner, with one source-axis step equal to a whole device pixel in whichever direction that axis runs. Skewed and freely rotated images keep the old path. The one call site now draws with that transform instead of a translation, and the `vendor/README.md` entry for patch (14) says what it covers.

## How you verified it

**Seen failing first.** Oracle with no external reference needed: on a synthetic page whose crop box and scale put every page edge on a whole device pixel, a `/Rotate` turn is a pure pixel permutation, so the turned render turned back must equal the upright one. The image itself sits at fractional coordinates. Before the fix:

Every kind of image that reaches the snap, on `main` (same at 90, 180 and 270):

| kind | `/Interpolate true` | `/Interpolate false` |
|---|---|---|
| 8-bit grey | worst 200, 72% of pixels | identical |
| 1-bit grey | worst 217, 73% | identical |
| stencil mask (`/ImageMask`, as CCITT scans often are) | worst 194, 73% | identical |
| image + soft mask of its own size | worst 177, 65% | ide…

title: M2: a thin stroke is one device pixel wide in every direction (#5532)
author: charlieruk
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5532 (the non-uniform-matrix case KenM76 isolated there).

hayro widens a stroke thinner than a device pixel, but by the **larger** axis scale of the CTM alone (`max_factor`). Under a matrix that shrinks one axis more than the other, a line running along the shrunk axis stays thin: under `1 0 0 0.25 cm`, a `0.3 w` horizontal line was 0.25 px of ink, a quarter as dark as it should be. Widening by the smaller scale instead would draw every vertical line four pixels wide.

Vendored hayro patch (28), `thin_stroke_pen`: when a stroke would be under the threshold (1 device pixel, 0.25 for stroked text, as before) in some direction but not by the same factor in every direction, it is drawn with a pen matrix `A` that stretches each principal direction of the CTM (its right singular vectors) by what that direction needs. The path is drawn as `A⁻¹ × path` with `CTM × A`, so it lies on the same device curve, and its round pen maps to an ellipse whose axes are all at least one pixel. A direction that was already wide enough keeps its width. Dashed paths are dashed in user space first, so dashes keep the lengths the pattern gives them. Patterns and Type 3 glyphs are still excluded. Uniform matrices (the common case) return `None` and take the old route, so their pixels are unchanged.

Basis: ISO 32000-2 §8.4.3.2 (a zero line width is the thinnest line the device can render, one device pixel).

Not changed (the other two cases in KenM76's comment):
- Thin **filled** rectangles still get no floor. That is a fill, not a stroke; #4433 covers zero-area fills.
- A hairline exactly on a pixel boundary still comes out as two half-dark rows (automatic stroke adjustment, §10.7.5).

title: feat(render): draw JPEG XL image XObjects (/JXLDecode), first frame (#4782)
author: helenkwok
body:
Fixes #4782.

PdfCraft now draws image XObjects whose stream is JPEG XL. They used to be dropped without a word.

**What changed.** A `JXLDecode` image filter in the vendored hayro-syntax, next to the JPX one (patch 29 in `vendor/README.md`), decoding with jxl-oxide 0.12.6 (pure Rust, MIT OR Apache-2.0, default features off). Only the first frame is drawn, as 8-bit grey or RGB with an optional alpha channel. CMYK and other layouts, more than 2^28 pixels, and a size that disagrees with the image dictionary are refused: the image is not drawn and the page carries on. The decoder runs under the `images` and `std` features, like the other codecs.

**The filter name.** ISO 32000-2 defines no JPEG XL filter yet. The PDF Association has said JPEG XL is its preferred solution for HDR images, and has published no filter name, so `JXLDecode` is a placeholder (the name the PDFium design doc uses too). It will follow the standard once there is one.

**Sources.** The PDF Association says it promotes JPEG XL as the preferred new image format for HDR and "encourages interested developers to join us" in adding it to PDF: [Chrome's U-turn on JPEG-XL, PDF in the Wild, 17 December 2025](https://pdfa.org/pdf-errata-makeover/). Its CTO named JPEG XL the preferred solution for HDR content in PDF at PDF Days Europe 2025: [heise, 11 November 2025](https://heise.de/-11073527). The PDFium design doc that uses the same placeholder name: [JPEG XL image support in PDFium (Rust-only), draft of 2026-02-02](https://gist.github.com/hjanuschka/4b23e2067344b88fe27a8dd4a2a6e048). The decoder is [jxl-oxide](https://github.com/tirr-c/jxl-oxide). Questions to the PDF Association about the intended filter name, colour, alpha and bit depth are open in [pdf-issues discussion 852](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/discussions/852); this PR follows whatever they settle.

title: M2: JPEG 2000 images decode on several threads
author: macocheung
body:
## What this changes

Large JPEG 2000 images (`/JPXDecode`: scanned plans, photos) now decode on several threads, with byte-identical samples. Until now a JPX decode ran on one thread and was most of the render time of a scanned page: on a 3320 × 4676 lossy RGB scan it was about 70% of the page, and every 1024 px tile decoded it again on its own worker.

`hayro-jpeg2000` 0.3.5 is vendored (upstream git `a2354aeb`) with PdfCraft patch 1. A tile of at least 2^18 coefficients decodes on up to 8 threads:

- **Bitplanes.** The code-blocks of each sub-band are grouped into stripes of whole rows. Each stripe is a disjoint slice of the coefficients (carved with `split_at_mut_checked`), and threads take stripes from a shared queue, each with its own bitplane context (`bitplane::decode_with`, split out of `bitplane::decode`).
- **IDWT and store.** These run one component per thread, each with its own buffers and its own `&mut` channel.

Every code-block and component is decoded by the same code from the same inputs into the same place, so the output does not change. Anything the planner cannot prove disjoint falls back to the existing serial path untouched: an overlapping or out-of-range code-block, missing decompositions, small tiles, one core, wasm, or no `std`.

Against 0.3.5, only `src/lib.rs` and `src/j2c/{mod,decode,bitplane}.rs` change, and `src/j2c/decode/parallel.rs` (about 350 lines) is new. The crate keeps `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

Measured on a 24-thread Windows 11 machine (`page_timing`, best of 3):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Scanned A3 page (3320 × 4676 JPX + 1-bit mask), open (backdrop) | 1,061 ms | ~600 ms |
| same page, fit to 2800 px | ~1,850 ms | ~1,180 ms |
| same page, four 1024 px tiles at 100% | ~2,100 ms | ~1,350 ms |
| JPX decode alone, that 3320 × 4676 scan, full / ½ / ⅕ size | 1,324 / 645 / 237 ms | 490 / 177 / 60 ms |
| JPX decode alone, synthetic 2000 × 1500 RGB, full size | ~3,500 ms | ~510 ms |

Page hashes in all three scenarios ar…

title: feat(optimize): store JPEG images as JPEG XL, losslessly and reversibly, and restore them (opt-in; builds on #5648)
author: helenkwok
body:
Builds on #5648 (JPEG XL read support, #4782): the first two commits here are that PR's, and only the last one is new. Merge #5648 first; then this PR shows only its own commit.

Optimise's Clean Up gets two options, both off by default: store JPEG images as JPEG XL, and turn them back into the JPEGs they were made from.

**What it does.** A plain JPEG image becomes a `JXLDecode` image from which the original JPEG can be rebuilt byte for byte, so nothing is lost and it can be undone. It is only done when the result is smaller. The new `pdfcraft-jxl` crate does the work: `recompress_jpeg` (jixel 0.4.2, pure Rust, BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0, pinned exactly), `reconstruct_jpeg` (the jxl-oxide decoder #5648 already uses) and `jpeg_frame`. Every call is panic-guarded, and the JPEG's declared size is checked against a 64 megapixel cap before the encoder allocates anything. Only grey and three-component JPEGs are converted.

**What is left alone.** An image with `/DecodeParms` (a `/ColorTransform` could make readers disagree about the colours), a dictionary size that disagrees with the JPEG's own, an image mask, an external file, a CMYK or four-component JPEG, and any image that would not get smaller. Asking for both directions at once does nothing.

**Why it is opt-in.** ISO 32000-2 has no JPEG XL filter yet, so the images carry the placeholder name `JXLDecode`, and a reader without JPEG XL shows nothing for them. The setting says so. Questions to the PDF Association about the intended name are open in [pdf-issues discussion 852](https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf-issues/discussions/852), and this PR follows whatever they settle.

**Where it is exposed.** Two checkboxes in the Optimise dialog's Clean Up tab, `jpeg_to_jxl` and `jxl_to_jpeg` in the `doc_optimize` automation tool (with schema and report counts), and the fields on `Settings` and `Report`.

**Spike before writing it.** On a synthetic 24 megapixel JPEG (7,736,750 bytes) jixel 0.4.2 recompressed it to 5,917,…

title: M10: Create ▸ Blank page uses the system region's paper (#5644)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Create ▸ Blank page always made a US Letter page (215.9 × 279.4 mm), even in regions that print on A4. It now uses the paper of the system region:

- **Windows:** the user's own Region paper size (`HKCU\Control Panel\International\iPaperSize`, `1` Letter, `9` A4), read in-process like the existing `iMeasure` read for Units. No `reg.exe` is spawned.
- **macOS:** the region of `AppleLocale`.
- **Everywhere else:** `LC_ALL`, then `LC_PAPER`, then `LANG`.
- **Letter regions:** CLDR's `paperSize` US-Letter territories (US, CA, MX, PH, PR, BZ, CL, CO, CR, GT, NI, PA, SV, VE). Every other region gets A4.
- **Region unknown** (the web, or a `C`/`POSIX` locale): Letter, which is the behaviour before this PR.

The parsing of the region from a locale tag moves out of `unit_for_tag` into a shared `region_of`, which both Units and paper now use. Units behaves as before.

The `doc_create` automation tool still defaults to Letter unless it is given width and height, so headless runs stay reproducible across machines.

Fixes #5644

title: M7: Myanmar text is shaped when its paragraph is rewritten (#5114)
author: charlieruk
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5114.

Myanmar text looked right while typing and came out wrong after deselecting, and stayed wrong in other readers. `source_shaping::required` left Myanmar out, so an edited paragraph was written one glyph per character in typing order. A medial ra (U+103C) and a vowel sign e (U+1031) are typed after their consonant but drawn before it, and a virama (U+1039) stacks the next consonant, so they landed beside the wrong letter.

- **Paragraph rewrite:** Myanmar and its Extended-A and Extended-B blocks now take the shaping path.
- **Fonts without GSUB:** the check in `shape()` now covers Myanmar too. Browser-made subsets have no GSUB, so they used to "shape" successfully and stay in typing order. They are now refused, and a loaded full face is used instead.
- **The refusal names the face to load:** `complex text needs the complete NotoSansMyanmar-Bold TrueType/OpenType face; load that font before editing`.
- **`text_edit` with `line`:** `replace_line` can't shape, so it now refuses Myanmar and points at the paragraph, with the page left alone.

Not changed:
- Add text still can't draw Myanmar, so it refuses it.
- There is no fallback Myanmar face, so a paragraph can't be rewritten until the full face is loaded. Every style in it needs its own face.
- Without a Myanmar face in the build, a character the font lacks gets the older `the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph…` error, which wrongly suggests an official release would help.
- Single-line edits of other complex scripts weren't changed or checked.

title: fix(optimize): resolve indirect subtypes and chained refs in cleanup and audit
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Summary

Hardens PDF Optimizer cleanup (`unused`, `links`) and space auditing (`audit`) when dictionary keys (`/Type`, `/Subtype`, `/S`, `/EncryptMetadata`) or object references (`/XObject`, `/Contents`, `/Dest`, `/D`, `/Outlines`, `/Names`) are indirect or chained (`ISO 32000-2 §7.3.10`):

- **`crates/optimize/src/unused.rs`**:
  - Follow chained `Object::Ref` entries in `graph()` so streams behind multi-hop indirect references are included in the reference graph and scanned before dropping XObjects, and downgrade shared dictionaries reached both as `/XObject` (`Use::Entries`) and non-picture dictionaries (`Use::Other`).
  - Resolve indirect `/Type` and `/Subtype` names in `own_xobjects()`, `data()`, and `remove_unused()`, as well as indirect `/EncryptMetadata` booleans in `plain_metadata()`, preventing image streams with indirect `/Subtype /Image` from returning `Data::Unknown` and aborting unused-XObject cleanup.
- **`crates/optimize/src/links.rs`**:
  - Resolve multi-hop indirect references and indirect `/Subtype` / `/S` names across destination trees, link annotations, `/GoTo` actions, and bookmarks; treat `/GoTo` actions missing `/D` as invalid destinations so broken `/GoTo` links/bookmarks are cleaned up.
  - Restrict `referenced_names()` to objects reachable from the trailer/catalog rather than scanning unreachable objects in `doc.object_numbers()`, so orphaned annotations or detached actions do not keep unreferenced named destinations alive.
- **`crates/optimize/src/audit.rs`**:
  - Resolve indirect `/Type` and `/Subtype` names and chained `/XObject` references in `Audit::claim()`, `Audit::resources()`, `Audit::appearance_resources()`, and `annotation_category()` so images behind chained references or with indirect `/Subtype /Image` are counted under `Images`, widgets with indirect `/Subtype /Widget` are counted under `Forms`, and pages with indirect `/Type /Page` are not claimed by links.

author: hazeliscoding
body:
## What this changes

Part of #3883.

"No colour" in Redaction Tool Properties (#2008) still gave a black box. `set_redaction_properties` (`crates/annot/src/create.rs`) wrote a mark with no fill with a black `/IC`, and applying draws each mark's box in its `/IC` colour.

A mark with no fill now has no `/IC`. ISO 32000-2 Table 195 says that when `IC` is absent, the redaction region's interior is left transparent. Apply already draws no box for such a mark (`crates/redact/src/overlay.rs`), and restyling a mark to no fill already removes `/IC` (`crates/annot/src/modify.rs`), so only making a new mark was wrong. Applying also skipped a mark with no `/IC` before its overlay text, so "No colour" with overlay text would have drawn nothing. The box is now drawn only when there is a fill, and the overlay text either way (`crates/redact/src/overlay.rs`).

This is only part of #3883. The reporter also says a colour they pick comes out black. On `main` a picked colour reaches the mark's `/IC` and the applied box, as mtlcl410's headless test on the issue showed, so that part needs the reporter's version and steps.

title: fix(render): JBIG2 arithmetic near the end of an i32 doesn't panic (hayro-jbig2 patch 12)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A JBIG2 stream can put a region, a reference or a symbol at the very end of what an `i32` holds, and the vendored decoder added to those numbers with plain arithmetic. In any build that checks overflow, that's a panic:

| Where | Input |
|---|---|
| `Bitmap::combine` | A region within its own size of `0x7FFFFFFF`, in either direction |
| The refinement context | A refinement region there, or a symbol refined by an offset as far as `i32::MIN` |
| A text region's corners | A symbol placed on a strip near `-2^31` |
| The integer decoder | A decoded value of 2^31 |
| A Huffman table | A value on a 32-bit range line past what an `i32` holds |

The last four now wrap, which is what a release build already did. `Bitmap::combine` saturates instead, and that gives the same result: a side is at most 65,535, so a location that overflows is past the end of any page either way. So what is drawn doesn't change.

Measured on 16,950 streams: a composition built in every arithmetic-coded region form, across the combination operators, both page defaults, striped pages and 25 locations, and four Huffman-coded text regions.

| Build | Panics | Compared with |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, dev | 2,200 | |
| This branch, dev | 0 | Same as this branch in release, on every stream |
| This branch, release | 0 | Same as `main` in release, on every stream |

2,462 of those streams are refused in every release build, and for those "same" means the same error. A further 8,740 streams at the limit of `combine`, with sides up to 65,535, came out the same in the run before the Huffman lines changed, which those streams don't reach.

The release profile doesn't check overflow, so these aren't crashes in a shipped build. In a dev build the renderer turns one into a page error through its `catch_unwind`. Export and Copy Image reach the same decoder through `crates/create/src/extract.rs`, and in the app they have no such net.

CodeRabbit raised the cast of a region's location on #5474,…

title: fix(create): a /Decode array needs two finite numbers to invert an export
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Export decides whether a JPEG or a stencil mask is inverted by comparing the two ends of its `/Decode` array. The comparison was between `Option`s, and `None` sorts below any number, so an end that was missing or wasn't a number could read as inverted. So could an end too long to hold, which parses as infinite.

| `/Decode` | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `[1]` | Inverted | Default mapping |
| `[1 /Name]` | Inverted | Default mapping |
| `[1 7 0 R]`, with 7 leading nowhere | Inverted | Default mapping |
| `[<400 digits> 0]` | Inverted | Default mapping |
| `[1 0]`, `[0 1]`, and either by reference | As before | As before |

Both ends now have to be finite numbers, or the default mapping stands, as on the lossless path. CodeRabbit raised this on #5539 after that PR had its last push, and #5539 merged without it.

### Not changed

- **An inverted grey or RGB JPEG.** With no transparency, it still exports as its file, a negative of what the page draws. That's for a valid `[1 0]` too, and it's the older and likelier problem here. #4992 is open for it, and leaves this comparison as it is, so the two don't overlap beyond a nearby line.
- **Redaction.** It reads only the first end of a stencil mask's `/Decode`, so on a malformed array such as `[1]` it and export now differ on which way round the mask is. The renderer doesn't draw such a mask, and the covered samples are overwritten either way, so no covered pixels stay.
- **The renderer.** It draws nothing for these malformed arrays, so export writes an image the page doesn't show. `[/Name 0]` already did that, as does the lossless path.

## How you verified it

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-create`
- [x] tests pass on `pdfcraft-create`: 2 suites, 60 passed
- [x] `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`

title: M3: a finger's drag scrolls the page in the Select tool (#5667)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5667. Refs #1231.

On a touch screen, one finger in the Select tool, which is the default, selected text instead of scrolling. A swipe up over a page highlighted the lines under the finger, and the page stayed where it was; the reporter of #5667 saw only the scroll bar flicker. Only the Hand tool scrolled.

A finger's drag now pans the page in the Select tool, as the Hand tool does and as a touch screen is expected to scroll:

- **What pans:** a swipe that starts on text, on empty page, or on a link, since a link takes only a click.
- **What still moves:** a drag that starts on something that uses its drag, such as a comment or a form field, still moves it.
- **Taps and pinches:** a tap is still a click (it follows a link, ticks a check box, selects a comment, clears a text selection), a double tap on a word selects it as a double click does, and two fingers still zoom.
- **Mouse and pen:** both still select text. winit 0.30 reports a Windows pen as touch, so PdfCraft tells a pen from a finger by the first pressure reading: a finger gives none, or Windows' default for a screen without a pressure sensor (512 of 1024, a force of exactly 0.5), and a pen gives its own.
- **Other tools:** the Hand tool and every other tool are unchanged. The markup and drawing tools still mark with a finger; #1108 plans their touch behaviour.

**How it works.**
- `PagePointer` gains `finger`: the press it holds began with a touch without a pressure reading of its own (`finger_down`). It is worked out on the frame of the press and kept until the next press.
- In the Select tool, the text layer neither starts nor moves a selection for a finger's drag (`TextGesture::pans`). Its taps still reach it, so they click as a mouse does.
- `document_area` pans for a finger the way it pans for the Hand tool, unless a drag of the press moves something on the page. It asks the router once, through `PageRouter::drag_moves_nothing`. That is true when nobody holds the press, w…

title: M10: Word export keeps a form's layout — rules, boxes, text in place, fillable fields
author: NAG473-s
body:
## What this changes

Word exports preserve rules, boxes, positioned text and supported AcroForm controls on pages selected by the layout heuristics. Ordinary pages retain flowing paragraphs and inferred tables. Flattened forms with too little artwork can still flow and omit that artwork.

- Preserve picture/path paint order through nested Forms. Mixed artwork uses one DrawingML group with a stable page extent; compound fills preserve even-odd and nonzero holes.

author: VoiceLessQ

## What this changes

Refs #5439. That issue also asks for a built-in file browser, which isn't here, so this PR doesn't close it.

**Edit ▸ Search a folder…** finds text in every PDF in a folder without opening them.

- Pick a folder, type the text, and press Search or Enter. Include subfolders starts on; Whole words only and Case-sensitive start off.

| Limit | Value | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Folder entries | 10,000 | A line says the folder is too large or too deep |
| Folder depth | 64 levels | The same line |
| File size | 512 MiB | Listed under Not searched |
| Matches | 1,000 (the tool can ask for up to 10,000) | The search stops and says so |

| Threads left running | 9, across searches | A new search is refused, and says why, until they exit |

title: M5: Replace Text keeps its replacement on the group's primary, the caret (comment.replace-text)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #5688

## What this changes

**The need.** Replace Text writes a strikeout over the text and a caret holding the replacement, grouped with `/IRT` and `/RT /Group`. PdfCraft made the strikeout the primary and put the replacement in the subordinate caret's `/Contents`. A group's text is read from its primary, so a reader following the standard shows the proposal as an empty strikeout and the replacement nowhere.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.2 (printed p. 480): "The group consists of a primary annotation, which shall not have an IRT entry, and one or more subordinate annotations, which shall have an IRT entry that refers to the primary annotation and an RT entry whose value is Group. Some entries in the primary annotation are treated as "group attributes" that shall apply to the group as a whole; the corresponding entries in the subordinate annotations shall be ignored. These entries are Contents (or RC and DS), M, C, T, Popup, CreationDate, Subj, and Open."

**The change**
- `add_text_replacement` (`crates/annot/src/modify.rs`) writes the caret as the primary: the replacement in `/Contents`, `/IT /Replace` and `/Subj (Replace Text)`. The strikeout is its subordinate: `/IRT` to the caret, `/RT /Group`, `/IT /StrikeOutTextEdit`, as before an empty `/Contents`. The two keep their own `/NM` (#2666), so XFDF's `inreplyto` now names the caret.
- Deleting either one deletes the other. Deleting the caret takes the strikeout with it through `/IRT`, as replies go. Deleting the strikeout also takes the caret it is grouped under; this applies only to a `/StrikeOut` with `/IT /StrikeOutTextEdit` and `/RT /Group` whose `/IRT` is a caret. A locked caret refuses the deletion, as a locked reply does.
- The Comments panel names a caret with `/IT /Replace` "Replace text", and Make Current Properties Default on it updates the Replace text tool, as for the strikeout.
- A click on the strikeout picks the proposal (the caret), as a click on the caret does (35725261b). With the …

title: fix(ui): don't check recent files on the UI thread at startup (#5682)
author: Elarionus
body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft no longer asks the file system about recent files on the UI thread at startup, so a recent file on a network mount that has stopped answering can't keep the window from appearing.

Restoring settings used to drop recent files whose files no longer exist by calling `Path::exists()` on each one, on the UI thread, before the first frame (`crates/ui-egui/src/app/prefs.rs`). On an unresponsive davfs2 mount that `statx` blocks in the kernel, which is the hang in the report.

Now:
- Restoring settings keeps every recent entry and hands the restored paths to a new `persist::recent_check`.
- Once frames run, a worker thread checks those paths with `std::fs::exists`. Each frame drops the entries the worker has found gone so far, and the worker requests a repaint when it finds one.
- An entry the worker hasn't reached yet, or can't tell about (an error rather than "not found"), stays listed, as the reporter asked, and can still be opened or removed by hand.
- A worker stuck on a dead mount stays stuck, but nothing waits for it. Nothing tries to cancel it, since a timeout can't cancel a blocked kernel call.

The worker follows the pinned folders' (`home/folders_ui.rs`): `run_inline` runs it inline in tests, and lock poisoning is handled. Only entries restored from settings are checked, the same set the old filter covered, so entries added while the app runs aren't affected. The web build has no file paths and skips the check, as it skipped the filter before.

Fixes #5682

title: fix: integrate persistent AcroForm script workflows with native prompts and appearance writeback
author: Doom666DE
body:
## What this changes

Interactive AcroForm documents can combine a number/PIN keypad, calendar-dependent fields, synchronous calculations, popup menus, response dialogs and button icons. Previously each event could recreate the JavaScript context, host APIs were absent or placeholders, and some field mutations never reached PDF dictionaries/appearances. A keypad could lose its buffer between digits, `calculateNow()` could return before dependent values changed, and a script could compute correct values while leaving its overlay or icons unchanged.

This is an integration contribution on main `9ce6d89f466416876a7bd62ecc81018f3c2d1ed9` (crate version 0.18.0). It builds on existing open contributions rather than proposing independent replacements. Related: #4154, #5211, #269, #344, #4751. It does not claim complete Acrobat JavaScript compatibility or close every related issue.

### Runtime and event ordering

- One Boa realm per open document, on a dedicated native worker. Document scripts initialize once as `Doc/Open`; button, console, format, validate and calculate events share globals and retained Field objects, with current field snapshots.
- Contexts reset on script-source changes, close/reopen, reload, Revert or JavaScript disable. Separate documents cannot share state or icon handles. PDF Undo/Redo restores PDF state, not arbitrary script globals.
- `calculateNow()` runs synchronously against pending writes, in `/CO` order, restores the outer event and limits reentrancy. Pure style/caption/geometry/display edits skip value recalculation. A single invocation uses the existing undo batch.
- The worker refuses another run while active, including while waiting for a dialog. UI events do not queue synchronous callbacks behind an unanswered prompt.

### PDF object and appearance bridge

- Normal button captions persist to every widget, including mixed captions when the first widget already matches. Uniform no-op assignments stay clean.

title: Fix Matrix::invert rejecting valid matrices with a small scale
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Matrix::invert (`crates/content/src/lib.rs`, around lines 732-735) rejected valid matrices with a small scale. It treated any matrix with an absolute determinant below 1e-12 as singular, so a uniform scale of 1e-7 (determinant 1e-14) returned `None`.

Header/footer, watermark and background additions and replacements now commit as one operation across all selected pages. If a later page fails, existing marks, page content, resources, background restoration state and pending caller edits stay unchanged.

The three public edit APIs share a staging helper: clone the COS document, run the complete existing operation, then replace the caller's document only on success. Original PDF bytes, cross-references, caches and unchanged objects remain shared; cloning copies the overlay table and document metadata. The choice embeds the existing craft-fonts face as a Unicode PDF font, measures its actual advances, uses the existing CJK line-break and punctuation rules, and survives save/reopen/retype. The automation tools `page_add_text` and `content_update` accept `font: "wenkai"` (also `"chinese"`). Missing faces, unsupported glyphs and bold/italic requests are refused clearly; the UI hides the choice when the build lacks the face and disables bold/italic when it is selected. Existing-paragraph and header/footer paths reject treating this added-item face as a standard-14 font.

Related to #864; this does not close the broader font/import request. I reviewed the related work in #2466, #3186 and #4200. This proposal is narrower: an explicit Add Text choice using the already pinned LXGW face, without changing the craft-fonts revision, adding font files, or changing forms/Fill & Sign. Arbitrary local font import remains outside this PR.

title: fix(ui): prevent panel resize handle collision with scrollbar (#5730)
author: Combiler01
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5730

When the All Tools panel (or any collapsible/docked side pane) is open, hovering near the panel edge triggers the panel-resize cursor/interaction (`CursorIcon::ResizeHorizontal`) over the panel's internal scrollbar, preventing reliable dragging or clicking of the scrollbar.

This occurred because `craft-ui` task panes render resize handles on an overlay `edge-layer` with an expanded hit rectangle. Combined with egui's hit-testing search radius, this caused the resize interaction zone to bleed inward into the panel body by up to ~10px, shadowing the vertical `ScrollArea`'s track.

2. Increases `left_panel`'s right frame margin in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/tools.rs` from 10px to 14px (`Margin { left: 14, right: 14, top: 12, bottom: 10 }`), establishing a symmetrical 14px internal gutter between the scrollbar track and the resizable boundary and maintaining visual balance with the 14px outer margin (complementing the hover wash adjustments from #5133).
3. Adds a comprehensive regression test `scrollbar_and_panel_resize_handle_do_not_collide_on_either_dock_side` verifying scrollbar precedence and panel resizing across both left and right docking configurations.

title: M11: Optimize runs when a category it discards holds nothing
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

PDF Optimizer's ticks for Remove Hidden Information's categories (links, actions and JavaScript, bookmarks, form fields and hidden layers under Discard Objects; comments, metadata, attachments, private data and hidden text under Discard User Data) go to `remove_hidden`. It refuses when its scan counts every listed category as 0 (`RedactError::NothingToApply`), and may have changed the copy by then: an empty outline root goes with bookmarks. So ticking only categories the file holds nothing of, such as "Discard bookmarks" on a file without bookmarks, ended the whole optimization with "there are no redaction marks to apply". `doc_optimize` with such a `discard` failed the same way. Now, when `remove_hidden` refuses, the optimizer keeps the copy from before the call: nothing is discarded, an empty outline root stays (as Remove Hidden Information leaves it), and the rest of the optimization runs. Every ticked category still goes to `remove_hidden`, which decides between them: with form fields ticked, discarding hidden text or hidden layers also takes what of them the flattened appearances bring onto the page, which no scan before flattening counts. Beside a ticked category that holds something, an empty outline root (and `/PageMode /UseOutlines`) goes with bookmarks, as on `main`.

`doc_remove_hidden` with listed categories that hold nothing gave the same message about redaction marks. It now checks first, as `redact_apply` checks for marks, and says "nothing to remove: the listed categories hold nothing (see doc_hidden_info)". It reads the same scan the removal refuses by (an AcroForm with no fields counts 1), so it refuses exactly when the removal would, and it is the scan the tool already took to count what was removed, so there is no extra pass. A document that can't be edited has no scan, and still gets the reason it can't be edited. One whose permissions forbid changes now hears that there is nothing to remove before it hears that changes are…

author: hermi72
body:
The AI assistant tools (ai.summary, ai.ask, ai.translate) were catalogue placeholders. They now open a Claude dialog with three tabs that sends the document's page-by-page text to Claude and streams the answer in.

Requests go to the Anthropic Messages API (claude-opus-5-5, streaming, server-side refusal fallback, the document cached for follow-up questions) when an API key is set in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or saved from the dialog (settings folder, mode 0600). title: fix(ui): prevent wheel lockup at edge in non-continuous view (#5713)
author: Combiler01
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5713.

Special thanks to [@arnav-hiwarkar](https://github.com/arnav-hiwarkar) for the crucial insight into how macOS reports mouse wheel notches in `MouseWheelUnit::Point` (~14 pt per notch on devices such as Logitech mice) and identifying the second lockup scenario after page turns.

### Problem
In non-continuous single-page display modes (e.g. **Fit one full page**), zooming in allows the mouse wheel to pan within the page until hitting an edge.
1. When a wheel notch turned a page (or pushed against a document boundary edge), `WheelPager` set `turned = Some(...)`.
2. Discrete mouse wheel notches do not produce trackpad touch phases (`TouchPhase::Start` or `End`), nor pause bursts on continuous input streams, so `new_gesture()` was never triggered to reset `turned`.
3. Consequently, `gesture_turned()` remained permanently `true`, causing `read_wheel` to set `paging_owns_vertical = true` and swallow every subsequent notch.
4. For devices reporting in `MouseWheelUnit::Point` (macOS), this suppressed `precise_scroll.y`, causing the wheel to completely freeze:
   - When attempting to scroll back up after pushing against the bottom edge of the last page.
   - When attempting to scroll down on a newly turned page (e.g., turning from Page 1 to Page 2, then trying to scroll down).

### Solution
1. **End turn gesture on panning notch:** In `WheelPager::motion`, if an incoming `notch` cannot turn (`!can_turn`), reset `self.turned = None`. A notch is its own discrete gesture, so a notch that only pans clears any previous turn latch so `read_wheel` stops swallowing wheel input.
2. **Unturn on boundary no-ops:** Added `WheelPager::unturn()` in `single_page_wheel` and `single_page_wheel_edge` when `step_page` is a no-op at document boundaries.
3. **Tests:** Added `Point`-notch integration tests (`single_page_point_notches_pan_the_page_a_notch_turned_to` and `single_page_point_notches_scroll_back_up_from_the_last_page_bottom`) that verify scrolling op…

title: feat(ui): host the document view from a shell, one frame at a time
author: Dc-xp
body:
## Summary

A shell that wants this app's document view inside its own window has no way in: `document_area` only
draws what the caches already hold. The bookkeeping that fills them lives in the app's `ui`, wrapped
around the area, so a host that calls `document_area` alone gets a blank page.

`host_document` runs exactly that bookkeeping for one frame, without PdfCraft's tabs and panels:

```text
PdfCraftApp::host_document(index, ui)      # new, canvas.rs
  i18n locale gate
  begin_render_frame(index, ui)            # demand a raster for the visible page
  document_area(index, ui, ...)            # the page area only
  finish_render_frame(index, ui)           # swap in whatever finished this frame
```

```diff
 impl PdfCraftApp {
+    pub fn host_document(&mut self, index: usize, ui: &mut egui::Ui) {
+        ...
+    }
 }
```

Additive: no existing call site changes, the app's own `ui` keeps its path.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a host calling `document_area` directly gets an empty canvas — the cache is never asked
  for a raster, and a raster that finishes is not swapped in.
- **After:** `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib a_hosted_document_renders_its_page` — the test
  hosts a real document, runs the frame, and asserts the page is painted. It fails with the old
  direct call and passes with `host_document`.
- Full crate suite: 680 passed, 0 failed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** none for existing users

A new public method on `PdfCraftApp`; no behavior changes to the app's own rendering path.

title: M10: macOS print jobs name their title and owner (#5743)
author: hasannadeem
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5743.

Printing from PdfCraft to a Kyocera queue on macOS never produces a page. The report traced it: `lp` sends no `com.apple.print.JobInfo.*` attributes, and the driver's filter crashes on a nil job name (`NSInvalidArgumentException`, `cups-filter-crashed`). On macOS, both `spool` adapters now add those two as job options. `craft-print`'s `lp_args` only passes option values that are printable ASCII up to 64 bytes without `/ : = "`, so the values are cleaned to fit: other characters become `_`, and text with nothing left, such as a title entirely in another script, falls back to `PdfCraft`. `-t` keeps the real title. title: M3: a protected file named before others at launch keeps its password prompt (#5756)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft locked.pdf other.pdf` opened `other.pdf` and nothing else: `locked.pdf` got no tab, no password prompt and no message. With the files the other way round the prompt appears.

The files named at launch open before the first frame, inline (`open_path_request`, `crates/ui-egui/src/app/files.rs`). An encrypted first file sets `password_prompt`; the next file then reached `finish_open`, which sets `password_prompt = None`, and the first file's prompt was gone.

Now a file opened while a password prompt is open goes to the background open worker instead of opening inline, as a `--two-paged` launch file already did. `poll_pending_opens` holds its result while the prompt (or any dialog) is open, so it opens once the password is entered or the prompt is cancelled.

- **Tab order:** after `locked.pdf other.pdf`, `other.pdf` comes first and the unlocked file second, in view: the other file is ready while the password is being typed. Before this change the protected file wasn't opened at all.
- **Last session:** reopening the last session takes the prompt aside while it opens its files (`reopen_last_files`), so its own opens are unchanged. A file named on the command line after it now waits behind a restored file's prompt instead of clearing it.

Fixes #5756

title: Expand header/footer tokens preceded by extra '<' characters
author: Silvertree2010
body:

Header and footer tokens are now expanded when the template has extra `<` characters before the token. title: M7: keep turned text readable in the editor (#5763)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Refs #5763.

Editing a line turned 90° or 270° used its narrow page-space box as its text width and its page-space vertical extent as its font ascent. The horizontal editor squeezed the glyphs together and gave a 14 pt line an excessively tall row. A 180° source also placed the editor baseline incorrectly and could leave its field partly outside the page.

Turned paragraphs now open in a **horizontal editing field** measured along and across their own baseline. The field uses the source's long-side extent, keeps glyph advances and caret metrics readable, and stays within the visible page. It shows the unchanged text immediately, soft-wraps long unchanged labels within the field, hides the source text before typing, and positions the field using its measured wrapped height; a horizontal field is not retained as a rotated-page preview after Apply. The edit crate exposes its existing read-only frame rectangle/origin methods so the UI uses the same geometry as rewriting.

**Limitation:** this does not provide a rotated in-place text widget. It provides the approved horizontal-field fallback. Apply/save already preserved the source text matrix at 90°, 180° and 270° on main; that write-back behavior is unchanged. This PR references the issue without automatically closing it because the editor itself remains horizontal.

## How you verified it

Synthetic Helvetica fixtures are generated in Rust, with no page `/Rotate`. The 90° fixture uses `0 1 -1 0 100 400 Tm`; companion cases cover 180° and 270°. Each test opens through two real double-clicks, then enters replacement text through the focused editor.

title: Fix whole-file insertion between Combine pages
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5768.

Dragging a collapsed PDF card between pages of an expanded PDF now inserts all its contributed pages at that exact gap, in order. This covers both cases in the ticket: multi-page PDFs dragged as one file and single-page PDFs that have no expanded view. Both use the same whole-file drop-target path, so they are fixed together.

title: Edit text: a paragraph across several subsets of one font keeps its width (#5769)
author: ljkx
body:
## What this changes

Editing a paragraph whose font is split into several subsets (Chromium's "Print to PDF" writes web fonts as Type 3 faces, one face across several resources with the same `/BaseFont`) rewrote every row stretched, up to `200 Tz`.

**What was wrong.** Since #3661, a line joins runs drawn through different resources of one font. The styled rewrite's width calibration (`calibration_factors` in `crates/edit/src/text_regions/styled.rs`) still measured the whole line with the metrics of its *first* resource. Each Type 3 subset encodes only its own glyphs, so the words only another subset can encode measured nothing. The line seemed narrower than it is drawn, and the factor `rect width / nominal width` went up to its `2.0` clamp, which every rewritten row then got as `Tz`.

**What changed.**
- `TextLine`'s private `runs` now also records each run's font resource. The public `TextLine::runs()` iterator is unchanged.
- When a line joins more than one resource, the calibration measures it run by run, each run in its own resource's encoding and widths. A space that joining put between two runs is measured in the line's font. Lines drawn through one resource are measured as before.
- A row the edit restyles into another face keeps its runs but is written in the new face, so it is still measured whole in that face, as before.
- `page_font_metrics` also reads each run's font past the first 256 page fonts, as it already did for each line's font.

Fixes #5769

## How you verified it

- New test `a_paragraph_across_two_subsets_of_one_font_keeps_its_scale`: a two-row paragraph drawn through two Type 3 subsets of one face (the first encodes the space, `a` and `b`, the second `c` and `d`). It edits the paragraph and checks that every rewritten run is `100 Tz`.
  - With the fix reverted it fails with `["180 Tz", "180 Tz", "180 Tz", "180 Tz", "100 Tz"]`.

author: KenM76
body:
M12: PRC reader crate (`pdfcraft-prc`) (#1297)

## What this changes

This adds `crates/prc`, a reader for PRC (ISO 14739-1), the 3D format a PDF `/3D` stream of `/Subtype /PRC` carries (ISO 32000-2 §13.6.3). It is an L0 standalone crate, with no dependency on any other PdfCraft crate. Refs #1297.

It reads:
- the container, with each section inflated under a byte ceiling;
- the bit-level primitives;
- the schema a newer producer uses to describe fields it added;
- plain tessellations (meshes, wires; markups read past);
- the product tree, into placed, coloured meshes (`PrcFile::placements`) and a model-tree listing (`PrcFile::model_tree`).

PMI markups, views, scene lights and clipping planes are read past so files that carry them still place their meshes, but they are not modelled.

**This is a library slice.** No viewer, adapter or `automation` tool uses it yet; those follow with the 3D viewing work tracked in #467 and #1297. `misc.3d-view` stays `planned`.

**Not yet done:** compressed tessellations are read to their end so later entities decode, but their triangles are not rebuilt. That is the next PR. Textures are read past.

title: Let Update header & footer edit each header, on every page it is on
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5785

**Cause:** Update header & footer reopened the dialog with one shared draft, which holds the settings and page range of the last header added. Header marks in the PDF were saved with only a `/PCMark /HeaderFooter` tag and no settings, so an earlier header could not be loaded back into the dialog or found by page.

**Fix:** Each page's header mark now also stores its settings in a `/PCSettings` dictionary. Update loads the header on the current page and finds every page that carries the same header. While the From/To range is left as loaded, OK applies to exactly those pages. If no range can select them exactly (for example pages 1, 2, 5, 6, 8), the dialog shows a range covering them all and adds a line naming the only pages that will change. If the user edits the range, OK applies to the edited range.

title: refactor(sign): encode and decode PEM with the base64 crate
author: smittie2000
body:
> **Stack: layer 5 of 33** (hand-rolled code replaced by std and existing helpers). **Depends on #5799** (and the layers below it). This PR targets `main` from a fork, so it also contains the layers below it: **review only the top commit**, "refactor(sign): encode and decode PEM with the base64 crate". Merge in order.

## What this changes

`crates/sign/src/x509.rs` had its own base64 encoder (in `to_pem`, Export certificate) and decoder (`fn base64`, which `load_certificates` uses for PEM `CERTIFICATE`, `PKCS7` and `CMS` blocks). Both now use `base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD`. The `base64 = "0.23"` crate is already a direct dependency of sign, and `pkcs12::decode_base64` already reads `.p12` files the same way: whitespace stripped, then `STANDARD.decode`.

- **Encoding is byte-identical** for every input length. `to_pem` of the two OpenSSL fixtures reproduces the files exactly.
- **Decoding follows RFC 7468's lax grammar**, which the RFC tells parsers to accept: zero, one or two `=` at the end, whatever the length. Up to two trailing `=` are dropped, and the rest is decoded with `STANDARD_NO_PAD`. So **unpadded and over-padded bodies still load, as they did before.**
- **It rejects only what isn't base64** and the old decoder silently tolerated (the old one dropped every `=` wherever it appeared and decoded whatever was left):
  - a `=` inside the body, or a third `=` at the end, which are outside the grammar
  - a one-character tail, which can't encode a byte and was silently dropped, hiding truncation
  - non-zero bits after the last byte, which RFC 4648 §3.5 lets decoders reject

  These now give `SignError::Malformed("PEM base64")` from the existing caller. Nothing the old decoder rejected is accepted now, and every body both accept decodes to the same bytes. Header lines such as `Proc-Type:`, CRLF line endings and trailing spaces behave as before.

title: perf(cos): an object that can't be read is searched for once, not on every read
author: KenM76
body:
**Update after #5548.** `main` now searches the file only once for an object that is missing, which covers the slow title redraw described below. What this PR still adds: other failed loads are cached too, most importantly a member of an object stream that cannot be decoded. On `main`, every read of such a member decodes the whole stream again (up to the 1 GiB stream limit each time); with this PR it is decoded once. The merge and its new test are described in the latest comment.

## What this changes

Reported by @SilverKn1ght, who found the slow redraw on one of their own files. Thank you.

A file whose document information dictionary can't be parsed, and that asks for its title to be shown (`/ViewerPreferences /DisplayDocTitle true`), makes the window redraw slowly, even while it is only being dragged.

The title is read several times a frame (window title and tab strip, through `Document::display_name` and `pdfcraft_organize::info`). `pdfcraft_cos::Document::try_get` kept only objects that loaded. An object whose entry points at something that doesn't parse falls back to `scan_for`, a search of the whole file for its header. When that fails too, nothing was kept, so the next read searched the whole file again: in an 18 MB file that was thousands of candidate parses per read, several reads per frame. Headless commands read the title once, so they never showed it.

`try_get` now keeps the load result, a failure as well. It is the same cache map, so failures get the same count and byte bounds, the same clears (authentication, reconstruction) and the same privacy in scan readers (`ObjectReader`), and clones share them as they share loaded objects. Edits are read from the overlay before the cache, as before, so a number that is set or freed still answers for itself.

A failure is kept from a nested load as well, just as a success already is; only a poisoned lock is never kept. Failures count towards the cache's object caps and hold no bytes of their own. Sharing the …

title: M12: add a 3D model (U3D or PRC) to a page with a poster (#1297)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

A new `model_add` automation tool and `Edit::AddModel3d` add a 3D model to a page, as Acrobat's Rich Media ▸ Add 3D does. Refs #1297.

The file at `path` becomes a 3D annotation (ISO 32000-2 §13.6.2) in `rect`:

- **The model** goes into a Flate-compressed 3D stream (§13.6.3) with `/Type /3D` and `/Subtype /U3D` or `/PRC`. The format is read from the file's first bytes (`U3D` and a zero byte, or `PRC`). Anything else is refused before the document changes. `/3DD` references the stream, so the annotation has its own instance.
- **Activation** (`/3DA /A`): `click` (`/XA`, the standard's default), `page_open` (`/PO`) or `page_visible` (`/PV`).
- **The poster** (`/AP /N`) is what prints and what a reader shows until the model is activated. It is the picture at `poster` (an image, or a page of a PDF kept as vector content) fitted inside `rect`, keeping its shape and centred. Without one, it is a light frame labelled "3D model".
- **`/Contents`** carries `name` (the file name by default) as the annotation's alternate description (§12.5.2).
- **Version.** A 3D annotation is PDF 1.6, and PRC is 1.7 (§13.6). A document whose header and catalog `/Version` both say less gets `/Version` in its catalog (§7.7.2), as the optimizer already does for JBIG2.

The edit is undoable ("Add 3D model"), needs the comments permission, and rebuilds only the comments view.

The poster path reuses the custom-stamp code (`mark_source`, `fit_picture`). The stamp's placement matrix moved into `appearance::picture_place` so both use it. That is an extraction: the stamp output is unchanged, and the stamp tests pass as before.

### fix(forms): take AFDate month lengths and weekdays from chrono

`crates/forms/src/af/format.rs` (`AFDate_FormatEx`, `util.printd`/`scand`-style date fields) had its own calendar code: a leap-year rule in `days_in` and Sakamoto's method in `weekday`. Both now use `chrono::NaiveDate`, and forms gains `chrono = { workspace = true }`: the std-only workspace entry, already in the graph through pdfcraft-cos, which builds for wasm.

`DateTime` is public and carries any `i32` year (`af.rs`'s `never_crash_tests` pin `i32::MAX`). A year chrono can represent goes to chrono as it is; past that range it is moved into its 400-year cycle (`rem_euclid(400)`), CLAUDE.md's one sanctioned calendar exception. The calendar repeats exactly every 146,097 days, a whole number of weeks. `days_in` mirrors the chrono-based `days_in` in `crates/js/src/formcalc/dates.rs`, which forms cannot depend on.

What changes:

- **Month lengths: nothing.** They are identical for every `(i32, u32)`, including negative years and invalid months, which still count 31 days.
- **Weekdays for years 1 and up: nothing.**
- **Year 0 and negative years: fixed.** Sakamoto's method used Rust's truncating `/` on a negative adjusted year, so January and February of year 0, and many negative-year dates, came out one weekday late. A typed year `0000` can reach this: 0000-01-01 showed "Sunday" and is now "Saturday".

They now show the day number for `ddd`/`dddd`, as engine's date formats do (#5809). `parse_date` already rejects such dates via `days_in`, so typed input never reaches this.

author: smittie2000
body:

>
> One PR with 6 commits on main. It now holds what #5815, #5818 and #5824 proposed; they are closed in its favour.
>
> 1. `1ca5661b` fix(app): decode file:// launcher arguments with percent-encoding
> 2. `c069a99d` refactor(engine): percent-decode mailto parameters with percent-encoding (was #5815)
> 3. `de3a5682` refactor(js): FormCalc url Encode/Decode through percent-encoding (was #5818)
> 4. `5e6a5fa0` test(js): pin that FormCalc url Encode escapes + and Decode keeps it
> 5. `0d555873` refactor: percent-encode URIs with percent-encoding in annot, ui-egui and xtask (was #5824)
> 6. `490886f0` test(xtask): pin file_url's escaping
>
> **Only the first commit changes behaviour.** The others replace hand-written `%XX` loops with the same crate and keep the output identical.

## What this changes

### fix(app): decode file:// launcher arguments with percent-encoding

Desktop launchers on Linux start PdfCraft with a `file://` URI (#382). `path_from_arg` (apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs) decoded its `%XX` escapes by hand, using `u8::from_str_radix` on the two bytes after each `%`. That function accepts a leading `+`, so **`file:///tmp/a%+1.pdf` opened `/tmp/a\x01.pdf`**, a different file. This is the same bug class #4586 fixed in FormCalc's url Decode.

The decoder is now `percent_encoding::percent_decode_str(rest).decode_utf8()`. It decodes `%` plus two hex digits (checked with `char::to_digit(16)`) and otherwise keeps the `%` and carries on with the next byte, exactly as the old loop did. Invalid UTF-8 still falls back to the argument as given.

Behaviour for every other input is unchanged: a lone `%`, `%2` at the end, `%zz`, a `%` before a multi-byte character, `%-1` (which `from_str_radix` already rejected for `u8`), and upper- or lower-case hex.

title: feat(cos): list the objects that could not be read in doc_info
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

A single object that can't be read is silent today. `get` reads it as null (ISO 32000-2 §7.3.10), the file opens, and `doc_info`'s `repairs` stays empty, because the repair log only records document-level repairs (a rebuilt cross-reference index, a page tree found by scanning). A file whose `/Info` dictionary doesn't parse opens with no title and no word about why.

Now `pdfcraft_cos::Document` records each object whose load fails, and `doc_info` lists them in a new `unreadable_objects` array, one line per object:

```
object 4 0 could not be read: syntax error at byte 210: …
```

- **Where it is recorded:** in `try_get`, when `load` fails, so every reader goes through it: `get`, `resolve`, scans (`scan_objects*` share the record, like clones do) and the indirect-`/Length` lookups. For an object stored in the file, the reason is what parsing it at its cross-reference offset found (a best account: the reader also tried other places, and this re-parse does not resolve an indirect `/Length`), or "no readable copy was found at its cross-reference offset or elsewhere in the file" when the offset holds another object and searching found none. A reference cycle refused by the load guard and a poisoned lock are not recorded. The reason is built only for an object not yet listed, so an object asked for again and again costs one extra parse in all.
- **Bounded and deduplicated:** at most 100 objects, keyed by number, first reason kept, reason cut to 160 characters. Past 100 a last line says there were more.
- **What resets it:** the same events that reset the object cache. Authenticating (objects read before the key was known) and rebuilding the index start it afresh. Opening the file again builds a new document. An edited or freed object drops off that document's list (a clone keeps it).
- **Kept apart from `repairs`.** Nothing was repaired: the object's content is lost, and the "This file was damaged and has been repaired" notice and the signature list…

title: M12: FormCalc prints numbers to at most 15 significant digits
author: seanGSISG
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5822.

FormCalc's number-to-text conversion (`num_text`, `crates/js/src/formcalc/value.rs`) printed every non-integer with **twelve fixed decimals**. When a value has six or more digits before the point, those decimals reach past the 15 significant digits a double holds, so the binary noise of the stored value shows:

| FormCalc | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1 * 279893.88` | `279893.880000000005` | `279893.88` |
| `1 * 291774.12` | `291774.119999999995` | `291774.12` |
| `Sum()` of five such amounts | `1466917.350000000093` | `1466917.35` |
| `1000000 / 3` | `333333.333333333314` | `333333.333333333` |
| `1 / 3`, `0.1 + 0.2`, `0.3 - 0.1 - 0.2` | `0.333333333333`, `0.3`, `0` | unchanged |

This shows up on real forms. USACE **ENG Form 93** (Payment Estimate, Contract Performance) is a dynamic XFA invoice form whose amount column is a FormCalc `qty * price` calculate and whose total is a `Sum()`. In PdfCraft 0.15.0 and 0.17.0 its amounts show as `…9893.880000000005` and its total as `…6917.350000000093`, where Adobe Reader shows `$279,893.88` and `$1,466,917.35`. One of our accounting users asked to switch back to Acrobat because of it.

The fix prints at most **15 significant digits and at most 12 decimals**, then drops trailing zeros:

- 15 digits is the most a double holds for every value, so a value typed with up to 15 digits prints back as typed, and noise past that never shows. The function's doc comment already said "up to 15 digits".
- The 12-decimal cap stays, so for `|n| < 1000` the output is byte-for-byte what it was. Sums that should be zero (`0.3 - 0.1 - 0.2`) still print `0`, not `-0.0000000000000000277`.
- With 15 or more digits before the point no decimals are left. Only a fraction loses its trailing zeros, so `1e20` keeps its zeros.

**Scope.** This fixes only the noise. The amounts still show without `$`, grouping or rounding to two places, because XFA numeric fields ignore their `num{…}` display picture. That…

title: M7: Arrange keeps a top-level inline image a unit of its own (#3146)
author: ljkx
body:
## What this changes

Arrange works out the stacking units of a page with `content_units` (`crates/edit/src/images.rs`). Its `BI` branch scanned forward for an `EI` op, but the content parser emits a whole inline image (`BI` … `ID` … `EI`) as a single `BI` op, so no `EI` op ever comes and the unit ran to the end of the scan. Everything after a top-level inline image became one unit:

- SendBackward on an image after a top-level inline image acted like SendToBack (it jumped behind everything, not one step).
- BringForward / BringToFront on an image in the swallowed region could silently do nothing.

A `BI` op is now a unit of its own, like `Do` and `sh`. Inline images inside `q`/`Q`, `BT`/`ET` or marked content are unaffected, since those sequences are still found by their own closing ops.

Fixes #3146
