title: fix(filters): inflate with zlib-rs everywhere, and charge the image allowance for what Flate reads
author: Piohrun
body:
Refs #5755.

## What this changes

The image allowance (#5569's `ImageBudget`) charged a Flate stage for the bytes it made, and for its input only as what the stage before it had made. But inflating does work for every block it reads, whether or not the block makes anything. A review of #5698 found a stream that exploits this, and the same pricing is in every `ImageBudget` user: clearing, Optimize, export, compare, and redaction's images and dictionaries. A 250-byte stream of four Flates over 32 MiB of empty blocks took 47 s and was charged about 34 million steps. From that, the review worked out about 7 hours before a 240 KB file of them is refused.

The cost comes from miniz_oxide, flate2's backend here: it took about 1.7 µs for every fixed-Huffman block, empty or not, against about 11 to 13 ns for zlib-rs. The Windows build was already using flate2's zlib-rs backend instead. `craft-update` turns on `zip`'s `deflate-flate2-zlib-rs`, and with both backends on, flate2 inflates with zlib-rs, which I checked by timing. Measured in a release build, ns per byte read:

| Stream | miniz_oxide 0.9.1 | zlib-rs 0.6.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Empty fixed-Huffman blocks, ten bits each | 1,383 | 9 |
| Fixed blocks of one literal | 768 | 6 |
| Empty dynamic blocks | 106 | 21 |
| Empty stored blocks | 2 | 1.3 |

Ordinary data inflates faster too. Each backend reading what its own encoder made, 16 MiB of text took 2.6 ms against 6.3 to 13.7, and a scan-like picture 38 ms against 53.

**Now:**
- flate2 is built with its `zlib-rs` backend on every platform. Other dependencies still build its default miniz_oxide backend, and flate2 prefers zlib-rs when both are built, as on Windows already. `a_copy_from_before_the_start_is_damage` fails under miniz_oxide, so it shows which one runs.
- zlib-rs refuses two kinds of damage that miniz_oxide read on from. One is a back-reference to before the start of the output, which zlib also refuses; miniz_oxide filled it with zeros. The other is a dynamic b…

`PrintStandard::of` (crates/organize/src/pdfx.rs) decides whether combined or inserted documents declare the same PDF/X standard. title: fix(automation): surface AcroForm calculation alerts and requests in apply
author: dikshant363
body:
## Summary
When running headless document applications with AcroForm scripts (`doc_apply`), JavaScript calculations triggering user alerts (`app.alert()`), viewer prompt requests (`app.beep()`, etc.), console diagnostics (`console.println()`), or script errors were executed but previously had their diagnostics silenced or consumed, leaving automation clients without structured feedback on calculation results and side effects.

This PR surfaces calculation alerts, viewer prompt requests, console messages, and script/document errors in `crates/automation/src/documents.rs`, records them in the structured `apply` response payload, documents `apply` for complete docstring coverage, and provides comprehensive regression tests in `tests/it/form_bulk.rs` verifying multi-alert delivery, console diagnostic preservation, document isolation, repeated call drainage, and undo/redo idempotence.

title: feat(annot): implement sound annotations (voice comments) with bounded RIFF parser per ISO 32000-2
author: dikshant363
body:
## Summary
Implements standard ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.15 Sound Annotations (voice comments) in `crates/annot`, with appearance stream generation and a clean-room bounded RIFF/WAVE parser in `crates/automation/src/wav.rs`.

## Changes
- `crates/annot/src/appearance/symbols.rs`: Add sound annotation speaker icon drawing.
- `crates/annot/src/create.rs`: Add `create_sound_annotation` with ISO 32000-2 compliant appearance dict. Validates channel count before computing frame size, requiring sample data to be a non-zero multiple of whole frames (2 bytes for mono, 4 bytes for stereo).
- `crates/automation/src/comments.rs`: Bound the file read in the WAV-loading path by 64 MiB (`MAX_WAV_FILE_SIZE`), inspecting file metadata before reading and reading at most `MAX_WAV_FILE_SIZE + 1` bytes without unbounded memory allocation.
- `crates/automation/src/wav.rs`: Implement a bounded, clean-room RIFF/WAVE audio parser:
  - Validates chunk headers, chunk ordering, and word-boundary padding.
  - Enforces 64 MiB allocation caps and checked arithmetic to prevent memory exhaustion or integer overflow on corrupt files.
  - Converts 8-bit unsigned and 16-bit little-endian PCM into big-endian signed 16-bit PCM per ISO 32000-2 §13.3.
- `crates/annot/src/tests.rs` & `crates/automation/tests/it/automation.rs`: Regression tests for mono and stereo whole-frame boundaries, empty samples, oversized files, and corrupt RIFF headers.

## Never-Crash & Security
- Safe by default: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]` in `crates/automation/src/wav.rs`.
- Memory bounds: Reject files exceeding 64 MiB prior to allocation, and cap reads at 64 MiB + 1.
- Clean error returns: All error states return structured `AnnotError::Invalid` or `WavError` and map cleanly to `ToolError::Failed`.

## Parity & Provenance
- Spec: ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.15 (Sound annotations) and §13.3 (Sound objects).
- Provenance: Clean-room implementation derived strictly from public specification…

Two protocol readers take line-delimited JSON-RPC from untrusted peers, and each had its own bounded line reader:

title: M12: an XFA page area keeps at most 128 content areas, so a subform split across them lays out within its budget (#5843)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A dynamic XFA `pageArea` with many short `contentArea` elements slices a flowed subform's paragraphs about one line to a page, so the subform is split across hundreds of pages. `split_block` (`crates/xfa/src/layout/flow.rs`) places the block one content area at a time and rebuilds and sorts the still-unplaced items on each pass, so with *L* paragraphs across about *L/66* pages the cost is on the order of *L²*. The file is valid and small — a 128 KB template took about 25 seconds, 16,000 paragraphs about 108 — before the 500-page limit finally returned `TooLarge`. The page limit and the measurement budget do not catch it: the work is spent before 500 pages, and the measurement budget covers container sizing, not this re-scan.

This PR bounds it in two places:

- **`split_block` spends the layout work budget** by the number of still-unplaced items it re-scans each pass. A block split across far more pages than a real form now stops in well under a second (128 KB: ~25 s to ~0.3 s), instead of running for tens of seconds before the page limit.
- **`parse_page_set` caps the content areas kept per page area** at `MAX_CONTENT_AREAS` (128), with a warning for the rest, as `parse_items` caps a choice list. This limits one of the amplifiers; the most on any one page area in the 500-form corpus is nine.

A deeper follow-up could make `split_block` find each cut incrementally instead of re-scanning every pass; that is a larger change to the layout core and is left out here.

Fixes #5843

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-xfa`
- [x] tests pass on `pdfcraft-xfa` (145 passed)

title: fix(optimize): make pictures under a stencil mask smaller
author: quincy-jc
body:
## What this changes

Reduce File Size and Optimize PDF skip any image that has a `/Mask`. That is right for a colour-key mask, which names sample values that resampling and JPEG would change. It isn't needed for a stencil mask, which is an image of its own with its own resolution (ISO 32000-2 §8.9.6.3): the picture can change under it, and the mask stays as it is.

With this change, pictures under a stencil mask go through the same colour and grey settings as other pictures. Pictures with a colour-key mask are still left alone, whether the array is direct or a reference. So is a picture whose `/Mask` isn't a stencil.

Some exporters put a stencil mask on every picture, even when it hides nothing, so whole drawing sets kept their pictures at full size. This is part of what people report in #5600. It doesn't close that issue.

With the Standard preset on two real drawing sets, the saving went from about 19% to 32% on one and from about 30% to 40% on the other. Run time barely changed. I can't share these files, and the tests use made-up PDFs.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-optimize`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize`; the tests matching "optimiz" and "reduc" in `pdfcraft-automation` and `pdfcraft-engine`
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` and `cargo xtask parity`

I ran each new test against broken versions of the check:

| Check changed to | Test that fails |
|---|---|
| The old `d.contains(b"Mask")` | `a_picture_with_a_stencil_mask_is_downsampled_under_its_mask` |
| No mask check at all | `a_picture_whose_mask_is_not_a_stencil_is_left_alone` |
| Only a direct array counts | `a_picture_whose_mask_is_not_a_stencil_is_left_alone` |

title: fix(redact): apply marks with an indirect /Subtype and judge inline annotations
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-200 / CWE-212: sensitive data left in a redacted file).

**What was wrong**
- `marks_checked` and the annotation passes read `/Subtype` with `Dict::name`, which does not follow an indirect reference. A Redact annotation whose `/Subtype` is `N 0 R` -> `/Redact` was skipped by `apply` (the audit, which resolves it, still counts it as a mark), so the other marks applied and the content under that one stayed while the operation reported success.
- `/Annots` entries written in place (direct dictionaries rather than references) were kept unconditionally, both in the per-page removal and in the cross-page reply/pop-up pass. Their own `/Contents` survived even when they lay under a mark, and an inline reply or pop-up kept a removed comment reachable through `/IRT` or `/Parent`.

**What changed** (`crates/redact/src/lib.rs`)
- New `subtype(doc, d)` helper resolves `/Subtype`; it is used everywhere redaction classifies an annotation (mark collection, inline-mark refusal, removal, the cross-page pass).
- Inline entries are judged like referenced ones: by rectangle overlap, as replies (`/IRT`) and as pop-ups (`/Parent`), on the marked page and across pages, and removed by their position in `/Annots`. An inline annotation's `/Popup` goes with it, since that is the only link it can have to its pop-up. An inline widget's owner is found through its `/Parent`.

**Blast radius**: `pdfcraft-redact` `apply` only. Documents whose annotations are all indirect with direct-name subtypes behave as before.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-redact --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: Finished, exit 0
- [ ] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact`: 169 passed, 1 failed, 1 ignored. The one failure is the wall-clock bound in `a_form_that_fans_out_or_loops_is_bounded_by_the_page_budget` (205 s against a 120 s limit) on a machine at load average ~170 with many concurrent buil…

title: M12: the XFA draw phase lays out text within an allowance, embedded field values included (#5851)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

`draw_value_text` lays a draw's text out more than once: when the text overflows the height it is given it is re-measured at up to five smaller scales to shrink it (up to six `text::measure_height` passes, then the final `text::layout`), and a repeating subform draws its text once per instance with no draw-phase cache. So large text drawn across many instances costs one full text layout per instance per pass, for seconds of work, and finishes with a valid layout — neither `MAX_PAGES` nor the measurement budget covers the characters the draw phase lays out.

`draw_value_text` now counts the characters of each pass against a new budget, `MAX_DRAW_CHARS`, the way `MAX_MEASURES` bounds container sizing. A real form's draws stay far below it; a template that lays out far more text stops with `TooLarge`. The budget is reduced under `cfg(test)` so the guard is exercised without laying out hundreds of megabytes.

A deeper follow-up could share a repeating subform's identical drawn instances through a cache and find the shrink scale in fewer passes; those touch the draw path more widely and are left out here.

Fixes #5851

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-xfa`
- [x] tests pass on `pdfcraft-xfa` (145 passed)

**Test.** `large_text_drawn_in_many_instances_spends_the_draw_budget` (`crates/xfa/src/tests.rs`) lays out fifty instances of a 20,000-character draw and asserts `TooLarge`, and that one copy of the same draw lays out. With the charge and check removed it fails (the many-instance form lays out instead of stopping).

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests
- [x] No indexing or slicing with input-derived positions; the budget uses saturating arithmetic

title: fix(create): decode an exported image or mask no further than its samples need
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

Export ▸ Image (and Save image as) decoded every lossless image and every soft or stencil mask with `ImageBudget::decode(doc, s, MAX_DECODED)`, a 1 GiB per-stage allowance, before `unpack` read only the declared `Width × Height` samples. A few KB of Flate on an image of one pixel could therefore inflate to a gigabyte of memory (and the matching CPU) for nothing, and a mask shared by many images could do it once per image.

## What changed

- `extract::decoded` takes the image's size, components and bits per component, and decodes within `allowance(...)`: up to three bytes per sample byte plus a predictor byte per row, plus 4 KiB, or for a fax image about a byte a pixel plus each row's end. These are the same bounds Optimize (`images::allowance`) and redaction already use. It is never less than the stream's raw length (already in memory) and never more than `MAX_DECODED`.
- `image()` reads `BitsPerComponent` before decoding so it can size the allowance. `gray_plane` uses the mask's own size and depth.
- Repeated decoding of a shared mask is still charged to the export's shared `ImageBudget`. That already caps total work across the export, so this PR does not add a mask cache.
- Regression test `image_data_far_past_its_samples_is_not_decoded`: a 1×1 image whose Flate stream inflates to 64 MiB is left out, and a mask like it is not applied. Data a little past the samples still exports. I reverted the fix and confirmed the test fails without it.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-create` image export only (`extract_images`, `image_file`, `image_file_within`). An image whose decoded data is more than about 3× its samples is now reported as skipped instead of exported. Redaction and Optimize already treat that case the same way.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-create -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create` (all pass)

## Checks not run

- Workspace-wide tests, `cargo xtask layers/a…

title: fix(content): bound parser recovery work and held operands
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

The content-stream parser (`pdfcraft-content`) did work out of proportion to its input in two places, and held an unbounded number of operands in a third.

- **Failed compound operands were retried from every byte.** When an operand such as `[`, `<` or `<<` failed after reading to the end of the stream, recovery rewound to one byte after where the operand started and read the rest again. `[[[[…` therefore took time quadratic in its length. In a release build, 20 KB of `[` took 5.5 s, 40 KB of `[` took 24 s, and 40 KB of `<` took 43 s. Failed reads now share an allowance of 8 bytes per stream byte, with a floor of 1 MiB. Until the allowance runs out, recovery is unchanged: retry from the next byte, so a stray opener in otherwise good content still loses only that byte. After that, a failed operand is skipped whole, as far as it read, the same way long unreadable numbers already are. Those bytes count in `skipped`.
- **Unreadable inline-image parameters were rescanned.** `BI /K ( EI` repeated made each `BI` read the unterminated string to the end of the stream, and recovery resumed at the next `EI`. That was superlinear too: 20 KB took 143 ms and 40 KB took 927 ms. The bytes these failed parameters read now come out of the same allowance. Once it is spent, an unreadable image ends where its parameters stopped reading.
- **Operands with no operator were all held.** `Ops::next` kept every operand until an operator arrived, so compressed content made of bare numbers built one `Vec<Object>` of tens of millions of entries. No operator takes more than a few dozen operands, so only about the last 1024 are kept now. The older ones are dropped and counted in `skipped`. Arity checks on the operator still fail, as they did before.

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-407, CWE-400).

## How you verified it

- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-content --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-content`: 32 passed
- `cargo fmt --check` on t…

title: fix(cos): a decode pays for the encoded bytes it reads
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`DecodeBudget` (one allowance shared by every decode of a page walk) charged each decode for what its filter stages produced. A stream that produces almost nothing still has to be read: a long whitespace-only `/ASCIIHexDecode` stream decodes to zero bytes, so a page whose `/Contents` names it thousands of times scanned the whole stream on every reference without spending anything. The work was quadratic in the file's size. Each empty result also kept a buffer sized from the input until the whole `/Contents` array had been collected.

## What changed

- `DecodeBudget::charge` charges each decode at least the encoded bytes it reads (`max(output, input)`), on success and on failure. A spent limit is charged as before.
- Successful results whose capacity is more than twice their length are shrunk before they are returned.
- New test `references_to_a_stream_that_decodes_to_nothing_pay_for_reading_it`: 1,000 references to a 64 KiB whitespace ASCIIHex stream with an allowance of ten reads. Ten decode and the rest are refused. `a_decode_that_gives_nothing_back_still_pays` now expects its input length (slightly more than it decoded).

## Blast radius

Only `pdfcraft-cos`'s `DecodeBudget`, which content walks in a11y, audit, edit, forms, fonts, organize, optimize, print and redact share. Legitimate content streams decode to at least their encoded size (Flate and LZW expand, raw streams are copied 1:1), so they are charged what they were charged before. Only streams that shrink, such as ASCIIHex, ASCII85 and failed decodes, now cost their input length. The page allowance (256 MiB) is unchanged.

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-400).

## Checks run

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos --lib`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-cos -- --check`

## Checks not run

- Tests of the downstream crates that use `DecodeBudget` (a11y, edit, redact, ...). None of them assert exact remaining amounts except `fonts` …

title: fix(create): image export reads a shared resource dictionary once
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`extract::collect`, which finds the images a page uses for Export ▸ Image, went through every form XObject's resources separately. It only remembered which forms it had entered, not which resource or XObject dictionaries it had already read, and it started over for each page. A file whose forms all share one indirect XObject dictionary listing thousands of forms made the work quadratic, cloning the dictionary for every form. It also pushed the same image reference once per form before the caller deduplicated them.

## What changed

- `collect` takes the resources as an `Object` and keeps one `visited` set for the whole export. The set holds forms and resource or XObject dictionaries given by reference, and none of them is read twice. A second set, `images`, holds the images found, so each image is collected once.
- `extract_images_within` shares both sets across pages. Output is unchanged: an image is still reported on the first page that uses it, as it was through `seen`.
- Regression test `forms_sharing_one_resource_dictionary_read_it_once`: 2,000 forms share one resource dictionary. The test checks that the dictionary is read once, the image is collected once, and the page export holds it once. With the shared-dictionary check disabled, the test fails.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-create` image export (`extract_images`) only. Total traversal work is now bounded by the number of objects in the file.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-create -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create` (all pass)

## Checks not run

- Workspace-wide tests, `cargo xtask layers/assets`, the wasm check (left to CI)

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-400).

title: fix(create): image export checks a JPEG's Extended XMP chunks before decoding it
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

The pinned `zune-jpeg` (0.5.15) re-sorts and rescans every incomplete Extended XMP chunk it has collected after each APP1 marker, so header parsing is quadratic in the number of chunks. Image import (`upright_image::turned`) already refuses a JPEG with more than `MAX_EXTENDED_XMP_CHUNKS` (1024) chunks before decoding it. Image export did not check: `jpeg_size`, `jpeg_of_size` (RGB, grey and JPEG masks) and `cmyk_jpeg_samples` passed a JPEG stream from the PDF straight to the decoder. A PDF image with tens of thousands of empty chunks could keep the export busy for a long time.

## What changed

- The import check is now `upright_image::decodable_metadata` (`pub(crate)`), used by import as before.
- `extract::jpeg_size` and `extract::cmyk_jpeg_samples` call it before they construct a decoder. `jpeg_of_size` goes through `jpeg_size`, which covers the RGB, grey and mask paths. When a JPEG fails the check, export treats it as one it can't decode: the image is written as is, or the mask is left out.
- The test helper that builds the chunk flood is shared (`upright_image::tests::with_extended_xmp_chunks`).
- Regression test `a_jpeg_with_thousands_of_extended_xmp_chunks_is_exported_without_decoding` covers a JPEG image with a soft mask and a JPEG soft mask, each with 5,000 chunks. Neither reaches the decoder. With the guard disabled, the test fails.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-create` image export only. Ordinary JPEGs, which have far fewer than 1024 Extended XMP chunks, are unaffected.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-create -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create` (all pass)

## Checks not run

- Workspace-wide tests, `cargo xtask layers/assets`, the wasm check (left to CI). JPEG decoding in other crates (render, optimize) is out of scope for this PR.

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-400).

title: ci(release): sign the Linux packages with LINUX_SIGNING_KEY
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Draft.** Merge after storytold/craft-common-actions#128 and #129. Until #129 merges, the shared release workflow doesn't declare `LINUX_SIGNING_KEY`, and passing it would fail the release.

## Why

Every ArtCraft Linux release is to be signed with one ArtCraft Linux release key, covering deb, rpm, Arch, AppImage, tarballs, the Flatpak bundle and the Flatpak OCI image. The key's fingerprints:
- primary key `2B76 741B 414A AD6C D33E 6312 13A0 05C0 B9D7 C3ED`;
- signing subkey `568D C1F6 8F8F AECC 797F 3C7B 006D AF6B B0EF 334E`.

The signing subkey is already stored as `LINUX_SIGNING_KEY` in this repo's `release` environment. storytold/craft-common-actions#129 does the signing in the shared release workflow, but only when the caller passes the secret.

## What changed

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** passes `LINUX_SIGNING_KEY` to the shared workflow. That signs the rpm and deb (embedded), the Arch package (`.sig`), the AppImage and tarballs (`.asc`), the Flatpak OCI image, and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
- **`packaging/linux/flatpak-bundle.sh`**, updated with craft-common-actions' `scripts/scaffold-flatpak-oci.sh`:
  - a release build signs the bundle's commit and embeds the public key, so `flatpak install` verifies the bundle. It does nothing without the key;
  - the bundle's origin updates from the ArtCraft OCI repository (`--repo-url=oci+https://getartcraft.com`). Prereleases get no update source.
- **`packaging/linux/flatpak-oci.sh`** is added where it was missing, so releases push the OCI image to GHCR.

## Before merging

- storytold/craft-common-actions#128 and #129 are merged.

title: fix(forms,xfa): find every password field before a save skips scrubbing it
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

Saves write a copy of the document without typed Password-field values (#3926, #3944). Three gaps could let that copy keep a typed password, because the checks that decide whether scrubbing is needed answered "no password here" when they had not looked everywhere the form's own field walk does:

- **`pdfcraft_forms::has_password_flag`** (the quick pre-check) stopped silently at its depth limit. Since it visits the tree depth-first, a field the field walk reaches near the top could be reached first at the end of a long branch and cut off there, and page widgets were only checked up their `/Parent` chain, not below the topmost field the field walk adopts. It now answers `true` (so the caller reads every field) whenever its walk is cut short or a `/Parent` chain is too long, and walks below fields adopted from page widgets.
- **XFA AcroForm password classification** (`acro_password_fields`) walked only 32 levels, shallower than editing and dataset synchronization (64). It now walks as deep as the field walk, and reports when it was cut short: clearing then returns an error, so the save is refused instead of written with a typed password in the datasets.
- **XFA datasets inspection** parsed the datasets packet of an XFA array on its own, so a packet using the `xfa`/`xdp` prefixes its preamble declares failed to parse and counted as holding no passwords, while the datasets writer (which wraps such a packet in those declarations) had written the typed value into it. It now reads the packet the way the writer does (`parse_datasets_packet`).

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-312, CWE-200).

Blast radius: save-time scrubbing in `pdfcraft-forms` and `pdfcraft-xfa` only; no public signatures change. Forms whose field tree is deeper than the field walk now always take the full password scan (slower, same result). Static XFA forms with a datasets packet whose AcroForm tree is deeper than 64 levels can no longer be saved, with an error saying why;…

title: fix(create): write a new document's page tree once
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`add_page` in `pdfcraft-create` added each new page to the page tree with `Document::update_dict`. That call clones the tree's dictionary, and the closure cloned the whole `/Kids` array again before pushing one reference. Creating `n` pages therefore copied O(n²) references. In Create PDF from text each form feed starts a page, and nothing caps the number of pages, so a small text file (or a generated report through `from_text_escaped`) full of form feeds could block the caller. In a debug build, 10,000 form feeds took 3.3 s and 40,000 took 108 s.

## What changed

- A private `Pages` builder reads the tree once (`Pages::of`), adds page objects while it collects their references (`add`), and writes `/Kids` and `/Count` in one `update_dict` (`finish`). `blank`, `from_images_with_resolution` and `set_text` (text creation) all use it.
- `add_page`'s ignored `update_dict` error is now propagated as `CreateError::Invalid`.
- Regression test `text_of_many_form_feeds_makes_its_pages_in_linear_time`: 40,000 form feeds give 40,001 pages with the right `/Kids` and `/Count`, in about 2 s instead of 108 s (debug). The test also checks that blank and image documents keep their page counts.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-create`: `blank`, `from_images*`, `from_text`, `from_text_escaped`. The resulting documents are unchanged: same page objects, order, `/Kids` and `/Count`.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-create -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create` (all pass)
- Timing comparison against `origin/main`'s `lib.rs`

## Checks not run

- Workspace-wide tests, `cargo xtask layers/assets`, the wasm check (left to CI)

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-407).

title: fix(redact): structure titles go with the descriptions of removed content
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

**What was wrong.** When redaction or hidden-content removal changed a structure element's marked content, it cleared `/Alt`, `/ActualText` and `/E` from the owning element and its ancestors but kept `/T`. Producers often fill the title with the element's text, so a redacted or hidden word could survive in the saved file's structure tree. Annotation removal used its own key list, which did include `/T`, so the policy differed between paths.

**What changed.** One `DESCRIPTIONS` policy (`Alt`, `ActualText`, `T`, `E`) in `crates/redact/src/tags.rs` now serves the owning element, ancestor cleanup, in-place description detection and annotation removal. Three regression tests in `tests/descriptions.rs` cover a redacted word, hidden text and a removed link annotation, each with titles on the owner and its ancestors, and check that an unaffected sibling keeps its title.

**Blast radius.** Only structure elements already being stripped of descriptions lose their title as well. Unaffected elements are unchanged. #1347 (open, conflicting with main since the ancestor cleanup was rewritten) proposed the same title clearing against older code.

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-212).

title: fix(redact): hidden-layer removal reads the default state as viewers do
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

**What was wrong.** Hidden-layer removal (`sanitize::hidden_layers`) computed the default optional-content state differently from the viewer:
- an indirect `/BaseState` was ignored,
- with `/BaseState /OFF`, a group in both `/ON` and `/OFF` was treated as visible, although `/OFF` is applied last (ISO 32000-2 §8.11.4.3).

The membership classifier in `interp/layers.rs` also read `/Type` without resolving it, so an OCMD with an indirect `/Type` was never evaluated. In each case content the viewer hides stayed in the "sanitized" file.

**What changed.** `/BaseState` is resolved, and a group is hidden when `/OFF` lists it, or when the base state is OFF and `/ON` does not list it. A `has_type` helper resolves `/Type` for every OCMD/OCG check. Scan and removal share this computation. Three regression tests cover an indirect `/BaseState`, OFF winning over ON, and an OCMD with an indirect `/Type`.

**Blast radius.** Limited to Remove Hidden Information's hidden-layer category. More content can now be classified as hidden, and only where the viewer already hides it.

Addresses CodeRabbit security findings (CWE-212).

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` (pdfcraft-redact)

title: fix(audit): read operands from the end and every rectangle a fill paints
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

The faux-redaction audit (`crates/audit/src/cover.rs`) could disagree with what the renderer paints, which lets a crafted PDF hide extractable text under a black box and still pass the audit:

- **Operand selection.** `g` read its *first* operand, and `gs` and `Do` read their first name. The renderer takes operands from the end and ignores surplus ones before them. So `1 0 g` paints black but the audit saw white, and `/Empty /Cover Do` draws `/Cover` but the audit followed `/Empty` (same for a translucent `/Clear /Solid gs`).
- **Compound paths.** Each `re` replaced the pending path, and a second `m` turned the whole path into "other". A fill paints every subpath, so `<cover> re <decoy> re f` only audited the decoy, and the real cover was never checked.

## What changed

- `g` reads its last operand (`nums::<1>`), the same way `rg`/`k` already did. `gs` and `Do` use `Op::last_name`, which the redaction crate already uses for the same reason.
- `Path` now keeps every rectangular subpath (`re`, or a closed axis-aligned `m`/`l` quad) with its winding. When the path is filled:
  - nonzero rule with all subpaths winding the same way: each rectangle is painted. Duplicates and rectangles inside another one are dropped.
  - even-odd, or windings that disagree: the painted region is computed on the grid formed by the rectangles' edges. Holes stay holes, so an even-odd frame around text is still not a cover. The work is charged against a per-page bound (`MAX_PATH_WORK`), and the audit fails closed past it. Above 32 subpaths every rectangle counts as painted. That can over-report text inside a hole but never misses a cover.
- These are unchanged: a CTM change mid-path and a clip (`W`/`W*`) still make the path unreadable, and curves still stop the current subpath from counting as a rectangle.

## Blast radius

This only touches `pdfcraft-audit` (the faux-redaction verification). Some documents that used to pass will now report a cover: ones with surplus opera…

title: fix(content): an inline image only the renderer reads counts as ambiguous
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`inline_image` in `crates/content/src/lib.rs` takes an inline image's end from the renderer's tokenizer. When that tokenizer reads an image but the parameters do not read here (for example a stray operand before `ID`), the function returned `image: None` with `ambiguous: false`. The `BI` was dropped from `ops` and counted only as skipped bytes, so redaction's interpreter never saw the image and `Parsed::ambiguous_images` stayed 0. Apply then reported success while the image the page draws stayed under the mark.

## What changed

- `crates/content/src/lib.rs`: an image the renderer reads whose parameters this parser can't is marked ambiguous (`ambiguous: !readable`). Docs on `Inline::ambiguous` and `Parsed::ambiguous_images` say so.
- Redaction already fails closed on `ambiguous_images > 0` (`RedactError::Unreadable`), so no change there.

Tests: `an_inline_image_read_by_the_renderer_but_not_here_is_ambiguous` (content) and `a_page_whose_inline_image_only_the_renderer_reads_is_refused` (redact).

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft_content::parse` consumers that look at `ambiguous_images`: only `pdfcraft-redact`. Pages with inline images whose parameters both tokenizers read are unaffected.

title: fix(audit): read content one operator at a time and charge hidden text and findings
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

The faux-redaction audit (`crates/audit`) did more work, and held more memory, than its bounds charged for:

- `filled_rects` and `walk_xobject` parsed a page's joined content and every form XObject into a complete `Vec<Op>` before walking it. A stream of millions of two-byte operators compresses to a few kilobytes and fits the page decode budget, but the operator vector is tens of bytes per entry.
- Every `Do` copied the whole `/XObject` table to pick one entry, every `gs` copied the whole `/ExtGState` table, and each form's `/Resources` was copied per draw. A large unused entry in a shared table was copied once per operator.
- `annots` cloned the `/Annots` array and deep-copied every annotation dictionary before reading its `/Subtype`, so one large dictionary listed many times was copied per listing.
- `hidden_text` charged a hidden line one comparison per run or word box, but then copied and trimmed its whole text once per cover, so a padded line (long runs of spaces around one word) under many covers was read far beyond what the bound saw.
- `report_text` charged only the text a finding reports: findings with no text (copying withheld, or one annotation list shared by many pages) grew the finding vector for free.

## What changed

- The walk reads operators one at a time (`pdfcraft_content::ops`, the existing streaming reader); `walk_ops` takes an iterator. `MAX_OPS` is unchanged and still fails the audit closed.
- XObject, ExtGState and form resource tables, and annotation dictionaries, are borrowed through the resolved `Arc` instead of cloned.
- A hidden line's text costs `len / TEXT_BYTES_PER_COMPARISON` (16) comparisons per cover, in both the copying and the copy-withheld branch.
- Every finding charges `size_of::<AuditFinding>()` to the output bound, text or no text.

Two existing exact-limit tests gained the new charges; three new tests cover the text-byte charge, the record charge on a shared annotation list, and the unchanged output bo…

title: fix(redact): remove a stroked path by the box its stroke paints
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`Walk::paint_path` in `crates/redact/src/interp.rs` tested the path's construction-coordinate box against the marks. `overlaps` is strict, so a horizontal or vertical stroke (zero-area box) never hit, and its `m`/`l`/`S` stayed in the content beneath the redaction overlay (line-based barcodes, rules, confidential vector artwork). A wide stroke whose points lie just outside a mark but whose ink reaches into it was kept as well.

## What changed

- `Gs` tracks `line_width`, `miter_limit` and `line_join`; `w`, `M`, `j` and an ExtGState's `LW`, `ML`, `LJ` set them (`q`/`Q` save and restore them with the rest of the state).
- For a stroking operator (`S`, `s`, `B`, `B*`, `b`, `b*`) the box is grown by `stroke_box` before the hit test: half the width (a width of 0 is taken as one unit), times the miter limit when the path has two or more segments and mitred joins, scaled by the CTM's Frobenius norm. Caps and joins never extend further, so the bound is conservative; when in doubt the path goes.
- Fill-only operators and `n` are unchanged.

Test: `a_stroke_is_removed_by_its_painted_width` (a 12 pt line centred 5 pt above the mark goes, a 1 pt line there stays, a line through the mark goes).

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-redact` apply/verify only. Strokes near a mark whose painted width (or mitred corners) could reach it are now removed where before they stayed; that is the fail-closed direction.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-redact --check`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` (168 passed, 1 ignored as on main)
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`

## Checks not run

- workspace-wide `cargo test --workspace` / `cargo clippy --workspace` (memory-bound shared machine)

title: M10: grayscale with Print as image prints on a driver that keeps no grayscale (#5806)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Refs #5806 (the Print as image half of it).

With **Print as image** and **grayscale** on, PdfCraft already renders each page as a grey picture, so the print-ready PDF is grey before it reaches the printer. The job still asked the printer's driver for grayscale as well. A driver that keeps no grayscale setting, such as Microsoft Print to PDF and many inkjets, made craft-print refuse the whole job:

> the printer's driver did not retain the requested grayscale; nothing was sent

So even the grey pictures never printed.

Now the job asks the driver for grayscale only when the pages aren't grey pictures already. The rule is one function, `print::driver_needs_grayscale(grayscale, raster)`, used by both the Print dialog (`PrintDraft::job`) and `doc_print`, so the two can't drift apart. Colour pictures, and ordinary vector printing, still ask the driver for grayscale exactly as before.

The `print.grayscale` parity note and the `doc_print` `as_image` description now say this, and the note names what is still missing (below).

On Windows 10 Pro 22H2:

title: fix(js): bound array text, month parsing, name registration and list work
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

Five places in `pdfcraft-js` did work, or kept memory, that the script limits (loop iterations, recursion, `MAX_STEPS`, `MAX_PAYLOAD`) did not charge for:

- `host::strings` (the field `value`, `textColor`/`fillColor` setters and `resetForm`) converted every entry of a JavaScript array into its own Rust `String` with no total. An array of a million references to one 64 KiB string, well within `MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH`, was 64 GiB of copies before a scalar field discarded all but one.
- FormCalc `parse_date` copied and lowercased the whole rest of the text for every month token (`MMM`) of the picture: quadratic in the picture and text lengths, neither charged.
- XFA global registration (`xfa/globals.rs`) checked each child's name against a `Vec` of every name defined so far: quadratic in a wide form, before the script's time starts.
- FormCalc `gather` charged one step for a whole collection, and `list_push` charged nothing for a duplicate it dropped, so `list.all` on a list of same-named siblings did one step's work per pair.
- `add_instance` reserved only the new root's SOM before `clone_subtree` copied the whole subtree; a subform with long names could be copied up to the instance cap regardless of the byte budget.

## What changed

- `strings` adds each entry's bytes to a running total and refuses the array past `MAX_PAYLOAD` (32 MiB), the same budget as the run's output.
- `parse_date` reads at most `LONGEST_MONTH` (9) characters of the text for a month token.
- `defined` is a `HashSet<String>`; registration order and precedence are unchanged (the set only answers "already defined").
- `gather` and `list_push` charge a step per node visited, kept or not.
- `subtree_bytes` adds up the nodes, names and SOMs a copy keeps, and `add_instance` reserves that with the root's SOM before copying.

Three new tests: an array past the byte budget is refused (and one within it is not), a month name is read from a bounded prefix, and instances of a subform with lon…

title: M2: a soft hyphen a substitute font lacks draws its hyphen (#5888)
author: hasannadeem
body:
Fixes #5888.

## What this changes

Hyphens in the reported production lists drew as `Ë`, or as `!` in bold. The text is set in `ArialMT` and `Arial-BoldMT`, which the PDF doesn't embed: Type 0, `CIDFontType2`, `Identity-H`, `/CIDToGIDMap /Identity`, so each code is a glyph index in the author's Arial. Their `/ToUnicode` maps the hyphen's code `<0010>` to **U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN**, not U+002D. Windows exporters do this, because Arial maps both characters to the same glyph.

hayro draws a non-embedded font with a standard substitute (here a CFF Helvetica) and finds each glyph through `/ToUnicode`. The substitute has no glyph for U+00AD, so `map_code` fell through to taking CID 16 as the substitute's own glyph index, an unrelated glyph.

ISO 32000-2 Annex D.2 notes that WinAnsiEncoding's 0xAD means soft hyphen but is "typographically the same as hyphen", and hayro-interpret patch (30) already reads WinAnsi 0xAD that way for simple fonts. This applies the same rule to CID fonts. In the CFF branch of `Type0Font::map_via_unicode`, a soft hyphen the substitute has no glyph for draws its hyphen. A substitute that has a soft-hyphen glyph keeps drawing it, and the text is unchanged: selection, search and copy still see U+00AD.

The patch is (75) in `vendor/README.md`, marked `PdfCraft patch:` in the source.

## How you verified it

- `raster::tests::a_soft_hyphen_a_substitute_lacks_draws_its_hyphen` renders `<0010>` from a synthetic non-embedded `ArialMT` and from `Arial-BoldMT`, once with `/ToUnicode` giving U+00AD and once U+002D. The two must draw the same pixels, and the control must draw ink. The text must still read U+00AD.
- **Reverted the fix and watched it fail**, at the pixel comparison, for both fonts.
- The reporter's attached file renders with correct hyphens on this machine (`pdfcraft-cli render`, page 1, before and after). I didn't commit it or anything taken from it.

- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-tar…

title: M10: Windows prints a large image whole: drawn as tiles under Windows.Data.Pdf's cap (#5131)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5131, following the plan agreed there.

Windows prints every page through `Windows.Data.Pdf`, which draws any image of more than 2²² pixels (~4.19 MP) from a copy shrunk to that size. #5023 / storytold/craft-libs#396 render the page at the printer's resolution, but a large scan still came out soft: a 6000 × 6000 image printed as 2048 × 2048.

This draws such images as tiles in the copy that goes to the spooler:

- **`pdfcraft_optimize::tile_large_images`** (new `crates/optimize/src/tiles.rs`).
  - **The replacement.** Each image XObject over the cap becomes a form XObject with the *same object number*, drawing tiles placed every 2000 px; with the 1 px overlap a tile has at most 2001 px a side. Whatever drew the image (pages, nested forms, patterns, appearances) draws the tiles, untouched.
  - **Samples.** They're copied as stored: any bit depth, any colour space (CMYK, Indexed, Separation, DeviceN, Lab, ICC), decode array, interpolation, colour key. Tile columns start on multiples of 2000 px, so every tile row starts on a byte at any bit depth. A grey or RGB JPEG is decoded with optimize's existing JPEG path and stored with Flate.
  - **Masks.** A soft mask or stencil mask of the image's size is cut into the same tiles.
  - **Overlap.** Tiles overlap by 1 px, as the plan asked, except under a soft mask (see "Anything a reviewer should look at first").

title: fix(ui): do not open right-click context menu on image in crop mode (#5835)
author: Combiler01
body:
Fixes #5835

## What this changes

In image crop mode, right-clicking on the image (or on the crop box and drag handles after moving the crop area) no longer opens a context menu.

### Root cause
1. In crop mode, `image_input` delegates immediately to `crop_input` and returns early without updating `image_menu_id`.
2. When right-clicking on an image in crop mode—particularly after moving or shrinking the crop box—hit detection in `draw_pages` previously tested against the image's unedited `visible_rect`. Secondary clicks outside the original bounds registered `over_image = false`, resetting `view.image_selection = None` and dropping crop mode to display the page/canvas context menu ("Rotate view clockwise", "Take a snapshot", etc.).
3. If a hit did match, the absence of an active `image_menu_id` caused competing popup states.

### Fix
- Added [`crop_contains_point(...)`](crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs) to detect clicks within the active crop box (with handle margins), the full uncropped image bounds, and rotated OBBs.
- In `draw_pages` right-click routing, secondary clicks within the crop session keep `over_image = true`, preventing image deselection.
- In `resp.context_menu`, an `is_crop_over_image` guard immediately suppresses the context menu (`ui.close()`, `egui::Popup::close_all`, and resets `image_menu_id`) so the crop session and its action pills ("Done", "Cancel") remain active and undisturbed.
- Right-clicking outside the image on the page still properly clears the selection and opens the standard canvas context menu.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings` (passed with 0 warnings)

title: M10: a booklet's both sides follow a driver that keeps its own two-sided setting (#5772)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5772.

**Booklet ▸ Both sides** always asked the printer for two-sided printing, flipping on the short edge (#2707). Some drivers don't take two-sided settings from other programs: printers without two-sided printing, ones that only offer manual two-sided in their Properties, and Microsoft Print to PDF. For those, craft-print refused the whole job: "the printer's driver did not retain the requested simplex/duplex setting; nothing was sent".

The reporter's Epson ET-2870 driver offers only `psk:OneSided`. Their normal two-sided prints work because PdfCraft's Two-sided is left on "Printer default" and the Epson's own manual two-sided setting does the rest. Booklet couldn't use it.

Now a booklet's both sides ask such a driver for nothing, so its own setting applies, as it already does for ordinary printing (#2422). Acrobat itself enables two-sided printing for a booklet only "if available" (the quote is already in `booklet_duplex`'s doc comment).

- **`print::booklet_job_duplex(subset, two_sided)`** is the rule.
  - Both sides: the short edge, as before; nothing on a driver that doesn't take two-sided settings (`Some(false)`); the short edge when support is unknown.
  - Front or back only: one-sided, as before.
- **The Print dialog** uses it with the chosen printer's support from the printer list. That lookup is one method, `PrintDraft::printer_two_sided`, now also behind the note the dialog already shows for such printers ("…so its own setting applies. Change it in Properties…").
- **`doc_print`** does the same. It reads the printer list only for a booklet's both sides, the one job the rule changes.
  - That job then goes to the printer it found, by name. For "default", the two-sided decision and the job can't end up on different printers if the default changes while the document is rendered.

title: M11: JBIG2 images share a symbol dictionary, up to 16 at a time (optimize.mono-compression)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

With Monochrome Images set to JBIG2, Optimize stored each image's letters in a symbol dictionary of its own, so a scanned or rasterised document of N pages carried its font's shapes N times. Now up to 16 of the images the run stores as JBIG2 share one symbol dictionary, in a `/JBIG2Globals` stream holding the marks found in more than one of them. Each image's text regions refer to it first, then to a dictionary of its own for the marks only that image repeats. Everything stays lossless: only exact copies share a symbol, as before.

An image is stored that way when it comes out smaller than coded alone, and a group only when what its images save together is more than the globals take. Each image is weighed naming the globals with the longest reference an object can have (`4294967295 65535 R`), so a group is shared only if it is smaller even then.

Measured on pages of 10 pt text rendered by PdfCraft at 300 dpi and thresholded to 1 bit, eight pages each:

| Text | Alone | Shared | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| Helvetica, 300 dpi | 154,796 B | 91,270 B | 41.0% |
| Times, 300 dpi | 157,532 B | 91,049 B | 42.2% |
| Courier, 300 dpi | 59,280 B | 53,111 B | 10.4% |
| Helvetica, 600 dpi | 195,312 B | 105,844 B | 45.8% |

Courier saves less: coded alone, its pages are already smaller (7,410 B a page against 19,349 for Helvetica), so a dictionary is a smaller part of each. By group size, Helvetica at 300 dpi saves 19.1% sharing between 2 pages, 32.6% between 4, 44.9% between 16 and 46.8% between 32. Coding a group takes about 30 ms a page on top of coding each page alone.

**Why 16.** Redaction stores again, without the dictionary, every image that shares a redacted one's dictionary (`restore_shared_jbig2`, since #5461), since its symbols can hold marks under the area. With one dictionary for a whole book, redacting one page would decode and store again every page, within one redaction's allowance, and a long book would be refused. A group of 16 keeps that…

title: feat(ocr): read Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian
author: kostyk348
body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft's Recognize text read only unaccented Latin (`ocrs`). This adds **Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian** (`ru`, `uk`, `be`) recognition — the largest OCR market after English, and the subject of #1859 and #744.

- **Model:** PP-OCRv5 mobile East Slavic (`eslav_PP-OCRv5_rec_mobile.onnx`, RapidAI v3.9.2's ONNX conversion of the PaddleOCR v3.1.1 model) with its character dictionary, Apache-2.0. It is loaded through the `rten` runtime the project already ships, so there is no new native dependency. Both files are `kind = "model"` entries in `ATTRIBUTION.toml`, SHA-256 pinned, fetched by `cargo xtask models` beside the Latin pair, and staged by the existing packaging scripts.
- **Where it plugs in:** the `ocrs` detector and its line grouping still find the text lines; each line crop is read by the PP-OCR recogniser (`crates/ocr/src/ppocr.rs`, 519 classes pinned: 517 dictionary entries + blank + space). One text item per line, which is what a line-level model returns.
- **Search text:** Cyrillic cannot be spelled with the WinAnsi Type 1 layer, so `crates/engine/src/ocr/layer.rs` adds an invisible (Tr 3) layer that uses a generated Type 3 font with a ToUnicode map and empty character programs. No font is embedded, the page pixels do not change, and save/reopen, copy, search, select and undo keep the Cyrillic. (Same approach as #2520; the Latin path is untouched.)
- **Reachable headlessly:** `ocr_recognize` / `ocr_recognize_files` accept the new `language` values, and their JSON schema now builds the `enum` from `ocr::LANGUAGES` instead of a hard-coded `["en"]`. `ocr_status` reports `available` per language, and `pdfcraft-cli batch --language ru` works.

author: ohagmann
body:
**Builds on #3545** (snap to drawing, F3): merge that first. This PR's own commits are the last two.

## What this changes

On plans, a screenshot or a scanned detail is often pasted onto the page and then lined up with the drawing. Two things were missing (a tester's report):

1. **Pictures as snap targets.** The walker went into form XObjects only, so an image gave nothing to snap to. An image drawn by `Do` (`/Subtype /Image`) or inline (`BI … EI`) now adds the unit square its matrix fills, as a filled rectangle does: F3's snapping, its marker and Tab reach its corners, the middles of its sides and its centre.
2. **Snapping while a picture or added text is moved** in Edit text & images. A picture moved in the image controller, and added text, now snap as a comment moved with the Select tool does (#3545): the corner that comes near a target lands on it, Tab / Shift+Tab pick another point of its box (side middles, centre), and the markers say where. Resizing and turning don't snap, and a turned picture moves as before.

title: fix(redact): remove a shading under a mark instead of clipping it
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`Walk::shading` in `crates/redact/src/interp.rs` kept every `sh` operator that met a mark and wrapped it in an even-odd clip around the marks. The rendered page hid the marked area. But the operator and its `/Shading` resource (function or mesh data, including what it painted under the mark) stayed in the content and in a full save, so a recipient could recover them. Verify mode did not look at shadings at all.

## What changed

- `Gs` carries `clip`, a device-space box around the current clip: the intersection of written clipping paths and form `/BBox`es. Clips this pass doesn't model (text clip modes) only make the box wider, so the test errs toward removal.
- `sh`: if that box can reach a mark, apply removes the operator (`Report::shadings_removed`) and verify counts it as residue. Shadings clipped away from every mark are kept unchanged. The `clip_out` helper had no other user and is deleted.
- `prune.rs`: the retire-and-unlink logic that existed for `/Properties` now also handles `/Shading`. `prune_properties`, `unlink_doomed` and `unlink_from_forms` drop a shading entry that no surviving content (or inheriting form) uses, so the samples leave the file.

Test: `a_shading_under_a_mark_leaves_the_saved_file`. Of three shadings, the unclipped one and the one clipped over the mark go and their samples are gone from a full save. The one clipped elsewhere stays. The verifier counts 2.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-redact` apply/verify/sanitize. A shading that can reach a mark now disappears entirely instead of everywhere except under the mark. For a full-page background gradient behind a small mark, that means the whole gradient goes. This is the fail-closed tradeoff the finding asks for, because no secure partial rewrite of shading data exists here. Sanitize passes no marks, so it never removes shadings, but it does now also prune `/Shading` entries no content uses on pages it rewrites.

title: fix(measure): charge snapping per filter stage and bound listing work
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

- `snap::geometry` decoded each content stream with `Stream::decoded_within` and charged only the final output to its 16 MiB bound. A `/ASCIIHexDecode /RunLengthDecode` (or Flate) stream that expands and then shrinks, listed many times in `/Contents`, did far more decoding than it paid for.
- Snapping parsed every content stream into a full `Vec<Op>` before checking its segment bounds.
- After a nested form truncated the walk, the enclosing operator loop kept going, resolving a form's resources on every further `Do`.
- `list` ran `validate_geometry`'s quadratic self-intersection check (up to 2,048 vertices, ~2M pairs) in full for every area annotation, with no listing-wide work bound, and re-read (and re-decoded the ratio string of) a `/Measure` dictionary shared by many annotations.

## What changed

- The snap walker holds a `DecodeBudget` (16 MiB, as before) and decodes through it, so every filter stage's output is charged on every draw.
- Operators are read with `pdfcraft_content::ops` (streaming).
- A form walk that sets `truncated` ends the enclosing operator loop.
- `list` charges `n²` vertex pairs per annotation against `MAX_LISTED_WORK` (50M) before reading vertices, reporting `truncated` past it, and caches scales by their indirect `/Measure` reference (failures included).

The viewport `/BBox` findings were already fixed on `main` (length checked before resolving, value borrowed).

## Blast radius

Only `pdfcraft-measure`. Pages whose content decodes past 16 MiB counting intermediate stages now stop snapping earlier; listings with more than ~12 maximal-size area measurements report `truncated`. Results below the bounds are unchanged.

## Checks run

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-measure`: 27 + 3 passed (2 new: repeated content pays for every stage; shared scale read once and boundary checks bounded)
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-measure --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-measure --check`

title: fix(redact): prune the resources of Forms a surviving Type 3 glyph draws
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`clean_type3_font` in `crates/redact/src/type3.rs` pruned a Type 3 font's `/Resources` to the names its surviving glyph programs use directly. It did not look inside Forms that those resources keep. If surviving glyph B draws `/Fm`, and `/Fm`'s own `/Resources` still names image `ImA` (drawn only by removed glyph A), the image stayed reachable through the Form and survived a full save.

## What changed

- `record_used` is split out of `collect_used_resources_in_stream`, with the same behaviour.
- New `prune_font_forms` runs after the font's own resources are pruned. For every Form the font's resources still list, and the Forms those list in turn, it prunes the Form's own `/Resources` to the names its content uses. That count includes child Forms that inherit the resources, via the existing `interp::resource_ops`. The walk is bounded by `MAX_DEPTH` and `MAX_HOLDERS` and uses a seen set.
- Only unused entries are removed, so updating a shared Form in place cannot break another drawer. A Form that won't decode or parse fails the redaction closed.

Test: `a_redacted_type3_glyphs_image_does_not_survive_in_a_surviving_glyphs_form`. A's image is gone from a full save, and the image B's Form draws is kept. The test fails on `main`. I checked this by disabling the new call.

## Related

#5197 (open) widens which drawers count when deciding which glyphs survive. It does not touch nested Form resources, so the two PRs are independent.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-redact` apply/sanitize Type 3 cleanup only. Forms reachable from a Type 3 font's resources lose resource entries their content never uses.

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-redact --check`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` (168 passed, 1 ignored as on main)
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: fix(organize): bound name-tree, attachment, pruning and dedupe work
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

Several `pdfcraft-organize` walks did work that grew with a hostile file's sharing rather than its size:

- **Name trees** (`import.rs` lookup/entries, `outline.rs` `/Dests`): visited indirect *nodes* once, but a shared or cyclic indirect `/Kids` array of *direct* child dictionaries was re-expanded under every node, exponential up to the depth cap. Entries copied every key with no total, so one long key string named by many entries was copied per entry.
- **Attachment names** (`import/carry.rs` `set_attachments`): every duplicate restarted its " (n)" search at 2, quadratic in the number of identical names.
- **`delete_pages`**: membership by `Vec::contains` for every page, quadratic in page count.

- **Dedupe** (`dedupe.rs`): hashed a large string behind a reference in full once per reference; resolved (deep-copied) direct `/Resources` and category dictionaries once per owner.
- **PDF/X** (`pdfx.rs`): decoded a `DestOutputProfile` for every listing of every output intent, with no count bound.

title: fix(preflight): follow every /Next action and bound colour and intent work
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

**Action policy (PDF/A 6.5.1) could be bypassed:**
- `walk_chain` followed an indirect `/Next` only when it resolved to an *array*; an indirect `/Next` *dictionary*, or a reference inside a `/Next` array, was never checked. - Conversion identified annotations only by `/Type /Annot`; a widget (found by the form reader through its field) without `/Type` kept its `/AA` scripts.

**Unbounded work:**
- Device-colour inspection decoded every content stream with the 1 GiB per-stream default and no total, and treated a failed decode as "no device colour".
- Forbidden annotations were removed one at a time, each walking every page and cloning its `/Annots`: quadratic on one page.
- Type 3 `CharProcs` shared by many fonts were enumerated once per font.
- `declared()` copied the identifier of every `/OutputIntents` listing, repeats included; indirect `/Next` arrays were deep-copied per root.

- `chain_forbidden`/`walk_chain` queue whatever an indirect `/Next`, or a reference in a `/Next` array, names (dictionary or array), each once under the existing `MAX_ACTION_CHAIN`, borrowed via `Arc`.
- `is_action` treats a dictionary whose `/S` is a forbidden action as an action even with `/P` and `/K`.

title: M3: one Windows device-name check, refused by automation with a root and without (carries #5945)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Windows treats some file names as devices whatever their extension: `NUL.pdf` writes nowhere and `aux.pdf` opens the auxiliary port. This PR does two things:

1. **One device-name check for the whole app** (carries #5945): `pdfcraft_platform::file_names::is_windows_device_name`, used by the desktop app and the automation tools.
2. **Automation refuses a device name on every path**, with `--root`, with the roots-only mode and with no root. Until now only the roots-only mode refused one (#4289).

### Carries #5945

@smittie2000 closed #5945 to cut down their open queue and left it for anyone to pick up. It conflicted with this PR in `crates/automation/src/file_access.rs`, so the two are now one PR. Its three commits come first, cherry-picked onto `main` unchanged, under its author's name:

- `fix(ui): one Windows device-name check for typed and attachment file names`
- `fix(platform): one Windows device-name check for automation and the UI`
- `fix(platform): device-name doc matches what windows 10 does`

**What they do.** The UI had two checks that had drifted, and automation had a third:

| | automation (before) | ui-egui (before) | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `COM¹`–`LPT³` | not refused | prefixed for attachment names only | refused / prefixed |
| `CLOCK$`, `CONIN$`, `CONOUT$` | refused | not prefixed | refused / prefixed |
| spaces before the extension (`nul .txt`) | refused | prefixed for attachment names only | refused / prefixed |
| a colon after the name (`nul:`, `nul:.pdf`) | not refused | can't reach the check: the UI turns `:` into `_` first | refused |

So a typed name like `nul .txt`, `COM¹` or `lpt³.pdf` now gets the same `_` prefix `NUL` already got. The device part ends at the first `.` or `:`, as `GetFullPathNameW` does (`C:\x\nul:.pdf` becomes `\\.\nul`), and only spaces before it are dropped, as Windows drops them (`NUL\u{a0}.pdf` is an ordinary file).

title: fix(export): package a repeated picture once in PPTX and bound HTML embedded pictures
author: dylanmtaylor
body:

title: fix(redact): refuse vertical text a CMap program or hidden-text pass can't place
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

- `is_vertical` (`crates/redact/src/interp.rs`) checked only an embedded CMap stream's dictionary `/WMode`. The renderer reads the writing mode from the CMap program (`/WMode 1 def`) and from a CMap it uses (`usecmap`, `/UseCMap`). A Type0 font vertical only through its program was laid out horizontally, so removal and verification missed the glyphs a mark covered, and `apply` reported success.
- Hidden-text sanitizing (`sanitize.rs` `content_pass`) laid out vertical Type0 text horizontally too. It classified on-page / off-page with the wrong geometry, so text wholly off the page could stay while the scan reported nothing or the removal reported success. The existing vertical refusal only fired for marks, not for hidden-text passes.

## What changed

- `cmap_vertical`: vertical if the dictionary `/WMode` is non-zero, `/UseCMap` names a `-V` CMap or a vertical stream (depth-bounded), or the program has `/WMode n def` with n ≠ 0 or `usecmap` of a `-V` CMap. A program that won't decode within 4 MiB, or has bytes the content lexer can't read, counts as vertical (fail closed).
- The result is cached with the font's metrics in `Scope::fonts`, so a program is decoded once per scope, not at every `Tf`.
- `show_text` flags vertical text during hidden-text sanitizing as well as under marks. `content_pass` then returns `RedactError::VerticalText(page)` when removing, and counts the page when scanning so the removal runs and refuses.

Tests: `a_cmap_vertical_only_in_its_program_fails_closed` (with a horizontal-program control that still redacts), `hidden_text_removal_refuses_vertical_text` (scan counts it, removal refuses, horizontal control is not counted).

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-redact`: apply, verify, scan, Remove Hidden Information. Pages with vertical text now refuse Remove Hidden Information ▸ Hidden text instead of producing a result based on horizontal geometry. Embedded CMaps whose program the lexer can't fully read are treated as vertical.

title: fix(redact): remove reply chains by walking a parent index once
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`remove_page_annotations` (`crates/redact/src/lib.rs`) found the replies of removed annotations with a fixed-point loop. Each pass scanned every reply on the page and called `removed.contains` on a growing `Vec`. A reply chain listed deepest first added one reply per pass, so the work was cubic in the chain length. The cross-page pass (2b) repeated whole-document scans of every page's `/Annots` until nothing grew, which is quadratic for a chain spread across pages. A modest annotation graph could stall `apply`.

## What changed

- Per page: replies (`/IRT`, not widgets) are indexed by parent once, then walked from the removed annotations with a worklist. `removed` is a `HashSet`.
- Cross-page: `hanging_annotations` indexes replies (`/IRT`) and pop-ups (`/Parent`) of every listed annotation once. One walk from `removed_everywhere` closes the set, then each page's `/Annots` is filtered once.
- What is removed, and how replies are counted in the report, are unchanged.

Test: `a_reverse_ordered_reply_chain_is_removed_in_linear_work`. 6 000 replies are listed deepest first, split across two pages. All go, and the report counts them.

## Related

#5849 (open) changes the same function to also judge inline annotations. Whichever merges second will need a small rebase.

title: fix(xfdf): bound field text, look up names, guard tab cells, protect fields
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

- **Expanded field names** (`common::walk_xfdf`): each field's full name concatenates its parent's, and nothing bounded the total, so a 1 MiB parent name over thousands of short children was gigabytes of names.
- **FDF value arrays** (`fdf::walk_fdf`): every string of a `/V` array was decoded and kept before the import budget was charged, so repeated references to one large string expanded before the check.
- **Quadratic name lookups**: `merge_csv` scanned all collected columns per field and each row per column; XFDF field export scanned siblings per name part; `apply_values` scanned all fields per imported value.
- **Tab-delimited export** kept formula-leading cells (`=…`, `@…`), which spreadsheets run; CSV already guarded them.
- **Protected annotations** (`import_protected`): checked an unresolved `/Subtype` and a local `/FT`, so a widget with `/Subtype 5 0 R` or an inherited field type could be replaced by a same-name imported comment, bypassing the form setter. `place` also deep-copied every existing annotation dictionary on the page per imported annotation.
- **Redaction marks**: an imported mark's appearance is clipped to `/Rect`, but removal uses `/QuadPoints`; quads outside `/Rect` removed content outside the visible outline.

## What changed

- `walk_xfdf` charges full names and values against `MAX_XFDF_TEXT` (64 MiB) and refuses past it.
- `walk_fdf` charges each value as it is decoded.
- Maps for columns/rows (`merge_csv`), export tree children and `apply_values`, keeping the first-match semantics the scans had.
- Tab export prefixes `'` exactly as CSV does (`csv_guarded`), and `tab_delimited` strips it (`csv_text`), so values round-trip.
- `import_protected` resolves `/Subtype` and walks `/Parent` for an inherited `/FT` (`is_field`); `place` borrows existing annotations.
- A redaction mark with drawable quads gets a `/Rect` that is the union of its `/Rect` and quads.

title: fix(sign): PEM and .p12 base64 through the base64 crate, with RFC 7468 lax padding
author: smittie2000
body:
> **Deck: PEM and PKCS #12 base64.** Based on main (a4d148bf), independent of the other decks. Review a4d148bf..37da3bba (4 commits).
>
> It also holds what #5800 proposed; #5800 is closed in its favour.

## What this changes

### refactor(sign): encode and decode PEM with the base64 crate

`crates/sign/src/x509.rs` had its own base64 encoder (in `to_pem`, Export certificate) and decoder (`fn base64`, which `load_certificates` uses for PEM `CERTIFICATE`, `PKCS7` and `CMS` blocks). Both now use `base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD`. The `base64 = "0.23"` crate is already a direct dependency of sign. (`pkcs12::decode_base64` still decoded with `STANDARD` after this commit; the next one moves it onto the same decoder.)

- **Encoding is byte-identical** for every input length. `to_pem` of the two OpenSSL fixtures reproduces the files exactly.
- **Decoding uses RFC 7468's lax grammar (Figure 2)**, a compatibility choice for this project; RFC 7468 §3 leaves the parsing strategy to context: zero, one or two `=` at the end, whatever the length. Up to two trailing `=` are dropped, and the rest is decoded with `STANDARD_NO_PAD`. So **unpadded and over-padded bodies still load, as they did before.**
- **It rejects only what isn't base64** and the old decoder silently tolerated (the old one dropped every `=` wherever it appeared and decoded whatever was left):
  - a `=` inside the body, or a third `=` at the end, which are outside the grammar
  - a one-character tail, which can't encode a byte and was silently dropped, hiding truncation
  - non-zero bits after the last byte, which RFC 4648 §3.5 lets decoders reject

  These now give `SignError::Malformed("PEM base64")` from the existing caller. Every body both decoders accept decodes to the same bytes. The one thing the old certificate decoder refused that now loads is a vertical tab in the body, which RFC 7468 counts as whitespace (next commit). Header lines such as `Proc-Type:`, CRLF line endings and trailing spaces beh…

title: refactor: one civil_from_days, cos's, for xtask, the app and ui-egui
author: smittie2000
body:
> **Deck: civil_from_days.** Based on main (a4d148bf), independent of the other decks. Review a4d148bf..6faf3659 (4 commits).
>
> It also holds what #5840 proposed; #5840 is closed in its favour.
>
> **Overlap:** #5814 conflicts trivially in `apps/pdfcraft/Cargo.toml`: this PR swaps the app's `chrono` for `pdfcraft-cos`, #5814 adds `percent-encoding`. Keep both.

## What this changes

### refactor(cos): export civil_from_days for xtask's demo stamps

`civil_from_days` converts days since 1970 into a proleptic Gregorian date. It lets chrono compute the date within one 400-year cycle and adds whole cycles back into the year: CLAUDE.md's sanctioned range extension. It was copied from `crates/cos/src/writer.rs` into xtask's demo-PDF `Stamp` (`xtask/src/demo_pdf/pdf.rs`), with an identical body.

cos's copy is now `pub` and re-exported from the cos crate root, next to `pdf_date`. xtask already depends on cos, so it now calls `pdfcraft_cos::civil_from_days`. The only thing xtask used chrono for was that copy, so its `chrono` dependency is removed (and `Cargo.lock` updated). cos already depends on chrono, so it gains nothing and stays standalone.

Behaviour does not change. The cos doc now says the function is total for any `i64`.

### refactor(ui, app): one civil_from_days, cos's

ui-egui's Combine "modified" stamp (`combine_ui/parts.rs`) and the app's log timestamp (`apps/pdfcraft/src/logging.rs`) each carried a `u64` copy of the 400-year-cycle date conversion that cos exports as `civil_from_days` (made public by the first commit). Both now call it. A `u64` second count over 86,400 is at most about 2.1e14, so it always fits the `i64` cos takes, and the year never saturates: the output is unchanged for every input.

The app's direct chrono dependency was used only there and gives way to `pdfcraft-cos`.

author: smittie2000
body:
> **Deck: PDF/X XMP.** Based on `main`, independent of the other decks. Review `ecdd1e65..d51c1656` (4 commits).
>
> It also holds what #5826 proposed; #5826 is closed in its favour.

## What this changes

### fix(organize): read PDF/X XMP properties with the shared XMP reader

`PrintStandard::of` (crates/organize/src/pdfx.rs) decides whether combined or inserted documents declare the same PDF/X standard. It reads `pdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion`, `pdfxid:GTS_PDFXConformance` and `pdf:Trapped` from the XMP packet when `/Info` lacks them. Its `xmp_value` had its own matcher and a five-call `replace` chain to unescape values. That duplicated `xmp.rs`'s `get_property`/`unescape`, which the document-information mirror already uses. pdfx now calls a new `xmp::text_property(xmp, name)`, a wrapper around `get_property(…, Shape::Text)`. `get_property` and `Shape` stay private.

**What pdfx reads differently (old → new):**

| Input | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| `pdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion="PDF/X-4"` (or `/`) | `PDF/X-4`: the replace chain missed numeric references | `PDF/X-4` |
| `xpdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion="bogus" pdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion="PDF/X-4"` | `bogus`: substring match | `PDF/X-4` |
| the property name inside another attribute's value, a comment, CDATA or a PI | could match it | ignored |
| an element with attributes (`<pdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion xml:lang="…">`), or whitespace around `=` | not found | found |
| an element whose content is markup | the raw markup | `None` |
| `<pdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion note="a > b">PDF/X-4</…>` (a `>` in the element's own attribute) | `None`: old matched only a bare `<key>` | `PDF/X-4` |
| an attribute value with surrounding spaces | kept | trimmed |
| element **and** attribute both present (conflicting RDF) | attribute wins | element wins |

title: fix(redact): read text-state operands from the end, as the renderer does
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`Walk::text_state` (`crates/redact/src/interp.rs`) set `Tc`, `Tw`, `Tz`, `TL`, `Ts` and `Tr` from operand 0. `select_font` read `Tf`'s name and size from operands 0 and 1, and `"` read its spacings from operands 0 and 1. The renderer, `Op::nums` and the `TJ`/`Do` handling here take the operands immediately before the operator and ignore any surplus. With `1 50 Ts`, the page raises the text by 50 but the interpreter used 1, so the glyph boxes sat 49 pt below the drawn text. A mark over the visible text then neither removed it nor saw it left behind.

## What changed

- The single-number text-state operators use the last operand (`op.nums::<1>()`).
- `Tf` uses its last two operands, and `"` uses the two numbers before its string.

Test: `surplus_text_state_operands_do_not_move_the_glyphs`. With `1 50 Ts`, nothing is counted at the unraised position, the raised text is counted, and a mark there removes it.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-redact` content interpretation (apply, verify, hidden-text sanitizing). Only content with surplus operands before these operators is placed differently.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-redact --check`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` (173 passed, 1 ignored as on main)
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`

## Checks not run

- workspace-wide `cargo test --workspace` / `cargo clippy --workspace` (memory-bound shared machine)

author: Hamza0101
body:
Part of #5873. It cuts **memory to about a twelfth and CPU by about 40%** when opening a PDF whose pages carry InDesign's `/PieceInfo`. What's left is named below.

## Measured

`pdfcraft-cli run` with one `doc_open` step, release build, same machine, `main` (`ea353f7a`) against this branch. The files are blank pages, each page dictionary carrying an inline `/PieceInfo` of small numeric arrays (the shape the report describes), written by a generator of my own:

| pages × `/PieceInfo` per page | file | CPU `main` → this | peak RSS `main` → this |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1412 × 0 | 0.2 MB | 0.02 s → 0.02 s | 20 MB → 20 MB |
| 1412 × 4 KB | 6.1 MB | 1.42 s → **0.86 s** | 255 MB → **68 MB** |
| 1412 × 12 KB | 17.6 MB | 4.21 s → **2.45 s** | 714 MB → **92 MB** |
| 1412 × 24 KB | 35 MB | 8.34 s → **4.83 s** | 1390 MB → **110 MB** |

## The three causes, found by profiling (`sample`) and RSS checkpoints

1. **Memory: inspection kept every `/PieceInfo` it read.** RSS checkpoints in `render::inspect` showed hayro's pass using ~50 MB, and `Inspector::fill` over `LazyStructure` taking it from 52 MB to **1.08 GB**. `LazyStructure` keeps every object it reads, converted to lopdf form, for the whole inspection, so each page came with its `/PieceInfo`. Nothing in inspection reads that key, so `convert_dict` now leaves it out of this read-only view. The file and the editing document are untouched.
