The cache is now an `ObjectCache` that measures each object once, when it goes in, and keeps the running total. Both byte caps now hold exactly after every insertion, where before it was "approximate between passes".

title: fix(ui): linear form diffing and grouping, bounded copy-all, checked output names
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

**Quadratic work on the UI thread:**
- `editing::form_edit_pages` looked each field up in the other list by linear scan, both ways, on every form edit.
- `calc_order_ui` grouped cyclic fields by scanning all groups built so far, every frame.
- `compare_ui::shading` tested each visual region against every retained region of the whole document.

**Unbounded memory:**
- Copy-all-text (`state.rs`) appended every page's text with no total; pages sharing a large `/ActualText` multiplied it.

**Paths and files:**
- Batch OCR (`ocr_ui`) and image/text export (`export_ui`) joined a document-supplied name onto the chosen folder without checking it was a plain file name.
- Combine folder discovery accepted symlinks (`path.is_file()` follows them) to files outside the chosen folder.
- Explicit Reload read the path even when it had become a FIFO, blocking the UI thread on open.
- A failed Reveal logged the raw file path, so control characters in a file name could forge log records.

**Policy:**
- The comment context menu's "Copy text" ignored the document's copy permission.
- A script's `SaveAs` requests each opened Save As; thousands in one batch meant thousands of saves.

## What changed

- Name → field maps in `form_edit_pages` (first match wins, as before); a root → group map in `calc_order_ui`; per-page region lists in `shading`.
- Copy-all stops reading pages once 256 MiB of text is collected.
- OCR and export outputs must pass `files::is_plain_file_name` (the existing helper); a failing name is reported, not written.
- Folder discovery uses the entry's own (non-following) file type.
- Reload checks the path is a regular file before reading it.

- "Copy text" is enabled only when `doc.allows_copying()`.
- At most one Save As per script output batch.

title: Ignore dictionary key order when checking signed pages for changes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5955

**Cause.** `page_change_kind` and the `/Page` arm of `change_kind` compared the signed and current page with `without()`, which sorts only the top-level keys. Nested values were then compared with `Dict`'s `PartialEq`, which compares entries in order. So when a later revision re-serialised an inline `/Resources` dictionary in another key order, the page counted as a page content change and the earlier signature was reported invalid.

**Fix.** Pages are now compared with `same_but_annots`. It sorts both dictionaries' entries by key (ignoring `/Annots`) and compares them pairwise at every depth, so nested dictionaries and stream dictionaries ignore key order, while arrays, stream data and all other values still have to match exactly. A missing, added or changed key at any depth is still a page content change in both directions.

## How you verified it

- Regression tests `pdf::changes::tests::reordered_inline_resources_are_not_page_content`, `pdf::changes::tests::a_swapped_nested_key_is_page_content_both_ways` and `pdf::changes::tests::reordered_arrays_are_still_page_content` fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign --lib pdf::changes::tests`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `content::format_text_lists_fit_the_narrowest_tools_pane_in_every_language` and `editing::a_custom_property_whose_name_the_tools_refuse_is_listed_and_left_alone`, which also fail on `main` without this change.

- [ ] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed
- [ ] tests pass on the crates I changed

## Never-crash

- [ ] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests, unless it is provably infallible with a comment saying why
- [ ] No indexing or slicing with input-derived positions (`get`, and strings only at char boundaries); checked or saturating arithmetic; allocatio…

title: fix(edit): stop rescanning what a loop already holds in wrapping, grouping and flattening
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

Four places in `pdfcraft-edit` repeated work that grows with the input:

- **Added-text wrapping** (`added/layout.rs`, `wrapped`). For Latin text each word built `format!("{line} {word}")` and measured the whole candidate. Negative character spacing (accepted from `page_add_text`, `content_update` and `/PCAdded`) keeps a line from ever reaching the box width, so the line grows to the whole text and the loop becomes quadratic in copying and measuring. The standard-14 widths add up (`Std14::text_width` sums glyph widths, no kerning), so each word is now measured once, `line_w + space + word_w`, and appended in place. The Arabic/Thai branch already worked this way, so both now share the code.
- **Paragraph grouping** (`text_regions/grouping.rs`). `block.lines.last().filter(|i| row.contains(i))` searched the row for every run. Rows don't share runs, so the predecessor is the last run this loop placed, and it is now tracked.
- **Flattening** (`flatten.rs`). Each flattened page called `page_list(doc)` twice, a full page-tree walk, which is quadratic in the page count. It now re-reads only that page's own dictionary over the inherited attributes it already has (`refreshed`).
- **Added-content font cleanup** (`added/store.rs`, `own_fonts`). It copied every `/PCAr…` token, duplicates included, out of an uncapped `decoded()`. It now decodes within `MAX_PAGE_DECODED` and keeps each name once.

title: fix(automation): a separate conversion never writes over an existing file
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

`doc_create_multiple` with `mode: "separate"` promises a new file per input. It picks the name with `unused(dir, stem)`, which tried `<stem>.pdf` and then `<stem> (2).pdf` … `<stem> (9999).pdf`. When all of them were taken it fell back to `<stem>.pdf`, the occupied first name, and `write_atomic` then replaced that existing PDF.

`unused` now returns `Result<PathBuf>` and fails ("no unused output name available for …") instead of handing back a taken name. Both callers propagate the error: `create_separate`, and `action_run`, which had its own `exists()` re-check for the same case and drops it.

title: fix(redact): mark changed marked-content spans in linear work
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`clean_replacements` (`crates/redact/src/interp.rs`) finds the marked-content spans (`BDC`/`BMC`) around operators that redaction changed, so their `/ActualText`, `/Alt`, `/E` and `/T` go too. For every changed operator it re-added the whole open-span stack to the affected set, ancestors already recorded included. A file nesting thousands of spans around thousands of redacted strings made that product quadratic CPU work.

## What changed

Each open span carries an `affected` flag. A changed operator sets the flag on the innermost span only. When a span closes (`EMC`, or at the end of the stream for spans left open), it is recorded if flagged and passes the flag to its parent. Every operator and every span costs constant work, and the set of affected spans is the same as before.

Test: `deeply_nested_spans_around_many_changes_are_cleaned_in_linear_work`. 5 000 nested spans, below the overlay's own nesting cap, surround 50 000 redacted strings. That was a quarter of a billion steps before. Every description is still removed.

## Blast radius

title: fix(print): index page labels once and cap how many pages a range selects
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

`select_pages` (Pages to Print, and `doc_print`'s `pages`) did two kinds of unbounded work driven by a short range string:

- **Label lookups.** `page_of` ran `labels.iter().position(..)` for every endpoint, and `hyphenated_label_range` ran `labels.iter().any(..)` for every `-` in a token. A string of dashes against a document with many labels cost the number of dashes × the number of labels before the parser rejected it. Labels are now indexed once per call (`HashMap<&str, usize>`, first page wins as before), and every lookup is O(1).
- **Selections.** Ranges were expanded with no total, so `1-,1-,1-,…` produced the page count × the number of repeats entries, each later a sheet placement. The running total is now checked before a span is expanded: at most `MAX_SELECTED` (100,000) pages, or the page count when the document is longer, so a long document can still print whole. Past the limit the parser returns `PrintError::Invalid("the range selects more than … pages")`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` (rustfmt on the file)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-print --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-print`: 55 passed, including the new `a_range_selects_at_most_the_limit` (exactly the limit passes, one more is refused, and a document longer than the limit prints whole) and `labels_resolve_through_the_index` (hyphenated label endpoints among 50,000 labels, 10,000 dashes rejected, the first duplicate label wins)

Not run: the workspace tests (CI).

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

Blast radius: a typed range that selects more than 100,000 pages (counting repeats) on a document shorter than that is now refused. The new message goes through `PrintError::Invalid`, so it isn't in `WORDINGS` and stays in English in translated interfaces. #4931 and #4282 also edit `range.rs`; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: fix(print,a11y): read summary scans one operator at a time and borrow form resources
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

Two read-only summary walks materialized more than they used:

- **Print orientation** (`print/src/sheets.rs`, `text_direction`, used by auto-rotate and labels). It ran `pdfcraft_content::parse(data).ops`, collecting every operator of a decoded stream into a `Vec` before reading any. Compact compressed content expands into millions of operator records within the byte allowance. It now iterates `pdfcraft_content::ops(data)` and keeps only the running score. For each `Do` of a form it also cloned the form's `/Resources` (or the inherited dictionary) *before* `budget.enter_form()`, so repeated invocations copied large dictionaries even after the visit allowance was spent. title: fix(redact): read inherited forms once for all names in resource cleanup
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

Resource cleanup (`crates/redact/src/interp/prune.rs`) unlinks removed images and forms (`doomed`) from page-tree holders and surviving forms. For each candidate name it called `content_draws`, which parsed the remaining content and decoded every form without its own `/Resources` (such a form draws through its caller's) again. A holder with thousands of aliases of one removed image, plus a large compressed inheriting form drawn elsewhere, decoded and parsed that form once per alias, with a fresh allowance each time.

## What changed

- `names_drawn(doc, content, xo)` walks the content once. It collects every XObject name drawn directly or through inheriting forms, reading each such form once, and reports whether anything could not be read (a form that won't decode, or nesting past `MAX_DEPTH`).
- `unlink_doomed` computes that once per user page of the holder, and `prune_doomed_xobjects` once per surviving form. Every candidate name is then answered from the set through `any_draws`.
- Fail-closed is kept: a name drawn somewhere is kept. A name not found while something could not be read is still an error (`Residue` / "could not fully inspect"). Otherwise it is unlinked.

Test: `many_names_of_a_redacted_image_are_unlinked_reading_inherited_forms_once`. 3 000 aliases of a redacted image sit in inherited `/Pages` resources, and another page draws a large inheriting form. Every alias leaves with the image, and the image is gone from a full save.

## Related

#5662 (open) also edits `content_draws` (resolving chained references). Whichever merges second will need a small rebase.

`pdfcraft-redact` resource cleanup after apply and sanitize. What is unlinked is the same. One edge case changed: when content draws the name through one form while another inheriting form can't be read, the result used to depend on which came first (kept, or a refusal). Now the name is kept whenever it is drawn. It is still in use, so nothing leaks.

title: fix(redact): bound structure-tree walks by their work, not only their references
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`clean_within` and `drop_object_refs_within` (`crates/redact/src/tags.rs`) walk the structure tree. `Parents::record` appended a parent relation for every listing of a reference before the seen check, and every element's kids were queued on each visit. Only distinct references counted against `limit`. An indirect `/K` array shared by many elements was therefore expanded once per element: 2 000 elements sharing one array of 2 000 repeats queued and recorded four million relations from a few thousand objects, and the pending stack and the parent map grew without bound.

## What changed

- `Parents` holds a `HashSet<Above>` per element (`Above` derives `Hash`/`Eq`), so repeated relations are stored once.
- `over_budget` charges every popped work item to a step allowance and caps the pending queue, both at `limit × 8` (`STEPS_PER_REFERENCE`). Past either, the walk returns `RedactError::Tags`: the cleanup can't be shown complete, so the redaction or sanitization is refused. A tree past the reference limit was already handled this way.
- The default limit (`MAX_STRUCT_REFS`, 2 000 000) gives 16 million steps, ample for real trees.

Test: `a_shared_kids_array_of_repeats_is_refused_not_expanded`. With a limit of 10 000, both walks refuse quickly.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-redact` tag cleanup in apply and sanitize. Structure trees whose walk would take more than 8 steps per allowed reference are refused instead of walked.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-redact --check`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` (173 passed, 1 ignored as on main)
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: fix(annot): bound link listing and URL recognition work
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

`links::list` (Edit a PDF ▸ Link, the engine's link cache) and `links::find_urls` (Create links from URLs) did work that a small document can multiply:

- **Destination pages.** `dest_page` ran `pages.iter().position(..)` for every link, which is O(links × pages). `list` now builds a page → index map once (first index for a page listed twice, as before).
- **Shared actions.** `action_of` cloned the resolved `/A` dictionary (inline URI bytes included) for each link that referenced it. It now borrows the resolved object.
- **URI budget.** A conversion that didn't fit the remaining `MAX_URI_BYTES` allowance (invalid UTF-8 grows ×3) charged nothing, so a shared invalid address was converted again for every link. A rejected conversion now pays for the bytes it read.
- **Unsupported action names.** `LinkAction::Other` copied the whole `/S` name into every item. It is now cut to its first 64 bytes.
- **URL recognition.** For a token like `http://http://http://…` with no dot, every `http://` started a scan to the end of the run, built a `String`, and was rejected, which is quadratic. A run with no `.` holds neither a web address nor an e-mail domain (an e-mail domain's dot is followed by a label, so trailing-punctuation trimming can't remove it), so the scan now resumes after the run.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-annot --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-annot`: 78 passed, including the new `a_long_run_without_an_address_is_scanned_once` (200,000 prefixes, then the real address is still found; e-mail after a dotless run still found) and `link_listing_indexes_pages_and_cuts_long_action_names`

Not run: the workspace tests (CI).

title: fix(xfa): index saved-state names once and bound existing-image discovery
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

title: fix(redact): classify hidden layers with sets, not list searches
author: dylanmtaylor
body:

title: fix(engine): coalesce script resetForm requests and bound console output per edit
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong
- `Session::run_javascript` turned every `resetForm` call of a script into its own `ResetForm` edit, and matched each against the form by comparing every field with every selector (formatting a `"{x}."` prefix per comparison). A short button script could ask for thousands of whole-form resets or a huge selector list and block the UI thread.
- `JsOutput::absorb`/`append` copied every script run's console lines and alerts into the edit's output with no shared cap, so a form with many calculated fields could retain gigabytes of console text from one fill.

## What changed
- All `resetForm` requests of one script become one reset of the union (`None` if any call names no fields), matched by looking each field's name and its dotted parents up in a `HashSet` of selectors (linear in fields x depth).
- Console output kept per output is capped at `MAX_CONSOLE_LINES` (10,000) and `MAX_CONSOLE_BYTES` (1 MiB), with one closing "left out" line; alerts at `MAX_ALERTS` (1,000).

## Blast radius
Engine only. A script calling `resetForm` several times now resets once (same end state; recalculates once). Extremely chatty scripts lose console lines past the cap.

Findings: 52590222, de5af5f9, b5e65d14 (CodeRabbit run 6).

- cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings

title: fix(engine): run the renderer redaction check on redactions applied inside a batch
author: dylanmtaylor

`run_edit` records the marks each `ApplyRedactions` consumes (as they were when it ran) and its overlays in `EditCtx`; `Session::apply` runs the renderer check whenever any were recorded, so nested redactions are checked against the final prospective document and the whole batch is refused on residue.

title: fix(engine): refuse PDF watermark/background sources that deny copying or assembly
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong
`mark_source` (watermark/background from a PDF page) opened the source and imported its page with `page_as_form` without checking the source's permissions, so a copy- or assembly-restricted page could be copied into an unrestricted document.

## What changed

title: fix(engine): bound XFA resetData matching and skip resets past the event budget

title: fix(redact): read the page tree once per sanitize pass, not per page
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`content_pass` (`crates/redact/src/sanitize.rs`) fetched each page with `pdfcraft_model::pages(doc).swap_remove(pi)` inside the per-page loop. That collects and copies the whole page tree every time, so a document of N pages costs N walks of N pages: 400 million page visits at 20 000 pages. Scan and sanitize stalled on many-page documents.

## What changed

The page list is read once before the loop, and read again only after a page is rewritten (its inherited `/Resources` are pinned by `localize_resources`, which can change the tree). Pages are cloned from the list by index.

title: fix(redact): remove primary actions from every annotation and form field
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

With Links, actions and scripts selected, `remove_hidden` (`crates/redact/src/sanitize.rs`) removed `/A` only from widgets, or from annotations that also held `/AA`. The scan counted only widgets with `/A` and no `/AA`. So:

- a page-listed Screen annotation with `/A` alone (for example a JavaScript action) kept its action, and the scan did not report it;
- a push button's own `/A` on its field dictionary survived, because only the page-listed widgets were cleaned. `button_action()` and `run_button()` consume that action later.

## What changed

- Any annotation's `/A` is removed (Links go whole already, and `/AA` is still handled by the owner sweep).
- `field_dicts` walks `/AcroForm /Fields` through `/Kids` (each object once) and the `/A` of every field dictionary is removed.
- The scan counts the same owners: annotations with `/A` but no `/AA` and not a Link, and field dictionaries with `/A`. Only dictionaries known as field owners are touched, so unrelated `/A` keys elsewhere stay.

Test: `screen_and_field_primary_actions_are_removed`. A Screen annotation and a push button field hold the same script. The scan counts 2, removal clears both, and the payload is absent from a full save.

## Blast radius

title: fix(xfa): scripts come only from the XDP's own packets and quote the date pattern
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

Two ways for passive data to become script:

- **Template discovery** (`parse.rs`, `parse`). When the XDP root was not itself the template, `root.descendants().find(is_template)` took the first template-looking element anywhere in the document, including inside `<xfa:datasets>`, which import data fills from outside files. An imported XML file could therefore supply the form's template and its `initialize`/`calculate` scripts. The search, and the one for the saved `<form>` state beside it, now looks only at the XDP root's children, where the packets are.
- **Date pattern** (`pdf.rs` / `pdf/common.rs`). `WidgetKind::Date(pattern)` went into `AFDate_FormatEx("{pattern}")` and `AFDate_KeystrokeEx("{pattern}")` as raw text, so a `"` ended the string and the rest ran as JavaScript in the written field actions. The pattern is now encoded with `js_string`, which escapes `"`, `\`, control characters and U+2028/2029 and wraps the result in quotes.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-xfa --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa`: 145 passed, including the new `a_template_inside_the_data_is_not_the_form` and `pdf::common::js_string_tests::a_pattern_cannot_leave_its_string`. The existing `the_xdp_template_wins_over_the_config_packets_template_element` still passes.

Not run: the workspace tests (CI). I didn't search a corpus for XDPs whose template is nested deeper than a root child.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

Blast radius: an XFA document whose `<template>` sits deeper than a direct child of the XDP root is now "no <template> element" (Malformed), where it used to be laid out. I know of no producer that writes that. Ordinary date patterns produce the same JavaScript as before.

title: fix(xtask): render-oracle writes page pixels into a private temporary folder
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

title: fix(cli): render needs the copying permission, as text does
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli text` already refuses a document whose permissions forbid copying unless the owner password is given (#1645). `pdfcraft-cli render` did not: with the user password, or with no password on a document that has an empty user password, it wrote the page as PNG/JPEG/TIFF/PAM. `render` now opens the document in a session first, the same way `text` does, and refuses with "render: the document's permissions don't allow copying its pages as images; pass the owner password with --password to render it" before anything is drawn or written.

title: fix(redact): read each Type 3 glyph program once per cleanup
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

`clean_type3_font` (`crates/redact/src/type3.rs`) decoded and parsed each surviving glyph program of a Type 3 font to learn which resource names it uses, for every font. Many small font dictionaries that list one compressed CharProc cost one decode and parse per font, with a fresh decode allowance each time and no cleanup-wide bound, so a small file multiplied the work.

title: fix(redact): place Type 3 glyphs with their whole font matrix
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What was wrong

For a Type 3 font, `Metrics::from_dict` (used by `show` in `crates/redact/src/interp.rs`) takes the font matrix's first element as the glyph scale, and builds the vertical extent from `/FontBBox` and the matrix's `d` element only. Translation (`e`, `f`) and skew (`b`, `c`) are left out, but the renderer paints with the complete matrix. A font whose matrix moves its glyphs therefore drew them outside the box that removal and the final verifier tested. A mark over the drawn glyph neither removed it nor reported it as left, and the glyph program stayed in the saved file.

## What changed

- `type3_glyph_box` computes the font's `/FontBBox` through its whole `/FontMatrix` (a box per unit of font size). It is tracked with the font state, for `Tf` and for an ExtGState `/Font`.
- `show` takes the union of that box and the previous one, so every position the old test covered is still covered. Removal and verification share this code, so both use the new box.
- No change for non-Type 3 fonts.

Test: `a_type3_glyph_is_placed_with_its_whole_font_matrix`. The matrix raises glyphs 5 pt at 10 pt. A mark over the top of the drawn glyph is seen by the verifier and removes it.

## Related

#3413 and #3241 (open) change how Type 3 glyph bounds are measured in the render and edit layers. This PR is limited to redaction's own interpreter, which is where removal and verification decide.

## Blast radius

`pdfcraft-redact` apply and verify for Type 3 fonts. The glyph box can only grow, so more glyphs near a mark may now be removed. That is the fail-closed direction.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-redact --check`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` (173 passed, 1 ignored as on main)
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: fix(a11y): collect a structure element once whatever generation references it

title: fix(cli): cap input reads, budget check's edit pass and escape its stderr records
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

Three input-handling gaps in `pdfcraft-cli`:

- **Unbounded reads** (`commands::read`, used by `info`, `text`, `render`, `edit`, `combine`, `split`, `check-one` …). It used `std::fs::read`, which buffers until EOF. A path to an endless readable device or pipe kept allocating before any PDF validation. It now reads through `take(MAX_INPUT + 1)` and fails past 512 MiB, the cap automation's `doc_open` already uses. `check-one --edit` re-read the file with `std::fs::read`; it now uses the same helper.
- **check's `--edit` pass** (`edit_round_trip`). Up to 20,000 streams each called `s.decoded()` with a fresh per-stream allowance, so many small bombs multiplied. One `DecodeBudget::page()` is now shared across the pass, failed decodes included, and the loop stops when it is spent.
- **stderr records** (`check`). Each failing file is one `[n/N] status name detail` line, and the file name and the child's detail went in raw. A file name with a newline (or terminal escapes) could forge more records. Status, name and detail are now written with `escape_debug`, and the directory-error line escapes its name too. The `--json` report keeps the original values.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cli --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cli --test it -- check`: 5 passed, including the new `a_file_name_cannot_forge_a_stderr_record` (Unix: a file named `bad\n[9] ok forged.pdf` gives exactly one record, escaped)

Not run: the workspace tests (CI); a long `check --edit` corpus run.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

Blast radius: inputs over 512 MiB are now refused by the CLI commands, as they already are by automation. Reading from `/dev/stdin` or a pipe still works below the cap. Non-ASCII file names in check's stderr are unchanged (`escape_debug` only escapes controls and the like); names with control characters show as `\n`, `\u{1b}` and so on.

title: fix(edit,a11y): font aliases share the metrics built for their font

title: fix(render): JBIG2 refinement reads 0 past its reference's width (hayro-jbig2 patch 13)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A JBIG2 refinement region now decodes to the pixels that were coded when its reference is a bitmap filled with 1s: a page whose default pixel is 1, or an intermediate text or halftone region whose default pixel is 1.

The decoder keeps each row of a bitmap in 32-bit words and filled a new bitmap whole, so with a default pixel of 1 the bits past its width in each row's last word were 1s too. A refinement reads its reference a word at a time, those bits included, so it read 1 where the standard says a pixel outside the reference is 0 (ISO/IEC 14492 6.3.5.2). Its contexts then differed from the encoder's, and the region decoded to other pixels whenever the reference's width wasn't a multiple of 32, in release builds too. That is wrong pixels on valid files: drawn so by the renderer, and, since Optimize (#5472) and redaction (#5461) decode JBIG2 and store the result again, written into the file.

`Bitmap::clear_padding` (vendored hayro-jbig2 patch 13) clears those bits when a bitmap is filled with 1s, as cutting symbols and patterns out of a collective bitmap already did. On valid data nothing else in the decoder writes past a row's width: generic and refinement rows set pixel by pixel, MMR rows and pattern blits stop at the width, combining masks to it, and typical prediction copies the row above as it is.

**Measured** on 140 streams coded by the standard's procedures: a refinement of the page on a page whose default pixel is 1, and of an intermediate text region and an intermediate halftone region whose default pixel is 1, at widths from 7 to 65, four pictures each, the regions as wide as their page or narrower.
- `main` decodes 72 of them to other pixels than were coded, every one at a width that isn't a multiple of 32. With the patch all 140 decode as coded.
- Ghostscript, run as an external process, reads all 36 page streams and all 52 text streams as coded. It doesn't take a refinement of an intermediate halftone region ("failed to find refe…

title: fix(xfa): one decoding allowance for all XFA packets
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

`read_packets` decoded each XFA packet stream with `decoded_within(MAX_XDP)`, a fresh 64 MB allowance per stream, and counted only the final output against the 64 MB total. A filter chain whose early stage inflates a lot and whose later stage discards most of it (Flate of hex whitespace through ASCIIHex, say) cost up to 64 MB of decoding per packet while adding almost nothing to the total. Repeating that over many distinct packets multiplied the work.

All packets now decode through one `DecodeBudget` of `4 × MAX_XDP` (256 MB). It charges what every filter stage produced, failed decodes included, the same accounting the page decoders use. Each packet keeps its 64 MB cap, and the 64 MB total of kept text is unchanged.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-xfa --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa`: 143 passed

Not run: the workspace tests (CI). There is no new test: a hostile case needs over 256 MB of decoding, which the test runner's memory cap doesn't allow, and `DecodeBudget`'s stage-by-stage charging is tested in `pdfcraft-cos`.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

Blast radius: an XFA form whose packets need more than 256 MB of total filter output to decode is now refused (`CosError` limit), where before only the 64 MB of kept text was capped. Real forms are far below either.

title: fix(annot): count ink points as strokes resolve and cap the eraser's samples
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

- **Stroke decoding** (`modify.rs`). `resize_ink` and `erase_ink` each had their own copy of the `/InkList` decoder, which resolved every entry with no total. One numeric array referenced thousands of times expanded into that many coordinate vectors, then scaled copies and new PDF arrays. Both now use one `ink_strokes` decoder that charges each stroke's points before reading them and refuses past `MAX_STORED_INK_POINTS` (1,000,000, ten times the 100,000 a new drawing may have).
- **Eraser densification**. Each segment became up to 2,000 samples with no overall limit, so a small eraser over a large stored drawing interpolated hundreds of millions of points in one gesture. The samples are now counted before each segment is expanded, and a drawing that would pass `MAX_ERASE_SAMPLES` (4,000,000) is refused with "the drawing is too large to erase at this eraser size". Nothing is changed in that case.

title: M3: the find bar's text box stays put while the search counts (#5957)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Fixes the first half of #5957: the find bar's text box no longer slides sideways while a search runs. The second half (a new search selecting the old query) is #4534, already covered by the open #4533 and #4849, so this PR leaves it alone.

**What went wrong.** The find bar floats at the top right of the document and is anchored on its right edge. Its status ("Searching… 37/400", "1 of 52+", "No matches") sits between the text box and the buttons. Whenever the status changed width, the whole bar widened or narrowed to the left, carrying the text box with it.
- It changes width constantly during a search. The count goes up, and Inter's digits aren't all the same width: a "1" is about two thirds as wide as a "4".
- So the box jittered while the user tried to click or select in it.

**The fix.** The status now keeps a steady width for as long as the bar is open (`Find::status_width`):
- It starts wide enough for "No matches" and for "Searching… N/N" with the document's number of digits, each the font's widest digit, so the counting phase never moves the bar.
- It only grows, when a status is wider still (thousands of matches, say), and never shrinks back.
- The status is still an ordinary label, so screen readers and the UI control channel read it as before. No strings changed.

## How you verified it

On Windows 10 Pro 22H2.

- **In the real app.** I made a 400-page synthetic PDF, opened the find bar through the UI control channel, and typed t, h, e, z one at a time. After each letter I sampled the text box's position and the status (scratch script, not committed):

  | | statuses seen | box's left edge |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main` | "1 of 10854+", "1 of 21600", "1 of 7200", "No matches" | 4 places: x = 932, 940, 945, 930 |

title: fix(sign): read OCSP responseStatus as ENUMERATED; drop redundant RSA leading zeros
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong**
- OCSP `responseStatus` is ENUMERATED in RFC 6960, but `OcspResponse::parse` required an INTEGER, so every standards-compliant response was rejected before its status was read; `validate.rs` skips parse errors, so applicable revoked evidence was ignored.
- `rsa_pad::encoded_message` built `BoxedUint`s from the raw modulus/exponent bytes. Redundant leading zeros inflated arithmetic width (and sidestepped the backend size limit) without changing the number.

**Changed**
- `der::Tlv::enumerated` + `tag::ENUMERATED`; `revocation.rs` uses it.
- `rsa_pad`: `trim_zeros` on n and e at the shared verification entry (PKCS#1 and PSS), so directly-constructed keys get it too.

**Blast radius** sign crate only. **Behavior change** OCSP responses encoded with an INTEGER status (non-standard) are no longer accepted; standard ones now are. Revocation can now turn a signature Invalid where it was previously silently skipped. Padded RSA keys verify exactly as unpadded.

**Checks run** cargo fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-sign --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign (118 pass). Tests: ENUMERATED fixtures, INTEGER status rejected, 64 KiB zero-padded key verifies. **Not run** workspace-wide tests.

Findings: OCSP responseStatus and RSA leading zeros.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected OCSP response status parsing to use the required encoding; responses with integer-encoded or invalid status values remain rejected.
  * Prevented oversized integer values from wrapping when decoded, while continuing to accept valid zero-padded values up to the maximum supported range.
  * Improved RSA signature verification for keys with redundant leading zero bytes in their modulus or exponent.

title: fix(create): refuse PNG headers the file cannot back; no truncating JP2 box length
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong**
- `png_image` zero-filled a buffer sized by the PNG header (up to 2 GiB) before decoding any pixels, so a file of a few hundred bytes cost up to 2 GiB of memory writes.
- `jp2_boxes` cast the 64-bit extended box length with `as usize`; on 32-bit targets (wasm32) the end could land before the payload and the slice panicked.

**Changed**
- PNG: the decoded size must also be <= file length x (1032 x 32) + 1 MiB. Flate expands at most 1032:1 and decoding at most 32:1 more (1-bit palette to RGBA), so no honest file is affected; the 2 GiB ceiling stays.
- JP2: `usize::try_from(len)`, falling back to saturating at the buffer end.

**Blast radius** pdfcraft-create. **Behavior change** only for files whose header claims far more pixels than their bytes could encode; they now fail with 'image too large' earlier.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-create (70 pass, new regression test). **Not run** 32-bit build of the JP2 path.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of large JPEG 2000 images on 32-bit systems, avoiding incorrect box-length interpretation.
  * Oversized PNG images are now rejected with a clear image error instead of proceeding with excessive memory use.
  * Added coverage for PNG files that claim an unusually large image frame.

title: fix(engine): unknown permissions on an encrypted document refuse copying and printing
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong**
`Document::permissions()` comes from the editing parser (COS). When COS rejects a file the independent renderer still opens (for example an unused array over COS's object budget, or a failed format probe), `editor` is `None`, `permissions()` is `None`, and `allows_copying`/`allows_printing` read that as 'unencrypted, unrestricted', so a restricted encrypted PDF could be exported as text/images or printed.

**Changed**
`Document::permissions_unknown()` = no editor and `info.encrypted` (the renderer's own flag); both checks now fail closed in that state. Unencrypted documents without an editor are unchanged.

**Blast radius** engine (copy/print gating, commands.rs enable state, exports). **Behavior change** for an encrypted file the editor could not parse: copy/print/export are disabled instead of allowed. Nothing changes for files that parse.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine (429 + 16 pass; new test). **Not run** workspace tests.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Encrypted documents that cannot be opened by the editor no longer allow copying or printing when their permissions cannot be determined. Unencrypted documents remain copyable, and documents with readable permissions continue to follow those permissions.

title: fix(render): charge inspection text (fields, tooltips, layers, bookmarks, blank comments) against shared allowances
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong**
Document inspection kept an owned decoded copy of text for every entry that referenced the same large string, with no aggregate bound:
- form field names/values/tooltips (`/T`, `/V` incl. arrays, `/TU`), each field also copying its parent's full name;
- layer (`/OCGs`) names, including one group listed many times;
- bookmark titles;
- unsupported link action names (`LinkTarget::Other`);
- comment text that trims to nothing: never kept, so the retained-bytes budget never saw it and every comment decoded it again.

**Changed** (crates/render/src/inspect)
- `Inspector::field_text` allowance (64 MiB, same size as `MAX_ANNOTATION_BYTES`) with `field_text`/`field_spend`/`field_charge` helpers built on the existing `spend`/`budgeted_text`; used for field T/V/TU, full-name copies (listing stops when spent), layer names, bookmark titles.
- A layer group listed more than once is one layer.
- Link action names use the existing link text budget.
- Comments charge the raw bytes of the strings they read, so blank shared text stops comment building at the existing 64 MiB limit.

**Behavior changes** None for ordinary documents (limits are far above real forms). Past the allowance, further tooltips/values/titles are left empty and field listing stops; duplicated `/OCGs` entries no longer produce duplicate layers.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-render (461 lib + 64 it; 2 new tests). **Not run** workspace tests; the same inspector pattern in `pdfcraft_annot`/`a11y` is separate.

title: fix(render): a JBIG2 region located past i32::MAX is off the page (hayro-jbig2 patch 14)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A JBIG2 region located past `i32::MAX` is now off the page: it draws nothing, and the rest of the page draws.

A region's location is a four-byte field (ISO/IEC 14492 7.4.1.3, 7.4.1.4), and "unless otherwise specified, all multi-bit values shall be treated as unsigned values" (5.4.4). The decoder took it for a signed one:
- a generic, text or halftone region drawn onto the page at 0xFFFFFFFC came back onto it four pixels left of the page's edge, and at 0xFFFFFFFE two;
- a refinement anywhere past `i32::MAX`, of the page or of a region, was refused as an overflow, and the whole page with it.

The vendored hayro-jbig2 gets patch 14 (13 is #5999):
- `Bitmap::combine_region` draws a region at its own location, holding one past `i32::MAX` past the page. All four kinds of region drawn onto the page (generic, text, halftone, refinement) go through it.
- A refinement of another region refines it where it is: "GRREFERENCEDX 0, GRREFERENCEDY 0" (Table 35). The decoder offset the reference by the difference of the two locations, which 7.4.7.5 says must be equal. On a conforming stream that is 0 either way. Where a stream has them differ, the refinement read the region shifted (or, with the region to its right, not at all), or past `i32::MAX` was refused; now it decodes as coded. Poppler, run as an external process, decodes 8 of 8 such streams coded with Table 35's zero offset as coded, and 1 of 8 coded with the difference of the locations.
- A refinement of the page reads the page at its own location, the page being at 0, 0. Past `i32::MAX` the offset is held to `-i32::MAX`, and since the page is at most 65,535 pixels a side, every page pixel the decoder reads is still outside the page, where pixels are 0 (6.3.5.2).

A conforming stream with its regions up to `i32::MAX` decodes as it did. A real encoder doesn't place a region there, so this is about files made by hand or by a fuzzer: the stream decodes as the standard says instead of drawing a stray regio…

title: fix(redact): Remove Hidden Information reads only what the chosen categories need (part of #5873)
author: ljkx
body:
Part of #5873: this fixes only its **second** problem, `doc_remove_hidden` with `categories: ["bookmarks"]` still running after 15 minutes. The first problem, slow opening, is the work of #5958 (merged) and #5183, and nothing here touches their files.

## What was wrong

Removing one category of hidden information did the work of all nine:

- `sanitize::remove_hidden` started with `scan(doc)`, which counts every category. That meant **two passes over every page's content** (hidden text, then hidden layers), a **walk of every object** the catalog reaches (metadata, attachments, actions and private data), and a walk of every page's annotations. Removing bookmarks needs none of it: it reads the outline and edits the catalog.
- It then rewrote every page's `/Annots`, even when no chosen category removes an annotation. On a textbook of 1,412 pages, each carrying InDesign's `/PieceInfo`, every page dictionary was copied into the edit overlay for nothing.
- The `doc_remove_hidden` tool did two more full scans, before and after the removal, to report `removed`. So the command in the report read every page's content **six times** and walked the object graph three times to delete an outline.

## What changed

- `pdfcraft-redact`: `scan_only(doc, which)` counts just the listed categories, in `HIDDEN` order, once each. The page annotations and the object walk are read lazily, the first time a listed category needs them, so hidden text reads the pages and metadata walks the objects only when they are listed. `scan` is `scan_only` over every category, so its results are unchanged.
- `remove_hidden` counts with `scan_only(doc, which)`. It rewrites pages' annotation lists, and cleans the structure tree of annotations that went, only when the choice can change them: comments, attachments, links/actions/scripts, or form fields.
- `pdfcraft-engine`: `Document::hidden_info_of(which)`, beside `hidden_info`.
- `pdfcraft-automation`: `doc_remove_hidden` scans only the listed categories, b…

title: fix(render): charge each ActualText replacement against a per-page allowance
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong**
`TextDevice::actual_text` decoded every `/ActualText` into a fresh owned string, and `end_actual_text` then kept it twice (in the merged glyph and in `replaced`). A property in `/Resources /Properties` reused by many spans therefore expanded a small page into gigabytes during text extraction; the existing redraw budgets only cap later copies.

**Changed** `TextDevice` has a per-page allowance (`MAX_ACTUAL_TEXT`, 32 MiB) charged per span by max(raw bytes, 2 x decoded bytes). Past it (or when one string alone exceeds what is left) a span opens no replacement, so its glyphs keep their own Unicode, as for a span with no `/ActualText`.

**Blast radius** render text extraction/search. **Behavior change** only for pages whose ActualText totals more than 32 MiB (about 16 MiB of replacement text), which no real document has.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-render (460 + 64; new unit test fails without the change). **Not run** workspace tests.

Covers 8e2d2ec9, 379dac4f (device.rs) and 902b6346 (named property decode). The redraw clone (be4c52c8) is already bounded by MAX_REDRAW_TEXT on main. Layout quadratic pair search (058a670a, dae5cadb) is not covered.

title: M3: Preferences can set the Zoom In / Zoom Out step (#5884)
author: ljkx
body:
## What was missing

Zoom In and Zoom Out in the document view always stepped through the standard levels (`DocView::zoom_step`: … 66%, 75%, 100%, 125%, 150%, 200% …). Between 100% and 200% that leaves only two stops, which is too coarse for some documents, and there was no way to change it (#5884).

## What changed

A saved preference, **Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ Zoom In and Zoom Out step**, offers four choices:

- **Standard levels**, the default. Nothing changes unless the user picks another step.
- **5%**, **10%** or **25%**: each Zoom In or Zoom Out moves by that many percentage points. The zoom lands on multiples of the step, so a fitted 87% goes to 90% on Zoom In and 80% on Zoom Out. Below the first multiple, Zoom Out goes to the smallest zoom (8%), and both directions stop at 8% and 6400%, the range `zoom_at` already clamps to.

Details:

- `canvas/zoom_increment.rs` (new) holds `ZoomIncrement`: its labels, its `ui.set` parsing (`standard`, `5`, `10`, `25`, with an optional `%`), its serde names, and `step()`. `step()` treats a zoom within 0.001 of a step as on it, so 110% stored as 109.99999 still goes to 120%.
- `DocView::zoom_step_by(up, increment)` uses the standard levels through the existing `zoom_step` unchanged, and otherwise `ZoomIncrement::step`. I left `zoom_step` itself alone because the rulers PRs (#4584, #4879) rewrite its STEPS list, and this way the two don't touch the same lines.
- All three Zoom In/Out entry points use it: ⌘+ / ⌘− (`canvas::shortcuts`), the navigation rail's Zoom out and Zoom in buttons, and View ▸ Zoom ▸ Zoom in / Zoom out.
- The preference is kept with the other settings (`persist` / `restore`). A missing or unreadable value keeps the standard levels. It can also be set headlessly with `ui.set zoom_increment`, which refuses anything else with "zoom_increment must be standard, 5, 10, or 25".
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml`: the `view.zoom-in-out` entry gets the new test as evidence and a "Beyond Acrobat" sentence…

title: Scroll: smooth wheel bursts and preserve precise movement
author: dotCooCoo
body:
<!--
Thanks for contributing to PdfCraft.

Base this on `main` — it is the only integration branch. `main` moves fast (it took
396 commits in the three days to 2026-10-12), so a PR that sits for a day usually needs
a rebase. Rebasing the same day you are asked keeps the work from dying of conflicts.
Delete any section below that does not apply.
-->

## What this changes

<!-- What behaviour is different afterwards, and why it is worth doing. If it fixes an
     issue, say `Fixes #123`. -->

Coarse wheel bursts currently ease their base distance through egui while applying accelerated surplus immediately. Route the base, bounded acceleration and Page-unit distance through one per-view motion queue. Point input stays direct. Fractional Line components stay direct on their own axes; explicit Trackpad/Momentum sources stay direct on both axes.

Read input once per egui frame, including discarded passes. Reversal and ownership interruptions cancel older motion without swallowing new wheel events. Clear egui's retained wheel copy before fresh input reaches other scroll areas, and synchronize the animation-off reader's gesture state with that reset.

Each axis accepts at most 16384 input points, retains at most 16384 pending points and emits at most 8192 points per frame. This preserves isolated base-plus-surplus bursts when capacity permits; sustained overload can exceed the finite admission limit.

Related: [#5563](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/5563) by @austin62jake and [#4840](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/4840) by @0xPyAI address overlapping cases, and parts of this change follow them. The per-view motion queue follows #5563's pending surplus (its frame-time clamp, the reset after a gap, dropping an axis on reversal, and the 0.9-in-0.1 s ease), and the direct routing of Trackpad and Momentum sources and of fractional Line components follows #4840's touchpad rule. title: fix(xfa): bound the name and path bytes data nodes and queued instances copy
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong**
- `DataNode::ensure` (the in-memory data tree scripts run against) gave each SOM-index-skipped sibling its own copy of the element name with no byte bound, so one long name with an index near 10,000 allocated gigabytes. The datasets writer (`Build::at`) already bounds this at 4 MiB.
- `write_data_ops` queued each `Instances` row with a clone of its parent path and name (twice); `MAX_ENSURED` bounds the row count but not the bytes, so a long ancestor was multiplied by up to 200,000.

**Changed**
- `ensure` returns `None` (nothing created) when the new siblings' names would exceed the writer's `MAX_NEW_NAME_BYTES` (now `pub(super)`).
- `write_data_ops` stops queueing at a 128 MiB byte allowance (`MAX_ENSURED_BYTES`), reported through the existing "instances not written past" warning.

**Blast radius** pdfcraft-xfa data model/writer. **Behavior change** none for real forms (names and paths are tens of bytes; 4 MiB / 128 MiB are far above them).

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-xfa --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa (145 pass, 2 new tests). **Not run** engine tests.

Covers 64b0bd57 (DataNode builder), 97c2a97d and f4bd3008 (Instances expansion; the intermediate-count quadratic was already removed on main by the `queued` map). 3a88c58b (Build::at name copies) is already bounded on main by NewNodes.

title: fix(xfa): charge live-form values, paths and messages to one allowance; walk shared fields once
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong**
- `Walker` (live XFA form tree) charged only script source against `MAX_EVENT_SCRIPT_BYTES`, but each event also copies its SOM path and validation message, and each field instance copies its value. Nested repeated subforms multiplied those into gigabytes before any script ran.
- `fields_by_som` walked `/Kids` once per path, so a graph of shared child arrays was expanded exponentially.

**Changed**
- Events charge script + SOM path + message; field values charge the same allowance (a field past it is built with an empty value and the form is marked `truncated`, as for scripts).
- `fields_by_som` visits each field object once (and stops past `MAX_FORM_NODES` visits).

**Blast radius** pdfcraft-xfa live-form builder (`form_tree`), `fields_by_som`. **Behavior change** none below 64 MiB of live values/scripts; a field object referenced from two parents is named by the first path found.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-xfa --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa (144), cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine xfa (49). title: fix(sign): read each existing DSS stream once and within a decoded-size allowance
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong** `dss::embed` (reached from `Session::embed_ltv`) rewrites the store as a union, so it decodes every stream the existing `/DSS` arrays list. `pull` decoded each array entry with the generic 1 GiB limit and then compared it with every blob kept so far, before looking for duplicates: an array repeating one reference to a compressed stream was decoded once per repeat, and a store of many streams could expand without any aggregate bound.

**Changed** `pull` skips a reference it has already read, tracks distinct content by SHA-256 (no quadratic byte comparison), and spends every decoded size from one `MAX_EXISTING_EVIDENCE` allowance (256 MiB, shared by Certs/OCSPs/CRLs). When the allowance is spent the call fails with "existing validation data is too large to extend" rather than dropping evidence the store holds. Undecodable entries are skipped as before.

**Blast radius** `pdfcraft_sign::dss::embed`/`Session::embed_ltv`. **Behavior change** only a store whose evidence decodes to more than 256 MiB now errors; output for ordinary stores is unchanged.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-sign --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign (new unit test for the dedupe and the allowance). **Not run** engine tests.

Covers 247962f8 and 097f1f11. Not covered: VRI entries each copying the whole evidence list (2d1bfd9c; needs a decision on per-signature evidence), and the validation-side reads in pdf.rs (68658db0, bce50d23).

title: fix(sign): judge a shared signature value once per listing; dedupe DSS evidence by object number
author: dylanmtaylor

title: M5: rotate signatures and other stamps by a rotate knob (#6030)
author: goratt12
body:
## What this changes

A signature added to a page can now be rotated. Fixes #6030.

- **Rotate knob.** A selected stamp or drawn signature has a knob on a stem above its frame, the same one pictures have in Edit text & images. Dragging turns it about its middle, showing the turned outline and the angle. **Shift** lands on 15° steps and **Escape** cancels.
- **Quarter turns.** The page's right-click menu has *Rotate clockwise* and *Rotate counterclockwise*.
- **One undo step,** labelled "Rotate comment" (`Edit::RotateAnnotation`).
- **Headless.** `comment_edit` takes `rotate` (degrees counterclockwise, ±360), and `comment_list` reports a turned stamp's `angle`.

All three kinds of signature work. Other stamps are stored like image signatures, so they get this too. Fill & Sign marks that are stamps (check, cross, dot, line) also get the knob.

**How it is stored.** A drawn signature turns its ink points: plain PDF, the same in every viewer. PDF has no angle for a stamp, so its appearance stays drawn upright and is turned by the form's `/Matrix`, with `/Rect` as the turned box's upright hull. Viewers map the turned `/BBox` onto `/Rect` (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.5), which is exactly that hull, so the stamp shows turned and unscaled.

- `/PCAngle`, `/PCSize` and `/PCBaseMatrix` record the turn. The box's size and place are always read from `/Rect`, so another program that moves or resizes the stamp without knowing these keys leaves it turned.
- A redraw (a new colour or opacity) draws upright in the stamp's own box and turns it again.
- A stamp turned back upright has none of these keys and its original `/Matrix` and `/Rect`.
- Each turn writes a new appearance stream, so a stamp sharing the old one stays as it is.

**A turned stamp behaves differently in a few ways:**
- It is hit inside its turned box, not in the corners of its hull.
- It resizes from its corners only, keeping its shape. Pulling one side of the hull would shear it. `comment_edit rect` likewise fits it, same sh…

title: fix(sign): bound the depth and name bytes of signature field discovery
author: dylanmtaylor

title: fix(edit): refuse a mark on top of content too large to read for open marked content
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong** `isolation()` decides what a mark on top has to close before it is appended (open `BDC`/`BMC` sequences, which may be hidden optional content). When the page content was too large to read in full (more than 100,000 streams, 128 MiB decoded, or 1,000,000 operators) it returned `Unknown { marked: 0 }`: "zero when unknown". The mark was then appended after content that may leave a hidden `/OC` sequence open, so the new mark (a stamp, watermark, header or Fill and Sign text) could be hidden.

**Changed** A new `Isolation::TooLarge` for exactly those size-limit cases; `place_tagged` and `check_on_top` refuse with "the page's content is too large to check for open marked content before adding anything on top of it", as they already do for nesting past `ISOLATION_MAX_DEPTH`. The refusal is checked before an edit changes anything, so the page stays as it was. Content that merely fails to decode or has stray bytes is unchanged (still wrapped whole, as before).

**Blast radius** pdfcraft-edit placement of marks on top. **Behavior change** adding something on top of a page with more than 1,000,000 operators, 128 MiB of content or 100,000 content streams now fails instead of placing a possibly hidden mark.

title: fix(content,edit): stop parsing a page's content at the isolation operator ceiling
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Stacked on #6044** (base branch `fix/sec-edit-isolation-too-large`; retarget to main once it merges).

**Wrong** `isolation()` parsed the whole decoded page content with `Pieces::parse()`, which builds every operator, and only then compared the count with `ISOLATION_MAX_OPS` (1,000,000). The decoded ceiling is 128 MiB, so a stream of two-byte operators (`q`, `Q`) could have tens of millions of `Op` values (each with a name and operand vector) built just to be refused.

**Changed** `Pieces::parse_limited(max_ops)` in `pdfcraft-content` reads through the same operator iterator and gives up (`None`) the moment it has seen more than `max_ops` operators; `isolation()` uses it and returns `TooLarge`. Output is identical to `parse()` when the stream fits.

**Blast radius** one new method in pdfcraft-content; the isolation scan in pdfcraft-edit. **Behavior change** none beyond lower peak memory when the stream is refused.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-content -p pdfcraft-edit --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-content -p pdfcraft-edit (31 + 436; new test for `parse_limited`). **Not run** engine tests.

Covers 547366c4 and 32b5f1f9. Other callers of `parse` on whole pages are not changed.

title: fix(optimize): bound each unused-resource decode by the remaining shared budget
author: dylanmtaylor

title: fix(render): a JBIG2 refinement reads a reference right of it from its first column (hayro-jbig2 patch 15)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A JBIG2 refinement whose reference is offset right of it now reads the reference from its first column. That makes refined text instances and refined symbols decode as coded.

A refinement takes in its reference at an offset, GRREFERENCEDX (ISO/IEC 14492 6.3). That offset is above 0 for:
- a refined text instance whose bitmap is wider than its symbol, or whose RDX is above 0 (⌊RDW/2⌋ + RDX, Table 12);
- a symbol refined in a symbol dictionary with an RDX above 0 (Table 18).

Both are ordinary in symbol-coded scans. While the reference column was still left of 0, the decoder emptied its buffers of the reference. At column 0 it didn't load them again. The context takes in the reference a column to the right of the current one (Figures 12 and 13), so the reference's first 32 columns read as 0. The arithmetic decoding then went out of step, and the page was refused or decoded to other pixels.

The vendored hayro-jbig2 gets patch 15 (13 is #5999, 14 is #6016), in `RefinementContextGatherer::maybe_reload_buffers`. Left of the reference, the buffers keep the words of its first column that each row starts with. With an offset of 0 or less the reference column is never left of 0, so nothing changes there.

Upstream hayro fixed this case together with offsets below −31 ("hayro-jbig2: Fix refinement with reference offsets above 0 or below -31", 1448, 2026-10-13). That code wasn't read: this fix comes from the standard and the decoder's own behaviour. A later bump of the vendored crate would take upstream's.

title: fix(a11y): heading titles decode their source strings within a shared allowance
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong** `Walker::heading` decoded a heading's `/ActualText`, `/Alt` and `/T` in full (`to_text()`) and only then cut the title to `MAX_TITLE` characters. Many headings referencing one large indirect string decoded it once each.

**Changed** `Walker::attr` charges the raw and decoded size of each source string against a per-document allowance (`MAX_TITLE_SOURCE_BYTES`, 32 MiB) and does not decode a string that no longer fits; that heading then falls back to its marked text, or is left out as a heading without text already is.

**Blast radius** pdfcraft-a11y headings (outline and report). **Behavior change** none for real documents.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-a11y --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-a11y (new test: 100 headings on one 512 KiB ActualText stop short of all 100). **Not run** engine tests.

title: fix(automation): clip each text_find match and bound the response's text
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong** `text_find` put `text.text_of(range)` into every match. A match is normally query-sized, but one glyph can stand for a large `/ActualText` replacement, and many matches (one per character of a long query, or a repeated query over a repeated glyph) can name that one glyph, so the response copied the replacement once per match. `limit` bounded the count, not the bytes.

**Changed** Each match's text is clipped to 64 KiB at a character boundary (`"text_truncated": true` is added only to a clipped match), and the response holds at most 8 MiB of match text; past that the search stops with the existing `next` continuation (`start_page`, `skip`) so nothing is lost or repeated. The first match is always returned, so a continuation always makes progress.

**Blast radius** automation `text_find` response. **Behavior change** none for ordinary text (matches are far below 64 KiB and responses far below 8 MiB); the new `text_truncated` key appears only on clipped matches.

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --lib (42, new clip test) and the `it` find/open_inspect tests (5). **Not run** the full automation `it` suite; no end-to-end ActualText fixture.

Covers f90e1d68.

title: fix(optimize): downsampling never enlarges a colour or grey image
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
**Wrong** For colour and grey images `process` resampled whenever the image's effective resolution was above `above_ppi` and `target_ppi > 0`, computing the new size as `target_ppi / ppi`. Public `Settings` whose target is above their threshold (for example above 100 ppi down to 4000 ppi) therefore made `k > 1` and enlarged a small image enormously: the destination (up to millions of pixels per side) was allocated by the resampler before the optimizer compared sizes and discarded the result. The black-and-white path already required `target_ppi < ppi`.

**Changed** The colour/grey path resizes only when `target_ppi < ppi`, so downsampling never enlarges and the destination never exceeds the source in either dimension. Recompression without resizing is unchanged.

**Blast radius** `pdfcraft-optimize` image pass. **Behavior change** only for inconsistent settings (target at or above the image's resolution), which now leave the size alone instead of enlarging it (the result was only kept if it came out smaller than the original, which an enlargement essentially never does).

**Checks run** fmt --check, clippy -p pdfcraft-optimize --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize (24 + 5 + 71, new test with 100 ppi threshold and 4000 ppi target). **Not run** the other crates.

Covers b138376b. Rejecting inconsistent settings at the public boundary (an error) would be a stricter option; that is an API decision. #5910 and #5897 also edit images.rs (other regions).

author: mfiaschi5

## What this changes

The first phase of an AI assistant (M13; `misc.ai-ask`, new `misc.ai-library`). It contains no network code, so it does not depend on the open outbound-network decision. Every piece that would send something is a seam that the app fills later.

**`pdfcraft-ai`** (new, L4, standalone, no I/O, builds for wasm):
- **Claude Messages API codec** (`anthropic-version: 2026-10-21`, streaming):
  - **Request.** Passages go out as `search_result` blocks with citations on, one text block per sentence. An image block is optional.

Fixes #5820.

A dynamic XFA number field (`numericEdit`, or a `decimal`/`integer`/`float` value) with a display picture showed its raw value: `279893.88000000` where Adobe Reader shows `$279,893.88`. title: fix(render): a JBIG2 refinement of the page refines only its area (hayro-jbig2 patch 16)
author: Piohrun
body:
**Stacked on #6016.** Until #6016 merges, this PR's diff includes #6016's three commits. This PR's own change is the last commit, 07f440388.

## What this changes

A JBIG2 refinement of the page now refines only the page's area under it, as the standard has it.

A refinement that refers to no other region refines "the current contents of the page buffer, restricted to the area of the page buffer specified by this segment's region segment information field" (ISO/IEC 14492 7.4.7.4). It does so at an offset of 0 (Table 35), and reads 0 outside that area (6.3.5.2). The decoder instead read the whole page at the refinement's location, the pixels around the area included:
- Wherever the page has ink next to the area, the refinement's contexts differed from the encoder's, and it decoded to other pixels than were coded. A refinement anywhere right of the page's column 31 also read its first two columns as 0 (the second half below).
- A refinement wider or taller than the page was refused.

The vendored hayro-jbig2 gets patch 16:
- `Bitmap::area` copies the page's area, a word at a time. It is 0 off the page, and past the page's width whatever the padding of its rows holds. Both refinement handlers, intermediate and immediate, refine that copy when they refer to no other region.
- Every refinement region now reads its reference at offset 0, as Table 35 says. The per-page offset that #6016 kept (`reference_offsets` and the `refines_page` flag) goes, since the page's area is already at the refinement's place.
- `RefinementContextGatherer::start_row` loads the reference's words a column left of where a row starts in it, as the reload would, not from column 0.
  - With the reference offset 32 or more left of a refinement, each row's first context read 0 for the reference column it starts at, and from 33 left for the one before it too. A refined text instance has that offset from a narrower bitmap or an RDX below −31 (Table 12), and a refined symbol from such an RDX (Table 18).

title: fix(ui): continuous view renders the pages ahead of the scroll
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

In continuous view a fast wheel spin moves past the pages near the window faster than a heavy page renders, so pages come into view blank. The view now keeps the direction it last moved and also queues the next two rows that way (four pages in two-up). Pages on screen stay first in the queue in their usual order. Scrolling the other way drops the queued pages, which cancels their renders, and a zoom or layout change clears the direction. The existing byte and page-count limits bound the prefetch. The web build renders on the UI thread and does not prefetch.

A raster that arrives over the allowance now evicts the pages the frame does not ask for first, then the pages behind the scroll. A prefetched page that is tiled at the current zoom keeps a sharper cached whole-page raster, as a tiled page on screen does.

I measured it with a test harness that drives `PdfCraftApp` through egui_kittest with a GPU renderer and real-time wheel input on two synthetic 320-page documents (mixed text, images and scans; and vector-heavy), at 1400x900 and 3440x1440. "Blank" counts visible page-frames drawn before the page's raster arrived, summed over all scenarios and runs:

|---|---|---|
| macOS (M2 Max), main | 146/8827 | 550/8931 |
| macOS, this change | 0/8863 | 0/8987 |
| Windows (D3D12), main | 296/2628 | 688/2614 |
| Windows, this change | 78/2585 | 304/2621 |
| Windows, with #6065 | 361/2653 | 628/2585 |

title: fix(ui): size the whole-page raster allowance to the pages on screen
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

Whole-page rasters shared a fixed 128 MiB allowance. In a 3440x1440 window with the left panel open, a Letter page at fit width is a 2,980 x 3,850 raster (43.8 MiB), so two pages on screen left no room for another, and scrolling back rendered the pages just passed again.

The allowance now holds eight rasters the size of the largest whole page on screen, between 128 MiB and 384 MiB (256 MiB in the web build). The size comes from the page's request at the current scale, or from the raster held for it while a zoom hold leaves the request out. A tiled page is on screen as a small backdrop and does not raise the allowance. Queue admission, keeping pages already rendered, and texture admission use the same allowance. Tiles keep their own 128 MiB allowance.

### Measured effect

A test harness drove the app through egui_kittest and egui-wgpu at up to 60 Hz pacing, on two synthetic 320-page Letter documents: a mixed one (text, an image on every page, a scan on every tenth page) and a vector one (6,000 curves on every page). "Scroll back" is 40 wheel notches upward at 20 per second over the pages just seen. The Windows runs compared `801fd3aa` with this branch. The Mac runs compared `ecdd1e65`, whose two later commits do not touch `crates/ui-egui`.

Windows, RTX 5090, D3D12, 3440x1440, left panel open. Other work kept the CPU 36 to 100% busy during the runs.

title: M12: headless renderer for PRC models (`pdfcraft-prc-render`), stacked on #5786
author: KenM76
body:
**Stacked on #5786** (the PRC reader). Three commits are new here: the renderer, a merge of #5786's review fixes, and the renderer's own review fixes. The rest is #5786 and will drop out when it merges. I'll rebase the same day.

## What this changes

Adds `pdfcraft-prc-render`, a headless CPU renderer for 3D models read by `pdfcraft-prc`. It's the first piece of the 3D renderer listed in #1297. It sits at L3, depends on nothing but `pdfcraft-prc`, and has no GUI dependency. The viewer, the `automation` tool and a rendered poster can all build on it.

- `assemble` places each product-tree occurrence's tessellation into world space, with the colour the tree resolves for it and per-face colours where faces are styled. A file with no tree draws its meshes where they lie.
- `Camera::fit` / `fit_meshes` frame the model from a direction, in perspective or orthographic projection.
- `render` fills depth-buffered triangles with headlight or unlit shading into a straight-RGBA image. Opaque triangles draw first, then translucent ones blend over them. Perspective views clip at a near plane 1/10,000 of the eye-to-target distance.

Not in this PR: lighting schemes, `/RM` render modes, materials and textures, shadows, ambient occlusion, picking and the GPU path. Each is its own follow-up, in that order.

This is adapted from my own engine, pdfcer (MIT, same author), at commit `912437c3`. It's trimmed to the camera, raster and headlight parts, rewritten to `pdfcraft-prc`'s types, and changed to keep the deny lints and checked indexing. pdfcer's full renderer took about 10 working days, 2026-09-30 to 2026-11-03.

title: test(fill-sign): fixed clock for the Escape-cancels save comparison
author: chamber074
body:
Fixes #6066.

`fill_sign_enter_adds_lines_outside_click_commits_and_escape_cancels` ends by comparing two saves byte for byte to prove Escape wrote nothing. The harness built the app without a clock, so each save stamped `/ModDate` from the system time, and the comparison failed whenever the two saves fell in different seconds.

Change (test code only, `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/fill_sign.rs`):

- `harness_bytes` now delegates to `harness_with_clock(fixture, clock)`; existing callers pass `None` and behave exactly as before.
- New `harness_fixed_clock()` installs a fixed clock (`1_700_000_000`, the value engine tests use) via the codebase's existing pattern (`std::mem::take` + `Session::with_clock`) before the document is opened.
- Only the byte-comparing test uses the new harness; the assertion itself is unchanged.

Proof, both directions:

- Before the fix, inserting a 1.1 s delay before the second save made the test fail every run; without the delay it passed only when both saves landed in the same second.

title: fix(fonts): a CMap's codespace ranges are at most four bytes and listed once
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
What was wrong: parse_cmap kept codespace ranges of any byte length and any number of repeats (up to 65536). Every decoded glyph searches them linearly, so repeated ranges multiplied CPU by text length; the last range's length was also used unchecked as an allocation multiplier in Metrics::encode (text.len() * code_len).

What changed: parse_cmap drops codespace ranges whose length is outside 1..=4 and exact repeats of a range already kept; code_len is clamped to 1..=4. A repeated range can never be the first match, so decoding is unchanged for it.

Blast radius: crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs only. Behavior change: a CMap with a codespace longer than 4 bytes no longer has that range (it could not be represented in a u32 code anyway); if the last-listed range is a repeat of an earlier one, code_len now follows the last distinct range.

Checks run: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-fonts --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts (new regression test included).
Not run: workspace tests, xtask layers/assets.

Covers CodeRabbit findings 5c3f8e2f (duplicate-range search) and 8ddeba40 (code_len bound). Not the indexed-lookup part for non-duplicate ranges.

title: XFA: pattern fills draw their hatch lines (#6074)
author: chamber074
body:
Fixes #6074.

## What happens today

An XFA `<fill>` with a `<pattern>` child is written as the fill's solid colour — the hatch lines are never drawn. In the XFA writer every fill was a single colour; patterns were not parsed at all.

## Change

- **Model/parse:** a `Hatch` type for the six patterns (`crossHatch`, `crossDiagonal`, `diagonalLeft`, `diagonalRight`, `horizontal`, `vertical`) and a `Pattern` carrying the type and line colour. `<pattern>` and its optional `<color>` child are parsed in both `<border><fill>` and `<rectangle><fill>`. A bare `<pattern/>` is `crossHatch`, and an unknown type falls back to `crossHatch` so the form still gets its lines; the line colour defaults to black.
- **Layout:** square fills and rounded boxes carry the pattern, and it survives page-break splits. Inside a draw turned 90°/270° the pattern is oriented to the page: horizontal and vertical swap, and the two diagonals swap.
- **PDF writer:** the background colour is filled as before, then the same path is filled again with a tiling pattern (`/Pattern` colour space), reusing the existing outline code — so rounded and inverted corners clip the lines too. One pattern object is shared per type and colour, listed under the page's `/Pattern` resources.
- **Geometry** matches what Acrobat itself writes for these fills, taken from the rectangle corpus file attached to #5558 (its saved appearances hold Acrobat's tiling patterns): a 9pt cell, hairline (0-width) lines, diagonals corner to corner. That also settles the directions: `diagonalLeft` falls (`\`), `diagonalRight` rises (`/`).

## Not covered

- A field's own `<ui>` border fill stays colour-only: it becomes the widget's background colour (`/MK /BG`), which has no pattern form.
- Gradient and stipple fills are still drawn as their colour in generated output — separate work, noted in the parity entry.

## Tests

- `pattern_fills_carry_their_lines_into_the_layout` — bare default, explicit type with a red `<color>`, unknown type, no …

title: fix(forms): comb detection ignores repeated boxes
author: dylanmtaylor
