title: XFA: gradient and stipple fills shade and blend (#6079)
author: chamber074
body:
Fixes #6079.

## What

XFA fills holding a `<linear>`, `<radial>` or `<stipple>` child were written as the fill's one flat colour. Now:

- **Gradients** are written as axial (`<linear>`) or radial (`<radial>`) shadings between the fill's colour and the element's colour, painted with `sh` on the same outline path the flat fill uses — so rounded and inverted corners clip the gradient too. Shading objects are shared per page for identical shadings, gradients turn with a turned draw, and a gradient cut by a page break carries on across both pages rather than restarting.
- **Stipple** is written as the one colour its colour blends to with the fill's at its `rate` — the rate read as the stipple colour's share, with a rate of exactly 0 read as 100, the way other XFA readers treat it (PDFium's `CXFA_Stipple::Draw` does the same, and the corpus file's saved appearances agree at the endpoints: rates 0 and 100 both render as the full stipple colour).

## Checked against the fixture

The geometry was pinned from the rectangle corpus file's own shading dictionaries rather than assumed: linear shadings run from the middle of one side of the box to the middle of the opposite side, and a radial's radius is the box's half diagonal (43.9436 pt on the corpus's 72 × 50.4 pt box) — the implementation matches both. The stipple rows and gradient rows of that file (§12) are the visual check.

## Scope notes

- A gradient on a field's own background (the widget's `/MK /BG`) still paints the flat start colour; widgets have no shading form there.
- Two-colour gradients only — that is all these elements express.

## Tests

Four new tests in the xfa crate (layout carry, page-break continuation, writer shading dictionaries and clipping, turned draws); the writer test fails with the `<linear>` parse reverted and passes with it. Full `pdfcraft-xfa` suite: 149 passed; clippy clean.

*Drafted with AI assistance; the fixture values and code checks behind it were run and verified by me.*

title: M12: model_render, a page's 3D model drawn to a PNG (stacked on #6069)
author: KenM76
body:
**Stacked on #6069** (the renderer), which is stacked on #5786 (the PRC reader). The commits new here are the tool, its follow-up, and a merge of #6069's review fixes; the rest drops out as those merge. I'll rebase the same day.

## What this changes

Adds `model_render`, the first way to reach the 3D renderer from outside: it draws a page's 3D model to a PNG, headlessly. With it, `misc.3d-view` moves from `planned` to `partial`.

- `pdfcraft-annot` reads a page's 3D annotations and the model each one shows. That is the `/3DD` stream, or the stream a 3D reference dictionary names under `/3D` (ISO 32000-2 §13.6.3). It's decoded through the stream's filters within 256 MB and typed PRC or U3D by `/Subtype`. `pdfcraft-engine` exposes both on `Document`.
- `model_render` takes `doc`, `page`, and optionally:
  - `model`, the 1-based position among the page's 3D models;
  - `width` and `height`, each 1 to 4096 (default 512);
  - `direction`, the view direction from the eye (default `[-1, 1, -1]`, Z up);
  - `perspective` (default true).

  It parses PRC with `pdfcraft-prc`, then frames and draws the model with `pdfcraft-prc-render`. It's read-only.
- U3D models give a clear error until a decoder lands (see #467).

Not in this PR: the in-app 3D view, the annotation's `/3DV` views, and everything listed as later slices in #6069. The parity note lists what's missing.

The renderer it calls is adapted from my own engine, pdfcer (MIT, same author), as #6069 says. The annotation reading and the tool are new code, written here from ISO 32000-2 §13.6 against this repo's types.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

title: fix(a11y): auto-tagging bounds the content it plans across all pages
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
What was wrong: autotag plan() decoded and parsed each page's content and kept an owned operator list per page. The per-page limits (16 MiB, 100,000 operators) reset for every page, so up to 1,000 pages sharing one compressed stream retained about 1,000 times the limit.

What changed: plan() also totals decoded bytes (128 MiB) and operators (2,000,000) over all pages and refuses the edit with the existing Unsupported error ("too much content to auto-tag in one edit") before keeping more. Nothing is modified on refusal (planning happens before any mutation).

Blast radius: crates/a11y/src/autotag.rs. Behavior change: a text-only document whose pages together exceed 2M operators or 128 MiB of decoded content is now refused; a real 1,000-page text document is far below that (about 2,000 operators per page would be needed to reach it).

title: fix(windows): a window that can't start says why instead of the app exiting silently
author: smittie2000
body:
## What this changes

When eframe returns an error because the window can't start (no usable GPU, a broken driver, a VM, or no desktop), PdfCraft now logs the reason and shows an error dialog: "PdfCraft's window could not start or stopped with an error: <error>. If this keeps happening, updating the graphics driver often fixes it." The same dialog shows for an error after the window was up, so the text names graphics only as the likely cause. An error from the app's own start-up (AppCreation, e.g. a --control file it can't write) only says "PdfCraft could not start: <error>", without the graphics advice. An error from winit, the windowing layer (on Linux, for example, no display session), gets the first sentence only: a driver update can't help there. Before, it logged the error and exited with code 1, with nothing on screen.

The approach is the same as FilmCraft's since 0.14.0 (storytold/filmcraft, `apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs`): a small `start_failure` module (message, dialog, tests) and a few lines in `main()`. It also adds `rfd` (already a workspace dependency) to the app crate, which adds one line to `Cargo.lock`.

## Why: WinGet

winget-pkgs validation installs each new version and starts the app without a desktop. There, `Surface::configure` fails (`Invalid surface`). An app that exits with an error or panics there is labelled `Validation-Executable-Error` and is never merged. An app that shows a dialog and keeps running passes. PdfCraft has failed this on every version since 0.10.1. A moderator published the backlog by hand on 2026-11-06; versions submitted since fail again (newest: 0.19.0, microsoft/winget-pkgs#473229).

FilmCraft went through the same thing: 0.13.0 panicked and failed validation three times; 0.14.0 added this dialog and every version since has passed. Root cause and evidence: storytold/craft-libs#565 (Current focus, step 12).

It also helps people on broken drivers or VMs, who today see nothing happen. Related: #5553 ("The Application does…

title: fix(optimize): the fragment search charges every operator of a group it reads
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
What was wrong: merge_page's search for fragment runs charged its allowance one unit per group read, but reading a group composes every `cm` in it. A page of overlapping groups with many `cm` operators each read about 16 x (operators) groups, each costing its `cm` count, so CPU was quadratic in the matrices per group.

What changed: the search is charged the number of content operators it covers (j - i) instead of the number of groups, and SCAN_PER_OP goes from 16 to 64 so a minimal four-operator group (q cm Do Q) is charged the same as before. Groups with extra `cm` operators now pay for them.

Blast radius: crates/optimize/src/fragments.rs. Behavior change: none for pages of plain four-operator groups; a page whose groups carry many `cm` operators and whose runs are repeatedly rejected reaches the limit sooner, and the rest of that page is then left as it is (the same safe outcome as the existing limit).

Checks run: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-optimize --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize. The new test (400 groups of 53 operators) fails on main (4.15M operator reads against a 1.7M bound) and passes here.
Not run: workspace tests.

Covers CodeRabbit findings 0053fa90 and d39b481f. Cancellation checks inside long unsuccessful searches are not added.

title: fix(sign): chain building hashes a certificate once for all candidate issuers
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
What was wrong: build_chain_noted tested every certificate in the pool that matched the issuer name with Certificate::signed_by, which hashes the whole signed part of the child each time. Many candidate issuers sharing one name hashed a large certificate once per candidate.

What changed: an internal signed_by_cached keeps the digest of the child's signed part across the candidates for one chain step; signed_by (public API) is unchanged and uses it with an empty cache. Ed25519 hashes inside verification and is unaffected.

title: fix(render): the named-destination index spends key bytes from one allowance
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
What was wrong: Inspector::new indexed the /Names /Dests tree by cloning every resolved key and hashing it before rejecting duplicates. A tree repeating indirect references to one large string key did full-length clone and hash work for every repeat.

What changed: name_tree_raw takes a key-byte allowance (the existing MAX_LINK_ATTACHMENT_TEXT_BYTES, 16 MiB) for the whole tree, charged for every key including repeats before it is hashed, and a key is copied only on its first occurrence. Entries past the allowance are not indexed, so a destination named there resolves to nothing, as an unknown name already does.

Blast radius: crates/render/src/inspect/{core,navigation}.rs. Behavior change: a document whose destination names total more than 16 MiB loses the later ones (a real 60,000-destination file is about 1 MiB).

Checks run: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p pdfcraft-render (new test: one 1 MiB key referenced 17 times exhausts the allowance before the real key).
Not run: workspace tests.

title: fix(forms): AFSimple_Calculate folds field values as it reads them, within an allowance
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
What was wrong: calculate() expanded every field listed in an AFSimple_Calculate list into one Vec<f64> before aggregating. Repeating a broad group name many times held (listings x group size) numbers at once, from a compact script.

What changed: the values are folded lazily as they are read (same iterator operations in the same order, so results are identical), and a list that expands past 1,048,576 values (MAX_EXPANDED_VALUES) is not calculated: calculate returns None, as it does for an unparsable calculation, and reading stops at the limit.

title: optimize: opt-in DeviceCMYK to DeviceRGB conversion for recompression
author: so-sai
body:
## What this changes

Adds an opt-in `convert_cmyk_to_rgb: bool` setting to `pdfcraft_optimize::Settings` (`false` by default, including in `Settings::default()`, `ImageSettings::REDUCE`, and `ImageSettings::MOBILE`).

When enabled, eligible 8-bit `DeviceCMYK` images are converted to `DeviceRGB` using the uncalibrated ISO 32000-2 §10.3.5 subtractive approximation (`R = (1 − C)(1 − K)`, matching `pdfcraft-create` and `pdfcraft-edit`), allowing the optimizer to downsample and recompress them as RGB JPEG or Flate streams when the resulting object is smaller.

Conservative fail-safe boundaries leave the original stream untouched when:
- The colour space is not direct `/DeviceCMYK` or `/CMYK` (4-component `/ICCBased`, `/Indexed`, `/Separation`, and `/DeviceN` are excluded).
- The image is drawn or listed where `/DefaultCMYK`, `/DefaultRGB`, or `/DefaultGray` is in force, or is referenced outside the walked page content streams (`used_elsewhere`).
- The image has a non-stencil `/Mask`, `/ImageMask`, `/SMaskInData`, `/OPI`, or an `/SMask` with `/Matte`.
- The image is under 64×64 pixels and is not being downsampled.
- A 4-component JPEG has `/ColorTransform 1` without an Adobe APP14 marker (YCbCrK), has an unknown APP14 transform flag, or its APP14 marker contradicts `/ColorTransform`.
- The `/Decode` array is malformed or the converted stream (measured via `stored_len`) is not smaller than the original.

title: optimize: opt-in dual-guard binarization for near-bilevel scans
author: so-sai
body:
## What this changes

Adds an opt-in `binarize_scans: bool` field to `pdfcraft_optimize::MonoSettings` (`false` by default, including in `MonoSettings::REDUCE`).

When enabled, `one_bit` can binarize pristine 8-bit `DeviceGray` and `DeviceRGB` scanned text images to 1-bit monochrome (compressed with `MonoCompression`, such as CCITT Group 4 or JBIG2) when they pass three conservative guards:
1. **Chroma Guard (RGB):** Rejects images containing coloured ink, stamps, signatures, or highlighters (`chroma > 30` at any luminance, or `chroma > 10` for non-paper pixels with `lum < 225`).
2. **Bimodal Histogram Guard:** Partitions all 256 luminance levels (`0..=65` dark, `66..=214` midtone, `215..=255` bright) and requires `extreme_ratio >= 0.98`, `midtone_ratio <= 0.005`, `dark_ratio >= 0.005`, and `bright_ratio >= 0.50`.
3. **Otsu & Content-Loss Guard:** Computes Otsu's threshold (rejecting degenerate single-level distributions), clamps to `[100, 180]`, and aborts if more than `0.05%` of total pixels fall in `[threshold..215)` so faint strokes are never bleached to white.

Images with `/SMask`, `/SMaskInData`, `/OPI`, non-stencil `/Mask`, `/Indexed` colour spaces, non-identity `/Decode`, page-level `/DefaultGray`/`/DefaultRGB` remaps, or references outside walked page contents (`used_elsewhere`) are left untouched.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-optimize` (and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`)
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize` (35 unit + 5 `jpeg_color_transform` + 70 `optimize` tests pass)
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`, and `cargo xtask parity`

title: feat(organize): export, import and copy bookmark trees (#6018)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Part of #6018 (the import/export part of the split ticket). Three new automation tools move a whole outline, or one bookmark's subtree, between documents:

- **`bookmark_export`** returns the tree as JSON. A node carries its title, page (1-based), open state, colour, bold/italic, children, and its view: the destination type (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.2, Table 149) with its values in PDF user space, exactly as the file stores them. With `out`, the same tree is written to a JSON file.
- **`bookmark_import`** takes that tree, inline or from the file, and adds it under any bookmark at any position, or with `replace` in place of the whole outline. It is one undoable edit, `Import bookmarks`.
- **`bookmark_copy`** does the same straight from another open document, mapping by page number.

What the ticket asked for and how this meets it:

- **Lossless round-trip.** Export, import into another document, then export again gives the same tree. Views stay in user space rather than the listing's display coordinates, so nothing is rounded.
- **Unmapped entries are reported, not dropped.** A bookmark whose page the target lacks keeps its place without a destination and is listed in `unmapped`, with 1-based paths into the given tree. It is never clamped to the last page.
- **Bad input is refused whole.** Every node is checked before anything is written: a non-blank title, page ≥ 1, colour in 0–1, a known view type with exactly its values (all four for `/FitR`), at most 100,000 bookmarks, and at most 33 levels counting the levels above the bookmark it goes under. The error names the node by its 1-based path, and a bad view lists the types and their value counts.

In `pdfcraft-organize`, `outline_tree` reads the tree and `import_outline` writes it. Writing is iterative, links go through the existing `relink`/`recount`, and a closed parent keeps its negative `/Count` (§12.3.3, Table 151).

title: Tests: a scratch folder removes itself when its test ends (#6028)
author: austin62jake
body:
## What this changes

Part of #6028: the six test helpers that left the most folders in the temporary directory now remove their folder when the test ends.

**The problem.** Most test helpers create `temp_dir()/pdfcraft-<what>-<pid>` and never remove it. nextest runs every test in a process of its own, so each run leaves a new folder per test. CI's runners are thrown away after each job, but Windows never clears `%TEMP%`: one machine held 22,390 of these folders, 1.35 GB, after six days of running the gate.

**`pdfcraft_testkit::{ScratchDir, ScratchFile}`.** The testkit crate is already the one place for test scaffolding, so the guard lives there, beside the `Pdf` builder.
- `ScratchDir::new(name)` makes an empty folder, `pdfcraft-<name>-<pid>-<n>`, and removes it with its contents when dropped, pass or fail.
- The process id and a per-process count keep tests running at the same time, as threads or processes, out of each other's folders.
- It creates the folder with `create_dir`, which fails if the folder already exists, and then moves on to the next name. A folder it didn't make is never emptied or reused. Process ids come round again, so such a folder may be one a killed run left, or one a live process with the same id made (containers with their own process ids can share a temporary directory).
- `ScratchFile::new(name, file)` is one file's path in such a folder, for helpers that hand out file paths.
- Both dereference to their `Path`, implement `AsRef<Path>` and convert to a `PathBuf`. So call sites written for the old `PathBuf` (`dir.join(..)`, `&dir`, `fs::write(&path, ..)`, an `impl Into<PathBuf>` argument) compile unchanged.

author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

Follows #6063.

In continuous two-page view at high zoom, the other page of a row can sit off to the side of the window, so it does not count as shown. title: Scroll: a touch zoom keeps zooming after its keys are let go
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

Follows #6031.

A touch gesture that starts with Ctrl or Command keeps zooming to its end after the keys are let go, as egui reads it. The document canvas read each wheel event's own modifiers instead. A motion that arrived after the keys were let go was scrolled by the canvas and zoomed by the app in the same frame. The canvas then reset the wheel state, so the rest of the gesture scrolled.

title: M6: forms decodes field values, renamed calculations and detected pages within shared budgets
author: Piohrun
body:
Part of #5755.

## What this changes

Three of the forms crate's four stream reads that had no shared allowance now decode through a `DecodeBudget`. Each read got a fresh 1 GiB allowance (`MAX_DECODED`), so a small file naming one compressed stream many times decoded it again for each name. Now each reading of the form, rename and page is bounded however often the file names the same stream. The fourth, the PDF/A declaration, is read within preflight's cap of 8 MiB a filter stage instead (below).

- **Field values.** A reading of the form (`fields`) decodes its fields' value streams (`/V`, `/DV`, which may be text streams) within one 64 MiB budget, as it already did their script streams (`MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES`). Past it, a value reads as none, as one that won't decode does. Values and scripts have budgets of their own, so a file can't spend one to hide the other.
- **Renaming a field** decodes the script streams of the form's calculations, to find those that read it, within one script budget. Past it, a calculation is left as it is, as one that won't decode is already, even one that reads the field.
- **Field detection** (`detect::page_shapes`, behind Prepare Form's auto-detect) reads a page's content within one page's allowance (`DecodeBudget::page`, 256 MiB), as the content walks do, however often `/Contents` lists a stream. It also reads the operators one at a time rather than collecting them: content dense with operators (`n n n …`) parsed whole held about 80 bytes for each byte decoded.
- **The PDF/A declaration** (`declares_pdfa`, which keeps `/NeedAppearances` out of a PDF/A document) is read from metadata each filter stage of which decodes within 8 MiB, the cap preflight's Standards panel uses, rather than within 1 GiB. Outside a PDF/A document it's asked only while `/NeedAppearances` isn't set, so once the first field the form can't draw has set it, the metadata isn't decoded again for the fields drawn after. A document with no `/AcroForm` has nowhere to set it…

title: M10: Copy Image and image export decode JPEG 2000 pictures (#6121)
author: hasannadeem
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6121.

**Copy Image** and **Copy Image in Original Format** refused every JPEG 2000 picture with "JPEG 2000 images can't be exported yet". So did Save Image As and Export ▸ Export all images. All four go through `pdfcraft_create::image_file`, which refused any `/JPXDecode` image outright.

`crates/create/src/extract.rs` now decodes a JPEG 2000 image with `hayro-jpeg2000` and writes it as a PNG, like the other lossless images. `hayro-jpeg2000` is the decoder the page is already drawn with: it is in the graph through `hayro-syntax` and is now a direct dependency of `pdfcraft-create`, as `zune-jpeg` is.

How the image is read (ISO 32000-2 §7.4.9 and Table 87):

- **Colours.** With a `/ColorSpace`, its components are the image's. Without one, the image has the colours its own header gives, with its palette applied.
- **Palette indices.** An `/Indexed` space reads each index at the codestream's precision. The decoder scales every component to 8 bits, so a 4-bit index of 8 would otherwise look up entry 136.
- **CMYK.** A 4-component codestream with no colour box reads as RGB plus opacity to the decoder. Under `/DeviceCMYK` all four are taken as inks.
- **Opacity.** The image's own opacity channel becomes alpha only when `/SMaskInData` is 1 and there is no `/SMask`. `/Decode` is ignored, as the spec says for JPEG 2000.
- **Allocation.** A codestream that isn't the dictionary's `/Width` × `/Height` is refused **before** it is decoded. So the decode allocates only what the export's existing pixel cap allows. The decode is also charged to the export's `ImageBudget`, like a JPEG.
- **Still reported, not exported:** JPEG 2000 behind other filters, a JPEG 2000 stencil mask, and data that doesn't decode.

"Copy Image in Original Format" gives a PNG for a JPEG 2000 picture, as the issue suggests: the clipboard has no JPEG 2000 format, and the pixel copy decodes the file it is handed.

title: xml: one bounded XML parse for the workspace (pdfcraft-xml)
author: smittie2000
body:
## What this changes

Every XML parse in PdfCraft now goes through one bounded parse in a new standalone crate, `pdfcraft-xml` (L0). That covers XFA templates, data files and datasets, XFDF and XML form data, and the PDF/A identification read from XMP. clippy refuses direct roxmltree parses anywhere else (`disallowed-methods`).

**Why: roxmltree 0.21.2 has quadratic loops, and xfa and xfdf only bounded depth.** These were measured against roxmltree directly (release build), not through PdfCraft:

| input | size | parse time |
|---|---|---|
| 60,000 attributes on one element | 633 KB | 9.8 s |
| 60,000 namespace declarations on one element | 1 MB | 9.2 s |
| root declaring 2,000 namespaces, 20,000 children declaring one each | 436 KB | 156 s |
| 11,000 prefixed attributes sharing one 100 KB namespace URI (extrapolated from smaller runs) | 221 KB | ~10 min |

xfa and xfdf checked nesting depth before parsing, but nothing else, so an XFA packet in a PDF or an imported data file in one of these shapes holds the parser for that long. preflight capped attributes per tag and in total, but those caps refused cheap packets and still admitted expensive ones. One example: a 1,024-deep chain of elements each declaring four prefixes is about 5·10⁹ comparisons. I found no existing issue or PR for this.

**How the bound works:** one linear scan, before roxmltree sees the text, refuses three things:
- a DTD;
- nesting past 1,024;
- more than a budget of roxmltree's superlinear work.

The work model follows roxmltree's own data structures and loops (`crates/xml/src/scan.rs` documents it loop by loop):
- It keeps an upper bound on roxmltree's in-scope namespace list. That includes repeated default namespace declarations, which roxmltree doesn't deduplicate, and attributes like `p:xmlns`, which roxmltree reads as default declarations.
- It stops collecting a tag's declarations once their duplicate check alone is over the budget, so its memory is bounded by the budget, not the input.
-…

author: hasannadeem
body:
## What this changes

Part of #6145: the logo, both separator lines, the green text and the ID at the bottom of the reporter's file can now be selected, moved and deleted in Edit text & images.

**Why they couldn't be.** In that file, all of them are drawn through two Form XObjects (`Fm0`, `Fm1`), and both give their `/BBox` top first: `[0 841.89 595.276 0]`. That is the page rectangle, written in the other corner order. ISO 32000-2 §7.9.5 lets a rectangle's corners come in either order and says readers normalise them, and the renderer draws these Forms correctly.

`pdfcraft_edit::images::page_images` read the four numbers as given and skipped any Form whose `y1 <= y0` as empty. So both Forms were missing from `page_images` (count 0) and `object_list`, and the Edit tool had nothing under the pointer to pick.

**Change.** `page_images` reads a Form's `/BBox` as the rectangle it is: `[min x, min y, max x, max y]`. A box with no area, in either order, is still skipped. The other `/BBox` readers already normalise, so they're unchanged:

- redaction's interpreter takes explicit min/max;
- appearance placement in `flatten.rs` and print imposition fold over the transformed corners;
- `Matrix::bbox` takes corners in any order.

**Not in this PR**, also reported in #6145:

- "the first text field can't be moved until it's resized or edited";
- "the second text field gives an error when edited";
- emptied text fields disappearing.

Headlessly, `text_edit` both edits paragraph 3 and moves paragraph 2 on the reporter's file without an error, so those are UI-path problems and need their own look.

title: fix(fonts): a Type 0 subset's program decides which glyphs it has, not /W (#6149)
author: fatihkunak
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6149.

On a Type 0 / Identity-H subset that keeps glyph ids (PyMuPDF, and similar producers), `/W` lists a width for every glyph of the full font, the ones the subset emptied too. `Metrics::has_glyph` took "CID is in `/W`" as "the glyph is there", so an edit that typed a letter the subset had dropped encoded it in the subset and the letter drew as nothing. The font name, size and text layer stayed right, so nothing showed that the page was wrong (`: Örnek, Şirin Çağlar Kaya` drew as `: Ö , Ş Ç K`).

Now, when the font is a subset and its TrueType program could be read (`outlined_cids`, #2153), the program decides: a glyph is there when it has an outline. A glyph with no outline is there only when its text is blank by nature (white space, soft hyphen, zero-width marks) and `/W` lists it, so spaces still encode. A subset whose program can't be read keeps the old rule (`/W`, `/DW`).

An edit that needs a dropped letter now fails `Metrics::encode` for that font, so it takes the existing fallback path, like the simple-font cases in #2378 / #4038 (#4044).

## How you verified it

- New test `a_composite_subsets_program_decides_which_glyphs_are_there_not_its_widths` (`crates/fonts/src/pdf/tests.rs`). It takes the repo's own Inter program, empties the `loca` range of `r`, `y` and the space, and lists all of them in `/W` and `/ToUnicode`. Without the fix it fails on `encode("r")` (`Some([3, 84])`: the dropped glyph is written); with it, `r` and `y` are refused, kept letters and a space still encode. I reverted the fix to see it red.

title: M7: a paragraph holding a tab edits when rewritten run by run (#6145)
author: hasannadeem
body:
## What this changes

Part of #6145: "the second text field cannot be edited in any way (it gives error)". With the reporter's file I reproduced it in the real UI. In Edit text & images, open the paragraph "• This text field cannot be edited at all", type anything (even an "e"), and click away. The edit is refused with:

> Edit text failed: the source font cannot show the replacement text

**Why.** That paragraph is a list item. Word drew the gap after its bullet as a glyph whose `/ActualText` is U+0009, so the paragraph reads back with a tab in it. Its two runs share a row, so it is rewritten **run by run** (`text_regions::styled`), and that path hands each character to a font:

- the source font, a subset of ArialMT, has no tab;
- the substitute check counts a tab as WinAnsi-safe, so the tab went to the substitute Helvetica;
- `source_show` then tried to encode a lone `"\t"` in Helvetica, which has no code for it either, and refused the whole edit.

The paragraph rewritten **in one style** never hit this. `rewrite::paragraph_text` already writes every white-space character except a line break as a space, and its doc says so ("other white space is written as one space").

**Change.** The run-by-run path writes a tab, and any other control white space (vertical tab, form feed and the like, which no PDF font has a glyph for), as a space, as the one-style path does. It's one line in `CharacterPreparation::prepare`. Line breaks keep their own handling above it. The ideographic space and NBSP are untouched, since neither is a control character.

The tab's gap becomes one space wide on rewrite, the same as on the one-style path. Laying out real tab stops is a separate feature.

Not in this PR, also from #6145: Form artwork with a top-first `/BBox` is #6151. "Can't be moved until resized" and emptied fields disappearing are still open.

title: fix(fonts): a subset that gives the space no width can't encode one (#6131)
author: fatihkunak
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6131.

Adding a word to a line of a LaTeX document made every space of the line disappear (the reporter's screenshot: `lonne est la loi de X pour une couleur d'yeux fixée.` became `lonneestlaloideXpourunecouleurd'yeuxfixéedanslaliste.`).

`Metrics::has_glyph` took code 32 as present whatever `/Widths` said (`Some(w) => *w > 0.0 || code == 32`). pdfTeX subsets write `/FirstChar` below 32 and a width of 0 for every code they never use, the space among them, and set the gaps between words with `TJ`. So `encode` accepted a typed space, `source_show` wrote it as code 32 at width 0, and the words ran together. The path meant for a font with no space (`source_encodes`, `source_show`: each space becomes a positioning gap of the font's space width) was never reached.

Now a subset that gives the space no width has no space glyph: `encode` fails for it and the edit sets the space as a gap, as it already does when the widths stop short of 32. A full (non-subset) font keeps its space whatever its widths say.

## How you verified it

- New test `a_subset_that_gives_the_space_no_width_cannot_encode_one` (`crates/fonts/src/pdf/tests.rs`): a TrueType subset with `/FirstChar 32` and a width of 0 for the space. Before the change `encode("a b")` is `[97, 32, 98]`; now it is `None`. A subset that does give the space a width, and a non-subset font with width 0, still encode it. I reverted the fix to see it red.
- End to end, on a synthetic page built the way pdfTeX sets text (a simple TrueType subset with no space glyph, words apart by `TJ` gaps, a second font for a letter in the middle of the line): appending ` dans la liste` to the paragraph with `text_edit` drew `lonneestlaloide  Xpourunecouleurd'yeuxfixée.danslaliste` before and draws `lonne est la loi de  X pour une couleur d'yeux fixée. dans la liste` after (rendered with `pdfcraft-cli render`).

title: feat(ocr): recognize Chinese pages read sideways and turn them upright
author: fdenny11gg
body:
## What this changes

A page scanned on its side came out of recognition as a string of single characters:

```
理
王
金
联
兴
文庄
```

The detector groups words into lines by their baseline, and a page read sideways has no
baselines to group by, so every character became a line of its own.

Recognize text now straightens a scanned page before it reads it, as Acrobat does:

- **Auto-rotate pages** (`auto_rotate`, on by default). A page scanned sideways or upside down
  gets the `/Rotate` that shows it upright.
- **Deskew pages** (`deskew`, on by default). A slightly turned scan image is turned level about
  its centre.

Both changes are lossless: the image's pixels are never resampled, and undo restores the page.

## Which turn is upright

The pixel side is upstream PR #3662's, unchanged: a projection profile of the ink finds the skew
(±15°, coarse 0.5° steps then fine 0.05°) and tells whether the text lines run across or down the
page.

**The choice of turn differs, because the text is not always Latin.** PR #3662 picks it by how
much the reading looks like Latin words (letters in one case pattern, or numbers). Han glyphs
neither case-fold nor read as digits, so that check never fires for Chinese — and measured on a
Chinese page it picked the *wrong* turn:

| reading | share of characters in plausible words |
|---|---|
| upright (correct) | 0.275 |
| turned | **0.480** |

So the turn is chosen per language:

- **Latin** keeps the word check (upstream behaviour, unchanged).
- **Chinese** reads the page at all four quarter turns and keeps the turn whose text the PP-OCR
  model decodes with the highest per-character CTC confidence. Measured on a Chinese
  official-document page, the upright turn scores **0.983** per character and every wrong turn at
  most **0.912** — the winner is unique. The share of common Han characters is *not* a usable
  signal (its ranges overlap across turns) and is not used.

## How it works

title: M12: floating fields show the values scripts give them, and the sheet number and count (#6160)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #6160.

**What happens.** Text in an XFA form can embed a field's value: a floating field, `<span xfa:embed="#id"/>`. Designer's "Runtime Properties" (viewer name, locale, version, sheet number and count, date and time) are hidden fields placed in text this way. On `main`, the text shows only the template's default value of each embedded field. A value that a script gives the field never shows, whether it comes from an `initialize`, `click` or `calculate` script. On the form in #6160, six of the nine lines stay blank.

**How common.** These numbers come from the fixed XFA corpus of 500 forms, 245 of them dynamic: real public forms collected for this work. The dynamic count is in brackets.
- 273 (178) forms embed a field in text.
- At least 110 (86) give an embedded field a value from its own `initialize`, `docReady`, `click`, `change`, `exit` or `calculate` script. That is 40% of the forms with floating fields. Scripts on other objects that set those fields are not counted.
- 10 (6) embed a sheet number or sheet count.

**Spec.** XFA 3.3 pp. 221–222 says embedded references "are resolved during the layout process. The referenced data is inserted at the point where the external reference appears". p. 1222 defines the `xfa:embed`, `xfa:embedType` and `xfa:embedMode` attributes.

With this PR:
- **Embedded values come from the data.** Layout reads each embedded field's value from the data, which is where script values go, and falls back to the template's default as a field does. Areas and unnamed subforms add no data level, as they have no data of their own.
- **The text is laid out again after an event.** When an event gives an embedded field a new value, the form is laid out again once, when the event ends. This covers values from scripts and from calculations. The template keeps the set of embedded ids, so the check is one lookup.

title: M11: PDF/A verify asks only the fonts something draws with to be embedded (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`, Standards ▸ Verify PDF/A compliance) reported compliant forms as broken on clause 6.2.11.4: "The font Helvetica isn't embedded", "The font ZapfDingbats isn't embedded".

author: fatihkunak
body:
**Draft: for discussion, off by default.**

## What this changes

Refs #5738, #6113, #6114.

Several Windows users report that the text and crosshair cursors can't be seen over a white page: the I-beam is drawn white (reported against AMD Radeon drivers, #5738), the drawing tools' cross is white (#6113), or no cursor shows at all (#6114). The system draws these cursors, so the app can't change their colour, and the reports don't say whether it is a driver fault or the cursor theme.

This adds an opt-in way to tell: with `PDFCRAFT_SOFT_CURSOR=1` in the environment, `PageCursor::resolve` (the one place the pages' cursor is set) hides the system cursor when the winning claim is a text or a crosshair cursor over the page, and the app draws its own at the pointer: a black line with a white halo (an I-beam with serifs, or a plus), on the top layer. Every other cursor (hand, resize, grab...) stays the system's, and so does any frame with no pointer position. With the variable unset nothing changes.

It is a draft because the real decision is the product's, not mine: whether this should be a setting (it needs a preference, a menu entry and catalogue strings), a default on Windows, or nothing if the reports turn out to be one driver's.

title: M6: forms copies field text within shared allowances, however often the file names it
author: Piohrun
body:
Part of #5755. Follows #6132, whose value and script budgets it extends from what forms decodes to what it copies.

## What this changes

#6132 bounds what a reading of the form decodes. This bounds what it copies. A field's value, script or name stored as a string, rather than a stream, was copied once for each field that named it or inherited it, with no total. The file stores the string once, and object streams compress it, so a small file could make opening it exhaust memory: a review of #6132 measured a reading of the form killed at its memory cap by a file under 2 KB (a list box whose value lists one 1 MiB string 16,384 times).

Every copy of text a reading of the form makes now goes through one of three allowances, each copy charged with the bytes of the `String` that holds it (so empty strings named a million times are paid for too), and each array entry read charged the same, text or not:

- **Values** (`/V`, `/DV`), 64 MiB: strings, names and array entries, with the text streams #6132 already charged here, which now also pay for what their text grows by once decoded (a PDFDocEncoding byte past 0x7F takes three in UTF-8). Past it a value reads as none, as a stream past it does, and so does a list of values one of which doesn't fit: a list read in part would be taken for the whole of it.
- **Scripts**, 64 MiB (`/JS` strings, with the streams #6132 charged, their growth as values' is), and the names of document scripts. Past it a script reads as none. Renaming a field reads each calculation it may rewrite within this allowance too, so it rewrites at most 64 MiB of them. A Calculate action several fields share by reference is still read and rewritten once, in place, as #6132 does it, and so now is an `/AA` they share that holds it, instead of a copy of it going into each field.
- **The rest of the fields' text**, 256 MiB, which had no bound: full names, `/DA`, options, tooltips, push-button captions, check-box on states, widget states (`/AS`), a list box's wid…

title: M7: an edit that changes nothing leaves the paragraph as it is (#6157)
author: Ansansan
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6157.

Applying a paragraph's own text with no formatting rewrote it anyway. On the single-style path the run was redrawn as one `Tj`, which dropped the source's `TJ` kerning. Every glyph after the first adjustment moved: 76.8 pt in the issue's one-line repro, `[(A)-400(V)-400(A)-400(V)-400(A)]TJ` at 48 pt. The rewrite also left an empty `BT … ET` behind. In the reporter's sweep, 52 of 102 everyday files changed this way.

Now an edit that changes nothing writes nothing:

- **edit:** one check, `unchanged` (the paragraph's own editor text and the default style), now serves both `TextSession::layout`, which already skipped such a draft, and `TextSession::commit`, which now writes nothing for it. `TextSession::changes_nothing` exposes the check. `rewrite_block` returns early on it, so an unchanged edit doesn't tidy away unused fallback fonts either. Every non-test rewrite goes through `rewrite_block` or the session (the engine's `EditTextBlock` and `replace_block`), so both entry points are covered.
- **engine:** an `EditTextBlock` that wrote nothing leaves the undo history and the dirty flag alone, as an empty Fill & Sign flatten already does. So `text_edit` with a paragraph's own text no longer adds an undo step or marks the file modified.
- `rewrite_block_with_limit` is now test-only (it lowers the glyph limit for tests). The production path is `rewrite_block` → the session.

What is **not** fixed: a single-style paragraph whose text does change is still rewritten without the source's kerning and line positions. That is the larger half of the issue (the report's "keep the adjustments between characters that still exist"). The parity notes for `edit.text-edit` say so.

title: M2: a TrueType subset whose hmtx keeps the full font's length still draws
author: andrisrekke
body:
## What this changes

Text set in an embedded TrueType subset whose `hmtx` entry in the table directory still records the length the table had in the *full* font (past the end of the subset) is drawn again. Before, the page rendered without that text, while text extraction and search still found it.

Cause: `read-fonts` can't read a table whose recorded range runs past the end of the font, so `hmtx()` fails, and `skrifa` builds no `glyf` outline without `hmtx` (it needs the advances for the phantom points), so every glyph of the font came out empty. CFF outlines don't need `hmtx` and weren't affected.

Fix, in vendored `hayro-interpret` as patch (76) (`OpenTypeFontBlob::new`): when `hmtx` can't be read but `glyf` can, the length `hmtx` needs comes from the OpenType definition: 4 × `hhea.numberOfHMetrics` + 2 × (`maxp.numGlyphs` − `numberOfHMetrics`). If the recorded length is longer and that range lies after the table directory and belongs to no other table, the font is drawn from a copy with only that length field corrected, and a `warn!` records the repair. The document itself is not changed. A font whose `hmtx` reads, one without `glyf`, invalid or non-fitting counts and fonts over 64 MiB are left exactly as they were.

I found this on a real-world PDF I can't share (it holds private data); the tests reproduce it with synthetic fonts built in memory. `vendor/README.md` records patch (76) and its tests in the hayro-interpret row.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-render --check`: clean. The vendored file, checked with its own style (`max_width=100`), only differs in code this PR doesn't touch.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `hayro-interpret` standalone (`--manifest-path vendor/hayro-interpret/Cargo.toml --all-targets --features logging`, its hayro patches pointed at the vendored crates): clean with `-D warnings` once `doc_markdown`, `unseparated_literal_suffix` and `manual_is_multiple_of` are a…

title: perf(cos): write_full_to streams a full save to any Write sink
author: DesignsByRay
body:
## What this changes

Adds `pdfcraft_cos::write_full_to(doc, opts, sink: impl Write) -> Result<u64, CosError>`. It does the same full save as `write_full`, but writes each object to the sink as soon as it is serialized (staged in ~64 KB chunks) instead of building the whole file in one `Vec`. Object offsets come from a running position, not from `out.len()`. `write_full` is now a thin wrapper that passes a `Vec` as the sink, so its callers and its output are unchanged.

**Why.** `write_full`'s output `Vec` grows by doubling. At the last doubling the old buffer and the new, twice-as-large one are both alive, so a full save peaks at the document **plus 1.5× to 3× the output**, depending on where the size falls relative to a power of two. For large merges (thousands of pages, hundreds of MB) that is the dominant memory cost. With a file or other `Write` as the sink, it disappears.

**Platforms.** The numbers below were measured on Windows, where growing a large buffer copies it. On Linux, glibc can often grow a large buffer in place via `mremap`, so the doubling transient there is smaller. What streaming removes everywhere is holding the whole output (at least 1× its size) in memory.

**Measured** (Windows x64, release, counting global allocator; a document of 20 merged 100-page PDFs with a distinct ~86 KB content stream per page, 172 MB output, object streams on):

| full save of the 172 MB document | peak heap | × output | added by the save |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `write_full` (into a `Vec`) | 439.5 MB | 2.55× | 265 MB |
| `write_full_to` → `BufWriter<File>` | 175.6 MB | **1.02×** | **1.1 MB** |

The 2.55× happened to land just under a power of two (capacity 176 MB for 172 MB). At 177 MB the last doubling would have been 176 → 352 MB, about 4× in total.

Also adds `CosError::Io(String)` for a failing sink. `CosError` derives `Clone` and `PartialEq`, so it holds the error text, not the `io::Error`.

title: M1: correct the COS object reference API example
author: MMexicann
body:

title: Windows: shortcuts take pdfcraft.exe's icon, so a taskbar pin keeps it
author: art804
body:
## What this changes

After every update, a PdfCraft pin on the Windows taskbar shows a blank icon. It still starts PdfCraft.

The cause is in `packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs`. The Start menu and desktop shortcuts set `Icon="PdfcraftIcon.ico"`. Windows Installer keeps that icon under `C:\Windows\Installer\{ProductCode}\`, and each release has a new ProductCode, so `MajorUpgrade` removes the old release's copy. The installer recreates the Start menu and desktop shortcuts with the new path. A taskbar pin, though, is a copy of the shortcut taken when it was pinned. It keeps the old path, for example:

```
TargetPath   : C:\Program Files\PdfCraft\pdfcraft.exe
IconLocation : C:\WINDOWS\Installer\{BCA75223-EBF4-4D7E-BCCE-BCD832AE4EEC}\PdfcraftIcon.ico,0
Test-Path    : False
```

This PR drops `Icon`/`IconIndex` from both shortcuts. With no icon set, the shell uses the icon `build.rs` embeds in `pdfcraft.exe`. That exe's path is the same in every release, so a pin keeps its icon. Release packaging already fails if the icon can't be embedded (`PDFCRAFT_REQUIRE_WINRES=1` in `package.ps1`), and the installer already points `Capabilities\ApplicationIcon` at `[#PdfcraftExe],0`. The `<Icon>` element stays, because `ARPPRODUCTICON` (Add/Remove Programs) still uses it.

When #57/#58 added the shortcut icon, the exe had no icon of its own. Now it has one, so the Icon table entry on the shortcuts is no longer needed.

A pin made from an earlier release's shortcut still names the removed path, so users need to pin PdfCraft again once after this ships. Related, but a different symptom: #2185 (Start menu pins disappear after an update).

## How you verified it

- [x] `packaging/windows/test-msi.ps1` now checks that both shortcuts have no Icon table entry (it previously expected `PdfcraftIcon.ico`, so it fails against an MSI built before this change). CI's Windows package job runs it.
- [x] Windows 11 ARM64: installed this PR's CI MSI (`pdfcraft-windows-arm64`) over a release install, p…

title: Test: the Fill & Sign multi-line test saves with a fixed clock
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

`fill_sign_enter_adds_lines_outside_click_commits_and_escape_cancels` saves the document, presses Escape over a new box and compares a second save with the first byte for byte ("Escape cancels without writing"). Each save stamps the current time as `/ModDate`. When the two saves fall in different seconds on a busy runner, the bytes differ and the test fails, though nothing was written.

It failed that way in CI on #5917 (run 41890292236). With the object stream inflated, the two saves differed only in `/ModDate (D:20261104185936Z)` against `…37Z`.

The test now gives the session a fixed clock before the two saves, as `viewer.rs` does for its own (`Session::with_clock`). Only the test changes.

**Tests.** The failure doesn't show on a fast machine, so I made it deterministic. With a clock that moves on a second each time it is read (`static T: AtomicI64`, `with_clock(|| T.fetch_add(1, SeqCst))`), the test fails with the CI message, on main and in this branch when that clock takes the fixed one's place. With the fixed clock it passes.

Test only, no product code.

author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes Copying selected page text now also puts **HTML** on the system clipboard, so pasting into a word processor or mail client keeps paragraphs, **bold**, *italic*, size, colour and font family. The plain text is exactly what Copy gave before, and goes on the clipboard as the alternative in the same set. - **export** (`clip.rs`): the clipboard model, built on the existing `esc` and `hex`. - `ClipText` is paragraphs of styled spans. `ClipBuilder` merges runs of the same style and stops at caps of 20 000 spans, 2 MiB of text and 16 MiB of HTML, marking the copy `truncated`. - `font_family` turns a BaseFont into the name a word processor knows: the subset tag and style suffixes come off, and camel case is spaced. - `clip_html` writes one `

Bold is `` and italic is ``, so a target that drops style attributes still keeps them. - A family name keeps only letters, digits, space, `-`, `_` and `.`, so a hostile font name can't leave the CSS string. - Text is escaped in one pass. C0 and C1 controls, a bare carriage return and the bidirectional overrides and isolates (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) are dropped, so they can't reorder or hide pasted text. - A font size is written within 1 to 1000 pt; a size that is zero, negative or not finite is left out. - **engine** (`rich_copy.rs`): `Document::rich_copy(page, text, glyphs)`. - The selected glyphs come from the text layer (view space). title: Fix/poor image rendering
author: jeielmosi
body:
<!--
Thanks for contributing to PdfCraft.

Base this on `main` — it is the only integration branch. `main` moves fast (it took
396 commits in the three days to 2026-10-12), so a PR that sits for a day usually needs
a rebase. Rebasing the same day you are asked keeps the work from dying of conflicts.
Delete any section below that does not apply.
-->

## What this changes

Scanned pages now keep their text at screen size and lose the staircases when zoomed. Images that do not ask for `/Interpolate` (most scans) used to be pre-shrunk nearest-neighbour — roughly one sample in N per axis — and then sampled again at a fractional offset. Now, outside Type 3 glyphs, a non-interpolated image drawn below its resolution is area-averaged to whole device pixels and drawn 1:1: each device pixel is the coverage-weighted mean of the samples it covers, so thin strokes survive and nothing is invented between samples. On a 13-page 300 dpi scan, every rendered sample at 96, 120 and 192 dpi is within 1 of the exact area average; before, 17–23% of samples were off by more than 1, by as much as 255. A non-interpolated image of page-scan size (shorter side at least 512 samples) is drawn bilinearly when enlarged by more than 1%, so a zoomed scan has no blocky edges; smaller images — icons, QR codes and pixel art — keep hard pixels. `/Interpolate true` is unchanged.

The new **Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ Smooth images** checkbox (on by default, matching Acrobat) makes that smoothing a choice. With it off, images without `/Interpolate` return to nearest-neighbour sampling at any size, keeping QR codes, barcodes and pixel art sharp. The setting applies to documents already open and to ones opened later, persists across restarts, and is reachable headlessly through `view_smooth_images` and the UI control channel (`ui.set`/`ui.state`). Changing it — including restoring saved settings — invalidates cached rasters and views.

title: Pass the Linux signing key to the release workflow
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
The reusable release workflow signs every Linux asset — `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.pkg.tar.zst`, AppImage, Flatpak, the OCI image and `SHA256SUMS.txt` — but only when it receives `LINUX_SIGNING_KEY`. This repo's `release` environment has the secret; the caller never listed it in its `secrets:` block, so the workflow published unsigned assets.

materialcraft, the only repo that already passes the key, ships `.asc`/`.sig` alongside every asset plus a signed `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and its deb, rpm, pkg.tar.zst and flatpak all verify against `ArtCraft Linux Release Signing Key`. This repo's latest release carries no signatures at all.

With this line the next release publishes them. Existing releases stay unsigned unless the workflow is re-run.

title: M11: PDF/A verify reports integers, reals, strings, names, CIDs and page boundaries past the implementation limits (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks PDF/A-2 clause 6.1.13. The clause keeps a file within the implementation limits of ISO 32000-1:2008 Annex C: Table C.1, and the page-size limits that follow it. Until now, files past those limits were reported compliant.

It now reports, under 6.1.13:
- **Integers:** an integer outside −2³¹ … 2³¹−1.
- **Reals:** a real number beyond ±3.403 × 10³⁸, or a nonzero one nearer zero than ±1.175 × 10⁻³⁸ (ISO 32000-1 Table C.1 lets a reader round those to zero; PDF/A-2 does not allow them, PDF Association TechNote 0010 A018). An integer token too long even for a real is read as one, so it is reported here too.
- **Strings:** a string longer than 32767 bytes.
- **Names:** a name longer than 127 bytes. The length is counted after decoding, so a name written with `#xx` escapes counts the bytes it stands for.
- **CIDs:** a CID above 65535 that an embedded CMap of a Type 0 font maps to. Three cases count (ISO 32000-1 9.7.5.4):
  - a `begincidrange` entry `<low> <high> cid` that reaches past it, at `cid + high − low`;
  - a `begincidchar` entry that names one;
  - either of these in a CMap the font uses through `/UseCMap`.

  A CMap given by name rather than embedded is a predefined one, so it is within the limit.
- **Page boundaries:** a page whose `MediaBox`, `CropBox`, `BleedBox`, `TrimBox` or `ArtBox` is narrower or lower than 3 units, or wider or higher than 14400. The boxes are read after inheritance, so a page that overrides its parent's box is judged by its own.

**What is read:**
- **Objects:** the trailer and every indirect object.
- **Page contents:** each page's `/Contents` streams, joined as one stream, since an operator's operands may end one stream while the operator starts the next (ISO 32000-1 7.8.2).
- **Other content:** every other content stream (form XObjects, appearance streams, Type 3 glyph procedures).
- **Bounds:** values are followed as deep as the parser nests them. Content is decoded with…

title: M11: PDF/A verify reports Separation spaces of one name that differ and DeviceN spot colours missing from /Colorants (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks the two consistency rules of PDF/A-2 clause 6.2.4.4 (*Separation and DeviceN colour spaces*). Before, files that broke them were reported compliant.

- **Same name, same definition.** Separation spaces that share a colorant name must use the same alternate space and the same tint transform. This includes Separation spaces held in a DeviceN space's `/Colorants` dictionary. Definitions are compared as objects, whether they are stored directly or by reference, at any depth (ISO 32000-1 7.3.10). Streams compare by their decoded data, whatever filter stores them, so the same tint transform under another object number or encoding counts as the same. Reference pairs found equal are remembered, so a structure many definitions share is compared once. `All` and `None` are compared like any other name.
- **Spot colorants are defined.** A DeviceN space must list each spot colorant it uses in the `/Colorants` dictionary of its attributes (ISO 32000-1 8.6.6.5, Table 71). The entry must be a Separation space for that colorant; a null entry, one that refers to no object, or a Separation of another name defines nothing.
  - The process colorants (`Cyan`, `Magenta`, `Yellow`, `Black`) and `None` are not spot colorants.
  - In an NChannel space, neither are the components its `/Process` lists.
  - Colorant names given by reference are resolved.

Colour spaces are found wherever they are written: resource dictionaries, images, shadings and other colour spaces, direct or by reference, as deep as the parser nests them. Each problem is reported once per colorant name.

The check is in a new `crates/preflight/src/spot.rs`.

**How often:** measured on the veraPDF corpus (CC BY 4.0), folder `PDF_A-2b`, against main at d22641a8. Its 986 files say in their names whether they should pass or fail.

| | before | after |

title: fix(redact): clear CMYK JPEG and JPEG 2000 scans in place (#283, builds on #2287)
author: daBOB
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #283. Redacting part of a scanned page removed the whole page image, leaving only the black boxes, whenever the scan was a JPEG or a JPEG 2000 image.

This builds on #2287 by @midasmatterhorn, which clears grey and RGB JPEGs in place. Its change is the first commit here, squashed onto current `main` with its author kept (its own branch is untouched). The commits after it add the rest:

- **CMYK JPEGs** (DeviceCMYK, YCCK included) are cleared in place. Samples stay as stored and the copy keeps the original `/Decode`, so an Adobe-inverted CMYK JPEG draws as it did.
- **JPEG 2000** (`JPXDecode`) in DeviceGray, DeviceRGB or DeviceCMYK is cleared in place. The Flate copy names its bit depth (8) and colour space (from the file when the dictionary gives none), and drops `/Decode` and `/SMaskInData`: JPEG 2000 ignores `/Decode` (ISO 32000-2 §8.9.5.1), but the Flate copy would apply it.
- **Shared decoders in `pdfcraft-filters`**: `decode_dct` and `decode_jpx`. They use the decoders the renderer already uses (`zune-jpeg`, `hayro-jpeg2000`; no new crates in the lockfile), run under `catch_unwind`, and refuse a header of another size than the dictionary before allocating. They replace #2287's `image`-crate decoder and its hand-written JPEG marker parser. `redact` no longer depends on `image` outside its tests.
- **Budget**: JPEG and JPEG 2000 decodes now pay from the run's `ImageBudget` first (`pay_jpeg`); #2287's JPEG path did not. A JPEG past the allowance now stops the run like a Flate image does. `a_flate_image_past_the_runs_allowance_stops_the_run` used to assert that a JPEG "spends nothing" and is updated.

Still removed whole (fail-closed), listed in the README and parity notes: JPEG/JPEG 2000 in ICCBased or Indexed spaces, JPEG 2000 with alpha, a JPEG with its own `/ColorTransform` (a `shortcut:` comment marks it), image masks, and data that doesn't decode to the dictionary's size.

title: M11: PDF/A verify checks the file header and Save as PDF/A rewrites it (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks the file header, PDF/A-2 clause 6.1.2 (*File header*). **Save as PDF/A** (`pdfa_convert`) fixes it. Before, a file with a PDF 2.0 header, or with no binary comment, was reported compliant.

- **The header line.** The file starts at its first byte with `%PDF-1.0` to `%PDF-1.7`, followed directly by an end-of-line marker (CR, LF or CR LF; ISO 32000-1 7.5.2 and 7.2.3). Data before the header, another version (`2.0`, `1.9`, `1.70`) and trailing spaces all break it.
- **The binary comment.** The next line is a comment: `%` and at least four bytes, each above 127 (ISO 32000-1 7.5.2). A blank line in between, a shorter comment, or a low byte among the four breaks it.
- **Edited documents.** A document whose next save rewrites it in full (after Save as PDF/A, a redaction or an encryption change) is judged by the header that save writes. The writer always adds a compliant binary comment, so only the version is checked.
- **Save as PDF/A.** When the header breaks the rule, conversion makes the next save a full rewrite. If the kept version isn't 1.0 to 1.7, it sets the version to 1.7. It reports "Rewrote the file header".

The check is in a new `crates/preflight/src/header.rs`.

**How often:** measured on the veraPDF corpus (CC BY 4.0), folder `PDF_A-2b`, against main at d22641a8. Its 986 files say in their names whether they should pass or fail.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| right verdict, for the right clause (all 986) | 464 | 473 |
| files testing the file header (10) | 1 | 10 |
| compliant files reported as failing | 13 | 13 |

Only the 9 failing header files changed verdict; no other file changed.

title: M11: PDF/A verify reports transfer functions, halftones and rendering intents a graphics state may not use (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks the graphics state settings that PDF/A-2 clause 6.2.5 (*Extended graphics state*) rules out. Before, files that used them were reported compliant. Every graphics state is checked for these settings:

- **Transfer functions.** No `/TR` entry, and `/TR2` only as `/Default` (ISO 32000-1 10.4, Table 58).
- **Halftone phase.** No `/HTP` entry: a PDF 1.2 key that ISO 32000-1 no longer defines.
- **Halftones.** `/HalftoneType` must be an integer (ISO 32000-1 Table 128), 1 or 5; no `/HalftoneName` (ISO 32000-1 10.5.5). This applies to halftone dictionaries and streams, and to the halftones a type 5 halftone holds for its colorants.
- **Halftone transfer functions.** A type 5 halftone's component for a non-primary colorant has a `/TransferFunction`, and no other halftone does (ISO 32000-1 10.5.5.6, Table 130). The primary colour components are those of the standard device spaces: Gray; Red, Green and Blue; Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Black (ISO 32000-1 10.5.5.6; ISO 32000-2 10.6.5.6). The `Default` component may have one or not.
- **Rendering intent.** `/RI` must be a name, one of the four intents of ISO 32000-1 8.6.5.8, Table 70.

A null entry counts as absent (ISO 32000-1 7.3.9).

Graphics states are found in the `/ExtGState` entry of each resource dictionary, direct or by reference. Resource dictionaries are those under `/Resources` (pages, forms, Type 3 fonts, patterns, annotation appearances) and the interactive form's `/DR`. A shading pattern's own `/ExtGState` (ISO 32000-1 8.7.4.3, Table 76) is read as the single graphics state it is. They are looked for in what the document reaches from its trailer, following references through a queue rather than by recursion. Private application data (`/PieceInfo`) isn't entered, so an object only that data refers to isn't read. A map shared by reference is read once, and each object once, whatever the generation its references give. Each kind of problem is reported on…

title: Signing a form that sets NeedAppearances no longer makes Acrobat ignore the signature
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #5939

Signing a form with `/NeedAppearances true` could make Acrobat ignore the signature. The first signature now removes that flag from inline or indirect AcroForm dictionaries. Before signing, the engine draws text and choice field appearances from their current values so viewers can display the signed result without generating appearances themselves.

The shared `pdfcraft_sign::has_signatures` check recognizes existing signatures and document timestamps, including unnamed ones, while excluding empty placeholders. Later signatures preserve the flag and existing appearances.

Appearance trade-off: when the field font cannot represent a character, an existing appearance that draws text is retained, including text drawn through nested Form XObjects. That preserves supported existing glyphs but may retain stale content. A background-only appearance is regenerated and can show `?` for unsupported characters. This is not a general font fallback implementation.

Validation: regression tests cover inline and indirect forms, earlier signatures and timestamps, empty signature placeholders, filled values, stale appearances, unsupported characters, and nested appearance text. The latest hosted CI gate passed. The author's earlier full local run reported one UI glyph failure; this review does not independently establish its cause. No new local build was run during the maintainer review.

This fixes the existing signing path; it adds no new command or tool and does not claim a new parity capability.

title: M2: a non-embedded Arial draws the glyphs its codes name (#5889)
author: sventurbo
body:
Fixes #5889.

## What this changes

In the datasheet from #5889, page 1 says "4Gb(128M x 32) **Low Power** DDR2 SDRAM" and "**AS4C128M32MD2A**". PdfCraft drew them as "@ck 'Dck Yf" and "AS4C128A 32MD25".

Those runs use `C2_6`, an `Arial-BoldMT` the PDF doesn't embed: Type 0, `CIDFontType2`, `Identity-H`, CIDToGIDMap Identity (by default), `Adobe-Identity-0`, and no `/ToUnicode`. So each code is a glyph index in the author's Arial Bold. hayro draws such a font with the standard CFF substitute (Foxit Sans Bold). With no Unicode route, `Type0Font::map_code` fell through to taking each code as one of the *substitute's* glyph indexes, so every letter shifted by a constant.

Arial numbers its first 172 glyphs in the standard Macintosh order of the TrueType `post` table (Apple's TrueType Reference Manual): `L` is 47, `o` 82, `w` 90, the space 3. Its next 86 follow that order without two of its glyphs, `nonbreakingspace` (172; Arial's no-break space is glyph 3) and `apple` (210). It also has `Euro` where the order has `currency`, and U+00AF and U+00B7 at 256 and 257. This PR adds vendored hayro-interpret patch (76) for that case. The case is a `CIDFontType2` font that isn't embedded, whose CIDs aren't of an Adobe character collection, and whose descendant `/BaseFont` is one of Arial's four faces. For such a font, a CID with no Unicode route goes through its `/CIDToGIDMap` to an Arial glyph index. That glyph's name in Arial (`arial_glyph_name`) is the glyph the CFF substitute draws, or .notdef when the substitute has no glyph of that name. `.null` and `nonmarkingreturn` draw the space.

The names come from `read-fonts`' `tables::post::DEFAULT_GLYPH_NAMES`, already in the tree through skrifa. `arial_glyph_name` reads Arial's index into it: the same index up to 171, one on for 172–187 and 189–208, two on for 209–255, and `Euro`, `macron` and `periodcentered` for 188, 256 and 257. There is no new dependency and no 258-entry table of our own.

title: M9: sort the digital ID picker, refresh it and jump by letter
author: Nero1Dev
body:
## What this changes

Four small changes to **Sign with a Digital ID**, for people with many certificates in the OS key store (an accountant signing for many companies, say):

- **Alphabetical order.** The picker lists IDs by name, ignoring case and accents (reuses `i18n::name_sort_key`). Before, they came in store order. Only the picker sorts: `digital_ids` keeps its order, so `SignDraft::selected` and the saved settings don't change. The default selection is now the first usable ID from the top.
- **Refresh.** A new button lists the OS key store again, so a certificate installed while the dialog is open shows up without closing it. The selection stays on the same ID. It only shows when an OS key store is in use (macOS, Windows), since Linux has nothing to list again. It also shows on the Configure step when the list is empty, and moves to the picker once there is an ID. A failed listing keeps the entries already listed.
- **Jump by letter.** Pressing a letter selects the next usable ID that starts with it and scrolls to it; pressing it again walks through the matches and wraps. Greyed IDs are skipped. This step has no text field, so nothing else listens to those keys.
- **Expired IDs.** The picker used to list expired certificates and sign with them. Expired OS key store IDs are no longer listed; an ID lasts to the second it expires. Entries now keep that moment in `expires_at`; settings saved before this have only the date, so those IDs last through that day. An expired ID file stays, greyed, because the picker is where it can be removed. Signing also refuses a certificate past its end, checked before Save As and again right before signing, which stops one that expired with the dialog or the save panel open. Importing an expired ID file is refused too, and nothing is added to the list. If every OS ID was dropped and nothing usable is left, a notice says why the list is empty.

`Refresh` is already translated in craft-i18n (`common.tsv`), so no catalog row is need…

title: M5: image signatures read upright at their size in macOS Preview and Quick Look (#5428)
author: sventurbo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5428.

**Which reports this covers.** The report doesn't say whether the pages were turned or the signature resized, and the file isn't available (the ticket came through the relay). On macOS 27 with the 0.18.1 release CLI, a signature on an unturned page that isn't resized already looks right in Quick Look and PDFKit, on one page or many (incremental save, duplicated pages, moved signatures). Only these two conditions produce the screenshot's small scribble on the line, and this PR fixes both. If the reporter's file turns out to have neither, the issue should be reopened.

macOS Preview and Quick Look don't fit a stamp's appearance into `/Rect` the way ISO 32000-2 §12.5.5 says. They draw it at the size of its turned `/BBox`. PdfCraft relied on that fit in two places, and both made a Fill & Sign signature look shrunk there:

1. **Turned pages.** On a page with `/Rotate`, a picture stamp (an image signature, an image stamp or a PDF-page stamp) had `/BBox` = `/Rect` (user space) and a rotation-only `/Matrix`. The turned box came out with its sides swapped, so it needed scaling back by different amounts across and down, e.g. ×0.27 and ×3.75 for a 120 × 32 signature. Quick Look drew it tiny and squashed.
   - Now the picture is drawn upright in `/Rect` turned back (`R⁻¹(/Rect)`), and the same rotation-only `/Matrix` turns it onto `/Rect` exactly, so there is nothing left to scale.
   - The matrix still has no offset, so it stays right after a move. `draw.rs`, which keeps a picture stamp's matrix on a restyle, needs no change.
2. **Resized stamps, any page.** A resize kept the old appearance, and Quick Look then drew it at its old size in the middle of the new box. People usually enlarge a signature to fit the signature line, so this is probably what the reporter saw.
   - Now a picture stamp or a typed signature, which PdfCraft draws from its own dictionary, is drawn again into the new rectangle. That is the same picture a fitting viewer sho…

title: M11: PDF/A verify checks the file identifier and Save as PDF/A adds one (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks the file identifier, PDF/A-2 clause 6.1.3 (*File trailer*). **Save as PDF/A** (`pdfa_convert`) adds one where it is missing or malformed. Before, a file without one was reported compliant.

- **Which trailer.** The check reads the trailer that the file's last `startxref` points to: the latest update's, or a linearized file's first-page trailer (ISO 32000-1 7.5.6 and F.3.4). An earlier trailer in the `/Prev` chain doesn't stand in for it, so an update that leaves out `/ID` is reported.
- **What it must hold.** An `/ID` that is an array of two non-empty byte strings (ISO 32000-1 14.4, Table 15). A missing or null `/ID` gets one message; any other shape gets another.
- **Save as PDF/A.** It gives such a document a new identifier of 16-byte strings, and an ordinary save keeps it. If the old first string is non-empty and within 32767 bytes (ISO 32000-1 Annex C), conversion keeps it, since it is the file's permanent identifier (ISO 32000-1 14.4), and makes only the second afresh. It then reports "Completed the file identifier"; when both strings are new it reports "Added a file identifier". A good identifier is left exactly as it is.

The identifier comes from the generator the writer already used for saves without one. That generator is now public in `pdfcraft-cos` as `new_file_id`, and the writer calls it too, so there is one generator. The check is in a new `crates/preflight/src/trailer.rs`.

**How often:** measured on the veraPDF corpus (CC BY 4.0), folder `PDF_A-2b`, against main at d22641a8. Its 986 files say in their names whether they should pass or fail.

title: M11: PDF/A verify reports SetState, NOP and Named actions other than the four page moves (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now reports three more kinds of action under PDF/A-2 clause 6.5.1 (*Actions*). **Save as PDF/A** (`pdfa_convert`) removes them, as it removes the other forbidden actions. Before, files that used them were reported compliant.

- **SetState and NOP.** These PDF 1.2 actions are no longer defined by ISO 32000-1. They join the forbidden action types.
- **Named actions.** A Named action may only name `NextPage`, `PrevPage`, `FirstPage` or `LastPage`, the four of ISO 32000-1 12.6.4.11, Table 212. The name may be given directly or by reference. Any other name, or none, is reported as "A Named Print action isn't allowed" and the like.

These are found wherever actions already are: `/A` and `/OpenAction` entries, actions standing alone, and the actions chained after them in `/Next`. Outline items are included.

The check for an action's own type is now one helper, `action_forbidden`, called from the chain walk. It reads the action type `/S` and a Named action's `/N` through references.

**How often:** measured on the veraPDF corpus (CC BY 4.0), folder `PDF_A-2b`, against main at d22641a8. Its 986 files say in their names whether they should pass or fail.

title: M11: PDF/A verify reports pages with transparency but no blending colour space, and blend modes ISO 32000-1 doesn't define (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks transparency, PDF/A-2 clause 6.2.10 (*Transparency*). Before, a page painting with transparency in a file without a PDF/A output intent, or a graphics state with a made-up blend mode, was reported compliant.

- **Blending colour space.** In a file without a PDF/A output intent, a page that contains transparency must name its blending colour space: its `/Group` dictionary has a `/CS` entry (ISO 32000-1 11.6.6, Table 147). Such a page is reported as "Page {} has transparency but no device-independent blending colour space or PDF/A output intent".
  - `/CS` must be a blending colour space (ISO 32000-1 and 32000-2 11.3.4): `CalGray`, `CalRGB`, or `ICCBased` with 1, 3 or 4 components whose profile header, when readable, says gray, RGB or CMYK to match `/N`. Lab, Indexed, Pattern, Separation and DeviceN are not, and a null `/CS` or one naming no object counts as none.
  - Like any colour space in a file without an output intent (6.2.4.3), `/CS` may be `DeviceGray`, `DeviceRGB` or `DeviceCMYK` only when the page's resources give that space a default (`DefaultGray`, `DefaultRGB`, `DefaultCMYK`) that is itself a blending colour space with as many components (ISO 32000-1 8.6.5.6); a null default is none.
  - An output intent stands in for the blending colour space only when its `/DestOutputProfile` is a stream.
- **What counts as transparency** (ISO 32000-1 11.6.4.4 to 11.6.6), reached from the page's resources:
  - a graphics state with `/CA` or `/ca` below 1, a blend mode other than `Normal` or `Compatible`, or a soft mask dictionary (`/None` or null is none);
  - an image with an `/SMask` stream, or `/SMaskInData` above 0;
  - a transparency group XObject (`/Group` with `/S /Transparency`).
- **Where it looks.** The page's resources, and through them the resources of form XObjects (nested), tiling patterns, shading patterns' graphics states and Type 3 fonts, plus the appearance streams of the page's annotati…

title: M11: PDF/A verify checks that predefined XMP properties have their value types (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks PDF/A-2 clause 6.6.2.3.1. A property of a predefined XMP schema must have the value type the XMP Specification gives it. Before, any value passed: `crs:Contrast` written as `25.0`, `xmpMM:DerivedFrom` written as plain text instead of a ResourceRef structure, `crs:RawFileName` written as an `rdf:Seq`.

**Namespaces covered.**
- From ISO 16684-1:2011 (XMP Part 1) clause 8, Tables 4–7: Dublin Core, XMP Basic, XMP Rights Management and XMP Media Management.
- From XMP Specification Part 2, Tables 24–34: Media Management (with its deprecated properties), Basic Job Ticket, Paged-Text, Dynamic Media, Adobe PDF, Photoshop and Camera Raw.

**Structures covered,** from Part 2 Tables 3–23, 31 and 32: Colorant, Dimensions, Font, Thumbnail, ResourceEvent, ResourceRef, Version, Job, the Dynamic Media structures (Time, Timecode, Marker, Media, Track, ProjectLink, CuePointParam and the three stretch structures), Ancestor and Layer.

**How a value is checked.**
- **Simple types** by their lexical form (ISO 16684-1 8.2.1):
  - Boolean is `True` or `False`.
  - Integer is an optionally signed run of digits.
  - Real is a decimal with an integer part, a fraction part or both.
  - Date is one of the six forms of 8.2.1.2, with its ranges, and a time zone of `Z`, `+hh:mm` or `-hh:mm`.
  - Rational is two integers around `/`, as Part 2 Table 20 writes it ("For NTSC, use 1001/30000").
  - The text-based types (AgentName, Choice of Text, Locale, MIMEType, ProperName, RenditionClass, URI, URL and the like) accept any simple value. Only they accept an `rdf:resource`, which makes the value a URI, on an empty element.

title: fix: cap print dialog height to the screen so it can't overflow top/b…
author: desingtorres-eng
body:
## What this changes

The Print dialog modal had no height constraint. On a short viewport — a small-screen laptop, or any screen once the driver's "Properties…" panel is expanded inline (it shows the printer driver's own PPD options directly in the dialog on non-Windows platforms) — the settings+preview area could grow taller than the available screen, and since the modal centers itself, it overflowed equally off the top and bottom, making Print/Cancel unreachable.

It reproduces with any printer, not a specific driver — it gets worse with printers whose PPD exposes more option groups, but the bug is in the dialog's own layout, not the driver.

Fix: wrap the settings+preview area in `egui::ScrollArea::vertical()`, capped to the viewport's available height (read through `input(|i| i.viewport_rect())`, which holds the last known size across frames — reading `raw.screen_rect` directly went blank on frames the backend didn't resend it, as the new test caught).
