title: fix(linux): the .deb and .rpm depend on libdbus-1, which every file dialog needs
author: diegodru
body:
## What this changes

The .deb and .rpm now depend on libdbus-1 (`libdbus-1-3`, `libdbus-1.so.3()(64bit)`).

rfd reaches the desktop portal's FileChooser by loading `libdbus-1.so.3` at run time (rfd 0.17.2, `xdg_desktop_portal/portal/ffi.rs`). Since it isn't an ELF `NEEDED` entry, nfpm.yaml never listed it, though its comment already lists the other libraries the app opens at run time for this reason. If it is missing, rfd falls back to `zenity`, which isn't a dependency either, and then every Open, Save and folder dialog silently does nothing: the picker answers as if it had been cancelled.

It's a hard dependency rather than a recommendation because without it the app can't open or save a file at all. Most desktops have libdbus already, so the practical effect is on minimal installs and on anyone repackaging from the .deb. I found this on NixOS, where a wrapper that didn't put libdbus on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` showed exactly this symptom.

Related, not overlapping: #4162 explains an empty answer when the portal's backend is dead (#3988). Its probe asks the bus directly, so it reports "fine" when only libdbus is missing; that case is what this PR prevents at install time. The Nix flake in #1511 already adds `dbus` to its wrapper.

- Built a .deb and an .rpm with nfpm from this nfpm.yaml (stage with placeholder binaries) and read the dependencies back:

title: perf(optimize): work out pictures on threads and skip needless page reads
author: quincy-jc
body:
## What this changes

- Pictures are worked out on up to half the machine's processors (at most 8, one on the web), and as many as 1 GiB holds of the largest picture. Those threads go at low priority where the system allows it. The document only changes in order on one thread.
- A page with no picture that could be a fragment, or too few `Do` operators for a run, is no longer read looking for fragments.
- Progress names the page being read, and the bar is weighed by where the time goes. "Removing user data" only shows when some is being removed.

On made-up files, on a 16-thread machine, median of 3 (scripts in #6222):

| File | Before | After | Output size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 120 large pictures (`make_tiled_pictures.py --count 120`) | about 4.2 s | about 0.8 s | same |
| 5 million line segments (`make_heavy_sheet.py --segments 5000000`) | about 9 s | about 3.7 s | same, to within 1 byte in repeated runs |

Outputs of repeated runs differ in the last object stream on both builds. I did not compare base and branch outputs byte for byte; the tests below compare 1 thread against several on this branch.

## The decoding allowance

`ImageBudget` was shared and spent in document order. To keep that exact:

- Each thread works within what's left at the start of a batch of 32, and reports what it used.
- What was used is paid in document order (`ImageBudget::charge`, new). A picture that can't be paid for, or was refused by its own allowance, is done again on one thread with the real allowance.
- Once a batch has used more than what's left, no more of it are started.

So the pictures refused are the same with any number of threads. Decoding work in a batch can go over what's left by what the running threads have in hand, up to one allowance each.

title: M11: PDF/A verify checks that TIFF, EXIF and aux XMP properties have their value types (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks PDF/A-2 clause 6.6.2.3.1 for three more predefined XMP namespaces. #6220 covers the rest. A property in these namespaces must have the value type the XMP Specification gives it. Before, `tiff:ImageWidth` written as `256 mm`, `tiff:BitsPerSample` with an `8.0`, or `exif:Flash` written as plain text passed.

**The source.** The September 2005 XMP Specification, the edition PDF/A-2 cites:
- "EXIF Schema for TIFF Properties": the `tiff` namespace, `http://ns.adobe.com/tiff/1.0/`, pages 58–60.
- "EXIF Schema for EXIF-specific Properties": the `exif` namespace, `http://ns.adobe.com/exif/1.0/`, pages 60–69.
- "EXIF Schema for Additional EXIF Properties": the `aux` namespace, `http://ns.adobe.com/exif/1.0/aux/`, page 69.
- "EXIF Schema Value Types", pages 83–87.

The current XMP Part 2 doesn't list these namespaces itself; it refers to the CIPA mapping instead. So these tables are taken from the 2005 edition, as the module comment says.

**How values are checked,** with #6220's checker:
- A Closed Choice of Integer is an Integer, a Closed Choice of Text is text, and "seq Integer" or "seq Rational" is an `rdf:Seq` of those.
- Rational is "numerator; forward slash; denominator" (page 84).
- GPSCoordinate is `DDD,MM,SSk` or `DDD,MM.mmk`, with `k` one of N, S, E or W (page 85). Degrees, minutes and seconds are whole numbers; the minute fraction may have any number of digits.
- The Flash, OECF/SFR, CFAPattern and DeviceSettings structures are checked by their fields (pages 85–87). Flash's Return and Mode are Closed Choices of Integer.

**How often:** measured on the veraPDF corpus (CC BY 4.0), folder `PDF_A-2b`. Its 986 files say in their names whether they should pass or fail.

title: M7: a font's metrics can be read within a caller's decode allowance
author: Piohrun
body:
Part of #5755: the fonts step of the plan in [this comment](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/5755#issuecomment-6626162862).

## What this changes

`Metrics::from_dict` reads a font's metrics from its streams: its `/Encoding` and `/ToUnicode` CMaps, its program (a Type 0 subset's, for which glyphs have outlines; a simple font's without `/Widths`, for its advances; and, since `main`'s fix for #3962 (merged through #6711) and its Mac OS Roman reading, a symbolic TrueType font's, for what its codes show by glyph name and as Mac OS Roman), its `/CIDToGIDMap`, and a Type 3 font's glyph descriptions, for their `d1` boxes. Each decodes within a limit of its own (16 MiB, 128 KiB for the map, 64 KiB for a glyph description and 4 MiB for all of a Type 3 font's), but afresh on every call. A caller that reads many fonts naming one large stream decodes it once for each, with no total.

The branch has `main` merged in four times: by FredApps at 0a7798707 (ef7f2f311), then at 25025fa27, b6cbf9bb3 and ba28458ad (the last with nothing to resolve, and no new font reads). It also carries two commits of FredApps': 6f5f36136, after which `Metrics::encode` refuses new text for metrics read past their allowance, and 5b204d595, after which `page_rules` refuses a page whose content didn't all decode (the same change is on #6341).

**Now:**
- `Metrics::from_dict_within(doc, font, &mut DecodeBudget)` charges each of those decodes to the caller's allowance, by what it decoded, usable or not. title: refactor(ui): tell Edit text, the text layer and links whether a press is theirs (router PR 4b)
author: alehel
body:
## Why

#5803 (router PR 4a) made the page view tell every module outside Edit text what the page has to do with a press: its owner's, the active tool's, or another page's. The Edit text group was left, because it held the open questions. Its paragraphs, pictures, added content and objects still asked the router for themselves and passed answers from one module to the next (`others_own_pointer`, `text_used`, `over_source`, `source_blocked`, `allow_interaction`). So what the pointer happened to be over at the release, or what an earlier module answered, could take a click from the module its press was on. Three other things were still outside the router:

- The text layer, image pick and link following read the router directly.
- Crop mode's hit had no point test, so its claim took the cursor on every visible page.
- The page's right-click menu chose from the selections in a fixed order, so a selection left from before outranked what was just right-clicked.

This PR is the last step of the page pointer router. After it, a page module is told whether a press is its own, and the compiler refuses a module outside `canvas` that tries to read the router.

## What this changes

The first ten commits are the change. The fourteen after them are fixes and tests from review, kept as commits of their own.

1. **Crop mode is a hit of its picture** (`edit_text_ui::crop_hit`, `PicturePart::Crop`): a grip of the box kept, the box, the picture outside it, or the rest of its page. A drag takes what its press was on, and the cursor is the hit's. Delete, Backspace and crop's Enter and Escape are read in one place (`picture_keys`).
2. **A press with Shift or ⌘ in Edit text is the objects'**, by their own hit (`object_ui::modified_hit`). `PagePointer.modifiers` replaces a raw event read.

title: M7: Edit text keeps Word's invisibly spaced words on their line (refs #156)
author: emcekare
body:
## What this changes

Edit text keeps a word on its line when its character or word spacing differs from the line's by less than a hundredth of an em. The previous limit was a thousandth (#3861).

Word's own PDF export (Word LTSC on Windows, "Save as PDF") draws each run in its own `q <clip> re W* n BT … ET Q` with an absolute `Tm`. It also puts `Tc` of up to about four thousandths of an em on single words, for example `0.0413 Tc` at 11 pt. Joining runs from different text objects allowed only one thousandth. So in a Word letter, Edit text split lines into separate paragraph boxes at those words: `Yu|karıda`, `dosya|da`, `İST|ANBUL`, `15|.0|6.2026`.

The new limit is ten thousandths, not four, because a line is compared with its first run. Two words nudged in opposite directions can therefore differ by twice Word's nudge (+0.0235 vs −0.036 at 11 pt is about 5.4 thousandths). Visible tracking is still well above the limit: `0.5 Tc` at 12 pt is about 42 thousandths, so those runs stay apart.

On a one-page Word letter I checked locally, `text_paragraphs` returned 18 paragraphs before this change and 8 after, which matches the letter's actual paragraphs. That letter contains personal data, so it is not attached. The test reproduces the structure synthetically.

Refs #156

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`pdfcraft-edit`)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit`: 444 passed). On one full run, `form_xobjects_that_fan_out_stop_at_the_visit_budget` and `forms_that_fan_out_a_hundred_ways_stop_quickly_and_say_so` failed while the machine was busy compiling. They passed when rerun, both on this branch and on `main`, so they look timing-sensitive and unrelated to this change.

**Tests.** `word_export_spacing_of_a_few_thousandths_of_an_em_stays_on_its_line` builds runs the way Word writes them, each in its own `q … BT … ET Q`, and checks:
- Word's nudges in opposite directio…

title: M7: a list item whose tab is an ActualText span moves (#6145)
author: hasannadeem
body:
## What this changes

Part of #6145: "the first visible text field cannot be dragged and moved until it either resized or its text content is edited". With the reporter's file I reproduced it in the real UI. In Edit text & images, drag the paragraph "• This text field cannot be moved until it's modified or resized". It doesn't move, and the toast says:

> Move object failed: These objects could not be moved. Select them again and try a smaller move.

Headlessly, `object_move` on either bulleted paragraph gives the underlying error:

> step 2 (object_move): a selected text operation cannot be moved

**Why.** Word drew the tab after each bullet as a glyph in an ActualText span: `/Span << /ActualText <feff0009> >> BDC … Tj EMC`. When a line is read with ActualText, the interpreter folds the span into one run and keeps its `BDC` and `EMC` among the line's operations (`extra_ops`). That way a rewrite drops the whole span with the text.

`translate_blocks` (`text/rewrite.rs`) moves a paragraph by patching each of its show operations in place. It then checked that every operation of the line got a patch. The `BDC` and `EMC` show nothing, so they never get one, and every move of such a paragraph was refused. An edit or resize rewrites the paragraph without the span, which is why the paragraph could be moved after one.

**Change.** The check counts only the show operations (`Tj`, `TJ`, `'`, `"`): those are what a move patches. The marked-content operators stay where they are, so the span and its tab survive the move. A show operation that can't be patched is still refused as before. The other users of a line's operations drop them (rewrite, delete), which already handles a span correctly, and this is the only count check.

Not in this PR, also from #6145:

- Form artwork with a top-first `/BBox` is #6151, and the tab paragraph's edit error is #6154.
- "Emptied fields disappear" is left as it is. Emptying a paragraph deletes it, as in Acrobat's Edit PDF. Listing the empty tex…

title: M7: preserve source fonts when editing grouped Thai text
author: xullul
body:
## What this changes

Editing existing Thai text can fail because the text is inside Form XObjects, its legacy Unicode map is damaged, or its embedded subset has no Unicode cmap/layout tables. Replacing the font can then change the text's weight and size.

This integration makes supported grouped text available to the existing paragraph editor and reuses the PDF's original THSarabunPSK Regular/Bold glyph programs and character codes. Point size, character/word spacing, horizontal scale, rise, colour and paint settings survive save/reopen. A missing source/contextual glyph produces an actionable error; choosing a different family is explicit.

Refs #3185, #2964 and #2142. These broader reports remain open because unsupported forms, incomplete subsets and mixed contextual styles still have limits.

**Builds on existing contributions:**

title: M11: PDF/A verify checks that XMP extension schema descriptions are complete (optimize.pdfa-validate)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Verify PDF/A** (`pdfa_verify`) now checks PDF/A-2 clause 6.6.2.3.3, the extension schema container schema. A packet that extends XMP describes each added schema in `pdfaExtension:schemas`, a bag of schema descriptions, and each description must be complete. Before, an incomplete description passed.

**The rule.** The schemas, their entries and their prefixes come from PDF Association TechNote 0009, "XMP Extension Schemas in PDF/A-1" (2008, CC BY 4.0), section 4, for PDF/A-2 6.6.2.3.3:
- **A schema** (`pdfaSchema`, `http://www.aiim.org/pdfa/ns/schema#`, §4.3) has `schema`, `namespaceURI` and `prefix`. Its `property` and `valueType` lists are optional.
- **A property** (`pdfaProperty`, `…/property#`, §4.4) has `name`, `valueType`, `category` and `description`.
- **A value type** (`pdfaType`, `…/type#`, §4.5) has `type`, `namespaceURI`, `prefix`, `description` and `field`.
- **A field** (`pdfaField`, `…/field#`, §4.6) has `name`, `valueType` and `description`.
- **Prefixes.** All five namespaces, the container's `pdfaExtension` included, are written with their own prefixes. "Unlike predefined XMP schemas, the namespace prefixes are not only preferred, but required" (§4.1). Binding the right namespace URI to another prefix breaks the rule.

TechNote 0009 was written for PDF/A-1 and calls `pdfaSchema:schema` and `pdfaType:field` optional descriptions. For PDF/A-2 both are required, as its conformance tests expect: a schema description without `schema`, and a value type without `field`, fail 6.6.2.3.3.

**How it reads a packet.**
- The container is one `rdf:Bag` ("bag Schema", §4.2); a container of another shape is reported.
- A description is an array item, written as `rdf:parseType="Resource"` or as an `rdf:Description`. A list written twice in one description is read each time.
- An entry counts as present as an element or as an attribute.
- Every metadata stream is read, as for 6.6.2.3.1.

**Reporting.** Each missing entry and each misused pref…

title: M7: an ff, ffi or ffl ligature named in /Differences reads in Edit text
author: hasannadeem
body:
## What this changes

Edit text dropped the `ff` ligature from TeX documents, and an edit then wrote the word without it. Open a paragraph containing "diﬀerent", change any other word, and the saved page reads, and draws, **"dierent"**. No error or warning is shown.

I found it with an edit sweep over the test corpus (below). The file is pdf.js's `bug1873345.pdf`, a LaTeX document in Computer Modern. Its paragraph 3 lists as:

> 1. Asection The standard permits **dierent** interval behavior via the ﬂavor concept…

while `pdfcraft-cli text` (the renderer's text layer) reads "diﬀerent" correctly.

**Why.** TeX's Type 1 subsets often hold the ligature in a small font of its own. Here `ISVWEG+CMR10` holds one glyph, code 33, and has no `/ToUnicode`. Its encoding is `<< /BaseEncoding /WinAnsiEncoding /Differences [33 /ff] >>`. `pdfcraft_fonts::glyph_text` reads such names through `encodings::NAMES`, which holds the Latin character set of ISO 32000-2 Annex D. That set has `fi` and `fl` but not `ff`, `ffi` or `ffl`, so the name read as nothing:

- the code had no text, and the glyph fell out of the line Edit text builds (and of every reader of `glyph_text_lines`);
- the paragraph's text became "dierent";
- a rewrite writes the paragraph's text, so the glyph left the page.

The renderer's text layer was fixed for these names in #3239, through the vendored `hayro` glyph list. The edit side goes through `pdfcraft-fonts`, which `hayro` doesn't reach (layering).

**Change.** `NAMES` gains `ff`, `ffi` and `ffl` as U+FB00, U+FB03 and U+FB04, beside the `fi` (U+FB01) and `fl` (U+FB02) it already had. Those are the names the Adobe Glyph List specification gives the three characters, and the Unicode code points of Alphabetic Presentation Forms. The table is binary-searched, so a new test checks it stays sorted and free of duplicates.

## How you verified it

On `8b8f9aec` (`main` `15c505d1`), macOS arm64.

| `cargo clippy` …

title: M11: a soft mask several images share keeps its size for the ones not downsampled (optimize.downsample-images)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Reduce File Size / Optimize** downsamples an image together with its soft mask, because ISO 32000-1 11.6.5.3 requires the mask to keep the parent's dimensions: "The image dictionary for the soft-mask image shall contain the same Width, Height, and BitsPerComponent entries as the parent image". The resampled mask used to be written over the shared mask object. When several images name the same `/SMask`, the ones that were not resampled were left with a mask of the wrong size.

Now the optimizer counts how many images in the document name each soft mask:

- **Shared mask, image resampled:** that image gets a resampled copy of its own, a new object. The other images keep the original mask at its original size.
- **Last image still naming it, or a mask only one image uses:** the mask is changed in place, as before. When every image sharing a mask is resampled, no unused copy is left behind.

The count covers every image stream in the document, not only the ones the page walk measured, so an image the walk didn't reach keeps its mask too.

Fixes #6259

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-optimize`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-optimize --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize`

**Test.** `a_shared_soft_mask_is_copied_for_the_image_that_is_resampled` (crates/optimize/tests/optimize.rs) shares one 800 × 800 mask between two 800 × 800 images.

- One image is drawn at 800 ppi and resampled to 150 × 150; the other is drawn at 72 ppi and left alone. The resampled one's mask is 150 × 150. The other still names the original mask, which is still 800 × 800.
- When both are resampled, each mask matches its image. The original is still in use, and only one copy was made.

With the in-place write restored, the test fails: the image that wasn't resampled is left with a 150 × 150 mask.

title: sign: anchor chains at the trusted certificate itself
author: chamber074
body:
Fixes #6221.

## What this changes

On `main`, validation builds its certificate pools from the document's own certificates first, so a chain can end at a *copy* of a trusted root — the same certificate cross-signed by another issuer, as a cross-signed root arrives in a timestamp token — and never reach the trusted certificate itself. A signature whose chain runs through a cross-signed root therefore validates as Unknown even though the root it anchors to is in the user's trust store.

The pools now put the trust store **first** at all three sites validation builds one (document chains, embedded timestamp tokens, the standalone token scan), so the chain builder reaches the trusted certificate itself and ends the chain there. Trust stays byte-exact: `TrustStore::trusts` recognises the certificate the user trusted, and nothing else — a copy is never judged as the anchor, because the signature on a copy is never verified and every field on it is its bearer's word. (An earlier version of this PR matched the anchor by name and key and judged copies by their fields; review showed that lets a copy claim the right to issue, a wider validity window, or a purpose the trusted certificate was never issued for, and that approach was removed.)

The cost, accepted deliberately: a chain the trusted certificate cannot head — the builder refuses it as an issuer, an expired root say — stays Unknown. It fails closed.

## How you verified it

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed

title: fix(render): a JBIG2 scan whose data starts with a JBIG2 file header draws instead of a white page (hayro-jbig2 patch 17)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A page whose scan is a `JBIG2Decode` image now draws, where it drew white, when the image data starts with a JBIG2 **file header**.

ISO 32000-1 7.4.7 has the data of a `JBIG2Decode` stream in the *embedded* organization of ISO/IEC 14492 (Annex D.3): segments only, with no file header. Some producers write the standalone file's header too: the ID string `0x97 4A 42 32 0D 0A 1A 0A`, a flags byte, and a page count unless the flags say it's unknown (D.4). Acrobat and PDFBox draw such streams. PdfCraft read the ID string as a segment header, decoding failed with "unknown or reserved segment type", and the page was left white, the "opens blank in PdfCraft, fine elsewhere" symptom.

This follows the readers rather than the letter of 7.4.7: every reader we checked draws these files, and refusing them loses the page.

- **Where:** `hayro_jbig2::Image::new_embedded`, which both PDF paths use: the renderer (through `hayro-syntax`) and `pdfcraft-filters`' `JBIG2Decode`. Data that starts with the ID string is read past the header, in the organization the header declares (sequential or random access, D.1 and D.2). Anything else is read as before.
- **Bounds unchanged:** the segments after the header count together with the globals' toward the existing segment and reference caps (patch 8). The random-access reader now takes that shared count instead of starting its own.
- **Malformed headers:** a header with reserved flag bits set is refused as before, an error and not a panic.

Recorded as hayro-jbig2 patch (17) in `vendor/README.md`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-filters`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-filters -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-filters`, `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/hayro-jbig2/Cargo.toml`

title: M7: character spacing that TJ adjustments take back reads as a word gap in Edit text
author: hasannadeem
body:
## What this changes

Edit text ran together two words of letter-spaced small caps. In pdf.js's `bug1873345.pdf`, a LaTeX document, the heading "1. A section" (set in `\textsc`) lists as **"1. Asection"**. Editing the heading writes the paragraph's text back, so the word space is lost from the page too. Change "section" to "subsection" and the saved page reads and draws **"1. Asubsection"**. The renderer's text layer (`pdfcraft-cli text`) reads "1. A section" correctly, so copy and Find were fine. The bug is in what Edit text lists and writes.

**Why.** TeX letter-spaces small caps with a wide `Tc` and takes it back with TJ adjustments between the letters of a word:

```
4.13346 Tc /R14 10.9091 Tf … [(As)378.015(e)377.986(c)379.009(t)379.009(i)379.009(o)378(n)]TJ
```

`Tc` is 0.38 em here, and each `378` moves the next letter back by about the same. So the letters of "section" touch. The only gap left is between "A" and "s", which sit in one string with no adjustment between them: the `Tc` after "A".

`show_text` (`crates/edit/src/text/interp.rs`) read a space only from a TJ adjustment and left `Tc` out ("Tc is already included in the pen advance"). So it never saw that gap.

**Change.**

- `Tc` now counts as the gap it opens after a glyph, as §9.3.2 adds it to every glyph's advance. The gap between two glyphs is the first one's `Tc` plus every adjustment between them, summed (a `0` among them included), and it is judged at the next glyph. The space test and the word-end test (which splits a line's ink into words) both use it.
- An adjustment after the last glyph still reads as a space when it is large, as before. The `Tc` before it doesn't, since no glyph follows it.
- A space is added only where the text doesn't already end in whitespace: a no-break space the font draws is the word gap, and an adjustment just before a space glyph no longer adds a second space.
- `tj_tracking` measures the letter gaps the same way, with `Tc` in them, and now runs for `Tj`, `'` and …

title: fix(render): a small image with a soft mask far larger than it draws in seconds, its mask averaged down once (hayro-interpret patch 82)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A page that draws a small image whose soft mask is far larger than the image, many times over, now renders in seconds instead of minutes.

The case that showed it is a PowerPoint slide (pdf.js test file `issue16263.pdf`). A form draws a 2 × 2 image whose `/SMask` is a 34,862 × 4,332 one-bit image (38 KB compressed, about 150 million samples), and the slide draws that form 40 times. On the page each copy is about 73 × 9 device pixels at 36 dpi. Each draw cost about 3.6 s:
- the soft mask was decoded straight from its stream, bypassing the decoded-image cache;
- it was too large for the cache's 64 MiB budget anyway;
- the renderer then staged an RGB image the size of the mask (about 450 MB) to draw it as a mask layer.

So the page took over two minutes, and `pdfcraft-cli check` gave up on it.

Now `ImageXObject::decoded_soft_mask` handles a soft mask (or `/Mask` image) that is larger than its image and more than twice as large on a side as the device pixels the image is drawn at:
- it is averaged down to that size rounded up to a power of two (each target sample is the mean of the source samples whose centres fall in it), and cached at that size (`DecodedImageKey::shrunk_to`); the image's raster is keyed by the same rounded size, so each draw gets the mask for its own size and draws a pixel apart share one;
- every size is made from one cached intermediate mask, at most 4096 on a side, so the full mask is decoded once however many sizes it is drawn at (the slide's rotated and scaled copies hit four).

The intermediate is at most 16 MiB and the averaged-down masks are small, so they fit the existing budget and **no limit changes**. Any other mask keeps its own resolution and is drawn as before. That covers a mask no larger than twice its drawn size, and a mask no larger than its image, which the renderer still samples onto the image's grid. The renderer already filters a shrunk mask rather than picking samples (#1649), so averaging it first keeps …

title: M2.6: never rewrite a content stream from the part before its damage
author: Piohrun
body:
Follows up the point CodeRabbit raised outside the diff of #5825 (its review of 01751aeb7e) and FredApps asked to track there: an edit of a page whose content stream decodes only partly.

## What this changes

A Flate stream damaged partway decodes to what came before the damage. `DecodeBudget::decode`, through which edit, accessibility, Optimize and Organize read page content, gave that part back as the stream's data: `Stream::decoded_within_counted` dropped the decoder's partial flag. Code that wrote the stream again from it lost everything after the damage on save, though the file still holds it and other readers may read it. Code that decided from it what a page draws missed whatever is drawn past the damage.

**Now:**
- `DecodeBudget::decode_with_damage` and `DecodeBudget::decode_contents_with_damage` read as `decode_within` and `decode_contents` do, and say whether each stream is damaged partway. What readers take as whole stays whole: a missing or wrong Adler-32, data after the end of the Flate data, a missing end-of-data marker. `decode` is unchanged.
- **Parameters given by reference.** Both take the document, and read a `/DecodeParms` given by reference, or a number in it, through it (`Document::decoding_view`). Before, as on `main`, content behind a predictor whose parameters were indirect decoded with the predictor's tag bytes left in, and was taken as whole: edit listed and wrote back the wrong bytes, and Organize dropped an image such a form draws. `decode_contents` is now the new method without the flag, so printing and accessibility's headings and figure bounds read them too, and so does a stamp or watermark made from a page, through `decode_contents_with_damage`.
- **Redaction.** `DecodeBudget::decode_strict` takes the document and reads parameters by reference the same way. Redaction reads page content and forms through it, and so do Remove Hidden Information (hidden text and layers), the redaction audit's check for text under an opaque cover, and …

title: fix(render): a stream with no endstream after it draws from its /Length instead of a blank page (hayro-syntax patch 36)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A stream whose `/Length` is right but which has no `endstream` keyword left after it in the file is now read as the bytes its `/Length` gives. Before this change, such a stream was a syntax error and its object was null.

ISO 32000-2 §7.3.8.1 says "the stream dictionary specifies the exact number of bytes". §7.3.8.2 says `Length` "indicates how many bytes of the PDF file are used for the stream's data".

Both readers trusted `/Length` only when `endstream` came right after it. Otherwise they searched the rest of the file for the keyword. Some producers write a misspelt `endstrea` after every stream. In such a file the search finds nothing, so every font, image and page content stream resolved to null. Each page then drew blank, text extraction returned nothing, and no warning was given.

- **`pdfcraft-cos`** (`parse_indirect_in`): a `/Length` that fits in the file is the stream's extent when it ends where `endstream` would be: before a misspelt `endstrea`, before `endobj`, or at the end of the file. This is checked before the search for `endstream`, so the search can't run on into a later object's stream and take its header and data as this stream's. When the search finds none, a fitting `/Length` is still the extent. A `/Length` past the end of the file, a negative one, or a missing one is still an error, as before.
- **vendored `hayro-syntax`, patch 36** (`parse_declared`): the same rule for the renderer. It runs first before `parse_fallback`, accepting only a `/Length` that ends before `endstrea`, `endobj` or the end of the data, and again after `parse_fallback` has found no `endstream` in the rest of the data, so the data is not searched a second time. `vendor/README.md` lists the patch and its tests.

Streams whose `endstream` follows their data are read exactly as before.

## How you verified it

- New tests:
  - `parser::tests::indirect_stream_without_endstream_is_its_length` (pdfcraft-cos). Three cases read the stream from `/Length`: `e…

title: fix(render): a page of stencil masks painted with a tiling pattern draws in seconds instead of running out of memory (hayro patch 30)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A page that paints many stencil masks (`/ImageMask true`) with a tiling pattern now renders in seconds. Before, it could run for minutes and then fail to allocate.

The public pdf.js test file `issue8078.pdf` ("File with many repeated patterns sortof freezes browser") is a 1701 × 2409 pt site plan. Its 25 MB content stream sets one coloured tiling pattern (`/R27 scn`, a 128 × 32 image cell under a `/Matrix` scaled about 11 × 78) and then paints 73,047 inline 16 × 16 CCITT stencil masks with it. `pdfcraft-cli check` gave up on page 1 after 30 s. `pdfcraft-cli render --dpi 36` ran for 5 min 18 s and then aborted with `memory allocation of 3491600 bytes failed`.

Two costs added up on every one of those draws:

- **A canvas-sized mask per stencil.** A pattern-painted stencil (ISO 32000-2 §8.9.6.2: the current colour, here the pattern, is painted where the mask's samples say so) was drawn through a luminance mask. vello_cpu only takes a mask the size of the whole canvas, so every draw rendered, converted and composited a full-page mask.
- **A new pattern cell per fill.** The cell pixmap of a tiling pattern (§8.7.3.1) was rasterized again on every fill, and every copy was kept until the page was composited. Here that is 3.5 MB × 73,047.

The fix has two vendored patches:

- **hayro patch (30), stencils.** The stencil is drawn under a clip of its device rectangle, padded by two pixels so that a stencil snapped to whole device pixels still lies inside. Under that clip the pattern goes into an isolated layer, and a second layer holding the stencil cuts it with `Compose::DestIn`. The coverage draw ignores Type 3 glyph image rules, as the sub-render it replaces did. A draw now costs what its rectangle covers.
- **hayro patch (30), cells.** A coloured tiling pattern's cell is drawn once for each setting of the pattern and each cell scale, through `Renderer::tiling_cell`. This covers repeated cells and the bordered one-cell case of patch (20). The cache (`…

title: fix(edit): break the row on every Unicode row break
author: MatrixMagician
body:
## Why

Editing a paragraph that contains U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR failed with "the Inter fallback font has no glyph for (U+2028)". U+2028 is an invisible break, so no face draws it. Text pasted from a browser or Word carries it, so real documents hit this. Refs #6272.

## What changed

- `row_break` in `crates/edit/src/text/blocks.rs` names the row-break characters once. The four rewrite sites that each spelled out `\n` and `\r` now call it.
- The set covers U+2028, U+2029, U+0085, the vertical tab, the form feed and the information separators U+001C to U+001E.

## Scope

Covers the break characters on both rewrite paths, the single-style one in `rewrite.rs` and the styled one in `styled.rs`. It also covers the Thai routes of the styled path (legacy subset, bundled face by choice, matching face), which kept their own coverage check and CR/LF row split. `covers_rows` in `styled.rs` checks each row and skips the breaks. `pdfcraft_fonts::embedding::covers` is unchanged, because signing relies on it refusing anything but CR/LF that Inter can't draw. Leaves out the second problem reported in #6272, that the original text shows through while editing. It is tracked as #6657, so this PR refers to #6272 without closing it. Leaves out U+FE0F, tracked as #4861.

## Tradeoffs

Normalising these to `\n` was the alternative to skipping them in the glyph check. Normalising keeps the user's break, which is what the character means; skipping the check would have dropped it and rejoined the rows.

## Blast Radius

Touches paragraph rewriting, which every text edit goes through. Two behaviours could regress and both have existing tests that still pass: `a_lone_carriage_return_breaks_an_edited_paragraph` and `carriage_returns_break_rows_on_the_styled_path` pin CRLF collapsing to one break on both paths. The new set is a subset of `char::is_whitespace` except U+001C to U+001E, which previously reached the font as literal characters.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit`: all t…

title: M1: a document that encrypts only its embedded files opens without a password (core.attachment-only-encryption)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A PDF that encrypts only its embedded files now opens without a password, as the specification says it should. Before, `pdfcraft-cli info` and the app refused it with "the document is protected by a password".

ISO 32000-2 §7.6.6, Table 25 (*Entries common to all crypt filter dictionaries*), `AuthEvent`:
> EFOpen: Authorization shall be required when accessing embedded files.

The same table says a filter used as `/StrF` or `/StmF` behaves as `DocOpen`, which needs the password when the document opens. So the exemption applies only when:
- the handler has crypt filters (V4 or later);
- `/StmF` and `/StrF` are `/Identity`;
- every crypt filter that encrypts (`/CFM` `V2`, `AESV2` or `AESV3`) has `/AuthEvent /EFOpen`. The embedded files use those filters through `/EFF`, or through a `/Crypt` filter of their own (§7.4.10).

No password and the empty password are treated alike.

Such a document's pages and strings are stored in the clear. This is the pdf.js test file `auth-event-ef-open.pdf` (V5, R6, `/EFF /StdCF` with AESV3). PDFium and Poppler open it, with 1 page and 1 attachment; MuPDF asks for the password.

**What the document does without its password:**
- **Opens.** cos (`Document::open`) and the renderer's parser (hayro-syntax, patch (37)) open it with no password. Its pages render and its text reads. Opening another revision of it with the same credentials (`open_with_same_credentials`) opens only what this rule would open by itself.
- **Attachments are listed but not read.** With no file key, the embedded files' data is held as stored, still encrypted. `Document::embedded_files_locked()` and `Document::reads_as_stored(&Stream)` report this. The encrypted bytes are never handed out as the file:
  - Asking for an attachment's bytes (`attachment_data`, the app's Save attachment) is an error: "the attachment is encrypted: open the document with its password to read it".
  - Combine refuses to copy such an attachment into another document.

title: fix(render): a TrueType font marked with an out-of-range loca format draws its letters instead of boxes (hayro-interpret patch 83)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Text set in an embedded TrueType font now draws its letters, where it drew boxes, when the font's `head` table marks its glyph offsets with a value other than 0 or 1.

The `head` table's `indexToLocFormat` says how the `loca` table stores glyph offsets: 0 for 16-bit (short) offsets, 1 for 32-bit (long) ones; no other value is defined. Some producers write 256 (the two bytes of 1 swapped). The glyph outline reader takes anything other than 1 as short, so such a font had its long offsets read as short ones: every glyph pointed at the wrong data, and a line of text came out as boxes. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler draw it.

ISO 32000-2 §9.9 ("Embedded font programs") has a `/FontFile2` stream drawn as the TrueType program it holds; this reads that program's offsets as they are stored.

- **Where:** `OpenTypeFontBlob::new` in vendored hayro-interpret, which every embedded TrueType path uses (simple and CID fonts). When the field holds neither 0 nor 1, a copy of the font is made with the field set to the format the `loca` table's length gives: room for `numGlyphs + 1` offsets of 4 bytes is long, room only for that many of 2 bytes is short (padding after the offsets is allowed), and a table too short for either is left as it is.
- **Untouched:** a font marked 0 or 1 is used as it is, with no copy.

Recorded as hayro-interpret patch (83) in `vendor/README.md`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: M10: applying recognized words refreshes only the page content they add (#6310)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #6310.

## What this changes

Applying recognized words (`Session::apply_ocr`, which applies `Edit::AddOcrText`) now refreshes only the content it changed. Before, it re-inspected the whole document.

`Edit::AddOcrText` stamps an invisible text layer onto its page and adds that layer's font to the page's resources. Nothing else in the document changes. Even so, `scope_of` sent it to `Scope::Full`, so every apply re-inspected the whole document and listed its signatures again, and so did undo and redo of it. A batch takes the scope of its parts, so `apply_ocr`'s batch was a full refresh too.

`AddOcrText` is now `Scope::Content`, like Add text and the other edits to page content. The content refresh writes the working bytes, the display copy and the renderer, and keeps the page tree, comments, fields, links and marks. The font list is read again on `refresh_fonts` (`fonts_stale`), as it is after Add text. The OCR stamp is not an Add-content item or a header, watermark or background, so the marker scan stays valid.

Measured with the issue's own fixture (generated by its inline `generate.py`, not committed). One injected word on page 1, three runs each, dev profile:

| Fixture | Apply before | Apply after | Undo / redo before | Undo / redo after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 567 pages, 60,102 fonts | 2.08–2.24 s | 80–90 ms | 1.81–2.16 s / 1.37–1.89 s | 40–47 ms / 45–58 ms |
| 567 pages, no fonts | 20–29 ms | 7.1–7.5 ms | 16–20 ms / 16–18 ms | 4.2–4.4 ms / 4.4–4.9 ms |
| 1 page, no fonts | 1.4–3.4 ms | 0.8–2.9 ms | 0.6–1.2 ms / 0.6–2.1 ms | 0.3–0.6 ms / 0.3–0.4 ms |

What remains is shared by every content edit: about 36 ms to clone the object graph and stamp the page, 12 ms to write the revision, and 40 ms for the renderer's page check. All of it scales with the file, not with its font resources.

title: macOS: open odoc-delivered files whose name is in the other Unicode form (#6324)
author: matheusg-tech
body:
# macOS: open 'odoc' paths whose Unicode normalization form differs from the stored name

## What this changes

On macOS, a Finder double-click, Open With, a Dock drop or `open -a PdfCraft file.pdf`
delivers the file as an 'odoc' Apple event (#73). Any path containing an NFC-precomposed
component is silently dropped — no tab, no error, nothing in Recents — while ASCII and
pure-NFD paths open fine, which is why this survived the original odoc work. Where the loss
happens is pinned in the linked issue, and it is *not* at the filesystem: the reporter's
volume folds NFC/NFD in lookups (probes open the NFD spelling of an NFC name), and a
mis-normalized path injected at `OsEvent::Open` opens the file there even without any fix.
The document is lost earlier, in fmv-macos-events' descriptor→path conversion
(`fileURLValue()` → `NSURL` → `url.path()`), whose `filter_map` drops these items with no
trace. The crate-side half of the fix — byte-preserving extraction of the URL's
percent-encoded path bytes — is what the issue asks for; fmv-macos-events is pinned `=0.1.0`
and the workspace forbids `unsafe`, so **this PR is the PdfCraft-side half it can carry
today**: it hardens the one point where OS-delivered paths enter, and makes every failure
that does reach the app visible.

Where a path does arrive in a form that differs from the stored name, this resolves it
**component by component**: where a component of the delivered path
names no entry, its NFC and NFD forms are tried (`unicode-normalization`, already in the tree
through `pdfcraft-crypt`'s stringprep — no new package enters the lockfile). The mechanism is
agnostic to direction: NFD delivered with NFC stored, the reverse, and any mix along the chain
(a whole-path re-encoding would not do, since one path can carry both forms). Where a later
component matches in no form, the walk goes back to the component before and tries its next
form, making at most three times as many lookups as the path has components after the one for…

title: M6: a multi-select list's picks reach its XFA data as one value element each (form.fill-choice)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Filling a multi-select list box in a form that also carries XFA data now stores the new picks in that data too. Before, the XFA data kept the old picks, and reopening the form, which reads its values from the XFA data, brought the old picks back.

XFA 3.3, p. 198 ("Choice Lists That Can Have Multiple Values"): a field with a multi-select choice list is bound to a data group, not a data value, and the field's value is that group's children joined by newlines:

```xml
<grains>
  <value>rye</value>
  <value>wheat</value>
</grains>
```

p. 199: when the user changes the picks, Acrobat discards values that aren't in the list. So new picks replace the group's `value` elements.

- **Where:** `pdfcraft-xfa`, in both places a value reaches the data:
  - `merge_values` writes the datasets packet;
  - `DataNode::apply` updates the in-memory data that scripts read before the packet is written.

  Both skipped any data node with child elements: the packet with a "structured content" warning, the in-memory data without one. A node whose children are all text-only `value` elements is now written as one `value` element per line of the new value. Nothing picked leaves the group empty.
- **Untouched:** any other structured node is still skipped with its warning, as before.

## Related work

- **#4784** (ours) is the radio-button counterpart in the same data layer: an option whose export value is a number selects its own button, and the XFA data holds the option's item rather than the button's position (`crates/xfa/src/data/values.rs`). author: matheusg-tech
body:
# Scroll: the wheel works in an unfocused window under the pointer

## What this changes

Since 0.18.2, scrolling the mouse wheel or trackpad over a PdfCraft
window that does not have keyboard focus does nothing — the input is
read and then silently discarded until the window is clicked. This
restores the 0.18.0/0.18.1 behaviour: the document scrolls, following
the macOS convention that scroll input belongs to the window under the
pointer however unfocused it is (Preview, Safari and TextEdit all
scroll unfocused windows). Windows' "scroll inactive windows" setting
(on by default since Windows 10) delivers the same events, so the fix
restores the earlier cross-platform behaviour, not just macOS.

Where the loss happens: the events *do* arrive. winit's macOS
`scrollWheel:` handler queues `WindowEvent::MouseWheel` unconditionally
(`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/macos/view.rs`), and egui pushes
`Event::MouseWheel` into the frame's input whatever `i.focused` says.
It is PdfCraft that drops them: 292f9c75 ("Scroll: smooth wheel bursts
and preserve precise movement") gave `read_wheel` an `enabled`
parameter and fed it `wheel_enabled = navigation_enabled && …`, where

the initial import. Until 292f9c75 that term gated only pinch-zoom and
presentation-style clicks — `v0.18.0`/`v0.18.1`'s `read_wheel` had no
`enabled` parameter at all, and the single-page pager (`single_page_paging`,

title: fix(ui): a window larger than its monitor is fitted to it
author: andydoc
body:
## What this changes

A window larger than its monitor is now fitted to it. The first-start 1440 x 920 window, or a size saved on a bigger monitor, runs off a smaller screen (1536 x 864 points at 125 % scaling), and with it the foot of every dialog and drop-down list fitted to the window. On Wayland this happens only on a smaller monitor beside a larger one, because eframe already clamps a window to the largest monitor.

- Once the window's size is known, a window that does not fit gets nine tenths of the monitor, frame included, and is never made larger than it was.
- It is also centred when its corner is within the monitor's size of the desktop's origin, which is taken to mean the main monitor. A corner up to 16 points past the origin counts too, because Windows' outer rectangle includes its invisible resize borders, so a window against the monitor's left edge has its corner at x = -7. egui does not say where other monitors are on the desktop, so a window with its corner outside that area is only shrunk. See the known limit below.
- Wayland gives a window no position, so there the size comes from what the window reports each frame, and the window is sized and not moved.
- Maximized and full-screen windows are left alone.
- A window that starts maximized keeps its too-big size to return to, so the size is checked again on coming back from maximized or full screen. Windows reports a minimized window as not maximized, so minimized frames are skipped and do not count as a return.
- A window up to 16 points past its monitor counts as fitting, so a window snapped to the full height of a screen is not disturbed by its invisible resize borders.

Refs #4455, #5317, #5528, #5733, #4973. This is deliberately not "Fixes": it helps when the window itself is larger than the monitor, while a dialog taller than the fitted window still needs what #3964, #4994 and #6223 are doing (making dialogs scroll). It does not compete with them: none of the three touches `window_state.rs`.

title: macOS: deliver odoc items whose names are NFC-precomposed, by vendoring a patched fmv-macos-events (#6324)
author: matheusg-tech
body:
# macOS: deliver odoc items whose names are NFC-precomposed, by vendoring a patched fmv-macos-events

## What this changes

On macOS, a Finder double-click, Open With, a Dock drop or `open -a PdfCraft file.pdf`
delivers the file as an 'odoc' Apple event (#73). On macOS 13 every such item arrives as a
**`'bmrk'` (binary bookmark) descriptor** — never a `typeFileURL` — and the bookmark carries
the path twice: its per-component records keep every name in its **exact on-disk bytes**,
while its embedded full-path string is **NFD-normalized**. `NSAppleEventDescriptor
.fileURLValue()` resolves that bookmark through the alias machinery, whose path fallback is
byte-sensitive: whenever **any** on-disk component is NFC-precomposed, resolution fails,
`fileURLValue()` returns nil, and fmv-macos-events 0.1.0's `?` on it silently drops the item
inside the `filter_map` (`lib.rs:63-68`). Zero paths → no `Event::Open` → the app launches
showing nothing, with no error. All-ASCII and all-NFD trees always worked, which is why this
survived the original odoc work. The byte-level evidence — descriptor hex dumps, the
`c3 81` vs `41 cc 81` records inside one bookmark, per-case `fileURLValue()` outcomes — is
pinned in the instrumented-build comment on #6324.

This PR vendors the crate with one patch: each odoc item's path is recovered in three steps,
in this order (`odoc_path::item_path`) —

1. **The item's raw descriptor bytes, verified.** `'bmrk'`: walk the contiguous chain of
   0x0101 component records (`[len u32 LE][01 01 00 00][utf-8 bytes][NUL pad to a 4-byte
   boundary]`), join with `/`, and deliver the result when it names an existing file — the
   components are the exact on-disk names, NFC or NFD or mixed, byte for byte. `'furl'`:
   percent-decode the URL's path — taken from the first `/` after `file://`, so absolute by
   construction; a `'furl'` with no such `/` yields nothing — and deliver it when it names an
   existing file, the same gate as a bookmark's (since `86bfe11a`).…

title: M6: show CAD component properties and fix schematic image selection
author: znk-ee
body:
## What this changes

CAD-generated PDFs can attach component properties to JavaScript link actions. Clicking those components now runs the existing sandbox and displays flat `app.popUpMenu` / `app.popUpMenuEx` labels beside the click, within the document viewport. Properties wrap long values, use the existing Lucide close button, and close with Escape without also leaving full screen. All popup requests from a script run retain their labels.

Link actions use `Link/Mouse Up` events and commit pending form typing before reading or changing fields. Link clicks do not also select background pictures. Grouped-artwork image picking follows the actual bitmap placements, including smaller pictures and reused image resources; a page-sized Form containing a tiny logo no longer makes the whole page selectable. The synchronous lookup and current upstream's background picture cache share the placement listing. A failed nested-image walk keeps direct images selectable and reports a diagnostic; uncertain Form bounds are excluded.

Failed JavaScript stream decodes are cached by resolved stream identity for the inspection, avoiding repeated inflate work for shared actions.

### Automation compatibility

`doc_info` retains `links[].target.other = "JavaScript"` for existing consumers and adds `javascript` (source or null) and `javascript_status`: `available`, `missing`, `empty`, `invalid`, `budget_exceeded`, or `decode_failed`. Source is omitted whole, never truncated. `js_run` accepts optional `"event": "link"` for the viewer's event context and reports `popup_menu` labels. title: M8: redaction keeps an image a form without resources still draws
author: Piohrun
body:
Found while reviewing #6289. The fault is on `main`, not caused by that PR.

This branch now has `main` merged in three times: at 25025fa27, at b6cbf9bb3 (no conflicts), and at ba28458ad. #5969, #5197, #5924 and #6474 changed the functions this PR changes, so the merge carries this PR's changes into their code (**The merge**, below).

## What this changes

When a redaction removes or replaces an image or form under a mark, it takes the name out of the page's `/XObject` resources unless the page still draws it (`interp::prune`). That check looked only at the page's own `Do` operators. A form without `/Resources` of its own draws through the resources of whatever draws it. So when such a form outside the mark drew the same image, the page lost the name, and the form drew nothing there after the redaction. A form the redaction enters and leaves as it was lost it the same way: its box crosses the mark, but what it draws doesn't.

**Now:**
- **Pages.** A page keeps a name that a form drawing through its resources still draws. `prune` finds such names with `resource_ops`, the walk the font and property cleanup (`prune_type3_from_resources`, `prune_properties`) already uses for these forms. Both callers use it: Apply Redactions and Remove Hidden Information.
- **What can't be read.** `prune` refuses the page, as that cleanup does, when it can't tell what the page draws: a form drawing through its resources doesn't decode (an image codec or a `/Filter` it can't run, say) or runs past the page's allowance (below), the walk passes 2,000,000 operators, or the parser can't read all of such a form or of the page's content. That includes bytes in a stream the redaction leaves as it was. On a page with fonts or properties to clean up, the operation was already refused. On a page with neither, the name used to go and the operation went ahead. When the page's own content is what can't be read, the error now says "redaction could not fully read the content that uses these resources",…

A page that embeds PdfCraft (`?host=parent`, or the page host mode) opens a file for a reason, to read it or to sign it, but the app always opened in the user's default workspace (All tools out of the box), with the tools panel over the document.

title: fix(render): a ToUnicode CMap reads its mappings past a token it can't parse (hayro-cmap patch 3)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Text set in a font whose ToUnicode CMap has a damaged header can now be copied and found. Before, PdfCraft read no text at all from such a font.

ISO 32000-2 §9.10.2 has a font's ToUnicode CMap (§9.10.3) as the first way to map its character codes to Unicode, and the mappings are in its `beginbfchar` and `beginbfrange` sections. Some producers write broken tokens in the header before those sections:

- a CMap name holding a `>`: `/CMapName /Adobe-Identity-UC> def`, where the `>` is a delimiter and left on its own can't be read;
- a CMap name with spaces in it: `/CMapName /-usr-share-fonts-…-Panton Family-Fontfabric - Panton.otf,000-UTF16 def`, where the `-` that follows the name can't be read as a number.

The scanner stopped at the first such token. So the CMap kept nothing, the font had no ToUnicode, and none of its text came out. Poppler and PDFium read the mappings that follow.

- **Where:** vendored `hayro-cmap`, the parser both the renderer and text extraction use. A token the scanner can't read is now stepped over and the scan goes on. A new scanner method in `hayro-postscript`, `Scanner::parse_object_or_skip`, moves one byte past where the failed read started, so every failure makes progress.
- **Bounded:** at most 1,024 such tokens per CMap. A failed read may scan to the end of the data (an unclosed string), so an unbounded run would cost the stream's length squared. Past the limit the scan stops, keeping what it read, as it did before.
- **Untouched:** a `begin…` block that can't be read still ends the scan, and a CMap that yields nothing still reports failure, as patch (1) has them.

Recorded as hayro-cmap patch (3) and hayro-postscript patch (2) in `vendor/README.md`.

## Related work

- **#6359** (ours, hayro-interpret patch 85) and **#6353** (ours, hayro-interpret patch 84) work on what happens after a ToUnicode CMap is parsed, in `Type0Font::char_code_to_unicode`: #6359 reads entries written with `begincidchar` / `begincidrange`,…

title: fix(edit): Update header & footer changes only the one chosen (#5785)
author: jweaver3
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5785.

**Update header & footer** could only reach the most recently added header/footer, and it removed every header and footer on the pages it touched. If you added a header and then a footer separately, Update brought up the footer and deleted the header.

Now:

- Each header/footer mark records its settings in a private `/PCHeaderFooter` dict on its content stream (and on its shrink `cm` stream). The document is the source of truth, so undo/redo and save/reopen keep working. Marks with equal settings count as one, across pages.
- `pdfcraft_edit::update_header_footer` replaces one mark, matched by its settings, and leaves the others. It refuses with an error if that mark is no longer in the document. `header_footers()` lists the marks, capped at 256. Recorded settings are validated (size, margins, colour, types), and invalid ones are not listed.
- Engine: `Edit::UpdateHeaderFooter { old, pages, settings }`, labelled "Update header & footer", with Content history scope.
- UI: when a page has more than one header/footer, the Update dialog shows **"Which header and footer:"**. Choosing one loads its settings and its own pages, and the dialog says "Replaces this header and footer, and no other."
- Automation: a new read-only `doc_header_footers` tool (index, 1-based pages, box text with tokens unexpanded), plus an `update` index on `doc_header_footer` (not allowed together with `replace`; defaults to the mark's own pages).
- `place.rs`: the read-only `content_list` is extracted from `check_on_top`, and `place` returns the new stream's `ObjRef`.

title: fix(render): an embedded CJK font without a usable ToUnicode reads its text through its collection's UCS2 CMap (hayro-interpret patch 84)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Japanese and Chinese pages whose fonts are embedded Type 0 fonts of an Adobe character collection (Adobe-Japan1, -GB1, -CNS1, -Korea1) now have text to select, find, copy and export when the font has no `/ToUnicode`, or has one that maps nothing for some codes.

ISO 32000-2 §9.10.2 gives the routes from a character code to Unicode: the font's `/ToUnicode` CMap first; then, for a composite font that uses a predefined CMap or whose descendant CIDFont uses the Adobe-GB1, Adobe-CNS1, Adobe-Japan1 or Adobe-Korea1 collection, code → CID (through the font's CMap) → Unicode through the collection's UCS2 CMap. The renderer took the second route only for fonts whose program is **not** embedded, so an embedded font without a `/ToUnicode` gave no text at all, and a `/ToUnicode` with a codespace range and no mappings hid the route for every code.

Now (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/cid.rs`, hayro-interpret patch (84)):

- the collection's UCS2 CMap is loaded for every Type 0 font whose collection has one, embedded or not;
- `char_code_to_unicode` tries `/ToUnicode` first, and for a code it gives nothing for, the code's CID in the UCS2 CMap. The routes stay in that order, ending with `None`, so a later route for fonts outside the Adobe collections can follow the UCS2 step.

Glyph selection is unchanged: a substitute for a font that is not embedded still picks glyphs through the same map as before.

The UCS2 CMaps are already bundled (`vendor/hayro-cmap/assets/cmaps.brotli`, BSD-3-Clause, in `ATTRIBUTION.toml`); no data is added.

### Real files (pdf.js test corpus)

Characters without white space from `pdfcraft-cli text FILE --page N`, against `pdftotext -enc UTF-8` (Poppler 26.09.0) and PDFium (`get_text_range`):

| File, page | Font | Before | After | Poppler | PDFium |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| issue13147 p1 | Identity-H, CFF, Adobe-Japan1, no `/ToUnicode` | 0 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| vertical p1 | Identity-V, TrueType, Adobe-Japan1, no `/ToUnicode` | 0 | 8 |…

title: fix(render): a page whose MediaBox or CropBox encloses no area shows its content (hayro-syntax patch 38)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A page whose `/MediaBox` or `/CropBox` encloses no area now shows its content, and its text can be extracted.

Before, the visible region of such a page (the crop box intersected with the media box) had no area. The page rendered blank and `pdfcraft-cli text` returned nothing. pdf.js's `boundingBox_invalid.pdf` has three such pages:

| Page | Boxes | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/MediaBox [0 0 0 0]` | blank, no text | "Empty /MediaBox" |
| 2 | `/MediaBox [0 0 800 600]`, `/CropBox [0 0 0 0]` | blank, no text | "Empty /CropBox" |
| 3 | `/MediaBox [0 0 600 800]`, `/CropBox [600 800 1000 1000]` (touches the media box at one corner only) | blank, no text | "Empty /CropBox and /MediaBox intersection" |

**Vendored hayro-syntax patch (38)** changes how `Page` reads its boxes:

- **Media box.** A `/MediaBox` without area is read as a missing one. The page then gets the default size hayro already uses for a missing media box (A4).
- **Crop box.** A `/CropBox` without area, or with no area in common with the media box, is read as a missing one. ISO 32000-2 §14.11.2, Table 33: "Default value: the value of MediaBox".
- **Inherited boxes.** A page's own box without area gives way to an inherited box that has area, before the default is used.
- **Logging.** Each box that is set aside is logged with `warn!`.

pdftotext and PDFium extract the same text from all three pages. PDFium also reports the media box as the page size on page 2.

**Changed test.** `text::tests::text_outside_the_crop_box_is_clipped` pinned "a zero-area or disjoint CropBox leaves an empty visible region". That assertion now checks that such a crop box gives the same text as a page with no CropBox at all. Its other checks, for text outside a real crop box being clipped at every rotation and UserUnit, are unchanged.

author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

`model_add` now takes a glTF 2.0 file (`.gltf` or `.glb`) as well as U3D and PRC. The scene is converted to a PRC mesh model and embedded with a default view fitted to it. The PRC is checked by reading it back through `pdfcraft-prc`'s own reader, and by eye in Acrobat Reader on a synthetic fixture (below). glTF is what most tools export today (Blender, CAD viewers, web 3D), and neither U3D nor PRC is easy to produce outside CAD. Closes #5789. Refs #1297.

- **prc, a PRC writer** (`write/`): `write_prc(&MeshScene)` writes a node tree of triangle meshes with materials and optional textures as a PRC stream that this crate's own reader parses back.
  - It writes tessellations, product occurrences, colours, materials and (PNG/JPEG) texture pictures.

  - Doubles use the reader's own Huffman table (`acof.rs`): `exponent_code`, test-only until now, is now a cached per-exponent lookup the writer uses.

title: sign: judge the signed page tree, catalog and form by their signed roles
author: benandez
body:
## What this changes

`classify_changes` judges an object changed after signing by the role it held in the signed revision. This extends that to three more roles, and narrows what counts as a form fill:

- **Page-tree nodes.** Every node of the signed page tree, from the catalog's `/Pages` down, is a page-tree node whatever its new version is labelled. A change to one is `pages added or removed`.
- **The catalog.** The signed catalog is judged by the catalog rules by its object number, not by the `/Type` its new version carries.
- **`/AcroForm /Fields`.** A field the signed form listed and the new one no longer lists is `other changes` at every DocMDP level. An entry counts only if it resolves, so one listed under a generation its slot does not accept does not count.
- **Signed widgets.** Changing a signed widget's `/Rect` or `/F` is `page content`: a form fill changes a field's value and appearance, not where its widget sits or whether it shows.

Overlapping open PRs, left to them: #5187 (an existing object judged by its signed role in general) and #5173 (P=1 and later signatures).

title: fix(render): a ToUnicode written with CID ranges gives its text (hayro-interpret patch 85)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Text in a Type 0 font whose `/ToUnicode` is written as a CID CMap now extracts.

ISO 32000-2 §9.10.3 builds a ToUnicode CMap from `beginbfchar` and `beginbfrange`. Word writes some fonts' maps with `begincidchar` and `begincidrange` instead, whose destinations are plain numbers: the Unicode values. pdftotext and PDFium both read those numbers as each code's Unicode value. pdftotext warns "Invalid 'begincidrange' operator in ToUnicode CMap" and then extracts the text anyway.

hayro-interpret already read such a map this way when it looks up glyphs for a substitute (`map_via_unicode`). Text extraction (`char_code_to_unicode`) asked the map only for bf entries, so every code read as nothing.

**Vendored hayro-interpret patch (85):** when a code has no bf entry, `Type0Font::char_code_to_unicode` takes its CID-map number as its Unicode value, in the same way `map_via_unicode` does.

Real file (pdf.js `issue9367.pdf`, a Word invoice in Tahoma, not committed):

| Page | Before | After | pdftotext |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 characters | 1,852 non-space characters: "RECHNUNG / SZÁMLA, Rechnungsnummer / Sz.szám, …, Nagykőrösi út 351" | 1,852 non-space characters |

The non-space character counts match pdftotext's character for character.

## Related work

- **#6353** (ours, hayro-interpret patch 84) adds the next step in the same function, `Type0Font::char_code_to_unicode`: for a font of an Adobe collection, a code `/ToUnicode` gives nothing for reads through the collection's UCS2 CMap. This PR widens what the `/ToUnicode` step itself reads, so its CID-range numbers come first. Both change the same lines; whichever merges second folds in the other, keeping the order bf entries → CID-range numbers → UCS2 CMap.

author: benandez
body:
## What this changes

`classify_changes` decides whether changes made after a signature are permitted under its DocMDP level. It compared each slot's newest object with the signed one, and keyed signed roles by the reference as written. This PR makes the comparison follow what a reader resolves, and keeps each object's signed role:

- **Generations.** A slot whose set of accepted generations differs from the signed revision's is refused. Other readers can follow signed references back to an older revision or another alias, so the newest object isn't provably what they display. The one exception: a damaged slot rewritten cleanly with fewer generations, when nothing in the signed revision refers to a generation it dropped. That case needs a new cos API, `Document::accepted_generations`.
- **Roles by object number.** Pages, annotation arrays, content, resources, `/Info`, XMP and XFA packets are keyed by object number, so a repaired generation alias is the same object. A resource reached both as a container and as drawn content keeps the drawn role.
- **Signed widgets stay widgets.** Changing a signed field's or widget's `/Subtype` or `/FT` is `other changes`. Value, appearance and signature changes are still allowed.
- **Annotation lists.**
  - Compared by the entries that resolve.
  - A widget removed from a signed page, inline or indirect, or moved or copied to another page, is `other changes`.
  - The same annotations listed through a new array object are no change; reordering them is a comment change.
  - Expanding annotation lists is capped per classification, and past the cap the change is refused.

Overlaps #6358, which also changes `changes.rs`. Whichever merges second needs a rebase.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign -p pdfcraft-cos -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign`: 38 unit, 124 integration
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos`: all suites pass

title: fix(render): preserve barcode regions during scan smoothing
author: ishveet
body:
## Summary

Preserve barcode readability on scanned PDF pages while retaining the text smoothing introduced by #3858. This PR detects **QR, Code 128, EAN-13 and UPC-A**, validates complete image-local ink and quiet zones, and restores sharp source pixels inside confirmed regions. Surrounding scanned text remains smoothed. No user preference is added.

## Changes

- Bounded image-local detection, checksum/payload validation and pixel-derived region reconstruction; decoder point boxes are not treated as complete protection rectangles.
- Preserve identical payloads at different physical locations, continue bounded search after rejected candidates, and include extended retail guard bars.
- Deterministic page admission and fixed per-image shares across image order, tiles and cache history; incomplete nested traversal is never cached as successful admission.
- Active viewer cancellation, consistent JPX detection-raster selection, conservative fallback and bounded positive/negative caches.
- Reuse exact cached pixels before RGBA expansion; allocate grayscale error strings only on failure; materialize scan rows with checked source slices/strides rather than repeated per-pixel coordinate checks.
- Fit Code128 module pitch using complete checksum-framed symbol geometry to improve low-resolution recognition without raising acceptance tolerances.
- Charge previously uncounted QR finder reads (49 per finder) and both inspected pixels per QR grid comparison, including cooperative cancellation/deadline checks; retain existing bounded region and image-wide fallback policies.

title: sign: under no-changes certification, only invisible document timestamps may follow
author: benandez
body:
## What this changes

Under DocMDP P=1 ("no changes allowed", ISO 32000-2 §12.8.2.2) `classify_changes` allowed any change it classified as a signature, at every level. So a document received with a no-changes certification could be re-signed, or have a signature widget added that paints over the signed page, and the certification still validated as `Valid`, `Allowed(["signature"])`.

P=1 now permits only validation data to follow: the document security store (unchanged), and document timestamps added for PAdES long-term archiving (§12.8.5), which draw nothing. A signature `doc` gained or changed since the signed revision breaks the certification unless it is an **invisible document timestamp** — a `/SubFilter /ETSI.RFC3161` value in a widget with no positive-area `/Rect`, or the Hidden/NoView flag set.

The check judges the signature objects themselves, not the `/AcroForm /Fields` listing, so a widget with no `/T`, or one reached only through a page's `/Annots`, is covered. P=2, P=3 and approval signatures are untouched.

This supersedes the P=1 part of #5173 (same author's approach, which keyed off the field listing and so missed `/T`-less fields, orphan widgets, visible widgets and unsigned widgets); its `/Perms` change handling is not duplicated here. Credit to #5173 for the direction.

title: M5: a text markup, line, polyline, polygon or ink comment whose points reach past its Rect is drawn through them (view.render-annotation-appearances)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A comment without an appearance of its own is now drawn where its points are when its `/Rect` doesn't contain them. Before, nothing showed. This covers:

- highlights, underlines, strikeouts and squigglies, through their `/QuadPoints` (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.10, Table 182: "the coordinates of n quadrilaterals in default user space");
- lines, through `/L` (§12.5.6.7, Table 178: "the starting and ending coordinates of the line in default user space") and their leader lines;
- polylines and polygons, through `/Vertices` (§12.5.6.9, Table 181: "the alternating horizontal and vertical coordinates, respectively, of each vertex, in default user space");
- ink, through `/InkList` (§12.5.6.13, Table 185: "an array of n arrays, each representing a stroked path").

§12.5.5: an appearance is mapped onto the annotation's `/Rect`. PdfCraft draws a display appearance for comments that have none (`pdfcraft-annot::with_missing_appearances`), and gave it `/BBox = /Rect`. When the file's `/Rect` lies beside what the points describe, the drawing fell outside the box and was cut off.

- **Where:** `pdfcraft-annot`. The new `point_reach` returns the `/Rect` grown to take in the points, or `None` when they already fit.
  - Once a point lies outside `/Rect`, the box also takes in half the border width, line endings (`/LE`) and a polygon's cloudy border (§12.5.4), so the strokes are not cut at their edge.
  - The box grows no further than the crop box (§14.11.2). More than 10,000 quadrilaterals, or 40,000 points, keep `/Rect`.
  - The appearance's box uses it (`appearance_context`), and `apply_appearance` writes it as the `/Rect` the appearance is mapped onto, as it already does for note icons.
- **Saved with an edit:** the same drawing runs when PdfCraft redraws a comment's appearance during an edit (a restyle, for example), so a `/Rect` that didn't hold the comment's points is saved widened to take them in, together with the new appearance.
- **Untouched:** a comment w…

author: mtlcl410

title: M9: add an ID Austria desktop signing preview
author: xfects
body:
## What this changes

Adds a desktop **ID Austria / A-Trust signing preview** through the public Security Layer endpoint, with an installed Chromium/Chrome/Edge browser showing the provider's original authorization pages. No application backend, developer client ID, API key or provider account registration is configured. Users still need an activated personal signing identity and explicitly consent to sending the entire prepared PDF to A-Trust.

The existing digital-signature dialog gains provider selection, visible/invisible placement, keyboard geometry controls and existing custom graphics. Immutable PDF preparation and strict external-CMS completion are shared by the engine, GUI and five opt-in automation tools (`sign_providers`, `sign_begin`, `sign_status`, `sign_finish`, `sign_cancel`). Returned CMS signatures must match the exact PDF digest, certificate/ESS binding and supported modern algorithms. Document edits/reloads invalidate pending results. Signing saves a new copy atomically, and a write failure can reuse the verified result without another authorization. Cancellation closes only the operation's private browser. P=1 certification, re-certification and read-only target fields are refused before upload. Browser control uses inherited private pipes, never a debugging TCP port; login DOM, credentials and authentication requests are not read or filled.

Refs #2596. This is a separate Security Layer adapter; CSC/Aruba work in #4045 is untouched. PDF-Over was assessed through its public documentation and licensing; no implementation code or assets were reused. title: M10: read Thai scans with an installed Tesseract
author: dajim10
body:
## What this changes

Scanned Thai can now be read and searched, through an installed Tesseract with its `tha` data.

- **Thai is offered.** The dialog, OCR Verify and the tools took their languages from the `ocrs` table, which holds only English, so no Tesseract language could be chosen. The engine now has its own `LANGUAGES` table (`en`, `th`), and `tha` joins the Tesseract allow-list.
- **Thai goes to Tesseract alone.** The built-in models would read it as Latin letters and report success, so `needs_tesseract` keeps them out, including from the Automatic ensemble.

title: sign: land the still-valid parts of #6358, #5187 and #5173
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Rebases the remaining signed-structure work onto `9afa1266` (after #6361 and #6364) and lands only the parts that are still true against the current classifier. Commit authors are preserved.

**From #6358 (@benandez).** Signed page-tree nodes and `/Kids` arrays of their own are page-tree changes; the signed catalog and an indirect `/AcroForm` are judged by their object number; a field dropped from `/Fields` is no permitted change at any level; a signed widget's `/Rect` or `/F` is page content.

**From #5187 (@LetoCoder26).** An existing object is judged by the role it had when signed, so an indirect `/OCProperties` rewritten with added form or annotation keys is still "other changes". **From #5173 (@LetoCoder26).** Under DocMDP P=1, the catalog's `/Perms` compared by content is a structure change, including an indirect `/Perms` rewritten in place. Its `later_approval_signature` predicate is not carried: #6364 replaces it with the object-based `only_invisible_timestamps_added` check, so only the `/Perms` rule and its tests land.

The P=1 gate that #6364 added is now in `only_validation_data` (split out to stay inside the crate's `clippy::cognitive_complexity` bound).

title: M7: open context menus without probing the system clipboard (#6169)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Copy followed by opening a page context menu could enter a synchronous native clipboard read on the UI thread and deadlock while PdfCraft owned the selection. Menu availability now performs no native read and offers image Paste optimistically.

Application-side Paste, the Ctrl+V fallback and Create from Clipboard read on a worker. The UI waits at most one second on Linux/BSD or five seconds on Windows/macOS, then shows “The clipboard isn't responding” and detaches the worker. Clipboard access uses `try_lock`, so a stuck reader cannot freeze later image/file Copy. Timeouts do not modify the document or paste a stale cached image; late worker results are discarded.

Windows review follow-up: austin62jake measured a successful 4000×4000 image read at up to 1.07 seconds. The five-second Windows/macOS budget gives headroom for these eager-data clipboard backends, while the one-second Linux/BSD selection-owner bound is retained. The UI can pause for the selected finite budget on an explicit action; menu opening remains probe-free. No Windows/macOS runtime result is claimed from the Linux-only follow-up checks.

Refs #6169.

Create from Clipboard falls back to readable text when the clipboard image is invalid (pre-existing behaviour, moved here).
