title: fix(clipboard): a right-click after Copy no longer reads the window's own selection back (#6169)
author: simonhull
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6169: after copying text in PdfCraft, a right-click in the document froze the app for good on Wayland.

**Cause**
- **The right-click check:** a right-click decides whether "Paste image" is enabled by reading the system clipboard on the UI thread (`document_area` → `can_paste_image` → `os_clipboard::for_image_paste` → `has_text` → arboard `get_text`).
- **Who serves it:** after a Copy, the selection is the text this window copied through egui, and the window's own event loop serves it. That is this same thread.
- **The deadlock:** the read waits for an answer only the blocked thread could give. arboard's Wayland read has no timeout, so the thread waits forever.
- **The evidence matches:** @Thaer99ob's diagnosis on the issue found the main thread in `read()` on the clipboard pipe, and `wl-paste` from outside hanging too once frozen.
- **Other UI-thread paths could do the same:**
  - Paste (⌘V) checks for text with `has_text()`.
  - Paste Image reads the clipboard through `for_image_paste()`.
  - Create ▸ Clipboard reads it through `read_clipboard()`.

**Fix: the app no longer reads back what it copied itself.** `PdfCraftApp::own_clipboard_text` remembers the text this window last copied through egui, for as long as it can still be what the system clipboard holds.
- **Set at the end of every frame** (`note_own_clipboard`, next to `finish_document_copy`) from the frame's `OutputCommand::CopyText`. That catches every text copy: the floating bar's Copy, Edit ▸ Copy, a text field's ⌘C, and a whole-document copy.
- **Forgotten** once the window loses focus (only then can another app replace the clipboard), on an empty copy, and when PdfCraft itself puts an image or a file there through arboard (Copy Image, Copy as file, the Snapshot tool).
- **Read first everywhere:** while it is set, the four paths above answer from it and never open the system clipboard.
  - Paste Image is disabled, since text supersedes an image, as `for_image_paste` already…

title: M10: a layer the document marks screen-only stays off the printed sheet (print.print-ready-pdf)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A layer that the document sets to print differently from how it shows now prints that way. A layer marked "on screen, not on paper" (`/Usage /Print /PrintState /OFF`) stays off the printed sheet, and one marked "on paper only" (`/PrintState /ON`) prints. Before, the print used the layers as they are shown.

**Basis.** ISO 32000-2 §8.11.4.3 (Table 99, `AS`) and §8.11.4.4 (Table 101):
- The default configuration's `/AS` holds usage application dictionaries that "specify how interactive PDF processors shall … automatically set the state of optional content groups" for an event.
- For the `Print` event and the `Print` category, a group's recommended state is its `/Usage /Print /PrintState`. "If all the entries yield a recommended state of ON, the group's state shall be set to ON; otherwise, its state shall be set to OFF."

**The change** (`pdfcraft-engine`, `layers.rs`):
- `print_layer_states` starts from the layers as shown (the Layers panel's choices, or the default configuration) and applies every `/AS` entry whose `/Event` is `/Print` and whose `/Category` includes `/Print`. title: fix(cos): a full save refuses an unreadable reachable object
author: mertkayacs
body:
## What this changes

A full save walked the object graph with the lenient reader, which turns any read error into `null`. So when an object that is still referenced can't be parsed, Save As and the other full rewrites wrote `null` in its place and the data was gone without any notice. The traversal now uses the checked reader. For a document that opened without reconstruction, the save fails with `object 3 could not be read; full save stopped instead of writing it as null` (the test's object) and the open document keeps its original bytes.

Save on such a document always does a full rewrite, so plain Save keeps working there. When open rebuilds a missing page tree (#1656) and the rebuild fails, the error now goes into the repair log, and the document opens as before.

Members of a freed, replaced or absent object stream are still written as `null`, as `a_freed_object_stream_is_not_found_by_its_header` expects. An incremental save of a document that opened without reconstruction still works and keeps the original bytes as its prefix.

title: M1: a V4 RC4 file with a 40- or 48-bit key reads and saves (#6397)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6397.

A `/V 4` document whose RC4 crypt filter has a 40- or 48-bit key, as Acrobat writes it, now reads and saves. Before, the page showed, but Save As failed with "the edited document could not be reopened: the file is not a readable PDF: no readable page tree or cross-reference data was found".

**Why.** For such a file, Acrobat extends the 5- or 6-byte file key to 16 bytes with zeros before it derives each object's key. ISO 32000-2 §7.6.3.2, Algorithm 1, uses the n-byte key as it is.
- The renderer's vendored `hayro-syntax` (`crypto/mod.rs`, "See pdf.js issue 19484") already pads such a key, so the page showed.
- `pdfcraft-crypt`, which `pdfcraft-cos` reads and writes with, did not. The object streams didn't decrypt and `/Pages` read as null. A full save then wrote the catalog with `/Pages null`, and the check that reopens a saved file refused it.

**The change.** `SecurityHandler::object_key` (`pdfcraft-crypt`) extends a file key shorter than 16 bytes with zeros for an RC4 crypt filter under `/V 4`, before Algorithm 1, as the renderer does for these files.
- Reading and writing go through the same function, so a save writes each object with the key it was read with.
- Authentication, `/P` and the file key itself are unchanged.
- AES-128 (`AESV2`) keys are left as derived: the standard has them 128 bits (Table 25), and Acrobat's extension is only seen with RC4.
- Every key PdfCraft writes under `/V 4` is 16 bytes already (AES-128), so its own files are unaffected. `/V 1` and `/V 2` files keep Algorithm 1 as the standard has it.
- The function's comment now gives Algorithm 1 its own clause (§7.6.3.2) and Algorithm 1.A §7.6.3.3.

This departs from the text of the standard. It follows how Acrobat writes these files and how the renderer, pdf.js (issue 19484) and Apache PDFBox (PDFBOX-5955) read them. PDFium, Poppler and MuPDF don't open them at all.

title: M7: Replace image keeps a grouped photo's frame
author: cst-art
body:
## What this changes

Edit a PDF ▸ right-click ▸ **Replace image** was greyed out for a picture inside grouped Form artwork. That is common: a photo cropped to a circle, as layout and office tools export it, is a Form that clips and draws one image. The only way to swap it was to delete it and place a new image, which loses the frame and the exact position.

Now a group that draws **exactly one** raster picture, directly or through nested Forms, can be replaced:

- The replacement goes into a **copy** of the group (and of each nested Form on the way), with only that one `/XObject` resource changed. The page's `Do` then draws the copy. The group's content stream (its clip, placement and anything else it paints) is reused unchanged, so the new picture sits in the old one's frame and keeps its round crop.
- The original Form is left as it was, because other pages or placements may share it.
- What counts is what the group **draws**: its `Do` operators, followed into nested Forms, not what its resources list. A picture drawn twice (or inside a Form drawn twice) counts twice, an unused resource doesn't count, a picture-free Form drawn twice (a frame) is fine, and an inline image counts as a picture that can't be swapped. A group that draws no picture or more than one is refused (the menu item stays greyed), so Replace never has to guess which picture you meant. So is one nested past the depth limit or drawing itself, since what lies beyond is unknown.
- A Form that a file marks as an added image is replaced through the same Form copy, so it keeps its frame.
- `PageImage` gains `replaceable`, which the image context menu now uses instead of `!is_form`. The engine checks the same flag before it embeds the new file, so a refusal adds no object.
- The `image_edit` automation tool already reaches this path through `Edit::EditPageImage { change: Replace }`, so it works headlessly too.

title: M12: headless orbit navigation for 3D models
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

`prc-render` gains a GUI-free `nav` module, the navigation half of a 3D viewer, which a viewer feeds input into and reads a `Camera` back from:

- **`Orbit`**: yaw, pitch, zoom and pan about an up axis and a Front.
  - **Named views:** `iso`, `front`, `right`, `top`, `back`, or any direction with its own up.
  - **Constant size:** every direction frames the model the same, a sphere fit on the farthest drawn vertex (`reach`), so turning it never makes it jump in size. Widening the picture doesn't change it either.
  - **Zoom at the pointer:** a wheel zoom keeps the point under the pointer still.
  - **Anchored turn:** a pressed point can be anchored, so the view turns about it and the picture doesn't jump when the turn starts.
  - **Limits:** pitch stops just short of the up axis, and pan and zoom are bounded. Non-finite input is ignored, and a model outside the finite range is a `RenderError`, not a panic.
- **`Axis` / `Upright`**: the up axis (±x, ±y, ±z) and the Front direction (any axis perpendicular to up), with the default Front for y-up models.

`model_render` takes an `orbit` object, so the navigation is reachable headlessly. The object is `{view, up, front, turn, zoom, zoom_at, pan}`, all optional. It replaces `direction`, and passing both is an error. An unknown key or a bad value is a clear error naming `orbit`.

**Deliberately not in this PR:**
- **On-screen controls:** nothing is wired to a viewer yet, so there is no UI change.
- **Walk and fly:** these need a pick index for collision, and come as a follow-up.
- **Tap-to-hide controls and a fisheye lens:** both are left out on purpose; they aren't ready.

title: fix(render): a Type 3 glyph shown again isn't decoded again (hayro-interpret patch 87)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A Type 3 glyph shown many times on a page is decoded once instead of once per copy, so a page that uses a Type 3 font as a fill pattern renders about twice as fast.

**The need.** The renderer ran every copy of a Type 3 glyph by decoding its glyph procedure again (`Type3::render_glyph` called `decode_content` on the `/CharProcs` stream each time). A Type 3 font used as a fill pattern draws one glyph a very large number of times.

**Basis.** ISO 32000-2 §9.6.4: a Type 3 glyph is described by its content stream in `/CharProcs`, painted each time the glyph is shown. Nothing in it changes between copies, so decoding it once gives the same glyph.

**The change** (vendored `hayro-interpret`, patch 87):
- `Type3::decoded_proc` keeps each procedure it decoded, by glyph name, and later copies use that.
- A procedure over 64 KiB isn't kept. Fonts live in `InterpreterCache` as long as the cache, and a document can have thousands of Type 3 fonts, so the bound is on the cache: its fonts keep at most 32 MiB together (`MAX_CACHED_TYPE3_PROCS`), each kept procedure counting its name and 64 bytes besides its bytes.
- A procedure holds its bytes within the page's content budget while its glyph is painted, whether it was decoded now or kept (`context::hold_content`), so once the budget is spent a page skips the same glyphs either way. One decoded with no more than 64 KiB of budget left, which the budget may have cut short, isn't kept.
- `InterpreterCache::type3_proc_decodes` counts procedures decoded, as `decoded_image_decodes` (patch 32) and `icc_profile_reads` (patch 48) do.
- `vendor/README.md` records patch 87 and its test.

### Real file (PDFBox issue tracker)

`c4ce2fcd_69.pdf`, attached to PDFBOX-956: a one-page document whose Type 3 font `/F44` has one glyph, an 8 × 8 image mask, shown in 10,725 strings of about 60 copies each, about 650,000 glyphs in all. With a release `pdfcraft-cli render --page 1 --dpi 72`:

title: M12: picking — the model point under an image position
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

`prc-render` gains picking, the inverse of the projection `render` draws with:

- **`Camera::ray_through(x, y, width, height)`**: the ray through an image position (pixel (i, j)'s centre is (i + 0.5, j + 0.5)), under perspective or orthographic projection. A zero size, a non-finite position or a ray that would overflow is a `RenderError`.
- **`pick(&[WorldMesh], &Ray) -> Option<Hit>`**: the nearest triangle on the ray, with its mesh, triangle, point, unit face normal and distance.
  - It matches what `render` draws: both faces count, triangles in front of the perspective near plane are not hit, and a fully transparent triangle is passed through.
  - A tie goes to the lower (mesh, triangle).
- **`PickIndex`**: a bounding-volume hierarchy over a model's triangles. It gives the same answers as `pick`, for many picks on one model (hover, measuring, collision). `pick_where` adds a distance limit and a mesh filter, for hidden parts.

`automation` gains **`model_pick`**. It takes `model_render`'s arguments plus `at`, a pixel position `[x, y]`. It returns `{"hit": {mesh, triangle, point, normal, distance}}`, with mesh and triangle counted from 1, or `{"hit": null}` over the background. `model_render`'s camera setup moves into a shared `model_view`, so both tools frame the model identically. A position outside the picture is an error naming `at`.

**Deliberately not in this PR:** no on-screen picking (there is no viewer UI yet), and no walk or fly. Walk and fly use `PickIndex` for collision and come next.

Adds a **Measurements** panel to the navigation rail, next to Comments, Bookmarks, Layers and Attachments.

title: M7: crop's Done and Cancel take their clicks over the text under the picture (edit.image-crop)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6420.

In Edit PDF, a picture in crop mode shows its **Done**, **Cancel** and **Remove Crop** pills just below the crop box (above it near the page's bottom edge). When the picture sits right above a paragraph, the pills lie on that paragraph's text, and clicking them did nothing: the paragraph's outline lit up instead and crop mode stayed open.

Why: the router already gives every press on the cropped picture's page to the picture (`edit_text_ui::crop_hit`). But egui reports a click on the release frame, and by then the router has let the press go. On that frame Edit text's paragraph input ran first, said it had used the pointer, and the picture's input, given `allow_interaction = false` because of that, dropped the pill's `clicked()`.

Now, while a picture on the page is being cropped, the page's paragraph input gets no interaction and the picture's input keeps it, on every frame of crop mode. The check reads the crop state directly rather than calling the hit test again, so the router guard (`page_modules_act_on_a_press_only_through_the_router`) still holds.

It checks that each pill lies on the text's line, then clicks **Cancel** (crop mode ends, nothing applied) and **Done** (crop mode ends, the crop is applied). title: M4: ⌘C, ⌘X and ⌘V copy, cut and paste pages in the Pages panel, also into another document
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

The Pages panel's right-click menu has Copy, Cut and Paste after, and the page grid (Organize pages) takes ⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘V for them. In the Pages panel the keys did nothing for pages: a thumbnail clicked in one tab, ⌘C, then a thumbnail clicked in another tab and ⌘V left both documents as they were. That is the usual way to move a page from one open file to another, and it only worked through the menus.

Now, while the Pages panel has the keyboard (a thumbnail was clicked) or the pointer is over it with nothing else holding the keyboard (the rule its Delete key already follows), ⌘C, ⌘X and ⌘V (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) run `page.copy`, `page.cut` and `page.paste` on the selected pages (the current one when none is):

- The copied pages are the app's (`page_clipboard`), so they paste into another tab, or another window, after the page selected there. Within one document it is a duplicate, as from the menu.
- The desktop delivers the keys as clipboard events (`Event::Copy`, `Event::Cut`, and `Event::Paste` with whatever text the system clipboard holds); in the panel a paste of anything pastes the copied pages, and nothing reaches the page underneath: no comment, picture or text paste.
- Copying pages (by key or from the menus) puts a line naming them on the system clipboard ("1 page from b.pdf"), as copying comments puts their XFDF there. On X11 and Windows egui-winit turns ⌘V into a paste of the clipboard's contents and drops the key when the clipboard holds nothing, so without it ⌘V did nothing after copying pages into an empty clipboard. This also makes the page grid's ⌘V reliable.
- Cut and Paste stay off where the document may not be assembled (the commands' own availability). The page grid keeps its own handling.

The keys are read where the other clipboard shortcuts are (`clipboard_keys`, before the panels draw), so the panel's rect is the one it was last drawn at, as for dropped files.

title: feat(cos): Document::canonical_ref, reference acceptance without loading
author: smittie2000
body:
## What this changes

Adds `pdfcraft_cos::Document::canonical_ref(r) -> Option<ObjRef>`: whether cos accepts reference `r`, and if so the object's number at its current `generation`.

Since #1143, a reference resolves only at a generation the slot accepts:
- the live generation;
- either generation of a slot whose damaged xref row was repaired;
- 0 inside an object stream.

`accepted_generations(num)` lists those for one object number. `canonical_ref` asks the same question of a single reference:
- It doesn't allocate, and it doesn't load the object, so an accepted literal `null` or an unreadable object still gives `Some`.
- It answers `None` for a stale, freed or absent reference.

The result is canonical within one snapshot only. Another revision may hold the same object at another generation, so compare across revisions by object number after each snapshot has accepted its own reference. The README and the doc comment say so.

Code that compares page or annotation references by `==` (destinations, `/P`, page lookup) can use it to compare references within one document without being fooled by a stale or alias generation.

- The existing `accepted_generations_are_the_generations_get_resolves` now also asserts, for every slot kind and generation 0–7, that `canonical_ref(..).is_some()` equals `accepted_generations(..).contains(..)`. The two APIs can't drift apart.

title: refactor(cos): read numeric arrays without losing positions
author: smittie2000
body:
## What this changes

Adds `pdfcraft_cos::numbers::NumberReader`, which reads numbers out of the object graph without losing their places.

Today numeric arrays are read in about twenty places with `filter_map(as_f64)`. That drops a bad entry and shifts every later one into its place. A `/QuadPoints` whose first corner is `null`, `[null 110 40 110 …]`, comes back as seven numbers. Callers then either skip the quad or read 0 for it, and they can't tell what was wrong or where.

`NumberReader` reads three shapes:
- **One finite number:** integer or real, after following references.
- **An exact `tuple::<N>`:** the length is checked before any entry is resolved.
- **A capped `sequence`:** every original slot keeps its own `Result`. An array past the cap (`MAX_NUMERIC_ENTRIES`, 65,536) is an error with no usable prefix, and the result `Vec` is reserved fallibly.

It follows references through `resolve`'s bounded chain. A chain that still ends in a reference (a cycle, or more than 32 hops) is `UnresolvedReference`.

A direct array is read in place, not cloned, so a huge one is rejected without being copied. `NumberReader::direct()` reads direct values only, for inputs that have no document.

It knows nothing of rectangles or colours, and it repairs nothing; interpretation is model's job. No caller changes here.

The README also said `resolve` follows one reference. It follows a chain of up to 32 more (since #5548), and now says so.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

title: fix(model): one bounded page-tree walk that fails closed at its limits
author: smittie2000
body:
> **Depends on #6429** (`Document::canonical_ref`); its commit is included here until it merges.

## What this changes

model's page access goes through one bounded walk instead of the unbounded recursion behind `pages()`:
- `PageNodes` walks every node of the page tree.
- `PageLeaves` gives just the pages.

**Bounded.** The walk stops at:
- `MAX_PAGE_TREE_NODES` (1,000,000) nodes;
- `MAX_KIDS_ENTRIES` (4,000,000) `/Kids` entries;
- `MAX_INHERITED_COPIES` inherited values.

Past a limit it yields `PageTreeLimit`. It never hands back the pages before the cut as if they were all of them.

**Cycles and shared arrays.** Cycles end at a seen set. A `/Kids` array object shared by several nodes is read once, so a hostile file can't make the walk re-read one array millions of times.

**Identity defers to cos.** A reference counts as a page only when cos accepts it (`canonical_ref`). Pages are told apart by object number at their canonical generation.

**One leaf rule.** A `/Type /Pages` node without `/Kids` lists no pages.

**Inherited attributes** (`/Resources`, `/MediaBox`, `/CropBox`, `/Rotate`) come from the nodes the walk came down through. `PageNode::inherited` and `inherited_from` expose them.

New fallible API for code that changes a document and must see every page or refuse:
- `try_pages`, `page(doc, i)`, `page_by_ref` and `page_refs`;
- `PageLeaves::nth_page` and `page_count`.

`pages()` keeps its signature as the lenient reader for display. `Limits` and `with_limits`, behind the `test-support` feature, lower the limits on one thread so callers can test how they handle a limit.

The public API change is additive only. Every crate that depends on model builds and passes its tests unchanged (below).

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos -p pdfcraft-model --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

title: M3: End shows the end of the document, the last page down to its bottom (view.page-navigation)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6434.

In a document of several pages, **End** went to the top of the last page, as Go to Last Page does. When the last page is taller than the window (Fit Width, or any zoom past Fit Page), its bottom stayed out of view, so End did not reach the end of the document.

End now scrolls as far as the document goes: to the last page's bottom edge. This is what browsers and word processors do with End.

How it works:

- A new `DocView::go_to_end` does what `go_to_page(last)` does (the view history, the current page) and then asks for the scroll at the last page's bottom (`goto` fraction 1.0).
- Pending scrolls are clamped to the content's maximum when applied, so a short last page still ends where the content ends.
- Home is unchanged: it shows the first page's top.
- Go to Last Page is unchanged: it still shows the last page's top.
- Shift+Ctrl (Shift+⌘ on macOS) with ↑ / ↓ or Page Up / Page Down now act as Home and End, and the Keyboard shortcuts dialog lists them with Home / End. Before, Shift+Ctrl+Page Up / Page Down turned one page, the same as Ctrl+Page Up / Page Down, because the Shift was ignored; now they go to the start or the end of the document.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`: 793 lib + 1485 integration tests pass (and the four smaller targets)
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`

New test `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/viewer.rs::end_shows_the_bottom_of_the_last_page`. On a five-page synthetic document at Fit Width, a page is taller than the window. The test presses End and checks that the current page is the last one and that its bottom edge sits at the window's bottom. Then Home brings back the first page's top at the window's top.

**Seen failing first:** with `navigation.rs` reverted, the last page's bottom ends up 600 px below the window, because only its top is shown.

title: xml: one bounded XML parse for the workspace (pdfcraft-xml)
author: smittie2000
body:
## What this changes

Every XML parse in PdfCraft now goes through one bounded parse in a new standalone crate, `pdfcraft-xml` (L0). That covers XFA templates, data files and datasets, XFDF and XML form data, and the PDF/A identification read from XMP. clippy refuses direct roxmltree parses anywhere else (`disallowed-methods`).

**Why: roxmltree 0.21.2 has quadratic loops, and xfa and xfdf only bounded depth.** These were measured against roxmltree directly (release build), not through PdfCraft:

| input | size | parse time |
|---|---|---|
| 60,000 attributes on one element | 633 KB | 9.8 s |
| 60,000 namespace declarations on one element | 1 MB | 9.2 s |
| root declaring 2,000 namespaces, 20,000 children declaring one each | 436 KB | 156 s |
| 11,000 prefixed attributes sharing one 100 KB namespace URI (extrapolated from smaller runs) | 221 KB | ~10 min |

xfa and xfdf checked nesting depth before parsing, but nothing else, so an XFA packet in a PDF or an imported data file in one of these shapes holds the parser for that long. preflight capped attributes per tag and in total, but those caps refused cheap packets and still admitted expensive ones. One example: a 1,024-deep chain of elements each declaring four prefixes is about 5·10⁹ comparisons. I found no existing issue or PR for this.

**How the bound works:** one linear scan, before roxmltree sees the text, refuses three things:
- a DTD;
- nesting past 1,024;
- more than a budget of roxmltree's superlinear work.

The work model follows roxmltree's own data structures and loops (`crates/xml/src/scan.rs` documents it loop by loop):
- It keeps an upper bound on roxmltree's in-scope namespace list. That includes repeated default namespace declarations, which roxmltree doesn't deduplicate, and attributes like `p:xmlns`, which roxmltree reads as default declarations.
- It stops collecting a tag's declarations once their duplicate check alone is over the budget, so its memory is bounded by the budget, not the input.

title: M2: a page past the rasterizer's coverage renders what fitted instead of failing (view.render-error-isolation)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Form XObjects may draw other form XObjects (ISO 32000-2 §8.10.1), so a page can paint the same content an exponential number of times. The page in a public test file attached to PDFBOX-5415 is 22 nested forms, each drawing the next twice: about 4.2 million fills of one vector drawing. The existing nested-paint budget (`MAX_NESTED_PAINTS`, hayro-interpret) stops the walk at 50,000 nested paints. That is still millions of path fills, each with its own coverage.

vello_cpu keeps every path's coverage (alpha) values in one buffer until the scene is rasterized, and a strip packs its index into that buffer in 31 bits, with `Strip::new` asserting it fits. On this page the buffer passed 2^31 values at about 7 GB, `Strip::new` panicked (`alpha_idx` too large), and the page failed to render.

Now the rasterizer stops taking paths once it has no room for one more, renders what fitted, and the page says content was left out. The pieces, all vendored patches:

- **vello_common (2):** `StripStorage::room_for_path{,_within}` says whether one more path's coverage still fits below 2^31 values, or below a smaller limit. A path's coverage is at most the whole surface; it is counted twice to be safe.
- **vello_cpu (1):** the single-threaded dispatcher leaves out fills, strokes, fast rectangles and layer clips once there is no room. It records this (`RenderContext::coverage_full`, cleared by `reset`) and can be kept to fewer values (`set_max_coverage`). PdfCraft renders single-threaded; the multi-threaded dispatcher is unchanged.
- **hayro (31):** `RenderSettings::max_coverage` (default `None`, the 2^31 limit) passes a limit down. A page whose paths were left out reports `InterpreterWarning::ContentTruncated`, which PdfCraft already shows as "content past the page's safety budget was skipped".

The largest raster PdfCraft draws is 64 million pixels. Twice that is far below 2^31, so an ordinary page always has room.

**On the page that panicked**, rendered at 72 dpi…

title: M7: added text can be gray or CMYK, painted with g / k, so print black stays 100 K (edit.add-text)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6440.

`page_add_text` only took `#RRGGBB` or a colour name, so text added to a CMYK print file was painted as DeviceRGB (`0 0 0 rg`). A last-minute proof line then printed as rich black instead of 100 K.

`page_add_text` and `content_update` now also take:

- `gray`: a level from 0 (black) to 1 (white). The text is painted in DeviceGray with `g` (ISO 32000-2 §8.6.4.2, §8.6.8).
- `cmyk`: `[c, m, y, k]`, each from 0 to 1. The text is painted in DeviceCMYK with `k` (§8.6.4.4, §8.6.8). `cmyk [0, 0, 0, 1]` is 100 K black.

Only one of `color`, `gray` and `cmyk` may be given.

How it works:

- **Model:** `AddedText` gets `ink: Option<Ink>` (`Ink::Gray` / `Ink::Cmyk`, exported by the engine as `TextInk`). `color` stays the RGB look used on screen, derived from the ink by §10.4.2.5 (each colour plus black, from 1).
- **Saving and reopening:** the item's `/PCAdded` parameters keep the ink as `/Ink` (one or four numbers), so it reopens with it. Items written before this have none and read as before.
- **Restyling:** the ink is used only while `color` is still its RGB look. Restyling the text to another colour, from the tools or from the Format panel, paints it in RGB again; the panel needs no change.
- **`content_list`:** reports `ink: { gray }` or `ink: { cmyk }` for such items.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `pdfcraft-edit`, `pdfcraft-engine`, `pdfcraft-automation`, `pdfcraft-ui-egui`
- `cargo test` on the same four crates, all pass
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`

title: M6: a widget whose /Parent names a missing object is a field of its own (form.field-list)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A widget annotation can name a `/Parent` that the file doesn't hold. Some producers write forms with an empty `/Fields` array and widgets whose `/Parent` points at objects that were never written. PdfCraft then treated that missing parent as the widget's field: the widget was adopted through it, its qualified name was built from nothing, and the field disappeared. On a public test file of this kind, 99 of 113 fields were lost.

A reference to an object that doesn't exist is the null object, and a dictionary entry whose value is null is the same as an absent one (ISO 32000-2 §7.3.9 and §7.3.10). So a widget whose `/Parent` doesn't resolve to a dictionary has no parent: it is a root field of its own.

- **Form reader** (`crates/forms/src/read.rs`): a new `parent_of` counts a `/Parent` only when it resolves to a dictionary. Both the walk that adopts unlisted page widgets (`unlisted_root`) and the qualified-name walk use it.
- **Document inspection** (`crates/render/src/inspect/annotations.rs`): `unlisted_field` applies the same rule, so `doc_info`, `form_fields` and the GUI's field list agree.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms` (232 pass) and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render` (477 + 64 pass)
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`

Tests, both on synthetic files:
- `pdfcraft-forms` `tests::a_widget_whose_parent_is_missing_is_a_field_of_its_own`: widgets whose `/Parent` names a missing object are read as fields, and one can be filled and saved.
- `pdfcraft-render` `inspect::tests::a_widget_whose_parent_is_missing_is_listed`.

**Seen failing:** with the fix reverted, the forms test adopts 0 fields where 2 are expected, and the inspection test lists none.

title: M6: a field whose /Kids loop back or name a root field keeps its other kids (form.field-list)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A field's `/Kids` may wrongly list the field itself, a field it descends from, or another root field. One public test file has a radio-button field that lists itself among its kids. Another has two root fields that each list the other.

A kid with `/T` makes its parent a non-terminal field, so these fields were read as having only field children. Those children had already been read, so the walk produced nothing, and the fields and their widgets disappeared from the form.

Root fields have no ancestors (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.3, Table 224), and a child field names its parent with `/Parent` (§12.7.4.1, Table 226). So a `/Kids` entry is now not counted as a child when it is:

- the field itself;
- a field the walk descends from (a loop);
- a root field (one `/Fields` lists) whose `/Parent` doesn't name this field.

The field then keeps its remaining kids, its widgets, and is read as the terminal field it is. The same rule is in both readers:

- **Form reader** (`crates/forms/src/read.rs`): `Seen.roots`, `Seen.path`, `not_a_child`.
- **Document inspection** (`crates/render/src/inspect/annotations.rs`): a `FieldWalk` struct and `not_a_child`.

### Widgets that name the field but are missing from its /Kids

A child names its parent with `/Parent` (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.1, Table 226). A page widget without `/T` whose `/Parent` names a field is now one of that field's widgets even when the field's `/Kids` leave it out. The form reader puts it after the listed kids and counts each widget once. In document inspection, a field with no widget among its kids takes the first page widget that names it.

Measured on two public files from [PDFBOX-4131](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-4131), with widgets counted per field by `form_fields`:

| File | Field | Before | After | MuPDF / PDFium |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fields_loop_kid_is_parent.pdf` | `radio` | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| | `texte1` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

title: Signature validation takes the certification from the catalog
author: oracola91
body:

title: Apply Redactions replaces the recovery snapshot at once
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

`PdfCraftApp::renew_recovery` drops the document's entry (`forget_recovery`) and writes a fresh one (`autosave_now`). The dialog code calls it after each of the three edits succeeds. title: Automation follows a path toward its root before looking anything up
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

In roots-only mode (`--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` without `--root`), `file_access::resolve` made every path absolute and ran `canonicalize` and `symlink_metadata` on it before `inside()` compared it with the root. The wording of a refusal also depended on what exists outside the root: "parent traversal below a folder that doesn't exist" through a missing folder, "outside the read root" through an existing one. With `--root`, `resolve_in_root` probed the joined path with `exists()` and `symlink_metadata` before its check too.

`file_access::follow` now walks an absolute path the way the file system reads it, one name at a time from the top, with links followed. A name is looked up only while the folder it is in is the root, inside it, or one of the root's own parent folders (all already canonical, so `..` means what it means to the file system). Leaving those gives `Toward::Outside` before anything beyond is touched. Another share or a device namespace is still refused by name first (`foreign_share`, #4289). Inside the root, a missing tail and the specific errors stay as they were.

title: Remove Hidden Information unlinks images nothing draws
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Delete Image takes only the `Do` out of the page, and Replace Image adds a new name and leaves the old image listed. Remove Hidden Information only pruned the names its own content pass replaced, so a deleted image stayed in the page's resources and in the full-rewrite save.

Every Remove Hidden Information run, Sanitize included, now unlinks the image and form XObjects that nothing draws from the page-tree resource dictionaries that name them (`interp::unlink_undrawn`). A name stays when anything drawing through the dictionary uses it with `Do` (`names_drawn`): the pages, their annotations' appearances, and every form, tiling pattern, Type 3 glyph and soft-mask group they reach, with `/Resources` of their own or not. Each stream is read once, against one `DecodeBudget::page()`; a page or stream that won't decode, or a spent budget, leaves the dictionary as it is. Unlike `unlink_doomed` this never fails the run. The page-tree walk is now shared with `unlink_doomed` (`resource_holders`).

title: Page copies bring only the form fields on the pages copied
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Extract Pages, Split, Combine and Insert Pages from File copied more of the source's form than the pages chosen. A copied widget followed `/Parent` to its field, and the field's `/Kids` brought every other kid along: fields and widgets on pages that were not chosen, with their values and appearances.

When only some of a document's pages are copied, `import_pages_mapped` now collects, before copying, the annotations on those pages and the fields above each widget (`fields_on`). A copied field keeps only the `/Kids` in that set. The repeated-page copier shares the set, and so does the copier for an annotation's other actions: a SubmitForm, ResetForm or Hide action keeps only the `/Fields` (or `/T`) entries in it. Fields named by text stay. When every page is copied the set is not used, so whole-document Combine and Insert keep every field, widgetless ones included, as before.

Rebased onto current `main`: `Copier` now lives in `import/copy.rs`, so `MAX_COPY_DEPTH` is shared with `import.rs` (`pub(super)`).

This is one of three parts of the fix from private report GHSA-h9rr-3hww-gfxh (see #6450), each sent as its own pull request so each does one thing. The three touch different code and meet only at the end of `crates/organize/src/tests.rs`, where each adds its tests: whichever lands first, I will rebase the others.

author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

`prune_unused_xobjects` (Extract and Split) only filtered the `/XObject` dictionaries it recorded a `Do` for. So a part whose pages draw no XObject kept every image of shared or inherited resources.

Every dictionary the walk meets is now recorded, also when nothing is drawn from it, and a page that is empty or has no `/Contents` is walked too. Such a dictionary is left as it is when it lists a tiling pattern or a soft mask with a group, or a page using it has an annotation appearance: the walk doesn't read those, and PdfCraft's renderer looks a name they don't define up in the page's resources. Their own resources, those of the forms, patterns and groups they list (up to the form depth limit) and those of Type 3 fonts there are left as they are too, also on a page without resources and on content that can't be read. That walk visits shared resources once and stops at `MAX_LEND_WORK` entries, font catalogs it scans included; past that the file is not pruned, as with the other limits. The safety rules on `main` stay as they are: content that can't be read whole keeps its dictionary whole (`unread`), forms nested past the limit or an overlarge glyph graph stop the pruning, and Type 3 glyph resources are not touched.

This is one of three parts of the fix from private report GHSA-h9rr-3hww-gfxh (see #6450), each sent as its own pull request so each does one thing. The other two, #6461 and #6463, are merged; this is the last one.

title: M1: hex digits are read with char::to_digit(16) (#6465)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6465.

Two crates decoded one hexadecimal digit by hand with the same `match` over `b'0'..=b'9' | b'a'..=b'f' | b'A'..=b'F'`:

- `crates/filters/src/asciihex.rs`: `nibble`, used by ASCIIHexDecode (ISO 32000-2 §7.4.2).
- `crates/forms/src/af/script.rs`: `hex4`, the `\uXXXX` reader in the AcroForm script parser.

Both now use `char::from(b).to_digit(16)`. It gives the same value for every hex digit in either case, and `None` for every other byte. `filters` stays standalone (AGENTS.md §5), so each crate makes the `std` call itself rather than sharing a helper. Behaviour is unchanged.

- **#5799** (closed) made this same change in three crates: `hexval` in cos, `nibble` in filters and `hex4` in forms, each to `char::to_digit(16)`. When it was closed, the cos part continued in **#6431** (`hexval`, together with one set of PDF character classes), and the filters and forms parts were left free to pick up. This PR is those two parts, following #5799's approach (`to_digit`, not `from_str_radix`, which accepts a leading `+`) and its exhaustive tests against the old table. title: Add text: gray or CMYK colour, painted with g or k (#6440)
author: ZIDAN44
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6440

`page_add_text` and `content_update` only took `#RRGGBB` or a colour name, so text added to a CMYK print file painted `0 0 0 rg`, rich black on press. They now also take:
- `gray`: a number from 0 to 1, painted with `g`;
- `cmyk`: `[c, m, y, k]`, each 0 to 1, painted with `k` (`[0,0,0,1]` gives `0 0 0 1 k`).

Only one of `color`, `gray` and `cmyk` is allowed per call. An out-of-range value, a wrong length or a non-number is refused, and so is `gray`/`cmyk` on an image.

How it's kept:
- `AddedText` has an `ink` (`Ink::Gray` / `Ink::Cmyk`, exported as `TextInk`) beside `color`, which holds the matching on-screen look (ISO 32000-2 §10.4.2.2 and §10.4.2.5).
- `/PCAdded` keeps `/Color` and adds `/Gray` or `/CMYK` only for ink items, so older files read as before and older builds still show the right colour.
- An ink applies only while `color` still shows its look. Picking another colour, also in the Format panel, drops it for good (no empty Undo step, and it doesn't come back). Picking the ink's own look (black on 100 K) keeps it. `content_update color` always paints in RGB.
- Gray and CMYK values are kept to three decimals, the precision they're painted with, so the stored value, `content_list` and the page agree (gray 0.50049 is kept as 0.5).
- A stored `/CMYK` must be exactly four numbers, checked before any entry is read and without copying the array. A stored ink that's malformed (a non-number inside `/CMYK`, a `/Gray` that isn't a number) or doesn't match its `/Color` (a hand-edited file) is ignored.

RGB text is written byte for byte as before.

This follows the approach described in #6442 by @mtlcl410, closed by its author, written separately here; it also refuses a non-number inside `cmyk`, which that PR's review pointed out.

title: M12: walking through a 3D model, headless
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

`prc-render` gains `nav::Walk`, a first-person camera at a body's eye height, with no GUI in it. It takes inputs (an `Intent` of forward, right, rise and run, plus a time step and `Rules`) and gives back a `Camera`. The model reaches it as a closure giving the nearest hit along a ray, normally `PickIndex::pick`.

- **Solid:** the walker stops at walls and slides along them, and falls onto the floor under it. With no floor under it, it keeps its height.
- **Going up:** it climbs a ramp of up to about 46 degrees at any pace and frame time. Steps depend on `stairs`: on, anything lower than a third of the eye height; off, only a floor seam. It never rises into what is over its head.
- **Ghost:** it flies through everything and rises and sinks as asked. Not level, it flies where it looks.
- **Level:** moving stays horizontal whatever the camera's pitch.
- **Heading and camera turn apart**, so looking aside doesn't change where you walk.
- **Scale:** every distance is a share of the model's radius, except an eye height set in model units.

`automation` gains `walk` on both `model_render` and `model_pick`: `{from, look, up, height, ghost, level, stairs, steps}`. Each step takes `forward`, `right`, `rise`, `run`, `turn`, `look` and `seconds`. It is refused together with `orbit`, `direction` or `perspective`. With no steps, the eye stays at `from`. `model_pick` shares `model_render`'s camera code, so on this stack it takes `orbit` too, and its schema now says so. No test picks through `orbit` yet.

**Deliberately not in this PR:** keys and sticks in the app (there is no viewer UI yet) and the drone and gimbal.

author: oracola91
body:

## What this changes

When a page lists a Type 3 font, `prune_type3_from_resources` (#5197) adds the operators of the page's annotation appearances without resources of their own. Each appearance was checked against the 2,000,000 operator cap on its own, so several under it could add up to far more, and the prune went on with a total no other path allows.

The appearances now share the running total. Passing it refuses the redaction with the same kind of error as the other caps ("redaction could not fully inspect annotation appearances"). Such pages are refused rather than judged on part of what draws through their fonts.

**Reference behaviour.** Not a reference-app question: it is PdfCraft's own resource limit.

title: feat(cos): content_entries, one bounded reading of a page's /Contents
author: smittie2000
body:
## What this changes

Adds `pdfcraft_cos::content_entries`, one bounded reading of a page's `/Contents` (ISO 32000-2 §7.7.3.3: one stream, or an array of them).

Sixteen sites in seven crates turn `/Contents` into a list by hand, and the copies disagree:
- **Reference chains:** five follow one reference with `doc.get` (preflight, sign, edit `added/store.rs` and `place.rs`), so a reference to a reference to the array reads as a single entry. The rest follow `resolve`'s chain, and redaction's verify uses `try_get`.
- **Caps:** only edit caps the array, at 10,000 (`objects.rs`, an error) and at 4,096 (`backdrop.rs`, a read-only prefix). Most clone the array whatever its length.
- **Values that aren't an array:** forms and a11y keep them only when they are a stream; the others keep any value.

`content_entries(doc, page.get(b"Contents"))` returns a `ContentEntries` view:
- **Absent:** no entries.
- **One resolve policy:** the value follows `Document::resolve`'s bounded chain. A chain that still ends in a reference (a cycle, or one too long) is `ContentsError::UnresolvedReference`.
- **An array:** its entries, borrowed in place. A direct array is read where it is, and an indirect one through the document's shared copy. It is never cloned.
- **Any other value:** one entry, exactly as the page holds it (a reference stays the reference), so callers can write the list back or keep each entry beside what it decoded.
- **One cap:** an array past `MAX_CONTENT_ENTRIES` (65,536) is `ContentsError::TooMany`, never a prefix. Callers rebuild, rewrite and redact from this list, so a silent cut would look like the end of the page. The cap is above both of edit's own caps, so neither one loosens.

What an entry means stays with each caller: a null, a non-stream or an undecodable stream can be skipped, read as an empty piece, or refused. Redaction and signing must fail closed where a reader may skip, so that is not unified here.

No caller changes here. `DecodeBudget::decode_contents` i…

title: Release: refresh contributor credits for each release (#6487)
author: Luis-0508
body:
Fixes #6487

## Problem

Help > About > Contributors is compiled from `contributors/contributors.json`, which nothing regenerates before a release, so contributors who joined after the last manual refresh are missing.

## Change

Opt in to the shared release-time refresh from craft-common-actions (storytold/craft-common-actions#110, storytold/craft-common-actions#123), as documented in its README under "Automatic contributor credits (opt-in)":

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: a new `credits` job calls `refresh-contributors.yml@main` with read-only permissions (`contents: read`, `pull-requests: read`). The `release` job now also needs `credits` and passes `contributors-artifact: ${{ needs.credits.outputs.artifact-name }}`. Existing jobs, permissions, inputs and secrets are unchanged.
- `docs/contributors.md`: one sentence saying release builds regenerate the file.

The snapshot is only bundled into the release builds and is not committed back. The shared generator derives `people_entry` from `contributors/people.toml` via `git blame`, which is the format `crates/ui-egui/build.rs` already reads, so no app code changes.

## Testing

This is the same change as storytold/deckcraft#1890 and storytold/photocraft#11426. Their first releases with it (DeckCraft v0.16.0, PhotoCraft v0.21.0) ran the `credits` job and every platform build successfully, and the bundled lists grew from 10 to 88 and from 189 to 512 contributors.

I could not run this repository's release workflow from a fork (it needs a push to `release` and the signing secrets), so the run here is untested.

## Risks

By design, a failed refresh or missing artifact blocks the release, so the first release run after merging is worth a look.

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Scan & OCR ▸ Correct recognized text (`ocr.correct`) opened the OCR Verify screen over the whole window: the tabs, menus and toolbar went away (on macOS the traffic lights sat on the PAGES caption), and the SOURCE PAGE pane was empty.

Why:
- `PdfCraftApp::ui` drew the screen and returned before `chrome::tab_strip` and `chrome::mode_bar`, so nothing of the app's chrome was drawn while it was open.

- A run shows the first page it reads (the current page, for the default "Current page" scope) instead of always page 1, where it found no words to box.

title: pdfcraft-web: window.pdfcraft, the page command API from craft-web-api, opt-in with ?control
author: helenkwok
body:
`window.pdfcraft` in PdfCraft's web build now comes from `craft-web-api` (storytold/craft-libs#413, with the fixes in #620), so a page drives PdfCraft through the same functions as every other Craft app: `request`, `execute`, `commands`, `docInspect`, `uiInspect` and `screenshot`. Part of storytold/craft-libs#193.

`?control` on the page's URL attaches the UI control channel (the one `--control` serves) and installs `window.pdfcraft`. It is opt-in because the channel keeps the accessibility tree of every frame. PdfCraft's methods differ from the other apps': `commands` is `ui.commands`, `execute` runs a registry command with `ui.command` (the `{command}` of `execute` becomes the `{id}` it takes), `docInspect` is `ui.state` and `uiInspect` is `ui.inspect`. The canvas has `id="pdfcraft"`, which the browser already exposes as `window.pdfcraft`, so the functions are added to that element. PdfCraft's control requests cannot be withdrawn, so a call that times out in the page still runs when the app reaches it.

fmt and clippy (native and wasm32) are clean, the crate dependency is pinned to the merged craft-libs commit, and the tests pass. I also loaded the built web app in headless Chromium: all six functions answer, a command changes the document, `screenshot()` returns a PNG in `data`, and an unknown method rejects with an `Error`.

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

The attachment `229205.pdf` on [PDFBOX-2250](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-2250) opens in PdfCraft as 7 pages instead of 23, and pages 1 and 2 are blank. Text and drawing from 18 pages are lost. Four intermediate nodes of its page tree have `/Kids` and `/Count` but no `/Type`. The renderer took each of those nodes for a single page, which had no content, and never read the pages beneath it.

With this PR alone, measured with release builds of `main` (f42fda734) and this branch:

| `229205.pdf` | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| pages (`pdfcraft-cli info`) | 7 | 23 |
| extracted text, non-blank characters (`pdfcraft-cli text`) | 3,345 | 33,894 |
| page 1 at 72 dpi, non-white pixels | 0 | 67,942 (14.0%) |
| page 2 at 72 dpi, non-white pixels | 0 | 36,153 (7.5%) |

pdftotext extracts 33,859 non-blank characters from the same file over 23 pages.

This PR changes the count of 1 of them, `229205.pdf` (7 → 23, which is PDFium's count). The other 28 are unchanged; their differences have other causes. title: fix(render): an image whose PNG predictor was declared but never applied draws its samples (hayro-syntax patch 40)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Real file:** [PDFBOX-3932](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-3932), attachment `PDFJS-8895-p1.pdf` (the cover page of the Apache Solr Reference Guide 6.6). The Solr logo is a 1692 × 855 RGB image with a 1692 × 855 soft mask. Both say `/Filter /FlateDecode /DecodeParms << /Predictor 15 … >>`, but the writer never applied the predictor: the image inflates to 4,339,980 bytes and the mask to 1,446,660, exactly 855 rows × 5,076 and 855 rows × 1,692 bytes, with no room for the filter-type byte that starts each PNG-predicted row.

- **Before:** PdfCraft took the first sample of every row for a filter type, so each row shifted and the image came out a row short. The page drew the logo as scattered fragments, and exporting the image failed with "the image data is shorter than its size says".
- **After:** the logo draws as it does in PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler, and the image exports.

**How common.** In a local corpus of 4,254 PDFs attached to Apache PDFBox issues, 37 files have Flate images with a PNG predictor, 1,465 images in all. 1,463 of them carry their row tags. The other 2 are this file's image and its mask. Three other local collections (671 scanner and fax PDFs, 651 XFA forms and 3 other files) have no PNG-predicted Flate images.

**What the specification says.** ISO 32000-2 §7.4.4.4 (LZW and Flate predictor functions, Table 10): a `/Predictor` of 10 or more means a PNG predictor is in use, and "the postprediction data for each PNG-predicted row shall begin with an explicit algorithm tag". This data breaks that rule, and the clause doesn't say how a reader should treat it. So this follows the readers. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler (`pdftoppm`) all draw the logo; none draws the fragments.

**The rule, and how narrow it is.** The data is used as it is, without the predictor, only when all of these hold:

- the filter is the image's last filter, and it is `FlateDecode`;
- it declares a PNG predictor (10–15);
- its inflated length is exactl…

title: M9: a signed string respelled in hexadecimal is no change after signing (sign.changes-after-signing)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

`acrosigned_signed_fix.pdf`, attached to the public Apache PDFBox issue [PDFBOX-2816](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-2816), carries two signatures. The update made after the second signature rewrites the catalog. That rewrite writes `/Lang` as a hexadecimal string where the signed revision had a literal string. The bytes are the same, and nothing else in the catalog changes. PdfCraft reports Signature2 as **invalid** with the change "document structure". pyHanko, used as a black box, reports the same signature as intact and valid.

| `acrosigned_signed_fix.pdf` | `main` (f42fda734) | #5962 alone (eb3cfd4ff) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Signature2 | invalid: modification `disallowed`, "document structure" | invalid: modification `disallowed`, "document structure" | modification `allowed`, "signature" (status unknown only because the test certificate is not trusted) |
| Signature1 | modification `none` | modification `none` | modification `none` |

A synthetic file made the same way (signed with a test key, then the catalog re-saved with `/Lang (en-US)` written as `<656E2D5553>`) gives the same result: `main` reports invalid with "document structure", and this PR lists no change (modification `allowed`, no changes).

**Why.** ISO 32000-2 §7.3.4.1 defines a string object as a series of bytes that "shall be written in one of the following two ways": as a literal (§7.3.4.2) or in hexadecimal (§7.3.4.3). The spelling is syntax, and the bytes are the value. `PdfString` records which spelling it was read with so that a save writes it back the same way, and its derived `PartialEq` compares that flag too. That is right for round-trips. The modification check, though, compared signed objects with that equality. So the respelled catalog failed the "unchanged" test and then the catalog comparison, and was classified as a structure change.

**The change** is in `crates/sign/src/pdf/changes.rs` only. `PdfString`'s equality stays as it is.

Every colour on them is written as a four-entry array with a null in the last place, for example `/C [1 0 0 null]`. PdfCraft drew none of the four. With this PR, the highlight, the filled circle and the square are drawn, in the colours PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler use. The line's colour reads as CMYK (0,0,0,0), which is white, so it is invisible in all four readers.

| page 1 at 72 dpi | non-white pixels | overlap with PDFium (IoU of the non-white masks) |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.25 % (page text only) | 0.164 |
| this PR | 1.36 % | 0.755 |
| PDFium | 1.62 % | — |
| MuPDF | 1.70 % | 0.919 |
| Poppler | 1.70 % | — |

The remaining difference is mostly the square's border width. The file gives it through an indirect `/BS`, which is a separate fix (see the last section). It also comes from the colours: PdfCraft converts CMYK with the plain formula of §10.4.2.5 (pure cyan, 0 255 255), while the oracles render it as 0 174 239.

title: fix(render): TIFF predictor 2 is undone a byte row at a time at 8 and 16 bits (hayro-syntax patch 42)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Real file.** https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-1350, attachment `40376536.PDF`. Page 1 holds 45 full-page 2445 × 4724 8-bit grey images, about 520 Mpx in all. Each one is Flate-compressed with `/Predictor 2`, the TIFF predictor. Rendering the page took:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| page 1, 96 dpi (three runs) | 20.8 / 22.9 / 25.4 s | 3.8 / 4.3 / 4.4 s |
| page 1, 72 dpi | 22.0 s | 3.7 s |
| page 2, 72 dpi | 3.1 s | 0.5 s |

The output is pixel-identical: the PNG files are byte for byte the same at both resolutions. For comparison, the same page at 72 dpi takes 1.7 s in PDFium, 1.3 s in MuPDF and 6.0 s in Poppler. Re-encoded without the predictor, it takes PdfCraft 2.7 s, so the predictor now costs about 1 s instead of about 19 s.

**How common.** Of the 4,255 PDF attachments in the PDFBox JIRA corpus, 22 files name `/Predictor 2`. In 12 of them, 417 images use it: 415 at 8 bits, one at 16 bits (`GWG181_16Bit_CMYK_X4.pdf`, PDFBOX-2549) and one at 1 bit. I rendered 170 pages with main and with this branch at 72 dpi. These were every page that draws one of those images, plus up to 30 pages of each of the other 10 files. All 170 came out byte-identical.

**Mechanism.** ISO 32000-2 §7.4.4.4 (Table 10, value 2) defines the TIFF predictor. It predicts each colour component of a sample from the same component of the sample immediately to its left (TIFF 6.0 §14). The vendored `hayro-syntax` (`lzw_flate::apply_predictor`) undid it for every bit depth through `BitChunks`/`BitWriter`. For each pixel, that path built a new `BitReader` over the output to read back the pixel to its left.

Now, when samples fill whole bytes (8 or 16 bits per component), `undo_tiff_bytes` works a row at a time on byte slices. Each pixel slice is added to the pixel slice to its left. 8-bit samples wrap at 256. 16-bit samples are read big-endian and wrap at 65,536.

Some behaviour stays the same:
- 1-, 2- and 4-bit samples still take the bit-level path. They…

| 16 | 0.0000 | 0.1509 | 0.1517 | 0.1530 | 0.1515 |

On main all 17 pages are blank. With this PR all 17 are drawn, and their ink is within 0.002 of PDFium and Poppler on every page. MuPDF's figures are lower, because it anti-aliases the downscaled scan.

**How common.** In the PDFBox JIRA corpus (about 4,255 public attachments, local only), 315 files contain a CCITT fax filter. Pages 1 to 3 of each render pixel-identical on main and on this PR, except for the three PDFBOX-771 pages above: 669 pages identical, 3 changed. Two files open on neither build.

**Mechanism.** In vendored hayro-syntax, `filter/ccitt.rs` asked the decoder for `max(/Rows, /Height)` rows. Patch 19 (#3308) added the `max` so that a `/Rows` below the height no longer cut the image short. Here, though, it asked for 1,084,975,104 rows of 2,592 columns. `ccitt_size_ok` refused that size, so the image was never decoded.

**Spec.** ISO 32000-2 §8.9.5, Table 87, makes the image's `/Height` (required) its height in samples. §7.4.6, Table 11, gives `/Rows` as "the height of the image in scan lines", with 0 or absent meaning "not predetermined". The two entries can disagree, and the spec does not say which one wins. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler all draw the image's `/Height` rows, which is how the image dictionary describes the picture. The f…

title: M1: the renderer reads a cut-off last update's objects, as the document model does (core.repair-broken-files)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**[PDFBOX-3934](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-3934), `PDFBOX-3934-KTUUMJNQ7NYGJJMEDGSY5OEU76G6JX2V.pdf`.** The last incremental update adds a cover page and a new page tree, and the file ends after that update's cross-reference rows: no trailer, no `startxref`, no `%%EOF`. The view showed 12 pages with every page shifted by one (the cover missing), while the document model, and so Extract, Save and every edit, had 13. PDFium, MuPDF, Poppler and qpdf all show 13 pages.

| | renderer pages (view, `info`) | model pages (`extract`) | page 1 against the three readers (mean grey difference) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 12 | 13 | 17.3–17.4 |
| this PR | **13** | 13 | **0.9–1.6** (the cover) |
| PDFium / MuPDF / Poppler | 13 / 13 / 13 | | |

The second attachment on that issue, `BCZSFNQAB62TUBURWG6B3ZOZCG5IH46P.pdf`, has the same shape: 1 page on main, **2** with this PR, as in the model and all three readers.

**[PDFBOX-3787](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-3787), `OLECK2R2YDFFW2RBVX5OBYR2DBLJRJPW.pdf`: the first page is now blank, and that is the intended result.** Its last update is cut off the same way, and in that latest revision the first page is an empty page. On main the view drew the older revision's page (ink 0.064), while the model, and so Extract and Save, already had the empty one. With this PR the view shows the blank page too, identical to PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler (mean difference 0.0; it was 16.4). Page count stays at 64.

### Cause

The two layers find the cross-reference data differently:

- `pdfcraft-cos` looks for `startxref` in the last 4 KiB of the file. It finds none here, so it rebuilds the table from object headers, and the latest definition of each object wins.
- Vendored hayro-syntax (`find_last_xref_pos`) takes the last `startxref` anywhere in the file. That is the older revision's footer, about 78 KB before the end, so it reads the older table and never sees the update.

title: fix(ui-egui): keep hotbar picker stationary while resizing
author: patel-vansh
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6603 where the Hotbar tools picker could unexpectedly reposition itself while dragging the **Toolbar size** slider.

Previously, the picker position was recalculated from the toolbar's current bounds on every frame. As the toolbar resized, this could cause the picker to flip to the opposite side or otherwise move during the slider interaction, disrupting the drag and potentially causing the toolbar size to jump.

The picker now retains its current position while the size slider is being adjusted, by pointer or by keyboard. A pointer adjustment lasts while the button is held. A keyboard adjustment starts with the first arrow-key press that changes the value and lasts until the slider loses focus. Once the interaction ends, the temporary position is cleared and the picker is recalculated from the toolbar's updated bounds. Focusing the slider, or releasing the pointer on it, does not by itself pin the picker.

Regression tests (`crates/ui-egui/src/hotbar.rs`):

- `picker_stays_put_while_resizing_hotbar`: pointer drag up to the largest size and back down to the smallest, in horizontal and vertical layouts, floating, docked and full-side. The picker stays put during both drags and takes a new position after each release.
- `picker_stays_put_while_resizing_hotbar_with_keyboard`: same checks driven by the arrow keys, ending with Tab to move focus away.

## How you verified it

title: fix(render): a form XObject that draws itself is drawn once (hayro-interpret patch 89)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Page 2 of `poppler-748-0.tgz-1.pdf` from [PDFBOX-5782](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-5782) (a fuzzed file) took **34 s** to render at 72 dpi (median of three runs). With this PR it takes **9 ms**, and the page matches Poppler's render: the stack of red copies the form drew of itself is gone, and the rest of the page is unchanged.

| poppler-748 p2, 72 dpi | Before | Now | Poppler |
|---|---|---|---|
| time | 34.3 s | 0.009 s | 0.1 s |
| ink | 1.38% | 0.53% | 0.55% |

PDFium and MuPDF can't open this file.

The page draws a form whose own `/Resources` map `/X0` to the `/Pages` dictionary, which isn't an XObject. The lookup then falls back to the page's resources, where `/X0` is the form itself. So the form drew itself twice at every level. The work only stopped when the page's nested-paint budget (`MAX_NESTED_PAINTS`, 50,000 paints) ran out, and every paint was a transparency group.

A form XObject is "a self-contained description" (ISO 32000-2 §8.10.1). A form that contains itself never finishes. hayro-interpret now keeps the forms being drawn on the interpreter context (`Context::enter_form`). A form that is already on that stack is skipped, whether it is reached directly, through another form, or through a pattern or glyph. The skip is reported as `ContentTruncated`, so the page doesn't count as a clean render. The stack holds at most one entry per nesting level (51).

Synthetic forms that draw themselves three times per level (`/X0 Do` naming the form directly, through a `/Pages` dictionary, through a missing object, or through a form with no resources) took 0.8 to 4.6 s before and now take 2 ms. On the same files MuPDF takes 0.3 s and Poppler 0.1 s. PDFium ran past the 2 GB cap on two of the four. MuPDF and Poppler draw a self-drawing form once, which is the result here.

**Kept: the fallback to the page's resources.** §7.8.3 says a form inherits the page's resources only when it has no `Resources` entry. Changing that would …

title: fix(render): a picture that doesn't decode is decoded once, not at every draw (hayro-interpret patch 91)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

[PDFBOX-1439](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-1439), attachment `PROCEDURE_OF_NOISE_MEASURMENT_6A800A002_.PDF`, is a scanned drawing stored as JBIG2 with `/JBIG2Globals`. The JBIG2 decoder refuses each of its three pages ("too many symbol instances"), and the refusal takes about 40–70 ms. A render worker keeps one cache for the preview, the final render and every tile of a page, and it ran that refusal again for each of them:

| Page (preview at 0.25, final at 1.0, four 512 px tiles, one shared cache) | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 253–332 ms; every tile 39–54 ms | 115–120 ms; every tile 0–1 ms |
| 2 | 257–350 ms; every tile 41–57 ms | 122–124 ms; every tile 0–1 ms |
| 3 | 320–438 ms; every tile 52–72 ms | 149–150 ms; every tile 0 ms |

(Two runs each, optimised test build (`opt-level` of the test profile), Windows. The preview and the final render each still decode once because a preview is keyed separately.) The refused picture is left out in both builds; only the repeated refusal goes.

A page that draws one broken picture many times costs the same again on every draw: an image (§8.9.5) or a stencil mask (§8.9.6.2) that doesn't decode was decoded again each time `Do` drew it.

**Cause.** The decoded-image cache in the vendored `hayro-interpret` (`DecodedImageCache`, patch 32) stored a failed decode as `None` and read `None` as a miss. So damaged data, or a JPX or JBIG2 stream its decoder refuses, was decoded again at every draw, tile and zoom.

**Fix (patch 91).**
- The cache keeps a failure under the same key (same object, decode target and mask flags) as the set of warnings the decode reported. A later draw reports those warnings again and gets nothing, as the decode did. A page that reported `ImageDecodeFailure` five times for five draws still reports it five times, and the renderer still turns them into one warning per page.
- A failure counts 128 bytes towards the cache's 64 MiB budget, so failures alone can't gro…

title: M2: `info` lists the repairs made while opening, as Document Properties does (misc.cli-inspect)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**[PDFBOX-2250](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-2250), `055794.pdf`.** Its cross-reference data cannot be read, so PdfCraft rebuilds the index from the object headers. The app says so in Document Properties, and `doc_info` lists the same notes in `repairs`, but `pdfcraft-cli info` printed nothing about it: the summary looked the same as for a sound file. With this PR `info` prints:

```json
"repairs": [
  "cross-reference data unreadable (syntax error at byte 27530: expected object header); rebuilding from object headers",
  "rebuilt cross-reference index from 37 object headers"
]
```

The other attachment on that issue, `113223.pdf`, and both [PDFBOX-3934](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-3934) attachments (no `startxref`) also list their rebuilt index now. A sound file prints `"repairs": []`.

ISO 32000-2 §7.5.4 and §7.5.5 define the cross-reference table and the trailer that locates it. How to recover a file whose table cannot be read is not specified, and PdfCraft records every such leniency rather than applying it silently. This PR shows that record in the CLI as well.

- **Where the notes come from.** `info` opens the document the way the app does, once. It reuses the engine session that the dynamic XFA summary already opened, and reads `Document::repair_log`, the list that Document Properties and `doc_info` show. That list includes notes the app adds after reading the objects, such as a page tree rebuilt from the pages found by scanning (#1656), which the object reader alone does not have.
- **No scripts run.** The session is opened with JavaScript turned off (`Session::set_javascript(false)`). An XFA form's initialize and calculate scripts, which the app runs on opening, do not run while `info` inspects an untrusted file. On `main`, `info` opened a session only for dynamic XFA forms, and their scripts ran there.

title: fix(render): glyph names read as text only in the glyph list's uni and u forms (hayro-interpret patch 92)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A simple font without a ToUnicode CMap gets its text from the glyph names its encoding picks (ISO 32000-2 §9.10.2: the name "can be looked up in the Adobe Glyph List and Adobe Glyph List for New Fonts"). For names not in the list, the Adobe Glyph List Specification has two forms: `uni` followed by groups of exactly four uppercase hex digits, and `u` followed by four to six uppercase hex digits, with no value in the surrogate range D800–DFFF and none past U+10FFFF.

The vendored hayro-interpret read any `uni…` or `u…` name as hex of any length and in either case. `uni65` and `u65` came out as "e", `uni20ac` as "€" and `uni+065` as "e". None of these is a glyph list name.

A synthetic page with eight names in `/Differences`, extracted with `pdfcraft-cli text`:

| name | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `uni65` | e | (nothing) |
| `u65` | e | (nothing) |
| `uni00e9` | é | (nothing) |
| `uni20ac` | € | (nothing) |
| `u1f600` | 😀 | (nothing) |
| `uni0065`, `uni00E9`, `u0066` | e, é, f | e, é, f |

- **hayro-interpret patch 92.** `glyph_name_to_unicode`, which supplies the text of a glyph, now reads these names with `agl_unicode_from_name`, which follows the specification's rule. This is the rule that `glyph_name_to_text` already applies to suffixed and ligature names (`uni20ac0308`, `f_uni20ac`).
- **Drawing is unchanged.** Upstream's lenient `unicode_from_name` is still used to find a glyph in a font: the TrueType `(3,1)` cmap lookup of §9.6.5.4, and accented letters in a non-embedded standard font.
- **pdfcraft-fonts.** `glyph_text`, which the editor uses to read existing text, already required whole groups of four digits and rejected surrogates. It now also rejects lowercase digits, so both readers apply the same rule.

## How common

Measured against the 4,254 PDFBox JIRA attachments and the pdf.js test suite (`test/pdfs` and `linked`). A screen of every file, raw and with its Flate streams decoded, for a `/u…` or `/uni…` name that the old and n…

title: redact: treat unusable /QuadPoints as absent in every reader
author: chamber074
body:
Fixes #6468

## What this changes

Four parts of the codebase read a markup annotation's `/QuadPoints`: redaction
apply (`marks_checked`), the renderer's annotation inspector, the comment
summaries, and generated appearances. They read them by different rules, so
they disagreed about which area a mark covers:

- an indirect entry (a number by reference) ended the fold: the quads after it
  silently vanished from the redaction, and the area stayed readable in the
  "redacted" file;
- a name or another non-number was folded as 0, inventing `(0, 0)` corners;
- `NaN` was read unbounded by one reader (a "redaction failed" error whose
  coordinates are `-inf`) and clamped to `MediaBox` edges by another, which
  for a `/Mark` with `/IC` derived an overlay `Rect` reaching `-inf`;
- a truncated array was index-shifted by the appearance builder, painting the
  surviving quads in the wrong places.

Now all four go through one helper (`pdfcraft_geom::quad_points::usable_quads`):
a quad counts only if all eight entries are present, numeric, and finite. The
finiteness is judged **as f32** — PDF reals are Annex C reals — so f32 and f64
readers agree on which quads are usable (a real like `1e300` counts unusable
everywhere). Usable values are returned **on the f32 grid** (each value put
through `f32` and back), so the readers also fold identical numbers: a value
`f32` cannot hold exactly, like 67108869, is 67108872 for every reader, not
just the ones that keep `f32`. An unusable quad contributes nothing (and never
shifts the ones after it); a mark left with no usable quad falls back to its
`/Rect` exactly as before, and to the caller's `unreadable` list when it has
neither. Appearance drawing resolves the array and its entries through the
document first, as the other readers do, so an indirect quad is drawn rather
than silently dropped.

Judgement call worth a reviewer's eye: judging finiteness as f32 (rather than
treating huge-but-finite f64 values as usable for the f64 readers on…

title: M2: a wide stroke of a path with `y` curves is drawn, not dropped (view.render-pages)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Real file.** [`pattern_colors_broken.pdf`](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/attachment/13031256/pattern_colors_broken.pdf) from PDFBOX-5250 strokes two "XX" letters with a 32 pt textured outline. Page 1 drew the letters without that outline. The cause is not the pattern: a plain `0 1 0 RG` stroke of the same path drew nothing either. With this PR the outline is drawn. Measured at 100 dpi (mean CIELAB ΔE, page 1):

| | PDFium | MuPDF | Poppler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 6.47 | 4.89 | 7.30 |
| this PR | 3.78 | 1.93 | 4.66 |

(The remaining differences are the tiling-pattern texture and anti-aliasing. The oracles differ from each other by 4.0 to 5.3.)

**Minimal repro.** `0 1 0 RG 16 w 21.4166 234.5928 m 19.9009 236.0303 18.9478 236.3428 y 19.2603 238.4209 20.8697 238.4209 y S` drew nothing at 16, 32 and 63 pt. It drew at the other widths from 1 to 64.

**Cause.** `y` appends a cubic whose second control point is its end point (ISO 32000-2 §8.5.2.1, Table 58), so the curve's derivative is zero at its end.

- kurbo 0.13.1 builds a stroke's outline from offset curves. It finds the cusps of an offset curve with a root search on the source curve's curvature, and that curvature grows without bound towards a zero-derivative end.
- At some widths the search stops on the end point itself. kurbo then normalises the zero tangent there, and the outline gets NaN.
- `vello_common::flatten::fill` drops any path that contains NaN, so the whole stroke vanished. §8.5.3.2 requires every segment of every subpath to be stroked.

Only an exact zero triggers this. Over 1–64 pt:

- 1,073 of 192,000 random `y`/`v` strokes came back with NaN.
- None of 192,000 strokes did whose end handle was 1e-9 long.
- None of 256,000 `v` strokes did (`v` puts the first control point on the start point).

**Fix.** This extends the NaN fallback that #4913 added to `flatten::stroke` (vendored `vello_common`, patch 4):

- When kurbo's outline comes back non-finite, the path is …

title: M3: copied and found text keeps each combining mark after its letter (view.copy-text, view.find)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6517

Some PDF writers draw each glyph with its own show operation (CAD and word-processor exports such as the CADCraft and WordCraft files in the issue). In those files a zero-advance Thai tone mark or above vowel starts at the pen after its base, give or take a small mark-positioning offset, and its ink is drawn back over the base. The text layer is in logical order, but `pdfcraft-cli text`, Copy and Find sorted each line's glyphs by x alone. A mark that started a hair past its base's advance ended up after the next letter (`ห้อง` → `หอ้ง`, `น้ำ` → `นำ้`), and the gaps between words were dropped.

Measured on a synthetic page with the issue's test string `ห้อง ก๋วยเตี๋ยว น้ำ ที่นี่`: one glyph per `BT … Tm … Tj ET`, Helvetica remapped by `/ToUnicode`, base letters 600 units wide, marks 0 wide, and words 260 units apart.

| Variant | `main` (f42fda734) | This PR | Poppler `pdftotext` | MuPDF | PDFium |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| marks 0.4 pt past the pen, no space glyph | `หอ้งกว๋ยเตยี๋วนำ้ทน` | `ห้อง ก๋วยเตี๋ยว น้ำ ที่นี่` | correct | right order, no spaces | marks moved, spaces kept |
| marks 0.4 pt past the pen, space glyphs | `หอ้ง กว๋ยเตยี๋ว นำ้ ทน` | correct | correct | correct | marks moved |
| marks at the pen, no space glyph | `ห้องก๋วยเตี๋ยวน้ำที่นี่` | correct | correct | no spaces | correct |

ISO 32000-2 §9.10.1 gives a processor the job of finding the information content of text for searching, indexing and export, and §9.10.2–9.10.3 map each code to Unicode. Ordering is left to the processor. Unicode stores a combining mark after its base, and in these files the content stream draws it in that order. Where Poppler, MuPDF, PDFium and pypdf (the issue's cross-check) agree, this PR follows them: marks keep content order (Poppler, MuPDF and pypdf) and word gaps without a space glyph become spaces (Poppler, PDFium and pypdf).
