title: fix(render): a CID-keyed CFF font with an emptied font dict still draws its other glyphs (hayro-interpret patch 93)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A CID-keyed CFF font picks a font dict for every glyph through its FDSelect, and a glyph's charstring needs the Private DICT of that font dict. Subsetters often empty the font dicts that no kept glyph uses, so those dicts have no Private DICT. Until now, one such dict dropped the whole embedded font. The text then drew with a fallback, which for a CJK font usually means nothing.

The public file `13069603-123.pdf` attached to [PDFBOX-5843](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-5843) shows this. It embeds a SourceHanSansSC subset (`/FontFile3 /Subtype /CIDFontType0C`) with 18 font dicts, and the subsetter emptied 17 of them. Every CID on the page selects the one dict that was kept. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler all draw 你好啊. PdfCraft drew an empty page.

After this change, a font dict that can't be read leaves only the glyphs that select it missing. The glyphs of the other font dicts draw as before. The program is still dropped when none of its font dicts can be read, as before.

Spec: ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.2 and §9.9 Table 124 (`CIDFontType0C` is a CFF CIDFont program, and its CIDs reach charstrings through the CFF charset). Adobe Technical Note #5176 (the FDArray and FDSelect of a CIDFont, and each font DICT's Private DICT). The file breaks the format only in font dicts that no glyph uses. All three readers draw the text, and this change follows them.

The change is in `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/blob.rs` (`CffFontBlob`): the subfonts are kept as `Vec<Option<Subfont>>` instead of failing the font on the first unreadable one. The ledger entry is hayro-interpret (93) in `vendor/README.md`.

## How you verified it

Measured on page 1 of `13069603-123.pdf` at 72 dpi. The value is the share of page pixels with ink, and `dis` is the fraction of ink with no matching ink within 2 px of the other render (0 means the same).

title: fix(render): a non-embedded SymbolMT draws Symbol's glyphs, whatever encoding it declares (hayro-interpret patch 98)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

`SymbolMT` is the name the Symbol font has as a TrueType font. Spreadsheet exports often reference it without embedding it, and declare `/WinAnsiEncoding` and the nonsymbolic flag. PdfCraft didn't recognise the name as the standard Symbol font. It drew the text with the Helvetica stand-in, so a `μ` written as code 0x6D came out as `m`.

The public file `13069708-exportByExcel.pdf` attached to [PDFBOX-5844](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-5844) shows this: a TrueType `/BaseFont /SymbolMT`, `/Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding`, `/Flags 32`, no font program, and the string `(m)`. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler all draw `μ`. PdfCraft drew `m`.

After this change, a non-embedded font named `SymbolMT`, or `Symbol` or `SymbolMT` with a `,` or `-` style suffix (`Symbol,Bold`, `SymbolMT,Italic`, `Symbol-Bold`), is the standard Symbol font. A subset prefix is ignored, as before. Like `/Symbol` itself, Symbol draws through its built-in encoding, so code 0x6D is `mu`. A `/Differences` array is still applied first. Names that only start with "Symbol" (`Symbolic`, `SymbolPS`) are left alone.

Spec: ISO 32000-2 §9.6.2.2 names Symbol as one of the standard 14 fonts and one of their two symbolic fonts, with its encoding given in Annex D. §9.6.5.1 says an `/Encoding` entry may override a font program's built-in encoding. Here the readers depart from that text: PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler all keep Symbol's built-in encoding when a non-embedded `SymbolMT` declares `/WinAnsiEncoding`. This PR follows them. It extends the existing rule in `StandardKind::new_with_standard`, which already ignores the declared encoding of a non-embedded Symbol or ZapfDingbats. The change only adds the names to `select_standard_font` in `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/standard_font.rs`. The ledger entry is hayro-interpret (98) in `vendor/README.md`.

title: M2: a CMap's bfchar mappings read codes at their codespace length (view.render-cid-fonts)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

[PDFBOX-1282](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-1282) has two attachments, `Characters_Arial.pdf` and `Characters_Arial_Modified.pdf`. Each embeds Arial as a Type 0 font with an embedded CMap. The CMap has the codespace `<0000> <FFFF>` and writes its CID mappings as `bfchar`. Page 3 shows codes 0x20AC to 0xFFFC, and PdfCraft drew every one of them as two glyphs: `<fe96>` came out as "þ–".

The cause is in the vendored hayro-cmap. `lookup_cid_code` falls back to the CMap's `bfchar` entries, but bf entries don't record how many bytes their code has. When the renderer tried the one-byte code 0xFE, the lookup matched the two-byte entry `<00fe>`. The same happened for every first byte from 0x20 to 0xFF, since each has a `<00xx>` entry.

ISO 32000-2 §9.7.6.2 says the codespace ranges specify how many bytes make up each code. A code matches a range when it has the range's length and each of its bytes lies between the corresponding bytes of the bounds. The code is then looked up "in the character code mappings for codes of that length", and that includes `bfchar`.

The fallback now applies only when the codespace ranges give the code the length being tried (`codespace_allows`, checked byte by byte). A CMap with no codespace ranges of its own defers to its `usecmap` base. If no CMap in the chain has codespace ranges, the old fallback stays. `lookup_bf_string`, which `ToUnicode` uses, is unchanged.

This is vendored hayro-cmap patch 4, and the ledger in `vendor/README.md` is updated. Patch 3 is in #6348, so the two ledger rows will need a merge whichever lands second.

This PR doesn't change what happens to a code that maps to nothing: it still advances one byte, as before.

**Measured** with the CLI at 150 dpi against MuPDF. The figure is the mean fraction of ink pixels with no ink from the other renderer within 2 px.

| page | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `Characters_Arial.pdf` p3 | 0.164 | 0.000 |
| `Characters_Arial_Modified.pdf` p3 | …

author: mtlcl410
body:

[PDFBOX-1988](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-1988) has one attachment, `Test1.pdf`. Its text font is written as `<< /Type /Font /Subtype / /BaseFont /Courier-Bold /Widths … >>`, so the `/Subtype` is the empty name.

title: M2: a page without a /MediaBox is US Letter (view.render-pages)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

[PDFBOX-4001](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-4001) has an attachment, `PDFBOX-4001-reduced.pdf`, whose page has no `/MediaBox`, either its own or inherited. PdfCraft rendered it as A4: 1241 × 1754 px at 150 dpi. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler all draw it as US Letter (612 × 792 pt), and so do PdfCraft's own page model and inspector.

ISO 32000-2 §7.7.3.3, Table 31 makes `MediaBox` required (inheritable) and gives no default. The readers agree on Letter, so the renderer now uses Letter too. The default comes from the vendored hayro-syntax, which was the only place in the workspace with A4: `crates/model` (`Page::crop`), the inspector's placeholder in `crates/render/src/inspect/core.rs`, organize and assemble already used 612 × 792.

The fallback in `Page::base_dimensions` for a visible region without area was A4 too, and it now uses the same Letter size. For a page with `/MediaBox [0 0 0 0]`, all three readers also use 612 × 792. Readers disagree when only the CropBox is degenerate (1 × 1, 300 × 300 or Letter), so no reader majority decides that case. It now gets the same default as a missing box instead of a second one.

This is vendored hayro-syntax patch 44 (a new `LETTER` constant; `A4` stays public), and the ledger in `vendor/README.md` is updated. Our open #6355 (patch 38) reads a box without area as a missing one and falls back to this same default. The two PRs touch the same line in `Page::new`, so whichever merges second takes the other's line. After both, a `/MediaBox [0 0 0 0]` page is Letter-sized and shows its content, as the readers do.

title: Poster: Pages to Print selects the generated tiles
author: rizaljzulfikar
body:
## What this changes

In the Print dialog, **Poster** now makes the **Pages to Print** choice count the *generated tiles*, the sheets the chosen pages are tiled into, instead of the document pages.

**Background:** I design posters as single-page A2 PDFs, and at home they only ever print on Letter or A4 sheets. Tiling one of those pages produces nine or more sheets, and I almost never want all of them: I proof a corner first, reprint a strip a smudge ruined, or print just the middle of a large design to check colors before committing a full ink-heavy run. Today the Pages to Print choice cannot help with that, because it counts document pages, and a single-page poster has only one. With this change I pick the tiles themselves: "5-9" for the bottom rows, "Current page" for the tile I am looking at in the preview, or odd tiles only when I want a quick ink-light sample of the whole poster.

Concretely:

- **All** prints every tile; **Current page** prints the tile the preview shows; **Pages** takes a tile range (`1-4`, `5-`, `2, 7`), with the odd/even subset and Reverse pages applying to the tiles.
- The range field's hint shows the tile count (`1-9`), a line says how many tiles will print, and Poster with All selected says the choice counts tiles.
- Every other layout (Size, Multiple, Booklet, Label) keeps counting document pages, as does `doc_print`; pages picked in the panel keep their document-page meaning in Poster too.

```diff
 print::Settings { pages, … }
+print::Settings { pages, tiles, … }        # which laid-out sheets print
 PrintDraft::settings(count, labels)
+PrintDraft::settings(&sizes, labels)       # poster resolves tiles after the sheets are laid out
```

Engine side this is `Settings::tiles: Option<Vec<usize>>`: positions into the sheet list `layout()` builds, kept by position (a repeated position prints its sheet again, as a repeated page does). It applies to the print-ready PDF, the preview count and the spooled job alike.

title: fix(engine): map URL text line rects with view_rect_to_user and filter non-finite coordinates
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Problem
In `Session::find_urls` (`crates/engine/src/session/view.rs`), each text line rectangle `v` was mapped through `PageInfo::view_rect_to_quad(v)` and folded with `f64::min` / `f64::max` seeded at `f64::MAX` / `f64::MIN`. Because `f64::min` and `f64::max` skip `NaN`, a non-finite coordinate produced the finite inverted box `[f64::MAX, f64::MAX, f64::MIN, f64::MIN]`, which bypassed the existing-link overlap filter and was emitted to the caller.

### Root Cause
1. `PageInfo::view_rect_to_user(v)` already computes the axis-aligned user-space rectangle directly from the two opposite view corners across all multiples of 90° page rotation.
2. Neither input view coordinates nor mapped user-space coordinates were checked for finiteness before returning candidate URL link rectangles.

### Fix
- Extract `line_user_rect(page, v)` in `crates/engine/src/session/view.rs` to verify input finiteness, map `v` via `page.view_rect_to_user(v).map(f64::from)`, and require all resulting user-space coordinates to be finite.
- Add unit and session tests verifying that `NaN` (full or partial), `±Infinity`, and non-finite crop coordinates are rejected while rotated pages produce finite, ordered user-space URL rectangles.

Fixes #6469

title: M2: a tiling pattern cell that blends is drawn over the page under it (view.render-transparency)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Real file.** `gs-bugzilla695975.pdf`, attached to [PDFBOX-4095](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-4095), is a watch drawn in Illustrator. The bracelet links are silver shadings, and a fill with a page-sized tiling pattern goes over them. The pattern's cell paints gold at `/BM /Color` `/ca 0.8` and then pale yellow at `/BM /Multiply`. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler all draw a gold bracelet with the silver highlights showing through. PdfCraft drew it flat pale yellow with no highlights, because the cell's blend modes never saw the silver underneath.

Measured on page 1 at 100 dpi, as the mean CIELAB ΔE76 per pixel (lower is closer):

| | PDFium | MuPDF | Poppler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 1.51 | 1.45 | 1.79 |
| this PR | **0.17** | **0.57** | **0.54** |

For scale, PDFium and MuPDF differ from each other by 0.52 on this page.

**Spec.** ISO 32000-2 §11.6.7: "the pattern definition shall be treated as if it were implicitly enclosed in a non-isolated transparency group: a non-knockout group for tiling patterns". NOTE 1 adds that "the effect in the general transparent case is as if the pattern definition were re-executed independently for each tile, taking into account the colour of the backdrop at each point". Treating the cell as an isolated group, evaluated once and repeated, is allowed only "in the common case in which the pattern consists entirely of objects painted with the Normal blend mode".

**Cause.** hayro draws every tiling cell into a pixmap on a transparent canvas and fills the shape with that pixmap. This is the isolated shortcut, used for every cell. A blend mode inside the cell then blends with transparency, which leaves the source colour unchanged.

**Fix (hayro patch 32).**
- While the renderer draws a cell, it records whether anything outside the cell's own groups paints with a blend mode other than Normal.
- A cell that blends is then drawn again in each tile the fill or stroke reaches, straight onto the page and cli…

title: fix(js): decode ', numeric, and HTML named character references in FormCalc Decode
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Problem
In `crates/js/src/formcalc/builtins.rs`, FormCalc `Decode(s, xml)` and `Decode(s, html)` only replaced `<`, `>`, `"`, and `&` via a chained `.replace(...)`, leaving `'`, decimal and hexadecimal numeric character references (`A`, `A`, `A`), and HTML named character entities (` `, `é`, etc.) unescaped.

### Root Cause
`(decode, html | xml)` used a four-entity `.replace(...)` chain instead of a single-pass XML/HTML entity decoder.

### Fix
- Replace the `.replace(...)` chain with a single-pass `decode_entities(s, html)` decoder in `crates/js/src/formcalc/words.rs`:
  - Decodes all five predefined XML entities (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'`) and decimal (`&#...;`) / hexadecimal (`&#x...;`, `&#X...;`) character references in both `xml` and `html` modes, rejecting `0`, surrogates, and out-of-range or malformed references by leaving them literal without panicking.
  - Decodes the W3C HTML 4 / XHTML 1.0 named character entity set (ISO-8859-1 ` `..`ÿ`, Latin extended, Greek, punctuation, and symbol entities) when the mode is `html`, while keeping non-XML named entities literal in `xml` mode.
  - Scans in a single linear pass so `&lt;` and `&lt;` decode to `<` rather than `<`.
- Add unit tests in `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs` covering `'`, decimal/hex numeric references, invalid/surrogate code points, single-pass decoding, and HTML vs XML named entities.

Fixes #6464

title: fix(render): a patch mesh painted through a path its own size draws every patch (hayro-interpret patch 99)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

[PDFBOX-1915](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-1915), attachment `asy-tensor-rainbow.pdf`, page 1: a rainbow arc is a type 7 (tensor-product patch mesh) shading used as a pattern to fill a single-subpath polygon (one `m` and 1,803 `l`) under two arc clips. PdfCraft left the blue and violet inner bands white, with a stray blue blob. With this PR the rainbow draws whole.

Mean CIELAB ΔE76 at 100 dpi (lower is closer):

| Page 1 | vs PDFium | vs MuPDF | vs Poppler |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `main` | 6.54 | 4.83 | 7.25 |
| this PR | **4.56** | **2.87** | **5.27** |
| the box holding the rainbow, `main` | 21.44 | 19.03 | 25.43 |
| the box holding the rainbow, this PR | **8.70** | **6.38** | **12.70** |

For scale, PDFium and Poppler differ by 1.95 on the page and 4.68 in the box; PDFium and MuPDF by 4.56 and 7.61. The rest of the page-level difference is the square gradient frame around the box, which this PR does not touch.

### Mechanism

ISO 32000-2 §8.7.4.5.8 builds a type 7 shading from bicubic patches, and §8.7.4.2 (Table 76) paints a shading "subject to the current clipping path", like any fill. The sampler cuts each patch into a fixed 19 × 19 grid (722 triangles) and, for each triangle, walked its whole bounding box, rounded out to whole pixels, inside a visit budget of eight visits per pixel of the painted area plus four per triangle (the budget that stops overlapping meshes from running for minutes).

Across a narrow curved band, the grid cells are a few pixels long and a fraction of a pixel wide, at every angle. A cell lying diagonally has a box many times its area: on a synthetic repro (twelve quarter-ring tensor patches, six bands, painted through a polygon of 1,803 short segments) at 100 dpi, the triangles' boxes average 14.7 pixels for 0.68 pixel of area. Painted with `sh`, the area is the whole page and the budget is ample. Painted through a path the size of the rainbow, the area is that path's box, and the budget ran out b…

Some simple fonts, mostly with no `/ToUnicode`, name their glyphs only by a number: `C70`, `C0071`, `MT72` (Windows printer drivers, the 3B2 typesetter), `G46` in hexadecimal (PageMaker). title: fix(render): a Type 3 font without /Widths advances by its glyphs' d0/d1 widths, and the page warns about it (hayro-interpret patch 90)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A Type 3 font that has no `/Widths` now advances each glyph by the width its glyph procedure sets with `d0` or `d1`. Before, every glyph got no advance, so a line of text was drawn as one blot and extracted as letters stacked on one spot.

The page also reports a render warning, so the reader learns the font is malformed and its spacing was taken from elsewhere: "a Type 3 font has no /Widths; its glyphs were spaced by the widths their glyph procedures give". `pdfcraft-cli render` prints the warning, and the automation render tools list it with the page's other warnings.

### Real file (PDFBox issue tracker)

`PDFBOX-2794_unc.pdf`, attached to https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-2943: a two-page invoice set in three Type 3 fonts. The key is misspelt, so the fonts have no `/Widths`. Each glyph procedure starts with `wx 0 … d1`.

| | `main` | This PR | PDFium | Poppler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Page 1, ink coverage at 72 dpi | 4.80 % | 7.79 % | 7.89 % | 7.47 % |
| Page 2, ink coverage at 72 dpi | 0.52 % | 4.57 % | 4.66 % | 4.70 % |
| Page 1, pixels that differ from PDFium | 4.23 % | 1.91 % | | 4.05 % |
| Page 2, pixels that differ from PDFium | 3.59 % | 0.80 % | | 3.20 % |
| Page 1, extracted characters (not counting spaces) | 805 | 911 | | 911 (`pdftotext`) |
| Page 2, extracted characters (not counting spaces) | 862 | 1055 | | 1053 (`pdftotext`) |

On `main` the letters of each word pile up, and text extraction keeps one of each stack, so the text reads as "Alpen…dische Schilderfabik Forstra…e 128073". With this PR the pages match PDFium and Poppler, and the text reads as in `pdftotext`. The file isn't committed here; the tests below are synthetic.

Out of the 4,255 PDF attachments on the PDFBox issue tracker, 121 files have Type 3 fonts. In 1 of them (this one) a Type 3 font has no `/Widths`. I rendered pages 1–10 of all 121 files with `main` and with this PR: that is 553 pages. 541 pages are pixel-identical, and the 2 …

title: M5: the hotbar settings button shows one tooltip (#6548)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Resting the pointer on the hotbar's settings gear showed two tooltips stacked on top of each other: "Hotbar settings" and "Hotbar settings / add tools". Now it shows only "Hotbar settings / add tools". The button's accessible name stays "Hotbar settings".

Cause: `icons::button` already attaches its `tooltip` argument as the hover text, and `hotbar::settings_button` then chained a second `.on_hover_text(...)` onto it.

I checked every `icons::button` call in `pdfcraft-ui-egui` (113 calls, including results stored in a variable and calls through wrappers such as `preset_arrow` and Combine's `tool`) for a second `on_hover_text`/`on_hover_ui`. The gear was the only one. Combine's `tool` adds `on_disabled_hover_text`, which egui shows only while the button is disabled, so it never stacks.

title: M10: Pages per sheet takes a custom grid of columns by rows (#6551)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6551.

**Pages per sheet** in the Print dialog's **Multiple** mode gains **Custom**. Choosing it shows two number fields, columns **by** rows, each 1 to 99, as the Acrobat user guide's Print dialog describes it ("Prints a predefined number of pages, or a custom number (up to 99), horizontally and vertically. If you select a predefined number from the menu, Acrobat automatically selects the best paper orientation.").

- **A custom grid is laid out as given.** Columns go across the sheet and rows go down, whatever the orientation. The sheet is not turned for the grid, so Auto prints portrait. The issue's case, A4 portrait with 2 columns by 1 row, puts two narrow pages side by side and uses the full height of the sheet. Four pages print on two sheets.
- **The predefined counts work as before.** 2/4/6/9/16 still turn the sheet to suit their grid with Auto, so 2 per sheet still prints side by side on landscape paper.
- Page order, page border and auto-rotate work the same with a custom grid. When Custom is chosen, Page order moves to its own row so the row fits the dialog.
- **Engine** (`pdfcraft-print`): `Layout::grid(cols, rows)` and a `custom` flag on `Layout::Multiple`. A custom grid may have up to 99 cells each way (predefined grids keep the 256-cell cap). A grid too fine for the paper is still refused with `PrintError::Invalid`, not drawn.
- **Headless**: `doc_print` takes `cols` and `rows` (1–99). They must be given together, without `per_sheet`, and only with `layout: "multiple"`. Anything else is an `InvalidArgs` error. The tool description and schema say so.

Print settings aren't remembered between prints on `main`, so this PR doesn't persist the grid. The issue's "save as default" request goes with the dialog's remembered settings.

ISO 32000-2: not applicable. Imposing pages onto print sheets is an application feature, and the specification doesn't describe it.

| | `Mitarbeiter` | 1 | **2** | 2 | 1 | 1 |

The first file writes a U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE on each side of every gap between words (`is` U+200B ` ` U+200B `made`); the second stores the word with U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN at its hyphenation points (`Mit` U+00AD `arbei` U+00AD `terinnen`). title: fix(render): a symbolic TrueType font in the Macintosh glyph order reads its codes as Mac Roman (hayro-interpret patch 101)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

The real files below are public test PDFs from the pdf.js repository (`test/pdfs`). Each is linked once and then named by file name.

`issue2017r.pdf` (https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/2017) ends with a line of accented letters. This is its extracted text, measured with each reader's own text extraction:

| Reader | Last line |
|---|---|
| `main` | `ˆ‰•Ž••”•™ŸÏÕ` |
| This PR | `àâçéèêîïôüœ’` |
| PDFium | `àâçéèêîïôüœ’` |
| MuPDF | `ˆ‰•Ž••”•™ŸÏÕ` |
| pdftotext (Poppler 26.09.0) | `ˆ‰•Ž••”•™ŸÏÕ` |

With this PR the line extracts as PDFium extracts it, character for character. Search and copy see the same text.

### Why `main` gets it wrong

The line's font, `HEJHEO+NewCenturySchlbk-Roman+2`, is an embedded TrueType font flagged symbolic (`/Flags 4`). It has no `/Encoding` and no `/ToUnicode`. Its `post` table is version 3.0, so it has no glyph names. It has a (1, 0) Macintosh Roman `cmap` subtable and a (3, 0) one, and code *c* and 0xF000 + *c* select the same glyph in them. With nothing else to go on, `main` reads every code as WinAnsi, so code 0x88 reads as `ˆ`. The glyph it draws is `à`.

### The rule

A code of such a font now reads as Mac OS Roman when two things agree:

1. **The (1, 0) subtable selects the glyph the code draws.** ISO 32000-2 §9.6.5.4 says that for a font with no encoding, "if the font contains a (1, 0) subtable, single bytes from the string shall be used to look up the associated glyph descriptions from the subtable". For a symbolic font it recommends a (1, 0) subtable and says a (3, 0) subtable, "if present, … should map from character codes in the range 0xF000 to 0xF0FF by prepending the single-byte codes in the (1, 0) subtable with 0xF0". The (1, 0) subtable is the Macintosh Roman platform encoding: its codes are Mac OS Roman codes.
2. **The glyph sits where the standard Macintosh glyph order puts that character.** This is the order of the 258 names of a version 1.0 `post` table. In `issue2017r.pdf`, code 0x88 dr…

title: M3: a space taken back under the next letter stays a word break, so right-to-left words are not split (view.copy-text)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

The public file `issue11656.pdf` (https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/11656) is Hebrew set in visual order. Its last line ends in "מבקר המדינה". Copied text read **"המדינ ה"**, with a space inside the word. The first two lines ended **"כולם ?"** and **"אמיתי ."**, with a space before the punctuation. Find did not match "המדינה" or "כולם?" (0 matches each).

The cause is in the content stream. Each right-to-left show string starts with the space that ends its word, then pulls the next letter back over it:

```
[<0003>324<02A402B002A902A3>4<02AE02A4> …] TJ     % " " then ה נ י ד מ ה, left to right
```

At 11.04 pt the space advances 313/1000 em, and the `324` adjustment takes back 324/1000 em. So "ה" starts 0.12 pt **left** of the space it is drawn after. Sorting the line by x put the space after "ה", inside the word.

ISO 32000-2 §14.8.2.5.3 describes this layout. A reverse-order show string "may have a SPACE (U+0020) … at the beginning or end to indicate a word break", and its NOTE 2 says such a space "provides an opportunity to realign the typography without visible effect". §14.8.2.6.2 then requires that space to be a word break in the character stream.

A blank glyph has no ink, so its box cannot place it relative to a glyph that covers it. Placement now keeps a blank in drawing order, before the glyph drawn right after it, when all of the following hold (`keep_taken_back_blanks` in `crates/render/src/text/order.rs`):

- the line has right-to-left text;
- that next glyph is a right-to-left letter or a neutral (punctuation, a symbol);
- it starts at or left of the blank's start and covers at least half of it;
- no glyph placed before it also reaches over the blank, as in a letter-and-mark cluster.

| `issue11656.pdf` | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| line 1 ends | `כולם ?` | `כולם?` |
| line 2 ends | `אמיתי .` | `אמיתי.` |
| line 4 ends | `המדינ ה` | `המדינה` |
| `text_find` "המדינה" / "כולם?" | 0 / 0 | 1 / 1 |

title: M2: a non-symbolic TrueType font reads its Unicode-platform cmap (#6581)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6581.

Text set in an embedded, non-symbolic TrueType font now draws its letters, where it drew boxes, when the font's `cmap` has only a Unicode-platform `(0, x)` subtable.

For a non-symbolic TrueType font, `EmbeddedKind::map_code` (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/true_type.rs`) reads a code as a glyph name through the font's encoding and takes that name's Unicode. It looked the Unicode up only in a Windows `(3, 1)` subtable, then (through Mac Roman) in a Macintosh `(1, 0)` one, then by `post` glyph name. A font whose only subtable is `(0, 1)` matched none of them, and every code drew `.notdef`. The file in #6581 embeds such a font, `/TT0` (`AZFTUD+HelveticaNeue-Bold`, `/WinAnsiEncoding`, `/Flags 32`). It sets almost all of the text on page 15, and its `.notdef` is a rectangle, so the page came out as boxes. The Type 0 font on the same page was not affected.

- **Where:** the non-symbolic branch of `EmbeddedKind::map_code`. When `(3, 1)`, `(1, 0)` and the `post` names all give nothing, a Unicode-platform `(0, x)` subtable is read as Unicode, like `(3, 1)`. `(0, 5)` is skipped because it holds Unicode variation sequences, not characters.
- **Order:** ISO 32000-2 §9.6.5.4 names only `(3, 1)` and `(1, 0)` for a non-symbolic font, so the new route comes **last**. A code the existing routes draw keeps its glyph. Only codes that drew `.notdef` before can change. The diff only adds lines; the existing lookups are untouched.
- **Untouched:** symbolic fonts (the #4156 path), CFF-flavoured programs, Type 0 fonts and substitutes.

The reason is recorded in a `PdfCraft patch (#6581)` comment at the change and in a `vendor/README.md` entry next to #4156's, so a future hayro sync keeps it.

**Relation to #2980.** #2980 (for #2159) also probes `(0, *)` subtables in this branch, among several other changes: `(3, 10)`, `post` alias resolution, `/.notdef` in `/Differences`, and `from_bits_truncate` for the flags. It no longer applies to `main` (`git app…

title: fix(forms): recalculate scripted fields after ResetForm
author: LMatt08
body:
## What this changes

`ResetForm` restores field defaults (`/DV`), but the existing `NoScripts` recalculation skipped custom JavaScript Calculate actions. A stale calculated value could then be saved. The expected result is a recalculation after defaults are restored.

| Scenario | price | total |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial | 42 | 84 |
| Before LF-003, targeted reset | 17 | 84 |
| After LF-003, targeted reset | 17 | 34 |

`reset_with` restores defaults using `NoScripts` for intermediate writes, then recalculates through the engine's `ResetScripts` adapter. Document bootstrap scripts may define helpers, but their field writes and host requests are suppressed during reset; the real Calculate and Format actions retain their effects. body:

Find and `text_find` miss a word when the page divides it with something the reader cannot see: a soft hyphen or zero width character inside it, or a line end in the middle of a Chinese or Japanese word. Counts are `text_find` hits on this branch; PDFium and MuPDF counts are their text-search APIs, Poppler's are occurrences in `pdftotext` output.

body:

Fixes #6517

Copied text, Find and `text_extract` read each line's glyphs in x order. Two kinds of file broke that order: right-to-left text where a space is pulled back under the next letter, and left-to-right scripts drawn one glyph at a time with zero-advance combining marks. **Right-to-left words split by a space.** `issue11656.pdf`, from pdf.js issue 11656 (https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/11656), is Hebrew set in visual order:

| `issue11656.pdf` | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|

## What this changes

On Windows, `apps/pdfcraft/build.rs` embeds two icons into `pdfcraft.exe`:
- Resource ID `1` (index `0`): `assets/app-icon/pdfcraft.ico` (the Lion application icon).
- Resource ID `2` (`-2`): `assets/app-icon/pdfcraft-document.ico` (the dedicated PDF document sheet icon).

When running the Windows **Portable** build or when a user manually selects `pdfcraft.exe` via Windows Explorer (*Open with ▸ Choose another app ▸ Browse*), Windows creates `HKCU\Software\Classes\Applications\pdfcraft.exe\shell\open\command` (or `pdf_auto_file`) without a `DefaultIcon` subkey and without `TypeOverlay = ""`. title: fix(cos,hayro): a number token with no finite value reads as null in both parsers
author: chamber074
body:
Fixes #6477.

## The rule

PdfCraft parses PDF numbers twice: `crates/cos` (model, redact, the editing crates) and the vendored `vendor/hayro-syntax`. For a number token with no finite `f64` value — word forms (`+inf`, `-nan`, `+Infinity`), integer overflow (1 followed by 400 zeros), real overflow (`1e400`) — the two disagreed: cos produced `Real(inf)`, hayro saturated integers to `f64::MAX`, read `1e400` as absent (the issue-994 check), and read `-inf`/`-nan` as `0` plus a stray token. Model geometry and the drawn page could therefore differ, which moves redaction areas (`crates/redact/src/sanitize.rs` works from model's `Page::crop`).

Both parsers now apply one rule, defined identically in each as `has_no_finite_value`: such a token reads as **null at its own slot**. Readers then fall back the same way on both sides (`/UserUnit` → 1, inherited or default box).

Null-in-slot rather than token failure, because failure invalidates the whole enclosing object in both parsers today: a direct `1e400` in hayro fails `Number::skip`, which fails the enclosing dict or array, and cos likewise rejects the container for a "bad number". Making only the `Number` read fail would also have added a crash — `ArrayIter::next` and `Dict::entries` unwrap reads that skip accepted. (Null is also what #2877's review asked cos for.)

## Changes

- **cos** (`crates/cos/src/parser.rs`): `number()` returns `Object::Null` for these tokens and never produces an infinite or NaN `Real`. The check runs only off the fast path, so the #5873 parsing speed work is untouched.
- **hayro** (patch **(36)**, recorded in `vendor/README.md` with `PdfCraft patch (36):` markers in source): typed reads (`Number`, `f32`, `Rect`, `dict.get`) find nothing for the token, `Object::read` returns `Null`, and `Object::skip` steps over it whole. This also fixes `-inf` reading as `0` plus a stray `inf` token. The patch-(8) test is updated: 400 nines now read as absent instead of finite.
- **Content streams are in scope**…

title: M3: "Always use my default zoom" holds for a file opened again (#6591)
author: Nghiathan13
body:
## What this changes

Refs #6591.

With **Always use my default zoom and page layout** on, a file opened again now opens at the default zoom and page display. Before, it came back at the zoom it was closed with. It still reopens at the page the reader left off on.

**Restore the last view…** is on by default. When a file is opened again, `apply_last_view` (`crates/ui-egui/src/persist/last_view.rs`) applies the file's remembered zoom, page display and cover page. It checked `restore_last_view` but never `always_default_view`. The "Always" option (#1618) landed four days before last-view restore (#1767). As a result it overrode only the document's own opening view, and the remembered view still replaced the user's default.

- **Where:** `apply_last_view`. With `always_default_view` on, it skips the remembered page display, cover and zoom, and still goes to the remembered page.
- **Why the page stays:** this matches how `apply_initial_view` already treats a document's own `/OpenAction` under the same option: only the page is kept (`always_my_default_view_keeps_the_zoom_and_goes_to_the_page_top`). The option's label is about zoom and layout, not position.
- **Untouched:** with "Always…" off, the remembered zoom still wins over Default zoom, as #1767 intends. A file opened for the first time is unaffected either way.

**What this means for #6591.** The report says Default zoom has no effect on a reopened file. It doesn't say whether "Always…" was ticked, and the reporter wrote in through Discord, so I couldn't ask.
- **"Always…" ticked:** this is the bug fixed here.
- **"Always…" not ticked:** a reopened file coming back at its last zoom is #1767's intended behaviour, and this PR leaves it as is. Before this change, the only way to get Default zoom on reopen was to turn off "Restore the last view…", which also loses the page. Now ticking "Always…" gives the default zoom and keeps the page.

That's why this says "Refs" rather than "Fixes". Please close #6591 with this PR …

title: fix(ui): keys under a dialog or a menu leave the pages alone (keyboard routing, part 1)
author: alehel
body:
## Why

The page pointer router gave a press on the pages one owner. Keys never got the same treatment: each page module reads egui's keys itself and decides for itself whether a dialog, a menu or a text field should stop it, and several don't ask. The pages are drawn before the dialogs, so they read the keys first. On `main` today:

- **Under a dialog:**
  - Delete or Backspace deletes the comment, added text, link or Prepare field selected behind it.
  - The Escape that closes a dialog also deselects what is behind it. With Edit text objects selected, the dialog doesn't close at all.

author: Nghiathan13
body:
## What this changes

Refs #6577.

The colour pickers' **Recent colours** row (the last five custom colours added with **+** / "Other colour…") now survives closing and reopening PdfCraft. Before this change it was empty at every launch.

The row lived only in egui's temporary memory (`recent_custom_colours` / `remember_custom_colour` in `crates/ui-egui/src/tools/comments/menu.rs`), which is never written to the settings file.

- **Saving:** `persist()` writes the row as `"recent_colours"` next to the per-tool comment styles. Order is newest first, each entry an `[r, g, b]` array.

Those rules are now one function, `push_recent`, used both by `remember_custom_colour` and when reading settings.

title: fix(edit): a space a subset cannot show is as wide as the line's own word gaps (#6609)
author: fatihkunak
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6609.

When no font of the family can show a space, an edit sets the space as a `TJ` gap, and the gap was a flat 0.33 em. pdfTeX justifies each line by its own amount, so the gaps in one paper run from about 0.2 to 0.5 em and a flat value matches few lines.

`source_space` now takes, before it falls back to 0.33, the median word gap the line being edited draws: the distance from the box of one word to the next (`TextLine.ink`) on an upright line, less the character spacing that follows a word (`source_show` adds it back). A line with no two words a gap apart keeps 0.33. Gaps outside 0.05 to 1.0 em (a column break, a gap a redaction left, touching words) are not counted.

It reaches the four places that ask for the space: `replace_line`, the paragraph rewrite (`source_font`) and the two in the styled rewrite. The styled rewrite keeps its once-per-font cache; the gap is measured from the paragraph's own lines in that font.

It only has an effect where a subset gives the space no width and #6158 sends that edit down the gap path. On `main` such a space is still written as code 32 at width 0, so the two PRs are independent to merge but this one shows its effect with #6158.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check` clean
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib`: 448 passed

**Tests.** `a_space_a_subset_cannot_show_is_as_wide_as_the_lines_own_word_gaps` builds a line with half an em between two words and checks that both spaces added to it are set at -500, not -330. It fails with the fix reverted (the flat value returns). `a_space_a_subset_cannot_show_is_a_guess_when_the_line_has_one_word` pins that a line with nothing to measure keeps 0.33.

**On real files.** I merged this with #6158 locally and edited eight body lines of pdf.js's `tracemonkey.pdf` (pdfTeX, Type 1 subsets) by appending ` dans la liste`. The words' gaps were read back with PyMuPDF and compared with each li…

title: feat(collab): real-time collaboration for PDFs behind a flag
author: copoka
body:
## What

Real-time collaboration for PDFs: several people comment, reply and fill forms
on one document while page structure changes are serialised by an authoritative
server. Off by default behind the `collab` feature; a normal single-user session
is unchanged.

- `crates/collab-proto` — the wire envelope: operations, versions, epoch,
  presence, commit, resync.
- `crates/collab-server` — one authoritative room per document: versions, the
  `opId` window, lease, roles, journal/tail, limits, forced compaction.
- `crates/collab-pdf` — the PDF adapter over the engine: annotations (typed
  shapes, restyle, font size, author/subject/icon, parts, move, geometry,
  pop-up, reply, delete/restore), form values, page
  rotate/move/delete/insert/duplicate/replace/blank insert/split/combine, the
  outline with its named destinations, page labels and links — plus its durable
  store.
- `crates/collab-annot`, `crates/collab-outline`, `crates/collab-link` — the
  typed wire forms of an annotation, an outline item and a link, with their
  bounds, shared by the server adapter and the client projection.
- `crates/collab-hub` — delivery to connected clients.
- `crates/collab-ws` — blocking WebSocket transport with RS256 or HS256 JWT
  sessions, an `Origin` check, message limits and backpressure.
- `crates/collab-client`, `crates/collab-client-pdf`, `crates/collab-session` —
  the client state machine, the operation ↔ engine edit projection (with
  inverse operations for undo), and one protocol driver behind a `Transport`
  trait with a native socket and a browser `WebSocket` implementation.
- `apps/pdfcraft-collab-server` — a daemon that serves rooms from the host's
  control plane (or a directory in development), commits atomically, publishes
  through a retrying queue and exposes `/health` and `/metrics`.

  `Session::apply_remote`, per-…

title: Word tables get outer borders only where the page rules them
author: bflatastic
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up to #5154. A table whose grid the page rules now gets Word's outer borders only on the edges the page draws a line along; the inside borders are unchanged. Before, a grid drawn with inside lines only (common in invoices and forms) got a box in Word that the PDF never had.

- `ruled()` in `crates/export/src/layout.rs` returns which outer edges (top, left, bottom, right) are ruled: a line over every column above the first row or below the last, or beside every row left of the first column or right of the last. It must sit no farther from the cells than the next row or column, so a page rule far above a table is not its frame. These checks spend the same comparison budget as the grid check.
- `Table::ruled` is now `Option<[bool; 4]>`: `Some` when the grid is ruled, holding the outer edges. `docx_table` writes `single` for the inside edges and the ruled outer edges, and `nil` for the rest.
- The `doc_export_office` tool description, the parity entry and `docs/file-format-parity.md` no longer say Word tables are always borderless.

title: M2 #6168: an Identity CID font named after an installed Windows face draws in that face
author: charlieruk
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6168.

The file in the report (a Taiwanese maintenance schedule exported by Acrobat PDFMaker from Word) draws its page heading `2.四行程速克達系列機車定期保養檢查表(250cc 以下機種適用)` without any of its Chinese characters: only `2.`, `(250cc` and `)` show. Other readers on Windows show it whole.

**Why.** The Chinese part of that heading is in font `C2_0`:
- a Type 0 font with `/Encoding /Identity-H`;
- its descendant a `CIDFontType2` of the `Adobe-Identity` collection, named `SimSun`;
- not embedded, and without `/ToUnicode`.

Its CIDs are SimSun's own glyph ids (`/CIDToGIDMap` defaults to Identity, ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.2). Only that face can draw them. The installed-face fallback (`crates/render/src/system_font.rs`) serves only the four Adobe regional collections, so the font got the standard Latin substitute: it has no glyph at the high ids the Chinese characters use, which drew nothing, and its glyphs at low ids are unrelated letters, so `128` drew as `34:`.

**Now.** On Windows the fallback answers an Identity CID font that names an installed face with that face:
- `WINDOWS_NAMED_FACES` lists the names Windows faces go by in PDFs and the file in the Fonts folder holding each: SimSun, NSimSun, SimHei, KaiTi, FangSong, MingLiU, PMingLiU, DFKai-SB, Microsoft YaHei and JhengHei, MS Mincho and Gothic, Malgun Gothic, Gulim and Batang.
- The file is only where to look. The face drawn is the one in it whose PostScript or family name is the requested name, compared without a subset tag, a `,Bold`-style suffix, punctuation or case.
- A `,Bold` name of a family whose bold is a face in a file of its own (Microsoft YaHei, Microsoft JhengHei, Malgun Gothic: `WINDOWS_BOLD_FACES`) is drawn with that bold face when its file is installed, as Windows does for a bold request, so the CIDs are the bold face's glyph ids. Only when that file is missing is it the regular face. The other listed families have one face, so `SimSun,Bold` keeps the regular face.

title: M14: Windows Explorer and Outlook PDF preview handler (supersedes #5646)
author: daBOB
body:
## What this changes

Supersedes #5646 by @Rees-FrischeMarkte, rebased on `main`. Their commits keep their authorship, including the thumbnail handler from #5645. Refs #3207.

- **Rebase.** The only conflict was `Cargo.toml`. The two new crates now take the workspace version 0.18.1, and `Cargo.lock` follows.

title: Draw Thai in Fill & Sign, text boxes, form fields, headers, footers and watermarks (#2354)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2354. Thai typed into Fill & Sign text, a text box comment, a form field whose `/DA` font can't hold it, a header or footer, or a text watermark used to be written as "?????" in Helvetica/WinAnsi. title: Edit a PDF: select all, copy, cut and paste page objects within and between documents (#5989)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What this changes

Refs #5989. Copy, cut and paste of existing page objects now work in Edit a PDF, as Acrobat's Edit PDF does, and Ctrl/Cmd+A selects every object on the page.

- **Ctrl/Cmd+A** fills the existing multi-object selection with every paragraph, artwork and added item on the current page. Arrows, drag and Delete then act on all of them, one undo step each. Inside a paragraph or text box that is open for typing, Ctrl+A still selects its text.
- **Copy** replays the page state up to the last selected object (transform, clips, colours, ExtGStates, text state), then paints only the selection. It keeps only the resources the selection uses.
- **Paste** runs the copy through Ungroup's resource merge, so names don't clash and patterns move with the offset.
  - Within one document, the same fonts and images are reused.
  - Into another document, objects are deep-copied first with organize's page copier: cycle-safe, depth-bounded and deduplicated, and capped at 20,000 objects or 256 MB, past which it says to copy fewer objects.
  - Pasting onto the same page lands 18 pt down and to the right, as Acrobat does. Elsewhere it lands in place, each further paste steps again, and anything that would fall off the page is centred.
- **Cut** is one undo step. Edit ▸ Copy, Cut and Paste are enabled for objects. The system clipboard gets the copied text or the first picture, and a newer copy made in another app wins the paste.
- **Headless:** new `object_copy` (selected objects or `all`, with `cut`) and `object_paste` tools; `object_move` also accepts `all`.
- **Ungroup:** a form with no resources of its own that names no resource no longer blocks a merge that renames resources, because renaming can't affect it. A form that does name a resource is still refused.

#4264 and #4268 handle added text boxes and images only. This PR reuses their idea of comparing the clipboard text, and nothing else.

title: Combine files: a drop is one undo step, in order, and names what it can't take
author: bflatastic
body:
## What this changes

Refs #4985. Main already adds files dropped on the Combine Files tab (`drop_into_combine`), as Acrobat's Combine Files does. Three things were wrong:

- **One undo step per drop:** a multi-file drop was added one undo step per file. It is now one step (`add_dropped_to_combine` → `stage_combine_with`).
- **Unsupported files:** a file Combine doesn't take (e.g. `.docx`, `.zip`) used to be added as a "Can't be read" row. Now it's skipped, and a toast names it: "Not added: …. Combine takes PDFs, images and text files." The check is the one `Session::as_pdf` uses, so a PDF with no extension is still taken.
- **Order on web:** the web build read each dropped file in its own task, so the order wasn't guaranteed. It now reads them one after another into a single request, in drop order.

Outside Combine, a drop opens each file as before. `Incoming::new` and a `dropped_name` helper replace five copies of the same code. title: fix(edit): editing an OCR phrase redraws only the words it changes (refs #3313)
author: TiagoCK
body:
What this changes
Refs #3313: the part the reporter asked about ("I am just trying to delete text"). #5454 fixed the size half. A closer substitute font is left out; I suggested on the issue that it become its own.

Deleting one word from a recognized line covered the whole line and redrew all of it in Helvetica, though only that word had changed. Now a text edit of an OCR phrase covers and redraws only the words it changes, and the rest stay as the scan shows them (still invisible text, so still searchable):

A deleted word is covered and leaves its gap. The words after it are pixels, so they don't move.
A replaced word is drawn in its place, at the phrase's size from #5454.
A replacement a little too wide is squeezed across to fit, by up to a quarter, so it ends by the middle of the gap before the next word. Without this, "kind" to "good" redrew the rest of the line: taking over the next word pushes that one along too, and so on.
A replacement wider than that takes over the word it would run into.
New words with nothing to replace take a neighbor with them.
A change of formatting or a typed line break still redraws the whole phrase, since those are about the whole phrase.
How it works (crates/edit/src/text_regions/ocr_words.rs): the words are aligned with the draft, and each changed stretch goes through rewrite_styled_block as a phrase of its own, which is how a phrase beside others in one OCR layer already rewrites. So there is no new content-stream writing. word_lines reads the layer with every show its own line, because words OCR sized alike otherwise share a run and couldn't be kept apart. The session asks for this (BlockStyle::changed_words_only) only when the edit came with no formatting.

The edit is tried on a copy of the document, and falls back to the whole-phrase rewrite if anything goes wrong: a word that would move (a layer whose words have no position of their own), or runs that aren't words (one per letter). Nothing changes in the document unless th…

title: Add colour-preserving dark reading
author: gnqgpsr495-ui
body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft's reading palettes currently turn coloured text into a luminance-based palette. Add an optional **Colour-preserving dark** preset that changes white paper to soft dark grey and black ink to off-white while keeping source hues recognizable.

The curve is independently implemented in Rust from the [public Sebyoshi mathematical reference](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/3281#issuecomment-6725501625). It uses the existing paint replacement path, adds no dependency, and leaves pictures and annotation appearances under the existing exclusions. Preferences, persistence, document seeding and `view_reading_colors` all expose the mode; older settings retain their existing mapping. Changing modes replaces the previous curve, including when both modes have identical paper and ink colours.

The first commit also fixes reading colours leaking into image exports. PNG, JPEG and TIFF output now use original colours for every reading palette, including parallel exports, while retaining unsaved document edits. The second commit adds the new reading mode and extends that regression test.

This branch includes main `8c99ec4e0` and complements the inversion proposal in #3281.

title: fix(render): a stream ending in endstrea is not read into a later object's stream (hayro-syntax patch 36)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Take a stream that ends in a misspelt `endstrea` and is followed by another object whose stream does end in `endstream`. Its `/Length` is now taken as written, so reading stops at the end of its own data. Before this change, both readers searched past it for `endstream`. The search found the later object's keyword and read that object's header and data as part of this stream. A page whose content stream sits in this position draws blank on `main`. In the test below, an ASCIIHex stream picks up the next object's header as hex data.

ISO 32000-2 §7.3.8.1 puts a stream's bytes between the `stream` and `endstream` keywords and says "the stream dictionary specifies the exact number of bytes". §7.3.8.2 (and the `Length` row of Table 5) says `Length` "indicates how many bytes of the PDF file are used for the stream's data".

- **`pdfcraft-cos`** (`parse_indirect_in`): a `/Length` that fits in the file is the stream's extent when the next thing after it, white space aside, is a whole `endstream` token, or the end of the file, or a whole `endstrea` or `endobj` token (or both) after which the object ends too: the end of the file, another object's `N G obj` header, or `xref`, `trailer` or `startxref`. A token runs on through regular characters (§7.2.3), so payload bytes such as `endobject` where a wrong `/Length` stops don't count, and neither does payload such as `endobj more`. This is checked before the search for `endstream`, and the check reads only the bytes right after the `/Length`. The search for `endstream` also takes only a whole token, so payload such as `endstreamer` is skipped. A `/Length` that is wrong or missing still goes to the search, and still falls back to a fitting `/Length` when the search finds nothing. The `/Length` is converted to `usize` with `try_from` before the check, so it can't wrap on a 32-bit target.
- **`pdfcraft-cos`** (`Document::scan_for`): an object found by the last-resort scan of the file, because its cross-referenc…

title: Do not send duplex to printers without two-sided support

Leave duplex unset for a printer reported as not two-sided, so that printer keeps its own setting, while printers that support two-sided or report no capability keep the chosen setting.

title: fix(preflight): resolve indirect spot families, null dict entries, and numeric equality
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary
- Resolve indirect colour space family names (`[/Separation ...]` and `[/DeviceN ...]`) in `Scan::walk` and `Scan::separation_named` when the first array element is an `Object::Ref` (ISO 32000-1 §7.3.10).

body: ## What this changes Fixes #6677. A ticked XFA check button now shows the mark its template asks for. title: M4: custom document properties are kept in XMP as pdfx: properties (organize.custom-properties)
author: Ethunxxx
body:
## What this changes

Custom document properties (Document Properties ▸ Custom, `doc_set_info`) were written only to `/Info`. Acrobat also keeps each one in the XMP packet, as `pdfx:<name>` in the `http://ns.adobe.com/pdfx/1.3/` schema. This was listed as missing in `organize.custom-properties`: "Not yet: mirroring them into XMP (pdfx:) as Acrobat does". Tools that read XMP (ExifTool, asset managers, search indexers) therefore saw an Acrobat-written file's custom properties but not a PdfCraft-written one's.

- **`organize::xmp::sync_info`** already keeps Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Creator and Producer in step. It now does the same for a custom property: `pdfx:<name>` as plain text, changed where it stands (element or attribute form), and removed when the property is cleared. The rest of the packet is untouched byte for byte, as before.
- **The same limits as the standard fields apply.** Only files that already have a packet this can edit safely are changed; a file without XMP gets none.
- **Names that can't be XML element names stay in `/Info` only.** `check_custom_key` lets through names XML can't use, such as `1st`, `Q&A` or `a:b`. Those are not mirrored, rather than written under an escaped name no other reader knows. `is_xml_name` follows XML 1.0 §2.3 `NameStartChar`/`NameChar` without the colon (`NCName`).
- **Standard entries XMP doesn't mirror here** (CreationDate, ModDate, Trapped) are not written as `pdfx:`.
- **PDF/X identification.** `GTS_PDFXVersion` and `GTS_PDFXConformance` are custom properties as far as `set_info` is concerned, so they can now have `pdfx:` copies. `remove_standard_id(PdfX)` (`standards_remove_id`) removes those copies along with the `/Info` entries and the `pdfxid:` properties. Detection still reads only `pdfxid:`, so the copies never change which standard a file declares.

title: Updates: a ready update starts its helper when the app exits
author: dotCooCoo

On macOS the process ends before `eframe::run_native` returns, so the `Updater` is not dropped. craft-update at 1b34eba41 starts the restart helper only from `Updater::start_pending_update` or from dropping the `Updater`, so after a ready update closes the app, the helper that installs the update and reopens the app does not start.

title: M2: masked images premultiply with integers, not through f32
author: Nghiathan13
body:
## What this changes

Pages with many images under soft masks draw faster, with the same pixels. Premultiplying went through `AlphaColor` and `f32` for every source pixel. That step runs once per source pixel however small the image is drawn, so on these pages it was the largest single cost in a `perf` profile of the renderer.

`premultiply_sample` does the same step with integers. It is used in `area_shrink_premultiplied` (images being shrunk) and `premultiply_rgba` (images drawn at or above their resolution). Both are existing PdfCraft patches in `vendor/hayro`, and the change is recorded as patch 32 in `vendor/README.md`.

### Measurements

Test file: a 31-page, 10 MB booklet with about 115 to 230 image draws per page, most of them under a soft mask. It isn't attached, because its fonts and logos aren't licensed for this repository (`AGENTS.md` §1). Measured on one Linux machine with 16 cores, against a release build of this PR's base.

Only enable app-drawn decorations on Wayland, keep native server-side decorations on X11, and ensure the minimum window size fits a quarter-screen quadrant.

title: Forms: report and edit each radio button's own mark (#6682)
author: IllusiveMilkman
body: Closes #6682. ## What was wrong `/MK /CA` is a widget entry (ISO 32000-2 Table 192), so the buttons of one radio group, or the widgets of one check box, can have different marks. PdfCraft drew each widget with its own mark, but read the style from the first widget and wrote a change to every widget. A mixed group was reported as the first button's mark, and changing the style silently replaced the others. ## What changes - **forms:** `check_styles` reads each widget's mark. `FieldProps::check_style_widget` changes one widget; an index out of range is refused before anything is written. Without it, every widget changes as before. - **engine:** `Document::field_check_styles`. - **automation:** `form_fields` keeps a single `check_style` when the widgets agree, and reports `"check_style": "mixed"` plus `check_styles` (one per widget) when they differ. `form_set_props` accepts the existing 1-based `widget` argument with `check_style`. Tool descriptions updated. - **Field Properties ▸ Options ▸ Button Style:** shows **Mixed** for a group whose buttons differ. OK without a choice keeps every mark; choosing a style applies it to every button, including when it matches the first button's. - **Shared Field Properties** (several fields selected): read only the first widget too. It now sees every widget's mark, and a chosen style reaches widgets whose first sibling already matched. - **parity:** `form.check-box-style` cites the new tests. Fields whose widgets agree (the usual case) report and behave exactly as before. ## Screenshots From the issue's `mixed-radio.pdf` (button `a` a check, `b` a star), after `form_set_props` with `check_style: square, widget: 1`: #### `a` selected, now a square: #### `b` selected, still its star:

title: M6: the Calculate tab shows and edits a field's custom calculation script (#6630)
author: ljkx
body:
## What this changes

A field whose calculation is a script of its own (anything that isn't an AF sum/product/… or simplified field notation) showed **"Value is not calculated"** on Field Properties ▸ Calculate. The script couldn't be read or edited in the app, and picking Simple or Notation replaced it with nothing to say one was there (#6630). Acrobat's Calculate tab has a fourth choice for this, *Custom calculation script*; this adds it.

- **`pdfcraft-forms`**: `af::Calculate` gains `Custom(String)`. Reading a field never produces it: an unrecognised script still goes to `actions.unsupported` and `actions.scripts.calculate`, where the JavaScript engine runs it, so nothing that reads forms changes. Authoring (`set_props`) writes it back as given, as a **text string** (as `set_field_script` / `form_set_script` write scripts), so a letter outside ASCII reads the same in other viewers; a blank one writes no `/AA /C` and leaves `/CO`. `Calculate::reads()` lists what it reads with the existing `calculation_reads`, and `af::calculate()` returns `None` for it (it is the engine's to run).
- **Field Properties**: `FieldDraft::new` maps a preserved calculate script to `Custom`, so the existing diff does the rest. An untouched OK writes nothing; an edited script is written; *Value is not calculated* removes it. Choosing another mode and coming back to Custom brings back the field's own script, not an empty box.
- **Calculate tab**: a fourth radio, *Custom calculation script:*, with the script in a monospace box that scrolls (at most 180 pt tall). A script longer than 256 KiB (forms read up to 64 MiB of script, and the JS engine runs nothing past 256 KiB) isn't edited: the box shows its first 256 KiB (cut at a whole character), read-only but selectable, with a note giving its size, and the script is kept as it is unless another calculation is chosen. An edit in the box that would take a script past that (a large paste; the limit counts bytes, as the engine does) isn't made, …

title: i18n: Hebrew (he) interface, right to left
author: yonatan-langer83
body:
Hebrew (`he`) becomes a PdfCraft interface language, right to left like Arabic, Kurdish and Persian.

## What changes

- **`LANGUAGES`** gets `he` (right to left) after Persian, and `english_name` gets "Hebrew". The catalogs are already in craft-i18n (`locales/he/`). The Hebrew letters come from the installed Hebrew face that `platform::system_fonts::hebrew_fallback` already finds.
- **Locale matching.** The older code `iw` (`iw_IL`, still reported by some systems and Java) resolves to `he` in `candidates`.
- **Date format.** Hebrew is also a date language (`DATE_LANGUAGES`), with Gregorian month and weekday names. After a day number the month takes the prefix ב (`8 באוקטובר`), through `months_with_day`.
- **macOS bundle.** `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` declares `he` in `CFBundleLocalizations`.

## Tests

- New: `hebrew_is_registered_and_persists`. It checks:
  - the name and the right-to-left flag;
  - CLDR one/two/other plural forms;

title: M3: a finger flicked with the Hand tool glides on after it lifts (#1231)
author: super1gta
body:
## What this changes

On a touch screen, a page flicked with the Hand tool now keeps moving after the finger lifts and slows to a stop, the way a page does on a phone or tablet. Before this change it stopped dead where the finger left the glass, so reading a long document on a touch laptop took a drag for every screenful.

This adds the "fling that keeps the page moving after the finger lifts" that #1231 lists as still missing. It reuses the touchpad glide from #531 (`canvas/fling.rs`): the same exponential decay, edge stop, stale-frame guard and speed cap, plus the same gate, so nothing glides with Animation effects off, in single-page paging, or under a dialog.

- **Touch only.** A mouse drag with the Hand tool still stops where it is let go, so mouse users see no change. A drag glides only if a finger on a touch screen started it (`InputState::any_touches` on the drag's first pass), so a finger touching the screen during a mouse drag doesn't make it glide.
- **A pinch doesn't glide.** If a second finger joins a drag at any point, letting go doesn't glide. This stops the last finger lifted after a pinch zoom from throwing the page.
- **Holding still before lifting doesn't glide.** This uses the same lift-speed window and `STILL` threshold as the touchpad glide.
- **Catching it.** A finger back on the page, a click, a key or a zoom stops the glide, as it does for the touchpad.
- **Longer coast.** A touch drag uses a longer decay (`DRAG_TAU` = 0.6 s, against `TAU` = 0.35 s for the touchpad), closer to how phones feel. A touchpad glide is unchanged.
- **No new setting.** Animation effects, and the system's reduce-motion setting it follows, already switch the glide off, the same way #531 did for the touchpad.

Refs #1231.

## How you verified it

On Windows 11 ARM64 (Snapdragon X Elite) with a touch screen: `cargo run --release -p pdfcraft`, Hand tool, long document. Flicks glide and settle. A finger down catches the page, a pinch zoom doesn't throw it, a mouse drag s…

title: M3: a password prompt keeps a place in the open queue for its retry
author: bflatastic
body:
Main's Windows gate fails in `editing::a_long_startup_list_behind_a_password_prompt_opens_every_file` (#5762):

> timed out waiting for every file: … password=("startup-long-locked-….pdf", Some("too many documents are waiting to open"))

The files named after a protected one fill the open worker's bounded queue (16). When the password is submitted before the worker has taken any of them, which happens on the slower Windows runner, the retry is refused and the prompt comes back with that error.

**Fix:** while a password prompt is open, the files waiting for the worker leave one place free (`open_slots`, used by both checks of the bound), so the prompt's retry always fits. Files past the bound still wait in order in `deferred_opens` and are submitted as opens finish.

**Test:** `a_password_prompt_keeps_a_place_in_the_open_queue_for_its_retry` holds the worker with the prepare gate, raises the prompt behind 20 other files and checks that one place stays free and the retry is queued. Without the fix the poll refills the queue to 16 and the first check fails.

Not run locally (GitHub CI only); `rustfmt --check` passes.

title: docs: explain missing printer settings on Linux (CUPS PPD permissions)
author: jagjordi
body:
## Summary

On Linux, **Printer properties…** can say "This printer offers no settings of its own." for a CUPS queue whose PPD has dozens of options, while GTK dialogs (Chrome, Evince) show them all. This adds `docs/linux-printing.md` explaining the cause and the fix, plus a two-line pointer in the README's Linux section.

## Cause

`printer_options_via_within` in `crates/print/src/spool.rs` opens `/etc/cups/ppd/<queue>.ppd` directly. CUPS writes PPDs as `root:<scheduler group>` with mode `0640` (`root:cups` on Arch Linux, `lp` elsewhere). A user outside that group cannot read the file, the error is swallowed, and the option list is empty. The following `lpoptions -p <queue> -l` call succeeds (it talks to the scheduler) but only adjusts defaults on options that were already parsed. The Flatpak is affected unconditionally: its sandbox has no `/etc/cups`, only the CUPS socket and `~/.cups`.

## What the doc says

- How to confirm the cause (`ls -l /etc/cups/ppd/`, `test -r`).
- The workaround: `sudo usermod -aG <group> "$USER"`, then log out and back in.
- Setting queue defaults with `lpoptions` as an alternative, and a note that vendor duplex keywords are not driven by the generic `sides=` option.
- Why the `.deb`/`.rpm` post-install script cannot do this (runs as root, does not know the desktop users, would widen access) and why the Flatpak cannot be fixed by docs.
- The durable fix for the print code: fetch the PPD from the scheduler (`GET /printers/<queue>.ppd`, what `cupsGetPPD` does, works over the CUPS socket), or build the option list from `lpoptions -l` when the file is unreadable. This PR does not change code; happy to follow up with that if maintainers want it in `craft-print`.

## Verification

Reproduced and fixed on Arch Linux, CUPS 2.4.20, PdfCraft 0.19.0, Konica Minolta PostScript queue with 93 option groups: Printer properties showed no settings; `lpoptions -l` listed everything; the PPD was `root:cups 0640` and unreadable by the user. After `usermod …

title: Windows: Tesseract and the --control tools start without a console window (#6732)
author: ljkx
body:
## What was wrong

Release builds of `pdfcraft.exe` are GUI-subsystem programs (`windows_subsystem = "windows"`), so the app has no console. A console program it starts without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` gets a new console of its own, and that console's window shows up while the program runs. Two places in the desktop app do this:

- `TesseractCli::run_capture` (`crates/ocr/src/tesseract.rs`) starts `tesseract.exe` for `--list-langs`, `--version` and each page of Recognize Text.
- `system_tool` (`crates/platform/src/owner_only.rs`) starts `whoami.exe`, `icacls.exe` and `powershell.exe`, which `write_control_file` runs at startup under `--control`.

## What changed

Both builders set `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (`0x0800_0000`) through `CommandExt::creation_flags` on Windows, as `craft_update::process::command` already does for the updater's helpers. Nothing else about the commands changes: tesseract still writes to its output and error files, and the `owner_only` tools still answer through the pipes `output()` reads.

The OCR crate is layer 4 and `pdfcraft-platform` is layer 7, so there is no shared place both can call; each sets the flag where it builds the command.

I checked every other `Command::new` in the repository. Explorer (Show in Folder, `tab_context.rs`) is a GUI program. The `reg`, `defaults`, `gsettings`, `dbus-daemon` and `lpoptions` calls are tests or don't run on Windows. `pdfcraft-cli` is a console program, so its children share its console. The rest are tests and xtask.

## Tests

Both are Windows-only and start PowerShell through the builder under test (`system_tool(POWERSHELL)`, and a `TesseractCli` whose program is PowerShell). PowerShell reports its console's window (`GetConsoleWindow`) and the processes attached to its console (`GetConsoleProcessList`), and the test checks:

- the window is 0;
- the test process isn't among the attached processes.

The second check matters because a child started without the flag by a process that has a console shares that con…

**The fix.** When one Thai word is wider than a row, Add Text splits it between shaped clusters. **The test.** `styled_thai_rows_end_between_dictionary_words` runs an unspaced Thai paragraph through `wrap_styled_rows`. It needs no Thai face, so it runs in default builds. The styled path has no overwide split, so it needed no fix.

title: fix(sign): a change to a field a signature locks invalidates it (#6757)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6757.

Validation read only DocMDP references. A signature field's `/Lock` (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.5) and the FieldMDP references in its value (§12.8.2.4) were ignored. So changing a locked field after an approval signature read as a permitted form fill, and the signature stayed **Valid**.

After this change:
- `crates/sign/src/pdf/locks.rs` (new) reads both from the **signed revision**: `All`, `Include` and `Exclude`. A listed name also covers the fields below it, so `address` covers `address.city` but not `addressee`. Both sources count, because signers write one or the other or both.
- The locked fields are compared between the signed revision and the document as it is now. That covers each field's dictionary and every dictionary above it (an inherited `/V` is its value too), plus its widgets. Tree links (`/Kids`, `/Parent`, `/P`) are left out of the comparison, and a page is compared by reference only, because adding an annotation rewrites it.
- A locked field that changed, disappeared, or gained a second field under its name adds the new change kind `kind::LOCKED_FIELD` ("locked field") to a **Disallowed** modification. The signature is then Invalid, whatever `classify_changes` called the change.
- A lock that is present but can't be read (an unknown `/Action`, a FieldMDP reference with no parameters, a non-dictionary `/Lock`), or a form too large to compare within the listing's caps, leaves the signature **Unknown**, never Valid. The detail is the existing "The signature could not be checked ({})." wording.
- New fields added under a locked field, and the form's `/NeedAppearances` (plus `/DA`, `/DR` and `/Q` when a locked field has no appearance of its own), count as changes to it. The signature's own field is compared when its lock covers it.
- `classify_changes` and `changes.rs` are unchanged. The check is wired in `finish_validation` (`validate.rs`).
- `parity`: `sign.field-mdp` moves from `planned` to `partial`, with what's still …

title: fix(engine,forms): redraw a laid-out XFA form from one reading of its fields
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

Laying out an XFA form gives every field its appearance (`xfa_redraw`). It called `pdfcraft_forms::redraw_field(name)` once per field, and that call reads the whole form to find its field, so each layout was quadratic in the number of fields. That was cheap while a repeating subform laid out at most 50 rows. Since #4608 raised the limit to 1,000, a script that adds rows can make about 2,000 fields, and each layout read the form about 2,000 times.

This is why `hostile_formcalc_scripts_cannot_hang_or_bloat_the_document` went from 3 s to 46–61 s on main's Ubuntu gate after the `merge/xfa2` merge (#6716). It now passes or fails its 60 s limit by chance, and it has failed CI on PRs that don't touch it (#6608). The test's click script loops on `addInstance` until the table has 1,000 rows, and that one event lays the form out twice.

- `pdfcraft_forms::redraw_read_field(doc, &field)` draws a field the caller has already read with `fields()`. `redraw_field` and `redraw_widgets` now share the drawing code (`draw_widgets`) and otherwise behave as before.
- `xfa_redraw` draws each field from the one reading it already makes. A redraw changes only that field's own widgets, so the reading stays valid for the rest. The signed-signature skip and the error text are unchanged.
- The XFA README's API sketch showed the per-name loop. It now uses the new call.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms`: 297 passed

title: fix(redact): redact an XObject or font whose /Subtype is a reference (#6750)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6750 (audit F-9).

Redaction kept an image under a mark when the image's `/Subtype` was an indirect reference (`/Subtype 8 0 R`, object 8 being `/Image`). `xobject()` in `crates/redact/src/interp.rs` matched on `s.dict.name(b"Subtype")`, and `Dict::name` does not follow references. The image fell through to `_ => None`, so the `Do`, the resource entry and the samples stayed in the saved file under the black box. The renderer still draws such an image.

- `xobject()` resolves `/Subtype` before matching, so an image or form named by reference is redacted like a direct one.
- `is_vertical()` does the same for a Type0 font, so vertical text in a font with a referenced `/Subtype` still makes Apply refuse rather than pass.
- The `_` arm now fails closed. An XObject with no `/Subtype`, or one the redactor doesn't read, is removed in Apply when its placement hits a mark. Verify counts it as residue there. Its placement is the unit square an image fills, or the `/BBox` under its `/Matrix` when it has one. Apply counts it in `forms_removed` and sets `removed_cut`, as it does for a form it cannot read. A placement outside every mark is left alone.
