title: fix(cos): a rebuilt xref keeps the generation-0 object the page draws (#6759)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6759.

When a file's cross-reference data has to be rebuilt from object headers, cos keyed the rebuilt index by object number only, so a later `N 1 obj` replaced `N 0 obj`. The renderer (vendored hayro-syntax, since #5580/#5584) keeps the real `N 0 obj` under `N 0 R` and draws it. So cos read `N 0 R` as null, a full save wrote `null`, and Sign signed a page without the object the screen showed (an opaque cover, say).

- **cos `reconstruct`** (`crates/cos/src/document/reader.rs`, the rebuild path only) now picks each number's object by the renderer's rule: the last real `N 0 obj` keeps N, whatever headers of other generations follow. When there is none, the last header stands in. Rebuilt slots are stored as generation 0, so `N 0 R` reaches the stand-in as the renderer's alias does, and the header's own generation still resolves through the existing `indexed_header_reference` check. The full writer already canonicalizes those aliases.
  - A number with headers of more than one generation gets a walk from the trailer that resolves those numbers as the renderer does. If the document reaches only one generation, that body takes the slot at its own generation. A newer revision that reuses `69 0` as `69 1 obj` and refers to `69 1 R` then still saves its page (PDFBOX-3785's `202097.pdf`, reported in review). A stream's `/Length` doesn't count as reaching an object. When several generations are reached (the #6759 case of a page drawing both `4 0 R` and `4 1 R`), the generation-0 rule stands. Whatever one slot per number cannot hold is recorded in the repair log (AGENTS.md §5, Fidelity).
- **Sign** (`crates/engine/src/session/save.rs`): `sign`, `sign_with_timestamp` and `timestamp_document` refuse an unedited rebuilt document whose index left a generation the document reaches unresolved (`Document::rebuilt_with_unsettled_generations`: two generations of one number reached, or the reachability walk gave up). Its page is drawn from the damaged bytes…

title: fix(sign): an unlisted body or an entry that leads nowhere is no permitted change (#6754)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6754.

A revision appended after signing could change what a signed page shows while `classify_changes` reported only permitted changes. The update carried a new body for the page's content stream that no cross-reference section lists, plus an entry, named from the trailer, that points at no object. cos kept reading the signed content object (its entry had not changed), and read the new number as null, which `classify` drops. The renderer instead rebuilds its object index from the file's `N G obj` headers when an entry leads to no object (`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/xref.rs`, `repair` / `fallback_xref_map_inner`), and there the last header for a number wins, so the page drew the unlisted body.

`crates/sign/src/pdf/changes.rs` now refuses both halves, each on its own:

- **An entry that does not locate its own object.** Every object whose place changed since signing must have an entry that `xref_entry_is_exact` accepts, whatever the object reads as. Before, this was checked only when the content equalled the signed object's. Reported as `other changes`.
- **A body the reader does not read.** `unlisted_bodies` scans the bytes after the signed revision for `N G obj` headers. For each number and generation, the last header there must be where the current entry for that number points. Otherwise the renderer's rebuilt index may draw it. Reported as `page content` when the number had a signed page role, else `other changes`. This holds whatever triggers the rebuild, including a damaged entry the signed file already had. The scan is linear and bounded: past 2^20 distinct headers the appended bytes are not judged and the change is refused.

The scan finds more headers than the renderer's (it does not skip dictionaries or check that an object follows), so it errs towards refusing. A writer that lists what it writes is unaffected.

- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign --all-targets -- -D warn…

title: fix(sign): a widget is signing only with a new signature, form fill only with a new value (#6755, #6756)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6755. Fixes #6756.

One PR for both because they are one code change. Both issues are decided by the same three places in `crates/sign/src/pdf/changes.rs`: `added_annots`, `acroform_kind` and the widget branch of `change_kind`. Each issue rewrites the same lines (the `Widget` arm returns `SIGNATURE` or `FORM_FILL`, and `added_annots` returns `SIGNATURE`, `FORM_FILL` or `COMMENTS`), so two PRs would conflict line for line.

Under a P=2 ("form fill and signing") certification, a later revision could paint over the signed page and keep the certification Valid:

- **#6755.** An empty `/FT /Sig` widget added with an opaque appearance, or the existing empty signature field's `/AP` rewritten, was reported as `signature`.
- **#6756.** A form widget given a new `/AP`, `/MK`, `/DA`, `/A` or `/AA` with its value unchanged, or a new widget added to the page and `/Fields`, was reported as `form fill`.

The rule now:

- **Signing is a new signature value.** An added or changed signature widget (or added `/Fields` entry) counts as `signature` only when its value becomes a signature dictionary that the signed revision did not hold, and its field held no signature when signed. The value can be the widget's own `/V` or its nearest ancestor field's, found by a bounded `/Parent` walk (64 links, seen-set). Pointing a widget at a signature already in the file signs nothing. Whether a widget belongs to a signature field is judged from the signed revision, so relabelling cannot make it one.
- **Form fill is a new value.** A change to an existing non-signature widget is `form fill` only when its value changed (own `/V`, or inherited, as for radio buttons and fields with several widgets) and nothing but `/V`, `/AS` and `/AP` differs.
- **Everything else is `comments`** (annotation creation or modification): permitted at P=3 and by approval signatures, refused at P=1 and P=2 (ISO 32000-2 §12.8.2.2, Table 257). That covers a widget changed in any other way, a widge…

title: fix(sign): "Add to trusted certificates" trusts the signer only (#6758)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6758.

One click on **Add to trusted certificates** stored the signer's certificate as a full trust anchor. If that certificate could also issue certificates (CA bit, `keyCertSign`), every certificate its key issued then validated as **Valid**, under any name. It would also have been accepted as a timestamp authority if it carried the time-stamping EKU.

After this change, trust has a scope:

- **`sign`**: `TrustStore` gains `signers` next to `certs`, which keeps its anchor meaning. A trusted signer trusts the signatures made with *exactly* that certificate. It never joins the issuer pool and is never a TSA anchor. Validation counts a signature as trusted when its own certificate is a trusted signer, or when its chain reaches an anchor. The embedded-token and document-timestamp paths keep using anchors only, so a signer-only certificate is never a trusted authority.
- **`engine`**: adds `Session::trust()`, `trusted_signers()` and `set_trust()`. `trusted_certificates()` and `set_trusted_certificates()` keep their meaning (roots) and keep the signers.
- **UI**:
  - The Signatures panel button now calls `trust_signer`.
  - The Certificate Viewer's Trust tab: **Add to Trusted Certificates** trusts as a signer too. For a certificate that may issue, the tab says what trusting it as a root implies and offers **Trust as a Root Certificate**.
  - A certificate trusted as a signer shows "You trust signatures made with this certificate. It does not vouch for any other certificate."
- **Automation** (`AGENTS.md` §3): `sign_trust` takes `scope`, `"root"` (default, as before) or `"signer"` (what the panel's one click does). It returns `trusted` (roots) and `trusted_signers`, and `clear` empties both. An unknown scope is refused with what's allowed.
- **Persistence**: settings now hold `trusted_roots` and `trusted_signers`.

author: FredApps

Follow-up to #2001 / #2103 (per-printer use case in [this comment](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/2001#issuecomment-6743471865)); also asked for in #5256.

Today the Print dialog saves only one paper size for all printers (`print_paper`). Someone with a 4 × 6 in label printer and an A4 office printer has to choose the printer, paper, Actual size and single-sided again at every start, and a wrong choice prints labels at the wrong size.

Copies, pages, orientation and the Multiple / Booklet / Poster / Label layouts stay per job. Save as PDF remembers nothing. Label's 4 × 6 stock is that job's: a printer used once with Label keeps the paper Label replaced.

title: FormCalc: a script its own clock stops is abandoned, as when the wait runs out first (flaky hostile_formcalc test)
author: FredApps
body:
## What this changes

`tests::hostile_formcalc_scripts_cannot_hang_or_bloat_the_document` (engine) has failed its 60 s bound at random since #6716 landed:

- main's Windows gate after #2103 (abb06c70): **60.11 s** ([job](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/42709212085/job/129473965662))
- a PR's Ubuntu gate: **61.16 s** ([job](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/42644456323/job/129491413555))

### Root cause: two equal time limits that report different outcomes

A FormCalc script run under a time limit is watched twice:

1. the caller (`XfaSession::run`, `run_within`) waits `timeout` for it, then reports it **abandoned**: error, no changes, and the engine turns the form's scripts off;
2. the interpreter reads its own deadline, set to the **same** `timeout`, every 256 steps (`Interp::charge`), and returns `the script ran too long` **with every change the script made so far**.

Which one notices first depends on the scheduler. In the test, the click script `while (1) do table._row.addInstance(1) endwhile` adds 1000 rows (`MAX_ADDED`, the most one run may add). After that, `addInstance` returns null and the loop spins until the 3 s click limit ends it. So the outcome is either:

- **the caller notices first**: no rows are kept, and the test takes ≈ 3.0 s;
- **the interpreter notices first**: 1000 `AddInstance` effects are applied. The form is laid out again with 1001 rows, then the first row's calculate adds one more row and the form is laid out again.

Until #6716, layout stopped at 50 rows per repeating subform, so the second outcome cost only ≈ 0.2 s more. #4608 (commit afdb3680, "XFA repeating subforms lay out more than 50 rows", landed in main with #6716 / d2139e58) raised `MAX_INSTANCES` in `crates/xfa/src/layout.rs` from 50 to 1000. Since then, laying out those rows takes 40–60 s in the test build, which is what blows the bound. title: M2: a JBIG2 mask with a large symbol dictionary draws, and one a decoder limit refuses takes its picture with it (#6722)
author: Piohrun
body:
Closes #6722.

## What this changes

#6722's test file is a scanned drawing's PDF with every image stream replaced by synthetic content. It uses mixed raster content: a JPX colour layer over the whole page, drawn through a 1-bit JBIG2 soft mask, 14,642 × 8,879, with one embedded symbol dictionary of 7,559 symbols. Where the mask is clear, the encoder fills the colour layer with whatever compresses best, so drawn without its mask the page is streaky colour noise. That is what PdfCraft drew. The reporter's second file, with the same structure and a dictionary of 392 symbols, drew correctly.

The vendored `hayro-jbig2` refused the larger mask: a symbol dictionary may decode at most 2^26 symbol pixels (`MAX_DICTIONARY_PIXELS`, patch 2), and this one holds more ("overflow in bitmap dimension computation"). With the bound raised, the mask decodes in 0.62 s and spends 220 million of the stream's 1,074 million steps of decoding work (measured by decoding the mask stream alone).

**Now:**
- **A dictionary may hold as many pixels as the largest page bitmap, 2^28** (`hayro-jbig2` patch 2). The 2^26 bound came with the decoder's first limits, when a fuzzed dictionary decoded for minutes and nothing else bounded it. Since then:
  - each symbol pays for its pixels out of the stream's decoding work before it is decoded (patch 10, `MAX_WORK`, 2^30), which bounds the time;
  - each is held in the bitmaps a page retains (patch 5, 64 MiB), which bounds the memory.

  The time a stream may take is unchanged: `MAX_WORK` still bounds it (the slowest stream measured, 16 refinement-coded dictionaries, stops at it after 5.05 s). The raised bound lets one dictionary take a quarter of `MAX_WORK` instead of a sixteenth. A file like the fuzzed one is still stopped, by the dictionary bound at 2^28 or by `MAX_WORK`, whichever comes first. The nightly finding itself isn't in the repository, so it wasn't run again.

title: feat(sign): trust a certificate for timestamps only (#6786)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Closes #6786.

> **Depends on #6774.** This branch is built on #6774's branch, so until that merges, the diff below includes its commits. The change here is the last commit. I'll merge `main` once #6774 lands.

After #6774, the only way to trust a timestamp authority (TSA) was to trust its certificate as a root. That also lets it vouch for signers and, if it's a CA, for every certificate it issues. This adds a third trust scope, **timestamp authority**: the timestamps signed with exactly that certificate are trusted time, and the certificate is trusted for nothing else.

- **`sign`**: `TrustStore` gains `tsas` next to `certs` (roots) and `signers`.
  - On the two timestamp paths (a signature's embedded token, and a document timestamp), a TSA is trusted when its own certificate is in `tsas` or its chain reaches a root, as before.
  - The existing checks still apply: issued for time stamping, valid when it stamped.
  - A TSA-only certificate never joins the issuer pool and isn't a trusted signer, so a signature made with it stays Unknown.
- **`engine`**: `Session::trusted_tsas()`. `set_trusted_certificates` keeps the signers and TSAs.
- **UI**: the Certificate Viewer's Trust tab offers **Trust for Timestamps** for a certificate issued for time stamping. It explains what that does and doesn't mean, and says so once the certificate is trusted that way. Trusting a certificate as a root drops its separate signer/TSA entries, since a root covers both.
- **Settings**: `trusted_tsas` is saved next to `trusted_roots` and `trusted_signers`. Settings without it read as no TSAs.
- **Automation** (`AGENTS.md` §3): `sign_trust` takes `scope: "tsa"` and returns `trusted_tsas`. `clear` empties all three lists.
- **`parity`**: `sign.trust-import` notes and evidence.

title: Booklet printing: creep compensation
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6777, which was split from item 5 of #6649.

A saddle-stitched booklet's inner sheets stick out past the outer ones once they are nested and folded. After trimming, the content on the inner pages sits closer to the outside edge.

`Layout::Booklet` now takes `creep`, in points per sheet, with a default of 0 so existing output doesn't change. Sheet k, counting 0 as the outermost, moves both of its pages toward the fold by `k × creep`. Each moved page is clipped at the fold, so it never prints onto the facing page. This works the same way for left and right binding.

`layout` refuses a creep that is not finite, is negative, or is over `MAX_CREEP` (10 pt per sheet). It also refuses one that would move the innermost sheet's pages by half a cell or more, whether from a thick booklet or a large creep.

title: fix(ui): a Chinese interface draws in the installed face, not the bundled Kai face (#6070)
author: kingfree
body:
## What this changes

Since the egui 0.37 migration every native build embeds **LXGW WenKai Lite** — a Kai (楷书) face — as its only `Hans` face, and `theme::installed_fallback_need` keeps the installed Chinese face *last* whenever a bundled `Hans` face exists. The machine's own UI face (Microsoft YaHei on Windows, PingFang SC on macOS) is then never loaded for Chinese at all, so every label is drawn in a document face. That is the regression #6070 and #6274 report ("the interface font changed from Microsoft YaHei UI to KaiTi"); #6318 has the same finding for 0.18.2.

This makes a Chinese interface ask for the installed face of its own script again, and puts it **in front of every bundled CJK face**, not only in front of the Japanese ones that LXGW now precedes:

- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`: `installed_fallback_need(cjk)` no longer takes `has_embedded_hans` — `zh-hans` always asks for `Need::Hans`, `zh-hant` for `Need::Hant`, everything else for `Need::Other` as before.
- `installed_face_position(stack, bundled_cjk, need)` is the placement rule, split out so it can be tested without an installed font: in front of the bundled CJK interface faces for a Chinese interface, at the end of the family otherwise.
- The bundled `Hans` face stays embedded and stays in the stack, *behind* the installed face. It still draws Chinese on a machine with no installed written-Chinese face, and it is all the web build has. Nothing changes for Japanese, Arabic, Telugu, Hebrew, Hangul or the other script fallbacks.

title: Fix drawing cursor visibility on light PDF backgrounds
author: HasanIbnAmir
body:
## What this changes

Fixes cursor ownership claiming during drawing gestures in `crates/ui-egui/src/tools/comments/input.rs`.

Previously, `(over_page || cv.gesture.is_some())` allowed any page to claim the custom tool cursor (e.g. `CursorIcon::None` or `CursorIcon::Crosshair`) when the pointer was in a page gap during an active drawing gesture, even if that page did not own the gesture. The condition is now updated to:

let owns_gesture = matches!(&cv.gesture, Some(Gesture::Draw { page, .. }) if *page == cx.page);
if pointer.is_some_and(|p| ui.clip_rect().contains(p)) && (over_page || owns_gesture) { ... }
```
This aligns input handling with the ownership check in `paint_gesture` (`paint.rs`).

title: Updates test: answer the startup prompt before clicking in Preferences
author: bflatastic
body:
`updates::preferences_turn_the_check_at_start_off` starts the app with the update check at start on. That check answers on its own thread, and the "is available" prompt it opens can land between the test's frames and take the click meant for the Preferences check box, so `update_check_at_start` stays true and the assertion at updates.rs:176 fails. It failed this way on the Windows gate of #6776 and #6784 today, and #6794 reports it failing once in a full local run.

The test now waits for the startup prompt and answers Later before opening Preferences, through a helper shared with `the_check_at_start_offers_the_prompt_and_later_dismisses_it`, which already waited the same way.

Test-only change. A race can't be made to fail on demand, so there is no failing-first run; the `full-ci` label runs it on Windows as well as Ubuntu.

title: M10: Enhance scanned file cleans JPEG 2000 scans (#4119)
author: RiceDee
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4119.

Scan & OCR ▸ Enhance scanned file (`page_enhance_scan`) reported a scan stored as JPEG 2000 and left it as it was. It now cleans it like any other grey or RGB scan.

- The image is read with `hayro-jpeg2000`, which is already in the tree through hayro: 8-bit grey or RGB, no alpha.
- It is written back as a JPEG at quality 90, in the same image object. PdfCraft has no JPEG 2000 encoder.
- A JPEG 2000 image may leave `/ColorSpace` to its data, so the rewritten image names it.
- A dictionary that contradicts the data (size, colour space, a remapping `/Decode`) is refused and reported, as before.
- A codestream that claims more than 65535 tiles is refused before decoding. A tile index is 16 bits, and the decoder allocates a structure per claimed tile, so a small file could otherwise ask for a great deal of memory.

`decode_samples` is used only by Enhance scanned file, so the Optimizer does not change.

title: M10: Enhance scanned file restores halftone 1-bit scans to clean grey (#4119)
author: RiceDee
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4119. **Stacked on #6811**: this branch contains that one, so please merge #6811 first.

A faint page scanned to 1-bit comes out as dots: a grey texture with thin, broken text. Enhance scanned file could only despeckle it, which does not help. This adds a halftone restore.

- **Detection** (`descreen::is_halftone`). A 1-bit scan is a halftone when both hold:
  - at least half of its 16 × 16 blocks are dither: their lone pixels (unlike all four neighbours, of either colour) are at least 3 % of the block and at least half of its rarer colour;
  - no more than 15 % of its black is crisp strokes: black in a straight run of 6 pixels or more that is at most 12 across.

  So crisp text is never taken for a halftone, at any size or density, and neither is a page of crisp text beside a dithered photograph, nor solid writing on speckled paper. The first version of this PR went by "neither solid paper nor solid ink in a 5 × 5 window", which dense text at fax resolution also is; see the review.
- **Restore** (`crates/engine/src/descreen.rs`). The dots are smoothed into tones at half size, the paper is lifted to white against its own local background, and the page is brought back to full size with bolder, smoother strokes. The result is stored as 8-bit grey (Flate) in the same image object, at the same pixel size.
- **Its own switch.** Restore halftone scans is a checkbox in the dialog and `restore_halftone` on the tool, on by default (off at level 0). Off, a dotted scan is a 1-bit scan like any other.
- **CCITT fax images are now read**, on their own or behind a general-purpose filter, for this and for Despeckle. A despeckled fax scan is written back as Group 4, so it stays the size it was.
- **Result window.** When a run restored a halftone, a movable window names the pages and has Text weight, Text contrast and Background clean-up sliders, for the page showing or all restored pages (radio buttons), with Next page to walk them.

title: M7: a font's metrics are past their allowance only when it refused a read
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

CodeRabbit found this on #6800, which landed #6239 on `main` ([its review](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/6800#pullrequestreview-5836243572)).

#6239 reads a font's streams against a decode allowance that the caller shares. `Metrics::past_allowance` says a stream the metrics come from was left unread because that allowance was spent. The Thai edit (`legacy_thai_font`) refuses when the allowance itself counted a refusal (`DecodeBudget::refused() > 0`). The two are meant to agree. A font of the face left unread for want of the allowance would count as unusable and silently change which subset draws the text, so the edit is refused instead.

They didn't always agree. `Reads::decode`, and the Type 3 glyph-box read, took any failed read for a refused one when nothing was left of the allowance after it. A read can fail with nothing left without the allowance refusing it. An empty stream behind a filter nothing decodes (an unknown name, say) fails before any stage runs, with any allowance, and `DecodeBudget` counts no refusal for a stream without data. So once an edit's allowance was spent to the byte, such a stream set `past_allowance` on a font's metrics with no refusal counted. The edit then skipped that font of the face (`LegacyThaiFont::from_pdf` isn't called for metrics past the allowance, so its program isn't read) and went through without it.

**Now** both take a read as refused only when `DecodeBudget::refused` grew during it. So `past_allowance` is set exactly when the allowance counted a refusal during the metrics read, and its doc says so. In the case above, the font's program is then read, the allowance refuses it, and the edit is refused with its usual reason ("the page's THSarabunPSK subsets need more than 64 MiB of font data for one edit; choose a replacement font for this text").

CodeRabbit also described a corrupt stream that spends the last of the allowance and then fails. These reads decode tolerantly: corrupt data giv…

title: fix(forms): tokenize JavaScript template literal substitutions in AF_Calculate
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Summary

Tokenize JavaScript template literal substitutions (`` `${...}` ``, ECMA-262 §12.8.6) in `pdfcraft_forms::af::calc::js_tokens` so `calculation_reads` and `rename_in_script` inspect expressions embedded inside template literals.

### Problem

Previously, `js_tokens` scanned backtick template literals with `scan_string(js, b'`', i + 1)`, consuming everything up to the next unescaped backtick as a single `Js::Other` token:

1. Any `this.getField(...)` calls inside a `` `${...}` `` template substitution were swallowed into the surrounding template chunk instead of being emitted as `Js::Ident` / `Js::String` tokens, so `calculation_reads` missed those field dependencies and `rename_in_script` left their field names unrenamed.
2. When an expression inside `` `${...}` `` contained a nested template literal (e.g. `` `` `${`nested ${this.getField(tax).value}`}` `` ``), the inner opening backtick prematurely closed the outer `scan_string(js, b'`', ...)` call, leaving the inner expression outside the string and the next backtick to open a spurious string over the remainder of the script.

### Solution

- Add `Delimiter::Template` and `scan_template(js, s, j)` in `crates/forms/src/af/calc.rs`.
- When scanning a template literal chunk, stop at an unescaped `` `${ `` and push `Delimiter::Template` while entering an expression context (`left = false`, `control_cond = false`, `expr_brace = false`).
- When the matching `}` for `Delimiter::Template` is reached, resume scanning the remainder of the enclosing template literal via `scan_template(js, s, i + 1)`.

- Added unit regression test `template_substitutions_read_and_rename_fields_without_breaking_outer_lexing` covering nested template literals, object blocks inside substitutions, regex literals after `}` inside substitutions, `for-of` headers with template substitutions, and `rename_in_script` inside substitutions.

body:
Fixes #6815.

While a file panel is in use, the menu bar is swapped for a small one. It has an Edit menu (Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All, `muda`'s predefined items with the usual shortcuts) and an application menu with Hide, Hide Others and Show All. The labels use the app's translations, and a panic while building the menu is caught, as in craft-menu.

`muda` (Apache-2.0 OR MIT) is already in the build through `craft-menu`, and this adds it to `pdfcraft-ui-egui`. It makes the AppKit calls, so the code needs no `unsafe`.

The fix could also go in `craft-menu` for every app that uses it. I kept it in PdfCraft so this PR changes one app, and can move it if you prefer.

title: fix(optimize): resolve multi-hop indirect references when discarding form actions
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Summary

Resolve multi-hop indirect references consistently across `Count`, `Walk`, and `holds_form_action` in `crates/optimize/src/form_actions.rs`.

### Problem

Previously, `Walk::without` resolved action values with `Document::resolve` (which follows up to 32 `Object::Ref` hops), whereas `Count::object`, `Count::entry`, `Walk::clean_dict`, `Walk::lists_form_action`, `is_or_refers_to_form_action`, and `refers_to_form_action` used 1-hop `Document::get` or `v.as_ref()`:

1. When an action entry (`/A`, `/OpenAction`, `/Next`, or `/AA`) referred to a form action or indirect `/Next` array / `/AA` dictionary through a 2+ hop reference chain (e.g. `4 0 R -> 5 0 R -> << /S /SubmitForm >>`), `Walk::without` stripped the form action, but `Count` missed it and returned an undercount (`0` instead of `1`), or failed to deduplicate a shared indirect action referenced via 1 hop by one entry and 2 hops by another.
2. When an action entry past `MAX_DEPTH` or inside a self-referential `/Next` array reached a form action through a 2+ hop reference chain, `holds_form_action` and `Walk::reaches_form_action` returned `false` instead of failing with `OptimizeError::ActionLimit`.
3. `Walk::clean_dict` and `Walk::without` keyed `shared` replacements and `self.chain` cycle detection on `v.as_ref()` (the first hop) instead of the terminal `ObjRef` holding the target dictionary or array.

### Solution

- Add `resolve_ref` and `target_ref` (following up to `MAX_REF_HOPS = 32` reference hops to a non-reference target) in `crates/optimize/src/form_actions.rs`.
- Use `resolve_ref` and `target_ref` across `Count::object`, `Count::entry`, `Walk::clean_dict`, `Walk::without`, `Walk::lists_form_action`, `is_or_refers_to_form_action`, and `refers_to_form_action`.

### Verification

- Added unit tests `chained_indirect_refs_count_and_clean_actions` and `chained_indirect_refs_enforce_depth_and_loop_limits` in `crates/optimize/src/form_actions.rs`.

title: fix(export): inspect multi-run boundaries and guard page span overflow in join_wrapped
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
### Summary

Inspect sentence endings, list-item prefixes, and word-space insertion across run boundaries in `crates/export/src/flow.rs`, and guard against page span overflow in `join_wrapped`.

### Problem

Previously, `wraps_into` inspected only `prev.last()` for `ends_sentence` and only `next.first()` for `list_item`, while `join_wrapped` checked only `right <= left` and inspected only `prev.last_mut()` when deciding whether to append a word space:

1. When a sentence ended in an earlier run followed by a closing parenthesis, bracket, quote, or trailing whitespace in a separate run on the same line (e.g. `[Run("for one year.", italic), Run(")", regular)]`), `ends_sentence(&last.text)` evaluated `")"` in isolation and returned `false`, merging the finished sentence into the next paragraph.
2. When a numbered or lettered list item's marker was split across styled runs (e.g. bold `Run("2")` + regular `Run(". Keep the premises clean")`, or italic `Run("a")` + regular `Run(") Keep...")`), `list_item(&first.text)` evaluated `"2"` or `"a"` in isolation and returned `false`, merging the list item into the full-width line above it.
3. When extreme page coordinates caused `right - left` to overflow `f64` to `+infinity`, `right - (FULL_LINE.0 * size).max(FULL_LINE.1 * (right - left))` evaluated to `-infinity`, treating every short line as full-width.
4. When `prev` ended with a trailing empty run after a hyphen or CJK character, `join_wrapped` inspected only the empty run and inserted a spurious word space.

### Solution

- Add `list_item_runs` / `list_item_chars` so list markers split across styled runs (as well as styled marker runs followed by unspaced item runs) are recognized while split decimal numbers (`"1."` + `"5 kg"`) remain ordinary text.
- Check `ends_sentence` across `prev`'s runs in reverse character order.
- Guard `!(right - left).is_finite()` in `join_wrapped` and inspect the last/first non-empty characters across runs when inserting word spaces.

title: M8: redaction reads forms through a view of them, once per check (#6341 follow-up)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A follow-up to #6341, which was merged through #6805 at ce2db2a31. The first three commits were reviewed on #6341's branch but reached it only after the merge. The fourth answers CodeRabbit's two nitpicks on this pull request, in tests only.

#6341 made redaction read the forms and glyph programs it follows with their `/DecodeParms` given by reference. There are nine such reads: `names_content_draws` (now in `followed`), `unlink_from_forms` and `resource_ops` in `crates/redact/src/interp/prune.rs`, and six in `type3.rs`. Two costs came with that:
- **A copy at every read.** The reads went through `Document::with_direct_parms`, which copies the stream's whole dictionary when the parameters are a reference. The unlinking check reads a form once for each page that draws it, so a form whose dictionary holds a large unrelated array was copied again for every page. With a quarter of a million numbers over 256 pages, the redaction took about 550 ms, against 20 ms with the parameters direct (test profile).
- **A parse at every page.** Resolving the parameters loads an object between one page's read of a form and the next. The document's object cache keeps at most 32 MB of parsed objects, and past that only the newest one. So a form whose dictionary is made that large was parsed again for each page that draws it. An array of a million numbers is about 56 MB parsed, from about 2 MB of file. With the view in place, 48 pages took 4.1 s against 0.48 s with the parameters direct, and 401 pages 29 s; with the copy too, 48 pages took 5.3 s and 401 pages 38 s. Before #6341, a page that drew only the form loaded nothing between its reads. One that also drew an image through the same dictionary loaded the image, so such a form was parsed again for each such page there too. #6341's by-reference read made every page do it.

title: M11: Optimize stores a picture's one-bit masks as monochrome images
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

PDF Optimizer's Monochrome Images settings (and Reduce File Size, which uses them) store black-and-white images as CCITT Group 4 or JBIG2. Until now they reached only the images a page draws by name. A picture's stencil `/Mask` and its `/SMask` are images too, but the pages don't name them, so the monochrome step never reached them (the colour and grey settings resample an eight-bit soft mask with its picture, but store no mask as Group 4 or JBIG2). `optimize.mono-compression` listed them under "Not yet".

That matters most for mixed-raster (MRC) scans: a colour layer drawn through a one-bit mask that holds the text. Most of the black-and-white data is in that mask, which stayed as it was written (Flate, say).

**Now**, after the pictures, each picture's stencil mask and one-bit soft mask goes through the same monochrome step (`mono`, through the new `decide_mask`). Each is stored once, however many pictures name it. It is stored again as the compression asks (Group 4 by default, JBIG2 when chosen) when that is smaller, at its size, with its bits as they were, so it masks exactly as before:
- **Not resampled.** The pass measures the resolution a picture is drawn at, not its mask's.
- **No shared JBIG2 dictionary.** Only images the pages draw by name share one (redaction can store those again without it).
- **A stencil the pages also draw by name** is stored as that image, as before; a soft mask they draw is still stored as a mask.
- **Masks past the image steps' limit of 80 million pixels stay**, as images do: #6722's JBIG2 soft mask, about 130 million pixels, is one.
- **A soft mask of more bits stays as it is,** even one of only black and white. The colour and grey settings resample a picture's soft mask with it only at eight bits, so packing it to one bit would stop the picture being resampled on a later run.
- **With Retain,** masks stay as they are.

body:
## Summary
This PR adds hardware document scanning support to PdfCraft:
- **Scanner Discovery & Acquisition:** Enumerates hardware scanners and acquires scanned pages via native WIA on Windows (with SANE architecture ready on Linux/macOS).
- **Feeder & Duplex Support:** Supports flatbed (platen), automatic document feeder (ADF), multi-page batch scanning, and duplex (2-sided) scanning.
- **Driver UI Modes:**
  - *Direct (PdfCraft):* Background silent scan with custom DPI, color mode, page size (A4, Letter, Legal, A5, Auto) and duplex.
  - *Manufacturer Driver UI:* Invokes WIA `UseDevicePage = true` to display the manufacturer's native configuration page (e.g., Fujitsu PaperStream IP) with all advanced hardware filters.
  - *Windows Basic UI:* Standard Windows image acquisition dialog.
- **Page Rotation:** Supports 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270° orientation correction for feeder scans.
- **Headless & Automation:** Exposes `scanners` and `doc_scan` tools under `pdfcraft-automation` and CLI with synthetic mock support for headless CI / hostile argument testing.
- **Quality Gates:** Fully compliant with `AGENTS.md` (`unsafe_code = forbid`, no panics/unwraps in production code, strict root confinement, passing `cargo test` and `cargo clippy -D warnings`).

title: M3: Copy with formatting keeps the text of standard-order glyphs and small caps the text layer can't name (view.copy-with-layout)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

This builds on #6733: until #6733 merges, its commits are included here, and this PR's own change is the commits after the last merge of #6733's branch. #6733 provides Copy with formatting, its recovery layer and everything rules share (the candidate policy, the standard orders, the width proof, Type 3 and CID-keyed CFF fonts as rule inputs). This PR only adds rules: two new ones, and a wider reach for the Macintosh-order rule. **Copy, Find and text extraction are unchanged**, byte for byte; only Copy with formatting (and `text_extract` with `format: "html"`) reads more.

### How this differs from #6733

Each rule reads one kind of font that tells a reader too little, through one clue the font still carries:

| Rule | Fonts it reads | The clue | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| #6733: numbered glyph names | simple fonts whose glyph names number the character (`/C83`, `/c246`) | the number is the character's code | PDFBOX-1793 |

title: fix(forms): draw field text the field font cannot hold from the bundled face instead of ?
author: chamber074
body:
Fixes #3913 (also reported as #6822, closed as its duplicate).

## What was wrong

The field value was never lost: `/V` is stored losslessly as UTF-16BE, and PdfCraft sets `/NeedAppearances`, which is why other viewers show the Greek correctly. The `?` is only in the appearance PdfCraft draws itself: when the field's `/DR` font can't encode the text, `field_appearance_fit` falls back to Helvetica/WinAnsi, and every character outside WinAnsi is drawn as `?` (and reported through the "This field's font can't draw…" notice).

## The fix

At that fallback decision, characters that neither the field's font nor Helvetica holds but the bundled Inter face does (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic) are now drawn as Type 3 glyphs built from Inter — the same mechanism Thai text already uses in field appearances. Characters no available face holds (e.g. CJK in a Helvetica field) are still drawn as `?` and reported, exactly as before. Text the field's font holds is byte-for-byte unchanged, and no font resource is added in that case.

## Behaviour change to be aware of

Date names in Russian, Czech, Greek, etc. in Helvetica fields (#5303) are now drawn in the date language rather than falling back to English — the "a font that holds them keeps them" rule applied to the bundled face. Japanese still falls back to English. Push-button captions are unchanged (still `?`); same mechanism, possible follow-up.

## Tests

- New forms test `greek_a_field_font_cannot_hold_is_drawn_from_the_bundled_face`: Greek, mixed Latin+Greek (multiline), and exact-WinAnsi strings in a `/Helv` field; asserts the `/V` bytes, no `?` in the appearance, a `PCLa` Type 3 font with ToUnicode, and no undrawn report; a CJK character is still reported. It fails on unmodified code and passes with this change.
- New fonts unit test for splitting a line between the standard font and Inter.
- Updated the engine signature test and the #5303 `form_date_language` tests where they pinned the old `?` behaviour.

title: packaging: RPM installs on openSUSE (no shared directories)
author: dennisklappe
body:
## What this changes

The PdfCraft RPM still can't be installed on openSUSE Tumbleweed, even with the soname requirements from #2205. The `/usr/share/` tree in `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml` makes the package own `/usr/share/mime` and `/usr/share/mime/packages`. openSUSE's `filesystem` package owns those with mode 555, so RPM refuses the install with a file conflict. The launcher only shows "the system installer stopped with error 4" (storytold/craft-launcher#341, storytold/craft-launcher#856).

The package now names its files in shared directories one by one, and keeps trees only for its own directories. The file list is otherwise unchanged. This is the same change as storytold/wordcraft#5369.

## How you verified it

Repackaged the 0.20.0 release binaries with nfpm 2.48.0 and this config. I didn't run a full `package.sh` build, and no Rust code changed.

- Tumbleweed container: `zypper install` works (the 0.20.0 release RPM fails with the conflict), and `pdfcraft-cli --version` runs
- Fedora container: `dnf install` works, and `pdfcraft-cli --version` runs
- Debian 12 container: `apt-get install` of the .deb works, `pdfcraft-cli --version` runs, and the OCR models are in `/usr/share/pdfcraft/models`
- Tumbleweed desktop: installed with the launcher's zypper command, `rpm -V` is clean, and `pdfcraft-cli info` reads a PDF

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

A new file under `/usr/share` outside `pdfcraft/`, `doc/pdfcraft/` and `icons/hicolor/` now needs its own entry here, or it won't be packaged.

Part of #6269. The rest is tracked in #6852.

`doc_print` gains a colour-management choice:

title: perf(render): premultiply image samples by table
author: quincy-jc
body:
## What this changes Drawing a large image under a same-size soft mask got about three times slower in 0.19.0. The area shrink (vendored hayro patch 21) premultiplies every source sample through `AlphaColor`'s float conversion at each draw, and that conversion took about two thirds of the shrink's time. Premultiplying now reads a 256 × 256 table that the same conversion fills once (`premultiply_rgba8`), used by the masked area shrink, the nearest-sampled masked shrink and `premultiply_rgba`. Premultiplying works on each colour sample alone, so the output is the same byte for byte. Recorded as hayro patch 32 in `vendor/README.md`. title: M12: the Destinations panel (view.destinations-panel)
author: ljkx
body:
Acrobat has a Destinations panel that lists a document's named destinations and creates, moves, renames and deletes them: https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/edit-documents/use-links-and-attachments/manage-destinations.html. PdfCraft had none: `view.destinations-panel` was `planned` in `parity/acrobat-features.toml`, and `docs/ui-parity.md` listed the panel as missing.

## What it adds

**View ▸ Side panels ▸ Destinations** lists the named destinations (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.4) of the `/Names /Dests` tree and of the PDF 1.1 catalog `/Dests` dictionary. A name in both is listed once, as a reader resolves it.

- The list is sorted by name; the Page label sorts it by page, the Name label sorts it by name again.
- A click goes to a destination, at its position and zoom.
- A right-click has Go to destination, Set destination (the view on screen: the selection's corner, else the top of the window, as a new bookmark), Rename and Delete.
- Destination options ▸ New destination names the view on screen "Untitled" (then "Untitled 2"…) and starts in rename mode.
- The edits need the modify permission and a document that is not read-only; without them the panel still lists and goes.
- Each edit is one undo step.

**Automation:** `destination_list`, `destination_add`, `destination_set`, `destination_rename` and `destination_delete`. Places are given as `bookmark_add` takes them: points from the top-left of the displayed page.

## Design

- `crates/organize/src/dests.rs` reads and edits the destinations; `Edit::AddDestination`, `SetDestination`, `RenameDestination` and `DeleteDestination` run it as undoable edits; `Session::named_destinations` lists them for the panel and the tool.
- An edit applies to every entry of the name, in the tree and in the old dictionary, so the entry a reader finds first and the one it would fall back to never disagree.

title: M8: the Type 3 cleanup charges the page only when there is a Type 3 font
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

CodeRabbit found this on #6805, which landed #6341 on `main` ([its comment](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/6805#discussion_r4520958738)).

The Type 3 cleanup (`prune_type3_from_resources`) prunes only Type 3 fonts a rewritten page or form no longer draws with. It reads what the content draws through its resources (`resource_ops`) whenever the resources list any font, and only then looks for a Type 3 font. Since #6341 that read is charged to what the content walk left of the page's allowance. So a page with only TrueType fonts and a large form without resources of its own could be refused, by Apply Redactions or Remove Hidden Information, for a read that prunes nothing. A 100 MiB form crossing the mark is read by the walk, by the page's check of what it still draws, and by this read: 300 MiB, against the page's 256 MiB.

**Now**, without a Type 3 font, the read is charged to an allowance of a page of its own; with one, to the page's, as before.

**Why not return early, as CodeRabbit suggested.** The read also refuses bytes the parser can't read in the streams and forms it reads, and an early return would drop that refusal on every page without a Type 3 font. The walk reads past such bytes, so where nothing else reads the same content, text that a stray `)` or `}` hides inside a `TJ` array under the mark would stay in the file, while Apply Redactions and Remove Hidden Information reported success. A review of an early return found exactly that: Poppler's `pdftotext` still extracted the text. So the read is still made whenever any font is listed. The read and the pruning tell a Type 3 font the same way (`is_type3`), so they can't come apart.

title: Previous view: restore the place on the page, not just the page
author: chamber074
body:
Fixes #6848.

**Problem.** Previous/Next view returned to the right page but always to its top: the view history stored page numbers only, and `view_history` restored `goto = (page, 0.0)`. Following a cross-reference from the middle of a long page and going back lost the reader's place.

**Change.** History entries are now places — (page, fraction down the page), the same form `goto` already consumes.

- A new `history_place` reads where the reader is from the last frame's page transforms. The page top is the fallback before the first frame, in the page grid, or when the page isn't on screen; a pending jump's own fraction counts when two jumps land in one frame.
- `go_to_page` records the place left — re-leaving the same page updates its entry rather than stacking a duplicate — and every jump that records history comes through it.
- `view_history` pushes the place left onto the opposite stack, so Previous then Next round-trips both spots, and restores the recorded fraction, clamped, and dropped to the page top when the page has since been removed.

Fractions are relative to the page's height, so a place left at one zoom comes back at the same spot on the page at another. Horizontal position and zoom are not recorded, as before.

**Tests.** Two new canvas tests in the existing style: Previous view comes back halfway down the page left (not to its top), and Next view returns to the place Previous view left. Both fail with the position capture disabled and pass with it; the existing view-history tests pass unchanged.

Gates: ui-egui lib 994 passed / 1 failed — the failure is `bidi::tests::arabic_ui_labels_use_an_explicit_paragraph_direction`, which fails identically without this change on this machine (a language-registration assertion, unrelated to navigation). `cargo fmt --check` clean; clippy clean.

title: M8: redaction refuses a page whose content it can't fully parse
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Apply Redactions could report success and leave text under a mark in the saved file. Remove Hidden Information could do the same with hidden text. This happens when the text sits beside bytes the content parser can't read, such as a stray `)` or `}` in a `TJ` array:

```
BT /F1 10 Tf 20 260 Td [(TAIL) ) (SECRET)] TJ ET
```

The redaction walk reads past such bytes, so it neither finds nor removes the text. Other readers still draw it: Poppler's `pdftotext` extracts the line above as `TAILSECRET`. Found while reviewing #6860.

**Before**, the only refusal came from the reads that follow the walk (the check of what the page still draws, and the font and property cleanups). Those run only when the walk rewrote something. They read what it rewrote as rewritten. The font cleanup reads only when the resources list a font. So the text stayed, with Apply reporting success, in these cases:
- **The walk rewrites nothing.** Either the only text under the mark is in such a `TJ`, or it is in a form with resources of its own.
- **The walk rewrites the stream.** It writes the array out as `(TAIL) (SECRET) TJ`, without the stray byte or the brackets, and the strings stay.
- **No font is listed.** The page sets its font only through an ExtGState `/Font`.

Remove Hidden Information never counted hidden text in such a `TJ`. Alone, it found nothing to remove, and Sanitize Document went on. Beside other hidden text, it removed the rest and left this.

**Now** the walk records when it meets such bytes (`Output::unparsed`, from `Parsed::skipped`, nested forms included):
- **Apply Redactions** refuses the page with `RedactError::Unreadable` ("page N has content that can't be read, so it can't be redacted safely"). It already did this for an inline image whose end is a guess.
- **Remove Hidden Information** counts such a page in its scan, so the removal runs and refuses it. It already did this for content that doesn't decode. It now refuses an inline image whose end is…

title: fix(render): keep overprinted runs of another size whole instead of splicing into host words (#5641)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:

- In `order::collide` (`crates/render/src/text/order.rs`), check whether an overlapping run is a genuine superscript or subscript on the host run via `is_script_run` rather than calling `is_script_on` on individual glyph pairs.

title: M8: the redaction walk reads a form's /Matrix entries by reference
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Apply Redactions could report success and leave a form's text under a mark in the saved file. This happened when the form's `/Matrix` moves it onto the mark and gives one of its entries by reference, as in `/Matrix [1 0 0 1 0 8 0 R]` with `8 0 obj 200`. That spelling is legal: an array's entries may each be an indirect reference (ISO 32000-2 §7.3.10), and Arlington's `XObjectFormType1` allows the matrix itself to be one.

The redaction walk read the matrix with `Matrix::from_operands` on the array as written. A reference there made the read fail, and the walk fell back to the identity. It then tested the form against the wrong place, found it away from the mark, and never walked it. Poppler's `pdftotext` places the text under the mark. Remove Hidden Information missed text that such a matrix moves off the page in the same way. Found in review of #6882.

**Now** the walk reads a form's matrix with the proof's own `matrix_of` (`verify/extract.rs`), which resolves the array and each entry.
- **A `/Matrix` that isn't six numbers** was also read as the identity. Now where the form draws can't be told, so Apply refuses the page with that reason. The scans count it, as they do a form past the page's budget, and Remove Hidden Information with hidden text (which tells hidden text by where it lands) and Sanitize Document refuse it, where they went on before. Removing hidden layers alone doesn't ask where content lands, so it walks such a form as it stands. A `/Matrix` of seven entries is one of these: Poppler draws it with the first six, and Apply left its text under a mark.
- **A null `/Matrix`**, given directly or by reference, is the identity in `matrix_of` now. A null entry is no entry (ISO 32000-2 §7.3.9).
- **A reference to a reference**, for the matrix or one of its entries, is refused as well. Readers disagree on following one (below).
- **The read is cheap at any length.** The walk reads the matrix at every `Do` of the form. `matrix_of` reads an…

title: fix: Continuous Scrolling toggle not working in Preference tab (#6780)
author: Combiler01
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6780

1. **Preferences immediately update active and open views**: Toggling `Continuous scrolling` or changing layout, zoom, or page gaps in Preferences ▸ Documents and view previously only modified `app.view_defaults`. Active document tabs were left unchanged, so users would see the document still in non-continuous mode. title: Compile Direct3D 12 shaders with FXC, not a dxcompiler.dll from PATH
author: lucasbraud
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6892.

On Windows, `configure_gpu` left the DX12 shader compiler at wgpu's default, `Dx12Compiler::Auto`. Without the `static-dxc` feature, wgpu-hal 30 loads `"dxcompiler.dll"` by bare name, so Windows walks the DLL search path, PATH included. PdfCraft doesn't ship that DLL, so another program's copy got loaded (seen: an Electron app's folder on PATH), at whatever version it is. A copy that loads but doesn't work isn't retried with FXC: DX12 fails and startup falls back to OpenGL (#392's `DXC compile error ... dxil.dll not found` looks like this).

Now DX12 uses FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows; System32 comes before PATH), unless `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` asks for something else, like the other `WGPU_*` variables `configure_gpu` honours. Other platforms are unchanged.

## How you verified it

**Nothing was built or run locally**: the machine I wrote this on has no MSVC build tools, and its Rust is older than the workspace's 1.95. This relies on Windows CI.

- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` (not run; lines checked by hand against `max_width = 150`)
- [ ] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (not run)
- [ ] tests pass on the crates I changed (not run)

What I checked by reading: `wgpu::Dx12Compiler` (re-exported from wgpu-types 30.0.1) has the `Fxc` variant and `from_env() -> Option<Self>`. It has no `PartialEq`, so the test uses `matches!`. `Auto` is its `#[default]`, and egui-wgpu builds options with `BackendOptions::from_env_or_default()`. Without the fix, the new test `dx12_compiles_shaders_with_fxc_so_no_dxcompiler_dll_is_searched_for` should fail on Windows with `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` unset, since the compiler is `Auto`. I have not watched it fail. Off Windows the test checks nothing.

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests
- [x] No indexing or slicing with input-derived positions
- [x] No `unsafe`

title: fix(sign): signing is refused when an earlier signature allows no further change (#6865)
author: asadosteaksnl
body:
## What this changes

Addresses the **signing** half of #6865 (`Refs #6865`; the validation half stays open, see below).

`sign_inner` added a signature without looking at what the signatures already in the document allow. A document locked by an earlier signature ("lock document after signing"), or certified with no changes allowed, got a second signature and no warning, and the earlier signature was broken. Acrobat shows it invalid, and PdfCraft's own validation already reports a signature added after a no-changes certification as a disallowed change (`only_an_invisible_document_timestamp_survives_a_no_changes_certification`).

Before anything is written, signing now looks at every signature field that is already signed and refuses, naming the field, when

- it is the document's certification (the one the catalog's `/Perms /DocMDP` names) and its DocMDP level is 1,
- its `/Lock` carries `/P 1` (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.5), or
- its value has a FieldMDP `/Reference` whose `/TransformParams` carry `/P 1` (what the reporter's Acrobat file has).

Details:

- `/P`, `/TransformMethod`, `/TransformParams` and `/Lock` are followed through references.
- A lock on a field that is not signed yet is not in effect and does not refuse, so the locked field itself can still be signed.
- `/P 2`, `/P 3` and no `/P` sign as before.
- Document timestamps and LTV data use other entry points (`timestamp_document`, the DSS writer) and stay allowed, as level 1 permits them. The error says a document timestamp can still be added.
- Where the form walk did not read the whole form (`walk_sig_fields` says so), signatures it did not list are found in one pass over the file, as `has_signatures` finds them, and the refusal says "an earlier signature".
- The certification check reuses validation's own reading (`docmdp_reference` + `names_certification`, through a new `validate::certifies_no_changes`), so signing refuses exactly what validation would then call a broken certification.

**Not in this PR…

title: Match trust anchors by name and key, not by encoding
author: kevbenavides1910
body:
## What this changes

`TrustStore::trusts` (`crates/sign/src/pdf/types.rs`) compared anchors by exact bytes:

```rust
self.certs.iter().any(|t| t.raw == c.raw)
```

RFC 5280 §6.1 makes a trust anchor a **name plus a public key**, so an authority that reissues or cross-signs its root keeps the same anchor, and a chain that runs through such a copy must still end where the user trusted. As reported in #6221, a DigiCert timestamp validates unverified unless the cross-signed copy (`G4 issued by DigiCert Assured ID Root CA`) is trusted too, even with the self-signed G4 root trusted.

The match is now on the subject and the **parsed `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`** (`t.public_key == c.public_key`: algorithm, EC curve and key material, instead of its BIT STRING alone; the parameters an algorithm fixes — NULL for RSA, absent for Ed25519 — cannot distinguish keys and are not compared), **but a different encoding anchors only when the trusted certificate may issue** — by `Certificate::may_issue()`, the same rule the chain builder applies to an issuer, legacy self-signed root included. Without that guard, whoever holds a trusted end-entity key could mint a CA-bearing copy of it — same name, same key — and anchor a hierarchy of their own under an identity the user trusted for one signer. The exact trusted certificate still anchors itself, CA or not, as before this PR.

Fixes #6221.

## How you verified it

A worktree from `origin/main` (`c735fb7d`), with only this change:

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign` — 26 unit tests and 119 integration tests pass.
- New test `pdf::types::tests::an_anchor_is_a_name_and_a_key_not_an_encoding`: a trusted root, a byte-different copy of it (as a cross-signed or reissued root is), an unrelated certificate, a trusted end entity with a byte-different copy of itself, a v3 certificate without `basicConstraints` (the case `is_ca || !has_basic_constraints` still let through), and the same key bytes under another algorithm.
- **Both behaviours fail before the f…

title: fix(sign): changes after a signature that locked the document are judged by its level (#6865)
author: asadosteaksnl
body:
## What this changes

The **validation** half of #6865 (`Refs #6865`). The signing half is #6899; with both merged the issue can close.

Validation judged later changes by the certification's DocMDP level alone. A signature that locked the document ("lock document after signing") sets a level too, and it was not read. After an approval signature with `/P 1`, a second signature read as `Allowed(["signature"])` and both signatures showed valid, where Acrobat shows the first one invalid (the report's file; pyHanko: `docmdp_ok: False`).

The level a signature set is now read from the revision it covers, from two places:

- `/P` of its field's `/Lock` (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.5), and
- `/P` in the parameters of a FieldMDP `/Reference` in its value, which is where Acrobat writes the document lock (`/TransformParams << /Action /All /P 1 /V /1.2 >>` in the report).

The stricter of it and the certification's level goes to `classify_changes`, which already knows the three levels, so nothing in `changes.rs` changes but a doc comment:

| Level | A later signature | A comment | A document timestamp, the security store |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/P 1` | disallowed | disallowed | permitted |
| `/P 2` | permitted | disallowed | permitted |
| `/P 3`, or no `/P` | permitted | permitted | permitted |

Details:

- `/Lock`, `/P`, `/Reference`, `/TransformMethod` and `/TransformParams` are followed through references.
- The level is the signed revision's: a later revision that rewrites the lock does not relax it, as for DocMDP (#1788).
- A level below 1 or above 3 is the nearest one, as the DocMDP level is clamped. A `/P` that is not a number sets none.
- `info.certify` stays the certification's level: a lock does not make an approval signature a certification, and the interface keeps saying "signed", not "certified".
- A signature that several fields of the signed revision hold gets one verdict (#6041), judged by the strictest lock among those fields: a field with no lock, listed first, does n…

title: fix(cos): a clone that edits an object stream or a /Length stops reading what other clones cached
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Clones of a `Document` share its object cache, its parsed object streams and its `/Length` memo. #5802 stopped a clone from *writing* results that depend on its unsaved edits into those shared maps. Nothing stopped it from *reading* entries cached before its edit. Three cases, all on `main` today:

- A clean clone reads member 3 of object stream 4. A second clone replaces stream 4 (or frees it) and reads member 3, but gets the old member. A single document that reads and then edits the stream does the same.
- A clone edits the indirect `/Length` of an object stream, then reads a member. It gets the member framed by the old length.
- The same, for a plain stream whose `/Length` is indirect.

The fix records what each load read. While a load runs, a thread-local frame collects the object numbers it touched, including what any cached entry it reused had read. Every shared entry (cached object, parsed object stream, length memo) keeps that list. A document whose unsaved edits touch an entry's list ignores the entry and loads again, privately. A document with no edits takes the same O(1) path as before. A reference whose generation doesn't match the file reads as null, and it counts as read too, because an edit that sets that generation makes it match. One case: an object stream's `/DecodeParms` given as `6 1 R` in a file that has only `6 0`.

The other direction is closed too. Whether a parsed object stream is the loading document's own is now decided after its indirect `/DecodeParms` are read, not before. So a clone that decodes the stream with edited parameters keeps the result private.

`space_audit_shares_an_object_stream_across_categories_and_survives_freed_or_edited_members` (`pdfcraft-optimize`) relied on that stale read. It broke an object stream's `/First` and still read its members. It now edits the stream with an unrelated key, so the members stay readable and are still sized on their own.

`forget_member_failures` is gone. It cleared fa…

title: fix(cos): a dictionary key written with raw spaces no longer fails the whole dictionary
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Some producers write an Info key with raw spaces in it, like `/Universal PDF(Acme)`. A name ends at white space (ISO 32000-2 §7.3.5), so the lexer read the key `Universal`, then the bare word `PDF` where a value belonged, and failed the whole dictionary. The object then read as null, along with its Title, Author and everything else, and every later read of it went to the whole-file search again. That's how the file in #5802 ended up unreadable.

Now `dict_body` joins bare words after a key into the key (`Universal PDF`), but only when a string or a dictionary follows them. That is the shape these producers write. Anything else keeps the old failure:

- a name, number or keyword after the words, which looks like a value that lost its slash (`/Type Catalog /Pages 2 0 R`, `/Filter FlateDecode`);
- `obj`, `endobj`, `stream`, `R`, `true`, `false` or `null` among the words;
- more than eight words.

In those cases the dictionary fails as before and goes to the existing repair paths, so entries aren't silently moved.

`an_unreadable_object_is_searched_for_once` used `<< /Odd Key(x) >>` as its unreadable object. That shape is now readable, so the fixture is `<< /Odd ) >>`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos`: 162 lib tests plus the integration suites, all passing
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` / `assets`: not run. No boundary or asset is touched.

Tests, synthetic:

- `a_key_with_raw_spaces_keeps_the_dictionary`: a one-word key, multiple words with a double space and a `#41` escape, a dictionary value, and `true`/`null` still read as values. It fails without the fix.
- `a_bare_word_that_is_not_a_key_still_fails_the_dictionary`: the missing-slash, keyword, property-list (`<< /S Span >> BDC`) and over-cap shapes all still fail. It fails against an earlier, broader version of this change that joined every bare word.

title: perf(organize): decode the XMP packet once for repeated document-information reads
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

`organize::info` falls back to the catalog's XMP packet when `/Info` has no value (#2373). The tab and window title reach it through `Document::display_name` (`crates/engine/src/document.rs`, called from `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` for each tab label) whenever the document asks for its title to be shown. That happens on every frame. For a file whose title is only in XMP, each read inflated the packet again (up to 16 MiB at `MAX_XMP`) just to find one property.

Now `xmp::info_value` keeps the last decoded packet per thread, keyed by the identity of its stream object. The key is a `Weak<Object>` compared by pointer, and the `Weak` keeps the address from being reused while it's held. `pdfcraft-cos` hands out the same `Arc` for an object until it changes: the overlay's for an edit, or the cache's otherwise. A `set` or `update_dict` installs a new one, and another document has its own. So an edited packet is read afresh, and a cache eviction just costs a re-decode. Packets that aren't UTF-8 are remembered as unreadable too.

This came out of #5802, where the title redraw was the symptom. That PR, together with #5548, fixed the whole-file search. This is the remaining repeat decode.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-organize --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-organize`: 223 lib tests plus the integration tests, all passing
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` / `assets`: not run. Nothing crosses a crate boundary, and no asset is touched.

`the_xmp_packet_is_decoded_once_for_repeated_reads` counts decodes with a `cfg(test)` counter. Twenty reads of an XMP-only title and author decode once. After `set_info` edits the packet, the next read gets the new title, which costs one more decode. A second document gets its own title, and the first document still reads its own. An unreadable packet is decoded once for ten reads.

title: feat(prc): PrcFile::units, the model's unit from its model file
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

The model-file reader parsed `units_from_cad_file` and `units_in_mm` (WD 7.3.3) and then discarded them. Now `ModelFile` keeps both, and a new public accessor reports them:

- `PrcFile::units() -> Result<Option<ModelUnits>, PrcError>`
- `ModelUnits { mm_per_unit, from_cad_file }` is `Copy` and `non_exhaustive`.

`mm_per_unit` is millimetres per model unit (1 for millimetres, 25.4 for inches). `from_cad_file` says whether the unit is the CAD system's own or the exporter's default. When it's the exporter's default, a measurement should say the unit is assumed.

`units()` returns `None` in two cases:

- the file stores no tree (`stores_tree()` is false);
- the stored unit is not a positive finite number.

A model file that is stored but does not read is an error, as it is for `placements()`.

This is engine groundwork for 3D measurement, which `parity/acrobat-features.toml` lists as missing. Nothing user-facing calls it yet, so there is no automation tool and no parity change, the same as `model_tree()`.

- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-prc`: 116 lib tests plus the integration tests, all passing
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` / `assets`: not run. No crate boundary or asset is touched, and there are no new dependencies.

`the_model_file_gives_the_unit_and_whether_it_is_assumed` builds synthetic PRC streams with the existing test writers and checks five cases:

- the default fixture reads as 1 mm, assumed;
- `25.4` with the CAD-file bit set reads as inches from the CAD file;
- zero, negative, NaN and infinite units read as `None`;
- no model file reads as `None`;
- a model file of the wrong entity type is an error.

title: CI: the workspace's tests on macOS each night (and on demand)
author: FredApps
body:
## What this changes

A new workflow, `nightly-macos.yml`, runs the workspace's tests on `macos-latest` once a night (02:41 UTC) and on demand. It calls the shared gate (`craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/gate.yml@main`) like `ci.yml` does, with `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast` and a 90-minute leg.

**Why:**
- Pull requests and `main` run Linux and Windows only. The org's 5 macOS runners are kept for release builds.

title: feat(prc): keep a wire's vertex colours
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

A `TESS_3D_Wire` can store a colour per point or per segment (WD 7.8.7.2). The reader read past them, so a coloured edge or outline lost its colour. Now `Tessellation::Wire` holds a `WireTessellation`:

- `polylines`: what `Wire` held before;
- `colours`: each point's RGBA colour, one list per polyline, parallel to `polylines`. It is empty when the wire stores no colours.

How the colours are read:

- An RGB colour reads as opaque.
- A reused colour repeats the last one.
- A segment colour goes to both of its points. An odd last point takes the last segment's colour.
- If the colour count doesn't match the point count, `colours` is empty rather than misaligned.

**This changes a public type.** `Wire`'s payload is now a struct, `non_exhaustive` and re-exported from the crate root. Nothing in the workspace matches `Wire`: `prc-render` falls through on non-mesh entries, and #6194, #6414 and #6472 don't touch it. A face's vertex colours are still read and dropped, as on `main`.

title: M8: redaction reads an operator's operands from the end, as the renderer does
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

An operator takes its operands from the end, and the renderer ignores any surplus before them. So `(x) /OC /MC0 BDC` marks a layer's block, and `(x) /GS1 gs` selects `/GS1`. Redaction read some operands from the front instead. A surplus then stood in for them, and what they named went unseen.

Found in review of #6882. There, Remove Hidden Information left the text of a hidden layer in `(x) /OC /MC0 BDC (LAYERSECRET) Tj EMC`, which both the app's renderer and Poppler hide.

**In what Apply Redactions and Remove Hidden Information decide**, each of these read from the front:
- **The layers walk** read a block's tag and property list, and kept a hidden layer's block.
- **The cleanup of `/ActualText`, `/Alt`, `/E` and `/T`**, for a block whose paint was removed, read and wrote the property list. It kept the name that still read the removed word.
- **The tags cleanup** read a block's `MCID`. The removed text stayed in its structure element's `/ActualText` and `/Alt`. It read a `TJ`'s array from the front too, so a block that still drew was taken for empty, and its structure element lost content the page still shows.
- **The property cleanups** read the name of a `BDC` or `DP` property list. They retired a property list the page, or another page or form sharing its resources, still draws with.
- **The walk's `gs`** read the ExtGState it selects, so a font set only that way was never set. `cs` and `CS` did the same, so after `(x) /Pattern cs` the walk dropped the pattern the app's renderer still paints with, and pruned it when its other paint was redacted.
- **The Type 3 cleanup's reads of `cs`, `gs`, `Tf`, `BDC` and `DP`**, which decide which resources and fonts are still used, dropped ones still drawn: a font an ExtGState sets, and one a soft mask's group selects.

**Path construction** was read from the front too: `m`, `l`, `c`, `v` and `y` in the walk, and `l`, `c`, `v` and `y` in the proof, whose `m` and `re` took only an exact count and so were…

title: M8: an inline image a decoding reader may end at another EI is ambiguous
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

The content parser ends an inline image where the renderer's tokenizer does, so that redaction removes what the app draws. That tokenizer looks for an `EI` it accepts, and can pass over the real one:

```
q 10 0 0 10 0 0 cm BI /W 2 /H 1 /CS /G /BPC 8 /F /AHx ID 00FF> EI Q /Fm Do q /GSEI gs Q
```

Here it rejected the `EI` after the ASCIIHex end-of-data marker `>`, because too few operators follow it and none shows text. It ended the image inside the name `/GSEI` instead, reading `Q /Fm Do q /GS` as image data. A reader that decodes the data ends the image at the marker. Poppler draws the form, and its text under a mark. Apply Redactions saw no `Do`, and reported success with that text still in the file. Found in review of #6882.

**Now** an image counts in `Parsed::ambiguous_images` when a reader that decodes its data may end it at another `EI` than the renderer's, because then where the page's operators resume is a guess. Such a reader reads the data until it has the samples the image needs, or until the filter's end-of-data marker. It then ends the image at the first `EI` byte pair after that, whatever surrounds it. An image it can't decode (damaged, behind a filter it doesn't know, or of a colour space named as a resource the page doesn't define) it ends at the first `EI` after `ID`; one whose named colour space the page defines it reads by that colour space's samples.

Where that reader stops is worked out like this:
- **With no filter, or one ASCIIHex or ASCII85 filter, and a layout this parser knows** (a device colour space the page's resources don't redefine, an Indexed array written in the image, or an image mask), exactly: by the layout, or by counting the filter's characters up to the renderer's `EI`. The image counts when the first `EI` after that stop is not the renderer's, or when that reader would read past it.

title: M11: Optimize stores one-bit images and masks past 80 million pixels as monochrome images
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

**Builds on #6825** (a picture's one-bit masks), whose commit is the first here. Until that is merged, only the last commit is this pull request's own.

The image steps of the PDF Optimizer leave alone any image over 80 million pixels, for memory. Decoded at eight bits a pixel or more, such an image would hold 80 MB a component and more. An image already of one bit a pixel holds a byte for each 8 samples of a row, though. A large black-and-white scan (an A0 page at 600 ppi has about 560 million pixels) was left as stored, even though its samples would take less than 80 MB.

**Now** the monochrome step takes an image of one bit a pixel as stored while its rows hold no more bytes than 80 million pixels of eight bits (`one_bit_bytes`): up to 640 million pixels when it is wide, and a strip one sample wide no taller than before. That means an image mask, or one bit in one colour component, a picture's one-bit mask included. In particular, a picture's one-bit masks past 80 million pixels, which #6825 left aside, are now stored again while their rows fit that limit.
- **An image packed from eight bits** keeps the 80 million limit, because it is decoded at eight bits first.
- **A fax image's code** (what the filters before its decoder produce) may take no more than 80 MB for its pixels, however large the page, and four bytes a row. It was allowed about a byte a pixel (`fax_code_allowance`).
- **When planning how many pictures run at once**, a one-bit image counts as the bytes its rows hold and one more a row, as decoding allows each row's end a few bytes besides its samples: for an image a few samples wide, as much again as its samples.

The optimize README and the parity note say which images the monochrome step now takes, and the note now states JBIG2's limit of 2^28 pixels in all, as the README does.

title: Share Type 3 glyph procedures across form fills
author: chamber074
body:
**Stacked on #6841.** The base here is `main` because a fork branch cannot be a PR base upstream; until #6841 merges, the diff includes its commit. The new work is the top commit, `404d61bf9`, and the diff reduces to it on its own once #6841 lands.

Fixes #6867, the follow-up from the verification of #6841 by @mtlcl410: every filled widget built its own Type 3 font, so a form drawing the same glyphs in many fields stored the same CharProcs streams over and over — on the real prefilled_f1040 form he measured the file growing 186 KB to 1.16 MB, with 176 fonts and 862 CharProcs for only 36 distinct procedures.

## Change

Appearance streams now go through a per-call `GlyphPool` (`crates/forms/src/glyph_pool.rs`, used by `store_streams_pooled`):

- A stream is reused only after a **full equality check** — raw bytes plus dict entries in order — against streams the document already holds. The hash is a lookup aid, never trusted on its own. `/Length` is excluded from the comparison because the reader sets it and the writer recomputes it; with equal bytes it carries no information.
- The pool is seeded from the fonts the fields already carry, so refills and reopened files share with what is already stored, not just within one fill pass. Seeding is capped and lazy: fills that never draw fallback glyphs pay nothing.
- Font dicts, codes, Widths, content streams and the drawn bytes are unchanged — only the storage of identical glyph-procedure and ToUnicode streams is deduplicated.

One test-helper change rides along: the shared drawn-as-generated comparison now compares numbers by value. The cos writer stores whole-number reals as integer tokens by design, and the tests reopen the saved file before comparing, so a stored `/FontBBox` reads back as integers where the in-memory reference holds reals.

## Tests

- Seven new forms tests: sharing across fields, across widgets of one field, on refill, in batches, and with the stored glyphs of a reopened file, plus hostile existing app…

title: Enable Russian and mixed-language OCR with installed Tesseract
author: Autodidactus15
body:
## What this changes

Russian scans are rejected by the language selector even though the existing Tesseract backend can read them. This adds `ru` and `en+ru` to Recognize Text, OCR Verify, the shared automation tools and batch settings. English keeps its current default. The existing editable-output renderer does not recover original fonts; Cyrillic typeface and spacing may change. Searchable-image output preserves the scan's appearance.

Relates to [#4160](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/4160) and [#1859](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1859). [#5913](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/5913) proposes a neural model approach; this change extends the existing optional Tesseract process backend.
