title: M8: a stroke under a mark is found by the width it paints
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A stroke paints its line width around its path. Apply Redactions took a path for under a mark when the path's box overlapped the mark, and the box of a horizontal or vertical line has no height or width, so it overlaps nothing:

```
100 120 m 140 120 l S
```

under a mark over `[90 90 150 150]` was kept, with the redaction proof passing it too. Neither counted the width either, so a thick line beside a mark whose paint reaches under it (`30 w 100 160 m 140 160 l S`) stayed, with a passing proof. #5876, merged since, fixed both for strokes in the walk (below). On `main` the proof still counts no width, and a fill with no height or width (`100 120 40 0 re f`) is still kept by both.

**Now** the proof tracks the line width as the walk has since #5876, and in both a stroke's box grows by the paint around its path before it is tested against the marks:
- **The width** comes from `w` (read as the renderer reads it, the last operand) and an ExtGState's `/LW`, read through a reference wherever one stands: the `/ExtGState` dictionary, the state, or `/LW` itself. title: feat(ui): colour JavaScript in the script boxes with egui's highlighter
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

The four JavaScript boxes now colour the script in them:

- the JavaScript Console;
- Document JavaScripts;
- Field Properties ▸ Calculate ▸ Custom calculation script;
- Field Properties ▸ Actions ▸ Run a JavaScript.

Keywords, strings, comments and called functions each get their own colour. Names, numbers and punctuation stay plain text.

The colouring is egui's own highlighter (`egui_extras::syntax_highlighting`). Our egui pin (storytold/egui 725a39fc) reads JavaScript with a keyword list of its own, without TypeScript's extra keywords (fork patch E22, storytold/egui#24). PdfCraft adds `widgets::script`, one script box that lays its text out with egui's highlighter, and the four boxes use it, so a script box added later is coloured too. There is no tokenizer of our own. This replaces the approach of #6343, which built one.

- **Colours.** They are set through `CodeTheme::format_mut`. egui's light theme leaves names at about 2.9:1 contrast on a white field and strings at about 2.1:1. That is under the 4.5:1 that `view.theme-light-dark` promises for every text colour. Ours keep at least 4.5:1 in both themes, and a test checks it.
- **A 16 KiB limit.** Longer scripts are laid out uncoloured, as they are today. egui's highlighter rescans the rest of the text for each line that opens a string and doesn't close it, so a crafted script takes time in the square of its length. In a release build, 16 KiB of such lines took about 0.1 s, 64 KiB 2.6 s and 256 KiB 34 s, each time a key was typed. Ordinary code of 256 KiB took 8 ms. Without the limit, a document's script could freeze Document JavaScripts. The limit can go up if egui's scan is fixed.

title: M8: redaction skips an operator of the wrong type, as the renderer does
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

**Builds on #6927** (operands read from the end), whose four commits come first here. Until that is merged, only the last two commits are this pull request's own.

An operator whose operands aren't of the types it takes is skipped by the renderer, and changes nothing: after `70 Tc /x Tc` the character spacing is still 70. Redaction's walk and its proof read such an operator as a reset to a default instead. A glyph after it was then placed where the renderer doesn't draw it:

```
BT /F1 10 Tf 70 Tc /x Tc 20 20 Td (AB) Tj ET
```

left the B, drawn at x = 95, under a mark over it, and the proof passed the page.

**Now**, in the walk:
- **`Tc`, `Tw`, `Tz`, `TL`, `Ts` and `Tr`** keep the state when their operand isn't a number. So invisible text (`3 Tr /x Tr`) stays invisible, and Remove Hidden Information takes it.
- **`Tf`** takes its size only with a font name to go with it, and its font only with a size, as the renderer's `Tf` needs both: `(x) 40 Tf` set the size alone, and `/F2 /x Tf` switched the font.
- **`g`, `rg`, `k` and `G`, `RG`, `K`** clear the pattern only when their components read, and **`cs` and `CS`** only with a name. After `/x g` or `/CSR 5 cs` the renderer still paints with the pattern, which was pruned when its other paint was redacted.

- **`Tj`, `TJ`, `'` and `"`** whose operands aren't of their types are left as they are, drawing nothing and moving nothing. `5 '` and `/x 70 (zz) "` moved the line, and `-50000 Tj` moved the pen 500 pt (its number read as a `TJ` adjustment), so the text after them stood where it isn't drawn; and under a mark such a `"` was rewritten into `Tw`, `Tc`, `T*` and `TJ`, which draw.
- **`Tr` outside 0 to 7** fills, as mode 0, as the renderer has it: text in `9 Tr` painted nothing, and its fill pattern was pruned.

The proof's `Tc`, `Tw`, `Tz`, `TL`, `Ts`, `Tf`, `Tj`, `TJ`, `'` and `"` do the same. And in the Type 3 cleanup, `Tf` switches fonts only with a size: after `/F1 /x Tf` it unlinked the glyph…

title: M8: redaction's resource cleanups prune a dictionary in one pass
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

**Builds on #6927** (operands read from the end), whose four commits come first here: it rewrote the same lines of `prune.rs` and `type3.rs`. Until that is merged, only the last two commits are this pull request's own.

The cleanups after a redaction drop the resources nothing left on the page uses: property lists, XObjects, patterns, Type 3 fonts and their glyphs. Their work grew with the square of a dictionary a file controls:
- **Each name went with `Dict::remove`**, which moves the entries after it and renumbers the dictionary's key index, every time. A page whose `/Properties` held 400,000 unused entries didn't finish in 5 minutes.
- **`prune_properties` and `prune_form_resources` searched all the content's operators again for each entry** to see whether it was used: names times operators.
- **The Type 3 cleanup looked a name up by copying the whole dictionary it is in**, for each operator that names one: `/Font` for every `Tf`, `/ExtGState` twice for every `gs`, `/XObject` for every `Do`, `/Pattern` for every `scn` or `SCN`, and a form's, pattern's or soft mask's own `/Resources` every time it was drawn, before finding it already read, in its scan of the glyphs still drawn; and `/ExtGState` for every `gs` in its pruning of the fonts no longer drawn, which also went through every font for each one that sets a font. And it removed each Type 3 font with no glyph left from every holder's `/Font` one at a time, copying the whole `/Font` again for each. 4,000 entries, each named once, took 2.4 s to 13.8 s.

**Now** `pdfcraft_cos::Dict` gains `retain`, which keeps the entries it is told to, in their order, in one pass, and rebuilds the index once. Each cleanup decides against a set (of the names the content uses, or of the objects that go) and keeps or drops the entries in one pass:

title: M8: redaction refuses a run rather than copy property lists past 16 MiB
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

**Builds on #6927** (operands read from the end), whose four commits come first here: it rewrote the operand reads in `clean_replacements`. Until that is merged, only the last commit is this pull request's own.

Marked content whose paint a redaction removed loses the replacement text its property list gives it (`/ActualText`, `/Alt`, `/E`, `/T`): a copy of the list without it is written in place of the list's name. Each such `BDC` got a copy of its own, so a large list named by many of them grew the content without bound. 1,000 blocks naming a list of 100 KiB wrote 102 MB of content from a 154 KB file, holding 568 MiB, as measured in review of #6927.

**Now:**
- **The bytes the property-list copies take are counted for the whole run**, against `MAX_PROPERTY_COPIES`, 16 MiB: Apply Redactions and Remove Hidden Information carry what is left from page to page (`Scope::with_property_room`), forms included. Past it they refuse, with `RedactError::PropertyCopies` naming the page. Apply changes nothing; the library's `remove_hidden` may have rewritten the pages before the one refused, which the app, running it on a copy, never keeps (the README says so).
- **A list named, or given by reference in the content** (`/Span 7 0 R BDC`, which content shouldn't hold, but the parser reads), is counted alike. One written inline in the content is stripped where it stands: its copy is no larger than what the content held. An operand that is neither a name, a reference nor a list strips nothing.
- **Each list is stripped once:** one by reference once for the page, however many forms drawn name it; one written in `/Properties` once for the stream. The copy is built from the entries that stay, so it costs what it is charged, however large the replacement text was.
- **A list with no replacement text is never copied**, which is told where the list stands; and once the allowance is spent, no named or referenced list is stripped.

title: Print: flatten transparent sheets for GDI (v3) printer drivers (#6155, #5838, #5940)
author: FredApps
body:
## What this changes

On Windows, PdfCraft prints through Windows.Data.Pdf into the XPS print API. XPS-native (v4) drivers print transparency correctly. GDI (v3) drivers are reached through Windows' XPS-to-GDI conversion, which mishandles it:
- **#6155:** `Render error 0x80004005` on every v3 driver tried (Kyocera, Canon, HP), on a page with many soft-masked images. Every v4 driver prints it.
- **#5838:** a Ricoh PCL6 v3 driver prints soft-edged transparent images with halos and smears. The same images flattened onto white print clean.
- **#5940:** a KIP large-format driver prints anything transparent as a black box.

For a GDI driver, the copy sent to the spooler now has each **sheet that uses transparency** drawn as a picture at print resolution. Sheets without transparency stay vector, and XPS drivers, PDF printers among them, are untouched.

- **`spool::gdi_driver` / `spool::xps_driver`:** read `PRINTER_DRIVER_XPS` through craft-print's new `xps_driver` (storytold/craft-libs#804), which uses winprint's `PrinterDevice::is_xps_driver` (storytold/winprint.rs#21).
- **`spooler::flattened(bytes, dpi)`:**
  - **Resolution:** 300 dpi, lower for a sheet that would go past 80 MP or 16,000 px a side.
  - **Tiles:** each sheet is drawn in tiles of at most 2000 × 2000 px, under Windows.Data.Pdf's 2²² px image cap, so even large-format sheets keep their resolution.
  - **Rendering:** each tile is rendered and Flate-encoded on its own over white, and placed through the page's view matrix. The sheet keeps its boxes, rotation and UserUnit.
  - **Never stops a print:** a sheet that fails to render stays vector, and pictures past 512 MB in one copy stay vector.
- **`pdfcraft_preflight::page_uses_transparency`:** preflight's existing transparency search, made public. A transparency group with only opaque content doesn't count: Word gives every page a page group, and that alone must not turn pages into pictures.

title: fix(sign): list signatures and compare set-aside xref entries in linear time
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

Two steps in reading a document's signatures took time quadratic in what the file declares. A small crafted file could stall them for minutes, and the first one runs whenever the file is opened.

**Placing a signature widget by its `/P`** (`list_cached`, `crates/sign/src/pdf/listing.rs`). A signature widget that no page's `/Annots` lists is placed on the page its `/P` names. `page_index` found that page with a fresh `pdfcraft_annot::page_refs` walk of the whole page tree for every such field, so the work was fields × page-tree entries. `annot_pages` already walks the tree once per listing; it now also records each page's index, and `/P` is looked up there. `page_index` is gone. `page_refs` lists each page once, so the index is the one `position` returned.

**Comparing set-aside cross-reference entries** (`classify_changes`, `crates/sign/src/pdf/changes.rs`). Each entry the reader sets aside in the current document (an in-use entry at offset 0, a second entry for one object, a reserved entry type) was searched for with `Vec::contains` among all of the signed revision's. That is quadratic in their number, and the reader keeps one per row with no cap beyond `MAX_XREF_OBJECTS`. The signed revision's entries are now collected into a `HashSet` first. Which entries count as new after signing is unchanged.

title: fix(ui): prefetched pages that arrive first keep the allowance that queued them
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

Follows #6065.

The render queue sizes the whole-page allowance from the raster the page on screen asks for. An arriving off-screen raster was admitted against the rasters already held on screen. After a zoom in, before the page on screen has its new raster, the held raster is the old, smaller one, so texture admission used the 128 MiB floor while the queue had used the larger allowance. Each arriving neighbor then evicted another queued neighbor, and the next frame queued that page again, until the page on screen arrived.

Texture admission now also counts the on-screen demand the queue used in the same frame, so both checks use one allowance.

On Windows, on `c04925c5`:

title: deps: take rustix 1.1.6 for RUSTSEC-2026-0486
author: dotCooCoo
body:
RUSTSEC-2026-0486 (https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0486) was added to the advisory database on 2026-11-11. It reports that rustix 1.1.5's extended-attribute functions in `rustix::fs` mark bytes as initialized that the system call never wrote when given a zero-length buffer. `cargo deny check advisories` rejects the locked rustix 1.1.5, so the gate's `deny` step now fails on every pull request (for example #6965), and main's next run will fail the same way.

This takes rustix 1.1.6, the patched release, with `cargo update -p rustix@1.1.5 --precise 1.1.6`. Only the rustix entry and the lines that name it change in `Cargo.lock`; `windows-sys` stays at 0.61.2, and rustix 0.38.44 is not affected.

Dependabot's #6891 also moves rustix to 1.1.6, together with 16 other updates.

title: M2: a segment after `re` begins at the rectangle's corner
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

`x y width height re` is `x y m`, three `l` and `h` (ISO 32000-2 §8.5.2.1, Table 58), so it leaves the current point at (x, y), and a segment after it begins a new subpath there. The vendored renderer (hayro-interpret) appended the rectangle but left its current point where it was. Since patch 61, a segment after a closed subpath starts with a move to that point. So a segment after `re` was drawn from the point before `re`. That was the last point of the path being built, or of an earlier path already painted, or the origin when nothing came before it in the content. For example:

```
6 w 120 120 10 10 re 180 20 l S
```

drew a line from (0, 0) to (180, 20), where the standard has it from (120, 120). After `40 40 m 80 40 l S`, the same rectangle and line were drawn from (80, 40). `v`, whose first control point is the current point, started there too.

**Now** `re` sets the current point to its (x, y), the corner it was written from, whatever the rectangle's sign: vendored hayro-interpret patch 105. A segment after it is drawn from there, by `l`, `c`, `v` or `y`. `vendor/README.md` lists the patch and its test.

Every render by PdfCraft's renderer reaches it: the page view, exported rasters, and printing as an image or flattened for a GDI printer driver. A vector print job is drawn by the system or the printer, as before. Other readers of page content already start a segment after `re` at (x, y), or take only the box of a path's points, and now agree with what is drawn:
- **Redaction.** The redaction walk and its proof take a path's paint to lie within the box of its points. A segment from the rectangle's corner does; one from an earlier path's point or from the origin did not, and neither of them saw it. The miter reach that #6939 adds starts the segment at the corner too, and states the gap. author: FredApps
body:
Port of #344 by @DWAA1660 onto the per-document script session that landed with #5699. title: Edit text: the clipping-path refusal says where the text can still be changed
author: RavenCrowe666
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3429, #4786. Not a fix for either — this is only the wording the user sees.

When an edit is refused, `editing.rs` translates the engine's error for one edit kind and passes
the raw string through for every other:

```rust
let message = if matches!(edit, Edit::MoveObjects { .. }) { move_error(&e) } else { e.to_string() };
```

`move_error` carries the comment that states the intent: *"Keep the UI refusal actionable and
translated; headless callers retain the detailed error."* Text edits miss it, so a refused
paragraph shows the engine's sentence verbatim, in English whatever the interface language:

```
text used as a clipping path cannot be edited: its glyphs mask the artwork behind them
```

It is accurate and it is a dead end. It says why this file cannot be edited and not where the
text can still be changed. That matters more here than for other refusals: in a Photoshop export
every text object is drawn as a clipping path, so on such a page this is the only answer the user
will ever get, once per paragraph they click.

This applies the existing pattern to text edits, for both the preview refusal and the commit
refusal, which the user meets at different moments:

```
This text is a mask the artwork is painted through, so editing it here would destroy the page.
Change the text in the file this PDF was exported from, then export it again.
```

## What is not changed

Every other refusal keeps the engine's wording, which scripts, headless callers and bug reports
read. The engine is untouched: no error text, no behaviour, no guard. Nothing becomes editable
that was not before.

## Notes

The mapping sits in its own function taking the message rather than the error, so it can be
tested from `ui-egui`: the crate depends on `pdfcraft-engine` but not on `pdfcraft-edit`, whose
variant carries the text, and `cargo xtask layers` keeps it that way.

title: M10: LibreOffice converts with no network on Linux and macOS (#6953)
author: max1e6
body:
## What this changes

Refs #6953 (Linux and macOS; Windows is not sandboxed yet, so this does not close it).

LibreOffice fetches a picture linked from a web address in a presentation **and in a spreadsheet** whatever its profile says: with the current profile, an ODP and an ODS with such a picture each connected to a local listener (LibreOffice 24.2.7, Linux). So the converter is now started with no network where the system has a tool for it:

- **Linux:** a network namespace of its own, through bubblewrap (`bwrap --unshare-net`) or, without it, util-linux's `unshare --user --net`. Nothing is reachable from inside, the machine's own services included.
- **macOS:** `sandbox-exec` with a profile that denies the network. Written from the tool's documentation; **not run on a Mac**.
- **Every system:** the throwaway profile sends web requests to a proxy that isn't there (127.0.0.1:9), which stops links to other machines even without a sandbox. LibreOffice doesn't use a proxy for the machine's own addresses, so this is a second layer, not the fix.
- **Windows, FreeBSD:** no sandbox; the proxy only. An AppContainer needs a new dependency, which I'd propose separately.

Which sandbox works is found once per LibreOffice by converting a small built-in document inside each candidate, since user namespaces can be turned off and a tool can start while LibreOffice fails inside it. Where none works, the conversion runs as before. `libreoffice_sandbox()` names the tool in use.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (create, engine, automation, ui-egui)

title: fix(js, engine, ui): XFA message boxes return the button picked (#4291)
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4291.

In XFA forms, `xfa.host.messageBox`, FormCalc's `$host.messageBox` and `app.alert` always returned 1 (OK). A form could never branch on No or Cancel. They now return the button picked: 1 OK, 2 Cancel, 3 No, 4 Yes. This is how AcroForm's `app.alert` already works since #5699.

**In the app:**
- **On a worker:** an XFA button click runs on a worker thread and goes through the same pending script that AcroForm buttons use.
- **Asking:** each message box in the click, and in the calculations it sets off, shows in the existing script dialog while the script waits. Closing the dialog gives the buttons' safe default: OK alone 1, Yes/No 3, otherwise 2.
- **Time limits:** the script's time limit and the event's budget stop while it waits for the user.
- **Undo and changes:** the click is kept as one undo step once it ends. It is dropped if the document changed meanwhile.
- **Limit:** a click may ask at most 32 times, as an AcroForm script may. The count covers the whole click, across every script session it uses. A script that toggles field highlighting starts a new session for the next script, and that doesn't reset the count. Past 32, nobody is asked and each message box gets its safe default.
- **Runaway scripts:** a click whose script runs away still turns the form's scripts off, even when the click itself is dropped.
- **Scrolling and zooming:** these don't drop a running XFA click, which reads no view state. A click dropped because the document changed says so in a notice. The app's backstop for an XFA click with no question showing is 60 s instead of AcroForm's 10 s; the click's own limits (engine start, click and calculation budgets, laying the form out again) can add up past 10 s.
- **A side effect:** the app stays responsive while an XFA click runs, including one that runs away.

**Headless:** `js_run`'s `answers` now reach XFA buttons. Every message box takes the next answer, OK-only ones included. Once the answers run out, a me…

title: feat: LaTeX animate playback — page actions, timers, getOCGs, view-only overrides (port of #4751)
author: FredApps
body:
Port of #4751 by @pyatsysh onto the per-document `ScriptSession` from #5699 and the document actions from #6969. The behaviour and most of the design are @pyatsysh's. This PR carries them over to the shared script realm, following the direction in https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/4751#issuecomment-6777308721. Each commit has a `Co-authored-by` trailer for them.

Fixes #169 (LaTeX `animate` animations play). Refs #269.

## What this changes

- **Timers** (`app.setInterval`, `app.setTimeOut`, `clearInterval`, `clearTimeOut`). They are kept in the document's realm and fire there, with #4751's bounds: 10 ms minimum period, 64 per document, 16 runs per call. A timer runs unasked, so its alerts and requests go to the console. The app pumps them each frame (`Session::run_timers`) and asks for a repaint when the next one is due (`next_timer`). Only the active tab runs.
- **Page actions.** When the page being read changes, the old page's close actions run, then the new page's open actions: the page's own `/AA /O` and `/C`, and its annotations' `/PO`, `/PV`, `/PC` and `/PI`, in order (`pdfcraft_forms::page_scripts`, `Session::show_page`).
- **`this.getOCGs()`** with `name`, `state` and `initState`. Setting `state` turns the layer as the Layers panel does.
- **View-only changes.** What page actions and timers show, hide or swap (`display`, `buttonSetIcon`) changes only the view. The renderer takes per-annotation visibility and appearance overrides (`RenderConfig::{annotations, appearances}`, hayro-interpret patches 104 and 105 in `vendor/README.md`, renumbered from #4751's 67/68). Playback doesn't modify the document, mark it dirty or fill Undo. Print and export draw the document as saved. Value changes from a timer are still one undoable edit. A button's changes go into the document as before, and the view's overlay for that field gives way.

title: fix(forms): deleting a field removes ancestors it leaves without kids
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Finding: deleting a redacted terminal field only removed it from its parent's `/Kids`. When the field inherited a confidential `/V` or `/DV` from an ancestor, the emptied ancestor stayed in `/Fields` (now a field of its own) with that value, and survived a full save.

An ancestor that still has a kid is left alone with its values. Test `deleting_the_last_kid_removes_the_emptied_ancestors_and_their_values` fails on main and passes now.

title: Add Tamil (ta) as an interface language
author: newsbaba24x7
body:
## What this changes

Adds Tamil (`ta`) as an interface and date-format language. The catalog is already in
craft-i18n (`locales/ta/`, included in the commit pinned by `craft-i18n.rev`), so this PR
registers it in PdfCraft's language lists, which have to stay in sync:

- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs`: new `LANGUAGES` entry (`ta`, left to right), `LANGUAGE_COUNT` 35 → 36,
  and a `"ta" => "Tamil"` arm in `english_name`. `ta`, `ta-IN`, `ta-LK` and `ta_IN.UTF-8`
  locales now resolve to Tamil automatically.
- `crates/engine/src/dates.rs`: new `DATE_LANGUAGES` entry (`ta`, name `தமிழ்`) with Tamil long and
  short month and weekday names; array length 35 → 36. `months_with_day` is `None`, since Tamil
  doesn't change the month name after a day number.
- `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`: `ta` added to `CFBundleLocalizations`, last, in `LANGUAGES` order.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/tests.rs`: new `tamil_is_registered_and_persists` test (name, preference
  normalization, locale matching, saving and restoring the language option).

After this, Tamil appears in the Preferences language dropdown and the date-format language list,
and a Tamil system locale selects it.

A Tamil speaker checked the short month and weekday forms.

### Tamil interface font

title: M8: a colour space the resources give as a Pattern space keeps the pattern
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

`cs` and `CS` reset the colour. The redaction walk took the pattern selected before them for cleared unless the operand was the name `/Pattern`. The app's renderer looks the name up, and keeps the pattern for any Pattern space: vendored hayro-interpret's `cs` clears the pattern only when the space isn't one. So after

```
/Pattern cs /P0 scn 20 140 100 30 re f /CSP cs 20 40 100 30 re f
```

with `/ColorSpace << /CSP /Pattern >>`, the second box is filled with `/P0`. With the first box under a mark, the walk took `/P0` for no longer painted and pruned it from the page, and the second box, beside the mark, lost its paint. ISO 32000-2 §8.6.8 has `cs` reset a Pattern space's colour to one that paints nothing, as Poppler draws it; the walk follows the app's renderer, so what that shows outside the mark stays.

**Now** the walk reads the name as the renderer does:
- **Built-in names.** `/Pattern` itself is a Pattern space, even where the resources give `/Pattern` as something else. A device space's name (`/G`, `/DeviceRGB`, …) never is. The renderer reads both before the resources.
- **Other names.** The scope's `/ColorSpace` entry for the name decides. `/Pattern` or `[/Pattern base]` keeps the pattern; anything else, `null`, or no entry resets it. The dictionary, the entry and the array's first element may each be given by reference, and a `/ColorSpace` that is a stream is read by its dictionary, as the renderer reads it.
- **Non-name operands.** A `cs` whose operand isn't a name is skipped by the renderer, and now keeps the pattern. It cleared it before.
- **Cost.** Only Apply prunes patterns, so only its walk of each page looks a name up; the proof's snapshot, Apply's check and Sanitize's walks read nothing more than before. That walk looks nothing up when no pattern is selected on the side `cs` or `CS` resets, as there is nothing to reset. What it reads by reference (an entry, an array's first element) is read once for the run, and a `/ColorSpace…

title: M8: a redaction refusal names its page and says nothing was changed
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

When a redaction's cleanup couldn't read what it needs to show something gone, it refused with a cos syntax error at byte 0:

```
syntax error at byte 0: a form XObject's /Matrix isn't six numbers given directly or through one reference, so where it draws can't be told
syntax error at byte 0: redaction could not fully inspect glyph stream syntax
```

Byte 0 is no place in the file, no page was named, and nothing said the document was left as it was. Twenty sites in `crates/redact` refused this way: the walk's `/Matrix` check (#6886), the Type 3 font cleanup, and the cleanup of the resources and properties a rewritten page or form draws with.

**Now** they are refusals of their own:
- **`RedactError::PageRefused { page, reason }`**: "page 2 can't be redacted safely: \<reason\>; nothing was changed", in the form of `RedactError::Pattern`'s message. It is used where one page's content or forms are the cause:
  - Apply Redactions' and Remove Hidden Information's walk of each page;
  - the cleanup of the forms, properties and Type 3 fonts a rewritten page draws with;
  - the Type 3 cleanup's scan of every page, marked or not;
  - the check of what other pages sharing a resource dictionary still draw.
- **`RedactError::Refused(reason)`**: "the document can't be redacted safely: \<reason\>; nothing was changed". It is used where no one page is: a Type 3 font without the entries its cleanup reads, or forms shared across the document.
- **Each reason says what stood in the way**, for example "a Type 3 font's glyph has bytes that can't be read", or "content that draws with its resources has bytes that can't be read, or more than 2,000,000 operators".

Two more refusals now name the page:
- **Content and forms past what one page may read** (a form its decode budget refused, or one past the forms it may enter) refused with the budget's cos error, "stream data could not be decoded: the page draws more than 50000 form XObjects", in the walk and in two cleanu…

title: M3: Copy and Copy with formatting read a text colour in the colour space cs selected (view.copy-with-layout)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Copy with formatting (and `text_extract` with `format: "html"`) gives each run the colour its text is filled with. For text whose colour is set with `cs` and then `sc`/`scn`, that colour was read from the number of operands alone: one number as DeviceGray, three as RGB, four as CMYK. The space `cs` selected was never looked at. So black text printed in a `Separation /Black` ink at full tint (`/Cs8 cs 1 scn`) came out `color:#FFFFFF`, and pasted into a word processor it is white on white. An Indexed colour read its index as a gray level.

### How common

Two public Taiwan government reports print every page in a `Separation /Black` spot colour (tint 1.0, its alternate an ICCBased RGB space through a sampled function):

| File | Pages | Runs in the HTML | `color:#FFFFFF` on `main` | characters in those runs | `color:#FFFFFF` with this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [Institute of Transportation, a study of valet parking services (2019)](https://www.iot.gov.tw/uploads/asset/data/66196fcb367376304acd4db7/%E4%BB%A3%E5%AE%A2%E9%A7%95%E8%BB%8A%E6%9C%8D%E5%8B%99%E5%88%B6%E5%BA%A6%E4%B9%8B%E7%A0%94%E7%A9%B6.pdf) | 334 | 2,409 | 2,358 | 40,241 | 0 |
| [MOTC, a study of freeway ramp capacity (2022)](https://www.motc.gov.tw/uploaddowndoc?file=datagov/1452905816947429376.pdf&filedisplay=13.111年_運輸計畫及陸運組_高快速公路匝道分匯流區容量及服務水準分析之研究(3_3)-快速公路分析及容量手冊研訂.pdf&flag=doc) | 338 | 14,393 | 14,134 | 108,370 | 0 |

The white text is the report numbers, section numbers such as `1.1`, the contents' dot leaders and page numbers. On the page it is black.

Across the 1,352 PDFBox JIRA and pdf.js files used for #6840, 91 files have runs whose colour changes (25,968 runs), and the runs given `color:#FFFFFF` fall from 47,129 to 9,604 (details under "How you verified it").

title: M2: a Type1C font file holding a Type 1 program draws with it (#6990)
author: charlieruk
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #6990.

PDFs exported by Calamus SL (Bridge 7.02 PRO) draw all their text in the standard substitute instead of their embedded fonts (Montserrat Light, IBM Plex Mono, …).

**Why.** Each font is a simple `/Type1` font whose descriptor has a `/FontFile3` with `/Subtype /Type1C`, which declares bare CFF. The stream actually holds a Type 1 program in PFB segments (`80 01`, `80 02`, `80 03`). The vendored `hayro-interpret` read every `/FontFile3` of a simple font as CFF; the CFF reader refused the data, and the font fell back to the standard substitute.

**Now.** When a simple font's `/FontFile3` isn't CFF, `hayro-interpret` reads it as Type 1 (vendored patch 104, `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/type1.rs`), as pdf.js and the other viewers in the report do. The Type 1 reader already takes PFB segments as well as cleartext and an eexec section. Real CFF is still tried first, so fonts that are what they say are read as before; data that is neither still falls back to the substitute.

title: fix(xfa): resolve row instance managers in SOM paths
author: sebsca
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #7019

XFA `resolveNode("Table1._Row1")` returned `null` because the SOM resolver only returned form nodes, not the instance manager named by a terminal `_Row1` step. The issue's add/remove-row click scripts therefore failed.

`resolveNode()` now resolves terminal instance-manager steps in their parent scope. The review follow-up also handles descendant paths such as `$form.._row`, selectors such as `table._row[0]`, and wildcard parent paths such as `table[*]._row`. When multiple parents match, it checks them in document order and gives a real named child precedence within its own parent. Unqualified manager names are checked one enclosing scope at a time, and descendant searches visit earlier child subtrees before later siblings. An indexed lookup stops at the first matching scope or descendant even when that scope lacks the requested instance, so an outer or later field cannot supply it. Terminal manager names and selectors are trimmed like ordinary SOM steps, including expressions such as `table. _row [ 0 ]`.

title: fix(render): an RGB colour in an isolated DeviceCMYK group blends in CMYK, as its ink
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4887.

#5228 blends an isolated `DeviceCMYK` transparency group in CMYK (ISO 32000-2 §11.3.4), but only
when every colour in it has process tints: `DeviceCMYK` or `DeviceGray`. One RGB fill anywhere in
the group makes the whole group blend in RGB instead. This gives an additive colour
(`DeviceRGB`, `CalRGB`, `Lab`, three-component `ICCBased`) the ink that draws back to it through
the CMYK profile pages are drawn with, so the group blends in CMYK.

- New module `hayro-interpret/src/cmyk_inverse.rs` (vendored patch (104)). Black is
  `K = 0.4·k₀² + 0.6·k₀⁸` with `k₀ = 1 − max(r, g, b)`. Cyan, magenta and yellow are then solved
  by at most 12 Newton steps against the profile's forward transform. Non-finite input, or a
  profile that can't be evaluated, gives no tints, and the group is drawn as before. The last
  colour is cached per thread, because a run of glyphs shares one colour.
- `Color::ink_tints` uses it for the additive spaces. `ICCBased` CMYK still gives none (it keeps
  its own profile), as #5228's review asked.
- A colour inside the profile's gamut draws as itself. One outside it lands where the clamped
  solve stops: pure red draws close to Acrobat's 238 32 37. I did not compare the green and blue
  primaries with Acrobat.
- Only isolated `DeviceCMYK` groups change. Pages and other groups draw as before.
- Cost: up to 12 Newton steps of four profile evaluations for each new colour. I have not timed
  it. The one-entry cache covers runs of one colour, not content that alternates colours.

The black curve and the profile route come from black-box observation of Acrobat Reader on
synthetic pages: RGB squares, and `/BM /Difference` with `0 0 0 1 k` to reveal the ink. Acrobat
does not use §10.4.2.4's black generation here. 50% grey under that Difference is about
137 112 106 in Acrobat, and 133 106 99 with this change. Grey made from black ink alone gives
near-black. The group's fallback to RGB blending, before this change, gives a…

title: fix(preflight): identify a file as PDF/A only when conversion leaves no problems
author: jayzed80
body:
Fixes #6845

## Root cause

`pdfcraft_preflight::convert` (`crates/preflight/src/lib.rs`, before this change at lines 1432-1440) always builds a new XMP packet declaring `pdfaid:part`/`pdfaid:conformance`, points the catalog's `/Metadata` at it, and records "Identified the file as PDF/A-xb". Only afterwards (line 1519 before, 1523 now) does it re-check the file with `verify`. The problems that are left (for example clause 6.2.11.4, fonts that aren't embedded, `fixable: false`) were returned in the report, but the identification stayed in the document. `Edit::ConvertPdfA` (`crates/engine/src/edit/run.rs:879`) applies the result as is, so the next `doc_save` wrote a PDF/A claim the file doesn't meet.

## Fix

- `crates/preflight/src/lib.rs:1434`: remember the catalog's `/Metadata` entry before writing the claim.
- `crates/preflight/src/lib.rs:1523-1537`: the re-check still runs with the identification in place, so the problems reported are the real remaining ones. If any remain, the catalog gets back the `/Metadata` it had (or none), the packet this run added is freed, and the "Identified…" line is removed from `fixed`. A conversion with no problems left behaves exactly as before.
- `crates/automation/src/a11y/documents.rs` (`pdfa_convert`): when the result is not compliant, the existing `warnings` list gets "not identified as PDF/A-xb: the file still has problems conversion can't fix, so conversion added no PDF/A identification". The tool description in `crates/automation/src/tools.rs` says the same.
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml` (`optimize.pdfa-convert`): adds the new tests as evidence and a note about the behaviour.

The detection rules are unchanged. #6843 (fonts added by `page_add_text` not detected) is handled separately in #6871.

## Tests

New (`crates/preflight/src/tests.rs`):
- `convert_writes_no_pdfa_claim_while_fonts_are_not_embedded`: a page using unembedded Times-Roman, Times-Bold and Times-Italic (built in the test). Converting reports 3 × 6.2.11.4, …

title: prc: rebuild compressed tessellations whose normals are recalculated (#1297)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-prc` reads a `TESS_3D_Compressed` (ISO 14739-1 / WD 7.8.9.7) to its end, but it does not rebuild its triangles, so `prc-render` and `model_render` draw nothing for it. Refs #1297.

This PR rebuilds the most common form: a compressed tessellation whose normals are recalculated (`must_recalculate_normals`), with three edge statuses per triangle. It becomes a `Tessellation::Mesh`:
- grouped by face like a `TESS_3D`;
- each triangle styled by its face's line attribute;
- `normals_recalculated: true`.

`prc-render` then draws it with no change of its own.

**How it is rebuilt** (`crates/prc/src/tess/compressed.rs`):
- The walk starts with a seed triangle.
- Each further triangle takes one apex: a reference to an earlier vertex, or the next point, in units of the tolerance. The point is in a frame built on the edge it continues across.
- Each triangle's edge status says which of its two free edges the walk continues across. A stack holds the branches still to walk; an empty stack starts the next component.
- The geometry follows the WD's `PrcPt::Length`, `Unitize` and `MakeOrthoRep` pseudocode (WD 12.3), as I read it. The working draft rounds the squared length to `f32` and takes a Newton root, so an exact `sqrt` drifts off the encoder's mesh over a long strip. A test pins this.
- Every slot, reference and point must be used exactly. Arrays that do not fit, and an edge shared by more than two triangles, leave the tessellation a `Compressed` (as today) rather than a wrong mesh.

**Left for later PRs** (this one is the walk and its geometry):
- compressed tessellations that store their normals: they need the stored normals to orient the walk;
- the one-status-per-triangle form;
- a planar-face bend check, and a best-fit search over the ambiguous cases;
- salvaging the part of a mesh that decodes when the rest does not.

## How you verified it

On this head, `-p <crate> -j 2`, Rust 1.99.1:

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfc…

title: fix(organize): Combine keeps tagged sources' structure trees
author: jayzed80
body:
Fixes #7025 (the main problem: tags and PDF/UA identification are dropped. The second problem in the issue, a warning when an input is untagged, is not part of this PR.)

## Root cause

Combine copies each source's pages with `import_pages_mapped` (`crates/organize/src/import.rs:199`). The page copier strips the keys that point into the structure tree: `/StructParents` on pages (`SKIP_ON_PAGE`, `crates/organize/src/import/copy.rs:7`) and `/StructParent` on annotations (`SKIP_ON_ANNOT`, `copy.rs:9`). Nothing in `Combiner` or `combine_grouped_with` (`crates/organize/src/import/combine.rs`) copied the source's `/StructTreeRoot`, `/MarkInfo` or `/Lang` afterwards. So tagged inputs always gave an untagged result. The XMP packet that combine writes (`crates/organize/src/pdfx.rs`) never carried `pdfuaid` either.

## Fix

New module `crates/organize/src/import/tags.rs`. Both `Combiner::add` and `combine_grouped_with` call it right after each source's pages are copied, and their `finish` steps write the result:

- **Elements.** Each element is rebuilt with `/P`, `/K` and `/Pg` pointing at the copies. Its other entries (`/S`, `/Alt`, `/ActualText`, `/A`, `/C`, `/ID`…) are copied without following any reference to the page tree or the structure tree. Each source's top-level elements go under one `Document` element, in input order. A source's own top-level `Document` element becomes a `Part`.
- **Parent tree.** It is rebuilt from the copied elements with new keys numbered 0, 1, 2… across all sources. The keys go on the copied pages and form XObjects (`/StructParents`) and on annotations and objects named by an object reference (`/StructParent`). Stale keys that copied form XObjects brought along are removed so they can't collide.
- **Merged maps.** `/RoleMap`, `/ClassMap` and `/IDTree` are merged. When two sources give the same name or ID different entries, the first source's entry is kept. This is documented in the module.
- **Catalog.** The result gets `/MarkInfo << /Marked t…

title: sign: refuse changes after signing that no permitted operation explains (part of #7032)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

Part of #7032 (stages A, B and C). Draft until the direction in #7032 is agreed and the changes are checked against a corpus of real signed files.

Validating changes after signing no longer allows whatever label a changed object's own shape earns. A snapshot of the roles in the signed revision is taken once. Every object a later revision changed or added must then be claimed by an operation the signature permits:

| Operation | Levels | May touch |
|---|---|---|
| Fill an unlocked field | 2, 3, approval | `/V` (and `/I`); its widgets' `/AS` and appearance when the value changed; `/NeedAppearances`; `/DR` entries only added |
| Sign | 2, 3, approval | a field or widget whose new signature signs the revision that writes it (only `/V` and `/AP` on an existing one), the form's `/Fields` and `/SigFlags` |
| Comment | 3, approval | a non-widget, non-link annotation added, changed, removed or restacked, with its appearance and pop-up |
| Document timestamp | all | an invisible field, or a standalone `/DocTimeStamp`, that signs its own revision |
| Validation data | all | the `/DSS` as `dss_parts` recognises it, and its data |
| Housekeeping | all | the signed `/Info` and XMP, `/Metadata`, `/NeedsRendering`, extensions, xref and object streams |

**Anything no operation claims is refused**, so a miss shows as a warning instead of passing silently.

**Field locks.** FieldMDP and `/Lock` are folded in. A fill or a signature can't claim a locked field's objects. #6763's comparison still decides removed or shadowed fields, and still gives Unknown when a lock can't be read.

**Field identity.** A signature is valid only in the field that held that exact dictionary in the revision its `/ByteRange` covers. The rule and its tests come from #5175 by LetoCoder26.

title: fix(fonts): the licence policy reads name-table records one at a time within a total allowance
author: dylanmtaylor
body:

title: fix(ui): colour swatch grid columns as wide as their swatches, and the picker as wide as the grid
author: jayzed80
body:
Fixes #6612

## Cause

`swatch_grid` (`crates/ui-egui/src/tools/comments/menu.rs`) builds its grid with `egui::Grid::new(..).spacing(vec2(6.0, 6.0))` and no `min_col_width`. egui then makes every column at least `interact_size.x` (about 40 pt) wide. Each 22 pt swatch is drawn at the left of its column, so swatches sit 46 pt apart, and an empty gap is left after the last column (the extra right margin).

The custom picker (`color_picker_color32`) sizes itself from `spacing.slider_width`, about 100 pt, so it sat at the popup's left.

## Fix

- The grid's `min_col_width` is the swatch size (`SWATCH_SIZE`, 22 pt). Swatches are now 28 pt apart (22 + 6), the same rhythm as the Recent colours row. The grid is 162 pt wide, and the popup's margins even out.
- While the picker is drawn, `slider_width` is the grid's width, so the picker fills the popup. It's scoped, so nothing else changes.

All `swatch_grid` call sites change together: comment colours, Comment Properties, bookmarks, redaction, form properties, text formatting and the others.

## Tests

In `crates/ui-egui/src/tools/comments/tests.rs`:

- `swatch_grid_columns_match_swatch_size_and_spacing`: neighbouring swatches have a 6 pt gap and a 28 pt pitch, and the first row spans 162 pt. On main the gap is 24 pt and the test fails.
- `the_custom_picker_is_as_wide_as_the_swatch_grid`: with the picker open, Apply sits more than a grid width plus the picker's bars below the swatches, because the picker's square is as tall as it is wide. That's 265 pt with the fix. With the default width it's 203 pt, and the test fails.

title: fix(js): each unit-test thread counts its own document script workers
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js` at the default thread count fails some `session::tests` at random with `document script worker limit reached`. With `--test-threads=1` or `4` everything passes.

The cause is in the tests' isolation, not the product: `crates/js/src/session.rs` caps live document script workers with one process-wide count (16 on 64-bit). Unit tests run as parallel threads of one process, so tests that each start a worker or two reach the cap together, and lingering workers from finished tests (a worker exits after its session drops) add to it.

Under `cfg(test)` each test thread now has its own count, checked against the same `MAX_DOCUMENT_WORKERS`. A `WorkerPermit` remembers the count it was taken from and releases that one, so a detached worker that exits on its own thread still frees its test's slot. Outside tests the count stays the single process-wide static, so the product cap and its behaviour do not change. `document_worker_capacity_is_bounded_and_reusable` still fills the cap, sees the refusal and recovers a slot.

## How you verified it

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js` five times at the default thread count (32 on the test machine):

| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | run 4 | run 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 3 failed | 5 failed | 2 failed | 2 failed | 5 failed |
| this PR | 213 passed | 213 passed | 213 passed | 213 passed | 213 passed |

The failures on `main` were `host_work_reads_globals_in_the_correct_document`, `document_worker_accepts_large_flat_libraries`, `persistent_document_properties_follow_the_current_snapshot`, `timed_out_jobs_never_share_the_next_realm`, `english_retry_is_isolated_and_obeys_the_remaining_time` and `cache_capacity_tests::every_exposed_field_keeps_identity_beyond_4096_entries`, each with the worker-limit error.

title: fix(hayro-syntax): a lone sign in a dictionary or array is unreadable, not a panic
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A dictionary or array item made only of signs crashed or truncated the object parser in the vendored `hayro-syntax`:

- `<< /A + /B 7 >>` and `<< /A ++ /B 7 >>`: `Dict::entries()` panicked on `unwrap()` (`dict.rs:104`), and so did `{:?}` of such a dictionary.
- `[0 + 7]`: `Array::raw_iter()` panicked on `unwrap()`, and `Array::iter::<Object>()` stopped at the `+`, so `7` was silently lost.

The first pass validates a dictionary or array by *skipping* each value, and `Number::skip` accepts a lone `+` or `++`, but `Number::read` reads no number from it (ISO 32000-2 §7.3.3 needs at least one digit). The iterators assumed every skipped value reads.

Vendor patch (46) makes such an item unreadable, like any other malformed value, without touching the number reader:

- `Dict::entries()` and `Dict`'s `Debug` leave the entry out, as `Dict::get` already returned `None` for it. A null value and a missing entry mean the same (§7.3.7).
- `Array::raw_iter()` and `Array::iter::<Object>()` read it as null in its slot (§7.3.9), so the items after it keep their positions. A typed read such as `iter::<f32>()` still ends at it, as it ends at any value of another type.
- The step over the bad item uses the same skip as the first pass and ends the iteration if the skip makes no progress, so it can't loop.

Sign runs that a number *is* read from (a lone `-` reads as 0 on `main`) read as before.

## How you verified it

New `crates/content/tests/hayro_sign_tokens.rs`:

- `a_dictionary_leaves_out_an_entry_made_only_of_signs` and `an_array_reads_a_token_made_only_of_signs_as_null_in_its_slot` over `+`, `++`, `-`, `--`, `+-`, `-+`, `+ -`, `+ +`.
- `short_sign_led_tokens_never_panic_in_a_dictionary_or_array`: a sweep over every sign-led token of up to five characters over `+ - 1 . e` and space (2,592 tokens), each in `[t]`, `[0 t 7]` and `<< /A t /B 7 >>`. It checks for no panic in `entries`, `raw_iter`, `iter` or `Debug`, that `raw_iter` and `iter` agree on the length, …

title: M1: an attachment-only-encrypted document's clear attachments read without the password, and saving an encrypted one asks for it (core.attachment-only-encryption)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

A document whose encrypting crypt filters are all `/AuthEvent /EFOpen` opens without a password (since #6312). ISO 32000-2 §7.6.6, Table 25, `AuthEvent`:
> EFOpen: Authorization shall be required when accessing embedded files.

This PR finishes what such a document does with its attachments.

**An attachment stored in the clear reads without the password.** `attachment_data` read every attachment through lopdf, which can't read the document without its key, so every attachment was refused. An encrypted document's attachments are now read through the document model (`pdfcraft-cos`), which decrypts each stream with the crypt filter that applies to it (§7.4.10, §7.6.6):
- An attachment that no crypt filter encrypts (`/Crypt` with `/Name /Identity`, or no `/EFF` and no `/Crypt` filter of its own) reads without the password.
- One that the `EFOpen` filter encrypts is refused with `ATTACHMENT_NEEDS_PASSWORD`, never with its encrypted bytes.
- With the user or permissions password, both read. lopdf also misread these documents with the password, because it decrypts `/StrF /Identity` strings and the name tree's keys stopped matching.

**Saving or opening an encrypted attachment asks for the password.** In the app, Save attachment and Open in a new tab on such an attachment show the password prompt: "The file attachments of “…” are protected. Enter the password to open them." This follows the user guide's "Encrypt Only File Attachments: Requires a password to open file attachments."
- The right password (user or permissions) unlocks the attachments (`Session::unlock` → `Document::unlock`), and the save or open carries on.
- A wrong password asks again.
- Cancel does nothing.
- From then on the document is read with that password, so its other attachments don't ask again. Unlocking isn't an edit: nothing is marked unsaved.

**The permissions password of an R4 document.** For R2–R4 the renderer authenticates only the user password, so `Session::unlock` gi…

title: M7: a form edit reads the document's fields once (form.fill-text)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Filling one form field read the document's whole field tree (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4: `/Fields`, the kids, inherited attributes, every widget on every page) several times per edit, almost always with nothing changed between two of those readings:

- **AcroForm, 4 walks per value:** `set_value_with` (to fill), `recalculate_values`, the engine's form refresh, and `display_bytes` (field appearances for the view).
- **Laid-out XFA form, 7 walks per value:** the same four, plus the XFA data sync twice (`xfa_field_data`) and the scripts' field table (`field_infos`).

Each walk costs time in proportion to the form: about 4 ms on a 1,000-field form, and 40–55 ms on a public provincial benefits application from the XFA corpus (1,540 fields after layout, tooltips set by its opening scripts). On that form the walks alone were 17.5 s of 29.6 s over 50 interactions.

**Cause.** Tracing every walk during an edit, and comparing the document's `pdfcraft_cos::ReadState` with the one the walk before it read, showed the document unchanged before 5 of the 7 XFA walks and 3 of the 4 AcroForm ones. The steps run one after another on the same state (the refresh, the view, and the next edit's fill all read what the last step left), so each re-read the same fields from scratch.

**Fix.** `fields_with_adopted` (and so `fields`) keeps its last reading on each thread together with the `ReadState` of the document it read, and returns a copy of it to a document that still reads as that state.
- `ReadState` is what cos already offers for this: it changes with every edit, save and unlock, and a clone or an undo snapshot that reads the same has the same state (the engine's text-block cache keys on it too).
- Any change at all reads afresh, so the result is always what a new walk would give. A form edit now walks the fields once, plus once more on an XFA form after its data is written.
- One entry per thread: one form's fields and the changed objects of the document they came from.…

title: fix(hotbar): dragging the floating bar keeps its grip under the pointer
author: jayzed80
body:
Fixes #7021

## Root cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/hotbar.rs:715-725` (on `main`) moved the floating bar by adding each pass's
`grip.drag_delta()`, divided by the travel, to `bar.position`, then clamped it to `0..=1`. Once the
bar reached an edge, any further outward movement was clamped away and forgotten. When the
pointer came back, the bar moved back at once, so the grip was no longer under the pointer.

## Fix

- When a drag starts, `Hotbar` now stores where the pointer pressed the grip, relative to the
  bar's top-left corner (a new `grab` field, marked `#[serde(skip)]`).
- On every dragged pass, the bar's top-left is the pointer minus that offset, clamped to the
  bounds as before.
- The field is cleared when the drag ends.

title: fix(ocr): undoing Edit's automatic text recognition says how to get it back
author: jayzed80
body:
Fixes #6655

## Root cause

When Edit text & images is turned on for a scanned page, `auto_ocr_scanned_page` marks the page as tried (`crates/ui-egui/src/workflows/ocr_ui.rs:460`) and recognizes it as one undoable "Recognize text" step. After that step is undone, `scan_to_read` returns `None` for the page (`crates/ui-egui/src/workflows/ocr_ui.rs:511`), so it is not read again. That part is deliberate. But Undo only said "Undid Recognize text" (`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs`, `history_step`), so the user had no hint that the step they never asked for was gone, or how to get it back.

## Fix

- `DocView` gets `auto_ocr_steps` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`): the undo depths just after each automatic Recognize text step.
- When an OCR result is applied (`poll_ocr`, `ocr_ui.rs`), entries at or above the new depth are dropped (that step replaces them), and an automatic step records its depth. A run that found no words writes no step and records nothing.
- `history_step` (`editing.rs`) checks before Undo whether the step about to be undone is "Recognize text" at a recorded depth. If it is, the notice reads: "Undid Recognize text, which Edit ran on this scanned page. Redo, or Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text, makes its text editable again." Every other Undo or Redo message is unchanged.
- Edit still does not re-run recognition by itself, as the issue asks.

## Tests

- `workflows::ocr_ui::tests::undoing_the_recognition_edit_ran_says_how_to_get_it_back` (unit test, made-up OCR result, so no models are needed). It covers: undoing the automatic step shows the notice; the page is still not read again; Redo restores the text and says "Redid Recognize text"; undoing a manual Recognize text at the same history depth says only "Undid Recognize text"; undoing another step shows no notice.
  - Without the fix (notice branch disabled), it fails with the toast `Undid Recognize text`. With the fix, it passes.
- `ocr::undoing_edits_own_recognition_says_how_to_get_the_text_back` (UI harness…

title: M1: encrypted files open with every password spelling and key length other readers accept, report crypt filter methods they can't decrypt, and read alike in the renderer (core.open-rc4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

The standard security handler (ISO 32000-2 §7.6) turns a typed password and the `/Encrypt` dictionary into a file key. PdfCraft does this twice: the document model (`pdfcraft-crypt` through `pdfcraft-cos`) and the renderer (the vendored `hayro-syntax`). This PR makes both read every encryption dictionary the way qpdf, MuPDF and PDFium read it, reports the crypt filter methods the standard says to report where those readers disagree (11, 12), and makes the two agree with each other on every file and password.

It started from three files of an encrypted-file survey that qpdf opens and PdfCraft read differently (1–3 below). A generated matrix of 579 fixtures, opened 2,277 times by PdfCraft and the three readers, then found the rest (4–10).

**1. A password PDFDocEncoding can hold, written as its UTF-8 bytes (R2–R4).** A synthetic R3 file made with `qpdf --password-mode=bytes` and the user password "pässwört" (ä and ö are 0xE4 and 0xF6 in PDFDocEncoding, which §7.6.4.3.2 Algorithm 2 step a asks for). The document model said "the password is incorrect" while the renderer accepted it, so the file opened read-only with `encrypted: false`. Now the UTF-8 bytes are tried for every password with a non-ASCII character.

**2. R3 with a key shorter than 16 bytes: `/O` made with the short rehash.** [PDFBOX-3276](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-3276) `annots-encrypted.pdf` (V1 R3, 40-bit). §7.6.4.4.2 Algorithm 3 step c rehashes the whole 16-byte digest; this producer rehashed only the first n bytes, and qpdf and MuPDF accept that (the matrix shows they accept only that reading for n < 16). An owner password is now tried with both rehashes, each accepted only when the user password it recovers passes Algorithm 6.

**3. `/V 4` with `/CFM /AESV3` and a 128-bit key.** [PDFBOX-5345](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-5345) `poppler-89422-0.pdf`. Algorithm 1.A (§7.6.3.3) uses the file key directly only for 256-bit keys; this file has 16 bytes…

title: M1: decryption keeps to what the spec encrypts: a page's metadata, a cross-reference stream's /ID, external file streams and a damaged /Encrypt (core.unencrypted-metadata)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Four places where reading an encrypted file decrypted more, or less, than ISO 32000-2 says, found by comparing PdfCraft with qpdf (as a black box) on 286 encrypted files, and a fifth found by reading §7.6.2 against `security.rs`: 257 from the PDFBox JIRA attachments, the pdf.js test PDFs and a scanner corpus, plus 29 synthetic ones.

### 1. `/EncryptMetadata false` covers the document's metadata stream only (ISO 32000-2 §7.6.2, Table 21)

Table 21 gives `EncryptMetadata` for "the document-level metadata stream", and as meaningful only when `/V` is 4 or 5. `security.rs` skipped every `/Type /Metadata` stream, so a page's or an image's XMP, which the producer encrypted, was read as its ciphertext.

That was more than a display problem. Each of these wrote the ciphertext out as if it were the stream's data, and nothing could read it again:

- **Remove Security.** A synthetic qpdf file (`--cleartext-metadata`, owner password, one page-level XMP stream), for both AES-128 and AES-256, came out with its page XMP as 80 bytes of ciphertext and no `/Encrypt`.
- **Changing the security.** The same file under a new AES-256 password: qpdf decrypts the page XMP to the old ciphertext.
- **Save As (full rewrite) with the same password.** In the two corpus files below, after decrypting with qpdf, every page-level XMP stream is garbage: 6 of 6 and 19 of 19.

Now only the stream the catalog's `/Metadata` names stays in the clear, and only with `/V` 4 or 5. Every other metadata stream is decrypted and encrypted like any other stream.

- **Reading** goes by the source's catalog, read when the document is authenticated. Editing the catalog's `/Metadata` doesn't change how the file's streams decrypt.
- **Writing** goes by the catalog as edited, since that is the catalog being written. It tells the stream apart by its number in the source document, because a full save renumbers.
- A `/Metadata` reference counts only when its generation reaches the object.
- Incrementa…

title: Auto-tag Apply tags headings by size and weight (#7062)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Auto-tag Apply now tags headings. Before this change it tagged every text object as `P`, and only the preview could propose an `H1`.

Fixes #7062. Lists follow in #7068.

How a role is chosen, in `crates/a11y/src/autotag_roles.rs`:

- **Body style.** The body is the font size, in half points, that shows the most characters in the document. It is bold when most of those characters are bold. Counting characters rather than text objects keeps a page of short captions from outvoting one long body.
- **Heading candidates.** A candidate is short: at most 3 lines, at most 200 characters, and at least one letter. Page numbers and long passages therefore stay `P`.
- **When a candidate is a heading:**
  - by size, when it is at least 1.15× the body;
  - by weight, when it is bold, at most 2 lines, at least 0.9× the body, and the body is not bold.
- **Levels.** Heading styles are ranked over the whole document, larger first and bold before regular at the same size, and capped at `H6`.
- **No skipped levels.** A level is never more than one below the heading before it, so the checker's `heading-nesting` rule passes on the result.
- **Size and bold.**
  - Size is the font size × the text matrix × the CTM, and `q`/`Q` are tracked.
  - Bold is `Metrics.bold`: the font name, `ForceBold`, or `FontWeight` ≥ 600.
  - Text in render mode 3 or 7 (`Tr 3`, an OCR layer; `Tr 7`, clip only) is not counted.

`AutoTagResult` gains a `headings` count, and `paragraphs` now counts only `P` tags. Mixed content, forms, annotations and existing tags are still refused, exactly as before.

title: fix(hayro-syntax): a dictionary key with no value before >> is left out
author: pakiat
body:
## What this changes

A dictionary key directly followed by `>>`, with no value, made the renderer's whole dictionary unreadable. A PDF editor writes Type 0 fonts like this:

```
<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type0 /BaseFont /XXXXXX+SomeFont /Encoding /Identity-H /DescendantFonts [ 52 0 R ] /ToUnicode>>
```

The font was then lost, and its text was drawn in the fallback font. In a Thai form edited that way, every line written in that font showed as a few stray Latin letters or nothing. Chrome (PDFium) and the editor itself show the form normally, and `pdfcraft-cos` already reads such a key as null (`dict_body`).

Vendored hayro-syntax patch (47), in `object/dict.rs`:

- `parse_dict_with_inner`: a key followed directly by the end tag is left out, as a null value would be (ISO 32000-2 §7.3.7), and the rest of the dictionary is read. The parse counts as repaired, so the dictionary is not put in the shared index cache.
- `Dict::skip`: the same, so such a dictionary inside another one doesn't make the outer one unreadable.
- An inline image dictionary (no `<<`, ending in `ID`) still refuses a key without a value.

`vendor/README.md` records the patch and its test. I numbered it 47 because #7053 proposes 46 in the same file.

## How you verified it

Run locally on Windows:

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render` (682 passed), plus `-p pdfcraft-cos -p pdfcraft-content`

hayro-syntax itself can't be linted or tested from this workspace. `cargo test -p hayro-syntax` refuses because it isn't a member and has dev-dependencies, and a standalone build resolves the unpatched hayro-jbig2. So the test is in pdfcraft-render, like the other hayro-syntax patches.

title: M8: each compatibility level writes the PDF version its encryption needs, and 128-bit RC4 can leave the metadata unencrypted (protect.encryption-level)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Two problems with how password protection is written, and the missing Acrobat 6.0 level, both found by checking the protect settings against ISO 32000-2 and the Acrobat user guide (Securing PDFs with passwords, Password Security settings):

**1. The saved file now declares the PDF version its encryption needs.** Before, a PDF 1.3 file protected at any level was saved as `%PDF-1.5` (the object streams' own version), whatever the encryption. ISO 32000-2 ties each encryption to a version: `/V 2` PDF 1.4 and `/V 4` (crypt filters) PDF 1.5 (Table 20), `/CFM /AESV2` PDF 1.6 (Table 25), and `/V 5` with `/R 6` (AES-256) PDF 2.0 (Table 20, Table 21). The guide lists the same versions for its levels. Now:

| Encryption | Declared version |
|---|---|
| 40-bit RC4 (`/V 1 /R 2`) | 1.3 |
| 128-bit RC4 (`/V 2 /R 3`) | 1.4 |
| 128-bit RC4 through a crypt filter (`/V 4`, `/CFM /V2`) | 1.5 |
| 128-bit AES (`/V 4`, `/CFM /AESV2`) | 1.6 |
| 256-bit AES (`/V 5 /R 6`) | 2.0; a file below 2.0 says `%PDF-1.7` with `/Extensions << /ADBE << /BaseVersion /1.7 /ExtensionLevel 8 >> >>` (§7.12) |

- The version is only ever raised. The header and the catalog `/Version` are read together, and the later one counts (§7.7.2).
- A change of security is always saved in full, so the header carries the new version. A catalog `/Version` below it is raised too, because an extension's `/BaseVersion` may not exceed either one (§7.12.4).
- An existing Adobe extension below level 8 against 1.7 is raised to 8, since levels only grow (§7.12.5). A higher level is kept, and so are other developers' extensions. One against an earlier base version is replaced, never paired with it in an array, because arrays of developer extensions are PDF 2.0 (§7.12.2). One against a later or unreadable base version is left as it is.
- A file that is already PDF 2.0, through its header or its catalog, gets no extension. PDF 2.0 defines `/V 5` itself.

**2. The guide's Acrobat 6.0 level, and unencrypted metada…

title: M10: manual two-sided printing for printers without duplex (#2860)
author: RiceDee
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2860. The spec is in #5407; its optional calibration page is not included.

Manual two-sided printing, for printers that print one side only.
- **Print dialog:** a new **Manual two-sided** option, with long-edge and short-edge flips and **Second side in reverse order**, which starts ticked. Print sends the fronts one-sided, then a window says how to put the stack back. **Continue** sends the backs; **Cancel** stops.

title: feat(print): add batch printing for open documents and folders
author: bagamyanaleks
body:
## What this changes

Adds a **Batch Print** feature allowing users to print multiple PDF documents sequentially with a unified print management dialog.

### Key Changes
- **Command & Shortcut:** Registered `print.batch` ("Batch print…", `Ctrl+Shift+P`) in the File menu.
- **Document Selection:**
  - Add all currently open tabs (`All open documents`).
  - Scan and select an entire folder of PDFs (`Add folder…`) using `pdfcraft_render::inspect` to read page counts and dimensions without polluting the active workspace.
  - Per-item checkboxes, "Select all", "Deselect all", "Clear list", and individual item removal.
- **Multi-Document Preview Aggregation:**
  - Aggregates page sizes and labels across all selected documents into `all_sizes` and `all_labels`.
  - Preview displays combined sheet counts (`Sheet 1 of Total`) and full page ranges (`Pages 1-Total`).
  - Implements live thumbnail rendering via `PageRenderer` so each sheet displays its actual rendered content and layout.

title: fix(render): a rebuilt table finds an object glued to the endobj before it (hayro-syntax patch 46, #7082)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #7082

## What was wrong

Some writers glue an object header to the `endobj` before it: `...endobj5 0 obj`. Microsoft Print To PDF does this for the `/Type0` font dictionaries in the issue. When the cross-reference table has to be rebuilt by scanning the file, two readers lost such an object.

- **hayro-syntax (the renderer):** `fallback_xref_map_inner` only tries an object header when the scan is on a digit. On `e` it skips the whole token `endobj5`, then reads the `0 obj` left over as **object 0**, a well-formed header in front of a well-formed dictionary. Object 5 never enters the rebuilt table, `/F1 5 0 R` resolves to nothing, and the page draws blank and gives no text. This is the issue's analysis, and I confirmed it in the code.
- **pdfcraft-cos (the document model):** `object_headers` accepts a header only after white space or `>`. It doesn't invent an object 0, but it loses object 5 the same way. A file whose table can't be used at all therefore opened with no pages and couldn't be saved.

## What changed

- **`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/xref.rs` (patch 46):** when the scan sits on `endobj` followed directly by a digit, it steps over the 6 bytes of `endobj` only, so the next pass reads the glued header. Every other token is skipped as before. The patch is marked `PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (46))` and added to the hayro-syntax row of `vendor/README.md`, with its tests.
- **`crates/cos/src/document/reader.rs`:** `object_headers` also accepts a header that starts right after `endobj`.

## QA report

The inputs are the three PDFs from the issue's gist (`01-valid`, `02-repair-only`, `03-repair-glued-header`), decoded from their base64. I didn't run the gist's `make_repro.py`. Both CLIs are debug builds: main is `origin/main` `d749fd806`, and the branch is `d887d8071`.

title: fix(xfa): an edit to one copy of a global field reaches every copy
author: jayzed80
body:
Part of #5485

## What was wrong

When a field has `<bind match="global"/>`, every copy is meant to show one shared value (XFA 3.3 p. 87 and p. 176). Copies on a master page (`pageArea`) already bind to one data node: `page_area_index` in `crates/xfa/src/data/path.rs:118` gives every copy instance 0, so on opening they all show what the data holds. Editing broke that:

- `Edit::SetFieldValue` (`crates/engine/src/edit/run.rs:739-749`) writes only the widget that was typed into. The other copies keep their old value on screen.
- After every form edit, `xfa_sync_datasets` (`crates/engine/src/xfa_form.rs:57-68`, called from `crates/engine/src/session/editing.rs:250` and `:296`, and again on save in `session/save.rs:86`) writes **every** field's value into the datasets. All the copies share one data path, so they compete for one node, and an unchanged copy wins. The data keeps the old value, and after reopening every copy shows it. The edit is lost, and nothing reports it. This is wireless89's `GLOBAL_VALUE` / `GLOBAL_CHANGED` case from #5368.
- With no data yet, nothing ever reaches the blank copies.

Script-driven changes already reach every widget bound to the node (`Runner::set_value` in `crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`). Only user edits missed the copies.

## The fix

- `crates/xfa/src/data/path.rs`: new `binds_shared_data(tpl, som)` tells whether the field at a SOM path shares its data node (`match="global"` or an explicit `bind ref`, the same `data_shared` flag `page_area_index` already uses), for page-area and body fields alike. New `has_shared_bindings(tpl)` lets forms without any such field skip the work. The page-area walk moves into `page_area_object`, which both use; `page_area_index` behaves as before.
- `crates/engine/src/xfa_form.rs`: new `xfa_share_bound_values`. It takes the fields an edit changed. For each one that shares a data node with other fields (same `data_path`, both shared), it writes that value into the node, then gives every other copy the value t…

title: M8: redaction looks a form's names up in its caller's resources where its own lack them
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

A form XObject with resources of its own was walked by redaction with those alone. The app's renderer, like Poppler, looks a name the form's resources lack up in the resources of the content that draws it (hayro-syntax `Resources::for_form`). So:

- **An image under a mark stayed.** A form whose `/Resources` lack `/Im1` draws the page's `/Im1` under the mark. The walk found no `/Im1`, left the `Do` as it was, and Apply reported success. The image stayed in the file, still drawn under the mark.
- **Text was placed with the wrong font.** Text such a form shows with a font only the page's resources give was placed with fallback metrics, so text under the mark could be taken for text beside it.
- **Paint beside a mark was lost.** A page pattern such a form paints with was never passed to the page, so the page pruned it, and the form's paint beside the mark went with it.

On `main` since a form's own resources were first read alone; found in review of #7006.

**Now** the walk, the proof's readers of forms (`Geo::form` in `verify/geometry.rs`, `Extractor::stream` in `verify/extract.rs`) and its image search (`Geo::has_image`, through the names as given, below) look a form's names up as the renderer does (`form_resources`):
- **The form's own resources first**, where they give the name as what its category holds: a stream for an XObject, a dictionary (not a stream) for a font or a graphics state, anything the file defines for a pattern. These are the names redaction looks up. It doesn't look colour spaces or shadings up by name (`cs` keeps a pattern for `/Pattern` alone, and `sh` is clipped as it stands), so those stay the form's own.

- **Marked-content properties** are the form's own where it has resources. A form without them reads the page's (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.3), as the renderer does, not its caller's, and one whose `/Resources` is present but no dictionary (`null` or a reference to nothing amo…

title: fix(view): arrows and wheel turn spreads again after End in two-page view
author: jayzed80
body:
Fixes #7087

## Root cause

In two-page view one spread at a time, the frame records whether the view is at its top or bottom edge in `single_edges`, keyed by the first page drawn: the left page of the spread (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:3475`, from `shown_row` at `canvas.rs:2962`).

↑ / ↓ only turn the spread when that record's page equals `view.current` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas/navigation.rs:561` before this change), and the wheel at an edge makes the same check (`navigation.rs:316`). End (`go_to_end`, `navigation.rs:116`) makes the last page current. Without a cover page and with an even page count, or with a cover page and an odd page count, that is the right-hand page of the last spread. So the two pages never matched and ↑ / ↓ did nothing. ← / → and Home still worked because they don't use the edge record, which matches the report.

## Fix

A new `DocView::shown_first()` in `navigation.rs` returns the page the edge record is kept for: in two-page view, the first page of the current page's spread (the existing `spread_first`); otherwise, the current page. Both the arrow-key check and the wheel-edge check now compare against it. `current` itself is unchanged, so the page box, view history and links still point at the page the user went to.

## Tests (each fails on main, passes with the fix)

- `viewer::up_and_down_still_turn_spreads_after_end` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/it/viewer.rs`): two-page view, not scrolling, fit page. One case is 4 pages with the cover off; the other is 5 pages with the cover on. Each presses End, then ↑ (goes back a spread), ↓ (comes forward), End again, ↓ at the end (stays), and ↑ (still turns).
  - Without the fix, cover off: `↑ goes back a spread (cover false)`, left 3, right 0.
  - Without the fix, cover on (run first): left 4, right 1.
- `view::two_page_wheel_at_the_top_edge_turns_back_after_end` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/it/view.rs`): 3 pages, two-page view, cover on, zoom 200%. After End, the wheel pans up and then must turn back to…

title: ci: lock workflow actions through an actions.lock lockfile
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Applies the lockfile setup from https://hugovk.dev/blog/2026/lock-github-actions/.

- `gh actions-lock` replaces the hand-maintained commit SHAs with tag refs such as `actions/checkout@v7.0.1`, and generates `.github/workflows/actions.lock` recording the commit each ref resolves to. A moved tag now shows up as a lockfile diff instead of silently running new code.
- Scopes `githubactions:S7637` off for `.github/workflows/**`, because that rule wants an inline commit SHA per action and does not read `actions.lock`. Sonar confirmed the limitation and tracks lockfile support: https://community.sonarsource.com/t/githubactions-s7637-false-positives-for-actions-pinned-through-native-actions-lock/190814. Verified on storytold/craft-common-actions#220, where the quality gate went green with this exact `resourceKey`.

After editing a workflow, re-run `gh actions-lock` and commit the lockfile with it.
