title: feat(organize, ui): add split pages feature to slice pages into multiple parts
author: Jithuaswin
body:
### Summary
Adds the ability to split single PDF pages into multiple sub-pages (e.g. 2-up booklet/magazine scans into individual pages, horizontal splits, 2×2 grid, or custom ratios).

### Details
- **Coordinate mapping**: Computes sub-page bounding boxes with full visual rotation awareness (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°) so that a visual vertical split cuts down the visible center on all pages regardless of orientation.
- **Dictionary sharing**: Sub-pages clone page dictionaries while sharing existing `/Contents` and `/Resources`, adjusting `MediaBox` and `CropBox` with zero file bloat.
- **Annotations**: Annotations and link areas are partitioned into the sub-page slices they intersect.
- **Undo / Redo**: Integrated with `Edit::SplitPages` in `pdfcraft-engine` with localized undo/redo labels.
- **UI**: Added a modal dialog accessible from the Organize sidebar ("Split pages" under Page Options), thumbnail context menu ("Split pages into parts…"), and top menu (`Pages > Split pages…`).
- **Headless automation**: Supported via the `page_split_parts` tool.
- **Testing**: Added unit tests in `crates/organize` and integration tests in `crates/automation/tests/it/split_pages.rs`. All tests pass cleanly and `cargo clippy` has 0 warnings.

title: fix(measure): read compound and fractional measurement number formats (ISO 32000-2 12.9.2)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Read compound (feet and inches) and fractional or truncated measurement number formats (ISO 32000-2 §12.9.2) instead of refusing them. Measuring inside an Acrobat-calibrated architectural viewport now works, and such saved measurements list with correct labels. Addresses the "compound (ft-in) and fractional formats" gap in `comment.measure-scale` / `comment.measure-distance`.

## What this changes

- **Before:** `Scale::read` refused any number format array of more than one unit, and `F /F` or `F /T` (`crates/measure/src/lib.rs` on main, 183-209).
  - `measure_distance` and the Measure tool failed inside such a viewport.
  - `list` put such annotations under `unsupported`.
- **New module:** `crates/measure/src/number_format.rs` reads number format dictionaries and formats a value with them. It reads `U`, `C`, `F`, `D`, `FD`, `RT`, `RD`, `PS`, `SS` and `O`, with their spec defaults.
  - Every element but the last shows whole units.
  - The last element shows the remainder in one of four ways: decimals to 1/D (low-order zeros dropped unless `FD`), a fraction in Dths (reduced unless `FD`), rounded (`R`), or cut off (`T`).
  - A last unit that rounds up carries into the unit before it ("1 ft 0 in", not "0 ft 12 in"). Carries only pass through whole conversion factors.
- **New `Scale.formats: Option<Formats>`:** set only when a scale is not single-unit decimal or rounded.
  - Readings are labelled with it, e.g. `3 ft 6 1/2 in`.
  - A measurement added with such a scale writes the arrays back. The first unit carries the scale's own label and factor.
  - A compound `Y` keeps its own units and its `CYX`.
- **Unchanged:** single-unit decimal and rounded scales (everything PdfCraft itself writes) read, label and serialize exactly as before. `formats` is `None` for them and is skipped in JSON.

title: fix(a11y): tag tools follow an MCR's /Stm into the form XObject
author: jayzed80
body:
Fixes #3221

## Root cause

A structure element can own marked content inside a form XObject through a marked-content reference (MCR) whose `/Stm` names the form (ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.1). The form numbers its MCIDs on its own, so MCID 0 in the form and MCID 0 on the page are different content.

The tag tools read only the MCR's `/MCID` and dropped `/Stm`:

- `crates/a11y/src/alt.rs:138` (`mcids`) returned bare MCIDs. `mark_decorative` (`alt.rs:518`) and `mark_tag_artifact` (`alt.rs:557`) then rewrote the **page's** `BDC` with that MCID and cleared the **page's** `/StructParents` parent-tree entry.
- `alt.rs:245` (`content_bboxes`) looked the MCID up in the page content, so `figures` reported the page figure's rectangle for the form figure.
- `crates/a11y/src/tags.rs:241` (`direct_marks`) kept `(Pg, MCID)` and dropped `/Stm`, so `tag_content` read the page's text for that MCID.

## The fix

- Marked content is carried as `(stream, MCID)` (`ContentRef` in `alt.rs`). `stream` is `None` for the page's own content. An `/Stm` that names one of the page's own `/Contents` streams counts as page content. An `/Stm` that isn't a reference is never matched, so it can't be taken for page content.
- **Figure bounds:** `content_bboxes` follows each form's `Do` with the form's `/Matrix` and the CTM at the `Do`, including forms nested in forms. Forms are entered only when some wanted content is in a form, so pages without forms take exactly the old path. The walk is bounded: depth 16, a cycle check for a form that draws itself, and the page's `DecodeBudget` (bytes and form entries).
- **Tag content:** `TagContentItem` gains `stream: Option<ObjRef>`. Text for form content is read from the form, using its `/Resources` or the page's when it has none. `accessibility_tag_content` now returns `stream` (`{object, generation}` or null).
- **Decorative / mark as artifact:** each form's rewrite is planned first, without changing the document. A form that lacks the content (for `mark_tag_artifa…

title: Redraw a page after an appearance-only field edit
author: GitVex
body:
## What this changes

A Field Properties edit that changes only a field's appearance — border colour, fill, line width, border style, or a check box's mark — leaves the page drawn as it was. The new appearance stream is correct, and a zoom or scroll forces a fresh raster and it appears, but nothing marks the page stale at commit time, so the field looks unchanged until the view happens to re-raster for some other reason. Setting a push button's icon has the same blind spot.

`form_edit_pages` decides which pages to redraw by comparing the form state before and after the edit. `FormField` and `Widget` carry none of those properties — no border, fill, width, style, nor a widget's own `/DA` — and a button's image is not in the model either, so an edit that changes one of them leaves the two states comparing equal and no page is marked.

The edit now says so itself: `appearance_edit_field` names the field an edit restyles, and that field's pages are marked changed whatever the comparison says. Writing it as one rule rather than a case per edit kind is deliberate — the general statement is that any form edit whose appearance effect the model cannot express must mark its field's pages, and `SetFieldProps`, `SetFieldImage` and `SetFieldImageTarget` all meet it.

The `unbaked` overlay is left exactly as it was, gated on the plain value changing.

## How you verified it

Per crate, on Windows:

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib` — 1002 passed
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test it` — 1885 passed, 3 failed

Those three fail identically with this change stashed, on an untouched `main`, so they are this machine rather than this PR:

- `comments::the_selection_bar_stays_inside_the_pages_area` — `"language must be one of auto, en"`; this checkout has no craft-i18n, so only `en` is built in.

title: fix(engine,xfa): run a static XFA form's template scripts (#7124)
author: stmmqtt731
body:
## What this changes

Part of #7124 (1 of 3, as planned in the issue).

A static XFA form, as LiveCycle Designer saves one, keeps its AcroForm, and its logic lives in the XFA template: FormCalc or JavaScript `calculate`, `exit` and `validate` scripts. PdfCraft loaded the template for scripting only when the form carried the `/PCXfaLayout` mark of its own layout, which a static form never has. So none of these scripts ran: totals stayed empty, and exit scripts did nothing.

With this PR:

- **The template is loaded for static forms too**, on open (`open.rs`) and after edits (`sync_xfa_state`), while the form keeps its XFA. Opening runs `initialize`, `layout:ready` and `calculate` scripts as for a laid-out form; a fill runs the field's `change`, `exit` and `validate` scripts and the calculations. A dynamic form that could not be laid out still runs none.
- **Fields are matched by their AcroForm names.** Designer names each field by its SOM path (`form1[0].page1[0].total[0]`), with `#subform[n]` for an unnamed subform, which has no part in the path. The runner maps a field only when that path is a field of the live form; a path two fields share is left out, so a script never writes to the wrong one.
- **The pages are never laid out again.** A static form's pages are the form, and laying it out from the template would replace them. Effects that need a new layout (presence, access, adding or removing instances) are skipped with a console note naming the object. `relayout` only writes the pending values.
- **Data import keeps its behaviour:** fields the imported data no longer holds are still emptied on a static form, now that it has a template.
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml` (`form.xfa-static`) and `crates/xfa/README.md` say what runs and what is still missing.

title: fix(ui): open the JavaScript console in an independent desktop window
author: sebsca
body:
## What this changes

Opening the JavaScript console previously occupied the document's modal dialog slot, blocking page input and replacing an existing dialog. On desktop it now opens in an independent native window, so the document remains usable and other dialogs stay open. Reopening restores and focuses the console; closing it preserves document dialogs. Its header identifies the active document, and its contents scroll at the minimum window size.

Console scripts commit pending form typing before reading or editing the document. Rejected input stops execution, and blank scripts leave the draft alone. If committing a field opens a prompt, the console script waits and the native document window is restored and focused. The Run button and execution guard share a modal check that exempts only the web console's own dialog; link, password and other prompts still block execution even beside that dialog.

The opt-in UI control channel exposes `ui.set` with key `js-console`, value `open` or `closed`, and `ui.state.js_console_open`. Console visibility participates in the input-target identity, discarding stale synthetic-input requests that have not started while allowing started requests to finish. The legacy `dialog=js-console` opener remains supported. The scripts-off notice uses the same opener, and frame-panic recovery closes the independent console.

The web console stays modal. Native backends without multiple-viewport support embed a movable window. Console-requested alerts and document dialogs bring the document window forward.

Validation below covers commit `462b13ee7` on Linux, using the catalogs pinned by `craft-i18n.rev` (`575cfdef63227b14daf173b8cc87928bfdfa325e`) through `CRAFT_I18N_DIR`, without the optional `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` input. The committed source was checked against the tested snapshot.

title: fix(startup): an OPENSSL_ia32cap naming a missing CPU feature no longer stops PdfCraft (#2916)
author: FredApps
body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft no longer stops at launch when an `OPENSSL_ia32cap` environment variable asks for a CPU feature the processor doesn't have.

aws-lc, the cryptography library behind digital signatures and TLS (through aws-lc-rs), reads `OPENSSL_ia32cap` when it detects the CPU's features on x86. For a feature the CPU lacks, it prints `Fatal Error: HW capability found: …, but HW capability requested: …` and calls `abort()`. On Windows that ran in a static initializer before `main`: exit code `0xC0000409`, no window, nothing in `pdfcraft.log`. Tuning guides and other programs leave the variable set for every program, so on those PCs PdfCraft (app and CLI) never started while the other Craft apps did. #2916 was this (closed once the reporter removed the variable). A user on Discord reports the same symptom on Windows 11 today; that cause isn't confirmed for them yet.

Three parts, because each alone fails:

1. **`.cargo/config.toml`** builds aws-lc with `BORINGSSL_NO_STATIC_INITIALIZER` (`AWS_LC_SYS_CFLAGS`, which both aws-lc-sys builders read). aws-lc then detects the CPU when `CRYPTO_library_init` is called instead of before `main`. FIPS builds of aws-lc always work this way.
2. **`pdfcraft_platform::crypto_env::run_without_cpu_override`**, the first thing in both executables' `main`: when the variable is set (x86, not macOS), it runs the same executable again with the same arguments and standard streams but without the variable, and exits with its code. Removing the variable in-process wouldn't work: aws-lc reads it through the C runtime's `getenv`, whose copy of the environment `std::env::remove_var` doesn't change on Windows, and the workspace forbids `unsafe`. The app logs a warning naming the value it dropped.
3. **`pdfcraft_sign::init_crypto`**, called next in both `main`s, runs aws-lc's CPU detection at start as the static initializer did. aws-lc-rs asks for it before most operations but not all: in a test build with the flag and without this cal…

author: indy2kro
body:
Fixes #7123

## What this changes

With a drawn annotation (or any comment) selected, Edit ▸ Copy is now enabled, and Edit ▸ Paste is enabled once comments have been copied, matching ⌘C / ⌘V.

**Root cause.** `run_menu_command` already sends the clipboard items as their keys (`menus.rs:561`: Copy pushes `Event::Copy`, Paste requests a paste), and `clipboard_keys` handles those by copying the selected comments when no text is selected and by pasting copied XFDF onto the canvas. - Copy follows `comment.copy` when a comment is selected and no text is. Selected text is what ⌘C copies first, so it is left to the existing text rule.
- Paste follows `comment.paste` when the comment clipboard holds something, outside Organize and Prepare Form, where the canvas does not take pastes.

title: fix(ui): split view's active-pane line is drawn under open menus (#7010)
author: indy2kro
body:
Fixes #7010

## What this changes

In split view, the accent line marking the active pane no longer draws on top of open menus. The menus from the menu bar, tab menus and other popups now cover it.

**Root cause.** The line was painted with `ctx.layer_painter` on a layer of its own at `Order::Foreground`. That is the order egui menus and popups use, but no `Area` owns the layer. egui's `GraphicLayers::drain` draws layers that are missing from the area order after every area of the same order. So the line was painted after the open menu, across it.

**Fix.** The line is now painted on the pane's own layer (`child.painter()`, `crates/ui-egui/src/panes.rs:623`), after the pane's pages. It stays over the pages and sits under every menu, popup and floating bar. Simply lowering it to `Order::Middle` would not do: it would still be a layer with no area, drawn after the `Middle`-order floating toolbar, find bar and camera bar.

title: fix(fonts): accept fonts released under the GUST Font License
author: stettberger
body:
## What this changes

`validate()` refused every font that has the Preview & Print bit (0x0004) set in OS/2
`fsType`, even when the Editable bit (0x0008) is set too. Fonts in the wild do set several of
bits 1–3. Most TeX Gyre faces (Heros, Termes, Bonum, Cursor, Schola, the Math fonts) and Latin
Modern carry `0x000C`, so they can't complete a source subset or be loaded with *Load font…*,
even though their authors mark them editable.

`permits_editable_embedding()` now applies the OpenType rule:

- For OS/2 versions 0–2 the spec says the least restrictive of several set bits takes
  precedence. For Restricted it says the sub-field must be exactly 2 for it to take effect.
  So Editable wins over Preview & Print and Restricted.
- Restricted alone (0x0002), Preview & Print alone (0x0004), both without Editable (0x0006),
  and Bitmap-only (0x0200, also with Editable) are still refused.
- No-subsetting (0x0100) stays allowed: PdfCraft embeds the full program anyway.

Refs #2077. On its own this doesn't make TeX Gyre usable, because its licence is not
recognised either. That is <PR-B>, which is independent of this PR.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-fonts --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts`: 157 passed

New test `embedding::tests::several_embedding_bits_resolve_to_the_least_restrictive` patches
`fsType` of the bundled Inter in memory and checks 0x000C, 0x000A, 0x0000, 0x0008 and 0x0108
are accepted and 0x0002, 0x0004, 0x0006, 0x0200 and 0x0208 are refused. With the old check

title: fix(fonts): several fsType embedding bits resolve to the least restri…
author: stettberger
body:
## What this changes

`validate_document_input()` only accepts a font whose licence record (name ID 13) names an
open licence. The TeX Gyre and Latin Modern families, the standard free fonts of every TeX
distribution, have no licence record. They declare their licence in the copyright notice
(name ID 0): "This work is released under the GUST Font License -- see
http://tug.org/fonts/licenses/GUST-FONT-LICENSE.txt". So *Load font…* and the installed-font
scan refuse them, and a PDF set in TeX Gyre can't be edited in its own typeface.

This accepts the GUST Font License from the licence record, or from the copyright notice where
these families declare it. Only the GUST licence is read from the copyright notice; every other
licence still needs name ID 13, and every other check (excluded families, Adobe-authored
fonts, `fsType`) is unchanged.

**Licensing decision needed.** GUST is not on the licence allowlist in `AGENTS.md`, so
this is for a maintainer to decide, and I'm happy to change or drop it. My reasoning:

- The GUST Font License is the LPPL 1.3c plus a request, not a legal requirement, to
  rename modified fonts. It is a free licence: Debian ships these fonts in main.
- As in #2077, this check is about a font the user picks from their own machine and embeds in
  their own PDF. PdfCraft doesn't bundle or ship it, so the project's asset allowlist isn't
  directly at stake.

Refs #2077. TeX Gyre also needs #7149 (`fsType` 0x000C); the two PRs are independent and
touch the same test module, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: ocr: return the file check in program_is_executable, for clippy 1.100
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #7145.

The Windows gate on `main` (be9fe433c) fails at clippy because of a lint new in Rust 1.100: "this `if` guard returns a bool literal and is followed by another", at `crates/ocr/src/tesseract.rs:133`. On non-Unix targets `program_is_executable` was `if !abs || !file { return false; } true`. It now computes `is_file` once and returns it, and on Unix it returns `is_file && <the executable-bits check>`. Behaviour is the same on both: the metadata check still runs only for an absolute path to a file.

The Linux and macOS jobs never saw the lint, because there the `#[cfg(unix)]` block follows the `if`.

## How you verified it

Windows, Rust 1.100.0:

- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings`, the clippy command `xtask ci` runs, plus `--keep-going`, passes with this change. On Windows that was the only error.
- [x] With the change reverted, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ocr --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails with the error CI reports. It passes again with the change restored.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-ocr` passes.
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ocr` passes (92 tests, Rust 1.99.1).

I did not run the Unix side locally. The Unix branch now evaluates `is_file && …`, which short-circuits the same way the early return did. CI covers it.

There's no new test, because nothing new is tested: this is a lint fix with no behaviour change, and the existing `program_is_executable` tests still pass.

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!`, no indexing, no `unsafe`.

Rust 1.100 is now stable, so any CI job that takes the latest stable will hit this lint.

title: fix(xfa): the script's node is in scope, and app.plugIns
author: hikashop-nicolas
body:
## What this changes

In Acrobat an XFA event script runs with its node in scope: `parent`, `rawValue`, `caption` and the node's other members can be read and written without `this.`. Forms rely on it (`globalSO.root = parent.parent;`, `this.rawValue = "INDIF" + (parent.instanceIndex + 1);`, `caption.value.text.value`), and here each such line threw `ReferenceError: parent is not defined`. The review's breakdown on #4948 counts 265 such errors in 12 forms ("node member read without `this.`").

- After the names in scope are set up, `install` defines a getter and setter on the global object for each of the node's members in `SCOPE_MEMBERS` that no name in scope already has. Reading one reads `this.<member>`, and writing one writes it. `resolveNode` and the `exec*` methods are bound to the node.
- The list leaves out the names a script would use for a variable of its own (`name`, `index`, `value`, `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`). A child named like a member still comes first, and a variable the script declares still hides the member.
- `app.plugIns` is an empty array, for forms that test `app.plugIns.toString().indexOf("ADBE")` before anything else.

- New test `a_scripts_node_members_are_read_without_this`: reads and a write without `this.`, a declared variable hiding the member, a child named like a member coming first, and `app.plugIns`. On `main` without the change it fails with `ReferenceError: parent is not defined`.

title: feat(xfa): choice list methods read and change the run's item lists
author: hikashop-nicolas
body:
## What this changes

A choice list's methods were not there (XFA 3.3 p. 392 names `addItem` and points to Adobe's scripting reference for them), so a call threw and the script stopped (#5009, Series 1: "Choice-list methods", 153 forms). This adds them, using the hook `HNode::items` that `props` left for them:

- `getDisplayItem(i)` and `getSaveItem(i)`: what entry `i` shows and saves, or `null`.
- `boundItem(text)`: what the entry showing `text` saves; text no entry shows comes back as it is.
- `clearItems()`, `addItem(shown[, saved])`, `deleteItem(i)` (whether there was one), and `setItems("a,b,c")` or `setItems("shown1,saved1,shown2,saved2", 2)` (`false`, with the list unchanged, when the texts don't make whole pairs).
- `length` (the entries a choice list shows) and `selectedIndex` (the entry the value is, by what it saves, else what it shows, or -1). Fields that aren't choice lists keep reading `length` as `undefined`.

The changing methods work on the run's copy of the lists (`HNode::items`), made from the template's the first time one is called. Everything the script reads afterwards follows it: `boundItem`, `length`, `items.nodes`, `getElement('items', 1)`. The saved list is the one the template marks `save="1"`. On a list with one `<items>`, an `addItem` whose saved value differs from its text adds a saved list.

What a script changes stays in the run: the list on the page, and what the save keeps, follow #7063's property changes taking effect. Once that lands, the list state can be handed to it.

Bounds: a list holds at most 10,000 entries from scripts, and each text is charged against the script's payload (`XHost::room`). Each `addItem` and `deleteItem` changes the list in place, so a loop filling a list is linear.

Part of #5009.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-js` (214 passed).
- New test `choice_list_methods_read_and_change_the_items` (`props_tests`): each method on a list with shown and saved items, a list with one list of items, a …

title: Print: poster tile labels (page, row and column on each sheet)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Poster printing (Print ▸ Poster) can now label each tile, like Acrobat's Poster Labels option, so the sheets can be put back together. The label here is the page, row and column only: every sheet carries a line such as `Page 2: row 1 of 2, column 2 of 2` in the margin above the tile. The parity entry said "labels pending".

- `Layout::Poster` gains `labels` (off by default, so existing posters print as before).
- The label is drawn as Helvetica (standard 14, WinAnsi) text in the 18 pt margin above the tile, between the corners' cut marks, at 7 pt, or smaller when the line would not fit a narrow sheet; a sheet too narrow for a 3 pt label gets none. It goes through a new `Sheet::texts`, written by `impose` with a sheet-level `/Font` resource only when a sheet has text.
- Headless: `doc_print` takes `labels` (boolean) with `layout: "poster"`.
- Print dialog: a Tile labels checkbox next to Cut marks (two new `tl!` strings). Catalogs live in craft-i18n; until it has entries for them they show in English, and I can open the craft-i18n change after this one lands. The preview draws the labels too, where they print, in the dialog's own font rather than Helvetica, so it is approximate.
- The printed label itself stays English and names no file or date: print output has no i18n today, and the label has to be readable by whoever tapes the sheets together, not only the person who printed it. Text that a standard 14 font can't draw prints as `?`. (The label is built from numbers only, so this is a guard, not a path in use.)

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

title: Print: printer's marks and bleed on the printed sheets (doc_print marks)
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Acrobat's Print ▸ Marks and Bleeds puts trim and bleed marks, registration targets, colour bars and a page information line around each printed page without changing the document. PdfCraft had the edit-time half (Add printer marks, `doc_printer_marks`), which changes the document; the print-time half was `planned`.

- `Session::print_pdf_marked(id, settings, marks)` prints as `print_pdf` does, and with marks it runs the existing `pdfcraft_edit::add_printer_marks` on the cloned print copy before `impose`. The document's bytes and its dirty flag are untouched.
- Marks the document already carries are replaced on the copy (`replace: true`), so a page never prints two sets.
- The page is widened for the marks exactly as Add printer marks widens it, so `fit` shrinks it to make room and `actual` prints it at size with the marks around it.
- Marks need the pages to print as they are, so they are refused with a print as pictures (Print as image or app-managed colour; a document that allows only low-resolution printing takes the same path, which the tests don't cover), with an error saying so.
- Headless: `doc_print` takes `marks` (a list of `all`, `trim`, `bleed`, `registration`, `color_bars`, `page_info`) and `marks_weight` (0.1 to 4 pt, default 0.25; both in the schema with bounds). The information line carries the open document's name (as `doc_info` shows it, not its path), the page number and today's date. They go with a one-page-a-sheet layout (fit, actual, shrink, custom). `marks_weight` without `marks`, an unknown name, an empty list, a multi-page, booklet or poster layout, `as_image`, `color_management: "app"` and `area` are refused as invalid arguments.
- `print_pdf` is unchanged: it calls `print_pdf_marked` with `None`.

No Print dialog panel yet: this PR is the engine and tool half. The parity entry is `partial` and says so.

title: fix(save): ask for an extended attribute's size with rustix's query (#7050)
author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #7050. Refs #7133 (likely the same bug; its report doesn't show the full error yet).

Since 0.21.0, every in-place save on macOS over a file that carries an extended attribute fails with "could not preserve the file's extended attributes; save a copy with Save As: Result too large (os error 34)". That covers files with Finder tags, downloaded files with `com.apple.quarantine`, and files with an Open With setting.

The cause is #6967's bump of rustix from 1.1.5 to 1.1.6. In 1.1.6, `getxattr`/`fgetxattr`/`lgetxattr` with an empty buffer return 0 instead of the attribute's size, and the size query moved to its own functions (`getxattr_query`, `fgetxattr_query`, `lgetxattr_query`). `preserve_target_xattrs` asked for the size with `&mut []`, got 0, allocated a 1-byte buffer, and the real read failed with `ERANGE`. 0.20.0 was built with 1.1.5, which matches what people report in #7050.

The change:
- `platform/src/staging.rs`: the size query and the after-read size check use `fgetxattr_query`.
- `ui-egui/src/platform/macos_association.rs`: the opening-metadata reader asks for the size with `lgetxattr_query`.
- Tests: the staging tests' own size queries use the query functions. Two tests (`oversized_binding_skips_repair_but_is_preserved_by_the_shared_writer`, `a_large_binding_does_not_block_a_document_save`) read back a 65,537-byte value with the `xattr` crate, which has the same problem under rustix 1.1.6: its size query returns 0, so a value over its 4 KiB first try comes back empty. They now check the size with `getxattr_query`. `xattr` is a dev-dependency only.

No other code in the workspace calls these functions with an empty buffer (`git grep getxattr`).

Also, as a separate commit: `home_recent_context_menu_reveals_the_target_without_opening_or_removing_it` (from #5559) read the reveal notice three frames after the click, but Reveal now runs off the UI thread, so on a loaded runner it failed (FreeBSD on this PR, and FreeBSD on main). It …

title: M7: edit legacy Thai subsets by their glyph layout, not their font name
author: xullul
body:
## What this changes

Edit text keeps Thai in a PDF's own embedded subset when that subset uses the legacy positional Thai glyph layout, whatever the font is called. Until now the editor only took that path for fonts named `THSarabunPSK`. Faces that share the same layout, such as TH SarabunIT๙, were refused with "complex text in … needs its complete source TrueType/OpenType font", even when the subset held every glyph the new text needed.

The check now reads the font program and the PDF's own maps instead of the name:

- `LegacyThaiFont::from_pdf` accepts a subset when every Thai character its ToUnicode maps sits at its legacy glyph (U+0E01–U+0E3A at 214–271, U+0E3F–U+0E5B at 272–298), or at an alternate slot for a mark, ฐ or ญ (342–368). A subset with its own Thai mark positioning (GPOS) is shaped by that layout, as before.
- `composite_glyph_maps` restores the Windows PUA alternates under the same order test. The existing checks still apply: ก at 214 and อ at 258, each kept alternate advancing as its form does, and agreeing with what the ToUnicode says it is.
- `embedded_sfnt_within` rebuilds the editor-only cmap for an Identity-H subset whose own cmap lacks Thai the ToUnicode maps, instead of keying that on the name. It reads only the ToUnicode for this, against the caller's allowance, and lists no copy when that read is refused.
- `legacy_thai_font` and `shape_source` drop their name checks.
- `shape_source` gives a Thai span that also holds other text needing shaping (Arabic joining, Indic reordering, combining marks) to a program that shapes it whole before the subset's existing codes, which encode every non-Thai character on its own. The existing codes stay as the fallback.

Fonts outside the legacy order are refused as before. The damaged-ToUnicode repair (`recovered_thai_map`) keeps its THSarabunPSK fingerprint, since it matches one exporter's broken output.

title: fix(xfa): SOM shortcuts, names out of scope, what the host stands in for
author: hikashop-nicolas
body:
## What this changes

Forms use a few names and calls that the host did not answer, so the script stopped at them: the SOM shortcuts as variables (`$.rawValue`, `$record.lang`), a field named once in the form but outside the script's scopes, and calls on objects the host keeps empty (`xfa.datasets.createNode(...)`, `xfa.layout.pageContent(...)`).

- `$`, `$form`, `$record`, `$data`, `$host`, `$layout`, `$template` and `$event` are variables a script may use (XFA 3.3 p. 91). `resolveNode` already took them in SOM expressions.
- A name the script uses that no scope reaches is the node of that name, when the form holds just one. A name the form holds more than once stays undefined, and the names in scope come first.
- Stand-ins for what the host does not model yet, which change nothing: `xfa.datasets` takes `createNode`, `resolveNode` (`null`), `resolveNodes` (empty) and `nodes`; `xfa.layout` takes `pageContent` (empty) and `pageArea` (`null`); nodes take `getDeltas` (empty), `getItemState` (`false`) and `setItemState`; a draw's `value` is its `<value>` element (`Rectangle1.value.rectangle.fill.color.value = …`); and a property stand-in can be called (`xfa.template.ui.resolveNode("#text")`), giving another one.

Part of #5009.

title: fix(xfa): names reach through unnamed subforms
author: hikashop-nicolas
body:
## What this changes

An unnamed subform is transparent to SOM names (XFA 3.3 p. 94, "Transparent Nodes"): its children are named as children of its parent. Here a name stopped at it, so `eForm.childhoodFunding.details.indicate.primary` was `undefined` when `primary` sits in an unnamed subform of `indicate`, and the script stopped with `cannot convert 'null' or 'undefined' to object`.

- `child_named` and `instances` look through unnamed containers (any node whose name starts with `#`), nested ones included, so a member read (`indicate.primary`), `resolveNode`/`resolveNodes` and the names in a script's scope all find those children. A repeated subform inside one has its instances and its `_name` instance manager as before.
- A named child of the parent itself still comes first, and `nodes` still lists the unnamed subform as a child, as before.
- The walk visits each child once and stops at the first match; it goes no deeper than `MAX_DEPTH`.

title: Fix macOS saves for PDFs with extended attributes
author: christianlappin
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #7050.

On macOS, saving over a PDF with nonempty extended attributes could fail with “Result too large (os error 34).” With rustix 1.1.6, a read into an empty buffer returns zero bytes. The save writer treated that result as the attribute size and allocated too little space.

The writer now queries the size explicitly before and after reading each attribute. Finder tags, binary and empty attributes, and resource forks survive the save. If a resource fork grows during the read, the writer refuses to replace the original with a partial copy.

Both affected crates now require rustix 1.1.6, which provides the size query APIs. Cargo.lock already resolves that version.

The Finder association reader uses the explicit size query as well. It can detect quarantine changes again and still skips association repair for values above its 64 KiB limit. The tests for larger attributes now read back and compare the actual bytes with a buffer sized to the fixture.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-platform -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-platform --locked` on macOS
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask parity`, and `cargo xtask wasm`

On base `d749fd80`, all 12 tests that failed in the [upstream macOS nightly](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/43143235183) passed locally, including editing, file watching, Finder associations, signing, and headless saves. The affected desktop suites passed 37 tests, and the automation suite passed 524 tests. After rebasing the same patch onto `175992b5`, all 32 macOS platform tests passed again, along with formatting and platform Clippy.

The macOS regression checks verify empty attributes before and after replacement, byte-for-byte preservation of a 65,537-byte Finder binding, and refusal when an attribute changes size during copying.

title: fix(print): 100 % asks CUPS for print-scaling=none, not only fit-to-page=false (#7207)
author: dnviti
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #7207.

PdfCraft applies every Size (fit, actual size, shrink, custom %) to the sheets itself and spools them as `Scaling::Exact`. craft-print sent that to `lp` as `-o fit-to-page=false` only. This legacy option does not override the IPP `print-scaling` job attribute, so a queue whose `print-scaling-default` is `auto` (the IPP Everywhere default) shrank A4 into its 3 mm hardware margins: 100 % printed at 97 %.

The fix is in craft-print: storytold/craft-libs#1193. Exact jobs now send `-o fit-to-page=false -o print-scaling=none`, and shrink-to-fit keeps `print-scaling=auto-fit`. This PR picks the fix up:

- `Cargo.toml`: `craft-print` and `craft-cms` point at `dnviti/craft-libs` `cebb31ca`. That commit is the craft-libs#1193 change cherry-picked onto the current pin, `60ede99`, so nothing else in craft-libs moves. `Cargo.lock` changes only those two `source` lines.
- `deny.toml`: allows that git source, with a comment saying why.
- **The fork pin is temporary.** Once craft-libs#1193 merges, the pin moves back to a `storytold/craft-libs` rev that contains it, and the `deny.toml` entry goes. That is why this is a draft.
- `crates/print/README.md`: says why both options are sent, whatever the Size.
- Tests: the `lp` argv contract tests in `crates/print/src/tests.rs` now expect `print-scaling=none`. A new `every_size_asks_cups_for_no_scaling` (`crates/ui-egui/src/workflows/print_ui.rs`) checks that the Print dialog's job for Fit, Actual, Shrink and Custom reaches `lp` with `fit-to-page=false -o print-scaling=none` and exactly one `print-scaling`.

What each backend gets after this change, for 100 %, custom % and fit alike:

| OS | Backend | Sent |
|---|---|---|
| Linux, BSD, macOS | CUPS `lp` | `-o fit-to-page=false -o print-scaling=none` |
| Windows | XPS print API, PrintTicket | `PageScaling` = `None` (unchanged; a driver that would scale is refused) |

title: fix(forms): Ctrl+Enter starts a new line in a multi-line text field (#7140)
author: Lcoding15
body:
Fixes #7140

## What this changes

In a multi-line form text field, Ctrl+Enter (⌘Enter on macOS) now starts a new line, as Enter, Shift+Enter and Alt+Enter already do, and the field stays open. Single-line fields and every other editor are unchanged.

**Root cause.** The field editor is egui's `TextEdit`, which starts a line only when the Enter key event's modifiers match its return key (`Modifiers::NONE`) logically. `matches_logically` tolerates Shift and Alt but not Ctrl/⌘, so Ctrl+Enter reached the field and did nothing.

**Fix.** `forms_ui::ctrl_enter_starts_a_line` runs before a multi-line field's editor is shown and, only while that field has the focus, hands it Ctrl/⌘+Enter (without Alt) as plain Enter. It reads egui's events itself, so it is listed in `NOT_PAGE_KEYS` with why: it is the field's own key, not a page key.

author: Lcoding15
body:
Fixes #7192

With **Print in grayscale** on, the print is now converted to grey before it is handed to the spooler on every system, not only on Windows. The driver is still asked for grey (`print-color-mode=monochrome` under CUPS), as before.

title: fix(ocr): main builds on Windows again (clippy needless_bool in program_is_executable)
author: FredApps
body:
pdfcraft's main CI has been red since 13 Nov 09:38 UTC. Every push fails `gate / gate (windows-latest)` in clippy, for example run https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/43430531001:

```
error: this `if` guard returns a bool literal and is followed by another
   --> crates\ocr\src\tesseract.rs:133:5
    = note: `-D clippy::needless-bool` implied by `-D warnings`
```

On Windows, `program_is_executable` loses its `#[cfg(unix)]` block and reads `if … { return false; } true`, which clippy's `needless_bool` (Rust 1.100) refuses. Linux and macOS keep the block and pass.

**Change:** `program_is_executable` is now `program.is_absolute() && program.is_file() && has_execute_permission(program)`. `has_execute_permission` checks the executable bits on Unix and returns `true` elsewhere, as before. Behaviour doesn't change on any platform.

`cargo fmt --check` is clean. I didn't run clippy 1.100 locally; this PR's Windows gate is the check. I found the failure through the nightly release dry runs and main's CI.

title: fix(ui): double-struck letters in interface text draw with an installed face (#7107)
author: asadosteaksnl
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #7107.

A bookmark title such as "Calculs dans ℝ" (what Typst and LaTeX's `\mathbb{R}` write) showed a box for ℝ in the Bookmarks panel. No face in the interface's font stacks has the double-struck letters: Inter and egui's default faces don't, and the general installed fallback on Windows is Segoe UI, which doesn't either. ∈, ∀ and ∃ come from the faces already there, which is why only ℝ and ℕ were boxes.

One more installed face is read, the way the per-script ones are (`crates/ui-egui/src/platform/system_fonts.rs`): the first candidate that has ℝ (U+211D).

| Platform | Candidates, best first |
|---|---|
| Windows | Segoe UI Symbol (`seguisym.ttf`), Cambria Math (`cambria.ttc`) |
| macOS | Apple Symbols, Arial Unicode |
| Linux | DejaVu Sans, Noto Sans Math |

**Where it goes in a family.** Last, after the general installed face, and not before it like the script faces. The faces that have these letters have much else too (DejaVu Sans has Arabic, Segoe UI Symbol has arrows and operators), and placed earlier would take over text the general face draws today, such as an Arabic file name on Linux. Last, it draws only what no other face has, so nothing that displays today changes.

That is why two existing tests change: `system_fallback_fills_missing_scripts` and `non_chinese_ui_keeps_the_installed_face_last` pinned the general face as the last entry of every family. They now allow this one face after it, and the second also checks that this face is the last.

It covers every place interface text is drawn (bookmark titles, tab titles, file names). Text drawn into a PDF is not affected.

author: hikashop-nicolas

## What this changes

A static XFA form keeps its own AcroForm, and until now none of its template scripts ran: the document kept no template after opening, its buttons did nothing on click, and changing a field ran no change, exit or calculate script. #5009 lists this as still missing ("Template scripts of static XFA forms", 204 of the 255 static forms in its survey).

**Static forms run their template scripts on their own fields.**
- On opening, a static form whose template has scripts keeps it (`xfa::template` already filters on that), and its initialize, calculate and ready scripts run, as for a dynamic form. The document notes it is static, so later edits keep the template (`sync_xfa_state` dropped it whenever the form had no PdfCraft layout).

Designer names them by the template's SOM steps; an unnamed subform is a `#subform[n]` step, which SOM leaves out, and its indexes count across those subforms; a page master's copies sit under the page set. So a field is matched to the next live field or exclusion group with the same named steps, in document order, and a page master's copies share the master's node. On the 57 forms below, 97.6% of the fields map.
- What scripts change reaches those fields:
  - a value is written to the XFA data, then to every field bound to it, as on dynamic forms;

title: Straighten scanned pages automatically, keeping the page size
author: liulian82
body:
## What

Scan & OCR ▸ **Straighten page** / **Straighten all pages** (`page_deskew`): measure a scanned page's skew and rotate its picture about the centre with a white fill. The pixel count does not change, so **the page keeps its physical size** — the same result ABBYY gives, without the page being rebuilt around a quad.

Two smaller things come with it:

- `page_enhance_camera` gains **`keep_page`** (default `true`): the straightened photo is centred in the page instead of the page becoming the quad's size. `false` keeps the old behaviour.
- The deskew commands report what they did in a dialog (what was straightened, by how many degrees, and which pages need a look by hand), because a 0.25° correction is not something you can see.

## How the measuring works

1. **Text lines** (`pdfcraft_ocr::preprocess::estimate_skew_detail`, already in the tree for OCR preprocessing) — trusted only when its peak beats 0° by the margin it asks for.
2. Pages whose text is too sparse to judge (a photograph with a caption frame) are scored on **their edges**: a Sobel edge map, each pixel voting for the angle that puts its row on a common line. A photograph's edges spread their votes; a rule's do not.
3. A page both estimators call flat is **straight**, not unknown. Only a page with a hint of a tilt of 1° or more, without the confidence to act on it, is reported for a human.
4. Every correction is checked on the **rotated picture itself**: if it does not leave less than 60% of the skew behind it is dropped, so a misread page is left alone rather than made worse.

## Two phases, and why

Pages are measured and rotated on the document **as it was**, in parallel, and only then put back one by one (`prepare_deskew` → `apply_prepared`, with `deskew_pages` doing both).

- A page is judged on the scan, not on a re-encoded copy of it: replacing page N re-serialises the document, and measuring page N+1 afterwards was measuring a different picture.
- Rendering and measuring are the whole cost…

title: Show the store's Friendly Name beside the subject in the Digital ID picker
author: Bra1nZ
body:
Fix #7232: the Digital ID picker shows only the subject and the issuer/expiration, so three PostSignum certificates made for several employers — the same subject for all — are told apart only by their dates.

**What this does:**

- `crates/sign/src/windows.rs`: the Windows listing now reads the store's Friendly Name for each certificate. rustls-cng 0.7.1 doesn't expose `CERT_FRIENDLY_NAME_PROP_ID`, so the store is read once more through **schannel 0.1.29** (new Windows-only dependency) and its certificates are matched to the listing's by the DER. Best effort: a store that can't be opened or a property that can't be read is no Friendly Name (`None`), and the picker falls back to the subject. The listing no longer puts the derived display name into the `friendly_name` slot — the field now carries the store's value.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/tools/sign_ui.rs`: a `display_name_for` helper (testable without a store) shows the Friendly Name beside the subject — "Jane Smith · Company A". Without a Friendly Name, or when it says the subject again, the name is the subject's as before; the existing truncation and hover behavior is untouched. The Windows branch of `refresh_os_key_store_ids` runs each entry's name through the helper.

**Tests** (the naming helper plus one harness test): two certificates with one subject stay apart by Friendly Name; a Friendly Name that repeats the subject (or is blank) adds nothing; without a Friendly Name the name is the certificate's as before; the picker rows show the Friendly Name beside the subject, two rows not one, and a long name is cut at the row's edge and said whole on hover.

**Out of scope / open questions:**

- PKCS #11 (Linux) keeps the token-level label — the per-certificate CKA_LABEL lands with #4968, not merged here.
- Granularity: duplicate DERs in one store share one Friendly Name (matched by DER); not measured with real middleware.
- The ` · ` separator — happy to change it.
- macOS Keychain labels are a separate follow-up.
